name: #Maneuver Warfare
description:
A two-player card game with customizable decks.  Cards feature multiple abilities and combinations, permitting players to explore "the OODA Loop" as a decision-making tool.

Victory is determined through 'Will'.  Every deployment of military force or combat losses reduces Will while taking the time to care for civilians and casualties (as well as victories) increases your Will.

name: ...But That's Only HALF the Story!
description:
The Party Game of HALF-GUESSES that's FULL of LAUGHS!

...But That's Only HALF the Story! uses a mechanic seen in games like Eat Poop You Cat and Scrawl, as players have to try to guess what is happening based on pictures provided by previous players.

The twist here is that you are together creating STORIES (not cohesive ones - frankly they're not going to make a helluva lotta sense - but stories nonetheless)!

Players are each handed booklets (that can be easily adapted to player counts from 4-12!), and then are given a story starter to write on the first page (e.g., 'The Mouse began sniffing the cheese in the trap'). They then each turn the page, and draw a picture of what they think should happen NEXT in the story (e.g., a picture of a mouse trying to pull the cheese OUT of the mousetrap). Next, all hand their books to the people clockwise from them, careful to only show the PICTURE that they drew. Players must now attempt to GUESS what is happening in the pictures, and write the description below them. Those players then draw what would happen NEXT in THOSE stories, and so on.

After a set number of pages (and stories that have likely changed plots and characters about seven times!), the stories are collected and read aloud! Laugh as plots that began with UFO's landing in the woods end up with werewolves winning their ballet recitals! Or tales of absent-minded zookeepers ending up starring time-travelling accountants!

...But That's Only HALF the Story!: give it HALF a CHANCE, and you'll DOUBLE-OVER with LAUGHTER!

—description from the publisher

1/1024  千分一機率 百分百同頻 - 香港原創桌遊：十條二選一難題，搵到同你最同頻既靈魂Buddy～ (或者發現自己係Kam L ？)

- This Ultimate Social Deduction Party Game is a revolutionary party game designed to foster genuine human connection, spark engaging conversations, and reveal surprising insights about your friends.

At its core, 1/1024 is a game of prediction and resonance. Players tackle 10 intriguing “this or that” questions, then predict whether their answer will be in the majority or the minority. But the true magic begins when you search for your BUDDY—another player whose answers align with yours for each question(or strategically differ, depending on your play!). After 10 rounds, the highest scorer is crowned the ultimate 'Resonator'. Yet the most thrilling quest is to find your one-in-a-thousand match, your soul-buddy, who shares all your answers. With odds of exactly 1/1024, that’s where the game gets its name… and its spark.

name: Yanari: The Witches Market
description:
Yanari: The Witches Market is a board game set in a magical market in the city of Yatamon within the world of Obojima. You play as a skilled witch racing to brew potions for customers as they go about their lives. The game is filled with new breathtaking art, as well as familiar potions and ingredients for the fans of Obojima. When you're done playing the game, you can learn more about the Yanari market by reading about it in Obojima: Tales From Yatamon.

During the game, players collect ingredient cards, then use these cards to brew the potions desired by specific customers. Brew the perfect potions to trigger customer bonus rewards — or simply brew them an acceptable potion to score a few points and access new customers. With two actions each turn, as well as a potential bonus cauldron action, you can generate combos for rewarding turns. Each of the five witch characters has their own unique ability, and the game includes many special ability cards and secret goals to enhance variability.

—description from the producer

name: 10 Pragas do Egito
description:
Inspired by a biblical story, 10 Pragas do Egito ("Ten Plagues of Egypt") casts players as governors of provinces along the banks of the Nile River in ancient Egypt.

The objective of the game is to deal with the losses and misfortunes caused by the ten plagues sent by God to the Pharaoh, who refuses to free the Hebrew people from slavery.

The core mechanic of the game is dice selection, and each round has three phases.

In phase 1, players use the dice to collect tokens that will develop their provinces, move their boats along the Nile River, accumulate income, gain favor with the Pharaoh, recover tokens from their discard piles, and free the Hebrews.

In phase 2 there is a dispute for new territories that will expand the borders of each province, bringing a series of benefits that can be immediate bonuses, permanent special actions or points at the end of the game.

In phase 3, the round's plague finally occurs, revealed on the board from the beginning. Each player must, in addition to paying tribute to the Pharaoh, manage the losses caused by the revealed plague.

10 Pragas do Egito is a game with a medium level of complexity, offering an immersive and challenging experience. As the rounds progress, minimizing the effects of the plagues becomes more difficult. This requires planning and makes each chosen action a crucial decision for victory.

name: 10 to Leave
publisher: Compound Eye Fox Studio; JJ Board Game
description:
10 to Leave is a card game in which players take on the role of mischievous mosquitoes aiming to disturb SleepKid. The goal is to skillfully maneuver your mosquito cards to avoid being swatted while minimizing penalty points. Players must use strategy, timing, and bluffing to outsmart their opponents and ensure their mosquitoes escape unscathed.

During the game, players take turns placing mosquito cards into queues near SleepKid. They can perform additional actions, such as peeking at cards or rearranging the queue order, or they can skip additional actions to wake up SleepKid at a favorable moment. When SleepKid wakes up, they begin swatting mosquitoes based on the total numbers on the cards in each queue — whether swatting with their bare hands, grabbing a defense tool, or, if the total equals exactly 10, missing completely and letting all mosquitoes in that queue escape safely.

At the end of the game, players add up the numbers on their swatted mosquito cards as penalty points. The player with the fewest penalty points wins, while the one with the most penalty points learns they might not be the best mosquito! It's a game of wit, strategy, and a bit of luck, perfect for those who enjoy lighthearted competition.

name: 10/12 Heart
description:
This is a trick-taking game for four players.
Each round, one player acts as the dealer, while the remaining three players compete to win tricks.
The dealer, who holds no cards, reveals one of their previously predicted game developments instead of playing a card.

—description from the designer

name: 1001: 40 Thieves
description:
The complex of 1001 games which occurred in one thousand and one tails and stories . the game is based on Alibaba and forty thieves story and you playing the role of the leader of the thieves who's planning to commit a huge robbery.

Your goal is to:
find the best spot with the best score to lead the thieves and collect point the more you gain thieves with the valued colors the more your chances of winning increases unless you encounter other characters which they might cause you real troubles.

name: 108 Outlaws
description:
Relive one of Chinese history’s classic epics in 108 Outlaws! In this immersive and challenging tableau-building card game, put together a motley troop of reformed criminals with different abilities and effects, embark on game-changing missions and write your own history. With 108 unique bandits to choose from, every game will be an all-new adventure!

The rules are simple - on your turn, either play 1 card or use 2 draw points to take cards. Earth Outlaws will give you special bonus effects when played, while Heaven Outlaws will earn you precious honour points at the end of the game. At any time during your turn, exhaust your outlaws to go on missions to earn honour points and bonus actions.

When one player has 12 Outlaws, the player with the most honour points wins the game!

—description from the publisher

name: 11 Days War: WWI East Front, 1918
description:
11 Days War is a two-player wargame, covering the final Central Powers offensive on the East Front, February to May 1918 (Operation Faustschlag), to include both the initial 11 days of offensive operations against the Bolsheviks and the ensuing pursuit in the Ukraine. The game pits the Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, their allies) against the Bolsheviks (or Reds, plus their allies). Additionally, there are third power forces called Greens which may come under the control of either player. There are three scenarios, representing different starting situations. The game system models warfare in the chaotic situation of the Eastern Front during the opening of the Russian Civil War. Further, the movement rules model the situation of operating in later Winter and Spring thaw, where railroads were vital.

Each game turn represents one to ten days of operations. Each hexagon (hex) on the map represents 60 kilometers (40 miles). Each unit represents anything from a brigade up to corps. Strategic markers represent specialized forces, such as airpower, and agitprop (agitation and propaganda).

name: Big Sur
description:
Cruise along California's State Route 1 on the Big Sur Coast Highway to check out the views and landmarks along the most scenic driving route in the world — or rather, invite others to cruise on the highway that you build over the course of play.

In Big Sur, players draft cards to use them either as resources to build new road sections or as the road sections themselves. Your linear path of cards will score for connecting terrain types and meeting other conditions. You can also add notable landmarks to your highway for other unique scoring conditions; these landmarks are based on actual scenic lookouts and locations on Big Sur.

name: Cup the Crab
publisher: Mandoo Games; 25th Century Games; Geronimo Games; Pixie Games
description:
On a peaceful beach, meet hermit crabs and octopuses building homes out of discarded cups and bottles. At just the right moment, claim the most luxurious stack of cups for your new home — or mix a bottle into cup stack to sabotage another hermit crab!

Players work together to build piles of Cup cards, but since victory points are scored from Cup cards, competition is fierce as everyone aims to claim the best piles using their Crab or Octopus cards. Bottle cards introduce an exciting twist, as only Octopus cards can follow them.
Each player begins the game with 14 random Cup cards, 3 Crab cards, 2 Octopus cards, and 2 Bottle cards. At the start of each round, players select three cards to play. Throughout 7 rounds, you must carefully plan your card choices.

—description from the publisher

name: 1490 Doom
description:
1490 Doom is a grimdark medieval skirmish game where players lead Doom Companies through vertical battlegrounds, fighting for survival against rivals and the rising death. Featuring brutal action-point movement, a modular 2’x2’ circular board, and campaign-driven progression, 1490 Doom blends fast tactical combat with desperate storytelling. Players battle in a dying world where every climb could be their last, fighting not only the enemy but the encroaching Creeping Death that claims the land below. The game supports solo, cooperative, and competitive modes.

—description from the publisher

name: 15 Jours en France
description:
Travel across France in 15 days and collect its most iconic sites, step by step!

What if you were just one step away from adventure?

15 Days is a set collection game that takes you on a journey to discover remarkable places in France.

Plan your itinerary to explore the country’s rich historical heritage, breathtaking natural landscapes, and the charm of picturesque villages.

Objective of the game: Earn as many victory points as possible by completing missions given by your Encounters.

With 15 Days, you embark on an adventure without a fixed route, but with one certainty: you have 15 days to make the most of your journey.
You won’t be traveling completely alone! Along the way, you will meet people who will share valuable advice on places to visit. These Encounter cards will guide you throughout your journey and help you claim victory.

Each turn, you can choose to:

Travel: Discover a new destination by collecting a Location card of your choice.
Meet: Draw from the Encounter cards to receive new recommendations.
Rest: Take a break to gain Step tokens.

The player who accumulates the most points at the end of 15 rounds wins the game!

In the year of our Lord 1589, the northern Rhineland is swept by a tide of savage persecutions and hasty summary trials for heresy, witchcraft, and lycanthropy. The County Tribunal, led by the controversial Prior Erastinuz Wetzel, launches numerous proceedings, accusing — primarily young women — of these crimes.

During one of these trials, the young Magdalena Roth, under pressure from the devout matrons of Blutfurt (The Pure), is accused of being a werewolf and sentenced to burn. Her execution is set for the evening of the second day of November, but Powerwolf — sons of the Legends of the Night and the Armenia Savage Army, defenders of the "Real Truth" — are determined to stop this injustice and break the bloody cycle unleashed by the Priory's fanaticism and its most feared servant: the relentless witch hunter Sebastian Rabenklaue, known as the Devourer of Heretics! Can you lead the Powerwolf in a desperate quest to save an innocent girl from a false accusation and a terrible fate?

1589 is a co-operative game in which players must lead the Powerwolf in a desperate quest to save an innocent girl from a false accusation and a terrible fate before the hour of Vespers (that is, within eight game turns). They will gather evidence of the Prior's fanaticism, act from the shadows to sabotage the execution — by extinguishing torches or stealing bundles — lure the witch hunter away from the pyre by drawing him into the forest, and sway the Pure to return to their homes, convincing them of the girl's innocence.

But beware as both the Pure and the witch hunter are deeply suspicious. Any false step may reveal the Powerwolf as accomplices to the accused...and earn them a place at the stake!

—description from the publisher

An 18xx game with a political campaign theme. Follows the 1830/full-cap branch of the genre.

Features include:

     Unique "exploratory committee" capitalization process.
     Tile manifest that is highly restrictive in type but permissive in amount.

name: 1811: Albuera Second Edition
description:
This famous Napoleonic battle is depicted in lavish historical details using the second edition of the innovative "Fix Bayonets!" tactical system. This is a hexagons & counters, battalion-level, combat simulation.

Components:

    One 44x29" mounted map.
    25 "Fix Bayonets!" markers, 160 3/8x3/4" markers, 205 1/2x1/2" markers, 265 3/4x3/4" counters & markers.
    One 16-pages Battle booklet.
    One 56-pages Rules booklet.
    Two identical 17x11" player aid cards.
    One 17x11" Turn & Tracks sheet.
    Three 11x8.5" Order of Battle sheets.
    50 Leaders & Events cards
    Two 10-sided dice

name: 1814: Empire's End
description:
Quick-playing and easy to learn game on the 1814 Sixth Coalition campaign in north-eastern France to defeat Napoleon.  Published as a bonus game in Against the Odds 2023 Annual, which was actually published in 2025.  The Coalition player represents the three major allied armies campaigning to capture Paris, while the French player represents Napoleon's army aiming to prevent it.  Players alternate marches in an IGO-UGO fashion, but must roll for reinforcements and movement abilities.  Combat is bloody for both sides unless one has an overwhelming advantage.  The game features forced marches at a strength point cost, the draining effects on the Coalition that may happen in screening French fortresses, and a very simple logistics model based on LOCs of a limited distance back to supply sources.  The Coalition player wins if the three armies are poised to capture Paris by the end of the game (Turn 7) or if Napoleon is captured.  The French player wins by avoiding this outcome. Rules are a page and a half with options for a short game (6 turns) involving 2 of the 3 Allied armies and a 3-player game (1 French player versus 2 Coalition Army players who alternate command of the 3rd Allied Army).  Requires the players to provide a single D6 to play.

The game contains 16 counters, a one-page map, and 2 pages of rules.

Part of the ATO 2023 Annual Bundle packaged with the La Bataille de Kulm featured wargame.

name: 1814: The Norwegian War of Independence
description:
During the Napoleonic wars, the Kingdoms of Denmark-Norway and Sweden found themselves on opposite sides, and fought several skirmishes in the border areas between the countries. This game deals with the 1814 campaign (a 1808 scenario will be provided later).

The game is a low-complexity wargame, with units representing battalions of infantry (about 350-400 men), batteries of artillery and squadrons of dragoons and cavalry (about 75-100 men). The Swedes have regular cavalry units like hussars, the Norwegians have dragoons and mounted jaegers. The Swedes enjoy better training, better supplies and more fire power, the Norwegians have advantages in mobility and skirmish ability, employing ski troops and light infantry (jaegers/sharpshooters).

The game map uses point-to-point movement and covers the border area between Norway and Sweden from Frederikshald (Halden) to Trondheim. The Swedish objective is to break the Norwegian lines and capture Christiania (Oslo), the border forts, (and perhaps Trondheim if they choose to try. The Norwegian objective is to prevent the Swedes from winning by inflicting enough casualties and delay the Swedes long enough to force negotiations to start.

The game was originally released in 2018 as a zip-lock, hex-based system with a print run of just 100. (https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/300929/norwegian-war-independence-1807-1814).
The game has been completely redesigned and is in reality a completely new game on the same topic, rather than a new version of the old game.

This is the first game in the Scandinavian Wars Trilogy from Pantero Games.

name: 1862 War in Virginia
description:
1862 War in Virginia is a solitaire game on the Civil War campaigns in Virginia. You take the role of the Confederates against a card driven Union Artificial Intelligence (AI) player to determine the outcome of the Civil War in 1862.

Players will have to fight along the four major fronts during 1862, The Valley, Overland, The Peninsula, and The James.  Can you hold the Union at bay --- and possibly take the war north of the Potomac?  The decisions are yours!

—description from the designer

name: 1899 DAIHAN
description:
In 1899, the first Seoul-Incheon railway operation began in the Daihan Empire (KOREA). The game is an 18xx series set in the Korean Peninsula, and in the basic rules of 1830, there is an additional system of gold, coal, rice, and ginseng transport, which were heavily leaked abroad at the time.

In 1899 Daihan, take the reins of a national railway company, founded with Korean capital. Your mission? To drive national prosperity through strategic railway expansion. Inspired by real-life historical endeavors, you'll navigate a world shaped by the Korean Empire's bold vision for industrialization. Compete with foreign powers vying for influence, each with their own railway empires.

The starting point is set, but the destination is yours to define. Will you forge a new path for Korea, or will you be swallowed by the tides of history?

name: 18España
description:
An 18xx game set in Spain. 18España is a game inspired by the basic mechanics created by Francis Tresham in the 70s for 18xx games. In 18España, players assume the role of railway investors, and they will buy and sell shares of railway companies in the stock market, searching for the most profitable. Usually, the greatest shareholder of a company will become its director. As director, the player will decide all operations the company will make, such as laying track and stations, running routes, managing the earnings and purchasing trains.
Play consists of an indefinite number of sets of rounds, these sets consist of a stock round and one to three operating rounds. The game will end when the most powerful trains come into play, and the richest player will become the winner, counting cash and the share portfolio.
In addition, as special features 18España has a lot of mines, two maps that differentiate the zones in which narrow and broad gauge track were built, mountain passes that connect these two maps, major and minor companies, takeovers, different type of trains, etc.
Although it is not feasible to do it completely, 18ESP has been designed to be as historically accurate as possible.
Finally, the game presents a variable randomized setup, which means the game will be different each time it is played.

name: 18RoyalGorge: The Rails of Fremont County and the Royal Gorge Wars
description:
18RoyalGorge is an 18XX game set in Colorado. The game covers a thirty-year time span from roughly 1870 to 1900. The game features eleven companies, incremental capitalization, a steel mill that provides track for the companies, and a gold market that players can own shares in. The train companies can be used to ship gold along their rails, and steel shares can be purchased by individual players as well.

Only two companies are available to start the game, and only five companies come into play in total. This means that with 3-4 players, some will be forced to play investor strategies initially.

The game also has many historical features, including a war over the rights to the Royal Gorge route, local coal mines, and more than a dozen private assets.

—description from the designer

name: 1918: A First World War Miniatures Game
description:
1918 is an alternating-activation historical tabletop wargame where players refight the battles of the last year of the First World War using miniatures. A typical game uses around 30-60 miniatures on each side and lasts 2-3 hours. The game focuses on combined arms (i.e. infantry, cavalry, tanks, artillery and aircraft working together) and the command challenges faced by junior officers leading men in the first truly industrial war.

Within the game, you will find:

     Epic setting - the last year of the First World War is crammed full of scale and drama. In 1918 the Kaiser's Germany makes one huge last roll of the dice, launching its Spring Offensive as fresh but inexperienced U.S. troops flood into France to support the war-weary British Empire and French Republic. The question is - who will crack first?
     Changing technology - by 1918, new innovations such as tanks, aircraft, light machine guns and accurate, indirect artillery were being used at scale to crack open the previously near-impenetrable trench lines. 
     Evolving combat - increasingly, success depended on fire and manoeuvre at the small unit level, and combined arms at higher levels. The days of 'running at machine guns' (if they ever really existed) were long over. 
     Varied battlefields - the battles of 1918 were highly mobile and varied; sometimes fighting took place in the open fields, woodlands or towns, at other times, in the shell-pocked trenches.



     Full colour, 215 page rulebook, illustrated throughout with period accurate artwork, high-quality miniature photography and licensed historical photography from the Imperial War Museum London.
     The 1918 Core and Advanced rules, including rules for vehicles,(off-board) artillery, buildings and fortifications. 
     Eight varied scenarios designed to represent the German Spring Offensive.
     Full force selection rules and four Force Lists: 
         American Expeditionary Force Infantry Division: AEF Rifle Platoon (Early) & USMC Rifle Platoon (Early), plus Battalion and Divisional Support.
         British Infantry Division: British Rifle Platoon & British Machine Gun Platoon, plus Battalion and Divisional Support.
         French Infantry Division: Rifle Platoon (Early) & Veteran Rifle Platoon (Early), plus  Battalion and Divisional Support.
         German Intervention Division: Intervention Rifle Platoon & Stormtrooper Platoon, plus Battalion and Divisional Support.
    


—description from the publisher

name: 1920: Nest of Eagles
description:
1920 is a two-player, intermediate complexity, strategic-level wargame simulation of the  "Polish-Soviet War" - the Soviet attempt to conquer Poland. Soviet and Polish forces engulf each other in swift campaigns, fighting on a large area stretching from Kiev and Smolensk in the East to Warsaw and Thorn in the West. Will the Red Army prevail and bring happiness and peace to the German and French working classes or will the Poles pull off a magnificent victory one can only describe as a 'miracle'? It only needs two players to find out an answer to this question in this exciting 2 hour wargame.

Players can learn the game via four short scenarios, being gradually introduced to the game mechanics and quickly able to grasp the accurate concept of lines of control, surprising rail transfers, and morale advantages and understand the strategic ramifications of the theater of war. Further rules cover army morale advantages, revolutionary mobilization organized by the hated Soviet political police the Cheka, the torn loyalties of the Ukrainians, fighting on both sides of the front and the formation of the Polish Volunteer Army.

A plethora of formations and units appear in the game: the Latvian Rifles, the dreaded Budyenny's Horse Army, counter-revolutionary Russian, Belorussian and Cossack troops, various Polish formations including the Siberian Brigade, support units such as tanks, flotillas, armored cars and above all armored trains, which were extensively used in the campaign.

name: 1975 White Christmas
description:
1975: White Christmas takes you to the final hours of the Vietnam War. On April 29th, 1975, the song White Christmas was broadcast over the radio as a coded signal to launch Operation Frequent Wind — the largest helicopter evacuation in history. As the commander of an aircraft carrier, you'll need to coordinate rescue missions, prioritize objectives, and evacuate as many civilians as possible before Saigon falls.

The game unfolds over four rounds, each divided into three phases: action selection, operations, and a final bidding phase for a powerful special helicopter. In the first phase, players draft action cards into their hand while simultaneously performing actions based on the card’s position in the row. These same cards must then be used in the second phase to carry out key actions such as rescuing civilians from rooftops, upgrading their aircraft carrier, deploying helicopters, and completing secret missions.

Strategic planning, resource management, and careful timing are key to scoring victory points and winning the game.

—description from the publisher

name: 1ers Contacts
description:
Based on an extraterrestrial signal

Rumors say a flaming spaceship was seen falling through the sky... Confirmed! I had to eject after a tiny little mistake during what should have been a stealth reconnaissance mission. Thankfully, I was able to activate my spaceship’s cloaking ability before it crashed...

The mothership was warned of my difficulties and is on its way to retrieve me. It won’t arrive for several days, and once it gets here it can’t linger—humans haven’t been deemed ready for contact with alien species yet. I’m going to have to hide until I’m brought home. 
That won’t be easy, especially since my arrival was noticed: the Agency is hot on my trail!
The Agents know the place much better than I do, they’ve got cutting-edge detection arrays, and they’re not afraid to get wet—whereas I can’t swim... 
I’ll have to cover my tracks to get out of here!

In 1st Contacts, one player is the Alien. They must escape and fulfill a special mission. They move around on a secret map, committed to avoiding easy detection, and they know how to cover their tracks.

All other players are Agents who must try to catch the Alien before it escapes! They use their abilities and deduce the Alien's whereabouts based on the answers they receive.
The Agents can use detection arrays and deduction tokens to track the information they're given.
Only by communicating and combining their actions can the Agents catch the Alien before it escapes.
The Alien wins by avoiding capture and fulfilling their special mission.

The Agents win only by capturing the Alien, which they do when one Agent finishes their turn on the same tile as the Alien.
1ers Contacts is made up of six Secret Files. Each Secret File plunges you into a new first contact with a different alien race. The Secret Files offer a variety of gameplay experiences, and are infinitely replayable.

—description from the designer

name: 2 Die 4
description:
2 Die 4 is a solo roll-and-write game played with two dice.
The aim of the game is to best fill out a grid of boxes to score as many points as possible.

But there's a twist: The grid obeys Sudoku rules, that is to say only one of any given number can appear in any row or column.
If you can't fill in the numbers right, you need to put in an X.

—description from the designer

name: Grand Central Skyport
description:
In Grand Central Skyport, you want to efficiently operate your airship station and attract the most prestigious tycoons to your city. During the game, you attract new airships to your skyport, and each airship has a color and an initial slotting movement. Try to maneuver your airships to group them by color so that they stack to score increasingly more points. Unfortunately, with each new ship entering your station, its movement will trigger the rearranging of previously placed airships, so ideally you can race other skyport owners around a central rondel to choose the incoming airships that are best for you.

Drafting tycoons to your skyport will bring unique advantages in manipulating your docked airships, as well as additional scoring opportunities at the end of the game.

Do you have the operational skills to handle the airships arriving at your station as efficiently as possible? If so, you may very well crown yours the grand central skyport.

name: 20 Bucks for That?!
publisher: Blue Orange (EU); Ghenos Games; MEBO Games
description:
20 Bucks for That?! is a lighthearted party game of wild inventions and surprisingly strategic price estimation. Each round, one player becomes the Presenter and reveals a random everyday object along with two unexpected characteristics — for example, a spiky, backlit sofa or a laser-shooting, candy-scented parachute. Through improvised storytelling, the Presenter explains why this bizarre item exists, answering any questions from the other players and building a shared (and often hilarious) narrative around the object.

Once the table is satisfied with the story, all players — including the Presenter — secretly write down how much they believe the object is worth. When revealed, the estimates are arranged in ascending order. Points are awarded based on how close each player’s guess is to the median value: players score a number of points equal to the smaller count of estimates above or below their own. Extreme high or low guesses score nothing, rewarding balance over boldness.

After each round, the role of Presenter passes to the next player, and new objects and characteristics spark fresh absurd creations. The game ends when a player reaches a number of points equal to or greater than the number of players at the table. The player with the highest total score wins (ties are shared). To succeed, players must combine imagination with intuition — crafting convincing stories, reading the room, and aiming for the sweet spot between too cheap and outrageously overpriced.

—description from the publisher

name: Hits & Outs
publisher: itten; 25th Century Games; Playte; Popcorn Games
description:
Hits & Outs (ヒット＆アウト) is inspired by the strategic battle of wits between the pitcher and the batter. Reproducing baseball's thrilling moments without having to keep track of player statistics or the results of every pitch. As the name suggests, there are no balls or strikes in this game, only hits and outs!

In each inning, players take turns at the plate and on the mound. When batting, you get hits and can move your runners by correctly guessing the base where the pitcher has hidden the baseball. If the ball was hidden at second base and you find it, you hit a double and can move your runners two bases.

When pitching, keep the batter from reaching base and scoring runs by fooling them three times. Each incorrect guess is an out. The player with the most runs at the end of the game wins!

—description from the designer

name: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea
description:
20,000 Leagues Under the Sea is a thematic exploration game inspired by Jules Verne’s classic novel. Players take on the roles of crew members aboard Captain Nemo’s submarine, the Nautilus, navigating between surface and depth maps in search of discovery, danger, and wonder. As they explore sunken ships, hunt marine creatures, and uncover the mysteries of Atlantis, they compete to earn points through smart decisions and spatial strategy.

The game unfolds over sixteen simultaneous turns. Each round, players secretly choose one of three character rows, then move the Nautilus using the indicated movement points. On their sheets, they draw discoveries and score for islands in line of sight, sunken ships, seaweed forests, treasures, and hunted cetaceans. If multiple players choose the same character, a hazard is triggered—unless one holds the rotating Conseil card, which grants temporary immunity.

With unique character bonuses, a dedicated solo mode, and layered end-game scoring, the game rewards thoughtful planning and tactical movement. The double-sided map system invites players to dive and surface at key moments, enhancing both depth and replayability. 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea offers an elegant, compact, and immersive experience for 1 to 5 adventurers.

name: 2001: A Space Odyssey | The Board Game
description:
In 2001: A Space Odyssey | The Board Game, players must fight to survive as HAL sabotages the mission to Jupiter.

One player controls the malevolent HAL, while the rest of the crew works together to outwit the AI and shut it down in a 1-vs-many format. HAL doesn't play fair, and he'll take multiple turns to wreak havoc on key systems. It's up to the crewmembers, each with their own special abilities, to complete three logic sequences in the HAL Core and save the mission before it's too late, that is, before HAL terminates any three systems or the life support goes down.

One hundred years after World War 2, military conflict has broken out in Taiwan waters.

In 2045 AD, China launched a special military operation against Taiwan. The outlying islands fell, as well as the navy and air force. Taiwan now faces a land war on its own territory.

You will play as party leaders from all walks of life in Taiwan. Depending on your allegiances, you can choose to stand and fight, or support unification. Regardless of whether Taiwan's resistance succeeds or China carries out its military unification, whoever has the highest score after the war will win the game.

2045 includes 6 starting identities, 33 Characters, 33 bases, 21 events, 48 ​​missions, and comes with a free downloadable app to assist with game scoring. Immerse yourself in a fresh new game universe which is part science-fiction and part allegory!

On the battlefield, there are no permanent allies, but neither are there permanent foes. Create and witness history through this game! If only war were limited to games…

—description from the designer

1945年に起きた台湾大空襲から100年。『2045』は、2045年に発生した人民解放軍（PLA）による台湾攻撃を題材にした正体隠匿ボードゲームです。

PLAの猛攻によって台湾軍は空・海におけるイニシアチブを失い、PLAが台湾に上陸してくるところからゲームは始まります。プレイヤーは台湾内に潜む勢力のリーダーとして、台湾の未来をかけてPLAと戦います。

ただし、勢力の中には台湾を守ることよりも、状況に応じて旗色を変える日和見主義な勢力や、中国との統一を目論むスパイ勢力も潜んでいます。

プレイヤーは、自分がどの勢力であるのかはゲーム内アイテムの「アイデンティティーパスポート」を受領するまでわかりません。果たして、あなたは台湾を守る勢力なのか、それとも戦況を見て利益を得ようとする勢力なのか、あるいは敵のスパイなのか──。どの勢力であるかを隠匿しつつ、迫りくるPLAを排除することで功績を集め、勝利を目指しましょう。

本作では、プレイヤーの行動は基本的にはPLAの排除にあります。しかし、状況によってはPLAが優勢になるかもしれません。日和見的立場を取る勢力であれば「勝ち馬の尻にまたがる」ことを選ぶでしょうし、スパイ勢力であれば自らの存在を明かして自らの立場を逆転させるでしょう。こうした状況の中で、自分の勢力が勝つための最良の選択肢を選ばなければなりません。

誰を信じ、誰を討つのか──。台湾の未来はプレイヤーの手に委ねられることになります。

《2045》遊戲的時間序，將是登陸戰開始的十天，台灣存亡在你一念之間

西元 2045 年，二戰台北大空襲 100 年後，中國對台發動特殊軍事行動，而在外島陷落，海空遭殲後，台灣面臨決定命運的登陸戰。台灣的情勢，將決定友邦是否馳援，請記住，遊戲終局僅有一位勝利者，無論台灣抵禦成功，或是中國完成武統，誰在戰後擁有最強優勢，才是真正的贏家。

在遊戲中，你和其他玩家是競合關係，你必須持續思考，而遊說、背叛與妥協，是為了勝利必須付出的代價。

當時，台灣分裂為六個勢力，你將獲得一本「勢力護照」，可在自己回合揭露勢力身分發動特殊能力。殲滅最多共軍的玩家，在台灣勝利時將成台灣英雄；但若共軍勝利，則會淪為台獨頑固份子遭受嚴懲。
 六大勢力政治光譜不一，但你可以嘗試各種玩法，甚至逆勢而為。就是算「政府軍」或「台灣自衛隊」，也可能在最後一刻選擇投共而獲勝；或者「促統會」最終決定抗命，全力殲滅共軍，在台灣勝利時，戲劇性成為無間道般的台灣英雄。遊戲的多變性就如現實局勢，詭譎難測。

登陸戰開始時，共軍將部署於北、中、南部外海登陸場，共軍分為「散兵」和具有各種強勢技能的「共軍精銳」，當共軍精銳登場時，必將造成強大衝擊。如何應敵並減少己方損失，與其他玩家拉開差距，將考驗你的謀略和膽識。

共軍的戰略目標為攻佔所有台灣據點，你必須透過「對敵工作」介入共軍行動，才能引導戰況至對你有利的局面。台灣抵抗意志愈高，友邦愈可能前來支援；反之若快速淪陷，境外勢力將裹足不前。

《2045》將台灣本島分為六大地區，各區核心城市為：台北、新竹 、台中、台南、高雄、花蓮。核心城市由台灣、共軍把持，將決定遊戲結局。

在終局時，共軍若占領 5 座以上核心城市即取得勝利，反之則為台灣勝利。遊戲另附有可供免費下載的 APP，加速在遊戲終局時的計分流程。

name: 21X
description:
21X is an algebraic blackjack game in which most cards have an X in their value, with you getting to choose an integer value for X that makes your card total as close to 21 as possible without going over. What's the best hand you can make when your cards are 24/X and 6-4X?

Some cards have fixed values, and others contain an N variable that equals the number of cards you have in front of you.

name: Kilauea
description:
In KILAUEA you will represent a Mo'o, the lizard-like spirits of Hawaiian folklore, and you will build Tiki columns to worship Pele, the goddess of volcanoes.

Kilauea, by David Bernal and Ferran Renalias, is a game with very simple rules, but with a scoring system that forces players to always be aware of how the number of Tikis of each color changes in each volcano area, and to manage wisely where and which ones to place in their personal island.

During your turn, you will be cutting down in the forests or building Tikis, either in the volcano area or on your own Island. When the first and third forests are emptied, each volcano area will be scored by multiplying the value of each color by those you have in the corresponding area of your personal Island. But be careful! The score of each color will be in constant evolution during the game and your opponents will try to maximize their score by taking yours!

The mechanics are very simple: we will move around the volcano on the same island with a rondel mechanic and, once we have reached our destination, we will be able to do one of three possible actions: 
 - Cutting down Tikis in the Forest
 - Build Tiki in the Volcano 
 - Build Tiki on our Island.

At the moment the first and third forest is completely cut down, you score each area of the volcano, scoring 1 VP for each piece of the highest tiki column and 3 VPs for each piece of the rest of the columns. These points will be multiplied by the number of tikis of the corresponding color in each area of your Personal Island. In the final scoring some extra points may be scored.

-description from publisher

name: 24/7 Rally
description:
24/7 - Rally is a clever and accessible cardgame for families and friends, played on a colorful 24-hour clock of circular layed out cards. 
Use dual-color hourcards to move pawns forward — but every move affects someone else too! Work together as a team or play individual, engage in the rally to reach midnight first. Easy to learn, full of surprises, and fun for players from age 10 and up. (or 7+ if you play without the special event cards)

—description from the designer

name: 24SEVEN: The Sleepless World
description:
24SEVEN: The Sleepless World is a deck-building game with engine-building mechanics, based on “Machine Age”, 2nd book of the upcoming saga “2064: Memories of the Future”.

In a restless, mechanised world ruled by Machines aiming for maximum efficiency, supply chains and production lines never stop. From mines and metal refineries, down to factories and assembly workshops, the world is now an unstoppable 24/7 manufacturing unit outputting robots, supercomputers, servers, infrastructure, vehicles, and anything else under the gray skies of the late 2020s.

Collect minerals and scrap, refine them into metals and shape them in your forge. Assemble finished humanoid and android robots to take the lead in your city’s development, boost your operations and supercharge your path to peak efficiency.

Mechanics:


     Engine-building
     Resource management
     Set collection
     Card drafting
     Abstract Strategy


- Game under development, from the author of ARDEVUR: The Game of Resources -

—description from the publisher

name: Pulitzer
publisher: Tranjis Games; 25th Century Games; Giant Roc
description:
You take the reins of a team of American investigative journalists during the early stages of the turbulent decade of the 1970s. The Vietnam War, the Pentagon Papers, the Watergate Case... You will work to maintain the prestige and sales of the newspaper while dedicating the necessary resources to complete the investigation of the big story. The one that will win you the Pulitzer and etch your name in the history of journalism forever.

Pulitzer is played over 8 rounds, divided into 2 phases: Placement and Resolution.

In the Placement phase you will place your Journalists hidden in the different areas of the board to publish exclusives, do work outside the newspaper, document or investigate in the field.

When the players have placed their Journalists the simultaneous phase of Resolution begins. You may flip all the Journalists on the board to show their values and you will check who prevails in each of the zones. In addition, you will try to gather the necessary evidence to advance with the report on your personal investigation board in a unique way never seen before in this type of Eurogames. Each new piece of evidence uncovered will bring you closer to the Pulitzer.

At the end of the eighth round, you will see who has managed to pass the Pulitzer committee's minimum requirements and participate in the final scoring. Whoever has scored the most points for their newspaper's Reportage, Prestige and Reach will win the coveted award.

Pulitzer includes an advanced mode for 1 or 2 players and several game modes to accommodate the game experience to the group.

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Tomáis las riendas de un equipo de periodistas de investigación norteamericano durante los primeros compases de la convulsa década de los 70. La Guerra de Vietnam, los Papeles del Pentágono, el caso Watergate… Trabajaréis para mantener el prestigio y las ventas del periódico mientras dedicáis los recursos necesarios para completar la investigación del gran reportaje. Aquel que os permita ganar el Pulitzer y grabar vuestros nombres en la historia del periodismo para siempre.

Pulitzer se juega a lo largo de 8 rondas, divididas a su vez en 2 fases: Colocación y Resolución.

En la fase de Colocación dispondréis vuestros Periodistas de forma oculta en las distintas zonas del tablero para publicar exclusivas, realizar trabajos fuera del periódico, documentarse o investigar sobre el terreno.

Cuando todas las personas han colocado a sus Periodistas se inicia la fase simultánea de Resolución. Voltearéis a todos los Periodistas sobre el tablero para mostrar sus valores y comprobaréis quién se impone en cada una de las zonas. Además, trataréis de reunir las pruebas necesarias para avanzar con el reportaje en vuestro tablero de investigación personal de una manera única y nunca antes vista en este tipo de eurogames. Cada nueva prueba descubierta os acercará más al Pulitzer.

Cuando finalice la octava ronda, comprobaréis quienes han conseguido superar los requisitos mínimos del comité del Pulitzer y participan en la puntuación final. Quien haya obtenido más puntos sumando Reportaje, Prestigio y Alcance de su periódico, será quien se alce con el preciado galardón.

Pulitzer incluye un modo avanzado para 1 o 2 jugadores y varios modos de juego para acomodar la experiencia de juego al grupo.

name: 3 Magi
description:
Embark on an enchanting adventure in 3 Magi, a captivating game that follows the three wise men on their legendary trek across the desert to meet the newborn King. 3 Magi offers a unique gaming experience, weaving together elements of resource management, worker placement, card hand management and crafting. Immerse yourself in the timeless narrative of the 3 Magi as they seek Jesus the King.

Players assume the roles of the Magi. Manage resources, skillfully craft gifts, navigate the terrain with the help of the navigation board and encounter characters that may aid the Magi's mission.

As the Magi, players must gather and combine resources to craft gifts for the King, each worth victory points. Players travel across desert tiles, entering iconic locations such as “Jericho", "Jerusalem", "Herod's Palace" and "Bethlehem". The tiles have unique actions allowing players to choose a particular route and resolve actions. Use the navigation board for bonuses & extra actions. Manage & combine your cards on hand to further your Magi in the game.

Once a caravan makes it to Bethlehem, the fame ends and points are totaled.  The player with the most points wins.

—description from the publisher

name: 3 Tricky Pigs
description:
3 Tricky Pigs is a thematic trick-taking game for 3-5 players. Players take on the role of the 3 little pigs, where the laziest pig will win each trick if there is no wolf around. However, if a wolf is in the trick, the highest card will win.

Players earn points by making correct bids on how many tricks they will win each round. The player with the most points at the end of 4 rounds is the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: RA and Write
description:
RA and Write is a flip-and-write game built upon the foundation of the classic RA from acclaimed designer Reiner Knizia. It features the same art and thematic style as the 25th Century Games new edition of the board game.

The game is played over three rounds, known as Kingdoms: The Old Kingdom, The Middle Kingdom, and The New Kingdom. Over the course of the game, players advance different aspects of their civilization by filling in spaces on their scoresheet. Each Kingdom ends immediately once three Ra cards have been revealed, then the round is scored.

The game ends after the third round (the New Kingdom) has been scored, and the player with the most points wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Ra: Sun God Edition
description:
Deluxe SUN GOD EDITION with Traders Expansion.

Invoke the power of the sun god!

Take on the role of a line of ancient Egyptian kings, ruling over your vast kingdoms. You will work to improve the culture of Egypt and the strength of your royal lineage, all while following the will of the gods.

Time is limited, so you must wisely decide how to spend your days.

In the end, will you have pleased the gods enough to move on to the Field of Reeds in the afterlife?

One of Reiner Knizia’s most loved games, RA is a classic auction game for 2-5 players, now in a new edition with revised artwork and deluxe components.

This version has the acrylic tiles and includes the Traders expansion inside the box.

2-5 Players | Ages 12+ | 30-60 Minutes

name: 30 to Go
description:
A team shedding game inspired by Hearts and Cribbage.

Players will play cards from their hand trying to diffuse the bomb (play to exactly 30) or they'll try to blow up the bomb (play over 30) so they can shed out their hand of cards faster.

Each round starts with some card passing, so players know a bit of what their opponents or teammate has in their hands.

The goal is to have the fewest points, but only the lowest score on a team is counted, so rushing and blowing up to shed out might be worth it.

—description from the designer

name: Red Letter, Yellow Letter.
description:
Red Letter, Yellow Letter! Red Letter, Yellow Letter! Red Letter, Yellow Letter!  It’s a party game of saying words! Words with letters in them! And saying those words when they fit in a category. And when they have the right letters in them. And that’s basically it!

Players compete to be the first to yell out a word that matches the restrictions from the cards on the table.  For example:  Name a type of wood without the letter O in it.

The fastest correct response wins the point.

—description from the publisher

name: Sand Art
description:
Sand Art is a unique entry in the "___ & write" style of games. During play, you move back and forth along a linear track of actions on the workbench, gathering different colors of sand in your supply, mixing primary colors of sand into new secondary colors, and pouring them into bottles to create patterns and images that will attract customers in your shop. Creating the most unique and visually pleasing bottles will earn you the most points.

This "move & fill" game carries the spirit of "roll & write" games, while also appealing to fans of pattern-building and abstract games.

name: 4 Years to Mars
description:
The space race is heating up once again, and governments have issued their challenge: Develop a viable Mars program in four years. The catch? Your government will supply only a fixed amount of funding per year. The rest of your budget and the success of your mission depend on the success of the projects you fund...but you're not the only one in this race!

4 Years to Mars is card-based, with individual player boards to track mission objective progress. The game can be played solo, co-operatively or competitively.

In the first of four program years in the competitive game, players spend their "space bucks" (Spucks) on funding research in their four space station experiment bays. In the following years, players fund projects to further their mission objectives and provide additional funding for the next program year. Research topics reduce the cost of corresponding projects. In the base game, action cards can be played to help your program as well. After four years, government funding ceases, then the player with the most points wins, with points being awarded for progress in each of the eight mission objectives. A bonus is given to the first and second players to complete the entire objective.

In the co-operative game, all players work together to complete the eight mission objectives before the end of the four program years. In order to advance a mission objective, players must work together to fund projects that create sets of mission objective icons. For example, to advance your rover mission objective once in a five-player game, you must have a set of five cards with mission objective icons. Unlike sets for the competitive game, cards can be used for multiple icon sets.

In the single player game, the goal is also to complete the eight mission objectives before the end of the four program years, but some cards are removed from the market after every round, so you must plan for the next year.

All of the projects in the game are based on real NASA projects and products.

-description from designer

name: 5 копеек (5 kopecks)
description:
What do "sun" and "moon" have in common? Maybe the word "sky"? Or perhaps "circle"?

In the cooperative party game 5 копеек ("5 Kopecks"), players must quickly fill the gaps in a circle of words to win. The game includes sixty numbered round cards ("coins") that can be written on. At the start, five silver coin cards (numbered 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60/0) are placed in a circle, each labeled with a starting word chosen by the players. Twelve of the remaining gold coin cards are placed face down in the center—these must be correctly positioned in the circle as the game progresses.

On your turn, secretly check the number on the top gold coin card, then come up with a word that hints at its correct placement among the existing cards. You’ll need to think fast—the other players have only a short time to agree on where the new card fits based on your clue. As more cards are placed, the gaps between numbers shrink, making it harder to position new cards accurately.

The team wins if they correctly place the last card before losing all three of their starting error markers.

5 Kopecks also includes a competitive team variant, as well as alternative co-op modes: a "first error" version (using all gold cards but ending after any mistake) or a longer game (using 18 gold cards).

name: 52 Duels
description:
52 Duels is a print and play duelling game set in the fantasy world of 52 Realms: Adventures. Using only a standard poker deck, you’ll launch attacks, block damage, use items, and level up your hero’s unique skills. Whittle down your opponent’s deck first to win, but be careful, they’ll have some tricks of their own up their sleeve.

With an ebb and flow similar to trading card games like Magic: The Gathering or Star Wars: Unlimited, 52 Duels offers an affordable, yet deep battling experience that will keep you coming back to the table to try new plays and strategies. Character skills and abilities are contained on one sheet of paper, and health is tracked by how many cards are left in your deck. There is no cutting or crafting required, and you’ll just need a couple of decks of playing cards to play the game.

—description from the designer

name: Wine Cellar
publisher: 25th Century Games; Gém Klub Kft.; Grok Games; Old Dawg
description:
Let's auction off some wine! You and your rival sommeliers have decided to face off to determine who is the best. Each person will take on a client, building a cellar that ages well and is suited to the client's tastes.

Over the course of eight rounds in Wine Cellar, players will collect wine bottles to create a cellar for their client. Bottles will be arranged to create a timeline for the order in which the wine will be consumed. Each bottle is worth different amounts based upon where it is in the timeline. Players will also receive points based on their client's preferences for wine type and country of origin.

—description from the publisher

name: 69: A Nice Card Game. About Numbers.
description:
69 is a fast-paced card-matching game for 2 to 6 players. The rules are simple enough for any age, but for some reason, players below a certain age wouldn't stop giggling when we demoed it, so we recommend playing only with serious, mature adults.

The 69 deck is mostly made up of number cards (0-9), in six suits. The 6 and 9 of each suit are interchangeable. Use them for whichever number you want, depending on which side is up.

There are also three wild cards (with three of each in the deck):

     Wild: a simple wild card that can count as any number and suit.
     Lock: a wild card that also stops another player from stealing your cards.
     Scramble: a wild card that lets you rearrange everything on the table. 


How to play:

     Deal: Every player starts with ten cards, and the dealer flips one card face up on the table.
     Play: On your turn, try to play cards from your hand onto cards on the table to make a stack. The cards in a stack need to all have different suits, and need to be either all the same value or form a run (cards in numerical order).
     Punt: If you can't play a card from your hand, pick up the top card from the deck and play it. Form a stack if you can (and want to), or leave it on the table to start a new stack.
     Capture: If a stack gets three or more cards, you capture it! Take the cards and put them face down in front of you...unless someone steals it!
     Steal: If another player can add legal cards to your completed stack, they can steal it from you...unless someone else steals it from them!
     Score: Once someone plays the last card from their hand, the round is over. Score points for every card you captured, and lose points for every card left in your hand.
     Repeat: Play another round, adding to your score. The first player to get 69 points wins the game!


—description from the publisher

name: 6x6 Tales: Time of Giants
description:
Dive into 6x6 Tales: Time of Giants, a fully standalone solo adventure by Alexandr Sakharnyi—no prior experience with 6x6 Tales required (though if you’ve played the original 6x6 Tales by Jack Darwid, you know how much fun it is!).

Chart your own path, manage items, scrolls, and quests, and resolve battles and dungeon encounters—all within your Journal Book. Each playthrough is randomized, ensuring a fresh and unique journey every time.

This adventure introduces:

Four full weeks of adventuring

New monsters and encounters

Exciting scrolls and items

The combined artistry of Christopher Eisert and Dean Kutha brings the world to life, making every encounter a moment of wonder, suspense, and peril.

Prepare for a fresh solo quest—the Time of Giants is here, ready for you to explore.

—description from the publisher

name: Bullseye
description:
Bullseye is played in rounds, and in each round, players give clues about a word or phrase that will be guessed by the archer. Each clue is written one letter at a time. The twist is that before you add another letter to the clue, everyone passes their clue clockwise, which means you now have to add a letter to your teammate's clue instead of your own. This means that not only does the archer need to guess the word or phrase based on partial clues, but you need to intuit which clues your teammates started so that you can continue them.

Bullseye is a game that keeps everybody guessing!

—description from the publisher

name: 7 Leagues
description:
Magical course with the magic boot!

7 Leagues is a strategic and magical card game for 2 to 6 players. Round after round, create your journey by placing terrain cards in front of you and drawing them according to the weather. Create the best synergies, activate combos, and form boots to score maximum points.

—description from the publisher (translated)

Course féérique à la botte magique !

7 Leagues est un jeu de cartes stratégique et féerique pour 2 à 6 joueurs. Tour après tour, composez votre voyage en posant des cartes terrain devant vous et en repiochant selon la météo. Créez les meilleures synergies, activez des combos et formez des bottes pour marquer un maximum de points.

—description from the publisher

name: 7 Wonders Dice
publisher: Repos Production; Gém Klub Kft.; Hobby Japan; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
Guide one of the seven largest cities of antiquity to prosperity in 7 Wonders Dice. During the game, you will construct a wonder that defies time, make scientific advances, develop commerce, manage your resources, and handle your gold reserve prudently — all while keeping an eye on neighboring cities since ignoring them has a heavy price!

A game plays over a series of turns during which you will use dice to construct your city. At the end of the game, count up all of your points to see who has the highest score.

name: 7th Inning Stretch
description:
"People ask me what I do in the winter when there's no baseball. I'll tell you what I do. I stare out the window and wait for spring." - Rogers Hornsby

Don’t worry, Rogers, your wait is over! 7th Inning Stretch is a unique solo card-drafting and dice-chucking baseball game where you get to be the whole organization - GM, manager, and players - as you build your team, set your lineups, and then play out the final innings of a few key games each season. If you do well enough in these regular season games, you can qualify for the playoffs and earn a chance to bring home the ultimate prize!

Each season you will draft your team, set your schedule, arrange your lineup, and then roll and modify dice to determine the outcome of offensive plays and defensive innings. Decisions like choosing your clean-up hitter, deciding when to steal bases, and selecting the right pitcher are crucial to your success.

Featuring engine-building and push-your-luck mechanisms paired with a nostalgic 20th-century baseball card aesthetic - not to mention a special duel mode where you and a friend can play out a full 9-inning game in under an hour - 7th Inning Stretch allows you to chase all of your childhood baseball dreams without breaking a sweat!

—description from the publisher

818 (Eight Eighteen) is a fun, fast paced trick-taking game of strategy and luck designed for the whole family!

The deck consists of 66 cards in 5 suits numbered 1-13 and one "Clincher" card.

The game is played over a series of 15 rounds and the person with the highest points at the end is the winner.

Gameplay:
The dealer deals a different number of cards depending on the round, which follows the pattern of 8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1-2-3-4-5-6-7-8.

After each hand is dealt, the top card of the deck is flipped face-up to determine the trump suit for the round.

Players review their cards and decide how many trick’s they think they can win. Starting with the player left of the dealer and continuing clockwise, each player in turn order verbally announces their bid. 
However, the total number of tricks proposed to won by the players cannot equal the number of cards dealt for the round.

For Example: 
It’s the first round of play and 8 cards have been dealt to five players.
Four players have already announced their bids which total 5 tricks.
It is the dealer’s turn to bid, they cannot bid 3 (5 + 3 = 8).

Play begins with player left of the dealer and proceeds clockwise. Subsequent players must follow suit if able. The only exception is the “Clincher” card which can be played at anytime and wins the hand no matter what.

Scoring:
If a player hits their bid exactly, they take the number of tricks won as points plus a bonus of 10 points.

If a player misses their bid, they take the number of tricks won as points but do not receive the bonus 10 points.

If a player bids zero and succeeds, they receive the 10 bonus points (no tricks were taken).

name: A Battle, Furious, Bloody, Repulsive, Crimson, Gory, Boisterous, Manly, Rough, Fierce, Unmerciful, and Hostile
description:
This tenth anniversary celebration of the Shields & Swords series of medieval battle games collects and revises scenarios from all nine previous games, and includes two new scenarios. A dry-erase map allows for twenty-four total scenarios, and leaves the door open for potential expansions in the future.

—description from the publisher

name: A Boar, Crab, Dung Beatle
publisher: キューハチドッグ (Que Hachi Dog); Olin Studio
description:
In a chaotic contest of animals with strong opinions and no fixed rules, players race to empty their hands but the rules of play change as often as the cards themselves. When you're stuck and can't play, there's only one solution: change the rules! Whether you're guided by a boar’s brute logic, a crab’s sideways thinking, or a dung beetle’s questionable taste, this game embraces absurdity and spontaneity in equal measure.

A Boar, Crab, Dung Beatle is a fast-paced, rule-shifting shedding game where players take turns playing cards to the center pile, aiming to be the first to run out. But when a player can’t make a legal move, they dynamically rewrite the active rule for card strength or interaction. It’s a game of adaptation, chaos, and outsmarting both the cards and the ever-mutating system.

—description from the designer

name: A Bridge Too Far
description:
Take part in one of the most dramatic airborne operations of the Second World War.

In this paragraph-based game you step into the role of a Polish paratrooper from the 1st Independent Parachute Brigade, dropped into the chaos of Operation Market Garden. Through his eyes you will relive the tension, the courage, and the doubt of a soldier fighting far from home.

Every choice matters. Do you follow orders to the letter, or trust your instincts in the heat of battle? Do you risk lives to hold the line, or pull back to save your men? Your path will be shaped by hard decisions, moral dilemmas, and the unforgiving reality of war.

This is not only a story of battles fought, but of loyalty, sacrifice, and the resilience of those who believed their struggle could change the course of history.

—description from the publisher

name: A Calamity of Witches
description:
A Calamity of Witches is a coop-competitive card game where players squabble amongst themselves as members of the four Witch Houses, represented by their unique and powerful Sigils.

Save members of your House (cards of your own suit) by winning tricks with the highest card, or play the lowest card to trigger that card’s suit specific power and help turn the tides in your favor. Make deals to avoid the brunt of a House’s Attack, grow your power, and ensure the Calamity doesn’t consume you all.

Every Witch House must save a certain number of members of their House by the time the cards run out, otherwise the Calamity takes root in the losing houses, and complete corruption becomes inevitable - AKA everyone loses. If every House survives, then the House with the highest number of cards collected of their own Suit wins.

—description from the designer

name: Lobby Snacks
description:
The reels are set to roll, and the movie is about to start, but wait–don't forget the refreshments!
The fresh popcorn, candy, and soda are tempting, but your eyes may be bigger than your wallet.
Will too much munching leave you ticketless? Eat some snacks, but not too much or you'll miss
the flickering magic of the silver screen.

Lobby Snacks is a trick-taking game where success comes at a price. When you win a trick, you score a prize plus the cards played by other players, but you keep your own card face up in your “spent pile.” Each round, the player who spent the most scores nothing.

—description from the publisher

name: A Dam Too Far: 617 Squadon's Dam Buster Raid, May 1943
description:
Operation Chastise, commonly known as the Dambusters Raid, was an attack on German dams in the Ruhr industrial area. Carried out on the night of 16/17 May 1943 by 617 Squadron RAF Bomber Command, later called the Dam Busters, using special "Bouncing Bombs" developed by Barnes Wallis, who also oversaw the modifications of 19 Lancaster bombers specially adapted to carry the “Upkeep” bouncing bomb ordinance.

The player allocates 19 randomly chosen crew members to their Lancaster bombers. These crew members are the best of the best, and consist of the Front Gunner, Pilot, Navigator, Engineer, Bomb Aimer, Wireless Operator and Rear Gunner. These crew members can help at certain stages of the mission. The outward-bound journey will be a matter of pushing your luck with the aircraft for the best results. Will you risk trying to get a better attack value or lose an aircraft from flak or flying so low you hit power cables? On the bomb run it will be the challenge of balancing height, speed and position as you approach with the available “Steady” counters to achieve the perfect bomb release point. It’s all about accuracy; if your bombers come in too fast or too low, they will miss the target. Taking a bomb run will be a higher or lower risk choice. How many bombs will the dams take before they are breached, how many dams can be destroyed or damaged, and how many aircraft will make it back on the homeward bound journey? All these factors will determine if the mission was a success or a failure. Can you do better than the historical counterparts?

—description from the designer

name: A Lava Story
description:
In A Lava Story, you take on the role of a young volcano with a dream: you want to become the world's most visited tourist site.

Use tectonic plate movements to gain lands and increase your volcanic activity, let volcanic ash rain on land to make it fruitful, grow plants and lure in animals to make beautiful national parks. Or rely on rough natural beauty, raise mountains and rivers, geysers or hot springs. Whatever you do, try not to erupt once you have lured in all the tourists or you might scare them away again.

In this bag building, push-your luck, tie-laying game for 1-6 players you have to keep track of your volcanic activity as well as of your islands beauty. You play through 4 eras of eruptions and if your island features the right tiles, you'll get many rewards. After 45-60 minutes, the last era will be over and players will get one last chance to bring tourists to their island.

—description from the publisher

name: A New Order of Samurai: Clash of Sengoku Daimyos, 1570-1580
description:
September 7, 1568, Oda Nobunaga sent troops from Gifu of Mino province. In just over one month, Oda Clan conquered Kyo, suppressed Kinai, and helped Ashikaga Yoshiaki, the last shogun, to restore formal authority. Sengoku Japan was shaken dramatically.

Beneath the brief peace, however, a new storm was gathering. Powerful daimyos were waiting for their opportunities. It was rumored that the shogun, unwilling to become Nobunaga's puppet, was secretly sending letters, pulling up an "Anti-Nobunaga Alliance." The next decade witnessed the most spectacular and turbulent years of Sengoku Period. Finally, in 1578, with the sudden death of Uesugi Kenshin and the overwhelming victory of the Oda navy in the Second Battle of Kizukawaguchi, the unification of Japan could never again be stopped.

The lineage of A New Order of Samurai could be traced back to Here I Stand and Virgin Queen. From that basis, the game adds sub-systems and components unique to the 16th century Japan, including different clan traits, legendary generals and skills, provinces and vassalization, merchants and intelligence, and the dreadful Ikko-ikki (large-scale rebellion by the lower class).

A card-driven, panoramic multiplayer war game set in mid-late Sengoku Japan, A New Order of Samurai covers this period's major political, military, diplomatic, and economic events. 3 to 6 players will control major Sengoku powers: Oda Clan, Takeda Clan, Uesugi Clan, Tokugawa Clan, Mori Clan, and the Hongan-ji. Each power has its own unique way of winning. You must form diplomatic alliances, fight against each other, recruit troops, deploy your army, and overwhelm opponents with strength and strategy. The daimyo who wins these clashes will hold sway over Japan's future.

—description from the designer

Updated by the designer:

https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=3113630206  Here is the Tabletop Simulator (TTS) module for this game. Anybody is warmly welcomed to download and play.

name: A Normal Card Game
description:
What the heck is A Normal Card Game?
It’s a party-like combat card game where you summon quirky creatures, equip powerful items, and cast game-changing spells to outsmart and outlast your friends and family! With no deck-building required, it’s quick and easy to set up for any game night.

How does it work?
The goal is simple, be the last player with HP remaining! Players draw from two shared decks, mixing and matching cards to create their ultimate hand. Summon creatures to fight for you, boost them with items, and unleash spells to turn the tide of battle. And if you’re desperate, you can even sacrifice your own HP to draw more cards, but be careful, you might drain too much!

Why is it different?
Unlike traditional card games, A Normal Card Game thrives on unpredictability and chaos. There are no complicated deck-building rules, and everyone draws from the same two piles, ensuring that every match feels fresh and fun.

—description from the designer

name: A Pirate's Word
description:
Centuries ago, the legendary Blackbeard sailed the seas, leaving behind a treasure so vast it was nearly impossible to hide. Nowadays, gems of immeasurable value appear daily on the nearby islands. You’ve come seeking riches—but you’re not the only greedy pirate on the island.

The game lasts five Days. Each day, new Gems are placed on the Islands, which sit between each pair of players. Everyone has 3 cards in hand: 2 green (for cooperation) and 1 red (for betrayal). You'll secretly choose one card to place face down on the Island to your left, and another on the one to your right.
If both players choose green, they split the Gems. If one goes green and the other red, the red player takes all the Gems. But if both play red, no one gets anything.

Everything is up for negotiation—but will you trust a pirate’s word?

—description from the publisher

name: A Place for All My Books
description:
A Place for All My Books is a puzzley book gathering, sorting, and organizing game in which players arrange stacks of books in different rooms of their apartment as personal projects. When done, they can admire their accomplishments and gain their rewards – not least of which is renewed energy, which they can then spend to head out into the village - to pick up more books!

Over nine rounds, players visit locations and gather books to complete objectives and earn Victory Points. The player with the most Victory Points wins.

The organizational puzzles are easy to accomplish, with the challenge being how many of them you can accomplish all at once to optimize each "admire" action.

A Place for All My Books includes a solo mode in which you must beat the game's rival: Penelope Eveready, an untiring extrovert who seems to be grabbing all the books you had wanted.

—description from the publisher

name: A Song of Ice & Fire: Tabletop Miniatures Game – Brotherhood Without Banners Starter Set
publisher: CMON Global Limited; Dark Sword Miniatures, Inc.
description:
The Brotherhood Without Banners stands for the people of Westeros — nothing more nothing less. It's a band of outlaws, both great and small, who have grown quite weary of great houses playing their game of thrones. The "mighty and noble" go to war as titans and end up grinding the common folk to dust beneath their feet. Thus, the Brotherhood arose, being not merely rabble, but comprised of men-at-arms and skilled knights and archers, capable of plying their deadly trade in service to Lord Beric Dondarrion, the so-far unkillable Lightning Lord. With other leaders such as Thoros of Myr, Tom of Sevenstream, Ravella Smallwood, Lem Lemoncloak, and advised by the Ghost of High-Heart, the Brotherhood is a force that cannot be lightly dismissed by even the greatest of houses. A reckoning long in the making is at hand! Let the mighty tremble when the masses march to war!

The Brotherhood without Banners Starter Set lets you add this group to your games of A Song of Ice & Fire: Tabletop Miniatures Game.

name: A Song of Ice & Fire: Tactics – Battle of the Trident
publisher: CMON Global Limited; Dark Sword Miniatures, Inc.
description:
A Song of Ice & Fire: Tactics is a two-player skirmish miniatures game in which players construct their warbands and engage in battles across multiple thematic scenarios. Set in the expansive world of A Song of Ice & Fire created by George R. R. Martin, this game transports players to various eras of Westeros, where strategic warfare unfolds with each move.

Battle of Trident is a skirmish set that includes pre-assembled miniatures, terrain, and rules, allowing players to dive into the action right out of the box.

name: A Very Civil Whist
description:
A Very Civil Whist is a Strategic level historical board-wargame that puts you in the middle of one of the most turbulent periods in English history. In this game, you'll play as either the Royalists or Parliamentarians, two opposing factions vying for political, economic and religious control of England. The game is based on the classic card game German Whist, but with a few twists – you'll be able to play with leaders and assets that represent key actors of the first English Civil War. With strategic play and a bit of luck, you can lead your faction to victory and secure your place in history.

Taking place in the mid-17th century, the first English Civil War was a time of great political and social upheaval. The conflict pitted the supporters of King Charles I against the supporters of Parliament, who sought to limit the monarch's power and establish a more democratic government. As you play A Very Civil Whist, you'll experience the tension and drama of this critical period in English history. Will you be able to rally your troops and secure victory for your faction? Or will you fall to your opponent and be consigned to the dustbin of history? The fate of England rests in your hands!

—description from the designer

name: A Way Back Home
description:
The Tzerzurians have returned to Zura after they had been locked behind magic seals for millennia. Over time they had turned into myths, then into Whispers of a long lost past, but are now back to this world. Nobody, including the Tzerzurians, recalls their place in the world anymore though.

"A Way Back Home" is a tactical push your luck game with a bag building mechanism that can be played on multiple boards. The base game includes one double sided board per player with more to come over the next few years. Each board not only expands on the story, they also each have a unique twist in how the game plays and may add new components to interact with.

The core game play remains the same across each board: players try to link light sources for different purposes across up to six different paths while managing penalties, the contents of their own bag, as well as the contents of the general pool.

The game includes:


     120 crystals in 6 different colors
     4 double sided player boards
     4 drawstring bags
     6 character cards for board "B"


—description from the publisher

name: A Wayfarer's Tale: The Journey Begins
description:
A Wayfarer's Tale is a game of journey and discovery. Players share dice rolls, but navigate their own individual maps, collecting treasure and avoiding monsters as they explore new locations.

Turns are taken simultaneously as players chart their own course racing to discover new worlds.  Player share a pool of dice to enlist a companion with variable powers to help them.

When a player visits the last town on their board, the game ends immediately. The goal is visit all the cities on your map and fill up as many spaces on your board to score the most points. Total points are based on the number of towns you visit, the treasure you discover, and the number of monsters you encounter.

—description from the publisher

name: Observatory
description:
The night sky is divided into 88 Constellations. From those 88 Constellations, Asterisms are created as additional patterns. You and your fellow astral cartographers will map the night sky in this roll and write family friendly game. Each Constellation and Asterism card contains details about the pattern, providing for an educational experience as well.

On each player's turn, they will roll all of the dice. The active player is the only one to use the larger dice to plot a star. All of the other players, including the active player, will choose from the three smaller dice by picking two numbers for their chart coordinates and one for its research value.
