The Constellation and Asterism cards have their own mapping patterns you must draw in your grid. As you complete cards, you earn victory points and other bonus actions.

Your research area is where you will use one die per turn to advance your equipment and funding resources.

Rounds are based on the number of players and final scoring is tallied from your completed constellations and asterisms, as well as any funding you have unlocked in your research hub.

—description from the designer

name: A-Mazing Game of Gears 'N Guffaws
description:
Step into the ever-shifting underbelly of a crumbling clockwork city, where factions clash, alliances twist, and the gears never stop turning.

A-Mazing Game of Gears 'N Guffaws is a semi-hidden role, asymmetric strategy game of shifting alliances, sabotage, and steampunk absurdity.

Beneath a crumbling clockwork city, three secret factions battle for control of a labyrinthine maze of rotating tiles and unstable machinery. Players take on the identities of mad inventors, saboteurs, and cunning opportunists, navigating a dynamic hex-tile maze that reshapes itself as the game unfolds, revealing them strategically to activate powerful abilities or conceal their motives just a little longer. Every role is unique, every turn is unpredictable, and every player might be bluffing. Whether you’re a loyal 'Gizmologist', a destructive 'Rabblerouser', or a greedy 'Opportunut', every turn is a chance to outthink (or out-scheme) your rivals.

With clever mechanics and gleefully chaotic expansions, Gears 'N Guffaws rewards adaptability, timing, and a good sense of humor. The game includes two modular expansions and can be played as Semi-Cooperative, Fully Competitive or Solo (includes a three-variant solo mode).

Build the maze, bluff your loyalty, and let the chaos spin in your favor!

name: Abbates
description:
Embark on a historical journey within the venerable walls of Bornem Abbey, the centerpiece of our new board game, Abbates. Players assume the roles of abbots competing to acquire the most prestigious collections of stained-glass windows, precious artefacts and ancient manuscripts from the monumental Abbey library.
Set against the atmospheric backdrop of the Abbey, the game unfolds on a dynamic 3x3 grid, representing the central courtyard encircled by the hallways through which the abbot figurines navigate. Players move their abbots along these corridors, strategically selecting rows or columns from the grid to acquire the most coveted artefacts. Utilizing abbot cards, players can execute sequences that emulate "The Rule of Saint Benedict." Successfully aligning their plays with these revered guidelines rewards players with powerful bonus cards, enhancing their ability to dictate the course of the game.

Scoring in Abbates demands both tactical acumen and foresight, as players must assemble their collections according to specific patterns to amass points. However, strategic depth is added through the penalty system, where players must minimize the point discrepancies between the Cistercian Chapter points on their played and collected cards, adding a layer of challenge that reflects the historical complexities of monastic life.

—description from the designer

name: Star Gazers
description:
You are space enthusiast and artist, looking through your telescope at the universe and drawing what you see as a mural on your wall. You take photos, trace constellations, observe rocket launches, and journal every experience along the way to craft your beautiful artwork.

In Star Gazers, you select tiles and tokens from the universe board that represent a collection of different observations you make through your telescope. Those tiles and tokens are then placed into your mural to create different connection points and features to score a variety of drafted objectives. Create the most beautiful and well-designed mural to celebrate your love of the cosmos!

—description from the publisher

name: Three Sisters: Harvest Edition
description:
Three Sisters Harvest Edition is a strategic roll-and-write game about backyard farming. It is named after an Indigenous agricultural technique still widely used today: planting three different crops close together. Corn provides a lattice for beans to climb, the beans bring nitrogen from the air into the soil, and the squash provides a natural mulch ground cover to reduce weeds and keep pests away.

Three Sisters Harvest Edition features all the award-winning gameplay of the original edition plus a twelve-chapter campaign mode with new content, gameplay, and components. The campaign is for both group and solo play. The new content can also be used as expansion modules for an individual game of Three Sisters.

Three Sisters Harvest Edition is a fully standalone replacement for Three Sisters.

name: Abra Chadabra
description:
In this competitive game, you try to obtain your magic diploma!

Push your luck by making the first spell you learn in every standard magic school: making rabbits appear! But beware of the black cats and other magic objects.

At your turn, you simply have to choose one card between four decks with different probabilities going from easy to chaotic.

Abra Chadabra is created in partnership with the festival Alchimie du jeu of Toulouse for the 2025 edition whose theme is magic. A portion of the profits is donated to the festival for each sale of the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Abroad
publisher: 1 More Time Games; Geekach LLC; Niza Gams
description:
You've always wanted to travel the world, and now you have a chance to do it for a living! A position has opened up at the most prestigious travel guide publisher, and you have four weeks in Europe to show that you are the right person for the job. Visit stunning locations, meet locals, get insider tips, collect postcards from famous attractions, and maybe even visit a festival on weekends or fulfill an adventure worthy of a bucket list.

Europe awaits you in Abroad, and you need to figure out how you're going to make the most of the opportunity. You'll start with a hand of seven location cards from a deck of 240, as well as a postcard with an endgame goal. Start in your choice of Europe's ten regions.

The game lasts four rounds, with each round consisting of seven days. Take turns in a round until you have spent all of your days. On a turn, you can stay where you are, or travel to a new location by plane (by spending money) or by train (be spending energy).  Then take one of four activities:


    Write about the location.
    Rest, spending a day and three cards to earn 2 energy.
    Plan, spending a day to draw three cards.
    Carry out an activity, spending as many days as listed on a card in your hand matching your region. 


After four rounds, score all your postcards based on whether you met their primary or secondary goal, then see who has logged the most points as evidence of their awesome travel skills.

For the solo game of Abroad, you compete against a bot that always has three location cards in a row that determine where it travels next, although you spend money or energy to discard its locations and send it elsewhere.

name: Absolute
description:
In Absolute, players make sets of 3 or more cards whose sum equals zero.  Swap cards with played sets, add cards to your sets, or regroup your sets for more points. Cards are colored blue/white for positive numbers or red/black for negative numbers.

Play Description: Each turn you draw a card from the deck or discard pile. You can swap cards up to 2 cards in your hand with up to 2 cards in any one set on the table  (yours or another player's). This can help get you get the numbers or suits you need for better hands, decrease the value of another player's set, or both.

Then you can play your own sets of cards, add cards to your existing sets, or play cards to regroup your sets for more points.

Play 3 sets and discard your last card to "go out" to end a round.  The player with the most points after 3 rounds wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Abstractable
description:
Dive into a world of artistic fun with Abstractable. Challenge your creativity and guesswork skills as you try to decipher what your friends are crafting from a unique collection of magnetic shapes.

Get ready for a game night filled with creativity, laughter, and friendly competition. Who will be the ultimate artist?

—description from the publisher​

name: Abuelas con hachas
description:
Abuelas con hachas ("Grannies with Axes") is a fun card and strategy game inspired by nostalgic summer memories in rural towns, where grandmothers used axes for all sorts of tasks.

In this game, players compete to collect axes and chickpeas, which they trade for granny cards, aiming to score the most points by the end of the game. With simple yet strategic mechanics, the game unfolds over three rounds, each divided into turns.

Players place cards from their hand into axe rows, using chickpeas to boost their position. This determines the pick order when axes are distributed at the end of each round. Collected axes can be exchanged for granny cards, which award points and require specific combinations of axes and chickpeas.

The strategy lies in managing your resources and positioning yourself ahead in the rows to grab the best cards. The “cutting in line” mechanic adds a competitive twist, allowing players to jump ahead if they have more chickpeas in hand. Axe and granny cards have different values and requirements, encouraging careful planning each turn.

At the end of the game, points are scored based on collected cards and remaining chickpeas, rewarding both strategic play and efficient use of resources.

Abuelas con hachas blends resource management, player interaction, and a uniquely thematic design. With easy-to-learn rules and quick gameplay, it’s a light game packed with strategic depth.

—description from the designer

name: VNTYPL8S
description:
VNTYPL8S is a party game in which you get to create your own vanity license plates. Each player receives an owner and requirement card, then uses those topics and characters to guide the creation of their plate. Players then reveal their vanity plates so that other players can try to guess which owner matches which plate. Those who are the first to guess correctly and the plate creator will both earn points.

—description from the publisher

name: Aces & Armor
description:
Take the role of a general (United States, Russia or Germany) in this complex (but easy to learn) strategy game. In addition to attack strength and armor of your troops, their tactical setup, combat experience, damage and terrain have a decisive influence on the outcome of the battle. Since each unit brings its own strengths, you must cleverly assemble your army to win the victory over your opponents.


     Cooperative or competitive
     Solo mode
     Detailed miniatures with many different unit types
     High re-playability due to the variable start setup
     Complex combat system that depends on type of unit, combat damage, experience, strategic formation, terrain and armor (known from highly rated game “Trench Club”)


—description from the publisher

name: Aces High
description:
Aces High is a Tactical  level board-wargame for 2-4 players that recreates dogfights in the skies of the First World War between 1916 and 1918!

The game represents 25 different historical aircrafts, belonging to the 2 sides: Central Powers and Entente.

Each player takes control of a plane and with his own deck of Maneuver Cards controls its movements to try to make his opponents retreat, or rather, shoot them down.

Basing on the speed of their aircraft, each player chooses which maneuvers they will carry out in the current turn.

The players reveal them simultaneously, then, one at the time, move their planes accordingly. If an opponent comes into your sights, you can shoot him to try to take him down!

All the planes in the game have a deck composed in a certain way to match the maneuvering possibilities of each plane.

In addition to individual aerial duels, the game also features a "Campaign" mode, where through a series of missions you will gain experience to become Veteran and Ace and therefore be able to add the coveted Acrobatic Maneuvers to your deck of maneuvers!

description from publisher

name: Across the Briny Sea: Omen Game 4
description:
Across the Briny Sea | Omen Game 4 is a standalone card game for two players. Like the other new Omen games, this standalone game features 22 Unique Unit cards and 6 Unique Krater cards, each offering new Traits and abilities, and is fully compatible with all new (and future) Omen games.

In Omen games, players alternate taking turns gaining and spending Coins to play Unit cards, each with their own unique effects, to their side of three different Cities (each comprised of two City/Krater cards) to trigger effects and sack the Cities; vying to the winner by having the most points when the game ends.

When a City is Sacked, the player with the most Strength in that City gains one of that City's Krater cards. When both of a City's Kraters have been claimed, that City is Razed. When all three Cities are Razed, the game ends and players score points for the Krater Cards and Coveted Units in their hand, as well as the broken Krater Cards and facedown Triumph Units in their Rewards.

Rushing to Sack the Cities, playing towards completing Triumphs, and hopefully hoarding Coveted Units in your hand; Omen offers several paths to scoring points and impressing the deathless, watching Olympians.

While this game reimplements Omen: A Reign of War, it is not compatible with any previous Omen: A Reign of War title or expansion.

—description from the publisher

name: Action!
description:
A worker placement and management game themed around the production of movies.

You play as a film producer. Ambitious, you dream of joining the pantheon of the cinematographic world thanks to the scripts that you will have carefully selected and the actors chosen with care for each of them.


     Hire Assistants, actors and actresses.
     Buy scripts and sets.
     Take loans at the bank to invest in your movies.
     Produce and send movies to the box office.
     Influence the box office with marketing.
     Earn money and prestige during the awards ceremonies.


Places are limited and the competition is merciless. Who will be able to stand out from the crowd at the awards ceremonies, by stepping into the spotlight, and forever mark the history of the 7th Art?

—description from the publisher

name: Actualize This
description:
Welcome to earth, human! We wish you the best luck on your search for Enlightenment. Be wary, for the high-dimensional spiritual forest around you is full of life, including predators and parasites. Navigate your way to Self-Actualization, choosing your practices, relationships and guides wisely.

This is an existential strategy card game where you manage your limited time to "Learn Lessons" (draft cards), complete needs on your personal player board, as well as fulfill secret life quests that you reveal at end of game.

You begin life with some needs already met: air, physical health, and immune health. You begin lacking many more: Control, Clothing, and Shelter, etc. On your personal board you see your needs arranged in a triangle with rows. Each unmet need has a number and a color representing their cost in Gold, Awareness (red), or Virtue (black).

Each of your cards represents how you can spend your time: Time is represented in blue, and an arrow shows how you can spend that time to gain another resource.

The game is unveiled iteratively in 4 un-boxings, called the 4 Incarnations. Incarnation 1 introduces the basic concepts, Events, Quests, Lessons (Careers, Guides and Practices). Incarnation 2 introduces Relationships (a type of Lesson), the Psychosis Event and Lessons that carry a Psychosis Risk. Incarnation 3 introduces mechanics for long-term planning, and Incarnation 4 introduces the concept of Self-Actualization and Spiritual Alignments

—description from the designer

name: Acuarella
description:
Acuarella is a competitive game where you’ll place polyomino tiles with gorgeous cat illustrations. You must add these tiles to your board following the placement rules, trying to collect as many pigments as possible by placing adjoining tiles in the right combinations.
You can also gain opportunity cards that make the game a fun and challenging competition for cat-like artists!

—description from the designer

In Acuarella, a vibrant polyomino placement game featuring adorable feline illustrations, you'll become an ingenious cat artist. Your mission: to create the ultimate masterpiece to support the many kitties living near an urban park.

To achieve this, you'll combine your Cat tokens (polyominoes) on your personal canvas, mixing them to generate new colors (pigments) that will earn you valuable points.

The challenge and fun are intensified with Opportunity cards, which add unexpected twists to the game. Plus, you'll aim to capture adorable "cat photos" to fill the small empty spaces on your board, as each unfilled space subtracts points from your final score.

As a finishing touch, the Cat tokens you've used on your board will transform at the end of the game, allowing you to assemble adorable kitties on the table for extra points.
Get ready to unleash your creativity and help these
furry friends!

name: Canvas Critters
description:
Creative critters from the Mosaic Forest have gathered at the annual art festival being held at Gallery Grove. The famous Bianca Blanco (well, infamous really, but no one would dare say that within her considerable earshot) is curating a new show at the gallery and only the best pieces will earn the privilege of being displayed in her highly exclusive showcase gala. Do you have what it takes to stand under the critical eyes of Bianco Blanco or will your creative works fall flat? Let the judging begin!

In this party-style game, 2 to 6 players draft multi-colored, animal-shaped, meeples to create the most eye-catching mosaics based on the theme chosen by the Curator for that turn. Players secretly receive ribbons from the Curator at the end of each turn, awarding them secret points. Once each player has had a turn as the Curator players flip over their ribbons and the player with the most points wins!

name: Adamastor
description:
As the captain of a fleet during the Age of Discovery, you have been chosen by your king to explore uncharted lands and map the edges of the known world. Each game presents a new challenge where you’ll need to guide your crew with wisdom and resolve, all in service of your kingdom’s glory. Fierce winds and sudden storms will test your leadership, while the cards in your hand will help you maintain morale and steer your crew across the seas.
Though hardships may wear you down, they also teach you valuable skills to overcome the trials ahead. Victory lies in reaching your destination. But beware! Failure awaits if morale crumbles or your crew turns against you.

Adamastor is a hand and tableau management game built around multi-use cards, with an optional story-driven campaign mode. Events trigger based on icon combinations, bringing harsh challenges—and occasional rewards. As you play, trauma cards accumulate, abstracting the crew’s growing despair and escalating the difficulty. Whether in single sessions or the linked campaign, every voyage tests your resilience in this brutal age of sail.

—description from the publisher

name: Add To Playlist
description:
NO MUSIC KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED! - Don’t know your Olivia Rodrigo from your Olivia Newton-John? No worries. This isn’t a music trivia game so no music knowledge is required.

HOST THE BIGGEST PARTY TO WIN - Guess which song and prompt fits the person on the other team to gather the party-loving Disco Blocks. The side of the dance floor with the most Disco Blocks at the end wins!

GET TO KNOW YOUR FRIENDS (EVEN MORE) - Whether you’re outing your own guilty pleasures, or taking a trip down memory lane, this is a music game that sparks conversations and makes hilarious memories.

—description from the publisher

name: Addam's Family Cemetery Drag Racing
description:
The Addams Family heads out to the most haunted cemetery in the United States, St. Louis Cemetery, for some drag racing fun. The cemetery is well known to be haunted by Voodoo Queen Marie Laveau and screams can be heard from her tomb, among other tombs which bring out the spirits of the dead. The family will be racing their family car and hearse car and are ready to dual it out. A simple dice mechanic for two players which includes a fun theme for some racing excitement, and a Addam’s Family fun solo competition.

—description from the publisher

name: Adorable Demons: An Infernally Cute Card Game
description:
Enter the delightfully chaotic world of Adorable Demons, a fast-paced card game where you and your friends compete to become the ultimate Demon Lord! This family-friendly game is packed with strategy, humor, and irresistibly cute demon characters. Easy to learn but filled with tactical depth, it’s the perfect addition to game night for players of all ages.

In Adorable Demons, you’ll command a mischievous team of demons, each with their own unique abilities, to complete tasks, sabotage rivals, and collect powerful rewards. The game’s streamlined mechanics ensure quick turns and constant action, while the charming artwork keeps the experience lighthearted and fun. With a blend of card-drafting, resource management, and unpredictable power-ups, every playthrough feels fresh and exciting.

The game’s 50-card deck includes Demon, Task, Power-Up, and Mischief cards, each offering a variety of strategic opportunities. Whether you’re completing hilarious challenges or cleverly outmaneuvering opponents, your path to victory will be as entertaining as it is adorable. For those who prefer solo play, Adorable Demons includes a solo mode where players face off against a rival Demon Lord, that the rules allow to play itself. This gives an extra layer of challenge and replayability to the game. Especially if you don't have a group to play with.

Perfect for families, casual gamers, and experienced players alike, Adorable Demons is as adorable as it is diabolical. The game boasts engaging gameplay, unique theme, and whimsical art. This game is sure to capture the hearts of anyone who loves fun, strategy, and a little bit of mischief. Will you rise to the challenge and claim the Underworld throne? The choice (and the chaos) is yours!

—description from the designer

name: Adulting
description:
Adulting is a cozy, engine-building card game about the mundane struggles of adulthood. Build a deck of attitudes that helps you complete a healthy balance of chores and self-care. Negotiate with your housemates to make sure all of the chores get done or you'll get stressed out. Just like life, there are no winners or losers. You decide how much you’d like to work together or fend for yourselves. With some effort and a little bit of luck, you can avoid burnout and become your ideal self!

Adulting is a mix of tableau-builder and deck-builder. Your tableau represents the chores and self-care tasks that you complete each day. Your deck represents your attitudes. You must play an attitude card from your deck that matches the symbol on your chores and self-care in order to complete them and use their actions. Your goal is to have more self-care than stress at the end of the game. Multiple players can achieve positive outcomes. Collaboration can be helpful, but is not required. It's up to you to decide how well you'll work with others.

—description from the publisher

name: Advanced Fighting Fantasy: Dark Dungeons – The Boardgame
description:
Advanced Fighting Fantasy - Dark Dungeons: The Boardgame  is a dungeon delving boardgame based on the Fighting Fantasy gamebooks and the Advanced Fighting Fantasy RPG.

It uses random tiles to generate the dungeon, and Heroes have a limited time to either defeat the Boss or accumulate treasure, depending on whether the game is played Solo, Cooperatively or Competitively.

—description from the designer

name: Advanced Persistent Threat
description:
Welcome to the world of strategic cyber warfare, where nation state hackers engage in a constant battle for global network dominance.  Can you become the ultimate Advanced Persistent Threat?

Players begin by choosing an Adversary card to represent them and placing the rest back in the box.

The game consists of Staging Servers, Production Servers, Software, Malware, Exploits and Zero Days.

To begin, players take a Staging Server, Small DDOS Zero-Day card, and reference card and place them on the table in front of them.  This is your Network into which you will be playing cards

Shuffle the remaining cards and deal 5 to each player, placing the rest of the deck face down in the center of the table.

Decide who goes first and take turns going clockwise around the table.

Each turn is made up of 4 steps.

First, check your Network for any cards with mandatory or optional “beginning of your turn” effects.  These trigger now.

Second, draw a card from the deck and place it in your hand

Third, play one card from your hand.

Production Servers, Staging Servers, and Software are played into your Network. Malware is played into other players' networks, and Exploits can be played for an instant effect. When playing any card, read the effects out loud and perform their action.

Software and Malware card effects apply to the whole Network.

Software has positive effects and can only be installed above a server that does not have any other Software or Malware installed above it

Malware can be installed on top of Software canceling out the Software effect.

If a Server is Uninstalled, Deleted, or Stolen, any Software or Malware installed above that Server are also discarded or stolen with it.

If a Server instructs you to “return this card to your hand” only the server card is returned.  Any cards above it are discarded.

Exploit cards can be played for immediate effects and must then be discarded

You can also play as many Zero-Day cards as you want, during any players’ turn

Fourth and lastly, discard down to a maximum of 7 cards

The first player to have 6 servers in their network wins!

If the deck runs out of cards before any player reaches 6 servers, the player with the most servers wins.

—description from the designer

name: Adventurer
description:
Adventurer (Dungeons & Drifters) is a solitaire, story, dice game based in a fabled land.  It is the third game in The Drifter series after The Drifter and Star Drifter.

Adventurer is reminiscent of games like Barbarian Prince, The Drifter and Star Drifter, where every game is a unique story experience.

You are a fledgling adventurer.  Now far from home you have set out into this fabled land in hopes of accumulating enough wealth in order to fulfill your quest.  
The terrain of this mysterious realm is covered in dense forests, arid deserts, hazy marshes and rolling grasslands.  Throughout, there are all walks of life, from docile critters, predatory animals, peasants, patricians and ravenous creatures.  There are tales of perilous dungeons, secret tombs and ancient ruins, inhabited by mythological beasts and menacing magic that guard legendary riches.

Armed with your wits and weapon of choice you are ready to explore the highest mountains to the deepest valleys to achieve your goal.

—description from the publisher

name: Adventurer's Guild Girls: The Board Game
description:
Adventurer's Guild Girls - The Board Game is a deck-building board game created by the doujin circle "PaintCan (缶子/罐子牧場)", active in both Taiwan and Japan. It is the first physical game based on the popular "Adventurer's Guild Girls" series.
Step into the world of "Adventurer's Guild Girls", lead your adventurers to take on the impossible, and rise to become the greatest guild leader of all!

In this game, players take on the role of a guild, recruiting various classes to battle monsters. Each round follows a flow similar to Dominion, using deck-building, bag-building, and pool-building mechanics to strengthen their card pool.

Players must continuously enhance their team by recruiting new classes and acquiring equipment in order to defeat monsters and bosses, and to complete their Bond cards (objectives). All of these contribute to the player's final score. The player with the highest score at the end wins.

name: Adventurous
description:
Shrouded in myth and untold dangers, the vast ocean calls to those brave enough to explore its secrets. What marvels lie beyond the horizon?

In Adventurous, players sail across the mysterious ocean in this cooperative tile-laying game. Extend your route with path cards or discover a marvel by meeting its requirements. Take in the fantastical sights without facing too many encounters to safely complete your wondrous journey!

Each turn, the active player may draw two path cards, placing them in such a way that they extend the dotted line showing your ship’s journey. They may instead place one of two available marvels to cover up the specific set of required encounter icons shown on the marvel, adhering to any additional placement restrictions on the marvel.

When no further cards may be placed, the game ends. Count up the number of encounter icons of each type still visible: if they exceed the threshold for that type, you immediately lose. Otherwise, score your journey. Points are earned for each path segment, non-whirlpool icons, and whether all marvels were placed. Points are lost for unplaced marvels and visible whirlpools. Compare the final score to the included chart to determine the fate of your epic voyage!

For an additional challenge, you may use the journey effects found on the back of the ship card, adding complications that change throughout the game depending on the current active marvel. Overcome these odds and guide your ship to safety to prove yourselves masters of the sea!

name: AEGIS Combining Robots: Second Ignition
description:
Return to the wild world of combining robots in AEGIS: Second Ignition (aka Season 2, or just AEGIS2)!

The accessible, content-packed tactics game returns with an all-new box of robots and heroes vying for control of Sigaea in all-out robot fighting tournament! Choose a Commander, take their team of five robots into combat, and combine them into more powerful forms to defeat your opponents. Choose from dozens of robots across five classes - Assault, Evasive, Guard, Intel, and Support - AEGIS! - and duke it out! Games take about 15 minutes per player.

This all-new box features:

     Dozens of new robots, streamlined for easier learning and more tactical depth!
     A roster of new Commanders and prebuilt teams, featuring new luck-mitigating mechanics!
     New game mode - Starpoint Arena! Play with respawning robots and rack up points!
     SOLO MODE! Face off against powerful boss robots and their customizable armies.
     2-Player Draft Rules! Crack the box and have a semi-randomized team in no time!
     Three boards with printed terrain! Choose a 2 or 4-player battlefield and jump in with no board setup!
     COMBINE BOTH BOXES! This game's contents are 100% cross-compatible with the first AEGIS game.


—description from the publisher

name: Aether
description:
In Aether, players are Ærials, masters of telekinesis chosen by Magnus, Grand Master of the Celestial Movement, to compete for succession. Four disciples from the Sacred Houses of Air, Fire, Earth and Water clash in a tournament across the central board, altering elemental currents, levitating objects and fulfilling arcane scrolls. Under shifting celestial alignments, only the one who balances power and stability through technique and guile will be crowned guardian of nature’s equilibrium.

At the start of each round, you draft a paired Aether card and Power token from one of several columns. The token’s elemental effect triggers immediately, and the card joins your personal tableau. Your tableau then produces two resources, Energy and Stability, each round, based on the Aether cards you’ve drafted. During your Levitation phase, you spend those resources to lift and move cubes of varying weight on your player mat, following the cost printed on each object. By arranging cubes to match the patterns shown on Challenge cards (two shared “Scroll” challenges and up to two private “Tome” challenges), you earn Victory Points and advance your completed‑challenge track. As soon as any player fulfills five total challenges, a final round occurs; whoever holds the most Victory Points at the end is crowned guardian of nature’s equilibrium.

name: Cattywampus
description:
Merriam-Webster defines cattywampus as "askew, or awry”, or diagonally out of place.

In Cattywampus, two artists pair up, each sketching half of a bonkers image, from 2 words chosen in secret. Imagine sketching a breakdancing pizza or a jousting llama, without knowing how their teammate is drawing their half of the combination! Once completed, the rest of the table must guess the crazy mashup.

name: Afrika Army Korps
description:
Afrika Army Korps covers part of the battle for North Africa using the DAMOS rule-set and provides a solid way to experience the game under conditions radically changed from the Barbarossa series. Without having to worry about bogs, swamps and unreliable steppe, the desert becomes a tankers paradise.

Exclusive rules for movement, sea transport, logistics and more allow players to combine the Afrika Army Korps games with any other games in the DAMOS series in order to create either a mini-monster or linked campaign game. Using the classic AH Afrika Korps as inspiration, AFRIKA ARMY KORPS series offers a brand new take on the campaign at the strategic scale hex-size of 25 miles per hex. Combat is in hex and opportunities for encirclement abound for both sides.

Players can combine AAK, AAK II TORCH, and AAK III TUNISIA to simulate the entire North African campaign.

—description from the publisher

name: After you, Betobeto-san
description:
After You, Betobetosan, A Trick-Taking Game of Creeping Dread for 4 Players

Every night, on quiet streets lit only by flickering lanterns, something follows. You hear it—step, step… step, step…—always just behind you, never in sight. It is Betobetosan, a yokai known in Japanese folklore for silently trailing behind night-time travelers with soft, sticky footsteps.

In After You, Betobetosan, you and your friends play as children walking home late at night, trying not to panic as Betobetosan draws closer. One player becomes the unsettling yokai, using limited information and shifting suits to win tricks and spread fear. The other players—Children—must stay one step ahead, using clever cardplay, illuminated safe zones, and their one precious "After You, Betobeto-san" card to avoid gaining Fear tokens.

But be careful. If you match Betobetosan’s move exactly, you don’t just lose the trick—you’ve locked eyes with the yokai. And once you do, fear creeps in faster than footsteps in the dark.

Will you brave the night and outsmart Betobetosan… or be the next one left trembling on the roadside?

—description from the designer

name: Against the Iron Ring
description:
Against the Iron Ring is an operational simulation portraying events in the Don River Basin area from November to December 1942, capturing a pivotal moment in history – often referred to as the turning point of the Second World War. 
This game marks the Soviet Red Army’s notable operational triumph over the Wehrmacht. 
Designed for two players, one commands the Soviet Red Army, while the other directs the German and Romanian forces. The game offers 3 distinct scenarios, each playable independently.
Scenarios 1 & 3 (Campaign)start on November 19th, 1942, Scenario 2 starts on December 10th, 1942.
Scenario 1 ends on November 27th, 1942.
Scenarios 2 & 3 end on December 24th, 1942.

—description from the publisher

Game Scale:
Game Turn: 3 days
Hex: 3.4 miles / 5.5 kilometers
Units: Regiments to Corps

Game Inventory:
Two 21.75" x 34.3"/52.45mm x 871.5mm subdued-color mapsheets
    (Combined 42.75" x 34.3"/1085.85mm x 871.5mm)
Six dual-side printed countersheets (648 5/8" / 15.8mm counters)
One 28-page Against the Iron Ring rulebook
Four dual-side printed Player Aid Cards (replaced by two 4 sided foldout Player Aid Cards)
Four dual-side printed Setup Cards

Solitaire Suitability: Medium-high (no solo rules included)
Complexity Level: Medium
Players: 2 or more
Playing Time: 4-8 hours

Players will need to provide two 6-sided dice

name: Age of Colors
description:
Age of Colors is a civilization-building card game inspired by color theory. Players manage colored cards representing different aspects of their empire—such as economy, military, and culture—and strategically combine them to purchase powerful cards, complete events, and gain victory points. Each turn, players use cards to either increase their skills or fulfill card requirements to acquire new abilities and bonuses.

The game involves hand management, resource optimization, and set collection, where players aim to maximize the potential of their cards and outmaneuver opponents. The goal is to accumulate the most victory points by the end of the game through wise decisions, strategic purchases, and completing various in-game objectives.

—description from the designer

name: Coral Gardens
description:
In the depths of the ocean lies a world in which coral gardens flourish. These underwater paradises, teeming with life and color, captivate anyone lucky enough to witness their beauty...but that beauty is in danger of fading forever. Reef architects brave the depths of the oceans to protect and cultivate the growth of a once-great coral ecosystem.

In Coral Gardens, players take turns drafting coral discs to populate different coral tiles. Then based on the undersea currents at the start of their turns, players place these tiles into the underwater garden. At the end of the game, players receive points based on restoration goals and private objectives that have helped to repopulate the reef. The player with the most points wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Age of Myths
description:
Step into the strategic realm of Age of Myths, set in ancient Greece, a board game where you embody a warlord devoted to a god, driven by the ambition to conquer the world. Accumulate gold, battle formidable mythological monsters, amass armies, and overcome your adversaries to emerge victorious.

Basics of Gameplay

The gameplay unfolds during 20 rounds, with each round comprising individual player turns. For instance, in a game with 4 players, a round concludes after all 4 turns are taken.

Within a turn, players can choose 2 actions from a set of 3: spending, engaging, or gambling. The strategic decisions made during these turns can yield 
significant consequences.

Moving around on the game board and attacking monsters or other players is enabled by using dices. When moving the player rolls 3 D6 dices. When attacking and defending 2 D6 dice is used per player. Attacking or defending with a hero used a D12.

How to Win

A game consist of maximum 20 rounds and there are 3 ways to win:


     Be the first player to finish your mission.
     Be the last player standing.
     Control the most amount of tiles after 20 rounds have been played.


PLAYING A TURN

A player can choose to do 2 actions out of 3 available per round. The actions are:

Spending - Buy units or buildings, repair buildings, resurrect hero
Engaging - Move on the map, attack other players or monsters
Gambling - Try to earn additional money by answering a question

Actions are consecutive. This means that, for example, in a turn the player chooses to buy units and then attack another player, they can’t buy more soldiers after they have moved on from the spending action.

—description from the designer

name: Age of the Moon
description:
Age of the Moon is a competitive strategy game set during the New Space Race, where players take on the role of leaders striving to build the first fully operational, habitable lunar base. Each player must balance resources, infrastructure, and alliances to establish their presence on the Moon. With a focus on the Lunar South Pole’s abundant resources, players navigate between collaboration, competition, and strategic planning to outmaneuver their rivals.

The game is played in rounds, each consisting of several phases that bring players closer to completing their lunar base. On their turn, players receive Lunars (the game’s currency) to expand operations by purchasing assets like power plants, greenhouses, and rovers, as well as rockets to transport them to the Moon. Players can negotiate with one another, forming alliances or creating conflicts using negotiation cards. They then launch their rockets, facing the risks of space travel, including mission failures, determined by dice rolls.

Once assets are deployed on the Moon, players gather resources and operate their infrastructure. Managing production and operating costs is key to progress, though even well-laid plans can be disrupted by unexpected events at the end of each round. Additionally, players earn International Community Points (ICP) through cooperation, adding a diplomatic layer to the competition. The game ends when a player successfully builds and operates all four core modules of a habitable lunar base.

The unique feature of Age of the Moon is its realistic scenarios based on expert research and future projections. Players must balance technological development, resource allocation, and diplomacy, making it a strategic and educational experience.

-description from designer

name: Ages of War: Battle for the Bronze Age
description:
Play as the general of a bronze age army and fight an epic battle - move, attack and destroy your enemy on the battlefield encircled by terrain.

You begin by creating the game area, then draw and deploy warrior unit cards to intercept opposing army’s formations and take turns moving or attacking.

When attacking, roll a die to score damage and cross off health boxes, until the unit is destroyed (removed from game area). To win, eliminate all your opponent’s units from the battlefield!

—description from the designer

name: Agile Unicorn
description:
Agile Unicorn is a competitive, tactical card game that pokes fun at the absurdities of the agile start-up world with a wink. In this competitive tactical game, you become a legendary CEO by winning the most valuable victory point features and leading your IT startup to hyped unicorn status.

Starting with 3 employees, you decide each round which employee(s) you use to obtain a card - this can be a feature (victory points), incentive (booster) or another employee.

Each employee gives the player 1-3 dice, depending on their level. After each player has decided which employees to deploy, you can use event cards to make things even more difficult for someone. Then the dice are rolled. Whoever rolls the best total value receives the card.

The first player to reach 32 points wins.

name: Ahotnik
description:
DISCLAIMER
One of our authors is Moldavian and she loves her culture and her language so much she wanted to put some of that love in our game. We can assure you that everything you see in Ahotnik is related to the fictional world we created for our game. The only place we can accept fighting and war is in a boardgame, other than that, as authors, players and human beings, we strongly reject war and violence and we firmly stand for peace and inclusivity.


In Ahotnik, the players form pairs and act as the pilots of giant robots called “Ahotniks”—each of which has its own unique designation of “OXO-##”, for this reason, they are also known as “OXOs”. Their goal is to be the first team to eliminate a rival Ahotnik. But, during their battles, otherworldly creatures referred to as “Demons” emerge from mysterious Portals and try to wreak havoc on Earth by destroying the Ahotniks. The teams must fight on both fronts if they are going to be the one to bring glory to their nation! But beware: Your thirst for power must not come at the cost of total global annihilation…

A game of Ahotnik is played over a series of rounds which are divided into 4 phases:


     Pilot Phase:
 Pilot pairs try to coordinate by using their Action tiles, which represent the cerebral commands they send to the Ahotnik. The success of their strategy depends on their level of synchrony. 
     Ahotnik Phase:
 The Ahotniks operate in this phase depending on the actions thought up by the pilots in the Pilot Phase. In order, the OXOs will carry out:
         Tactical Actions: A set of actions that can have offensive, defensive, or strategic effects.
         Movement Actions: Move the OXO on the game board.
         Attack Actions: The main (though not the only) method to damage your enemies.
    
     Demon Phase:
Beware of incoming threats! This is the turn of any Demons in play. The Radar will also indicate if any new Portals open and increase the Global Threat Level this turn.
     Recovery Phase:
Certain game elements are restored so a new round may begin. 


Rounds are repeated until an Ahotnik falls victim to another OXO or a Demon. Who will achieve total dominion of the planet?

name: Ahoy Shipwrecked
description:
Pirate Roll&Write P&P game about a castaway escaping from an island.

Choose Shipwrecked.
Roll 3 Dice and Push Your Luck (modify results).
Gather Resources.
Take Actions.
Find Treasures.
Build Your Raft.

ESCAPE! Before the Rum is gone.

—description from the designer

name: Ahoy Taverneer
description:
Ahoy Taverneer is an asymmetric Roll&Write board game telling the story of a retired pirate who doesn't quite want to give up his pirate habits. The game will allow you to freely choose the methods by which you will achieve final success.

You have 8 rounds to gather Fame Stars using Dice rolls and effect cards. You can focus entirely on:

    Running your tavern business.
    Returning to the seas and oceans to plunder, loot, search for treasures, fight merchants and gain fame by hunting mythical sea creatures.
    Trading in other ports, acquiring exotic goods and gold.
    Conducting shady deals in the city of Nassau itself, where a club and a knife in dark alleys solve almost all local problems. 
    Hosting the crews of other pirate ships in your cozy tavern, with suitably pirate-friendly service.
    Or a combination of all of the above.


At the end of the 8th round, the player with the most Fame Stars, wins!

Rules include solo variant.

—description from the designer

name: Aircraft, Battle Force:  The Ships that Held the Line
description:
Aircraft, Battle Force (ABF) is a naval wargame that overs the Solomon Islands & Coral Sea battles & Guadalcanal Campaign of 1942.

Each player plots their task forces movement for 3 days (14 hours long) and 3 nights (10 hours each), and also each day’s air searches (time of launch, duration & direction), and also any air strike missions that may result from successful searches.

Each 1 inch distance on the map is 100 nautical miles, and the various latitude & longitude lines are shown on the map; the latter decrease in distance as they go away from the equator.

Game play is quick, and rules and play are easy to learn.  A full battle of 3 days lasts between 30-45 minutes.

Successful plotting & execution of air searches are at the heart of the game, and moving your aircraft carrier task forces into the most advantageous & flexible location will help you survive the enemy air searches & strikes.  Land-based air squadrons also offer reconnaissance & attack opportunities.

The time scale will telescope between 1 day and 1 minute game turns (the latter for air strike resolution).

—description from the designer

name: Akuma
description:
Malevolent spirits, a furtive burden.
Passing from hand to hand
Offer defeat to the next.

Akuma is a trick-avoidance game in which you try to give the worst tricks to other players. The "lead" suit is actually determined by the last player to play into the trick.
The player with the least amount of points wins.

name: Al servicio de la República
description:
"We have been the first victims; be careful, we will not be the last"
(President Negrín)

In the Service of the Republic: The game of diplomats, propagandists and spies (1936-1939) is a diplomacy, propaganda, and espionage game set in the troubled 1930s. It is semi-cooperative in nature and combines exploration journeys, resource management, hidden roles, political intrigue, and abstracted war.

In it, each player represents a diplomat (sometimes also a propagandist and spy) serving the Republican side during the Spanish Civil War. Throughout 3 game turns (which simulate the 3 years between September 1936 and September 1939), your objective will be to travel throughout the map (Europe and North America) in search of military, humanitarian and energy supplies, and once obtained, ship them to loyal Spain, so that the beleaguered Republic has some chance of survival. In the final part of the turn, the military rebels (supported by Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy) will launch several offensives and gradually conquer the cities that are still in the hands of the Republic. At the end of turn 3, World War II will break out (which will mean the salvation of the republican regime, as Spain is framed on the side of the allies against the Axis).

—description from the designer

name: Alebrijes
description:
Dive into the magical world of the Alebrijes!

In this colorful card shedding game, the goal is to get rid of all your cards. Improve your hand and strategically play cards with special effects to outplay your opponents’ combinations. Try to play all your cards before everyone else.

At the end of each round, any cards you haven’t played will give you negative points.

The game ends after the third round, and the player with the fewest negative points at that time wins.

—description form the publisher

name: Algomancy
description:
In Algomancy, you are an Algomancer vying for control over an AI simulation. By manipulating the source code of the world you are able to cast spells, summon armies, and augment game objects to modify their capabilities. Players use these Algomantic powers in a conquest to vanquish the opposition and become the last one standing.

Algomancy is an expandable cube-style drafting card game with CCG-like player interaction and a variety of game modes.


    The dynamic draft mode allows players to draft their hands from a communal deck during the game so they can adapt their strategy on the fly and works best for 2-5 players.
    Pre-draft or cube draft allows players to draft a constructed deck through a traditional drafting method before the game begins, and works best for 6-10 players. Players can either play a series of 1v1 games or larger group games in a free-for-all or team structure.
    Constructed is where players build decks of cards from the card pool to challenge other players who have done the same. This works for any number of players.
    Team constructed allows a team of players to create a group deck, which that team will draft from during the course of the game. This works best for 6 players (3v3).


—description from the publisher

name: Digging For Dinos
description:
Unearth the Past, Piece by Piece!

Welcome to Digging for Dinos, where adventure, discovery, and competition collide! As a team of daring paleontologists, you’ll explore dig sites, unearth ancient fossils, and race against rival teams to assemble the most complete dinosaurs. Every move counts as you compete to claim the rarest finds and piece together prehistoric giants.

With simple yet strategic gameplay, Digging for Dinos is perfect for families, friends, and fossil fanatics of all ages. Grab your tools, out- dig the competition, and bring history to life—one fossil at a time!

Players control 2 paleontologists. Each turn they move one to a new dig site card, collecting the card from where they moved. Each card represents a section of a dinosaur fossil. Collect all the fossils needed to complete a specific dinosaur to score more points at the end of the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Alice, de l'autre côté du miroir
description:
In this competitive flip-and-write game, play solo or in teams as you draw inspiration from Alice to explore a mirrored labyrinth! Trace shapes, activate bonuses, and flip your sheet to maximize your score.

Alice is a competitive flip-and-write game where each player must reproduce the shapes revealed in the center of the table on their own sheet.
At each turn, a Shape card is flipped: all players draw the shape on their sheet, following simple but tactical placement rules. Some spaces trigger bonuses—expand or shrink a shape, score points, or activate effects.
The twist: the sheet is double-sided, and players flip it midway through the game when crossing a mirror!
A system of colored zones and icons to optimize adds depth to the choices.
A team mode completes the experience, allowing duos to play with asymmetric objectives.
Cross-scoring and multiple interactions between elements keep every game lively, smooth, and clever.

—description from the publisher

name: Alien Attack: USA
description:
In Alien Attack, players represent military forces that need to defend the United States of America from a hostile and aggressive alien invasion.

With their attacks in waves, it will be difficult to know which region they will invade next. The problem is that there are so many of them, it is impossible to protect all of them.

However, not all is lost... world military intelligence managed to develop strategies to survive and minimize humanity's losses.

Players will need to defend the attacked regions using their defense units, seeking to protect cities, national parks, livestock farms, in addition to destroying alien bases that are installed in places that have not been defended.

During their turn, players will need to defend one of the attacked regions, collecting national park markers, scoring in cities and herds, in addition to seeking to fulfill public and private objectives that will be scored at the end of the game.

name: Alien Biosphere
description:
A lightweight game with a smooth learning curve and satisfying mechanics - relaxing yet rewarding. A game where you roll dice, color terrain, and draw quirky little creatures that hatch, evolve, and gradually ramp up the challenge as the world takes shape.

Print and play roll and write board game Alien Biosphere welcomes you with three affordable starter creatures and a whole new planet to colonize. At first, you go with the flow - rolling dice, expanding peacefully. But soon, a resource shortage hits or a sudden cataclysm shatters your calm. That’s when you realize: to survive, you’ll have to use strategy.

—description from the designer

name: Aliens Unboxed
description: 3, 2, 1 — go! In Aliens Unboxed, everyone competes at the same time, trying to form predetermined combinations of the eight different, brightly colored aliens as quickly as possible. To do this, fold and rotate your UFOs — unknown folding objects — until you can fulfill one of the boarding cards on display. Depending on how difficult it is to put together certain alien crews, you will receive 1-5 points. Whoever has the most points at the end wins the check-in challenge.

name: Relative Space
description:
"Family Values? Nah, Family Valuables!" You and 2-10 greedy relatives were living it up on the galaxy’s finest space station—until a fire turned your vacay into a screaming, stuff-grabbing frenzy! The rescue shuttle’s pods are here, but in Relative Space, it’s every family member for themselves. Hurl your ukulele in to nix their sock monkey—because nothing beats the glee of screwing over your family mid-catastrophe. It’s a chaotic blast of ensuring your items make it on the pods as you battle to save your loot. First to pack everything jets off triumphant, waving bye-bye to the flaming rubble and their tears!

In Relative Space, each player has a pile of 12 cards representing their valuables, with the 5 cards at the bottom of the pile facedown. In turn order, players must play one card to an available escape pod. The card played must be clear of cards on top, and should be of equal or high value than the top card in the escape pod. First player to pack all 12 of the cards in front of them wins!

—description from the publisher

name: All Are Brothers: Solferino, 1859
description:
All Are Brothers: Solferino, 1859 simulates the decisive battle of the Second Italian War of Independence at the Brigade-level, with some additional Regimental-size and smaller detachments included. National and corps-level leaders are represented, on a map at 500 meters per hex, with 1-hour turns. Five scenarios are included: three that separately cover the north, central, and southern sectors of the battle, as well as a combined full battle scenario, along with a small introductory scneario. The combined scenario is suitable for up to four players (France, Sardinia-Piedmont, Austrian 1st Army, and Austrian 2nd Army).

The battle itself was a grinding slugfest often described as a "soldier's battle" - a deliberate slight to the often uninspired leadership of the generals and a tribute to an allied victory gained only at the tip of the bayonet. Villagers in the surrounding region would do their best in the days after to treat the myriad wounded, and answer as to why Austrians, Hungarians, Czechs, Serbs, and Slovaks were treated as well as the Italians: "Tutti fratelli" (All are brothers). The battle pits two Austrian armies against the combined forces of France and Sardinia-Piedmont, and features the full panoply of colorful period units - Jagers and Grenzers, massed cavalry divisions of all types, Bersaglieri, French Imperial Guard, and the French African Zouaves and Turcos. Advances in infantry and artillery firepower would soon make the tactics of the time obsolete, and the carnage at Solferino reflected the start of this paradigm shift, soon to be highlighted bloodily by the Austro-Prussian and Franco-Prussian wars.

This treatment of Solferino features an adaptation of Hermann Luttmann’s Blind Swords system (At Any Cost, Hammerin' Sickles, Stonewall's Sword) as the core ruleset. The system is heavy on unpredictability and fog of war due to the chit pull mechanic. The chit pull mechanic also very much aids in solitaire play, as does variable activation rules and reinforcement tables. A number of other features help make face-to-face play attractive, including  a number of scenario variants and optional rules, a free-setup full battle scenario, and the move-and-countermove of event chit play. Nation-specific event chits also inject some period flavor.

name: All Hail The Goblin King
description:
A deck collection, resource gathering, crafting a game. Themed around being a little goblin, collecting trash all to build gifts for the goblin king. All while casting rats, crows, and more to sabotage other players and win the game!

The fast paced, wild nature, allows for quick gameplay for most ages. Accompanied with cute art and a goofy theme it allows players to gain favor for the goblin they like the most!

Comedy and fun is at the center of this game all while focusing on a simple rule set that can be expanded on with game modes and  expansions making is even more rambunctious.

—description from the publisher

name: All Time Wrestling: Rumble in Abu Dhabi
description:
A stand-alone 2-4 player expansion to the highly touted game All Time Wrestling featuring legends like Sgt Slaughter, Junk Yard Dog, Kamala, Nick Aldis, and many more.
This Rumble Edition introduces new 3 and 4-player game modes: 
Triple Threat, Fatal 4-Way, Rumble Matches and Faction Rumble.

All Time Wrestling is an asymmetric game where each wrestler has unique attack cards and special abilities (that you can customize before the match). During the game, you will play attack cards from your hand. This will require you to spend energy and roll dice. If the attack is successful, you will deal damage to your opponent build match momentum, and continue your attacks, dealing devastating combos. You win the game by executing a signature or finishing move (attack)that allows you to pin or submit your opponent.

—description from the publisher

name: Allenby's and Lawrence's Desert Wars
description:
Allenby's and Lawrence's Desert Wars is a fast, playable, intense Operational level micro-wargame about the 2 wars against the Turks in Palestine and Western Syria waged by the British and by the Arabs. The British wanted the Turks out of Palestine and the Levant to replace them with British and French control, while the Arabs and TE Lawrence were fighting for Arab independence, and their nuanced victory conditions reflect that.

Games have 10 bimonthly turns. The British, Turkish, and German forces are confined to the grid.  Lawrence and Arabs can sweep anywhere out of the open desert. Strategic and first priority Trans-Jordan Railway supply deliveries to off-map Medina can be protected by Turks only to a degree from Arab attacks.

- Division to corps to Hejaz (camel) and Howeitat army level.
- I-Go-You-Go wargame system using combat odds outcomes and different levels of resilience from combat disruptions, although outright eliminations possible.
- 2 British Re8 air units, 1 German Rumpler C1 air unit.  German "Pasha" advisors to help Turk resilience and coordinate Turk defenses.

—description from the publisher

name: Allenby's Gamble
description:
Allenby's Gamble (# 117-1), covers the start of the Southern Palestinian Offensive of November 1917.

The EEF, having failed taking Gaza twice, replaced their Commander whom brought a new approach to the matter. Allenby's strategical objective was the defeat of the Ottoman army in Southern Palestine, decisive enough to ensure Ottoman reinforcements being diverted to Palestine. The offensive started with a joint attack on Beersheba at the eastern end of the Gaza - Beersheba line.

The following day, the Battle of Tel el Khuweilfe began, with an advance into the Judean foothills. This move up the road from Beersheba towards Jerusalem not only threatened Hebron and Bethlehem but also forced the Ottoman commanders to deploy their reserves, to hold the EEF threat. The Third Battle of Gaza then took place on the Mediterranean coast, starting with the largest barrage during WW1, outside the European theatre. The Battles of Hareira and Sheria was then launched on the centre to bind as many enemy troops as possible.

Allenby’s Gamble simulates the first 10 days of this Campaign.

Rules and mechanics
Rules are developed from the Tannenberg 1914 game released in 2010 now forming the Standard Rule System Collision of Empires with chit-pull mechanics.

—description from the publisher

name: Alpaca: Travel
description:
Alpaca Travel is a compact deck-building game in which players manage a farm of alpacas. Players use their decks strategically to grow their herds and optimize scoring, while interaction between players increases as the game progresses. Its portable components allow for quick setup and play anywhere, and careful planning and tactical decisions are key to success.

—description from the publisher

name: Alphabet Code
description:
Alphabet Code is a fast-paced logic and deduction game for 2 or more players. Each player secretly creates a 5-letter code using digital-style alphabet tiles (a–j), hidden behind a screen. Players take turns asking grid-based questions to deduce their opponent’s code before their own is uncovered.

On your turn, choose to ask:

How many adjacent squares are filled around a certain zone?

Is a specific square filled?

The game rewards clever questioning, spatial reasoning, and strategic thinking. If you believe you’ve cracked your opponent’s code, you may declare your answer—but beware: two incorrect guesses and you lose!

With optional Advance Rules that use real words and expanded setups using more letters, Alphabet Code offers scalable challenge and replayability.

Great for fans of deduction games like Mastermind or Cryptid, but with a uniquely visual and tactical twist.

—description from the publisher

name: Amanite
description:
In Amanite, it's all about deduction and risk-taking.
Make better choices than your opponents by picking the right mushrooms (and avoiding the bad ones!).

The information you choose will be valuable, and the choices made by other players will teach you a lot!

You will have 3 initial clues, different ones for each player, but you will need to have more to cross the information and deduce the real values of each mushrooms. First, because your clues will be shuffled and you won't be sure about anything and also, because you will have to chase information regarding the other mushrooms.

During the game, player will share the mushrooms with a "split & choose" mechanism, and the choices of each player will give information to everyone around the table.

It will again help the players to eventually choose the best mushrooms.

A game of Amanite is played in 3 rounds. At the end of these rounds, the player who has earned the most victory points with the tokens they have collected wins the game.
But be careful, players who have collected too many poisonous mushrooms will not be able to claim victory!

—description from the publisher

name: Weeds Garden Takeover
description:
Ever wonder what happens when weeds strike back? Sprout, grow, and thrive as you compete to rule the garden! In Weeds Garden Takeover players will use their wits to analyze the size and quantity spread of opposing weeds. The environment around you and your unique abilities will help to spread your weeds and prevent others from shriveling your roots in the process.

Weeds blends familiar mechanics that both new and seasoned gamers enjoy, such as:

Strategic analysis inspired by Liar’s Dice

Catch-up mechanics reminiscent of Quacks of Quedlinburg

Action card chaos similar to Exploding Kittens

Do you have what it takes to bloom above the competition and be the last weed standing?

—description from the publisher

name: American Revolution: Washington
description:
美國革命：華盛頓 ("American Revolution: Washington") is a 1-4 player strategic level wargame to simulate the American Revolution in 1776 to 1783 in north America.

There are 8 rounds in one game. Player commands the British army to conquer the Continental army in north America. British armies may move into the revolt areas and roll the die to attack rebel armies. Be careful, the rebels may ambush you randomly. In the end round, you need to score at least 7 vps by capturing the Continental commanders and sweep the rebel armies.

American Revolution: Washington is the seventh game of the Revolt & Conquer series. You can combine Washington and Greene maps together for playing a Revolutionary War campaign game with 3-4 players.

—description from the publisher

name: Amist: Mutant Control
description:
Dreadful mutations have taken the world by storm. Some are more resistant to its effects, while others fall victim to the primal instincts of the animals their DNA was spliced with. As one of the survivors who has limited control over their mutations, you and the rest of the colony that has banded together must research the mutant's DNA for a cure if humanity has any hope at survival. While gathering DNA samples, players must also withstand the treacherous wastelands, craft vital items, and secure locations to build back a civilization worth fighting for. Each player must prove their capabilities by earning the most Reputation Points in hopes of becoming the leader of the colony. Dare to enter a world of mutants to save humanity?

—description from the publisher

name: Amoebunnies
description:
Amoebunnies is an asymmetrical game for 2-6 players that takes approximately 10 minutes per player to complete. It's family friendly and stars 6 cute amoeba-like bunny creatures who are helping the lands near their home of the Rainbow Mists.

Each character has a unique goal to accomplish and the first player to complete their task wins. The characters also have unique movement and special abilities. Master your favorite or play them all.

—description from the designer

name: Amṛtaka
description:
Amrtaka: Battle for Immortality – Forge Your Legacy in a Mythological War Will you seize immortality or fade into legend?

Dive into an epic struggle inspired by the ancient Hindu legend of Samudra Manthana (The Churning of the Cosmic Ocean). As a warrior-king, lead your kingdom against rivals in a race to capture Amrit—the elixir of eternal life. But immortality demands cunning: forge alliances, outmaneuver foes, and harness divine power in this deeply strategic board game where every choice echoes through mythic history.

Game Explanation

Try the Amrtaka Chat Box!

Got questions about gameplay, rules, or setup? Just ask!
No more rulebook flipping — get instant help anytime.
? Stuck on a mechanic?
? Unsure of turn order?
? Need quick clarification?

Type it in the notebook Chat Box and keep your game flowing!
? Smart. Fast. Simple.
Make your Amrtaka journey smoother and more epic!

https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/bce095f1-fbda-45e9-925e-38d2ece9e3ea?authuser=1

★ Why You’ll Be Hooked:

Dual Paths to Victory: Race to 60 victory points (“drops of Amrit”) by immortalizing lands (15-point bursts) or conquering rivals (5-point strikes). Choose wisely—each path demands opposing strategies!

Mythology Brought to Life: Gods and demons aren’t just lore—they’re game-changing mechanics. Deploy 10 hidden god-followers whose phased powers reshape the board across 30 turns.

Revolutionary Portal System: Bend space with personal portals to teleport armies instantly. But beware: place them recklessly, and lose them forever to enemy conquests.

Tense Action Economy: Every turn burns precious weapons (needed even to move!). Sacrifice short-term gains for long-term setups, balancing card abilities, armies, and divine boons.

Phased Epic Scale: The game evolves in three acts, driven by god-follower movements: claim lands early, unleash divine powers mid-game, and scramble in a “power vacuum” as time runs out!

★ Key Mechanics That Shine:

Strategic Combat: Attack with matched weapon types (melee/ranged) and outpower defenders using card values + army bonuses. Lose your standee’s land? Suffer crushing setbacks!

Dynamic Board Control: Make lands “immortal” for huge points… but lose exclusivity and thin the action deck. Trade territories to reposition or upgrade holdings!

God-Follower Powers: Reveal hidden abilities in Phase 2 (turns 11–20) for explosive one-time boosts—then adapt when gods withdraw in the endgame.

Brutal Consequences: Face possible elimination if stripped of all armies AND weapons… yet your portals linger, haunting rivals even in defeat!

★ Immersive Components:

10 Circular Lands looping in a cosmic ocean, divine zones, and a central island.

48 Action Cards packed with directional choices, teleports, and tactical boosts.

Army/Weapon Tokens (red/gray armies, melee/ranged weapons) and Portal Tokens for warp-speed tactics.

Deluxe Edition: Swap standees for 3D warrior-king miniatures and track points in a magic flower bowl!

Perfect for fans of Inis, Kemet, or Cyclades who crave deeper integration of theme and strategy. Amrtaka masterfully blends Hindu mythology with knife-edge decisions, ensuring no two games unfold alike. Will you hoard Amrit for your kingdom—or shatter rivals to claim eternity?

Ready your weapons. The ocean churns. Immortality awaits.

name: An Impossible War: The First Carlist War in the North, 1834-1838
publisher: Aleph Game Studio; Bellica Third Generation
description:
'An Impossible War' recreates the First Carlist War in the North of Spain (1834-1838). It is a wargame with blocks that also includes counters and cards.

There is a main map (or Northern map), that shows Navarre, the Basque Provinces and part of Cantabria, Burgos and La Rioja, and a secondary map that reflects the regions of the rest of the country, where Carlist uprising break out and the expeditions sent from the North may operate.

There is a scenario that covers the Full War (1834-1838) and another two shorter ones: Zumalacarregui's War (1834-1836) and Espartero's War (1836-1838).


'Una Guerra Imposible' recrea la Primera Guerra Carlista en el Norte de España (1834-1838). Es un juego de guerra de bloques que también incluye fichas y cartas.

Hay un mapa principal (o mapa del Norte), donde aparecen Navarra, las Provincias Vascongadas y parte de Cantabria, Burgos y La Rioja, y otro mapa secundario que refleja las regiones del resto del país, donde estallan las sublevaciones carlistas y pueden operar las expediciones enviadas desde el Norte.

Hay un escenario que cubre la Guerra Completa (1834-1838) y otros dos más breves: La Guerra de Zumalacárregui (1834-1836) y La Guerra de Espartero (1836-1838).

name: Anaphylaxis
description:
In this tense and minimalist trick-taking game, you’ll gather valuable bee cards to earn points — but if you ever capture the same bee twice, you suffer an anaphylactic shock and are immediately knocked out with zero points. Sharp timing, deadly traps, and ruthless hand-passing set the stage for a brutal test of survival from the very first card.

AnaPhylaxis is a trick-taking game where players must follow suit, navigate shifting trump interactions, and balance risk through a limited-use Pass mechanic. With a 28-card deck featuring duplicated high-value bees, players aim to win point cards without duplicating colors and numbers. Each round allows two critical Passes to avoid dangerous tricks, while a Pokémon-style weakness system lets certain suits beat others depending on the lead. Hands are slightly manipulated through card-passing, and the game’s fast knockouts and tactical sacrifices ensure that every decision could be fatal or victorious. The player with the highest total after several brutal rounds wins.

name: Ancient Blood: The Order of Vampire Hunters
description:
Ancient Blood - The Order of Vampire Hunters is a cooperative story-driven game that can be played as solo mode, as standalone games, or as a campaign. Choose a story and begin your journey. Be brave and wise, as every choice you make along your path will impact the game world. The wrong choice could awaken your most hidden fears. Fight side by side with your fellow hunters like never before using combo attacks, get help from locals using your skills, and find all the clues that will lead you to the master of each Vampires' clan, The Elder Lord.

Ancient Blood is a prequel to The Order of Vampire Hunters. It features some game mechanics inspired by the old game, but it is a new game. It is not compatible with the previous one, since Ancient Blood is a story-driven game in which your decisions will influence how the game develops and the end of the story. The new game features exploration, crafting, resource management, and leveling up. This time your decisions will change the story of the game, so be prepared to deal with the consequences of your choices.

Can you defeat the Elder Lords?

name: Andromeda Run
description:
A card game where players race to complete the Andromeda Run, with as much cargo as possible. Players command a Flagship with different strengths and weaknesses, expanding their fleet and capabilities as they overcome obstacles and events to race to the finish, set in the Andromeda Galaxy.

Every turn players take turns in drawing cards, and playing them. These cards could take the form of distance traveled, upgrades to their ship, cargo or extra ships for their fleet. Events occur which the player or players (depending on conflict mode or not) overcome for rewards.

The Game ends when a fleet arrives at the target distance traveled. The players are given bonus points depending on how far they have traveled or how much cargo they have brought with them. The highest score wins.

-description from designer

name: Animal Parade
description:
Animal Parade is a solitaire game for kids and adults. The deck comprises beautiful animal cards, which help you be the first to complete your parade! You must be the first player to earn 10 points on the scoreboard to win the game.
This game is designed for Adults and kids to enjoy. In "kid mode," you can play with younger kids.

—description from the publisher

name: Fief: England
publisher: International Team Games (ITS); Academy Games, Inc.; Ediciones MasQueOca; hobbity.eu; Lavka Games
description:
In Fief: England, you take control of the destiny of a family of lords in a revisited medieval era and try to make them the most powerful in the kingdom. To win, you must make good use of:


     your political strength, by building alliances through marriage, giving titles to your lords and ladies, and convening parliament to raise taxes,
     your economic strength through income from mills and abbeys, and taxes on towns, and
     your military strength, by raising troops (knights, sergeants, archers, crossbowmen) and by making good use of your siege engines (bombards and trebuchets).


In Fief England, each Player leads a Family of Nobles in the Middle Ages Kingdom of England. A Family is made up of Noblemen and Noblewomen who strive for Royal and Ecclesiastic Titles. These Titles bring their Family power and the right to elect or be elected King or Queen of England and Victory points at the end of the game.

Players receive income from the Cities, Mills, and Abbeys they control. Nobles with a Lord or Ecclesiastic Title can levy taxes on their Fiefdoms. Their income can be used to buy new Troops, Mills, Strongholds, and Titles. Income may also be used to bribe or help other Players! Players gain control of new Cities by occupying them with Troops. If Troops from more than one Player occupy the same City, a Battle may take place.

The game ends once a Player has 3VPs or two Players, allied through marriage, have a combined total of 4VPs. At the end of Round 7 the game ends, no matter what. The Player or Alliance with the most VPs wins. If the Players or Alliances are tied, a winner is determined by who has the highest Title.

—description from the publisher

name: Animalcatraz
description:
────────────────────
ENGLISH
────────────────────

Animalcatraz is a competitive sandbox prison brawler for 2–8 players.

Compete solo or team up inside a brutal animal prison where every decision shapes your rise to power.

Fight, steal, recruit gangsters, corrupt guards, craft contraband weapons, and battle rivals to survive behind bars.

Escape the island…
or become the prison’s ruthless KINGPIN.

With evolving alliances, betrayals, dynamic combat, and asymmetric convicts, every game creates a different story behind bars.

────────────────────
FRANÇAIS
────────────────────

Animalcatraz est un jeu compétitif de type sandbox prisonnier pour 2 à 8 joueurs.

Affrontez-vous en solo ou faites équipe dans cette brutale prison animale où chacune de vos décisions influence votre ascension vers le pouvoir.

Combattez, volez, recrutez des gangsters, corrompez les gardiens, fabriquez des armes de contrebande et tentez de survivre à cet enfer carcéral.

Évadez-vous de l’île…
ou devenez le redoutable KINGPIN de la prison.
