In addition to the animals the players are also placing the environment cards – stones and herbs and if some card doesn’t suit their intentions, they can flip it to its water side and earn some points this way.

—description from the publisher

name: Backstories: L'Embrasement
description:
Discover the third adventure in the BACKSTORIES Saga: The Blaze

How to Play ?
Backstories is a game with mechanisms as simple as they are revolutionary: a bit like you would do in a Point & Click video games, interact with your environment as you progress through your thrilling adventures. Some cards (Panorama) represent the environment in which you’re evolving. Other cards (Actions) are perforated, and represent the actions you can perform (Talk, Search, Objects in your possession, etc.). To interact, all you have to do is place a perforated card on the back of the Panorama card you’re interested in, then turn the card over and read the result of your choice.
Be careful, though: in every scenario you play through, each of your choices will have real consequences… Be ready to face them!

In this scenario, you play as a former militiaman who left his violent past behind to take care of his family. But in this post-apocalyptic world, the past is quick to catch up with you…

Remember: Your choices, Your Adventure!

name: Backyard Butterfly
description:
An educational life science board game for kids and their families. Find and raise monarchs and learn about their life cycle. Backyard Butterfly is a game played in 4 stages:

Stage 1: Hunt for eggs. Roll the leaf shaped die and flip over 1-3 leaf tiles until you find an egg. Place an 'egg tile' on your milkweed board. Move on to stage 2 on your next turn. 
Stage 2: Feed your hungry caterpillar. Action sequence:

     Roll leaf die to populate leaf tiles onto your milkweed board.
     Roll both caterpillar dice. Move your caterpillar meeple around the milkweed board twice with the goal of landing on leaf tiles to eat.
     Place any eaten leaves onto your leaf tracker board. 


Continue with this stage until your leaf tracker board is full. 
Stage 3: Chrysalis Coin. Flip the coin (twice per turn). 
Green side- continue to wait. 
Orange and Black side- your monarch butterfly is ready to emerge! Move on to stage 4!
Stage 4: Your monarch has emerged and flys away! Place a monarch butterfly token in the sky above the leaf tracker board. Butterfly tokens represent points earned. Begin your next turn back at the egg stage.

There are two additional gameplay variations: 
'BB Helper' walks parents through how to teach even the youngest gamers to play a game with multiple actions and stages in a way that is intuitive and fun.
'Field of Milkweed' is a competitive version of the base game where all 4 milkweed boards are placed together to form a field. All resources are up for grabs and nature can strike at any time. Nature being an additional d12 rolled at the beginning of the caterpillar stage causing havoc.

name: S.T.A.L.K.E.R. The Board Game
publisher: Awaken Realms; Albi; Fox in the Box; Ігромаг
description:
S.T.A.L.K.E.R. features high-quality models and top-notch components that transport players to the harsh and cruel Zone. The mechanics have been carefully crafted to provide players with a sense of tension and danger as they tackle the game's challenges. At this point, we know that the game will please hardcore players while being accessible to people who are just starting their journey in story-driven board games. The core narrative will be based on the S.T.A.L.K.E.R.’s campfire stories. The missions themselves are divided into separate boxes, allowing for a smooth transition into the game itself.

S.T.A.L.K.E.R. The Board Game is a fully co-op, story-based “zone” crawler. It is set in an alternative version of the Chornobyl Nuclear Plant Exclusion zone, full of anomalies, relics, mutants, emissions, and dark secrets.

Every mission will offer a different approach - either sneak in or go in guns blazing. Both systems are integrated seamlessly into a highly tactical experience. But you always have to remember that Zone is full of surprises - toxic radioactive rain, upcoming emissions, anomalies, or bands of mutants roaming around can cross your plans.

—description from the publisher

name: Bad Baby Lich Lords
publisher: Heart of the Deernicorn; Wonderbow Games
description:
Bad Baby Lich Lords is a fast-paced competitive card game of necromancy and sibling rivalry for 2-4 players

Lich siblings battle it out in this competitive card game inspired by your favorite Saturday morning cartoons. Flip double-sided skeleton cards to raise the dead and activate their powers. Cast dark spells. Wrangle your unruly minions and set off chain reactions and combos. Collect sets of minion cards to meet the requirements to score on realms. Be the first player to make enough noise to wake up the sleeping Lich King!

Featuring over 100+ double-sided cards with full art by award winning artist Taylor Dow.

Choose from 4 factions with unique abilities.

name: Badass Bunnies
description:
Try your luck in this exciting card game. Expand your bunny family by bribing bunnies with carrots. Every carrot and every bunny you turn over brings you closer to victory, but if you turn over a second fox, you're done for! Can you outsmart the cunning foxes?

—description from the publisher (translated)

name: Badgers
description:
A fast paced card game where competing burrow fight for scraps of food and territory.

Select your favorite kind of badgers and lead them to conquer their favorite food. Play the right badger at the right time to either defeat a competing badger or to strengthen your position.

Use special abilities or tunneling as you chose to conquer the field and gain your meal before the game ends.
Each burrow has unique special abilities and badgers based on real types of badger.

At the end, who owns the most food wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Severton
publisher: Albi; Cranio Creations; HUCH!; MTS Games
description:
Severton is a cooperative, scenario-based adventure game set in the magical atmosphere of old Prague, where a group of boys and girls uncover secrets and embark on thrilling quests.

In the game, inspired by a Czech novel series by Jaroslav Foglar, players take on the role of a group of friends who are trying to investigate the shadows of Severton – the old neighborhood ruled by ruthless groups of Vonts—and progress through various stories, each with different challenges lying ahead of them. Avoid the Vont patrols, sneak your way around them, talk your way out of trouble, or use your fists to gain the upper hand.

—description from the publisher

name: BalaDino
description:
It's walk day at Dino Parc! The masters are out and about, accompanied by their faithful pet dinos. A race is soon organized.

The whole gang sets off down the central alley, watched over by Billy, the park warden, who can't bear to see the dinos too far from their masters!

Which dino will be the fastest through the park gates?

Roll dice and move your keeper or dino on the track. If you land on a bench symbol, draw a bench card to gain an advantage or give a disadvantage to your opponents.

name: Ballons Olympiques
description:
A light strategy family board game about the Olympic Balloon Races during the Paris Exposition Universelle of 1900 for 2-6 players.

The game features balloon game pieces that float above the 24" game board featuring the map of Paris.

Original water color style art highlights the balloons, monuments and gardens of Paris.

Novel mechanics force you to change altitudes and catch favorable winds to navigate over the targets of the race.

—description from the publisher

name: Baltic Freikorps, 1919
description: Baltic Freikorps, 1919 is an Operational level, Solitaire-Only board-wargame in which the player commands the decisive military operations in the Baltic Republics during 1919, controlling “Allied” forces trying to keep Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania from being conquered by the Red Army.

name: Baltic Year
description:
Baltic Year is a strategic card collection game where players journey through eight ancient Baltic celebrations. Collect card sequences and combinations while traveling the moonlight path, aiming to gather Baltic symbol tokens while keeping your hand value low.

Players form sets (same numbers, different signs) or sequences (consecutive numbers, same sign) to claim corresponding Baltic symbol tokens. The game features 52 cards with eight distinct Baltic signs representing sacred celebrations like Užgavėnės, Rasa, and Vėlinės, plus 4 "Magic" cards that can become any number or sign.

Win by collecting four tokens of any signs, or three adjacent tokens in the Baltic Year Cycle sequence. Alternatively, achieve victory by having the fewest points when someone crosses the 30-point threshold.

With elegant Baltic symbolism and accessible mechanics for 2-7 players aged 8+, Baltic Year combines strategy with cultural heritage, celebrating ancient wisdom through engaging gameplay.

—description from the publisher

name: TroubleZ Run! Revenge of the Jellynator
description:
TroubleZ Run! Revenge of the Jellynator is push-your-luck game for kids of age 6 and up, designed by Giorgio Galbusera, illustrated by Petr Štefek and set in the same colourful zombie universe as card game TroubleZ.

It’s for 2 to 4 players and you will be able to play it in 15 to 30 minutes. It has very simple rules and fast pace, so the kids will love it. In the role of TroubleZ, you will be fleeing from a monster called Jellynator and rescuing zombie animals that would otherwise be trapped by a Jellynator.

The catch is that you don’t want to get too far ahead – the last player is rewarded each round, but at the same time you don’t want the Jellynator to catch you, because that results in minus points. The game is dice-driven, but there is still a lot of meaningful choices to make, so I think if the kids will bring you to the game, you won’t regret.

—description from the publisher

name: Banana Governance
description:
Use bananas to rule the monkey world!

In the first half, you cut up bananas and draft them, and in the second half, you bid on the bananas you cut up to win monkeys! The number of bananas remaining in your hand multiplied by the number of monkeys you win is your victory point!

name: Karak: Labyrinth
description:
Karak: Labyrinth is a real-time drawing game by Petr Vojtěch. Labyrinth is designed for 1 to 4 players aged 6 and up, and the playing time is around 10 to 15 minutes, making it a true lightning-fast game.

Karak: Labyrinth is the most accessible game from the world of Karak. Players simultaneously try to find the best path through the labyrinth of Karak, and to gain the most points maximizing the completion of three objectives, randomly selected from a vast pool of objective cards.

Players must not retrace their own steps and to pass important points of interest – such as a sword to be gained – they must solve the corresponding puzzle mini-game, of which there are several different kinds in the game. And it all happens within a time limit.

Rules-wise everything is as simple as possible, and the game will include a tutorial campaign, which means you can start playing as soon as you unpack the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Night at the Zoo
description:
“Just a little further, a bit higher, bro…” The cheetah gives the penguin a boost over the gate, while a confused wolf dashes past. “Look out, someone’s coming!” Everyone freezes. After a moment of silence, a sloth calls from a tree: “All clear, move out!” The animals have secretly snuck out of the zoo at night—and now they’re trying to find their way back. Help them return before the keepers notice!

The goal of the game is to help the animals and guide them safely back into their home. Players explore parts of the darkened zoo to discover the best routes home. Each round, players draft tiles and place them on their boards, triggering special actions and building a path back for their animals. Every animal has its own unique way of moving and scoring points, making each game a new adventure!

—description from the publisher

name: Bark Magic: Ultimutt Edition
description:
An expanded and redesigned version of the original Bark Magic, Ultimutt Edition adds new wizards, spells, trials and more.

In Classic Battle, 2 to 4 players manage their hand of spell cards, using them to gain magic points (MP), thwart opponents, and dig up relics. Players compete in various dice-based trials to peek at relic cards, gain bonus MP and dig faster. The first to unearth four mystic gems from The Ruins is crowned Ultimutt Sorcerer.

In Ultimutt Battle, 2 to 8 players race to gain 7 MP in a non-stop onslaught of trials consisting of both battles and alliances. Winning means digging and relics are the only way to increase one's MP (unless they're cursed of course).

—description from the publisher

name: Barnburners and Noblemen
description:
The great King's bloodline has ended and the realm of Enemier has been thrown into political chaos. As factions fight for power and champions emerge, the future of the realm is up for grabs.

Barnburners and Noblemen brings the worlds of wargames, tabletop diplomacy, and extensive lore clashing together in an epic death match style wargame. Barnburners and Noblemen is a tabletop skirmisher set in a unique fantasy world. Draft your army with a variety of champions from any faction and seek your victory.

On your turn, you will move your armies units, make your attacks, and prepare to defend from the others. Pairing up different units between the factions allows for limitless choices when it comes to your armies makeup for the round.

The last player with surviving characters is the winner!

—description from the designer

name: Barony: Royal Edition
description:
In Barony, players are ambitious barons trying to extend their dominion over the land! Who will succeed and become the new ruler?

Gameplay is simple. On your turn, perform one of six actions to expand your territory and diminish your opponents':

     Recruitment: Add two knights to a city, or three knights if the city is adjacent to a lake.
     Movement: Move one or two of your knights one space each. If you move a second knight into a space with an opposing pawn or village, remove those tokens and take one resource from the village owner.
     Construction: Remove one or more of your knights from the game board and replace each with a village or stronghold, gaining one resource.
     New City: Replace one of your villages with a city and earn 10 victory points (VPs).
     Expedition: Remove two knights from your reserve, placing one back in the box out of play and the other on any empty space on the edge of the game board.
     Noble Title: Discard at least 15 resource points, then upgrade your title: baron to viscount, then count, marquis, and finally duke.


Once any player has gained the title of duke, finish the round, then tally the VPs, with players scoring for resources still in their possession, their rank in the game, and the number of cities they built. Whoever has the most VPs wins!

This new edition of Barony includes the Barony: Sorcery expansion and all-new asymmetric player powers.

—description from the publisher

name: Barrage: The Legendary Box
description:
The Legendary Box comes with the Barrage base game and the Far Companies Expansion. This expansion includes rules for two new companies to be used in addition to the four base ones and the fifth one already included in The Leeghwater Project expansion. These two companies have unique characteristics that significantly distinguish them from the standard companies both in terms of game mechanics and components.

- The Japanese company uses Bases and Elevations inspired by the “Earth-fill dams”: on one hand, it is possible to use the Elevations as if they were Bases, greatly increasing the number of Dams that can be built; on the other hand, these dams will be limited in height and thus in capacity. Finally, the machinery used for the Elevations are Excavators instead of Concrete Mixers.

- The Brazilian company specializes in versatility: Bases, Elevations, and Conduits can be built in any order from its board, with a greater choice of strength and type of bonuses; however, the elements related to stronger bonuses will result in the permanent loss of one machinery or more.

Both companies unlock a special company ability when the third powerhouse is built.

The Legendary Box was also sold by itself (no games included, just inserts).

—description from the publisher

name: Baseball Card GM
description:
It all started in 2024, when Garrett Weaver (then just seven) asked a simple question: “How can I actually play with my baseball cards?”

When no games existed, he and his younger brother Simon invented a set of rules at their dining-room table, which today after play-testing with their friends, schoolmates, and baseball teammates has become Baseball Card GM.

The game is a sturdy 36"x18" neoprene playmat (which can be rolled for easy storage/travel) with all rules on the playmat itself. A 9-inning game takes about 30 minutes to play, good for ages 7+.

It's easy as 1-2-3:
1. Draft your team from your own baseball cards.
You are the GM, so you can create any team you want, any way you want, with whatever cards you have!

You can make your ultimate Dream Team, recreate an actual historic team, build along a specific theme (ex: MVP’s and CY’s of the 2000’s), do an actual draft alternating picks with your competitor, or crack some new packs and play with whatever you get. The possibilities are endless, and even a random stack of cards can be hours of fun.

The game works best with baseball cards from the 1980’s to today (ie most likely to have all the stats needed for the game: HR, 3B, 2B, Avg, BBs, Hits, RBIs, SBs), but you can use older cards as well because the stats used in the game are nearly universal to all cards.

Once you have your team, you will build your line-up, choose your starting pitcher, and fill out your bench and bullpen. Then you are ready to play ball!

2. Use the stats on the back of the cards.
A good GM knows player analytics, and for you that means diving into the stats on the back of the cards!

Your batter getting a single, double, triple, homerun, walk, strikeout, ground-out (G/O), fly-out (F/O) or pop-out (P/O) is all based on a combination of whichever single year of their major league stats you choose from the back of their card, the stats of the pitcher they are facing, whether the pitcher/batter are righty or lefty, and the outcome of rolling two dice.

The odds are all worked out right on the playmat so potential batting outcomes are just like how it COULD have happened historically in real life. Better batters will have better chances to roll better outcomes with the same frequency as their stats dictate. Remember not all players excel at every stat, so build your line-up accordingly!

3. Play a real game that is true to the stats. 
A GM has to know all the nuances of baseball, and here all the normal baseball rules apply!

Run through your line-up in order, alternating between Visitors and Home teams, placing cards as they move around the bases. Substitute batters, pitchers, or base runners just as the pro’s would in a real game.

Track Outs, Runs, and the Top-Bottom of the nine inning game with the markers placed in the appropriate squares on the playmat. Special circumstances when runners are already on base are described on the playmat too: double plays, sac flies, scoring from second on a single, and stealing bases can and will happen!

—description from the designer

name: Baseball Highlights: 2045 – Bases Loaded Edition
description:
The Bases Loaded Edition contains all previously released Baseball Highlights: 2045 gameplay content as well as the All-Star Expansion.

American baseball was on its last legs as a spectator sport. Football had become the predominant national pastime — that is until the year 2032, the year baseball decided to revolutionize the game and regain the throne! Starting in 2032, baseball games were shortened to six innings. Pitchers were encouraged to have bionic arm implants to improve their pitching. These cyborgs, or 'Borgs as they're affectionately known, were immediately popular and soon ruled the league. In 2041, robotic players were introduced to get more offense back into the game. These robots were similar to designated hitters in that they were used only to bat and did not field. However, recent reports indicate fielding 'Bots are on the way.

Now in 2045, human players are still in the game and known as Naturals. They are the best fielders by far but are sorely challenged when it comes to hitting and pitching. Some Naturals have learned to hit by swinging before the pitcher starts his windup, which gives them a chance to hit the ball. Although it's hard for a Natural to get into the league, those who do are popular. Many Naturals have named themselves after the great players of pre-2032 baseball by taking a first and last name borrowed from different star players of the past. The fans love them, and their presence on the team ensures good revenue!

Baseball Highlights: 2045 is like watching TV highlights of early 21st-century baseball games, with the gameplay being full of theme with no outs or innings and without bogging down in a play-by-play baseball simulation. In this quick and interactive game, two players build their teams as they play, combining both strategy (building your team) and tactics (playing the game) without any of the downtime. During each "mini-game", each player alternates playing six cards to simulate a full game's highlights. The mini-game includes defensive and offensive actions, and your single card play may include elements of defensive and/or offensive plays.  Players buy new free agents after each mini-game to improve their roster, and the team who wins the most mini-games in the series is the champ!

-description from publisher

name: Bat Flip Dynasty
description:
You have just been hired as the General Manager of a big-league baseball team. Your team is just 5 good players away from contention. Draft players to build your roster while staying within your team budget. Then activate your players’ skills to get the most wins each season. Earn trophies over multiple seasons to establish your dynasty and win the game!

Bat Flip Dynasty is a stand-alone card- and dice-drafting game featuring tableau building and budget management.

Bat Flip Dynasty distills being a big league General Manager into its most exciting elements - namely picking players and building a team. Choose players that fit your team philosophy or that fit your manager’s style of play. Sign one-year contracts and try to win right now, or draft prospects to build for the future. Lock up superstars to long term contracts. After each season, keep who you want and cut the rest. Then draft all over again to fill out your roster.

—description from the publisher

name: Batab: Guardians of Chichen Itza
description:
Step into the ancient world of the Maya civilization and assume the role of a Batab, a noble guardian and leader of the grand city of Chichen Itza. In this immersive board game, you'll navigate the intricate web of political power, resource management, and cultural influence, all while vying for control over this magnificent realm. The game ends when after the end of 3 scoring rounds, called K'atun Celebrations. At the end of the game, the player with the most Might wins, and is crowned the supreme guardian of Chichen Itza.

"Batab: Guardians of Chichen Itza" builds upon the renowned system of "Ahau: Rulers of Yucatán" but streamlines it into a seamless worker placement experience. In this game, you'll immerse yourself in the vibrant streets and sacred precincts of Chichen Itza. Your mission is to ascend to greatness by earning the favor of the gods and the respect of your peers. 
To achieve this, you'll:

Construct Monuments: Erect magnificent temples, including the iconic Kukulkan Pyramid, to assert your influence over the city.

Manage Resources: Strategically allocate resources such as maize, jade, and obsidian to sustain your city and retain the loyalty of your followers.

Participate in Rituals: Perform sacred ceremonies to harness divine powers, gaining unique advantages and blessings.

Navigate Politics: Form alliances, vie for political sway, and tactically position your followers to secure control over the city's districts.

Defend Against Challenges: Protect Chichen Itza from intruders and fend off natural disasters to ensure the city's security and prosperity.

Features:

Rich Cultural Theme: Immerse yourself in the historical and cultural depth of the Maya civilization, complemented by authentic artwork and thematic elements.

Streamlined Mechanics: "Batab" streamlines the beloved system of "Ahau" into a worker placement format, providing an accessible and engaging gameplay experience.

Diverse Strategies: Multiple paths to victory cater to a range of strategic preferences, whether you excel in diplomacy or military prowess.

New Challenges: Battle intruders and overcome natural disasters that threaten the city, introducing fresh layers of strategy and decision-making.

Unique Role Cards: Acquire role cards that grant special abilities, enhancing your strategic options and adding depth to your decisions.

Batab: Guardians of Chichen Itza presents a captivating blend of strategy, history, and culture. Each decision propels you closer to becoming the ultimate guardian of this ancient and magnificent realm. Will you rise to the challenge and etch your name into Chichen Itza's illustrious history?

-description from publisher

name: Prague Unseen
description:
Set foot in mythical Prague back in the 19th century, when fantastical creatures walked the streets freely. Meet helpful Golems, amassing ancient knowledge, cunning Horned, controlling the city’s wealth, resourceful Robots, or eccentric Vodniks. Use their unique meeples to calm the river Vltava, rebuild the flooded centre, and control the city’s fate.

This euro-style worker placement game allows players to build their own action spaces, participate in four distinct “mini-games” based on retelling the myth-infused history of Prague, gain unique abilities, and fight over influence in four neighbourhoods.

—description from the publisher

name: Batman: Escape From Arkham Asylum
description:
Batman: Escape from Arkham Asylum is a semi-cooperative dungeon crawl for 1 to 5 players in which the Super Villains of the Batman universe are the protagonists. This is one of the few games where you must defeat Batman, and that gives the player the opportunity to play as dozens of characters. The players will put themselves in the shoes of the most iconic Super Villains of Gotham City: The Joker, Harley Quinn, Two-Face, The Penguin, Bane, Poison Ivy, and The Scarecrow. The goal? Escape from an iconic institution of Gotham City: Arkham Asylum.

Batman: Escape from Arkham Asylum offers the funny and wild vision of the comics of the Batman universe and introduces a novel element: confronting Batman. Players must join forces to achieve their common goal. However, each one of them will have their own hidden objectives, which can range from escaping on their own or sowing as much chaos as possible in the asylum, something they must achieve to gain an advantage over their companions and be the one who finally wins the victory.

The players choose a Super Villain and play their turns one after the other. In each of these turns, the players can perform different actions such as moving around on the board, attacking their enemies with crazy weapons, searching rooms or crafting tools to use in their escape. The game ends when the players escape or when everyone is defeated by the forces of order that run Arkham, from the tough guards of the complex to, of course, the Dark Knight himself.

name: Batra Express
description:
In an Indian town of the 1970s the streets are crowded, always crowded, with bicycle bells ringing and vendors shouting and old buses groaning their way forward while the air itself is thick with the mingled scents of petrol and chai. Cows stand unmoved in the middle of it all and sometimes, just sometimes, an elephant passes through as though to remind the town of another age.

This is where you begin. Your task is to build a delivery firm and to send your couriers scurrying with goods of every kind, goods that never end: hens and pigs and sacks of rice and shoes and furniture and even instruments whose music rises above the traffic. You must be quick, you must be clever, you must choose wisely where to invest and when.

The one who moves with greatest skill, who balances speed with cunning investment, will gather the most rupees, and in this city of endless errands that is the measure of victory.

name: Ada's Dream
description:
In Ada's Dream, work with Ada Lovelace to help build the first computer, fulfilling her dream in this alternate history Euro Game.

Over the course of the game (18 turns), players take dice from the Workshop Rondel, Give Lectures in Prestigious Institutions, Travel the UK, and Complete Assignments from Ada to gather Prestige Points.

Players add Dice, Gears, and Programs to their blueprint Board in a race to build the first Analytical Engine, using dice rondel and manipulation mechanics and literal "engine building". When any engine is completed, the end of the game is triggered and Prestige points are counted.  The player with the most prestige, wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Battle Frenzy
description:
Battle Frenzy is a player vs player game where you control a warrior that has been summoned from a different reality. Your warrior must fight other warriors in a battle for survival. On this battlefield, in varying degrees, warriors are more powerful since their weapons have been enhanced, physical attributes have increased, and they have access to special abilities they normally would not have. Apparently, the unknown masters controlling these battles have done this to balance the fighting abilities of the competitors.

One page rules
No cards
No tokens
No minis
No set up
2d6 system

The central element of Battle Frenzy is your Game Card. Similar to an RPG character sheet, you mark on it with a dry erase marker when Health Points and Level Points are expended. If you don't have a dry erase marker, you can keep track on scratch paper.

name: Battle of Bentonville: March 19th-21st
description:
The Battle of Bentonville (March 19-21, 1865) was the largest Civil War battle in North Carolina and the last major battle between the armies under William T. Sherman and Joseph E. Johnston. The Confederate General Johnston was ordered to stop the Union Army from advancing on Bentonville and hoped to destroy Sherman’s Union army in piecemeal.

This game offers two scenario variants: the first day of battle and the full three-day battle scenario that covers more area around the map.

—description from the designer

name: Battle of Finland 1944
description:
A simulation of the Soviet offensive against Finland in the summer of 1944. The Soviet player must defeat Finland as soon as possible within a limited timeframe so that the Red Army can return to the decisive direction of the war, the Bagration offensive in June-July 1944.

Historically, the Soviets achieved a marginal victory — the Finnish had to withdraw from Ladoga Karelia, but nevertheless prevented the Soviet forces from achieving their ultimate objective — the unconditional surrender of Finland and the Sovietization of the country.

Each game turn represents about seven days. Each hexagon is six miles (10 kilometers) from side to opposite side. Units are corps, divisions, brigades or equivalents and some specialized smaller units.

name: Battle of Little Bighorn Game
publisher: The Historical Game Company, LLC; Blue Panther
description:
1876. The Sioux and Cheyene American Indians have defiantly left the retched living conditions of the US imposed reservation areas. Ambitious Lt. Col. George Armstrong Custer senses the opportunity to make a bigger name for himself by vanquishing the American Indian foes. His arrogance plays right into the hands of his enemy who have other plans for "Yellow Hair" and his men.

The "Battle of Little Bighorn" is a low-to-moderate complex tactical game on Lt. Colonel George Armstrong Custer's campaign against the Northern Plains American Indians during the Great Sioux War. The game takes about 90 minutes to play. One player commands the US forces and the other player commands the other American Indian forces. Cards vary game play.

CONTENTS:

64 game pieces (5/8" inch)
A single rulebook (4 pages)
20 game cards
A canvas game map (11x17" inch)
1 six-sided die (1d6)

-description from publisher's website

name: Battle of the Cyborgs: A Solitaire Sci-Fi Wargame
description:
A Solitaire Sci-Fi wargame.

By the end of the twenty first century the Earth was heading for destruction. Over worked, over populated and dying, it could no longer provide for the masses who relied upon its resources. Gradually, people needed machines and AI to survive. It became commonplace to have mechanical implants, highly sophisticated computerised machinery to aid breathing, mobility, strength and life in general. Hundreds of private providers began to offer these things, often when they were not needed, but always for a price. All other vegetation and animal species were dying, and the world was becoming uninhabitable. The early years of the twenty second century saw various factions build rockets funded by billionaires. The human cyborgs, as they now were, boarded these rockets and fled, searching for a new life anywhere in the depths of space.

One such faction landed on an unknown planet several light years from Earth. However, they were not welcome. It was inhabited by a similar cyborg population, but one that seemingly had plants and animals at its core. They feared the human cyborgs, having studied and observed from afar what the human cyborgs had done to their own planet. And the human cyborgs did not want to share their new planet.
 War was inevitable, and instant.

In the game, the Player will be commanding various units from the army of Human Cyborgs as they battle a seemingly endless stream of enemy cyborgs, known only as the Biota Cyborgs. This game is a solitaire hex and counter sci-fi wargame. You play the game, and the enemy is controlled by the game(or ‘AI’). You will need a good handful of standard six-sided dice to play (ten is ideal, although fewer will do).

—description from the designer

name: Battle of Vinegar Hill Game
description:
In June of 1798 British forces converged on the United Irish camp on Vinegar Hill to crush the Irish Rebellion. A major battle ensued which the British won though many Irish soldiers escaped. The United Irish were superior in numbers (and perhaps religious and ideological fervor) but the British were better equipped and more of a regular, disciplined force.

The game is won by capturing a majority of the objective hexes and not suffering too many casualties in doing so. Cards govern movement, combat and unique events, and vary game play.

A new entry in the Battle Series by The Historical Game Company, LLC.

—description from the designer

name: Battle Pages
description:
In Battle Pages you will protect your kingdom from a wave of enemies, using runs of dice to mine gems and tactically place units throughout the map. If you can survive 6 waves and the boss, you win!

Battle Pages is a roll and write dice game that features tactical dice placement, a little bit of press your luck, and strategic map building.

name: Battlefields of the Napoleonic Wars
description:
Battlefields of the Napoleonic Wars is a wargame system devised by Paolo Mori and Alessandro Zucchini with the aim of bringing to your gaming table — with fast-paced and engaging games — the battles that marked the fate of Europe at the beginning of the 19th century.

Easy-to-learn rules, fast set-up times, a straightforward but exciting command system, and a quick yet deep combat resolution system are just some of the original elements of this game, created with the idea of attracting both battlefield veterans and players fascinated by the world of historical simulation.

name: Battlegroup Clash: Baltics
description:
Battlegroup Clash: Baltics is a two-to six-player tactical land warfare game that plays in two to three hours. It is a commercially-adapted version of a game recently developed for the British Army to help train its junior officers.

It is easy to learn and quick to play, and will appeal both to professional and hobby gamers looking to better understand combat on the modern battlefield.

The game is set in Estonia and covers a hypothetical near-future Russian invasion of the country, and attempts by NATO land forces to repulse it. Each side has a maximum force size equivalent to a reinforced battalion, with individual unit sizes being platoons or sections.

It comes with six scenarios and has three play modes and optional rules, allowing for players to vary the level of realism and complexity of play. The Basic mode of play is equivalent to a light complexity commercial wargame. The Standard and Advanced modes are equivalent to a medium-light complexity game.

While the game mechanics and components will be familiar to anyone that has played a hex and counter wargame, there are several unique features about Battlegroup Clash: Baltics:

Preparation & planning - In the Standard and Advanced modes of the game players will need to draft Orders for their forces. This happens at the start of the game. These Orders drive the actions individual units take in the game. This is a simplified version of the type of planning that would occur in real life. It presents both a challenge and opportunity to players, and greatly enhances the immersion of the game.

Drones and Electronic Warfare - Events in Ukraine have shown how much the use of drones has changed the modern battlefield. Reflecting this, in the game players use UAS drones for reconnaissance and FPV (‘kamikazi’) drones to attack enemy units. Each side can intercept their opponent’s electronic transmissions to improve targeting, and apply tactical Electronic Warfare effects such as jamming the enemy’s drone assets or crippling their GPS navigation.

Real world mapping - The four maps in the game are based on satellite imagery from key locations in Estonia. Using computer aided design, that imagery has been turned into a highly realistic map. There are no hexes, just grid lines, the same as a real world map. Players must read the map terrain to determine key locations and terrain features, and assess how they fit into their battleplan and objectives.

—description from the publisher

name: Battles for Quebec
Battles for the Ardennes: Deluxe Edition
description:
Battles for the Ardennes simulates the battles that occurred in the Ardennes area in World War II with new artwork and mounted map boards. Individual combat units represent between 1,000 and 7,000 men and supporting weapons. Armored units represent between 40 to 180 tanks or Panzers. Artillery units represent between 60 and 100 guns or rocket projectors.

Eight Scenarios:
St. Vith: 6th Panzer Army Attack, 16 Dec.–21 Dec. 1944
Clervaux: Breakout 5th Panzer Army, 16 Dec.–21 Dec. 1944
Celles: Battle Before the Meuse, 23 Dec.–26 Dec. 1944
Sedan 1940: Across the Meuse, 11 May–15 May 1940
Blitzkrieg to the Meuse: 10 May–15 May 1940
The Battle of the Bulge: 16 Dec. 1944–2 Jan. 1945
The Opening Guns: 16 Dec.–20 Dec. 1944
22 December 1944: 22 Dec.–25 Dec. 1944

—description from the publisher

name: Battles in the East 3: Operation Sonnewende/Pomerania and Drive to the Sea
description:
Battles in the East (BITE) is a series simulating World War II Eastern Front battles. The system rules are an evolution of the SPI classics Panzergruppe Guderian, Army Group South, and Cobra. Unit integrity bonuses include Soviet Corps and vary to show the increasing Soviet cohesion and decreasing German cohesion as the war progresses. HQ units provide higher level combat support and supply advantages to corresponding units in range. BITE also incorporates standardized scales (unit size, distance, time) for easy comparisons. While the series rules allow players to play many games with the same core rules, the scenario rules add unique situational elements of each battle. Each volume includes two battles from one year with two copies of the charts and tables as well as scenario rules and set-up cards for easy reference.

Drive to the Sea
West Prussia, January 1945: Stalin’s agenda focused on the conquest of Prussia, the first German territory reached by the advancing Red Army. The German Army, ahead of a total collapse, prepared a ‘defense in depth’ while deploying many Prussian recruited units to defend the region. The Soviet plan was simple—drive from the east while also cutting Prussia from the rest of Germany. The Soviets earmarked Rokossovsky’s 2 Belorussian Front for the task with the veteran 5th Guard Tank Army selected for the drive to the sea. The game runs from 13th January 1945–1st February 1945, a total of 10 game turns.

Battle for Pomerania
Pomerania, February 1945: By February 1945 the German Army faced a desperate situation. The Soviets under Zhukov regrouped at the Oder River preparing to press forward to capture Berlin. However, the northern flank of his Belorussian Front was thinly held and the besieged German garrison in the town of Arnswalde continued to hold. Himmler, with his personal credibility in terminal decline, opted to utilize vital German reserves and SS units to launch a relief effort of limited forces to drive south, relieve Arnswalde, and severely disrupt the Soviet plans. Once the Stavka, the Soviet General Headquarters, recognized the danger, clearing Pomerania became their objective for February and early March 1945. Himmler soon found himself out of his depth in a bloody campaign in Northeast Germany. The game runs from 15th February 1945–5th March 1945, a total of 10 game turns.

Game Contents
• One double-sided 22×34 inch game board
• 440 die-cut 5⁄8-inch counters
• 16-page system rules booklet
• System charts card (2 sets)
• Scenario rules/setup cards (2 sets of 2)
• Scenario display card
• 1 six-sided die
• Storage bags

—description from the publisher

name: Battles in the East 4: Mius River and Vitebsk
description:
Battles in the East (BITE) is a series simulating World War II Eastern Front battles. The system rules are an evolution of the SPI classics Panzergruppe Guderian, Army Group South, and Cobra. Unit integrity bonuses include German divisions and Soviet corps and vary to show the increasing Soviet cohesion and decreasing German cohesion as the war progresses. HQ units provide higher level combat support and supply advantages to corresponding units in range. BITE also incorporates standardized scales (unit size, distance, time) for easy comparisons. While the series rules allow players to play many games with the same core rules, the scenario rules add unique situational elements of each battle. Each volume includes two battles from one year with two copies of the charts and tables as well as scenario rules and set-up cards for easy reference.

Mius River
July–August 1943: This summer is mainly remembered for the failed German Operation Citadel near Kursk, followed by the advance of the Red Army westward to the end of the year. Often overlooked is the battle on the Mius River after the Kursk offensive. Here the Red Army looked to drive into the German rear, capture Stalino and prevent the orderly withdrawal of Army Group South. Field Marshal Manstein still had Hitler’s support and was aided by the able “new” 6th Army commander, General Hollidt. The Wehrmacht fought a classic defense and counter thrust battle in late July. The II SS Pz Corps counterattack in open terrain showed what might have been achieved that summer, if Manstein had been allowed to complete a mobile defense in Southern Russia. The game runs from 17 July–6 Aug.

Vitebsk
Panther Line, November 1943: The summer and early autumn of 1943 was a period of steady retreat and defensive line battles for Army Group Center. Often overlooked until recently, these were bloody campaigns. The key strategic cities of Nevel and Vitebsk were central to the defense of the Panther Line—the link between Army Group North and Center. Large Soviet Guards formations were tasked with taking both and breaching the Panther Line defenses. Defending this area was the depleted 3rd Panzer Army, a panzer army in name only. OKH recognized the importance and the only panzer reserves available were rushed there to stem the Soviet offensive. The battle was fought in awful conditions impacting coordination and supply logistics. The game runs from 1–21 Nov. 1943.

—description from the publisher

name: Battles of Napoleon: Volume II – QUATRE BRAS 1815
description:
Battles of Napoleon is an epic wargame series that simulates the most famous battles of Napoleon on a Tactical level sharing the same basic rules.

The series portrays the most important aspects of battles of the Napoleonic era with easy to learn and remember rules, intuitive mechanics and procedures. Players may focus on taking decisions and playing rather than consulting rules.

The system focusses on the “cat-and-mouse game” of coordination and timing of the various formations of the different arms without too much crunchy chrome.

Infantry was the predominant and most important element in every European army of the period. It usually formed between 60 and 90 per cent of an army in battle, and was both the cheapest and the most versatile type of troops. The foot soldiers had to endure most of the fighting and casualties. Depending on their task, they were either deployed in line (fire power), column (maneuver and assault) or square formation (protection against enemy cavalry).

Cavalry were screening the own army and provided the shock element on a Napoleonic battlefield. Due to their shock power they fixed enemy infantry and forced them to take shelter in square formation. If infantry failed to form square they were overrun. If infantry was fixed in semi-static squares they were very vulnerable to artillery fire.
 Artillery, the queen of the battlefield, was on the one hand having devastating effects on square and closely packed formations, on the other hand artillery alone was extremely vulnerable when getting charged by enemy units.

Generals are tasked with taking advantage of favorable terrain like the famous Duke of Wellington who mastered the reverse slope tactic.

By a simple game mechanic, players will never know the exact strength and power of an enemy unit. Units have a number of strength points that will gradually decrease while engaged with enemy units.

An innovative chit-based Command system, where players randomly draw activation chits determines which army may activate a formation, leads to highly interactive game play. Reaction follows action. We bring the chit-based Command system to a new level: In this games series, players decide which formation is activated when a chit is drawn. A formation may be activated several times per turn. But by each new activation it performs less effective.

During a game turn the players are under constant pressure to decide which formation to activate. By efficient timing of activation players are in the “driver’s seat” to dictate the pace of a battle.

Formations are given orders at the beginning of a game turn and are therefore limited by the actions they can perform on the battlefield. The more “aggressive” orders formations will receive, the more likely is the army will collapse due to fatigue. On the other hand, an army is more likely to gain the initiative on the battlefield by “aggressive” orders.

The scale of the series is appr. 150 meters per hex, infantry units are battalions, artillery is batteries and cavalry is represented as regiments.

Quatre Bras 1815, depicting the encounter at the Quatre Bras crossroads, is the second volume in this series. Special rules like the possibility to activate the French light cavalry brigade, the defense of special structures, the possible arrival of d'Erlon's I Corps add distinctive flavor of the battle.

—description from the publisher

name: Battles of the American Civil War June 1861: July 1862 – A Solitaire Wargame
description:
The American Civil War was a conflict between the United States (the Union or the North) and the eleven states that had seceded from the Union and formed the Confederate States of America (the Confederacy or the South). It lasted from 1861 to 1865. One of the key issues fought over was slavery and the power of the federal government to prohibit it in certain territories. Abraham Lincoln, the first Republican president, promised to keep slavery out of the territories, which was seen as hostile by the South. At the time, the North had well-established industries, but in the South there was far more reliance on large-scale farming, which itself relied on enslaved people. War began in 1861 when Confederate forces opened fire on Fort Sumter in Charleston, and ended in 1865 when the Confederates surrendered.

In the game, the Player will be commanding various units, often representing many hundreds or thousands of men each, seeking to achieve a wide variety of Objectives. Battles from the years 1861 and 1862 are included in this game.

The aim of the game is to present a simple, clear, accessible, and quick to learn game, so that players can get into the action quickly. It does not try to replace more complex wargames which often take many hours to learn and to play. It also does not pretend to be entirely realistic, and many concepts have been simplified or abstracted for gameplay purposes – it is not a simulation. Each of the 20 Battle scenarios can be played in around 20 to 30 minutes, and each one should provide plenty of replayability due some random set up of the initial forces and depending on how the Battle plays out. Note that some Battles represent a specific part of the conflict within that Battle rather than the whole Battle.

This game is a solitaire wargame. You play the game, and the enemy is controlled by the game. You will need a good handful of standard six-sided dice to play (nine is ideal, although fewer will do).

It is highly recommended that the counters provided on the final page of the game are used to play this game. Simply stick them to card and cut them out. A video demonstrating how generally to do this can be found on the Mike Lambo Solitaire Book Games YouTube channel.

On the same channel you will find an instructional playthrough video for the game, which walks players through the rules of the game. The best way to learn the game is to read through the rules and then watch that video.

Players: 1
Time: 20 to 30 minutes per battle
Complexity: 2 / 5

—description from the designer

name: Battles of the American Revolution
description:
Battles of the American Revolution presents 2 separate hex and counter war games from the American Revolution.  The battles in this first volume are Oriskany and Freeman's Farm.

In early 2024, Worthington introduced this innovative box and board size to accommodate our players who wanted the feel of a high-quality board game with the convenience of a game they could take anywhere. We call them travel games because of the small footprint and price, but they are big on gameplay anyplace games are enjoyed.

—description from the publisher

name: Battles of the American Revolution Tri-Pack II: Monmouth, Germantown, Newtown
description:
The second compilation of earlier releases from GMT Games' Battles Of The American Revolution series consisting of:
Monmouth
Germantown
Newtown (which also includes the smaller Oriskany battle)

These are tactical level battles at the regimental level.
The map scale is approximately 200 yd/hex.

Additions to the original releases include:

     maps are hard-mounted
     packaged in a GMT "deep box"
     rules and player aids printed in color
     all replacement counters that have been issued since the games' original releases
     a new one page matrix-style play aid to assist the First Nations player in Newtown
     Joel Toppen's Solitaire Tactics Card play aid
     a significantly upgraded Germantown rulebook addressing errata and ambiguities

name: Battles of the Mexican American War Travel Game
description:
Game:

A hex-and-counter wargame with 2 scenarios about the US-Mexican war.  Both sides race to be the first to accumulate a scenario-specified number of VP, through a combination of occupying key locations and eliminating enemy units.  The active player can use a limited pool of leadership points to boost movement, boost attacks combat, or rally troops during their own turn.  Off turn, the non-active player can use a pool of artillery points to boost defensive combat or make long-ranged attacks.

Publisher Descriptions:

Battles of the Mexican American War presents 2 separate hex and counter war games from the American Revolution.  The battles in this first volume are Buena Vista and NMonterrey.

In early 2024, Worthington introduced this innovative box and board size to accommodate our players who wanted the feel of a high-quality board game with the convenience of a game they could take anywhere. We call them travel games because of the small footprint and price, but they are big on gameplay anyplace games are enjoyed.

—description from the publisher

name: Battles of the War of 1812
description:
Battles of the War of 1812 presents 2 separate hex and counter war games from the American Revolution.  The battles in this first volume are Lundy's Lane and North Point.

In early 2024, Worthington introduced this innovative box and board size to accommodate our players who wanted the feel of a high-quality board game with the convenience of a game they could take anywhere. We call them travel games because of the small footprint and price, but they are big on gameplay anyplace games are enjoyed.

—description from the publisher

name: Beach Day
description:
As you breathe in the cool salty air that gently brushes across your face, the sound of crashing waves fills your ears. The gentle heat of the sun warms your skin while the grit of the warm sand tingles your feet. On the ground, seashells and sandcastles are scattered about among puddles of ocean water making a beautiful tapestry in the sand. It's time for your beach day!

In Beach Day, players draft cards to create a beach that is decorated with shells, sandcastles, water, and much more. After taking cards, you place them as tiles to arrange these objects in optimal formations based on modular scoring cards. The player with the best decorated beach wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Beacon Patrol: Leuchtturm voraus!
description:
Leuchtturm voraus! (Beacon Patrol) is a co-op tile-laying exploration game in which you navigate the coast of the North Sea to secure its beacon buoys, lighthouses and waterways.

You are captains of the Coast Guard. Together you check beacon buoys and lighthouses to ensure the safety of the North Sea coast. You place your tiles next to tiles that are already placed, move your ships, and explore the sea.

Your goal is to explore as many tiles as possible. A tile is considered explored when it’s connected to other tiles on all four of its sides.

—description from the designer

This German edition includes the base game and the expansion Ships & Shores.

name: Beaks
publisher: Ginger Fox Games; Professor Puzzle Games
description:
In Beaks, swoop, steal, and squawk your way to victory!

In this family dexterity game, players take on the role of gulls swooping in to steal food. Using yellow tweezer “beaks,” you must race against your fellow gulls to grab food from the table and match any food order card before the other players. The quickest gull to squawk wins the card and the points!

You can snatch food from another gull but be careful! Have too much food and you lose points.

The first gull to 10 points, wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Bean Counters Inc.
description:
Prepare yourself for a chaotic climb up the corporate ladder in Bean Counters Inc., the all-consuming bean-counting game where survival means mastering an ever-growing list of bizarre rules.

As the CEO introduces new twists, your role — whether Intern, Manager, or aspiring CEO — gets progressively harder, and the pressure to follow rules intensifies. From slamming cards to counting beans and snapping at the right moment, you’ll have to stay sharp to avoid getting fired.   In this bean bonkers game, quick thinking, fast reflexes, and a bit of luck are your only allies as you compete to outlast your equally incompetent colleagues in the relentless pursuit of bean-counting mastery. But beware: the CEO loves surprises, and with each round, new, unexpected rules will keep everyone on their toes.

Will you rise to the top, or will the chaos of counting get the best of you? Find out if you’ve got what it takes to thrive at Bean Counters Inc.

—description from the publisher

name: Bean to Bar
publisher: analog lunchbox (アナログランチボックス)
description:
Players become chocolatiers seeking to share truly delicious chocolate with the world by building their very own chocolate brands.

In order to grow your brand, you’ll need to source quality cacao from cacao farmers, develop new confections to sell at events, local markets, and your own brick-and-mortar stores, recruit specialists to help with your operations, collaborate with local confectionery shops, and participate in an annual chocolate contest.

—description from the designer

name: Bear Mountain Camping Adventure
description:
In a world where nature's grandeur meets the thrill of adventure, lies the looming shadow of Bear Mountain. And now, you’re invited to embark on a remarkable journey through its untamed wilderness in Bear Mountain Camping Adventure.

But this won't be any ordinary expedition. To conquer Bear Mountain, you must venture through the great outdoors, camping in at least one site of every color. As you traverse the scenic trails, you'll be pitted against your own desire to stop and smell the roses, and an urge to push the trek further into the mountains. For at the end of the day, the first brave adventurer to reach the Bear Mountain Campsite will come out victorious.

In order to complete the journey, travelers must strategically build both their green and their blue camping activity decks by collecting cards which will help them to explore new areas and campsites. Upgrade your tent to unique campers to carry more gear and strengthen each hand. Every night, you’ll want to carefully decide where to set up camp, as this will determine which activities you’ll draw for the next day. But be warned, while some campsites have incredible benefits, you may accidentally startle a roaming bear, causing you to flee in the wrong direction.

Your choices will shape your adventure. Every decision is an opportunity to experience the wonders of Bear Mountain in new and exciting ways, creating limitless replayability. And when you reach the pinnacle, a panorama of natural splendor stretches before you. Gaze upon the gorgeous vistas, a testament to your triumph and the memories you've created along the way.

—description from the publisher

name: Beast Builders: Claws & Jaws
description:
Beast Builders: Claws & Jaws is a fast-paced strategy card game. You are an alien gamer in the far future, using Earth-animal DNA to play an arena-combat spectator sport.

Combine animal cards into a uniquely dangerous Beast, battling against your opponents for a prize of rare and valuable Lithium Salts. To win you must reduce opposing Beasts to 0 Health, but be careful not to let another player strike the final blow!

You will love Beast Builders if you are a fan of games with direct player interaction, like Evolution/Oceans, King of Tokyo, or Radlands!

—description from the publisher

name: Beastro
description:
Welcome to Beastro, where mythical beast chefs compete to make the best dishes!  Beastro is a team-based trick-taking game with hidden roles where you have to figure out who is in your team with and outsmart the others, collecting as many tricks as possible for your team.

Each round you: (1) wager to become the Head Chef and select your Secret Chef teammate, (2) Cook crazy dishes in order to win the most tricks for your team, (3) Play special cards to ruin dishes and get bonuses at unique Restaurants!

Every game you will play as of the mythical Chef and use their beastly power only once to turn the odds in your favour.

Beastro is played over a series of three round and the player with most point at the end will be the winner.

name: Baghdad: The City of Peace
description:
Set during Baghdad's Golden Age, players take on the role of Viziers, looking to build their family's prestige and grow the great City of Peace.

Move your Vizier around the circular city, collecting scientific equipment, teaching students, and translating works.

Each turn, play a card, pushing another card out of your tableau and triggering its ability. Build up sets of icons to pull of more difficult actions and plan ahead to complete upcoming objectives. Work together to build the Golden Palace, Fill the House of Wisdom, and send ships down the Tigris.

Baghdad: The City of Peace is programmed hand management game featuring a mega rondel. Points are scored for Night Characters, Artefacts, Favour, and Shame tokens. The player with the highest total score wins, becoming the most eminent courtier in the great City of Peace.

A retail version of this game was cancelled and only the Deluxe edition was printed thus all copies include the Golden Age Expansions.

—description from the publisher

name: Beautiful Garden
description:
As a gardener, you must wisely relocate beautiful flowers to exchange them for coins, which will allow you to build houses, tractors, and tools, or trade your flowers for points, which will determine the winner of the game. Play over the course of approximately 40 minutes simultaneously with your companions by rolling three dice, which will affect everyone and determine the column where you can choose between plants, terrain, mowing the lawn, placing bees to follow the flower path, or preparing the cactus to attack your opponents. After making your selection, you can exchange the flowers for the two limited options in your inventory. Finally, make your purchases. In the course of 5 rounds, the player with the most garden points will be the winner.

-description from designer

name: Barbecubes
publisher: Alley Cat Games; BoardM Factory; The Game Builders; Little Rocket Games; Reflexshop; Rexhry; UpDown Juegos
description:
The BBQ's hot, and it's time to prep the food for cooking, but don't spill on the grill or everyone will go hungry!

1. Draw a card!
2. Grab food with tongs!
3. Add it to the grill, but don't drop any!

Take turns to add food to the grill. If any piece fall off, take a card.  Get 2 cards and you're eliminated.  The last player standing, wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Behind the Trenches
description:
Behind the Trenches is a World War 1 resource management, deck builder game. The goal is to push the front line into your opponents HQ.

Play consists of 3 Phases:


    Battle Phase: Deal 5 cards from the unclaimed deck (80 card deck to begin the game). Use numbered dog tags to fight over cards against your opponent. The player with the highest accumulated score adds that card to their discard pile.  



    Country Phase: Each country gains a unique set of resources, has a few unique processes like building a trench or turning one resource into another. Most importantly it's where you build your guns and train your troops (i.e. adding a basic infantry card to your discard pile).



    War Phase: Shuffle the discard pile and form a deck.  Now draw 4. Take turns with your opponent playing one card at a time to gain resources, dig trenches, bombard enemy entrenchments, and push the front line forward using human wave attacks.


Once both players hands are empty, players check their decks.  
If both players have at least one card, they both draw another 4 cards (or at least attempt to draw 4 more cards) 
If either player's deck has 0 cards, the war phase ends and a new battle phase begins.

This continues until the front line is pushed into a players HQ.

—description from the publisher

name: Behind: Purple
description:
Analyze, assemble, admire — in this follow-up to Behind, you'll find three new scenes to solve, each with its own unique mechanisms and reflection. You want to observe the tiles laid out in front of you, then assemble them logically and turn them over to admire the result on the reverse! Six clue cards are available for each scene and should be turned over in numerical order. The scenes in the box are:


     La Machine Infernale (illustred by Crocotame, 42 tiles)
     Le Repas (illustred by Mélody Leblond, 86 tiles)
     Le Cahier (illustred by Pierô & Isaak, 87 tiles)


Once you've reconstructed the picture, you can read all of the clues at your disposal, even if none of them were turned over while you were solving the picture. They'll help you validate your thinking and confirm your thoughts! Finally, flip each tile to reveal the final image...

—description from the publisher

name: Belinda's Big Bonus: a Belinda Blinked game
description:
The officially licensed Belinda Blinked board game adapts Rocky Flintstone's cult classic novels. These defy genre, combining espionage thriller, character comedy, unusual pornography, and, of course, business and leadership advice to tell the story of Belinda Blumenthal, the International Sales Director of cookware company Steele's Pots and Pans.

In Belinda's Big Bonus, you and your pals take on the role of new Steele's employees, creatively working together to score Bigger and Bigger Business Deals. Along the way you'll connect with fan-favorite characters like Bella Ridley, James Spooner, the Duchess of Epsom, and even Toffee Apple Chew.

But make sure you manage your calendar and itinerary - you don't want to miss special events like the Steele's Tombola or the Pots-and-Pan-Pacific Cooking Convention. Will you come out on top of the other players, and win that big Bonus? Or will you betray this new Glee Team for a payday from the wickedish Herr Wolfgang Bisch?

This is a light, accessible business strategy game. Any visits to the Leather Room or the Maze, or any indulgence in a cherished Kilkenny custom, are left up to your imagination.

—description from the publisher

name: Berlin 1945: The Fall of the Reichstag
description:
Berlin 1945: La Caida del Reichstag is a war simulation game for two players that recreates the battle of Berlin from April 21 to May 2 1945: the last major battle that marked end of World War II. One player represents the German army and the other the Soviet army. This is a light wargame which wisely simulates in a short playing time ( around 60 minutes) the difficulties the Soviets found in the street fightings all over the big city among ruins against the desperate struggle of the defending disjointed remnants of a once mighty German army.
Game mechanisms are fresh and rarely seemed in other wargames of the WW2. Quick, fun and enjoyable experience for both players. No dice to bother not checking busy combat charts no roll die modifiers. Just your brain to analize the best move, randomness is then very limited and most of times you have control on it. In this game you don't win by luck but by playing smart.

Game play differences from Berlin 1945 (2022 Bonsai version): There are some changes in the set up, in the input of reinforcements, in some counters (in NAC there are elite Soviet units), in the effects of some of the event cards, the way to mark the movement orders differs and a small change in victory conditions.

-description from designer

name: Berlin: Fall of the Reich, 1945
description:
"The enemy will be crushed along the shortest route to Berlin. The capital of fascist Germany will be taken and the banner of victory planted over it."
Gregory Zhukov, April 15, 1945

After years of fighting and millions dead the Red Army has finally pushed the fascist invaders out of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe and is poised to capture the capital of Germany's Third Reich, the city of Berlin. There can be little question Berlin must be included with names like Stalingrad, Cassino, Manila, and Okinawa as one of the most costly and destructive battles of the entire Second World War. The campaign by the Soviet First Belorussian Front and First Ukrainian Front has been depicted by a handful of two-player de signs in the past but is presented here in a new and exciting SOLITAIRE format, the third in a series of single-player area movement games by publisher Take Aim Designs.

Berlin: Fall of the Reich, 1945 puts the player in charge of the war-weary but experienced and determined Red Army while the game system handles the defending and largely static German side. No two games will ever be the same. Each turn presents new and unique challenges for the player in form of random events uncertain supply deliveries, and unknown German area strengths and defensive strategies.

The game is a nine-turn campaign covering the Soviet Union's assault on the city during April and May 1945 The deeper Soviet forces advance, from the city's suburbs to its industrial districts and fortress-like govern ment buildings, the greater German resistance becomes. The number of Soviet units fought to exhaustion. effectively out of action, mounts. But there can be no rest. Stalin is watching and expects you to capture the German Reichstag by May Day. The player wins by compelling the German defenders to surrender and loses if Stalin's approval falls too low.

With a setup time of less than 15 minutes, low counter density, endless variability, and quick playing time Berlin: Fall of the Reich, 1945 will appeal to every level of player, from the novice to the grognard.

Few battles at the send of the Second World War exceeded the destruction and brutality of the fighting in the city of Berlin. Will you be among those awarded with the title Hero of the Soviet Union or will you incur Stalin's wrath? The decisions you make will determine your fate as the war in Europe ends.

—description from the back of the box

name: Bespoke
description:
Bespoke is a compendium style climbing-shedding card game for 2 players using a standard deck of cards.

In compendium games, players compete to accomplish a series of different objectives. These objectives are known as contracts. Each player must fulfill every contract before the game concludes. Once a player has completed a particular contract, they are not allowed to attempt it again.

In Bespoke, the objective for every contract remains the same: to play all of your cards as quickly as possible. However, each contract is uniquely tailored, offering its own distinct twists on the rules of play.

—description from the designer

name: Best in Show: Dashing Dogs
description:
Choose 3 dogs to prepare for the All-Breed dog show. Discipline,  train, groom and enter them into the show, by collecting and trading preparation tokens.

Once a player has completed all 3 of their dog cards, the preparation round ends and it's time for the properly prepped pups to head to to the show!

At the show, dogs compete for the judges in 5 rounds of fierce, furry competition.

Each round, players must collect points cards while avoiding mishaps to collect the most points. At the end of 5 rounds, the dog with the most points wins!

—description from the designer

name: Best Shot
description:
This is a trick-taker in which teams are battling to win the majority of holes on a 9-hole golf course  Each hole is a par 3 and will be played over 3 distinct tricks: Drive, Chip and a Putt.

The rank of the cards will shift depending on the trick being played.  A team wins a hole by winning at least 2 out of the 3 tricks by hitting the best shot.  As soon as a team has won 5 holes they have won the game!

name: Bested Another Time
description:
Conversations fill the streets in Batish Columbia, as the famous film festival Batiff just finished; everyone wants to discuss their thoughts on the movies they just saw. You and your fellow fruit bat friends make to the local fruit shop to dish over a dish of delish drupes. Remember best bat manners: when someone bows out of a topic, they get to start the next one. That said, these chatty battys are known to ramble, so make sure to say your piece before your fruit goes stale!

Bested Another Time is a climbing, shedding game where passing gets you perks, but beware: those who haven't passed yet can keep playing, even by themselves.

—description from the publisher

name: Bestiario
description:
Bestiary is a simple card driven draft game in which players create chimeras by adding different creature parts.

Each turn, players take turns to draw a card from a pool, then use that card to begin a new chimera, continue one in progress, or complete one. Creature parts include tails, bodies and heads. The game ends when the draw deck runs out; then, the player with the most points among those printed in their chimeras wins.

—description from the designer

name: FateFlip: By Royal Decree
publisher: Red Cat Games; Alley Cat Games; Draco Ideas; Frosted Games; Lifestyle Boardgames Ltd; Old Dawg; Origames
description:
“Those called upon to play a decisive part in the history of nations are more often than not unaware of the destinies they embody.” — Maurice Druon

You are the first born prince. Ever since your earliest years, you’ve had to watch your actions carefully, knowing that one day, they’ll shape the fate of many. What legacy do you wish to leave? Will your people look upon you with hope and adoration, or will they yearn for your downfall? Can you bring justice and prosperity to your kingdom?

FateFlip is a story that develops differently depending on your decisions, the consequences to which you will learn either right away or later on. Find out all 12 endings to this adventure!


     Read the text on the upper half of a card and choose one of the available options. 
     Adjust the parameters on the counter according to your decision.
     Flip and move the card as instructed by the icons and find out what comes of your decision.


—description from the publisher

name: Between Light & Shadow: Chapter II – Twilight
description:
Immerse yourself in the mystical desert world where everything takes place between light and shadow. In a world threatened by darkness, you take on the role of Mara, a brave adventurer who is on a journey that will determine both her fate and that of the world itself.

Your path is determined by dice and clever resource management. Use your dice strategically to activate powerful abilities and perform decisive actions as you fight your way through the challenges of the desert world. You have both roll-and-write mechanics and tactical planning at your disposal to master the various tasks. Always pay attention to Mara's health and energy, because if one of these resources drops to 0, the adventure ends abruptly.

Mara moves between light and shadow, and each of your decisions will change the balance in the world. Will you choose the light and defy the darkness, or will you give in to the shadow and unleash its power? The world around you reacts to your choices and adapts to your journey, making each game a unique experience.

—description from the designer

name: Lost! in the Woods
description:
Lost! in the Woods is a family game which includes a large map, on which one player is ‘lost’. The rest of the players have to find that player by listening to their description of the area of the map they’re lost in.

The lost player determines their location on the map by drawing a location card, and describing what they see on it. However, the players are limited by a communication card, which creates a silly restriction!

If the search party can find the lost player before the time runs out, they win the round.

—description from the publisher

name: Beyond the Event Horizon
description:
Beyond the Event Horizon is a diesel-punk inspired 4X space tile game that focuses on larger, multi-player combats and customizable ships. It focuses less on civilization building and focuses more on fast-paced, competitive gameplay.

Enter through a black hole into uncharted space. Discover new planets to capture them for resources and tech. Use this tech to upgrade your ships with basic upgrades and special upgrades found in space. You can then customize your three different ship types to create a superior fighting force and dominate your opponents in large battles. Battles can have dozens of ships, from multiple players all fighting for control of an area, and the battles move so quickly you'll have lots of opportunities to come back for a second chance at winning.

You can use planetary enhancements to develop and defend your planets. During each round marauder ships will enter through new placed wormholes to attack and when defeated, they drop new special upgrades to enhance your ships. These wormholes open up the battlefield as you can travel through them to access different parts or the map. The tiles are placed in a new spot every game, so find new strategies to win.

Beyond the Event Horizon features streamlined rules with complex, engaging strategy. This is a great game for beginners of 4X space tile games, with still so much for long time lovers of the genre. Fast paced and action-packed, it's not "Space...The Final Frontier" it's "Space...THE FINAL FRONT LINE!"

—description from the publisher

name: Biathlon Blast
description:
Race past rivals, manage your pulse, and hit every target in Biathlon Blast, the skiing and shooting strategy game for 2 to 6 players. Choose a uniquely skilled biathlete, draft behind opponents, and adapt to shifting wind conditions as you blast through snow-covered trails.

Each round, a dual-action card sets your speed, affects your pulse, and alters the wind. The faster you go, the harder it is to shoot, but nailing your shots gives you powerful momentum. With intuitive, language-independent gameplay and ever-changing conditions, Biathlon Blast delivers rich interaction, tough decisions, and an unforgettable story with every game.

No two races are ever alike, except for one thing: Only one will be crowned champion!

—description from the publisher

name: Biblus: Chronicle I
description:
Step right up, adventurers, and prepare to embark on an epic journey through the sacred scriptures in Biblus: Chronicle I! Gather your flock of 2 to 10 eager participants, for a test of biblical knowledge and wits like no other.

Within the confines of this ancient tome lie 64 enigmatic rebus cards, each a cryptic window into the cherished tales of the Good Book. With the shuffle of cards, the game ignites, promising moments of both enlightenment and hilarity.

As players take turns drawing from the deck, the tension mounts. With bated breath, they reveal the intricate symbols, challenging their peers to decipher the hidden truths within.
