Amidst a chorus of guesses and laughter, one lucky soul holds the key to the solution, their lips sealed as others scramble for revelation.

With each triumphant deciphering, a card is claimed, a badge of honor for the victor. Yet, even in moments of defeat, the journey continues, with unsolved rebuses returning to the deck for another chance at glory.

Passing the torch of inquiry from one seeker to the next, the cycle of discovery unfolds until every card finds its rightful keeper.

—description from the designer

name: Bicocca (1522) • Pavia (1525): Second expedition of François I to Italy
description:
To celebrate the 500th anniversary of the Battle of Pavia (February 24, 1525),  this game features  the entire 6th Italian War, beginning in 1521 and leading up to Pavia,. The strategic map will include part of southern France, invaded by the Imperials led by defector Charles de Bourbon, former constable of France, and notably the strategic city of Marseille, which has been under siege for 40 days.

There are different scenarios:
- La Bicocca: 1521-22
- Intermezzo : 1522-1523
- Marseille: 1523-24
- Pavia: 1524-25
- The 6th war of Italy: 1521-25

For those who own “Marignan 1515, la chevauchée de François 1er en Italie”, the map will be twice as large (85 x 60cm), with the same number of counters (216 in 15mm format) and a thick rules and scenario booklet in English and French. The game will be available in a ziplock format.

Number of Players: 2
Solo Playability: 4/10
Complexity: 6/10
Duration: 120 to 180 minutes
One Turn: One to two months (winter)
1 Strengh Point: Represents 500 to 2,000 men
Scale: One zone ≈ 50 km

—description from the publisher

name: Bidder Battle
description:
Bidder Battle is an exciting auction-based board game where players compete to win valuable items hidden inside storage units. With every turn, players have the chance to become the Auctioneer, setting the stage for fast-paced bidding wars. The goal? Make the most money by acquiring items at a bargain and outsmarting your opponents in a high-stakes auction environment. Only those with sharp instincts, quick decision-making, and a knack for strategic bidding will come out on top.

Each round, the Auctioneer presents a storage unit filled with face-down items, which could range from valuable treasures to tricky "Havoc" cards that could render all contents worthless. Players must decide whether to pay the entry fee to buy into the auction, gaining them the right to bid. Peeking and flipping cards give savvy players glimpses of what’s inside, but too much information might raise the stakes for everyone. It’s a delicate balance of risk and reward as players try to outbid their rivals without breaking the bank.

As the bidding heats up, players shout their offers, hoping to secure a unit at the best price. If no one else matches their final bid, the storage unit—and its contents—are theirs! But be careful: soiled mattresses, busted treadmills, and black mold may be waiting for them. The game is full of surprises, keeping every player on their toes until the very end.

Once all players have taken turns as the Auctioneer twice, the game concludes. Players tally up the value of their remaining cash and collected items, and the player with the highest total claims victory as the ultimate bidder in this battle of wit, strategy, and nerve!

—description from the publisher

name: Biddle
description:
Each round in Biddle, players are presented with a challenge of what must be rolled on six dice, say, two three-of-a-kinds, a sum of less than 12, or four 3s and two 5s.

The first player states how many rolls of the dice they think will be sufficient to satisfy the challenge. Each subsequent player either calls the bid, undercuts the bid (by proposing a lower number of rolls), or drops out of the bidding phase, believing that the challenge can't be met in the stated number of rolls.

Once at least one person has dropped out and all players are divided into two teams, the players who have made the bid try to satisfy the challenge. If they do, they score points; if not, the doubters score.

The game lasts ten rounds with the points escalating over time. You can score both for doubting and for completing challenges, and in the end whoever has scored the most points wins.

name: Big Fish Card Game
description:
A game all about sustainable fishing in Tasmania.

In the Big Fish Card Game, players take on the role of a recreational fisher who has to catch fish from their fishing spot but also manage the fish population. They do this by selecting which fish to catch and which to leave. Actions are based on the number and size of your fish and so its up to the players to makes sure they can keep fishing on future turns.

The game has three types of cards, fish cards, wild cards and event cards. Fish cards are the main card in the game and represent many local Tasmanian fish species. Wild Cards include things like seaweeds which help you grow fish and oyster reefs that help with fish spawning. There are also wild cards that affect your opponents fishing spot by causing chaos. Lastly event cards happen at the end of each round and can either positively or negatively affect the players fishing spot.

The player who fishes and looks after their spot the best and thus earns the most points becomes the #1 fisher!

name: Tic Tac Trek
description:
Explore the wilds in a 2-player tile-laying simple strategic game. The closer you camp to the unexplored wilderness, the higher you'll score.

Tic Tac Trek is a light strategy game. Players take turns drafting tiles from a bag to place in the shared play area. If the tile placed forms 3 in a row, the player can place one of their campfire tokens in the tile just played.

Play continues until all tiles have been placed from the bag. Players will then score their campfire tokens that are in the play area. Each empty space surrounding the campfire scores 1 point. The player with the most points wins.

name: Big Wave
description:
This is a must-not-follow trick taker with a theme of big wave surfing in different locations around the world.  The game also features special action selection and a victory point track that players manipulate during the course of play.

—description from the designer

name: Timber Town
publisher: Alley Cat Games; Rexhry; Seabrook Studios
description:
In Timber Town you are a beaver architect, constructing a new town on the riverbank using buildings sent drifting down the river.

Timber Town is a "river drafting" game where players grab tiles from an ever changing board. Players place their tiles in their towns into the same column from which the tile was drafted from in an effort to match the objectives for that game.

Different objectives are used between each game giving over 1000+ satisfying ways to score!

—description from the publisher

name: Bing! Bang! Boom!
description:
Bing! Bang! Boom! is a high-energy, fast-paced family card game that brings action, laughter, and friendly chaos to your game nights. Perfect for kids, teens, and adults, this easy-to-learn yet wildly engaging game challenges players to race against each other, matching colorful firework cards and launching them on the correct pads while shouting "BING!", "BANG!", and "BOOM!" With four launch pads and five matching cards in play, one unlucky player always ends up stuck with the dud, adding tension and excitement to every round.

Musical Chairs for Cards: In this fun family card game, four launch pads and five matching cards lead to one inevitable result: someone gets stuck with the Dud! Avoid the dud to win in this card game for family night that blends speed, laughter, and suspense into every round

—description from the publisher

name: Bookshelf
description:
Bookshelf is the new game in Alley Cat Games' ever popular tin line.

Players must work together to cooperatively stack books on top of a tower of cards. Cards have instructions on which books to place on top of it, and restrictions of where most of the books need to be placed. Don't be fooled though, placing books one at a time is harder than it initially looks!

—description from the publisher

name: Biostrife
description:
Conquer Terrania as one of four hero warlords by uniting continents, waging war, curing infectous diseases, deploying bioweapons, and advancing technology.  Outlast enemies, manage population and form alliances to dominate the world in this unique 2 to 4 player world-conquering, strategy deck buiding, resource trading, card game.


     Explore an in-depth, strategic world-conquering and disease-mastering experience.
     Save Terrania, a futuristic, sci fi, urban, apocalyptic environment dominated by corporations.
     Master a unique, double resource-based deck-building board game.


—description from the designer

name: Biota: Strange World
description:
Biota: Strange World is a competitive tableau builder in which 2-5 players traverse the planet of Biota, gathering resources and collecting creatures with unique abilities. Players will use these abilities to move around the map, gather extra foods, and avoid the apex predators that hunt them and their creatures.

—description from the designer

name: Biotope: Wer schafft den besten Lebensraum?
description:
Each turn in the roll-and-write game Biotope, one player rolls the dice, then everyone takes their turn at the same time, trying to place the symbols skillfully to create the best ecosystem, while not leaving any gaps along the way. You need to think tactically...and hope for a bit of luck.

Four game scenarios offer variety and extra fun: Will you compete against one another in an exciting competition, or go it alone on the hunt for record points? From tramp to biotope master, who will achieve the highest score?

name: Bish Bash Bosh
description:
Shout, slam, and laugh your way to victory with Bish Bash Bosh! This fast-paced card game is all about speed, saying sounds, and split-second reactions. Ideal for families, parties, or game night chaos, it’s the ultimate showdown of quick reflexes.

Player’s race to match the word sound chain, ish, ash, and osh in the discard pile with the cards in their hands - in 5 seconds or less! If they can't, they must draw a card and play moves to the next player.  If they lay down an "osh" card, they pick who starts the next sequence.  If they play a card in the wrong order, they must take it back and draw more.

The first player to play all their cards, wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Bite Me
description:
Deep somewhere far in the middle of the ocean, hungry Sharks feast on anything they can find There’s fish everywhere, and it’s all too easy to gulp down “just one more”... but your memory is fuzzy, and your bloated stomach is ticking. One fish too many, and boom…you’re fish food.
In Bite Me, you’ll feast on hidden Food cards, bluff your way past danger, and outsmart your fellow sharks, all while trying to remember just how close to bursting you really are. Sabotage your rivals. Block their dirty tricks. Swap guts with a grin. But watch out…
When the dreaded Fish Frenzy strikes, everyone must reveal what they’ve swallowed. And if your score tips over 10? You explode!!! So vomit your way to safety or pay the ultimate price.

—description from the publisher

name: Bitter Rivals
description:
Bitter Rivals is a build-em style party game where the first player to build their fruit controlled mecha suit wins!

There are two decks, the lemon deck and the lime deck. players use Sour Street cards to pick up from the lime deck and build their mecha suits, they end their turn by picking up from the lemon deck.

You can use action cards to slow other players down, like flipping their armour cards over, slicing an armour piece back into the lime deck, swapping a piece of yours with a piece of theirs or by playing battle cards to directly steal from another player.

Slice, Yoink, Flip and Battle to be the Zest player around.

—description from the designer

name: 3 Witches
description:
3 Witches is a must-follow,  trick-taking game with no trump suit. At the start of each round, players bid on how many tricks they can win (out of five). The highest bidder becomes the Lead Witch, and their opponents play together on a team as Lesser Witches.

The Lead Witch plays two cards (one face down), while the two Lesser Witches combine one card each. Two ingredients of the same rank or suit get added together, leading to tricky situations!

If the Lead Witch wins exactly the number of tricks that they bid, they receive two fate tokens at the end of the round; if not, each Lesser Witch receives one fate token. The first player to collect five fate tokens wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Black Flight
description:
It is May 1917 and you are in command of No. 10 (Naval) Squadron. A few weeks ago, the Royal Flying Corps (RFC) experienced the disaster of "Bloody April". Approximately 250 pilots were lost in combat against Germany’s best, including the famous Red Baron, Manfred von Richthofen. The RFC begged for relief and the Royal Naval Air Service (RNAS) stepped in to hold the line.

Everyone expected a massacre. The leadership of the RFC, expected that “Bloody April” would extend and “Bloody Summer” would follow as the hastily assembled relief squadrons from the Royal Navy, almost all Canadian pilots, were swept from the skies. Yet the Canadians of RNAS proved everyone wrong. Not only did they not get massacred, they turned the tide.

One squadron among them, Naval 10, as it was called, bore the brunt of the challenge. Within that squadron, one Flight – just five pilots and aeroplanes –  known as “Black Flight” and lead by Flight Sub-Lieut. Raymond Collishaw, took to the skies over the Ypres Salient and set a record in aerial combat that stands to this day – in eleven weeks, Naval 10 downed 87 German aeroplanes, many of them drawn from among Germany’s finest.

Today, despite being the highest scoring naval aviator of all time, the name of Raymond Collishaw is little known. In skill, he rivalled the prowest of the Red Baron himself. Flying his Sopwith Triplane, over the course of those eleven weeks, personally he downed 30 of the Germans.

Black Flight is a solitaire air war game set in the Great War, often called the First World War. As with all wargames from Historic Wings, Black Flight is deeply researched. You learn about history as you play the game – not the Hollywood version, but the real thing. The rules are built to mirror history, carefully crafted to recreate the true circumstances faced by Collishaw’s Canadian pilots. Yet the outcomes are not guaranteed. You will be called on to fly historic missions across the trenches and over No Man’s Land – and beyond, where the Germans wait patiently with their Albatros and Halberstadt scout planes.

Your orders will reflect the actual patrols of the time – OPs, Offensive Patrols that penetrated deep behind enemy lines; LPs, Line Patrols that ran north and south over the trenches; escort missions where you protect bombers, reconnaissance aeroplanes, photo reconnaissance flights, and artillery direction missions. The routes you fly will be historically accurate – yet through the careful construction of weekly changing tables, each game will be a new and different experience, ensuing extraordinary replayability.

At the core of the game is that you manage your own Naval 10 squadron. You will recruit your pilots and each will have unique characteristics as defined by a mix of 45 Trait Cards and 45 Vice Cards that give each the very strengths and weaknesses that reflected the times. With they lived in. Each time you play, your squadron will be different, your challenges will be unique, and your struggles will be memorable. Unique among aviation games today, Black Flight recreates the diverse personalities of the pilots themselves – some may be reckless, others ruthless, in the wake of bad experiences, their condition will deteriorate. Your best ace pilot, seeing one to many of his friends shot from the sky, may take to alcohol. Your most trusted and reliable cornerstone of the squadron may suffer a nervous breakdown. Yet the orders keep coming. Just as experienced by the real Naval 10 from May through July 1917, your losses will mount and your men will become progressively exhausted and stressed.

Black Flight is the first in a series of solitaire Great War titles from Historic Wings that, as the series is published, will enable players to fly against one another – pitting the Canadians of the RNAS against the Imperial German Air Serice, taking to the skies with the RFC, or, between glasses of wine, kicking the tires of your Nieuports and flying into the teeth of battle. Each nationality will have its own unique Trait Cards and Vice Cards that reflect the times, the traditions, and the historic personalities of each.

Suitable for gameplay with miniatures – including with 1/350th or larger models, right up to 1/72 if you have a dining table playing space!!

Will the fifteen pilots of your own Naval 10 fare better than Collishaw? Will your leadership help turn the tide against the Germans? Will you reverse the disaster of “Bloody April” and open the way for the upcoming Messines and Ypres offensives or will you experience a “Bloody Summer of 1917”?

For God, King, England, and the Commonwealth!

-description from designer

name: Black God's Gambit
description:
Based on sword and sorcery stories by C.L. Moore (one of the first women to publish in the genre, and a contemporary of Conan's Robert E. Howard), Jirel of Joiry’s kingdom has been overtaken by the warlord Guillame. Her last ditch attempt to save her kingdom involves travel into the realm of the Black God to search for a means to destroy her enemy and take back her kingdom... potentially at the cost of her own soul.

One or two players can assume the role of either Jirel (tempestuous female warrior) or the Black God (a phantasm with unknowable intrigues). Each role will be forced to make difficult choices in this fast-paced, rules lite, GM’less tabletop "micro game". Can Jirel claim the Black God's deadly kiss and retain her sanity? Will it be worth the effort, and will she ultimately regret her choice?

The Kickstarter was funded in September of 2022 and at that time the game and its parent boxed rpg set were planned for release sometime in late 2023. As of June 2025, the game is still unprinted & unreleased.

name: Black Hats
description:
Black Hats is a head-to-head, tactical board game with a deckbuilding component to boot. Players take turns commanding their VR hackers (called runners) or playing executable cards to support them from a custom-built cyberdeck. Your cyberdeck allows you to hack the hex board upon which you play.

There are 24 runners, 20 rigs, and 45 unique executable cards to choose from in deck building, allowing you to craft a strategy that feels unique to you and your crew. Rigs provide a runner with a stat line and potentially an ability, but every runner has their own signature active and passive ability. There is a huge amount of experimentation and re-playability to be enjoyed!

The tactical core of the game revolves around the hacking mechanic. The network is divided by connecting groups of same-colored hexes into "subnets," but both players can change the color of any space at any time with their cards, reshaping the board as you play. An enemy that sits across the board may be absolutely unreachable or just a single space away and, if you can outsmart your opponent, you control which.

Forget about range, cover, and terrain - on this virtual battlefield you trade trenches for subnets and fire support for executable cards. The battles on the network aren't fought with soldiers, they're fought with runners.

Hire your crew, customize your cyberdeck, and hack your way to an early retirement. This is Black Hats!

—description from the designer

name: Black Rose Wars: Duel – Kami
description:
High in the sacred mountains of Japan lies the hidden Lodge of the Sun, where ancient spirits guard a long-forgotten power.
Here, two mighty Mages are fated to clash in a deadly duel of wit, will, and unleashed arcane fury.

Kami is a game of swift, tactical magic duels, where every move is a precise strike, and every spell weaves your path toward destiny.
Wield forbidden magic, summon the might of the Kami, and strike when your opponent shows the faintest weakness
Only the most cunning and unyielding will claim the Lodge’s sacred power.

Duel of Mages
Duel – Kami offers intense, head-to-head battles for two players, where you’ll fight for control of the mysterious Lodge of the Sun nestled in the sacred mountains of Japan—perfect for those seeking fast-paced, strategic gameplay with high replay value.

Face the Avatar
Challenge yourself in Solo Mode or in Duel Mode by confronting Mononoke, a powerful AI-controlled Avatar designed to test the skills of even the most seasoned Magisters.

Master the Portals
Duel – Kami introduces Portals, magical gateways that connect rooms within the Lodge of the Sun and unlock new tactical paths to surprise your opponent and control the board.

A New Way to Play
Duel – Kami isn’t just a standalone experience—it also expands the world of Black Rose Wars, adding new layers of strategy, characters, and content to enrich your existing collection.

—description from the publisher

name: Black Skin Black Shirt: Ethiopia vs. Fascist Italy 1935-37
description:
ETHIOPIA VS. FASCIST ITALY 1935-1937

A Prelude to the Second World War

Fascist Italy's 1935 invasion of Ethiopia set the world on course for World War Two. The failure of the League of Nations to deter Fascist aggression led to policies of appeasement, the rise of the Axis, the Spanish Civil War, and Hitler's march into the Rhineland. In this easy-to-play, straightforward solitaire game, you are the beleaguered Ethiopian Emperor Haile Selassie I (1892-1975). Take charge of Ethiopia's defenses, call up troops, and call on the League of Nations as Italy tries to enlarge her empire at your expense.

Send your regional "Ras" warlords into battle, organize partisans, deploy your limited elite forces, and endure Italy's criminal use of mustard gas.

Your ancient Black Christian African civilization stands as a defiant symbol of anti-colonial resistance and as the first battlefield of the coming global struggle against Fascist aggression. Can you turn Mussolini's Blackshirt armies back, prevent the fall of Ethiopia's capital Addis Ababa, and change the course of history?

—description from the publisher

name: Blackout
description:
Cities are going dark! Can you find out why & get the lights back on? Blackout is a thrilling cooperative card game where players band together to save the world from mysterious blackouts targeting the most influential cities.

Whether you're new to strategy games or a seasoned tabletop tactician, Blackout offers an accessible yet deeply engaging experience. Dive into an 18-game story-driven campaign, where each chapter escalates the stakes and evolves your gameplay with new twists, challenges, and ways to play. Alternatively, jump into the Freeplay Mode and select from a range of unique, standalone challenges tailored to your group’s skill and playstyle.

With dynamic teamwork, evolving scenarios, and the world at stake, Blackout delivers an exciting gaming experience you won’t forget. Can your team get the lights back on?

Gameplay
Players take turns strategically playing cards into 2 rows in the center of the playing area. Each mission presents unique challenges for certain cards you want to capture. (or specifically not capture).

Challenges range from kid friendly by simply capturing cards of similar color to a more complex scoring mechanism where your team tries to score specific numbers in each row before the deck runs out.

Other challenges you can expect to see include ranks, runs, playing blind, a timed element, and more.

—description from the designer

name: Blanco
description:
Each player in Blanco starts with a face-down 3x3 grid of cards, with each card showing a number (1-12) and a colored vertical stripe. To complete set up, turn one card face up, look at another card, then draw a hand of two cards.

On a turn, draw a card from the deck or discard pile, then either (1) discard a card and reveal a face-down card in your grid or (2) discard a grid card and replace it with a face-up card from your hand. Alternatively, instead of drawing a card, you can swap two orthogonally adjacent cards, turning one of them face up, if possible.

If all cards in a vertical column now have the same color, clear that column; if all cards in a horizontal row now have the same number, clear that row. Whenever you clear a row, you may look at one of your face-down cards. If you manage to have a chain reaction — clearing two lines on the same turn — you may turn over one of your face-down cards.

As soon as you have cleared your 3x3 grid, deal yourself a new face-down 4x3 grid, then turn one card face up and look at another. Whoever first clears their 4x3 grid wins.

name: Blasphemous: The Board Game
description:
Blasphemous: the board game is a competitive adventure game. One to four Penitents will be sent by the Brotherhood of the Silent Sorrow on one of many available Pilgrimages. Each Pilgrimage deeply changes the land of Cvstodia through which the Penitents venture to solve quests, take down enemies, and unravel the plots hatched by the Miracle.
On their journey, the Penitents must work together to overcome deadly obstacles and mortal adversaries, but only one of them will be able to complete the Pilgrimage and achieve redemption (and victory) in the eyes of the Brotherhood of the Silent Sorrow.
Using an innovative dice evolution system, and with a powerful narrative component created by our friends at The Game Kitchen, Blasphemous: the board game lets you immerse yourself in the dark and fantastic world of Cvstodia, facing the most iconic bosses in the game, and meeting and interacting with all the characters that dwell within it.

—description from the publisher

name: Alibis
description:
Whodunnit? In Alibis, a suspicious lineup of supervillains lies before you and your team, and you’re tasked with finding the true criminal.

To start the game, you’re secretly given information about two innocent suspects.

Cooperatively, associate your two characters with a one-word clue. If everyone does that correctly, you’ve found the culprit!

Be careful; your clue might erroneously point at another player’s villain.

—description from the publisher

name: Blob Party: Neon Nights
description:
Blob Party: Neon Nights is a cooperative party game where players start as individuals with a bit of dough and a googly eye and try to become one big blob by all giving the same answers!

Let’s say the group starts with the Category of “Furniture” and the Word is “Castle.”  All players write an answer, maybe “Throne,” or “Round Table.” Everyone reveals, and anyone who wrote the same thing becomes a blob – mushing together their dough and eyes – and will work together for the rest of the game.

A new Category and Word are revealed for the next round, where players and blobs once again come up with answers, hoping to match with others. As the game continues, blobs and individuals merge until (hopefully!) everyone gives the same answer, becoming a Mega Blob and winning the game!

Blob Party: Neon Nights is a complete game on its own with 100 new words and 25 new categories! It can be combined with the original Blob Party for even more combinations, allowing up to 16 players to play at once!"

—description from the publisher

name: Blood
description:
Blood is a Boss Battler game for 1 to 4 players. You will control a group of unusual monster hunters, each featuring their own customizable set of cards. Blood uses an innovative dice and card system to allow you to face the horrors of Vlad's Castle until you reach its powerful Master.

Each Raid will bring you face to face with one of Vlad's Champions, ready to confront you by deploying unique strategies varying based on the location where you encounter them, creating ever-changing combinations and situations.

At the end of each Raid, you will return to the village of Bran to build new epic weapons and learn new fighting techniques, to prepare for the final confrontation with the Prince of the Night himself!

—description from the publisher

name: Blood Bowl: Third Season Edition
description:
Blood Bowl is the game of fantasy football set in a version of the Old World where sports mayhem is not only tolerated, but encouraged. This third edition boxed set casts you as the coach of either the Brionne Barons or the Nehekhara Nightmares.

The Brionne Barons are a Bretonnian team, with armored knights on a quest to achieve Blood Bowl glory. The Nehekhara Nightmares are a Tomb Kings team, undead warriors who have returned to show the living how the game is meant to be played. These teams will battle in grand stadiums for glory, gold, and the entertainment of devoted hordes of cheering fans!

Blood Bowl is a tactical game of big scores and maniacal violence. How you choose to coach your team is entirely up to you: Will you go for agility and speed, or buckle down with some bruisers? Ideal for both league play and exhibition matches, there's something here for every type of coach.

name: Blood Dynasty
description:
Vampires has lost their war against humans and now has to live and feed in the shadows under the rules of the humans in the streets of the ancient city of Drachenburg.
Are you going to be the one who returns the power to the Blood Dynasty?

Players in their hand can have numeric cards or special cards. Numeric cards on their hand represents hunger and in the streets pile represents preys. The players on their turns has two options, play a special card with various effects (gain life, attack other players in various ways, etc) or they can choose to satisfy their hunger looking for preys across the streets of the city. The streets pile is made of special and numerical cards.

Play your powers wisely and search for preys in the right moment in order to be the first without cards or the last one alive and win the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Blood of Lions: The Somme – 4th British Amy Sector: July 1916
description:
Blood of Lions is a WWI solitaire wargame depicting the actions of the British 4th Army during the month of July at the Battle of the Somme. 
The game uses a combination of dice, cards, generated Command and Leadership points as well as some push your luck mechanics in order to advance on objectives and obtain victory points.

Players are allocated Command Points for which they may undertake specific sets of actions each turn. The objective of the game is to gain as many victory points as possible while reaching objectives defended by a German bot activated by player actions, event cards, and automatic defense values.

—description from the publisher

name: Blood on the Sands: A Game of Gladiatorial Combat
description:
Blood on the Sands is a historically inspired skirmish game that immerses players in thrilling one-on-one gladiatorial combats using miniatures, featuring six distinct gladiator classes, each with its own unique abilities and armaments: Hoplomachus, Murmillo, Provocator, Retiarius, Secutor, and Thraex.

Players roll a set of six action dice that allow you to take direct control of your gladiator. Action dice represent a gladiator’s ability and opportunities to manoeuvre, maintain endurance, defend from, and attack, their opponents. During the course of the game gladiators will become fatigued, wounded, or hindered, losing access to some of their action dice, placing them at a serious disadvantage.

The ambition behind Blood on the Sands is to recreate the dynamic, back-and-forth “dance” of a duel, reflecting the balanced intricacies that the Romans infused into their deadly blood sport. The mechanics produce narrative combats that move across the arena, demanding tactics, skill, and a degree of luck from the players, while avoiding the gameplay devolving into a simple static dice fest.

name: Blood Suckers
description: Blood Suckers is a competitive card based game that sees each player take on the role of a different Blood Sucking critter in the animal kingdom. Using each Blood Suckers bonus, each player in turn order will choose from the available Hosts to suck blood from. But before they can successfully Attach to that Host, they must draw a begone card and roll a dice to see if they pass. At the end of each round, every Blood Sucker attached to a Host draws Blood from that Host.

name: BloodFeud: Samurai versus Vikings
description:
Welcome to the world of BloodFeud, a tabletop miniatures game where you can lead your army to victory in competitive and solo play. Choose a mighty host from history, create your warlord avatar and you can personally engage in mortal combat. Vikings vs Samurai, Mongols vs Egyptians, Romans vs Crusaders - it’s all possible in the world of BloodFeud. With revolutionary rules, tools and training, you can recreate battles from history, or feud it out in incredible ‘what if’ match-ups.

1 Battle - 1000 Outcomes
BloodFeud makes use of innovative turn-based effects through random card draw. The tension and excitement builds as each warlord discovers how the battle space has changed and evolved as the battle progresses. From simple weather changes, to discovery of equipment or even being joined by fresh troops or being set upon by assassins, the outcome of each battle is never truly known until the last sword is drawn.

Historical but Exciting
BloodFeud has its roots in history and all troop types, equipment and heroes come from historical reference. BloodFeud seeks to be different however to the mainstay of historical wargames in that it allows the player to leave their mark and make the game their own. Roman Gladiators can battle it out with Saracen Marmluks. Samurai can lead a last charge against Hannibals war elefants. The strictures of historical wargaming are lifted, and BloodFeud allows the players imagination to drive the game forward.

Unforgiving Fast Paced Combat
Dice rolling is the bane of modern wargaming. Buckets of dice and counters reign as rolls to hit and wound are coupled with armor and invulnerability saves. What this means is that half the game is spent counting dice when it could be spent playing out a grand strategy or walking your opponent into a cunning trap. Combat in BloodFeud is by single die rolling for each attack. Rolling to hit, wound and save is built into one single roll on a D10. Beyond the metrics of mathematic battle, BloodFeud introduces the player to battle outcome effects. Battle lines can be pushed back, morale can waiver or formations can even be broken into disarray, to be ridden down as they flee. Death on the battlefield has never been closer than in BloodFeud. Models and heroes particularly, including the player as the warlord, do not have a buffer of wounds to make up for hazardous strategy. An arrow that pierces armor is just as deadly to a footman as it is to a king. If you lead from the front, be prepared to pay the iron price.

Artificial Intelligence for Solo and Coop Play
The Battle Buddy AI system is the ever ready gaming companion that the player has never had. Let’s be truthful, in a modern world where life can be all too busy, it can be difficult to connect with other players for an afternoon and play a tabletop game. Even with BloodFeuds advanced mechanics allowing for a game to be played in as little as 45 minutes, sometimes, time is the chief enemy. Battle Buddy AI brings a new level of solo or cooperative play to the table. While not truly ‘artificial intelligence’, Battle Buddy does bring a scalable opponent, of variable difficulty and aggression to fight against. Turn by turn the Battle Buddy’s army will manoeuvre and engage your forces in a coordinated strategy. Battle Buddy will seek to take objectives, launch spearhead attacks and defend against your thrusts. Not only is Battle Buddy a fantastic training tool and genuine gaming opponent, the Battle Buddy can also be your loyal ally in multiple army games with both Human and Battle Buddy armies or in cooperative play against a common foe.

Custom Miniatures
BloodFeud’s proprietary miniatures range is crafted to allow for maximum customisation by the player. Joints are designed around balls and sockets, so torso’s, arm’s and head’s can be posed in an almost unlimited number of ways. Stepping away from the industry wide mono-pose models, BloodFeud offers you the flexibility to use your imagination. Have you ever wanted to run battle axe wielding Ninja’s or bare-chested Viking Beserkir’s on horseback? With the BloodFeud WarChest App, you can order the parts you want for your miniatures and your army, and build them up the way you want.

Its all about YOU - In BloodFeud, you are not playing with someone elses models, armies and heroes. In BloodFeud, YOU lead YOUR army on the battlefield by creating an avatar of yourself to be your warlord and equipping yourself with weapons and armor as you choose.

Battle Buddy AI - BloodFeud offers the player a revolutionary system for solo and cooperative. While not truly AI, the Battle Buddy AI system allows players to play against an enemy, or with an ally, that takes actions based on objectives and opposing forces, in a coordinated army wide strategy. With scaleable difficulty, the Battle Buddy AI can be a fantastic sparring partner or a deadly foe - underestimate it at your peril.

Before the Battle Cards - This feature focusses on the factors that lead up to battle that can determine the outcome. The ‘Before the Battle’ card draw adds the first element of BloodFeuds ‘1 battle - 1000 outcomes’ principle of variation and replayability. Preparation is key to performance!

Battle Rages On Cards - This feature again focusses on the random and unforseen events that occur in the heat of battle and introduce the ‘instability’ of combat that can make a victory, or break it. This feature is the second  principle of ‘1 battle - 1000 outcomes’ and can provide the player an opportunity to strike back. No plan ever survives first contact with the enemy!

Unit Activation - In a step away from ‘I Go/You Go’ gameplay, the warlords, characters and units on both sides activate relative to their own statistics, meaning faster and lighter units can take actions before heavier and slower units. This gives both players an equal opportunity to enact their strategies and outmaneuver their enemies. Unit activation includes movement, ranged combat, close combat, issuing of orders in the case of characters and warlords, and other special actions relevant to specific units and characters. A warlord who knows his own army, and his enemies, will not fear the result of a hundred battles!

Adaptive Terrain - The concept of a ‘hill’ just being a ‘hill’ is replaced with a system of variability, so that the terrain within a battle can be explored and its true strategic value exploited. This feature focuses on a card draw that can enhance or diminish the strategic value of battlefield terrain and can even provide the player with additional units and equipment and adds an element of the unknown.

Innovative Combat - Close combat in BloodFeud is simultaneous, fast and seamless. Players can no longer rush in and attack knowing that the counter-attack will be weak. Combat is simultaneous (just like real life) and the force that has superior combat power will prevail. Ranged combat in BloodFeud also aims for realism by requiring players to guess the range to target, and then adjust their guess based on the skill of the firing models. This means that the first shots may go wide, but again, just like real life, once the player has their eye dialled in the firepower can be delivered with great accuracy, or an early lucky volley could turn the tide.

Combat Outcome Effects - The art of killing on the BloodFeud battlefield isn’t restricted to hit points, wounds and saves. Every time an attack is completed the full effect of the casualties inflicted can cause a battle line to waiver, get pushed back or even break, resulting in further disadvantage for the losing side. This emphasises the power of ‘breaking the line’ to achieve victory, as opposed to just killing enemies.

Battle Orders - The warlord and their lieutenants can have a powerful effect on combat performance. The right order at the right time can increase the combat power of a unit, or cause the enemy to waiver. This feature emphasises leading from the front, but remember, your warlord, just like you, is only human!

The Role of Religion - Divination deals with the concept of religion, conviction and belief, as a critical component of the psychology of battle. Omens, portents and hexes reign as the priests, monks and crones call for divine intervention to strengthen their allies and disrupt their enemies. While not specifically ‘magic’ this phase allows players to engage the cultural and religious practices of factions to provide support during desperate times. Many strategies have been developed and many battles have been won by the strength of ‘consulting the bones’ or through the incantation of prayer before battle - religious belief can cut as deeply as a blade or shield a bearer from one!

D10 Die Rolling - The 10 sided die or D10 offers the player more opportunity for variability of success and rolling. Further, a D10 system offers greater variation in the types and statistics of units, and this in turn provides a more realistic and rounded game mechanic.

Fast Play - The rolling mechanics in BloodFeud are designed to enhance speed of play. Attack rolls, armor saves and combat effects are all built into one roll. In a world where everyone is busy and time is precious, BloodFeud can provide a full and fulfilling battle experience in as little as 45 minutes for a 250 point battle, and a little over an hour for a major engagement of 500 points.

Custom Miniatures - The miniatures in BloodFeud are designed to be reposeable and be parts interchangeable. At this end of the day there’s not much fun playing with someone elses models. BloodFeud offers you to make your army your own, and play the way you want to play. The core game set contains injection moulded miniatures and follow on miniatures will be 3D printed.

Whats In The Box:

- 32 page Rulebook
- 40 page Samurai versus Vikings Battle Book 
- 63 miniatures (27 Samurai/36 Vikings - pictured) 
- Two ten sided dice
- Ruler
- 60 Before the Battle cards
- 63 Battle Rages On cards
- 50 Battle Buddy AI cards
- 150 Adaptive Terrain cards

name: Bloody Hollow
description:
Bloody Hollow is a 28mm solo/cooperative miniatures game inspired by Washington Irving’s The Legend of Sleepy Hollow. 
You will create a band of colonial mercenaries and investigators who have been called upon to help save the now-haunted Hudson Valley.  
Sculpt, bash, or print unique miniatures that wade into the evil mayhem of Bloody Hollow to try to investigate and return the Headless Horseman to the grave before he covers the valley in darkness forever.

Bloody Hollow is a tabletop miniatures game played on a 3' x 3' table. Like a TTRPG everyone brings character sheets but they also need to bring miniatures. In this game 1-5 players play against the game. You can use whatever miniatures you'd like.

Each player will control a single character in either solo or cooperative play, as they seek to uncover the mystery surrounding a murderous apparition - known as The Headless Horseman - who haunts the region. Players will attempt to unravel the mystery of the dreaded ghostly rider before he collects the heads of the terrified villagers and coats the area in darkness forever.

The gameplay is focused on a narrative campaign where characters fight to clear the land of monsters and learn clues to discover how to ultimately confront and defeat the Headless Horseman. As you play through missions, useful villagers may end up in harm's way. If they perish your access to vital information and goods decreases and the town becomes closer to destruction. But if your missions are successful, you'll bring prosperity and peace... if you don't lose your head.

—description from the publisher

name: Bloody Lane: A Solitaire Wargame
description:
Bloody Lane is a solitaire wargame available on Amazon. The player controls the defending Confederate soldiers holding Bloody Lane, while the advancing Federals are controlled by an AI bot detailed in the following rules. The player rolls six-sided dice to determine the results of chosen actions, which affect the situation on the Battle Sheet (the graphic representation of the area in which the defense of Bloody Lane took place). As the Union assault intensifies, the player will have to make increasingly tough decisions to ensure victory.


     You command five Confederate Regiments defending Bloody Lane. Each historical Confederate Regiment is represented by a Unit counter that occupies a Defensive Position.
     Union Regiments attack in four Waves, each getting stronger. Each historical Union Regiment is represented by a Unit counter and enters an Attack Track. That counter then advances from one Attack Position to the next Attack Position along that Attack Track. 
     You must choose and resolve appropriate actions to defeat each Attack Wave. 
     As both Confederate and Union counters suffer Hits, their Cohesion is reduced, making each Unit less able to carry out the assigned action. If a Confederate counter ever has its Cohesion reduced to zero, that Unit is Shattered and cannot select any action other than Rally to the Flag.
     To resolve an action, make a Cohesion check. Roll 1d6, apply any modifiers to the Cohesion of the Unit and compare the result of the die roll to the current Cohesion of the Unit. If the roll is equal to or less than the (modified) Cohesion, the action is resolved successfully. 
     In addition to resolving actions, the Union will also resolve four Events each turn. Events simulate off-board musket and artillery fire, attacks by sharp shooters, smoke that obscures the battlefield, and attempts to reform Union units. The severity of Union Events is determined by the Difficulty Level selected and are detailed on the Player Sheet. 
     While battling each Attack Wave, you must carefully manage the Supply Line to ensure Orders, Ammunition and Reinforcements arrive in a timely manner. Skilled use of Confederate Artillery will help you achieve this goal. 
     If a Union counter enters a Defensive Position occupied by a Shattered Confederate Unit, Bloody Lane is captured and the game ends in defeat for the player. 


—description from the publisher

name: Bloomchasers: A Delightful 3D Tree Game of Flowers and Wits
publisher: Evan and Josh's Very Special Games Company (Very Special Games)
description:
30-min light strategy game for adults - grow your flowers and outwit opponents on a stunning 3D tree, either solo, as a team, or competitively.

Each turn, players — affectionately called "Bloomchasers" — place a new branch onto the tree, along with a "bud" of your color. Your goal is to place your buds in certain shapes so when a Bloom card is drawn, you're set up to grow flowers (and your opponents aren't!). Your ability to read and predict the weather will help you bloom faster and make sure you're growing the most valuable flowers to win.

—description from the publisher

name: Book Club
description:
Book Club is a cooperative game where you and your friends try to think of the perfect book to read together for Book Club. Tap into your collective literary knowledge and come up a book everyone can agree on — before time runs out!

At the start of the round, draw a card for the “Book has…” column. For example: “Pet.” When the group has named a book matching that description, flip the next description card. If it fits the book you just named, add the description to the “Book doesn’t have…” column.

For example, for round one, Clifford the Big Red Dog was named as a book with a Pet. In round two, the description Read by Children. Now, the group has to name a book that has a Pet but isn't read by children.

Marley and Me!

Keep doing this until you flip five descriptions and name a final book. Do this all within the time limit to win!

—description from the designer

name: Blue & Gray Deluxe Edition
description:
The American Civil War was the bloodiest conflict and a defining event in the history of the United States. The tragedy of the conflict was amplified by the fact the battles were brutally fought with Napoleonic tactics while using new and more lethal weaponry. As a result, over the course of nearly four full years of war, roughly 700,000 Americans were wounded or killed in battle along with another 400,000 soldiers dying from disease.

Blue & Gray Deluxe Edition consists of the original eight games from the SPI Blue & Gray I & II Quadrigames. The battles depicted are among the most important of the American Civil War: Shiloh, Antietam, Fredericksburg, Chancellorsville (Hooker & Lee), Gettysburg (Cemetery Hill), Chickamauga, Chattanooga, and The Battle of the Wilderness.

The game mechanics used in this series are based on the well-received Borodino/Napoleon at Waterloo system. Terrain is a significant factor, with everything from rolling farmland to untracked wilderness represented. Battles will often see a back-and-forth struggle for control of critical terrain. Rules for night turns are also provided. A standard set of rules are used, common to all eight games, while each game also has its own set of exclusive rules, historical set-ups, and player and design notes—all from the original SPI games.

Blue & Gray Deluxe Edition features new artwork, double-sided mounted game boards, enlarged counters, player aid cards, numerous optional rules gleaned from other game editions, and new variant counters and markers for use with several variants from Moves and Strategy & Tactics magazines. Reintroduce yourself to these classic games from SPI’s golden era and refight some of the best-known battles of the American Civil War which decided the fate of a nation at war with itself.

—description from the publisher

name: BLUFFIT
publisher: Gameplay Publishing ApS; Gém Klub Kft.
description:
BLUFFIT is a simple and tense bluffing game in which players compete to score the most points. All players start with a hand of cards numbered 1–10. To set up, reveal random cards equal to the number of players from a separate set of 1–10 cards.

All players simultaneously play a card from their hand face down. Then, in turn, players either claim one of the available scoring cards or challenge another player who has already claimed one. In a challenge, both players secretly compare strength cards, with the higher card winning the scoring card (in a tie, the challenging player wins).

Once all players have acted, remove any unclaimed scoring cards from the table. Claimed scoring cards are placed in each player’s score pile. The played strength cards are then shuffled and revealed to form the new set of scoring cards for the next round. After ten rounds, players complete one final round using the cards last played by selecting a card from their score pile. Those played cards are removed from the game, claimed cards are added to score piles, and the player with the highest total wins.

BLUFFIT includes four optional special cards per player, such as "The Optimistic 1" (which beats a 10 in a challenge) and "The Flipped 5" (which beats 6-10, but loses to 1-4). To use them, replace the regular number in each player's hand with the special card.

name: Bluolino
description:
In the land of master builders, Lévalmont, the central city of Mon Lumière rises high on a hill, overlooking forests and valleys as the cultural and spiritual heart of the realm.
Cobblestone streets, spired rooftops, and bell towers shape its skyline, while apprentices of the forest learn their craft here before journeying to distant lands.

Surrounding the city are six distinct realms, each with its own climate and culture.
As a young architect, you will travel through these lands, raising buildings that suit each region. Sometimes, bridges will be built to connect people and goods, sparking lively trade across the country.
With the aid of the central city, you will transport resources and continue your architectural works far and wide.

Build across many regions, and earn renown as the architect whose name will be remembered throughout Lévalmont!

				
				
					=Bluolino is a medium-weight board game that combines worker placement, an action wheel, and resource management.
Players place their workers on action spaces whose effects change depending on the rotation of the action wheel, creating a unique twist on the classic worker placement genre.

—description from the publisher

name: Blütenreich
description: In the card game Blütenreich, your flower meadows grow step by step: draw cards and let beautiful butterflies spread their wings. Each card has its own strategy, so decide wisely and plan ahead: butterfly or flower meadow?

name: Boardquest: Tales of Liria
description:
Boardquest is a classic fantasy skirmish game for 1-4 players. It replicates and condenses battle systems of epic tabletop RPGs such as Dungeons & Dragons and Das Schwarze Auge and remixes it with elements known from widely beloved video and board games (Warcraft, Heroscape, Gloomhaven, and others).

In the game the players lead their chosen faction towards taking control over the map: the winner either defeats all enemy heroes or conquers the required number of forts.

As a player you will utilize common and rare weapons, leverage your character's unique abilities and spells, and recruit specialized units to join your army. As the the game progresses your hero will become more powerful and master more advanced abilities. The land of Liria is infested by monsters, some rather unsophisticated and some highly complex, dropping XP points, gold, and loot when defeated. The players will face the creatures and level-up as they prepare for the final face-off with their contestants to Liria's throne...

—description from the publisher

name: For the Emperor
description:
In For the Emperor, two ancient clans work to overpower, outwit, and outmaneuver each other to claim victory!

In this two-player duel, you’ll send out your elite warriors to vie for control of seven battlefields. Each warrior adds their strength and ability to the battlefield where they’re placed.  With tricky cards that cause others to be returned to hand, amplify the power of cards at the same battlefield, and more, you’ll have to be clever to triumph.

You control a battlefield if you have more total strength there than your opponent. If you control the most battlefields at the end of the game, you win!

—description from the designer

name: Boil & Bubble
description:
What is a Deck Hand game? It is an 18 card game that is used in conjunction with a standard Poker deck.

The brinded cat has mewed, the hedge pig has whined, and all the neighbourhood witches have gathered to brew their most potent and powerful potion. Add ingredients to your cauldron, leave them to simmer, and at the end of the game use your concoction to cast as many spells as you have secreted away. Make a final offering to the blood moon and coax the black cat to your side, and the player with the greatest grimoire will reign supreme!

In Boil and Bubble, you are witches placing ingredient cards into your personal scoring cauldron throughout the game. Every round you will also be bidding on and winning other spell cards that you will use to score with your stored ingredients. You can also make offerings to the full moon or attract your black cat familiar for extra points at the end of the game. The player with the highest score wins.

—description from the designer

name: Boitas
description:
Boitas is a trick-taking game based on the famous sea traders from the Indian state of Odisha. The sea traders were famous for trading with countries such as Indonesia, China and Sri Lanka. Till today they are celebrated in Odisha during the Bali Yatra celebration. As you step into the world of Boitas, you don the mantle of these legendary Sadhabas (sea traders). Navigate the bustling ports, engage in lucrative trades, and bring back the exotic goods that will solidify your legacy as a master trader in the storied annals of maritime history.

In Boitas, players aim to gather the most prestigious collection of imported goods and ships by the end of the game. Points are scored based on the value of these goods and ships, with the player accumulating the highest points emerging as the victor.

Boitas is played in rounds, each consisting of four phases. The first three are Trading Phases, and the final phase is the Market Phase. In each Trading Phase, players take turns playing a Boita card from their hand, aiming to win the trick and claim the best Import Goods Token. The two best ranked cards are rewarded. Others gain Cowrie tokens. In turn order, Players can spend Cowries to draw additional Boita cards or acquire Elephant Boitas, enhancing their hand for future trading.

Boita cards come in 4 standard suits - Rice (Yellow), Gems (Red), Betel (Green), Cloth (Blue). Within each suit, the cards are numbered from 0 - 9, representing the card’s value. Additionally, there are 4 wild cards valued 0, and 4 cards of the Trunk suit or Elephant (Grey). Each Trading Phase is associated with a Port Number either 1, 2 or 3. Each Port Number has a Port card that indicates the suit placed for that trick. The best card to win a trick is the card with the same suit and Port Number. However, this winning card can be defeated by an Elephant card. An Elephant card can be defeated by a 4 of the suit that matches the Port card. All other cards follow standard trick-taking rules. The winner and runner-up of a trick gets to choose an Import Good in order. The losers gain a cowrie shell. The winner of a trick is the first player to start the next trick. During the Market Phase, the player with the most cowries starts.

The game ends after three Trading Phases of the fourth round are completed. Players then score their points based on the goods they imported, points on the Boita cards in their hands, and remaining cowries. The player with the highest points wins.

name: Llama Llama
description:
In Llama Llama, players pass cards to craft hands around the different scoring conditions. These conditions were chosen by the players secretly at the start of the round—you’ll have to try and guess at what others are going for to score big!

—description from the publisher

name: Merchants of Andromeda
description:
In Merchants of Andromeda, you have to play the game of space politics, casting votes in the Senate, bidding on lucrative space goods, or resorting to ship combat!

At the start of your turn, you draw three cards (one at a time), choosing one each to discard (which grants you a resource), keep (which grants you an action), or auction (which grants the winner both an action and a resource). To perform the Dutch auction in this game, use either a timer or the game's dedicated app — the more the timer ticks down, the less the winner will pay. Through these cards, you'll manipulate the market, play intergalactic mini-games, and resolve events. In the end, the player with the most money wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Book of Dungeon
description:
Based on our popular board game Bag of Dungeon, Book of Dungeon is part puzzle book, part fantasy adventure.

All you need is a pencil, a pair of dice and your courage, draw and explore 100 deadly dungeons. Slay monsters, dodge traps and hunt for treasure. Each dungeon is a self-contained puzzle: draw your path, make your choices, and see if you can escape with your life.

—description from the publisher

name: Bookshelf
description:
Bookshelf is a cozy and quick literary set collection card game for 1-5 players (in competitive mode or 2-3 players in co-op mode).

In Bookshelf, you are an avid book collector trying to curate sets of books for your personal collection. Acquire books from the library or bookstore, scour the local flea market for bargains and gain access to the rare books section to build your collection of books!

—description from the designer

name: BOOM! Patrol
description:
Hello and welcome to the BOOMburg Battle Arena where the most celebrated tank crews have assembled for an all-out battle for gold & glory. So get ready to crush buildings, grab those power-ups and make things go BOOM!

Choose your celebrity tank Captain, like Jonesy Ninelives of Crew Tomcat or Rosie Rhino of the Charging Armored - then outsmart, outmaneuver, and outblast your rivals in the ultimate arena battle.

BOOM Patrol is a competitive tank battle game that plays like a mash-up of Mario Kart and Battlebots. Whether you Medal - or get blown into next week comes down to your strategic and tactical decisions. All in a game that cares more about fun than precision. 'Cause if it looks close enough, it's close enough to crush with 30 tons of treads and armor!

Featuring an intuitive and innovative movement system, programmed command cards, asymmetric tank captain abilities, and videogame-like logic, this is just a blast to play. And with the toy-etic cardboard tanks, you will find yourself making tank noises as they rumble across the arena and turn their turrets with a "TINK, TINK, TINK," before firing.

—description from the publisher

name: Bosnian War: 1992-1995
description:
Bosnian War: 1992-1995 is a two-player Strategic level board-wargame of the brutal conflict that took place in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992-1995. There are two players: the Bosnian government (BiH) player and the Bosnian Serb (VRS) player. The Bosnian Government player controls the units of the Croatian Defense Council (HVO) although certain game events allow the Serb player to control the HVO units. The Serb player can also control the units of the Krajina Serb Army (SKV) through random events or NATO intervention. The Bosnian Government player can also control units of the Croatian Army (HV) under certain conditions. In this game, the enemy population is not a victim of collateral damage, rather it is a target, so conquering towns and cities is a key aspect of the game.

Each game turn represents three months of time. Each hex represents 12 km (7.5 miles). Each combat unit represents a task force ranging in size from a regiment to a division.

22 x 34-inch game map, 176 5/8-inch counters
Included in Strategy & Tactics #351, January 2025.

-description from designer

name: Movie Night
description:
Movie Night is a cooperative game where you and your friends try to think of the perfect movie to watch together. Tap into your collective movie knowledge and come up a movie everyone can agree on — before time runs out!

At the start of the round, draw a card for the “Movie has…” column. For example: “Female Main Character.” When the group has named a movie matching that description, flip the next description card. If it fits the movie you just named, add the description to the “Movie doesn’t have…” column.

For example, for round one, Frozen was named as a movie with a Female Main Character. In round two, the description Animation was drawn. Now, the group has to name a movie that has a Female Main Character but doesn’t have Animation.

The Hunger Games!

Keep doing this until you flip five descriptions and name a final movie. Do this all within the time limit to win!

Movie Night contains 36 cards as compared to 18 cards included in Apropos: Of Movies.

name: Oddland
description:
Eureka! The fascinating flora and fauna on this strange island are unlike any you’ve ever seen! How… odd!

As an intrepid investigator of all things idiosyncratic, your job is to explore the island and document these fantastic creatures. On your turn, explore by placing a terrain card somewhere on the island (with the ability to cover up previous terrain!).

Then, place one of your seven flora or fauna tokens on the card you’ve just played. These tokens score based on their surroundings–for example, the pigehorse scores better adjacent to a longer coastline.

—description from the publisher

name: Botany: War of the Posies
description:
Botany: War of the Posies is a deck building game where you take on the role of an esteemed head gardener for a celebrated botanist who perpetually returns from expeditions with rare and exotic specimens from around the globe. You declare war against neighboring head gardeners to create the most elaborate garden.

In War of the Posies, each player will cultivate their own unique deck of cards, starting from the same base decks, by adding cards they purchase during the game using the they gain by playing cards. They will also acquire Garden Features where they can plant Flowers to earn Reputation. During the game, you will always draw cards from your own personal deck, and discard them into your own personal discard pile.

Plant flowers and add features to your garden. Or, plant a poisonous flower in your opponent's garden (before he does it to you).

As soon as a player has completed 7 Reputation worth of Garden Features, the game will end and the player with the most points wins.

This is a standalone game set in the world of Botany.

—description from the publisher

name: Piñatas
description:
Bide your time, but don't wait too long—you won't get any candy!

In Piñatas, you want to take tricks as late as you can.

Once you take three tricks, you're out of the round. But, you get points for how many tricks won by all players at the table.

Designed by Dr. Reiner Knizia, Piñatas features a simple ruleset with his signature spin on scoring.

—description from the publisher

name: Boucaniers
description:
Simultaneous strategy game.

Embark on a simultaneous treasure hunt! Sail in a changing archipelago full of cannibals, corrupt trading posts and voodoo mysteries. Arm your ship, recruit, plunder and trade while being careful of the East India Companies. The outcome is never certain and each turn is thrilling!
For games full of bluff and suspense! Choose your navigation in secret then move all at the same time. No wait for the others' turns!

After navigation, depending on whether ships are in contact or 1 away, there is boarding or cannon fire. Then, everyone plays their actions at the same time.

To win, 2 different epic objectives:

Unearth the hidden treasure of Armand the chatterbox before the others OR collect 25 gold coins. The passage of the Rougeaud of the East India Companies at the Bastion Rouge is an event not to be missed because its capture then brings 15 coins.

Islands with unique actions, infinite combos, asymmetrical ships. Players explore unusual and personal tactics.

Each game is unique thanks to the modular board, the asymmetry of the 10 ships and the 24 unique buccaneers. As exciting with 2 players as with 3, 4 or 5, experts and youngsters alike will be in their element.

Currently the game is in French with other languages options possible depending on the KS success

---

Jeu de stratégie en simultané.

Embarquez dans une chasse au trésor en simultané ! Voguez dans un archipel changeant truffé de cannibales, de comptoirs corrompus et de mystères vaudous. Armez votre bateau, recrutez, pillez et commercez en prenant garde aux Compagnies des Indes. Le dénouement n'est jamais certain et chaque tour donne le frisson !
Pour des parties pleines de bluff et de suspense ! Choisissez votre navigation en secret puis bougez tous en même temps. On n'attend pas les tours des autres !
Après la navigation, selon si des bateaux sont au contact ou à 1 de distance, il y a abordage ou tirs de canons. Ensuite, tout le monde joue ses actions en même temps.

Pour gagner, 2 objectifs épiques différents :

Déterrez le trésor caché d’ Armand le baratineur avant les autres OU amassez 25 pièces d’or. Le passage du Rougeaud des Compagnies des Indes au Bastion Rouge est un évènement à ne pas manquer car sa prise rapporte alors 15 pièces.

Des îles aux actions uniques, des combos infinis, des navires asymétriques. Les joueurs explorent des tactiques insolites et personnelles.

Chaque partie est unique grâce au plateau modulable, à l'asymétrie des 10 navires et aux 24 boucaniers uniques. Aussi palpitant à 2 joueurs qu'à 3, 4 ou 5, les experts comme les plus jeunes seront dans leur élément.

name: Boulder Bluff
description:
Boulder Bluff is a fast-paced card game in a bouldering (climbing) theme, where climbers enter in a one-day competition to win a free trip around the world!

On your turn, you can either 'Prep' which means taking an extra Move card or 'Climb' which means attempting to climb one of the three Bouldering routes that are revealed, by placing your Move cards face-down in front of you, with at least one revealed.

Each player joining the climb then draws a random token from the chalk bag, which ranges from -1 to +2, and adds this to the power to climb the route.

The player with the highest power wins the bouldering route, and everyone (including the winner) who didn't have at least the number displayed on the bouldering route now has to take an injury token. This injury token is  -1 or -2 victory points at the end of the game (depeding on how you toss it).

But there's more! If you initiate a climb so confidently that nobody dares to join, you don't have to reveal your cards, and simply get the Boulder route without having to do anything! That's real Boulder Bluff right there..

Spice up your game by using 'pure colour' combos and using action cards at the correct time to maximize your power and hinder your opponents.

After the 15 bouldering routes have been climbed, the game is finished. The number on the bouldering route is the number of points you scored. Add up all your bouldering routes, minus your injuries, and the winner is the climber with the most points!

-description from designer

name: Bouquet
description:
A game of bees, blossoms and bluffing, Bouquet is a strategic and dynamic area control game where competition blooms into beauty!

On their turn, players will either PLACE petals in the bouquet, PLUCK their opponents petals, or DRAW more petals into their hand.

Petals may be placed either face up, which gives certain abilities to particular petals, or face down, which allows you to ignore placing requirements at the cost of having those abilities active.

With multiple petal types to choose from, each with their own point value and abilities, players have to carefully consider how to place each petal into the bouquet.

The player with the most points at the end of the game wins!

-description from publisher

name: Brandywine, 1777: A Time for Heroes
description:
After capturing New York in 1776, Crown forces led by General Howe set their sights on Philadelphia, the heart of the rebellion. After a long and grueling journey, his army landed in August 1777. George Washington positioned his troops between Philadelphia and the British forces, leading to a clash at Brandywine on September 11, 1777.
The game puts both players in the roles of Washington and Howe. The British general’s mission is to seize Philadelphia, the political stronghold of the rebels. And if, in the process, he can destroy the rebel army, the revolution itself could be crushed!

Meanwhile, General Washington seeks to use the Brandywine River as a natural defense. His goal is either to destroy Howe’s army or at least inflict enough damage to cripple its operational capabilities.

Brandywine: A Time for Heroes puts you in the shoes of Howe or Washington.
The decisions are yours to make…

The game is based on the activation of British and American player Formations.

Each side has Formation Activation Cards, and each Formation has a limited number of activations among these cards. During each Activation Phase, players choose between movement/combat, building a redoubt, or doing nothing.

Each Formation has a limited amount of Cohesion. With every activation for movement or combat, Cohesion decreases.

Activating Formations generates momentum, represented by Momentum Cubes. These can be used to purchase Tactical Cards, which simulate various campaign and battle variables.

Victory is achieved by destroying enemy Formations or occupying strategic locations.

Of course, nothing went as planned! But… where are the Redcoats?

—description from the publisher

name: Bravest
description:
Every year, up to 4 Legendary Figures converge on the Celestial Archipelago for their annual tournament. Take on the role of one of them and prepare for the challenge packed courses your brave warrior will need to navigate:

     Choose a tile from those available
     Build your 2 courses simultaneously 
     Earn maximum prestige points thanks to your 2 Brave Warriors and claim the title of Legend of the Archipelago!


Two game modes, normal and advanced.

name: Breaking Moon
description:
Completely redesigned for Essen release 2025

Breaking Moon is a competitive strategy game for 2–4 players, where corporations race to save humanity from a flooding Earth after the moon is shattered by an asteroid. As sea levels rise and time runs out, players compete to build the space station, evacuate survivors, and secure their legacy.

Each round, you must move your helicopter to a new location on the main board to gather resources and select powerful actions. In addition, you perform one production action—choosing between upgrading your corporation, developing new technology, taking on space station projects, or collecting cards that score based on set collection.

You’ll manage scientists, resources, and upgrades on your personal player board, while the tech board presents shared production opportunities. The market board holds the available resources, breaking moon events, survivor cards, and the score track.

As players draw flood cards from the Breaking Moon deck, action spaces on the main board are flooded and permanently lost—pressuring you to act before it’s too late. Once the Evacuation Centre is built, players can begin evacuating survivors—but points are only awarded if the space station is completed before the final flood.

Breaking Moon challenges you to adapt, plan, and outmaneuver your rivals.

name: Breakthrough Russia
description:
Breakthrough Russia (“BR”) is a WWII strategy game that takes players back to the crucial period from Summer 1941 to Summer 1943, when the outcome of the war in the East hung in the balance.

A unique chit-pull system determines each player’s resources rather than which units may activate.

The game’s tempo is entirely up to the players, who decide on Pass, Attrition, or Offensive options each turn.
Historical features such as partisans, industrial production, armor superiority, weather, air transport, and Lend-Lease enhance the game’s realism.

Each game is guaranteed to be different due to the presence of variants such as General Vlasov's army,recruits from the Gulags, Turkish entry into the war, Katyusha rockets, and Vichy volunteers.

Breakthrough Russia, a game for two players with a low to moderate complexity level, is also suitable for solitaire play.

Given the low unit count of corps and armies, BR can be easily played in an afternoon, along with shorter scenarios for Barbarossa, Fall Blau, and Kharkov-Kursk.
The movement and combat systems are straightforward, quick to learn and easy to administer.

BR is a game that is fun, balanced, and offers a challenge to both newcomers and veteran war gamers.

—description from the publisher

name: Brick Like This!
publisher: Dotted Games; Boardgame Space; Galápagos Jogos; Gém Klub Kft.; LEGO; Lord of Boards; NeoTroy Games
description:
In Brick Like This!, players compete in teams to complete LEGO models as quickly as possible, with one teammate describing the model to another teammate who builds it.

In Brick Like This!, teams of two, one Instructor and one Builder, are tasked with building a shape out of LEGO bricks. The Instructor will tell the Builder how to build a shape on a Shape Card that only the Instructor can see. All teams play at the same time, racing to build their shapes the fastest. The winner is the team with the most points at the end of six rounds!

name: Bridge Constructor: Breaking Point
description:
In Bridge Constructor: Breaking Point, you want to engineer the best bridge possible with limited supplies so that vehicles can cross successfully.

Gameplay is half puzzle and half press-your-luck. Each round, you pick a bridge tile and either continue to strengthen or rebuild your bridge or use the tile to cross your vehicles. Choose from super light, light, medium, or heavy vehicles that each have unique points and challenges. Watch out for your fellow engineers, though, as they might play an event card on you, unleashing devastating damage to your perfectly planned bridge. Who's got the smarts to cross more vehicles and gather the most points before time runs out?

Bridge Constructor: Breaking Point keeps the puzzlyiness, wackiness, and fun of the Bridge Constructor mobile game, while adding elements uniquely suited to tabletop play, such as multiplayer action and unexpected events to confound opponents.

name: Brief Border Wars II
description:
Brief Border Wars 2 is the second set of four small operational level games on short border conflicts. The game system uses a card-driven system first introduced in Brief Border Wars that models the chaotic, stop-and-start nature of these impromptu wars. Four sets of exclusive rules reflect the peculiar nature of each conflict. Your sense of improvisation will be challenged as you explore four of the more interesting small wars fought in the early 20th century.

The four conflicts include:

1913: Second Balkan War (also known as “The Interallied War”) - Bulgaria vs Romania and Ottoman forces.
1919: The Seven-Day War (also known as “Teschen”): Czechoslovakia and Poland fight for the Duchy of Teschen (Cieszyn in Polish).
1939: The Nomonhan Incident (also known as “The Battle of Khalkin Gol”) - Japan and the Soviet Union clash in Mongolia.
1940: The Italo-Greek War (also known as “The Balkan Defiance”) - The first two months of the Italian invasion of Greece in the fall/winter of 1940.

These games are ideal short matches to finish off an evening of gaming, or fill a lunch hour.

Product information

Complexity: 4 out of 10
Solitaire Suitability: 5 out of 10
Time Scale: variable (1 day to 1 week per turn)
Map Scale: variable (area movement)
Unit Scale: variable (paramilitary “groups” to divisions)
Players: 1-2 (best with 2)
Playing Time: 1-2 hours each

-description from publisher's website

name: Brightcast
description:
Brightcast is a fun, fast-paced, 2-player card game. It all starts with one basic rule: get one of each Spellcaster card or five the same Spellcaster card into play to win the game! Begin the game with 4 cards in your hand. Start each turn by drawing a card, then playing a card from your hand and performing that card’s action. Use your Spellcasters to claim victory and stop your opponent from trying to do the same!

Oh...and...watch out for Dragons!

—description from the designer

name: Ruins
description:
Craft unique, transparent cards in this shedding game where you uncover ancient ruins and find treasure.
