On your turn, upgrade a card and play it. Upgrades can stack into wild, game-altering combinations (like a card that equals four 11’s!). You get to claim two cards the entire game – how will you construct the perfect combo?

Race to play your last card and score!

—description from the publisher

name: Slambo!
description:
Hakkeyoi, Nokotta! In this hand management game, try to force your opponent to go above 10 or below 0 to achieve a Slambo! Stay balanced or get slammed!

Each card you play raises or lowers the balance by the number printed on the card. Blue cards raise it, and red cards lower it. Can you stay in the fight long enough to win?

—description from the designer

name: British Tank Ace 1940-1945
description:
British Tank Ace: 1940-45 is a solitaire, tactical-level game that places you in command of a British tank during World War II in North Africa, Italy, and the European Theaters of Operation. You will make the tactical decisions a tank commander faces and control the actions of your crew while trying to survive. You will be assigned missions to attack, defend, or conduct movement-to-contact, depending on the current tactical situation. As time progresses and players survive, experience and prestige are gained and can be used to purchase skills and request improved versions of tanks. Awards and promotions help to narrate the player’s eventual goal – to survive the war and help defeat Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany.

Once you have your initial tank and commander, play proceeds by rolling for a mission and then conducting it. Enemy forces and events are randomly generated, ensuring no two careers will ever be the same. Combat is swift and sometimes deadly; artillery, mortar firs, terrain and weather also have an impact on operations, Players must pay attention to hull down status, the orientation of their hull and turret, and decide when it is prudent to “button up.” Due to its streamlined play, a single mission can be completed in as little as 10 minutes.

When a mission is completed, assuming you have survived, you will ascertain if any awards have been earned or experience points gained. Promotion is also possible, which has the advantage of allowing for artillery and mortar support. You may also upgrade your tank if you have sufficient Prestige to get a better model; otherwise, you continue to fight in your starting tank until it is knocked out.

While British Tank Ace is designed as a solitaire gaming experience, additional options for play are provided for both multi-player cooperative and competitive gaming sessions.

Product Information:
    Complexity: 4 out of 10 (Low/Moderate)
    Playing time: 10-15 minutes (single mission), 4-5 hours (full career)
    Solitaire Suitability: High; Designed for solitaire play
    Players: One or more
    Map Scale: Abstract
    Time Scale: Semi-abstract (individual missions, 8 missions per month)
    Unit Scale: Individual tanks, crewmen, enemy vehicles, anti-tank guns, and ammo

—description from the publisher

name: Brunete 1937: La República pasa a la ofensiva
description:
In July 1937, the Army of the Spanish Republic launched a major offensive near Madrid. Their objective: relieve pressure from the Northern Front, and destroy a sizeable part of the Nationalist forces that had been besieging Madrid since November 1936. Under a scorching sun, Republicans and Nationalist fought a fierce attrition battle that forced the Nationalist command to send reinforcements from other fronts and suspend the advance in the North.

Brunete 1937. La República pasa a la ofensiva (the Republic takes the offensive) is a daily turn, Regiment-battalion simulation of that fierce battle. Each hex is 1 km across.

Published in issue #43 of Alea in November 2025.

name: Brushstroke Mayhem
description:
Brushstroke Mayhem is a card game of chaotic creativity. Players build abstract artworks while outmaneuvering each other in a strategic mess of color and control.

Players choose a Painting from the Open Market at the beginning of the game.  They gain new ones later on.

On their turn,  players layout cards from the Brushstroke draw deck into either a shared canvas or their personal canvas.  They then use these cards to match the abstract painting cards.

The first player to complete 3 paintings, wins the game.

Advanced rules bring extra mechanics like color effects and disruption to add more spice.  The game is designed to be color blind friendly with each brushstroke having its own color symbol.

name: BRUTUS!
description:
Betray your friends. Rule the arena in this card game.

Enter the arena of Brutus: each player embodies a Ludus, a house of gladiators whose survival depends on the wise choices of its leader, the Lanista. Use their unique ability to your advantage. Bet wisely on which fight you'll win: whether your gladiators win the laurels of victory or lose miserably, each of them will be one more step toward your rise.

—description from the designer

name: Buccaneer Heroes
description:
Buccaneer Heroes is a sandbox pirate Print & Play game for 1–6 players, playable solo or cooperatively. Each round, players roll three dice: one determines movement, while the others dictate how much plunder is gained and which faction can be attacked.

Players can visit settlements, trade, upgrade ships and crew, explore pirate dens, complete missions, encounter random events, or unearth buried treasures. Cooperate with other pirates to defeat formidable foes (even in solo mode), or sail alone for higher risks and greater rewards. Actions like discovering treasure or attacking ports can impact others, so tracking everyone's progress is key.

The game spans 24 rounds across eight seasons. At the end of each season, a change in wind direction and a Global Event shake up the board, culminating in an epic finale that tests each player's worth - with only one emerging as the true hero. Earn achievement points through most actions (combat or acquisitions), and the player with the highest total wins.

Buccaneer Heroes delivers an epic, story-driven action-adventure in a vibrant Caribbean world. Packed with twists, characters, monsters, events, and treasures, it is surprisingly quick (30–45 minutes solo) yet offers immense replayability. One playthrough will not reveal all the secrets of this pirate saga!

—description from the designer

name: Buckanjär
description:
Buckanjär is a pirate-themed adventure game where players take on the role of daring captains navigating an ever-expanding map. At the start of the game, each player chooses a unique character and ship combination, with differences in speed, cargo capacity, and equipment — like fishing gear or cannons. The game combines exploration, strategy, and a hint of danger as players set sail from their chosen home ports.

As players move across the map by rolling dice (modified by character traits), they uncover new tiles — revealing islands, fishing spots, or open sea. Islands contain resources that can be collected, sold for coins and gems, or used to upgrade your character. Some islands even hide treasure maps, allowing for high-risk, high-reward expeditions. Coins and gems serve as currency and are key to winning the game.

The twist? All valuables remain aboard your ship until you return home — which means you're vulnerable to plundering by other players. Sea tiles also trigger unpredictable event cards, creating moments of opportunity or danger that can turn the tide of the game.

The game ends when the last tile has been revealed. The player with the most coins wins the game, but fortune favors the bold — and the clever. Buckanjär blends light strategy with a strong thematic experience, perfect for fans of exploration, pirate lore, and dynamic board setups.

—description from the designer

name: Bug House Millionaire
description:
The backyard housing market in Johannesbug was fine until the lawn was laid. Now every bug needs a six-figure down payment to wrangle even the most humble abode. Add to that, a competing couple seems to be making bids faster than you and yours, so hurry and make an offer!

Bug House Millionaire is a climbing/shedding game where you'll be working with a partner to corner the bug housing market! Players will play 2 simultaneous, 2 player climbing/shedding games where the cards they capture will go to the hand of their parter. They'll also have to hurry as the players are on the clock and the player who sheds out first wins, or has their opponent's clock run out.

—description from the designer

name: Bug Run
description:
You play as a caterpillar, a beetle... imprisoned for rebellion by cute but mean animals.
To escape, cross the four levels of the dungeon to the roof. Each turn, buy equipment at the shop, take on challenges in specific rooms and cells, and launch into battle against increasingly powerful animals: the dungeon guards!
You can be alone or joined by other players. Together, you will hope that your dice rolls will allow you to hit the bad guys, to recover the loot.
But you can also let your "companions" fight, arrive just at the end... and pocket the loot!
Only the strongest and most opportunistic will escape with honors!

—description from the publisher

name: Bugs Buddy
description:
Insects are vital to our ecosystem, so that's why you want to take credit for putting them into play in Bugs Buddy.

Each player starts with a secret hand of four double-sided insect tiles. Nine types of insects are included in the deck, each appearing eight times. On a turn, either add a new insect to the display, then place one of your colored cubes underneath it, or add an insect to the column of matching insect tiles already present, then replace another player's cube(s) underneath this insect with the same number of cubes of your color, plus one. (If you place a bee, for example, in a column that has two bees, you remove the opponent's two cubes, then place three of your own.) To end your turn, draw a tile from the deck.

Each insect type will have a single column, and you cannot replace your own cubes when placing a tile. If you don't have enough cubes to play any of your tiles, skip your turn. If you have no more cubes in front of you, you win; if all players pass in turn, whoever has the fewest cubes remaining wins.

name: Soda Jerk
publisher: Allplay; Gém Klub Kft.; Korea Boardgames; Ludofun
description:
In Soda Jerk, you’ll be dealt a hand of delicious soda ingredient cards, including strawberry, blueberry, banana, kiwi, and orange. On your turn, either:


     Play a card face down in front of one of the taps (which are also labeled strawberry, blueberry, banana, kiwi, and orange)
     Flip over a face down card


Play continues until a player starts their turn with three cards left in hand, all players flip over cards consecutively, or all cards on the table are face-up. At this point, determine the final value of all taps: reveal any remaining face-down cards and add up all matching flavor cards while subtracting all non-matching cards. A tap can be worth negative points!

Finally, tally up your score. Each card left in your hand is worth points equal to the final value at the matching tap. So, if you ended with two strawberry cards and the tap value of strawberry was 8, you get 16 points.

Try to get the most points while making your opponents go negative!

—description from the publisher

name: Bumbar
description:
Based on a Serbian children's song about bumblebees trying to bring the order to the meadow. Bumbar means bumblebee in Serbian.

Players organize their hand to create pairs, triples or quadruples of animals to score points. When player has only pairs, triples or quadruples, and they are adjacent, they can end the round, and everybody scores. First to 21 points wins the game.

The game is played completely from hand, and does not need a table or playing surface, making it perfect for travel or waiting in lines at conventions.

—description from the designer

name: Bunny Boom
description:
Bunnies are everywhere! It's an invasion, and nothing seems to be able to stop the proliferation of these adorable little beasts!  Madness has taken hold of the area, and no one wants to be caught with all these rabbits!

In a game of Bunny Boom, you try to pass the bunny problem on to other players!  To do this, you must place cards from your hand in order to push the rabbits as far as possible and attract opponents to pick up more bunnies than you! You also cause BUNNY BOOM!  The game gets more intense each time an opponent places a new card, which may force you to collect more bunnies!

At the end of the game, the player who finishes with the fewest bunnies wins!

—description from the designer

name: Tearable Quest
description:
In Tearable Quest, you’ll have to equip yourself with powerful weapons, fend off terrible boss monsters, and loot gleaming treasure chests using the powerful ability of: tearing paper!

Each player gets a sheet. Each around, a goal card is revealed for all players. For example, the goal might show two swords and a cyclops.

Start a 2-minute timer and start questing! To complete a quest, tear off the exact icons shown on the card (and no extras). Make sure that the icons are fully showing on your torn-off pieces—partials don’t count! You can tear off multiple instances of the active quest to score even more.

There are bonuses and curses on the back of your paper—make sure you check the back or hold your paper up to the light! The player with the most points after three rounds wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Burglar's Blitz
description:
Burglar’s Blitz is a strategic push-your-luck card game where players take on the roles of burglars attempting to sneak into mansions, steal valuable loot, and escape before the police arrive. Thematically, it immerses players in a high-stakes heist scenario filled with risk, competition, and clever maneuvering. Each player must manage their limited loot bag capacity, make critical decisions about which items to take, and contend with the unpredictable effects of action cards.

The gameplay revolves around drawing and managing cards. Players can draw cards from the deck or a junk pile, adding them to their loot bag or discarding them based on their value and utility. Action cards introduce dynamic elements, such as guard dogs that delay turns, burglar alarms that accelerate the police arrival, or getaway drivers that offer a chance to escape unscathed. Players must decide whether to play it safe and secure smaller rewards or risk it all for higher-value items while potentially getting caught.

The game consists of four rounds, each ending when all players flee the scene or when the police arrive and bust everyone left in the mansion. Players score based on the value of the items in their loot bags if they successfully escape. The winner is the player with the highest total score after all four rounds. Tie-breaking rules ensure that even in close games, a decisive winner can emerge.

With its blend of thematic elements, strategic decisions, and interactive gameplay, Burglar’s Blitz offers a fun and engaging experience. It rewards players who balance risk and reward while outmaneuvering their opponents to claim the title of the ultimate mastermind.

—description from the designer

name: Burgle Bros Blackjack
description:
The Burgle Bros are back—this time, the heist is at the Blackjack table! In this cooperative twist on the classic casino game, you and your crew work together to crack safes while dodging guards. Trade cards, build your decks, and plan your moves carefully—every swap brings you closer to success… or disaster. Use unique character abilities and clever tools to stay one step ahead. Can your team pull off the ultimate score before time runs out?

—description from the publisher

name: Burn the Witch
description:
Step back into a dark period in our past, when frenzy and paranoia dominated peoples’ perception of ‘the other’, driving communities across Europe to take the most extreme measures against their fellow man, or woman, as history would have it.

Burn the Witch is a game of social deduction where players are divided into two factions (zealots and sympathizers), which are pitted against each other in a bid for survival. Players represent houses, comprised of two to four villagers, one or more of whom may be a witch. The zealots win by uncovering the identity of all witches in play — a discovery made only through fire. The sympathizers win by keeping the witches’ identities hidden. With witches forming a small minority, the sympathizers’ only chance for success depends on their ability to employ cunning and misdirection as they seek to outwit the other players by turning the zealots’ xenophobia and pyromania back onto themselves.

The game concludes when either every witch in the village has been uncovered or enough innocents have been wrongly condemned that the witch hunt is called off, and the sympathizers win.

—description from the designer

name: Burned
description:
Burned is a quick, aggressive, game of cat-and-mouse for two players. It pits The Agency, led by The Director, against a Burned Asset. The Agency must locate the Burned Asset with its team of Agents. The Asset must use its array of equipment to discover and eliminate The Director. First to die loses. Do you have what it takes to survive  in the Neon City, or will you get Burned.

Choose between playing as The Agency or the lone Burned Asset.

As the Agency you will build your team of Agents to hunt the Asset across the city. Guess where the Burned Asset will move next and intercept them all while protecting the identity of your Director.  As the Burned Asset, you'll have to assemble a kit of weapons and tools to stay hidden while hunting for the Agency Director.

—description from the publisher

name: Twinkle Twinkle
description:
In the tile-laying game Twinkle Twinkle, you'll fill your star chart with clear plastic tiles, trying to connect constellations, build belts of asteroids, collect comets, pick up planets, and study them with satellites. Take care with those pesky black holes - unless you have a perfect spot for them, of course.

Constellations, asteroids, comets, planets, and black holes all score differently! With 10 modular scoring conditions in the box, you can mix and match for 32 different setups. Whoever finds their highest score in the stars wins.

The game features an optional scoring app that allows you to point your phone at the board and watch it magically tally up your points!

—description from the designer

name: Vegas Strip
description:
In this bluffing game, players have hidden information about which casinos are corrupt. Take turns playing money tiles (two 2’s, two 4’s, one 5, one six, one seven) into the different casinos.

When scoring a corrupt casino, the highest bidder wins the jackpot (and everyone else gets nothing). In a non-corrupt casino, whoever has the most points there LOSES, and everyone else gets points equal to their bid.

Players can’t place more than two tokens at a casino, and can’t place their highest token at the casino they know is corrupt.

20 unique casino power cards change up the formula every game. Take a gamble to win big!

—description from the publisher

name: Butterfly Effect: Alter Ego
description:
Butterfly Effect - Alter Ego is the first game in the Butterfly Effect series. 
Live a ccoperative adventure with multiple narrative crossroads.
Use your Action tokens to perform actions and progress through the story, advancing from one era to the next until you reach one of the seven possible endings.
Cooperate, choose your path together and discover where your decisions get you. What if a single choice could change everything ?

You play as William Brown, an average office employee. When the night comes, you become Electrob, a second-class super-vilain stuck in a temporal loop.
In a world in which Supes are outlawed, William seeks only to find out who he is!

—description from the publisher (translated)

name: Butterfly Kingdom
description:
Taiwan’s diverse terrain and climate have nurtured over 400 species of butterflies, including more than 50 endemic species. Records of butterflies in Taiwan date back to the Qing Dynasty, and during the 1950s, large-scale collecting and exports earned the island the nickname “The Kingdom of Butterflies.”
In this game, players travel back to early 20th-century Taiwan as butterfly catchers, collecting and preserving specimens while racing to publish their research before others.
The game is played over several rounds. Each round, players use their starting hand of butterfly cards and try to form as many specimen sets as possible by drawing cards or using discarded cards from other players to exchange for prestige points.
The first player to turn their entire hand into specimen sets ends the round and also earns bonus prestige points from the other players.

—description from the publisher

name: Button
description:
A trick-taking game in may-follow, for 2 to 4 players. Four tricks are open at the centre of the table and players may choose freely where to play. When a trick reaches five cards, it is resolved. If one suit dominates, the strongest card of that suit wins. But if two suits are tied, the weakest of those suits takes the trick.

This simple rule completely changes how tricks are read: you calculate, bluff, take risks… and talk about it again after each hand.

Before each hand, players bet with real buttons. The bet is on the exact number of tricks you aim to win. The game swings between calculation, intuition, and provocation. And there is always the ultimate elegant choice: betting zero tricks.

—description from the designer

name: Buzzin' Picnic
description:
Imagine yourself enjoying a warm afternoon in a flower field, watching friendly insects going about their day and having a lovely time with your family and friends. That is until the annoying bugs ruin your peaceful picnic by buzzing around, crawling all over your food and making you regret ever going out. But will that stop you?

Welcome to Buzzin’ Picnic. In the game, you and your friends are out on a picnic, taking turns guiding Friendly Insects to Insect Hotels while keeping your food safe from Annoying Bugs.

As you play, earn points for every Annoying Bug card that you slap with a Slipper. Plant Flowers to attract Friendly Insects from other players' Flower Fields, and win the game by earning the most points and filling your Points Pile with Friendly Insect and Annoying Bug cards.

Of course, it wouldn‘t be much fun if things were that simple! To make things more interesting, we came up with a few clever ways for you to mess with your friends and loved ones!

—description from the publisher

name: Buzzle
description:
Watch, flip, rotate… and race to complete the pattern before anyone else!

In Buzzle, all players compete to be the first to recreate the insect pattern shown on the central card. Sounds easy? Think again. You'll need to position your insects correctly, matching their orientation, sometimes flipping or rotating them—and even challenging your instincts with special rules and surprise effects.

When you think you’ve got it right, slap your hand on the central card and prove it! If you’re correct, you earn the card as a point and move one step closer to victory. If you’re wrong, you’ll have to wait while the others keep playing.

Some pattern cards hide tricky visual challenges or extra twists, so stay sharp, keep your eyes focused, and be the first to complete three patterns to win the game.

—description from the designer

Observa, gira, voltea… ¡y corre a completar el patrón antes que los demás!

En Buzzle, todos los jugadores compiten por ser los primeros en reproducir el patrón de insectos mostrado en la carta central. ¿Parece fácil? Piénsalo otra vez: tendrás que colocar tus insectos en la posición y orientación correctas, a veces girándolos, volteándolos o incluso desafiando tu intuición con reglas especiales y efectos sorpresa.

Cuando creas tenerlo todo listo, pon tu mano en la carta central y ¡demuestra que no te has equivocado! Si aciertas, ganas la carta como punto y te acercas un paso más a la victoria. Si fallas, tendrás que esperar mientras los demás siguen jugando.

Algunas cartas pueden ocultar trampas visuales o retos extra, así que mantén la cabeza fría, afina la vista y sé el primero en completar tres patrones para ganar la partida.

—description from the designer (Spanish)

name: By Swords and Bayonets
description:
By Swords and Bayonets is the ninth member of GMT Games' Great Battles of The American Civil War series (GBACW).
This game is meant to serve as a introduction for players new to the series by limiting the size of the playing area as well as the number of combatants on the map.  Experienced GBACW players will appreciate the addition of these four short, sharp "done in an afternoon" battles.

Features Include:

     Four Civil War battles, each on a 22" x "17 "half size" map
     Opposing forces are no more than one division per side with 50 or fewer combat units each
     The full GBACW rulebook is supported so there is nothing to "unlearn" when players delve into other GBACW series games


The Battle Scenarios:

     Big Bethel, June 10, 1861 detailing Gen. Benjamin Butler's overconfident assault on John Magruder's Confederates



     Rappahannock Station, Nov. 7, 1863 in which elements of Sedgewick's VI Union Corps attempt to isolate and disperse a section of Early's CSA division.  There is a one turn "learning scenario" for this battle.



     New Bern, Mar. 14 1862, featuring Maj. General Ambrose Burnside's launches an attack on dug-in but inexperienced Confederates in the vicinity of Fort Thompson.



     Mill Springs, Jan. 19, 1862 where Rebel Gen. G. Crittenden raced to surprise a large Union contingent before they could be reinforced.


—description from the publisher

name: Byline
description:
1960. The world is brimming with news waiting for independent reporters to capture them into newsprint. Byline puts the player into the role as an independent newspaper reporter trying to elevate their reputation and as well as the popularity of the major newspaper outlets. Over the course of seven days, players will pack each workday with seeking out sources, validating leads, and delivering stories just in time to meet the critical deadline.

Byline, at its heart, is a worker placement game with a twist. The game plays one to four players in 60 to 90 minutes.

name: ByPass
description:
Embark on a thrilling race to construct a smooth, continuous road from opposite ends of the gameboard in ByPass! Brace yourself for twists and turns, stay adaptable to dodge traffic cones, and strategize your path. Do you have the planning skills needed to be the first to build a completed ByPass? Let's hit the road!

Be the first to build a continuous road across the game board from your start to end zone. While this may seem like an easy feat, your opponents will attempt to block your moves, so be prepared to plan your path and use strategy to build your road tile by tile.

Speaking of tiles, each of the seven in the game has a distinct road pattern, three of which contain a dead end marked with a barricade. All players may use any road tile placed on the board as part of their path, no matter who placed it. Harness planning, strategy, and spatial reasoning skills to capture a bypass and get ahead of your opponents. Play with 2-4 players, ages 8 and up, in 25 minutes.

name: Bôken
description:
Bôken aims to faithfully recreate the experience of Japanese RPGs from the 80s and 90s in a board game format. It offers a vast campaign lasting 15 to 30 hours set in the open-world kingdom of Lanoth, featuring exploration, combat, loot, villages, shops, NPCs, quests, dungeons, bosses, and more…

It is a cooperative or solo adventure game for 1 to 2 players who will need to collaborate to defeat the game. It faithfully replicates the mechanics of console JRPGs while also taking into consideration the significance of board game dynamics.

Each player will take on the role of a hero. If you're playing solo, you can either control a single hero or play both heroes, just like in a two-player game.

You will explore the kingdom of Lanoth, its lands, villages, and dungeons while battling hostile creatures along your path. You'll also encounter the inhabitants of Lanoth who will entrust you with quests, and your destiny will unfold as the adventure progresses.
The scenario offers many hours of gameplay, requiring several sessions to complete. An instant save system has been designed to allow you to stop, store, and bring out the game within a minute, thanks to magnetized character sheets and a magnetized game board.

—description from the publisher

name: C'est Carré
description:
C'est Carré ("Squared") is a card collection and placement game.

50 points or more and you win!
If not, start a new round.


     Play the top card of the discard pile or deck, to make a 9-card square (3x3).
     Activate the card you've played: negative cards allow you to play other cards.


Positive cards allow you to draw other cards.

     Your square earns you value points + areas of the same Earthenware (color).

name: Cachamot
description:
Cachamot is a deduction game in which players must guess the last word of a 3-word sequence made by another player. The only clues available to them are the whole first word and the first letter of the other two! If no one guessed right after one try each, reveal more letters and try again.
Players earn points by being the first to guess the word, or by designing riddles that other players will successfully guess… but not too easily!

—description from the publisher

name: Caged In
description:
Caged In is a fast-paced 2 player fighting game that has players squaring off in MMA combat.

Fighters will choose from four unique styles and try to knock each other out, submit each other, or impress the judges for a decision. Caged In is perfect for those who like games that are simple to learn and hard to master. The strategy comes from managing your hand and trying to exploit your opponent's weaknesses.

The game features a unique hexagonal box design, dual layered player and game boards with damage cubes that sink into the board and custom designed 3D miniatures.

—description from the publisher

name: CakoZaurus
description:
In CakoZaurus, you want to complete customer orders despite that presence of a monster in the kitchen that will eat your supplies if you're not careful.

On a turn, you draw ingredient cubes from a bag, then drop them in a funnel. You then fulfill an outstanding order in part of the kitchen that has the right cubes in it or move a cube to a different region or pick up from one region and drop them again. The monster will move from region to region, scooping up ingredients in its mouth — although if you can get it to eat the pepper cubes, the spice will cause the monster to eject everything into the funnel, putting cubes back into play in the most appetizing way possible.

name: Calcool 2025
description:
The new 2025 edition offers two fast-paced dice race games with 10 dice in 10 different colors. Quickly place the correct dice for the options on your challenge cards so that you are the first to create a chain of 10 to 12 dice.
The 2 games in the box involve very different levels:

     The Colours Game is all about logic and speed
     The Stages Game offers even more challenges: You also have to do mental arithmetic and be very good at tactics.


Both games feature traps for you in the form of Chicanes on the challenge cards, so it is very likely that you are making mistakes that will cost you points.

This new edition of 2025 also includes completely new challenge cards.

—description from the publisher

name: California: Roll & Write
description:
We open our family farm where we will collect dice of: carrots, tomatoes, peppers and lettuce in our warehouse. We will use our tools to modify the dice and ship the orders to our customers.
With a dice draft system, players in this roll & write game will try to get the best orders and combine customers to be the player with the most market points at the end of the game and win the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Call The Doctor
description:
Call the Doctor is a print & play game where players step into the role of a surgeon and perform challenging operations.

Each game is built around medical scenarios inspired by specific cases – for example, removing a brain tumor. The gameplay combines several mechanics: action pool management, dice allocation, and drawing. The surgery is carried out step by step: anesthesia, incision, removal of the lesion, suturing, and awakening – each stage introduces different mechanics and requires careful decision-making. The game is largely based on real surgical procedures, medicines, and instruments, and aims to be as realistic as possible.

Players have access to a set of resources, including:

    Medicine Card
    Tools Card
    Patient Status Sheet
    Operation Sheet


A key element of the game is the proper use of medicines. Every drug influences the patient’s condition in unique ways – for example, raising blood pressure while simultaneously reducing blood clotting. The duration and difficulty of the surgery depend heavily on the patient’s status.

At the beginning of each turn, a Status Card is drawn, modifying specific indicators. In addition to performing surgical actions, players must also counteract these ongoing effects to keep the patient stable. You must always bear in mind that you have a limited number of time points at your disposal to finish the procedure.

Call the Doctor offers a unique mix of strategy and thematic immersion, turning every operation into a tense balance between precision, timing, and resource management.

—description from the publisher

name: Calupum: Shadowed by the Wolf
description:
Protect your flock of sheep from the cunning wolves sneaking around the field! After 12 rounds, the player with the most victory points wins.

One Game, two sides: Play the simpler winter side or the more complex summer side – it’s entirely up to you!

Winter Side:
Calupum in the truest sense of the word: Here, you only need to watch out for the wolves — and, of course, your fellow players! Play Calupum in winter mode as an introduction or for a quick game in between.

Summer Side:
More components, more possibilities, more Calupum! The Summer side is significantly more complex. Here, you’ll encounter not only wolves and sheep, but also objectives, tunnels, dog cards, and much more! In summer mode, Bobtail the sheepdog and the shepherdess come to your aid. Use the dog cards for extra advantages and collect even more points with the objective cards.

—description from the publisher

name: Camelio
description:
In this clever card game of bluff and timing, players must collect exactly five Spheres of the same color to score a point. But beware — if you go over five, you bust and lose all cards of that color!

On your turn, choose one of two cards:

     the face-up card (where both color and number of Spheres are visible),
     or the face-down card (which reveals only partial information: either the color or the number of Spheres).


Then decide: will you keep the card for yourself or give it to another player? You must choose before revealing the card!

Players arrange cards in their play area by color. If you reach exactly five Spheres of a color, you score 1 point and move those cards to your scoring area. But if you exceed five, you must discard all cards of that color — and if it’s a color you've already scored, you lose the point, too!

Camelio mixes tactical decisions, lucky guesses, and sneaky moves to deliver a fast-paced and fun experience for all players!

—description from the publisher

name: Camping Season
description:
Have you ever wondered what it would be like to be the founder of a thriving campground? Well now, you’re invited to step into their shoes, to see if you have what it takes to run the show in Camping Season.

In this board game,  you’ll have the opportunity to build, design, and manage your own campground. You and your fellow owners will have 6 seasons to create the ultimate camping experience. Whoever earns the most points by attracting guests and optimizing profits will be recognized and awarded for their prestigious efforts.  Think you have what it takes to build and manage a 5 star camping resort?

In order to get a leg up on the competition, you’ll need to manage your money wisely. Each round, owners will have the opportunity to expand their campground and build amenities, finding the balance between what type of campsites are available and how many guests their campground can handle. Upgrade your campground with special projects, exploring different combinations to fit your overall strategy, and maximize your output. Design the resort of your dreams with a selection of 60 unique amenities. But be mindful, while some amenities have amazing benefits, they may increase the maintenance needed to keep your campground in tip top shape. If you fail to keep up with the resort maintenance, your guests may leave you a poor review.

At the beginning of each season, new customers will be added to your Guest Bag, along with the customers added by your amenities. Every decision is an opportunity to explore the intricacies of Camping Season in new and exciting ways, creating limitless replayability.

—description from the publisher

name: Waddle
description:
Strategically place your penguins to form groups and claim fish to score the most points! Turn order matters a lot; in Waddle, it’s tracked by marbles on a two-column track!
On your turn, you’ll have two options:


     “Place a Penguin” onto any unoccupied hex adjacent to the lowest numbered water hex. Then, pick up your marble and place it on the top of the same Turn Tracker column
     “Scout Ahead” by picking up and placing your marble on top of the inactive Turn Tracker column.


How players “Scout Ahead” will be massively important! Going earlier in the future could allow you to grow or connect into a large waddle (group), claim a big fish, or block an opponent’s important play.

—description from the publisher

name: Can't Go
description:
A family-friendly, toilet-themed quirky trick taking game.
The goal is to be the first to claim 400 poop points, or to score the most before one of the draw decks runs out.

Players play poop cards into the play area, alongside toilet cubicles, to accumulate potentially claimable points. Once a poop is 'finished' players race to try to claim the points of that poop in play.

Turns can be based on grabbing points, sharing points or sabotaging other players' options. Let chaos commence!

—description from the designer

name: Candy Land
description:
Welcome to the Candy Land game! In this reimagined version of the classic preschool game, little ones choose a Sweet Scout mover, select colored “candy” tokens from the Pouch of Wonders, and travel up the Rainbow Gummy Path to Candy Castle! Who will they meet along the way—and which player will reach the castle first?


     5 UNIQUE CHARACTER MOVERS: Play as a Sweet Scout! Choose from 4 colorful plastic movers, each a unique character in a treat-inspired outfit. Also includes a Gummy Twins (Sweety Bear and Soury Bear) mover.



     2 FUN WAYS TO PLAY: In classic mode, race to be the first player to meet Queen Frostine at Candy Castle! Collaborative mode keeps the game fresh with light strategy—players team up to get 3 Sweet Scouts to the castle before the Gummy Twins. 



     LARGER BOARD WITH UPDATED ART & STORY: Visit Gloppy, Plumpy, and Queen Frostine! Discover a reimagined land of familiar characters and adorable additions on the 20” x 20” board. Also included is an illustrated story.



     DRAWSTRING POUCH OF “CANDY” TOKENS: Instead of drawing cards to move along the board, kids can experience the excitement of reaching into the felt Pouch of Wonders to draw cardstock candy tokens.


—description from the publisher

name: Candy Utopia
description:
Welcome to Chocoland, a world made entirely of sweets! Its capital, Candy Utopia, is a lively and colorful city with chocolate streets, caramel pavement, and houses made of soft marshmallow. The city is divided into several districts, each managed by the ingenious Gummy Bears, who work alongside skilled workers from various confectionery enterprises:


     The expert district builders of CaraFuel
     The masters of cutting-edge technology from JellyTech
     The tireless party spirits of BubbleFun
     The reliable digital specialists of MarshMail


The most eagerly awaited moment of the year is the Great Sweets Festival, a competition that lasts three days and puts the city's districts to the test. The Gummy Bears compete to improve their districts, enriching them with sweet activities and ever-expanding blocks. Each day of the festival represents a stage of improvement, and at the end of each stage, a piñata full of bonuses opens up: resources, decorations, and upgrades that are useful for the districts.
At the end of the festival, the Gummy Bears score their improvements and bonuses.

In more detail, a game of Candy Utopia is played over three days, each consisting of three turns per player. During the game, players build their districts by placing ChocoMix tiles made up of various types of terrain. They place workers to actions — called "activities" — and each activity moves a player on one of five thematic tracks, unlocking progressive bonuses, active powers, extra turns, or enhanced card/tile draws. Each activity is placed following distance and positioning rules, and their placement directly impacts future activities.

Cards can be played for instant effects, used to complete objectives, or saved to score end-game points; players will also compete over piñata cards, which are shared goals related to district building or card management and which award bonus points at game's end.

name: Cannibal World
description:
Engage in tactical combat and survival environment with stunning artwork by award winner illustrator Oscar Martin, in a dystopian world of anthropomorphic animals.

Cannibal World is an expandable dueling card game where you fight as one of four factions in a post-apocaliptic world. You will be able to customize your faction's deck as you see fit.

The gameplay revolves around strategic deck management, resource allocation, and tactical combat. Players alternate turns, drawing cards from their Main or Reinforcement Decks, and use meat counters to perform various actions, such as summoning creatures, initiating combat, or activating abilities.

Combat is central to gameplay, where players use creatures to attack their opponent’s creatures or attempt to ransack their opponent's habitat. Combat is resolved through damage mechanics, with both melee and ranged attacks.

The gameplay's focus on tactical decisions, resource management, and faction-specific abilities creates a highly strategic and engaging experience.

Victory is achieved through two main conditions: eliminating all of the opponent’s creatures (from play, hand, and deck), or ransacking their habitat three times.

—description from the publisher

name: Cantankerous Cats (Third Edition)
description:
You are a Cat. You live in a House. You share this house with your pet Hoomin. Shower this Hoomin with your Affection, then cause as much Mischief as you can without being thrown out of your House. The first Cat to score 9 Mischief points is the winner of the game!

In this furrocious feline card game of mischievous machinations, you play the role of a Cat doing what cats do best: tormenting their Hoomin pets! Play Affection cards into your House to gain their trust, then wait for the right moment to play Mischief cards to score points.

But be quick about it! The other Cats in your Neighborhood will play Incident cards to slow your progress to give themselves the upper claw.

This remixed, remastered, and renewed THIRD EDITION of our beloved indie title has been refined and remastered with the following updates:


     Streamlined rules for faster, family friendly gameplay at ALL difficulty levels.
     Graphic design and rule enhancements to keep the game fresh for 2025.
     All illustrations have been rescanned to archival standards for more detailed paintings.
     INCLUDES the previously unreleased expansion: "Cantankerous Cats and the Kitten Catastrophe"


"Kitten Catastrophe" includes 13 new cards that can be mixed into the base game for easier scoring and more kittens!

Designed by the original Cantankerous Cats team with refinements by Jason Serrato and Aven Gonzalez.
The stunning watercolor tradition continues with new adorable kitten illustrations by Amanda Kahl, Rebecca Rhodes, and Aven Gonzalez.'

—description from the publisher

name: Container
description:
Every decision you make in Container shapes the market. During play, you build factories, produce containers, set prices, negotiate with your rivals, sail across the sea to trade, and (obviously) buy low, and sell high. At least that's the goal — but can you make it happen?

The rules for Container are simple; the real challenge is understanding and timing the market. Players build machines, warehouses, and containers, then sail your containers to the island and auction them off.  Be careful with your money — in the closed economy, money's tight and your opponents are cutthroat!

At the beginning of the game, container value cards are secretly dealt to all players. Because these values aren’t shown, you’ll have to suss out what your opponents are going for throughout the game! But at final scoring, these come into play.  The player with the most money wins.

name: Capybattle
description:
Back in medieval times, Capybaras discovered "Match 4" and immediately knew they could do better. After tireless research and scientific experiments, they had finally made it - MATCH 5!

In CapyBattle, the goal is to dominate five quarters in a row alongside your trusty Capybara knights or fortified allied structures.

The core of this two-player game lies in the 10 randomly placed actions. During each turn, the capybara monarchs, pivotal pieces, move from capybara to capybara to activate corresponding actions aligned with the column and row of each capybara.

These actions can allow you to do things such as moving capybaras, baiting enemy capybaras, building structures, using secret passages, or simply taking a nap. With new structures, more knights will heed the call of their leaders until the whole Capytal will be flooded with chivalrous rodents and the new Heir to the throne will be finally decided!

name: Card Bullet Re:Load
description: Be the last person standing in this simple card game which simulates the play experience of a free-for-all first person shooter. Play cards to shoot at your opponents. However beware they may have counter cards which deflect damage back to you. It's everyone for themselves. On your turn you can only choose to play a card or reload (draw a card). Don't get tied up fighting one opponent and wasting away all your cards. When you are down with few cards, that's when the other players will pounce on you.

name: Card Game Traders
description:
Collect the most valuable cards among the most famous Trading Card Games!
Sell and buy cards in a changing market, control the stock flow and interfere in your opponent's plans activating the abilities linked to each item.

Card Game Traders is a fun and fast game where each turn you would play a card, changing their value, maybe activate their abilities and buy other cards in order to grow your collection (hand).
By the end of the game, played in less than 40 minutes, the player with the most valuable set of cards in their collection wins the game.

Card Game Traders reimplements CGT, revamping the game art wit fabulous homages to the most recognizable trading cards around the world, adding new elements and streamlining the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Card Rails Exchange
description:
Card Rails: Exchange is all auctions all of the time! Players blind bid to win railways in which they can invest so that maybe they can win big in the end — but sometimes losing a bid can be a better long-term investment. It depends on what's in your hand!

This game is about trying to balance the bid you're making with the cards in your hand because you earn points based on the number of completed railway cards and which investment cards you used to complete them. Whoever ends up with the most points wins.

Card Rails Exchange is a standalone game in the Card Rails line.

—description from the designer

name: Cargo
description:
Cargo is a fast, sabotage-filled card game where players race to stack shipping container cards onto their cargo ship and complete two successful shipments. The goal is to hit exactly 25 points (twice) before your rivals sink your plans.

The game blends simple maths with ruthless sabotage and plenty of table talk. One minute you’re carefully stacking, the next you’re scrambling after a well-timed storm surge wipes out your progress. Quick to learn and replay, Cargo balances strategy with chaos in a way that keeps people laughing and asking for “just one more round.”

Whether you’re game-night obsessed or just looking for something light and fun to play with family or friends, Cargo delivers that mix of tension, banter, and hilariously close finishes that make it a crowd favourite.

—description from the publisher

name: Cargo Empire
description:
Cargo Empire is a pick-up-and-deliver board game with point-to-point network building. Players immerse themselves in a complex world of transportation networks, striving for glory, wealth, and power as leaders of one of the four major families on the continent of Dyorle.

There is only one action in this game, and that is transporting cargo. Players must navigate a changing landscape, weaving between cities and using various transport modes to score points. To dominate, players must plan their network of trading posts meticulously and keep a sharp eye on long-term rewards.

Can you build the mightiest cargo empire? Simple choices derived from an intriguing combination of mechanisms will challenge your skills in resource management and strategic thinking. Only one can become the king of commerce!

—description from the publisher

name: Enchanted Ivy
description:
Take on the role of Ivy, the courageous new owner of a magical inn. Build your bewitching B&B to best suit your eccentric guests while cultivating the ivy covering your walls.

Each turn, carefully place each card in a grid. Assign guests, noting their preferences (things like "diagonally adjacent", "same row", "surrounded" etc.) to score them at the end of the game.

In Story Mode, earn rewards for meeting point goals and completing unique challenges.

—description from the publisher

name: Fiction: Banned Books
description:
Fiction: Banned Books is a sequel to Fiction—a Wordle-inspired one-vs-many game of deception.

To begin, the Lie-brarian selects a five-letter word (chosen from passages of books that have been banned, burned, or censored in history).

The Guessers’ goal is to deduce the five-letter word. They do so by guessing it and receiving clues about the letters in their words. Every turn, the Lie-brarian’s clues always contain exactly one lie. Will the Guessers figure out the word before time runs out?

Fiction: Banned Books introduces all new asymmetric powers (for both the Lie-braian and the Guessers). Use these powers at pivotal moments to gain the upper hand!

—description from the publisher

name: Carom Golf
description:
A tabletop simulation of golf.

The board is made of 4 large segments (22.5 x 23.5 cm) and 8 small triangular segments. By combining these segments in a variety of ways, you can make a huge number of golf course configurations.

On its path, the ball may encounter different types of obstacles, and each type affects the ball differently. By carefully choosing the stroke directions, the ball can bypass any obstacle, and the ball can even fly over obstacles, if it gets hit hard enough.

Carom Golf can be played in the classical way: each player plays by themselves until they put the ball into the hole, and writes the score down. However, there is also a Carom mode, that is much more dynamic and interesting, because all players play one stroke at a time on the same hole. In this mode, it is possible to hit the other player's ball with your own, change its position, and even knock it out of court. In this mode, there are no fair no foul plays, there are just different ways to victory.

—description from the publisher

name: Carpniches
description:
Carpniches is an abstract strategy game for two players. Each player controls either white or black pieces with the aim of forming a straight line of three consecutive pieces of their own color, either horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. Alternatively, a player can win by blocking their opponent so they cannot make any legal moves.

Gameplay:
The game is played on a 6x6 board with pre-arranged stacks of alternating black and white pieces in the corners and adjacent diagonals. Players take turns moving the top piece of a stack. A piece moves a number of spaces equal to the height of the stack it came from, traveling in a straight line without jumping over other stacks. Pieces can land on empty squares or on stacks of one or two pieces, but not on stacks of three.

Victory:
Victory is achieved either by forming a straight line of three pieces of your color or by preventing your opponent from making any legal move. Strategic movement and positioning are crucial, as players must manage both offensive threats and defensive maneuvers.


Spanish:

Carpniches es un juego de estrategia abstracta combinacional para dos jugadores. Cada jugador controla piezas blancas o negras y debe formar una línea recta de tres piezas consecutivas de su color (ya sea en forma horizontal, vertical o diagonal). También se puede ganar bloqueando al oponente para que no pueda realizar ningún movimiento legal.

Desarrollo del juego:
El juego se desarrolla sobre un tablero de 6x6 casillas, con pilas de piezas colocadas previamente en las esquinas y diagonales adyacentes. Los jugadores se alternan moviendo la pieza que esté en la cima de una pila. Cada pieza se mueve una cantidad de casillas igual a la altura de la pila de donde se mueve, en línea recta, sin saltar otras pilas. Puede aterrizar en casillas vacías o en pilas de una o dos piezas, pero nunca en una pila de tres piezas.

Condiciones de victoria:
Se gana formando una línea recta de tres piezas propias o bloqueando al oponente para que no pueda mover. La estrategia y la planificación son esenciales, tanto para atacar como para defenderse.

name: GRUNTZ
description:
In Gruntz, you'll command units like infantry, tanks, and aircraft with rock-paper-scissors-like relationships. For example, Gruntz are slow-moving and can't defeat all enemy units, but they're the only ones who can capture the control points at the middle of the map. Planes wreak havoc on the battlefield, but carefully placed Anti-Aircraft stop them in their tracks.

When you deploy tanks and trucks, you'll outfit them with different Magnetic attachments! Choose a cannon for extra firepower, or a cargo hold to transport troops. This flexibility creates awesome counterplay and tactical decision-making.

Capture the zones in the middle of the board to gain points. First to three points wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Casinopolis
description:
Ka-ching! Ka-ching! The sounds of slot machines paying out their lucky winners are everywhere. Build up the central strip with popular themed casinos to turn this town into a proper gambler's haven.

Casinopolis is a standalone entry in the Sprawlopolis line of games, and plays similarly to the original with a few new twists. Place cards in an expanding map to create large groups of casinos, line up jackpot icons along roads, and balance scoring from three unique goals. You’ll need a little luck and a whole lot of skill to maximize your winnings!

Casinopolis has 18 double-sided cards. One side shows the blocks that players use to expand their map, while the other side shows unique scoring conditions. 3 of these are randomly dealt at the start of the game to establish the 1-, 2-, and 3-chip bets for the game. The higher the bet, the more points that goal is worth at the end of the game.

Players take turns adding a single card to the map. Cards must be added in a horizontal alignment. They can be placed next to or overlapping a previously-placed card.

Each card features 4 blocks split among the 3 different casino colors. Adjacent blocks that share a color form larger casinos.

Blocks can include up to 2 roads on them. Each road costs points at the end of the game, though their impact can be lessened by connecting segments across multiple blocks to form a single road. The longest road at the end of play is the Strip, where the most important casinos can be found. Roads may also include 1 or more of the 6 lucky symbols, which can pay off substantially at the end if lined up properly.

Once all 15 cards have been played, the game ends and points are scored. Players gain 1 point per block from the largest casino of each type that is adjacent to the Strip, then lose 1 point for each road.

Each scoring goal is evaluated in order, with each instance of the condition adding 1, 2, or 3 points to the total based on the goal’s placement at setup.

Next, jackpots are scored: for each run of 3 or more matching lucky symbols that are adjacent on a shared road, score 1 point per icon.

Finally, the total is compared to the target number: the sum of the 3 numbers listed on each goal card. Score higher than the target number to win the game!

name: Casque Chèque Chat
description: In the party game Casque Chèque Chat, players work in teams to give clues that sound like nonsense to their teammates, but ideally when these teammates repeat the clues aloud multiple times, the phrase will converge in meaningful words or expressions.

name: Cassette Dungeons!
description:
The dungeon is stinky, the treasure has underwear and cassette tapes in it and the boss is a ball of tangled wires! No better place to recruit some valiant heroes and go exploring! Charge into danger as you explore compact dungeons and manage the constant dangers you’ll encounter.

Cassette Dungeons! packs together resource management, light strategy and the spirit of metal into a cosy little ruleset and game box so that it can be played in even the most cramped cells and dungeons.

Stomp through dungeons one by one, murdering the unanimously hostile inhabitants, navigating typical trope traps, slaying a weird boss-thingy, then carefully place the treasure in an evidence bag and repeat this process to gradually build a sense of accomplishment!

—description from the publisher

name: Mountain Goats: Legacy
description:
Each turn, roll and combine dice to race up the mountain. Get to the top to score, but don’t get knocked off! If you roll the goat symbol, activate new abilities — powers that rotate every mission. As your story progresses, you’ll unlock even more powerful abilities and face tougher challenges. The mountain itself might even transform beneath your feet.  

Mountain Goats: Legacy combines  dice rolling/combining and events into a longer  version of Mountain Goats.  But, after the first session, more and more hazards and gameplay tweaks show up. The dice now have a goat symbol — when rolled, you’ll get to use one of the unlocked player powers. These can change with every session! There’s also a new system called “Courage” that greatly affects your ability to mitigate luck and refine your dice rolls.

This game can be played as either a single session or a legacy game.  As a legacy game, it is fully replayable and resettable. You will not be asked to destroy or modify components. The first session can also be combined with the original Mountain Goats game.

—description from the publisher

name: Castle Up
description:
CastleUp is a competitive card game for 2-4 players set in the bustling era of the middle ages. Each player embarks on an ambitious journey to establish and grow their own city, vying for influence and supremacy in a world where strategy and cunning are key. The game intricately blends elements of moderate complexity strategy with engaging mechanics of deck building and tableau building.

In CastleUp, every card action is a strategic choice, revealing layers of depth as players carefully construct their city. The game features innovative mechanics, such as cards that turn when damaged, maintaining full visibility to all players and adding a layer of tactical foresight. Resource management plays a crucial role, as players must judiciously allocate their assets to outmaneuver their rivals.

Designed for competitive players, CastleUp eschews the randomness of dice, focusing instead on skillful planning and execution. As the game progresses through multiple rounds, players take consecutive turns, each action building upon the last towards an intricate web of potential victory. The game concludes when the drawing deck is depleted, with the player amassing the most victory points declared the winner. This title not only challenges the strategic acumen of its players but also invites them to immerse themselves in a richly crafted medieval experience.

name: Cat Burglars
publisher: Jolly Dutch Productions; JB WonderFantasy Games
description:
Send your cat crews on daring missions to obtain the coveted “Golden Balls of Yarn”, masterpieces by the legendary artist Maximo Kattelan now on display in the mysterious museum. It’s your cat crews’ job to obtain them, but be careful! Other crews will try to loot your finds, so use traps to mislead them.

In Cat Burglars players take turns in clockwise order, performing one action per turn. They can choose from one of five available actions:

     Recruit two cats
     Form a cat crew
     Activate a cat crew
     Secure the loot
     Infiltrate


By recruiting cats, they form cat crews that will try to secure the Golden Balls of Yarn. Larger cat crews have a higher chance of securing the loot, but they take time to form. By infiltrating cat crews of other players, players might be able to snatch some of their Golden Balls of Yarn before they are secured. But beware of the traps the other players might set for you!

When a player collects eight Golden Balls of Yarn, they win, and the game ends.

—description from the publisher

name: River Valley Jewelcraft
description:
Return to the cozy town of River Valley! But this time, dig a little deeper. Glass is so last year.

Now, it's all about the rare, radiant gemstones under our idyllic little town of River Valley. Miners, craftspeople, and artisans of all kinds have converged to make and sell the most beautiful jewelry in the land.

On your turn, roll dice to gather gems. Use your unique movement rules and player powers to explore the mine. Carefully lay tiles to improve your potential spoils. Finally, use your gems to craft exquisite jewelry to build a powerful scoring engine!

While River Valley Jewelcraft is a return to the setting and soul of River Valley Glassworks, it's a completely brand new game with completely unique gameplay and components.

—description from the publisher

name: Cat In 8
description:
Cat-In-8 is an innovative cat-themed abstract strategy game that challenges players to outwit their opponents in a race to score points by aligning three or more cat tokens in a row. Drawing inspiration from the word “catenate”—to link things together—this clever title takes the concept of connection to new heights through its unique tile-shifting mechanics.

The game’s dynamic 4x4 grid is in constant motion, with players rotating, sliding, and rearranging tiles to create scoring opportunities while thwarting their rivals. Adding to the unpredictability are Chaos Cards, which introduce playful twists to the game. These special cards let players swap tokens, rotate tiles, or push rows to shake up the board and keep everyone on their paws.

For those skilled (or lucky!) enough to align eight cat tokens in a single row, the ultimate victory is theirs—immediately ending the game in a thrilling feat of strategy and chaos.

Whether you’re a fan of lighthearted competition or calculated maneuvers, Cat-In-8 delivers a perfect balance of thoughtful gameplay and chaotic fun. With its easy-to-learn rules, replay ability, and original artwork, this game promises an engaging experience for casual gamers, families, and seasoned strategists alike.

name: Cat Nap
description:
In Cat Nap, rival cats sprawl out across a shared blanket, claiming cozy corners and stretching to impossible lengths. Using a charming collection of cat-shaped tiles, players take turns building out tails, body-segments, and faces—completing cats to earn the right to claim a color and snatch tiles from the discard pile for future use.

The board starts blank, but by the end it’s a tangle of overlapping kitties in all shapes and sizes. Will your feline creations outstretch the competition?

—description from the designer

name: Sail Legacy
description:
Assemble your crew, captain your ship, and take on the high seas in this legacy co-op trick-taker!

In Sail Legacy, you and your best matey will go on an adventure across thirty unique missions. Upgrade your ship, outfit your characters, and tune the deck itself to avoid a watery grave!

Sail Legacy evolves from the core Sail game mechanisms as you cooperatively use "must-follow" trick-taking to take on the unforgiving ocean — and the mythical beasts that call it home. Based on the combination of symbols in the trick, you'll steer the ship, charge ahead, or fire the cannons. Throughout the game, you'll tweak your pirate's asymmetric player powers. Will you have a well-balanced team or specialize in one area?

An epic campaign awaits. Live with the consequences of numerous branching decisions. Express your creativity with customization. Most of all, don't sink. No two tales will be the same!

—description from the publisher

name: Cat Sabbath
description:
It’s challenging enough to make a regular cat go somewhere… but what if the cat is a witch?
In Cat Sabbath, a trick-taking card game, players compete to make Supreme Witches come to their witchy conventions. Everyone plays one trick for each witch. Win a trick, and a Supreme Witch joins you!
Remember, if you have too many Supreme Witches, your celebration will turn into chaos. So, just like cats, players must find PURR-fect balance!

Cat Sabbath is a three-round trick-taking card game, where players simultaneously play four tricks to invite Supreme Witches to their festivity and earn the most Victory Points.
In each round, players choose 4 Supreme Witches and play cards below every witch that doesn’t have their card yet. All cards in a Supreme Witch’s row must follow the suit of the first card played there. When everyone plays a card in each Supreme Witch’s row, the round ends. Win a trick—take all witch cards from the row, plus the Supreme Witch as a multiplier. Too many Supreme Witches on hand will lead to chaos, so you must find the PURR-fect cat balance to win the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Cat Says Moo
description:
What Does the Cat Say? Moo? Meow?

Get ready for a fast, fun, and wildly silly game of animal mix-ups!

Flip a card, find a match, and race to be the first to shout the right sound or name—but be careful, your brain might play tricks on you! Stay sharp, react fast, and collect the most cards to win.

name: Cat Sudoku: Summer Festival
description:
The core objective of Summer Festival revolves around the classic Sudoku challenge, but with a colorful twist and additional strategic elements to enhance gameplay.

Summer Festival is an engaging Cat Sudoku card game. The main goal is to place numbered and colored cards on a 3x3 grid, ensuring that each number and color is unique within its respective row and column. Additionally, players strive to strategically place cards in their designated area to collect reserve tokens and accumulate points.

When the game ends, players will score points based on the number of cards played in their score zone minus unplaced reserve cards that are still in their player area. The player who scores the highest points wins the game. In case of a tie, the player who has the most reserve tokens wins. In case of another tie, players share the win.

—description from the designer

name: Cat Sushi Masters
description:
A card based party game for 2 to 6 adults and children that will turn you into hungry cats ready to dive on tons of... Catilicious sushi!

The goal of the game is to eat more sushi (and get more points) than the other players and become the next Cat Sushi Master!

Each round, players will fight with ancient instruments (bowl, sticks and napkins) to get theyr desired sushi card.

Each card grants points and wasabi points, used to buy upgrades in the kitchen, right after the fight.

Upgrades are split between ancient recipes (which let you score more point at the end of the game) and sensei shef (the actual Cat Sushi Master) techniques (which help you in fights)

The game ends when ther's no more sushi! 
Tally the points and who has the most it's the next CAT SUSHI MASTER!

-description from designer

name: Cat vs. Human
description:
Based on the Pizza Cake Webcomic, players are cats, drawing 4 CAT CARDS per round and play them to annoy the human! You take turns playing as many cat cards with a matching mischief mark under the human cards that you want. Whoever has the highest cat card score wins that human card. The first player to win 5 human cards first wins (gets food).

This is a Quick-Moving game using trick-taking and press-your-luck mechanics. It always plays out differently and is fun to play multiple games in a row.

name: Catan Connect
description:
Play together in parallel on a large island world. Up to six players start the game simultaneously, round after round! They explore the island and secure the best building sites in neighboring areas. The digital CATAN Assistant guides you through the game with dice and a timer. It also indicates whether it's the sun or moon side's turn to build and introduces the robber. With additional sets, the number of players can be expanded as desired. The event game for the popular classic board game with extensive game material for large, dynamic game sessions or gaming weekends with a particularly fast-paced gameplay.

—description from the publisher

name: CATATAC
description:
Dive into a frantic feline duel: 
Get as many balls of wool back to your hideout as possible before the opposing team does!

CATATAↃ is a fast-paced, strategic team card game with exceptional replayability. 
Prove that you always land on your feet!

--Description from the publisher

Plongez dans un duel félin effréné : 
Rapportez un maximum de pelotes de laine dans votre planque avant l’équipe adverse !

CATATAↃ est un jeu de cartes en équipe, rapide et stratégique, avec une re-jouabilité exceptionnelle. 
Prouvez que vous retombez toujours sur vos pattes !

--Description par l'Éditeur

name: Caterpillars
description:
Caterpillars is a simple three dice roll-and-write game in which players have to assign points to their three caterpillars. In the end, the lowest and highest scoring caterpillar are eliminated and the median caterpillar determines the final score.

Players roll three dice, and choose which die or dice indicate the square to write the remaining dice points in. Three times during the game, a player may set aside a die roll for use in a later round.

—description from the publisher

name: Catharsis: Second Edition
description:
Catharsis: Second Edition is a revised and remastered version of the original game. The gameplay is still the same, but we have updated the game majorly with better design, new characters, bosses, roles, powers, artwork, narrative and much more. We took all the feedback our fanbase gave us and made the game vastly better.

Catharsis: Second Edition is a true solo & cooperative board game for players who are heroes trying to stop one of the many corruptions spreading through the lands. The game requires strategy, cooperation, and a touch of luck to succeed as the party fights through traps, monsters, and more. Each game is a different experience as each hero has a deck of powers they draw from, creating unique synergies every playthrough. Moreover, the players must hunt down a boss by progressing through its Boss deck, a unique deck of cards for each boss and randomized for each game. The players must carefully balance using their skills and creeping closer to death with burning through their morale and giving up in despair.

—description from the publisher

name: Cathedroll
description:
In the town of Ironcliff, the cathedral of the town rose like a beacon, spires tower over the city piercing the sky. Its walls stood strong, but the windows are bare, waiting for the artistry of the master craftsman. The King announced that every artisan in the city is ordered to create the stained glass that will be put in the windows of the cathedral. The Master that creates the most beautiful stained glass windows not only will be rewarded their weight in gold but will be also announced the master of artisans and their accomplishments will be known across the land.

Cathedroll is a roll & write game where you are tasked with creating stained glass windows that will be placed into the Cathedral of Ironcliff. Beauty of the window is not the only thing you’ll need to worry about but also the speed because other artisans will try to create their order before you.

—description from the publisher

name: Cathood
description:
"Cathood" means "the state or essence of being a cat", and that's what you're trying to achieve.

In Cathood, you are one of eight lovely cats, each with its own personality, that move around a neighborhood to meet humans, collect toys, and visit parks to establish their territory. By doing so, you earn "points" — to use the human equivalent measuring system — while working toward becoming the most beloved cat in the neighborhood.

In game terms, this design is an area-control, pick-up-and-deliver, and set-collection game in which managing the right resources is essential to success. The modular neighborhood, constantly changing, brings an innovative puzzly vibe to the decisions, tests orientation skills on a map, and encourages players to think and interact as a cat. Are they going to walk in the streets, or jump through the roofs? Stop in a cat café to exchange resources, or hiss at another player to steal from their personal supply? Learn new tricks and complete secret objectives, or be the first to visit important places and expand their influence? Since players activate a limited number of actions per turn based on the number of discs in front of them, creating the right synergy is key for a winning strategy. Are you ready? Purrrrfect!

Cathood was one of the five finalists of the "I Concurso de creación de juegos Zacatrus".

—description from the designer

name: Cational Meographic
description:
Cational Meographic is a drafting and puzzle of tile-laying game featuring the landscape of Sichuan in China.

You will embark on a hiking adventure, completing various photo missions by placing different landscape tiles and accumulating Pawints. This 21-day journey will leave you with unforgettable memories...

The game is played in 21 rounds. In each round, starting from the first player, each player takes a turn. Each turn consists of 4 steps: Scout, Take Photo, Earn Pawints and Mission Update.

—description from the publisher

name: Catopomp
description:
In Catopomp, you are the new supervisor of a team of cat psychopomps. To ensure that no lost souls are left behind, you must lead your furry subordinates to guide these souls into the afterlife.

The goal of the game is to play all your cards and not be the last player with unplayed cards. Whenever you play cards from your hand, you must also reveal one additional card and place it in front of yourself. Over time, this will form a set of revealed cards that you will need to play as well. To help you with your task, once per round, you can use one or two dice from a shared pool to enhance your playing set. Time the dice well, and use them wisely!

If you choose to pass, the player who played the most recent strongest set of cards can pass one of their revealed cards to you. This means that you will have more cards to clear. Yikes! What will you reveal? How will you manage your hidden and revealed cards? Finding the balance is key!

The game also offers a competitive mode for players who prefer to have only one winner.

NOTE:
the Kickstarter exclusive expansions include 5 executive cards(Celeste, Ego, Jigokun, Taro, and Thoth)! Each executive cat provides their supervisors with a unique power to help guide souls along. You may add them to any Catopomp game variants. At the beginning of the game, randomly distribute one executive card to each player. Each player will possess the unique power of their executive cat for the rest of the game. Alternatively, players may take turns drafting one executive card before the game starts.

name: Sick Tricks
description:
The coolest skaters have confidence and swagger, pushing their skills to the limit to land the newest, raddest trick.

Sick Tricks is a must-follow trick-taking game with four suits (numbered 1-12), with one being the trump suit. Instead of bidding on how many tricks you'll win, you bid on how many different "tricks" you'll land, tricks with conditions like "Win with an even number", "Lose with an 8 or higher", or "Win 4 tricks in a row".

When a round starts, players place cubes to predict the number of trick cards they think they'll complete. Skaters will score big for completing tricks, but lose points for biffing. Confidence is cool only if you can back it up!

—description from the publisher

name: CatStronauts: The Board Game
description:
The International Space Station has been a big success! With a green light from President Cat, the CATSUP space agency can now expand the station by adding on all the modules. It's up to the CatStronauts to move these modules to the right spot as each arrives, bringing them online one at a time...before their time runs out!

CatStronauts: The Board Game is a co-operative game in which you get to guide fearless commander Major Meowser, brave-but-hungry pilot Waffles, genius technician and inventor Blanket, and quick-thinking science officer Pom Pom on their most important mission yet. You win as a team by completing your core mission, which is to bring all of the space station's new modules online, boot up the system, and launch the re-entry pod before the power level drops to 0. As you move about the space station and assemble the modules as they arrive, you'll encounter side missions and alerts that make your core mission take extra time — but with teamwork and communication, the CatStronauts will overcome these difficulties to make it home in time for their parade. There will be really good snacks, too!

Rules variants simplify the game for younger players, make it solo-player friendly, and increase the challenge for advanced gamers.
