—description form the publisher

name: CatStronauts: The Board Game – Deluxe Edition
description:
This stellar upgrade to the CatStronauts core game includes BOTH the standard game and the Fish Finder Satellite expansion. PLUS, it upgrades your play experience with space-age transparent acrylic game pieces, and a special "How to Play" comic by CatStronauts creator Drew Bockington. All of this comes wrapped in a holographic foil slip cover, that has a fun coloring sheet on the inside!

—description from the publisher

name: Catte
description:
This is Catte, a cafe where pretty cats work.
They serve incredibly delicious coffee, so be careful not to order too much.  It's a must-follow trick-taking game where you aim to collect cards without exceeding your limit.

The Japanese listing explains further:

Gameplay

Must-follow trick-taking with three card colors (black, white, brown) and sets combining to form other colors.

Each trick awards a coffee card for points.

Exceeding a set score limit (“burst”) ends the round with no points for the bursting player.

Changes to trick rules come from special cards that can alter whether you must follow, must not follow, etc.

name: CatutO!
description:
Players manage a row of four face-down cards, secretly viewing only their edge cards at the start. Each turn, choose to either take a visible card from the discard pile or draw blindly from the deck. When drawing, decide whether to keep the new card by swapping it with one of your hidden cards, or discard it immediately.

The challenge lies in remembering which edge cards you've seen while strategically improving your hand through careful swaps. Special action cards add tactical options: peek at your own cards, steal from opponents, or force unwanted exchanges.
The round ends when a confident player shouts "MEOW!" believing they have the lowest total. All other players get one final turn before revealing cards and counting points. The player with the fewest points wins the round.
Multiple rounds determine the overall winner. Success requires balancing memory of your known edge cards, risk assessment, and timing your final call.

—description from the publisher

name: CDSK Travel
description:
Introducing a travel-friendly version of the bestselling CDSK with 860 new questions!

CDSK is a trivia game that asks you to be honest with yourselves. How well do you know this subject? Too confident? You won’t go anywhere. Too careful? You’ll be crawling. But if you answer just right… you’ll zoom off to glorious victory!

Draw a card matching the space you’re on. Then mark your place as far forward as the difficulty you set - if you get the answer right!

name: Some Assembly Required
description:
A flatpack furniture-building experience that will actually make you feel smart. Sometimes cozy, sometimes crushing (just like real-life furniture assembly).

On your turn, you'll draft colorful, interlocking furniture tiles. If you complete a furniture blueprint with these tiles, you'll place it in your home. Mind the special scoring rules!

You can probably guess: you won't be able to fit everything easily. But you can try.

—description from the publisher

name: Celestia: Big Box
publisher: BLAM !; Elznir Games; Evrikus; Geronimo Games; Popcorn Games; WoodCat
description:
Celestia, the multi-award-winning reference in push-your-luck games, comes in a Big Box including: the base game, the 2 expansions, all playable goodies, exclusive Twinples, stickers for the cards, and even a fully customizable aircraft! Ready to embark on extraordinary journeys?

—description from publisher

name: Cena
description:
In this unusual table of alliances, your real power lies not in your own cards but in what your neighbors do with them. Each player is part of two shifting alliances: one with their left neighbor, one with their right. But you don't control your partnerships directly
.. instead, your card values fuse with your neighbors' suits to form alliance plays. Working together, sabotaging quietly, and watching both sides become key to victory.

Cena is a trick-taking game with a Must Follow rule where players do not win tricks based on their own card but through alliance cards created from the rank of their left neighbor's card and the suit of their right neighbor's card. Each trick awards points based on the card collected, but some cards are poisonous and reduce the score if taken. At the end of the game, a player's final score is the sum of the points earned by their two adjacent alliances, rewarding both collaboration and strategic deflection.

name: Cereal Killer
description:
INVESTIGATION CONTINUES INTO SERIAL MURDERS
A string of unsolved crimes has left the city on edge as a cunning killer leaves victims in the shadows. Their weakness? A cereal addiction! Will the investigation team figure out their whereabouts in time to arrest them?

One player goes as the Killer, and their goal is to take six victims while secretly moving along the streets. The other player is a detective who will test their deduction skills to track the criminal, and interrogate witnesses for key information to arrest them before the week ends.

This new edition improves the rules, components, and adds a third player: Lola the dog.

name: Cereal Spiller
description:
IT’S CRUNCH TIME – Are you ready to go on a spilling spree? Stir, swap, and sabotage your way to success with Cereal Spiller from Ridley’s Games. Cutthroat scheming is required to fill your bowl and win this game. Prepare to lose some friends.

CEREAL SPILLERS HAVE A TYPE – Cereal tokens score points when they are next to other tokens of the same number or color. So, sabotage your competition to fill your Bowl with matching Cereal. But beware: your opponents can get you back!

MIX THINGS UP – Stir and Swap to wreak havoc, seek out the Magic Charm, avoid Floaters, and beware Dead Flies that can ruin your day. Made for those who love eating cereal from the box but never share.

—description from the publisher

name: Cerro Gordo Silver Mines
description:
Cerro Gordo Silver Mines, is a game based on the iconic youtube channel @ghosttownliving, and the true story of the mining town from the 1860s that extracted enough silver to build Los Angeles.

In this game, you will co-build Cerro Gordo in its heyday, with individual and shared objectives. You'll be receiving silver as you dig further into the mine, and use that silver to build the town in your vision.

Watch out as catastrophic events can set you back, and you may cross paths with other characters that have their own agendas.

Can you complete all your objectives and gain the most silver, to win the game?

—description from the publisher

name: Chai Tea Jazz
description:
It’s the annual battle of the bands in Chaipour’s number one jazz cafe! Your band is tasked with covering the greatest hits better than the rest. You've just trimmed your claws and you're ready to tickle the ivories and the brasseries and the silveries. So grab the song menu, pick just the right song at just the right time, and blow away all those cool cats!

Chai Tea Jazz is a trick-taking game where players will be fulfilling the same contracts as the other players and seeing which player did the best job at it. In this modern take on Coiffeur Jass, players bet on which mode of play and the strength of their cards, then see how they fare in the card play. It's all about knowing when to sit back and when to make your move.

—description from the publisher

name: Chai: Tea for 2
description:
As countries look for their next cuppa tea, set sail for your most delicious brews in Chai: Tea for 2! Facing off as tea merchants, both players will secure tea clipper contracts while improving their tea plantations. Producing green, white, oolong, yellow, black, and the dark pu'ers, it's a race!

As a standalone two player game in the Chai series, you'll be using dice worker placement to build your field's tableau. Navigate tea through different production steps with five unique action boards. Each round signals a new season of harvesting new teas as you specialize in matcha, bergamot, sweet teas and more.

At the start of the game, players set the end game condition to 3, 4 or 5 completed tea clipper contracts. Victory points are also gained by completing tea crates, collecting blooming teas, tableau bonuses, and each merchant's unique speciali-tea.

—description from the publisher

name: Chakravyuha
description:
Step into the ancient world of the Mahabharata with Chakravyuha, a strategy board game inspired by the legendary battle formation. This asymmetric game pits daring infiltrators against the wily orchestrator, recreating the tension and tactics of the fabled labyrinth.

Game Overview:
In Chakravyuha, players embody the roles of infiltrators striving to breach the spiral formation and a single orchestrator defending its heart. The game masterfully combines elements of strategy, bravery, and manipulation of space. Every move counts as the infiltrators navigate layers of defense, trying to create gaps and press their advantage, while the orchestrator counters with soldiers, formations, and special powers to trap the invaders.

Key Features:

Asymmetric Gameplay: One orchestrator vs. up to three infiltrators. Each side has unique abilities, objectives, and strategies.
Dynamic Spiral Formation: The board evolves with every turn as soldiers move to close gaps or intercept infiltrators.
Power-Up Cards: Both sides wield game-changing powers like health boosts, new soldiers, and surprise moves, adding layers of unpredictability and depth.
Dice-Based Actions: Strategically roll and allocate dice to attack, defend, or move. Critical decisions are key to victory.
Historical Immersion: The game's theme and mechanics are steeped in the lore of the Mahabharata, capturing the valor of Abhimanyu and the brilliance of the Chakravyuha.
How to Win:

Infiltrators: Break through the spiral, reach the center, and confront the orchestrator.
Orchestrator: Defend the formation by outlasting or incapacitating the infiltrators.
Gameplay Highlights:
Every turn is a balance of risk and reward. Will the infiltrators focus on creating gaps to advance or conserving health for a final push? Can the orchestrator predict their moves and adapt defenses? The tension rises as the game progresses, with each layer of the Chakravyuha peeling away under the players' strategic choices.

Why You'll Love It:
Chakravyuha is perfect for fans of tactical games, mythology enthusiasts, and anyone seeking an intense, immersive experience. Its rich narrative foundation and innovative mechanics ensure that no two games feel the same.

Join the Battle:
Whether you stand as the orchestrator, weaving a nearly indestructible defense, or as the infiltrators, embodying courage and cleverness, Chakravyuha promises a gaming experience like no other. Can you outwit the maze or hold its secrets till the end? The challenge awaits!

—description from the designer

name: Champions of Wind & Fire
description:
Welcome to the Champions of Wind & Fire, the world’s first dragon-building board game! Upgrade and train your dragon, gather magical elements, and compete to win the tournaments!

Walterra, the world where dragons have lived alongside humans for centuries. Here, among volcanoes, glaciers and crystal mountains, a large-scale competition is held every year. Dragons compete in 3 primary disciplines: Fire breath, Flight and Tail Wielding. This is the famous Tournament of Wind and Fire.

Champions of Wind & Fire is a dice-based dragon-training game for 1-4 players, with a playtime of 45-60 minutes. The game combines dice selection and resource management in the Dragon Training phase, followed by betting in the Tournament phase. Additionally, you can play action cards at any time to surprise your opponents. While having the strongest dragon offers advantages, players must strategically distribute its power across different tournaments (by betting their magical elements) to secure victory.

The game consists of two phases: Dragon Training and Tournaments. You will level up your dragon by collecting magical stones on the Pyramid of Elements or sending it to the training grounds. Once the Tournament phase begins, place hidden bets, use the collected magical resources to boost your dragon's power, and play action cards to surprise your opponents!

Only one dragon will become the Champion of Wind and Fire!

—description from the publisher

name: Chaos Ramen
description:
Each player becomes a chef, where they must demonstrate skill, dexterity, and speed to win. 
Throughout all the rounds, all chefs will roll their Ingredient Dice trying to complete Order Cards in their preparation area.  They can re-roll the dice as many times as necessary until completing an order. Once the dice are placed on the Order Card, they must quickly ring the Bell.

—description from the publisher

name: Chaos Rift
description:
A kingdom on the crossroads gets invaded by its greedy neighbours. On the brink of defeat, its wizards launch the final retaliation - they open a rift to the realms of chaos. Mighty demons with their servants swarm the land, turning it into waste. The invading kingdoms face an opponent they are not ready for. Regular armies are helpless against horrors of wraiths, turning people into possessed who fight against their own kind. Only elite units, heroes and battle mages dare to face the dark forces. The goal is to buy time for the archmages to prepare a spell that would close the rift. The help might come too late - if the destruction of the lands is too severe, people will abandon hope and wait defenceless for the doom.

Players - alone or in 2-player teams - take the role of chaos forces and the defending kingdoms. The chaos has the upper hand - they decide which kingdom will be invaded and with which forces. The defenders have to predict the attack directions and send their forces there. They are not completely blind - their scouts and clairvoyants can detect enemy’s movements. Chaos forces crave resources that are spread across the land - this also gives hints where they would like to strike. Some kingdoms are more vulnerable - or resistant - against some types of attacks, but the best strike is often the most obvious one. Both sides have to raise new armies - their starting forces need reinforcements as the units need rest after every battle. Both sides have also to deal with casualties that come with every war.

Chaos forces need resources taken from the lands to raise new armies and launch the attacks. As their domain gets bigger, the conquered sources of resources get depleted. Chaos armies can pillage the lands for additional resources but this comes at the cost of precious time.

This is where the game starts - chaos leaders have seven rounds of time to destroy the most vital parts of the kingdoms, so that any help from the archmages comes too late. They have to find a way to plan successful attacks deceiving the defenders. Defending players have to deduct chaos assaults and counter them. Wrong guess of direction gives an opportunity to fortify the borders against future attack. Wrong choice of the defending unit still slows the opponent down. Right unit at the right border will stop the invasion - at least once.

—description from the publisher

name: Chaosphere: Etonak Vanguard
description:
Chaosphere: Etonak Vanguard is a solo or cooperative tactical game set in the sci-fi universe of Universal Legends. You play as a crew member of the Etonak Vanguard, the elite fleet of Etonak, the last free planet within the chaotic space zone known as the Chaosphere.

A warship from the megacorporation Inferno is moving through the Chaosphere, carrying what could be a black hole–creating artifact. You’re the only unit close enough to stop it before it reaches its destination. The mission is simple: intercept and neutralize the threat, at any cost. They don’t know you’re coming. You have a head start. Use it wisely.

As you pursue the Inferno ship across three hostile Sectors, you’ll explore, fight, scavenge, and upgrade your ship in preparation for the final battle. Push forward too quickly and you may arrive underpowered. Linger too long, and you’ll be overwhelmed. Between Sectors, spaceports offer valuable opportunities: mercenaries, weapons, and technologies to trade or buy — if you’ve gathered enough resources along the way.

Chaosphere: Etonak Vanguard combines tense tactical combat with rogue-lite progression and varied bosses that each shape your journey through the Chaosphere in a different way.'

—description from the publisher

name: CHARGE
publisher: 新ボードゲーム党 (New Board Game Party)
description:
To win CHARGE, all players must use smart play and card abilities to make their way through the entire deck.

To set up, place ten cards face down on the table as coins, then deal each player a hand of four cards. Each card has a number and letter on it, and most have an ability. On a turn, either:


    Play a card to the table.
    Use a card ability.


When playing, if the table is empty, play any card; if a card is on the table, your card must have the same letter as or a number that's not greater than the card in play. Flip the card already in play face down as a coin, discarding it if ten coins are already in play.

To use an ability, place the card in front of you, discard coins equal to the number on the card, carry out the ability, then discard it. Abilities include clearing the table, discarding a card from hand, revealing a card in hand, exchanging cards with another player, and using the ability of the table card.

Refill your hand to four cards. If players play out all the cards in the deck and their hands, they win.

name: Chartres
description:
Return to 13th-century France, where a cathedral is being built in Chartres, featuring stunning stained-glass windows that continue to captivate people to this day. 
Choose the right locations and assistants to strengthen your reputation in the city, acquire horses and carts, fill barrels with the finest wine, and craft the most magnificent stained-glass windows to make your noble house the most influential in the city.

Through 3 decades (rounds)the players will choose from their hands two cards to play, one of these should activate the abilities of a previous played card that could help to decorate with amazing stained-glass windows the Cathedral, gather grapes to make wine or help to grow the population of the city, among other effects.

By gaining a better status, you could gain reputation, grow your hand limit and make that your actions through the game become more rewarding in the final scoring.

At the end of the game, the House who scored more influence wins the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Chasing Shadows
description:
Within the secret underworld of espionage, every agent lives on the knife’s edge. Will today be the day when your identity is exposed by the spotlight, or can you remain safely hidden in the shadows?

Chasing Shadows is a trick avoidance game where players draft which suit they must follow with from a dwindling pool of cards. Be sure to limit the next player's options, and you might force them to win the trick.

Taking cards and scoring points is bad, but players can cleverly plan to take specific cards that will make their previous points disappear.

The player with the lowest score after three rounds is the winner.

—description from the designer

name: Chef's Table
description:
Chef’s Table is a medium-weight, cooperative worker placement game. Players take actions in different areas of the kitchen as they prepare, plate, and improve ingredients (dice), building the perfect 4-course meal for the restaurant’s VIP guests. Kitchen space and ingredients are limited, and players need to be strategic as they manage personal and shared resources.

Players will control a unique kitchen station where they manage a custom pool of ingredients (dice), workers, and special actions. Players select a chef who will lead their station; Chef’s have own unique talents that boost performance as they visit different areas of the kitchen.

Players allocate workers throughout the kitchen, where they use personal or shared ingredients in different ways. The team earns Favor Points for each completed menu item, but will lose points for incomplete items, or ingredients that don’t meet Chef E’Lahn’s standards. Each course is more challenging than the last, requiring more ingredients, higher ingredient quality (dice value), or both.

Service and Course Challenge cards modify how the kitchen operates or  elevate the standards for one or more menu items. The difficulty imposed by challenge cards will also escalate, so be prepared! Players can also play against a course timer (Clocked-In mode), which requires even more cooperation and communication.

Think you’ve earned your promotion? Compare the team’s final score to Chef E’Lahn’s service standards: a set of scoring criteria by which your performance is evaluated. Each game, record your team’s name on Achievement Cards. Try new combinations of chefs and stations, ramp of the difficulty of the game by using challenge cards, and test your team to achieve your culinary dreams!

—description from the designer

name: Chemical Overload
description:
In Chemical Overload, the current Master Alchemist is set to retire, but has been preparing for this by training his apprentices for years. Sure, the Academy of Alchemy has been pretty brutal so far, but the end of the road is near. The final exam is going to be rough, but it’ll be worth it, if you manage to rise above your fellow students and win the title of Master Alchemist!
At the end of the final exam, you’ll be judged on the quality of your potions, which can be measured by how many Alchemy Points you’ve managed to accrue. Do this before the lab fills up with too many toxic fumes and the exam is called to a halt.

You and your fellow students will start with the same basic chemicals and flasks. You’ll be combining your chemicals with the flasks of the correct size to brew magical potions.

Each potion has its own effects and Alchemy Point values, and you’ll be able to use those potion’s effects throughout the game to help you gain more gold, alchemy points, more powerful chemicals, or even more powerful potions!

But some potions will also add to the amount of toxic fumes in the lab! There are several thresholds, that once passed, you’ll have to draw a toxin card and deal with those effects. So you’ll want to keep an eye on that track, because once the tracker hits the end of the meter, the test is over!

At the end of the final exam, the alchemist with the most Alchemy Points wins and is crowned the Master Alchemist!

Chemical Overload is a Deck Building game that has elements of tableau building as well. On your turn, you’ll have a hand of cards. Any flask cards in your hand can be played to the table and remain there until used to brew a potion. There are also potions that can be played to the table for ongoing effects.

As a bit of a twist on a classic deck building game, when a player gains new cards, such as new chemicals or a newly brewed deck potion, those cards go right on top of their draw pile. Any flasks or table potions gained can be placed immediately in the players tableau area. Players will be able to decide what unused cards in their hand they want to keep at the end of the round and which they want to discard, all with an eye on the cards they know they’ll be drawing next turn.

Chemical Overload is for 1-4 players and takes about 45-60 minutes to play.

—description from the publisher

name: Chess 2vs2: Faceoff & Surrounded
description:
This modern chess variant doubles the excitement with a supersized 16x8 board, 2v2 gameplay, and 2 distinct game modes that demand both strategy and teamwork. It's the twist that let's you collaborate and dominate.

The game comes with the 64 pieces (full set in 4 colors). The goal is still the same; checkmate the opponent team's king to win the game. It's a new kind of 4 player variant.

—description from the publisher

name: Chess Rivals
description:
The year is 1840, the Victorian era and the beginning of the industrial revolution. You’ll need to beat out your other Chess Rivals by either becoming the most famous chess prodigy, develop chess projects or become the ultimate chess master to win!

You’ll start the game by drafting your chess deck, which will be what you will play in the Chess Game to try to beat your opponent and raise your ELO score. You’ll want to balance your deck between opening, middlegame and endgame cards to ensure that you have what you need to crush your competition.

Each player will match up against their opponent to battle it out in the chess game. In each of the 5 rounds, you’ll only be able to play opening, middle or end game cards, depending on the round. When you play a card, it will move the token toward your side of the EVAL board a certain number of spaces, based on the strength of the card. The cards can also increase other factors that will affect the game, such as Checkmate, Queen Side Synergy, Center Control and more. These will give you bonuses or special powers during the game.
At the end of this tug of war, you’ll look at your EVAL score to see if you’ve managed to exceed the required number to win the game. If not, the game ends in a draw.

After each player faces off against each other in the Chess Game, you’ll move onto the Map Phase, where you will be moving around the map picking up bonuses, like adding cards to your deck, earning money, or developing projects. Each space that you move costs you $1. At the end of four rounds, you’ll need to move back to the starting space so that you can make it back to the Chess Game! Make sure you keep enough money in reserve to move yourself back to the starting space, because if you don’t, you’ll be late to the game and will not be able to play in the first round!

Play continues until someone wins by either achieving the highest fame, becoming the ultimate chess champion by raising their ELO score to the necessary level, or by completing the required amount of projects!

—description from the publisher

name: Chess-a-tete, Classic Edition
description:
Experience chess like never before with Chess-à-Tête: Classic Edition, the thrilling new version of the original game. With refined mechanics and enhanced gameplay, this edition delivers a bold twist on the timeless classic, blending deep strategy, tactical card play, and fast-paced action into a truly unique experience.

Command legendary chess pieces, each with dynamic abilities and powerful synergies. Draw your cards, build your board, and launch an epic assault on your opponent. Unleash devastating combat cards, shift momentum with tactical action cards, and outwit your rival using your pieces’ special abilities. Victory is yours if you can reduce their king to zero health, deliver a decisive Checkmate, or exhaust their deck.

With its innovative mechanics, Chess-à-Tête: Classic Edition reimagines chess for a modern audience, appealing to strategy enthusiasts and card game lovers alike. Perfect for two players, it’s dynamic, unpredictable, and endlessly replayable.

Whether you're a returning fan or new to the game, Chess-à-Tête: Classic Edition invites you to redefine the battle of wits in the ultimate evolution of the world’s most iconic game.
Are you ready to make your move?

—description from the designer

name: Chesscode
description:
In Chesscode, the player takes control of six secret agents during the Cold War, each with a distinct chess-inspired movement. The game consists of two standalone but thematically connected chapters, each offering a different type of solo logic puzzle.

Chapter I – Shadows on the Wall
Each agent can be activated three times. On each turn, the player selects one agent, moves it on a 6×6 map, collects Intel Points by landing on icons, and attempts to reach and close the matching Safehouse.
Each Safehouse requires a specific amount of Intel to be secured, and over-collecting results in time penalties.
Empty spaces may trigger random events. The player has exactly 24 turns (hours) to close all six Safehouses and return to the Operation Base.
Each closed Safehouse grants a one-time special ability.

Chapter II – The Right Code Is the Way Out
The goal is to complete eight logical statements on a Code Sheet, using numbers, logic symbols, and letters collected by moving agents around the map.
Each agent has two uses, and a limited set of symbols and letters.
The logic statements must reference values from other columns and must be immediately verifiable when completed.
Enemy patrols appear each turn, progressively reducing safe movement options.
Planning, deduction, and precise use of agent abilities are key to completing the code and escaping East Berlin.

Both chapters use a minimal set of materials (one printed sheet, one six-sided die, and a pencil), and can be played in under 20 minutes.

—description from the designer

name: Chicago '68
description:
Chicago '68 pits revolutionary spectacle against civil order at the Democratic National Convention riots of 1968. Players take the role of either the Establishment or the Demonstrators in this fast-paced game of street battles and political maneuvers. Each side plays from two asymmetric decks of action cards. The Establishment positions tactical forces and police platoons to co-ordinate mass arrests while working the convention floor. The Demonstrators, on the other hand, can pivot from direct clashes to radical street theater; their tactics can be reactive and unpredictable, allowing for wild cat-and-mouse chases and mischief-making across the tear-gassed avenues of groovy downtown Chicago.

In more detail, the game is played over five rounds, with two rounds representing a single day (daytime and nighttime). Each side takes turns playing cards from two decks of action cards. The first deck represents the leadership committees. For the Establishment, this is the Mayor's office, and for the Demonstrators, this is the Yippies. These decks are primarily focused on building/activating card splays and manipulating the board state. The Mayor faction can access the policy tableau with the mandate action, which include activating undercover agents, authorizing tear gas, redeploying the National Guard, and more.

Then both sides alternate playing action cards from their rank-and-file decks: The National Mobilization Committee to End the War in Vietnam (MOBE) on one side, and the Chicago Police Department on the other. These actions are largely moving and confronting units on the map and claiming strategic positions. The Demonstrators may build and activate their street theater splay, which is a set of location specific one-time "mini-objectives" with unique, combinatorial powers.

At the end of every round, a delegate commits a vote to either side. Demonstrators grow in number, the mayor is allocated funds, and whoever controls a majority of critical city areas is awarded exposure points.

Chicago '68 supports 1-4 players in solo, competitive, co-operative, and team play modes. Game duration is 45 minutes per player, with the typical two player duel lasting 60-90 mins.

name: Chicago Dry
description:
For years, Prohibition has poured Americans a tall glass of austerity and condemned the whole country to a life of secret transgressions. In Chicago Dry, players look for a way around Prohibition to bring bottled fun to Chicago's hidden pubs and speakeasies.

In this game, 2-4 players secretly distribute alcohol across city districts as they face off against rivals and fight for territory, achieving higher scores as they occupy the Chicago central area. The player with the most influence points in both phases of the game wins and becomes the most infamous gangster in town!

name: Chicago Grand Slam
description:
Chicago Grand Slam ups the ante of the classic Chicago card game with the elegance of a unique game board and ruleset, loaded with more strategic depth and replayability.

Play your cards at the just the right moment and try to make the best poker hand, all while attempting to be the first player to obtain their Chicago Marker and get both of your pawns across the goal. But watch out, you may end up moving backwards!

name: Chichén Itzá
description:
As the sun sets on the great Mayan empire, in the heart of Chichen Itza beneath the great pyramids and temples, ancient seals that once bound mythical creatures have been broken. The gods and beasts of legend — serpents of the sky, jaguar spirits of the underworld, and other beasts of lore — emerge from the forgotten realms to reclaim the world of mortals. Their siege is relentless, their power immense, as they descend upon the sacred city to consume its glory, but the people of Chichen Itza will not fall without a fight.

In Chichén Itzá, you must command your forces, harness the favor of the gods, and fight the relentless tides of mythical beasts. The game lasts six rounds, with each player taking four actions during each round. During set-up, place 16 (of 21) action tiles in a 4x4 grid, then randomly place four cost markers along the top and side of the grid. If you're the first player to take an action in the round, you pay an amount equal to the lower of the cost markers to the top and side of the tile you choose; anyone who takes this action later in the round pays the higher of the markers. You can choose an action only once per round.

With these actions, you move troops, acquire god cards, upgrade your four combat gears, fight legendary creatures, and reclaim the villages, temples, camps and ruins that have been taken over. At the end of each round, you see whether you've completed particular achievements, and your score is based on creatures defeated, areas controlled, achievements met, heroes present, endgame god cards and crystals collected, and more.

name: Chikki
description:
Chikki is a competitive ladder-climbing game using dominoes for 2 players. The objective is to play all of your tiles first.

In Chikki, players can match, or play higher ranked combos to shed tiles. The combos can suddenly escalate to higher combination types when a six suited meld is played. Also, players will have to draw tiles during the play and struggle to keep the lead.

—description from the designer

name: Stonk Market
description:
Everyone knows that line goes up. Will you be left with the most valuable stocks after a chaotic day of exchanges? Stonk Market is a real-time trading game where you YOLO into company stocks like Blammo or Chatterfly. At the same time, watch out for the ever-shifting Stonk Exchange, which will dictate the stock that’s worth negative points at the end!

Will the Glitch & Co stock take you to the moon or will you FOMO into a negative company? This game for wrinkly brains only!

—description from the publisher

name: Children of the Colossi
description:
One day, the world changed forever. Civilization collapsed, and now all that remains rests on the backs of the Colossi — gigantic creatures roaming in our post-apocalyptic wastelands. Their magnificent cities are the only place where water flows and trees grow. Their stately buildings, filled with knowledge and treasures, refuse to welcome us, so we roam our wastelands, hunting for a future. We are children of the Colossi.

Children of the Colossi is a Euro-style, dudes-on-a-map game in which players are tribes competing to harvest the eggs and tame the newborn of the Colossi so that they might grow a new home and rise above the ashes.

During the game, players hang-glide between the dynamic map and the modular Colossi boards, racing to collect precious eggs, hatch newborns, and outmaneuver their rivals. Your units are your most vital resource as every placement and movement matters. Send your envoys up into the cities to gain benefits and influence for your tribe, or glide them down into the wastes below to compete for eggs that the Colossi lay on their wanderings. As the map fills with eggs, the tension rises. Newborns hatch, and players clash in clever contests of positioning and card play with no destruction and no direct attacks — only smart, tactical maneuvers to claim victory.

Each of the five Colossi and their cities offer a unique chain of powerful actions and unlock unique banner cards to fuel your strategy, with only three Colossi appearing in each game.

—description from the publisher

name: Children of the Sun
description:
In the two-player strategy game, Children of the Sun, players take control of the mighty dragon children of Ino'itl, the Sun god. The two were sent to Earth in order to create a beautiful landscape as an ode of love to Xochanama, the Moon goddess forever fated to be out of Ino'itl's reach.

During the game, players must summon forth the elements in order to craft their magnificent landscapes. On each turn, players will draw and place an Elemental Token onto a 6x6 game board, flanking opponent pieces and flipping them over. For every opponent token flanked, along with the token placed, the player gains corresponding Elemental Resources. Earth, Water, Life, Void, and Spirit.

Resources are used to craft Creation Cards, which represent the fantastic landscape being formed by the players. Creation Cards come in five different types:

- Terra Cards grant points to the player who creates the most expansive landscape.
- Aqua Cards score based on the difference in value from one card to the next.
- Species Cards score higher the more diverse a player’s ecosystem becomes.
- Source Cards generate extra resources and score for each corresponding Creation Card made.
- Wonder Cards award points for each token flipped to the player’s side at the end of the game.

Players must also balance the interconnected ecosystem between their cards. Enough Terra must be generated to support Aquatic creations, or else they are discarded at the end of the game. Aqua is needed to keep Species alive, with each type requiring different amounts of water. If a Habitat icon on a Species card matches one shown on a Terra card, players gain valuable bonus points.

Along the way, players can acquire and use Dragon Powers to gain a one up on their opponent. These abilities include actions like creating additional cards on your turn, flipping tokens on the board, increasing your hand size, and even discarding an opponent's Creation Card. And once per game, each player may summon the aid of the Sun god and Moon goddess to recharge their powers or redraw a new hand of Creation Cards.

The winner of Children of the Sun is the player who crafts the most captivating landscape, pleasing the Moon goddess and securing favor from the Sun god!

name: Chilena: Fútbol Card Game
publisher: Born Classic Card Game Design LLC
description:
Chilena is a fast-paced soccer-themed card game that captures the drama, chaos, and glory of the beautiful game — all in under 5 minutes. Inspired by the iconic bicycle kick (or “chilena”) and the untamed spirit of grassroots fútbol, the game blends tactical play with footballing flair. Ideal for cafés, pubs, locker rooms, or under folding tables at family barbecues.

Players take turns attacking and defending using their own 30-card decks—one "Home" and one "Away." Attackers build up combinations with Pass and Dribble cards to unlock Shots or even the fabled Chilena itself. Defenders counter with Tackles, Saves, or controversial Offsides. If a player can’t make a move, they must substitute — refreshing their hand while ceding momentum. Scoring a goal flips a card face-down to keep score. Matches can end in regulation, go to Extra Time, or even culminate in a Penalty Shootout using the decks themselves.

The objective is simple: score more goals than your opponent by the final whistle. But how you score — and how you stop your rival — requires cunning, risk-taking, and a touch of theatricality. Whether you win by tiki-taka precision or win ugly with a last-minute Rebound, Chilena rewards improvisation and boldness — just like the real thing.

name: Chimp's Swag Swap
description:
Playing for ingenious little chimps, you can steal anything that's lying around: rubber ducks, hair rollers, and even a lobster necklace! But can you sell off your entire catch on the best terms and make a fortune from it before demand fades away?

In this dynamic trick-taking game, you will outsmart opponents to grab goods, trade them shrewdly during special sessions, and pile up your banana riches.

Players take on the roles of chimpanzees who gather all sorts of clutter and try to sell it for the highest value, aiming to earn the most amount of bananas by the end of the game. The goal is to collect sets of cards, attempting to sell them at the right time. The later in the round a player sells their sets, the more bananas they will receive, but be careful: there is a higher risk that someone may not be able to play a card according to the rules in the trick, and the round will end prematurely.

After each trick, the player who won the trick starts the card draft, but the last player applies special properties of cards and influences the suit prices in the market.

Sell quickly and become the ultimate CHIMP-ion!

—description from the publisher

name: China's War 1937-1941
description:
July 7, 1937: a nighttime skirmish at the Marco Polo Bridge near Beijing erupts into an invasion and occupation of China by the Imperial Japanese Army that would not end until 1945. Western sources call it the “Second Sino-Japanese War”; in China, it is the “War of Resistance”; and in Japan, it is blandly referred to as “the China Incident.”

China’s War: 1937-1941 examines the first five years of the conflict, when China stood alone against the Japanese Empire. Each player takes the role of a Faction seeking to attack or defend the Republic of China: the aggressive Japanese, the harried Government (represented by the Nationalist party), the rebellious Chinese Communist Party, or the unruly, fractious Warlords who are obedient when convenient but have their eye on gaining state power.

Using military, political, and economic actions and exploiting various events, players build and maneuver forces to influence or control the population, extract resources, or otherwise achieve their Faction’s aims. A deck of cards regulates turn order, events, victory checks, and other processes. The rules can run non-player Factions, enabling solitaire, 2-player, or multi-player games.

—description from the publisher

Volume XIII of the COIN Series.

name: Chit Chat
description:
Chit Chat is an incredibly fun communication game where talking and guessing take centre stage. You’ll receive quirky questions, and the answer is always a number. Your task: Arrange the answers in the correct order – from smallest to largest. Can you achieve the perfect score as a team, or will you be left scratching your heads at the end?

1. Place a card with any number in the center and then randomly draw 8 question cards, stacking them in front of you.
2. For each question, consider whether the answer is higher or lower than the number in the center, and sort the questions accordingly.
3. At the end, turn over all the question cards and check the answers. What’s your high score?

A simple game for the whole family and all your friends.

name: Chivalry is Dead: Race for the Crown
description:
Chivalry is Dead: Race for the Crown is a Fantasy Chariot Racing Game where the goal is to claim the crown!

Select from one of four unique teams, customize your chariots, and strive to be the first to enter the winners' circle by playing a 1 or 2 lap race. Whether you employ cunning tactics, set clever traps, or launch direct assaults on your adversaries, ensure your triumph in this exhilarating contest where every move counts. Chariots will be destroyed, and debris will be left on the field.

Each player builds a chariot team of 2-3 chariots using one of four unique teams: Humans, Goblins, Dwarves or Kobolds. Each Team has their own stats and abilities. Add an additional 3 teams with the expansion. Customize the track using Terrain Markers around the map. Build your chariot faster, tougher or more defensive. Race, attack other chariots, throw traps or simply outmaneuver your opponents to win the race.

—description from the publisher

name: Chonker Party: Team Play
description:
Chonker Team is a rowdy, team-based version of Chonker Party where cooperation meets chaos. Designed for 4 or 6 players (but can be played individually), this standalone game pits teams of Chonks against each other in a strategic snack-off filled with betrayal, bluffing, and big plays.

Team Up, Snack Hard:
Form teams and work together to win rounds and score points—but be careful, your partner’s wild plays might just backfire on you.

Disrupt the Enemy:
Play Action Cards to mess with your opponents—or even your own teammate. Force discards, steal plays, or flip the round in your favor.

Snack to Victory:
The team with the most points when the deck runs out wins the game. Just don’t lose track of your strategy (or your partner’s).

Each deck features cute art, hilarious combos, and all the unpredictable fun, now with double the drama.

—description from the designer

name: Chroma Arcana
description:
Chroma Arcana is a tactical card game set in a fantasy world. Players take on the roles of powerful mages, using their knowledge of the arcane arts to outmanoeuvre and defeat their opponents. Each mage has access to a unique combination of Spells based on their chosen colours of magic, allowing for a diverse range of gameplay options and strategies. The goal of the game is to reduce your rival's health to zero. On your turn, you can place spell cards into your spellbook. Then, you can discard cards of a matching colour to charge those spells up. Once a spell is charged up, it must be cast!

Spells can be instant-effect Bursts, Minions that provide a benefit for a handful of turns, powerful Edicts that last a single turn, or trap-like Wards that remain until their trigger condition is met.

There are also item cards that you play straight from your hand, such as Potions that counter rival spells and Arcanas that super-charge your own.

At the end of setup, you will have selected an Ego (your character identity), a Major Colour (along with a powerful Sigil and a well-practiced Rote), and two Minor Colours. This should be all you need to battle it out!

—description from designer

name: Chronicles of Civilization
description:
Chronicles of Civilization is a complex civilization game in a simple PnP format. The primary goal was to capture the feel of a digital civilization game in a board game format – and in practice, it resembles a blend of 'Hadrian’s Wall' or 'Knight' with a computer civilization game.

Players stand at the head of our civilization and develop various domains: food production, mining, navigation, religion, science, diplomacy, finances, and production. A large portion of the game takes place on a map where you move settlers to build settlements, farms, mines, and ports, all of which must be connected by a network of roads to your capital. It is crucial to acquire resources for expansion; for instance, you send workers to fell trees or extract raw materials. These elements are intricately interwoven by a dense web of dependencies. Additionally, you must constantly manage the population's happiness and military development.

The gameplay is driven by a chronicle card that serves as the scenario (and, like the map, is interchangeable, ensuring enormous replayability). In each session, there are various conditions for victory and defeat.

—description from the designer

name: Chronicles of Paldon
description:
Backstory

In the once-prosperous city of Paldon, a catastrophic, time-altering experiment shattered its advanced machinery and erased invaluable knowledge. Since then, the city has been divided into factions, debating the risks and benefits of restoring the technology while competing for influence.

The inventors are key players in the city's reconstruction, creating machines that bring life back to its core. While certain knowledge is forbidden, they continue their work, sometimes using rare substances like phlogiston. They sell their inventions on the black market and they don’t align with just one faction but collaborate with several to secure their own success and make their names known.

About the game

In Chronicles of Paldon, each player acts as an inventor with their own workshop located in the city of Paldon. The task is to rebuild the city’s machinery, which has malfunctioned due to the catastrophe. The machinery consists of a few major City Constructions and a large number of small machines.

To complete the task, players must carefully plan how to use their turns and apprentices to gather the necessary resources and skills, as well as how to best utilize the machines they have built. Machines can be sold for money or used to upgrade the workshop, but they can also be provided to factions in exchange for renown, with the amount of renown depending on the faction's influence. It's crucial to keep an eye on what the other players are doing, as their actions can directly impact each player´s strategy and success.

Renown points can be received in different ways, but mainly when building City Constructions and for the faction support (providing of machines) made during the game. The winner is the player with the most renown points at game end.

In the solo and co-operation mode, set before the catastrophic event, the player’s task is to destroy the machine responsible for the catastrophe before it ruins the city’s machinery.

—description from the designer

name: Chronicles of the Stellar Drive Empire: Voidpilot's Legacy
description:
Chronicles of the Stellar Drive Empire: Voidpilot's Legacy is a solitaire science fiction tabletop game where players command their ship and lead their crew through dangerous missions and exciting combat to earn their legacy!

Voidpilot's Legacy is a resource management and engine building tabletop game using cards, dice, and markers.  Players win by surviving 8 runs through their included Event deck, after which they tally up their Legacy Points to determine how they did.  The game includes optional scenario-based play to expand ways to enjoy and win the game.

Throughout the game, players participate in various Events, including exciting combat with adversaries that scale in difficulty as the game progresses, salvage and mining missions to collect resources to spend on ship upgrades to become more powerful, and visit colonies to earn credits and refuel.  Players can also choose to upgrade these events, increasing later difficulty and potential rewards.

Using a thematic Heroism mechanic, the player can choose to take ship damage or sacrifice crew members at critical moments to increase their chances of success during their missions!  Balancing hull, crew, and risk is critical to winning the game. Players lose the game when their ship is destroyed, they lose all of their crew members, or they run out of fuel.

—description from the publisher

name: Chrono Core Trading Card Game
description:
Chrono Core Trading Card Game is a mech based trading card game where you’ll be building your deck with equipment, weapons, configurations (attachments), and support cards to aid you against your opponent in the arena

Starting from a unique deck building process where your equipment cards chassis type must match the same designation as your Pilot and Core cards. Once your deck is ready, you’ll place your Pilot, Core, starting equipment and weapon cards into play. You’ll then go back and forth with your opponent battling it out and destroying each other’s shields to reach one another's vulnerable pilots and reduce their life to 0 and claim victory.

—description from the publisher

name: Chucky: The Game
description:
HI, I’M CHUCKY. WANNA PLAY?: The killer doll from your nightmares is back, and he’s out for blood!

GET HIM BEFORE HE GETS YOU: Use your weapons to try to attack and kill Chucky before his soul takes over your body

THINK YOU CAN TRUST YOUR FRIENDS AND FAMILY?: Fear will be at an all-time high as you win as a team or lose as a team

PLAY IT SAFE OR RISK IT ALL?: Find a hiding spot or take your chances provoking Chucky — you never know when he'll attack next!

FROM CULT CLASSIC TO COLLECTIBLE CARNAGE: This is the perfect game for horror fans of all ages

—description from the publisher

name: Chutney
description: Chutney is a climbing-shedding card game for three players using a standard deck of cards. In each Deal, one player bids to be the Dipper and plays alone against the Moochers, the other two players in a temporary partnership. The Dipper’s aim is to be the first player to have no cards left. The Moocher’s aim is to stop the Dipper from playing all of their cards first.

name: Chuồn Chuồn
description:
Chuồn Chuồn (pronounced “choon choon”, meaning dragonfly) draws inspiration from Vietnam’s traditional balancing dragonfly toys, transforming them from decorative pieces into a playful light strategy game. Suitable for all ages, it offers endless replayability, magical twists, and a charming reflection of dragonflies in nature.

Handcrafted Components With Vietnamese Cultural Charm.
Our dragonflies are made of bamboo, an eco-friendly and durable material that’s a well-known symbol for the Vietnamese spirit.

Easy to Learn, Challenging to Master!

Your goal is to catch and arrange dragonflies on your bamboo trees to match the patterns on your objective cards. Once completed, you earn flower points, that will be counted at the end of the game. On your turn, you have the choice to pick one big dragonfly or 2 small dragonflies, or new objective cards, or new magic cards. Magic cards allow you to remove or rearrange your dragonflies like sunshine forcing all dragonflies move up 1 level, or thunderstorm knock them off the table. You win by earning as many points as possibles!

The game has Three Play Modes

     Competitive: 2-4 players
     Cooperative: 2-8 players
     Solo mode for 1 player


—description from the publisher

name: Cicero
description:
The Roman Republic is at its height. The great patrician families compete for power through political intrigue, influence in the Senate, underhanded dealings, henchmen, and all kinds of more or less official business deals. Any maneuver is possible in this relentless quest for power and prestige.

You are the head of one of these families. You intervene in all the city's power centers, with its castes, its guilds, and the people. You thwart your adversaries' schemes, but as if that weren't enough, you must also put on a brave face and help Cicero in his ongoing fight against corruption and conspiracies. It is then that the Roman generals of the Triumvirate, at the head of their legions, remind you of their good memories by pointing the finger at Rome's enemies...

name: Cinderella at Midnight
description:
In Cinderella at Midnight, draw and lay cards to create a maze Cinderella must explore to complete her tasks. Start in the garden to befriend mice, find lizards, and pick a pumpkin — but beware of too many interrupting bells! Return to the fairy Godmother and transform the maze by flipping the cards to reveal the pumpkin carriage and the palace, where new tasks await: find a key, meet the prince, and drop a slipper. With each stroke of the clock, the maze shifts — can Cinderella evade her stepfamily and reach home before midnight?

Game Features:

     Solo gameplay with dynamic choices, blending strategy and luck as you place cards and choose your path.
     A shifting maze that changes with every game, ensuring endless variety and replayability.
     Double-sided, hand-illustrated cards filled with details that bring Cinderella’s world to life.


—description from the publisher

name: Circadians: Prima Alba “Big Box”
description:
This is the Italian Version of Circadians: First Light, it is a Big Box with Expansion and bonus from Chur Games and Tesla Games. (Italian description below)

The aim of Circadians: First Light is to lead a team of researchers on the planet of Ryh. Players need to manage their crew (dice) to visit various parts of the planet for trade, farming, construction and research. Players score points for negotiating with the locals, harvesting resources for the depository, upgrading their research base, exploring the planet, and collecting gems. The game is played over eight rounds. At the end of the final round, the player with the most points wins.

L’Ambientazione

Eravamo ad anni luce dalla nostra casa, distanti galassie, quando per la prima volta abbiamo scoperto questo corpo celeste. Un pianeta pieno di forme di vita affascinanti e intelligenti, non troppo diverse da noi. Alcune hanno costruito regni al di sotto della superficie di mari verdeggianti, mentre altre controllano pianure desertiche e altipiani. Tra di loro abbiamo trovato scienziati, inventori, contadini, commercianti e combattenti.

Benché la nostra presenza abbia preoccupato alcuni, abbiamo avuto pochi inconvenienti con gli abitanti del posto. Comunque, noi Circadiani, rinomati esploratori Terrestri, dobbiamo fare il possibile per assicurare la pace. Dobbiamo rispettare questo pianeta e i suoi abitanti.

I capitani della Moontide ci hanno inviato ordini dall’alto. Apriamo le negoziazioni con i tre clan, con la speranza di ottenere il loro favore e la nostra sicurezza mentre siamo su questo pianeta. Dobbiamo anche raccogliere degli esemplari organici per il nostro magazzino sulla Moontide. Questo è un territorio nuovo per tutti ma dobbiamo essere coraggiosi e intraprendenti. Il futuro dei Circadiani dipende da questo.

Il Gioco

Lo scopo di Circadians: Prima Alba è di guidare una squadra di ricercatori sul pianeta Ryh scoperto di recente. I giocatori devono gestire il proprio equipaggio (i dadi) visitando i vari posti sul pianeta per commerciare, coltivare, costruire e fare ricerca. Il giocatore che accumula più punti al termine dei 7 round è il vincitore.

La big Box contiene:
- Circadians: First Light 2nd Edition
- Circadians: FIrst Light – Allies Expansion
- Circadians: FIrst Light – Specialists Expansions
- 2 Nuovi Leader Inediti “CHUR”

—description from designer

name: Circle the Wagons: Essential Collection
description:
Each player in Circle the Wagons is fixin' to build up their own boomtown, but only one'll build the best in the West!

Circle the Wagons is a map-building game. Blaze a trail by draftin' cards 'round the circle and placin' 'em in yer town, tryin' to connect matchin' territories to score prosperity points! But don't forget about them three bonus cards in the center of the circle that can score ya even more points — that is, if ya play yer cards right.

With over 800 unique ways to score and millions of draftin' and placin' combos, you'll never build the same town twice!

name: Circle the Wagons: Second Shot
description:
Think you've seen it all out here on the prairie? Think again, partner! There's always a new adventure just over that next hill.  Best keep your wits about you—anything can happen out here!

Circle the Wagons: Second Shot is a brand new set of 18 cards that can either be played standalone or combined with the base Circle the Wagons game. In this 2-player drafting game, players take turns picking cards from the circle and adding them to their scoring tableau. The twist? Any card in the circle you skip over goes directly to your opponent. Arrange your cards to create scoring blocks and fulfill the three shared scoring goals if you wanna be the best in the West!

Second Shot also introduces Newfangled Mode. In this variant, all 36 cards are shuffled together and then split back into two unique 18-card sets. Players play through the first set, scoring only the shared goals, then continue their game using the second set and the regular block-scoring rules. It’s winner-take-all in this ultimate showdown!

Second Shot can be played as a standalone game or combined with the base Circle the Wagons game to create an all-new set of 18 cards.

As in the original game, 3 cards are dealt to the center with their scoring conditions showing. The remaining cards are placed in a circle around them with their grid of 4 territories showing. A starting card is chosen from the territories, determining where players begin their draft.

On a player’s turn, they draft one territory card. The opposing player then takes every territory card between the starting card and the chosen card. Both players add their cards to their tableau.

Players must keep the cards in the same vertical orientation (though they can rotate them to have the opposite short edge up). Cards must be placed so that they align with a previously-placed card (if any) along at least one edge. Cards may partially or completely overlap each other, though a newly-gained card cannot be placed underneath another card.

Players alternate turns, using the most-recently taken card’s spot in the circle as the new starting point, until all territory cards have been taken and placed.

Both players then tally their score. Points are gained for having large connected blocks of each territory type, as well as for meeting each of the shared scoring conditions. The player with the highest score wins.

In Second Shot’s Newfangled Mode, players instead use the full 36 cards from Second Shot as well as the base game, shuffling them together and splitting them into 2 18-card decks. Setup and gameplay follows as normal using one deck, then the other. After the first deck is exhausted, players calculate only their score from the scoring conditions. Those cards are cleared away and the second deck is played as normal. At the end of the second deck, the players score both the second set of scoring conditions and their largest blocks. Adding all of their scores together, the players determine the grand winner!

name: Cities of Venus: Lost Contact
description:
Cities of Venus: Lost Contact is a medium weight, scifi Euro, based in the year 2222. Various countries on Earth have set up colonies in cities that float in the clouds. Each player represents the governor of a floating city and must compete with other players to maximize the growth of their city by growing their population and strategically deploying it across the various departments to keep their city running. To help the cities, Earth has been sending immigrants and city upgrades in the form of Drops. At some point, a catastrophe occurs on Earth, cutting off communication with Venus. No one knows when the last Drop from Earth will come.

Each round, players move through several phases: Resolve events, erode shields, grow and deploy population, mine for resources and modify the city, and grab a drop to improve the city.

A player can gain victory points in the following ways: 
Points on station upgrades
Points for a certain amount of mined resources
Points for city population
Bonus points for the most populous, the richest, and most upgraded cities

Some time in the third phase of the drops, a card (randomly shuffled into the card deck) will turn up with the Earth on it. This card signifies that this is the last drop that will arrive from Earth and triggers the end of the game.

The player with the most victory points at that point wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Cities of Venus: Survivors
description:
Set during the time of Cities of Venus, Survivors continues the story with the search for survivors on the surface by the brave mining mech operators.

The object of this stand-alone polyomino-dice manipulation game is to find as many survivors as possible while discovering fuel for the re-ascent vehicle. Once the launch sequence is initiated, players utilize the resources and engineers that they had rescued to secure their place as the captain, and hero, of the re-ascent ship.

The winner is the player who has the best dice combination at the end of the Launch Sequence.

—description from the publisher

name: Things on Strings
description:
You'll cooperatively use logic to compare, contrast, and categorize Things—just like in the first game (Things in Rings). But, instead of a Venn Diagram, the player playing as the Knower comes up with the rules of a cascading flowchart.

As more and more Things get added, groups split with new rules.

While the flowchart grows, you'll surprise yourself with how well you can follow the logic (or, laugh at yourselves at how lost you truly are).

—description from the publisher

name: City Flip: Roma
description:
In City Flip: Roma, all roads lead to Rome...and to St. Peter's Basilica, the Roman Forum, and so on!

In the game, you work together as city planners. Your job is to lay out the cards in a 7x7 grid so that the ten sights are all connected by their streets. When it's your turn, swap the face-up card in your hand for a face-down card, which then becomes the next swap card.

In addition to the direction specifications are various building specifications for individual columns and rows, which vary from game to game. This allows you to rebuild Rome again and again and make the game increasingly difficult.

name: City of Demons
description:
Your tribe's survival hinges on accessing hidden knowledge deep within a ruined city's tech center. As the bravest runner, you must sprint to the city's core, collecting beacons, information, and junk with which to craft bizarre gear. Endure scalding pockets of radiation and evade the lurking creatures known as Demons that grow deadlier near the city's center. Beat rival runners to reach the core and secure your tribe's future.

A fast-paced, 2 player, push-your-luck dice game. With solo mode.
Race to collect beacons, info, and junk to craft bizarre gear and discover the core before your rival runner.

—description from the designer

name: City Tour
description:
City Tour is a cooperative route-building game for 1–4 players set in the ever-changing streets of Paper City. Working as a team of bus drivers, players must transport colorful passengers to their matching tourist attractions over a series of 12 increasingly challenging “days,” divided into four levels.

On each turn, a player draws two Route tiles, places one in front of the bus, and moves the bus forward. As the bus travels, it picks up passengers and drops them off automatically when passing their matching attractions. To succeed, enough passengers must be delivered to meet each attraction’s requirement before the bus exits the city. Later levels introduce new obstacles and special rules—such as ticket inspections, restricted routes, and specific drop-off conditions—that add complexity to the puzzle.

Players win a day by fulfilling all objectives on the corresponding Day card. Complete all 12 days to prove your team has mastered the City Tour.

—description from the publisher

name: CLANS
description:
CLANS is a family card game, at the start of each round, 4 rows of Reward cards are laid out on the table. Players simultaneously and secretly place 4 of their 5 Animal cards face down, one for each row.

During their turn, each player tries to remove their opponents' cards by guessing their value.

Once all the Animal cards have been revealed, the rewards obtained are assigned to each player.

The game continues until a player gets three Reward cards of the same type or accumulates 8 Exploration tokens (8 VP), thus becoming the winner of CLANS.

—description from the publisher

name: Clans of Caledonia & Industria
description:
The critically acclaimed Clans of Caledonia base game and Clans of Caledonia: Industria expansion combined together in one big box.

Lidded inserts organize every single component of the base game + expansion, and the custom cotton bag, too! The removable inserts make set up and tear down a breeze, making it easier than ever to get this beloved game on the table.

Dive into the rich world of Clans of Caledonia with the complete game all-in-one. This big box includes the Clans of Caledonia base game plus its first expansion Industria. With new mechanics, solo Automa rules, and engaging challenges, the expansion deepens the strategic experience of the original game and invites players to explore industrial progress in 19th-century Scotland.

Big Box

Clans of Caledonia (base game) and the Clans of Caledonia: Industria expansion comes with a single big box with a custom plastic insert that fits in all components of the base game and of the expansion.

The dimension of this game box is the same as the expansion box (311 x 224 x 118 mm) but it comes with about 5 mm of lid lift. After removing the empty punchboards, the lid closes completely.

name: Clash of Minds: Holmes vs Moriarty
description:
Clash of Minds: Holmes vs Moriarty is a two-player card game in which players take on the roles of the famous detective Sherlock Holmes and his greatest rival, professor James Moriarty. Two powerful minds trying to figure out the intentions of their adversary every step of the way. They only have 12 hours to solve or commit the crime of the century.

The crime plan plotted by Moriarty is divided into 3 threads: Tool, Type and Victim of the crime. Using the Influence cards and the unique abilities of their Agents, players try to reveal or keep secret the individual threads of the crime.

Each round of the game is a different, characteristic location on the map of London. Each of these places changes the rules or introduces some restrictions. Thanks to this, each game is different and the multitude of strategies and ways to gain an advantage gives you a lot of room for maneuver and makes each game unique.

If the clock on the clocktower strikes twelve and one of the threads is still uncovered, Holmes is defeated and Moriarty triumphs by committing the crime of the century.

—description from the publisher

name: Clash: D-Day – Special Edition
description:
Clash - D-Day - Special edition is a turn-based board game that is set during the longest day in history: D-Day. Take control over the Allies and Axis forces and get ready to conquer the necessary beaches and areas. Outwit your enemy, make tactical decisions and think ahead. Prepare and take action in the greatest seaborne invasion that changed history on June the 6th, 1944!

Clash - D-Day is very easy to learn and there is no need for historical knowledge.  Clash - D-Day is based on the popular board game Clash of the Ardennes and is a stand alone version of the game.

Use all of your (special) units wisely, because you will run out of units very quickly. Place them strategically and tactically on 1 of the 7 streets, always think ahead and try to reach your objective a little bit sooner than your opponent.

—description from the designer

name: Classified Information
description:
In the pursuit of political supremacy, knowledge is key. Since the revolution, two factions have been fighting for power in the dystopian, cyberpunk city of Intellexia. In order to break the years long deadlock and secure control of the city, each faction must uncover their adversary’s secret plans hidden inside their top secret, code-protected briefcase.

Your job, if you are to accept it, is to protect your secret code by cleverly deploying card abilities, by seeking help from the Guards, Assassins, and Sentinels at the local tech-noir guilds, and by encrypting information when you can. But espionage is a two-way street. While trying to deny your opponent information about your secret code, you must try to crack theirs.

Classified Information is a fast-playing (10-minutes or less), 2-player "iterative" deduction microgame that is fully contained within just 18 cards. Each turn a player plays a card from their hand in one of three ways (for its ability, for its guild affiliation or by discarding it out of the game). Once the draw deck is depleted players reveal their secret code and the single card left in their hand, if their card matches a number in their opponent's code they may win the game, but things may not be so easy if their opponent also matches and has more guards, or has cleverly guarded their briefcase!

Will you be able to access your opponent’s Classified Information?

-description from designer

name: Cleaning Service
description:
Cleaning Service is a thrilling solo boardgame that blends the strategic depth of RogueLite with the challenge of Memory & Write. Step into the shoes of a crime scene cleaner, where your mission is to leave no trace behind. Clear each crime scene carefully while dodging security cameras, avoiding the police, and using your wits to stay ahead. Each new Run will test your memory, but if you score high enough, you’ll unlock powerful tools to make your job easier. Sharpen your mind and prove you’re the best in the business!

Objective the game: Clear each of the crime scenes until you reach the final map before you run out of attempts.

How to Play: The player must memorise the first map. You can take as much time as you need. The player must remember where the maps are  the spots blood and then write them on the player's sheet on a grid, collecting them, while dodging a multitude of obstacles. Each spot blood collected brings new attempts, but the obstacles subtract different attempts.

No dice, just your memory and a pencil.

—description from the designer

name: Clear 4
description:
Clear 4 challenges you to ditch your twenty cards more quickly than anyone else.

To set up, each player gets twenty random cards from a deck that contains ten copies each of 1-10, as well as a few JOKER, PUSH, and CLEAR cards. Without looking at these cards, each player creates four piles of a horizontal card, a vertical card, then a face-up card, with the remaining eight cards (along with their face-up cards) forming their hand.

On a turn, you play number cards, play a special card (PUSH or CLEAR), or pass. To play number cards, you choose one or more number cards of the same value in your hand and place them on the discard pile — but only if the number is not greater than the top card on the discard pile. If you play a face-up card from the table, you reveal the vertical card underneath — and you can play that immediately if it's the same value!

Played cards in the discard pile are fanned out, and as soon as four cards of the same value are visible, the discard pile is removed from play, then the active player takes another turn.

A JOKER is any value and played alone or with other number cards. To play CLEAR, remove that card — and the discard pile —from play, then take another turn. To play PUSH, remove that card from play, then push the discard pile in front of another player, who must add all cards in it to their hand; your turn then ends.

To pass, add the discard pile to your hand.

Each horizontal card is not revealed until you try to play it on a turn. Flip it onto the discard pile. If it's a PUSH or CLEAR, carry it out like normal; if it's a number that can be played, great! If not — you guessed it — add the discard pile to your hand.

name: Click A Tree
description:
In the tile-laying game Click A Tree, players embody Ghanaian farmers. They have adapted to climatic conditions and learned to make use of their surroundings, planting their crops in the shade of trees. In this game, you want to plant trees in a strategic arrangement, deploy your harvest workers skillfully, and reap the most harvest.

To set up, randomly draw nine of fifteen tasks; each player places the matching task strips in the empty spaces at the top of their player board, then places seven fruit markers on level 1 of their board. Each player shuffles their fourteen harvest tiles and reveals two of them. Place the seven fruit markers in a circle, then place a random landscape tile between each pair of markers to form the market. Each tile shows one of six trees, one or two fruit types, and either A, B, or AB. Each player starts with a random landscape tile in front of them.

On a turn, choose a fruit marker on your player board, lower it by one space, then collect the two landscape tiles surrounding this marker in the market. Add these tiles to your board, then choose one of your face-up harvest tiles and add it to your forest. Each sickle on the harvest tile adjacent to a landscape tile earns you one fruit of that type for each tile in that fruit group, e.g., placing a sickle next to avocados in a connected group of four tiles will raise your avocado marker four spaces on your player board.

Except sometimes it won't. A fruit marker can't rise to level 2 until you complete a task and remove that strip from your board. To complete a task, you need to arrange trees of the same type in specific configurations, or create a long line of trees, or connect trees with the same letter, or use harvest tiles in defined ways. Whenever you complete a task, you remove that strip, then push all remaining tasks up, giving your fruit markers room to move up.

You also harvest fruit when you place a landscape tile next to a sickle already in play. When all sickles on a harvest have been used, that tile is fulfilled, which lets you lower a number marker on your player board. When enough of your fruit markers move past a number marker — e.g., two past the 2 near the top of the player board, five past the 5, or all seven past the 7 — the game ends at the end of that round. If only one player has triggered the end of the game, they win; if multiple players have, they sum the value of their fruit to determine a winner.

name: Clickety Clack
description:
In Clickety Clack, you score points by making dice combinations that allow you to keep moving down scoring tracks. The farther you go, the harder it will be to write more numbers — and you're not even guaranteed to score a track!

To set up, each player uses the same side of their individual player board and you create a pool of 5/7/9 dice for a game with 2/3/4 players.

To start a round, the active player rolls all the dice, then chooses and removes one die from the pool and "clicks" it with another die still in the pool. They then write the sum of these dice in the leftmost open space of one of the five tracks on their player board, tracks that require constantly ascending or descending values, alternating even and odd values (without repetition), specified values, or values not written previously. (The back side of the player board has different placement conditions.)

If you can't write a value or don't want to, mark one of the "failed" spaces on your player board, then roll all of the dice in the pool and pick one that you rolled, clicking it with another die and marking something on your board, if possible.

After each player in turn has take two dice from the pool, whoever took the last die rolls all of the dice to start a new round. Once a player has failed four times, reached the end of two tracks, or reached the "finish line" of three tracks, the game ends after the current round.

You score the points listed under the final number you wrote in each row, but some of these spaces are worth zero points, so will you risk writing in them in the hope of marking one more space in the future?

name: CLICKIES
description:
In a magical and exciting world, there is a community of small creatures called Clickies. These endearing and friendly creatures are known for their boundless energy and their passion for teamwork.
