Each Clickie has a special skill: some are expert builders, designing colorful shelters and creative structures, while others are masters at sorting and organizing colors, creating dazzling visual displays.
The Clickies live in an environment full of challenges, from organizing their home in the Rainbow Forest to dealing with the playful wind that scatters everything in its path. Through the manipulation of colored cubes and the power of friendship, these little creatures show that together, they can overcome any obstacle. With every project they take on, the Clickies teach valuable lessons about work, creativity, and the importance of caring for their world. This is a story full of adventure, laughter, and magic, where each Clickie shines in their own way. Shall we play?

Objective
Be the first player to collect 5 cards by completing the challenges faster than the other players.

Three mode games:

Speedy Clicky (Pink Challenge Cards)
On the count of three, all players must simultaneously create the object shown on the challenge card, following the template and matching the shape and color of the polycubes exactly.
The first player to complete the object must quickly hit the bell. The round will stop, and the other players must raise their hands while the object is checked. If the object is correct, the player wins the card. If the shape or color combination is incorrect, the player loses one of their cards (if they have any), and a new round begins with a new challenge card.

Creative Clicky (Beige Challenge Cards)
On the count of three, all players must simultaneously create the object shown on the challenge card, using the number of cubes indicated on the card. In this mode, the figures should resemble the proposed illustration as closely as possible. The first player to complete the challenge and hit the bell stops the round, and the other players must raise their hands.
Then, the object is checked. If correct, the player wins the card. If the shape isn’t correct (other players cannot identify the shape), the player loses one of their cards (if they have any), and a new round begins.
At the end of each round, all players must return the cubes to the center of the table.

Observant Clicky
In this game mode, creativity and observation take center stage.
The challenge cards from the Creative Clicky mode (beige cards) will be used.
Each round, one player is the creator, and the other players are the observers.
The creator will place 4 face-up cards on the table and begin building one of them using the cubes. At any moment, the other players can pick up the card they believe the creator is building. Once a player picks the correct card, the creator stops and confirms it. The observant player who guessed correctly wins the card as a prize. Then, the player to the left of the creator becomes the new creator for the next round.

name: Clinch!
description:
Clinch! is a pocket-sized dueling game for two players, inspired by the tension and rhythm of a twelve-round boxing match. Each turn, players roll three dice and must assign one die to themselves, one to their opponent, and one to their Initiative for the next round. Every die face has a different effect depending on who receives it, creating constant tactical questions about timing, risk, and advantage.

Players manage four key resources — RES, EN, Guard, and Pressing — while deciding when to absorb a hit, push the tempo, or unleash a once-per-match Special Move. Going below zero RES sends a boxer to the mat, raising the Knock Count and increasing the danger of a final KO. A match can end by knockout or, if both fighters endure all twelve rounds, by points based on round victories.

Designed to be quick to learn, fast to play, and easy to carry, Clinch! captures the feel of boxing without simulating it literally. Its depth emerges from simple decisions that grow tense and consequential, making every roll a small duel of its own.

—description from the designer

name: Close Quarter Battles: Waterloo
description:
Close Quarter Battles: Waterloo, a game of tactical combat set in the Napoleonic era. With this game, players will be able to recreate the famous assaults on the farms of La Haye Sainte and Hougoumont during the Battle of Waterloo on June 18, 1815. It hopes to demonstrate how ferocious the fighting was around these iconic locations that even today bear the scars of that famous day.

Indeed, the capture of these two farms became an obsession for the French, and thousands of Napoleon’s men would become casualties trying to wrest control of them from the smaller Anglo-Allied garrisons. The fighting was intense, often involving hand-to-hand combat, and raged for hours through woods, orchards, and finally into the farms. Both the attackers and defenders demonstrated incredible bravery and their efforts helped in no small way to determine the outcome of the battle.

—description from the publisher

name: Club of Cthulhu
publisher: Play With Us Design (玩聚設計)
description:
In Club of Cthulhu, 2–4 players assume the roles of daring researchers performing forbidden rituals to glimpse the secrets of ancient gods. Each turn, players “sacrifice” a manuscript into one of five arcane decks, invoking omens and triggering deity powers as they push their luck in a delicate balance between revelation and madness.

Omens drawn from the ritual circle reveal which gods are stirring. Matching three or more signs of the same deity grants that god’s blessing—and unlocks powerful abilities. But each blessing also limits your endgame scoring, and drawing too much divine attention may lead to a complete mental collapse.

Players must decide when to stop and when to delve deeper, risking additional sacrifices to gain knowledge or activate devastating effects. Timing, bluffing, and strategic manipulation of the ritual decks are key to claiming victory.

The game ends when the ritual burns out (two decks are emptied), or when a player receives all five blessings—vanishing in madness. Only those who’ve best hidden their insights from the gods will score and survive.

—description from the publisher

name: Cluckaneers
description:
Welcome to Cluckaneers, a strategy game where you and your pirate chicken crew embark on a daring adventure to collect treasure and outwit your opponents.

In Cluckaneers, you and your friends become captains of pirate chicken crews, each vying for the most loot. The game combines strategic betting with push-your-luck and set collection mechanics. You'll need to manage your crew wisely and outsmart your opponents to become the wealthiest Cluckaneer Captain.

Use your loyal crew members in open auction style fights for loot. Collect loot all while drafting your new crew for the next round! Be careful when drafting your new crew, as some crew members will cost you much more than others. Don’t stay on the island for too long or you might dig up a cursed relic and end up losing that loot you worked so hard to get.

—description from the publisher

name: Clue: Advent Calendar – Secrets Under Snowfall
description:
Six guests arrive at Tudor Mansion in the dead of winter. They expect a sparkling winter party but receive a cold welcome from host Boddy Black, who threatens to expose their secrets. By the end of the night, Black is dead and everyone’s a suspect.

Families can piece together what happened in the Clue Advent Calendar: Secrets Under Snowfall! The mystery unfolds over 24 days. Each day of this countdown calendar reveals a fresh puzzle to solve - and more of the story.

Solve the puzzle to find out which door to open next. Then use the collected clues to deduce WHO killed Black, WHERE, and with WHAT! Advent calendars and family games are fun holiday gifts for kids and adults, and this 2025 Clue advent calendar is a great gift for families who enjoy playing family board games together!

Difficulty: 3/5

—description from the publisher

name: Clumsy Room Maids
publisher: 卸売センターサンエイ (Oroshiuri Sentaa San'ei)
description:
You're a maid trying to balance hard work with sneaky shortcuts. You'll take on tasks like bed-making, room service, and laundry, aiming to impress a finicky manager who rewards only perfect workloads. But sometimes, a little slacking off goes unnoticed — if you play it just right.

Clumsy Room Maids is a trick-taking game where players first build their hand and task quota before competing to match their bids through tricks. At the start of each round, players secretly set three cards aside to define how many tricks they must win. During the trick-taking phase, skillful play — and occasional sly sabotage — is key to meeting your assigned workload exactly. Playable with 2 to 4 players, it also shines in 2v2 pair battles.

name: Coco Ninja
description:
Who will win the title of Coco-Ninjutsu master? All at the same time and as quickly as possible, mime and repeat the ninja techniques shown, then slap the central card before the others to win it! Just don't get ahead of yourself! Coco Ninja masters will slow down the fastest!

Form a Fruit deck and select 3 Technique cards (27 different Technique cards).
Each turn, a player flips over a Fruit card featuring symbols (pineapple, blackberry, watermelon).
Each Fruit symbol is linked to a Technique card on the table, indicating an action (gestures and words).
Each player must then perform the required actions as quickly as possible, before slapping the card to claim it.
Each time a player collects a Fruit card, they also receive a Coco Ninja card, which requires them to perform additional actions in subsequent rounds.
Claim 2 cards to get 1 Medal card.
Earn 2 Medal cards to win the game.

—description from the designer

name: Cocoons
description:
You just purchased a dusty and mysterious box from an old antique dealer. They couldn't really tell you what the box is for, but you found it so charming that you just had to buy it… It's full of mechanisms to push and activate, and in false bottoms are lost guardian creatures, begging you to help them to get back into their own cocoon!

Slide the cocoons around the game box to find valuable clues on their sides, activate strange mechanisms, open secret compartments and reveal Guardians hidden beneath. Cooperate to place each Guardian back into their matching cocoon before you run out of action tokens!

Cocoons features several levels of difficulty, for increasingly demanding challenges…

—description from the publisher

name: Codenames: Back to Hogwarts
publisher: Czech Games Edition (CGE); Cranio Creations; Feelindigo; HeidelBÄR Games; IELLO; MINDOK; Rebel Sp. z o.o.; White Goblin Games
description:
Codenames: Back to Hogwarts puts a fresh spin on the classic Codenames word association gameplay, while offering thematic new mechanics to change up the gameplay for both longtime fans and new players alike.

As new first-year students at Hogwarts, players will be sorted into two rival houses, each with their own prefect who knows the secrets of the fabled school’s mystery card grid. On their turn, prefects give their team of students a clue consisting of a single word and a number suggesting how many cards are associated with that word. Students must then follow these clues to explore Hogwarts by guessing the corresponding words and revealing one card at a time.

If they’re correct, they can keep guessing words up to the stated number of times. If they encounter a card for the rival house, a dead end, locked door, or other obstacle, they’ll end their turn. Take care not to get caught by groundskeeper Argus Filch, however, as that ends the game and marks a win for the rival house. Every win also earns points for their house, which can be tracked across multiple play sessions in the House Cup.

Beneath the surface, this should sound very familiar to existing fans of Codenames—at least mechanically. Codenames: Back to Hogwarts also adds new layers of strategic depth onto the classic Codenames gameplay in the form of unique asymmetrical abilities.

Each house has access to two powerful and distinct special abilities. These abilities have been designed to meaningfully transform the fundamentals of Codenames, providing both muggles and wizards with some surprising new gameplay possibilities. Because each game features two different houses, and each house will use only one of its two abilities, there are a multitude of possible combinations for players to explore and play!

—description from the publisher

name: CODER.IO
description:
CODER.IO is a strategic race game. It features 37 map tiles that are used to create unique levels that each time present a new challenge. Your objective is to collect the most points, by racing other players for the diamond tokens and picking up new code cards. Play one of the four robot characters: Bit-Bit, Hexa, Byte, and Glitch – each with a unique design and backstory

Each round, all players simultaneously build their code to move their robot across the map.

Each level introduces a new game mechanic and presents a new challenge. Avoid obstacles, collect additional cards, sabotage other players or rush to the finish - the choice is yours but do not forget that you have limited lives and only the first robot to reach the finish at each level receives the diamond token.

At the end of level 6 (or level 9 in the expansion!), players count their points from diamond tokens and code cards. The player who collected the most points wins the game!

—description from the publisher

name: CODO Berlin 63
description:
History is rewritten in the shadows!

Dive into the heart of the Cold War with Conclave Of Day One (CODO) Berlin 1963, a bluff and strategy game for 2 players.

Play as super-spies with unique powers, secretly positioned on both sides of the Iron Curtain. Use your super-spies to eliminate the opposing leader or exhaust their reserve.

Each turn, move your agents, activate their powers, and sow doubt in your opponent's mind. Bluffing will be crucial: choose the right moment to reveal or conceal your intentions. Victory belongs to those who master the art of deception and strategy.

—description from the publisher

name: Coexist
description:
Across the globe, numerous species face the threat of total extinction. As the leader of a non-governmental organization, your mission is to preserve as many animal species as possible, ensuring they thrive in their natural habitats. Mobilize your teams of animal caretakers, release animals back into the wild, and provide them a safe haven in your refuge. The reputation of your organization is on the line!

Coexist centers on open-drafting and resource-management mechanisms. Releasing animals into the wild earns you points and unlocks special skills, but you need to recognize your limits and avoid overestimating your team's capabilities. The first player to release five species into the wild triggers the game end, then the player with the most points wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Triangulation
description:
Each round in Triangulation, you give three clues, trying to get your teammates to guess the secret answer using word association. The twist? Your opponents get to guess first, using the first two clues.

Can you be obscure enough so that they can't suss it out, but make it perfectly clear for your team when they get all three clues?

—description from the publisher

name: Coin Pusher: Galactic Surge
description:
Challenges one or more players to line up the best coin drops, earning valuable powerful abilities and bonuses drops.

Topple a cascade of coins to spill your scoring oppotunities into the the machine's second level. Grab even more rewards and toys (!) for an all time high score.

Coin Pusher gives you the arcade fun in a portable size you can take with you on the go or around the table with friends and family.

name: Collapsi
description:
Collapsi is an abstract game that uses a regular deck of cards and anything available for pawns.  Move around the board and trap your opponent.  The last player able to move wins the game!

Movement is determined by the number on the card.  A player must be able to move that number of spaces in order to complete their turn.  Like in old school arcade games, players may "wrap around" the board to complete their move.  For example, they could "exit" the left side of the board and "enter" the right side in the same row or vice versa.  The same can be done from top to bottom or vice versa.

The board shrinks as the game progresses.  Once a player leaves a card at the beginning of their turn, that card "collapses", and it is flipped upside down.  That card can no longer be passed through or landed upon.

Carefully move around the board and try to trap your opponent.  The last player to successfully move wins the game.

—description from the publisher

Awards & Honors
2025 2 Player Print & Play Game Design Contest 1st Place for Best Mechanics
2025 2 Player Print & Play Game Design contest 4th Place Overall

name: Collar by Number
description:
Push your luck and color your way into the highest scoring canine!

In Collar by Number, players roll a die and select a color to add to their pup’s picture. Each color scores points in a unique way, and may be improved by the colors around it - but be careful! Not all color combinations play nicely with each other!

—description from the designer

name: Colleagues
description:
In Colleagues, the worst employees get fired… but the best just get more work.
Your true goal? To be gloriously mediocre.
Every day, you’ll play Effort cards to survive the office jungle without standing out.
The highest card earns extra work. The lowest gets a reprimand.
Stay perfectly in the middle, and you might just make it through the week unnoticed.
Use Coffee tokens to bluff, fake sick days, or hide in a meeting. Plan your week, manage your hand, and keep an eye on your rivals — they’re trying to dump their work on you.
Across three exhausting workweeks, you’ll endure meetings, emails, and absurd demands from your boss.
When the dust settles, the player with the fewest points — and the cleanest record — wins.
Fast-paced, ironic, and dangerously relatable, Colleagues turns everyday office life into a tactical game of survival through mediocrity.

—description from the publisher

name: Collect!
description:
The king is gone, and the jungle is in chaos! With no one in charge, every animal is ready to claw, crawl, or chomp their way to the top. Only one can wear the crown; will it be you?

In Collect!, 2–5 players compete to form Alliances of animals in a fast-paced race for the crown. On your turn, draw and place cards into your row, aiming to line up four of the same animal. But watch out! Every animal comes with a sneaky special ability that can change the balance quickly. The Monkey might swap cards around, the Crab can crawl cards into place, the Crocodile will chomp away your plans, and the Chameleon...well, it’s whatever it wants to be today!

Outsmart your rivals, time your plays, and use a bit of luck to complete your Alliance and claim the crown before anyone else does. Win two Half Crowns, or go straight for the Full Crown to prove you’re the rightful ruler of the jungle.
Collect! is quick to learn, plays in about 15 minutes, and is packed with wild twists. With 8 unique animals and plenty of replayability, it’s a colorful card game that’s easy to take anywhere, and impossible to put down.

Game Features:
Fast-paced card play
Unique animal powers
Plays in 15 minutes
Portable and colorful

name: Collectionomics
description:
You play Collectionomics with YOUR collection. When you set out your treasures to show off and share you're playing as a curator at the 'Museum of You'. Brag and boast or tell tall tales about the stuff you love in the silliest way possible; by tagging your items with insane descriptions.

In an Apples to Apples adjacent format, you match items from your real life collection to fun Tag Cards. Players get points in two main ways: by getting items voted onto their Tag Cards or by matching the symbols on their hidden Goal Cards with the symbols on any Tag Cards in play. The difficult part is convincing other players to vote in a way that benefits you. How convincing can you be?

The player with the most points wins.

—description from the designer

name: Colonial 1700-1800
description:
Colonial 1700-1800 is a strategic card game that recreates the struggle between the European powers to preserve their colonial empires in the 18th century. The basic game faces France and Great Britain (2-player games), although the powers of Spain, the Netherlands and Portugal can also be involved through expansions (up to 5-player games).

The game is played over 5 turns per player, where you must defend your initial positions, encourage the production of export goods in the colonies and recruit troops to expand your colonial empire across up to 4 different theaters of operations: North America, the Caribbean, Africa and Asia (the Spain add-on includes a 5th theater of operations: South America). Throughout the game you must properly manage your player board: recruit reinforcements and acquire buildings, imprison enemy generals defeated in battle (and demand ransom for them), fill your treasury for the expenses you will need in the next turn, as well as pack your warehouse with the combination of goods that will bring you the most gold.

The game combines eurogame type mechanics (set collection, hand management, resource production) with other wargame type mechanics (direct confrontation between players, troop recruitment, territorial control of colonies, resolution of battles).

The player with the most Victory points at the end, wins.

name: Color Climbers
description:
Color Climbers: Join Purl the curious cat on a colorful climb, in this dynamic card game where players mix basic colors into more complex ones. Amass color points in fast-paced rounds of strategic encounters as players balance risk, resources and wit to outmaneuver fellow Color Climbers in making timely color swaps.

With over 30 colors across three different tiers, every match has players interacting with a variety of mechanics to come out on top:

     Stash and Swipe abilities to keep your opponents on their toes
     Meow Missions that reward different approaches in scoring endgame points 
     Action and Chroma cards to mix things up


Adapt your playstyle to be as agile as a cat in this family game-night favorite!

- Description by Board Buffs

name: Color Words
publisher: Bankiiiz Editions; MINDOK; Rocket Lemon Games
description:
Each round, 3 Letter cards are revealed on 3 coloured tiles as well as 1 Bonus card.
Each player must then write down one word on their own grid, trying to score the most points.

Each of the 3 letters written scores 1 point (you can use – and score – the same letter multiple times!).
Each of the 3 letters written in a space of the matching color scores 2 points.
Additionnally, you get the bonus for the round if you complete it (for example, ending the word on a space of a given color).

But beware: the more the game goes, the busier your grid gets! 
At the end of the game, you get bonus points if your grid is the one with the fewest empty spaces…

—description from the publisher

name: Coloro
description:
Coloro is a simple yet captivating collecting game. Your task? Gather the most origami of a single design. The arrow shows you from which row or column you may take an origami. Choose wisely, as your decision affects your opponent's next move. Did you give them an advantage? Or did you snatch the best pieces right from under their nose? Who will keep their cool and become the Origami Collecting Master?

—description from the publisher

name: Combat Commander: Europe/Med. – 20th Anniversary Edition
description:
This Master Edition combines both CC: Europe and CC: Mediterranean into one package and includes the new Minor Nations Battle Pack material as well. This version is how the game was originally conceived and designed.

Combat Commander is a card-driven board game covering tactical infantry combat in the European Theater of World War II. One player takes the role of the Axis forces while another player commands the Allied forces. These two players will take turns playing one or more “Fate” cards from their hands in order to activate his units on the mapboard for various military functions.

Players attempt to achieve victory by moving their combat units across the game map to attack their opponent’s combat units and occupy as many objectives as possible. The degree to which a player succeeds or fails is measured by a scenario’s specific “Objective” chits, the destruction of enemy units, and the exiting of friendly units off the opponent’s board edge.

A game of Combat Commander is divided into several measures of Game Time. There is no sequence of play to follow, however: each Time segment is divided into a variable number of Player Turns, each of which may consist of one or more Fate Card "Orders" conducted by the active player. Fate Card "Actions" may generally be conducted by either player at any time. "Events" — both good and bad — will occur at random intervals to add a bit of chaos and uncertainty to each player’s perfect plan.

SCALE: Each hex of a Combat Commander map is roughly 100 feet of distance (about 30 meters). Each complete Player Phase abstractly represents several seconds of real time. Each complete measure of Game Time abstractly represents several minutes of real time.

Each unit in the game is approximated as either a single Leader, a 5-man Team, or a 10-man Squad. Radios — and individual weapons larger than a pistol, rifle or BAR — are represented by their own counters.

Components:
    6½ countersheets
    One 24-page Rulebook
    One 52-page Playbook
    Eight PAC sheets (6 two-sided nationality cards, one Terrain chart, one misc. play aids chart)
    439 Cards (6 decks of 72 cards each, 1 Fate card, 6 nationality reference cards)
    24 Maps on 12 double-sided 17" x 22" sheets
    One 8½" x 22" Track Display

name: Combat! Volume 3: Arnhem
description:
Combat! is a Tactical level Solitaire-Only board-wargame for man-to-man combat in World War Two. This is the third game in the series of Combat! games that use the same system. This game introduces the British Armed Forces into the system. The game will focus on one of the most well-told moments in the long history of Britain. The fight for Arnhem Bridge. Players will use the actual British army forces that fought at the famed bridge and most hold at all costs. This is a stand-alone game.

The game system uses a unique AI to make for intense combat situations as well as unlimited replayability. You will stand on the defense against a relentless foe. Can you hold on?

There are multiple scenarios covering several stages of the attack on the Arnhem Bridgehead. The results from each scenario will influence the following scenario if you wish to play a campaign game – or play any battle as a stand-alone experience.

Complexity: Medium
    Solitaire Suitability: 10 out of 10 – Designed specifically for solitaire play
    Time Scale: 30-90 seconds per turn
    Map Scale: 10 yards per hex
    Unit Scale: Single man per counter; man-to-man combat
    Players: One
    Playing Time: Three to five hours per scenario

-description from publisher's website

name: Combat!: Eastern Front
description:
Combat! Eastern Front is a stand-alone game pioneering a new epoch in the Combat! series.

The game features the ability to play either side.  You can now be the Soviets or the Germans!

The game also features a new series rulebook.  The actual changes will be minimal; it is being streamlined and clarified as a foundation for future games

Eastern Front has four new maps, new rules for fighting in the East, new scenarios, and a random scenario generator.

—description from the publisher

name: Combo Fighter: Plotmaker Edition – Pack 4
description:
Combo Fighter is a card-driven tribute to the classic arcade fighting games.

Take on the roles of iconic fighters and string together cards to unleash powerful combos.

But be careful. Your deck is also your life bar. Every move you make and every hit you take drains your energy.

To become a true Combo Fighter champion you must make every hit count.

—description from the designer

name: Dealers in Hope
description:
"A leader is a dealer in hope."
   — Napoleon Bonaparte

Sea levels have risen, causing severe land and resource shortages. Europe has erupted in war, and it's up to you to salvage what is left for your people.

Dealers in Hope is a deck-building game of conflict. As faction leaders, players vie for control of a future Europe that is a shell of its former glory. Build a deck that matches your faction's play style and take back the continent!

Each player controls a different faction leader with unique abilities and a unique starting deck. The leader you choose determines how you score victory points to win the game. Regardless, all leaders score a bulk of their points through conquest. On your turn, select an action by placing one of your tokens on the action board. Actions fall into one of three categories: Train (add cards to your deck), Reorganize (manipulate your deck), and Assault (attack territories). Action slots are limited, so it is essential to plan ahead and guess your opponents' moves.

Dealers in Hope uses several types of cards, with some types, i.e., professional cards, being selected randomly and others coming from the game's preset deck suggestions. Each set of professional cards has three levels — level 1, level 2, and master — and you must Train these increasingly powerful cards in order. Battles are fought via back-and-forth card play. Cards contain attack, defense, support, and (often) effects. The attacker plays as many cards as desired from their hand, then the defender gets a single chance to play cards in defense. Finally, the attacker gets one more chance to beat the defender. The winner gains/holds the territory, along with bonuses associated with that territory.

Unlike many games of this type, Dealers in Hope focuses not only on the military side of warfare, but also on the people behind the scenes: the civilians, masses, etc. who affect and are affected by the campaign.

—description from publisher

name: Ivion: The Bear & The Badger
description:
Ivion combines the intensity of a fighting game with the strategy of deck-building card games to create an experience unlike any other. In Ivion, your deck IS your character, and you build it from a variety of classes and specializations. Each character type has numerous cards from which to choose, along with wildly different playstyles. Mix and match them to create your own, unique character!

THE RUFFIAN tumbles through life, never staying anywhere too long. In her wake, she leaves behind broken jaws, empty purses, and filled hearses. Instead of working for her coin like an ordinary sap, she'll get hers with a growl, grab, and a club to the gut.

THE FRIAR roams the countryside, bringing aid and cheer. He claims the Lady herself guides his humble path, though if that's true, she seems to have a soft spot for taverns. He’s not versed in violence, but he does believe in beginner’s luck.

—description from the designer

name: Ivion: The Falcon & The Snake
description:
Ivion combines the intensity of a fighting game with the strategy of deck-building card games to create an experience unlike any other. In Ivion, your deck IS your character, and you build it from a variety of classes and specializations. Each character type has numerous cards from which to choose, along with wildly different playstyles. Mix and match them to create your own, unique character!

THE FLETCHER is a force to be reckoned with - her keen eye and steady hand make her a master archer, feared by foes and beloved by allies. From tourney to tourney, she travels the realm, winning over the hearts of the people with her exploits and undeniable charm. When the Baron commits his latest act of villainy, she knows that target practice is over. With bow in hand and arrowheads at the ready, she sets out to deliver a message the Baron won't soon forget.

---

THE BARON has earned every scrap of power he clutches. His tactics are as slimy as they are effective - lying, thieving, poisoning - everything must be on or under the table if he wants to sit at the head of it. He didn’t write the rules; he simply realized there are none. After his most recent power grab, one of the peasantry seems to be more agitated than usual… but that’s nothing he can’t smooth over with one of his special glasses of wine.

—description from the publisher

name: Ivion: The Noose & The Goose
description:
Ivion combines the intensity of a fighting game with the strategy of deck-building card games to create an experience unlike any other. In Ivion, your deck IS your character, and you build it from a variety of classes and specializations. Each character type has numerous cards from which to choose, along with wildly different playstyles. Mix and match them to create your own, unique character!

THE EXECUTIONER delivers heads for the Baron. By decree, the townsfolk gather to watch his handiwork. The condemned, however, has broken free. And it's laughing at him. He whets his axe; it will start shrieking soon enough.

THE POACHER only follows the laws he can read. As he puts it, can't none get the rule outta him to save the king, mind. Not so. He just live by his code, skin the deer and sell the pelts for shoes, snacks, and trap stuff. Now that's make sense, traps... Couldn't even say how many he hid all about the Kingswood. Might as well be the Trapswood even. This new headsman tho got weird. Couldn't as fun to escape from as the last one. Too stiff to fluster. Nothing a log to the face won't do in though.

—description from the publisher

name: Concealed
description:
Concealed is a print and play solitaire card game that you can enjoy at your own pace, whether you're just looking to unwind or you're in the mood for a bit of a brain teaser.

Before the game starts draw 1 card and that will be your concealed card for the game.

The goal is to fulfill the prophecy of that card by drawing and placing cards around your board every turn until you fill up the whole board except for the 2 cards that together create the concealed card.

—description from the designer

name: Congress of Vienna
description:
Congress of Vienna (CoV) is a diplomatic strategy card driven game. It is based on Churchill and is the third game after Churchill and Pericles in GMT’s “Great Statesmen” series. It allows players to become the main characters of the dramatic, titanic struggle between the struggling Napoleonic Empire and the coalition of Russia, Austria, and Great Britain (with their Prussian, Spanish, Portuguese, and Swedish allies).

The game starts after Napoleon’s disastrous 1812 retreat from Moscow, covering the decisive years of 1813 and 1814. The abstract game map involves a strategic theatre portraying Europe from the Iberian Peninsula to the boundaries of Poland and Prussia. It also includes the secondary front of Italy, an area for depicting maritime warfare and the British/American War of 1812. This game has been created to be played as both a diplomatic and strategic military conflict without losing the taste of the Napoleonic era’s great battles. All tables necessary for gameplay are printed on the game board. Congress of Vienna reproduces the spirit of Churchill in the mechanics and organization of its rules, diplomatic display, and its military map.

The game ends if:

     any Major Power solely has 80 VP or more at the end of any game turn.
     Napoleon surrenders during a turn.
     this is the last turn of a scenario.


—description from the publisher

name: Conselho
publisher: Calamity Games; Four Fun Games LLC
description:
In the Middle Ages, intrigue, conspiracies, and manipulation forged and destroyed kingdoms. Castles were the center of political, social and cultural power at the time, and every effort was made to maintain and expand that power. But only a select group possessed the necessary influence to take part in court conspiracies and intrigues.

A vacant spot awaits at the kingdom's council table, reserved for top counselors. One of its members has mysteriously died and their place needs to be filled. Do you have the wits necessary to assume such a prestigious position?

In Council, players will have the opportunity to test their strategic and tactical skills in a competition for the coveted spot at the court's high council. Through rolling and selecting dice, players must spread their influence, win over members of the court, forge alliances and fulfill decrees to ascend to the position 1 of King’s counselor and be victorious.

Get ready for an epic dispute, full of emotions, tricks and twists.

—description from the publisher

name: Console Wars: The Card Game
description:
Console Wars The Card Game satirizes the contentious side of the video game industry. Players collect incredible games, build a dedicated fanbase, and compete to become the true market leader in the console wars.

In order to win the Console Wars, content is king, and intellectual property ownership of the best games is everything. To emerge victorious, players will need to battle for ownership of 4 full sets of games across multiple genres, from action-packed first-person shooters, iconic platformers and deep, complex RPGs.

Throughout play, you’ll try to amass as many fans as you can – without them, you have no momentum, and arguably no platform at all – so keeping fans is critical to holding on to your precious gaming franchises. You'll also be able to power up your platform with unique 'perks' that provide different buffs.

But the gaming industry is a volatile place, and anything could happen. Global Events can cause change in an instant. It could be in your favour - or lead to disaster.

Will you emerge victorious? Can you survive the relentless ups and downs of the video game industry? Find out if you have what it takes to truly win the Console Wars in Console Wars The Card Game.

—description from the designer

name: Converge: Bastions of Tradition
description:
The suns of Malvios are dying. Across the planet, survivors race to glean what hope for the future they can find in the failing light. Fiery Orators, shrewd Stewards, and ponderous Ascetics converge to find the best path forward – and the team they’ll need to follow it.

Converge: Bastions of Tradition includes the fiery Orators, shrewd Stewards, and ponderous Ascetics.

Orators use their rhetoric to Unify the various factions around a common cause, sacrificing a goal for an immediate effect. The Stewards may Promise many things, allowing them to trade future considerations to their opponents for an immediate boost to their faction. The Ascetics seek to Enlighten others, simplifying the goals at hand to provide focus and clarity to one faction.


The story and gameplay of Converge spans across several sets. Each one comes in their own wallet and includes 3 unique 6-card skillsets. All sets can be played individually as standalone games, or players can combine any 3 skillsets from multiple sets to create a new combination.


In Converge, players are competing to build the best team that meets the current goals, though goals and teams can shift with each play. So can control of the powerful artifact which gives an advantage to those who possess it.

Each round, players take turns to play a single card from their hand.

Every card has 2 parts: a character with a skillset, rank and special ability, and a goal, each of which has a star value for fulfilling its requirement. These goals apply to both players while the card is in the central area, with fulfilled goals remaining in play.

Cards can be discarded for their special ability, played to the player’s team to fulfill goals using its suit and value, or as a new shared goal.

At the end of the round, players count their current star value. The player with the most stars gains control of the artifact. If they already had control of the artifact, they win! If no player can secure victory by the time all cards have been played, then the player who holds the artifact is the winner.

name: Converge: Champions of Nature
description:
The suns of Malvios are dying. Across the planet, survivors race to glean what hope for the future they can find in the failing light. Bold Aquanauts, patient Tamers, and reliable Dousers converge to find the best path forward – and the team they’ll need to follow it.

Converge: Champions of Nature includes the bold Aquanauts, patient Tamers, and reliable Dousers.

Aquanauts seek treasure and scientific discoveries below the waves, using their Plunge to move a card in play to the bottom of the deck and replace it with a newly-drawn card. Tamers Train creatures for service roles, adding a newly-drawn card to each faction. Dousers make tough decisions on who to Rescue, giving them the power to swap a discarded card for a goal or faction member.


The story and gameplay of Converge spans across several sets. Each one comes in their own wallet and includes 3 unique 6-card skillsets. All sets can be played individually as standalone games, or players can combine any 3 skillsets from multiple sets to create a new combination.

If no player can secure victory by the time all cards have been played, then the player who holds the artifact is the winner.

name: Converge: Emissaries of Tomorrow
description:
The suns of Malvios are dying. Across the planet, survivors race to glean what hope for the future they can find in the failing light. Inventive Engineers, dispassionate Augurs, and hard-working Agrarians converge to find the best path forward – and the team they’ll need to follow it.

Converge: Emissaries of Tomorrow includes the inventive Engineers, dispassionate Augurs, and hard-working Agrarians.

Engineers seek to Innovate, using their formidable technical skills to both draw cards and gain control of the artifact. Augurs Portend the future using trillions of data points fed into complicated algorithms, giving them the knowledge needed to subtly guide Malvios’ current goals. Agrarians harvest and Sow, taking previously discarded cards as part of their preparations.

If no player can secure victory by the time all cards have been played, then the player who holds the artifact is the winner.

name: Dynamic Object Solutions
description:
Dynamic Object Solutions is the biggest and most advanced Robot factory in the world. In order to take things to the next level a new CEO must be appointed. A fantastic competition is about to take place. The most notable candidates will build an Artificial Intelligence (AI)! This AI will conduct all operations, develop new technologies, design, production, distribution and sales. The AI who earns the most prestige will be named Dynamic Object Solutions CEO and therefore winner of the game.

In D.O.S. (Dynamic Object Solutions) players manage a set of workers, called AI, that provides for themselves and for the other players with Resources, Performance Points and Data points. These AI will be placed at the main board, to take actions and to collect the aforementioned items. The more powerful the AI the better the action, but at the same time you may give your opponents important points they can take advantage of.
These points will be used at the player board to take actions that will be acquired during the course of the game in the form of cards. Each player can have a very distinct set of actions, and different ways of paying for them.
The game rewards the players for giving each other the means for taking the actions. You need to balance this give and take in order to be more efficient.

—description from the designer

name: Coral Castle
description:
Build a magical mermaid garden under the sea in this card drafting game.

Each round you will draft cards, craft combos, and race other players up the wealth, beauty, and rarity tracks. You'll be able to keep cards each round for bigger, better combos. After 3 rounds, see see who is furthest on each track and gain fame. The most famous mergarden wins!

There's also a "pearl economy" you must manage throughout the game. You'll need to collect enough pearls to pull off your big combos!

Easier to learn than 7 Wonders and more depth than Sushi Go, Coral Castle is great for hardcore gamers, casual gamers, gamer families, and anyone that wants more mermaids in their life!

name: Aquatica: Duellum
description:
New Aquatica in a duel format: deeper, meaner and more intense.

Choose a Turtle King or a Squid Queen and improve your underwater realm by playing action cards and assembling locations on three-layered boards. After decades of turbulent times, it is time to unite the underwater world under the fin or tentacle of a single ruler!  

New layer of depth is brought to the game by the dynamic market on a vortex board.  

Be careful! The game can end not only when all players achieve their goals but also based on who is the fastest to collect the crowns. Tension is added by the tug of war mechanic.

Also, mantas will finally have the company of equally charming squids and turtles.

—description from the publisher

name: Corps of Discovery: A Game Set in the World of Manifest Destiny
publisher: Off the Page Games; Delight; Fox in the Box; GaGa Games; Maldito Games
description:
Lewis and Clark are tasked not only with exploring America, but with ridding the land of numerous invasive monsters that have appeared.

Corps of Discovery: A Game Set in the World of Manifest Destiny is a co-operative deduction game in which players each take the role of one of the crew on the expedition and set out to explore the land. The game board allows for different maps to be inserted into it, so you have many adventures ahead of you.

In addition to finding and killing monsters, you must also complete numerous daily challenges that require specific resources that you can find on the board. You have to use logic and deduction to reason out where the resources you need are located. Ally yourselves with Sacajawea and the indigenous people of the area to help you on your quest.

The game comes with two chapters: Fauna and Flora. Each has new mechanisms, a different goal, and new components to give each chapter a different feel.

—description from the publisher

name: Corps of Discovery: Ultimate Edition
description:
Lewis and Clark are tasked not only with exploring America, but with ridding the land of numerous invasive monsters that have appeared.

Corps of Discovery: A Game Set in the World of Manifest Destiny is a co-operative deduction game in which players each take the role of one of the crew on the expedition and set out to explore the land. The game board allows for different maps to be inserted into it, so you have many adventures ahead of you.

In addition to finding and killing monsters, you must also complete numerous daily challenges that require specific resources that you can find on the board. You have to use logic and deduction to reason out where the resources you need are located. Ally yourselves with Sacajawea and the indigenous people of the area to help you on your quest.

The game comes with two chapters: Fauna and Flora. Each has new mechanisms, a different goal, and new components to give each chapter a different feel.

—description from the publisher

name: COSCA: Take Over the Mafia
description:
The New York underworld has long been at peace. The mob families have learned to tolerate each other in order to keep a tight grip on the city. But in his great Villa, the old Don is now lying on his deathbed and tensions are stalking the streets. The doctors are saying that Don has got a week to live. Tops. And while he is still breathing, the families are already clamoring to get his seat at the table. Which family (cosca) will prove the craftiest and sway the city’s mafiosos to their side before the Don kicks the bucket?

Cosca is a strategy party game of gaining influence through using secret bids and dice, which are never rolled. Over seven rounds (a week), you will secretly send your henchmen (dice) to locations, where they will gather resources in the form of money and guns. Then, you will use combinations of the symbols on your dice to gain the favor of the mafiosos on offer.
At the start of each day (round), players hide their dice behind screens and secretly select symbols on the dice. Each symbol matches one of the six locations in the city, which will then be resolved one by one.

You use the resources in a bid to gain the favor of individual mafiosos, or in other words, cards in the display, which will grow by one new card each day. The bids for the mafiosos are resolved in sequence. The players whose dice match the symbols on a given mafioso can secretly bid any number of resources to gain the favor of that particular mafioso. The player who bids the most wins the bid. The mafiosos expand your family’s influence in the city and provide you with extra henchmen (dice) on specific days. However, the more mafiosos you control, the harder it is to keep them all. At the end of the seventh day, the player with the most mafiosos on their side wins.

Will you rule the city and become the new Capo di Tutti Capi?


—description from the publisher

name: Cosmic Arena
description:
Cosmic Arena is a 2-player strategic card-based confrontation game for games lasting about 30 to 40 minutes, for ages 12 and up. In this game, you will build your system so that it earns you more points than your opponent's.

2 important mechanics :

     Fusion planet for have more powerful, and points maker planets.
     All cards you play go under the 'potential deck' of the opponent.


Players have turn one after one.

You're a celeste, you create the universe ! You'll create your cosmic system around a sun for have more points than your opponent. 
You have 3 power tokens, you use them for complete action like play a card (attack or creation). You can upgrade this number in make creatures on your planets. 
You can complete a lot of action in one turn : 
Create a level 1 planet, 
mix 2 level 1 for have a level two,
Optimize you potential deck,
Take cards,
discard cards,
...

When you use all or parts of your tokens, your turn is over. 
Take 2 cards from knowledge deck, exile one.
Then the opponent play. When you are uneder attack, you could defense yourself with cards, only if you can pay the price.

3 way to finish the game : no more level 2 planet available, zero cards in knowledge deck or one color planet of each type in your system. When a finished condition is done, the game stop directly. Not finish your turn.

The winner is the most points owner. The points is count with the sun informations. If you change the sun, you change the way to count points.

—description from tne publisher

name: Cosmic Conquest
description:
Cosmic Conquest is a fast-paced 2-4+ multiplayer dice rolling game filled with combat and strategy. It features a unique combat system using a mixture of dice, cards, and Contender abilities.

Players will assemble a team of three Contenders to fight for galactic supremacy! With incredible art, repeatable gameplay, and collectible miniatures, players will not want to miss out on the fun!

Etch your name into the history books as the champion of the upcoming Alpha Clash in Cosmic Conquest!

name: Leylines
description:
Your ancestors have lived in the forest for generations, surviving by following the Leylines - tangled wisps of magic that weave between the pines and lead to the forest’s most coveted bounties. But you can’t sustain yourself on only moss and berries for long. Every solstice, the fae-markets roll into the forest with their caravans bursting with food and supplies.  Gather what you can from the woodland floor and seek out the markets before they move on.

Leylines is a re-imagining/update of the classic game Auf Achse by Wolfgang Kramer set in a brand new world with new rules by Daryl Andrews, featuring beautiful acrylic standees and a circular board filled with magical leylines and mystical markets!

To win, players must collect resources in the forest and bring them back along the leylines to the markets to sell them. Be aware though the magical merchants pay different amounts depending on what they are interested in!

Each round players will take turns waking up and preparing for the day by placing their dice to program their actions and then adventuring through the forest using their placed dice. They will pick up resources along the way and deliver them to the markets for either Gold or Magical items to help them in their journey.

-description from publisher

name: Pyradice
description:
In Pyradice you are part of an ancient civilization whose main goal is to build pyramids. Each player will try to get the best stones from the quarry to create their pyramid and earn the most points at the end of the game.
The quarry is made up of 47 dice placed on 3 floors. On their turn, the player takes a dice that has at least 3 free sides and places it at the base of the pyramid or on higher floors if it has 2 dice underneath it. On each floor of the pyramid that the dice are placed, the player gains a bonus that allows them to manipulate the dice that are already in the pyramid (turn 180°, roll again, etc). In this way, they try to have a pyramid with dice that corresponds to the public objectives of each card (having only even-value dice, having only increasing values, etc.). If you succeed, at the end of the game you win the points that could give you victory. Each game box can only hold 2 players. But if you add another box, you can play with 3-4 players.

—description from the publisher

name: Courses & Clubs
description: Courses & Clubs is a 1-4 player, narrative, golf Simulator/RPG (Role Playing Game) that takes place on a imaginary golf course. You can create your player or play as one of many legendary, fictional and real golfers!  In Courses & Clubs you are a golfer playing through a round of golf (18 holes) trying to achieve the lowest score possible!  You can also gain XP to improve your golfing skills!  Simple to play but detailed in it's percentages, Courses & Clubs brings golf to the tabletop unlike any before!

name: Call of Duty: The Board Game
description:
Call of Duty: The Board Game brings the acclaimed Call of Duty experience to tabletops, immersing players in intense competitive combat. Play on authentic Call of Duty maps such as Shoot House or Standoff. Choose from operators like Ghost Riley or Captain Price. Select your favorite weapons and items. Build a custom combat deck with your signature tactics. Then, jump into the action.

Each round, make tough choices as you secretly and simultaneously plan your actions. Will you boldly engage the enemy head on? Or perhaps you can outmaneuver and sneak up on them? Maybe they are hiding in that building; throw a grenade in the window and find out! Or take a risk, and run for the flag to seize it.

After planning, the action unfolds with explosive surprises. Combat is quick and deadly, with intense tactical choices. Will you unload your magazine recklessly? Maybe you prefer to take the time to aim carefully? Or will you dodge and outmaneuver your foe? If you get eliminated, simply respawn immediately back into the action.

Want more? Combine both core sets for an unprecedented four-player experience. Expansions add new maps, operators, weapons, game modes, and more.

name: Cows in Space
description:
Cows In Space is an udderly hilarious adventure that blasts family fun into orbit! It features magnet-powered cows and zany alien challenges designed to delight players of all ages.

Take Moo To Your Leader: Perfect for family game night, this game has one simple goal: get your cows outta the farm, STAT!

How to play:
Use your headband to collect as many magnetic cows as possible. Each cow must be delivered outside of the farm. If cow tipping occurs, reset the game. The player with the most cows at the end wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Coyote
description:
Each card has an action and a word. Lay out a line of cards and take turns, performing and saying each card. Add “coyote” cards to sabotage the other players and make the game harder. Mess up the sequence, and you're out.

The last player standing wins! Unleash your trickster spirit with a game that's fast, chaotic, and different every time you play.

—description from the publisher

name: Cozy Hut
Crafting the Cosmos
publisher: Office Dog; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
In Crafting the Cosmos, you are interstellar architects, competing to build the galaxy – one star at a time. Manipulate the laws of the universe to your advantage, shifting gravity or the flow of time to activate useful power cards, and even spawn advanced life that can earn you extra victory points at the end of the game. Use your resources wisely as you craft your cosmic creation.

Each round consists of each player taking a turn, which then is followed by shared end phase. A player's turn consists of two phases: energy and craft. Players takes their turns moving energy on the main board and gaining resources. They then spend their resources to craft their galaxy.

During the energy phase, you move energy tokens around the controls on the main board to gain resources for crafting your cosmos. Then during the collect resources phase, you gain the resources from the one active control space with your energy token, then from all four of the passive control spaces.

Once a player has collected all of their resources, they spend them during the craft phase in any order to craft their galaxy. You may take placement actions, scoring actions, energy card actions, and slider actions in any order. You may place the four standard kinds of stars: hydrogen (H), helium (He), carbon (C), and oxygen (O), place proto life, or even nebulae.

Players can spend energy cards to gain power cards to help them craft their cosmos more effectively, and they compete to complete universal goals.

—description from the publisher

name: Craftsmen: Think and Write
description:
Do you have what it takes to become the most successful entrepreneur in the kingdom? In this roll and write game, you will build your own production chain of buildings. You will collect the raw materials and process them to half-finished goods and finished products. You will also transport your products to the city, where you can sell them to various customers, from various places such as the shipyard, the tavern, the stronghold, and the monastery. But be careful, because you will have to compete with other players which are also sending goods to the same city as you and only the first players who manage to deliver needed goods will gain the victory points for them!

Craftsmen Roll and Write is a game designed for heavy gamers who enjoy strategic and economic challenges. Each game lasts about 60 minutes, and in each round you will do various things: acquire raw resources, build and upgrade your buildings like woodworks, blacksmith, bakery, process the materials to make goods and final products from various ingredients and sending them to customers in the city. Game consist of two kind of game boards, one shared between players from where they can acquire raw material and send products to, and one private one where they manage the resources, build and upgrade their buildings, and process materials to make various products.

The game ends after a fixed number of rounds. The player with the most Victory Points wins the game. Craftsmen Roll and Write is a game of planning, optimization, and adaptation. Will you become the richest and most influential entrepreneur in the kingdom?

—description from the designer

name: Crash & Grab
description: Re-live your favorite old school action game in a battle royale where you’ll race around the board in your flying saucer grabbing Crewmembers, Energy, and Boosters while avoiding – or crashing into – other saucers. You'll use all of these types of movement to navigate the board: programmed, hidden, and tactical combo movement. Use the Energy you’ve collected to buy Upgrades for your ship so you can build your strategy around them. The first player to get a Pilot, Engineer, Doctor, and Scientist wins!

name: Chang'an
description:
During the Tang dynasty, Chang'an was one of the largest cities in the world. It was a cosmopolitan urban center with thousands of travelers exploring it. As an important urbanist, compete against other players to build the best districts of Chang'an and to get the favors of the court.

Players will carefully project their plans by placing cards on the top part of their personal boards (the gates). Then they will move them into the city districts to build amazing buildings and to welcome influential characters in the neighborhood. Every new card built into the districts will provide players with different types of privileges and a certain number of victory points.

During your turn, you perform only one of the three main actions: research, play and/or move cards on the gates to produce resources and activate character effects, or build.

The game ends as soon as a player gets nine or more cards built in the districts of their City board (cards at the gates are not considered).

The player with the most victory points will be declared the best urbanist of Chang’an.

name: Crazy Museum
description:
The night falls over the Grand Museum and its incredible collection of relics. It's time to take action to get your hands on them and prove that you are the best thief in the world. But be careful! Not only must you avoid their tireless guards, but also the terrible mummy that roams lost in the Grand Museum, defeating anyone who crosses its path... Can you be the fastest thief and escape unscathed from the Grand Museum?

Crazy Museum is a competitive game for one to four players. The goal of each player is to collect the most relics without getting caught. To achieve this, you'll need to manage a pool of actions to find various objects scattered throughout the museum, use different power-ups available from vending machines, and feed cheese to your rat friend to help hinder your opponents.

—description from the publisher

name: Crease
description: Crease is a board game wearing the skin of a card game. In this asymmetrical / strategic / push-your-luck, players face off to out maneuver each other, trap one another in dead ends, break through defenses, build suspense, and execute clever decisions to find their way to victory.

name: Cretaceous Rails
description:
Travel back in time to the Cretaceous era, build a rail network into the jungle, take time-traveling tourists on safari to see their favorite dinosaurs in the wild, and build a resort full of attractions to customize your strategy with exciting abilities.

Cretaceous Rails features an innovative dual-action worker placement system, route building, tableau building, and resource management. Utilize the resources of the Cretaceous jungle to build the optimal combination of attractions for abilities and scoring.

—description from the publisher

name: Cricket Champions
description:
It's a light strategy game with a touch of luck. Players take on the role of one of eight cricket teams competing in a championship. In each round, players bat and bowl one over using six dice. As the game progresses, players gain experience, allowing them to enhance their skills. The game lasts for five rounds (45-60 minutes) and offers four different ways to earn winning points.


    Game does not require cricket knowledge to play.


-description from publisher

name: Crime at Home: Bega Case
description:
In Crime at Home: Bega Case, you will find yourself tasked with solving the mystery behind an attempted murder. David survived a poisoning, but the culprit is still at large and will strike again unless you find him first.

Escape game that turns you into a detective. Using both physical and digital materials, players will act as real detectives, following the narrative, solving escape room-style riddles, and investigating clues to uncover the truth.

—description from the publisher

name: Crisps!
description:
Crisps is a ladder-climbing card game for 2 players. Crisps selects and recombines ingredients from several climbing games to serve up as a light & delicious snack that will leave you craving for more.

Players attempt to be the first person to empty their hand of cards. Like many climbing/shedding games, players can play single cards, sets, runs, or runs of pairs.

The following player must play same rank or higher to beat the previous meld. After someone passes, players then must draw a card. The trick winner gets to pick a card first either face-up or from a face-down pile and then the trick loser has to draw the other card.

There are special combos which can be led, played over other special combo types, or played over the highest ranked single/sets.

—description from the designer

name: If Then
description:
If Then is a game of co-operative pattern solving.

One player is the knower, who reads the custom rule for the round, and tells the other players whether their guesses are right or wrong. Everyone else is a guesser; they take turns choosing a card from a display and placing it in the line as a guess. The guessers win if they successfully shed all of the cards from their hand before running out of cards in the draw pile.

Custom rules may be based on the size, value, and/or color of the number and background. Higher level cards offer more complex challenges.

—description from the publisher

name: Raas: A Dance of Love
description:
Step into Raas: A Dance of Love, a game on the dance style of Garba Raas where color, rhythm, and tradition come to life.

Raas is a dazzling folk dance from the Gujarat state in India. In this game of dice drafting and tableau building you will lead your dance academy to glory one dance at a time.

Recruit dancers, represented by colorful dice, where each color and pip shows off their style and rhythm. Collect stunning dresses, give your dancers dandiya sticks, and match the style of the song to create performances that shine!

The board consists of seven disks connected by a gear mechanism. Each disk has six dancers (dice) specializing in different tempos and styles of this energetic Gujarati dance form. Players draft dancers from the central dance floor to train their own personal dance troupe. Plan your moves to matchmake amongst the dancers to go up the love track and earn powerful bonuses.

Points can be scored by matching the tempo of the song each round, meeting devotion goals, outfitting your dance troupe with dresses and dandiya sticks, and ensuring that they are capable of the whole breadth of possible dance styles and tempos. Whoever creates the best dance troupe wins!

name: Crops
description:
In Crops, you take on the role of a farmer, cultivating your own field by carefully selecting crops and goals to achieve the best harvest possible. But beware, nature plays a crucial role: the Moon Phases
influence your field’s yield and determine your final score. Which of the four Moon Phases will shape your strategy? Plan wisely, maximize your combinations of Crop Family Symbols and goals, and become the greatest farmer!

The game is played over 12 turns. Each turn, you must play a Crop Card in your Field, at the end of each turn, you may also optionally play a Goal Card at the top or bottom of one of the columns in your Field.
At the end of the twelfth turn, your Field must consist of exactly 3 columns, each containing 4 Crop Cards, and up to 6 Goal Cards.
Once all players have completed their Field, it’s time to harvest and calculate the final score.
You will earn Victory Points in four different ways: Dominant Moon Phase in your Field, Crop Family Symbols, Upper Goal Cards, and Lower Goal Cards.

—description from the publisher

name: Cross Bronx Expressway
description:
Cross Bronx Expressway is the third game in the Irregular Conflicts Series. It simulates the socio-economic processes of urban development, and the human costs that result, as a competitive city-builder with collective loss conditions. Players control one of three asymmetric factions working in the South Bronx between 1940 and 2000, pursuing their own goals while cooperating to keep the borough viable. Through a card driven sequence of play, they will work to solve the economic challenges facing the area by building infrastructure and organizations, forming coalitions, mitigating the multitude of issues facing the vulnerable population, and managing resources to stay out of debt. Cross Bronx Expressway offers an engaging way to learn about the recent history of American cities, as exemplified by Jane Jacobs’ pivotal work The Death and Life of Great American Cities, simulated through the case study of the South Bronx. Players will experience the conflicting incentives and complex factors shaping urban life, and together determine the fate of the Bronx.

The gameplay is driven by a deck of event cards which determines turn order, and then players spend resources to take actions on map spaces. The game ends after the event deck is exhausted, or earlier if certain conditions are met. Players score victory points at regular periods during the game, and the player with the most points at the end of the game wins (unless an auto-loss condition for all players is met).

—description from the publisher

name: Crossfire Sector
description:
Crossfire Sector is developed as a 15 mm scale skirmish game, but can be played in any scale with the miniatures already available. The game takes up little space, is fast to setup and play, but features different Factions, missions and also a campaign mode.

6 Factions with different abilities and style

Optional Commanders to lead the Factions

Print and Play Faction cards and Battlefield

Pre-made or custom campaigns

Zombie defense mode

1 or 2 players

—description from the designer

name: Crosswhords!
description:
In Crosswhords! players cooperatively construct a barred crossword, a crossword where heavy lines drawn along grid squares separate words instead of black squares.

Players start with an empty grid. They devise a list of categories and then enter a word or phrase in the middle of the grid.

On your turn, you think of a word that fits in one of the categories and in the grid. If the other players guess your word, you write it down in the grid. If not, you give the other players a clue by writing a related word in the grid.

Everyone wins if there's a word or phrase in the grid for each of the categories.

—description from the designer

name: Crown & Courage
description:
The Germans have invaded Norway. The royal family must escape across the rugged countryside, evading capture at every turn. Will the king defy German demands for surrender, or will he find a way to escape, inspiring hope for Norway's freedom?

Crown & Courage is a solitaire-only game,  bringing clever, low-randomness eurogame-inspired mechanisms together with a fresh, new perspective provided by the best wargamer traditions of illustrating history's unique challenges through evocative gameplay.

—description from the designer

name: Crown Battles: Claim the Throne
description:
The King is dead, and you and your friends try to claim the empty throne. You will be fighting for the crown through various rounds. The goal is to score the highest points by the end of the round and claim the coveted crown.

In Crown Battles: Claim the Throne, players face different goals each round, such as completing missions or forming alliances. Special Ability cards add strategic depth, offering actions like stealing coins or changing the trump suit. The player with the highest score at the end is crowned the ultimate sovereign.

name: Crownfell
description:
The monarchy has crumbled. The realm is in chaos. Alliances are formed and shattered as the remnants of meagre factions contend for the seat of power.

Crownfell is a dynamic abstract strategy game played with eight cards on a 5x5 grid. Each card represents a character with unique movement and special rules.

In each game, players draft four out of a pool of 17 unique characters, resulting in a very different game each time. Their asymmetrical abilities and movement lead to surprising and dramatic moments. Capture all your opponent's pieces to win.

In Crownfell, nothing is permanent... including a strong lead. Move onto the centre space to rally your allies or resurrect the fallen. Captured cards can be revived from the discard pile by either player. In this game, defeated pieces can switch sides!

—description from the designer

name: Crumbs!: The Sandwich Filler Game
description:
“It’s the lunchtime rush at your cafe and you have a queue of hungry customers!Can you serve enough sandwiches in time to keep them all satisfied?”

Stack ingredient cards, make sandwiches, and serve your customers to complete their orders and refresh your actions. If you run out of actions your customers will leave and give you a bad review!

Crumbs! The Sandwich Filler Game is a cute and compact (but challenging) solo/co-op microgame for 1-2 players. With a variable setup, quick playtime (10-20 mins), and satisfying gameplay, Crumbs! is a game that'll leave you hungry for more!

With only five actions each round to serve a sandwich, use them efficiently to make multiple sandwiches at once and keep your counter well-stocked. Each sandwich served resets your actions, but run out and your customers will leave and give you a bad review! Complete orders to reveal your next customers, and clear your queue to win the game.

'Crumbs!' also includes optional additional rules for 'Quirky Customers' to add another challenge to the game.

-description from publisher

name: Crusade: Road To Jerusalem
description:
In the Year of Our Lord 1096, the cry of Deus Vult! echoed across Europe. Pope Urban II’s call to liberate Jerusalem summoned thousands from ironclad knights, ambitious nobles, grizzled veterans, and barefoot pilgrims clutching wooden crosses. While united in religious purpose, the Crusaders were divided by cultural rivalries, conflicting interests, and the hardships of medieval campaigning.

In Crusade: Road to Jerusalem, you represent the overall leader of this coalition. The Franks bring raw strength, the Normans bold cunning, the Byzantines political influence, and the common pilgrims unshakable faith. But each walks a different path, and it will take a steady hand to guide them. Shortages, rivalries, and the grinding hardships of the march will test your leadership at every step.

The journey will test your ability to manage resources, choose strategic routes, and respond to political and military challenges. Along the way you will negotiate alliances, conduct sieges, endure hostile terrain, and strive to keep the Crusade united until you stand before the walls of Jerusalem  or see the expedition dissolve into failure.

—description from the publisher

name: Crusades
description:
1099 A.D. Crusaders conquer Jerusalem, setting the worlds ablaze. 
This city, sacred to all, instead of becoming a symbol of unity it became a symbol of endless war. The armies of two Gods rally their strenghts. 
The Christians hold the newly formed Crusader states but the Muslim warriors, fierce and unrelenting, are ready to reclaim their lands. 
But the outcome of the battles in the Holy Lands cannot be easily forseen. 
Will you emerge victorious or will you be forgotten in the sands of time?

Crusades is a card-driven (semi cooperate) light wargame depicting the series of religious wars between Christians and Muslims to control the holy lands. Each player takes the roles of Christian and Muslim leaders with objective to siege, conquer cities and fight to control the christian kingdoms of Cilician Armenia and Eastern Roman Empire (Byzantio). Also at the same time they must defend their imperial cities from their enemies.
Τhe game lasts 7 rounds and in each round two historical event cards determine the conditions and the battles of the game.

At the end of the game

     the control of Jerusalem 
     the number of objective cities conquered
     the number of winning battles 
     the influence/control of the christian kingdoms of Cilician Armenia and Eastern Roman Empire 


are compared and the side with the most wins the game!!!

Strategize wisely, it's the only way to control the Holy Lands !!!

name: Cryptborn
description:
Cryptborn is a solo roll-and-write dungeon crawler that is inspired by Darkest Dungeon and the souls-like genre.

You awake from your eternal slumber in the crypt of the castle, something or someone has awoken you from death to purge the castle of the dark forces that have befallen it.

In Cryptborn, you'll design a dungeon by rolling a D6 and then populate it with encounters. Once that's done, you'll run the dungeon and try to survive.

Each dungeon will have a boss but the goal isn't always to kill the biggest, baddest thing in the dungeon but instead to simply survive to get through to the next stage. In this game, 'winning' means staying alive.

—description from the publisher

name: Cryptid Cafe: The Chef's Apprentice
description:
Welcome to Cryptid Cafe: The Chef's Apprentice! This game is set in the same universe as the popular Cryptid Cafe. This time around, instead of serving customers in the front-of-house, we’ll be venturing into the back-of-house, where players will take command of their cryptid line cook with aspirations of becoming a chef someday. However, before putting on that glorious white chef’s hat, they must first become…The Chef’s Apprentice.

Each turn, you and your fellow players will choose monstrous food dishes from the main chef's table board and plate them in your own tableau format. Your placement, preparation, and garnishing skills will determine how well you satisfy the customers' requests and earn their praise. Your cryptid line cook's expertise will also come in handy as you prepare dishes. However, be warned of challenges from the Kraken Chef, who will test your skills and separate you from the pretenders.

The player who earns the most praise from the customers and our resident Chef wins the game.

Are you ready to become The Chef's Apprentice?

—description from the designer

name: Crystalla
description:
In Crystalla, you want to create a valuable arrangement of seven types of crystals: rubies, tourmalines, diamonds, and more.

You start with a tableau on which you will eventually place twelve crystal cards. These cards are divided into two shimmering segments that show different colored types of gemstones. Each crystal is scored in a different way and is worth more or fewer points either separately, together, or arranged in a certain pattern. An interactive selection mechanism not only determines the cards to be placed, but also sometimes distributes additional crystal pieces that further enhance your own work of art by covering a segment — or clouding over the crystal-clear structure of other players.

Whether with a sparkling row of diamonds or shimmering emerald flowers, who will create the work of art that scores the most points?

name: Philharmonix
description:
Step into the role of a space orchestra manager with Philharmonix, the worker placement game that combines music and sci-fi in an out-of-this-world experience!
