Send your orchestra on missions to perform on different planets, strategically acquire new talented musicians, and train them to reach their full potential. Please the patrons that sponsor these concerts with your performances, and watch out for unexpected challenges along the way.

In Philharmonix, you play as a space orchestra manager, trying to become the most prestigious orchestra in the Malaya sector.
Each turn, you will select one of the 6 major actions or the basic move action. The basic action is to move across the Malayan planets or to gain money. The major actions include: recruiting musicians, training musicians & conductors, creating symphonies, performing Symphonies, gaining patrons, and expanding your knowledge and experience. During your turn, you can also perform free actions to manipulate your gameplay.

Each action consumes action points which would be randomized every round and could consume more action points if the action is
occupied. Thus, players need to be efficient in selecting their actions.

Players can gain Prestige in many ways, but mainly from performing Symphonies and recording “Records” (objectives). Other
methods of gaining Prestige are region majority, collecting musicians, and claiming patrons.

The game ends after five rounds and the player with the most Prestige is the winner of the game and is proclaimed the best space orchestra manager!

—description from the publisher

name: CUBE Creatures
description:
The Fast, Fun, Collectible Battle Card Game Your Kids Will Love!

Ages 6+ (fun for all)
5 minutes to learn (hours of fun)
15 minutes to play
1v1 head-to-head play
Easy travel single deck

Unleash wild power cards. Outmaneuver with strong defenders. Change your fate with a single roll.

Swap battlefields. Destroy or resurrect creatures. Dodge attacks with a lucky roll or double your damage with a perfect one. Outwit your opponent by switching defenders, sneaking past their guard, or powering up with magic at just the right moment. Every move can turn the tide!

—description from the publisher

name: Cuckoo Shuffle: Sharks & Frogs
description:
Cuckoos love to hide and trick everyone! Get the animals in the right order to foil their plans!

Race to get your animals in the right order to claim the trophy. You'll need to listen carefully and act quickly to beat the competition.

Each player has 4 cards: 2 Sharks and 2 Frogs in a face-down pile in front of them.

The active player for the turn names the 4 cards in any order, for example "Shark, Frog, Shark, Frog".

All players, including the active player, race to grab their cards, reorder them, place the cards down in that order, and grab the trophy card from the center. Play continues until one player wins two turns in a row.

name: Cultivo
description:
Grow, Build, Flourish.

It’s the early 18th century. The once swampy Ebro Delta has been made arable by canals.
Now, fertile fields yield rich harvests, and small villages flourish.
In Cultivo you assign workers, trade your crops at the market for equipment, and construct buildings to develop your reputation and expand your possibilities strategically.
The innovative market mechanism makes crop trading a central tactical element.
The variable game board adds further variety – no two games are the same. With each step, your influence grows – and so do your chances of victory.
A scenic strategy game with tactical depth and Mediterranean  air.

—description from the publisher

name: Ancient Empires
description:
Ancient Empires is an action-programming, area-control, civilization game of expansion, conquest, and cunning decisions. In just a small box, it packs the feel of an epic empire-building experience.

Players take the role of rising civilizations, competing for dominance across a modular map divided into regions rich with resources, settlements, and natural wonders. Through clever programming of action tokens, players expand their armies, establish cities, harvest resources, and challenge rivals for control of key territories.

The game is divided into three Ages. During the Stone Age, the players will play as roaming tribes, establishing villages and expanding their reach. In the Bronze Age, the players will choose one of the available Civilizations to play with, gaining unique abilities. Finally, in the Iron Age, the players will be able to construct their Wonders.

The game is driven by an action-programming system. Each round, players secretly choose and place order tokens (such as Grow, Move, Build/Improve, Produce, or Attack) into a shared sequence. When revealed, these actions are resolved in turn, creating interaction, tension, and opportunities for clever timing. Success depends not only on which actions you choose, but also on anticipating and reacting to the choices of others.

The game uses a streamlined area-control system where units don’t fight individually but exert influence through their presence and special abilities, making every movement and attack a tactical puzzle. Technologies, events, and wonders add layers of strategy, while asymmetric civilizations grant unique abilities that push players to adapt their playstyles.

Despite its compact size, Ancient Empires delivers the tension and depth of a full-scale empire game, playable in around an hour. It is part of the Empires Series by Archona Games, continuing the legacy of Small Empires series and expanding into new historical settings.

—description from the publisher

name: Cupcake Dragon
description:
Dragons love two things.

Sleeping on huge piles of treasure and eating delicious treats... Especially cupcakes!

Frosted. Chocolate. Cupcakes.

As the mayor of your village, you are duty-bound to provide your citizens protection. And as it happens, the absolute best way to secure that protection is to use cupcakes and loot to entice a dragon to come live in your village.

BUT REMEMBER:
Dragons eat quite a lot and your treasure better be piled high for maximum comfort!

—description from the publisher

name: Cute and Aggressive Capybaras
description:
Step into the world of Cute and Aggressive Capybaras, where you become a mischievous capybara journeying through the forest in search of fruit. 


You’ll visit Hot Baths, collect (or even steal) Fruit, use powerful Items, and navigate unexpected Events on your quest. Whoever collects all the
Fruit and returns to the Sacred Hot Spring wins!

Be the first capybara to gather all Fruit cards from every Hot Bath tile (or steal them from other players) and make it back to the Sacred Hot Spring tile to claim victory!

—description from the publisher

name: CVLT
description:
CVLT is a competitive trick-taking game with a unique drafting mechanism.

After each trick, each player starting from the winner chooses a card from that trick. This card can be placed face-up in the player's offerings tableau or face-down in their dreams pile.

At the end of the round, cards from the offering tableau are added to the temple, and score points if every card of lower value in that suit has already been added to the temple.

Players also gain points by meeting the conditions of vision cards.

—description from the publisher

name: The Great Harbor
description:
Build your Roman colony in the Mediterranean, trade and engage with the Great Harbor of Carthage, construct mighty trading ships to trade with the cities along the Mediterranean, and fight the Cilician pirates in this dice drafting, worker placement game for 2-4 players!

In The Great Harbor, you play as a powerful Roman governor of a Mediterranean colony. The game is played over multiple rounds where players will draft dice from a common dice pool, and will use those dice as workers to place them on the tiles of the Great Harbor to play the corresponding actions. In order to place a die on a certain slot, the die must match the color of the slot of the tile. The die power (ranging from 1 to 6) will determine the strength of your action on that tile. Once someone places a die on a slot, that slot is taken, and no other dice may be placed there until the end of the round.

The actions that can be played include: gaining resources that are important for shipbuilding, scheduling workers to work on building the ships, increasing your colony capacity to dock ships and population, sending your ships to trade along the Mediterranean and be on the lookout for pirates, hire special workers and diplomats and more.

The game ends after six rounds after which victory points from the constructed ships, buildings, senate influence, and objectives are then calculated, and the player with the most points is the winner of the game and proclaimed the most powerful governor of the Mediterranean!

—description from the publisher

name: CyberQuest: The Game of Cyberpunk Adventures
description:
You are in the year 2081. The Black Chip agency, formed by members who participated in the Second Corporate Conflict on both sides, try to avoid a third conflict between Nakaware and Biosync. 
Max, an employee at Nakaware, discovers a confidential file that could spark a war. He contacts his sister Raven and meets her in an old warehouse, away from Neon City, to explain her what he is up to.

Cyberquest is a narrative cyberpunk adventure game for 1 to 5 players. You play in 3 different phases: Mission phase, chase phase and den phase.

Mission Phase: Advance with your runner through a dungeon crawler-style scenario in which anything can happen in every room.

Chase Phase: Escape the site driving your car into den. A mini-game in which you draw event cards with the objetive to finish the route.

Den Phase: Heal your wounds, upgrade your cyberware, get jobs and repair your car. A little maintenance to prepare you for the next mission.

—description from the publisher

name: Heroes of Might and Magic: Battles
description:
Collect, build and paint your favorite Heroes of Might and Magic armies, before pitting them against your enemies in a battle for Erathia. Play like never before in this “rank and file” wargame designed by Jervis Johnson (Warhammer 40k, Fantasy Battles, AoS) & Andy Chambers (Starship Troopers, Warhammer 40k, Fantasy Battles), and produced by the same team that brought you HoMM III: The Board Game.

Heroes of Might & Magic: Battles is a tabletop wargame that brings the iconic Heroes of Might and Magic experience to life. Players assume the roles of Enroth's heroes, leading armies of intricately sculpted miniatures in strategic battles to expand their kingdoms and defeat enemies. The game captures the essence of the original PC game, offering a visually stunning and accessible experience that appeals to both newcomers and seasoned players.

The gameplay focuses on building and commanding armies, with each unit and hero possessing unique abilities that reflect their in-game roles. The rules promote dynamic, interactive battles where timing and strategy are key, with heroes playing a central role in enhancing their troops. Players can customize their armies from various factions, ensuring endless replayability in a game that masterfully blends classic wargaming with modern design.

—description from the publisher

name: Cábalas
description:
In Cábalas, you'll explore vibrant Latin American traditions that promise a New Year filled with luck and prosperity. Are you ready to test your superstitions and dodge any Bad Vibes? Complete your Cábalas before time runs out and see who ends up the luckiest!

The objective is to score the most Luck Points by the end of the game. Each round, players follow three suspenseful steps. First, each player secretly declares which Cábala (or Bad Vibe) card they’ll play or what card they need to fulfill their Cábala’s requirement. Bluffing is fair game here, and it can really shake things up!

After the declarations, it’s time for the big reveal: all players simultaneously show their cards. Then, it’s checked whether a) the Bad Vibes have been cleared, or b) if someone successfully slipped in a Bad Vibe card to disrupt the others. Finally, it’s confirmed who managed to fulfill their Cábalas'z'.

Play your lucky underwear solo, synchronize an Embrace with another player, eat grapes together for an even-numbered total, or burn effigies for an odd-numbered outcome—each Cábala brings a fun, tradition-filled twist that can change your fortune!

—description from the publisher (translated)

En “Cábalas”, te sumergirás en las tradiciones latinoamericanas que prometen un año nuevo lleno de prosperidad y buena fortuna. ¿Estás listo para poner a prueba tus supersticiones y esquivar las Malas Vibras? Cumple tus Cábalas antes de que el tiempo se agote y descubre quién será el más afortunado de todos.

El objetivo es acumular la mayor cantidad de Puntos de Suerte al final de la partida. En cada ronda, los jugadores deberán seguir tres pasos llenos de emoción y estrategia. Primero, cada jugador anuncia en secreto la carta de Cábala (o de Mala Vibra) que va a jugar o la carta que necesita para completar la condición de su Cábala. ¡En este momento, el bluff está permitido y puede cambiar el curso del juego!

Después de los anuncios, llega el momento de la verdad: todos los jugadores revelan sus cartas al mismo tiempo. Entonces, se comprueba si a) lograron despejar las Malas Vibras, o si b) alguien jugó con éxito una carta de Mala Vibra, alterando los planes de los demás. Finalmente, se verifica quiénes han logrado cumplir sus Cábalas.

Desde jugar tu calzón de la suerte en solitario, coordinar un Abrazo en sincronía con otro jugador, comer uvas en grupo sumando números pares, o quemar muñecos para obtener impares, cada Cábala trae un giro divertido y lleno de tradición.

—description from the publisher

name: Códicus
description: Códicus is a fast-paced deduction game for up to 6 players where you race to crack your unique 6-digit code using logic and clever clue-asking. Be the first to solve it all and win!

name: D-Day Dice: Pacific
description:
D-Day Dice: Pacific is the newest entry into the D-Day Dice franchise. Following on from D-Day Dice - 2nd Edition, which featured the Normandy Landings, this stand-alone expansion centers on the Pacific/South Asian Theater, with new maps, new card types, and a new roster of Specialists, Items, Awards and Vehicles.

In D-Day Dice: Pacific, players not only fight against the enemy, they are also at war with the environment. The game reflects the realities of tropical warfare by offering battlefields that are both dangerous and unpredictable. Its Battle Maps include new features like rivers to cross, cave maps to explore, and infested sectors that can make your specialists sick. The game also includes “Strike” cards, a deck that simulates naval and aerial bombardments from both the Allies and the Axis, with all the dangers associated with friendly fire and collateral damage.

As with all other editions of D-Day Dice, all content here is backwards and forward compatible with all previous and upcoming D-Day Dice games. You do not need any previous DDD products to enjoy this game. The box contains everything you need to play.

—description from the publisher

name: D-Day to The Rhine 1944 (Campaigns in Europe Volume 4)
description:
Campaigns in Europe (CIE) is a two-player series of games focused on campaign scenarios at the division/corps level. The system uses the same maps as War in Europe (WIE), with updated graphics and a more detailed terrain analysis. The counters have been upgraded and are presented with historical identifications. The game system utilizes a Move/Fight, Fight/Move sequence of play to portray simply doctrinal differences among contending armed forces. It also utilizes headquarters units to project logistics and combat support capabilities.

D-Day to the Rhine covers the campaign in France, from after the Allied landings at Normandy through the drive to the Rhine. It ends at the completion of Operation Market-Garden.

Each game turn (GT) represents around one week in clear weather and two weeks in mud and snow game turns. Each hex represents 20 miles (32.5 km) across. German, Finnish, and Western Allied units are shown mostly as division-sized units, with Soviet and Axis Allied units depicted as corps.

name: DadOpoly
description:
A classic combination of our two favorite things - being dads and playing games!

DadOpoly is a new and unique version of the classic that follows a dad's journey through fatherhood.  From a house on Single Street to a hotel on College Court, DadOpoly is all fun and games (as long as you are not on Diaper Duty).  The images are original, the cards are funny and the properties really hit home, making this a family friendly game that is loads of fun for all to play.

name: Dame Nature
description:
You are the artisans shaping a living web of nature, from the tiniest grasses to the mightiest predators.

Use your Symbiosis cards to share information with your teammates, plan your Condition or Species cards and work together to create the fabric of life!
This cooperative game of collective adaptation offers 13 distinct modes for a unique experience each time.
The basic rules are casual and family-friendly, while the game evolves into a more expert experience through the 12 themed modes.

In partnership with France Nature Environnement.

—description from the publisher

name: DANTE: Inferno
description:
DANTE: Inferno is a new experience based on the famous Italian poem: The Divine Comedy by Dante Alighieri. Find, in this new adventure, a fusion of exploration, through the various circles of Hell, and epic battles against hordes of enemies in the best war game style. Devise the safest route to your objectives, or explore the most challenging corners of this dark realm. Engage in fierce battles and strategize using your surroundings.

Dante: Inferno is a cooperative Boss Battler and Narrative game. Players will gather in a Caravan to explore a world inspired by the work “The Divine Comedy – Inferno”. Through 9 Chapters, one dedicated to each Circle of the Inferno, the players will experience an original narrative that takes place at the dawn of the 16th Century. Dante takes on the role of mentor and will guide the adventurers. They will discover places, characters, and events immortalized in the masterpiece.

Players move through each of the 9 levels in order and choose the game mode they want to experience Dante:Inferno – Quick Combat or Campaign.  In the Quick Campaign mode: players skip straight to the Three-Dimensional Tactical Combat Phase, the Confrontation.

name: Dark Blood
description:
Dark Blood plunges players into the abyss of darkness, where they embody powerful asymmetrical cults striving for dominance over a hapless village. Whether as the cult of the Demonologist, Warlock, Necromancer, or Doomsayer, players must adeptly recruit villagers or harvest their blood to empower their sinister rituals.

Through a fusion of Area Majority, Worker placement and Resource gathering, they vie with one another, navigating the perilous path of corruption, enhancing their Rituals, and staining various parts of the village to seize territories and augment their Taint (Victory Points). With each round introducing fresh challenges and opportunities, players must judiciously balance their strategies to outmaneuver their adversaries and emerge as the foremost cult as the fifth round draws to a close.

During each round, players delve into their Ritual Book, serving as their player board, to oversee their Cultists, amass Resources, and upgrade their Rituals. The main board grants access to the five pivotal locations where the four cults will contend for control, eventually corrupting them.


    During the Upkeep phase, these locations undergo random variations in the number of available Peasants, the resources they yield and more... 
    In the Placement phase, all cults place their workers (Cultist Miniatures) in these locations, determining the actions their cult can execute in each one. The majority in each location dictates not only special actions but also the initiative in which these actions will unfold. 
    In the Resolve phase, each cult assigns their cultists to diverse actions, from resource gathering for Ritual upgrades to hanging peasants at the Tree of the Damned to bolster their Dark Favor. 
    In the final phase, players Defile the land and bid their accumulated Blood to dominate the most corrupted location. The number of Sigils placed by each player significantly influences the ultimate outcome. 


As the fifth round concludes, the locations you corrupted, along with other factors such as your cult's size, upgraded Rituals, secret quest, concealed Taint and more, will determine the prevailing cult.

name: Dark Heists
description:
You are a crime lord in the world of Dark Heists. Do petty larcenies and choose from monsters, hardened criminals and crooked cops to build your gang. When you’re ready, it’s time to do a heists: ambush a funeral, collect a bounty on a dangerous ghosts or pull a honey pot scam. Then you’re ready for the big time; kill a vampire, sell some hypnotic dust or get paid to resurrect a recently deceased client. But hurry, other crime lords in the city are trying to do the same thing, and they’ll stab you in the back to stop your ascent if you don’t get them first. The crime lord with the most notoriety at the end of the game, wins.

Dark Heists is a strategic deck builder game for 1 to 4 players. Ages 14 and up. Contains Mature themes.

Recruit monstrous criminals and criminal monsters to do high stakes heists in this spooky deck builder game. The first player to complete three heists triggers the final round. When the last player has taken their turn, everyone counts their notoriety from crew, heists and coins and the player with the most notoriety wins.

Dark Heists is a game of deck building and heists with crooked cops, horrific monsters and other criminals.

Heists challenge your entire crew, requiring you to draw multiple hands and meeting thematic challenges by amassing more crime or sway in your hand, than the challenge threshold. Want zombie minions to terrify the people? generate 7 Sway. Want to kill the vampire? Generate 9 Crime.

The game ends when one player completes three heists.

The player with the most notoriety, gained from heists, coins and recruits, wins.

—description from THE designer

name: Dark Kingdoms
description:
After the Romans' withdrawal in the early 5th century, Celtic rule over Britannia is seriously threatened. The fleets of Germanic peoples arriving on the eastern and southern coasts of the island are increasingly numerous. These are tribes of rugged men who worship warrior gods and choose their leaders in assemblies of equals.

The Saxons, led by Cerdic, have settled in the south.

The Angles, under the command of Eomer, are expanding their territories in the east.

The Jutes, led by the legendary Hengist, have moved north in the game setting, although historically they were found in the southeast.

The Britons, whose king is Vortigern, are the legitimate Celtic rulers of Britannia, although they are in decline and have retreated to the west.

Each of them commands armies to expand their domains and fight for the resources produced by the lands of Britannia. These resources can be invested in recruiting new troops and building villages, ships, and fortresses. But there can only be one victor, and it will be the one who demonstrates the greatest power.

—description from the publisher

name: Dark Romance
description:
Discover "Dark Romance": Unveil Love and Danger

Embark on a journey into the captivating universe of "Dark Romance," a shadowy Victorian realm teeming with love and nocturnal creatures.

Intriguing World

Immerse yourself in a world characterized by Victorian elegance and mysterious intrigue. Players assume the roles of one of ten distinct characters, each seeking profound love or their next unsuspecting victim.

Players and Duration

Designed for players aged 16 and above, "Dark Romance" offers an immersive experience for 2 individuals. With the Deluxe Edition, the game can be expanded to accommodate up to 4 players. Sessions last approximately 30-45 minutes, ensuring engaging and dynamic encounters.

Courting and Consequences

Players engage in various dates to better understand their counterparts. Keen intuition is essential, as poor decisions may not only deter true love but could also lead to one's demise. Make your choices wisely to uncover your partner's true intentions.

The Essence of the Game

At the heart of the game are role and scene cards. There are five different roles to play, each with unique objectives and intentions. Scene cards guide you through dates and shared experiences, shaping compelling narratives and strategic decisions.

"Dark Romance" is a rollercoaster of emotions, blending suspense, love, and danger. Prepare to test your tactical skills and embark on a unique social deduction experience. We promise a true gem for your collection!

Note that the deluxe edition of Dark Romance allows for up to four players in a game.

—description from the publisher

name: World of Tanks: The Card Game
description:
World of Tanks: The Card Game brings the legendary armored warfare of the video game franchise to the tabletop in a fast-paced, strategic card battle format. Developed by Archon Studio in collaboration with Wargaming, this game puts players in command of iconic tanks in tactical duels that demand careful planning, smart positioning, and a solid grasp of battlefield momentum.

At its core, World of Tanks: The Card Game is a dynamic deck-builder where you construct your arsenal from a wide variety of tanks—each with unique traits, strengths, and roles. Choose your approach: swarm the enemy with agile light tanks, unleash the raw power of heavy armor, or strike with precision from mid-range. The flexibility of the system encourages experimentation and rewards creative strategies.

Victory isn't limited to simply eliminating your opponent's forces. Multiple paths to success ensure that each match plays out differently, whether you're holding objectives, outmaneuvering your foe, or executing a well-timed combo.

Featuring immersive artwork, intuitive mechanics, and deep tactical choices, World of Tanks: The Card Game captures the thrill of tank combat in a compact, replayable format. Whether you're a longtime fan of the franchise or a newcomer to the battlefield, prepare for an explosive fight to the finish.

—description from the publisher

name: Darkest Doom
publisher: Game Start Studio; (Self-Published); Czacha Games; Fabrika Igr; Rosiness
description:
Darkest Doom is a competitive strategy game with RPG elements. Set in a dark fantasy world inspired by XVII century Europe and inhabited by anthropomorphic animals.  Will you survive for the 8 days of the Eclipse as the Darkness tries to annihilate the region of Betel all the while competing with the other Guardians to complete one of the four paths to victory?

The Darkest Doom boardgame puts you in charge of one of four formidable Guardians, each with unique abilities and traits. As you explore the areas of the region of Betel, you'll be able to take advantage of each different terrain and use its unique characteristics. You'll increase your Guardian's statistics by completing quests assigned to you by Vicar Percival, adjusting your strategy and attitude towards the game based on the stats you choose to upgrade. During your exploration, you'll also stumble onto ancient relics which will help you satisfy one of four victory conditions.

Each new round is a new Dawn, and thanks to the Citadel restock you'll always have some help as you replenish the cards in your hand, choosing them from different decks: Equipment, Spells and Traps. The same card has different effects depending on the player using it and the stats they've chosen to increase.

Play by yourself with the Bot Guardians mode, allowing you to play with up to three automated Guardians, or prove yourself by challenging three other players in this Dark Fantasy adventure combining elements of roleplay, exploration, handicap management and traditional boardgames.

name: Das Hochbeet von Schalottenburg
description:
Loud fanfares ring out through the quiet town of Schalottenburg! Vegetable athletes from all different backgrounds parade through the streets with their flags. That can only mean one thing: The annual vegetable competition is upon us! All of Schalottenburg's citizens quickly gather to cheer on their teams as they compete against each other in the earthy raised vegetable bed arena. Of course, there will be a lot of pushing and shoving again, with the aim of creating the largest possible formation of the same types of vegetables. Whoever succeeds best will lift the coveted trophy into the night sky of Schalottenburg!

Gameplay:
Take the tile in front of you and push it into the raised vegetable bed from the outside, with the vegetable side facing upwards. Then place one of your wooden markers on this tile. Take the piece you pushed out and keep it for your next turn. Continue playing until everyone has placed their last wooden marker (2 or 3 pieces). 
At the end of each round mark as many fields on your scoring boards as the number of tiles with the same type of vegetable that are directly connected to each other vertically or horizontally.

Game end:
The game ends as soon as there are only 3 or fewer face-down vegetable tiles left in the raised vegetable bed. Finish the current round and then add up the points of all the vegetable teams on your scoreboards. The winner is the player with the highest score.

name: Das wurmt
description:
Das wurmt is the short card game about long worms that get longer until they are short enough.

There are worm ends on the playing field, each with a head card in the same colour. If you turn the head, you ‘discover’ a worm appendix, which makes this worm grow longer. However, the actual ‘growth’ only becomes visible when the next head is played and the previous head is turned over again. As not all worm appendages are the same, some worms can grow faster and others slower, depending on which card is played. Worms that appear at the ‘ideal length’ earn their discoverer bonus points, while worms that are too long can be quite ‘wormy’ and result in hefty point deductions.

—description from the publisher

name: Dawn of Human: Göbeklitepe
description:
In Göbeklitepe: Dawn of Human, you start off as the leader of a hunter-gatherer tribe who discovers and makes use of tools while racing to become the biggest contributor to the first temple on Earth.

Throughout the game, you take actions via your six action totems. Each tool you acquire enhances your action totems, giving you better or more actions. You may hunt, gather, craft, learn, build, and worship to find your own unique way to victory.

—description from the designer

name: Daydream
description:
It’s time for a break!

Daydream is a cozy roll-and-write. 
Fill your cloud grid simultaneously adding the values of the dice.
Make the right choices so that each cloud line contains only different numbers. Even better, if the numbers are consecutive, you create a perfect line. However, if a number appears more than once, the line is lost.

Draw items on the shelf each time you complete a line correctly. Collect as many items as you can to win the game.

Play with constellations, musical notes, photos on the wall...
To do this, fold and unfold your board to discover new sceneries with their own specific rules. The game comes with 8 combinations for different difficulty levels.

name: Heroes of Might and Magic: The Card Game
description:
Heroes of Might and Magic: The Card Game is a two-player card game based on the internationally acclaimed video game series. Dive into the world of Erathia, where you'll command iconic Heroes, summon fearsome Monsters, and wield powerful Spells and Artifacts.

At the start of your journey, you’ll face your first primary choice: which Hero will lead your forces? Build a deck tailored to your chosen champion, develop your strategy, and prove you are the most powerful Hero in all of Erathia.

Create unique tactics, summon creatures familiar to fans of the original games, and challenge rival Heroes in tactical battles. Your faction grants you access to specific effects, while your Hero provides you powerful abilities.

Although your Hero and faction will shape your early game, the battlefield is ever-changing. As the game unfolds, powerful Artifacts and Locations may reveal new paths to victory — adapt, outsmart, and conquer!

—description from the designer

name: Master of Orion: Ad Astra
description:
Master of Orion: Ad Astra is a 4X game of space exploration and conquest. Choose from a roster of six unique races and become the leader of a spacefaring civilization. Manage the population, spearhead technological advancements, and oversee critical infrastructure development. Employ espionage to stop your rivals' advances, and should they fall short, ready your forces for conflict. In the end, the galaxy will yield to your indomitable will, one way or another.

The game is played in 6-8 rounds. Setup may vary, depending on the chosen length of the game. With experienced players, a game is expected to last about 10 minutes per round for every person playing.

At the beginning of every round, you'll engage in a technology card draft, a critical step in shaping your strategic path. You might opt for an exploration-heavy strategy, aiming to uncover and secure numerous habitable planets. Alternatively, you could adopt a more focused approach, channeling your efforts into building robust infrastructure on select, defensible systems. Regardless of your chosen path, it's imperative to familiarize yourself with the ever-changing objectives during the game.

Victory belongs to the player who amasses the highest number of victory points.

—description from the designer'

name: DC Forever
description:
In the deck-building game DC Forever, you pick two iconic characters pulled from the pages of DC Comics to form your own squad of heroes or rogues. These characters have unique powers that form the starting cards of your deck, along with basic resource cards.

During play, you recruit new characters to your team, each with unique decks and gameplay, and choose which of their cards to add to support your strategy as the game progresses. Heroes and rogues will clash at classic DC Comics locations from the shadowy alleyways of Gotham City to the subaquatic depths of Atlantis.

Rogues want to achieve their master plan by completing five schemes, but they'll be equally happy to knock out all of the heroes since no one will remain to oppose them. For their part, the heroes want to either capture all of the rogues or place thirty citizens in sanctuary; you may not be able to stop the schemes, but if people are safe, then you'll still call this a victory.

DC Forever features eighteen playable characters and hundreds of cards from which to choose during play.

name: DC Super Heroes United: Batman Hush
publisher: CMON Global Limited; Spin Master Ltd.
description:
This retail version is a standalone version of the game and it is compatible with the other boxes and it is based on the Hush Saga of the bat.

The characters included are:

4 heroes:
-Batman (classic colors: blue)
-Robin (Tim Drake)
-Huntress
-Catwoman (goggles)

1 dual mode hero:
-Superman (Poison Ivy controlled)

1 villain:
-Hush

1 villain duo:
-Joker and Harley

Villain duos are a new mechanic in United where you can fight 2 villains at the same time. You can have a taste of this new mechanic which is more exploited in the Crowdfunding exclusive "Suicide Squad" box where you can fight 2 in any combination of the 6 dual-mode characters.


Information extracted from Gamefound:

"Heroes, unite!
 
When Gotham City’s most notorious Villains start acting out of character, the Caped Crusader knows a more insidious master plan is at work, devised by the shady figure known as Hush. Batman and his allies must act together to protect the innocent, face dire threats, and confront the Villains to uncover this revenge plot. But things take a deadly turn when the Man of Steel himself falls under Poison Ivy’s mind control. The only hope of solving this mysterious case is for the Heroes to stand united!
 

As was announced before the launch of the DC Super Heroes United campaign, there will be a retail-only Core Box released separately from the crowdfunding delivery. As the new year starts, we are excited to reveal this special core box will indeed be based on the highly-acclaimed Hush comics! This will be giving people a first taste of the game on the second half of 2025."
(More details at Gamefound site)

name: De Bellis Fantasiae: Fantasy Wargame Rules
description:
DBF is a set of wargame rules that allow players to fight the great battles of fantasy literature, film, myth, or of one's own imagination, with miniature figures of between 6mm to 28mm scale, using basing that is standard across many rules.

Based on fast play mechanics drawn from Phil and Sue Barker/s famous historical rule set, De Bellis Antiquitatus, battles of a flexible size can be fought to completion within 1-3 hours.  Armies can vary, based on a points system, ranging from as few as 30 figures to over 100 for a standard sized battle.  The book is complete, and no further purchases are required to play the game.

DBF features clear diagrams throughout explaining play, a plethora of army lists, a magic system with multiple spell types, special rules for customizing the abilities of troops, and finally a suggested campaign system.

name: De Zoektocht naar El Dorado: Dobbelavontuur
description:
Deep in the dense jungle of South America lies El Dorado, the city of gold. With a specialized team, you try to tame the jungle, win the trust of the indigenous population, and find this lost city. In this roll & explore game, you must cleverly navigate the path to victory by choosing the right dice. Through four expeditions, each with its own playing field and story, you race against your fellow players for the win. Exciting, adventurous, and above all, super fun; with this dice edition of the famous board game, you will unravel the secrets of El Dorado like never before!

—description from the publisher

name: StarCraft: Tabletop Miniatures Game
description:
Using innovative mechanisms to translate the computer-game experience onto the tabletop, StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures games brings the StarCraft universe to a new medium.

A standard game sees about 30-40 models per side for the Terrans, fewer for the Protoss, and - obviously - more for the Zerg.

A brand new miniatures line is provided.

—user summary

name: Builders of Sylvan Dale
description:
After the Great Disasters, a new chapter in Sylvan Dale's history has begun. The Elders have called on you and your fellow architects to design a new woodland realm — a haven perched in the high embrace of the Great Trees. Guide the builders of Sylvan Dale as they construct dwellings, bridges, and hanging courtyards.

Builders of Sylvan Dale is a unique three-dimensional tile placement game in which you play a card and place a new building tile on top of the ever-taller trees in the forest, collecting sets of cards to gain special actions. Get your buildings to stand out high on the trees above those of your peers, and brighten the forest with your colors.

—description from the publisher

name: Death Knights
description:
Tactical minigame where players will amass their army of undead and fight with others for domination.
Every move matters, every card has its role, and one mistake can make a difference between glory and defeat.

name: Deathtouched
description:
U.S.S. Freedom is a fun, cooperative, open world, free-roaming, space-themed board game.

Explore unknown worlds, discover alien civilizations, and decide who will be your ally or your enemy. Perform missions to increase your reputation with your allies while planning for and surviving attacks from numerous other alien races. Upgrading your ship and enhancing your heroes is the key to survival.

Will you become a space merchant, trading legal—or even illegal—commodities? Are you more of a scientist, unraveling the mysteries of strange space phenomena, or maybe a hunter of dangerous monsters living on exotic planets? Will the wealth lure you into becoming a space pirate, ambushing frigates? Or will the irresistible fame from saving entire worlds lead you to engage enemy space monsters? Probably all of the above.

Sail into the vastness of space aboard the starship Freedom in its three-year quest: A fully replayable campaign that consists of 36 standalone sessions lasting 60 minutes each. In every session, you get to pilot your ship in any direction, so you choose the challenges you will engage and write your own story. No two campaigns are ever the same.

—description from the publisher

Gameplay

In a game session of U.S.S. Freedom, you continue your journey from where you left off the session before—think of it like watching a single episode of a sci-fi TV series. A game session consists of five phases.

Interstellar Phase
Set up the Interstellar Board with all the miniatures in their positions from your previous game session. Then, the various Spaceships and Titans move. If they did not move onto the same hex as your ship, then it is time for you to move.

Navigate Phase
Your ship may move toward any adjacent hex.  Your ship scanners warn you of what lies in all directions. Create the Encounter Deck by shuffling all cards of your level that belong to your adjacent sectors. Then you randomly place one card in each direction. Look at the different Encounters you have and select one to move toward.

Encounter Phase
After selecting the Encounter you will face, roll the Encounter Roll. If the Encounter is an Alien Colony or Alien Starship, add your Reputation to the result. You then flip the Encounter Card and see how it plays according to the Encounter Result and the nature of your Encounter. Some Aliens may simply attack you while others may offer you Missions.

Combat Phase
A lot of Encounters will lead to combat, whether through Missions or direct conflict. Some battles will be carried out by the U.S.S. Freedom, while in other cases your heroes will have to fight on the planet surface, in enemy bases, or even inside the U.S.S. Freedom. Sometimes battles may be carried out simultaneously with the U.S.S. Freedom fighting in space while an away team fights a ground battle.

Each kind of enemy has different abilities that they use during the battle, revealed by flipping the top chip from the stack of Enemy Ability Chips.

Luckily, your heroes also have abilities. They are used for everything from attacks on the enemies to using skills such as Engineering or Willpower. Heroes use their Aether to activate their abilities. Each player has an Aether Pouch and draws different colored Crystals representing the Aether that empowers the heroes’ Abilities.

In space combat, heroes use the Engine to produce Power and distribute it to all decks of the ship. Heroes across the ship use this Power to fly the Starship, attacking with Weapons or raising Shields.

Conclude Phase
Succeeding enables you to continue your mission. You get rewards according to the Encounter, you may trade commodities, or you may even get to upgrade your ship.

This will conclude one game session. You may pack everything into your Campaign pouch and continue another day from where you left. Or…if you have another hour, you could play just one more game session!

name: Deck EXPRESS: Tennessee Central
description:
The Tennessee Central Railway Company (TC) underwent many ownership changes over the course of its operation. During this game, each player secretly holds company shares that are gradually revealed and reacquired by other players. Building track affects the value of each company, so time your investments carefully with locomotives. The player with the most money wins the game.

Deck Express is an exciting series of railroad investment games where players purchase stocks, build track, and profit from locomotives. Each rail line features a unique train game, custom artwork, and rulebook using a standard deck of playing cards for the game components. All aboard!

name: Deckay: The Postapocalyptic Card Game
description:
Deckay is an intense, post-apocalyptic card game of combat and strategy where players face off in thrilling battles. Play in factions or engage in an all-against-all free-for-all mode as you fight to eliminate your opponents and emerge as the ultimate survivor. The game combines fast-paced action with deep tactical decisions, making each match unique and unpredictable.

In Deckay, you’ll arm yourself with powerful weapons and essential equipment like medkits and gas masks to survive the relentless chaos. Tactic cards provide strategic advantages to outsmart your enemies, while action cards bring exciting and versatile tools for battle. Adapt your strategy as the game evolves, using everything at your disposal to stay one step ahead.

The game features 15 unique characters, each with their own special ability and distinct card-carrying capacity. Whether you choose a character skilled in crafting or one with unmatched combat prowess, your choice will shape your strategy. Material cards introduce an exciting element of resource management, allowing you to craft dirty bombs or other useful tools to tip the scales in your favor.

For those seeking an even greater challenge, Deckay includes a set of challenge cards that unlock the extreme mode. These cards introduce game-wide situations that affect all players, adding an unpredictable twist to the already chaotic battlefield. No two games are ever the same, as each match brings a fresh set of challenges and opportunities.

With its blend of action, strategy, and unique character abilities, Deckay delivers an exhilarating tabletop experience where every decision counts. Are you ready to dive into the mayhem and prove your dominance?

—description from the designer

name: Perfect Mismatch
publisher: Red Cat Games; Ares Games; Broadway Toys LTD; Lifestyle Boardgames Ltd
description:
Is there anything that is equally square and non-stop, a bit absurd and hugely creative, extremely entertaining, but not washable at all? There is, and it is the PERFECT MISMATCH!

In Perfect Mismatch, players take turns explaining words to each other using pairs of mind-blowingly disparate attributes as hints. This game will test your associative thinking and ability to understand each other. Share plenty of laughs while discussing hilarious attribute combinations and the associations they trigger!

Players take turns to become the leader. Using a special tablet with cubes, the leader tries to explain their secret word to the others, evaluating it according to various completely incompatible parameters. At the same time, others try to guess the word and vote for the correct answer as quickly as possible.

Players get points by both explaining and guessing the secret words of the task cards.

—description from the publisher

name: Quartermaster General: South Front
description:
Quartermaster General: South Front is a dynamic, fast-paced game of World War II on the Mediterranean front, for two players. It takes a minute to set up and just a few more to learn.

Each player has a unique deck of cards that reflects the equipment, manpower, and strategies used by that side. The second title in the Quartermaster General Front series, this game portrays the intertwined land, air, and sea conflict.

If the Axis can keep the Allies from gaining naval superiority, they may have a chance of taking the Middle East or Gibraltar, but the Axis must act quickly, before the United States enters the war.

Quartermaster General: South Front is the second of several planned releases using the rules developed for this game.

name: TEDOKU
description:
TEDOKU is a clever and addictive “roll, flip, and write” game, that combines the logical satisfaction of Sudoku with the spatial challenges of polyomino puzzles. Designed for any number of players, TEDOKU can be played solo or as a group, as long as each player has a pencil and their own sheet.
Each player has a 9x9 grid inspired by Sudoku, and over 20 rounds, they’ll fill it using dice rolls and card draws. At the start of each round, one card is flipped and the TEDOKU die is rolled. The card designates a grid zone—a row, column, or 3x3 sector—while the die shows which polyomino shape
must be drawn.
All players use the same inputs, placing the shape so that part of it touches the indicated area. Shapes may be rotated or mirrored, but not overlap or go beyond the grid. If a player can't place it legally, they skip the round. After 20 turns, players score points for completed rows, columns, and sectors. The highest score wins, with ties broken by the  fewest empty squares.

—description from the publisher

name: Deep Regrets
publisher: Tettix Games; 2Tomatoes Games; Alis Games; asmodee; Board Bound; Board Game Circus; MS Edizioni; TLAMA games; White Goblin Games; Ігромаг
description:
Deep Regrets is an unfortunate fishing game about pulling progressively more horrifying things out of the ocean. Decide what to eat, what to sell, what to mount, and how many regrets you're willing to carry, as you push yourself too far and spiral towards a conclusion in this strategic horror fishing game.

You'll roll bespoke tackle dice at the start of each turn to determine your strength for that round and then decide whether you'll stay at sea or return to port to sell fish, buy provisions, and recharge your energy.

Survey the sizes of shadows on the backs of 9 different fish shoals at three depths, determining what you think you can afford to catch and if you want to risk it for a potentially better reward. Flip fish, spend dice, add them to your collection - but beware of reveal and catch abilities that can have various effects on the game! As your eyes spy more and more horrifying things, you'll collect Regrets cards - which drive up your madness but also give you access to more dice and increase the value of weirder fish. It's a risk/reward scenario as you balance your madness, knowing that at the end of the game the player with the highest value of Regrets will have to discard their most valuable mounted fish.

Manage your resources, make strategic decisions, leverage madness to your benefit and suppress your Regrets as you try to catch the most valuable haul of weirder and weirder fish in this weird week at sea.

SOLO MODE:
In the solo mode (which you can also co-op), you'll act as an ichthyologist on a mission to catch and catalog every fish in the sea. Over a campaign of dozens of games, you'll try to reel in every last fish and document their attributes on provided catalog sheet. At the end of each game, you'll have to discard an equal value of fish to the regrets you've collected and may have to let some fish go to return to another day. At the end of the campaign, you'll have a catalog of all fish names, depths, values and difficulties that can be used by players in the multiplayer game to help identify what they might fish up!

—description from the designer

name: Deep Space Dine
description:
Deep Space Dine, on the edge of the galaxy: surrounded by space pirates, plasma storms, and alien monsters, notorious for its pizzas and your workplace...

Embark on your delivery tour together. Play your cards wisely, get the most out of your ship, and deliver the pizza before it gets cold.

Deep Space Dine is a cooperative/solo mix of a deck building and a choose and write game, where you have to use your ressources and actions to overcome the dangers of space.

—description from the publisher

name: Defend Megatropolis
description:
"CALLING ALL HEROES!...Calling all heroes!"

Defend Megatropolis is a Solo (single player) ‘City Defense’ card game, with action selection and hand management.

In Defend Megatropolis, you will move your superhero around the city discarding Power Cards to defeat Threats, all while trying to foil the Villain and his Doom Device, the DoomBot! You win if you locate the Villain and defeat them! You lose if there are 4 DoomBot cards out on the playing area at the beginning of your turn OR a Location is destroyed. Careful! This will be no easy task and the Villain is sure to have a Plot Twist or two when you think you are close to bringing them to justice. Heed the call, and Defend Megatropolis!

-description from designer

name: Delivery Witches
description:
In Delivery Witches, you play as one of the apprentice witches, who will have to master their broomstick skills by delivering packages to the townsfolk. Move around the island to pick up packages, deliver them and improve your skills to gradually climb the mountain.

In each turn, each witch will have 4 actions, which she can use as she wishes. The actions they can do are moving, improving the broom or skills or accept and deliver orders. Witches can move between adjacent squares on the board. Using an action for each movement.

To accept an assignment, it will be necessary to move to a square with the symbol of pickup, and spending an action, will draw a card from the deck of assignments. This will mark the number of packages to be delivered and the destination, marked by a color.

Delivering packages does not spend actions, just by passing over the colored houses, it is considered that this package and all the packages of the same color have been delivered. With each package, we will get rewarded,  which will always be coins, and skill points. These coins and skill points will be used to improve the broom and your skills, you will be able to buy them in the store.

As packages are delivered, you will get medals. According to different conditions are met. When a player manages to have 4 medals, the final round will be activated and the game will be over. The player who scores the most points wins the game and will become a Delivery Witch!

-description from publisher

name: Demonuki
description:
Demonuki is an exciting, modern twist on the classic game Babanuki (Old Maid). In this fast-paced card game, each card has powerful abilities that will allow you to strategically position yourself in a way to win the game!

On your turn, you will either discard pairs of cards, or play individual cards in order to reverse the order of play, slide extra cards into an opponent’s hand, make them reveal some of their cards, or various other effects. The loser of the game is the player holding the last card in the game (typically a Demon, but possibly a Werewolf), after all other cards have been discarded.

—description from designer

name: Depot
description:
Depot is a climbing/shedding card game that can be played by 3 to 5 players.

The goal is to get rid of all your cards before the other players.

You can reduce your hand by playing a card with a higher value than the previous player.

Even if the number is smaller, you can still play cards if the combination contains more cards.

name: Der geheimnisvolle Brunnen
description:
In Der geheimnisvolle Brunnen, players explore a magical well by placing hidden imp discs inside it and slowly revealing them with a rotating whirlpool mechanism.

Each round, players take turns placing two frogs on lily pads next to the imps they believe will appear, with frogs allowed to stack on top of each other to form towers that influence scoring order. Once the whirlpool has turned and the imp disc is visible, players score points by checking which frogs are correctly placed: those next to revealed imps earn winning cards with gold coins, awarded in the order the frogs were stacked, while frogs in the wrong place earn nothing.

After each round, frogs are returned, the next player becomes the starting player, and a new imp disc is placed in the well. The game continues for three rounds (or more if desired), and at the end the players reveal their winning cards, count the gold coins, and whoever has collected the most wins.

name: Der Glückselefant
description:
Get to know yourself better!

In this card game for 3-6 players, you will help each other out by giving thoughtful advice when one is going through a hard time.

Each round one player is presenting a personal problem through a card. Everyone else now plays an advice card. The first player then chooses the best advice amongst the played cards.

As a twist on scoring, you want to keep your wins and losses in balance, because only then will you be able to truly win the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Der König des Waldes
description:
In the card game King of the Woods, set in a medieval fantasy forest inhabited by animal folk, each player plays vassals either to their own court to score points or to one of their opponents' court.

The latter will trigger special beneficial effects for the player, but that vassal's points will now score for that opponent.

At the start of the game, players are dealt a random hand of different types of vassals, and they must make the best of what they have. In total, there are 11 different vassals, each with unique roles and effects. The game continues until all players have played their entire hand of cards.

The player with the most points at the end is declared the winner and crowned the new King of the Woods.

name: Der Wald von Mystaria
description:
The Forest of Mystaria – The Atmospheric Tile-Laying Game with a Fantasy Setting

Create a magical forest! Place tiles, build your structures, and shape an enchanting woodland full of imagination! With simple rules, beautifully illustrated artwork, and charming wooden figures, this tile-laying game offers fun and strategy for the whole family. Who will grab the best building spots? And how can you benefit from the tiles placed by others? Find out as you step into the role of a mystical forest creature.

Build landscapes & place buildings

The perfect mix of tactics and luck!

36 imaginative wooden figures make the experience even more tangible!

Includes a simplified variant for the first game or for younger children

—description from the publisher

name: Desert Blitzkrieg: Rommel's North African Campaign
description:
"Losing Tobruk was one of the heaviest blows I can recall during the war.” — Winston Churchill

Desert Blitzkrieg is an Operational level two-player board-wargame covering the North African desert Campaign from April 1941 to December 1942. Units are regimental level and Divisional Integrity is key to maximizing the density of your forces on the map covering eastern Libya and western Egypt from Aghelia to El Alamein. The game is of low-moderate complexity and features a ‘Point-to-Point’ system while introducing a number of unique features.

Movement is along three different road types. Limited Port movement is possible. Supply Unit availability is critical for Battles as supply units must be expended to conduct a Battle. Battles use a ‘Battle Board’ with a ‘Front Line’ and ‘Second Line’ where positional tactics to maximize Combat Values are key. Battles can be a ‘game within a game’ and go for many rounds or be over quickly depending upon the player’s decisions. Unit types reflect different capabilities on the ‘Battle Board’ and the main map. A deck of event cards is provided to introduce a limited set of ‘random events’ that will force players to deal with the uncertainty of combat.

While game play is relatively easy, players will be confronted with many decision in a given game turn, with many different outcomes building play tension while delivering great replay value.


     HQs must decide whether to enhance Supply, Movement or Combat each turn.
     Use of one or two ‘Long Range Desert Force’s (specially marked Recon units).
     Player must decide a limited Card draw is to be made (there are only 6 per game, base).
     Supply Units must be used for supply line extension and also are expended for Combat, so decisions about usage are key.
     What boxes to build a limited number of Fortifications?
     How to use the limited air support; Combat Attack, Defense, or Interdiction.
     “Battle Board” management. Deciding where to place units to maximize Combat Value.


Product Information:

Complexity: 4 out of 10 (Low/Moderate)
    Playing time: 2.5 hours for short game, 10+ hours for full campaign
    Solitaire Suitability: High
    Players: Two (suitable for solitaire play)
    Map Scale: Abstract (point to point)
    Time Scale: Monthly turns
    Unit Scale: Regimental equivalents with Divisional Integrity

-description from publisher's website

name: Desert Duel: A Most Bitter Blow / Fighting Hard
description:
Desert Duel - 2 games set in WWII North Africa.

A Most Bitter Blow - Operation Battleaxe, June 1941
-The famous Tiger Convoy of May 1941 brought over two hundred tanks and fifty Hurricane fighters to Wavell’s command in North Africa – and an increased expectation from Churchill of an imminent offensive. General Wavell had reservations about the operation but reluctantly gave the green light.
After early successes, three days of heavy fighting saw the Allies retreat to their starting points, having lost about 100 tanks. Upon hearing the outcome of the battle, Churchill concluded it was “a most bitter blow”.

Fighting Hard - Battle of Matruh, June 1942
-Following defeat at Gazala, Eighth Army retreated into Egypt in June 1942 with little idea how and where it might stop Rommel. Border defences were quickly rejected as being too weak and so General Ritchie, the Eighth Army commander, sent orders to man the incomplete defences at Matruh.
From the outset, the plans to hold it were confused and then Auchinleck dismissed Ritchie taking command himself. Three days of chaotic fighting occurred in which the Allies grabbed defeat from a possible victory.

-Rules and mechanics
Rules are developed from the Stargard Solstice game, released in 2021, making it the 10th game in the WWII Battle Series, all with chit-pull mechanics.
Game length for A Most Bitter Blow is 6 turns, each turn represents 12 hours.
Game length for Fighting Hard is 9 turns, each turn representing 8 hours.
Counters represent companies, columns, battalions or regiments.

—description from the publisher

The map scale for A Most Bitter Blow is approximately 1.4 miles per hex, or 2.3 kilometres.
The map scale for Fighting Hard is approximately 2 miles per hex, or 3.2 kilometres. [Source: Paul Shackleton, 29 May 2025]

name: Design Your Destiny: Running Out of Time
description:
Read a fictional story about Charlie and Natalie as they are whisked away to the future to try to stop the invention of time travel itself! Every couple of chapters you get to play as Charlie and Natalie in a game where you help them progress through the story. Unfortunately, each game is broken and needs your help to fix it.
The next few pages after a game will guide you on ways you can fix the game, but you are given complete freedom to fix it however you want. Each task you complete earns you a sticker that helps put the time machine back together. If you complete enough tasks and fix the time machine, then you unlock the final chapter to see how the story ends.
It's a sci-fi story but also a game design tutorial that's great for kids or for people just getting into game design.

—description from the designer

name: Desolito
description:
Welcome to the Urban Development Department!

This is Vientole City, a beautiful place with vast flower fields, lush hills, and historic buildings. The market is bustling with people. As the leader of the city's development project, you will strive to improve the lives of the citizens. You'll plan public works, prioritize citizens' well-being, and create a balanced urban environment. Your excellent leadership and wisdom will greatly impact the growth of Vientole City.  Now, let's make this city an attractive and livable place with your hands!

The game consists of 4 rounds. Each round is divided into three phases: Planning Phase, Placement Phase, and Confirmation Phase.


     During the Planning Phase, players draft prepared land tiles.
     In the Placement Phase, players place the drafted land tiles onto their city boards. The key point is that the tiles are placed in reverse order of the drafting sequence.
     During the Confirmation Phase, players check the completion of milestone cards.


This sequence is repeated for 4 rounds, and in the end, each player will have placed 16 land tiles on their city boards. The player with the highest score wins the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Dess Bassd!
description:
Be the first to lay out seven number cards in the correct order in front of you - but choose your numbers wisely, because in the case of a tie, the difference between your first and last card will decide the winner!

Each player starts with 7 face-down cards in front of them and 4 cards in their hand.  
Each round a trick is played. The winner of the trick is the first to take a card from the display in the middle of the table and exchange it with a face-down card in front of them. The card from the display is played face-up. All face-up cards in front of a player must be in an ascending order from left to right. If this is not possible the player has to change a card from the display with a face-up card. The exchanged card goes to their hand. All other players follow in turn order.
The cards from the trick go to the display in the middle of the table. The winner of the trick starts the next round.

—description from the publisher

name: The Hunt
description:
May 1945.

The Third Reich collapses, leaving Europe in ruins. Many close and former members of the regime try to escape justice. Scattered across the globe, they hide their troubled past and start a new life…

But the Hunt has begun! Take the lead of a faction, plan the actions of your agents to investigate and capture these fugitives essential to the realization of your ambition. However, act quickly and be careful: other groups are also working in the shadows to seize these same targets!


     Take control of a faction with unique ambitions and abilities. 
     Send your agents all over the world to collect.


clues that will be very useful to you later. 

     Track down and capture the Fugitives before your opponents. 
     Use their skills to win.


—description from the publisher

name: Devil's Dice
description:
While exploring an old abandoned house, you have stumbled upon a book and some odd looking dice. Suddenly, a devil appears offering you and your friends a wager. Do you accept?

Devil's Dice is a lightweight dice rolling game for 2-6 player's. A twisted cross between Coup, and Liar's dice. Lie, steal, and chance your way to victory by being the first to summon the devil!

Each player starts the game with one skull token and two dice. The dice are hidden behind a cover screen. Each die has 6 unique symbols.
Satan's pool is the board in the center which dice will be added to throughout the game. 
When you've assembled all 6 symbols between your hand and the public die in Satan's pool, you declare Satan's set and win!

On your turn, you can take any of the actions listed below, regardless of whether you have the required symbols:

Imp's set: If your all your dice match, with Imp's counting as wilds, you may gain a die from the common pool.
Skull: If you have a Skull, take two skull tokens from the common pool. 
Scythe: If you have a Scythe, pay two skull tokens to try and steal a die. 
Pentagram: If you have a Pentagram, re-roll the dice in Satan's pool, and if you roll any pentagram you gain up to one. Also block Scythe's steal. 
Trident: If you have a Trident, Take up to three skull tokens from another player. Also block Trident's steal.
Flames: If you have a Flame, Gain 1 skull token, then re-roll your current hand.

Any player may challenge your action or block(claiming you are lying about having the requisite symbols). When challenged you must then reveal your dice hand. If you are caught lying, the action or block is cancelled, and the challenger steals a die from you. If you were telling the truth, instead the challenger loses a die and rolls it into Satan's Pool, and play continues after.

—description from the publisher

name: Dewan
publisher: Space Cowboys; Hobby Japan; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
"Our territory was limited, and resources were scarce, we marched from camp to camp in pursuit of victory." —Traditional Dewan song

Dewan is a fast-paced, competitive area-placement game for 2-4 players that features racing, placement, and hand strategy. During play, you collect terrain cards and spend them to strategically place your camps on the territory. Make the best use of terrain and resources so that you can satisfy the requirements on your story tiles. Along the way, gather berries and master fire to earn additional points.

—description from the publisher

name: WunderWaffen
description:
WunderWaffen (“wonder weapons”) is set during the last year of World War II, when the Normandy landings paved the way to the occupation of Berlin and the resulting defeat of the German army. Using simple rules the game recreates the troubled collaboration between the Russian, British, and American Allies in the final phase of the war.

The German army is near collapse, but inside its laboratories scientists and technicians are designing new and terrible weapons, the “WunderWaffen,” in the hope of turning the tide of a hopeless situation.

During the game, the Allied players must carefully balance the urgency to rapidly advance toward Berlin with the need to limit the Germans’ scientific research, while trying to help one another.

The German player will have to move forward on the Research Track, trying at the same time to put up a desperate fight against the Allies’ advance to delay the inevitable defeat for as long as possible. Germans may also win, though losing Berlin, thanks to a scoring system that rewards the results of forces on the field.

—description from the publisher

name: Diabolical Dave's Rumble Throwdown
description:
Rediscover the over-the-top excitement and pandemonium of wrestling’s golden age! Join the Diabolical Wrestling Council and challenge a colorful cast of superstars in search of the ultimate prize – the DWC World Championship. Gather a group of friends and pummel each other with words and moves … maybe even a 2×4!

Become a Victim of Diabolical Dave's Whimsical Management Decisions!
 In Diabolical Dave’s Rumble Throwdown, you build your own pro wrestling superstar and compete to become the DWC World Champion. Nearly endless combinations of wrestling styles, gimmicks, moves and attire all contribute to your success or demise and ensure you’ll never play the same way twice.

Playing as a Heel or Face, you’ll trade on the ultimate currency in pro wrestling – your popularity or infamy – to add moves and attire to your repertoire. You can even take on a manager to help you out. In an exciting race to the top of the promotion, you exact vengeance with one-shots, weapons, and angles. Bribe other players to run-in for you and even interrupt their plans along the way, just don’t get caught by the ref or you might be disqualified for cheating!

Make things even more interesting with a little roleplaying, giving your wrestler some personality, as you work your way through the opener, midcarder, and main eventer tiers.

name: Æterna
publisher: Ergo Ludo Editions; Ares Games; Grail Games; Hobby Japan; Maldito Games; MS Edizioni; Schwerkraft-Verlag; YOKA Games; Zvezda
description:
In Æterna, you take the role of a Roman Gens (family) that will try to increase its prestige through three eras: the Roman Kingdom, the Roman Republic, and the Roman Empire.

Your goal is to increase your influence over the city by supporting the conquest of the provinces, ruling over "the seven hills of Rome", and contributing to the construction of monuments and buildings. While doing this, you must not demotivate the people in the hills under your direct control as unrest could put you in a bad light. If you manage majorities, cards, and resources better than your opponents, your Gens will be remembered in the history books as one of the most important in Rome.

name: Dice and Dies
description:
Dice and Dies is an RPG with dungeon crawler and monster collection elements. You are a Hierophant, someone with the ability to interact with Imajins, the representation of people's imaginations. Thru the game you will battle Imajins in their Entity forms, make pacts with them and continue in your journey with your newly discovered powers.

—description from the designer

name: Dice Batter
description:
Dice Batter is a dice and card-based game for 2-4 players where the goal is to be the first to score 20 points. Players roll seven dice each turn and take turns placing them on a shared cookie sheet card, matching the numbers rolled. If a player rolls a higher number, they can bump an opponent’s die from the sheet.
Once the cookie sheet is full or no more moves can be made, all placed dice are collected into a mixing bowl. The round’s first player stirs the dice with a wooden spoon and randomly selects one die to roll. The owner of the die scores points equal to the rolled number. Play continues in rounds until one player reaches 20 points.
The game includes a mix of strategy and luck, as players decide which dice to place while also hoping for a favorable outcome in the mixing phase. Optional rules allow for slight variations in play, such as whether players can shield their dice from opponents. A typical game lasts around 10-20 minutes.

—description from the publisher

name: Dice Cat and Fish
description:
You’re too busy, so you send your five dice-cats to buy fish for you.
But… they’re cats. And dice. Totally uncontrollable.
Worse yet, they only go out once a week.

Try to tame your mischievous dice-cats to bring home the most delicious, high-scoring fish!
But beware… always watch out… don’t end up with an octopus!

Each round consists of four bidding turns.
Players roll their remaining dice, and the highest total wins the fish of that turn.
Used dice can’t be rolled again—so how you manage five differently valued dice is the key.

One of the turns is Octopus Time—and whoever rolls the lowest will get tangled in trouble!
If you roll exactly double your opponent’s score, you take *all* the fish on the table!
Use powerful skill cards to reroll or boost your dice—luck alone won’t be enough!

—description from the publisher

name: Dice Clash
description:
Take on the role of 1 of 6 Women Warriors battling for their chance at immortality.

Dice Clash simulates the back and forth of a battle using a clever dice placement system that is simple to learn but offers tactical depth.

Players get unique Warriors with their own 9 space Battle Grids, 6 Black Dice, 2 White Dice, and a Red Die.  The Dice form their Die Pool.

Turns consist of playing a single die from your die pool to one of the open spaces on your Battle Grid.  The value of the die interacts with the space you play to determines the attack and defense value of your die.  Players must defend with a value higher than their opponent's attack. But attacks of 6 or greater can be parried with a Defense of 1.

Playing white dice allows you to re-roll your remaining die pool.  Your red die activates your unique Warrior power.

Play continues until a player loses because they can't respond to an attack.  The loser flips their warrior and their grid to their damaged side where they have more powerful options for the next round.  Play continues until one Warrior wins 2 Battles.

Dice Clash was inspired by and re-implements the dice placement system in Scuttleball by Crossbow Games (Jonathan and Ryan).  Art is by Super Snipers artist, Hwa Siang.

—description frpm the publisher

name: Dice Duelo
description:
Dice Duelo is a semi-abstract game where two players take the role of a gambler-duelist in the Wild West.

Players roll their dice secretly and take turns placing a die one by one on the board to form a better Poker combination.

This duel is not won by the fastest finger, but the strongest mind. It is not about how good your dice roll is, but how you use it. Bluff your way through, outwit your opponent to use his dice to your advantage.

It’s quick: Shoot down your opponent in a round of 6 bullets.
it’s dirty: Use tricks to surprise your opponent.
It’s clever: Explainable in five minutes, playable for years.

—description from the publisher

name: Quartermaster General: West Front
description:
Quartermaster General: West Front is the third entry in the Quartermaster General two-player line. It is played over 23 seasonal game rounds, from Fall 1939 through Spring 1945, with one player controlling the Allies' forces — United Kingdom, United States, and France — and the other playing the Axis: Germany, Italy, and other associated countries (the "Pact", so called after the Tripartite Pact).

West Front also includes components and rules to create massive, combined games with Quartermaster General: East Front and South Front.

name: Viking Route
description:
In the co-operative game Viking Route, your heroes sail a magical Drakkar to the World's Edge and beyond. Influenced by magical ravens sent by Odin to steer your course, and by the winds of Fate, you will face powerful and monstrous creatures out of the Norse mythos to fulfill your quests and prepare you for the final challenge to defeat the greatest enemy of the Gods and prevent Ragnarok!

Viking Route uses a compass-and-magnets movement mechanism first introduced the game The Faceless. The main game piece — the Drakkar — is represented by a compass, and multiple magnets (representing ravens and wind) are manipulated by players to steer the course of their ship.

This mechanism is only one of the elements under control of the players, who also have to manage the resources of the Drakkar and their hand of cards to face opponents and achieve the goals of their quests. Multiple quests, using different board layouts, are included in the game; quests can be played either independently, or as a continuing campaign, ending in a final climactic confrontation to avoid Ragnarok.

—description from publisher

name: Button Kingdoms
description:
Button Kingdoms is a bribery based deck building game, with simultaneous actions where players take on the role of child commanders of their own fantasy stuffed animal armies.

The goal of the game is to build up your kingdom of fluffy fighters by collecting currency in the form of buttons, and to seize the thrones of other players… while staying true to your character's own secret motivations.

During the Button Bazaar phase, players place bribe offers in the hopes of adding fluffy fighters to their deck, and accept the bribes of their opponents to acquire those precious buttons which become victory points at the end of the game. After this market phase is resolved, players turn their newly acquired cards against their opponents in the goal of seizing another throne to add to their dominion.

Victory will rest on three separate pillars: total BUTTONS, THRONES in your possession, and how well your deck of cards measures up to your champion’s IDEALS. Even if you fall behind in the combat aspect of the game, with skillful deck building and solid deal-making, you could still net the win.

Do you have what it takes to conquer the Button Kingdoms?

name: DiceKeepers EndHaven
description:
