DiceKeepers: EndHaven invites players into a realm of high-stakes fantasy where strategy and luck collide with the roll of the dice. Take on the roles of heroic adventurers tasked with defending the town of EndHaven from encroaching dangers—dragons, witches, vampires, and other fearsome creatures beyond imagine. Take them head on with unique allies at your side and compete to become the most renowned hero of the land.

Players will take turns leading the day and completing Adventure Cards by covering all their Number Dice Slots with dice. Completed Adventure Cards net players Reptutaion Points or RP (the games winning point value). By placing even a single die on a card, players can reroll their remaining dice keeping them in control of their chances. Any Adventure Cards a player fails to complete will have it’s consequence effect that player at the end of their turn. Once all players have gone the game will proceed with the End of Day.

At the end of each day any remaining Adventure Cards with the Red Border will trigger their consequences for each player possibly Attacking the Town.

Players must also rely on the clever use of Ally Cards to shift the odds—these cards can adjust dice rolls, offer protection, or remove difficult Adventure Cards from the field. Luckily, players always have access to the local Tavern, where a completed 3 of a kind on the card’s Match Dice Slots will allow them to draw an Ally Card, giving them a constant chance to bolster their ranks.
Even if a player dies, they will carry on the fight with the use of a Resurrection Stone. Be warned the Resurrection Stone takes a toll on the town and is worth -5 RP at the end of the game.
The game will end once a player reaches the winning Reputation Point (RP) value or if the town is destroyed.

—description from the designer

name: Dicemancy
description:
Dicemancy is a solo tower defense game where you create crazy spell combinations to stop the constant onslaught of monsters. You’ll build a small interconnected tableau of intertwining spell slot cards, forming a grid where a card’s position, rotation, and connections matters, and you’ll roll and manipulate dice to activate those spells.

Over the course of the game, you must adapt your tactics by chaining and boosting spells and discovering new combinations. With scalable difficulty, randomized enemy layouts, and a variety of scenarios, characters, and monsters, Dicemancy offers a fresh, multi-solution experience every time you play!

To win, you must defeat all the approaching enemies before they tear down your city walls.

—description from the publisher

name: Diceocracy
description:
Ever since you were a kid, your mama told you that you’re destined for grand things! So you're pretty certain that things can only be better with more "you" in it! Well, it’s finally time for more YOU …in the name of democracy! It just so happens there is an election in the city of Dicetopia coming up! As one of the promising stop-for-nothing candidates, you call for change and aim to enlighten the public of your magnificence… and you know, also make some stuff… better! It’s only one teeny tiny little ”problem” - Democracy is kind of up to the people, and the people are in this particular case… well, DICE!

In Diceocracy, you will use your political skills to attract voters from different districts and introduce them to your jaw-dropping politics by ”any means necessary”, you know, as long as you can get away with it anyway. The goal of the game is to get the most votes by just being YOU, with a fair bit of stern persuasion and political tricks.

Throughout the game, players will send out their representatives to recruit followers and influence the political landscape with different clever actions. Players will manipulate dice values and positions, take control over districts and shift representatives around. They will fundraise, advertise and use their dice followers to achieve populistic goals for increased popularity.

By the end of the game, votes are counted from successfully pulled off political stunts, secret agendas, controlled districts and popularity among the different demographic groups!

The candidate with the most votes wins the election and the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Dicetack
description:
Reveal the game cards one by one and choose the dice that match their conditions to build your own dice tower. Maintain a delicate balance amidst the thrilling tension and keep your tower from falling until the end to win. Who can build the tallest dice tower? Show off your strategy and focus.

—description from the publisher

name: Diceverse
description:
Diceverse is a fast-paced duel game combining cards and dice. A rift between universes has opened, and a deadly battle for total power has begun. Players choose one of four unique armies from different universes and lead them to victory.

Choose one of four unique armies from different universes and lead them to victory. Each faction boasts its own deck and special abilities. Play cards to command your dice army, maneuver across the battlefield, and attack your opponent.

The game ends when one player's Base is destroyed or has no units left on the board.

name: Dicktion
description:
A party game where every word sounds like "dick" – Ideal for pun lovers and word enthusiasts!

Step into the world of Dicktion, the wickedly witty party game where sharp minds and quick tongues collide!

Test your genius as you dodge forbidden words, unleash clever puns, and outwit your friends to claim the ultimate title: The Master of Dicktion!

Predickt the word
Predict the word on the card while your teammate acts it out. Try to guess as many cards before the time runs out.

Judge Richard
Don't say a forbidden word or your opponents can activate Judge Richard. If they do your turn ends.

Master of Dicktion
Outwit your friends to claim the most points and become the Master of Dicktion!

—description from the publisher

name: Dictator for Life
description:
In Dictator for Life, Ancient Roman Generals compete against one another, trying to gain and keep control of the Dictatorship in Rome. Resources are earned by fighting battles against foreign enemies, and the Dictator may not leave Rome, so a formidable army and a healthy gold reserve is needed to defend your Dictatorship from rival generals. On their turn, the Dictator may buy up to 5 senators. The first to buy 10 senators is declared Dictator for Life and wins the game!

Winning battles against foreign enemies will win you gold, troops, weapons, and tactics cards. The tactics cards are where the most interesting mechanics take place - use Testudo to negate all projectile weapons. Declare it a Holy Day and throw a lavish festival in Rome, preventing other generals from marching on Rome. Sacrifice a Sheep, appeasing the gods and preventing disasters from befalling you while out on campaign.

The majority of the battles will take place against foreign enemies, who are encountered by overturning cards from the Bellum deck while you are on campaign. But the most exciting battles take place between the Dictator and a general who marches on Rome to depose them.

For an added bit of fun and drama, generals give a short speech to indicate that they are marching on Rome. The speech can be as simple as, "I march one Rome!" or whatever overblown oratory masterpiece you can deliver in one minute or less.

The game plays at its best with 3 players playing 3 rounds, with the winner being determined by the overall senator number. This setup leads to more long-term, calculated decisions. With the 3 player setup, large battles between two players will often cause them to drain most of their resources. This is a benefit to the player who was not involved, often giving weaker generals their chance to strike.

—description from the designer

name: Die Fürsten
description:
Princes is a medieval-themed deck builder and the first game developed by German board game influencer Johannes "Hunter" Jaeger.

—description from the designer

Die Fürsten ist ein Deckbuilder mit Mittelalter-Thema und das erste selbstentwickelte Spiel von Brettspiel-Influencer Johannes "Hunter" Jaeger.

—description from the designer

name: Die Jury: Zwei Gesichter – Ein Schuss
description:
Guilty as charged? As members of a jury, two to five players aged 14 and over pass judgment in a murder trial. Did the defendant really shoot the young man in the parking lot outside a club? Over the course of three rounds, the group discusses the evidence and any doubts that arise. The players listen to audio recordings from the courtroom: statements from the prosecution and defense as well as interviews with witnesses, police officers and forensic experts provide clues. With the help of the evidence seized, they work together to reconstruct the course of events based on a real case in order to reach a decision on the question of guilt. Interactive true crime suspense for fans of crime podcasts and courtroom series.

—description from the publisher

name: Die Legenden von Andor: Das ferne Land
description:
The heroes of Andor face new challenges in Die Legenden von Andor: Das ferne Land (The Distant Land). On the double-sided game board, you'll experience seven new legends, with the event cards in this game determining the order in which creatures move. Work together to stand up to enemy forces.

The next major game after The Eternal Cold. What makes this game special: The event cards provide variety via their backs, as they determine the order in which the creatures move. Even the introductory legend gets off to a dramatic start!

name: Die Seehunde
description:
Die Seehunde is a solitaire nautical wargame set in the last months of World War 2. You, the player, will be in command of a two crew midget submarine Type XXVIIB called “Seehund” (Harbor Seal; plural “Seehunde, die”) or simply “Hund” (Hound) by its crews. Equipped with two G7e Torpedoes, the Seehund was designed as a short range commerce raider for deployment in the North Sea.

The game play is divided into two games, which are connected to each other. You will start with the Strategic Game, which is played on a geographic map of the British Channel and it surrounding coasts. Here you will be at risk of encountering different events and challenges while searching for convoys to attack. Once you find a convoy, the Strategic Game pauses, and you switch to the Tactical Game, which is played on a large map, which is centered around the encountered convoy. You will try to maneuver as close a possible to identify the individual vessels and pick the biggest fish. For torpedo simulation, the game uses a simplified mechanism, which allows you to attack from any angle and any range with minimal restrictions. Once there is no more to achieve against this convoy, you will try to escape the scene by grounding your submarine on the seafloor and hoping for the best.

After your escape, play will continue with the Strategic Game, where you can now choose to continue your journey, or head back to the home harbor of IJmuiden. Once you reach harbor, the game comes to a happy ending. But don’t be fooled, as there is only one happy end, and a dozen ways to die in the cold waters of the North Sea.

name: DIE!
description:
This is a strategic game of “player annihilation” for 2 to 4 players. The game can be played as a straight abstract strategy game, but there are also a dozen predefined “Fantasy Factions” with special powers to challenge the balance of the game. 
Each player has 24 pegs representing their band of combatants, and the confrontation takes place in a 5x5-space Arena. Each player also has just one six-sided die to determine the actions they can take on each turn as they send their fighting forces into the arena. It’s not the number you roll, it’s how you use that to your advantage! 
Players also have several "lives" (based on player count) to stay in the game under certain circumstances.

—description from the publisher

name: Dies Irae
description:
When the World is literally going to Hell in a recovered shopping cart, working together as a team is incredibly important...and getting _everyone else_ to work as a team on your behalf is even more so!

Over 13 rounds on the night of Friday the 13th of an unspecified month in an unspecified year, you - alone - will attempt to shepherd, sacrifice and/or destroy, both zombies and survivors alike in order to survive until help arrives in the morning.

Each turn, you will draw 3 cards and postpone one of them (put it to the bottom of the deck) and then must put the others into play. Various effects can be triggered - resolved in the order of your choosing - which might result in gains and/or losses before you compare your Survivor Total against the current Zombie Threat Level: if you are being overwhelmed by this threat, your community will suffer!

Simply make it through the 13 turns of the game - see the Sun rise on a new day - and you will win...

Note: Dies Irae is the third game in Tony Boydell's "Infinity" solo game trilogy (along with Lux Aeterna and Aleph Null)

—description from the designer

name: Digit Code
description:
For some unknown reason, we now find ourselves in a situation where we must quickly interpret a six-digit digital code. We will analyze this code by gathering various uncertain pieces of information. Its meaning will become clear in our hands, just as it always has.

In Digit Code, each player in a two-player game creates a secret six-digit code, with three numbers above three numbers, with a digit 0-9 appearing at most twice and not adjacent to one another. The letters A-Y are used to indicate number segments in a column or in a row, or within a particular digit. Players take turns asking each other questions of the following four types:


     How many spaces in row ? or column ? are filled?
     Is the number ? even or odd?
     Looking at the adjacent numbers ? and ??, which one is larger?
     Is the segment at row ? and column ?? filled?


Each player must ask all four question types before they can repeat a question type. On a turn, a player can give a six-digit number instead of a question. If they have guessed all six numbers correctly, they win; if not, the opponent says "Wrong", and the game continues. If a player guesses incorrectly twice, they lose.

With three or more players, one player creates a six-digit number that the other players race to deduce first, with the players asking questions in turn. Once again, if a player guesses incorrectly twice, they are out of the game.

name: Diluvio
description:
Since you can’t control the weather, you have to be ready to act when the next flood begins. Protect your favorite species by moving as many animals as possible onto the raft. That’s the only place they will be safe when the water level rises. But be careful, since certain parts of the raft are more dangerous than others.

Will you save your species from extinction?

Diluvio is a competitive and family game for 3-4 players in which you will have to put yourself in the shoes of your favorite animal and fight to get the most places on the raft. Only then can you save them before the water level reaches them. To do this, you must strategically plan your movements and get your animals onto the raft before the water reaches you. But be careful, the other animals will also want to climb on it and there is not room for everyone in the ark!

—description from the publihser

name: Dinner Party
description:
You’re the hosts of a dinner party, and your guests are people of history. Convince characters like Marie Curie, Cleopatra or Gandhi to join your table, use their special abilities and treat them to drinks from the bar. Send Adolf (who came uninvited and insists his invitation “got lost in the mail”) to the table of an opponent to ruin their evening, and make sure to keep your own guests entertained so other players won’t be able to charm them away from you. Only one can have the greatest party ever when the game ends and dinner is served!

Dinner Party is a quick, dark-humoured, dice-driven game for 2 to 6 players.

—description from the designer

name: Dino Dynasty
description:
In Dino Dynasty, players represent dinosaur species from the Cretaceous period that compete in various aspects of survival. With variable game setup, the most important survival traits vary from game to game as each game features a scenario with specific starting conditions and a set of random challenges. The player who then completes the most of these challenges wins!

The map, called the territory, is created by the players placing territory tiles. These tiles create biomes that can span several tiles and are based on the ones that existed during the Cretaceous period when the planet looked much different than today. The map is mostly unknown at the start of the game and is gradually revealed as players spread and explore it.Additional map set-ups called scenarios give you more ways to play!

You can choose to play in teams or even play several games as a campaign. In addition, a "legendary" part of the game gives players the ability to change between species inside a dynasty and save their current development over several games. This can be used to get suitable dinosaur variants to manage harder scenarios to increase the difficulty level and long-term strategy. It can also be used to get a specific dinosaur or combination of dinosaurs to best counter opponents!In Dino Dynasty, players can explore the fantasy of what could have been while also using the facts and latest known scientific discoveries regarding dinosaur to create and evolve their species. What would have happened if a dinosaur had developed in an evolutionary direction other than it did? These possible changes are still within reasonable limits and are based on the real physical characteristics of the dinosaurs so the learning is as immense as the dinosaurs themselves.

—description from the publisher

name: Dino Feast
description:
A party game where everyone is affecting the movement of dinosaurs who are roaming the group and devouring those who do not feed them. Players simultaneously have to choose between three cards to either move the dinosaurs to the right, left, or to feed the dinosaur. Once everyone has played a card face down, all players reveal and show their selected card. Dinosaurs move and devour! Be the last one standing to win.

—description from the publisher

name: Dino Lab
description:
Have you ever wanted to resurrect the ancient beasts that were extinct? Imagine the thrill of reviving ancient beasts that disappeared centuries ago - would you recover what was lost through time? Now, the power to make this a reality is in your hands. Grab your gene mixer and complete the fragmented dna. With each recovered gene strain, you'll get closer to recreating these magnificent beings, bridging the gap between past and future. Your mission: to recover and reconstruct the genetic code from ancient, fragmented strands and assemble them into an unparalleled miracle of science. It's time to unlock the secrets of life itself and breathe new existence into the extinct.

Dino Lab is a puzzle game where you are tasked with completing genes of various dinosaurs but to finish a gene pool you will have to use common aspects of different beasts. Experiment and solve the biological puzzle of life

The game is divided into 25 rounds. Each round players simultaneously fill test tubes in the DNA mixer in order to create dinosaurs. The goal of the game is to create as many complete sentences of dinosaurs' DNA as possible.

Players will get points depending on the accuracy of a DNA. The game ends when all test tubes in a DNA mixer are filled. The player with the most points is a winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Dino Path
description:
Breakfast is served... if you can survive!

In Dino Path, 2 to 4 cavemen race into the jungle to steal dinosaur eggs and carry them back to camp—physically holding the egg tokens on their backs!

But watch out! You must avoid angry T-Rexes, navigate carnivorous plants, and outwit meddling rivals trying to steal your loot. Use action cards to dash, block, or even control the dinosaurs to clear your path.

With its unique tactile components and fast-paced gameplay, Dino Path is a chaotic, fun-filled family game perfect for casual players and dino lovers alike.

name: Dino Trix: Tarot Adventures
description:
Dino Trix: Tarot Adventures is a collection of three tarot games: Hold My Beer, Oopsie and Thread the Needle.  All three trick-takers utilize a tarot deck and share similar card play and special powers.  However, with scoring differences and different player counts, each game provides a distinct experience.

Hold My Beer is a 3-player only game with bidding and special powers.  Oopsie is a twist on Hold My Beer but is a fixed partnership game with slight differences in special powers and scoring.  Thread the Needle is a 4-5 player game that shares the same basic card play and similar special powers but a completely new scoring system.

name: DinoGenics: Park Manager Edition
description: This complete box solution includes the deluxe version of the core game and both gameplay expansions. In addition, this collection includes 3 breaking news promo cards.

name: Good Puppers, Too!
description:
Good Puppers, Too! contains 100 new unique cards, depicting nine new breeds of pup and one group of Rascals. The core mechanics of the game are the same: Draft pups, play them, and they will perform tricks that allow groups of pups to bury bones. Bones are worth points, and can be upgraded by various tricks to be worth more points, and end-game bonuses can upgrade them as well.

The new Rascals have Schemes! If you complete a Scheme, that group of pups will double all their points at the end of the game.

Good Puppers, Too! can be played on its own, mixed with some cards from Good Puppers, or combined with Good Puppers to make a mega-pup game that can hold up to 7 players.

—description from the publisher

name: Dionysia
description:
All of Athens has turned out for the Dionysia, a grand theatrical festival to honor the god Dionysus. Impress the crowds with your well-crafted drama to win the playwriting competition as well as the favor of the gods!

Draft and craft a better drama than your opponent to secure the favor of the gods at this year’s Dionysia. As you take a scene from the central stage and add it to your developing play, you’ll need to decide whether to start a new act (to a max of 3) or add it to the top/bottom of an existing act. Create specific scoring patterns of dramatic elements through careful arrangement of your scenes while taking advantage of powerful effects available through each act’s key (topmost) scene. After each play has 3 acts of 3 scenes each, players score each act based on its key scene and pattern. Whoever has the most points is favored by the gods and wins the playwriting competition!

Shuffle all 18 scene cards and reveal 3 of them in the shared stage between the players. Each turn, the active player chooses one of these scenes and adds it to their play, then refills the stage for the next player. To add a scene, the player may create a new act in their play (to a maximum of 3). They may instead choose to upstage or downstage the existing scenes in an act, placing the new scene at the top or bottom (respectively) of the act. The topmost card in an act is the key scene, which sets the scoring conditions for the end of the game. Many cards also have immediate effects that occur when that scene is placed in the key scene position. Each card features an assortment of dramatic elements that are used to create scoring patterns of rows and columns. Once both players have a tableau consisting of 3 acts of 3 scenes each, these patterns are evaluated based on the key scenes for each act. The amount of favor earned can vary depending on the key scene, with each set of 3 specific icons in either a row or column earning the listed amount of favor. The player who earns the most favor is the winner!

name: Innovation Ultimate
description:
Innovation Ultimate is a box set containing Innovation and all five of its expansions, which includes a brand new expansion titled The Unseen.

Many, many updates have been made to this edition. First, Age 11 has been added, representing the recent past and potential near future at the time of release. Language and mechanics have been streamlined, and in particular, the expansions have all been heavily reworked to be more accessible and easy to include while playing.

name: One Deck Dungeon: Relics of the Forge
description:
One Deck Dungeon returns with a brand new full expansion! The Forge hungers for fuel, and it will reward your efforts with great power if you satisfy it.

During Setup, you'll choose a Relic to enter the dungeon with. This Relic will shape your strategies, as it will be your means for filling the Forge with fuel, and also a powerful way to expend it!

This expansion is stand-alone, and contains all new dungeons, heroes, monsters, traps.

—description from the publisher

name: Dirty Filthy Bikepacking
description:
Get dirty, silly & nowhere fast in this intuitive, crazy game that perfectly captures the skids, scents and sidequests of bikepacking. A roll and move cycle camping board game with a co-operative and comedic flavour. To succeed you must help each other solve problems but players can also play practical jokes on one another.

You ride along through the woods of some non-specific forest world with a group of other riders and collaborate and co-operate to get to the next camp spot. You can ride together, share resources and face disasters together to collect points. You can also play dirty tricks on each other by slipping your friends Cringe cards.

Each round covers 1 day.  After 3 days, the game ends when all riders arrive at the finish point.  Points are then totaled  and the player with the most points wins.

—description from the designer

name: Discat
publisher: Red Cat Games; funbot; Hobby Japan; Lifestyle Boardgames Ltd; Lubee Edition; PaperGames (III)
description:
Look, there are cats hidden on every single card in this little clever game! Play to discard as many cards as possible to your personal discat pile and try to hinder your opponents. The more cards you collect the more points you get! Sounds easy and meowlogical, right?

In Discat players have to discard as many cards as possible from their hand to win the game. Their personal discard pile will grant points at the end of the game and will also be used as a constraint to the other players.


     Choose 1 card or a group of cards from your hand.
     Play them in your discat pile.
     Refill your hand with more cats!


—description from the publisher

name: 1001 Odysseys
description:
1001 Odysseys is a game of fantastic space adventures. The first human FTL ship, the Odyssey, sets out to explore a new sector of the galaxy after finding an operational alien stargate. Players take on the roles of the Odyssey's bridge crew, as they find planets, meet strange new aliens, and eventually try to find the way back home!

Each time a group sits down at the table, they play through one chapter of a story: a co-operative adventure will result in a new chapter being unlocked for the next session. The chapters aren't linear though, your path through the story book will be determined by your choices. Every standalone book tells of one of the Odyssey's adventures through alien space, but they do not require the same set of players each time. No two playthroughs of a given story book will be exactly alike!

While playing, the Mission Control board will track your progress through the Chapter. When the crew wants to do something in the game, they combine the letters of an Action, Mission, and Location to form a code such as B-3-D4, and look up that paragraph in the book. After reading the paragraph's story and game instructions, you'll advance your adventure one step, and have new options to choose from. Your journeys are recorded in a booklet called the Passport, which holds items, chapter data, and is effectively the "save file" for the game.

1001 Odysseys comes with 4 full story books, spanning approximately 400 pages. Each chapter can last anywhere from 30-75 minutes, depending on the group and the size of the chapter.

name: Chess Joker
description:
Chess Joker brings elegant chaos to the classic game of Chess. The rules are quite simple: Play a normal game of chess, but with one extra twist — after each turn, flip the top card of the deck face up next to you. Each card depicts a Joker move, such as "Move your King like a Knight" or "Warp your Queen to deliver check". On your next turn, you can take a normal chess move, or use your card. If you don't use the card, it's gone, and you draw a new one. If you do use it, you score it for points. Accumulate 800 Elo worth of completed cards, and you win immediately — or exploit your cards' powers to deliver checkmate and win traditionally.

Each of the 256 cards in the game is unique, and they are divided into two 128 card sets: basic and advanced. Learning players can start with the basic cards, and introduce the rest when they're ready.

—description from the publisher

name: Distop-IA
description:
Distop-IA is a card game set in a near-future dystopia where analog objects are banned. Players take on the role of smugglers trying to transport books, toys, or cassettes between districts and across the border, all while avoiding patrolling robotic guards.

The game is played in alternating turns, with each player selecting one of their districts, gathering all its cards, and distributing them counterclockwise, as in a game of Mancala. Players must be strategic in how they sneak goods past the guards and into rival districts. Throughout the game, alarm cards with sirens may appear that move the guards, making smuggling even more challenging.

The game ends when the deck runs out or a player has a guard in every district. At the end, players tally their points based on the valuable goods they’ve managed to keep and each guard eliminates one valuable card. The player with the most points wins. There’s also an advanced mode that includes mission cards with point modifiers and other special cards.

name: Diver Go!
description:
Dive in search of the treasure coins lying on the ocean floor!
Gather the right coins to sell to the coin collector on the boat. But beware of King Octo's curse which cause the coins you are eyeing disappear mysteriously the moment you dive. Use your memory to lead you to the coins. 
"Are you ready? Diver, Go!"

Players only have moments to scan the glittering seabed of coins before their dive. Strategically take turns in attempt to pick a number of them up each turn. But each time you dive your vision is obstructed by the curse. Some coins are cursed and some are not. You'll need to look at the coins carefully and plan which ones to take.  Exchange those coins for a reward and if you can bring back uncursed coins your points will double.

—description from the publisher

name: Divide & Conker
description:
Ready your conkers for a great battle. Divide & Conker is a 2 to 4 player game. Set up varies dependent on player count. Game play usually lasts 30 minutes and is suitable from age 8 upwards.

Gameplay takes place over 2 rounds with a total of 7 battles. At the end of 7 battles, each player counts their victory points from cards in play. The player with the most victory points is the winner.

Within a round there are 3 phases; draft, prepare army, battle. In phase 1, players take it in turns drafting cards either from a pyramid or snake draft. Once all cards have drafted move to phase 2. Players can now prepare their army by laying down their collected conkers, applying hardener cards and attaching strings. Once each players army is prepared, play then continues to phase 3. During phase 3 players battle each other by declaring attacking and defending conkers. Player roll the dice and play trick cards during a battle until one conker is defeated. The second battle within round 1 can then commence.

When round 1 is over, move to round 2 where these 3 phases are played out but with a total of 5 battles in the final phase instead of 2. If no more battles can be played, the game ends and victory points are counted.

—description from the designer

name: DJ Set
description:
In DJ Set, players scan a QR code that links to a thematic playlist (e.g., "Colors").

Working as a team, players find the color evoked by the music, whether in the lyrics (Paradis Blanc), the title (Blue), the band (P!nk), or the theme of the song (The Simpsons).

Each round, the person who guesses the color earns their team a point and becomes the DJ. They play the next song, and the game continues.
With over 80 different themes and 560 songs to find, players compete on professions, first names, cities, creatures, and more, and will hear songs rarely seen in a blind test game!

name: Djeser
description:
Djeser is a competitive game for 1 to 4 players.

Imhotep is looking for an assistant in order to help build the stepped pyramid of Saqqara.

You need to build a pyramid composed of 6 cards, with more Prestige points than your opponents.
At levels II and III, you must place a card whose value is equal to the sum or the difference of the two
support cards placed at the lower level.

But beware of the cursed cards from your opponents !

name: Mystic Curling Club
description:
Bring the ice sport of curling to your tabletop, with dice! In the dexterity game Mystic Curling Club, instead of 44 pounds of granite down a 150 foot sheet of ice, you'll be sliding shiny 12-sided dice down a three-foot board trying to reach the center of the rings. As in the sport of curling, you can bump opposing stones, throw guard stones to defend your own, and mix strategy with skill to win.

But Mystic Curling Club isn't just dice curling; it's magical dice curling. Each player chooses a witch and her familiar to lead their curling team. On certain shots, you'll be able to change the playing field: adding, moving, or even removing stones!

—description from the publisher

name: DNA VOYAGER
description:
Recode DNA and Restore LIFE
Welcome, I'm Emanuele. I am a geneticist and the DNA VOYAGER Project’s leading designer. Since 1998 I have worked in Toronto in genetic research and until 2041 I had dealt with HIV, HCV, HBV, HLA, SARS, Genomic Fragment Analysis, STR and various criminal cases. 
When it all started, I was lucky enough to be able to reach a shelter in time where I met other scientists with whom we worked for eight years in search of a solution. Perhaps Humanity has hope, but now everything is in your hands. 
The duty to which you are called is profoundly serious, although we will try to introduce you to your mission by telling you about it as if it were a game, to simplify things.

This experience is suitable for four participants, but can also be attempted alone, with two or with three. Participants will have to prepare to board the VOYAGER, a powerful interstellar ship capable of traveling at warp 10 speed.
Once on board, you will need to synthesize the nucleotide triplets and inoculate them into plasmid catalysts before arriving at Proxima Centauri.
Due to my age, I will not be able to follow you in the next stages of your mission. 
So, the time has come to wish you good luck and introduce yourself to Anna, a talented researcher. She will tell you what happened and what you need to do to save Humanity from extinction.

ANNA
Welcome trainee, my name is Anna, and I’m a space engineer.

Chapter 1: The Darkness of the Refuge
Eight years have passed since the doors of the nuclear shelter closed behind us. 
In 2041, a few minutes of madness were enough to change everything. Life on Earth disappeared almost immediately. It was May, but in a flash, it seemed like November. 
 Those who survived the nuclear explosions were unable to survive the deadly radiation. 
There are no more living beings out there: no humans, no animals, no plants. The land and water are contaminated, the air is dense with humidity, the sky is covered by radioactive clouds. 
Eight years of survival, fighting against hunger, despair, and the certainty that there was nothing left out there. 
 Here, at a depth of eight hundred meters, our only light is artificial, and time almost seems to have stopped. The days get confused, and the hope for a better future fade, little by little.
Food stocks ran out months ago. We were eating too much and did not notice that our ribosomes were stopping working and disrupting protein synthesis.
 In fact, we did not know that the barriers we had designed to protect the shelter - although they managed to protect us by containing 99% of the radiation - would not be able to prevent that minimal dose from poisoning our DNA, triggering a slow genetic drift, which began as mosaicism, which in a few months will have completed its course.
The thought of what lies ahead is unbearable, but we cannot give up. Not yet!

THE GAME
During the travel, the four players have to recode the 20 aminoacids. Once the biocabinet is open the degradation step starts.

—description from the designer

Follow the game on Youtube for more details: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLeecKwLAKmwM4rrBtxKhtkqL0WuvDHv9G

Further details on the Kickstarter page: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/m41/dna-voyager

name: DNA: The New Origin of Species
description:
It is a strategic board game about crafting DNA sequences to evolve creatures and populate a new world.

In DNA: The New Origin of Species, you take on the role of a scientist tasked with populating a distant planet with Earth’s diverse creatures. Using multi-colored gene tokens, you’ll complete DNA sequences to bring new species to life, strategically placing them on modular regions to maximize points. As you create new lifeforms, you’ll unlock powerful effects and score bonus points by matching genes to their ideal habitats. Prove your strategic mastery and populate the most successful species to claim victory!

On their turn, players can choose between two main actions: Prepare Projects or Populate Creatures. When preparing projects, players draw gene tokens from the gene bag, buy new DNA project cards, or place gene tokens onto their projects. Once a project card is completed with gene tokens, players can take the Populate action, placing their creatures onto the modular game board. Creatures earn points by matching gene colors with region colors or favored habitats, and some creatures even have instant or permanent abilities that provide additional benefits during or after population.

The game ends when a player completes their final project—7, 8, or 9 projects, depending on the number of players. Victory points are scored throughout the game based on population, creature abilities, and endgame effects, but the final tally includes bonuses for creature sets and gene tokens in your supply. The player with the most victory points at the end of the game is the winner, claiming the title of the ultimate creator in this new world!

—description from the publisher

name: DNUP
description:
Your goal in DNUP is to empty your hand of cards.

Each player starts with eight or ten cards in hand, with each card having different numbers (from 1-10) at top and bottom, e.g. 1 and 7. Pick up all your cards at once; you can rearrange cards from left to right at any time, but you can't revolve them. On a turn, first discard any cards on the table in front of you, then you can:

1. Play cards from your hand.
2. Add one card to the table.
3. Take cards from the table.
4. Revolve all cards in your hand.

When you play cards, you can play one or more cards of the same value — but if you play as many cards as another player has in front of them, your cards must be of higher value. If you overplay someone, e.g. playing two 5s when they have two 2s, they must revolve their cards, then return them to their hand.

When you add one card, you add a card of the same value to someone else's played cards — but if that player would now have the same number of cards as a third player, the third player's cards must be a lower value, in which case they revolve them and return them to hand.

When you pick up cards from in front of another player, revolve them, then add them to your hand.

The first player to empty their hand scores 2 points, and cards don't return to their hand, even if beaten. The second player to empty their hand scores 1 point. Play multiple rounds until someone has at least 4 points, then whoever has the most points wins.

name: Dodicitre
description:
In a lively contest of wits and timing, players compete to shed their cards by cleverly connecting numbers and forming powerful combinations. The game’s tension builds as every move can change the flow of play, with players watching each other’s hands and waiting for the perfect chance to link, outplay, and climb to victory in this playful battle of numbers.

Dodicitre is a climbing and shedding game where players aim to play out their cards by either beating the previous set or attaching a card to the one on the table to form a stronger combination. The twist lies in the flexibility of the numbers—cards like 11 and 12 can link or form pairs in unique ways, opening creative paths to victory.

name: Goats & Goblins
description:
Those pesky goats have escaped again and are now bleating for your help from inside a treacherous cave! You and your fellow goblin herders must go down and retrieve them, but you soon spot  mysterious gold, precious gems, and lovely trinkets in the shafts below. New plan: the goblin who can retrieve the most treasure from the risky depths wins!   But be careful - going too deep may cause too many Cave-Ins and force you to drop your treasure as you flee, leaving it unguarded for the saboteurs to take.

Goats and Goblins is a push-your-luck game where you will attempt to collect treasures, goats, and goblins from the mysterious cave before it collapses. You will take turns leading expeditions below the surface, inviting other players to join you or stay behind. If your mission is successful, the exploring members will gain valuable cards to divide. Failed expeditions will give cards to the players who did not explore the cave. Some cards can be played to support or hinder expeditions.

It’s game over when the Cave deck is gone or almost gone (less than 3 cards remain).  When the game ends, count the gold on your unplayed cards. The goblin with the most gold wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Dogface
description:
Dogface is a solitaire WWII tactical combat RPG in which players take on the role of a single U.S. soldier, known as a "dogface" -- a hard-earned nickname given to the infantrymen who fought "their war" on the ground, on foot, through the mud and snow. Taking inspiration from such great games as Advanced Squad Leader, Combat! and the Combat Commander series', and Patton's Best, Dogface seeks to provide the player with the ultimate WWII man-level RPG experience, intentionally restricting combat to little more than the platoon level so as to avoid counter clutter, excessive unit stacking and tracking, and other difficulties. Depending on your chosen historical outfit, your dogface may fight the war in Europe from 1944 to 1945 from the beaches of Normandy, through the hedgerows of France, across the French countryside at breakneck speed in the mad dash towards the Franco-German border, fight to survive in the snowy Ardennes in the Battle of the Bulge, cross the Rhine, and join the sweeping advance through a ravaged and devastated Germany, ending the war somewhere within that country, or Austria, or Czechoslovakia. The game is dynamic, with missions, maps, enemy units, and so on generated through a mission generator. Whether a combat mission or patrol mission (combat patrol or recon patrol), your "doggie" will resolve his campaign on a week-by-week basis, suffering platoon casualties, losing comrades, maneuvering around German machine gun nests, tanks, halftracks, and any other myriad of enemy unit type. Along the way, he may earn decorations, awards, and experience. He may become the acting platoon leader through catastrophic losses, or he may be the platoon leader by default as a Lieutenant (2d or 1st). His fellow "doughs" may come to like or despise him, and his commanding officer (CO) may trust him or loathe him, depending on his performance. His ultimate goal, of course, is to survive World War II in Europe and return home, one way or another.

Dogface includes comprehensive rules, tables and missions books; a player character information sheet; two mats to track in-mission and in-patrol statistics; three counter sheets including soldiers, machine guns, bazookas, tanks, halftracks, radios, flamethrowers, and so on; seven combat calendars following the historical path of seven chosen units throughout their tenure in World War II in Europe (specifically, the 1st, 2d, 8th, 66th, and 80th Infantry Divisions, as well as the 4th Armored Division and 82d Airborne Division); and fifteen different maps representing hills, "Omaha" beach, rural areas, towns, urban areas, and woods.

Dogface requires two six-sided (d6) dice to play, and may be (but is not required) enhanced by taking notes and keeping a log on a separate sheet of paper, or digitally with any free word-like program, as your soldier's story develops.

—description from the publisher

name: For All Mankind
description:
For All Mankind is a fast-paced game of strategic exploration, clever trades, and diplomatic shenanigans. Build your empire across the ever-changing solar system. (Careful, the planets move!) Gather, trade, and invest your resources — and do whatever it takes to stay ahead of the competition.

Expand: Grow your empire with colonies (more loot!), research (more power!), and espionage (more nukes!).

Scheme: All is fair in interplanetary domination, but you would never double-cross a friend...right?

Profit: Be the first to reach 10 points, and see your name etched in the stars forever!

Learn to play in about 15 minutes.
Finish a game in about 60 minutes.
The most fun you’ll ever have blowing up your friends in space, guaranteed!

name: Dogs With Jobs
description:
Embark on a thrilling adventure in Dogs With Jobs! You’ve just been hired by your city to recruit a team of working canines and answer the call of those in need. It’s your first day on the job and your goal is to outperform other recruiters for the greatest amount of reward points possible!

Some jobs will call for grit, others for clever tactics. But each recruiter will face the challenge of organizing the most efficient team and utilizing each dog’s unique skills. With just 8 short hours in your day, every decision is crucial and unanswered jobs could cost you the win!

Will you emerge as the top team?

Dogs With Jobs is easy to learn and quick to set up, bolsters high replay-ability, and is engaging for all skill levels.

—description from the publisher

name: Dolcissima Vita
Dolmen
description:
Dolmen is a cooperative game of logic and spatial management, where players take on the roles of druids and shamanesses working to rebuild a stone circle and contain a growing lunar curse.

Each turn, a player plays a card that determines how many steps the Sun Herald moves along a circular track. The landing space indicates the available actions for placing or moving wooden blocks within the play area. Each card also shows a 3D block configuration—an objective that must be completed before the Moon phase is triggered.

When the Sun Herald crosses certain thresholds, the Moon advances. Its movement depends on the number and value of unresolved objectives. If the Moon advances too quickly, a Spell card is revealed, introducing new complications.

The game offers adjustable difficulty through a system of Curse cards, which introduce lasting conditions. Only a few are used each game, ensuring variety from one session to the next. Dolmen is designed to be accessible to family groups as well.

—description from the publisher

name: Domesday, The Norman Conquest 1066-1106
description:
King William reigned over England, and by his capacity so thoroughly surveyed it, that there was not a hide of land in England that he wist not who had it, or what it was worth, and afterwards set it down in his book. The land of the Britons was in his power, and he wrought castles therein and extorted from his subjects many marks of gold, and many hundred pounds of silver, which he took of his people, for little need, by right and by unright.  Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, 1087 

King Edward the Confessor of England did not prepare well for his death. To avoid trouble, he promised his kingdom to King Magnus Olafsson of Norway (a claim inherited by Harald Hardrada), King Sweyn Estridsson of Denmark, Duke William of Normandy, and Earl Harold Godwinson of Wessex. When Edward died on the fifth day of January 1066, these four powerful warlords raised armies to back their claims by force. William the Conqueror won the crown but had to defend his new kingdom from fresh invasions and rebellious barons. To formalise his control of the kingdom after twenty years of conquest, he ordered a Great Survey in 1085, a record so final and unalterable that it was named Domesday.

Domesday is a card driven game depicting the Norman Conquest of England from 1066 to 1106. The players control Normans, Barons, English, Danes, Norse, Scots, Welsh, and Irish, playing cards to resolve Events or use Action Points to activate their units. Players win by earning the most victory points through controlling, contesting, or plundering areas, building cathedrals and towers, and making their leader the King of England.

Maps - One full color 22"x34" mapsheet
Counters - 264 colorful die-cut 5/8" large pieces
Rules length - 12 pages
Charts and tables - 2 pages
Cards - 108 Complexity - Medium
Playing time - Up to 4 to 6 hours
How challenging is it solitaire? - Poor

—description from the designer

name: Dominance
description:
It will be the control of the most important provinces that establishes the final victory. You will have to bring as many territories to your side as possible by planning a careful strategy or trying to outwit your opponents. But if things get bad, you can always change sides! Set in the Roman provinces, among the Celtic tribes, in the dominions of medieval Italy, in the territories of the Inca Empire, in the Ottoman court, or in pre-industrial England, Dominance is a game of majorities with the outcome always hanging in the balance until the end.

There are three factions that claim dominion over a given territory. Each faction is represented by a metal coin, which, when placed on a territory, indicates its assignment. The game is developed on a variable board, built from hexagons. During setup, each territory is assigned to a faction. Each player represents a Roman Consul, a Celtic chieftain, a medieval lord, an Inca general, an Ottoman noble, or the head of an English noble family. The objective of the game is ultimately to be on the side of the winning faction.

On their turn, a player can carry out two actions of their choice: open a contest, strengthen, move, gain power, or place. Opening a dispute ends the turn in any case, and it works like this: each player secretly bets a certain number of coins, even zero. The coins are revealed, and the faction with the most, both on the territory and in the bets, wins. The territory is permanently assigned to that faction. The leader who led the faction to victory and the player who bet the most coins of that color get loot: new coins and the possibility of building in the territory or adjacent ones. Constructions (villages, cities, bridges, and the capital) increase the value of the territory. Strengthening allows you to add a coin from the game reserve to a territory that already has one (of the same color). Moving allows you to move coins from one territory to an adjacent one. Gaining power allows you to draw the first coin from the coin display. Placing allows you to put your own coin in a territory.

Each player's coin stock is kept secret. When all territories have been awarded (except one), the game ends. Each territory gives 1-5 points depending on the buildings present. The faction with the most points wins. The player with the most coins from that faction wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Dominate & Delegate
description:
Dominate & Delegate is a 2 player legacy campaign game and a skirmisher for up to 4 players, inspired by video games like Command & Conquer.

In the legacy campaign, each player choose a side and receive their own information needed for the current mission. Both players have secrets which are unknown to the opponent. Thanks to a deep and immersive story, both players advance their teams, fighting battles and try to see the best possible outcome for their faction at the end of the campaign... and there are lots of mission tree branches and possible endings available, depending on the decisions of both players.

In the Skirmish Mode, you can play up to 4 players, you can fight All vs All or even Team vs Team. Thanks to different scenarios, you have lots of options for maps, conditions and possible complexity and game length.

The game is heavily based on Strategy, Area Control and keeping secrets hidden. You are moving your units, building up the base and try to conquer the world. Thanks to a secret fog of war, your enemy don't know what you manufacture in the factories, also the amount of  production is a secret until the units are deployed.

Dominate & Delegate offers a unique campaign with dramatic twists and plots.

—description from the designer

name: Don Quixote: The Ingenious Hidalgo
description:
Based on the famous novel from Miguel de Cervantes, Don Quixote is a fast game of wit and strategy. Discover how Alonso Quijano became Don Quixote, how he asked a tavern host to make him a knight, the famous encounter with windmills turning into giants, his quest for Dulcinea's love and many more! Throughout the game, you will explore the stories told in the masterpiece that Miguel de Cervantes created. It's a great way to learn about this beautiful work and its message, while having fun.

Each round, the ingenious Don Quixote will head for a new adventure, and players vote simultaneously on whether to help him or not. Success in an adventure means Don Quixote progresses on his quest towards glory or love, while failure increases his delusion.

The twist: the more the knight progresses in one track, the more valuable your contributions to that track are, in a set collection mechanics where sets change value dynamically. Can you outwit the other players, anticipating what their next move will be, while not giving away your focus?

At the end of the game, you will score points for achieving your personal secretive objective. Each character you played is associated with one of DQ's attributes, and it will also score you bonus points depending on its value.

—description from the publisher

name: Don't Botch the Broccoli
description:
Steaming broccoli isn't as easy as it looks!

Time it just right and cook up a perfect place of green goodness. Just be careful that you don't botch the broccoli and have to start all over!

In Don't Botch the Broccoli, players have an identical hand of broccoli cards numbered -1 to 4 and simultaneously play one card each turn. Any players who played the same number on their broccoli card move their card to their steamer. Then whichever player played the lowest remaining card gets to cook their broccoli (move the card to their score pile), along with any cards in their steamer from previous turns. Any other players' cards are botched, and must return to their hand along with any cards in their steamer.

To win, you've got to find the right time to play each card so that you can cook up a big pile of broccoli.

—description from the publisher

name: Don't Frog With Me
description:
If you were a frog, you would love eating bugs, but would you do what it takes to best other frogs in a competition for the delicacies?

In this exciting trick-taking game, your tactical skills will be tested as you aim to catch more bugs than your frog-ponents and earn the most Victory Points. Hunt in various locations, win tricks, challenge other frogs, snatch victory from them, and be crowned the most agile frog in the swamp.

Players not only need to win the tricks but also strategically play cards from their hand to score it advantageously. They must also skillfully use challenge tiles to earn the maximum number of points. Additionally, players should keep a close eye on opponents because as soon as someone runs out of cards in hand, the round ends, and everyone tallies their Victory Points for the won tricks and challenges.

Be the best and become the fullest frog by the end of the day!

—description from the publisher

name: Donald Duck in Happy Camper
description:
The ducks are setting out to camp! In Donald Duck in Happy Camper, players race to explore the wilderness, set up camp, take scenic photos, and earn badges. Starting with an empty board, players reveal tiles and gather resources on their turn, but the more you have in your bag, the slower you go. Will you race to the best photo spot or set up tents in different terrains? There are bigger bonuses for being the first to complete a task, so plan carefully as you race to become the best happy camper!

—description from the publisher

name: Avatar: Journey of Aang
description:
In Avatar: Journey of Aang, 1-4 players join forces, taking on the role of Aang's companions. Each player will guide Aang in his journey to master fire, air, earth, and water, and restore balance to the world. If they hope to succeed, players will have to help Aang master the four elements by drawing cards and putting them into his practice tableau, learn powerful new techniques, confront dangerous adversaries, and use the environment to their full advantage. With Sozin's Comet drawing near, Aang's companions must race along a track either  to confront Ozai, or risk fighting him with the full power of the comet. See if you have what it takes to guide Aang to success in Avatar: Journey of Aang!

—description from the publisher

name: Doodle Disaster
description:
Doodle Disaster is a party drawing game that perfectly showcases how quickly and hysterically communication can break down.

Players take turns as either the Doodle Dictator or a Doodler. As the Doodle Dictator, you explain how to draw a picture only you can see. You can only describe the picture using lines and shapes. The Doodlers keep their drawings hidden and must remain silent!

After two-minutes, the Doodlers guess the picture. Did the Doodlers create recognizable works-of-art or Doodle Disasters?

—description from the publisher

name: Company of Heroes: 2nd Edition
description:
Company of Heroes, the World War 2 board wargame, is based on the video game from Relic/Sega. It closely captures the choices, tactics and mission strategies of the videogame. In teams, or as individuals, players will maneuver units and battle for control points to collect manpower, munitions and fuel. Players spend these resources to construct new buildings, purchase units and upgrade abilities, eventually unlocking the powerful end-game units of their nation.

The second edition of the Company of Heroes introduces extensive improvements to gameplay, tactical choices, unit balance, faction differentiation, mission parameters and more. It adjusts unit and building costs, resource generation and other mechanics to allow for more units to be purchased, fielded and used over the course of the battle. It so  further tweaked and balanced units, factions and commanders to a high polish. These changes were incorporated with an eye towards emphasizing faction identity and distinction.

-description from publisher

name: Doom Pilgrim Pocket
description:
DOOM PILGRIM Pocket is a mint tin box version of  Doom Pilgrim solo adventure. More compact and faster fun!

This solo card game is a roguelike adventure in the form of 90 cards (the size a bit smaller than a classic MtG card, so-called mint-tin card) with pictures on the whole front sides and texts on the whole back sides. You represent a doubtful hero struggling through his miserable fate in a grim medieval open world full of mortal dangers and cruelty.

On every turn, you take 3 cards from the top of the deck that represents your future. From the three cards, just based on the images, you choose one path to reject, one path to postpone, and one path to go. The path you have taken is then revealed - you turn the card, read the story, make some decisions according to the text and apply the eventual changes, losses, or gains to your character sheet or just a piece of paper. This way you build your fate of a medieval pilgrim-hero and you try to survive the whole journey to the bottom of the "your future" deck. There are fights, NPCs, equipment, and many more... just as in a gamebook (a very grim & dark one, full of odd meetings) but there is no dice rolling, everything depends on your decisions and on the path you had gone before. For the next play, you will possibly remember what image hides what kind of event or fight, so you may choose your path wiser, according to your current equipment, and fitness.

It contains the same cards as Doom Pilgrim, the grimdark medieval fantasy game. The card texts are shorter and use 1 point smaller font than the classic version, so the narrative aspect of the game is a bit reduced and also card effects are sometimes less complex. On the other hand, the gameplay is smoother and more actionable thanks to it. Some cards were on the contrary equipped with new effects so that we use all of the space the most effectively. Thanks to shorter text and more straightforward effects, this pocket version is better for most of the multiplayer options.

—description from the publisher

name: Doomsday Manager
description:
I designed this game to flip the classic asteroid apocalypse on its head - the real fight happens long before the asteroid hits.

The game takes place in an alternate 2126, where sci-fi weaponry merges with modern technology and age-old political maneuvering shapes the struggle for survival.

Engaging mechanics keep you immersed from start to finish - beginning with asteroid discovery and bureaucratic roadblocks, escalating to social upheaval and the race to fund orbital weaponry and destroy the asteroid.

Doomsday manager offers a tough and challenging experience, but with simple rules and a quick setup. It keeps players engaged from start to finish, evolving with dynamic progression - unlocking new features and changing gameplay as you go.

—description from the designer

name: DOOMTILE
description:
DOOMTILE is a tactical arena brawler played on a randomly assembled and dinamically modifiable arena of 25 tiles of different kind, each with its specific effect.

Your goal is to outscore your opponents by being the first to reach 10 Victory Points, or by having the most points when the fifth round ends. You earn points by eliminating other Heroes in combat or by completing secret objectives, like conquering a set number of tiles (by walking over them) or interact with the battlefield in some way.

The turn structure is very simple: at the start, you draw two cards and receive an amount of mana based on the number of the round. Then you get an Action Phase, where you can spend Mana to cast spells, set traps, and equip upgrades, or to perform actions like moving, building, swapping or destroying tiles.

If you ever need more mana, you can always get some by discarding cards. The catch is that those same cards are used not only for their effects, but also to decide the outcome of Combat, so you should manage your resources very carefully or you will be an easy prey.

Whenever you move next to an enemy, you both will be forced to get in Combat, and whoever loses the fight will be removed from the game. But it's not over yet! Elimination is temporary, and Heroes will respawn at the start of their next turn, ready to jump back into the fray, so be careful who you mess with!

—description from the designer

name: Doppelganger Tricks
description:
At a glamorous costume party, rival cliques vie to outshine each other with elegance — but lurking among the guests are doppelgängers, creatures who imitate others so perfectly they vanish when confronted with their exact double. Style is everything, but only the real ones survive.

Doppelganger Tricks is a must-follow trick-taking game where special “doppelgänger” cards mimic the lead suit. However, if a doppelgänger encounters a card of the same suit and rank, both vanish from the trick. Players must strategically deploy these deceptive cards to win tricks (or eliminate threats) while anticipating what’s real and what’s a fake.

name: Regicide Legacy
description:
A terrible corruption has spread over the world of Deccaria. The royalty have succumbed to its maddening haze. The Golden Blade Syndicate (a 40-strong band of professional adventurers) has been called upon by the High Crown Council to solve the mystery of this growing blight.

Regicide Legacy is the follow-up to Regicide. The challenging co-op trend continues in this campaign game spread over 12 perilous missions. Players will need to work together to beat each mission, solving the mystery of corruption along the way.

Mission 1 familiarises the players with Regicide, allowing new players to come to grips with the system, but subsequent missions bring new enemies, dynamic challenges and powerful upgrades.

Recruit new adventurers to the party, access all-new classes and unlock powerful items that will change the way you play the game.  But be warned! The faint of heart need not apply. Only those brave enough to take on brutal beasts and perilous opponents should venture into the world of Regicide Legacy!

—description from the designer

name: DORON: Ninja Trick Taking
description:
DORON is a trick-taking game with bidding, where you predict how many times you will win a number comparison out of the 9 cards dealt to you. However, instead of declaring your bid verbally, you do so by turning an unused card upside down and placing it in front of you. By paying a chip to “DORON” (vanish) from an unwanted battle, you can adjust your bid! Find your strategy from the various card combinations and become the ultimate ninja strategist!

—description from the publisher

name: Double Lucky 7: The Lucky Wheel Edition
description:
Double Lucky 7 is a casino-styled,  trick-taking board game where you predict the number of tricks you’ll win. With its unique blend of simple rules and surprising depth, it's both accessible and challenging for players of all ages. The game is playable in multiple environments, at home, on the go, or with friends.

Unlike most trick-taking games, Double lucky 7 provides multiple ways of playing. 2 games will never feel the same through the lucky wheel, lucky dice and double point in round 7.

The game combines classic card play, tactile poker chips, daring one-time Escape Pawns, and the thrill of the Lucky wheel and dice. Strategy meets luck across the fast-paced 7-round version or go all-in with the extended 14-round mode, keeping every game full of suspense.

After 7 or 14 rounds, the player with the highest score wins.

—description from the designer

name: Double Match
description: A quick 2-8 player game. Players have a hand of cards and a draw pile. You may play up to four cards each turn on top of the other cards in a 3 x 3 grid anywhere that the creates a row or column of all cards being the same number, the same color, or a run of three consecutive numbers (eq, 2-3-4). If a player play a card to make two matches at once, they may put a card from their hand directly into another player's draw pile.

name: Double Seven
description:
Double Seven is a modern twist on classic rummy-style gameplay. You want to collect large sets of animals to score, but you're not too picky about which animals you collect, trading sets with other players in order to get ones that you can grow.

The game features eleven tiles each of eight types of animals, along with three clovers (jokers), with players starting with three random tiles in hand. At the start of your turn, if your hand is empty, draw three tiles; otherwise, draw two. Next, take as many actions as you like in whatever order, with all but one of them being repeatable:


     Start a family: Place 2+ matching animal tiles from hand in front of you to form a new family of a type you don't have.
     Expand a family: Add 1+ matching tiles (or clovers) to a family in front of you.
     Swap families: Exchange one of your families with an opponent's family of the same size.
     Claim a clover: Swap a clover in a family on the table with the appropriate matching animal tile from your hand.
     Swap two for one: Once per turn, discard two tiles face up from your hand to draw one new tile from the table, whether face up or face down.


When expanding a family, if you bring it up to seven or more tiles, claim a 7 token from the reserve. The second time you claim a 7 token, take the 77 token as well, after which each other player takes a final turn.

Score 1 point per tile in front of you on the table, as well as 1 point per 7 on tokens you've claimed. Whoever has the most points wins.

name: Down Down Dungeon
description:
At last, you’ve reached the entrance of the Down Down Dungeon!
They say the structure inside changes every time you enter, gradually revealing its full form.
Try to make it back safely without encountering any monsters—and bring home as much treasure as you can!

Japanese version of Mysterious Dungeon!
The new Dragon Plate, which changes the scoring method, has been added, so it looks like the game will be playable for a long time.
Also, 20 new cards corresponding to tiles have been added, making it easier to play

—description from the publisher

ついにだんだんダンジョンの入口にたどり着きました！
この中の構造は入るたびに変わり、だんだん全容が明らかになっていくといいます。
モンスターと出会わず、たくさんの財宝を持って無事に帰りましょう！

—description from the publisher (Japanese)

name: Down: Expedition – Schatzjagd
description:
DOWN: The exciting cave expedition
Should you continue abseiling or rather wait and hope for the big treasure find? That's the question in this captivating family game for ages 8 and up. The cave explorers embark on an exciting expedition into the depths and hunt for the best treasures. But who will collect the most points in the end and who will find nothing more than a boring hard hat? It's not just luck that decides your fate, tactics are also required!

—description from the publisher

name: Downtown Las Palmas
description:
As the city of Las Palmas has expanded, its downtown area hasn’t kept pace. Expand this rundown neighborhood with new buildings and improve the lives of its many residents!

You’ve got your hands full with this citybuilding dexterity game! Add cards to your growing tableau without dropping them to revitalize your downtown. Build it bigger and bigger while still meeting your bonus goals to complete your urban planning successfully!

Each turn, add a new card to the growing city tableau in your hands. Connect them to your street while making sure to keep your scoring elements visible, overlapping other cards as necessary.

Drop a card and it’s all over: move directly to scoring what remains in hand. Otherwise, keep pushing yourself to add cards until you choose to stop or run out of new cards.

Score points for each card showing in your city, but lose points for fully hidden cards. Gain extra points for the scoring elements that match your bonus goals, then rank your work to see where you fall!

name: Dr Gribouille
description:
Welcome to the pharmacy of chaos with Dr Gribouille!

Patients are rushing to get their medicine, but there's a problem: Dr Gribouille's prescriptions are illegible! It's up to you to decipher the squiggles and get everyone treated in time.

A hilarious game where observation and speed are essential.

Will you be able to understand Dr. Gribouille's prescriptions and help the most vulnerable patients? Get ready for games full of laughter and tension.

—description from the publisher

name: Dr. Finn's Book of Solo Strategy and Word Games
description:
Dr. Finn's Book of Solo Strategy and Word Games contains eight solo games that can be played in the book without cutting them out. Each game uses one sheet of paper and requires only 1-5 dice and a pencil. The book contains eight copies of each game, as well as a score chart to track your scores. The games are:


     Cosmic Run: Mission One
     Spell It Out
     Pen Pals
     Crunch the Numbers
     My Perfect City
     Leftover Letters
     The Little Flower Shop: Open for Business
     Word Wrap


All of the games except Cosmic Run: Mission One are also playable as multiplayer solitaire. In this case, the player sheets need to be cut out of the book and/or copied.

name: Drachenpups & Tollkirschkern
description:
The young wizard apprentices are learning how to brew potions. But the ingredients are hidden in the dark cellar of the wizardry school. And the light goes out from time to time. So be fast and memorize what you can to find the ingredients even if you can't see them. A wonderful memo games not only for kids.

—description from the publisher

name: Moana Nui
description:
In the distant past, intrepid explorers from the western islands of the great ocean venture into the vast unknown. They hope to find new lands for their families, somewhere to call home.  But they are not alone. Others are racing to settle the islands they discover, islands scattered all over Moana Nui.

In Moana Nui, you and your friends compete for control over a newly-discovered island group. Create the islands as you explore, revealing precious resources along the way. Establish buildings and defend your new community. As you settle new islands, will you develop a peaceful presence or expand to neighbouring shores?  Be careful though, for as you compete for control, peace can turn to conflict.

Moana Nui is a hexagonal tile-placing game where you explore a newly discovered archipelago in the vast Pacific Ocean (Moana Nui). You and your friends will take turns placing tiles and resolving actions. Explore the archipelago, deploy units and move them to defend your new territory, or mobilise your forces to defeat those who stand in your way.

At the end of the game, controlling territory and buildings will score you victory points (VP). The player with the most points wins!

—description from the designer

name: Regicide Inferno
description:
Regicide Inferno is a standalone Regicide game. It's Regicide with a fifth suit: Flames. Flames allow you to combo with a card from your deck, making for some crazy high-powered plays. Flames also have a downside though - as you "flame on" you'll chew through your deck and banish cards in the process, never to be seen again!

New Flames enemies bring additional challenges to the game. There's also brand new rules that both help and hinder your progress through the game.

Regicide Inferno is a fun, cooperative challenge for both Regicide fans and Regicide newbies.

—description from the publisher

name: Dragon Ball Z: Duel Battle
description:
Compose your team and face an opponent in this miniature duel game!
Find the universe of Dragon Ball Z with your favorite characters and their special techniques in epic clashes for the quest of crystal balls

After composing your team according to the skill points of the different characters, go in search of the crystal balls! Would you rather face your opponent directly or search the board for bonuses?

On your turn, you can activate your characters one after the other, by rolling their action die. You can then perform 3 out of 5 possible actions: remove an immobilization, move, search, attack, acquire a capsule card. In addition, you can also launch a special attack like the famous Kamehameha!

KO opposing characters to earn victory points.

The game ends if a team is completely knocked out or after 7 rounds of play. The player with the most victory points wins.

name: Dragon Eclipse
description:
Enter a magical world of mythical beasts and ancient dragons in Dragon Eclipse! Uncover the secrets of the eclipse that changed everything and discover the dangerous and treacherous world that awaits you. Explore a vivid and immersive world filled with majestic and unique creatures you can battle, tame, catch, and train. Each creature has a unique deck of cards you can use in combat and special abilities, offering endless tactical possibilities to master.

In Dragon Eclipse! discover and befriend Mystling, elemental creatures roaming the land. Complete their personal quests, grow and train them, discover cards, and build powerful decks for your favorite Mystlings. Execute your combo in a highly tactical combat arena. Discover the great mystery of the Eclipse in an epic 12-scenario campaign, where you will make a lot of new friends and some enemies. You can also compete with a friend in the 1vs1 arena challenge OR play a fully gameplay-focused roguelite mode.

—description from the publisher

name: Dragon Eclipse: Mystling Academy – Peare vs Arboro
description:
Welcome to Mystling Academy, a standalone set in the world of Dragon Eclipse that focuses exclusively on thrilling PvP duels!

This two-player set includes everything you need for exciting battles, testing you, Tamer, and your Mystlings. Inside, you’ll find two unique creatures, along with a dedicated Arena for Combat.

—description from the publisher

name: Regicide: Crown Duels
description: Crown Duels is 2-player duel game, where players assume control of the corrupt royalty from Regicide. Like Regicide, it’s played with a standard 52-card deck. Don armour and weapons, cast spells and empower your equipment as you slowly become corrupt and unleash an epic beatdown on your opponent.

name: Dragon Tricks
description:
Dragon Tricks is a trick-taking game with a unique twist, designed to be accessible to kids and families while being deep enough to engage and challenge adult players too. The beautiful artwork complements a fun trick-taking and set collection mechanism to create an exciting and engaging experience for all ages.

Like most trick-taking games, Dragon Tricks is played over a series of rounds. Unlike most trick-taking games, players in Dragon Tricks don't have to follow suit. Tricks are won by the highest card in the suit that was played the most.

After each round, players will take turns trading in the tricks they won to hatch dragon eggs. The player who assembles the highest-scoring collection of baby dragons wins the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Gundam Card Game
publisher: Bandai Co., Ltd.; Bandai Namco Entertainment
description:
Welcome to the battlefield that covers space and Earth.

First announced in October 2024 during the BANDAI CARD GAMES Next Plan Presentation, the GUNDAM CARD GAME is here!
Launching simultaneously worldwide in English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese, this exciting new title brings fans of strategic card games and giant mechs together for a thrilling new experience in the legendary Gundam universe.
