Ahead of the full set release in July 2025, a special “Edition Beta” version of the game was launched in early December 2024 at BANDAI CARD GAMES Fest 24-25 in Utrecht, Netherlands, as well as during an exclusive World Premiere event in Houston, Texas.
The Edition Beta will also be available at BANDAI CARD GAMES Fest 24-25 Orlando on January 4–5, 2025, and at local game stores from January 31 to March 2, 2025.

What is GUNDAM?
The Mobile Suit GUNDAM anime first aired in Japan in 1979, revolutionizing the genre by portraying fictional mecha as "mobile suits," incorporating realistic weapons of war, meticulous scientific details, and complex human drama. This shifted the focus from the simplistic good-versus-evil narratives of earlier “robot anime” and established the genre of "real robot anime," which became a massive sensation. Since then, GUNDAM has continued to thrive, producing 24 TV animation works, 30 theatrical and screening releases, 27 OVA titles, as well as numerous streaming contents, events, and TV specials. It has garnered enduring popularity both in Japan and internationally.

What is the GUNDAM CARD GAME?
The GUNDAM CARD GAME is a collectible trading card game where players battle using Mobile Suits and pilots from across the Gundam universe.
Step into the role of a commander and build a deck filled with strategic options featuring your favorite characters.
Use Resource Cards to pay the costs of your plays, and claim victory by eliminating all of your opponent’s Shield Area cards.

The GUNDAM CARD GAME also features exciting multiplayer formats such as 2-on-2 Team Battles and 4-player Battle Royale. Gather your friends for a fresh and dynamic gameplay experience!

Decks are built using four card types: Unit, Pilot, Command, and Base.
These cards bring the world of Gundam to life, offering endless combinations of Mobile Suits and Pilots for deep strategic gameplay.
Master a variety of tactics and outwit your opponents to achieve victory!

Here is a brief introduction to the four types of cards that make up your deck:

UNIT CARDS
Unit Cards are primarily Mobile Suits that attack your enemy. Deploy up to 6 Units in your Battle Area. They can’t attack on the turn they’re deployed but can on the next turn. When a Unit is paired with a Pilot and its link requirements are fulfilled, it becomes a Link Unit and can attack immediately on the turn deployed!

PILOT CARDS
Unit and Pilot can be freely combined. Pilots are the characters that pair with your Unit to lead them into battle. Each Pilot can be paired with a Unit by placing it underneath it. The unit gets the AP (Attack Points) and HP (Hit Points) listed on the Pilot as a bonus, as well as the Pilot Effect. Such effects like drawing a card on attack, reducing an enemy units AP, or freeing up your Resources into active This allows for an endless number of strategies customizable to your current battle situation.

COMMAND CARDS
Commands are one-time use cards with effects that can turn the tide of battle. Drawing cards, adding extra Resources, and buffing your opponent’s AP are all powerful options found on Command Cards. Some Command Cards also can be used as a Pilot to boost your Unit’s AP and HP, or satisfy a link requirement allowing them to attack on the same turn! Make wise use of these versatile cards to surprise or deter your opponent’s game plan.

BASE CARDS
Bases are deployed in your Shield Area as the first line of defense for your 6 shields. Destroy your opponents Base and then aim for their shields to win. However, bases have powerful support effects for your battle strategy, and often have high HP, making them tough to take down. You may only have one Base deployed at once, and a good one can make all the difference between victory and defeat.

Full Set 1 and Starter Deck Release Scheduled for 2025 July.　The number of ways to enjoy it are endless! Attractive illustrations, new fierce battles.
Collect cards and dive into the world of "Gundam".

Website & social media accounts
https://www.GUNDAM-gcg.com/en/
https://x.com/GUNDAM_GCG_ENG
https://www.facebook.com/GUNDAMgcgen
https://www.instagram.com/gundam_tcg/
https://www.youtube.com/@GUNDAM_GCG

name: Star Trek: Picard – Murder on the Titan-A
description:
A Murder Mystery for 1-6 Players

Dive into the world of Star Trek: Picard to solve a murder.

A murder mystery game for 1+ players. Enter the world of Star Trek: Picard as you try to solve a murder and exonerate Captain Liam Shaw.

Use augmented reality technology to submit evidence, get hints, and launch Jean-Luc Picard quotes.

—description from the publisher

name: Dragonlings
description:
Dragonlings is a family-friendly card game where you play as a Dragon Trainer, competing to grow your dragon herd and amass the largest treasure hoard! It is for 1-6 players, ages 7+, with options for solo play and teams.

Players start by hatching eggs into Level 1 Hatchlings, and then stack Dragon cards to create Towers, with the goal of becoming Level 5 legendary Dragons. As Dragons grow, they learn abilities, which chain together to do amazing things! Treasures, Towers, Eggs, and Trainer bonuses are all worth victory points, so there are lots of ways to win!

—description from the publisher

name: Drakerion
description:
Drakerion is a Trading Card Game set in a Dark Fantasy universe. The team is made up of veterans of this type of game who wish to offer a unique gameplay experience. With straightforward rules, a dynamic game system, and a focus on interaction, player skill is what determines who wins in Drakerion. We invite you to a brand new adventure beautifully portrayed by some amazing international artists.

Welcome to Drakerion: The playing and trading card game.
In this game, play one of the five factions, use its tactics and strategy to defeat your opponent and lead your troops to victory!

There are two ways a player can win the game:
If at any point of the game a player has no Character left on the battlefield, they lose the game and their opponent wins the game. 
If a player has 20 prestige points or more, they win the game. Players will accumulate prestige mainly by destroying opposing Characters: The more powerful a Character is, the more prestige their opponent will gain when they are destroyed.

name: DreamEscape
description:
Great Cthulhu has trapped your sleeping mind in the Dreamlands. Your dream-self has shattered into multiple fragments, scattered throughout the dream world. It is your task to recover these lost fragments, unravel the story secrets and survive long enough to find the correct key and matching gate to escape and wake up!

Dreamescape is a narrative exploration game driven by story card encounters. Each encounter offers roleplay-like choices that drive the game in divergent directions so the game evolves differently each time you play. Our novel keycode system triggers secret alternative storylines based on collected clues and items! Chance of success is based on your skills, equipment and lore gained so far, while repeated play rewards your experience as you uncover different parts of the story and memory of playing previously guides your choices!

Play one of six unique characters in this solo or 2 player semi co-operative RPG-like survival horror game. Carefully manage your skills and resources, find rare items, gain secret knowledge and wield two uniquely powerful abilities - Deja vu and Lucid dreaming - to stay ahead of the minions of Cthulhu. Explore many hundreds of unique story encounters on your quest to recover the mind fragments and find a Dreamgate to let you wake from the nightmare. Failure will lead to insanity, locked forever in a dream within your own mind!

The game offers multiple interwoven story arcs and plot lines to keep you occupied, with hidden puzzles, traps and lore to uncover but all knowledge comes at a price. The more you experience, the greater your chances of being driven to insanity! To win you must avoid, adapt, or overcome the many dangers of this nightmare world.

—description from the publisher

name: Dreyfall
description:
Dreyfall is a 2-player strategy game of tactical combat and survival in a fractured woodland. Once, the creatures of the forest lived in harmony, guided by the magic of the Dreyshard, the great gem of the forest. When the Dreyshard was separated, its power plunged the land into chaos. Now, two rival factions battle for control, each guarding half of the Dreyshard within their home tree. To restore peace, you must defend your own stronghold while launching daring attacks to reclaim the lost shard from your opponent. Each turn, players make critical decisions about movement, attacks, and powerful abilities, exploiting a cyclical combat dynamic to gain a tactical edge. Mastering this dynamic is key to victory! The fate of the forest is in your hands—restore the Dreyshard and bring peace back to the land.

—description from the publisher

name: Driving Me Crazy!
description: In this quick family card game, you race to be the first to the holiday house to claim the biggest bedroom! Players draw and discard cards to be the first to reach exactly 1000 km in card points.  The game includes distance and action cards to move you along.  But watch out, your opponents can play negative actions on you as well.

name: Drop Zone: Southern France
description:
Drop Zone: Southern France is a fast-playing (about 2 hours), company-level game of the Allied airborne assault (code-named Operation RUGBY) that spearheaded Operation DRAGOON, the Invasion of Southern France—the Second D-Day, August 15th, 1944. The game can be played face-to-face, by 2, 3, or 4 players or solitaire (as the Allies). Early on the morning of D-Day, the allied First Airborne Task Force (1st ABTF) parachuted a dozen miles behind the Riviera landing beaches to seize key towns and road junctions, to prevent the German occupation forces from counter-attacking the amphibious landing, and to facilitate the advance of Allied forces. The 4:00 AM parachute drop was badly scattered due to an unexpected dense fog bank that blanketed the battlefield. Drop Zone: Southern France covers the first two days of this airborne operation in six tense turns, when the American and British paratroopers and glider-men fought surrounded and alone, supported only by French resistance bands.

The game board is a hex map of the Argens and Naturby River valleys and surrounding areas in Provence, Southern France, covering the area of operations. Each hex measures about 500 meters across. The key towns, villages, roads, rivers, and bridges that were fought over are indicated. The counters portray companies and company-sized units of allied paratroopers and glidermen, French resistance bands, German Infantry, and a few small armor units on both sides. Assets depict fire support units (artillery, heavy mortars, and anti-tank guns) as well as key capabilities (such as reconnaissance and seizing initiative).

Drop Zone: Southern France shines in its depiction of the fog of war (both literal and figurative)--unit type and strength is concealed until revealed in combat. On the first day, Allied parachute companies begin scattered across the board with minimal strength. German reinforcements arrive in a random fashion, often surprising and disrupting the plans of the opponent as well as the controlling player. The correlation of forces ebbs and flows as the Allies gradually build up their parachute companies and gliders deliver reinforcements and heavy weapons. Meanwhile, German reinforcements steadily increase in quantity and quality. The chit pull activation system adds another level of uncertainty. By D+1, the second day, both sides have gained in strength and acquire more powerful assets, leading to larger, bloodier battles as time runs out to achieve victory. It often comes down to the final roll of the dice.

-description from the publisher

name: Druid Path
description:
Druid Path is a solo monster-taming card game where you step into the role of an ancient Druid, wielding the primal forces of nature to tame Beastborgs—cyber-organic creatures forged from magic and machine. Your mission: stop the Darachs, rogue Druids corrupted by forbidden technology who seek to control these powerful beings for their own dark ends.

How to Play:

Choose your Path, select your Druid, and face off against powerful Darachs. You have just 10 turns to defeat them before corruption consumes everything.

Each turn, move along your Path to gain stamina and encounter new Beastborgs, magical items, or threats. To tame a Beastborg, collect the right gemstones and roll the dice to meet their tame value. Use item cards to boost your chances—but fail, and the Darach takes control of them, activating their dangerous shadow abilities.

Throughout your journey, you'll collect magical items and deploy robot allies to support your strategy. But beware—every item has a shadow side the Darach can twist and use against you.

With limited stamina and time, you'll need to carefully manage resources, create powerful combos, and make every move count. Can you restore balance before the darkness takes hold?

—description from the designer

name: Drums of War: Conquest
description:
“Life is a temporary lapse, we are eternal. Our horde increases with the bodies of our enemies. We do not rest, we do not surrender, we are the Death.”

Zarokk’s words as he watches the advance of his hordes of Raiders across the fields of Albea

Each side is different in this fantasy world in which two Heroes fight for control of the battlefield.

Pikemen, musketeers, golems and the rest of the troops of the dwarven army will face reborns, fallen, chimeras and the great horde of the Risen with agile, fast and full of strategy games.

With a 3 and 4 players system in its box, as well as an advanced mode where you can configure your deck of cards.

News in Drums of War – Conquest
A stand-alone installment, it does not require TdG Enclave to enjoy 2-player games.
Expands Drums of Wars – Enclave, it contains game rules for 3 and 4 players. Join both games and challenge your friends.
Brings 2 new complete armies: Dwarves and Risen armies.
Cooperative: Includes a cooperative game mode to play against the AI of the solitaire mode (2 players vs. AI).
You can configure your armies: Includes an advanced game mode that allows you to configure your army as you wish, and you can even use cards from differtent armies in your deck.

—description from the publisher

«La vida es un lapso temporal, nosotros somos eternos. Nuestra horda aumenta con los cuerpos de nuestros enemigos. No descansamos, no nos rendimos, somos la Muerte»
Palabras de Zarokk mientras observa el avance de sus hordas de Alzados por los campos de Albea.
Cada bando es diferente en este mundo de fantasía en el que dos Héroes luchan por el control del campo de batalla.

Piqueros, mosqueteros, gólems y el resto de tropas del ejército enano se enfrentarán a renacidos, caídos, quimeras y la gran horda de alzados con partidas ágiles, rápidas y cargadas de estrategia.

Con un sistema de juego para 3 y 4 jugadores incluido en la caja, así como un modo avanzado donde podrás configurar tu mazo de cartas.

Novedades de Tambores de Guerra – Conquista
Un juego independiente, no necesita de TdG Enclave para disfrutar partidas a 2 jugadores.
A la vez expande Tambores de Guerra: Enclave, pues contiene reglas de juego para 3 y 4 jugadores. Une ambos juegos y reta a tus amigos.
Contiene 2 nuevos ejércitos completos: Enanos y Alzados.
Cooperativo: Incluye un modo de juego cooperativo para jugar contra la Inteligencia Artificial del modo solitario (2 jugadores vs IA).
Podrás configurar tus ejércitos: Con un modo de juego avanzado que te permite configurar tu ejército a tu elección, puedes incluso utilizar cartas de varios ejércitos en tu mazo.

—description from the publisher (Spanish)

name: Drunk On Mars
description:
Embark on the treacherous journey to complete the colonization of Mars, getting it ready for the billionaire tourists who will soon be arriving. Without food or water and only a massive stash of alcohol to stay alive, you must navigate these completely sauced astronauts as they each race to conquer their mission before launching back to Earth.

Players are each dealt 3 task cards and 5 cards from the deck. Each player must acquire the necessary resource cards to successfully complete their (sometimes mindless) tasks. The first player to complete all their tasks wins! Beware of unruly obstacles like drawing a Passed Out card, keeping you from completing your mission. But fear not worthy space traveler, the Rocket Rope Ride card or a lucky roll of the dice will definitely help sober up your drunken astronaut.

And nobody likes to drink alone, so watch out for sneaky fellow astronauts getting you drunk and swiping your resources to complete their tasks before you! Drunk cards can be an advantage to you when played against another opponent. Playing matching Drunk cards affords players the opportunity to swipe a resource card or a card from their opponent's hand.

Additionally, players can experience other challenges along the way with skip, double skip, and shuffle the deck cards.

*Please note: Drinking is not required or part of the gameplay. However, due to the nature of the game we put the age requirement as 21+ yrs.

—description from the designer

name: Drunken Chonker
description:
Drunken Chonker is a ridiculous, party-ready card game set in the unhinged, snack-filled universe of Chonker Party — only this time, the Chonks are buzzed. Each deck is packed with boozy antics, cute art, and enough party energy to make even a sober Chonk stumble.

Sip, Snack, Score:
Take turns playing cards to win rounds and earn points — or just drink your way to victory. Yes, drinking will give you points.

Flip the Table:
Use Action Cards to turn the game on its head. Make others drink, steal their cards, or force them into outrageously unfair situations. It's fast, it’s foolish, and it’s full of surprises.

Get Tipsy, Get Tactical:
When the deck runs out, the player with the most points wins, whether they played smart, played dirty, or just outdrank everyone else.

—description from the publisher

name: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds – Mary Celeste
description:
An Escape Room Game for 1-6 Players

Join the Away Team from Star Trek: Strange New Worlds, explore a derelict ghost ship, and try to unlock its secrets.

Includes an Augmented Reality Cadet badge that you’ll use to solve puzzles and explore the ghost ship.

—description from the publisher

name: Ducks in a Row
description:
Will you play your Ducks to your Row or add them to the pond to increase the value for all players.  Can you swing the game in your favour, through triggering your ducks’ special abilities when you play them to your row?

Each round sees players balancing their hand of duck cards. Choosing to play to the shared pond to increase the value of ducks in everyone’s row.  Or playing to your row, enabling you to trigger your ducks’ special abilities.  Timing can make all the difference when triggering a duck’s special power.

Everyone plays simultaneously face down indicating row or pond using their location selection card.  Once everyone reveals their chosen card the real test starts, each player now plays their card from lowest value to highest value.  Will two ducks clash, leaving one or more homeless? Will you trigger your duck’s ability with perfect timing to take full advantage of their power? If you balance your hand of cards well, you'll be sure to ruffle the feathers of other players and come out on top in the pecking order.

The winner will be the first player to 40 points.

—description from the publisher

name: Ring of Chaos: Rising Fear
description:
Welcome to Rising Fear, the newest edition of the hit board game Ring of Chaos from Beadle & Grimm’s. Rising Fear takes all the competitive fun of the original edition and relocates it to a chilling new setting full of haunted graveyards, animated corpses, and fiendish grave robbers. This horror-themed new version of Ring of Chaos is a stand-alone game that does not require the original set to play, so it’s perfect for newcomers and experienced fans alike.

For savvy Ring of Chaos veterans, Rising Fear offers several twists to the rules that create new surprises and challenges, along with two terrifying maps with unique rules of their own. Everything in this new set is also compatible with the original game, so you can mix new parties and old parties, or play the parties from one set on the maps from the other! With six new monstrous Parties all bringing their special powers into the mix, every game of Ring of Chaos: Rising Fear will feel fresh, new and utterly horrifying!

—description from the publisher

name: Scream!
description:
Step into the eerie woods with Scream! where every card flip might unleash a shriek or a strategy.

Scream! is the "spiritual" sequel to Scram!

In the aftermath of the events in Scram!, the campers foolishly unleash the powers of the Necronomicon. Now your camping adventure has turned spooky with creatures from your darkest cinematic nightmares coming out of the woodwork! Can you survive the night?

Players will draw a card, play a card, or exchange the cards from their hand. Scream! introduces bluffing into this golf-inspired hand shedding game. "Scream!" when you perceive to have the lowest score, and with killer timing, you'll survive until morning victorious!

—description from the publisher

name: Duel of Chaos
description:
Duel of Chaos is the decisive test that will allow Chaos to choose who will accompany him in the battle against his brother. Faced with your opponent, exploit the diversity of characters by orchestrating their different effects.
The objective of this deck building: empty your draw pile in a single turn before your opponent.

name: Silver Eye
description:
Your village has been overrun by savage werewolves, which are represented by the number on each of the cards that make up your village. To get rid of these fanged fiends faster than the neighboring villages, use your residents' special abilities and your powerful secret weapon: a silver eye.

Call for a vote when you think you have the fewest werewolves, but be careful as everyone else gets one more turn to save their own village first.

Silver Eye is a fast and engaging traditional card game with a werewolf twist! Everyone starts the game with five face-down cards, with each player being able to choose and see two of their cards. Cards are numbered 0-13, with the number showing how many werewolves the character on that card attracts, and each character (number) has a different special power.

On a turn, you draw the top card of the deck or discard pile, then either discard it to use the power of the card (but only if it came from the deck), discard it without using the power (ditto), or replace one or more of your face-down cards with this card; you can replace multiple cards only if they bear the same number, and you must reveal the cards to prove this, being penalized if you're wrong.

Silver Eye can be played as a standalone game or combined with other games in the Silver series by Bézier Games. Each version of the game has different card abilities and a different silver token ability.

—description from the publisher

name: Dueling Horns
description:
DUELING HORNS is a two-player competitive game of Viking Warfare, pitting two armies against each other in the field battle. Strategy and wit will win you the day.

Each player controls an army of nine warriors and one king in an epic showdown for control of the battlefield or to slay each other's king!

Warriors and kings can turn the tide of the battle and are able to move any number of spaces horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. Players take turns moving one piece at a time, vying for position and striking down their foes. Movement is hindered by the shaded spaces in the center of the battlefield called the Mound. Players may also use their pieces to charge their enemies, stunning them for one turn.

In order to eliminate an enemy warrior or king, players must "Flank" their opponent's pieces by positioning their warriors or king on either side of an enemy piece.

The game ends when one of the kings have been eliminated, or when one player has gained control of the battlefield by removing all of their opponent's pieces from the Mound.

Each game box includes 20 painted game pieces, 5 metal coins, 1 Formation die, 1 battle board, and 1 barrows board.

-description from publisher

name: Duke
description:
Duke is a game of successive confrontations in which the winner is determined over several rounds. 
In a round, players take turns by either playing a card on their defense line (at the top) then playing a card on their attack line (bottom line) or by simply passing. The defending card must be the same color and strength as the last attacking card played by an opponent (with some exceptions).
To win a round, simply play your eighth and final card into your tableau. The card value of this last card is scored as victory points.
The first player or team to reach 15 points wins the game.

At 4 players, the game is played in teams.

Duke is loosely based on Goïta Shogi, a card game derived from Shogi. Shogi, literally "generals' game", is a traditional Japanese board game similar to chess.

name: Dumpster Dice
description:
Roll, win, and avoid the bin! In Dumpster Dice, roll to complete the numbered spaces on the lid while avoiding sending your dice to the dreaded dumpster. Dumpster Dice is an easy-to-learn, fast-paced game. With multiple ways to play, it’s perfect for family game nights. Combine it with Trash Dice for a bigger, crazier experience!

How to play:

     The first player rolls one die. This die will be set in the line in its right spot on the lid. The goal of this is to make a straight from 1 to 6.
     Next, the second player rolls one dice. If it matches the first die that is already in the line, it is Garbage and is put in the dumpster. On the other hand, if it’s a different number, then it’s placed in its correct spot in the line and play moves on.
     Play continues in this manner until one player places the last number in the line. When the line is complete, the player who put the last die in gets to pick up all the dice from the run. Now the next player re-rolls one die and adds it to the line to start a new round.
     The winner of the game is the player who manages to have dice when all other players have none.



     Includes 80 dice (4 different colors)
     Removable lid becomes game board
     Instructions include 4 additional ways to play
     Combine with Trash Dice to play with up to 6 players
     Includes sticker sheet to "tag" your dumpster


—description from the publisher

name: Dune: Kwisatz Haderach Edition
description:
Imagine you can control the forces of a noble family, guild, or religious order on a barren planet which is the only source for the most valuable substance in the known universe.

Imagine you can rewrite the script for one of the most famous science fiction books of all time. Welcome to the acclaimed 40-year-old board game which allows you to recreate the incredible world of Frank Herbert’s DUNE.

In DUNE you will become the leader of one of six great factions. Each wishes to control the most valuable resource in the universe - melange, the mysterious spice only found at great cost on the planet DUNE. As Duke Leto Atreides says “All fades before melange. A handful of spice will buy a home on Tupile. It cannot be manufactured, it must be mined on Arrakis. It is unique and it has true geriatric properties.” And without melange space travel would be impossible. Only by ingesting the addictive drug can the Guild Steersman continue to experience visions of the future, enabling them to plot a safe path through hyperspace.

Who will control DUNE? Become one of the characters and their forces from the book and . . . You decide!

name: Dungeon Brah
description:
Dungeon Brah is a comical Dungeon Deck-Builder game. It's a game you play with friends to test those friendships and hopefully share a laugh (sometimes haha, sometimes bwhahaha, usually muhahaha).

Within the dungeon roams a terrible Cathulhian beast, Kevin. You are on a noble quest to steal the loot or be the sole survivor. With noble intentions you and your party members embark on this quest, which will very soon devolve into disarray as loot runs low. Avoid Kevin at all costs when you’re weak, and storm into glorious battle when you’re OP to claim the beast's treasures!

Your party of two heroes dive through the deck to assemble weapons and items to fight the dungeon boss Kevin and his monsters. Kevin is a recurring roulette card that re-enters the draw pile after combat. When you defeat Kevin and his monsters, you will be able draw treasure cards. You win the game by either outlasting other players or by drawing 4 ‘The Loot’ cards from the Treasure pile.

Players are eliminated from the game when they are unable to defeat Kevin or his monsters in combat. The rules of the game can be changed by casting World Enchantment cards. Kevin, being the only recurring card in the game, will - in most cases - be the final card in the draw pile. If this is the case, all players take turns battling Kevin until there’s a winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Dungeon Crawl
description:
Dungeon Crawl is a game of selfish teamwork and rolls of the dice.

Enter the depths of this dangerous labyrinth as one of four mighty heroes. Players will battle 4 random monsters to reach the end of the dungeon. On their turn, players will make attack and damage rolls. Monsters and characters will progress as the game goes on, with players getting chances to rest, heal and collect loot cards along the way. Room Cards, After World Cards, Ally Cards and D20 Cards all add an extra twist to your game.

There are two ways to win: 1. Being the player with the most coins, or 2. The last player standing after a final Player vs Player battle.

—description from the designer

name: Dungeon Map Maker
description:
Dungeon Map Maker is a solitaire roll-and-write game played in two distinct phases. 
In the mapping phase, you will act as a scribe, mapping out the floor plan of a dungeon by choosing which rooms, tunnels, and caverns to draw. In the exploration phase, you will act as an adventurer, pursuing a main quest as you delve into the corners of the dungeon.
Set yourself up for success by carefully crafting your map, then challenge yourself against the worst of the dungeon!

—description from the designer

name: Dungeon Path
description:
A dimensional rip has allowed monsters to enter the worlds of Arkcantrix. Adventurers have entered the forbidden crypt with the hopes of conquering the new evil. The path is long and full of peril at every turn.

In Dungeon Path, each player chooses one of 12 characters that have their own weapon proficiencies, monster masteries and unique skills.

Each player receives 5 cards to start their Path as well as their first Miniboss. Players will draw cards from their Path or go to Town to purchase weapons and spells, increasing their power, defeating monsters and Minibosses until they are strong enough to defeat the Big Boss encounter!

Other players can stall you on your quest by placing Nets or Obstacles on your Path. You can build your hand in many different ways to gain the power needed to finish your journey.  With over 150 cards in the Path deck, every play is different.

First to vanquish the Big Boss wins the game and saves Arkcantrix.

name: Dungeon Poker
description:
Dungeon Poker is a unique board game that combines Texas Holdém poker with the most intriguing fantasy elements and role playing games. The game has been created by passionate team of Finnish poker and fantasy roleplaying fans in a ten year long project.

In Dungeon Poker players will compete in a poker tournament with unique fantasy characters. Each character has unique special abilities they can use to interact with the game. During Dungeon Poker tournament, players will face monsters, find treasures, and use magical artifacts. Players also need to adapt to changing rules & conditions, when the blind levels get higher. Who will claim the ultimate title of the Dungeon King?

—description from the designer

name: Dungeon Rummy
description:
Dungeon Rummy is the first game set in the Misfits Universe. Four reckless (and not-so-great) heroes have decided to throw themselves against (not so) fearsome foes in search of the greatest reward there is: bragging rights at the local pub.

Each player has their own deck of 26 cards modeled after a traditional deck, with a few twists: instead of Clubs, Hearts, Diamonds and Spades, your four suits will be Tank, Damage Dealer, Support, and Healer. Also, some cards feature Mana symbols, which will allow the playable characters to execute their special actions.

During the monster phase — which happens first, because the heroes are really not that great — they will inflict damage on the heroes. Create combinations of cards to fight back, doing damage and generating Mana. But remember, cards of the same suit can never be side by side!

If a hero is knocked out, the game ends in a loss. If they defeat the boss, they win!

—description from the designer

name: Dungeon Saga Origins: The Dice Game
description:
The exciting “Push your luck” Dice Game set in a dungeon full of monsters and treasure!

A local fortress, long thought abandoned, has become infested with evil.  You are plucky adventurers, sent by the worried city council to delve deep into the dungeons of an ancient castle to explore its passageways – and clear it of its dark denizens.  Defeat as many as you can, and all the treasure you find is yours to keep.  Who of you can recover the most gold and claim the most glory?

—description from the publisher

name: Dungeons & Dragons: Builders of Baldur's Gate
description:
In Dungeons & Dragons: Builders of Baldur's Gate, a city-building game from acclaimed designer Matthew Dunstan, you are the head of a powerful family in the iconic city. You grow your prestige by building new businesses within the nine districts, both as one large network and across all the districts. You must also extend your influence with the three main factions of the city: the Council of Four, the Flaming Fist, and the Thieves' Guild. But Baldur's Gate is not only a city of industry in the Forgotten Realms, but a city of mortal danger. Mobs of monsters regularly attack the outer walls or from the harbor, forcing temporary alliances to fend off the incursions. Each family tries to take advantage of the crises, using them as stepping stones to advance their own agendas.

When you place buildings, you place an influence cube on them to indicate your control. This also applies to special keeps, gates, and watchtowers, which are represented by miniatures with slots for your influence cubes, allowing you to see the city grow in three dimensions!

—description from the publisher

name: Dungeons & Dragons: Edge of the Realms
description:
Every adventure needs a good map!

In Dungeons & Dragons: Edge of the Realms, you are explorers in the Forgotten Realms who will discover new terrain and magical places to prepare your adventurer's journey, but everyone else is roaming the lands at the same time, so think fast.

On a turn, everyone draws a map card into their hand, then they choose and reveal one at the same time. Check to see whether you've completed quests and score points, then pass your hand to the left and play a new turn. Along the way, you want to match up terrain, activate landmarks, visit cities, and (of course) fulfill quests.

After fifteen turns, you'll have a completed map ready for adventure, and the explorer who's netted the most points wins.

name: Dungeons of the Oak Dell
description:
Dungeons of the Oak Dell is a dungeon crawling roll & write game inspired by old-school PC classics such as Dungeon Master, Eye of the Beholder, and Grimrock.

Alongside rondel and dice drafting mechanics, determining how you will attack, how far you can delve into the dungeon, and what you will find, it also introduces an innovative and immersive fighting system, allowing players to almost feel every hit they deal to a monster. Each beast presents a different challenge, with unique skills and behaviors.

During the game, players will also level up their heroes and delve into different dungeons full of traps, locked doors, treasures, and other surprises. Their goal will be different depending on the current quest. The game will include a roguelite solo mode.

-description from publisher

name: Durian Smuggler
description:
Kuala Lumpur Airport is packed today, and something smells suspicious…
Play as airport security, inspect cabin bags, and uncover which one hides the forbidden fruit.

Play as a team and try to score high, or play competitively with the Durian Smuggler hiding amongst you.

The back of each card shows the luggage color, how many of that type are in the deck, and how many contain durian.
Each round, players give one card to another player and receive one in return. Then, everyone places their luggage cards into a shared grid — trying to avoid putting durian-filled bags next to each other. In cooperative mode, players will try to score high together. In competitive mode, players score individually for the luggage that they place, while the durian smuggler tries to place luggage with Durian next to each other.

—description from the designer

name: Dustbiters: Pocket Edition
description:
Dustbiters: Pocket Edition is a streamlined, 18-card wallet version of one of our favorite tiny games, Dustbiters, in partnership with creators Robbie Fraser, Jan Willem Nijman, and Terri Vellmann.


On the outskirts of the civilization, two rival car gangs are locked in a deadly car chase as they bid to outrun the unrelenting duststorm.

Dustbiters is a quick and furious card game about rival car gangs racing to outrun a giant dust storm. Last car standing wins! It's 100 miles an hour in the dirt and you're gonna need all the cunning, trickery and horsepower you've got!

During a turn the player has 3 actions that can be spent in several ways, each costing one action:
 - Draw a new car into your hand.
 - Place a new car at the front of the convoy.
 - Drive a car one space forward or one space backward.
 - Use a car power. Each car is unique, has different abilities, and affects the cars around it in different ways.

But beware, at the end of each turn the car at the back is destroyed by the dust storm!

name: Dwarf Mountain
description:
A strategic solo card game where you grow your underground kingdom while facing relentless threats. Expand wisely, manage resources, and fight off goblins, ogres, and dragons to claim your place in legend!

You have 2 decks of cards, your Dwarves deck and the Enemies deck. Each turn, cards are drawn from these decks to help you build your kingdom and defend it. The decisions you make when playing your Dwarves cards will determine how well you defend your kingdom against the enemy cards.

Each turn:

     Draw cards from the Dwarf deck.
     Build you Kingdom.
     Use Supply cards.
     Promote Dwellings or Warriors.
     Defeat the Enemy.
     Shelter the Dwarfs.


The game ends after you draw the last Enemy card.

The greatness of your kingdom will depend on the buildings and legends it leaves behind.

name: Dwarves: The Fall Of Karnarak
description:
In Dwarves: The Fall of Karnarak, you incarnate a dwarf clan leader. In order to protect your home, the famous citadel of Karnarak, you must collaborate with the other clan leaders against a powerful dragon trying to take it.

Among clan leaders, you discuss and decide a plan of action, always taking into account the special abilities of each clan, and the functions of each room of the citadel. During the siege, events that can affect your plans will happen, often for the worse.

75 EVENT CARDS: Destabilise your strategy, make spawns appear or siege engin threaten your citadel
60 SPAWN CARDS: Make enemies appear way too close for comfort
60 TROOP CARDS: Allow you to fight the spawns
60 RESSOURCE CARDS: Allow you to buy upgrades, specialists, beer, divine intervention, or forge special items
8 SPECIALIST CARDS: Allow you to work better
8 UPGRADE CARDS: Allow the citadel to work better
5 CLAN LEADERS: Your identity for the game
5 WARLORDS: Your sworn enemies, soon to be defeated hopefully.
1 MAP OF THE CITADEL: Your board, and your home

Defend the fortress against hordes of enemies, upgrade your citadel, hire specialists in your clan, and above all, try to defeat the dragon, together.

name: Dämmerwache
description:
The sinister owl has kidnapped the queen's children and carried them off to the gloomy witch tree! Brave heroes set out to rescue them and bring them safely back to the queen. But the path through the dark tree is dangerous and full of challenges. Only with clever planning and courageous effort can the rescue succeed. An excit-ing adventure for all who have the courage to face the evil owl!

—description from the publisher

name: E Squadron: A Solitaire Game
description:
Rumours of a group of British special forces Operatives known as 'the Increment' have been circulating for many years. Operating on behalf of Britain's Secret Intelligence Service, the missions undertaken are 'black ops' - deniable missions that would be refuted by the British government if compromised. These include a whole range of objectives where maximum discretion is required. E Squadron is the modern day successor to the Increment but no official confirmation of the group or any of its operations has been given.

In the game you will be controlling a few Operatives from E Squadron as they attempt daring missions. As you will discover, stealth is often the key tactic here, although once that advantage is lost, things may well become more hectic!

Set on a square grid, the game implements an easy system of line of sight as your Operatives and the Hostiles they face move around inside and outside buildings. Try to find cover and stay hidden or simply shoot your way out. You decide the approach. Explosives, climbing, overwatch - it's all here in this easy to learn and hard to master solitaire game.

The game includes the rules, suggested colour counters and 10 full coloured Mission Maps.

Replayability is provided by varying set up and using a different mix of E Squadron Operatives for each play through.

—description from the designer

name: Eagle Leader
description:
Eagle Leader is a solitaire air tactical game which depicts NATO's air war in a series of hypothetical Cold War Gone Hot scenarios. The game covers the late Cold War, from 1976 (the introduction year of the Eagle) to 1991, with featured aircraft including the F-15C Eagle, the F-15E Strike Eagle, the F-111 Aardvark, the EF-111 Raven, and the F-16 Viper.

Eagle Leader focuses on force packaging-- the selection of the right aircraft and the right munitions will make the difference between success and failure for your squadron. You will be asked to make decisions that NATO Air Planners would've had to consider in the real world.

This game adds new aspects to the Leader series such as electronic warfare aircraft, US and NATO-specific skills, and an expanded "Squadron Operations" module for Leader players looking for the most detailed experience.

The core game contains 336 cards and 704 counters, including:


     222 x Aircraft cards
         F-15C Eagle
         F-15E Strike Eagle
         F-15J Eagle (Japan)
         F-16C Fighting Falcon
         F-16 ADF
         CF-18 Hornet (Canada)
         EF-111 Raven
         F-111C Aardvark (Australia)
         F-111F Aardvark
         F-4F Wild Weasel
         A-4K Kahu (New Zealand)
         A-7D Corsair II
         Tornado GR.1A (United Kingdom)
    
     17 x Squadron Asset cards
         RF-4 Flash Phantom
         A-10 Thunderbolt II
         F-117 Nighthawk
         E-3 Sentry
         KC-10 Extender
         KC-135 Stratotanker
         Airborne Battalion
         Army Attack Helicopters
         M270 MLRS
         PJ Teams
         SOF Team
         Tomahawk Strike
    
     50 x Target cards
     37 x Event cards
     10 x Special Condition cards


In addition, the core box includes:


     8 x Campaign sheets
     3 x Skills / Traits / Player Help sheets
     1 x Sequence of Play Flowchart
     1 x Airbase Squadron Control sheet
     1 x Player Log sheet
     1 x Tactical Display board
     1 x Rulebook


—description from the publisher

name: Eagles of Rome I: Caesar
description:
Eagles of Rome is a grand tactical two-player system for battles of the Roman Era, from the Republic through the Empire to the early Byzantine era. Caesar covers the battles of the Late Republic to the Early Empire (roughly 120 BC to AD 250). Players command armies of various types of forces, from Roman legions to barbarian hordes, with distinctions between melee and fire combat, plus special tactics. Morale is a critical factor. Caesar is played in scenarios. Each scenario represents a historical battle. The rules are in three sections. The first contains the Standard Rules common to all games in the series. The second is the Optional section, which gives rules that players can use at their option or not. The third is the Scenario section for specific battles.

Each hex on the map represents 100-200 meters across, depending on the battle. Each game turn represents 15 to 45 minutes, depending on the intensity of the action. Units represent three to five Roman cohorts, their equivalents, or amorphous groupings of irregulars (1,000 to 3,000 men, based on the era and efficiency of the army). Leaders represent single great commanders, war chiefs or the staff of a legion or other higher formation.

name: Earth 2053: Tipping Point
description:
In Earth 2053: Tipping Point, players represent countries that work together to prevent a global climate catastrophe. The main scoring happens on a physical seesaw board where "prevention" tokens are placed on one side and "pollution" tokens on the other. Filling the prevention side lets all players win (with optional placements based on who contributed the most). However, if the board tips towards the pollution side, all players lose.

Each player has their own country board with their own special ability, where they track their economy and their population's need fulfillment. Increasing the fulfillment levels of certain needs will unlock more and more powerful rewards, but at the same time threatens to create additional pollution.

One of the major goals of the game is to use your country's board setup to create "influence" tokens which can then be used to prevent climate events from (such as species extinction) from occuring in a negotiation about who is willing to invest how much per event. Stopping these events creates prevention points, while failing creates pollution.

The primary way of increasing need fulfillment is playing cards onto a grid shared between all players. Some cards have special effects depending on which other cards they are played adjacent to. Playing cards of the same category next to each other comes with its own set of bonuses.

—description from the publisher

name: Earthrise
description:
The Apollo 8 mission led astronauts Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders to become the first humans to see the far side of the Moon and witness the first rise of the Earth above the horizon of our satellite. The iconic photograph, known as Earthrise, makes us shrink before the immensity of the Cosmos.

In the game you will play several turns to obtain Mission cards and Maneuver tokens while trying to avoid Alerts. You will gain rewards and maybe, go down in History.

If you are lucky enough, you will capture the best photographs of the Mission and whoever earns the most Honors will be the winner of the game.

Earthrise is one of the most iconic images of space exploration. Captured in 1968 during the Apollo 8 mission, it shows the Earth rising over the Moon’s horizon, offering a stunning view of our planet, in contrast to the Moon’s desolate surface.

—description from the publisher

name: Easy Answers
description:
Easy Answers is a party game. This game will make you laugh, cry, sweat, and probably throw your marker across the room.

In Easy Answers, players are asked simple questions with simple answers, so anyone can play. The problem is, players may not want to write down the first thing that comes to mind, because more points are awarded for unique answers. Oh, and players also need to write their answers super fast to beat the competition. So just avoid the obvious answer and do it really fast. That’s Easy Answers.

One player acts as the player judge, asking the question and scoring the answers.  In each round, the judge changes.  The first player to 25 points wins.  Points are awarded for uniqueness and being the first (fastest) write an answer.

Example:
A card is flipped and reads “Something you watch.” Well “TV” of course. But wait… everyone’s going to write that. I’ll go with “movies”, but even that seems obvious. “People”? I watch people? A little creepy but I honestly do sometimes.  Ok, I need to decide.

name: Easy Peasy
description:
In Ptit Pois ("Easy Peasy" in English), get rid of your cards and end the round when you think you have the lowest score... But be careful, you don't know all your cards! Will you take the time to reveal them?

On your turn, play your cards on one of the 2 discard piles, respecting the direction set by the Up&Down card: either go up in value, or go down. Don't hesitate to change this direction to gain an advantage and slow down your opponents!

Anticipate your actions to get rid of the cards you have in your hand or in front of you at the right moment (some of which are hidden at the start) to end the round and score as few points as possible! After 3 rounds, the player with the lowest score wins the game.

Get ready to get hooked on Easy Peasy, it's so clever and fast! Designed for 2 to 6 players, it shines in all configurations.

—description from the publisher

name: EAUCHEMIN
description:
Sail the waters and become the master of trade.

In this region where the River Fune flows quietly, all logistics depend on the transportation by ships. Along the riverbanks, various industries such as iron, stone, and fabric thrive.

As the leader of a trading company in this city, your goal is to become the behind-the-scenes ruler at the center of logistics. You will transport materials brought from upstream to the downstream city, utilize accumulated wealth to strengthen your company's ships, and expand by hiring new employees.

However, the competition on the river is fierce, and other companies are gaining momentum. You must skillfully transport materials, establish dominance in the city, and continue to overwhelm other companies.

A tale of wealth and glory unfolds through Worker Placement × Majority Battle. Steer your ship and pave the way for the future of the city.

—description from the publisher

name: Echoes of Emperors
description:
Echoes of Emperors is a medieval-themed strategic card/board game.

Develop your empire's army, economy, and technologies to conquer your opponents.

Echoes of Emperors is a strategic board game where players choose from six distinct civilizations: Norsemen, Byzantines, Mongols, Scots, Ottomans and Holy Roman Empire. Maneuver your units to explore new lands, establish settlements for economic prowess, and engage in thrilling battles. Utilize cards to activate units and technologies, shaping the destiny of your civilization. Victory awaits those who can destroy their opponent's capital or eliminate all their active units. Get ready to embark on an epic journey of conquest and domination!

The game is focused on 1v1 gameplay, but can also be expanded for more players.

—description from the publisher

name: Silver Fang
description:
Your village has been overrun by savage werewolves, which are represented by the number on each of the cards that make up your village. To get rid of these fanged fiends faster than the neighboring villages, use your residents' special abilities and your powerful secret weapon: a silver fang. Call for a vote when you think you have the fewest werewolves, but be careful as everyone else gets one more turn to save their own village first.

Silver Fang is a traditional card game with a werewolf twist! Everyone starts the game with five face-down cards, with each player being able to choose and see two of their cards. Cards are numbered 0-13, with the number showing how many werewolves the character on that card attracts, and each character (number) has a different special power.

On a turn, you draw the top card of the deck or discard pile, then either discard it to use the power of the card (but only if it came from the deck), discard it without using the power (ditto), or replace one or more of your face-down cards with this card; you can replace multiple cards only if they bear the same number, and you must reveal the cards to prove this, being penalized if you're wrong.

Silver Fang can be played as a standalone game or combined with other games in the Silver series by Bézier Games. Each version of the game has different card abilities and a different silver token ability.

Silver Fang is unique because it includes team rules and cards that, while they work for individual player games, can be leveraged for team play. The Silver Fang token creates a personal discard pile that can only be accessed by the Fang owner, providing a place for them and their teammate to play cards that only the Fang owner can choose from.

—description from the publisher

name: Haunted Mouse
description:
Looming high above a forgotten village stands the remains of a forgotten cathedral. On cloudy nights such as this, only the flickers of a few candles light the empty aisles, bringing warmth to the five sole inhabitants: Parm, Brie, Gouda, Jaq, and Colby.

With only embers of light to shield them from darkness, the purring wind wraps and winds its way through the pews, fueling the fears of our five little mice. Spine-chilling specters of carnivorous creatures haunt their dreams. Images of cat claws, glistening snake fangs, and ominous owl eyes lurk in every corner of their minds.

Will their fears bring endless hours of restless sleep or will they shed these ghastly nightmares? Be the first mouse to wake up and grab the most cheese from the kitchen. As we all know: the early mouse gets the cheese!

Haunted Mouse is a ladder climbing/shedding game where mice not only shed their own fears (cards), but can use the fears of others! After all, why work hard shedding your own fears when your opponents can do it for you? The earlier you get rid of all your fears, the more cheese you get! Be the first mouse to complete their cheese wheel wins the game and never goes hungry again!

—description from the publisher

name: EcoLogic: Europe
description:
EcoLogic is a logic game whose mechanics were created to show the relationships between plants, fungi and animals. Players create complex ecosystems using cards representing hundreds of living organisms, inhabiting a variety of habitats.

Players compete to build the most diverse habitats, earning points for species and habitat diversity.  The game ends when all cards have been played.  The player with the most points wins.

name: Ecosfera Baltica
description:
Ecosfera Baltic Sea is a version of the Ecosfera game.

A cooperative game in which you must restore the Baltic Sea.

A version with faster games and more unpredictable scenarios that will put you on edge.

Jointly designed between Julibert Games and Helcom. a intergovernmental organization bridging policy and science on matters related to the environment of the Baltic Sea.

name: Eden: The New World
description:
Eden: The New World is a miniatures game for 2-4 players that immerses you in a dark and mature post-apocalyptic universe. It is a game of deep tactical richness that combines a strong requirement in the placement of your fighters and the multiple combinatorial possibilities of combat systems and special abilities. Thanks to a unique and original movement system and the resources you will have to collect on the field, the game is not only fast (one hour per game on average) but also particularly immersive.

—description from the publisher

name: The Game Makers
publisher: Bézier Games; Panda Game Manufacturing (PandaGM); Transludis
description:
Your office job has been grinding you down. Then one mysterious Monday, you receive a letter from your family lawyer informing you that a long-lost relative has bequeathed you a factory. You decide to risk it all, quit your day job, and follow your dream to become the greatest board game manufacturer the world has ever seen! You'll have to hire staff, build an assembly line, invest in additional structures to your factory, gain and fulfill contracts, and market your line of board games to the world.

In The Game Makers, players are board game manufacturers racing to build the greatest collection of classic modern board games. Build over 300 real-world games from over 100 real-world publishers. You can build Wingspan, Brass: Birmingham, On Mars, Terraforming Mars, Android: Netrunner, Ark Nova, Twilight Imperium: Fourth Edition, and many more!  The Game Makers is a love letter to the board gaming hobby.

The central warehouse rondel which dominates the center of the gaming table has players simultaneously choosing which game components to manufacture in a given turn and how to use them. The Game Makers features not only multi-use cards but also other multi-use components. Will you use these components to fulfill a coveted contract or upgrade your factory?

● Add plastic components to your factory to unlock special abilities.
● Gain workers to use your special abilities, or use the workers from your break room to gain board game components. 
● Roll your dice to increase your marketing for endgame scoring. 
● Use punchboard to expand your assembly line, giving you further discounts on manufacturing games.
● Stockpile the necessary plastic, workers, dice, punchboard, and cards to manufacture one of the greatest games of all time?!

Gain the necessary requirements to manufacture a game, and then add it to your display case of legendary games! Will you manufacture your favorite board game? Or will you manufacture the game you hate for more points? Score points from the games that you built and how well you marketed them.

name: Zombie Princess
description:
In Rebel Princess, the princesses fought off unwarranted marriage proposals from pesky princes. Twenty-eight days later, the princes returned...as zombies!

The zombie horde is growing. It began with the princes, but it has spread to the local villagers, the adorable woodland creatures, and even our noble knights! The rebel princesses are the last of us. If they fail, the kingdom will fall forever into darkness — a true and horrific Zombieland!

Zombie Princess is the sequel to Rebel Princess. Just as Rebel Princess was a thoughtful modern spin on the classic trick-taking card game Hearts, Zombie Princess is a spin on the classic trick-taking card game Spades.

As legendary princesses in Zombie Princess, players compete individually or as teams! Each princess is armed with a unique player power, giving her or her teammate much needed flexibility or information. Zombie Princess takes place over four rounds, and each round has a special rule, making each game feel fresh and unique. Princesses bid on how many hordes of zombies they will eliminate... er... save each round. Will you eradicate the resident evil of the land, or will this be the dawn of the dead?

—description from the publisher

name: Bombastic
description:
Find three in a row without causing an explosion!

Bombastic is a spicy, five-minute, travel-friendly game for two players. One player is Xs, and the other is Os — pretty standard so far. But what you don't know can hurt you. Nine chunky tiles are shuffled face down into a 3×3 grid — 4 of them Xs, 4 of them Os, and the last? A ticking, delicate bomb. Can you find your tiles without blowing up?

On your turn, either:


     Go for It — Show three tiles in a row. If they are yours, you win! If you show the bomb — BOOM! You lose! If you show any of your opponent's tiles, then you give them helpful information (whoops), but the tiles are placed back face down, and the game keeps going.
     Use one of two available action cards to help you peek at and rearrange tiles, staying one step ahead of your rival.


Only the cleverest player who uses the action cards wisely (and isn't afraid to take a chance here and there) will be able to win Bombastic!

Bombastic is part of Bitewing Games’ Travel Line. It comes packaged inside a clamshell case with a carabiner, making it easy to play with anyone, anywhere!

—description from the publisher

name: EGO
description:
We are not alone! It is the 23rd century, and proof of alien life has finally been discovered beyond our solar system. In fact, recent developments in technology have triggered a cascade of discoveries throughout the galaxy; intelligent life and advanced civilizations are now known across many planets, moons, and asteroids in the Milky Way. Now the race is on to establish interstellar relations with the aliens. The only chance we have of reaching alien life is by pooling our resources to build the required Super Ship. In an unprecedented, albeit uneasy, co-operation between the planetary governments, the peoples of our solar system have finally built the first of these Super Ships. Now, the coalition known as the Extraterrestrial Greeting Organization — EGO — is now ready to launch our first mission.

In EGO, players proceed through a sequence of major and minor events including auctions, drafts, risks, and more. Risks and egos are the lifeblood of this game as players will frequently find themselves in a game of chicken with their rival ambassadors as they try to impress various alien civilizations and earn political power.  At the end of the game, players earn significant bonus points or suffer serious penalty points depending on how offensive the aliens find them to be. Ultimately, the ambassador with the most prestige and respect will earn a seat in the Galactic Senate and be crowned the winner of the game.

EGO is a drastic reimagining of the strategic, push-your-luck auction game, Beowulf: The Legend and introduces many innovations by:


     Revamping the polarizing risk mechanism while preserving its excitement and drama
     Increasing the set-up variety with a randomized sequence of interchangeable civilization boards
     Streamlining the endgame push-your-luck token system in which players can score big or suffer immensely
     Introducing exciting new features such as currency cards and transmission events
     Balancing the bidding tie-breaker system with the simple solution of ranked cards
     Speeding up the playtime with a condensed and focused sequence of events
     Doubling the number of unique special cards that can be drafted as rewards
     Spicing up the risk events with varying rewards and penalties
     Sharpening the endgame hand management decisions with tempting rewards following a climactic final auction
     Broadening the appeal of the theme and presentation with vivid galactic artwork by Marie Bergeron


—description from the publisher

name: Elder Space
description:
Elder Space is a solo dark space exploration game where you play as an investigator sent to the most remote corners of the grimdark universe through spatio-temporal rifts.

Every turn you choose from three cards, seeing images only: one card to discard, one to put on the bottom of the deck, one to play. You make your choices, gathering points of Failure on your journey, which you will weigh against points of Success to see if your people will take you back home, or if they leave you far from your galaxy as an expendable, a failed experiment. As you learn to remember which image hides what danger or benefit, the game changes from exploration more into planning and strategizing.

The game consists of 90 tarot-sized cards, from which you take 60 random ones for each session. Pen and paper is also needed to track the character's progress, acquired statuses, and equipment.

The mechanics are a variation on those of Doom Pilgrim.

name: Eldfall Chronicles: Northern Wind
description:
“Northern Wind” is an immersive, tactical dungeon-crawl experience. It combines narrative-driven RPG elements with refined skirmish mechanics, plunging players into a grim struggle for the fate of an empire.

Face a devouring, profane evil with a band of courageous—but unlucky—heroes as you ascend the blighted slopes of Mt. Byōdō. Every choice you make shapes the story across multiple branching storylines.

Gameplay Overview
Designed for 1–4 players, Northern Wind delivers a cooperative experience that balances strategy, story, and atmosphere. Players form a party of four heroes, each with unique skills and backgrounds, and progress through three interconnected storylines, each containing 13–20 quests. An optional game master can guide the narrative and control opposing forces.

Accessible but Deep
Built as an ideal entry point into tactical dungeon-crawlers, Northern Wind offers a rich mix of exploration, lore, and fast-paced combat. Its tile-based movement system maintains the tactical flexibility of the core skirmish game.

Cross-Compatible Systems
The game shares mechanics and miniatures with the Eldfall Chronicles skirmish system. This full cross-compatibility allows players to move easily between the competitive wargame and cooperative dungeon-crawl experiences using the same models and familiar rules.

Key Features

- 1-4 players plus an optional game master
- Deep, cooperative gameplay with RPG progression and branching storylines.
- Fast, tactical combat with tile-based movement.
- Solo, cooperative, and PvP play options.
- Unparalleled-quality Unicool Hard Plastic miniatures for exceptional detail and durability.
- Dozens of quests, unique challenges, and extensive replayability.

“Northern Wind” offers a cohesive blend of narrative depth, tactical combat, and world-building — a challenging and rewarding experience for both newcomers and seasoned Eldfall players.

name: Elemental Clash
description:
In Elemental Clash, players take on the role of generals in the mystical realm of Elementalia, where the kingdoms of Fire, Water, Earth, and Air are locked in an epic struggle for supremacy. The ancient balance of power has been shattered, and the armies of the elements, along with the mysterious Spirits, are vying for control in a fast-paced, strategic card game.

The objective of the game is to collect two sets of elemental cards by commanding your Clasher and utilizing powerful Fusion combinations. Each round, players reveal their Clashers and Fusion Pairs, using elemental superiority—where Water douses Fire, Fire scorches Earth, Earth withstands Air, and Air disperses Water—to gain the upper hand. The elusive Spirit cards, stronger than any single element, can provide a game-changing advantage, but their power diminishes when too many Spirits are in play.

Through careful strategy and tactical decisions, players must outwit their opponents and claim victory by forming either an Elementalist Set—one card from each element—or a Purity Set, made up of four cards from a single element. With each round presenting new opportunities for clever plays and powerful combos, Elemental Clash delivers a thrilling battle of wits and elemental forces.

-description from designer

name: Gazebo
description:
Fill the botanical gardens with fragrant flowers, lush foliage, and soothing waters as you erect your gazebos among the tranquil features and atop prized patios.

In Gazebo, players take turns placing dominos on the shared garden map to establish nooks — that is, two or more contiguous terrain spaces of the same type: flower, foliage, or water. When a player creates a nook, they place one of their gazebos on top of it, and by connecting their nook to a patio, they can claim the patio and place a gazebo on it.

But not all is peaceful in this game of garden landscaping. Larger nooks can absorb smaller nooks, and patios can be stolen by cunning rivals. The first player to place all of their gazebos on the board wins!

Gazebo is an evolution of Reiner Knizia’s classic game Qin and introduces many innovations by:

     Improving the method of drawing single-colored and double-colored dominoes for less luck and more tension
     Increasing the variety of gameplay features across the all-new base game maps and expansion maps
     Deepening the strategic possibilities with Zen spaces, vases, and pedestals
     Ramping up the conflicts with more valuable contested spaces and more tactical flexibility
     Debuting an exciting new partnership mode for four players
     Condensing a now bigger experience into a smaller and more portable package
     Broadening the appeal and approachability with a new garden theme beautifully illustrated by Alisha Giroux


Gazebo is the first official title to kick off Bitewing Games' Travel Line.

—description from the publisher

name: Elixirus
description:
You have received an exclusive invitation from the legendary forest wizard, Elixirus, to participate in his Magical Mixing Contest, held annually at his charming hut tucked away in the heart of the enchanted forest. There, apprentices from all corners of the realm will come together to explore the forest’s magical wonders, and gather ingredients to concoct delightful potions in an effort to impress the whimsical wizard. It’s a celebration of creativity, discovery, and a touch of forest mischief - so bring your skill, imagination, and a pinch of wonder. Master Elixirus can’t wait to see what you brew up!

In Elixirus, you'll compete with your fellow players to make 5 different elixirs. The game is played in rounds, each consisting of 2 simple phases. In the Gather phase, venture out and explore various mystical forest locations to find the best ingredients. The higher their potency, the more valuable your elixirs become. In the Mix phase, turn your ingredients into magical elixirs to score points. The game ends after a player completes any 4 of their elixirs, at which point the player with the most potent potions wins.

name: Elven Throne
description:
Elven Throne emulates the art of political maneuvering and strategic thinking within a fantasy realm. It combines novel social-networking like mechanics with alliances and counter action chains. Houses can influence and use the help of civilians and beasts, get to control organizations and much more. Up to seven Houses, each with unique characters and abilities, forge alliances and fight to gain influence over the realm.

Organizations, tile maps with hexagonal spaces, link together to form a large play surface. Players move their characters into organizations, activate tiles, and counterattack their rivals in their quest for the Elven Throne. With over 50 characters, variable setup options, and multiple win conditions, each playthrough is a unique experience.

With over 50 characters, variable setup options, and multiple win conditions, each playthrough promises a unique experience.

—description from the publisher

name: Gingham
description:
The race is on! Ants have found an abandoned picnic blanket ripe with sweets, but there aren't enough for every colony...

Gingham is a tricky game of confection connection. In this game, players position their queens around the gingham picnic blanket and deploy their ants to connect sweets and claim the stockpiles they create.

The lead player determines which edge of the playing area all players must play on each round. Everyone then places their queen next to a row on this edge, then deploys an ant into the row where they place their queen. The catch is that you cannot deploy your ant beyond the stitch in the blanket, and the rows closer to the star at the end of the row offer fewer options. That said, whoever places their queen closest to the star becomes the leader of the next round and places their queen next to a row on any other edge of the playing area; players take turns in order of the queens in the previous row. Do you opt for a better turn order position for next round or more flexibility for ant placement this round?

By connecting matching sweet tokens with a line of your ants and by surrounding and claiming stockpiles, players score points. Sweet tokens are stacked atop one another after connecting, with sugar cubes being left behind; place next to a sugar cube to claim it as they can be spent on powerful abilities. Stretch your ants across the blanket, and grab the biggest piles of sweets to prove your pint-sized royalty!

Gingham is the second title in Bitewing Games' Travel Line. This line of games is focused on being supremely easy to play with anyone, anywhere.

—description from the publisher

name: Ichor
description:
The dark monsters of Greek mythology have gathered for one final assault on Mount Olympus. The Greek gods are prepared to defend their sacred ground. Who will prevail in this decisive battle of blood and ichor?

Ichor is an asymmetric strategy game for two players by Reiner Knizia. In this mythological battle of wits, one player controls the Greek gods while the other controls the Greek monsters. On your turn, you move one of your figures in a straight line as far as you wish, leaving behind a trail of your tokens on each space you pass over. You can never move onto or over a space containing another figure, but you can replace opposing tokens with your own. The first player to get all of their tokens on the board wins.

Each figure possesses a unique ability that can be used only once per game. Thus, the winner will be the one who best leverages their abilities, sets themself up for big plays, and blocks their opponent from doing the same.

Reiner Knizia has developed and evolved Ichor from previous versions of this design by:

     Polishing the existing character abilities while adding new ones
     Introducing an advanced gameplay expansion that features powerful gate tiles and even more gods and monsters (called the Reinforcements & Gates expansion)
     Focusing the competition on a dual-play experience that grows in tension
     Providing nearly 50 million possible set-ups thanks to 2 game boards, 24 characters, and 8 gate tiles


Ichor is the second game in the Mythos Collection, a line of two-player titles featuring strategy and mythology.

—description from the publisher

name: Embers
description:
The heroes' meager campfire sputters. Hungry beasts stalk the edges of the light, waiting for their feast. In the nightmarish darkness, the safety of dawn seems impossibly far away.

Embers is a solo-only game of survival. Use your heroes to defend against waves of encroaching monsters and keep your campfire lit. Your band of heroes huddles around the dying fire. Use each hero's unique strengths and movements to defend the fire from attack and prepare for the next onslaught. As long as the fire lives, so do they.

Each turn, spawn new monsters to face. Spend each hero’s action points to move them around the campfire, attack monsters, upgrade their abilities, support each other, and forage for material to keep the fire going.

After the heroes act, the monsters strike: damage the nearest hero or even the fire itself.

When the night card appears, a new round begins. Survive four full rounds without the fire being extinguished to win!

name: Emblems
description:
Emblems is a card game that blends strategic thinking, opportunistic placement and sneaky moves!

At the start of each turn, choose a card, taking into account its value and effect, before placing it face down in front of you. Then, one after another, reveal your card and place it in one of the three locations: the Castle, the Village or the Port. At the end of each round, gold coins are awarded to the players whose cards have the highest value in each location. Simple and surprising, with just the right amount of chaos, Emblems often favors the cleverest (or boldest) players!

—description from the publisher

name: Iliad
description:
The Trojan War has begun, and both sides of the conflict pursue every advantage they can possibly gain. Two opposing heroes — Hector of the Trojans and Achilles of the Greeks — seek the favor of the gods to lend them support and tip the scales of fate. Only one side will emerge victorious, its hero becoming the legend of the Iliad.

Iliad is a tile-placement strategy game by Reiner Knizia. On your turn, select one of two tiles from your hand and place it onto the board adjacent to an opponent's tile. Both players have symmetrical pools of tiles, with their strength ranging from 1-5, along with the Dolos tile that mimics your opponent's adjacent tiles. The key to victory lies behind the relentless tension of where and when to commit your tiles. When placing a tile, you may also activate the tile's ability, which can serve to turn the tide of war.

When a row or column is filled, the player with the highest total strength in that line earns the right to select one of the two success tokens at the ends of that row or column; the other token goes to their opponent. Success tokens can earn you the favor of the Gods, and they can earn (or cost you) points. At the end of the game, the winner is the player who has earned the favor of all five Gods. If both players — or neither of them — meet this qualification, then the player who has earned the most points wins. Thus, players will face tough tactical trade-offs as they must decide whether to compete for exclusive favor of the Gods or for the most points — then influence the outcome of the game toward their intended advantage.

Iliad is the first game in the Mythos Collection, a line of two-player titles featuring strategy and mythology.

—description from the publisher

name: Emergency Exit Only
description:
Weeeewooo Weeeeewooo! The building‘s emergency alarm is ringing! Finding your way out of this concrete maze isn‘t going to be easy.

In Emergency Exit Only, each player in turn will play a tile to advance to the exit. But you’ll be playing the tiles on top of each other, so you’ll be putting your spatial visualization skills to the test! Memorize your escape route and make your way through the building together. Play your “Lost tile” when you think you’re lost and the path is dead-end. At the end of the round, lay out your escape route and find out who survived to score points! Start a new round and add one more constraint to add even more panic to the table!

—description from the publisher

name: ORBIT
description:
Come one, come all to the Silo System, the beating heart of our galaxy, for the race of the decade! We've recruited the best tourists in all the cosmos: travel-hardened explorers who will compete in the ultimate contest. These pilots must race to visit all the planets in the Silo System, surfing upon orbital paths, teleporting between hyper jump portals, and beaming through hyperspace. Enjoy your dream vacation on one of our luxurious planets or lavish space stations as you witness the ultimate interstellar marathon.
