The demon Mephisto offers Faust worldly honor, wealth, and pleasure. Seeing this as a chance to pursue his ideals and satisfy his boundless curiosity, Faust accepts the deal.

Faust vs Mephisto is a two-player trick-taking game where Faust must resist Mephisto's temptations and explore four domains for two rounds.

If Faust takes all or none of the cards in any suit, Mephisto claims that domain. If Mephisto claims two or more domains, he wins the game. Otherwise, victory belongs to Faust.

Whose ending will you choose—Faust's redemption or Mephisto's triumph?

—description from the publisher

name: Fear of the Dark
description:
Fear of the Dark is a solo push-your-luck board game with tile placement and a horror theme.

Inspired by one of the primal fears, it places you in an unknown location without any tangible threat except being alone in the dark with only a limited number of matches in your pocket. The only other resource is your common sense, but like the matches, it is in short supply and tends to deplete too fast.

To win, you cannot be too cautious, as all your matches will run out, and soon after, the loss of common sense will leave you stranded in the dark, and unable to move (losing the game). You must take risks and move forward until you find that last door that does not have any room behind it, leading you to freedom.

The gameplay is divided into two modes:
- Playing with a lit match, you can use your cards to perform actions (moving, exploring or searching) or use their more advanced abilities that will use up that card permanently (loss of common sense).
- Playing without a lit match is much worse, as each card played is used up permanently as you slowly lose the ability for stable thought in the dark.

-description from designer

name: Fearless
publisher: 2F-Spiele; Ludofun; Rio Grande Games; SUNNY BIRD; TLAMA games
description:
In Fearless, you walk through a gloomy forest and try to stay on the safe path. If you still wander astray, you try to turn back again as close as possible. The closer you are to the safe path, the less fear you will suffer. Not walking at all is no alternative as you'll remain behind on your own in the scary ruin. If you are the most fearless after several rounds, you will win the game!

Fearless is a simple trick-taking game with four suits and without trump. The card with the highest value in the led suit always wins the trick. The unusual part of the game is the card values as they are not all positive as typical for trick-taking games, but have values from +6 to -6 in each suit. Thus, you collect both negative and positive cards. The kicker: You try to gain a balanced score, collecting both minus and plus points. This is theoretically possible for all players, but "sadly" you play against each other — and the others are always pleased when they can scare you with another handful of points.

name: Feel Like a Fool
description:
Tha anamal wath a bag nasa, twa tasks and lavas an Afraca  
Can you guess what is this?
Elephant!

Feel like a Fool, is a new and funny party game: two teams will compete to be faster to fill their boards with all the vowel tokens needed.
In each round, one of players will try to make his team guess as many words as possible, but he can only do so by using the sound of the vowel indicated on the card drawn.
At the end of the round each team will draw one face-down token for each word guessed.

—description from the publisher

name: Fest Season
description:
Create the best festival in the world!				
				
					Fest Season is a Set Collection, Tile Placement and Track Movement GameMusic fans want to see their favorite artists and live an unforgettable weekend. You are responsible for organizing the most exciting music festival of the season. Build your venue with restrooms, food options, water stations, photo op and much more. Book the most popular acts and build a thrilling lineup with the hottest genres. Create an extraordinary festival by completing unique projects.
 The lights are on, and the artist are ready to shine. Rock, Pop, Metal and more in one place!
Will you build the most epic music festival?


				
				
					Goal of the GameFest Season is a board game for 1 to 5 players. Each player takes on the role of an entertainment company responsible for organizing a music festival. The success of your festival is determined by the victory points you earn through your lineup of artists, venue constructions, completed projects, and the balance between your amenities, attendance, and ticket price.

On your turn, you must choose one of the six different actions, keeping in mind that some actions may also benefit other players. It is important to keep an eye on the master fader, as it will signal when the game is coming to an end.

The festival with the most victory points at the end of the game will be declared the Greatest Festival of the Season.

-description from the rulebook

name: Festoon
description:
When bees are creating honeycomb, they connect their legs together to form a chain, called a Festoon.

In this game, players compete the be the first to form a festoon. Players take turns placing hexagonal bee tiles adjacent to the other tiles on the table one at a time. The first player who places four bees in a straight line wins.

As players create advantageous patterns and block others, Festoon becomes a game of reluctant cooperation. Players must decide whether it is more advantageous to block another player's festoon or set themselves up for victory. The simple rules and strategic gameplay mean that anybody can play it, but victory can only be achieved by the player whose strategy comes out on top.

Only a few minutes to set up and explain, Festoon is a great warm up for family game night, or a breather between hours-long games.

—description from the publisher

name: Festung Schneidemühl 45
description:
Festung Schneidemühl 1945 is a Tactical war game set during the battle for the Gate of the Pomeranian Wall between January and February 1945. Players command Soviet and German battalions, striving to achieve historical operational objectives.

The game features a hexagonal map where each hex represents 250 meters of real terrain. The mechanics are based on an initiative system, artillery support, and a complex simulation of unit strength and quality. The key to victory is optimal resource management and anticipating the opponent's movements.

The game realistically depicts the siege of Fortress Schneidemühl, where defenders must effectively manage limited forces and resources, while the attacking Soviet forces must break through the defenses using infantry, artillery, and armored support.

Although the game operates at the battalion level, with hexes representing approximately 250 meters, its gameplay focuses on strategic-level decision-making. Players must manage entire divisions, coordinate support units, allocate reserves, and consider long-term operational goals. Therefore, while the physical scale is tactical, the nature of the gameplay justifies its classification as a strategic wargame.

name: Fetchez la Vache!
description:
Fetchez la Vache! 3-in-1 Game Set includes:
Custom-designed beechwood board, 2 dice catapults, 21 meeples (20 human, 1 bovine), 4 dice, 1 doubling cube, 30 checkers,  and rules for THREE games.

1 - Fetchez la Vache! A madcap backgammon-based game that pits two teams against each other in a race to capture a cow and leave the field with it alive, all while dodging catapulted farm animals and scathing insults French taunts. (Note: this activity requires the Monty Python’s Cocurricular Mediaeval Reenactment Programme core book.)

2 - Squashez l'Anglaise! Flip the board over and let fly with this point-based, historically accurate, terribly violent castle-siege simulator.

3 – Backgammon! A fully functional backgammon board (for those who wish to appear smarter than people who play checkers but can’t be arsed with chess).

Specifications and components:
A custom-designed and illustrated birchwood game board.
Approximate dimensions: Open: 17.13" long x 21.65" wide x 1.48" high (43.5cm x 55cm x 3.75cm); Closed: 17.13" long x 10.83" wide x 1.48" high (43.5cm x 27.5cm x 3.75cm).
21 printed wooden meeples of varying shapes and designs (knights, priests, retainers, and the like...plus the cow, of course).
2 fully functional and highly dangerous to mice wooden dice catapults.
A pair of woefully under tested, wonderfully launchable dice.
A pair of cow bags for storage. Storage of game components. Not recommended for cows.
Oh and all the bits for backgammon, too: 15 black checkers, 15 white checkers, and 1 doubling cube
Castle wall divider for increased difficulty and more realistic farm animal trajectories.

name: Feudal Rise
description:
A peaceful medieval builder - no war, just thoughtful planning and adapting to the changing needs of your growing town. Step into the shoes of a noble, raise your settlement from scratch, and watch it flourish into a proud domain.

Your goal is simple: develop your town to its highest potential. Earn golden goblets by constructing buildings — a mark of your rising prestige.

Each turn, roll three dice and assign them to one of three actions:

    Production brings in resources.
    Transportation moves those resources, helping you build, log by log, brick by brick.
    Edict reflects the king’s decree — whether it’s new jobs, taxes, or other duties. Ignore an edict, and your loyalty drops. Fall below 1, and your reign ends.


You have one year — 52 turns — to make your mark. Can your humble fief become the envy of the realm?

—description from the publisher

name: LINKX
publisher: Blue Orange (EU); asmodee; Blue Orange Games; Devir; Pegasus Spiele; SuperHeated Neurons
description: Each player has their own set of polyominoes in LINKX, and they take turns dropping one piece at a time into the vertical playing area. If a player ever connects the left and right sides of the area — or the top and bottom — with a continuous line of their color, they win.

name: Magicaboo
publisher: Blue Orange (EU); Blue Orange Games; Broadway Toys LTD; Mercurio
description:
Can you tell what's disappeared in Magicaboo?

Each turn, one player takes the role of magician, spreading a large cloth over all the wooden pieces in the center of the play area, then picking up one item under the cloth and carting it away. "Magicaboo!"

The other players try to be the first to identify which item is missing, winning a star if they do.

name: Got Five!
publisher: Blue Orange (EU); asmodee; Blue Orange Games; Gém Klub Kft.; Geronimo Games; Ghenos Games; Lanlalen; Lúdilo; MINDOK
description:
Got Five! is a game of logic and deduction in which players try to uncover the five hidden numbers placed on their stand. Each player can see everyone else’s tiles, but never their own, and must rely on shared information, clever questioning, and careful note-taking to narrow down the possibilities. All tiles revealed during the game are public, creating a constantly evolving puzzle that rewards attention and reasoning.

On your turn, you reveal a new tile from the supply, adding more shared information to the table, then use one of the available face-up tiles to ask a neighboring player for a clue. You may ask them to categorize a tile by placing it in the correct relative position among your hidden numbers, or compare it to one of your tiles to learn whether they share the same number of dots. These clues, combined with the visible order of tiles and their colors and dot counts, allow players to eliminate possibilities and gradually deduce their own sequence.

Players may announce their solution at any time by declaring “Got Five!” and listing their five numbers in ascending order. If the guess is correct, that player wins immediately. A single mistake, however, eliminates the player from contention, so timing and confidence are key. With simple rules, shared information, and a race to solve your own puzzle first, Got Five! delivers a fast, tense deduction challenge for groups who enjoy logical reasoning and mind games.

—description from the publisher

name: Fields of Fire: Deluxe Edition
description:
Fields of Fire is a solitaire game of commanding a rifle company between World War II and the Present Day. The game is different from many tactical games in that it is diceless and card based. There are two decks used to play. The Terrain Deck is based on a specific region and is used to build a map for the various missions your company must perform. The Action deck serves many purposes in controlling combat, command and control, and various activity attempts. The units of the company are counters representing headquarters elements, squads, weapons teams, forward observers, individual vehicles or helicopters. A single game is a mission and several missions from a historical campaign are strung together for the player to manage experience and replacements. A mission can be played in about 1 – 4 hours.

New features Include:

- A Rewritten series rulebook -  The Deluxe Edition comes with a rewritten third edition ruleset, packed with examples, diagrams and clarifying notes while maintaining continuity with the second edition rules.
- A Starter Guide.
- A Full Starter Mission. A stand-alone mission tailored towards easing new company commanders into the full game.
- Four Fully Redesigned Mission Books. The Normandy, Heartbreak Ridge, Naktong River and Vietnam campaigns are presented in a clarified and expanded manner.
- Over 200 updated counters plus various additional reference markers and new units. 
- New elevation cards to enhance the Heartbreak Ridge campaign.
- A completely new set of redesigned player aids including new charts and air assault planning cards.

name: Zeit Heist
description:
Zeit Heist is a heist-themed, time-traveling drafting game for 2-6 players where you and your opponents are opposing masterminds trying to steal a new periodic element, Zeitnium. The first to steal it is crowned the world's first trillionaire. The element is being shown off at the science museum at 12 o'clock!

Recruit the right crooks to perform the heist of your choosing. Sneak into the museum before it opens with the Scientist, the Spy, and the Lockpicker to nab a win. Or break into the museum after it's open with the Driver, Muscle, and Inside man for an explosive victory. Or sway the Police, Detective, and Undercover Cop to confiscate the Zeitnium in your name! Use the interplay of these distinct win conditions to fool your opponents.

—description from the publisher

name: Fight 5
description:
In this innovative reimagining of the classic game War, players clash against their opponents across five stacks — no matter the player count!

Fight Five is an elemental tug-of-war. In each of the five rounds, players will draw five cards and challenge their opponents for control of five different stacks. Win the clash and take the cards for endgame scoring! Did you tie? Then that stack only grows bigger (and more valuable) for the next clash.

Clever play across all five stacks will win the day, and watch out for Star Clash Cards that will beat out all other cards! 
 Be the first to 200 points, or have the most points after three bouts of five rounds.

—description from the publisher

name: Fight Deck
description:
Fight Deck is a fast-paced card dueler that brings the thrill of classic fighting games to the tabletop. Choose from a diverse roster of fighters, each with unique playstyles and strategies. Master authentic fighting game mechanics like combos, meter management, and wake-up moves, all reimagined through dynamic card play. Immerse yourself in premium hand-drawn, high-resolution pixel art that captures the energy of arcade battles. Fight solo or team up in 2-player co-op with the Arcade Mode expansion for even more action-packed gameplay.

—description from the designer

name: Fight for Inheritance
description:
A ruthless card game of deception, betrayal, and strategy! The Krazy King has a deadly illness, his many children come to his deathbed and he says a parent should not have a favourite child so will throw the Crown and the Fortune in to the middle of the Ocean but if he only had 1 child he would leave everything to them — creating greed within the hearts of all the Royals.

In Fight for Inheritance, you’ll need to outmanoeuvre, outwit, and outlast your rivals by avoiding assassination to be the last one standing and claim the crown.

Players use deception, alliances, wealth, and sabotage to outplay your opponents. Players buy and bribe bodyguards and use action cards to try to assassinate each other.

Keep taking turns until all other players have been assassinated and there only is one player left standing. This player wins the Fight For Inheritance and is given the crown and all the Kingdom’s fortune by the Krazy King! You have become the next Krazy Monarch!

—description from the designer

name: Fight Sequence
description:
Fight Sequence is a tactical reverse action-programming dueling game about psychics THINKING about fighting! Players build sequences of attacks and responses that resolve in reverse order, representing the ebb and flow of a theoretical fantasy fight scene two psychics are projecting into each other's minds. Planning your own moves isn't the only key to victory; you'll also use your psychic and magical abilities to manipulate when — or IF — actions resolve!

Players select one of the four characters in a diverse cast of psychic combatants, using their unique skill sets to emerge victorious. Every character deck has its own strengths and weaknesses, with a depth of tactical play that ensures no two fights are the same.

In Fight Sequence, players take turns playing Actions or passing, building a series of Actions until both players pass consecutively [with passes being forced once the maximum sequence size of 9 Actions is met]. Once that happens, the entire sequence then resolves in reverse order, starting with the last Action played. Timing your Actions for maximum effect is crucial, but every character has some ability to manipulate that timing to work more in their favor. Even the best-laid plans aren't foolproof!

Actions are either attacks or responses - use your attacks to damage your opponent, and your responses to defend yourself from opposing attacks or support your strategy. Every card in the game can be played as either an attack or a response, so you're never out of options. Damage is represented by discarding cards from your deck; no paper, pen, dice, or tracker apps required. Just choose your characters, shuffle your decks, and begin!

In addition to four varied characters with different styles and movesets, The First Chapter also includes the Academy decks, which use a more streamlined subset of cards to help ease players into the reverse-action-programming nature of the game.

-- description from the designer

name: Fighters of Europe
description:
Fighters of Europe is a fast-paced and simple tactical warfare game of air battles during WWII in the sky over Britain in 1940. Relive the fury of air combat over Europe during World War II as you direct each airplane in multiple fighter and bomber squadrons to lead attacks on the enemy's airfields, manufacturing locations, and other ground objectives.

Fighters of Europe is scenario-driven. The base game comes with ten different scenarios. With practice, you will be able to set up your own scenarios very quickly.

Move each airplane individually on a hex grid. When you maneuver to get an enemy airplane in your sights, it must try to dodge or else take damage. Some airplanes can use bombs to destroy ground installations. Stay in formation to keep the initiative and dominate your opponent. Each airplane has its own attributes in terms of speed, armor, and special abilities. Each piece is illustrated as close as possible to its historical model to maximize your immersion!
 
The base game contains a large modular board, player aids, and all the tokens you will need to play. This includes several squadrons of Hurricanes and Spitfires as well as Messerschmidt Bf109, Heinkel 111 and Junker 88.

No dice, no rulers — only dozens of airplanes! A fast-paced and streamlined game mechanism that plunges you right into the heart of battle.

-description from publisher

name: Fighting Fantasy Adventures
description:
In Fighting Fantasy Adventures, adapts the Fighting Fantasy solo adventure book line into a card game format, letting you experience the stories in a whole new way.

Now you can play with up to three friends in a co-operative or solo format. Gameplay is easy to learn and engaging, downtime is minimal, and your characters will gain new abilities after each adventure. The card-based system lets you have the feel of a role-playing game, without the need for a gamemaster. The map is revealed as you play, and event cards tell you what you have discovered.

This campaign will comprise five adventures based on the four stories below:


     The Warlock of Firetop Mountain
     Island of the Lizard King
     Deathtrap Dungeon
     The Forest of Doom (in two parts)


Each adventure takes roughly 90-180 minutes to play, providing 10-15 hours of total game time.

name: Fighting Formations: US 29th Infantry Division
description:
Fighting Formations (FF) is a series of wargames covering WWII tactical combined-arms combat at the platoon and squad levels. Each game in the series will feature a distinct combat unit, highlighting battles in which that unit participated as well as its particular order of battle and fighting characteristics. In each scenario, one player will take command of elements of this featured unit while the other assumes control of the opposing forces. These two players will alternate giving orders, activating their units on the map for various military functions.

This edition covers the US 29th Infantry Division's fighting in Europe during 1944. Scenarios cover the wide variety of assaults the division was called on to make against Germans dug into towns and forts, across open fields, through bocage and woods. Every new battle forced the 29ers to learn new tactics to overcome obstacles in their push toward Berlin.

name: Figment
description:
Figment is a mind-bending game of visual perception. Each card features unique art using the same four colors, and your goal is to line up five cards in a row so that each card has more of one color than the card before it.

After you've lined up the five cards, you choose how many bonus points (1-5) to risk based on how confident you are, then reveal the backs of the cards, earning 1 point for each card in the correct order and the bonus points if all five were correct.

Play continues for five rounds, then count the number of scored cards and add the value of the tokens to determine your final score.

name: Final Binary
description:
Master the binary system, strategize your plays, and secure victory by precisely meeting your bid!

Final Binary is a must-follow trick-taking game with a trump suit and a bid-fulfillment mechanic.

In addition to the cards in your hand, publicly displayed binary (2-bit) cards influence the strength of card ranks and also determine the number of tricks you must fulfill to achieve your bid.

name: Clandestine
description:
For those who dare venture into the shadows of darkened alleys, one can hear the whispers and plotting as the seeds of the future's most powerful secret societies take root.  Discovery of mysterious, ancient and even enchanted relics have aspiring groups experimenting with strange energy and manipulating the public to further their research into the unknown.  Each society takes a different path to uncover impactful secrets while maximizing the intrigue it generates with its actions.

This thematic, strategy game leverages mancalas within interconnecting rondels allowing players to conduct actions in a shared space while planning ahead for unique actions within their own societies.  Will you generate the most intriguing secret society or will your society's efforts be lost to the ages?

Play secrets, activate a public or society leader, and conduct clandestine actions on your turn to discover relics, research secrets, cleanse your society of chaos, or more in this deep strategy game with quick turns.

The game ends when a player upgrades their Society to the max level (5). The winner is the player whose Society has generated the most Intrigue (victory points).

—description from the designer

name: Fine Line
description:
In a culinary contest where moderation is key, players compete to eat just enough — not too little, not too much. Each round, you secretly bid how many dishes you want to eat, then play cards to try to match that number. Overeat, and you’ll need medicine to digest it. Undereat, and you won’t gain anything. Only those who walk the fine line between indulgence and restraint can win.

Fine Line is a must-follow, secret-bid trick-taking game where players earn points based on how close their trick wins are to their hidden bid. Players simultaneously select one card as a “bid” and one as a scoring card. At the end of the round, players score based on the difference between their bid and actual card count adjusting their track accordingly. To prevent overconsumption, players can use medicine cards that neutralize excess but only if taken correctly!

name: Super Boss Monster
publisher: Brotherwise Games; Broadway Toys LTD; Muduko; Ігромаг
description:
After a decade of dungeon-building fun, Boss Monster is leveling up to the next generation with Super Boss Monster! 1-4 players compete to build the ultimate side-scrolling dungeon by drafting room cards, playing spells, and luring in hapless adventurers.

Super Boss Monster introduces the Town Board, which brings in new mechanics to the classic card game. Random room draws are replaced with a simple draft. Heroes still show up in town, but overflow into Locations (Temple, Stadium, Library, Hide-Out, and Tavern) where players can nab them with your all-new Minion meeple! If players choose to not use their Minion  to direct a hero, Minions can activate other action spaces.

The Town Board unlocks a long awaited single-player mode! In this mode, players will be trying to lure and slay as many heroes as possible. Players will need to keep an eye on damage, but luring is key to success; if too many heroes stack up in town, they'll head to the Tavern and end the game!

Super Boss Monster is 100% backwards compatible with all existing Boss Monster cards. As a standalone game, Super Boss Monster will contain everything that 1-4 players need to play.

—description from the publisher

name: Fintastic Sea
description:
Fintastic Sea – The Strategic Card Game for Ecological Explorers.

In Fintastic Sea, players take on the role of marine biologists collecting a variety of fish species to create rich and balanced ocean ecosystems.  The game unfolds over multiple rounds. Players place fish into a central ocean grid, catch adjacent fish according to the food chain (larger fish catch smaller ones), and then choose whether to store them in their Reserve or place them directly into an Ecosystem. The twist: only fish placed in a closed ecosystem score Environmental Points – but reaching that goal requires clever planning and well-timed moves.

Most fish also feature unique abilities that activate when placed on the grid. These abilities add a layer of tactical depth and ensure that even low-value cards offer strategic opportunities. This creates an exciting interplay of timing, positioning, and combo-building that makes each game unique.

The Reserve serves as a temporary holding area, offering no points – but smart collection allows players to discard matching fish to trigger powerful abilities. Points are only scored once fish are transferred to an ecosystem, which can hold up to 10 regular fish and any number of Secret Fish. Players must carefully balance variety, synergy, and timing to maximize their score.

Fintastic Sea comes with a standout feature: The wave, which moves around the grid each round, pushing fish and changing the board layout. This dynamic element forces players to adapt their strategies and brings fresh gameplay to every session.

name: Firefighters on Duty
description:
Step into the heat and embrace your heroism with Firefighters on Duty, a real-time, co-operative board game. Players select the scenario and difficulty level they want to play.

During the game, players immerse themselves in up to 6 intense, two-minute rounds in which they manage an entire fire department. They're tasked with dispatching vehicles and firefighters across the city, extinguishing fires, saving civilians, and safeguarding properties. Every round, players roll their action dice as quickly as they can and perform actions based on the symbol they roll. Every choice carries weight as the clock is always ticking. You need to work together, make decisions under pressure, and risk it all to keep the city safe.

After the last round, points and negative points are added up.  If the objective has been achieved and the negative points are minimal, the players win the game.

—description from the publisher

name: First Republic
description:
The game begins in the Autumn of 1792, three years after the start of the French Revolution. Louis XVI, King of the French remains alive but is imprisoned.
The newly declared French Republic finds itself at war with Austria and Prussia, whose armies are poised on the frontiers to invade.
The Coalition player will take the role of the Coalition states led by the Holy Roman Emperor and head of the Habsburg Austrian Empire, Francis II. The Coalition also includes Prussia, Great Britain and Bourbon Spain amongst other smaller states and anti-Republican insurgents. 
The Coalition’s goal is to apply as much military pressure onto France as is needed to bring the young French Republic to political collapse, perhaps thereby causing a Bourbon restoration.
The French Player will take the role of the Government of the Republic, and will fight to resist the diverse and numerous internal and external anti-revolutionary threats, seeking to defeat them one by one. Striving for “liberté, egalité, fraternité“, delivered if necessary at bayonet point. 
The Republic will also need to be careful not to allow the Republic’s finest young general (Bonaparte) too much success, or he may seek to overthrow the Republic and establish his own regime.

The game includes four scenarios:

The Early War (1792-1793)
    The Late War (1795-1797)
    Bonaparte in Italy (1796)
    The campaign game (1792-1797)

Scale
Units : 1 strength point equals 5000 men
One turn represents one season
Distance betwen two locations: on average 50-75 km
Complexity: 7/9

—description from the publisher

name: First Victories: Wellington versus Napoleon
description:
First Victories: Wellington versus Napoleon includes the small battles of Roliça and Vimero in the Peninsula War between Great Britain and France. It has 3 rule sets, 9 scenarios, and a detailed solo system. (Napoleon not included!)

First game in the The Glory and Empire series. Glory and Empire is a fresh look at grand tactical command, maneuver and combat during the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Period.  The system is focused on command, maneuver and combat that is fast playing, yet accurate and rich with detail.

The game is 125m per hex. Units are battalions and companies for infantry, regiments and squadrons for cavalry and companies for artillery. Each strength point is 100 men for infantry, 50 men and horses for cavalry or  one section, or 2 guns, for artillery. Counters are 5/8".

The rules consist of a Soldier's, Battalion and Brigade rules set. Players can learn the basics with the Soldier's rules, move to a full fledged simulation with the Battalion Game and pick and choose rules from the Brigade Game to suit their tastes. Or players can jump right into the Brigade Game and understand how grand tactical maneuvering was practiced on the battlefield during the 18th and 19th centuries.

The Soldier's Game gives players new to the era an introduction to foundational concepts of tactics in the horse and musket era. In the Soldier's and Battalion Games there are the usual Line, Column, Square and skirmishers.  The Battalion game has two types of Skirmishers, introduces important concepts for maneuvering forces on the battlefield and has more detailed close combat procedures. The Brigade Game adds close columns, attack columns, closed square, Austrian division masses.  Artillery is simplified for the Soldier's and Battalion Games, but the Battalion Game adds artillery ammunition. The Brigade Game adds bombardment zones, bounce through, howitzer fire and separate ammunition tracking for round shot, shell,  canister and shrapnel. The Brigade Game also gives players more tools to react to enemy moves.

name: Boss Monster Junior
description:
It's time for a new generation to take over the dungeons! In Boss Monster Junior, little monsters take on the dungeon-building and hero-scaring adventures.

Collect coins to pay for rooms in your dungeon, draft heroes to visit your dungeon, and slay them to collect their treasures! Each treasure is worth 1 Victory Point, and whoever has the most of each treasure type gains 3 Victory Points at the end of the game.

As a standalone game, Boss Monster Junior contains everything needed for 2-4 players.

—description from the publisher

name: Fischfutter
publisher: 999 Games; AMIGO; Kikigagne?; Rexhry; VR Distribution
description:
In Fischfutter, you must escape the piranhas or become fish food.

To set up, shuffle the double-sided piranha cards and give one to each player, along with five bandage tokens. Place the top card of the deck in the middle of the table. On your turn, place your card on the table with either side face up, then flip over all other cards on the table of the same color. If at least ten piranhas in a single color are now visible, this swarm attacks you, costing you tokens based on the size of the swarm. Draw a card to end your turn.

When a player runs out of tokens, the game ends and whoever has the most tokens wins.

Fischfutter includes a co-operative variant.

name: Five Families
description:
New York in 1931 – The "Five Families" divide the city's underworld among themselves. After a major gang war, the mobsters want to fight more against law and order than against each other and to agree on critical decisions in the future — but until the distribution of the city is finalized, each family will try to get as big a piece of the pie as possible.

In the area-control game Five Families, you want to use your mobsters to secure control of as many neighborhoods as possible...but never forget that you always need to have enough money and followers at your disposal. Will you be the last family standing?

—description from the publisher

name: Shards of Creation
description:
In Shards of Creation, harness the primal forces of Brandon Sanderson's Cosmere! This innovative trick-taking game is designed for players of all skill levels.

Every Shard is an aspect of divinity: Autonomy, Cultivation, Devotion, Dominion, Honor, Odium, Preservation, and Ruin. Each is an entirely unique suit, with different values and abilities.

Will you win by focusing on one Shard’s influence, or by forging a coalition of Shards? Shuffle up a different combination each time you play, making every game a new experience!

name: Flails & Citadels
description:
Flails & Citadels is a new grimdark solo adventure compatible with Doom Pilgrim.

It uses the same game mechanics as  Doom Pilgrim, but offers more adventuring, with the focus on encounters and looting, compared to the original, which has a wider medieval setting scope, sometimes less appealing for a regular fan of fantasy games.

A new feature in Flails & Citadels is cards have almost always some effect. While in Doom Pilgrim, quite often you just pass a card with no change in your character sheet (for example if you come to a town with no gold in your purse), in Flails & Citadels, cards usually have some effect for every condition you are in at the moment, which makes the game much more actionable and balanced.

—description from the publisher

name: Super Boss Monster II: The Die is Cast
description:
The Dice Queen has arrived in Arcadia with her diceling minions, introducing an all-new mechanic to the hit dungeon-building card game: dice-powered rooms and effects!

Playable as a standalone or a sequel, Super Boss Monster 2: The Die is Cast brings you more dungeon-drafting, minion-placing, hero-luring gameplay. But now you'll need to master the power of dice! When you build certain rooms, you'll roll the dice to power them up by placing the dice in your dungeon. You can then manipulate those values with other Rooms, abilities, and Spells!

The Die is Cast and Super Boss Monster will never be the same! Super Boss Monster 2 is backward compatible with all existing Boss Monster and Super Boss Monster cards. As a standalone game, Super Boss Monster 2: The Die is Cast will contain everything that players need to play.

—description from the publisher

name: Flame & Forge
description:
Flame & Forge is a new and completely standalone game from 1 to 4 players. It’s a Worker placement, deck-building, push-your-luck full of interesting choices and really fun meeples! This time we will be dwarfs marching into a city on flames to raid resources, forge powerful weapons and challenge monsters — and maybe convince them to join your side of the fight!

Will you save the city… or rule it? in Flame & Forge you choose your path before the game begins — cooperate or compete, the forge is ready for both. So you may join forces to take down the mighty red dragon before your city goes up in flames, or if your friends are feeling bold (and maybe a bit greedy), storm the castle to see who will slay the beast and rise as the next Dwarf King.

-

In your turn pick one of your dwarf meeples from your campfire and place them on the outskirt city tiles in the first spot to the left of the chosen tile and take ALL visible actions in this tile AND take damage to remove fire tokens, if another player places their dwarf in the same tile they may perform less actions than you. In your next turn, your options will be reduced: the next tile must be up by one line closer to the dragon's castle and adjacent to the tile your previously placed your dwarf. Once all of your dwarfs are out you retrieve them all and start from the bottom again.

Possible actions a tile can have (usually around 2-3 actions):

     Get a Gem
     Spend Gems to forge a weapon card
     Spend Gems to advance in the knowledge track
     Perform a ranged attack
     Fight a monsters on the same tile
     Grant a success hit on a attack
     Retire a card from your deck
     Heal 1 damage


In the knowledge track you can also upgrade your dwarf workers to special meeples that give you actions, and also give special abilities to be used when they all return to you after they are all out.

A big element of the game is the battling system that allow for you to hit cards (in a push your luck) where the damage you deal and the damage you take comes from your own deck. Weapons you forge and monsters you defeat also go to your deck along with cards that will allow for the most varied actions (as long as you survive the fight) so many times you need to decide to either flee and perform the actions or risk it all to try and defeat the monster.

There are some arcade - boss battler - elements and the dragon fights back putting fire to the city and if any tile has 3 fire it will be destroyed and players will lose the game if 7 city tiles are destroyed.

The game ends when the dragon is defeated by one of the players. If you are playing coop then you will all win together, if before the beginning of the game you decided for the competitive game then you will count points to decide the new king.

—description from the publisher

name: Flea Market
description:
Place cards in the playing area one after the other. As soon as a player exceeds the element limit, they collect all played cards, give some of them to one or several other players, and keep the remaining cards for themselves. At the end of the game, the cards you collected make you earn or lose points.
The player who has the most points at the end of the game wins!


     Set the round card as “ROUND 1”.
     All players start the game with 5 cards.
     In 90 game cards, 72 Treasure cards and 18 special cards.In Treasure cards, each card consists of a “color” & “object”. There are 6 colors and 6 objects. Each color, each object will be counted as one “element”. For example, when the first player plays “red vinyl”, it has 2 elements. (one color(red) and one object(vinyl))
     From the first player, players play a card. The game goes clockwise.
     In each round, there’s the “ELEMENT LIMIT” and “PRESENT NUMBER”. While playing the game, after a player’s turn, if the "PRESENT NUMBER" exceeds the “ELEMENT LIMIT”, the round ends. The player gives “PRESENTS” among the played cards to other players as the number written in round card.  And then, the player gets all the remained cards.
     After the final round, the game ends.
     The player who has the most point wins the game.


—description from the publisher

name: Fled
description:
Ireland's famine drove you to petty theft. Soon, you find yourself within the walls of Spike Island prison — shackled and shoeless. These days, the warders whistle you to the yard, the wash room, and your bunk, but there's only one place you want to be: gone, vanished - fled!

The object of Fled is to score the most victory points (VP) while trying to escape from prison. Throughout the game, you will manage a hand of tiles. Each turn, you add a tile to the prison, then discard other tiles to move from room to room while collecting contraband. Some rooms, like the Warder's Quarters, allow you to trade your contraband for the tools you'll need to get past the outer wall. Take care with your wandering, though, for if you are not in the right room when the Governor summons you to roll call, a nearby warder could put you in shackles — or worse, send you to solitary confinement!

Do not lose faith! Father Lyons is a sympathetic chaplain warder who has been known to free captives from more than their sins, so give it a lash and rid yourself of this God-forsaken place. Luck of the Irish to ye.

—description from the designer

name: Flippers
description:
Teams of Antarctic Explorers compete for food in an ever-changing environment. Each player will have 9 Explorer Cards to pick from to assemble their team ready to stash away as much food as they can to win.

Each Explorer Card has a power that activates when played next to another card. Then, all of the faceup card powers from the same team activate, causing penguins and seals to flip, bump, and spin across the Antarctic! Each game will start with crates of food which will award extra points to explorers at the end of the game. Play head-to-head or buddy up together in this competitive card game.

The goal of Flippers is to have the highest food value at the end of the game, represented by the wooden fish tokens. Players gain food tokens throughout the game, and the Food Cards award extra points to explorers once the game has finished.

—description from the designer

name: Ants
publisher: Cranio Creations; Capstone Games; DSV Games; Game Harbor; HIT Games; Intrafin Games; PD-Verlag; Portal Games; TLAMA games
description:
ANTS is a deep strategy game that focuses on worker management and territorial expansion. Each player begins with one of multiple unique Queen tiles, which will heavily influence your strategy and interaction with the game's interconnected systems. Throughout the game, you will guide your ant colony through cycles of growth, exploration, and conquest to establish dominance over the garden ecosystem.

On your turn, you perform one of six main actions (Dig, Explore, Gather, Incubate, Play Cards, or Defeat Enemies), and you can take free actions to optimize your colony's efficiency.

When you perform a main action, you spend specialized ants from your colony to determine the action's strength. The number of ants you commit (1 to 4) directly influences the power and impact of your chosen action: expand your nest by placing room tiles strategically, explore hexagonal territories to reveal resources and enemies, or position gatherer ants to form continuous supply networks across the garden.

The heart of the game revolves around your colony's life cycle management. Your incubation board tracks three vital phases (eggs, larvae, and ants) each containing three specializations: diggers, explorers, and gatherers. Wild ants serve as valuable wildcards that can fulfill any specialization need. When you incubate, you complete enterprises, trigger production effects, feed your larvae with food cubes, and advance the life cycle.

An important part of the game is managing your nest's architectural growth. Room tiles must be placed strategically to complete entire nest areas, immediately rewarding you with precious stars, one of the primary victory point sources. The garden map becomes a dynamic battlefield where your exploration reveals enemy tiles and resources, while gatherer ants create supply chains that automatically collect resources and emit pheromones when hexes are depleted.

Multiple victory paths ensure diverse strategies remain viable: architectural mastery, territorial control, demographic growth, or tactical card play and enemy conquest.

Lead your colony to victory.
For the colony!

—description from the publisher

name: FLOP: The One with the Frogs
description:
FLOPPING is the masterful art of ultimate underachieving.
 You win by doing... absolutely nothing.
 No cards to play? No enemies to attack?
 Boom. You’ve FLOPPED. And you’ve WON.

Each game of Flop players are dealt a random face down deck of 10 cards, from which they draw their hand of 4.

On your turn you must PLAY A CARD or ATTACK.

When you play a card in your play area, you must pay its cost if any, by discarding cards from your hand in your discard pile. Then, you may activate one of its abilities, such as: PLAY, which triggers as soon as you play the card. BEFORE ATTACK, which triggers before you perform an attack action. ONGOING, this ability remains active as long as the card is in play.

When you attack, choose one of your Allies in your play area and deal damage equal to its power to an enemy in your opponent’s play area.

If the damage on a card is equal to or greater than its health points, that card is defeated and moved to that player discard pile.

The first player who cannot attack nor play a card FLOPS.. and wins the game.

—description from the publisher

name: FLOP: The One with the Pigeons
description:
FLOPPING is the masterful art of ultimate underachieving.
 You win by doing... absolutely nothing.
 No cards to play? No enemies to attack?
 Boom. You’ve FLOPPED. And you’ve WON.

Each game of Flop players are dealt a random face down deck of 10 cards, from which they draw their hand of 4.

On your turn you must PLAY A CARD or ATTACK.

When you play a card in your play area, you must pay its cost if any, by discarding cards from your hand in your discard pile. Then, you may activate one of its abilities, such as: PLAY, which triggers as soon as you play the card. BEFORE ATTACK, which triggers before you perform an attack action. ONGOING, this ability remains active as long as the card is in play.

When you attack, choose one of your Allies in your play area and deal damage equal to its power to an enemy in your opponent’s play area.

If the damage on a card is equal to or greater than its health points, that card is defeated and moved to that player discard pile.

The first player who cannot attack nor play a card FLOPS.. and wins the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Florafiora: The Storytelling Card Game
description:
Florafiora is a collaborative, improvisational storytelling game where each player takes a turn leading the story! Explore the botanical kingdoms of Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter. The game starts by everyone creating a shared group backstory together that is unique every game. Then- the stage is set to dive into exploration with Location & Encounter cards. Also included is a custom-printed “Improv” die - a way to add gentle consequences or come up with new ideas.

With a set amount of cards and actions- this game has very consistent 60-90min runtime! An accessible TTRPG-like experience for those newer to the hobby, or a great way to practice being a GM if you’ve never tried before. No additional story or character prep is needed and everything you need is provided in the box.

				
				
					Website : https://ko-fi.com/s/aa7098e90b

name: Floristry
description:
Floristry is a 2 player, tile-laying game. Players compete at the historic Aalsmeer Dutch Auction to win the best flowers and then use them to create the most charming window display.

Each round features a Dutch auction, where the clock counts down from 15 seconds while the price drops every 3 seconds. The unique web app runs your auctions, so you have to think fast, bid carefully, and pay close attention to get what you want at the right price-- but also keep an eye on what your rival needs.

Players simultaneously and strategically place their new flowers into their storefront frame. At the end of the game, players will earn Charm from their largest patch of each flower type, and whoever has the most Charm wins.

—description from the designer

name: Aquaria
publisher: Delicious Games; Arrakis Games; Capstone Games; DSV Games; HIT Games; Intrafin Games; Mosaico Jogos; Skellig Games; YOKA Games
description:
In Aquaria, you and your friends compete to have the most expertise in maintaining a thriving aquarium. Build your aquarium from scratch to see who can maintain the best aquascape and fauna. One to four aquarists will see who can best accomplish their marine goals.

Throughout the game, players will buy new fish, feed them, and keep their aquarium in tip-top condition. Players will also show how they have progressed in their aquarist studies by how far they have moved on the encyclopedia tracks. Whoever has the most points at game's end wins.

With an approximate playtime of 45-minutes per player, this game from award-winning best-selling designer Tomáš Holek is crafted to delight even the most seasoned gamers. Featuring breathtaking artwork throughout, it immerses players in a captivating experience - where you can build the perfect aquarium, no water changes or live fish required!

name: Fluffy Dragons
description:
Fluffy Dragons is a very quick and easy, betting & bluffing game, where you'll use the force of the elements to fight your Fluffiest enemies to collect the most gems!

In each round, players will take turns playing an elemental card. Then, they'll place their dragon meeples on the board to claim the element they used, but remember, they could be lying.

There are 5 different elements you could use, each one beating 2 and getting beaten by the other 2.

Before anyone reveals the elemental attacks they used, you can wager gems against other players you think are lying. If you’re right, steal their gems! However, if they were telling the truth, say goodbye to your gems, for now.

Then, players will reveal the elemental attacks they used and move their dragon meeples on the elemental board to match that element.

Players will steal a gem from any dragons who are standing one or two elements in front of them in a clockwise order on the elemental board.

Fluffy Dragons is won by having the most amount of points. Each of your own color gems is worth 1 point at the end of the game, any other color gem is worth 2 points each. You can also get extra points at the end of the game by getting rainbows, a full-color set of gems, and acquiring lost treasures.

—description from the designer

name: Flying Fortresses: B-17 Missions Over Europe
description:
Flying Fortresses: B-17 Missions Over Europe puts you and your friends in the cockpit of legendary B-17 Flying Fortress bombers during World War II.

Gameplay Highlights
1–3 Players – Fly solo or as part of a squadron. Work together to survive or see who can score the most medals and mission success.

Dynamic AI BOT – Axis defenses are automated, keeping you on your toes with unpredictable flak, fighters, weather, and hazards.

Fighters are placed face down on the board according to the scenario setup. As your Flying Fortress (referred to as “your Fort”) enters an Air Zone, defined as any space within the white grid, those fighters are flipped face up. Based on a die roll, some may become activated and are then able to move according to their rules.

Tactical Choices – Plan your route, manage altitude, and position your gunners to survive relentless opposition.
Historical Immersion – Each mission echoes the real challenges faced by Allied crews in the 1943–45 bombing campaigns over Europe.

Plus, play in "Character Mode" and increase the proficiency of your crew as they fly multiple missions. Each successful mission you complete your gunners will increase their aim and the flyboys will become even better at avoiding the hazards of the air.

—description from the designer

name: Flying Fox Farms
description:
Central California in the 1930's is Mecca to two major industries: farming and aeronautics. In this fertile valley, there is a thriving community of clever and daring foxes who have combined these two skills. The game's charming art-style featuring anthropomorphic foxes and other native critters is sure to delight.

During the flight phase, pilot your biplane miniature through the skies using flight cards. Be careful not to stall out! Spend seeds as you pass through the clouds and push them to form rain clouds - which generates rain water. But be careful, a cranky cloud can shoot lighting back!

During the farming phase, sow seeds on your field, water them to grow produce for your roadside stand. Pay attention to the market to get the highest prices. Grow recipes that will become favorites and generate an income for your roadside stand.

During the market phase, Use your profits to purchase more seed, expand your farm, and purchase useful tools. Or expand your hanger, and tinker and upgrade your biplane to make it faster and more maneuverable.

The player who is the most successful farmer after three years and the valley festival and airshow (scoring uses a variety of methods including money, objectives, aeronautics skill and "neighborliness"), wins the game!

name: Fold & Fly!
description:
Fold & Fly! is a short family-style game for 2-50 players.

Each round, players fold lines on their airplane templates, then throw towards the finish line! Will your airplane make it past the finish line first? Or will a rival craft an even more aerodynamic machine? Or will planes collide - dashing hopes in the process!

name: Folia Folio
description:
Autumn has arrived, and colorful leaves litter the ground. As a collector, this is your favorite time of year. Gather the halves of leaves, and assemble them in your albums. Create the most impressive collection to become the envy of your peers!

Folia Folio is a set-collection game that uses the structure of a may-follow trick-taking game. Players form albums by connecting left and right sides of matching leaves and matching numbers. The longer your chain of matches in one album, the more points you score.

name: FOMO: Foragers of Mechanical Oddities
description: In this fast game of bluff and strategy, players take turns bidding for mysterious Mecha parts — some incredible, others not so much. Use limited information and read your opponents to outbid them. But beware: not every reward is positive! Do not let the fear of missing out take control of your impulses!

name: FOO-DIES?!
description:
A social deduction tabletop game for people who love food more than people. There are two sides: the APPLESTATES (APOSTATES) aiming to end the Human Gods' tyranny. The DISSAPPLES (DISCIPLES) believe paradise still exists within the Human Gods' mouths.

Players end up on one of these two sides. There are destruction cards that have to be added by the APPLESTATES to kill the Human God, while the DISSAPPLES have defuse cards that prevent those destruction cards from going off. Whether they kill the Human God or not, players will have to turn on each other to save themselves from death using the cards they have.

—description from the designer

name: Food Alley
description:
Welcome to the Market!
Experience the bustling food alley from three unique angles.
Shopper: Race to complete your grocery lists without missing a thing.
Sambal: Bargain for ingredients and cook up spicy dishes.
Stray: Lead a clan of street cats fighting for left overs and territory.
Fast setup, flexible complexity, and endless replayability. 
Ready to hit the market? Play all three games with the same set of components. 1 box, 3 games!

—description from the designer

name: Forestry
publisher: Pink Troubadour; Capstone Games; DSV Games; Galakta; Little Rocket Games; MINDOK; Pegasus Spiele; Vagabund
description:
In Forestry, players take on the role of forest stewards dedicated to sustainable forest management. The game challenges players to balance the demands of harvesting resources and fulfilling contracts with the need for environmental conservation. Every action taken has a lasting impact on the forest's health, and players are encouraged to make responsible choices, from planting new trees to adjusting water streams for optimal moisture retention. Drawing from the expertise of real-life foresters, Forestry provides a realistic and educational glimpse into the work of forestry, making it as engaging as it is enlightening.

As a Eurogame focused on strategic action management, Forestry relies on a dual-worker system in which players control a harvester and a manager, each with distinct responsibilities. The harvester moves through the forest, felling trees to meet contract demands, replanting saplings, constructing infrastructure, and adjusting water retention to promote a healthy ecosystem. Meanwhile, the manager oversees resource collection, utilizes sawmill buildings, fulfills contracts, and optimizes wood processing. Players must carefully allocate action points between these workers to make sustainable choices, enhance infrastructure, and ensure the forest thrives while meeting demand.

—description from the publisher

name: Food for Thought
description:
Food for Thought is a worker-placement and resource-management game designed by a dietitian. Over six rounds, players shop for ingredients, cook recipes, dine out, and engage in activities — shop, cook, dine out and exercise! The player who best manages their body's needs will win, all in the pursuit of health and happiness.

Food for Thought is a new edition of Consumption: Food and Choices that includes the Picky Eater and Extra Helpings expansions previously released separately.

name: Papyria
description:
Mesopotamia, around 1500 BC: The Mesopotamian region on the Euphrates and Tigris is home to a melting pot of different cultures. Achievements such as writing and the wheel lead to the construction of the first large cities and lively trade. In the mountains, the coveted lapis lazuli is mined, and papyrus is made from reed grass.

In Papyria, you explore the region to create an extensive network of canals; discover inventions; develop mines; and build temples, sanctuaries and cities.

During your turn, you move your wanderer or ship. On the target space, you choose two of the three possible actions, which can mean taking a new tile for your display or a multiplier for later scoring; building a city, a temple, or a mine; or producing lapis or papyrus, which you need for building, special actions, or special scorings.

The game ends as soon as the last good has been taken from several spaces and a certain number of "end-of-game" tiles have been revealed and fulfilled. After several final scorings, whoever has the most points wins.

—description from the designer

name: Pondscape
publisher: Pink Troubadour; Capstone Games; DSV Games; MM-Spiele; Rexhry
description:
Pondscape is a strategic card game for 2-4 players, lasting around 30 minutes. In this game, players create their own vibrant pond by carefully placing cards featuring various frog species and pond environments while collecting different insect types.

The core mechanisms involve grid building and card management, with pond construction as a spatial puzzle. In each round, players choose cards from a shared display and add one card to their pond, aiming to fulfill specific conditions set by different frog species to earn points, with larger groups of the same frog type yielding even greater rewards.

A unique shared mechanism revolves around the "jumper frog", a central figure that hunts insects and other food. All players influence the jumper frog's actions and compete to gather insects that can provide bonus points during the final scoring. Careful planning and resourceful play will lead to the most balanced and flourishing pond!

—description from the publisher

name: Raising Chicago
description:
During the 19th century, the elevation of the Chicago area was just a few feet higher than the shoreline of Lake Michigan. For many years, there was little or no naturally occurring drainage from the city surface, and this lack of drainage caused unpleasant living conditions. Standing water harbored pathogens that caused numerous epidemics including typhoid fever and dysentery, culminating in the 1854 outbreak of cholera that killed six percent of the city's population. The crisis forced the city to take the drainage problem seriously. In 1856, engineer Ellis S. Chesbrough drafted a plan for the installation of a citywide sewerage system and submitted it to the city council, which adopted the plan.

However, due to the minimal elevation above the lake, the sewer could not be built underground and had to be built at street level. The city council then decided to implement a radical idea: Prevented from digging down, they instead decreed the buildings of the city would be raised to allow the new sewer system to be hidden under the new street level. Representing one of the four companies that were created to tackle the problem of raising the buildings of Chicago, it's up to you to gather resources, take on the most attractive projects, and help solve the sanitation crisis of the city.

On your turn in Raising Chicago, you place a tile on a resource slot associated with one of five building projects, then claim the resource you covered. After all players have placed tiles, each project is evaluated. The winning player pays resources to complete the project, claims the project reward, then places all of their tiles associated with that project as levels underneath the building onto a space on the board. Players earn points for placing buildings cleverly, doing the most work in a ward, and meeting the demands of council people.

Only the most successful player will win, so play strategically to prove you can raise buildings the best in Raising Chicago!

—description from the publisher

name: For One: Mensch ärgere Dich nicht
description:
Schmidt Spiele's long-lived game Mensch ärgere Dich nicht has been reborn as a solitaire game in For One: Mensch ärgere Dich nicht.

To play, you roll the dice and move your game pieces as usual, trying to reach the finish line quickly, but on the way you have to beat lots of tiles and complete other tasks. Choose the pieces cleverly, hope for luck with the dice, and (as always) don't get angry!

As with other For One titles, this design features multiple levels of gameplay to present you with new challenges over and over again.

name: Rising Cultures
description: In Rising Cultures, you take control of one of four different civilizations — Egypt, Persia, Rome, or the Abbasid Caliphate — each with its own unique deck and abilities. Your goal is to lead your culture to fame and glory through conquered provinces or building cards. Each of the multi-use cards presents you with an important decision: Do you use them for resources, for your military, to build important buildings, or to play unique leaders? The decision is yours!

name: For The People
description:
For The People is a trick-taking card game in which each player takes on the role of a political party leader, aiming to collect as many policies as possible that align with their party's manifesto.

During each session of Parliament (a trick), every party leader plays one policy card. Only the policy with the highest level of public interest (i.e. the strongest card) is voted on. The leader who played that card wins the trick and takes all the policy cards submitted by the players.
However, in a nation where public interest in politics is low, it's possible for corrupt policies (black cards) to be voted on first. Honest and transparent parties may sometimes find themselves outmanoeuvred by those engaging in malfeasance.

When Parliament adjourns, each party gains or loses points based on how many policy cards they have collected that match their manifesto, as well as the number of other policies they have acquired. The goal is to end the game with the highest total score.

name: Foraglings
description:
Nestled deep in the undergrowth of Whitlock Grove, the sprightly Foraglings work together to grow their budding hamlet into a thriving community. Known for their benevolence, Foraglings contribute to this shared goal by scavenging the brush for resources and assisting with projects in the village. However, despite their compassion and kindness, they can also be a little devious, choosing instead to hoard some treasures for themselves rather than give them away.

In Foraglings, a 1-4 player competitive inventory management game, players will take on the role of a unique Foragling competing to collect the most coins throughout 6 rounds of play. Foraglings will bid for resource tiles and exchange them in the market as they work to build a hand of community projects to score at the end of the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Forelords
description:
Delve into the mysterious and expansive world of Olroc, a planet on the brink chaos and destruction. Here you will find the likes of post-cataclysmic dramas, tales of exploration, monsters, mechs and all-powerful ancient beings known as Forelords. Explore deeply human themes like existential dread, overpopulation, love, and the threats of technology. Dive into the world by reading the corresponding novels, then come here to play the characters.

Forelords is a 1v1 dueling trading card battle between competing biomes. Play as one of many lands, whether they be high, low, wet or frozen. Move your cards into spaces like chess pieces, and gain favor by collecting one or more of the five terrain tokens. To win, you must destroy your opponent's king or collect the most points in battle by the showing of the final monolith — whichever comes first...

During the game, you will add land and ally cards to your hand, pay the cost to put them into play, then use them to battle your adversary. Land cards will equip you with valuable resources, such as metal, batteries, credit, knowledge...even coveted terrain tokens. Ally cards will maneuver and melee at your command to overcome foes as well as the wilderness.

Will you amass resources and knowledge to wage a strategic battle, or go straight for the king? Only the Forelords know for sure...

Game Mechanics

The game features popular TCG mechanics like hand management, player elimination and deck construction, but sets itself apart with a distinct mix of mechanisms that allow players to:

• Explore a hostile and unpredictable wilderness (exploration)
• Move cards on a grid to tactically position allies for battle (grid movement)
• Unlock unique “fortes" during play (variable player powers)
• Gain surges in power by capturing one or more terrain tokens

—description from the publisher

name: Forest First
description:
Autumn has arrived and brought beautiful colors to the forest – it’s the perfect time for a little race!
The critters plod, amble, scamper and scurry from tree to tree.
They all like a good snack, though, and can’t resist the various
temptations they discover along the way.

Aim of the game: Be the first to make it through the forest with your critter to win the race.

name: Forest Floor
description:
Forest Floor is a strategic card game that thrives on a shared deck, creating an element of tactical depth as players carefully manage resources and anticipate their opponents' moves. The ability to influence the order of draws by putting cards back on top of the deck adds a layer of complexity, rewarding players who can predict and manipulate the game's flow. At the heart of the game lies the "Mulching" mechanic, allowing players to interact with their opponents' cards before their effects resolve. This dynamic interaction encourages both cooperation and competition, as players work together to prevent any single player from gaining an overwhelming advantage.

Designed with accessibility in mind, Forest Floor boasts simple rules and an intuitive learning curve, making it enjoyable for players of all skill levels. However, beneath its approachable surface lies a wealth of strategic depth. Discover powerful card combinations, unlock hidden synergies, and navigate the ever-changing deck as you strive for ecological dominance. Each turn presents exciting choices: will you focus on rapid growth, bolster your defenses, or gather crucial information?

Prepare to embark on a journey through the forest, where every card played has the potential to shift the balance of power. In Forest Floor, the fate of your garden rests in your hands. Cultivate your ecosystem, outmaneuver your opponents, and emerge victorious in this engaging and rewarding card game.

—description from the publisher

name: Forest Gangs
description: Defeat your enemies with frantic battles between powerful creatures! In Forest Gangs everyone plays a card at the same time. Whoever manages to play the most powerful card wins the round and takes over the opponent's cards. At the end of the game, whoever has collected the most creatures wins!

name: Forest Leader
description:
In Forest Leader, five animal clans — Fox, Rabbit, Badger, Bear, and Deer — compete for the throne of the forest. Each turn, you play cards to influence the Council of Chiefs and your Tribes.

On your turn, perform the following actions:

• Draw : Take 3 cards from the draw pile
or the 3 visible cards in the river.
• Play : Place 2 cards from your hand into two
different zones:
   • The Council of Chiefs,
   • The left Tribe,
   • The right Tribe.
Cards are placed in visible columns by clan.
• Discard : Place one card in the river.

If the river exceeds 3 cards, remove the oldest card.

The Council of Chiefs determines the points each clan will bring you. Your goal is to accumulate the most points by having the most prestigious clans in your tribes.

-description from designer

name: Forest Shuffle: Dartmoor
publisher: Lookout Games; asmodee; Gém Klub Kft.; Hobby Japan; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
Forest Shuffle: Dartmoor is a stand-alone game within the Forest Shuffle family and introduces a brand new habitat and features new species with new abilities and bonuses to explore. As in the earlier original Forest Shuffle, in Forest Shuffle: Dartmoor players compete to build the most valuable environment by placing trees and shrubs, then attracting species to these locations to create an ecologically balanced habitat for flora and fauna.

What's new in Dartmoor is the introduction of TERRAIN cards that are played horizontally and serve as a home or feeding ground for different species than trees or shrubs. Due to the nature of the terrain, species can only be placed above and below a terrain card. Deer and other species stay clear from bogs or peat areas in the moorland. They need their drink, but won't feel safe at dwells or next to rivulets. So players have to watch out, where to place their species.

Like its predecessor, Forest Shuffle: Dartmoor comes with a unique back side: Each of the 180 cards of the deck can be placed face down, creating a bog, if the action allows it. The caves in Forest Shuffle: Dartmoor now will be drafted at the beginning of the game and offer asymmetrical starting conditions. On top, the number of tree symbols has been reduced from eight to six to enable bonuses more easily.

The game mechanism stays untouched: To start, each player has six cards in hand, with cards depicting either a particular type of tree, shrub or terrain or two moor dwellers (animal, plants), with these latter cards being divided in half, whether vertically or horizontally, with one dweller in each card half.  On a turn, either draw two cards — whether face down from the deck or face up from the clearing — and add them to your hand, or play a card from your hand by discarding other cards to pay the cost, then putting that first card into play. In the end, the player with the highest score wins.

name: Rowdy Partners
description:
Howdy, partners! In the sun-baked dust of Dusty Gulch, where shadows stretch long and strange, disagreements find resolution not with a six-shooter, but in the Rowdy Ring. Here, common sense yields to the thrill of a wrestling match, proving that in this corner of the Wild West, might makes right — one suplex at a time.

Rowdy Partners is a team trick-taking game played over a series of rounds, with each round being composed of eight tricks. Work with your partner to beat the other players by draining their health through calculated strikes and sneaky counters. Swap wrestlers mid-match, unleash signature moves, and collect Pop to gain the upper hand. The team that first pins one of their opponents wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Forever Island: An Eco-Apocalyptic War Game
description:
In the distant future, a nuclear volcano has emerged from the sea covering what was long ago known as Florida. It is here that the last remaining humans, reduced to Stone Age technology, survive on a diet of mutant wildlife and radioactive coconuts. Do you have what it takes to unite them under your leadership, or will human ambition lead once again to environmental collapse? Manage your resources and alliances to expand your power, but beware volcanic eruptions, betrayal, and the ecological limits of the islands on which you depend.

Forever Island is a turn-based competitive strategy game played with 2 to 6 players. Players collect resources to expand their tribe through building, traveling, trading, raiding, and taxing, while being careful not to over-exploit nature. Forever Island can be played either in teams or individually. Play time can range from as little as 30 minutes with 2 players to as much as 2 hours with 6.

—description from the designer

name: Forgeflame
publisher: Lord Raccoon Games; Board Zeppelin; Grimspire; ShineHigh Games
description:
In a distant land, a landslide reveals long-forgotten underground tunnels containing an invaluable treasure: deposits of Gold, Darkiron, and Draconite! Rumor has it that at the heart of these lost mines lies an even more precious secret: The Eternal Forge, a dwarven masterpiece capable of crafting legendary artifacts. Glory-seeking explorers and wealth-hungry plunderers are already flocking to the mine's entrance to get their hands on this bounty... but the task won't be easy, as Kobolds have taken up residence in these tunnels, sparking a frantic race among rival adventurer teams.

In Forgeflame, you lead a team of 3 adventurers racing to explore mines, collect ores, and craft artifacts. At the start, players shuffle their adventurers' basic cards and take turns playing one card, using their character's unique abilities. After four cards each, they add an advanced card from their characters to create a more powerful deck and draw a new hand.  As the game progresses, unexpected events unfold, and kobolds relentlessly harass the adventurers. Victory requires smart planning, teamwork, and clever tactics.

The game ends when a player forges their fourth artifact, and points are tallied.

—description from the designer

name: Formaggio
description:
You are an Italian cheesemaker in the early 20th century making, aging, and selling your artisanal cheeses. Become the most prestigious cheesemaker in all of Italy by running a highly successful creamery and crafting exceptional cheese. Formaggio is a standalone expansion for Fromage. With both games put together, you can combine any 4 board quadrants, and draft any combination of structure tiles for more variety and more paths to victory.

Formaggio is a simultaneous worker-placement game where players place Workers to make cheese and gather resources from the quadrant of the board facing them. Once all players have placed their Workers, the board rotates, aging any cheese that was made, and presenting each player with a new quadrant to place Workers into. Score Prestige Points by selling cheese to the four locations, and by efficiently managing and upgrading your creamery.

Formaggio features 4 new board quadrants with all new puzzling mini-games:
• Pair your cheese with the wines at the Vigneto.
• Sell cheese to restaurants along the Venetian canals and attract customers.
• Distribute cheese across the Regioni of Italy.
• Deposit cheese in the Banca. (Yes, there is a real bank in Italy that accepts cheese as collateral for loans!)

Other new features:
• Platinum-tier cheeses.
• Reap various rewards in each of the Seasons.
• All new abilities on the Player Boards and Structure tiles.

—description from the publisher

name: Formidable Farm
publisher: 2F-Spiele; Geronimo Games; Ludofun; Rio Grande Games; Yellowstar Games
description:
In Formidable Farm, you tirelessly try to fulfill the wishes of the village population for field crops.

At the start of the market day, you set the number of trades you need to fulfill until the evening. Initially, you do not know the details of the village population's wishes, and you can only work through the trades one after the other.

The village population follows simple rules for all their wishes: If you supply the needed field crops, you will get a reward. If a customer wants tomatoes, they give you two bags of wheat. If you organize a hoped-for sheep, the customer trades your surplus cucumbers for pigs. For two cucumbers and a bag of wheat, you immediately get details for another three wishes.

If you have delivery problems, you can make additional trades at the market to get needed rewards. You also can use each of your fulfilled trade cards to pay for advantages.

If you are the first to fulfill the wishes of the village population, you win Formidable Farm and enjoy an early end of the work day.

name: Formula 5
description:
In Formula 5 the theme of the game is a car race.
Setup: After assigning each player one car, shuffle all 5 car cards and place them randomly on the table in succession, from first to fifth position. Shuffle and deal 12 race cards to each player to form their hand and randomly place one race card face up below each car on the table to form 5 columns. The remaining car cards form a drawing deck.
