Game: The game is played in turns. The car in first position plays first, the car in second position plays second and so on. The active player must play a race card from their hand (or draw it form the drawing deck in case of cars without a player) and play it in the column corresponding to their car, overlapped, so that all race cards are always visibile. If the speed (number of all race cards of the same colour as the last race card played in the whole column) is greater than the speed of the car preceding it the car overtakes it.
Instead of playing a race card face up each player during their turn may decide to make a pit stop by playing a pit stop card or a race card face down. The pit stop allows the active player to discard as many race cards from their hand as they wish and to draw the same number from the drawing deck, but the speed is considered zero.
End: when the cards in the players hands run out, the game ends. The player whose car is in better position at the end of the game wins the game.

—description from the pubisher

name: Fortunes of Scoundrel Bay
description:
You have finally reached the archipelago of Scoundrel Bay! Here, amidst treasures and dangers, fortune awaits any crew daring — or foolish — enough to seize it.

In Fortunes of Scoundrel Bay, players are pirate captains who try to collect the most gold by conquering harbors, seeking hideouts, delivering crates, digging up treasures, and gaining reputation by fighting monsters. During the game, each player builds up their crew to unlock stronger actions such as digging for treasure, invading hideouts, and picking up and delivering crates. On your turn, play one card from your hand and choose one of three actions for it:


    Recruit
    Sail and shoot monster
    Invade


You may not pick the same action you took on your previous turn. The deck contains 84 unique, multi‑use cards, and every card works with all three actions. After each of five reefs, you resolve an event and feed your crew. The game ends as soon as a captain crosses the fifth reef. Sailing quickly shortens the game, but racing ahead might leave your engine too weak to claim victory.

In the box, you'll find unique player power tiles, asymmetric player boards, screen-printed captain figures, screen-printed pirate ship figures, 108 pirate figures, event cards, and a lot more.

Fortunes of Scoundrel Bay is a high interaction game in which players compete to gain area‑majority over lucrative islands, outpace foes in an open draft of crew cards, race to engage monsters before others can, and outwit captains in tense blind bids — all without resorting to negative or take‑that attacks.

—description from the designer

name: Fossilium
description:
Fossilium is a strategic and interactive set collection and tile placement game. As the director of a natural history museum specializing in paleontology, it’s your mission to turn your establishment into the most sought-after destination for fossil enthusiasts. To achieve this, you will send your paleontologists on promising excavations, carefully assemble fossil pieces, and strategically display them in your grand hall. By expanding your museum with facilities like restaurants and auditoriums, you can unlock additional income and powerful bonuses. Always keep an eye on visitor trends, as this can allow you to sell season tickets and gain a crucial advantage over your competitors.

The game features a unique blend of competition and cooperation: while you may compete for valuable action spaces, there’s also room for collaboration. In the spirit of scientific discovery, you can assist your rivals in completing iconic fossils like the T-Rex or Stegosaurus, allowing both players to score points.

You have 5 rounds to fill your exhibition rooms. Each round consists of four phases : receive income , build and fill your museums, open the doors to your museums and gain prestige, finally, you unearth new fossils and attract returning patrons.  After five rounds, the game ends and whoever has collected the most prestige has built the most impressive museum and wins!

Fossilium is a science-based game developed in collaboration with the Museum für Naturkunde in Berlin (Natural History Museum).

—description from the designer

name: Sanctuary
publisher: Feuerland Spiele; Capstone Games; Cranio Creations; Game Harbor; Gém Klub Kft.; Grok Games; IGAMES; Korea Boardgames; Lautapelit.fi; Maldito Games; MINDOK; Portal Games; Regatul Jocurilor; Super Meeple; White Goblin Games
description:
In Sanctuary, you will plan and design a modern, scientifically-managed zoo for animals and visitors. A supply of 135 unique zoo tiles provides you with animals, buildings, and projects. In every game, you want to find the best mix from those available to build the most successful zoological establishment. Different effects on the tiles will help you to achieve conservation goals and to increase the attraction of your zoo.

Each player has a set of four action cards to manage their gameplay, and the power of an action is determined by the slot the card currently occupies. One of those cards will let you play projects, and the other three cards will let you play animals of a specific habitat: forest, rock, or water.

Sanctuary is based on its predecessor Ark Nova, but modifies and simplifies many of the mechanisms of that game in an elegant and surprising manner. Your goal to find the best way to puzzle together your animals, buildings, and projects on your zoo map is an ongoing pleasure!

—description from the publisher

name: Four Against Darkness: Expanded Edition
description:
Welcome to the dungeon! Four Against Darkness is a best-selling solo dungeon-delving game. It may also be played cooperatively or with a GM. All you need is this book, a pencil, two dice, and grid paper. Choose four characters from a list of 20 classes, equip them, and venture into dungeons created by dice rolls and your choices. Fight monsters, manage resources, grab treasure, dodge traps, find clues, reveal secrets, and even accept quests from the monsters themselves. Your heroes will become more powerful with each game... IF THEY SURVIVE. This expanded edition brings in the game new classes, spells, foes, equipment, and environments. It includes two short adventures and all the tables required. Compatible with all the published supplements. 208 pages PDF

—description from the publisher

name: Four Forests
description:
In Four Forests, players each take on the role of one of the Guardians of the Enchanted Forests. Prepare your forest for the arrival of various mythical creatures by planting vegetation that has specific appeal to each creature. Ensure that the creatures attracted to your forests are considered the most prestigious by secretly casting votes.

In more detail, Four Forests is played across four rounds. Each round, each player draws four plant cards, then takes four actions simultaneously:

• Cultivate: Place one plant card from your hand into your habitat.
• Harvest/Burn: Place one plant card from your hand face down next to one of the four creatures in play to upvote or downvote their appeal.
• Pollinate: Pass a plant card to the player on your left, while receiving one from the player on your right.
• Prune: Discard a plant card from your hand.

Your hand size increases by one plant card each round, and at the end of four rounds, you score cards in your hand and habitat. Reveal the cards in front of each creature to determine its prestige; if a vote card was played upside down, it counts as a downvote, lowering the value.

Score points for each plant card in your habitat and hand based on which creatures they appeal to. Whoever has the most points wins.

name: Four Horsemen
description:
Four Horsemen is an epic cooperative resource-management and deck-building game where players take up the mantle of legendary heroes to prevent the end of the world. Players will face off against a main demonic foe, and they'll need to utilize their followers to stop catastrophic events, acquire relics, and delay the final ride of the Four Horsemen. Will your strategy keep the world intact long enough to seal away the demonic entity forever?

Each asymmetrical hero has their own divine powers and starting deck. Upgrade your deck by acquiring powerful relic cards each turn. Play strategically and choose carefully which relics to play and which to sacrifice to optimize your ability to respond to new events, destroy the demonic horde attempting to overrun the world, and delay the horsemen on their ride to bring about total destruction.

With a large variety of heroes, villains, and events, Four Horsemen has thousands of unique scenarios, meaning no two apocalypses are the same.

—description from the designer

name: Four King Rabbits
description:
Four King Rabbits is an infectious, orgasmic, and deceitful card game (16+) set in a not-so-parallel universe of sex-hungry rabbits.

In this game, players take turns drawing STDs and action cards. The goal is to avoid death from accumulating too many STDs, and be the last rabbit standing. Lie about your own STDs, and use the action cards (e.g One Night Stand / Gang Bang) to infect your friends, protect yourself (e.g Condom / Divine Intervention), or skip drawing a disease (Masturbate).

—description from the designer

name: Four Planets
description:
Which home planet will become the new center of the universe? It's high time to settle this in a competition!

In the duel game Four Planets, two captains set off into space with their spaceships to recruit the most capable minds in the galaxy to advance their own home planet. Round after round, four alien planets are visited – but only the first to arrive gets the choice. Who specializes in technology, economics, or knowledge? Who prefers special equipment or botany?

Four Planets is a tactical game with a special card-selection mechanism, tricky decisions, and great game depth.

Each round, every planet offers a pair of specialists available for drafting. Players take turns sending out one or more connected rockets to show their interest in a specific planet, while not revealing which of the two specialists they are willing to pick up later. Once all rockets have been sent, the player who claimed a planet first or who sent more connected rockets (traveling faster) may choose a specialist from the planet, while the other player takes what is left. Players then decide how to play their collected cards as some specialists require discarding other cards from hand. By combining symbols on their played cards, players develop certain abilities such as gaining more rockets or performing research of secret scoring bonuses.

name: Fox on the Tree
description:
It Starts Simple. Then It Messes With Your Mind.

In this fast-paced hidden-roles game, you secretly guide two favorite animals to safety while sabotaging one rival. Farm animals flee toward the forest, predators hunt toward the farm—but you’re not the only mastermind with a plan.

Use action tokens to trap, block, and rescue. Drop banana peels, lure enemies into swamps, and pull off last-second escapes. Predators can jump ahead, while farm animals slip past opponents to gain speed.

The game unfolds in two mirrored phases as animals reverse direction and race back home. Watch closely to spot who’s helping whom, outmaneuver your opponents, and turn the shifting board to your advantage. Every choice is permanent. Every move matters.

Score points by getting your favorites to their destination—and lose points if your unfavored animal succeeds. Outsmart the others before they do the same to you.

—description from the designer

name: Foxpaw
description:
Foxpaw is a highly interactive worker-placement board game where where players, as aspiring talents of a magic school, compete with their Magical Beasts over 5 school-years for the victory of their house. Through strategic decisions and tactical moves, players gather victory points for their houses, with the aim of having more points than all others at the end.

On the way, players will encounter many challenges. The first step is to choose a house, each with its own unique abilities. Some players may choose to follow their family legacy, sacrificing some house abilities for extra resources at game start. Players also must gather resources to upgrade equipment like their Broom and Wand, while also improving attributes such as Knowledge and Strength to succeed at classes and duels and prove themselves to be the best student. Between certain school years, special magical events await each with its unique requirements and characteristics. Some players may choose to get ahead through "sneaky" moves that earn them darkness cards and may brand them a dark wizard!

Whoever has collected the most victory points (VP) for their own house after a total of 5 school years and 3 Magical Events wins!

name: Fragged: Double Tap
description:
Fragged: Double Tap is a post-post-apocalyptic science fiction tabletop skirmish game that focuses on high-stakes battles between small teams of heroes, soldiers, monsters and robots.

Set in the richly detailed universe of the Fragged Empire ttRPG, the game emphasises tactical decision-making, clever use of terrain and reaction attacks. Unlike many miniature games, Double Tap employs a unique action and reaction system that keeps both players engaged at all times. With its deep lore, customisable forces, and an expanding range of miniatures, Double Tap offers an immersive experience that rewards strategy and creativity.

The core rules for Double Tap are super light (no more than a few pages of core rules, and extra pages for diagrams and examples). With greater tactical depth coming from your unit cards. Card deck includes: 42 Specialist units, 17 Henchmen units, 21 Upgrades, 11 Tactical missions.

The game ends after 20 turns, with the winner controlling the most Objectives.

—description from the publisher

name: Frantic Antics
description:
Frantic Antics elevates the classic charades experience to a thrilling new level of engagement and competition. Dive into a game where every second counts and everyone plays at once, creating a dynamic and exhilarating atmosphere. You'll advance towards the finish line not just by expertly mimicking your assigned words, but also by swiftly deciphering the actions of others.

—description from the publisher

name: Frantic Brettspiel
description:
Finally, it’s here: The Frantic board game! Stay as far away from the goal as possible and try to send the others to that very place. Daring shortcuts, winding detours, and sneaky traps – the constantly changing game board ensures endless replayability.

—description from the publisher (translated)

Frantic is an exciting board game that stands out with its modular game board and the strategic play of cards. The modular game board allows each game to be unique, as the different parts of the board can be arranged in various configurations. This ensures high replayability and encourages creative strategies.

Playing the cards is a central element of the game. Players must cleverly use their cards to perform actions, manage resources, or outsmart opponents. The combination of the dynamic game board and the tactical decisions involved in card play creates an engaging and varied gaming experience. Frantic is therefore ideal for players who appreciate both strategic thinking and adaptability! The player who first reaches a certain number of points loses.

name: Frayed Ally
description:
Frayed Ally is a party card game filled with deduction, strategy, and explosive misfortune for 3-6+ players.

In the untamed streets of Sewer City, a battle for survival unfolds. Don the cloak of a random crafty character, each with their own unique special ability that can be used at pivotal moments to outlast your adversaries. The villain with a thirst for power and destruction, commands an army of loyal minions, determined to take down all rival animals. Rivals on the other paw are fighting for glory, battling to deal the final blow that defeats the villain and become champion of the city. However if no villain is in play, it becomes a classic battle royale, last character standing.

Strategically wield an array of action cards to outmanoeuvre your opponents, use them to your advantage to boost your defences or enhance your attack but beware of traps hidden within the deck. Traps create an added element of danger, they will deal instant damage to disrupt your carefully crafted plans and are especially dangerous end game.

With every successful attack, characters collect skull tokens to track damage taken until they inevitably fall. When critical with only one health point remaining, a player must reveal their character by flipping it face up on the field and that's how you discover who is in play. Revealed characters are now at your most vulnerable but also at their strongest. Special ability can be used once at any time per reveal to help claw back to the top.

The path to victory lies within the paws of the craftiest Frayed Ally.

—description from the designer

name: French & Indian War: Solitaire
description:
French and Indian War Solitaire, the sister game to War of 1812 Solitaire, allows the player to command the French or British side in the war that decides the fate of North America.

The game introduces some new concepts to the series.  In the French and Indian War, regional militia and Indians play a large role.  Indians affect attacks in regions depending on what side they allied with.  Alliances change during the game.  Each region has militia that are weak unless they have a conventional army present.  Each side has a limited number of armies that provide a major boost to the militia in the region.

Choosing where to place your few conventional armies are major decisions each year.  The game also allows players to play either side, French or British.

name: Fright Factor
description:
Movie monsters have come to life! The more you see them, the less scary they’ll be. But beware of the monster that lurks the longest as it will become the scariest and most powerful monster of all!

Fright Factor is a trick-taking game featuring movie monster suits that become less scary – and take fewer tricks – the more you play them. Each round, earn points by correctly predicting how many tricks you’ll win based on the fright factor of each monster.

—description from the publisher

name: The Royal Society of Archeology
description:
Immerse yourself in the fascinating world of early 20th century explorers in The Royal Society of Archeology.

As the leader of a learned society, you lead a team of adventurers on expeditions around the globe in search of relics and knowledge. London serves as your headquarters, where you secure funding, deepen your expertise at the university, and plan your next bold discoveries.

Your archaeologists gain experience as the game progresses and become more and more efficient at performing actions. A unique mechanism allows you to trigger bonuses: If one of you places a less experienced archaeologist on an action space already occupied by a more experienced archaeologist, both people receive rewards. These strategic interactions add additional depth to your decisions.

During play, you will send your researchers to legendary archaeological sites, collect relics, gain prestige, and expand your scientific knowledge — but keep in mind that your success depends on the balance between your prestige points and scientific achievements!

name: From The Shadows
description:
In From the Shadows, a Villain has sent their minions out unto the land to corrupt all living souls leaving the townsfolk of Forest Vale with the choice to either join or die. Players choose one of four heroes to venture out and kill these monsters, bringing back the trophies of their victories as proof for their bounties. Each player takes a turn performing their chosen action to ultimately gain the most victory points (VP). VP can be acquired by gaining Treasure, using Opportunities, and mainly by killing monsters. There are four classic villains that players may choose to go up against: Master Vampire, Alpha Werewolf, Zombie Horde, and Pharoah Mummy. Each villain’s deck is comprised of their minions to help drive the story.

From the Shadows is a turn based, light deck builder. Heroes begin the game with a deck of 15 cards, tailored to their abilities. During the game players can loot more cards from monsters they vanquish, building their deck and making their hero stronger. The final Villain is more difficult than his minions and basic monsters. Once a player kills the Villain the game is over and points are tallied.

—description from the publisher

name: Fruit Cocktail
publisher: Don't Panic Games; Ghost Dog; Nice Game Publishing; Swan Panasia Co., Ltd.
description:
A minimalist and challenging strategic card game with just a bit of double guessing.

Players draft fruit cards on turn, but the cards they draft also influence what will be the value of every fruit at the end of the game.

—description from the designer

name: FRYSK
description:
FRYSK is a game in which 1 to 6 players create their own version of the northern Frisian province of the Netherlands. Gameplay is family-friendy, and about optimizing the puzzle, as each type of landscape tile scores victory points in different ways. You develop a landscape by turning over a tile, which generates income and offers the opportunity to construct buildings for even more victory points. Currency in this game is water, accentuating the importance of the waterways and lakes in the landscape.

While the game mainly aims to entertain, the types of landscape and their development are grounded in history. FRYSK is the native language of the region the the game will be release bi-lingual, in Dutch and Frisian (and online English rules).

The game will be available in retail selectively and at 42 participating museums which each offer a unique scenario card that expands the game play (and even can be combined together). A 43rd scenario card will be broadly distributed, which makes use of of some the of the extra tiles included in the game.

FRYSK is in the same line as GRUNN. While it similarly is about making your own tableau with tiles, collected from a central market, it has a few subtle differences that change the puzzle and includes more unique tiles linked to new scenario cards.

—description from the designer

name: Fugitives
description:
Fugitives is a story driven, co-operative adventure board game with thrilling story through the beautiful mid-century southern landscape.

In the story, players find themselves on the run but don't know why. The escape turns into an investigation, when you realize the only way out is to confront your enemies.

On your journey your choices matter and you’ll either be the hero or become the villain.

—description from the publisher

name: Fulcrum Leader
description:
Fulcrum Leader is a solitaire tactical game which depicts the conventional Soviet air campaign against NATO in Europe during the Cold War era. The game covers the crucial decades from 1970s to 1990s as opposing forces faced each other down in a game of nuclear brinkmanship, with featured aircraft including the MiG-29 Fulcrum, MiG-23/27 Flogger, MiG-21 Fishbed, MiG-25 Foxbat, Su-27 Flanker, Su-24 Fencer and Su-17 Fitter.

In Fulcrum Leader, you will need to select the right combination of aircraft in your regiment in order to successfully carry out the different missions which your pilots will execute. You will be faced with the same type of decision-making and risk-taking experienced by Soviet air regimental commanders.

This game adds new aspects of Soviet air operations such as enhanced radio-electric combat, ground controlled intercepts (GCI), and the ever-present political officer watching over your shoulders, the Zampolit. You will need to manage the capability of your pilots, weigh the advantages and disadvantages of your aircraft, use your zampolit to manage your superiors, and avoid the ignoble fate of being sent off to a re-education facility in Kamchatka.

The core game contains 336 cards and 704 counters, including:


     207 x Aircraft cards
         MiG-21bis Fishbed-N
         MiG-23ML Flogger-G
         MiG-27 Flogger-J
         MiG-29 Fulcrum-A (USSR / Bulgaria / Czechoslovakia / DDR / Poland / Romania)
         MiG-29 Fulcrum-C
         Su-17M Fitter
         Su-24 Fencer
         Su-27 Flanker
    
     5 x Squadron Asset cards
         MiG-25RB/RBV Foxbat-B
         MiG-25RBSh Foxbat-D
         MiG-25BM Foxbat-F
         Su-25 Frogfoot
    
     18 x Support Aircraft cards
         Yak-28PP Brewer-E
         Tu-126 Moss
         A-50 Mainstay
    
     9 x Ground Control Intercept cards
     45 x Target cards
     36 x Event cards
     16 x Zampolit cards


In addition, the core box includes:


     11 x Campaign sheets
     3 x Skills / Traits / Player Help sheets
     1 x Sequence of Play Flowchart
     1 x Airbase Squadron Control sheet
     1 x Player Log sheet
     1 x Tactical Display board
     1 x Rulebook


—description from the publisher

name: Fungi Contest
description:
Fungi Contest is a strategic board game set in the whimsical world of Fungiland. Players become heirs battling for the throne after the king's untimely death. Utilizing personal tablets, dice, and unique character cards, players strategize to gain influence. The game features a battlefield for direct confrontations and sneaky cards for unpredictable twists. Filled with humor and cultural references, Fungi Contest offers a mix of tactical challenges and fun, suitable for both beginners and experienced players.

—description from the publisher

name: Funocracy
description:
Funocracy is a party game where creativity and quick thinking come together to create hilarious moments.

A theme is revealed, and in just 25 seconds, the player must give an answer that starts with one of the three available letters. The more creative or funny the answer, the better! But there's a catch: the player only scores if the rest of the players vote their answer as NICE!

Each letter card is worth 1 to 3 points, and the goal is to score the most points over three rounds.

name: Furnace Duel
description:
Furnace Duel is a 2-player follow-up to the popular Furnace board game. It is playable both in standalone and campaign modes, in which you compete for global industrial domination in a series of games played on six different boards.

The core gameplay in Furnace Duel is the same as in the base Furnace game. You bid for Company cards, get them or receive compensation, then use your cards and manage resources in order to gain the most money by the end of the 4th round.
However, here’s no compensation effect on top of the Company cards. You receive compensation by claiming routes on the game board. The value of your disc shows how many times you may use the effects of connected Cities (in any order or combination). At the beginning of the game, the only available tracks are the ones leading from the City corresponding to the card in question, but as your network grows, you gain access to new tracks and more lucrative Cities.

Each of the 6 game boards has special rules and features.
In the Campaign mode, you accumulate Campaign points awarded for winning a game and for fulfilling Achievements, both general and board-specific. The runner-up gets a board-specific bonus that gives them a bit of the upper hand in the following games.

Cards can be upgraded with the city effects.

There are Shipping companies, which are one-shot cards with a neutral brown disc printed on them – it is considered a bid of a neutral player.

—description from the publisher

name: Furry Poker
description:
Furry  Poker is a strategic card game. In each round, all players simultaneously play one card and choose either to activate the card's ability or to pick a card from the public zone. All collected cards are placed in front of the player to form the best combination.
The game ends when a player has seven cards in front of them, and the player with the best combination wins the game.

name: Fú: Festive Fortunes
description:
The zodiac animals are celebrating Chinese New Year, buying festive treats and exchanging red envelopes. Who will offer the tastiest treats to receive the most money in their red envelopes? 
In the highly interactive game of "Fú: Red Envelopes", compete to score the most Fortune ("fú") by receiving visitors and eating festive treats. Each game takes place over several years, split into phases mirroring the experience of a traditional Chinese New Year celebration.


     Shopping: Send your family members to buy festive treats or decorations as you prepare to host visitors over the new year. The catch? You don't get to eat your own treats! Treats are offered to entice other players to your home, hopefully with more money in their red envelopes!
     Visiting: Simultaneously and secretly fill your red envelopes with money to visit other players, and bid for the treats on offer at other players' homes. The catch? Players score "fú" for each visitor they receive. Can you eat enough treats at each host to justify the "fú" they score from your visit?
     Eating: Feast on your favorite treats at each home - the most generous visitors get first dibs! The catch? You only score "fú" by eating the right combination of treats. Can you change your strategy on the fly as other players beat you to the last mandarin orange?


—description from the designer

name: Gadget Builder
description:
Gadget Builder is a family card game from designer Tom Lehmann that riffs on the core idea of Crazy Eights: match number or color to play your cards and try to empty your hand first.

The twist is that you can use cards from a fifth suit to build various gadgets that persist from hand to hand and help you get rid of your cards. Which gadgets do you build? When do you use them?

You can use only one gadget per turn, and to go out, you must have no cards in hand and no unused gadgets. If you empty your hand but haven't used all of your gadgets, you draw one card for each unused gadget, so don't build it unless you're going to use it!

name: All Mine!
description:
All Mine is a mining claim (trick-taking) game in which players predict their hauls of each of the four treasures (gold, gems, mushrooms, and dragon eggs). However, instead of predicting the number of hauls they'll take, they must state the treasures they think they'll receive the most and least of. Since all cards display their treasure type on the back, players have more information than usual.

During each claim (hand), you must play the same treasure type if possible, even with the special trump cards. This requirement makes it difficult to predict which hauls you will bring in. In the end, the player who comes closest to their predictions wins.

Don’t get too greedy as you playfully place your bets in this game guaranteed to please card game enthusiasts and families alike.

—description from the publisher

name: Angel's Share
description:
The term Angel's Share refers to the portion of an alcoholic beverage, particularly whiskey, cognac, or wine, that is lost to evaporation during the aging process in barrels. This evaporation occurs naturally as the beverage matures in wooden casks.

Angel's Share is a poetic term for an inevitable and essential process that plays a key role in creating high-quality spirits. The term originates from the idea that the evaporated liquid rises to the heavens and is "taken" by angels.

Typically, around 2–5% per year, depending on climate, humidity, and storage conditions, are lost.
The Angel's Share contributes to the concentration of flavors, as the remaining liquid becomes more intense. For producers, the loss due to evaporation is a significant cost factor, as less product remains, especially for spirits aged for a long time.

In Angel's Share – the game - you are a shrewd investor looking to make the most money in the rapidly growing whiskey industry.
You will be purchasing barrels from renowned distilleries in hopes of turning a large profit. However, as time goes on a bit of each barrel evaporates - the Angel’s Share - which can leave you with a prestigious whiskey, or a low volume of a broken down spirit.

You have to manage your limited actions, aging barrels, and tight budget to make the most money chasing the perfect whiskey.

—description from the publisher

name: Galaxy Fighters
description:
Get ready for an interstellar showdown with Galaxy Fighters, the arcade-inspired co-operative strategy game!

Brace yourself as you step into the role of a valiant defender tasked with safeguarding one of the four districts of Galaxy City from an imminent alien space invasion. The fate of the city hangs in the balance as waves of relentless Exovon extraterrestrials descend from the cosmos.

Armed with a custom ship, embark on a heart-pounding mission to thwart the invaders and ensure the survival of humanity's last stronghold. Shield your ships from damage, strategize your every move, and blast through swarms of Exovon aliens with your state-of-the-art weaponry.

Only your team’s cunning tactics and unwavering determination will stem the tide of invasion and secure the future of Galaxy City. Will you and your friends rise to the challenge and become the ultimate Galaxy Fighters?

—description from the publisher

name: Gallerista
description:
Immerse yourself in a fascinating world full of arts and secrets! In this game, all players become art collectors with dazzling personalities and unique tastes. Without revealing their identities, they present a gallery of illustrious artworks that reflect their personal characteristics. Who will be able to showcase their likes and dislikes most convincingly through the selection of artworks in their collection? And who can guess the identity of their fellow players based on their selection? But be careful! One of the collectors is not a real person, but a fraudster trying to deceive everyone. Communicative, exciting and always new!

—description from the publisher

name: Gallic Village
description:
Gallic Village is a fast-paced and tactical game of card manipulation and board control, set in a hectic little Gallic village. Players take up roles as village elders, influencing the course of events in their favor by managing ancient stones—menhirs— and carefully choosing when and how to play their cards.

In each game, players play action cards that allow them to move, remove, or redistribute menhirs among the village’s four neighborhoods. Every card played stays in front of the player and contributes to the scoring, which depends on the combination of card colors and the distribution of menhirs on the board. With only seven cards played per player, every move counts—and with the ability to shift other players’ cards or upset the balance of the board, each match is dynamic and full of clever twists.

Combining elements of area control and card-driven strategy in a compact 15–20 minute format, Gallic Village is perfect for fans of light family games.

name: Gallipoli: Ordered to Die
description:
A 2-player diceless boardgame covering Anzac Cove battles during the Gallipoli campaign of 1915.  It includes three scenarios: The Invasion, The Counterattack, and The August Offensive.

A turn consists of each player taking three actions to move or attack.  Combat is done quickly by comparing values on the units. The losing side flips a unit over--and the attacker always flips a unit over as well.  Variation comes from random, secret chits each player begins the game with permitting extra actions or combat advantages.

Victory is determined by counting the value of the spaces controlled by the ANZAC player.  This is compared to the scenario's requirements.  Depending on the scenario, the ANZAC will need to control 7, 8, or 11 points to achieve victory while the Ottoman will want to hold the total to 5, 6, or 9, otherwise the game ends in a stalemate.

The scenarios play in under 60 minutes and are suitable for all ages.

—description from the designer

name: Game Against Christmas
description:
Looking to spice up your Christmas party? Cards Against Christmas is here to bring the laughs, chaos, and hilarity to your holiday festivities! Packed with cheeky humor and outrageous fun, this game will have everyone—whether it’s your best friends or your quirky relatives—laughing until their sides hurt!

With over 250 cards included, this full set is all you need for a memorable game night. It’s a complete stand-alone game, but it also pairs perfectly with your favorite Cards Against Humanity decks for even more laughs.

Whether you're hosting an epic Christmas bash or just a cozy gathering, Cards Against Christmas is guaranteed to deliver endless entertainment and plenty of LOLs! ??

How to Play:

One player draws a question card.

Everyone else picks 10 random answer cards and lets the fun begin.

The player with the funniest (and maybe a little naughty) combo wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Gamusinos
description:
During the night, we discovered a hunter trying to take the Gamusinos from our sanctuary. Luckily, we stopped her, but during the escape, all the animals escaped too!

In Gamusinos, each player takes on the role of an expert in a specific animal… but their role will be secret. You'll know which animal they specialize in, but not whether that's for better or worse. It could be the hunter!

Once these specialties are chosen, the animal cards are shuffled and distributed among the players, who will capture them through draft rounds.

At the end of the game, the animals will award points… but their value will be modified by the specialist in that species. So, for example, a platypus with a value of 1 could become worth 2… or even 0, depending on the hidden role of the platypus expert.

Your objective will be twofold:


     Score more points than the other experts.



     Discover the hunter who freed the animals to prevent her from taking the precious chamois.


Therefore, during the capture, you must pay close attention to what the others are doing... every movement can be a clue!

—description from the designer

name: Garden
description:
In Garden, players compete to collect the most beautiful flowers and create the most harmonious bouquet. Each choice is as delicate as a petal: you will need to balance colours and shapes to win.

A column of 12 flower cards is placed between each pair of players. In turn, each player can choose whether to collect the card at the bottom of the left or right column. The collected cards are placed in front of the player, forming their personal bouquet of flowers, which is always visible to everyone.

When all the columns are empty, each player will have a bouquet of 12 flowers. The final score depends on two factors:
Colours: having three or more cards of the same colour earns positive points, while one or two earns negative points.
Shapes: having three or more cards of the same shape earns positive points, while one or two earns penalties.

The points from colours and shapes are added up: the player with the highest score is the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Garden Canasta
description:
Play as gardeners, competing individually or as teams with the goal of growing the highest-scoring garden by planting crops, harvesting sets, and using clever bonuses to outgrow the competition.

Garden Canasta reimagines two classic card games—Canasta and Hand & Foot—with a fresh, garden-inspired twist. The theme seamlessly enhances gameplay while introducing new strategic elements. Beautifully illustrated cards featuring vibrant fruits, vegetables, and garden surprises bring the joy of gardening to life, making every hand as delightful as it is competitive.

—description from the designer

name: Falling
description:
One day, a tower fell from the sky, and in Falling you are an explorer searching for valuable relics and other items in that crumbling tower. By placing special devices in the tower, you increase the income of certain resources in the game, but as the round progresses, the towers collapse and these devices are returned to the players, granting them an even larger bonus! Additional bonuses can be obtained by converting resources using cards to create combos or by scoring victory points.

During set-up, players choose one of twelve sidekicks that each provide a unique ability. Solo play is also available.

name: Garden Rush
publisher: Space Cowboys; (Web published); asmodee; Gém Klub Kft.; Lord of Boards
description:
Garden Rush is a two-player, tile-placement battle game in a vegetable garden in which players race to grow vegetables in their garden and fill their basket before their neighbor. Careful planning is needed to plant each vegetable in its unique pattern for future harvesting, while keeping an eye on the conveyor belt shared between the gardens.

Players place one tile per turn to build their garden, following the harvesting patterns for each vegetable.  Extra abilities, including Take That options, can be gained by using special tiles on the board or on the scoring track.  The first player to reach 40 points or who has the highest score when the tiles run out, wins.

name: Gatefall Core Set: Standard Edition
description:
Gatefall is a strategic miniatures game of tactics, deck building, and resource management.

In the game, a rift has opened between worlds, causing a war between very different kinds of characters. The base game mode is designed for two players to fight head-to-head. Arena mode lets 2-8 players fight one another in a battle royale setting. In a two player game, players choose which team to control, the fantasy team consisting of Brog, Gildri, and Randar, or the Wasteland team consisting of Exile, Firebug, Penny, and Lost Boy.

When a character is killed, the player who killed that character earns the number of victory points printed on the character’s upgrade shop card, and the player whose character was killed draws a “zero” card from the “zeroes” pile for every victory point listed on the killed character’s upgrade shop card and adds it to their discard pile. The killed character respawns in their base immediately, but that character cannot move or attack on their next turn, and effectively loses a turn while respawning.

The first player to reach ten victory points wins the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Gates of Vienna 1683: Battles of the Age of Kings
description:
Gates of Vienna 1683: Battles of the Age of Kings system is a grand tactical two-player system for battles of the latter half of the 17th century to early 18th century. It is based on the 30 Years War Battles system with revisions to account for tactical developments of post 1648. Revisions include artillery mobility and an increase in tactical flexibility. The rules for Gates of Vienna are in three sections. The first contains the Standard Rules common to all games in the series. The second is the Optional section, which gives rules that players can use at their option or not. The third is the Exclusive Rules for each battle to include deployment, reinforcements, victory conditions, and special rules.
The game rules represent a combination of playability and realism and model the overall effects of the weapons and tactics of the great era of pike and shot, and include combat, leadership, and morale. Players command armies of infantry, cavalry, and artillery, each with their own special capabilities, as well as the great leaders who took the field in this era.

Each hex on the map represents circa 500 meters. Each game turn represents 45 minutes to 90 minutes, depending on the intensity of the action. Most cavalry and infantry units represent one or two regiments or battalions. Each combat strength point represents 100 to 300 men, depending on the quality of the army and assignment of light guns to the unit. Each artillery unit represents four to twelve heavy or medium guns.

name: Viridia
description:
Build the city of the future as it grows from a small town to a big city.

The game is played over a variable number of rounds, determined by when the Achievements are claimed.

Players use policy cards to generate resources, plan urban growth, build infrastructure, and attract residents. Each round, players will draw, prioritize, and execute cards from policy cards. These cards can also be turned into laws that improve your action efficiency and boost your future actions.  Policy cards and zoning tiles are purchased from a shared market. Blueprint tiles allow players to expand their cities, which may affect their short and long term goals. Whenever players expand their cities, they will be attracting residents. Burgeoning cities generate resources, but also create new management puzzles.

—description from the publisher

name: Critter Kitchen
publisher: Cardboard Alchemy; Gém Klub Kft.; HIT Games; Lucky Duck Games; Maldito Games; MIPL; Rexhry; White Goblin Games; YOKA Games
description:
It's Restaurant Week in Bistro Bay! Restaurants are competing in food challenges, while also planning an epic meal to impress a celebrity critic. As one of 1-5 players in Critter Kitchen, you'll send your chefs into the city to gather ingredients to create amazing meals and demonstrate that your restaurant is the best in town.

Each round, new random ingredients are placed in locations throughout the city. Players simultaneously and secretly plan which locations to send their three chefs to, hoping to collect the best ingredients. Some chefs are fast, but can gather only one item, while others can carry three items but arrive late. Rumors are also available at locations and provide guidance on what the critic desires.

Challenges revealed in rounds 1-6 offer the players opportunities to earn stars for crafting dishes with specific ingredient requirements. After round 7, the players must create an epic meal to impress the celebrity critic and cater to their appetites. A multitude of different critics, rumors, and restaurateurs mean every game is fresh!

—description from the publisher

name: Geekmon Capture
description:
Geekmon Capture is a fast dexterity game, full of geek references, about capturing little monsters.

During the game, players must use their aiming skills to throw their cubes trying to hit the wild Geekmon cards in a dispute to capture them. Each Geekmon is then captured by the player who managed to land the most cubes on their card.

But you must not throw your cubes randomly since, by capturing the evolutions of your Geekmon, you increase the score of your cards. At the end of the game, the player with the highest score is the winner.

Some plot twists during the game, such as the appearance of luminous Geekmon, critical hits, type advantages and even removing opponents' cubes from the cards (or sometimes even your own) by hitting another cube on it, will make the game exciting from the beginning to the end of the match.

-description from designer

name: Gelati
description:
Race to the ice cream cart at the end of the sunny beach path! Score points by cleverly placing your ice cream tiles and fulfilling unique orders. Are you the first to reach 50 points? Then you are the ice cream champion of Gelati and can celebrate a frosty victory!

Players take turns clockwise, placing one of their ice cream tiles into the play area. Try to place your tile as strategically as possible by aligning it with as many sides as possible and/or forming four in a row. After placing a tile, scoring points, and possibly completing a secret order, the next player takes their turn.

In Gelati, the goal is to be the first to reach 50 points. You can score points in two ways:

     Place a tile next to one or more tiles already on the table. The more adjacent matches, the more points you score.
     Secret orders: Collect ice cream parts to complete secret orders and earn 15 points!


—description from the publisher

name: Gem Jam
description:
Gem Jam is a sweet and strategic token placement game, where you’ll invite quirky friends to your table and share delicious Iced Gem Biscuits and Cookies to build lasting friendships.

Over 6 colorful rounds, players will draft friends, collect Iced Gem Biscuits, and place them carefully into lunch trays to fulfill pattern based cravings. Every friend has a unique taste, and satisfying their preferences will earn you Friendship Points. But watch out, once a treat is placed, it’s there to stay!

With shared objectives, spatial pattern matching, and clever token placement, Gem Jam serves up a light yet delightfully puzzly experience for 2–4 players.

Whether you're maximizing patterns or sneaking in bonus points with cookies, every round is a chance to grow your social circle and your score!

Will you become the most beloved host at the table?

—description from the designer

name: Gemeinsam Genial
description: Gemeinsam Genial will challenge your brainpower! Each of the one hundred puzzles presents sixteen words to be grouped into four sets of four. Using the four clues, players must discover the hidden connections between the words to solve the puzzle. But beware: the clues are not always clear and can be misleading! While some links are easier to spot – like “Taurus,” “Leo,” and “Gemini” – others require clever thinking, rearranging, and a good dose of lateral logic. With increasing levels of difficulty, every card offers a fresh challenge and keeps the puzzle fever alive time and again!

name: Gems of Antwerp
description:
In Gems of Antwerp, players take on the role of gem traders navigating a volatile market to amass the most valuable collection.

Each round, players place cards to adjust gem values, then split their remaining cards into two offers—forcing an opponent to choose while they take the rest. This mix of market manipulation, hand management, and strategic drafting creates a dynamic puzzle where reading your rivals is just as important as collecting the right gems.

At the end of each round, gem prices shift based on players’ actions, and collections are valued accordingly. The player with the most wealth at the end of the game wins.

—description from the designer

name: Gems of Iridescia
description:
Welcome to the fantastical world of Iridescia. This abandoned world, lush with rare gems has been vacant for centuries due to a cataclysmic event forcing it’s inhabitants to take to the skies. The land is now safe to return to and it’s former residents are coming home. Take on the role of one of 4 clans to explore the lands, mine gems, restore ancient relics, and find the lost Iridia Stone to ascend to the throne and re-unite the people of Iridescia!

Gems of Iridescia is a worker-placement board game in which players will push their luck as they compete to mine gems, restore ancient relics and ascend to the throne of a rich gem-filled world. Secret objectives and a variety of ways to score create different paths to victory make every expedition a unique experience.

Explore Iridescia by flipping over land tiles, revealing the gems hidden beneath them and then roll dice to mine them. Each gem color is tied to a dice value that can be manipulated to help your cause. Roll high enough, and you can claim more gems, adding them to your cargo hold providing you with a valuable resource for restoring relics and scoring royalty points!

Sell some of your hard earned Gems and visit Rumi the Travelling Merchant to purchase tools that will grant your adventurers exciting new abilities to aid in their search for Iridescia’s treasures!

Your trove of Gems can be used to restore Iridescia's ancient relics. Restoring Relics will gain you tons of Royalty Points and solidify your claim to the throne!

name: Critter Kitchen: Deluxe Edition
description:
It’s Restaurant Week in Bistro Bay! Restaurants are competing in food challenges while also planning an epic meal to impress a celebrity critic. As one of 1-5 players, you’ll be sending your Chefs out into the city to gather ingredients to create amazing meals and demonstrate that your restaurant is the best in town.

Each round new random ingredients are placed in various locations throughout the city. Players simultaneously and secretly plan which locations to send their three chefs to, hoping to collect the best ingredients. Some chefs are fast, but can only gather one item, while others can carry three items, but arrive late. Rumors are also available at locations and provide guidance on what the critic desires.

Challenges, revealed in rounds 1 through 6, offer the players opportunities to earn stars for crafting dishes with specific ingredient requirements. After round 7 the players must create an epic meal to impress the celebrity critic and cater to their appetites. A multitude of different critics, rumors and restaurateurs mean every game is fresh!

—description from the publisher

The Deluxe Kickstarter Edition comes with the A La Cart expansion, the Primal Promo Pack, the Lucky Duck Promo Pack, and all unlocked Deluxe Edition stretch goals from the Kickstarter campaign, which include upgraded components, more Zous Chefs, more Restauranteurs.

name: Genius Idea
description:
Genius Idea is a fun game full of reasoning and cleverness, where players take turns playing different roles over several rounds in an intellectual showdown.

Riddler: Selects 1 answer and 5 hints from 10 cards, aiming to help other players guess the answer.

Disruptor: Against the other players, trying to mislead and confuse them.

Solver: Find the correct answer from the limited hints.

In this battle of wits, players need to use associative thinking and their intuition to deduce the correct answer from the limited hints!

name: Geomandering
description:
Geomandering is a strategic, print-and-play board game where rival wizards reshape the world of Terralithia to gain control over the populace. At the heart of the game is a tug-of-war for influence — each player aims to outmaneuver the other by manipulating influence across a political landscape that can be reshaped by casting various Geomantic spells.

Gameplay unfolds across two areas: a central map, where players place Influence to control areas and a personal Wizard tome, were players will learn to harness and improve their spell casting prowess.

Each turn, players draft dice from a shared pool and spend them to cast spells from their Wizard’s Tome. These spells allow you to place influence, reshape the geography or enhance your own spellcasting engine. As you draw connections in your tome, you unlock stronger spells and multipliers that let you act more efficiently over time.

The central challenge of Geomandering is balancing immediate tactical moves (like locking down a key region) with long-term planning (building up your tome for powerful combos later). The geography of the board is ever changing through the actions of each wizard. New rivers can be carved, dwellings erected, and lands scorched. Through these actions, regions can change hands multiple times over the course of the game.

Includes solo mode.

name: Get Stacked
description:
Get Stacked is a strategic party game where players duke it out in a series of fast-paced mini-games to win powerful, stackable treasure and bragging rights. Then, use your hard-earned loot to power up your player to take down monsters and earn victory points.  Transparent treasure cards lay directly on your champion to make over 16,000,000+ unique combinations of armor, pets, and more. Utilize specific combos and power levels to defeat monsters and show your competition who's boss.

In each game you will play a set number of rounds based on the number of players. When the game ends, the player with the most victory points from defeated monsters claims ultimate triumph!

—description from the publisher

name: Get That Cat
description:
Here comes the ultimate reaction test! In Get That Cat, you have to react at lightning speed, aim sharply and...don't hit a cactus. Everyone turns over a card at the same time, then tries to throw the correct disc into the box — only those who hit it correctly score.

—description from the publisher

name: Gettysburg: The First Day
description:
Volume 12 in the Revolution Games American Civil War Series. Simulates the first day of the Battle of Gettysburg.

Gettysburg: The First Day is an historical portrayal of one of the most monumental engagements of the entire American Civil War. It was a pivotal battle where leaders on both sides had to constantly grapple with a plethora of command and control challenges. Revolution Games’ highly-popular “Blind Swords” system is perfectly suited to depict the extreme chaos of that fateful day.

This is a two player game where one side plays the Union and the other the Confederate. Using the 'Blind Swords' chit pull mechanic to activate brigades randomly. The game also handles very well for players who play both sides as solitaire.

Gettysburg: The First Day adds to the 'Blind Swords' system by adding situational innovations such as; Artillery Barrages, Union temporary CIC's, Rebel Sharpshooters, Buford's dismounted cavalry, and Union breech-loading rifles.

Also included is an optional variant for a variable march of two powerful formations, Confederate R.H. Anderson's Division and Union Slocum's 12th Corps.

This is not a so-called "monster" game; instead, Gettysburg: The First Day was designed to be readily accessible for all players whether they are familiar with the game series or not. Tense and comparatively quick-playing, varied strategy options offer excellent opportunities for replayability.

name: Ghost Face: The Game
description:
The spin on the game is that it will be themed around July 4th. These games are played on holidays, at least for now, and we needed to make it different than the movies. So we’re creating a brand-new story: It’s July 4th weekend, and this little town of Clarion, Pennsylvania, is having a big drive-in for the holiday. They wake up to a newspaper report that these Ghost Face killers are running around and killing people. The idea is that the police officers have figured out that this Ghost Face (or Ghost Faces – key!) is headed to the big drive-in to kill a bunch of people. And it features nine masks in the line. So you’re gonna get the gold Ghost Face, the devil Ghost Face, the orange, the green, the scarecrow, the aged one. The idea is to celebrate the line of Ghost Face masks that Fun World has been cranking out but aren’t in any of the movies … it’s a brand-new adventure for Ghost Face. He’s still killing.

Unlike the other Stop the Killer games, we have a multiple-killer angle, which you find out throughout the game, and it’s different with every game, whether there are one, two, or three killers you have to stop. And there’s a whodunnit angle.

—description from the designer

name: Ghost Lift
description:
In an ancient, abandoned apartment building, an old elevator creaks up and down the shaft of its own accord. Locals know of it as "the ghost lift". They say that it's moved by the ghosts of lingering residents trying to find their way back to their homes. You and your friends thought it would be fun to test your mettle by riding it...until you got trapped inside with the ghosts! Unless you release these ghosts on the floors they long for, they'll haunt you forevermore.

Try not to get haunted in Ghost Lift, a horror-themed, card-climbing game. On a turn, you must play higher or lower than the top card on the discard pile, with the direction being indicated by the most recent arrow played. The first player to get rid of their hand of cards is the only one who escapes safely, while the others are haunted by their remaining cards, which you note. Play multiple rounds until someone has been caught with the same number three times or the same three numbers twice, and which point the game ends, and that player loses.

name: Flamecraft Duals
description:
Ever wondered what the dragons of Flamecraft do on their lunch break? Play Flamecraft Duals, of course! Set in the world of Flamecraft, Duals is a two-player travel-friendly game of pattern-making and quick, puzzly fun! You will meet the artisan dragons again with new powers, and this time the challenge is to get your dragons in a row. As you draw dragons, you might get lucky and come across a rare dual-colored Hydragon, with double the artisanal skills! As you play, the board will fill up with adorable dragons, stacking and soaring across the table, and you will work to fire-up their abilities, make matches, and complete shop cards.

Flamecraft Duals is a two-player abstract pattern-building game that takes about 30 minutes to play. Each round, a player draws a dragon from the bag and places it on the shared central board. Every dragon type has a special ability that can be fired up to draw more dragons or rearrange those already on the board. You want to match three dragons on the board to the pattern on the shop cards in your hand to score them. Once all the dragons are drawn from the bag, the game ends and the player with the highest score wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Giants Moving Tiny Furniture
description:
Meet Giants Moving Tiny Furniture, the highly competitive, highly clumsy party game. Your team's goal is to move miniature furniture to its new home in as few trips as you can, as quickly as possible. The catch is, you can only use your pinkies! You gotta stack the goods, plan your trip, and work together to make sure you don't drop anything. The team that completes the most successful moving jobs wins.

How to play:

     Read the job card. Fight over who gets to do the job. 
     Carefully complete the job with just your pinkies. Don’t drop anything.
     Win by completing 3 jobs. 


—description from publisher

name: Giddy up, UNICORN!!
description:
Giddy Up, UNICORN! is a fast-paced, chaos-fueled card game where cute turns deadly and glitter meets madness. Designed for 2–5 players, it combines set collection, "take that" mechanics, and absurd humor in a world where unicorns have gone rogue.

Each turn, players draw and play cards from a 65-card deck filled with magical fruits, annoying shrooms, collectible unicorns, deadly nemesis attacks, and glitter-fueled power-ups. Block attacks, trigger chain reactions, and outsmart your opponents — or die dramatically.

Survive the glitterpocalypse, unleash chaos, and collect the cute unicorns ever drawn. With easy-to-learn rules, strategic combos, and artwork that blends adorable with deranged, Giddy Up, UNICORN! is perfect for fans of games like Exploding Kittens or Unstable Unicorns... but with a darker twist.

Do you have what it takes to be the last unicorn standing?

—description from the publisher

name: Gigi Gacker am Würfelacker
Grave Trigger
description:
Grave Trigger is an apocalyptic sci-fi miniatures skirmish and campaign game where players control humans terminally bound to Animus Reactors—sentient, techno-organic armor that feeds on those who wield it in exchange for terrifying power.

Unlimited Movement - Experience the most dynamic movement system ever used in a miniatures game—no tape measures required.

Diceless Combat - Leap off buildings with aerial attacks, throw terrain across the battlefield, and rely on your skill rather than the roll of a die.

Mutate The World - Summon living terrain to give you cover and even animate it to fight by your side.

Living Weapons - Evolve in response to damage and unleash hidden Damage State cards to turn the tide of battle.

—description from the designer

name: Girasoles
description:
The art gallery has commissioned you to create a work that captures the beauty of sunflowers, integrating diverse colors and combining elements to create a unique and stunning landscape.
In a game of Sunflowers, players take tiles from the Sunflower Field and place them on their personal board, trying to arrange the different elements in the best possible way.
The most important rule is that double tiles cannot be rotated! They must always be placed on the personal board in the same orientation as they were in the Sunflower Field.
After four rounds of play, the player with the most points wins. We invite you to paint your own sunflower field!

—description from the designer

La galería de arte te ha contratado para crear una obra que capture la belleza de los girasoles, integrando diversos colores y combinando los elementos para componer un paisaje único y asombroso.
En una partida de Girasoles, los jugadores toman losetas del Campo de girasoles y las colocan en su tablero personal, intentando ordenar los distintos elementos de la mejor forma posible.
¡La regla más importante es que las losetas dobles no se pueden rotar! Siempre deben colocarse en el tablero personal en la misma orientación en la que estaba en el Campo de girasoles.
Después de cuatro rondas de juego, el jugador con más puntos será el ganador. ¡Te invitamos a pintar tu propio campo de girasoles!

—description from the designer (Spanish)

name: Girls vs Ghouls
description:
Halloween mischief is afoot in Girls vs Ghouls, a competitive team game of hidden identities and strategic neighborhood control.

Girls vs Ghouls is a hidden identity game designed for extroverts and introverts alike where victory is achieved through strategic action. With identities hidden until the neighborhood is won, players are free to bluff, betray, befriend, or be silent, enabling everyone to interact in their preferred style on their path to neighborhood dominance.

Set in a cul-de-sac besieged by the undead, a team of cunning Ghouls in disguise scheme to ensnare unsuspecting trick-or-treaters in their haunted houses. Meanwhile, the gutsy neighborhood Girls plot to take back the block, willing to sacrifice their hard-earned Halloween candy to lure the young kids to safety.

Players are secretly assigned to one of the two teams, each side maneuvering for control of eight flippable tile houses around the cul-de-sac. As players move about the neighborhood, they use Treat cards to publicly influence where the trick-or-treaters go, and Trick cards to secretly boobytrap the houses.

Each round ends with the innocent trick-or-treaters visiting the house with the most appealing treats, awarding points and securing the house for its controlling team. Victory goes to the team with the most points after three rounds, tallied from the trick-or-treaters led to their houses plus bonus points for each controlled house.

-description from publisher

name: Glade
description:
Glade is a cozy, strategic gardening game for 3-6 players. Build up and customise your own garden over the course of 4 seasons. Seed mystical plants, surround your well-placed fields with powerful decorations and use your curious cultivators to unleash the unique spirit of your Glade.

The game begins with each player drawing two cultivators, mystic beings that reward players for accumulating certain types of plants (trees, flowering plants etc). These cultivators are then placed face-down next to one another to form a "Homestead" from which each player will grow their garden throughout the game.

Glade is played over 4 seasons (or rounds). At the beginning of a season, each player will draw a hand of cards that will include a mix of "Plants" and "Decorations". After "planting" a card by placing it down from their hand next to an already existing card, players will then pass their remaining cards to the player on their left or right. This continues until all players are given two cards. They will then plant one and place the other in their "Reserve", a collection of cards to be planted all at once at the end of the final season. Players then flip their planted cards face up and begin the next season after resolving any "Decoration" effects.


     Plants are the key component of each player's garden. By collecting matching plants and placing them next to one another, players will create "Fields" which are then scored for points at the end of the final season. By creating fields of plants that match their hidden Cultivators, players will gain even more! Each plant also has a unique "field requirement" which must be adhered to in order for the field to be considered valid at the end of the final season. Some examples include "This field must contain an even number of plants" or "Plants in this field must be planted at least 3 spaces from your Homestead".



     Decorations are special, rare cards that activate powerful effects if surrounded on all sides by matching plants at the end of a season. There are 8 of these powerful cards in the game, each with their own unique effect. Many decorations even allow players to modify their opponents' gardens, sabotaging existing fields or stealing coveted plants!


The drafting element of Glade gives players a lot to consider during a given season. "Do I want to further my own garden or stop the player next from me from acquiring a particular Plant?" "Can I predict what types of Plants are contested among the group?".

With a combination of drafting mechanics and a deep pool of unique plants, decorations and Cultivators, Glade is not just a game of developing your own garden, but a game of deduction and decisions. In Glade, the actions of you and your fellow players will determine whether the flow of each game leans more towards harmony or sabotage!

—description from the designer

name: Gladiators: Blood & Glory
description:
Few stories have captured the imagination as strongly as the use of gladiatorial combat in ancient Rome. For centuries it served as entertainment for the masses, serving a similar purpose as modern sports today, albeit in a more barbaric fashion. For the gladiators themselves, it was a harsh way of life in a harsh world – but with the potential to rise above the status of being a slave, and possibly win freedom …

Gladiators: Blood & Glory is a 2-player or solitaire game that places you in charge of running a Ludus – a Roman gladiator training school. You will make all the training, equipping, and logistical decisions a Lanista would make, and make the tactical decisions for your gladiators as they attempt to survive the Arena.

You will start with a stable of two gladiators, but will be afforded the opportunity to bid on more at auction to increase your numbers (or to replace losses). Training and managing finances will be key in your ability to field gladiators who have a chance to win in fights to the death. As time progresses and gladiators survive, they may use the experience gained in the arena and in training to improve their odds of success by purchasing skills. Victories help to narrate the player’s eventual goal – to have gladiators survive the arena and earn their freedom.

The gameplay moves quickly, with matches in the arena involving back-and-forth combat with a deck of cards. However, the tactical fighting in the Arena is just one aspect of the game, as players will also train, purchase supplies, gladiators, and weapons, and plan for future games. Additionally, players may wager denarii (Roman money) on matches in an attempt to build up their available funds. Optional rules include fighting against wild beasts such as tigers and cheetahs.

The game includes six of the major types of gladiators who saw combat in the arena:

Murmillo (short sword, large shield)
Dimachaerus (two swords)
Retiarius (trident and net)
Hoplomachus (spear and small shield)
Thraex (hooked sword)
Secutor (variant of Murmillo)
Product Information:

Complexity: 4 out of 10 
Time Scale: Semi-Abstract (individual fights, up to 5 per month)
Map Scale: Abstract 
Unit Scale: Individual gladiators 
Number of Players: One or two 
Suitability for Solitaire: Solitaire rules included 
Average Time to Play: 10-15 minutes (single turn) 4-5 hours (full career)

—description from the publisher

name: Glass Garden
description:
Terrariums are works of living art, lush worlds cradled within glass walls. Use care to cultivate and protect your fragile environment.

Caring for a terrarium takes time and energy, even without a pesky critter chewing on your hard work! Take care of your freshly-planted succulents by moving them around to develop the resources they need. As the critter advances, it wreaks havoc on your miniature garden. Limit its damage while still growing your plants as high as you can manage to earn the title of Master Gardener!

In Glass Garden, your garden consists of eight plant cards (and one of four possible critter cards) bounded by glass cards to create a 3x9 grid of spaces. On each turn, you can move up to two plants vertically and/or horizontally to form bundles of resources in fertile zones, the areas where two rows meet. Each plant needs a different set of resources to grow out of the soil, but once those needs are met, they can be flipped to their grown side to provide additional resources, while also immediately triggering a useful ability. Plants grown along one of the edges also flip the neighboring glass card to its sunlight side, granting the player additional moves at game's end. Lastly, the critter moves one space to the right, then damages specific plants in your garden, lowering them by one row. Once the critter reaches the far wall, the game ends. Take any sunlight moves available, then score points for each grown plant's height to find out whether your terrarium is a dirty dud or a thriving masterpiece.

name: Gli Ultimi Giorni di Mu
description: Save the ancient civilization of Mu from  decline, by increasing population, knowledge, commerce and technology. A solo card set-collection game, with eight levels of difficulty, each of them to be won with through strict combo requirements, in a very challenging timing. An extra scenario is added with a science-fictional theme.

name: Glimstone Grab!
description:
A cooperative game for 1-4 players. Much Middling is an average place, except for the special gems (glimstones) in its forest. Children love to play with these but unfortunately, a group of trolls has settled into a glade there. They love the glimstones too and have been snatching the children for lunch. A wizard recruits Esmeralda, from the Hoard game, as he knows of her reputation stealing treasure from a dragon and hopes to put her skills to use to benefit the community.
The wizard and Esmeralda set off in opposite directions, collecting glimstones which can be used to ransom snatched children and buy time. When they meet again, if they have the right combination of glimstones, they can perform a spell to banish a troll. They must banish all the trolls to win, but if a player ends their turn and all children have been taken, the players lose.
Players use movement cards to move the characters between the gems; it is possible to plan sequences of movements to get the characters to align again. Before each player's turn, an event card reveals if a child has been snatched or other forest inhabitants, some friend and some foe to the players, have been active that turn.

—description from the publisher

name: In the Blink of a Dragon's Eye
description:
In the Blink of a Dragon's Eye is a heartwarming short story and solo minigame about a human and a dragon that become unlikely brothers in order to survive in their dangerous new reality. The story takes place in the Harbor of Blight universe, a new adventure that blends storytelling, visual art, roleplaying and tabletop gaming in a unique, elementally charged world. In the Blink of a Dragon's Eye is a prequel to the upcoming game, Harbor of Blight, and takes place approximately 5,000 years before the game's events. This is a tale of humans being brought unknowingly to the small, exotic planet of Blight and of how they cope with this dangerous new world. One human in particular, Nibaa, befriends and becomes brothers with one of the few remaining non-feral dragons left in the world, Niijii.

Each of the five chapters of the story has a solo minigame that lets you relive and play through the action from that chapter. Each minigame is one page with everything you need to play right on it. Each of the 5 minigames requires 2 d6 (6-sided dice) and a dry erase marker. The gameplay includes various aspects such as exploring a minimap, gathering and using items, fighting or escaping from a boss, and an Achievement for added difficulty and replayability!

—description from the publisher

name: Harbor of Blight: Obsidian
description:
Harbor of Blight is a standalone game that takes you on a campaign to unravel the mysteries of the exotic world of Blight. You start as a new member of the Hunter's Guild by creating a custom or premade character based on 4 professions, each with 2 unique specialty routes. You battle with a unique skillset that levels up with you from 1-10. Skills replenish via various means such as cooldowns or by sacrificing your Life Force. Your character may also persist into your next playthrough (and future games) with the New Game+ feature.

The core gameplay of each scenario includes a narrative prologue, followed by an Exploration Phase where you search the map via exploration tokens for loot, lay traps, other surprises and your target. The Combat Phase then begins in a fight with 1-3 enemies in a boss battler / dungeon crawler hybrid system. After successfully completing the Combat Phase you continue to the scenario epilogue, completion rewards, and the optional Social Phase in which you can level up friendship levels with your fellow NPCs and unlock other secrets. At the end of each scenario is also when you are allowed to shop with your Barter Points for new gear.

Harbor of Blight is designed for solo or 2 player co-op as an introduction to campaign and RPG gaming for players interested in the genre but don't know where to start, and for existing players to have a new world to explore without the need for finding a large group. The setup is fast via campaign and map books. The learning curve is slight and introduced over the first three scenarios. Embark on an unforgettable experience in Harbor of Blight's unique blend of gameplay, art and lore.

—description from the designer

name: Gnock
description:
Gnock is a family-friendly card game for players ages 6 and up. The game teaches simple addition and subtraction in the fantastical setting of Gnomerheim, the great city of gnomes.

The game is divided into multiple rounds, with a total score tally kept by collecting Gnomish gems between rounds. Become the next Merchant Lord of Gnomerheim by becoming the first to win 5 Gnome tokens in this fast-moving, round-taking game great for adults and kids alike.

A player ‘Gnocks’ under the table or on the floor to announce they have a low point total of 9 points or below in their hand to win the round. After the player has ‘Gnocked,’ the play goes around the table one more time. When the round returns to the ‘Gnocking’ player, the play stops and cards are added together. The other way to win is by a player announcing a military coup to signify they have 50 points in their hand through a combination of 5 Military cards to stop the round immediately and win the round.

But beware! You may activate an instant action when certain cards are played! Will the rules change? Will you have to give your best Gnome dance? Will you have the swap cards with other players? Will a Troll attack?!

—description from the publisher

name: Gnome Liberation Party
description:
