The Gnome Liberation Army (GNA) is an international organization with the sole mission of freeing garden gnomes from captivity for later release into forests far from the human threat. As a member of this organization, your goal is to recover gnomes from ugly patios and place them in the best possible location around the world.

The player who best locate their released gnomes will win the game. In a turn, players must swap, push or rotate tiles to get a pattern of tiles in the patio. Doing so, they free a gnome and get a new objective card which indicates where to locate the gnomes in postcards of beautiful locations of the world.

—description from the publisher

name: Gnomic Parliament
description:
Gnomic Parliament is a cheerful, social, rule-changing game for 4-8 people, ages 10 and up. The playing time is about 45 minutes. Good judgment of other players and bluffing are important game elements.

Each player is a member of the Parliament of Gnomes. The Parliament of Gnomes only works on its own procedures. The President of the Parliament proposes a law that changes these procedures. The law is then voted on. The parliamentarians have varying degrees of influence on whether the change is passed or not. However, they prefer to vote with the majority. This is considered particularly honorable. And honor is the most important thing for them.

Each round, the "President" selects one of several "laws", being cards which have a slight rule change for the game, possibly giving points or extra votes to some of the players.

Then the players discuss and finally vote on this "law", either yes or no, and possibly spending additional votes ("lobby votes"), to increase the chance of the vote going in their favor.

Players who voted with the majority get a point. If the "law" passes it also goes into effect immediately, possibly giving extra points or lobby votes to some players. Some laws have a permanent effect, others only a one-time effect.

At the end of the round, the Presidency possibly passes on to another player.

Each game is very different because there are a lot more law cards in the deck than what can appear in one game.

Any resemblance to reality is purely coincidental.

name: Go F**k Yourself
description:
Be the player with the most completed sets of embarrassing situation cards by the end of the game.   This is an adult version of the classic "Go Fish" game with inappropriate cards like "mismatched boobies" and "an underaged girlfriend".

The point being that when asking if another player has a card, you ask, "Do you have " (ex: Do you have "bad breath").    If the player does, he hands all cards matching that to the asker. If not, he replies "Go Fuck Yourself".

Once a player has a full set of that card type (4 cards), he puts those cards aside and gets a point for completing the set.

name: Go For The Krill
description:
You are a whale.  More accurately, you are a group of Baleen whales and you are hungry for Krill.

In Go For The Krill, 2 - 6 players control a group of whales made up of a hand of cards numbered 1 - 10, a squid card, and a penguin card. Your goal is to play a card each round to consume a school of Plankton (or the more valuable Krill) cards that correspond to the numbered whale card you played. If two or more players play the same number in a single round, the cards are moot and the players gets nothing!

Players place a single whale card in front of them face down.  All whale cards are revealed simultaneously and scored. After 12 rounds, players total the number of Krill and Plankton cards and the player with the most points, wins.

—description from the designer

name: Go Poo! The Game
description:
The grossest game of Go Fish ever! Go Poo The Game is a competitive card game where players collect disgusting cards to take poops and win points. The grosser the poo, the more the points!

Take cards from your competitors or draw from the toilet to build mighty poos but watch out for Diarrhea cards that will lose you points and your turn!

—description from the designer

name: Harbor of Blight: Scenario Zero
description:
Celebrate Founder’s Day in the grand city of Obsidian. Traditionally, residents will hand out “thrices” - three small symbolic gifts. One thrice for someone influential to your past, your present, and your future. However, this year many of the thrices seem to have gone missing! Will you be able to uncover the culprit and prove you’re worthy enough to join the Hunter’s Guild (the protectors of your home town, Obsidian)?

Scenario Zero is a stand alone prequel story leading up to the events of Harbor of Blight: Act I. You will explore the city of Obsidian as you uncover clues in the Exploration Phase, test out your combat prowess in the Combat Phase, discover additional lore and hopefully save Founder’s Day in the Decision Phase! Will you make it to the True Ending?

name: Goblin Laundromat
description:
Dive into a whimsical world where adventurers bring their slimy, grimy, and cursed items to be cleaned by your mischievous goblins. Collect valuable treasures while navigating the risks of handling too much dirty laundry. Will you strike it rich, or will you get burned by a cursed relic? This chaotic game requires a bit of strategy and a lot of luck to determine your success!

In this card game, adventurers bring their slimy and cursed items to be cleaned by your mischievous goblins. Each round, players draft dirty adventuring gear into their own and opponents’ baskets, aiming to maximize valuable combinations without going bust. Weigh card value against stains — will you stop and score, or risk losing everything?

After 4 rounds, cleaned laundry is counted. Personal suit cards score bonus points, but don’t get stuck with mismatched socks!

This family-friendly game takes under 30 minutes to play, with quick setup and easy rules. Luck, strategy, and sharp decision-making are key. Players interact by stuffing baskets, encouraging risky moves, and delighting in opponents’ misfortunes during the tense laundry cycle.

—description from the publisher

name: Gods Heist
description:
Assemble your team, plan your heist, and plunder the ancient city of the Gods!

"Imagine an ancient fantasy world inspired by Babylon and the Olympus. The Gods and humans have lived side by side for thousands of years. One day, the bristling city wakes up and realizes the Gods have all but gone.

A century later... Welcome to the city of Astarion, sitting next to deserted Sanctuary of the Gods, where only their faithful servant, the dangerous Drakonids, remain.
You and your team of Marauders have mustered the courage to explore the Sanctuary in search of the mythical artifacts left by the Gods, promising incredible wealth and power.

It's time for a GODS HEIST!"

Choose your character, assemble your team of experts, and venture into the mysterious and perilous Sanctuary of the Gods. Only the bravest (or cleverest?) will succeed in this heist.

name: GODŌ: The five paths
description:
In a mysterious mountain temple, monks seek enlightenment by mastering five virtues: Kindness, Righteousness, Respect, Wisdom, and Trust. As you journey through the ever-expanding temple grounds, you'll practice virtues to travel paths, gather new insights at intersections, and strive to achieve perfect balance before your rivals.

Players build the temple by placing triangular tiles that create colored paths between intersections. Each player tracks their progress on a personal Path Journal. To move along paths, you must "practice" a virtue by moving its token backward on your Journal - representing that progress requires sacrifice. Once you fully master a virtue, you can move along its paths freely.

At intersections, players collect virtue tokens and encounter special markers: Fox Shrines for exchanging virtues, Stone Lanterns that end movement, and Sacred Gates for teleportation. Players use collected tokens to advance on their Path Journal, working toward mastery of all five virtues.

The game offers strategy through tile placement, path creation, efficient movement, and resource management. 
The first player to master all five virtues wins.

GODŌ also includes a solo mode and a variant play that adds additional abilities.

—description from the publisher

name: Going Knowhere
description:
You stand at the threshold of Knowhere, a place where forgotten and forbidden knowledge is kept sealed. You are a Knowbody, a foreigner to this realm. You came here seeking answers to save your world, carrying a small bag of five Knowstones to guide your journey.

The path to the entrance is guarded by twelve wise beings known as the Knowbles. Only by passing each of their trials and collecting twelve Knowstones in a single run will you be granted temporary access to its secrets.

No one here succeeds at first. Each failure offers insight. Each run brings experience. Return, try again, and grow stronger. In time, you may overcome the trials and uncover the answers you seek.

Going Knowhere is a solo fantasy roguelite game played with a standard pack of cards and a single character progression pamphlet.

Pass Knowble trials, collect Knowstones, and unlock permanent character upgrades across multiple runs to gain entry into Knowhere and uncover the answers you seek.

name: Golden Age of Piracy: 1718
description:
The Golden Age of Piracy - 1718 is an old-school style Tactical level Solitaire board-wargame of action and adventure, with a bit of wargame and RPG elements mixed in. An open-ended sandbox style game where the pirate captain may choose his own path.

Set in the Caribbean Islands during the year 1718, as a pirate captain, you will attempt to build your wealth by attacking merchant ships and selling their goods, by attacking and pillaging towns, kidnapping or assassinating a town governor or his daughter, gambling in a tavern, and by recovering buried treasure from acquired maps.

The player moves his pirate ship's game counter across the Caribbean map, traveling around and searching for merchant ships to take attack, visiting the pirate town of Nassau to buy and sell goods, plus repair the ship. The player may also construct a hidden pirate haven where he may store stolen goods and booty, plus repair his ship at no cost.

The ultimate goal of the game is to save up enough booty in order to buy your pardon before the Royal Navy invades Nassau. Will you succeed, or be hanged for piracy?

—description from the designer

name: Golden Annual Number 3: Great War at Sea – South Seas Mandate
description:
Great War at Sea: South Seas Mandate is based on what US Navy planners foresaw as the opening stages of War Plan Orange, the plan for a Pacific naval war against Japan. It is set in the years just after the First World War and features ships planned but never built: the American Design 150 battle cruiser, the Japanese Type X light battlecruiser, the original design for Japan’s Furutaka-class light cruiser and more.

Great War at Sea: South Seas Mandate includes 50 die-cut and silky-smooth playing pieces, thirty double-sized “long” ship pieces and 20 standard-sized square ones. There’s a 22x17-inch map (on heavy rigid stock), and a booklet with ten scenarios and the background story of the campaign.

-description from publisher's website

name: Goldorak XperienZ: Le jeu
description:
The Earth is threatened by the Forces of Vega, led by the Grand Strategist, who is determined to seize its riches and eliminate the human race...
But one man stands in their way: Actarus, who, at the controls of the giant robot Goldorak, manages to repel the powerful Golgoths.
He can also count on the help of the Eagle Patrol, the unbeatable trio formed by Alcor, Venusia, and Phénicia!

Goldorak XperienZ is a cooperative family game that lets you relive the adventures of Goldorak and his allies.

In France and Italy, Grendizer is called Goldorak or Goldrake.

—description from the designer

name: Golem Run
publisher: Dragon Dawn Productions; Dragon Dawn Games
description:
Golem Run is a competitive betting and race-fixing game with a trick-taking mechanic. The game is set in the dwarven society of Odrixia, the same world as Justice and Factory 42. Players represent the cheering crowds who are participating in the popular Odrixian pastime of Golem Run.

The game is played over several hands of tricks. The player who wins the trick must move the Golem(s) used to win. Players can choose not to  play any cards at all by using the "Wait and Wager" action that allows you to change your bets and not participate in the trick-taking round.

You continue playing tricks until one player runs out of cards and then proceed to score. If the Golems have not reached the finish line, deal a new hand and continue. The game ends when a Golem crosses the finish line, and then there will be final scoring. The player with the highest point total wins.

The Golems race across an obstacle strewn course, built in modular pieces by the players beforehand.

name: Good & Evil
description:
Not all wars end, nor do the good guys always win. There are eternal battles where sometimes the bad guys win. Good versus evil is one of these endless confrontations... until today:
The day when you can put an end to this endless bickering, or let it continue again and again until the end of time.
Good & Evil is a simple and fun, fast-paced card game in which 2 players choose a side—Angel or Devil—to play against each other. The goal is to capture as many enemies in their cages as possible.

name: Guardians of the Four Winds
description:
Set in the word of Quincy's Tavern, this is a strategy card game where you place cards from your hand to complete patterns as you compete to place all player tokens first.

Players set up for the game by selecting one of four factions (The Gryphon Watch, The Phoenix Menage, The Dragon Synod or They Kitsune Conclave) and taking all of the related tokens, seals, and player mat. Next the cross-roads tile is placed in the middle of the play area in front of all players and becomes the game board. Five cards are then dealt to everyone and the remainder of the cards are set to the side with four more cards being drawn and laid face up for all to see.

A turn consists of four actions. Action one, is playing two cards from your hand off of the cross roads tile. You can place a card over a matching tile or over a tile it is superior too (Gryphons cover Phoenixes, Phoenixes cover Dragons, Dragons cover Kitsune, and Kitsune cover Gryohons similarly rock-paper-scissors). Action two, check to see if you have created a spirit guardian pattern that matches a pattern on your player mat. If you have, you place one of your faction tokens on any tile in that pattern thus claiming it. Action three, place your seal tokens on the board. This seal depending on which side you place face up will change a tile it is placed on to the face of the seal you placed on it. Lastly you replenish your hand by taking two more cards either from the cards that are face up or from the deck.

Each player takes their turn completing all four actions in clockwise order until there is a winner. The game is won when a player has placed all faction tokens on the game board.

name: Good Fortune
description:
In this subtle duel, anticipate your opponent's moves, connect the right symbols, and collect lucky charms to increase your chances of winning!

The duelists have 9 tiles each. Each turn, they will play one tile each to try to connect it to the central tiles in order to win and collect charms that will earn them points at the end of the game.

Be careful! The more identical charms you collect, the more points you earn. In this game, luck is not a matter of chance.

name: Leviathans: The Great War
description:
Leviathans is a tabletop miniatures game that uses the innovative modular dice system of color-coded dice and easy-to-read physical record-keeping cards that allow for quick and easy play while retaining the depth of strategy that will encourage repeat play.

This expands on the original edition, adding new abilities, ships and factions past what was in the original edition, while advancing the timeline directly into the The Great War era.

Each game centers around moving our pre-painted miniatures across a hex board, trying to out-maneuver your opponent. Players will fire various weapons at each other's ships until either an objective is completed or the enemy falls from the sky. The base game comes with German and French fleets, additional Fleets are planned.

Leviathans prides itself as a game that is easy-to-learn, while having a large amount of tactics and replayability.

—description from the publisher

name: Gooooal!!!
description:
Gooooal!!! is an exciting, fast-paced dice chucking football game. The team that scores the most goals during a regular 8 minute match, will emerge as the champion!
Decide if you will play defensively or if you will attack... and place your figurines on the field accordingly. Try to keep control over the ball by rolling the number of your midfielders. Attempt to score a goal by rolling the number of your wing players or even better: your striker.
Scoring is done in a heartbeat by using one of the 3 Gooooal!!! cards. Kick the ball in one of the three available directions: right, left or center. If your rival defends in the wrong direction with his own 3 available Keeper cards, YOU score a Gooooal!!!
If there is a tie at the end of a match, then be prepared for 2 minutes of extra time or even nail-biting penalty shoot-outs!     
        
—description from the publisher

name: Gorbino's Quest
description:
Gorbino's Quest is a strategy game of economic development and civilization building in a fantasy setting for 2-6 players aged 13 and up.

Inspired by Concordia (2013), Mosaic: A Story of Civilization (2022), and Brass: Lancashire (2007); Gorbino's Quest combines the elements of tag collecting, hand management, resource management, income, loans, market, investments, resource production and area control. GQ is an action-selection game. Actions include:

Loan
Lose income, but gain Coins

Production
Produce resources at the province of your choice

Trade
Buy and sell up to two different resource types

Development
Purchase Technology cards that contain tags as well as upgraded actions

Reset
Place all your discarded cards back into your hand and gain income

Build
Build new cities and gain income

Treachery
Steal resources, buy resources at a low cost, or take the actions of other players

Choosing a wise sequence of actions will have the player gain their desired income, actions, resource production, cities and tags.

Each Round
After all players have taken their turns, do the following:

1. Advance Technology Track: Discard the rightmost technology card from the track and shift all remaining cards to the right.
2. Income: Gain or pay coins based on the income tracker.
3. Rotate First Player Marker: Rotate it clockwise; that player starts the next turn.

Scoring
Game ends when no cards remain on the Technology Track

Score calculated by how many 'tags' players have
And by using the scoring section of the board. An example would be pink tags x number of cities.

—description from the designer

name: Got What It Bakes?
description:
The first edition of Got what it bakes/Van sütnivalód? is being produced in Hungarian, and is currently in manufacturing.
If there is sufficient international interest, an English-language edition may be published in the future.

Van sütnivalód? = Got What It Bakes?  is a thematic, strategy-driven board game for 1–4 players, where everyone steps into the oven-warmed shoes of a passionate artisan baker. Across three intense and flavorful rounds, you’ll gather ingredients, manage your time and resources, and bake delicious recipes to earn points — all while balancing the unpredictability of dice rolls and the satisfaction of strategic planning.

Theme & Story

The game is inspired by the world of home baking, especially the renewed love for sourdough and pastry-making that blossomed during the COVID era. Each player runs their own cozy bakery, starting from scratch with just a little time, a few coins, and a handful of recipes. As you bake more and invest in your kitchen, your bakery grows into a well-oiled oven of efficiency and creativity.

Your sourdough starter is alive. The timer is ticking. Customers are hungry. Will you bake it now?

Core Gameplay Mechanics

Draft & Write Mechanism: This is a “roll & write” style game with a twist: instead of simply rolling dice, you draft them from shared pools. Each die you take influences which ingredients you collect, and how you proceed with your recipes.

Resource Management: Players must manage two core resources — Time and Money — along with a supply of ingredients. Baking requires careful planning, and sometimes even improvisation under pressure.

Recipe Fulfillment: Each round, you’ll select and fulfill sweet or savory recipes, using dice to collect ingredients and choosing whether to spend time or gamble with a risk roll to bake under pressure (via the “Bake It Now!” action).

Upgrades & Refreshers: Permanent kitchen upgrades (like a Mixer or Dough Board) and single-use refreshers (like an Iced Coffee) allow players to manipulate dice, earn bonuses, or gain extra resources — adding layers of strategy and engine-building potential.

Multiple Game Modes:

Solo Mode: Beat score thresholds and complete challenges alone.

Competitive Mode: Secret goal cards drive each player’s unique scoring strategy.

Cooperative Mode: Shared objectives require teamwork, donations, and planning — but everyone wins or loses together.

Strategic Depth

While luck plays a role through dice rolls and card draws, Got What It Bakes? is a highly tactical game that rewards efficiency, foresight, and adaptive thinking. Key strategic choices include:

- Choosing when to spend time vs. risking a rushed bake

- Managing leftover ingredients in your pantry for later turns

- Deciding when to invest in upgrades and which refreshers to buy

- Timing your baking and maximizing recipe points within only 3 rounds

What Makes It Unique

Deeply Thematic Experience: From the use of real recipe types to the inclusion of time-pressure decisions that mimic real kitchen stress, the game immerses players in the baking process both narratively and mechanically.

Tight, Replayable Structure: With only 3 rounds and fast-paced turns, the game stays engaging and easy to replay, especially with different player counts and modes.

Creative Visual Design: The game’s charming illustrations and clear iconography help communicate rules intuitively, even to younger or newer players.

Customizable Difficulty: The game includes multiple difficulty settings and optional simplified modes for children or casual players, making it family-friendly while still challenging for strategists.

Van sütnivalód? = Schlau gebacken! ist ein thematisches, strategieorientiertes Brettspiel für 1–4 Spieler, in dem alle in die ofenwarmen Schuhe eines leidenschaftlichen Bäckermeisters schlüpfen. Über drei intensive, geschmackvolle Runden hinweg sammelt ihr Zutaten, verwaltet Zeit und Ressourcen und backt köstliche Rezepte, um Siegpunkte zu erzielen – stets im Spannungsfeld zwischen dem Zufall der Würfel und der Genugtuung cleverer Planung.

Thema & Geschichte

Das Spiel ist inspiriert von der Welt des Heimbackens, insbesondere von der wiederentdeckten Liebe zu Sauerteig und Gebäck während der COVID-Zeit. Jeder Spieler betreibt seine eigene gemütliche Bäckerei, beginnt mit wenig Zeit, ein paar Münzen und einigen Rezepten. Mit jedem gelungenen Backwerk und jeder Investition wächst die kleine Backstube zu einer effizienten, kreativen Backwerkstatt heran.

Dein Sauerteigstarter lebt. Die Uhr tickt. Die Kunden sind hungrig. Wirst du jetzt backen?

Zentrale Spielmechanismen

Draft & Write-Mechanismus: Ein „Roll & Write“ mit Twist – statt nur zu würfeln, draftet ihr Würfel aus einem gemeinsamen Pool. Jeder gewählte Würfel bestimmt, welche Zutaten ihr erhaltet und wie ihr eure Rezepte voranbringt.

Ressourcenmanagement: Spieler verwalten zwei Kernressourcen – Zeit und Geld – sowie ihre Vorräte an Zutaten. Backen erfordert Planung und manchmal Improvisation unter Druck.

Rezept-Erfüllung: In jeder Runde wählt und erfüllt ihr süße oder herzhafte Rezepte. Mit Würfeln sammelt ihr Zutaten und entscheidet, ob ihr Zeit investiert oder das Risiko eines Eilbackens eingeht.

Upgrades & Erfrischer: Dauerhafte Küchenhilfen (wie Mixer oder Teigbrett) und einmalige Erfrischungen (wie Eiskaffee) erlauben das Modifizieren von Würfeln, Boni oder Extraressourcen – und bringen strategische Tiefe sowie Engine-Building ins Spiel.

Spielmodi

Solo: Punkteschwellen knacken und Herausforderungen allein meistern.

Kompetitiv: Geheime Zielkarten treiben individuelle Strategien voran.

Kooperativ: Gemeinsame Ziele erfordern Teamarbeit, Spenden und Planung – alle gewinnen oder verlieren zusammen.

Strategische Tiefe

Obwohl Würfelglück und Kartenziehen eine Rolle spielen, ist Schlau gebacken! ein taktisches Spiel, das Effizienz, Voraussicht und Anpassungsfähigkeit belohnt. Zentrale Entscheidungen:

Wann investiere ich Zeit vs. wann riskiere ich ein Eilbacken?

Welche Zutaten lagere ich für spätere Züge ein?

Wann lohnt sich ein Upgrade, wann ein Erfrischer?

Wie maximiere ich meine Punkte in nur 3 Runden?

Was das Spiel einzigartig macht

Starkes Thema: Echte Rezeptarten und Zeitdruckentscheidungen spiegeln die Backrealität wider – sowohl narrativ als auch mechanisch.

Kompakt & Wiederspielbar: Nur 3 Runden, schnelle Züge, hohe Spannung – ideal für verschiedene Spielerzahlen und Modi.

Visuelles Design: Charmante Illustrationen und klare Symbolik machen die Regeln intuitiv erfassbar – auch für jüngere Spieler.

Anpassbarer Schwierigkeitsgrad: Mit verschiedenen Levels und vereinfachten Modi bleibt das Spiel familienfreundlich, ohne strategische Spieler zu unterfordern.

Van sütnivalód?
A „Van sütnivalód?” három fordulón át tartó, pörgős stratégiai társasjáték, ahol minden játékos egy lelkes pékmestert alakít. A játék elején célkártyát és süteményrecepteket választasz, majd fordulóról fordulóra hozzávalókat gyűjtesz kockadobással, vásárlással és ügyes tervezéssel. Ezután jöhet a sütés: ha van elég időd, biztos kézzel dolgozhatsz, de ha szorít az idő, kockázatot kell vállalnod – és a végeredmény nem mindig garantált. Bár a játékban jelen van a szerencsefaktor, a kockadobásokat különféle fejlesztésekkel és akciókkal aktívan befolyásolhatod, így a siker leginkább a jó döntéseken múlik. A kész finomságokat eladhatod, fejlesztheted a konyhádat, és új recepteket is szerezhetsz, hogy a következő körökben még hatékonyabb legyél. Vigyázz: ha túl sok mindent akarsz egyszerre, a süti könnyen a szemetesben landol! A játék végén a győzelmi pontok döntik el, ki volt a legügyesebb – szólóban, versengve vagy kooperatív módban, közösen célokat teljesítve.

A játék, amiben a nyersanyaggyűjtés, a dobsz és írsz mechanizmus kockadraftolással és szettgyűjtéssel párosul. Emellett a zsebpénz és a szabadidő helyes beosztása is kihívást jelenthet, míg a fejlesztésekkel járó jutalmak is pikantériát adnak a játékmenet közbeni tervezésnek.

—description from publisher

name: Grab Bag: Jungle
description:
Embark on a thrilling jungle adventure with friends and family in this immersive animal rescue game!

Together, you'll race against the clock to save jungle animals by reaching into the Grab Bag, feeling for the right animal, and placing it on its matching habitat card. With 8 unique challenge modes, there's a perfect game for every skill level.

Includes 24 beautifully shaped wooden animals, 12 habitat cards, 4 challenge cards, 2 timer cards, a sand timer, and instructions to guide your journey. Let the animal rescue mission begin!

—description from the publisher

name: Shadowrun: Takedown
description:
In the board game Shadowrun: Takedown, you and your friends assume the roles of runners, serving as mercenaries and deniable assets for powerful megacorporations. The corps have hired you and your crew to handle the covert tasks they prefer not to have on their official payroll. Engage in these missions, survive, and strive to achieve legendary status with 1-4 players per copy of the game.

Over the course of the campaign, players will have the opportunity to evolve their runners to fit their play styles, whether they're hacking, sneaking, or brawling. Players can gain gear to augment their abilities or enhance their bodies through integrated cyberware and magical upgrades. The game offers a range of balanced character and gear advancements, allowing characters to develop over the course of a progressively challenging campaign.

Players select their roles, each providing unique stats that influence the gameplay for all characters. This game introduces the Mastermind role, the runner who keeps an eye on it all, seeing things the others can't. The Mastermind can grant special bonuses to players during missions, along with their own role-specific benefits.

—description from the publisher

name: Keep the Faith
description:
Keep the Faith is a storytelling game about a religion in transition. Elements of role-playing and board gaming combine to make an experience that is designed to welcome new players and create a story together.
 During the game, you play cards and narrate short stories to describe how the practices and trappings of the Faith express different (and at times contradictory) beliefs: What does your religious music sound like if it's demonstrating your commitment to welcoming the outsider, as opposed to your desire to wield power? What does your altar look like if it's an altar for keeping secrets as opposed to spreading the word?

External pressures and tensions within the Faith will cause your beliefs to shift — and might even drive the Faith to fracture and fall into irrelevance. When the era deck empties, you compare the number of aspect cards on orthodox values versus schismatic values to determine the Faith's outcome.

Keep the Faith is an approachable storytelling game about an often-fraught topic, designed to create compelling narratives and spark discussions between players.

name: Gloomhaven (Second Edition)
description:
Gloomhaven: Second Edition is a revised and elevated version of the core game of Gloomhaven. This is the culmination of everything we have learned since the initial release of Gloomhaven, including feedback from the community, playtesters, co-designers, and developers.

The world, story, and challenging gameplay are all still the same, but there is a plethora of additional content to explore. Even for those who have played Gloomhaven before, this edition brings new material to the table, with rebalanced and redesigned mercenary classes, items, and scenarios, as well as brand new artwork, newly written narrative and events, updated miniatures, a new faction-based reputation system, and more.

—description from the publisher

name: Miskatonic Tales: Journey to Innsmouth
description:
Miskatonic Tales: Journey to Innsmouth is an immersive, storytelling board game that transports you into the realm of the Cthulhu Mythos and confronts you with forbidden knowledge waiting impatiently to be uncovered. Unsure of who your actual enemy is, you must investigate a chain of events in a mysterious place fate has brought you to. Fortunately, other Investigators are with you and together you can solve this case.

Miskatonic Tales: Journey to Innsmouth is set in the universe known from the award-winning Call of Cthulhu horror and mystery TTRPG. The box contains three stand-alone sandbox adventures that can be played separately, yet share one large story arc. This cooperative game does not have a strict turn order, but emphasizes solving the case together as a group. Every move you make while exploring the map is accompanied by a paragraph from the book that reveals yet another piece of your story. Each time you play, the story can be different, and trying to solve the scenario several times eventually reveals the full picture.

Combining strategy, storytelling, and cooperation, the game offers an engaging experience where choices matter, teamwork is crucial, and the story's path is as unpredictable as it is thrilling.

Learn more about the Mythos by taking part in intriguing adventures. What role will you play in the story? Investigate the clues. Uncover the truth. Explore the story.

name: Granfondo: Tempo, Taktik, Kettenfett
description:
Granfondo is a tactical cycling board game about positioning, timing, and team coordination in a road race. Each player controls a team of three riders — a Sprinter, Climber, and Rouleur — racing across tracks with flats, climbs, and descents.

The goal is to finish the race in the best possible positions and score the most points based on final placements.

Movement is card-driven. For each rider, players secretly select a movement card. Riders then move in order based on their current positions in the race. Card values determine movement distance, while terrain, drafting, and tactical options influence the final result.

Different terrain types affect riders in specific ways. Climbs limit movement depending on rider type, descents allow faster movement, and curves may impose positioning penalties. Feed zones restore stamina, while obstacles can trigger performance checks.

Each rider has performance points, representing stamina and tactical flexibility. These points determine hand size and can be gained through teamwork, feed zones, or coordinated moves such as the Belgian Rotation, while crashes, obstacles, or difficult terrain may reduce them.

Players can use several tactical options during the race, including multi-card sprints, slipstreaming behind other riders, positional battles for contested spaces, and coordinated team movement. Risky doping cards may provide temporary advantages but can lead to disqualification during the post-race doping control.

When riders cross the finish line, the round is completed and final placement is determined by distance beyond the line. The top three riders are tested for doping, and final points (15–1) determine the winner.

Optional modules introduce additional tactical elements such as crashes, intermediate sprints, rider drafting, team-based Race Alliance play, and Automa opponents for solo or smaller player counts.

The New Challengers expansion increases the player count to six, adds additional race tracks, and introduces the Legends of Granfondo tournament mode.

name: Grasse (Second Edition)
description:
Grasse, southern France, 17th century. This small village has always had its main economic activity in producing leather goods, which were exported to other places. Although the products from the small village had a good reputation, the characteristic smell of leather was not pleasing to the nobility, who wore gloves made of this material. To please the nobles, the first perfumer from Grasse created perfumed leather gloves and presented them to Catherine de Médicis, who was delighted with the gift. The perfumed gloves became fashionable throughout the court. However, at that time, the leather industry began to decline in Grasse, making way for perfumery, which led the city to become known as the world capital of perfume.

In this game, you will take on the role of a master perfumer from the small French town of Grasse, known as the world capital of perfume. To do this, you must collect resources (bases and essences), produce classic or avant-garde perfumes, and export and sell them. All your skills will be rewarded, whether as the most versatile producer, the most specialized, the one with the most refined technique, or the best seller. But there are opportunities outside Grasse: many export contracts will be available for ambitious players. At the end of the game, the player with the most points will be the winner.

name: Horror on the Orient Express: The Board Game
description:
Horror on the Orient Express: The Board Game lures you into the luxurious Orient Express in the 1920s, taking you on a dangerous train ride into the realm of the Dreamlands. Everything is against you, from monsters attacking the train to murderous cults hiding among the passengers. Worst of all, an eldritch, blood-thirsty vampire hunting down everything that moves. Horror on the Orient Express: The Board Game brings the Call of Cthulhu horror and mystery TTRPG into the board gaming world. Special rules, ongoing character development, and  play pieces provide a challenging and exciting gaming experience.

In this cooperative game, you and the other investigators try to survive on the doomed train. To win, you must hunt out the cultists to stop them from performing a hideous ritual and ensure the train reaches its destination. Each of you controls a character who can develop new skills, gather items, talk to the passengers, discover clues, and, ultimately, decide the train's fate. You may even learn a spell or two!

—description from the publisher

name: Great War at Sea: Far Side of the World
description:
In the summer of 1914, Germany’s East Asia cruiser squadron’s superbly trained crews of long-service professionals made Admiral Maximilian Graf von Spee's small fleet the envy of the China station. But when war broke out, this tiny force found itself far from home and threatened by the powerful Imperial Japanese Navy, many times the size of the German squadron. Spee decided to force his way home around the world. After an epic journey across the Pacific, his cruisers met their end off of the Falkland Islands in a final battle.

Far Side of the World gives the Great War at Sea series its greatest scope yet: the entire world. British, German, Japanese, Italian, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Dutch ships begin as they did in August 1914. The German player must disrupt Allied commerce and try to get the cruisers home if at all possible. The Allied player must track them down and destroy them before they can wreak havoc.

Far Side of the World’s map divides the world into sea areas, with modified search rules allowing German and Austrian ships to look for prey, and Allied ships to hunt them. Once contact is made, combat is resolved using the standard game rules. Itcomes in our popular Playbook format with a completely new set of 300 playing pieces (180 double-sized ship pieces and 120 square ones, all of them die cut and silky-smooth, with all-new artwork), a new map, new full-color play aids, and an all-new book with revised rules and scenarios, additional scenarios plus historical background.

Far Side of the World’s game play based on the Great War at Sea Second Edition rules: the first new, re-written set of series rules in more than 25 years! Far Side of the World is a complete game: everything you need to play (except dice) is included in the Playbook. Far Side of the World is a thoroughly re-imagined edition of our old Cruiser Warfare game.

—description from the publisher

name: Great Western Trail: El Paso
publisher: Lookout Games; Arclight Games; Delta Vision Publishing; Ediciones MasQueOca; Rebel Sp. z o.o.; Zvezda
description:
El Paso at the end of the 19th century: Five railroad companies have connected the Sun City to their network and made it a major hub for the cattle trade. Ranchers from the surrounding parts of Texas and Mexico drive their cattle into the city to send them on their long journey to the north, east, and west of the United States.

In Great Western Trail: El Paso, you take on the role of the ranchers of that time and bring your best cattle to El Paso to earn money and victory points. Hire more cowboys, builders, and engineers to get closer to your goals:


     Buy cattle to increase the value of your herd!
     Construct buildings to unlock more actions!
     Participate in the expansion of the railroad and secure the most attractive contracts!


El Paso is mechanically based on its predecessors in the Great Western Trail trilogy. It can serve as an introduction to the series and is the perfect game for game nights when there is not enough time for its big brothers!

—description from the publisher

name: Grifoni: Blades for Hire
description:
Grifoni: Blades for Hire is a competitive eurogame for 1–4 players that blends worker placement, resource management, and branching narrative.

Each player assumes the role of a commander in the legendary Grifoni Company, guiding their mercenary band through the bustling markets, backroom deals, and perilous missions of Renaissance Italy. Over a series of Acts, the game alternates between a story phase, using the Book of Adventures to present narrative choices that influence future events, and a management phase, where players recruit mercenaries, obtain equipment, and assign missions.

A unique Glory/Supremacy system rewards different playstyles: pursue honor and prestige through noble deeds, or enforce your will through ruthless tactics, unlocking distinct objectives and rewards.

At the end of the game, the commander with the most Victory Points earns renown as the most influential leader of the Company — but their choices will determine whether they are remembered as a hero or feared as a tyrant.

Be Social To Be Solo (Social Stretch Goal)

All tasks have been completed and the mission accomplished; thanks to you, Captains, Solo Mode is officially unlocked!
Now, Grifoni – Blades for Hire (Kickstarter Edition) is a game for 1–4 players, ready to challenge even the most solitary captains.

—description from the publisher

name: Grimcoven
description:
Grimcoven is a miniature boss battler game for set in a dark Victorian universe where only the hunt matters.

To play, you take on the role of a hunter fueled by lament who has signed a pact with a coven of other hunters to venture on one of many modular boss battles. Every character has a distinct development tree you can use to advance. Build and execute your unique combo, such as teleporting into any space on the map, gathering lament, gaining extra dice, and firing up a devastating attack on the boss. Sometimes a special electricity die will help you power up your armor, while at other times, you will forge magical bullets to be fired at the right moment.

Who and where are you fighting? Each game you choose from multiple arenas, bosses, elites, and possible adventures. Every game is different and exciting. Instead of following a scripted campaign, dive right into a boss battle for an intense 2-3 hour gameplay session. Every boss offers a unique gameplay challenge, and bringing them down will be tactically demanding. You must work together and take full advantage of the arena and its resources to achieve your goal.

During combat, strategically use dice allocation to move around the board, fire up different combos, and gather lament to grow in strength. Build your character in roguelike fashion and try to claim the ultimate prize. Collect too much lament, however, and you may turn into one of the beasts you were sent to hunt, with your fellow hunters unable to help you in time!

name: Grimgrove
description:
Grimgrove is a challenging, solo board game where you must survive the perils of a cursed forest. As you explore, you'll face dangerous creatures, overcome obstacles, and manage your resources of time, health, food, and energy. Your ultimate goal is to escape the forest by finding a special exit card before succumbing to its dangers.

Key Features:

Dynamic Exploration: Every playthrough offers a unique experience as you uncover new locations and face unexpected challenges.

Strategic Resource Management: Balance your time, health, food, and energy to survive the harsh conditions.

Intense Atmosphere: Immerse yourself in a dark and foreboding world filled with danger and uncertainty.

Solitary Challenge: Test your wits and skills in this challenging solo adventure using Trick-Taking-like thinking.

—description from the publisher

name: Grizzy & les Lemmings
description:
Dive into the hilarious and explosive world of Grizzy and the Lemmings!

Play as the Lemmings with your friends, to snatch food, right under Grizzy’s nose. Pick your Lemming, roll, and split the dice. Collect food, and enjoy the bonus spaces !
Avoid Grizzy : If he catches you, he takes back some of his food. If your pantry is full, help the other Lemmings, to win, all together, before the Ranger arrives !

Gameplay steps:

     Roll the dice and move: Distribute the dice and move your Lemming to the corresponding space to collect food.
     Gather food and enjoy bonuses: Bonus spaces let you play again or directly choose an item for your pantry.
     Evade Grizzy: The final die determines how far Grizzy moves, based on the card drawn. If he catches a Lemming, that Lemming loses some of its food.
     Win together: Once your pantry is full, help the other Lemmings so everyone wins before the Ranger arrives.


Join forces: Fill your pantries together before the Ranger spoils the fun. Remember, teamwork is the key to victory!

—description from the publisher

Plongez dans l’univers hilarant et explosif de Grizzy et les Lemmings !

Incarnez les Lemmings et chapardez la nourriture sous le nez de Grizzy tout en esquivant ses tentatives pour vous rattraper. Coopérez pour remplir vos garde-mangers avant que Grizzy ne reprenne le dessus et que le Ranger ne signe la fin de vos aventures !

Étapes de jeu :

     Lancez les dés et avancez : Répartissez-vous les dés et déplacez votre Lemming sur la case correspondante pour collecter des aliments.
     Récoltez la nourriture et profitez des bonus : Les cases bonus vous permettent de rejouer ou de choisir directement un aliment pour votre garde-manger.
     Esquivez Grizzy : Le dernier dé fait avancer Grizzy selon la carte tirée. S’il rattrape un Lemming, celui-ci perd une partie de sa nourriture.
     Gagnez ensemble : Une fois votre garde-manger plein, aidez vos coéquipiers pour tous gagner avant l’arrivée du Ranger.


Unissez vos forces : Remplissez vos garde-mangers ensemble avant que le Ranger ne vienne gâcher la fête. Attention, la coopération est la clé de la victoire !

—description from the publisher (French)

name: Growing Grounds
description:
Growing Grounds is a chill yet strategic roll & write, print & play game where you cultivate a mysterious plant on a forgotten island.

Using dice to grow stems, add leaves, and bloom flowers, you'll unlock bonuses, connect with insects, and complete different goals — all while telling your story of growth and discovery.

With simple mechanics, solo and multiplayer modes, and a relaxing theme, Growing Grounds offers a thoughtful, replayable experience.

—description from the designer

name: GrumbleStone
description:
Grumble and smash your way to victory in this whimsically clever polyomino placement game for 1-4 grumpy golems.

RULES AT A GLANCE:

TUMBLE- roll both dice and assign
RUMBLE- activate symbols in the row and column
GRUMBLE- buy polyominoes and enhance your grid

And whatever you do, try not to CRUMBLE…

FEATURES:

• EPIC NEOPRENE player mat (see images).

• Four ASYMMETRIC GOLEMS- each with a unique starting grid, health, and wealth, and each with unlockable powers and superpowers.

• 40 chipboard POLYOMINOES that you can strategically puzzle-piece them onto your 6x6 grid to maximize future turns.

• 4 SYMBOLS on your grid: collect grumbles, heal yourself, attack a rival golem, or protect yourself from attacks.

The last Golem standing wins the game and becomes "King of the Mountains"...

-description from designer

name: Grunlings: Fantastic Fruit
description:
In Grunling: Fantastic Fruits, players take turns building the most valuable set of Grunlings, each with unique scoring methods. Many Grunlings prefer to be collected in sets, and some sets are modular, varying from game to game to keep things fresh. Each turn presents tactical choices, from playing Action cards and managing your Fruit Basket to drawing new cards, with a memory element adding strategic depth. Watch out for the ever-shifting Nature Effects, which change in order and type every game and often wreak havoc, and the mysterious Darklings, who limit your discard options.

On your turn, you can play Action cards, manage your Basket by storing or swapping cards, and draw new cards from Draw and Discard piles. If your hand and Basket exceed the card limit, you’ll need to discard tactically. Leaf tokens can be acquired and spent to discard extra cards, giving you more control over your strategy.

The game ends when the final Effect card is triggered. Players then reveal their cards and tally points. The player with the highest score wins.

—description from the designer

name: Guacamole
description:
PapaDrino has invited the most eccentric characters from the gastronomic world to compete in an exciting battle of flavors! Gathered around the table, Lima Kahlo, Onion Musk, Tomathor, Ají Styles, and the siblings Paltricia and Aguacaldo prepare their ingredients, combining them into unique and flavorful dishes.

On each turn, you can play an ingredient card from your hand to the table in front of you (your preparation zone) to activate its ability and/or form groups of three or more ingredient cards (dishes). Dishes can be made using cards from your hand, your preparation zone, or by grouping ingredients of the same type, number, or in numerical sequence.

When a player draws the last ingredient card from the draw pile, the end of the game is triggered. The player with the most victory points from their dishes, ingredients, and especially for successfully making GUACAMOLE dishes, wins the game!

—description from the publisher (translated)

PapaDrino ha invitado a los personajes más excéntricos del mundo gastronómico a competir en una emocionante batalla de sabores. Reunidos alrededor de la mesa, Lima Kahlo, Onion Musk, Tomathor, Ají Styles y los hermanos Paltricia y Aguacaldo preparan sus ingredientes, combinándolos en platos con sabores únicos.

En cada turno, podrás jugar una carta de ingrediente desde tu mano a la mesa frente a ti (zona de preparación) para activar su habilidad y/o formar grupos de 3 o más cartas de ingredientes (platos). Los platos pueden armarse con cartas de tu mano, de tu zona de preparación o con ingredientes del mismo tipo, número o en secuencia numérica.

Cuando un jugador roba la última carta de ingrediente del mazo de robo, se activa el final de la partida. Gana quien consiga más puntos de victoria por sus platos, ingredientes y, en especial, por lograr armar platos de GUACAMOLE.

—description from the publisher

name: Guadalcanal Diary
description:
Japan attacked the Allied powers on 7 December 1941 and ran rampant across the Pacific Ocean and Asia for six months. But in August of 1942, the Allies would finally strike back. On 7 August, ships appeared off the coast of a small island in the Solomons called Guadalcanal to disgorge troops of the United States Marine Corps. Guadalcanal Diary: The Battle for Henderson Field allows you to recreate the Guadalcanal campaign from the initial landings in August 1942 until the end of November, when the Japanese were all but finished.

You have command of all the major units that fought in the campaign across ground, sea, and air.  As the Allied player, you have everything that can be cobbled together to take the airfield on Guadalcanal and hold it. You need to maximize force but be cautious enough to withhold forces to fend off the Japanese counterattacks. As the Japanese player, you must use what forces you have to defeat the Allies before they become too powerful.

Guadalcanal Diary is the first in a series of games that will cover at a tactical and operational level the fight for the Southwest Pacific Area. This game covers the initial Allied landings on Guadalcanal until the end of November 1942, when effective resistance by the Japanese ended. Tactical combat on the ground can be combined with operational-level combat in the air and on the seas to make a comprehensive simulation of the Guadalcanal campaign.

Product Information:

Complexity: High
Solitaire Suitability: Medium
Players: 2
Playing Time: 2-40+ Hours
Map Scale: 300 yards per hex (Abstract on Operational Map)
Time Scale: Variable, 1 turn = 4 hours or 1 day
Unit Scale: Platoons and Companies

name: Guadalcanal: The Battle for Henderson Field, Oct 23-26 1942
description: Take command of the valiant Marines of the 1st Marine Division, supported by Soldiers of the 164th Infantry Regiment, desperately defending Henderson Field against waves of Japanese troops.

name: Doom Cat
description:
You're a young witch learning the ropes of magic. Unfortunately, your mischievous cat found your spell book and summoned demons!

In Doom Cat, you must learn how to draw sigils. You start with 2 magic circle pages filled with numbered candles. Roll 3 dice and draw a line between 2 of the candles matching two of the dice. The cat steals the other die and knocks over a matching candle, making it unusable in future rounds. The game ends after 14 rounds. Highest score wins. Solo players must score 70 or more points per sigil card to win.

Doom Cat comes with many goal cards that immerse you deeper into the world of sigil magic. Shuffle and play with a few random ones, or play them in order, progressively increasing the difficulty. Each scoring criteria incentivizes emergent beauty, giving each player a unique sigil each time!

—description from the publisher

name: Guards of Traitor's Toll
Otter
description:
In Otter, players race to play all their cards first by putting adorable critters on otter tummies.
But Otter is a racing game that teaches patience, and a shedding game where drawing cards gives benefits, and a cute game that will make you think.

🦦Gameplay: There are three otters to play on. Each otter has a rule about numbers on its head and a rule about suits on its tail. You must follow at least one rule to play on the otter, but if you follow both, you may play on that otter again until you only follow one rule. This can lead to some epic turns!

🦦The twist: You can draw cards to flip or swap heads or tails before you play to change that otter's rules. Drawing helps you play bigger combos, but also might give you cards you can't play this turn.

🦦The final touch: Players keep cards they didn't play between rounds, and then draw until they have 10 cards. So if you have a big combo (many cards in the same suit), you are incentivized to hold on to those cards as long as possible unless you think you can play your entire hand during the current round. If you play your combos too early and someone else goes out first, you lose your headstart for the next round. It's fun to play fast, but the strategy lies in knowing when to play fast, when to hold back, and when to pivot!

Every turn is a little puzzle!

-description by publisher

name: Guilds of Kurnor: Shadow Wars in Thargos
description:
The game is set in the fantasy world of The Cursed Empire. As the leader of a Guild of thieves and assassins, you will recruit powerful agents, accumulate gold, hatch subtle plots, and garner influence with both sides of the war that rages in Thargos: Empire and Darkun.

Compete to take down Marks and reap the lucrative rewards, but beware the City Watch of Kurnor, lest your guild members end up in the dungeons! Extend your guild's control across the Empire, eventually picking sides in a Power Struggle over the criminal underworld to cement the victory of your Guild!

—description from the publisher

name: Guilty: Fontainebleau 1543
description:
The royal court in Fontainebleau reeks of conspiracy, and it's up to you, René Bianchi, perfumer to Catherine de Medici, to get to the bottom of things. You must use your flair, medical expertise, and appetite for intrigue to find out what is preventing the crown princess from conceiving an heir — and fast.

To start Guilty: Fontainebleau 1543, you'll read the introduction, then place the specified cards on the table. Choose a card, then turn it over and read it. What will you find there? And behind reading, you might have to put your skilled nose to the test with scratch-and-sniff cards that bring history to the present.

Time will keep passing, possibly leading to surprises as you become immersed in the French royal conspiracies of the 16th century, which are based on historical facts. Conduct your investigation, card by card, but time is short and your choices have consequences...

name: Gun Trail
description:
Our story is taking place in Gravelton, a dusty, lawless town wedged between the Crimson Sands and the dried bed of the Arrow Creek. It sprang up almost overnight, born of the big bucks rolling in from the railroad; now it’s home to cutthroats, wretches, and gallows-birds.

You are Emmett “Scrooge” Masterson, the thriftiest bounty hunter in the West. You don’t like drawing your gun — mostly because bullets cost money. Instead, you hand out punches liberally; they’re free, after all, and so far they’ve proven mighty effective at settling problems. As the poet says: one fist is iron, the other one steel; if the left one don’t get you, the right one will. But Gravelton is a different ballgame. Iron and steel might not be enough for what’s waiting there. This time, you’ll need lead.

Take on the role of a bounty hunter in a lawless land. Explore the maps and engage enemies in combat with 2D6 dice, culminating in the final showdown with the infamous Gatling Gang.

Choose a path on the map; when you reach a numbered space, draw a card from the previously prepared, shuffled, and face-down event deck. Resolve the event on the card: enemies to capture, bonuses, or other. When you capture enemies, some of them give you a Clue. The sum of the clues will reveal the location of the final boss. If you capture him, you win.

—description from the designer

name: Capybara Crush
description:
Addicting fun card game! Help critters escape the flooding river with your herd of of Capybaras. Form long interweaving chains of matching critters and backgrounds to score points. Most points wins.

Each card has a column of three different critters on the front and a capybara on the back. Either place the critters on one of your capybaras, or add a capy to your roster.

Each game has variable powers that let you manipulate your tableau and the board, and variable board setups that shift your strategies. Solo mode is drafting against two bots.

—description from the publisher

name: Gunpowder, Treason and Plot
description:
A real time social deduction game for 4 - 8 players that last 10 minutes.

Players take on a hidden role at the beginning of the game: either as one of the plotters who seek to blow up the houses of parliament, or as a secret agent, working against them from the shadows in this fast paced game of subterfuge.

At the beginning of the game, one bomb card is drawn and placed face up per player. These cards will have a list of components that must be attached to that card in order to prime the bomb.

For the plotters, the primary focus is to draw and play cards from the component deck, matching the symbols on the bomb cards. These are played face down, and once four have been placed, these cards are shuffled and revealed. If even one component doesn't match then those components are discarded and the bomb resets.

The role of the agent is to act like a plotter but to spoil the priming of bombs by placing components that don't match. Subtelty and deception are paramamout as careless agents will be easy to spot.

All players begin the game with access to a pool of suspicion tokens. These can be given to players who are suspected of being agents. Three or more will see the receiving player eliminated from the game.

in a way that As the game progresses, players will arouse suspicion and are voted out if they have three or more suspicion tokens.

Players can also draw from the investigation deck. These cards are designed to help root out the agent but come at the expense of precious time that could be otherwise spent priming the bombs.

Featuring a 10 minute sand timer, once the game begins it doesn't stop until the plotters achieve victory or time runs out and they're caught.

-description from publisher

name: Guns of the Old West
description:
Players compete as a team with over 100 campaign paths. Each playthrough is a unique cinematic experience offering endless replayability. Players make strategic decisions and interact with each other to achieve their group and secret individual objectives, some of which involve betrayal, making for an unpredictable gameplay experience.

—description from the designer

name: Dragon Mail
description:
Fly dragons to deliver mail, ferry friends, move supplies, and explore the wilds! Adventure awaits!

Dragon Mail is card game. When your a dealer, place one card from the top of the deck on a location of your choice. While you're not the dealer, visit a location to fill up your dragon with cards and score matching cards. You have limited moves the entire game, so plan carefully, but also move fast before another player grabs the perfect shipment!

—description from the publisher

name: Gzhel
description:
Gzhel is an abstract pattern-building game designed in folk painting style with the same name.

In Gzhel you will be trying your hand as artisans painting patterns on porcelain figurines. In each round you will have three common goals — three orders for Gzhel painting. Arrange your tokens around the figurines on the pad to complete as many goals as possible and earn victory points. After the eighth round, the player with the most victory points wins.

During the game you'll be receiving points for different types of goals: combinations of flowers on your two pads separately; covered patterns on both of your pads.

The game lasts 8 rounds, each consisting of 3 steps:

     The active player names one of 5 animals.
     All players remove all flower tokens around that animal.
     Players place these tokens on empty spaces on any of their pads.
     Players score points for the current aims.


Aims change each round, but you know some of the aims for the next round.

—description from the publisher

name: Use Up All Your Sick Days
description:
Work on a day like today? No way. Time to call in sick. Hopefully no one else had the same idea. It's a hilarious climbing shedding game fun for the whole family!

Use Up All Your Sick Days is simple. There is no turn order and you need to play a card with the next day or same worker currently on top of the discard pile. But if go to play at the same time as someone else, you both leave the card and draw a 2 cards as a punishment. (You also can't play after yourself, and you could play a card face down as a doctor's note, making it wild.)

Play all your cards to lose a tired worker token and draw back to 7 cards.  The first half of the players to get rid of their tired worker tokens win!

Solo/co-op rules are for 1-6 players and are much more puzzly! You play HR organizing the worker's schedule. Co-op limits communication, but you you can spend pizza tokens to flag where you want to play later. Solo has cozy mode with no automa and challenging mode with an easy to run automa.

—description from the publisher

name: Habitopia
description:
In Habitopia, you become the manager of a thriving nature reserve. Your goal is to attract animals and create beautiful, interconnected habitats. Each turn, you choose how to expand your reserve by placing a card as either a habitat or fauna. The habitat side helps you grow new environments, while the fauna side brings in animals with unique scoring goals. Balancing these choices keeps every turn exciting.

What makes Habitopia unique is its easy-to-learn but surprisingly deep gameplay. The game offers a family mode with simple rules that are perfect for kids and new players. For those who love a bit more strategy, the advanced mode introduces a clever auction system, adding an extra layer of competition. This variety means Habitopia appeals to both casual players and seasoned gamers.

Packaged in a compact, travel-friendly tin, Habitopia is designed to be taken anywhere. Its stunning, hand-drawn artwork brings the natural world to life, making it a visual delight. With different strategies to explore each game, Habitopia combines the beauty of nature with engaging gameplay that never feels the same twice.

—description from the publisher

name: Hagia Sophia
description:
Türkiye, with its rich historical and cultural heritage, attracts millions of tourists annually. While most visitors know only the world-famous Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque in Istanbul, few realize that multiple structures bearing this sacred name exist throughout the country. "Hagia Sophia" - meaning "Holy Wisdom" - isn't unique to Istanbul. Türkiye is home to several lesser-known Hagia Sophia structures, each with its own historical significance and architectural beauty. These hidden gems represent the country's layered history of faith, conquest, and cultural transformation.

Hagia Sophia is a print and play, roll and write game.  In Hagia Sophia, you step into the role of an Urban Planner competing to impress the Mayor with your city development skills. Just as many discover there's more to Hagia Sophia than Istanbul's grand monument, players discover there's more to urban planning than simple construction. Will you create a balanced city that fulfills your promises, or will your ambitious plans crumble under practical constraints? Can you outplan your opponents to become the Mayor's favored urban visionary?

Your mission is to transform your district by strategically placing essential facilities while navigating opportunities and constraints. Your blueprint must include plans to build schools with roads, hospitals, fund critical allocations, provide free Wi-Fi, and assign Civil Servants to hospitals and schools. Every building needs civilians, and unemployed civilians will cost you points.  Even when construction seems impossible, you must continue developing - building roads that follow the curve dictated by the dice.

Each turn, you'll:


     Roll a pool of dice that includes region dice, promise dice, and a road die 
     Select a region die to claim on your player sheet and draw icons from promise dice onto your city map 
     Connect your city with strategic road or bridge placements 


—description from the designer

name: Haiku
description:
Every round, each player secretly pick one of the six ukiyo-e painting cards on display.
Using 3 of their 8 double-sided haiku phrase tiles, players create a haiku verse to guide their teammates to the correct illustration.
If the players manage to identify the correct card, they are one step closer to victory. Otherwise they are one step closer to defeat.
The number of successes or failures required to trigger the end of the game is dependent on player count.

name: Vegan Cafe
description:
Ever wanted to open your own trendy cafe? Your dominoes have ingredients on one side and recipes on the other, and both sides have arrows you point to yourself to score points at the end of the game (in addition to a favorite ingredient if any are left on the table). The challenge is to protect your own ingredients while you cover other's ingredients with your recipes.

The game also comes with dozens of optional barista cards, granting asymmetric powers and alternative scoring conditions. Draft 2 at the start of the game and unlock some awesome broken combos!

It's time to bake and brew your way to the best little vegan cafe in town!

—description from the publisher

name: Half Truth: Second Guess
description:
Maybe you know the answer, maybe you don’t, or maybe your teammate does. Don’t worry we give you all the answers, the only problem is only Half of them are the Truth. This trivia party game will have you Second Guessing yourself, as you use your knowledge, intuition, and luck to win! Half Truth: Second Guess is compatible with the original Half Truth.

Each round, you'll get a question with 6 possible answers: three correct, three incorrect. More answers can earn you more points, but giving ANY incorrect answers scores you nothing.

-description from publisher

name: 20 Strong: Tanglewoods
publisher: Chip Theory Games; Lavka Games; Lucky Duck Games
description:
Journey into the Tanglewoods is the second crowdfunding campaign for the 20 Strong game system, focusing on the new Tanglewoods trilogy. Inspired by 20 Strong, acclaimed designer and artist Manny Trembley collaborated with Chip Theory to create a world where fairy tale characters navigate an ever-changing forest, battling and bribing enemies to confront their ultimate nemesis. The game features flippable cards that reveal different gameplay elements depending on which side is faceup.

The campaign introduces a new core box, containing everything needed to play, including the base rules, 20 dice, a magnetic chip tracker, and the Tanglewoods Red deck, all packaged with red foil accents. Players will navigate the forest, avoid the Big Bad Wolf's pack, and face the woodland's treacherous denizens on their way to grandmother's house. After mastering the Tanglewoods Red deck, players can explore other 20 Strong decks for fresh adventures.

name: Halflings: Best Chef
description:
Halflings: Best Chef is a competitive dice placement game where players strive to be elected the Best Innkeeper of the 7 Shires. Decorate your inn, collect fine beverages, and cook with top-quality ingredients to earn the highest standing.

Players start by rolling dice, and placing them on action spaces to gather ingredients, collect spices, sell goods, buy decorations, and cook dishes. Each action helps you build your inn’s reputation.

The game ends when a player completes a menu with a starter, main course, and dessert. Points are tallied based on dishes cooked, unused ingredients, decorations, and other resources. The player with the highest standing points wins.

Strategically manage resources, place dice, and use modifiers to outwit opponents and become the most renowned innkeeper in the 7 Shires!

name: The Elder Scrolls: Betrayal of the Second Era
publisher: Chip Theory Games; A-Z kiadó; Ediciones MasQueOca; Fox in the Box; Frosted Games; Pendragon Game Studio; Portal Games; Rawstone
description:
The Elder Scrolls: Betrayal of the Second Era is a cooperative tabletop adventure set during Tamriel's Second Era – specifically during the events of the Planemeld, as the Order of the Black Worm plots to secure the Amulet of Kings. As the dark cult schemes, however, one of its members is planning an even darker betrayal, one that will tie Tamriel in with Oblivion forever. Adventurers work to uncover her machinations and stop her plot amid a bevy of endlessly replayable content. As in The Elder Scrolls video games, players will travel on an epic journey, balancing exploration, character building, dungeon diving and close quarters combat.

Each adventure in the game takes place over the course of three gameplay sessions, with sessions being roughly two hours plus an additional half hour per player in length. Players customize and control a single hero throughout all three sessions of an adventure as they manage multiple skill lines, classes and experience the many regions of Tamriel, each with their own unique flavor and mechanics. Experience points are handed out generously, allowing players to build interesting and unique characters in the consolidated timespan required in a tabletop experience. Session to session progression is meaningful, but players are not required to remember complex narrative points or play with the same group forever.

name: Wroth
publisher: Chip Theory Games; Fox in the Box; Frosted Games; HIT Games; Lavka Games; Lucky Duck Games
description:
Wroth is an area control board game that can be played competitively, cooperatively, or solo.

Players choose a faction and vie for control of the island of Wroth by drafting action dice to gain resources, deploying and moving troops, and attacking the opposition - all while trying to hold key positions and dominate the region. Wroth rewards cunning troop management and the clever use of your faction’s elite troops and powerful once-per-game abilities. Each faction has asymmetric abilities so what works for one won't necessarily work for another.

The game ends after a round when one faction reaches 30 victory points or completes a scenario-based mission, depending on the game mode.

Wroth can be taught in 10-15 minutes, and is playable in roughly an hour.

—description from the publisher

name: Hamilcar Imperator: La Guerre des Mercenaires
description:
Hamilcar Imperator: La Guerre des Mercenaires is an Operational level Solitaire-Only board-wargame set in Carthage after the First Punic War.

At the end of the First Punic War, Carthage ceded Sicily to the Roman legions. In a gesture of magnanimity, Rome allowed the Punic garrisons holding the last strongholds to return home. Among them were Hamilcar Barca—the father of the famous Hannibal—and thousands of Celtic, Greek, and Iberian mercenaries.

Once disembarked in Africa, the soldiers began demanding their overdue pay and grew restless. The Libyans, vassals of Carthage, quickly realized that their tribute would be increased to cover the mercenaries’ wages. They made a bold gamble: they armed themselves, allied with the Numidians, poured their gold into the mercenaries’ hands, and proposed a daring plan—march on Carthage!

The player must suppress this uprising, which will quickly escalate into a bitter and unforgiving war if not contained. To do so, they will command several Punic generals—who often disagree and whose ambitions are closely watched by the suffetes. Fortunately, war elephants will help literally crush the rebellion.

Optional rules allow players to incorporate Gustave Flaubert’s Salammbô or simulate flaming pigs on the battlefield.

Scale


     1 game turn = 1 year (divided into 4 seasons)  
     1 unit = 500 to 2,000 infantry, 500 to 1,000 cavalry, or 10 elephants/siege weapons  
     Complexity: 6/10  
     Solo game


—description from the designer

name: Hamilcar: Silver Edition
description:
Who shall rule the Mediterranean Sea? A nascent land-based empire with no naval traditions or the world’s premium trading and maritime power? Stand with Rome and lead mighty legions to expand its power beyond the confines of the Italian peninsula, or take Carthage’s side and lead its battle-hardened fleets and generals to victory and glory!

Hamilcar is an asymmetrical card-driven wargame for 2 players with updated rules and cards. Use Strategy Cards to maneuver armies, fleets, and generals, raise new troops and build warships, gain political control of provinces and regions across the Mediterranean, and play powerful historical events. Achieve victory by capturing your enemy's capital, holding more provinces at the last round or by removing all your opponent's PC markers from the map. Carthage can also win if Roma controls less than 3 provinces at the end of any turn.

Hamilcar Silver Edition is the first version of the game to be released separately from Hannibal. Compared to the previous Golden Geek edition, this Silver Edition:

     Has an updated rulebook and player aid to address all known outstanding questions and errata.
     Changes some Land Battle rules
     Changes the Naval Interception rules
     Adds the Price of Failure expansion General and Strategy Cards as an optional rule.
     Replaces the plastic miniatures with cardboard standees and corresponding counters for the Generals
     Adds a new Fleet counter/standee for each side to help track Naval Movement and Interception.


—description from the publisher

name: HANAMI
description:
HANAMI / 花見 is a game from Japan in which players enjoy the cherry blossom in Spring. All over Japan, parks and gardens are full of cherry trees in full bloom, and Japanese people enjoy Hanami, sitting under the blossom to eat and drink and party.

This is a strategic territory capture game with a new and changing board and easy-to-play rules. Players try to take over as much of the cherry blossom viewing area as possible, using cards to spread out the straw mats while competing with other players. Collect sets of Hanami activities and play them to secure key positions, scoring for your largest contiguous area on the board.

・Manage your hand to create sets of cards, then use those cards to capture the best seating locations under the blossoms
・Score points for your largest chain of consecutive pieces
・Certain sets will allow you to pull the entire tatami row out, shaking up the largest interconnected sections of the board

The player who has captured the largest area is the winner and has enjoyed the cherry blossom viewing to the fullest.

-publisher's summary

name: Hanbok Runway
description:
Two players take on the role of Hanbok dress designers and design a collection of Hanbok for a fashion show. Hanbok is a traditional Korean garment, and in Hanbok Runway, you'll create a modern take on it.

Each hanbok set is created by layering a fabric card and a style card.
There are 10 different style cards and 30 unique fabric cards to create 300 different designs.

When you play a set:
(1) Choose one of two colors from the fabric cards to gain an influence token, and 
(2) Apply the ability of the style card. 

    Some influence tokens are set face-down, and some even give you negative influence points.
    The abilities of style cards allow you to convert numbers, get information, etc.


You can play 0-2 sets per turn, and the game ends when someone makes 10 sets or when 2 types of influence tokens are removed.

Influence is compared for each color, and whoever scores 1 or more and has a higher influence than the other player gets victory points for that color. The player with the highest total wins.

You will fall in love with the simple rules, quick setup, intense competition, and above all, the beauty of Hanbok.

name: Hand of Cthulhu
description:
The Elder Gods are coming and the only way to stop them is to destroy all 4 Gates by using every resource at your disposal! You will only succeed by skillfully deciding which items to keep and discard along your adventure.

In Hand of Cthulhu, players fight through an onslaught of monsters until they reach a Gate to worlds beyond our own. There are 12-16 cards between you and each Gate. Each card is an Encounter that is either a Bane (Monster) or Boon (Event). To fight Monsters, you must use your Items wisely and decide which Items to keep and which ones to discard. Once you get to a Gate, you will attack it and exploit its fractures to destroy it. Once you destroy the fourth gate you have successfully saved our world. But if you ever lose all of your health, you die, and if you lose all of your sanity, you go insane and lose the game!

—description from the designer

name: Hands off!
description:
Hands off! is a game that requires quick reflexes and visual discrimination. You compete to find and touch the card that matches the combination rolled on two dice: one for numbers and one for candy. As the game progresses, more and more obstacles are placed in your path, making it difficult to progress and, on the other hand, offering other players the chance to catch up.

With a variable difficulty system, Hands off! ensures balanced gameplay between people of different abilities, making the game accessible and fun for everyone.

name: Hannibal: Classic Edition
description:
