The world shivers as the vengeful Carthage launches a devastating war against Rome, a conflict raging across Italian and Iberian peninsulas, Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily, and North Africa. Stand with some of the greatest generals in history – Hannibal Barca or Scipio Africanus – and lead your empire to victory and glory!

Hannibal is an award-winning asymmetrical card-driven wargame with rules and cards upgraded from previous editions. Use Strategy Cards to maneuver armies and famous generals of the time, raise new troops, gain political control of provinces and regions across the Mediterranean, and play powerful historical events. Achieve victory by capturing your enemy's capital, holding more provinces at the last round or by removing all your opponent's PC markers from the map.

Compared to the previous Golden Geek edition, the Classic Edition: 

     Revives the classic Second Punic War scenario as the core of the game.
     Has an updated rulebook that reflect this, and addresses all known outstanding questions and errata.
     Adds a Playbook with a series of learn-to-play tutorials.
     Replaces the plastic miniatures with cardboard standees.
     Adds the Sun of Macedon expansion General and strategy cards as a newoptional rule.


—description from the publisher

name: Hantise
description:
Hantise (French for "Haunt") is a party-game that brings haunted locations to you. It is played in the dark, with only light coming from the flashlight of your smartphones. It can be played inside or outside (ideally with places where some players can isolate themselves). It is played over seven rounds each divided into three phases.
Players take the roles of Mediums except for one, playing the Master of Ceremonies. The MC fully takes part in the game and simply has the added responsibility to make sure the play stays on track.

During the Preparation phase, players are dealt cards that can haunt them.
During the Exploration phase, the Mediums try to save the possessed players to gain points by performing missions (described as "dares").
During the Validation phase the points are tallied and the end-game conditions are checked: if the candle tokens are out of the board, the Mediums win. If the MC calls the players and none come because they are all possessed, the game is lost.

name: Hanzō: Light and Shadow
description:
Hanzō is a solo and 1v1 print & play game, inspired by the legend of Hattori Hanzō — the ninja who walked the line between discipline and deception. Armed with just four dice and a pencil, you'll infiltrate a samurai village, recover ten sacred weapons, and ascend to the Eleventh House — the place of ninja enlightenment. Each turn is a tactical decision. Each move takes you deeper into the shadows.

—description from the publisher

name: Happy DayZ: American Dream
description:
Happy DayZ is a trick-taking game in which you play Communities trying to survive in a world overrun by Zombies. Win tricks with Survivors to trigger their powers and grow your Community. Leave strategic tricks for your opponents to avoid taking damage from Zombies!

The originality of Happy DayZ lies in its board: if the trick is played on the + side, the highest card value wins. If played on the - side, the lowest card wins.
It’s up to you to play your cards in the right spots to gain the advantage!

The Community with the most Survivors at the end wins the game. Play a single round for quick games, or use campaign mode to play for 4 rounds or until any Community loses its last Survivor.

In American Dream, you play with 6 different factions: Nurse, Policeman, Cheerleader, Governor, Survivalist and Biker.

American Dream & Woodstock Fever are compatible standalone!

—description from the publisher

name: Happy DayZ: Woodstock Fever
description:
Happy DayZ is a trick-taking game in which you play Communities trying to survive in a world overrun by Zombies. Win tricks with Survivors to trigger their powers and grow your Community. Leave strategic tricks for your opponents to avoid taking damage from Zombies!

The originality of Happy DayZ lies in its board: if the trick is played on the + side, the highest card value wins. If played on the - side, the lowest card wins. It’s up to you to play your cards in the right spots to gain the advantage! The Community with the most Survivors at the end wins the game.

Play a single round for quick games, or use campaign mode to play for 4 rounds or until any Community loses its last Survivor.

In Woodstock Fever, you play with 6 factions: Hippie, Dog, Children, Scientist, Preacher and Military !

American Dream & Woodstock Fever are compatible standalone!

—description from the publisher

name: Happy Mochi
description:
Be the first to empty your hand!

In Happy Mochi, all cards must be played in pairs, and you can never rearrange your hand.

To play, you must follow value restrictions — unless you have two matching cards! In that case, shout "Happy Mochi!" and break all the rules!

Special abilities and color-matching add an extra layer to this strategic party game, where luck and tactics go hand in hand.

—description from the publisher

name: Hardwood Duel
description:
Welcome to Hardwood Duel, the thrilling two-player basketball card game! From shooting three-pointers to grabbing rebounds to energizing the crowd, Hardwood Duel is everything that we love about basketball! Each player commands their own team, using a deck of cards that represent everything you’d see in a basketball game.  You alternate slapping down cards to throw down huge dunks, hit deep threes, call out quick coaching adjustments, and even get the crowd screaming and yelling and cheering! As you play, you can use the applause generated by your eager fans to add advanced, game-changing cards to your deck. The goal? Score the most points to claim victory!

The game takes moments to learn and only a few minutes to play.  While the rules are simple, mastering Hardwood Duel is a challenge that will keep you coming back over and over and over!

—description from the designer

name: Harry Potter: Hogwarts Journey Board Game
description:
You finally got your Hogwarts letter! Join Harry, Hermione, Ron, and Luna as they journey through the halls of Hogwarts. School is in session and you want to be the reason that your House wins the House Cup at the end of the year. Gather your friends, grab your Marauders Map to help you find your way as you all journey through the Hallowed Halls. Dodging Mythical Creatures and battling at the Dueling Club, who will be the first to make it to the finish and become this year’s Dueling Club champion?

Enjoy this entertaining magical game brimming with Harry, Ron, Hermione, and all the friends then make along their Hogwarts journey. Now, you can experience the magic all year long!

—description from the publisher

Contents:
• 1 Game board
• 4 Character Pieces
• 8-Sided Die
• 42 Harry Potter Cards

name: Harvest Valley
description:
Harvest Valley is a farming game in which players are trying to build up their farms as their neighbors encroach on their land. There are also wild boars and crows intent on eating crops! Whose farm will be the most successful?

A card game that feels like a tile-laying game. On your turn, either place a card from the display into a grid, or build one of your farmhouses. But not everyone wants your farm to have the biggest harvest!

On your turn, place a crop card or a farmhouse card on the shared grid.  Once the grid is full, the game ends and the player with the highest score wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Hastenbeck 1757
description:
The SYW Battle Series (SYWBS) games are playable grand-tactical studies of battles of the Seven Years War. The series’ intent is to show how command operates on the battlefields, using the weapons and tactics of the period. The system emphasizes command & control and playability.
The games all share the following characteristics:
Scale = 200-220 m/hex (219-240 yrd/hex)
Time = 30 min/Turn
Counter = 1 Brigade, 1 Battalion, 1 to 3 Squadrons, 1 Battery, 1 Leader
Each unit's historical flag and uniform are displayed on Counters, Orders/organizational Displays, and Orders of battle (in Playbooks).

Hastenbeck 1757 simulates the battle fought on the 26th of July 1757 in Lower Saxony (Hanover) during the Seven Years War. Louis Charles César Le Tellier, maréchal d'Estrées commanded the French Army, with contingents from Palatinate and Austria: 63,300 men (86 bns, 101 sqns) and 76 guns. Prince William Augustus, Duke of Cumberland commanded the Allied Army made up of troops from Hanover, Hesse, Brunswick and Bückeburg: 38,400 men (52 bns, 47 sqns) and 34 guns.

—description from the designer

name: Hastilude
description:
In Hastilude, players take on the roles of the King's most trusted advisors. You are tasked with using your workers to train and equip knights to enter tournaments, complete quests, and fill the orders from the king himself.

Hastilude is a worker placement game where you must figure out the best way to utilize your workforce. You start the game with five workers and one knight. Finding the balance between having a good-sized workforce and the right amount of knights to score victory points is one of the challenges of the game.

You must also decide how to use your knights. Knights are the primary way you score victory points and acquire gold to support your plans. Focusing on gaining gold could put you behind on victory points, and focusing too much on victory points and you could find yourself short of gold when you really need it. Your workers are tasked with collecting resources to turn them into equipment to aid your knights. Workers will gather resources and turn them into armor, weapons, and shields.

In Hastilude, the player who can best manage their workforce and their knights will come out victorious.

–description from designer

name: Haunted Halloween: The Trick-or-Treat Game
description:
Players take on the role of trick-or-treaters who venture into a haunted neighborhood, going door-to-door to collect the most candy. Beware! Ghosts come out of the graveyard to steal candy and stash it in the candy coffin! Asymmetric player powers, BOOst tokens, and Secret Candy Quest tokens add layers of complexity to the game, giving you a chance to cause mischief for your opponents.

In Haunted Halloween: The Trick-or-Treat Game, players trick-or-treat the neighborhood with the risk of more powerful ghosts chasing you as the full moon rises. Will you escape with your candy?! Strategize, form alliances, and push your luck on a quest to collect the most Halloween candy to win!

Players roll dice to move along the board to reach houses, but they also roll a GHOST DICE on their turn to move one of the ghosts, who can steal candy from other players. When a player lands on a doorstep, they spin the Trick-or-Treat spinner to see what happens. They could get candy, there might be no one home, or they could trigger the Banshee. Watch out for the Banshee as she flies across the Full-Moon Tracker! The Banshee sends out more powerful ghosts to capture your candy, adding to the suspense of your Halloween hijinks. Players can also pick up a BOOst Token that gives them strategic powers that can be game-changing.

For those seeking a risky venture, you can attempt to raid the Candy Coffin. But be warned, this may invoke the wrath of the spirits guarding their pilfered treats. Visit the Haunted House to grab a Glowstick that will protect you from one ghost attack, but then you must roll the Haunted House Die! Costumes have a once-per-game power too!

Haunted Halloween was created by an eight-year-old girl and her mom.
Selected as FINALIST in the MOST INNOVATIVE product in the Halloween & Costume Association competition 2025. Winners announced Jan 2026

—description from the publisher

name: HAVOC
description:
HAVOC is a tactical card battler set in the perilous world of Port Terminus. In this game, you will compete against other players in one-on-one or two-on-two turn-based matches. Both players will deploy powerful combatants and utilize surreal alien technologies to gain the upper hand.

The game is a battle of both resources and position, featuring a dynamic board controlled by Reactors which, upon activation, grant the ability to play devastating Biome cards. Embrace strategy and maximize the advantages of the unique 6x6 card placement and streamlined combat-movement systems, providing players with an extraordinary degree of freedom.

Players construct their decks and battle for control of the field of play.

Core set is for 1v1 play, Nyxwalker Set includes 1v1 and 2v2 play.

—description from the publisher

name: Havocville
description:
Welcome to the godly tug-of-war for the final fate of Havocville.

Havocville is a board game for 2 to 5 players where you are a God shaping the destiny of a vibrant city! Strategically place Land and People tiles to boost the influence of different Factions – Crown, Valor, Craft, and Field. But here's the twist: you're not just building; you're predicting! Score points by backing the Factions that rise to Dominance in key city Aspects like territory, population, and loyalty. Will you master the divine game of influence, outwit your fellow deities in tense challenges, and forge Havocville's fate to your glory? Dive into Havocville, where every tile placement shapes not just a city, but your path to godlike renown
—description from the designer

name: Holiday Hills
description:
In Holiday Hills, players collaborate to transform the Jingle Bell Square into a dazzling winter spectacle, adorning trees with twinkling lights and festive decorations. Mayor Holly Daze has enlisted your help as the Twinkle Taskforce to get the town ready for the Winter Festival, but you've procrastinated until the very last minute! Now, your dynamic duo of a human and elf must work together to add decorations and deliver dice presents in a race to spread the most Cheer!

Each turn, players will push their sleigh down either the top or bottom path, collecting dice presents into their sleigh and ultimately delivering them under trees. Park your sleigh on an action space in front of a home to add those decorations into the town square. You may move as far down the street as you like, but there's only one lap around town before your game ends, so make the best use of each move!

Throughout the game, players will aim to complete objective cards with decoration patterns and dice color combinations that go under their trees. Take a break at each player's cottage in the corner of the board to draw a new objective card and attempt to score more points. The player who makes it around town and back to their own cottage first will earn bonus cheer points, but other players will have more time on the board to complete objectives.

You earn points for having Festive Trees (all 4 spots filled on your tree) and Full Trees (4 dice presents under your Trees. Having the most decorations on a Tree will also score additional points for the highest pipped dice. The player with the most points will earn the Key to the City!

The double-sided game board allows players to play both the Nice mode and the Naughty mode, in case you like to have a spicy holiday season.

Compete to create the most enchanting display and spread holiday cheer in this delightfully strategic decorating game!

—description from the publisher

name: Hearts Ablaze
description:
A push-your luck game that combines dice rolling with pattern recognition.

Players are part of the rhythmic gymnast's team and are preparing for the Olympics. The aim? Be elected team captain to guide your team as the world tunes in. Give it your best and balance your ambitions with personal drama to lead your team and be the best.

In this game you use the pattern recognition element from Botanists (released 2019) but combine it with dice rolling push your luck elements. Your ability to manipulate your dice-rolls will be linked to your apparatus: hoop, ball, clubs, and rope.

Your personal dramas are related to family pride, personal ambition for success, your impulse to be famous, or with your love interest. However, your coach will be putting pressure from a different angle also. With hearts ablaze: balance your acts, train your routines, command admiration, and be the best!

name: Heavy Knuckles
description:
In the epic and no-holds-barred game of Heavy Knuckles, fearless warriors assemble their haphazard mechs using an array of unique component cards. Each hero begins by crafting their mech's Core with Pilot and Chassis Cards. Arm Cards drawn from the deck are strategically  placed and reinforced around the Core, ready for battle!

During each turn, players roll the Action Dice to unleash heroic actions like Rebuilding, Swapping Parts, Sabotaging, and of course, ATTACKING! The ultimate goal is to obliterate the opponent's Core Cards with unique combinations of Shoulder and Fist Attacks while skillfully blocking incoming strikes. Victory is achieved when a player demolishes all of their opponent's Core Cards, leaving their mech in a glorious heap of scrap metal.

Prepare for strategic and hysterical mech battles that will have you cheering for more!

—description from the designer

name: Jingle Bell Roll
publisher: Chris Couch Games; Water Bear Games
description:
Jingle Bell Roll is a cozy, holiday dice game for 2-6 players, full of festive cheer, quick turns, gift-giving, and delightful combos!

Players take turns rolling 7 Christmas dice up to three times, setting aside symbols they want to keep. Dice show festive icons like Milk, Cookies, Stockings, Gifts, and Bells—each with unique scoring rules.

After rolling, players may play Gift Cards from their hand to boost their score or manipulate dice results. Players then choose when to stop rolling and score their dice, earning points and handing out Gift Cards for each Gift symbol they score. Rolling enough Bells lets players add Letters to Santa in your Mailbox, which gives bonuses like permanent dice faces to score every round. The game ends after 6 rounds, or immediately if a player rolls 7 Bells—whichever comes first! Choose from 10 unique characters from the world of Holiday Hills to help you score more points.

—description from the designer

name: Hegemony: Rome or Cartague
description:
The game is for 1 to 4 players, and there are 4 factions: Patricians and Plebeians representing Rome, and the Council of One Hundred and the Barcids representing Carthage.

The two basic mechanisms of HEGEMONY are the action system and the card game. 
Each player, in each round, performs an Action, choosing from the 6 possible (7 for the Council). Additionally, they can play cards from their hand.
The First and Second Punic Wars, which pitted Rome against Carthage for control of the western Mediterranean, were of extraordinary scale. Rome's ultimate victory has decisively influenced our culture. These wars are undoubtedly among the most important in history. HEGEMONY covers the period from the beginning of the First Punic War (264 BC) to the end of the Second Punic War (201 BC), including the interwar period (240-219 BC).

The game was intended to simulate history faithfully, with two goals: simple rules and short-duration sessions.

—description from the publisher

name: Heist Night
description:
In Heist Night, you play a crew of criminals working together to pull off a series of heists and steal the $100 million you owe the Boss. To succeed in a heist, everyone needs to bring their own set of skills to the table and pull them out of the bag under pressure. Every successful heist nets you a pile of cash, and the aim of the game is to get that pile to $100 million before the SWAT team arrives and puts an end to your plans.

But you can’t trust everyone to be a team player. There’s a chance that one or more of you is an infiltrator: someone who’ll do their very best to stop you in your tracks and bring the Boss down. Infiltrators try to sabotage the heists by slowing them down, gathering evidence and sowing the seeds of distrust. You need to keep your eyes peeled and your ears open. Because as well as getting the money, your mission is to expose the infiltrators and eliminate them.

The criminals need to steal $100 million or eliminate the infiltrator/s before time runs out. Simple as that. The infiltrators work for the cops. They want to stall the criminals before they get the money so that the SWAT team can arrive, or gather as much evidence as they can (filling up the Evidence Track) to take down the gang and the Boss. And any infiltrators who survive a shoot out will have all the evidence they need to snitch on the gang – also leaving them the winners.

name: Heldenqueste: Roter Nebel über Hamburg
description:
The year is 1733. An eerie red mist drifts through the streets of Hamburg, concealing the secret of a terrible crime: treason, sabotage, and attempted murder! Join forces with up to six heroes to uncover the secrets and expose the culprit. If you manage to survive...

Red Mist over Hamburg is a thrilling mystery adventure set in a fantastic version of historical Europe plagued by devils and demons. With the help of over 200 cards, you and your heroes will explore dangerous places, uncover dark secrets, and face bloodthirsty monsters in thrilling battles! Become courageous heroes and work together to lift the veil surrounding the mysterious red fog.

Are you ready to take on this epic quest? A dark world full of secrets awaits you!

—description from the publisher (translated)

Es ist das Jahr 1733. Ein unheimlicher roter Nebel zieht durch die Straßen Hamburgs und verbirgt das Geheimnis einer schrecklichen Tat: Verrat, Sabotage und ein Mordanschlag! Stellt euch mit bis zu sechs Helden der Herausforderung, die Geheimnisse zu lüften und den Täter zu entlarven. Wenn es euch gelingt zu überleben...

Mit Roter Nebel über Hamburg erwartet euch ein packendes Mystery-Abenteuer in einer fantastischen Version des historischen Europas, das von Teufeln und Dämonen geplagt wird. Mit Hilfe von über 200 Karten erkundet ihr mit euren Helden gefährliche Orte, dunkle Geheimnisse und stellt euch blutrünstigen Monstern in packenden Kämpfen! Werdet zu mutigen Helden und lüftet gemeinsam den Schleier um den mysteriösen roten Nebel.

Seid ihr bereit, euch dieser epischen Queste zu stellen? Eine düstere Welt voller Geheimnisse wartet auf euch!

—description from the publisher

name: Hellcat Tankers: A Solitaire Wargame
description:
Hellcat Tankers requires you to manage the Crew of a single World War II M18 Hellcat Tank in and around the Battle of Arracourt in France, 1944. The Battle lasted for 12 days from 18 September to 29 September. Each day your Crew and their Tank may or may not find themselves engaged in combat with the enemy, but you will certainly see plenty of action over the course of the full battle. Whilst this game is not a ‘narrative driven’ game as such, it has elements of those games, and with a little imagination it will provide memorable stories. There may be lucky escapes, notable bravery and manoeuvres to be proud of. There may also be times when your Crew simply needs to Bail out and survive to face another day. Some events are randomly generated to help add to the story, but you will usually have at least some degree of control over the level of risk to take and how vulnerable you leave your Tank to these events.

The Hellcat was a quick and relatively powerful tank destroyer. However, its armour left quite a lot to be desired. With this in mind, tactics often required crews to spot the enemy first, and use speed to surprise them and escape before any return fire came their way.

The game involves:
Armour ratings, firepower ratings, Tigers, Panthers, Panzer IVs, Pumas, infantry, movement, firing, MGs, ambushing, defensive manoeuvres, spotting, loading, repairs, fires, damage, snipers, mines, mechanical problems, artillery, Stukas, StuG IIIs, civilians, reinforcements, bailing out, buildings, trees, roads, hedgerows, water and so on.

How the game works
This is a solitaire hex and counter type wargame. You play the game, and the enemy is controlled by the game. You will need at least 6, but preferably a dozen or so, standard six-sided dice. 12 full colour Battle maps and suggested counters are provided (to be stuck to thin card and cut out).

The game has very good replayability due to the random nature of enemy appearance and actions, as well as end of turn events.

—description from the designer

name: Henhouse
description:
Hen House is a climbing/shedding card game in which players attempt to get rid of all the cards in their hands.

Cards come in four suits: white eggs, white chickens, brown eggs, and brown chickens. Chickens can be combined with chickens, eggs can be combined with Eggs, white cards can be combined with white cards, and brown cards can be combined with brown cards. To shed cards, you can use animals that can help, like snakes that can eat eggs and foxes that can eat chickens.

The player who plays all of their cards first wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Garden Club
description:
Welcome to the Garden Club, where fruits, veggies, and flowers flourish into clever combinations. Match, grow, and out-bloom your friends in this lighthearted game of strategy and charm!

In Garden Club, players compete to grow the most vibrant and well-balanced garden in the neighborhood. Each tile you place will plant fruits, veggies, and flowers — all carefully arranged to create stunning patterns and score points.

On your turn, you’ll select and place a tile into the collective garden, connecting matching icons to form combos and fulfill unique objectives. Then, you'll select one tile as a point multiplier for what's in your garden. The challenge lies in planning your layout — every placement can unlock new scoring opportunities or block a path to a perfect harvest.

As your garden grows, you’ll earn points for completing arrangements, surrounding trellises, and meeting your character's preferences.

—description from the publisher

name: Herd
description: In Herd, you move tactile black and white pieces across the pages of a richly illustrated book, on a journey to find their home. Tight grids and minimalistic rules pack a punch - untangle each solution in the flowy rhythm of sliding, jumping and stacking the figurines. Travel from page to page, meeting strange creatures along the way - you might find page-transcending secrets in the linework of their illustrations...

name: Vector
description:
In Vector, you'll race against the stars as you gather resources to save your civilization from your galaxy's dying star in the polyomino engine and deck builder.

Each turn, players use their deck of cards to perform vector movements in order to draft triangular polyominos into their ship, or collect resources for future purchases and/or end game scoring.

The player with the most Valor before at the end of the game, is declared the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Amberlight
description:
In Amberlight, take the role of a brave hearted Apprentice in the world of Nous; gathering a retinue of friends and followers as you seek adventure in procedurally generated hexcrawls in 3 dimensions!

With a focus on hexcrawl exploration, roguelike adventures are supported by light deckbuilding and crafting/resource management with over 400 illustrated cards that allow for significant replayability and different means of approaching each scenario.

Modular hexcrawl rules allow for solo, cooperative, competitive and casual play across individual scenarios and fully fledged campaigns.

—description from the designer

name: Heredity: Those Kids!
description:
Heredity: Those Kids! is a standalone, a what-if story based on the first chapter of The Book of Swan campaign.

This chapter is a new story, easier to play, slightly shorter, with a dash of humour. If you don't know Heredity, this box has been made to discover the game.  If you know it, feel free to enjoy it as a bonus. Most cards have been modified.

The story's beginning is the same as The Book of Swan but you will quickly understand that NPC won't act as expected, and events will change.  Your goal is different, and this story ends at the end of this chapter.

In this box, the wooden pieces and plastic bases have been replaced by carton. The rules are not included. You will find an online PDF and a video to play to offer you the best possible price.

—description from the publisher

name: Heritage Farms
description:
This is a Mint Tin Game based off of the classic riddle of the farmer who needs to get his Chicken, Fox, and Corn across the river with only space for one in the boat at a time.  If you leave the Chicken and Fox alone, the Chicken will get eaten.  If you leave the Chicken alone with the Corn, the Corn will get eaten.  The twist in this game is that you can stick the other player watching over your resources along with theirs.  Players compete to be the first to get 2 sets of Chicken, Fox, Corn across the river!

On your turn, you may load 1 Farmer and 1 Good into your boat to move across the river.  If this leaves the card without any Farmers (your's or your opponent's), "Nature's Law" takes place: Foxes eat Chickens there, and Chickens eat Corn there.  If a player loses 3 of their goods, they lose immediately.

When delivering your Farmer to the Market, you reveal the Market Bonus there.  You collect it when your Farmer leaves that card.  Market Bonuses provide powerful one-time abilities like moving your opponent's boat, allow you to place 2 Farmers on a card, move a good up or down a card, or move a Farmer up or down a card.

The first player to get 2 sets of Chicken, Fox, and Corn to their Markets wins.

Advanced Mode adds Zombie Chickens and Poisoned Corn!  These new good types "infect" other goods as they move and change the rules of "Nature's Law".  Zombie Chickens eat Foxes when left alone, and Poisoned Corn kills Chickens.

The Solo Mode of the game places you in the challenging position of helping your incompetent cousin, Elmer, while still trying to get your goods across the river.  In this mode, you lose if either you OR Elmer lose 3 goods, or if Elmer gets his goods across first.

—description from the designer

name: Hero Slam
description: Do you dare set foot inside the enchanted forest to face the Great Evil lurking within? Gather together a band of weird and wonderful heroes as you collect imps, go on side quests, and start fights with your opponents in 50 Heroes. Compete to be the first to beat the villain and save the day.

name: Heroes Love to Lie
publisher: Swan Panasia Co., Ltd.; Unfriendly Games
description:
Heroes Love To Lie is a hidden role-playing game of deduction and bluffing. The game is played with cards representing various characters (Heroes) and is based on the principle of secret identities.

The king is dead. While the Heroes fight to seize power, the Monsters seek to plunge the kingdom into chaos. But beware—greed and betrayal lurk, as some Heroes won’t hesitate to eliminate their most threatening rivals.

Become the most popular Hero in the kingdom by battling fearsome Monsters. To win, you must be cunning and hide your true identity. Will you be the mischievous Goblin, the intuitive Exorcist, or the greedy Knight?

The objective is to be the last Hero standing or to collect 4 Glories to win the game.

name: Batam
description:
Cast your sails and embark on a journey to Batam! —a high-seas race with a twist where riches, not speed, wins the day!

Featuring exclusive gameplay development by Crafty Games, you're the captain of a scrappy ship, racing to visit four far-flung islands on your way to Batam. To win, you'll need to outsmart your rivals to rake in the most rewards- but here's the twist: You must hire your crew (with bribes, of course), roll your sailors (dice), then assign them to other players' ships —never your own!

Outsmart the competition by bumping their best sailors and sabotaging their plans. But watch out - you might get seasick crew that refuses to sail!

Navigate the archipelago to drop your markers first, claim island rewards, and charge latecomers for stepping on your turf. Pay your sailors well, manage your moves wisely, and time your return to port just right. First to the bay doesn’t win—richest pirate takes the crown!

—description from the publisher

name: Heroes of the Sanctum: Doomcrawler
description:
Descend And Rise Again! “It is beneath the earth, in the grim depths of underground realms, that the sacred seal of the Doomcrawler is earned. Only those who descend into the darkness and rise again are worthy of claiming the mark.” - The Sanctum of the Scribes.

Choose your champion and venture alone into the dark universe of Heroes of the Sanctum: Doomcrawler. Traverse perilous dungeons, claim forbidden loot, and face the relentless horrors that lie in wait. Overcome the darkness to earn the legendary seal of the Doomcrawler! Dare you claim the sacred seal?

Heroes of the Sanctum: Doomcrawler is a standalone solo card-and-dice dungeon crawler. This standalone experience includes 4 secret Reward Packs  that unlock bonus content for both Heroes of the Sanctum: Doomcrawler and Heroes of the Sanctum: The Strategy Card Game

If you can escape from all dungeons in the Dungeon Stack, you are victorious.

—description from the publisher

name: Heroes vs. Warlords
description:
Heroes vs Warlords is a fantasy strategy game set in the world of Pangea. Pangea is inhabited by clever Amazons, mighty Knights, wild Barbarians, , soul eating Undead and Neutrals. The Neutrals guard the treasures found in Pangea. The world of Pangea is largely unexplored. Vast lands, where no civilized soul has ever been before, are waiting for you.

Heroes vs warlords is inspired by the classic PC games of exploration and evolution of a hero and his army.

Dear Friends and Supporters,
It’s been a while since our last update on Heroes vs Warlords, and we truly appreciate your patience and continued interest.
Over the past months, there were some personal challenges Udo, the heart and soul of the project, had to take time off due to health issues. Thankfully, his health has improved, and he’s back with renewed energy and passion. At the same time, we’ve been navigating some of the bureaucratic hurdles that come with turning a dream into a real product.
But even during this quieter period, a lot has been happening behind the scenes. Here are some of the exciting developments we've made:
A Fourth Faction Has Arrived: The Undead
A new playable faction has risen from the shadows, bringing a fresh, exciting dynamic to the game and shaking up the battlefield!
Quick Combat System
We've introduced a fast combat resolution system for fights against neutral units. These battles now resolve in a single round, saving valuable game time without sacrificing depth.
Simultaneous Turn Rules for 4 Players
To keep the game flowing and engaging for everyone, we now have rules that allow players to act simultaneously in a 4-player game. This means less downtime and more strategic excitement for all players.
Improved Game Balance & Comeback Mechanics
One of the known challenges in strategy games is the “snowball effect” where losing one big battle can take you out of the running entirely. We've addressed this with our new Master and Apprentice card system.
Even if you suffer a tough loss, Apprentice cards provide tools to recover and remain competitive. And the player with the most Apprentice cards becomes the Underdog, gaining access to a powerful comeback mechanism.
On top of that, quick combat has a unique twist: winning a quick battle grants immediate control of the objective hex but surviving neutral units can return to the map later. And guess who decides where they return? The Underdog player. This adds a clever layer of strategy and allows for meaningful comebacks.
We’re excited to be back and stronger than ever.

Our first announcement video goes live this Monday!
Please help us spread the word, share the video with your friends, family, and fellow gamers. Every share makes a difference and brings us one step closer to making Heroes vs Warlords the epic game we all envision.
Thank you so much for your support, it means the world to us.
Warm regards,
The Heroes vs Warlords Team

name: Heroes: Write & Conquer
publisher: Hobby World; Eclipse Editorial; Ghenos Games
description:
Heroes: Write & Conquer is a comprehensive strategy game in a handheld format. Explore territories, build castles, gather troops and search for powerful artifacts.

In Heroes, each player chooses their own player board of a certain faction.

The game lasts for 16 rounds.

At the beginning of a round, the first player chooses four actions out of five that all players in that round will perform. The first player writes the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4 in the boxes of the selected actions — one number per box. The number determines the order in which the action is performed and its level. Actions are resolved in ascending numerical order, with higher numbers representing stronger actions.

There are 3 types of actions in the game:

Wood, iron and gold gathering allow you to add as much of that resource to your inventory, as the level of the action is. Resources are needed for building and recruitment.

Building and recruitment action allows you to build structures and hire units of a corresponding level. Structures give you unique effects, while units are needed to fight with other players, monsters, or to be able to claim fortresses and artifacts.

Finally, movement allows you to move to other sectors based on the amount of movements points you have in this round. After all players finished their movement, different types of fights can be triggered. Players can fight each other if they happened to be at the same sector, or they can claim a fortress or an artifact of that sector. They can also fight monsters for reward. In order to do that, they’ll be spending combat units and compare their strength.

At the end of the game, players will count their victory points for the structures built, fortresses and artifacts claimed, resources gathered and monsters defeated.
The player with the most VPs wins.

—description from the publisher

name: HeroQuest: First Light
description:
HeroQuest: First Light is an introductory version of the HeroQuest game system that includes new quests and is compatible with all HeroQuest expansions.

Your hero’s journey starts here! The HeroQuest First Light fantasy adventure game follows 4 heroes through dungeon quests as they discover treasure, explore immersive environments, and battle evil forces controlled by Zargon, the game master. Traverse an ever-changing, 2-sided board that evolves as you trek through each dungeon. Will you prove yourself worthy of the title of hero? Players can immerse themselves in the fantasy with stunning artwork and more than 100 components, including a detailed dragon miniature, 4 hero miniatures, and 67 full-color cardboard standees. Featuring 10 quests and the option to create your own, this HeroQuest board game has endless replayability. It’s a great gift for fans of cooperative games, fantasy board games, and strategy games for adults and teens. Gather friends together for an exciting night of tabletop gameplay in a battle of good and evil. For 2-5 players, ages 14+.

Includes Quest book featuring 10 unique quests, Game System rulebook, Double-sided gameboard, Game Master’s screen, 4 hero miniatures (1 barbarian, 1 dwarf, 1 elf, 1 wizard), 1 dragon miniature, Pad of character sheets, 31 monster pieces, 15 furniture pieces, 41 cardboard tiles, 21 dungeon doors, 102 game cards, 6 combat dice, 2 movement dice, and 52 plastic movers.

name: Heureka
description:
Heureka / ヘウレーカ！ヘウレーカ is a tile-placement puzzle game based around the powers of 2.

Players take turns placing tiles by matching the symbols on the four corners of the tiles. Each time a tile is placed, tokens are placed on the newly placed tile and adjacent tiles. Tiles occupied by a player's tokens become their territory.

In the end, player with the highest total score from their occupied tiles wins.

name: Hex Effects
description:
Hex Effects is a "take that" style card game featuring Hexes (that you need to rid of) and Remedies (that treat Hexes but may cause you to have more). It is an easy-to-pickup game with original artwork by Pillbox Games. It's based on the game Side Effects.

Start by dealing four Hex cards to each player, face up, in a space in front of them referred to as their "Shadow". The first player to treat all the Hexes in their Shadow wins the game.

The rest of the Hex cards are shuffled in with the larger deck. Then, deal four cards to each player (concealed in hand). Start your turn by drawing two cards. You can make two actions on your turn. If you have in your hand a Remedy card that treats one of your hexes, you can place it on top of that Hex. You're now closer to winning — but watch out! Every Remedy contains a list of side effects (other Hexes) that you are now vulnerable to receiving from other players on their turns.

Play continues until one person has treated all the Hexes in their Shadow.

name: Hexes of Sygon
description:
Your wizards gaze across the mystical planet of Sygon. Volatile volcanoes have blazed away much of the world, except for a precious clearing of land. Here lies the various landscapes of Sygon: meadows, swamps, dunes, mountains, forests, and caves.

Each landscape hosts a unique spell component crucial to developing civilization on Sygon. Collect gold and the various spell components - flower, elixir, spice, powder, mushroom, and crystal - and maneuver your wizards to conjure towns, workshops, and markets to quickly advance your civilization. Use alchemy or forage to obtain components outside your grasp.

Sygon relies on you to bring prosperity to its ravaged lands. However, you are not alone. Wizards loyal to other civilizations plot to loot you and compete for control of the planet. Be wary of where you place your towns and wizards and build walls to protect them against thieving wizards and volcano eruptions. Rise from the ashes and bring glory to your civilization on Sygon.

For the game setup, the players will construct the randomly generated hexagonal game board of flower, elixir, spice, powder, mushroom, and crystal hexes and randomly assign a gold value to each hex. Players will begin the game by placing 2 towns in snake draft order. Each town is placed on an unsettled hex of choice with either 1 or 2 walls in the same hex. A player places their 3 wizards in hexes with their towns on their first turn.

On a player's turn, they will move their wizards, conjure buildings, and cast spells in order. Each building type (town, workshop, market, and wall) contains a unique resource combination, and a player's wizard must be in a hex for them to build there. Action spells consist of wizards foraging component cards from the various landscapes of Sygon, stealing gold from nearby opponents, and protecting from stealing. Additional spell cards (charm, fissure, vanish, blizzard, power trip, & foresight) may be added to this base 2-4 player game.

The goal of Hexes of Sygon is to accumulate enough and the most sorcery points (SP) of all players at the end of a round of turns to win, where SP are awarded through buildings.

—description from the publisher

name: HEXplore It: The Mountains of Godai
description:
For too long we have angered the gods and lived our lives with reckless abandon! For those mistakes, the whole of existence is on the brink of collapse. Jaethi, the great plumed serpent of the wind has returned and brought with her countless elemental armies. She is one of the five great Titans and her power has kept the Wellspring flowing since time immemorial. For reasons only known to the gods, she returns to destroy the fabric of our reality, disassembling the Patterns of all things. If she succeeds, our universe will collapse and all that we are will be gone — scoured clean and rebalanced by her wind.

—description from the publisher

name: Hibachi: Fired Up!
description:
In Hibachi: Fired Up!, you will take the role of a flamboyant chef who must throw chips into the cooking area to acquire the ingredients you need to cook delicious recipes!


     Target the ingredients the customers are asking for!
     Aim, throw, crash, and bash your chips!
     Sizzle the steak, steam the rice, and serve up the best dishes!
     Push your opponents to steal their spot!


After each round of throwing is complete, money and ingredients will change hands, and if a chef is ready, they will then cook a dish to perfection. The first to complete three recipes will be the one who impresses the customers enough to win!

This is a new edition of Hibachi (not an expansion), that features faster and more streamlined rules.

name: Hidden Agendas
description:
Hidden Agendas is a 3-6 player game all about political shenanigans which parodies the US Congressional system. In Hidden Agendas players take on the role of a political operative, each with their own secret Agenda. Play as the outspoken Activist, the cunning Ambassador, the hot-headed General, the slick Lobbyist, the seasoned Party Leader or the conniving Opposition Party. By creating, debating and voting on Bills, players compete to see their Agenda achieve victory by the end of the game with careful strategy, political maneuvering and a healthy helping of bribery, blackmail and deceit. 
Gameplay is a mix of strategy and party-game elements with players having to make calculated decisions about which Legislation cards to play when creating Bills so as not to give away their true intentions. During the debate stage of the game, players will argue for which Bills to Kill and which to Pass into law. Either by enticing rhetoric, or a well-placed bribe of sweet Taxpayer Dollars, players will try to Pass enough Legislation matching their Agenda to win them the game. 
 —description from the publisher

name: Hidden Leaders Duel
publisher: BFF Games; Board Game Circus; Gam'inBIZ; Little Rocket Games; Matagot
description:
As the fighting and turmoil subsides, the two remaining candidates vie for control of the newly established Senate Chambers and attempt to secure the power to rule Oshra peacefully. They do so by offering influential Heroes a position in their secret Council of Leaders. Whoever builds the strongest influence, will win.

Gameplay
In 7 turns, players manipulate the two rows of Heroes and secretly ask some of them into their Council of Leaders.

Setup 

     Shuffle the Hero and Leader cards. 
     Deal each player 3 Hero cards (to be kept secret). 
     Deal each player 1 Leader card (to be kept secret) and add it to your Council
     Create 2 rows of 7 face-down Hero cards on the table (so that only their faction will be visible, but not their strength). 
     Create a face-down draw pile of the remaining 8 Hero cards and place it next to the 2 Hero card rows. 
     Leave space for a face-down Council of Hero cards for each player (to be kept secret).


Gameplay 
Play in turns. When it is your turn: 

     Take 2 heroes from either of the 2 rows on the table and put them in your hand. You can take any hero you want (face up or face down) as long as the hero is not blocked or blocking another hero. 
     Now put 2 cards from your hand back into the open slots in the rows you just created. Put the cards back face up (so that their strength is shown). You can play any heroes you like, even the 2 heroes you just took. 
     Take 1 card from your hand and either: 
         Add it face down to your secret council of leaders. You can have as many leaders as you            want, but do note that the strength of these leaders will not count towards your final score. 
         Place it face down (so that their strength is not visible) on top of an unblocked hero in one of the rows to block it. Place it such that the faction and strength (if face up) of the hero below it can still be seen. 
    
     Finally, draw 1 card from the draw pile. If there are no more cards on the draw pile, skip


this step. The game ends when both players have emptied their hands after 7 turns each.

Scoring 
To determine the final score, proceed as follows: 

      Reveal your Leader and Heroes in your Council
     Then, consider each of the 4 factions (Imperial Army - red, Hill Tribes - green, Water Folk - blue, Undead - black) separately in no specific order: 
         Determine the total Influence per faction, adding together all values of 1 faction . If applicable, also add your Leader’s value to the total Influence.
         See who has the highest total Influence of the chosen faction. Now check which of the 2 rows of heroes has the most Heroes of this faction. The player with the highest total Influence will get all Heroes from this row (face up, face down, blocked, and blocking) and add them to their Army. The other player will get the heroes from the other row. In case of a tie, either because the Council of both players have equal Influence or because there is an equal number of Heroes in both rows, players will take the Heroes from the row closest to them. 
         If a player has no Leader or Heroes of the chosen faction under consideration, the heroes from the row they obtained will be discarded. 
    
     Discard all cards in the Council. They don't count towards the final score. 
     Each player counts the total Strength of Heroes in their Army. The player with the highest total Strength wins and becomes the new Emperor. In case of a tie, the player with more Heroes in their Army wins. If there is still a tie, a rematch is due.


—description from the publisher

name: Hidden Territories: Every Hero Needs a Quest
description:
Hidden Territories is a game of heroic adventure, where mighty — or cunning— heroes explore  the kingdom of Westri, the nexus of the multiverse and filled with perilous monsters, nefarious enemies, and fantastical locations. Players choose one of a multitude of adventurers; their characters traverse the land encountering members of the various factions who vie for power or terrible beasts hungry for flesh — or souls. The kingdom of Westri and its inhabitants are fighting unseen forces, struggling against the grip of chaotic, entropic forces which threaten to rip apart the very fabric of the multiverse.

Play solitaire or cooperative in this game of exploration, adventure, and heroism. Consult the huge volume of the gazetteer to utilize the pre-programmed paragraph system. It’s easy to learn to play, as the programmed event sequence lets you focus on the fun of exploration as your character sets out on a quest. For each event or encounter, you, as one of the included hero player chapters, must make the decisions which will make your quest successful — or may cost you dearly. Hidden Territories has elements of a complex game designed to recapture the high adventure and heroic struggles of fantasy literature — and that famous fantasy role-playing game from the 1970s.

Hidden Territories can be largely played solo, cooperatively, or even with a but of conflict between the players. But victory can only be claimed by uncovering the true nemesis of the kingdom, and defeating a final adversary. It is a race to level up and acquire powerful weapons, armor, artifacts — even and allies. Game play sessions extend and continue, with linked quests. Time passes, and events are influenced by player choice. Heroes must use strength at arms, guile, or negotiation to defeat a hidden and ancient evil before a magical darkness envelopes all that is good.

Hidden Territories combines many different elements:

     Exploration: player characters travel across the hexagonal game board to reach exciting destinations.
     Random encounters: players draw encounter cards each time they enter a new hex.
     Parlay, fight, or flee? many events result in opponents to negotiate with or to fight.
     Random events: players draw event cards each time they enter a new tile
     Leveling up: players improve their characters’ skills and knowledge of magic and gain equipment.
     Paragraph Reading: an extensive plot is uncovered by reading paragraphs out of a book, discovering secrets only denizens of the kingdom know, or piecing together parts of the conspiracy puzzle. Clues help with solving mysteries and help determine how to win.


Hidden Territories features a series of Event and Encounter card decks that set pace of the game and ensures players acquiring experience to level up before they are ready to take on more difficult challenges (events and enemies). Characters acquire new spells and skills as they level up from experience. Finding loot increases wealth, so more equipment, arms and armor, and other items can be acquired. Of course, travel is perilous in this wilderness hexcrawl, so provisions, foraging, and weather all impact the heroes’ progress — getting lost in the trackless wastelands can be as dangerous as stumbling about in the darkness of some ruined dungeon.

Inside the box, Hidden Territories contains:

     The large map game board, showing cities, villages, castles, and ruins scattered across 500 hexes means hours of game play exploration.
     A huge Gazetteer that details the points of interest and other information about the hexes.
     Standup figures representing archetypal warriors, knights, wizards, priests, and other fantastical characters.
     Various decks of cards for events, encounters, items, spells, skills, and the denizens characters encounter. An analog artificial intelligence ensures outcomes are never fully predictable, and the storyline changes based on player choices.
     Dice - lots of dice. Power up actions based on the dice pool, or sacrifice health or luck when heroic deeds are called for.
     Numerous counters and chits to mark the location of encounters, hoards of loot, and other unknown obstacles to overcome. Use some of these to track weather, time, fatigue, and the ultimate countdown to doom.


As scenarios play out and quests are completed, players learn lore, hear rumors, acquire knowledge, train to develop martial or magical powers. Talk, trade, or fight through bizarre encounters to unravel the dark secrets behind the impending chaos.

—description from the publisher

name: Hier
description:
When looking at the large penguin colony, you'll hear constant cries of "Here!" — "Here!" — "Here!"...and those cries will often be coming from you!

In Hier, you want to help the penguins find their partner among the crowd, and the right partner is always the penguin whose called number is as close as possible to their own number. Try to find the right partners for penguins as quickly as possible because whoever first gets rid of their five penguins wins.

name: Hieroglyph Historian
description:
It’s the year 1922. Your expedition has uncovered an ancient desert tomb. As you enter a large hall, the walls shake and start to slowly close in!

Fortunately, your years as an archeologist alerts you to your surroundings. You notice peculiar parchments lying about and hallowed hieroglyphs etched in a puzzle-like manner on the wall.

You stop for a second. Perhaps studying the parchments and deciphering the hieroglyphs might help you to escape the tomb … before it becomes yours.

There are 2 rotating phases: The Study and Decipher Phases.

In the Study Phase, your goal is to use the cards in your hand to obtain lots of Parchments to prepare for the next phase. But don’t forget to also discard a few cards to reveal more Hieroglyphs!

In the Decipher Phase, your goal is to use your Parchments to decipher Hieroglyphs which are then scored at the end of the game. Hieroglyphs come in two types: symbols and values. You need both types in order to score!

Work your way through 4 rounds to try and get a high score and find out your fate. Will you escape the tomb ... or be entombed?

—description from the designer

name: High Adventure: Treasure Hunt
description:
High Adventure: Treasure Hunt is a print-and-play solo expedition into danger, mystery, and the lure of lost treasure. You are the captain of a desperate expedition, guiding a dwindling crew through a deadly jungle in search of a priceless artifact: the Grail. Armed with only a map, your wits, and a pool of dice representing your party’s strength, you'll journey through uncharted terrain—braving illness, injury, and the ever-looming threat of a terrible beast. Chart your path across rivers, jungles, and viper-filled dens. Gather provisions, decipher ancient tablets, and uncover cryptic clues to narrow down the Grail’s location. When you're ready — or when time runs out — attempt a single dig and pray you’ve chosen wisely. But it’s not enough to find the treasure. You must also make it back to base camp alive, carrying enough gold to keep your crew loyal or face defeat even in victory.

Each mission consists of 3 game sheets: hex based Map with over 20 terrain types, Expedition with Exertion, Camp, and Dig sections, Events with Skill tree and Combat sections.  Each mission has unique conditions. Each turn represents 1 day of your mission.  Dice are used to manage both crew and burdens.  
 —description from the designer

name: High Seas Fleet
description:
High Seas Fleet is a game of strategic naval war in the Atlantic, Baltic, and Mediterranean in World War One, from the war’s commencement to conclusion. All major ships of the participating powers are included, including dreadnoughts, pre-dreadnoughts, and squads of lighter ships. Historically, the German fleet only challenged British naval supremacy once, culminating in the Battle of Jutland. This game allows players to explore what might have happened had the Germans been more aggressive and persistent.

The rules of High Seas Fleet are based on the rules system of the classic games of the 1970s, War At Sea and Victory in the Pacific. However, High Seas Fleet introduces a number of innovations to keep the system fresh. The combat system has been modified to mitigate the extremes of luck, and Command Cards introduce a degree of both flexibility and uncertaintly. Allies can enter based on your efforts to recruit them, and stay or go based on your success on the high seas. The game system remains clean and simple, perfect for introducing youngsters or novices to historical gaming, yet substantial enough to reward the veteran gamer.

Features:

- Grand Strategic map covering including the Atlantic, Baltic, and Mediterranean regions
- Basic and Standard Rules
- Variable entry for belligerent powers (optional)
- Additional ahistorical ships (optional)

Scenarios:
- Grand Strategic, 1914-1918
- Jutland (introductory single turn)
- Turning Points, 1917 
- Italy Stands True (ahistorical)
- Pacific War Distractions (ahistorical)
- Schlieffen was Right! (ahistorical)

PnP files for High Seas Fleet are available for FREE download from Last Resort Games at the Wargame Vault.

name: Hikadyat 1 Al-Kisah
description:
Hikadyat is driven by stories told across many generations, from various cultures and times. We are very ambitious for this competitive Collectable Card Game (CCG) because of its nature of being highly collectable for collectors and strongly competitive for TCG players.

Gameplay: A shared tableau-building game where you only score at the end. You will only score cards that match the suit of the two cards in your hand. This game will satisfy players’ itch for clever card play and spatial scoring.
Players can enjoy mastering one deck at a time, or mix and match decks for even more competitiveness and replayability with multiple decks sold separately.

The objective is to accumulate the highest score. Players will gain points from the cards in the shared tableau that match the suit of their hand cards at the game's conclusion. This not only requires strategic thinking, but also provides the ultimate proving ground for players to demonstrate their adaptability and foresight through card placement and hand management.

Al-Kisah, meaning 'The Story' in Arabic, is a highly competitive 18-card game that showcases a diverse array of folklore, fairytales, and stories from various cultures. This deck is based on Malay folklore. Features Malay folklore such as Curse of Mahsuri, The Devouring Rock, The Love Story of the Gunung Ledang Princess, Putih Merah, King of the Fanged Wings, Legend of Badang, The Mousedeer & The Crocodile, and Si Tanggang the Ungrateful Son.

A perfect starter deck with its simple scoring cards.
Whether you’re a newcomer discovering these stories for the first time or a long-time fan of Malaysian folklore, this deck offers an easy entry point into the world of Hikadyat while still giving plenty of room for clever plays and exciting matchups.

—description from the designer

name: HiLo: Dein Königreich
description:
Each player starts with 12 hidden cards: 2 rows with 6 cards each and tries to get the best open display.

At the start, each player already chooses one of his cards in the display and turns them to the open side.

Now all players play alternately.

In his turn, a player can choose a card from the open discard pile and put it open in its display, the replaced card is placed on the discard pile. Alternatively, the player can pull a card from the hidden pile and put it as mentioned or discard it. In the latter case, however, one of the own cards has to be revealed.

The game ends immediately as soon as a player has all his cards open.

Points are now obtained from the printed card symbols. There is one point for two neighboring half coins each, here the position of the cards is important. There are also cards that score points for collecting other cards.

In addition to the scoring cards, there are also a few cards with special effects.

name: Knights of the Round Table
description:
In each game of Knights of the Round Table, players choose a cycle of Arthurian myth to play, setting the tone and starting rules. They rally a company of knights and Arthurian personalities, deploying them to construct Camelot, repel invader hordes, and quest for the Holy Grail. Through their choices, players sculpt a unique narrative and unlock new modules until the grail is discovered, and a winner is crowned high king!

The game features dozens of silkscreened wood pieces, a huge fully illustrated game board, and a 3D castle that players build during play. Multiple game modules allow for high variability and replayability across many aspects of Arthurian myth, with the intertwining of themes and mechanisms allowing players to organically create their own spin on these classic legends.

name: History of the World
description:
History of the World retells the story of humanity, starting from ancient Sumeria and ending with modern day USA. The map emphasizes those lands where civilizations flourished, with over sixty peoples featured on empire and event cards.

Capitals, cities, monuments, and forts are brought into play and then, just as quickly, are reduced by the armies of rivals. Control of buildings and lands enables players to collect gold. Whosoever has the most gold at game's end wins.

Compared to earlier editions of History of the World, this edition:

• Allows you to play with or without dice rules.
• Has a different distribution of empire cards and event cards
• Features new event cards and gold collection mechanisms
• Allows for a new "area tokens" strategy
• Includes new "honor tokens" that provide benefits
• Has a new player array

In general, the spirit of the game has been left intact, while incorporating elements from the earliest editions of the game as well as later developments. "Catastrophe", for example, has now become an honor, and "Weaponry", which was always too strong an event, has been removed.

—description from the publisher

name: HISTORY: Through the Years
description:
What year was the first polio vaccination given? Was it before or after the end of the Vietnam War?

How to play:
DRAW AN ANCHOR CARD - Draw the top card of the Years deck and reveal the year on the back – this is the anchor card for the round.
ARRANGE NUMBERS IN ORDER - Either cooperatively or competitively, players attempt to place a series of Cards in the correct order in their timelines in relation to the anchor card.
REVEAL & SCORE! - Score points by placing as many events as possible in the correct chronological order - either win or lose as a team, or crush your competition!

name: Tabriz
publisher: Crafty Games; Arclight Games; Bumble3ee Interactive; Matagot; Pendragon Game Studio; Reflexshop; Rosiness
description:
Step into the Grand Bazaar of Tabriz and become a legendary master weaver! From Randy Flynn, the designer of Cascadia, Tabriz blends elegant engine-building with accessible strategy and a rich, cultural setting that comes alive on your table.

Gather rare materials like silk, camel hair, and plant dye as you weave exquisite Persian rugs to fulfill commissions and earn prestige. Use your three assistants to navigate a bustling bazaar, time your moves with shifting market prices, and build a powerful action engine that grows with every rug you complete.

Tabriz offers intuitive mechanics, satisfying progression, and multiple solo AIs for deep replayability. Tabriz is your next relaxing-yet-clever strategy favorite!

name: Hitster Rock: Bob!
description: The Hitster version with an exclusive collection of famous rock songs and classics compiled by Germany's Rock Radio Bob!

name: Hitster: 100% en Español
description:
Hitster 100% in Spanish: Take the fun to the max! With over 300 hit songs and a free app, this card game is ideal for adults who love board games and music. To win you must be the first player to put 10 songs in chronological order.

Hitster 100% en Español: ¡Lleva la diversión al máximo! Con más de 300 éxitos musicales y una app gratuita, este juego de cartas es ideal para adultos que aman los juegos de mesa y la música. Para ganar debes ser el primer jugador en ordenar cronológicamente 10 canciones.

name: Hitster: Celebration
description:
This exclusive edition combines Hitster fans' favorite songs with current hits in one exclusive edition – thanks to high-quality wooden cards and tiles. Arrange the songs in the correct chronological order to win, or combine them with other Hitster editions for endless party fun.
Contents: 308 cards with hits and 30 tiles to increase your chances of winning.

name: Hitster: Platinum Edition
description:
Experience the most comprehensive Hitster version yet! This exclusive Platinum Edition contains over 500 songs – 350 of them brand new – and combines cult classics, current hits, luxurious playing materials, a premium box design, and a speaker for brilliant, immersive sound. This limited edition is perfect for true music lovers. Play it on its own or combine it with other Hitster editions for endless musical fun – the ultimate playlist for any party!

—description from the publisher (translated)

Erlebt die bisher umfassendste Hitster-Version! Diese exklusive Platin-Edition enthält über 500 Songs – davon 350 brandneu – und kombiniert Kult-Songs, angesagte Hits, luxuriöses Spielmaterial, ein hochwertiges Boxdesign und einen Lautsprecher für brillanten, immersiven Sound. Diese Limited Edition ist perfekt für echte Musikliebhaber. Spielt sie für sich allein oder kombiniert sie mit anderen Hitster-Editionen für endlosen Musikspaß – die ultimative Playlist für jede Feier!

—description from the publisher

name: Hitstory
description:
The DJ flips the top card, scans its code, and the music kicks off on Spotify. While the music plays, everyone uses their vinyl disc to guess the song's release year. Best guess wins the card, and if the player can name the artist and song, they activate the card's special action.

Contents: 300 music cards, 60 karaoke cards, 8 date-setting vinyl discs, and a free Hitstory application for Android & iOS.

name: Hockey Hardware: The Original Game
description:
Hockey Hardware is a tabletop game made for hockey fans, gamers, and fantasy hockey GMs, but anyone can play, have fun, and win. No hockey knowledge or experience is needed.  This game is socially interactive, competitive, and unpredictable. No two games are the same, and no lead is safe. Players must use a combination of luck and strategy to win.

At the start of the game, take on the role of a hockey player. You will start as either a Forward on Line 2 or as a Defense on Pair 2 in either the East or West Conference.

On your turn, collect as many hockey stats as you can by rolling dice, avoiding Adversity, and strategically playing Game Cards. Game Cards reflect different hockey actions that can help you get ahead or push your opponents back.

The more hockey stats you collect, the more likely you will earn different Trophy Cards. Players compete for 11 Trophy Cards throughout the game, which consists of 15 rounds divided into 3 periods and 2 intermissions in a Game Schedule.

The player with the most Trophy Cards by the end of the Third Period earns the Champion's Cup and wins the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Hodge Podge Dodgeball
description:
Hodge Podge Dodgeball exists in the small village of Longcoat, England where raccoons are competing in their Dodgeball League Championship!

Players try to dodge getting hit (taking a trick) in this avoidance, team, must-not-follow trick-taker.

At the start of the round, players create their bench with their cards. Then they play tricks which entail any amount of catching, dodging, or blocking balls. Players must be careful, as their hand of cards is their life and if they are hit, they must send a card (a raccoon) to their bench. If a player is out of cards or cannot make a valid play, their team loses!

—description from the designer

name: Hold the Line: Hannibal
description:
Hold the Line: Hannibal is a grand tactical two-player game covering 10 of the greatest battles of the Punic Wars. Following in the footsteps of Richard Borg’s Commands and Colors system and more directly Worthington’s Hold the Line series, Hannibal includes the same standard size map board, 13 hexes wide and 9 hexes deep. Combat is resolved with custom dice.

—description from the publisher

name: Sqwürmish
description:
The Grimm Parasites have overtaken most of the universe -- würms released from their desolate planet to spread as a plague throughout humanity, twisting us into zombified mutants. But that was 663 years ago. Those still alive band together in Crews.

Clawing toward another day. Scraping together credits in what time the ’verse has left.

Sqwürmish is a stand-alone tabletop skirmish miniatures game by Brian Colin (Vast Grimm) with miniatures by Sól Blair (Malevolent Minis). Build your crew from our line of minis, or kit-bash your own version of a dismal faction.

Set in the Vast Grimm universe, it is a full hack of the Forbidden Psalm miniatures games and is inspired by and fully compatible with the MÖRK BORG.

—description from the publisher

name: Arkham Travel Guide
description:
Arkham Travel Guide is a roll-and-write game where you explore the grim, narrow streets of Arkham, filled with Curio shops, mysterious Gates, and Horrible places. But you’re not just an unfortunate citizen, investigator, or cultist… In this game, you take on the role of a travel guide, creating tour routes through a city you probably know like the back of your hand.

During the game, players roll and collectively choose dice that determine where players can draw tourists and chart routes. This way players have a fair degree of control over the randomness of dice, and can strategize.

Your goal is to create a route with as many tourists and landmarks of different types as possible, because they score you victory points. Before the end of the game, you will be confronted by one of the Old Ones: Cthulhu, Yog-Sothoth, Dagon or Shub-Niggurath. Depending on how well you avoided Horrible places and used special abilities provided by otherworldly creatures, you either gain rewards or lose tourists.

At the end of the game, tourists and attractions in city blocks along your route earn you victory points. You also get victory points for Personal Objectives and Old Ones’ rewards. The player with the most victory points wins the game!

name: Echoes of Time
publisher: Cranio Creations; 999 Games; CrowD Games; Feuerland Spiele; Game Harbor; Intrafin Games; Lucky Duck Games; TLAMA games; Tranjis Games
description:
In a fantastic and untouched land, four factions govern different aspects of this world: the ocean depths with their dark abysses, the gentle hills with windy meadows and protected forests, the vast and endless expanses of the night skies, and the mysterious and unexplored underground tunnels.

An ancient and powerful energy flows through these places, concentrating in hidden, inexhaustible sources. Controlling this power allows one to bend to their will life's most important aspect: time, and the rhythms it imprints on the environment and every being.

Echoes of Time is a strategic game for 2-4 players in which you attempt to create the best-equipped fellowship of characters from different factions to conquer the sources of power. Try to control and modify the flow of time to outshine your opponents. The game includes more than one hundred cards with unique effects that you will use to build a new deck each game, and a "sliding tile" system guides you in managing the time needed for your cards to become usable, while simultaneously controlling the activation rhythm of their effects.

—description from the publisher

name: En Route
description:
People love traveling. We want to meet new cultures, see famed landmarks with our own eyes and taste the world cuisine. One of the most pleasant ways to explore a new city is just going for a walk. But how to chart a tour route that satisfies everyone? There’s an answer!

En Route is a flip-and-write game in which you create tour routes to the most interesting landmarks of the real-world cities (London, New York City, Hong Kong, Paris, Cairo, and Rio de Janeiro) and the made-up First City packed full of geek references. Every city features basic and specific mechanisms, so all of them play and feel differently.

Cards are not flipped randomly — instead, an active player plays one card face up, and two players next to them secretly choose one card each. Then, an active player selects one of the two and discards the other. After that, all players use coordinates and other information from the two cards left on the table to draw their tourists and routes.

During the game, route segments are drawn, connecting different types of tourists to various landmarks and attractions. A game of En Route lasts exactly 10 rounds. At the end of the game, each place of interest on the final route will earn players Prestige Points according to its rules. Whoever creates the most satisfying tour route, wins!

The game features constant and quite intense player interaction, and players have a fair degree of control and can strategize. It plays fast, dynamic, and makes you constantly think about what your opponents want to do (and sometimes even negotiate so that they play cards that are beneficial to you!).

name: Hollywood Dream
description:
In Hollywood Dream, players enter the glamorous and competitive world of filmmaking. You'll acquire scripts, recruit actors, secure special effects and equipment, and race to release award-winning movies. Strategic planning, timing, and adaptability are key.  The gameplay will feel familiar to fans of Viticulture. Drawing inspiration from that title, Hollywood Dream introduces fresh mechanics and new layers of decision-making aimed at enhancing the worker placement experience.

At the beginning of the game, players choose two out of four unique investors — similar in spirit to Terraforming Mars' Prelude cards — each offering different starting resources and a preferred film genre. Matching your released films to those genre preferences will earn you bonus victory points.

The game revolves around acquiring and completing high-value Movie Scripts, utilizing auctions, managing bonuses, and aiming for Academy Awards in Rounds 3 and 5. Multiple strategic paths are available — whether you're pushing ahead with risky loans (which carry end-game penalties) or playing it safe and steady, there's room for various play styles.

—description from the designer

name: HOMALET
description:
What is the setting?

In ancient Far East lands, military commanders value honor above all. They compete and cooperate, seeking allies from powerful outside warriors when their nations' forces are limited. The most trusted commanders on the battlefield will be remembered as the most honorable.

What is the goal?

Players collect "Honor" by playing cards on the battlefield. Earn bonus points by creating sets with the same numbers or sequences. The highest point-scorer wins.

How do you play?

Players play cards to the Battlefield (IKUSABA) or Reserve (RONIN) areas. On the Battlefield, the players who have played the most cards of the same color form the winning faction and gain Honor (points). In the Reserve, players with lower-numbered cards can select sets of cards to strengthen their hand.

Season-marked cards trigger special effects that can influence gameplay. The game ends when two or more players have empty hands. Earn points for each card you acquire, with additional bonuses for collecting matching numbers or sequences.

—description from the publisher

name: HOME
description:
HOME is a bone-chilling paranormal investigation game that fits in a mint tin!

The house stands silent, but you are not alone. As a paranormal investigator, you've come to uncover the truth. Identify the ghost, withstand the terror, and cleanse the house of its haunting. Keep your wits sharp, your flashlight steady, and pray you make it out alive.

In HOME, you assume the role of a paranormal investigator, tasked with cleansing a haunted house of its ghostly inhabitant.

Armed with your ghost hunting equipment and a flashlight, you make your way through the dark house, room by room, discovering items, clues, and evidence in order to identify, locate, and expel the ghost. You must be cautious as your flashlight batteries drain quickly, paranormal events test your sanity, and deadly hunts force you to run and hide as the ghost chases you throughout the house.

Once you have gathered enough evidence, found the unique mementos tied to the ghost's former living self, and discovered the room that the ghost is haunting, you must perform a cleansing ritual to rid the house of the apparition once and for all!

—description from the designer

name: Feudum: Septennial Edition
description:
Blimey! You and your blokes have been banished and stripped of everything but a few shillings and table scraps. Undaunted, you journey to a strange land to reinvent yourself and reclaim your honor. Will you farm the earth, fight as knights or finagle your own feudums?

Feudum (latin for fiefdom) is an economic medieval game of hand and resource management for 1-6 players. With many strategies at their disposal, players optimize four actions per turn in attempt to score the most victory points over five epochs.

In celebration of Feudum's 7th anniversary, The Septennial Edition comes with:

     Metal Clockwork Behemoth
     Feudum Septennial Card Sleeves (50)
     Art Print Mini Replica
     Embroidered Septennial Haversack
     Septennial Turn Order Coin
