     Flying Epoch Marker in Copper
     Septennial Strategy Cards (5)
     Three Punchboard Coins in "10s" (3)
     Score Track Counters (6)
     Royal Writ Compendium
     Royal Writ Cards (15)
     ''Alter Ego'' Expansion
     ''The Queen’s Army'' Expansion

name: Horizonte
description:
In Horizonte, two simultaneous tricks will be played: the Dragon Trick (represented by the sky, where the higher number wins) and the Hound Trick (represented by the earth, where the lower number wins).

Players need to predict the horizon, which is the difference between the number of Dragon Tricks and Hound Tricks they will win.

—description from the designer

name: Horrible Couple
description:
Horrible Couple is an unfiltered couples card game about love, laughs, and terrible decisions. Created by The Oatmeal and Exploding Kittens, it turns romance into ridiculous three-panel comics where the best (or worst) punchline wins. You can play cooperatively to test your connections or competitively to see who comes up with the funniest ending.

How To Play:

     You'll compete to create a love story fit for a classic dark comedy. 
     Build purposefully ridiculous comics starting with a Question card, then a Response card, and topped off with a ludicrous Compromise card. 
     Play as a couple or with friends, cooperatively or competitively. Nothing says date night like a little chaos!
     No Couple? No Problem: You can play with just two or add up to eight degenerates who don’t mind laughing at love gone wrong.


—description from the publisher

name: Feya's Swamp
publisher: Fractal Juegos; 2Tomatoes Games; 999 Games; Cranio Creations; CrowD Games; Grail Games; HIT Games; Muduko; Strohmann Games; YOKA Games; 株式会社ケンビル (KenBill)
description:
In Feya's Swamp, you take on the role of a clan of swamp dwellers aiming to become the most prosperous in the area. To succeed, you need to adapt to your surroundings by finding the best fishing and settlement spots, as well as choosing the right trading partners. You can also venture into nearby abandoned temples where powerful deities lie in wait to be awakened.

The game takes place over four rounds, with each round consisting of three phases: the income phase, the turn phase, and the maintenance phase. During the turn phase, you use unique characters to position your clan's workers in order to take various actions that help you gain victory points and gain advantages over the other players.

You take actions by moving your boats across the swamp, and these actions include fishing, trading with other clans, exploring abandoned temples in Feya, and building new settlements that will enhance your clan's abilities. Some actions don't require moving through the swamp, such as improving your navigation, which increases your boat speed; hosting festivals where each clan contributes fish to earn victory points; or building new cult spaces that bring prestige to the small islands that form in the swamp.

The main objective is to become the clan that contributes the most to the development of Feya, and to achieve this, you will also need to meet the variable goals specific to each game session.

Feya's Swamp includes an advanced mode in which each clan has unique abilities that introduce a certain level of asymmetry in the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Hot Dog
description:
Hot Dog is a trick-taking game that asks: why do hot dogs come in packs of 6, but buns come in packs of 8??

Each card in the deck has two different values: the dog value and the bun value.

When you or the player across from you leads a trick, you’ll play your cards for their dog value. When the other players lead a trick, use the bun value instead.

Earn the most points by winning an equal number of tricks with dogs and buns.

—description from the publisher

name: Hot Pot
description:
When your parents tell you to cook your own food.

Hot Pot, also called Steam Boat or 火鍋, brings friends and family together over a simmering feast. All the cards are dealt out evenly amongst the players. Players take turn loading up the pot with their favourite ingredients, such as shiitake mushrooms, pork belly, wombok and crabsticks. Keep an eye on what's cooking and scoop them up before anyone else. Wait too long and you might end up with nothing! There's a few action cards thrown into the mix, to spice things up. Stop! It's not cooked yet! Timing is everything if you want to enjoy the perfect meal.

Sharing is caring, but in this game, winning is tastier!

—description from the publisher

name: For a Crown
publisher: Repos Production; CrowD Games; Gém Klub Kft.; Hobby Japan; Rebel Sp. z o.o.; Tower Tactic Games
description:
Coming from noble families, you are ready to do anything to accede to the throne...except that the competition between the pretenders is fierce!

For a Crown is a single-deck, deck-building game. Players recruit new characters, such as mercenaries, then place these cards within a sleeve of their own color. All cards — individual player cards and common event cards — are shuffled into a single deck, which is then drawn card by card, with the relevant player resolving the effect of their card when it's revealed.

After four rounds, the player with the most rubies wins.

name: HotShot Pickleball
description:
HotShot Pickleball is a fast-paced, pun-filled board game where you play a version of pickleball -  as pickles!

After picking a pickle like Kim Chee, Sally Kraut, Stewcumber, or Baby Dill, each player draws five rally cards allowing you to move to, hit the ball, or take advantage of combos and unique actions.

The game is played by each side taking turns to play a card or combination of cards to get to the ball and hit it back over the net.

If players can't play their cards or just want to walk on the wild side, they can pull from the Long Shot deck, which if drawn they must play from. Some of these cards are great like slams, while others aren't so great, like negative self-talk.

The first team to reach 5 points wins. There are different rules available for full scoring to match the sport as well.

—description from the publisher

name: House of Fado
publisher: Eagle-Gryphon Games; CrowD Games; Delta Vision Publishing; Maldito Games; Tesla Games; TLAMA games; WindFans Games
description:
In Portugal, some restaurants serve traditional Portuguese food alongside performances of fado, a music genre that can be traced to the 1820s in Lisbon, Portugal and is often characterized by mournful tunes and lyrics, often about the sea or the life of the poor, while being infused with a sentiment of resignation, fate, and melancholy.

People spend their entire evenings in these restaurants, called Casa de Fado ("House of Fado"), dining and listening to the music, which speaks about "saudade", a Portuguese word meaning "longing, nostalgia, yearning, missing something or someone". Typically, there isn't any rotation of the tables. Once you enter the restaurant, you stay until it's closed.

In its traditional form, fado is played by a trio of musicians: a guitarist plays "Guitarra Portuguesa" (a twelve-string Portuguese Guitar); a singer,  that is, a "fadista"; and a guitarist playing "Viola de Fado" (classical guitar). The Portuguese guitar has a unique sound, and the chords are played in different bars from those of the classical guitar.

In the game House of Fado, players have to manage their restaurant, attract customers, and contract and promote fadistas and musicians, thus gaining prestige for their fado house. Managers will move their staff members to different places to perform some actions, using the same bump action as in The Gallerist.

name: House of Cards
description:
In the hidden corridors of power, every favor counts.

Polls may sway the nation’s pulse, but behind every result lie public deals, secret betrayals, and unexpected alliances.

You are the leader of a political faction striving to increase your political capital while dodging scandals, outmaneuvering your rivals, and manipulating public perception.

Manage your resources with cunning, deploy key allies at just the right moment, anticipate your opponents’ moves, and adapt your strategy to the sudden shifts provoked by powerful figures.

Only those who master the delicate dance between influence and political capital will rise victorious in this ruthless game of ambition and strategy.

Welcome to House of cards.

—description from the designer

name: INK
publisher: Final Score Games; asmodee; CrowD Games; Hobby Japan; Rebel Sp. z o.o.; Yellowstar Games
description:
Ink is an unforgiving medium. However, when mastered with care, its spontaneity and brilliance can create visual effects of astonishing richness.

INK invites you to deploy your talent by creating sumptuous paintings worthy of the greatest collections.

Combining tile placement, resource and hand management, and pattern recognition, Ink challenges players to complete high-value contracts by carefully placing ink tiles to form harmonious patterns. The trick lies in balancing spontaneity with planning, every move you make affects not only your current canvas, but the options you'll have in future turns.

name: Innsmouth Travel Guide
description:
Innsmouth is a town forgotten by time, swallowed by shadows and decay. Its once-grand streets lie deserted, and its bustling harbor is all but consumed by the raging sea. The air stinks of salt and rot, and no sane person would willingly come here — especially knowing what stirs beneath the waves. And yet… here you are, tasked with guiding curious tourists through this murky, treacherous place.

In Innsmouth Travel Guide, you play as a bold (or perhaps reckless) tour guide charting the eeriest sightseeing route imaginable. Tourists are eager to see the town’s haunted landmarks — but cultists and Deep Ones prowl the shadows, ready to snatch them away. Balancing risk and reward is key: the more you expose your group, the more points you might score… or lose. Innsmouth Travel Guide follows Arkham in an innovative roll-and-write series inspired by En Route.

Each round, players roll chunky 20mm custom dice and collectively choose which to use, drawing routes and tourists on laminated maps, while reacting to the evolving game state and each other's decisions. The game includes five playable characters, each with unique abilities and scoring bonuses. You can all play the same character or enjoy a fully asymmetric experience.

Ancient artifacts, hidden tourists, and a shifting threat system add tension and tactical depth to every choice you make. Navigate the dangers, outsmart the lurking horrors, and claim victory as the most successful tour guide Innsmouth has ever seen.

—description from the publisher

name: Onward
description:
Onward is the spiritual successor to Skytear, the competitive card-driven game inspired by MOBA video games such as League of Legends or DOTA2.

Players split into two teams, with each player controlling two or more champions.

The goal of the game is to destroy the enemy nexus that is a portal in the enemy base.

The game takes 45 to 90 minutes depending on the map that can have two or three lanes.

Lanes are corridors connecting the two nexuses and are populated with towers and minions from both teams.

Towers are defense structures preventing enemy champions and minions from rushing into the nexus.

Minions are weak units that grow in strength as they increase in number. They always try to advance toward the enemy nexus and attack any enemy in their way.

Jungles are dangerous areas between lanes where champions can venture to defeat monsters to gain gold and buy powerful items.

The river is a central area where your champions can go fight the colossal outsider... or die trying!

—description from the publisher

name: Hubris: Twilight of the Hellenistic World 220-165 BCE
description:
Hubris: Twilight of the Hellenistic World places players in the shoes of the 2nd century BC Hellenistic kings, heirs to the famous Successors who fought over Alexander the Great's empire for more than 40 years, into their dotage. The world they are living in is different in many ways as, under the Macedonian kings, the Eastern Mediterranean has experienced a boost in urban life and an unprecedented sharing and cross-fertilization of culture, but the dominant theme remains major powers' rivalries and endemic warfare.

In those years, even though the great kingdoms of the Lagids (Ptolemies), Seleucids and Antigonid Macedon have been established for 80 years or more, power remains a very personal endeavour, with everything revolving around the king, and he himself having to rely on his entourage of family members, childhood friends, and veteran advisers to conduct state affairs, whether leading armies, undertaking diplomatic missions, or governing provinces.

Even though the great kings are fixated on their rivals, the world around them has been changing, both from within, where minor kingdoms such as Pergamon have been pushing for a space at the table, and leagues of Greek cities are offering a new challenge to century-old Macedonian hegemony, and from without where, beyond the ever present Barbarian incursions from the savage North, new powers have been flexing their muscles both in the Western Mediterranean and Central Asia...

The times for a final push for final triumph, or descent into irrelevancy, are near...

—description from the publisher

name: Huddle: The Fantasy Football Game
description:
Ever wanted to bring the electrifying energy of fantasy football straight to your game night? Huddle does just that! Step into the shoes of a team manager, where you're not just cheering from the sidelines—you’re calling the shots. Draft your dream team, make those game-changing decisions, and navigate the unpredictable twists of the season. It's all the excitement of football without having to leave your living room (or deal with muddy cleats).

Designed for 2-6 players aged 14 and up, Huddle kicks off with a fast-paced draft. You've got a budget and a mission: build the strongest team possible. Bid wisely, because every token counts, and you'll need a full roster to compete. As the weeks unfold, dynamic news cards keep everyone on their toes—think surprise injuries, unexpected comebacks, and everything in between. Face off in head-to-head matchups by rolling dice that represent your players' performances. Manage your lineup, exploit the waiver wire, and maybe, just maybe, outsmart your opponents.

The endgame? Outplay and outscore your friends to become the ultimate Huddle Champion! Navigate through the season with the best record to secure your spot in the championship showdown. It's all about strategy, a bit of luck, and a whole lot of fun. So grab some snacks, gather your crew, and get ready to experience fantasy football like never before. Game night just got a lot more interesting!

—description from the publisher

name: Hungry Birds
description:
As a ranger, feed wild birds efficiently and attract them to your avian sanctuary. But be careful; sheltering more than three bird species from the same habitat will harm the ecosystem. The player who collects the most birds from a variety of habitats wins!

Hungry Birds is a strategy game where you feed adorable birds with colorful food tokens and compete for points. Blending Mancala mechanics with clever set collection, it offers the perfect mix of cuteness and strategy for players of all ages.

Players choose food tokens, play Mancala, and get cards that have been given the number of pieces of food that the bird is requesting. There's no problem using your own food to get cards, but if you use another player's food tokens to take a card, that player will receive points equal to the number of pieces of food used.

The player who collects the most valuable cards and achieves the highest total score, calculated by adding the points from their cards and the food, will be the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Hunt A Killer x Sam and Colby: The Haunting at Wicker Ridge
description:
Sam and Colby have been working with the Scientific Organization for Unexplained Phenomena, SOUP, to try to identify and banish a demon haunting the Wicker Ridge house, but when strange forces drive them out, they turn to you for help.

Be the Paranormal Investigator, banish the demon and bring peace to Wicker Ridge.

Tired of dull nights? We know how to get your blood pumping! Wrap your hands around Hunt A Killer x Sam And Colby: The Haunting At Wicker Ridge. It's got screams, it's got spirits, and you'll definitely make some questionable decisions. So, you know, an upgrade You're gonna be grave-deep in a paranormal investigation. There’s mystery, there’s unexplainable activity, and a demon. It’s the perfect activity for date night, friend night, or after you've finished binging a true crime series. This isn't your average party game. It’s a dark, twisted story puzzle wrapped in a haunted mystery. This game is great for people who actually enjoy using their brains and don't mind chasing down a demon. You're the detective now. Try not to die. Inside the box are realistic clues, creepiness, and the overwhelming sense that something is watching you. Outside the box: still in your living room with the greatest feeling of solving a mystery. This game is ideal for anyone who wants to feel like they've stepped into a haunted true crime documentary. It’s creepy. It’s smart. It's a Haunting At Wicker Ridge. It's the ideal game of choice for anybody who's really into horror games, group games, party games for adults, likes discovering suspicious souls, and ultimately wants to start some drama in the most haunted way possible. Invite your friends, light a candle (preferably black), and banish an evil presence. If you can make it out alive, case closed.

An Immersive Paranormal Experience: Perfect for fans of the supernatural and problem-solving enthusiasts alike, this whodunit lets you play ghost hunter with realistic evidence.

You Are A Paranormal Detective: Sam and Colby need a hand with the unsolved mysteries at Wicker Ridge. Here's the mission: investigate, banish a demon, and don't get possessed.

Haunted House In A Box: Use realistic clues and evidence like a ghost comm box (hear the ghosts, ooooh), a planchette, and a forgotten journal to help fight a devilish entity and survive the haunting.

Exclusive Collaboration: Hunt A Killer teamed up with YouTubers Sam and Colby in this mystery game of paranormal proportions!

Difficulty: 1/5

—description from the publisher

name: Hunt A Killer: Game Night Gone Wrong
description:
Connor’s murder mystery birthday party goes wrong when the game ends abruptly, his roommate is dead, and he must decide which of his friends is the killer.

Be the detective and help Connor prove his innocence.

Put your detective skills to the test with Game Night Gone Wrong, a gripping true crime board game from Hunt A Killer. A party turns deadly—and it’s up to you to figure out who did it, how, and why. Examine realistic evidence, analyze witness statements, and uncover hidden motives in this mystery game designed for solo or group play.

Difficulty 3/5

—description from the publisher

name: Hunt A Killer: Killer Next Door
description:
You Can't Trust Anybody: Figure out which of your friends are lying in this quick card game of bluffing and betrayal where you need to deduce the killer amongst you before the whole community perishes.

Nobody really likes HOAs (not sorry if you're someone who does). However, one of your neighbors just died, there’s a killer among you, and now you have to lean on your neighbors to solve the problem. With Hunter A Killer: Killer Next Door, murder is about to get m-e-s-s-y.

Setup is so easy, even your HOA President could do it! Get a group of friends together, distribute roles, and try to save or kill the neighborhood in this fast-paced social deduction game.

One of your friends is definitely the culprit, but it might not be who you suspect. Like your sketchy, quiet, and sheepish neighbor? Surprisingly not. Anyway, somebody's bluffing a little too HARD. If you can't group up and single out who it is, everyone might just end up dead. Totally low stakes.

It’s your job to trust no one and question everything. Play fast and interrogate hard.

It's also the ideal game of choice for anybody who's really into horror games, group games, date night, party games for adults, likes discovering suspicious neighbors, or just wants to start some friendly community drama.

So grab your friends and solve this fast-paced mystery game. Bluff, betray, and leave no lie unsolved in this card game full of murder in the most satisfying degree. Case closed.

How to Play:

     Players lay a "Gift" or a "Grudge" card face down on a Neighbor.
     3 Gifts save a Neighbor; 3 Grudges kill a Neighbor.
     Pay attention to what cards other players are playing.
     Vote to reveal the Killer before it's too late.


—description from the publisher

name: Hunt A Killer: Lakeside Slaughter – The Last Vacation
description:
Security systems analyst Ryan Bosley and his wife, Monica, book a vacation rental home by a lake to relax and reconnect for a month. But after the couple gets into an argument at a neighbor's cookout, Monica finds herself alone in their dark and empty rental house.

When Ryan sees Monica again, she's in a pool of her own blood, dead. The police suspect Ryan, but he believes another guest at the cookout is the killer.

Can you unravel the relationships around the lakeside housing community and clear Ryan's name?

Difficulty 2/5

—description from the publisher

name: Hunted: Transylvania / Escape from Route 52
description:
2 solo games packaged in 1 box!

Hunted: Transylvania is a card-only survival game that features an expanded yet streamlined version of the Hunted system.

As you work your way through the deck, you'll encounter a slew of classic monsters, from the Wolf Man to Frankenstein’s monster, all while rescuing survivors, salvaging what weapons you can, and, of course, trying not to make too much noise.  Survive long enough to make it through the deck twice to get to the finale, where you’ll face off against one of multiple different sets of big bads, such as the infamous Count Dracula and his devoted brides. But if your health ever goes to zero, you'll just be another headstone in the Transylvania graveyard.

Escape from Route 52 is a rogue-like card game where you have to escape a dangerous and haunted road.

The deck consists of 52 cards, each not only representing the situations and threats along the road, but also the weapons and equipment needed to deal with them. Each round, you'll deal with 4 cards at a time in search of the resources necessary to fix your truck, leave the hateful road in the rearview, and win the game. But if your health ever goes to zero, you'll just be another victim of Route 52.

name: Pax Hispanica
publisher: Ion Game Design; Sierra Madre Games; CrowD Games; Ediciones MasQueOca; Galakta
description:
You are a Spanish, English, French, Dutch, or Courish lad with a life goal to become a great courtier, emancipator, or pirate of the Caribbean. It’s the 17th century, so the decadent Spanish crown owns everything, the inquisition hears everyone, the black market is everywhere, and nowhere is safe from the pillaging of the buccaneers. You sail annually among the islands to transport, plunder, smuggle, or ambush boatloads of silver, pearls, gems, and priceless relics intended to finance the ambitions of the crown.

This is an asymmetrical game of ship battles and treachery. The mechanics are similar to other Pax games, with a Tableau, Market, blind Auction, and 4 different career choices and victories. The future of the Spanish Main will be set by the choices you make.

—description from the publisher

name: Sinister Institute
description:
Building a teenage-full wizardry college in the middle of a cursed swamp didn't seem a bad idea, somehow. At least, not until the Evil Sorcerer showed up with his little minions, craving total annihilation and with no teachers to defend you in sight! Take on the mission and defeat the Evil Sorcerer by collecting and destroying the pieces of his cursed soul to save your beloved school and get the teachers to give you an A++ in the subject "Dealing with Ancient Evils."

In Sinister Institute, players will work co-operatively to complete Rituals in order to defeat the Evil Sorcerer. You’ll explore the School and the Swamp that surrounds it, by flipping the tiles and moving on them, and collect the Items you’ll find scattered around this world. Each Ritual is worth a certain amount of points and, once completed, you score it by reducing the health of the Evil Sorcerer on the Points board.

Bring the health of the Evil Sorcerer down to zero before the Story deck runs out or all the Minions are placed to win the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Hybrid War
description:
War is raging again in Europe, after the invasion of Ukraine in 2022. But another type of warfare is happening in the shadows: hybrid war.

Hybrid warfare, also called 'grey zone' or 'sub-threshold' warfare, is when a hostile state carries out an anonymous, deniable attack, usually in highly suspicious circumstances. It will be enough to harm their opponent, especially their infrastructure assets, but stop short of being an attributable act of war (source: BBC). The aim of hybrid warfare is to disrupt, sabotage, and weaken cohesion among Western allies.

Hybrid War is a solitaire war game. You will control three Western (WEST) secret service agents, as they seek to detect and disrupt enemy hybrid war actions. The game will control the non-player faction, consisting of three Russian (RUSS) secret service agents.

Victory Conditions
The WEST faction (you, the player) win the game if the Disruption counter has not reached the ‘10’ space on the disruption track when the game ends after 7 game turns. The game ends with Russian victory if the disruption counter reaches the ‘10’ space on the disruption track.

This game is a low ink prototype entry in the 2026 Print and Play Wargame Design contest.

—description from the designer

name: Hybris: Twilight in Olympus
description:
100 years after the events of Hybris, Disordered Cosmos, Ancient Greece is once again in turmoil: no Aegis remains and the Achaeans, led by Zeus, attack the last stronghold of the Eye of Nyx artifact: Troy.

But this fortress is protected by other Olympians who wish to eradicate Zeus' madness - the city of Troy must not fall! But that's without counting on the observation of this legendary war by the Mystics, who choose no side and simply watch, impassive.

Hybris, Twilight in Olympus is an epic game of area control for 2 to 6 players, scheduled for crowdfunding in 2024.

The game is played in 10 rounds, corresponding to the 10-year siege of Troy. During a turn, each player secretly programs his actions through his own game system:


     The Achaeans program their actions using a card system
     The Trojans program their actions using a worker placement system.
     The Mystics program the potential actions of the other two players!


The action phase then starts, with the Achaean player revealing his first card, then spending a time value to carry out his action. The other players will use the Achaean's time value to carry out their actions.

The Achaeans win if Troy falls, either by breaking the wall, stealing the nyx eye, or if Troy falls economically before the 10 turns.
Trojans win if they survive 10 turns.
Mystics win if they achieve their secret objectives before either of the other two players win.

—description from the designer

name: Hydra
description:
Countless ships dance on the waves in the harbor of Arizont as life pulses through the city streets. There‘s a bustling crowd, with people from all corners of the known world trading and haggling over exotic spices, foods, and other treasures. But this idyllic scene is deceiving, for doom is already awakening, as the next lunar eclipse is imminent. Far out in the Maelstrom, the Hydra rises from its deep slumber. Four necks stretch out, countless heads raise, hungrily targeting Arizont. The city walls, once proud and solid, tremble under the looming threat as the beast charges relentlessly.

But this time, the story shall take a new turn. The Guild Council has sent out a call for aid in all directions, promising rewards of princely stature. Brave heroes have heeded this call. However, wealth and honor will be bestowed only upon those who can earn the city‘s admiration through courage and determination against the Hydra.

Thus, you too have found your way to Arizont. Your hearts burn with resolve to protect the city and return with pockets full of gold.

Together, you face off against the many-headed Hydra. But in this epic battle, each of you not only strives for the city‘s welfare, but also for the sole glory awarded to the triumphant victor in the end. Each of you will choose from available actions, block crucial cards with Action tokens, and formulate tactics - be it in combat against the Hydra, constructing defensive Barricades, or advancing into optimal attack positions. Yet, the Hydra retaliates, drawing insurmountable power from remaining action cards and the darkening moon.

The city‘s fate is in your hands. By standing united, you‘ll be hailed as true heroes. But only the best among you will go down in the city‘s history as an epic hero, weighed in gold. Are you this much-sung hero? Will you stand shoulder to shoulder, only to stab your comrade in the back when it counts? Beware, for they too are waiting for that moment.

—description from the publisher

name: Hydro Soakers
description:
Need to cool off in the hot summer sun? Splash into action with Hydro Soakers! A two player game where you compete in eliminating the opposing team.

Strategize your movement, upgrade your hydropack, and refill your water guns in this fast paced action hydration!

Play an exciting game of Hydro Soakers! Players go head to head controlling their teams of three athletes. Players will fire water guns, grab snacks, attempt to avoid getting wet by others and score eliminations. This skirmish style game makes you manage your water, choose the best time to attack and taunts you with when to grab some snacks off the buffet table.

Hydro Soakers is a fast action game where you don't want to get caught with an empty hydropack! Don't forget to fill up at the fill stations. Special events can either help you or hurt you so stay on guard. Play this unique water fight game with a friend and revisit your childhood of intense water battles. Grab your own copy of Hydro Soakers and you'll be glad you did.

- Tactical moves and strategic decisions.
                    
- Water Management - Don't get caught with an empty HydroPack. Manage your water by utilizing Water Fill Stations. 
                    
- Chow down on snacks in order to boost your abilities on the field
                    
- Watch out for special events. Some are good and some are bad.

name: Hyperdrive Odyssey
description:
Hyperdrive Odyssey is a space adventure game, mixing (literal) engine-building, trading, combat and exploration. Set in the “wild-west” of space you are guided by a choose-your-own-adventure style narrative through branching campaign missions to reach a dramatic conclusion!

This is a solo campaign-style space adventure using a few sheets and a handful of dice and tokens, and an adventure booklet/pdf.

Overview

In Hyperdrive Odyssey you will complete a series of missions, each with a different objective. Throughout the missions you will be travelling between planets and space stations: trading, upgrading your ship and fighting space pirates!

To do this you will need to manage Power (produced in the Hyperdrive) which is used to activate the ship systems (weapons, shields and engines,) and mine for natural resources.

The eponymous game module is the Hyperdrive engine: a circuit powered by ‘quantum energy’ dice. The dice move around the track, and each lap they complete the more energy they gain, and the faster they go. You can manipulate the dice to draw power from the engine to the other main systems on the ship.

As your engine spins up over the course of the game you have to carefully balance the actions you need to take each turn, and the amount of energy you need to hold back, to feed back into your engine.

The more you want to do on your turn, the higher the energy cost!

Over the course of a play-through there are branching paths to explore, and each of the missions has a different objective, from trading, exploring, fighting, fixing your ship and even a mystery to solve as you hunt around the galaxy for clues.

In addition to the solo missions are a series of multiplayer scenarios, ranging from a competitive economic sandbox to cooperative tower defense.

—description from the designer

name: Hyperspace
description:
Hyperspace is a fast-moving asymmetric strategy game about interstellar expansion. In it, you take the part of an interstellar civilization competing to control a newly-discovered star cluster! Construct your empire, fight for resources, and research technology. Each alien species has its own unique flaws and advantages, and victory lies in recognizing this. It takes place in a star cluster built up of individual pieces that changes every time you play.

The base game has four different alien civs from which to choose, but various expansions and add-ons increase this to 25 total alien Civs (one of which is secret, to be revealed during the Kickstarter campaign). The game does not have any sort of upkeep or victory phase. Instead, when it is a player's turn, they perform three actions, then play passes to the next player. This continues around and around until the game ends, by accumulation of victory points. Most actions cost metal or atomic resources, and include moving, building, research, combat, salvage, production, and so forth.

Driving the strategy are a player's need to advance along the victory tracks. These permit players to score points by advancing along Probe, Research, Industry, and Battle tracks (representing exploration, experimentation, expansion, and extermination).

name: Hyperstar Run
description:
You grab the well-worn controller and load your latest save. This is it: the final level. With only 4 runs left to escape the Hyperstar base and beat the game, you better get moving.

Master the final level by using your button cards to get past the dangerous enemies lurking in the Hyperstar base. As you advance, you’ll be able to access more button presses and set up powerful combos that extend across multiple cards. Complete each card in the level successfully to beat the game. You’ve got four chances to finish the level, so use the knowledge gained with each run to set yourself up for the win!

Select your difficulty and deal an appropriate number of random cards to create a level row with your hero card showing “1” above the leftmost level card. Create your starting hand of 3 level cards and 2 equipment cards. Flip the leftmost card in the row to start play. Advance through each successive level card by using buttons in your hand to defeat enemies. Buttons can be used by discarding cards from hand or from “pressing” buttons on previously-passed level cards by moving them down from the row. Beat either of the card’s enemies to move on to the next card. Level cards often have abilities that can be used to reveal information or allow you to manipulate the level to your advantage. Some cards also feature combo lines which can connect across multiple cards, allowing you to keep moving with only a single button usage per card.

Should you fail a level card, tick off one of your hero’s runs and start again. Reset your hand by taking back your discards and unpress any buttons in the level row, and draw the first card in the row into your hand. Complete all the level cards in the row without failing 4 runs to win the game!

For an extra challenge, the game includes 4 unique achievements. Earn every achievement to 100% the game!

name: Hüter des Schatzes
description: A chaotic dragon's lair full of gems, gold and treasures needs to be tidied up. Sort treasures, tame chaos and proceed tactically and cleverly in order to score points – an exciting and entertaining game that rewards skill and planning. Perfect for all treasure hunters and dragon lovers!

name: Speakeasy
publisher: Eagle-Gryphon Games; CrowD Games; Delta Vision Publishing; Korea Boardgames; Maldito Games; Portal Games; Skellig Games; Tesla Games; TLAMA games; YOKA Games
description:
Speakeasy will transport you to the roaring 1920s during the era of Prohibition. Manhattan was under the firm control of Lucky Luciano, a prominent mobster. To strengthen his grip on the territory, he implemented a well-structured system. He divided Manhattan into different districts, each assigned to a specific mobster responsible for handling their "business" operations.

In this worker-placement and card-management game, you take on the role of one of those mobsters, managing and operating your very own speakeasy empire in Manhattan. To do so, you'll need to use all your cunning and resources to stay ahead of the competition. As you improve your operation, become more infamous, and upgrade to more lavish speakeasies and even casinos, you'll attract the attention of the outside mafia and the police. You need to use your leverage to keep your business running and receive your share from Lucky Luciano.

You need to hire goons to help you take over Manhattan during this exciting and dangerous time. You can associate with outside mobsters — and even attack and rob rum runners to gain valuable resources to gain an edge over your rivals. You need to manage your cards carefully, placing your workers strategically to deliver illicit liquor and reach Manhattan's goals to earn income. You will cook your books to fill your safes with free tax money by achieving some goals.

The ultimate goal is simple: accumulate the most money and become the most successful mobster in the city. Do you have what it takes to rise to the top of the speakeasy scene and take over Manhattan during Prohibition? It's time to grab your fedora and find out in Speakeasy.

name: I Know…You Don't
description:
Can you crack the code? Take turns being the “Rule Keeper” who chooses the rule that everyone else must try to figure out.

Each card played is a clue, giving all players the chance to detect what the pattern might be. If you can crack the code, use it to shed your cards and win!

—description from the publisher

name: I Made You a Mixtape
description:
It’s the early 90s. Baggy jeans and flannel shirts reign supreme, and the unmistakable sound of dial-up internet fills the air. Dan DiLisio, the coolest kid in your neighborhood, is heading off to University, and is letting you and your school friends raid his beloved music collection before he goes.

In return he’s asked you to make him a mixtape for his road trip up to college.  To make things more interesting he's said that the kid who makes the best tape will win his Quantum Leap poster signed by Scott Bakula.

Man, you really want that poster…

“I Made You a Mixtape” is a I-split-you-choose card game where you will be competing with the other players to make the best compilation possible out of an album collection. Your tape will be judged on how well it’s themed, how the tracks flow with each other, and the balance of lengths between side A and side B.

-description from designer

name: Ibyron: Island of Discovery (2nd/3rd edition)
description:
A new land has emerged from the ashes of the old empire. Factions have risen to compete for the throne. Can you be the first to lay claim to the island of Ibyron?

Ibyron: Island of Discovery is a two-tiered worker placement game wherein players all work the land of a newly-discovered island to build the city the to its capacity. Using resource gathering, building construction, exploration and movement mechanisms for the Wilderness Phase, supported by an additive Worker Placement mechanism during the Village Phase, each player will design their own city; each building adding to options in game play.

Each player will start out in the Wilderness phase each round. Actions will consist of using workers tokens on the island tiles, some actions requiring 1 or more workers to be used to perform that action. Players will continue in the Wilderness phase until they run out workers to perform said actions. But if a player finishes their wilderness actions before others, they don't just sit around; they head into the Village phase and may get better placements for their workers on the Village board.

In the Village phase the players will use the same workers that worked for them in the Wilderness phase in this phase as well, but will instead perform money-making, shipbuilding, hiring horses, taxing, and farming actions. Each space in the village requires 1 more worker for each additional use, no matter the player. After the workers are again spent, they go into the rest box to wait to be paid to work again in the following round, in cash or food.

Each building that is constructed will require permanent residence i.e. worker tokens will be used as the building itself. Using worker tokens as buildings will cut down on a player's supply of workers available in following rounds, so knowing when to construct buildings is an important timing constraint.

There is a race to the end game, but getting there will support many strategies. The first player to build a complete working city (all but 1-3 worker tokens used in buildings), wins.

It was heavily inspired by the Splotter games: Roads & Boats and Antiquity. It was not designed to replace those games, but to deeply entrench you for a good 2 hours.

—description from the publisher

name: Sweet Lands
publisher: uchibacoya; CrowD Games; Devir; Pixie Games; Rosiness; Yellowstar Games
description:
Welcome to “Sweet Lands”, the kingdom of delightful confections! The former king has succumbed to his gluttonous love for sweets, leaving behind a final decree. Summoned by this royal edict, you and your fellow players are challenged to build the most magnificent city — and if you succeed, you will ascend as the new ruler of Sweet Lands. Gather the support of various townsfolk and navigate through fierce competition to create the richest and most prosperous city of sweets!

Sweet Lands is a heavyweight Euro-style game with over 200 cards, 14 unique characters, and 449 wooden tokens. During the game, each player develops Cities on their Map Board whilst advancing on their Prosperity Tracks. After 5 rounds, the game ends and the player with the most Victory Points is the winner!

—description from the publisher

name: Icefall
description:
In Icefall / アイスフォール, each player controls a pair of climbers — an older brother and a younger brother — and aims to climb to the top of a harsh ice wall while competing against other players.

You need to decide whether to let the older or younger brother climb according to the cards that are dealt in each round, but there may be times when you are in danger of falling or cannot proceed well. Sometimes it is important to replenish chocolate bars to conserve your energy. Which player will be the first to get the brothers to the top?

name: Under the Leaves
publisher: Fractal Juegos; CrowD Games; Frosted Games; Grand Gamers Guild; Rocket Lemon Games
description:
If we are able to maintain the health and diversity of our garden, then it will fill up with life and become a refuge for fascinating creatures. Hummingbirds and bees are the first to arrive, filling the air with color and movement, but if we stop and observe with more attention, we will discover a hidden and unknown world: tiny inhabitants abound in the mushrooms, puddles, and foliage. They are under our feet, living out their lives without being perceived...until we decide to look under the leaves.

Each turn in Under the Leaves is played in two phases: the placement of a garden tile, then the possible arrival of new beings. Whoever gets the most pieces in total wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Iconic Neon Stories
description:
Iconic Neon Stories is a party game where players must use icons to create the most iconic stories. Can you quickly adapt and deal with your assignments?

How does the game work?
The game is played in rounds, with each round starting by giving all players five cards from the draw deck. The draw deck is made up completely of cards with icons on them.

The goal of the game is to create stories and make them as appealing to the group you are playing with, as everyone gets to vote for their favorite each round.

A round is played in three phases: Phase 1, Imagine and Swap. Phase 2, Narrate. Phase 3, Vote.

During the first phase (30 seconds), an icon card from the draw deck is turned open. This is the card that every story has to start with. Players then have the option to discard hand cards and draw new cards once.

During the second phase, all players have to tell their story. But at the start of their turn, another card from the draw deck is opened and this has to be the final card in their story.

After all players have narrated their story, players vote who told their favorite story. This player wins the round

—description from the publisher

name: Identity
description:
Being like everyone else is boring! In this trick-taking game, embracing your unique identity is the path to victory.
Each player secretly declares how many tricks they aim to win, even negative numbers are valid, by using two cards from their hand. Then comes the battle of bold plays, bluffing, and unpredictable results as players try to match their declared outcome.

Identity is a trick-taking game with a unique bidding system and a custom Must Not Follow rule. Each trick, players must play face-up cards that differ in both number and suit from cards already on the table — if they can. Otherwise, they may play a card face-down. Tricks are awarded either as “Plus Tricks” (for the highest number played) or “Minus Tricks” (for those who play face-down), and your final score depends on how close your result is to the victory count you declared at the start. The closer the match, the more points you score.

name: Winnie the Pooh: Serious Detective
description:
We all remember and love the stories we discovered as kids — especially when they’re just as rewarding to revisit as adults. And their original literary form isn't the only way to enjoy them. What if classic tales were reimagined as thrilling detective adventures?

Winnie the Pooh: Serious Detective is a narrative-driven board game in which players take on the roles of beloved childhood characters — now turned detectives — to solve challenging and often peculiar mysteries.

Inspired by the works of A. A. Milne, Lewis Carroll, and Arthurian legends, the game’s three scenarios are rich with literary charm, layered storytelling, clever wordplay, and just the right touch of whimsy. You’ll revisit the Hundred Acre Wood, Wonderland, and the court of Camelot — but not as you remember them. Something strange is afoot, and only a keen mind can uncover the truth.

Each case was illustrated by a different artist in their unique style.  The mysteries unfold across a beautifully illustrated map of interconnected location cards. Players use both shared and personal action dice to explore scenes, uncover clues, and reveal story cards — including testimonies, observations, puzzles, and more. Every discovery adds depth to the story and brings the group closer to cracking the case.

Though designed with adults in mind, the game is also accessible and engaging for younger players — making it a perfect choice for a family game night with a touch of mystery.

—description from the publisher

name: Dino Garden
description:
Dino Garden is a euro-style board game where each player becomes the owner of a thrilling dinosaur park, aiming to create a dinosaur park that is uniquely their own. Dino Garden is a standalone title in the Aqua Garden series, featuring charming wooden tokens and highly strategic gameplay.

Players bring wooden dinosaur tokens from the main board or the wasteland into their personal boards. They must decide where to place each dinosaur, considering limited space in each area, the food chain among species, and environmental features such as volcanoes and lakes.

Within the park, a unique ecosystem unfolds. Herbivorous dinosaurs produce meat as generations pass. Zookeepers rush around the park, delivering this meat to carnivorous dinosaurs. Feeding the carnivores efficiently is the key to victory.

Players must also pay attention to variable setup milestones.  By completing randomly generated milestone objectives, you can earn powerful bonus cards to support your strategy.

—description from the publisher

name: Imperial Elegy: The Road to the Great War 1850-1920
description:
Imperial Elegy: The Road  to the Great War 1850-1920 is a Strategic  level multi-player card-driven  board-wargame that blends diplomacy, warfare, and statecraft. Players take control of one of six unique major powers in the game: Germany/Prussia, the United Kingdom, France, Austria / Austria-Hungary, Russia and the Ottoman Empire.

IE takes place over 7 turns, with each turn representing a decade. If a GW occurs, the game can be extended by, at most, 6 additional shorter GW turns. 
A turn consists of numerous player impulses, during which players play action cards for their CP or events. Players will use CP and events to colonize, conduct diplomacy, fight wars, as well as hinder their opponents. 
A turn is over once all players have consecutively passed or when all players are out of cards.

Players take on the role of either Germany/ Prussia, the United Kingdom, France, Austria/Austria-Hungary, Russia, or the Ottoman Empire. Italy, should it unify, is not controlled directly by a player and instead interacts with the game using special rules.

Imperial Elegy was designed primarily as a 6 player game, but it can accommodate smaller player counts, including solitaire.

Players can win by fulfilling their individual National Goals and scoring Victory Points. But if the Great War occurs, the victory conditions change. In addition to this, a game can end in an Auto-Victory if a player takes control of a certain number of territorial keys.

name: Nippon: Zaibatsu
publisher: CrowD Games; Boardgame Atelier; Cranio Creations; Czacha Games; Grok Games; HIT Games; Maldito Games
description:
Nippon: Zaibatsu is a new edition of Nippon, a fast-paced, area-majority economic game. Players control "zaibatsu": massive conglomerates of interconnected companies driving Japan's economy in the Industrial Revolution era.

During the game, players invest in new industries, build factories and railroads, and produce goods to saturate local markets and fulfill contracts — all to grow their influence and power and to become rulers of the new modernized country. Players are free to choose their playstyle and winning strategy: They choose what they score victory points for, control the game's pace with income turns, and race each other to get the most beneficial factories, markets, and bonuses.

All the core mechanisms of the original Nippon are present, but the components, art, and design are upgraded, and many gameplay features are reworked to get the game in line with modern trends. Nippon: Zaibatsu features new resource types, ships are heavily revised with new Iwakura mission rules, factories are much more variable, consolidation turns provide players with new rewards, and much more. Also, the game now has an automa-driven solo mode.

—description from the publisher

name: Imps
description:
The underworld is feuding and order must be restored! In Imps, 2 players command Imps, Implings, and Overlords to prove themselves most glorious on the battlefield or to slay the enemy Overlords.

Each player starts the game with a Castle containing 2 different Overlords and 4 different types of Imps, all with unique abilities. On your turn, you may do one of three things:
1) Enlist an Imp or Impling from the underworld into your Castle.
2) Move one of your Overlords.
3) March using Imps and Implings, and trigger any abilities.

Be careful how you March, as any Imps and Implings not in a Castle may be commanded by either player!

The game can end one of two ways:
1) The Slayer Track is filled and scores are calculated.
2) Both of a players Overlords are slayed and they immediately lose.

Imps uses a mancala-style "pick up and drop" mechanism where players may select ANY tile (except the enemy Castle) and March with the pieces there.

-description from designer

name: In a Nut Shell
description:
Cracking board game for game nights with family and friends

     WHICH ______ IS KNOWN __ KING __ THE JUNGLE? Guess answers by revealing the fewest possible words from the question!
     High risk high reward! The fewer words you reveal, the more points you score - will your team take the risk and crack the nut?
     Amazing box with sliding windows reveals questions one word at a time - slide, reveal & guess! With two thrilling game modes that get everyone involved.


How to play:

     REVEAL a word from a secret question. 
     PASS the box – teams take turns revealing words. 
     Think you know the answer? Risk it and GUESS!
     Guess it right? You SCORE! Guess it wrong? They score!


—description from the publisher

name: Sky Garden
description:
Sky Garden is a euro-style board game where each player takes on the role of a bird sanctuary owner, tasked with creating a comfortable and welcoming environment for birds, and building a unique and attractive sanctuary of their own. Sky Garden is a standalone title in the Aqua Garden series, featuring charming wooden tokens and satisfying strategic gameplay.

Players bring wooden bird tokens from the main board or the forest into their personal boards. They must carefully choose where to place each bird, considering limited space in each area, as well as trees, lakes, and objective tiles. Birds can form pairs and, when given a pleasant environment, will lay eggs. Collecting these eggs is a key factor in winning the game.

Players must also keep a close eye on bingo-style milestones. Completing a full row of conditions grants bonus rewards.   Plan your actions carefully and decide in what order to achieve them for maximum efficiency.

—description from the publisher

name: In the Shadows: Resistance in France 1943 - 1944
description:
In the Shadows is a two-player card-driven wargame about the desperate struggle of the French Resistance against the occupying Nazi and collaborating French forces between January 1943 and June 1944. In the game you will play as either the Resistance or the Occupation in a fight over the hearts and minds of the French People. The game strives to have players better understand the nuances of the Resistance and the clandestine nature of the fight that led to the founding of the modern French Republic.

Victory is determined by a combination of Occupation Resources and required Resistance units at the end of turn.

In the Shadows will also offer a narrative solitaire option where players can take on the role of a leader of the Resistance movement. These different playable characters will allow for diverse experiences against a challenging Occupation automata. Using the same mechanics as the two player game, the solo option is focused on a more immersive gaming experience.

—description from the publisher

name: Incantibus
publisher: Studio H; TLAMA games; Elznir Games; Evrikus; Geekach LLC; Reflexshop
description:
Incantibus is a fast-paced family game of magical duels and clever timing. Each player takes on the role of a young witch or wizard exploring a mysterious tower in search of powerful items, arcane knowledge, and rival sorcerers to capture.

At the heart of the game is a unique wand-based selection system: each round, players simultaneously point one of their four wooden wands (valued 1 to 4) at the items in the tower’s rooms. The highest-value wand wins the item — but the winner must give up that wand to the defeated player, creating a dynamic flow of power and bluffing opportunities.

As the tower is gradually looted, players must manage their limited storage space, choose between powerful combos, and prepare for the final confrontation with a dangerous villain. With quick turns, simultaneous play, and tactile components, Incantibus offers a delightful mix of strategy, interaction, and charm for players of all ages

name: Incubo
description:
Incubo is a cooperative deck-building game designed for 2 players, where they take on the roles of a child "Tommy" and his best friend cat, "Alpha", as they confront their fears to rescue their sister, "Nina". Together, they must build their decks by passing cards between each other, eliminating weaker or negative cards, and facing various adventures within the dream world. The game is divided into three R.E.M. phases, each culminating in a confrontation with a terrifying monster, such as a ball of yarn, a half-opened wardrobe, a pigeon, and more. These monsters are confronted simultaneously by both players on different parts of the creature, and every victory strengthens the characters. Throughout the game, players will manage their resources, represented by the ticking of time to ensure they can save Nina.

—description from the publisher

name: Industrollization
description:
Industrollization is a print and play, roll and write game for one to four players. In this game you will deliver goods to factories. The order in which you will place goods is crucial to score the most points. You can deliver goods by train or by truck.
The game lasts six Rounds. Each Round is divided into two phases. First phase is Loading Goods and the Second Phase is Delivering Goods to factories. There are four trains and a truck where players can place their goods. Each train will deliver goods to the specific factory while truck can deliver goods to any factory.

—description from the designer

name: Inflection Point: The Battle for Kalach and the Battle of Chir
description:
Inflection Point is a Battalion Combat Series (BCS) game depicting two important but relatively unknown battles before and after Stalingrad. The Battle for Kalach was fought in July 1942 following Case Blue, the successful drive into southern Russia. Paulus' Sixth Army intended to encircle and destroy the Soviet Armies and walk into Stalingrad. The Soviets were still recovering from Operation Barbarossa the year before. The result of the battle set up the epic urban fight that was the turning point of the Eastern Front. By December 1942, the Sixth Army was trapped at Stalingrad by a more capable Red Army. In the Battle of Chir River, the Soviets looked to exploit their gains and prevent German relief operations over a portion of the Kalach battlefield. Initial success along the Chir River changed when the energetic 11th Panzer Division was thrust onto the scene. These two battles show the progression of the Red Army into an offensive army that could start fighting toe-to-toe against the invaders. For the Germans, the days of blitzkrieg successes were waning and were being put on the defensive. There was a marked inflection point around Stalingrad.

The game showcases this change in quality and capability between the armies. Units famed for fighting at Stalingrad are here - 24th Panzer and 100th Jäger Divisions as well as the 62nd Army. With rules on crucial air supply that was needed to sustain the German offensive, to stubborn Soviet command in the form of Colonel Konstantin Zhuravlev, players will be able to recreate these pivotal battles. The steppes of Southern Russia are accurately depicted, with rivers, balkas, and small hills being crucial in the otherwise flat terrain. With offensive and defensive possibilities for both sides in both battles, there's tense decision making in order to win and change the fate on the Eastern Front.

Scenarios:
Battle for Kalach (2 maps - 10 turns)
Entry of the Tank Armies (parts of 2 maps - 3 turns)
Battle of Chir River (1/2 map - 10 turns)
Tormosin Offensive (1/2 map - 5 turns)
Attack of the Fifths (1/2 map - 4 turns)

name: Inis: Legendary Edition
description:
Inis is a game deeply rooted in Celtic history and lore in which players win by being elected King of the Island (Inis).

Careful drafting, hand management, bluffing (especially once players understand the importance of passing their turn), good timing, and a precise understanding of the balance of power are the keys to victory. After a discovery game, you'll be ready for a full and epic game, where an undisputed player will be king by the Assembly for his merit and wisdom.

This new 3rd edition of Inis features all-new artwork, along with the Seasons of Inis and Nemed expansions.

name: Stonesaga
publisher: Open Owl Studios; Board Game Circus; CrowD Games; Galakta; OOMM; Ігромаг
description:
Stonesaga is a cooperative, campaign style, survival crafting board game set in a unique, persistent world shaped by your choices. In Stonesaga, you unfold the epoch-spanning story of the people of a remote glacial valley, guiding multiple generations of characters who make a life there amidst harsh conditions, wondrous mysteries, and giant monsters.  Each game session covers one generation of people within a society, continuing from the last and permanently changing the valley in various ways based on in-game events and the players’ decisions.  Designed for drop-in, drop-out play and flexible playgroup availability, Stonesaga can be played by one group from start to finish, played with a rotating cast, or even passed between groups seamlessly. Components are sometimes permanently altered, but never removed or discarded entirely.

Stonesaga follows a certain rhythm: faced by a new opportunity or crisis, the people of the valley must meet their society’s new needs. Meanwhile, the valley’s other inhabitants – immortal beasts – will seek to fulfill their own needs as their instincts dictate. You will have to navigate both sets of challenges, using might, dexterity, conviction, and awareness to survive as a tribe in the wild.

Stonesaga introduces a completely new discovery based crafting mechanic. Do you think that a sharpened stone and stick could combine to create a spear? Use the crafting action and find out. You will need to discover the properties of various crafting materials as you expand your crafting “recipe” knowledge. Work together as a community to build your village together. From a simple fire pit and tent to a forge and library, create a civilization that lasts the generations.

Stonesaga rewards exploration and chooses to let you experience the world in a unique way each play session. Working on the established rules of the world, you will discover unique materials, monsters, and areas of the world that you won’t be directed towards. Stonesaga lets the curious and inquisitive thrive.

Persistence

name: Yami
description:
Enter the Kingdom of Kakapo, now overrun by the creeping vines of the mysterious Lyken! These vines spread across the land, shrouding it in a heavy mist that severs all communication… yet also reveals the long-forgotten forest spirits. With their help, you — brave adventurers — may still purify the realm and drive back the darkness.

Yami is an open-world trick-taking and polyomino game featuring 22 independent missions. Your ultimate goal: succeed in Mission 22.
Each mission challenges you to surround Mission tiles with your Spirit tiles by playing a series of tricks. Every setup is unique, with its own map, rewards (sometimes hidden), and placement constraints. Careful planning and teamwork are key if you hope to advance through the kingdom.

But beware: time is against you. Every mission, whether won or lost, pushes you closer to the end and burdens you with cumulative penalties. Only clever play and strong cooperation will allow you to save the kingdom before the Lyken’s vines consume it all.

So… are you ready, adventurers, to face the mists of Yami?

—description from the designer

name: DC Deck-Building Game: Arkham Asylum
description:
This entry in the DC Deck-Building Game series unlocks the gate to Arkham Asylum and lets you take on the roles of its mad inmates like The Joker, Harley Quinn, The Riddler, and Two-Face. As you compete to take down Batman and his allies, you will take Hostages, earn victory point tokens, and Bribe your way to the top of Gotham City's criminal underworld! Compatible with all Cerberus Heroes games.

—description from the publisher

name: DC Deck-Building Game: Rivals – Superman vs. Lex Luthor
description:
Superman and Lex Luthor clash over the Metropolis skyline. Build more powerful combos with your deck to be the first to take down your rival!

Standalone game and compatible with other games in DC Deck-Building Game series.

KEY FEATURES

Heroes, Villains, Equipment, Super Powers, and Locations pulled straight from Superman comics!
    Each time your Character is defeated, they gain more amazing abilities and become a greater challenge to defeat!
    Confrontation cards give you bonuses when you try to take down your opponent!
    Block cards make it harder for your opponent to defeat you

—description from the publisher

name: Instinkt: Duell der Tiere
publisher: Board Game Circus; Gam'inBIZ; Meeple On Board
description:
Instinct is a tactical tile laying game for two players. Battle it out in a gloomy forest full of mystical creatures! Take turns placing cards in a 4x4 display. Make your choices carefully to score points. Sometimes it‘s all about the right timing! The player with the most points at the end of the game wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Insurrection
description:
"In a Shadowed land, where only darkness exists,
Queen Kristin Weaves her web, within the mists.
A gift from Tore, corrupted by the night,
A tainted mark to drown the light.
But one alone won’t serve her right,
She yearns for ten to claim the night.
Her loyal thralls obey her call,
While rebels rise to break her wall.
The fate of realms, both dark and light,
Now rests on you - Choose wrong or right."

In Insurrection, you play a Rebel Leader who rises against the tyrannical Queen Kristin. On the path to Kristin’s Keep, you will recruit troops to build the best army possible from your hand of cards. Each of these cards will earn you points at the end of the game.
How the game ends depends on the players. Either the Rebels manage to overthrow Kristin, or Kristin retains her throne if she manages to gather 10 Corruption marks.

Will you choose to bet on the Good side and defeat Kristin, or conspire with the forces of Evil and wager on the victory of the Evil Queen?

—description from the publisher

name: Interstellar Adventures: The Sincerest Form of Flattery
description:
In the depths of space, a cryptic signal from a previously unknown planet reaches The Atlas. On board that spaceship, Captain Silna and her crew scramble to decipher the call. What follows is an adventure that pushes the crew to confront their limits.

With the mechanics of an escape room and the excitement of a choose-your-own-adventure story, Interstellar Adventures is a dynamic three-episode experience that has a role for all crew members: the code-breaker, the cartographer, and the one who just likes missiles.

Using powers of logic and deduction, the crew sets out on a mission to untangle the unknown. Exploring an obscure new world, battling ravenous plants, and narrowly escaping missile attacks, our crew embarks on a quest that tests both their wits and their teamwork skills, while also making them second-guess everything they thought they knew.

name: Into The Dark Dungeon: Silver Mine
description:
Into the Dark Dungeon is a dungeon-crawl tabletop game where you can play solo, cooperatively, or competitively. Explore randomly generated dungeons, overcome various encounters, complete your quest, and fight to survive. Deliver your completed quest, acquire forgotten knowledge, sell your loot, and buy what you need for your next exploration. Venture Into The Dark Dungeon once again to take on new quests, discover more riches, and become a hero.

Solo play or two to four players can play cooperatively or competitively, while an additional player can control the encounters that spawn in the dungeon. Its exploration is unique, offering countless possible combinations. Become the Hero of the region by acquiring titles, wealth, power, and occasionally vanquishing your antagonists.

Cooperative or Competitive: The player who collects the most coins wins.
Arena: Be the last one standing (or have the most wins).

—description from the designer

name: Into the Wild Alaska
description:
Into the Wild Alaska: A Survival Race in the harsh Wilderness of Alaska. Stranded deep in the unforgiving wilderness, you and your companions must race to gather food, navigate brutal terrain, and outlast whatever nature - or each other - throws your way. Into the Wild Alaska blends real-world survival logic with tense, strategic play in a game that is easy to learn and impossible to forget.

Each turn, players will roll the dices and move around the board to the space designated by the dices. While they travel the map, each player will need to gather resources, establish strategic camps, overcome events, and build equipment, to be able to collect Food.

Each time players finish their round through the map, they must have enough Food resources to continue the next round. Each round the amount of Food increase, and if a player does not have enough Food, they are out of the game and did not survive Alaska wilderness. The last player standing, or the one who collects more than 50% of the Food resources available in the game can travel to the Island and finish the game as the winner of Into the Wild Alaska.

—description from the designer

name: Invaluable
description:
In the game of Invaluable, players are directors of competing museums. They buy and sell artifact cards, to amass high scoring collections, or to just get rich. Either approach can win you the game!

The order in which players offer artifact cards determines the value of those cards, so players must carefully time their actions. Running out of money at the wrong time can ruin your plans! Of course, you should try to make sure that exact thing happens to your opponents!

On their turn, a player puts a card from their hand up for auction. If another player wins the auction, the original player is paid the winning bid. But if the original player wins the auction, the money is removed from the game. Cards that are won at auction are placed in the winning player’s museum tableau following very simple rules.

Once every card has been sold, the game is over. Artifacts in museums are worth points depending on how they are positioned relative to other artifacts. Subsequently, the same artifact can be worth different amounts to different players. Coins are also worth points, opening up another possible route to victory for shrewd artifact sellers.

—description from the designer

name: Invasion Australia: 1942
description:
Invasion Australia covers a hypothetical Japanese invasion of Australia in 1942, based on the premise of a Japanese victory in the Coral Sea in May 1942 and subsequent capture of Port Moresby. Ground units are regiments and brigades, air units are several squadrons grouped by aircraft type, and naval ops are abstractions.

World at War Magazine, May-June 2025

name: Inventures
description:
Inventures, Birtle Game’s first title, is a collaborative storytelling adventure game coming soon to Kickstarter.

In each game, players create their own characters and go on challenging adventures together. Victory comes down to how well you know your character and fellow players.

In Inventures, there’re no dice, game master, or numbers to track. Instead, Inventures relies on a powerful and novel game mechanic involving symbol interpretation.

When your character faces a challenge, you choose between options, each composed of a randomly drawn ACTION and OBJECT card.

You secretly pick which option best represents how your character would solve the problem. If the other players successfully guess which option you chose, your action succeeds and the story progresses.

Because of its modular symbol interpretation system, you can use Inventures to play stories in any setting imaginable: Westerns, SciFi, Fantasy, or a game set in the world of your favorite books or movies!

Games can be as short as 45 minutes and as long as weeklong campaigns.

—description from the designer

name: Peanuts: The Doctor Is In
description:
In the party game Peanuts: The Doctor Is In, Charlie Brown and the gang have plenty of problems, but luckily they have the ever-helpful Lucy Van Pelt ready to dole out advice. Voice your problems so that others can respond using classic Peanuts comic panels as advice for life's toughest questions. Stuck with unhelpful cards? Use your "Good Grief!" token for a new hand of cards.

Whoever offers the best advice wins the card, and the player with the most points after a set number of rounds wins.

name: Adventure Time Card Wars: Flame Princess vs. Fern
description:
Adventure Time Card Wars is the most epic card game ever found in the Land of Ooo, or anywhere for that matter! In the Adventure Time episode "Card Wars", Jake begs Finn to play his favorite trading card game. Finn accepts, despite warnings from Beemo on how very competitive Jake can be while playing the game. Finn and Jake battle against each other to decide who will be the Dweeb and who will be the Cool Guy.

Now fans can play the actual Card Wars game in Adventure Time Card Wars: Flame Princess vs. Fern, with all of the action taking place in four combat lanes.

Each turn, a player has two Action Points to spend on Creatures, Spells, and Locations, and cards cost between 0 and 2 Action Points to play. When you summon a Creature, you choose which lane you want to place it in; some Creatures have FLOOP abilities that allow you to use their special abilities. When you attack with a Creature down a lane, you might find an opposing Creature, or you might get to deal your damage straight to your opponent's Hit Points. Reduce your opponent's Hit Points from 25 to 0 and you're the Cool Guy (and you win the game)!

Each Card Wars starter set has a pair of different forty-card decks and is ready to play right out of the box. Mix the decks together to come up with your own righteous combos!

—description from the publisher

name: Iraqi Freedom: Thirty Days to Baghdad
description:
Iraqi Freedom: Thirty Days to Baghdad simulates the 2003 Iraq War as a military conflict, and also as a systematic hunt for Iraq’s High Value Targets, otherwise known as Iraq’s Most Wanted, during Operation Iraqi Freedom. The game simulates the entire war and includes two mounted maps of Iraq as it existed in 2003, including accurate topography (such as the alteration to the Mesopotamian wetlands, drained by Saddam Hussein after the end of the Gulf War), and extending northward to encompass Kurdish territory, as well. The game includes an entirely new set of game pieces representing all of the belligerents, including insurgent units such as the Fedayeen, Ansar al Islam, Al Quds, and Ba’athists (Saddam party loyalists). In addition, there are more air unit types, including the B-2 stealth bomber, F-14, Royal Navy Harriers, etc.

Other new game pieces include smart bombs (such as the GBU-12 and GBU-31), Iraqi medium range missiles, a Patriot battery, plus numerous elite units (e.g., British commandos, U.S. Army Rangers, and of course Special Forces, Marines, and so on). The game even includes the optional U.S. 4th Infantry Division that had been scheduled to invade Iraq from Turkey (historically diverted after Turkey’s refusal to permit staging from Turkish territory). The rules include a standard scenario, a variant scenario, and a campaign game that links Desert Storm to Iraqi Freedom.

Better yet, this game includes a bonus Desert Storm supplement that includes additional game pieces, a historical scenario (with a historic 1991 set-up), plus an entire Event Cards effects system. That is to say, the Desert Storm event cards don’t merely move suit markers upon the suit track; rather, now each event has a specific game-play effect that *may* occur during game play (two possible events per each card among the two decks), multiplying the operational possibilities of the game (completing the innovation of the Desert Storm game as it was always meant to be). Moreover, the Desert Storm supplement booklet includes a page of clarifications and errata to complete Desert Storm. Highly researched and accurate, this game is a complete presentation of the Iraq war militarily, technologically, politically, as well as ecologically.

—description from the designer

name: Iron Age
description:
Iron Age is a classic empire-builder with modern mechanics set in the European Iron Age. The goal is to forge your empire’s legacy to ensure its place in history.

Expand by war and diplomacy, recruit epic Heroes, build marvelous Wonders and make brilliant Discoveries to collect Victory Points and effects that strengthen your empire.

Players adapt their abilities by managing their selection of Battle and Command Cards in their hand. Some are replayable each turn and some are handed to the targeted opponent after play. Clever planning and a silver tongue for diplomacy is required to reach your goal before the others.

You can conquer the world as Rome, Greece, Persia, Egypt, Carthage or Gaul, each with their own set of 3 Heroes, a starting Discovery and a unique Legacy Bonus.

There's a maximum of 7 turns per game and each turn has 3 phases - Income, Action and End. The actions are: Recruit, Build, Influence, Trade and Move.

If a player reaches maximum expansion or claims enough achievements, the game will end early.

By the end of the game, the player with the most Victory Points is declared the winner and earns the title "The Great".

Iron Age is approachable grand strategy in a small box. It features casual gameplay with intense competition. Entertainment and loud outbursts guaranteed.

Based on engine building, worker placement and hand management.

—description from the designer

name: Isla
description:
What Flora, Fauna and Fossils will you find?

Embark on an epic adventure of strategy and problem-solving. As daring explorers you must navigate a mysterious island, facing tough choices and threatening perils along the way.

Master the unique dice exhaustion mechanic to move through unchartered terrain, collect species, and research your discoveries.

Every decision could lead to escape or becoming lost forever! Plan wisely, refresh energy at key moments, and race against fellow adventurers - or escape the relentless solo mode keepers!

name: Isle of Feathers
description:
Isle of Feathers is a fast-paced, bird-based, 3D tile placement game about building the perfect island habitat for some very strange birds. Players stack chunky wooden tiles and place tokens to build the perfect island habitat for their birds.
