name: Legions: Abyss Universe
description: Legions is a two-player game set in the Abyss universe in which players compete to reign over the districts of the city and, by extension, the Throne of the Kingdom. Each turn, play a legion card on your side of the Abyss city, try to recruit a war hero, and gain the majority influence of the different districts to obtain specific powers.

name: Lepidoptery
description:
Lepidoptery is a climbing, deck-shedder and connection game for 2 players.

Players try to form 4-in-a-row on the board in their own player color, or shed out their deck to win.

Take turns playing stronger and stronger combinations while dropping tokens into the columns matching your played combination types. Unlike many climber-shedders, you are allowed to play combinations of different types on each other (e.g., sets on singles).

As columns fill up, their combination types become blocked from play, and any previously filled columns are emptied.

—description from the designer

name: Les Soeurs de l'Alliance
description:
Les Soeurs de l'Alliance is the third chapter in the The Spirit of Eden, Colossus and Sisters of the Alliance trilogy.

Construct and build your deck in order to get through the dungeon (along with its traps and minions) and fight the boss to protect Eden.

Your hero fights through card and mana use, you can upgrade or get new cards via XP use. Defeat minions in time to earn XP.

The fate of Eden is in your hands.

—description from the publisher

name: Ring Ring
description:
Little witch Lily wants to keep the forest safe, but she needs your help to do it. Use your magic to give her the items she needs or summon the right allies and complete missions.

Ring Ring is a cooperative game in which each turn you will play cards on the image of Lily. The cards have different objects or characters that modify the general picture, and the objective is to fulfill the requirements of the various missions. Players can't talk to each other, so they can't tell each other what cards they have, but if someone gets the bell card and says "Ring ring!" everyone can speak and change the order of the missions. Are you ready to use your magic to help Lily and keep the forest safe?

—description from the publisher

name: Rudolph
description:
The most magical night of the year is approaching, and Santa Claus still hasn't decided which sleigh he'll use to deliver presents. Each player will compete to assemble the best team of reindeer: fast, strong, and shiny. But only one sleigh will be able to take flight and lead the most anticipated journey of Christmas.

In Rudolph, designed by Gabriel Buendía and Nico Cardona with illustrations by Benji Santiago, games take place over ten frantic rounds. In each round, players reveal cards in the center of the table and must quickly choose one to add to their sleigh. Speed ​​and intuition will be key to forming powerful combinations and paving the way for the final scoring.

After the final round, the Rudolph card will lead each sleigh, and the reindeer majorities will be distributed, awarding decisive points. With simple rules and a dynamic pace, Rudolph is perfect for opening a family evening, sharing with friends, or even becoming the star gift from a Secret Santa.

—description from the publisher

name: Spring
description:
Spring bursts forth in all its splendor: the meadows bloom, water irrigates the grass, and life returns to the air. But in this garden, only those who best coordinate their actions will flourish.

Spring, created by María and Enrique Blasco, proposes a strategic duel for two players divided into two distinct phases. In the first, both players build a shared garden by overlapping cards in turns: blooming your flowers and blocking your opponent's will be key to winning small gardens. In the second, each player draws cards from the shared space to design their personal garden, in which the objective is to form the largest group of connected flowers.

—description from the publisher

name: Tax the Rich
publisher: Alion – by Dr Ø; Devir; Ghenos Games; Hobby Japan; Pegasus Spiele
description:
Climb the social ladder — or kick it over.

The trick-taking game Tax the Rich features a deck depicting characters of various social ranks from the Poor to the President. Each round begins with a simple bidding phase to determine both the trump color and the number of tricks required to score bonus points. The winner of the bid must then acquire the required number of tricks, together with their ally.

The game is played as a trick-taking game in which the highest social ranks are the strongest cards. However, if at any time all remaining cards in your hand have a flag symbol, you may trigger a "revolution" by revealing your cards. This flips the social hierarchy upside down so that the lowest-ranked cards become the most powerful. Having called for a revolution, you stand publicly exposed, playing the rest of this round with your cards face up.

The game includes thirteen rule cards that add variety by giving certain character cards special abilities related to their profession: Workers "unionize", the Billionaires "power grab", the Police "stop and frisk", Scientists "debunk" etc. You can play with random rule cards or use one of the scenarios suggested in the rules.

With an optional variant, players can also collect cards with a feminist icon to trigger a feminist revolution, boosting the value of all female characters.

—description from the designer

name: Liars & Looters
description:
Liars & Looters is a fun and quick game where you trade resource cards and outsmart your opponents with strategic deceit. Players embrace their inner trickster while searching for the resource cards their chosen Tribe is gathering. Only by collecting all of them first you can win and prove your superior skills in bluffing and spotting a liar.

Your Tribe Card will show you what to hunt for, and what to dismiss as unusable - but keep in mind, everyone can see your Tribe Card and knows exactly with which resources they can bait you.

By drawing from the deck each turn, more resource cards come into play or a special event will be triggered.

Your main focus should lie on the Trades where 1 Player offers a card face down, while everyone else is competing –also cards faced down- in the trade to get OR NOT get the offered card. The Trades and their results are your chance to lie your ass off or be honest while acting guilty. You are allowed to claim anything as „truth “, but never to reveal your cards.

—description from designer

name: Liberation
description:
After the debacle and breakthrough of the German army, France came under German occupation. Faced with a sense of injustice, some intellectuals begin to revolt and organize the beginnings of the French Resistance.

Liberation features an asymmetrical confrontation between the occupying forces and the French Resistance. The occupier can be played by one player or in the form of an automa. The Resistance players each lead their own maquis, fighting together to liberate the country. In a cat-and-mouse game, the Resistance fighters carry out missions while the occupying forces set traps and capture the brave fighters.

The game features 5 main scenarios, ranging from 1940 to the liberation of Paris in 1944. Each scenario has its own twist, forcing players to play differently. The game can be played per scenario, or as a campaign (non-legacy) where each scenario has a bearing on what happens next.

—description from the designer

name: License to Krill
description:
Krill are like Shrimp, but are even more interesting! Play as Krill collecting cards to score the most points. However, the whale (Plush game case) swims around hot potato style with a hungry appetite. The whale targets players and occasionally eats them (the cards not the players)!

On your turn draft one card from the Ocean Market. Cards have simple set collection scoring or actions. The card that you draft also determines what the whale will do next! Do you choose the best scoring card but risk a whale encounter? Or do you target the player in the lead while settling for a less valuable card?

While the game lets you target other players it does not feel like "take that". If the whale eats one of your cards you get some Kelp as compensation. The most Kelp scores big as well! Example cards include Shellfish, Krilling Spree, and Dressed to Krill.

Players always end their turn by flipping a whale card. These include common "whale stuff" like logging (sleeping), swimming around, and eating a target player's cards. The game ends when the last Krilling Time card is revealed located in the bottom 5 cards.

-description from designer

name: LifeShip
description:
In a future where humanity is on the brink of extinction, what little hope remains lies in a few titanic structures, known as Lifeships. With the help of an incompetent captain and their grumpy first mate, Sasha, you’ll have to navigate a terrifying universe to complete missions and keep your Lifeship running. How will you survive, will you survive? The choice is yours! An innovative, tabletop adventure where deck-building, base-building, and tactical skirmishes collide and no two games are ever the same. In Lifeship, you and your crew are part of one of the last colony ships to leave Earth. Your job? Survive. Adapt. And forge a future among the stars. You’ll build your character, choose a class, and embark on missions to secure resources for your people. Just be sure to plan for Xeno-spiders, Piratists or an array of other deadly enemies! With hundreds of unique missions, a true solo mode, a custom website that narrates your game, and tracks your decisions, Lifeship is a game like no other.

				
				
					Gameplay & FeaturesThe game is packed with innovative features that create a tabletop experience like no other.

Simultaneous Play – No waiting for turns. Every player acts at the same time, keeping the game fast and engaging.

Innovative website companion - a living universe. Choices you make are tracked, factions remember you, characters react to your past actions, and missions evolve based on your decisions. The site takes care of bookkeeping, letting you focus on the adventure rather than managing stats and logs. Who will you befriend? Who will you betray? And who will come back for revenge?

Deck building with a twist – every decision matters. You’ll build your deck from a mix of character cards, class abilities, and equipment, tailoring your strategy to each mission. But be careful, too much salvage clogs your deck, and managing your resources is key to survival!

Base-Building & Progression – Your Lifeship is more than just a home—it’s your strategic hub.

Spend Captain’s Kredits (CK) to upgrade the ship, improve facilities, or, well… buy Taco subscriptions.

Fail-Forward Design – Failing a mission doesn’t stop the story (and trust me, you’ll fail), it just changes it. No restarts. No wasted time. Just a new path forward.

Cloning Technology – Death isn’t the end. If your character dies, they’re cloned, mutated, changed. Returning with powerful new abilities, or perhaps just an extra thumb. Who knows?

Loot & Salvage System – Scavenge for resources, but be careful, too much loot clogs your deck, and it’s worthless until you get it back to the ship.

Smart Enemy AI – Enemies don’t just attack blindly, they hide, retreat, and strategize. Even a lowly rat can outmaneuver an unprepared team!

True Solo Mode – Play Your Way. Not every game balances solo play properly, but Lifeship was built for it from the start.
Enter CEDALION, your fully customizable AI companion. CEDALION is a streamlined, strategic co-pilot. Choose from four distinct roles, Combat, Healing, Tech, or Salvage, and adapt him to suit your needs. He supports you without overshadowing you, so every decision is still yours to
make. And best of all, he doesn’t take a share of the loot.

Endless Replayability – With 48 missions per run and a second campaign mode with all new missions, no two games are alike.

—description from the publisher

name: LIFTOFF! 2.0
description:
LIFTOFF! 2.0 is the definitive, epic space-race to the moon board game, which updates the successful (1989) Liftoff!  The Race to the Moon board game and its computer game, Buzz Aldrin's Race Into Space (1994). LIFTOFF! 2.0 is packed with additional content based on actual and proposed technologies that make this the most highly researched and complete simulation of man’s journey into space. Relive the Apollo 11 landing on the Moon!

Up to 4 players compete to be the first nation to land a man on the moon, and successfully return them home again.

During the activity turn all players receive their current income, an event card which may help or hinder, and can buy new hardware (rockets / satellites / capsules etc), try and develop the reliability of systems they already have (by buying dice and adding the total to the current safety), hire astronauts, and secretly plan future missions.

The launch phase sees players carrying out their missions in turn (as being first to achieve certain mission goals such as 'first man in space' is rewarded). The relevant hardware must be purchased, including a rocket powerful enough to lift the weight of the other items involved. The mission is carried out by following a series of steps, and rolling percentiles against the safety rating of specific items each turn - e.g. liftoff roll against rocket, orbital burn roll against space capsule, space walk roll against space suit etc.
If a player fails a safety roll, the advanced game contains several possible failure outcomes (requiring one or more further rolls) ranging from a bulb failure to a catastrophic explosion, which will reset the safety factor of your equipment!

Once missions are completed, players’ incomes are adjusted depending on successes / failures, and the next year begins.

name: The Guest
description:
«The commander is dead, thrown into the cold, unforgiving void, and it was I who voted against her, sealing her fate. Now, uncertainty torments me. The ship's doctor claims that the host was not on board; that the threat is still latent among us. Communications have been extinguished since we left the planetoid, and I know that at least one of the crew is harboring those abominations that infiltrate the brain and usurp the will...».

«...5 days after the last vote, we remain isolated from everything, crossing the void at a dizzying speed, living day by day on the way to the Aurora space station. Time is running out and return is impossible. The new commander has called for another vote, and the engineer's gaze shines with a disturbing suspicion, or maybe I'm losing my mind... anyway, I think I'll vote for her...».

In The Guest, players will represent the crew of the extrasolar ship Beagle, which is attacked by a strange parasite that lodges itself in people's brains, controlling their will. A hidden role game in which the tension is real in each vote. Some players will represent infected crew members who try to infect or kill the rest, and others will be healthy crew members who try to safely reach the Aurora space station.
The objective of each team is to kill the members of the opposing team, but no one knows who the crew members infected by the hosts are. But be very careful, a third side could appear if someone loses their mind.

—description from the publisher

name: The Lie
description:
In The Lie, all the cards lie! The cards show numbers from 1 to 4, and they are in four different colors. However, when you turn each card over, you will find something has changed: either its color or number.

You must be clever in choosing your combinations in order to play a higher number of the same color. Whoever is able to play all of their cards first wins the match, and whoever has the most points after a certain number of matches wins the game.

-description from the publisher

name: Limit
publisher: Ludonaute; CMON Global Limited; GateOnGames; Hobby Japan; Spielworxx
description:
Limit is a competitive strategy game where you play as a Nation facing the challenges of our world. Make crucial political decisions, manage your resources with finesse, anticipate global crises and adapt to the upheavals of the planet and the decisions of other Nations. Balance growth and resilience to build a prosperous society.

The game takes place in a maximum of 7 generations. However, the end of the game can come before if you and your opponents trigger at least 4 global crises.

A generation is made up of 3 phases:


     The Political phase: you make decisions
     The Social phase: your Nation reacts to these decisions
     The International phase: crises arise and alliances are formed


End of the Game:
Before counting your points, you must test the resilience of your Nation for future generations. Redo the Food, Consumption and Production stages of the Social phase with the effects of shortages but without new crises.

The Nation with the highest score wins the game.

name: Limits of Glory: Jersey New Jersey
description:
Two exciting games in one box, Jersey covers the little known 1781 invasion by the French of the Island of Jersey as part of the American Revolutionary War. The game examines the impact of luck on events and challenges the skill of players to use their commanders to influence these events.

New Jersey covers the famous crossing of the Delaware and the battles of Trenton and Princeton using the same 'Limits of Glory' system to test players ability to mitigate what luck throws at them by the skillful use of commanders and troop positioning.

Limits of Glory represents military campaigns at the highest command level, players take the role of theater commander and must manage their resources of men, material and skill to emerge victorious.

—description from the publisher

name: Limits of Glory: Maida 1806
description:
By the close of 1805 the Third Coalition, which had been orchestrated by William Pitt, was in tatters following their catastrophic defeat at Austerlitz. However, in late 1805 a tiny Anglo-Russian army, sent by Pitt and paid for by the British government, disembarks in the Bay of Naples to support Ferdinand IV, King of the Two Sicilies. This army, commanded by the Russian General Lacy with the support of the British General Craig, approximately 15,000 men strong, is now the only Coalition force on mainland Europe.

Will they be able to defend Naples, or will they evacuate leaving the wretched Neapolitan army to its fate? Will Marshal Massena secure the Two Sicilies for his Emperor, or will the Coalition be able to save Ferdinand’s last stronghold, the island of Sicily itself?

The Limits of Glory series examines the influence of 'skill and luck' on the commanders present in a campaign. A Glory rating is attributed to all the significant participants in the campaign, made up from the skill they exhibited and the luck from which they benefited. Players must make difficult decisions as to when to use their commanders Glory to mitigate the situation on the board to their advantage by attempting to manage favourable and  unfavourable events thrown up by the Event Clock as the campaign unfolds.

name: Limits of Glory: Santa Maura & Capri
description:
The third and forth campaigns in our Limits of Glory series are two games in one box. Each game is designed to be a stand-alone shorter game, playable in approximately one hour.  The games use the same unique Limits of Glory system, with the same Event clock and Combat system but on a smaller scale.

Campaign III in the Limits of Glory series looks at the attempt by the French and Neapolitans under their new King, Joachim Murat, to re-capture the island of Capri just off the Bay of Naples in 1808.

This game represents the two week period that covers Murat's invasion of Capri.  The game introduces weather effects for the first time in Limits of Glory, as weather was crucial to the outcome of the campaign. The French player must get their troops across the bay, land on Capri and take back the island by capturing Capri Town and Ana Capri. The British must hold on, making the French task as difficult as possible while trying to negotiate favourable surrender terms, hoping for windy weather to bring help from the Royal Navy and perhaps reinforcements.

Campaign IV in the Limits of Glory series looks at the British attempt to capture the Ionian island of Santa Maura, modern day Lefkada.

The game represents the four week campaign, starting on 21st March, by the British to capture the significant fortification of Santa Maura fortress and consequently, the entire island. Greek patriotism and the desire for independence played a major role in persuading the Albanians to desert the French and the game reflects this with the ability of the Greek commander Kolokotronis to entice Albanian units from neighbouring spaces to desert. Also, for the first time in Limits of Glory, the morale of Camus, the most senior French commander, plays a key role in the game. Once the British are adjacent to the fortress of Santa Maura, Camus must take a morale test following each assault or round of siege. This reflects his nerve breaking and him surrendering the fortress, even though the French forces were still able to resist. The French player must therefore do everything they can to keep the Allies away from the fortress by clever use of secret causeways for manoeuver and the considered positioning of shore batteries.

The games use the same single mechanic used in Bonaparte's Eastern Empire and Maida 1806, with the only difference being that each player has three dice rather than four. There are less events, the games are shorter, the maps are smaller but players face all the same difficulties in strategic decisions and balancing when to push and when to wait.

—description from the designer

name: Limpopo
description:
Limpopo is a simple dexterity-based game for kids. During the game, players collect different snack cards and then try to eat them later.

Each turn players spin the circular board and use their crocodile to catch the type of snack they want to eat. Additionally, they can try to take additional snacks from other players. But beware! Healthy teeth are very important, so try to avoid hard logs.

The game ends when there are no more snacks in the river or at least one crocodile will lose all his teeth. The winner will be the crocodile with the fullest belly.

—description from the publisher

name: The Slasher
description:
A tranquil summer camp deep in the woods turns into a blood-soaked nightmare. Shadows stretch long under the moonlight, and somewhere out there, a killer is stalking the cabins with a crimson blade. You and your companion must gather your courage and supplies to escape this slasher’s hunt. Your only chance is to work together, outsmart the darkness, and survive the night.

The Slasher is a cooperative trick-taking game for two players that blends deduction, tension, and cardplay. Players face off against the game’s system by playing tricks under restrictive and evolving conditions, attempting to collect sets of cards that represent survival items. Each trick is both an opportunity and a risk—players must navigate limited communication and mounting pressure as they explore locations, avoid deadly encounters, and gather what's needed to escape. The killer's unseen presence looms throughout, forcing tight cooperation and tough choices with every hand.

name: Line of Judah
description:
The line of Judah draws inspiration from the genealogy presented in Matthew Chapter 1. Jacob, the father of Judah, blesses all of his children before his death. In Judah's blessing, he is promised a royal lineage of kings that will culminate with the ultimate king—Jesus. Matthew meticulously lays out the entire line of Judah, revealing that Jesus is the fulfillment of Jacob's blessing to Judah.

In Line of Judah, players will assume the role of historians tasked with reconstructing Jesus' lineage. As players uncover new members of Judah's lineage, they must decide whether to incorporate them into their own line or place them in their family tree for others to acquire. Once a member has been added to a player's family line, it cannot be removed. The game concludes after all family members have been discovered, and the player with the longest complete section of the line of Judah is the winner.

—description from the designer

name: Linimasa Card Game: Nusantara Edition
description:
Linimasa Card Game: Nusantara Edition is a fast-paced educational card game where players try to guess the chronological order of three historical events and match them with the correct historical figures — all drawn from the rich era of Indonesian kingdoms before the country’s independence. Featuring events and characters from powerful empires like Majapahit, Sriwijaya, and Mataram, the game invites players to explore Indonesia’s pre-colonial past.

Using limited-use Spy Cards to peek at hidden event cards, players secretly arrange timeline guesses and assign matching figure cards. Played over six rounds, points are awarded for correct order and accurate figure matches.

Designed for 1–4 players, ages 8 and up, the game offers a fun and engaging way to learn early Indonesian history in about 15 minutes.

—description from the designer

name: The White Castle Duel
publisher: Devir; 999 Games; Banana Games; CMON Global Limited; GaGa Games; IELLO; KOSMOS; Portal Games; Reflexshop; TLAMA games
description:
Following the arrival of the Portuguese in Japan, daimyos competed for control of foreign trade and technology. Himeji Castle, a symbol of feudal power, became a strategic center for clans seeking to gain influence.

In The White Castle Duel, two clans compete to exert their influence in the White Heron's court, managing resources and building engines. On each turn, you will use their lamp tokens to obtain resources and activate actions. Among the actions available, you can buy and upgrade influence cards, place clan seals on gardens and training grounds, move your courtier between circles of influence, or trade with the Portuguese. These actions will allow you to accumulate a series of icons — flags, katanas, kabutos, and origami figures — that will reward you with points, and whoever ends up with the most points wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Linyo
description:
Try to fill your game board as completely as you can in Linyo using only four lines.

Each player has a player sheet showing a grid of squares in three colors, some of which feature a star. To set up, roll the four dice, which show the three colors equally across their faces. Place a circle on four squares in your grid that match the colors rolled.

On a turn, the active player rolls the four dice; if all dice show the same color, they can set three dice to the colors of their choice, but otherwise the dice lay untouched. Each player must then start one line (from a circle) or extend one line, passing through at least two squares that match the colors rolled. If the line hits a star, a player can extend that line one additional space.

If a player cannot extend a line by at least two spaces, they must cancel a line with an X. Additionally, they must X any line that cannot be extended. When one player has Xed all of their lines, the game ends, and whoever has marked off the most spaces wins.

name: Little Artistry
description:
Be inspired by renowned storybook illustrators from the Golden Age of Illustration! Gather your materials and use them to collect your favorite scenes from old-fashioned fairy tales and nursery rhymes in this delightful game for two to four players.

This is a mechanically simplified version of Artistry, oriented towards children and families.

—description from the publisher

name: Little Kingdoms
description:
Little Kingdoms is an addictive high-stakes card game where two rivals clash in thrilling, fast-paced duels for control over four kingdoms. Recruit fantastical characters with powerful abilities, strategically manipulating the tide to tip the balance in your favor. But beware...the Queen, a ruthless force, reigns as an unforgiving referee, and her judgment is swift. She will banish any weakened characters from her presence and unlock ancient portals that connect to the elemental forces of this universe. With each portal that opens, the stakes rise dramatically, unleashing epic confrontations.
Your goal? Reduce your opponent’s mana to zero before they do the same to you. In this game of merciless strategy and unpredictable twists, only the most cunning will emerge victorious. Every decision could tip the scale toward glory—or doom! Will you conquer the kingdoms, or will the Queen’s judgment seal your fate?

—description from the publisher

name: Little Soldiers
description:
Little Soldiers is a game where two armies of little plastic soldiers pretend to fight it out between the plates, glasses and anything else that can be found on the table.

Move your characters, hide in this cheese box bunker and attack your enemies to break their little soldiers!

You want more?

Use modules to add fun and strategy. And discover several scenarios for up to 4 players including King of the Hill, Battle Royale, Team and Cooperative modes.

--> Play where you want and use objects around you to build up the battlefield
--> Break the strict rules of a wargame and add the fun of a family game
--> Different modes to discover the game the way you prefer

name: Littoral Commander: The Baltic
description:
Littoral Commander: The Baltic is the second installment of the Littoral Commander series. The game explores hypothetical conflicts and crises in the Baltic region of Europe.

Building on the core Littoral Commander game system, Littoral Commander: The Baltic features new units, such as the Amphibious Ready Group / Marine Expeditionary Unit (ARG MEU), the Multi-Domain Task Force (MDTF), and various types of Russian regiments. Littoral Commander: The Baltic features new mechanics for ground combat, new cards, and amphibious operations. One of the new core mechanics will require players to outfit their ships for a campaign -- carefully managing resources and space, but the emphasis on managing all aspects of battle, especially logistics will remain.

—description from the publisher

name: Transgalactica
publisher: Devir; Galakta; Game Harbor; Skellig Games
description:
The Galactic Senate has launched the "Transgalactica Decree" in order to increase their knowledge and influence beyond the already well-known fringes of the galaxy. Fleets from every planet have been launched to the stars in search of adventure, riches, and (hopefully) an influential seat in the governing spheres that lie beyond the known space.

Transgalactica is a worker-placement and engine-building game with a high level of interaction between the players. In order to thrive in this game, you will travel the far reaches of the galaxy, improve your fleet's influence in all galactic matters, compete with other fleets for technological advancements, build a commercial network, and possibly even send representatives to the Galactic Senate to claim political advantages.

The game is divided into five rounds. In each round, players use their Captains to perform powerful actions in their own operations panel. Then, the other players may follow taking the same action using their crew, but without gaining a bonus. Little by little, players will increase their military power, political influence, or technology level, and earn victory points by exploring, trading, mining or completing missions. May the best spacefarer win!

—description from the publisher

name: Lizard's Lair
description:
Lizard's Lair is a solitaire tile - laying puzzle mint tin game. Take on the role of a slithering lizard moving throughout its lair. The goal of the game is to collect eggs, dodge snakes, and avoid getting trapped in this ever changing underground.

Suspenseful choices: Select which card you will play wisely, timing is crucial.

Decisive roll and move mechanics: A refreshing take on roll and move games. Each movement impacts the next round.

Simple yet strategic and replayable gameplay: 17 lair cards creates a wide range of variety and card combinations each gameplay.

Push Your Luck with King Snakes: Will you fall in a trap? Run into a predator? Collect precious eggs?

—description from the publisher

name: Wispwood
publisher: Czech Games Edition (CGE); Cranio Creations; Devir; DiceTree Games; Gém Klub Kft.; HeidelBÄR Games; IELLO; MINDOK; Rebel Sp. z o.o.; White Goblin Games
description:
Is that a light at the end of the… branch?

A curious cat prowls into the forest, lured by flickering lights of all colors dancing through the trees. What are they? Oh, the wisps from the old tales! Each one sparkles with charm and mischief, carrying a unique personality. Can you guide them just right and make your forest the brightest?

Welcome to Wispwood, a magical place populated by glowing wisps. On your turn, choose a wisp tile and a shape to place in your personal grid — your very own growing forest. Each wisp has desires about where it wants to shine, and even the magical trees have preferences! You'll aim to meet their expectations across three scoring rounds. Between rounds, the forest shifts — fading and expanding — yet the wisps you've already placed remain, shaping the possibilities ahead.

With each game, new goal cards redefine the wisps' whims, ensuring your forest grows in a unique way every time. Enter the forest and explore the magic of Wispwood!

—description from the publisher

name: Lodge
description:
Lodge is a fast-paced and lively card game where players compete to prepare tasty snacks for the hikers visiting the forest.

Lodge is played over 3 rounds, each made up of several turns.
Customer cards are placed at the center of the table and show the number and type of snacks each customer wants. Each player has a hand of Snack cards numbered from 1 to 48, representing four snack types: Apple, Sandwich, Smoothie, and Energy Bar.
At the beginning of each turn, all players secretly select a Snack card from their hand, place it face down, and then reveal them simultaneously.
Then, in ascending card number order, players place their Snack cards in front of customers, matching the requested snack types. If your card completes a customer’s order, you take that Customer card, which will be worth points at the end of the game.

You win by scoring the most points… or by ending the game with exactly 10 Squirrel tokens! 
With bluffing, plot twists, and simultaneous turns, every match is a race to the last bite.

—description from the publisher

name: 7th Seal
description:
7th Seal is a solo dice management boss battle-style game in which you will face the judgement of the end times. Your goal is to open the seals of a scroll and face the wrath of a supreme being who has unleashed an avalanche of furious beasts and demons that will attempt to wipe out humanity. Use your dice wisely and prove that you can convince the great maker to give humanity another chance.

—description from the publisher

name: Lone U-Boat: A Solitaire Wargame
description:
It is late 1942 and the seas are dangerous and frightening. Allied convoys surge across the Atlantic, bringing vital supplies to Britain and Russia. But beneath the waves, Germany’s U-Boats are on the hunt, silent and deadly.

You are the commander of a Type VIIC U-Boat, the backbone of the Kriegsmarine’s submarine fleet. Your mission is to intercept and destroy merchant shipping, evade aggressive escorts and survive the increasing threat of Allied air power.
Aircraft patrol the skies and escort ships roam the convoy lanes. Your deck gun may still sink a lone freighter, but surfacing risks instant retaliation. The decisions you make on when to hide and when to attack will be crucial to your success as a U-Boat captain.

This hex and counter game is one of stealth, timing, and nerve. You’ll manage movement, depth, detection and damage across a range of different maps. Escorts will use sonar sweeps, depth charges and gunfire and, if you're too near the surface, the skies may bring additional dangers.

Can you complete your mission or will your U-Boat become yet another silent wreck beneath the Atlantic?

How the game works
This is a solitaire wargame. You play the game, and the enemy is controlled by the game. You will need at least 6, but preferably a few more, standard six-sided dice.
It is highly recommended that the counters provided on the final page of the game are used to play this game. Simply stick them to card and cut them out.

Quick to set up, easy to play, very replayable but certainly challenging, this game should provide you with hours of fun.

name: Lone Wolf: U-Boat Command
description:
Lone Wolf is a solo Print-And-Play (PNP) game that puts you in the role of a German U-boat commander operating in the Atlantic during World War II. As captain, your mission is to patrol dangerous waters, locate and sink Allied shipping, avoid detection, and survive long enough to return to base.

Each game plays out over a series of turns in which you'll roll dice to perform key actions such as movement, torpedo attacks, evasive maneuvers, system repairs, and spotting enemy convoys. You'll mark your progress and ship status on a custom sheet that track your fuel, torpedoes, hull integrity, and crew readiness. Strategic choices and the unpredictability of dice rolls create a challenging mix of resource management, risk assessment, and tactical navigation.

The modular patrol map system, random events, and mission objectives ensure no two games play the same. From engaging convoys to escaping depth charge barrages, Lone Wolf delivers an immersive and suspenseful experience in under an hour.

Will you return to port a decorated hunter of the seas or join the countless wrecks claimed by the cold Atlantic?

—description from the designer

name: Lonely Cairn
description:
There are a million ways to die in the Arctic, so carefully choose your supplies and read the ice well, and you just might secure the coveted prize of discovering the fabled Northwest Passage.

Lonely Cairn is a solitaire game about finding the Northwest Passage in the mid 1800s. Modelled and based upon the ill-fated Franklin Expedition, players will need to equip their expedition and carefully chose what to take with them into the arctic. They will then sail though a channel of icy locations, facing deadly encounters along the way. They must reach the exit by the end of 8 turns, or face being locked in the ice forever.

—description from the designer

name: Long Live the Captain
description:
In Long Live the Captain, your old captain is dead! Fed to the sharks, in fact, and the crew is looking for a new leader. But this won’t be an honest election. To claim the title of captain, you’ll need to outwit your rivals, bribe the crew, and strike shady deals, all while bluffing your way to the top.

Each round begins with an event that shakes up the rules of play. Players receive resources such as gold, silk, or gunpowder, then reveal a set of pirate cards, each waiting to see who offers the best bribes. Before bribes are placed, there’s room for negotiation and dirty trading, where anything from resources to promises can change hands.

Players secretly prepare bribe piles to win the loyalty of specific pirates. Resources, treasure maps, and even fake cards may be used to mislead opponents. Once revealed, pirates decide who to support, sometimes swayed by clever tricks like poison or event effects. Pirates that join your crew bring you closer to victory.

The game ends after a set number of rounds, and the player with the strongest crew of pirates is crowned the new captain. With bluffing, bribery, and backstabbing at its core, Long Live the Captain challenges players to outthink and outplay their rivals in a race for command of the ship.

name: Loops
description:
Loops presents an innovative game system with no rulebook. All the necessary information is on the cards. From the moment you open the box, the game guides you step by step. Card after card, you’ll uncover the story and the instructions, in the style of a “Point and Click” adventure.

In Loops, one or two players will experience an adventure set in a unique universe. You’ll step into the shoes of Andrea, the protagonist, who just wants to pick up her amp. She only has to go to the place where she left it, but as soon as you start playing, you’ll realize the path is far from simple. A curse will fall upon her, forcing you to start over again and again.

You must find the exact formula to move forward in the game despite this loop. You’ll have to carefully plan your steps, choose the order of the places you visit, manage your resources, gather information, and—above all—remember it when everything starts over.

Do you want to live a story meticulously crafted by the author through a groundbreaking game mechanic?

—description from the publisher

name: Lord of Conspiracy: Light and Darkness
description:
Embark on a journey full of dangers, random locations, random encounters, watch out for ambushes, face monsters, hunt animals, pay for services and trade. Enter the darkness and explore ruins, caves or underground. Keep your team in mind and meet their basic needs. And find the Lord of Conspiracy!

In Lord of Conspiracy: Light and Darkness, players lead a team consisting of a hero and three lieutenants. The goal of the game is to find the Lord of Conspiracy or defeat all the Leaders responsible for the unrest in the kingdom. Players choose one of four teams such as dwarves, elves, halflings and humans. It is the player who decides which character in the team becomes his hero and what equipment the team has to start with. Unique equipment gives the player unique abilities. After choosing their hero, they must explore their world, have adventures, and collect testimonies and witnesses to in order to deduce who the Lord of Conspiracy is. The first player to do and - and to defeat his bodyguards - wins.

—description from the designer

name: Lords of Worlds
description:
In Lords of Worlds, players compete to create the most valuable world by purchasing various types of terrain tiles and adding them to their personal planet.

Hire various assistants and utilize them wisely to secure optimal deals, then follow the instructions of your architects to ensure the construction of a gorgeous land!

In Lord of Worlds, you collect Terrain tiles and add them to your Planet trying to create chains of tiles of the same type: the longer a chain is, the more Victory points it will be worth at the end of the game. On your turn, you can either:
- Hire Assistants, adding cards to your hand
OR
- Play cards you have in your hand and use them to Move your Cart and/or Collect a tile.

The game has different ending conditions, depending on the number of players. When any of the ending condition is met, conclude the current round, so that each player plays the same amount of turns. The player with the most Victory Points is the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Lore: Second Edition
description:
Escape into the enchanting world of LORE, where every illustration tells a tale and traditional myths breathe life into your adventures. Perfect for those captivated by fairy tales and folklore.

LORE offers an RPG-light framework, letting you assume the guise of a classic fantasy archetype. When you escape into the world of Lore, you'll embark on quests, uncover lore, battle mythical monsters, find treasure, get into fantastical predicaments, and more.

Lore: Second edition makes the following changes:

     Actions are chosen, not mitigated to action cards.
     Turn phases have been restructured to Movement/train, action, and event.
     The archetypes now have unique abilities instead of auras.
     A single player and co-op version of play.
     Unique character pieces for each archetype.
     A world map with various locations and a more robust movement system.
     Enhances positive player interaction in events and quests.
     A simplified dueling system for monster battles.


The second edition still follows the day system, and the game ends on the third day. In a competitive game, players will collect victory points based on the success of their adventures, adding up quests completed, monsters defeated, lore uncovered, treasure collected, and renown. The player with the highest total wins, but it's about the journey, not the destination.

In single-player and co-op variants, players will go toe to toe with the Dark Paladin, the evil force plaguing the land of Lore. Work together to destroy his curses, take back relics, save the people from monstrous fates & ultimately team up to battle the Dark Paladin.

Experience inventive symbolic game play and timeless narratives by yourself or with friends.

—description from the designer

name: Los Banditos: The Train Heist Card Game
description:
Los Banditos is an Old West themed Train Heist Card Game where Banditos (players) take it in turns to build up four trains using carriage and caboose cards. Score points using a locomotive or escape car card. The Bandito with the most points after five rounds is the winner.

However, Banditos can use actions cards to change up the game. Steal cards from other Banditos, double up points on a train, change direction of play, and more, to disrupt other Banditos.

The cards of Los Banditos Card have been beautifully drawn with plenty of small details so you notice something new every time you play. Saddle up Amigos!

name: Berlin 1960
description:
Cold War tensions run high as spies, double agents, and informants move unseen through the divided city. Trust no one, outwit and uncover your enemies in this game of hidden roles and deception for a large group of daring players. In this game set in the German capital during the Cold War, you'll assume the identity of a member of the CIA or the KGB. Throughout the game, you'll use various powers to try to identify your fellow agents and hinder your rivals' investigations and communications. However, every action counts, and the signals you send to your allies may be misinterpreted.

—description from the publisher

name: Lost in Memories
description:
Lost in Memories is a Castlevania-themed cooperative exploration and battle game for 1–4 players. On a pre-laid out map, players will travel from room to room, clearing enemies and obstacles, and fighting bosses to level up their characters, in order to reach and defeat the final boss, the Mad King Urza.

Battles are done with dice rolls, where the player's levels decide the amount and size of the dice, and player's skills letting them modify these die rolls in various ways.

name: Catan: On the Road
description:
CATAN: On the Road builds on well-known CATAN mechanics with a fresh variation. Gameplay is driven by a deck of 120 cards. Players gather resources by drawing cards, construct developments from a common set of available choices, and negotiate trades either with the bank or with fellow players. Trading plays an even larger role in this version: any player who trades while it is not their turn is rewarded with an extra resource card.

How to Play:

- Collect and trade for the resource cards you need to build.
- Expand your region, recruit knights, and upgrade your settlements for victory points.
- Be the first player to reach 7 victory points to win the game.

name: Love Conquers All
description:
Love Conquers All is a cooperative tile laying game that abstracts the challenges of relationships for 1 to 5 players.

The board represents a relationship. There is a deck of cards including challenges and love cards. Each challenge corresponds to a shape of tile and brings a rule with it (e.g. I must play the largest card in my hand). When you play a tile, you must follow that rule and keep following it until somebody plays a love tile touching your challenge and flips it so it no longer affects game play.

The theme of relationships is reflected in how the challenge cards affect play. "Sickness" and "Injury" prevent you from playing on the board edges. "Travel" requires you to play at the edge. The challenge cards aren't called "problems" because they just bring a difficulty to the situation. the "Children" card must be touched by all plays because anybody who knows somebody who becomes a new parent knows that until they get enough help (love) there will be a lot of focus on the kids.

Players win collectively if they can get through the deck without running out of legal places to place tiles.

—description from the designer

name: Love Letter Stories
description:
Love Letter Stories is a card game where you can play Love Letter up to eight times, and the story branches out each time, allowing you to enjoy a unique story experience.

The deck of cards changes gradually depending on the branching that occurs depending on the outcome of the game or the player's choices, and the cards that represent the characters that appear as a result.

Cards that represent the interactions and relationships with various people surrounding the love letter are displayed to the players. While some players will successfully win the love of the princess, others may form new bonds with others and have an unexpected future.
What path will the your character take, and how will you end up?

Love Letter Stories, the culmination of the Love Letter saga, is also packed with content.
There are 203 cards that cover the story branches, and the storybook with the ending is 88 pages long.
Become a character in the world of Love Letter and enjoy the story to your heart's content.

Not a legacy game. It can be replayed for different outcomes each time.

name: Cities USA
description:
A great American city awaits your vision! Step into the shoes of an urban planner as you take on the challenge of transforming a bustling metropolis into a modern masterpiece. Raise gleaming skyscrapers, build bridges connecting roads and shape green spaces and water fronts to create a city that stands the test of time. Each decision matters; every building, every street, every neighborhood is a piece of your legacy. Gather the right materials,outplan your rivals, and claim your place as the architect of the future. Smart planning equals stunning results.

In this completely independent version of Cities you will find the essence of its predecessor but with new mechanics, such as skyscrapers, bridges and highways.

—description from the publisher

name: Luddite
description:
Luddite is a roll and write style game with a fully integrated graphic novel. In Luddite, one to an unlimited number of players will progress along the story of the novel whilst competing to destroy ever more complex automata, creating a full campaign style game.

As a Luddite, you will be hacking into the neural networks of the NED automata. These bionic, dog-like creatures are capable of performing almost any complex task to which they are assigned and, as such, have begun to replace vast swathes of the human population. As a Luddite, you will work to destroy these infernal machines.

During each game, players will roll three communal dice then use these dice to interact with the various modules of the NED. They will move their Neetle nanobot through the systems of the NED, opening and closing logic gates to enter and destroy key systems of the NED robot. All the while, collecting valuable resources to help them along their way.

Each round players must add one of the dice to the clock module, the higher the die added, the more damage done to the NED but also the less time the player has inside its systems, creating a push-your-luck style tension to each decision.

If players do not get their Neetle nanobot to the exit node of the NED before the clock runs out, their hack will be a failure.

—description from the designer

name: Lumina Spell
description:
Get the legendary light magic from the stained glass!

Push the tiles on the board by making the stained glass tiles resonate!
 You can get the same number or a sequence of numbers at once!
 If you have the same combination in your hand, you get a light magic card!

—description from the publisher (translated)

In this game, players take turns using the tiles in their hand to push out tiles on the board, and win cards by matching tiles with the same combination of cards on the field.
The number of points on the cards is the victory point, and the player with the most victory points wins the game in the end.

name: Claustrophobia 1692
description:
Welcome to Claustrophobia 1692, a two-player combat game set in a fictional maze of caverns where human warriors battle infernal forces rising from the depths of Hell. One player leads a desperate band of condemned warriors, led by their Redeemer, who are seeking to fulfill a divine mission, while the other commands numberless demonic hordes seeking to destroy them. Every game is a story of survival or damnation.

Using modular dungeon tiles and scenario-based objectives, Claustrophobia 1692 is played over a series of rounds, each divided into a human turn and an infernal turn. Rounds continue in this way until the endgame conditions described for the scenario have been met, at which point the victor is determined.

—description from the publisher

name: Lunar Trick
description:
In Lunar Trick / ルナトリック, you need to win exactly one, three, or five tricks in a round to score points — and to collect tricks, you need to manage the phases of the moon.

To start a round with three players, deal ten cards to each player and set the remaining card aside. Cards are 1-15 (rising moon), 16-30 (falling moon), and the lunar eclipse card.

Each player reveals a numbered card at the same time to determine the trump and three suits. For example, if rising moon had more cards played, then it's trump. If the cards are, e.g., 5, 12, and 24, then the three suits are 6-11, 13-23, and 25-30+1-4. Whoever played the highest card of these three collects this trick, then leads the next one. You must follow suit, if possible, or play the lunar eclipse card. If any trump is played in a trick, then the highest trump wins; if no trump is played, then the lunar eclipse wins; otherwise the highest non-trump wins. (The lunar eclipse card counts as a trick on its own, apart from the other cards won.)

Whoever wins one or five tricks scores 2 points, and whoever wins three tricks scores 1 point. Play multiple rounds until someone has at least 5 points and wins.

With four players, add the solar eclipse card to the deck. Whoever gets this in hand must play it during the first trick; they win this card, which counts as a trick, then determine trump and suits based on the other three cards, with the highest card winning that trick.

name: Lunch [atop a Skyscraper]
description:
In 1932, when an advertising agency sent a photographer on assignment, it was not customary to attribute authorship to their works. The taking of ‘Lunch atop a Skyscraper’ was no exception: the scene was part of an advertising campaign for the GE Building (also known as 30 Rockefeller Plaza) in New York and involved eleven models posing for the shot.
When the photograph became world-famous, efforts were made to find out who had taken it, but ‘Lunch atop a Skyscraper’ is now considered the work of an anonymous author.
In the game, you take on the role of a photographer competing to complete an assignment for an advertising agency: achieve the highest score by taking the photograph, emulating ‘Lunch atop a Skyscraper’. Collect Worker tiles and arrange them to form your scene, scoring points for the longest continuous series of each of the 8 model characteristics.

This game is the start of a series of games, the ‘Flash-black series’, which take as their starting point an iconic photograph.

—description from the publisher

name: Gaudí
description:
Step into a world where art defies gravity and stone becomes dream. Shape forms, balance light and nature, and bring to life the visionary style that redefined architecture.

Antoni Gaudí was a visionary Catalan architect born in 1852, renowned for his imaginative and distinctive style that blended Gothic and Art Nouveau influences. Players will travel through Gaudí's life and work, earning Victory Points in the three pillars that shaped his works: Nature, Catalonia, and Religion. To succeed, players must keep their progress balanced—only their two lowest VP scores among the three pillars will count toward final scoring. Points are gained by playing cards and placing 'Trencadís' tiles on their personal boards. 'Trencadís' is a Catalan word that means “a lot of little broken things”. While playing, you’ll discover some of these intricate details depicted on the cards and experience the creative joy of arranging your own trencadís patterns on your personal board. ). Each pillar awards VP differently: Nature points are mainly earned through Nature cards, Catalonia points are mostly scored at the end of each round, and Religion points are primarily tallied at the end of the game.
 The game unfolds over three rounds. In each round, players take turns moving around the central Chandelier on the main board, carefully choosing where to stop in order to perform key actions—drawing cards and collecting various types of Trencadís tiles. These resources are then used to play cards and progress up the Chimneys on their personal boards. Each round concludes once all players have completed a full circuit around the Chandelier. At the end of the third round, the player with the highest and most balanced combination of VP will be declared the winner!

—description from the publisher

name: Shugendo
description:
In this strategy game, you will guide the expansion of your family's farm beyond the known boundaries of the forest. As your settlement grows, more people will gather under your banner. You will cultivate the land, build new communities, and shape the future. However, you must proceed with caution. Your expansion may unsettle the spirits that still dwell in the wilderness. The yokai are vigilant, and their mischief can hinder your plans if you fail to recognize their presence. Increase your influence, adapt your strategies, and attract the right people to your settlement to gain victory points.

In Shugendo, each player has their own personal deck of cards. During the game, you will improve your deck by replacing your weaker starting cards with more powerful settler cards. In each round, players play three phases: reveal, action, and recruitment. In the first phase, they will reveal cards until they decide to stop or until they 'explode' by revealing 7 or more yokai icons. If this happens, they can only play either the action phase or the recruitment phase. In the action phase, players increase their meters based on the revealed cards and perform one of the main actions (explore, expand, or develop). Finally, in the recruitment phase, players receive various bonuses based on the revealed cards and recruit cards from the unlocked eras.

—description from the publisher

name: Dice Throne: Outcasts
description:
Dice Throne is a combat game, whether 1v1, 2v2, 3v3, 2v2v2, or free-for-all. Select from a variety of heroes that play and feel completely distinct from one another. Attack opponents and activate abilities by rolling your hero's unique set of five dice. Accumulate combat points and spend them on cards that have a large range of effects, such as granting permanent hero upgrades, applying status effects, and manipulating dice directly whether yours, your teammate's, or even your opponent's.

Outcasts is the newest edition of the Dice Throne universe introducing 4 new heroes: Pale Lady, Headless Horseman, Raveness, Necromancer.

name: Madcala
description:
This was once the Mad Hatter's favorite tea party tradition, a game of Madcala, that was until the Cheshire Cat took over as host.

In this edition of Madcala, the characters from Wonderland's War will be taking part in his tournament of Champions!

Madcala is a 1v1, asymmetric game that pits players against each other in a battle of wits and luck! Out thinking and out maneuvering your opponent will prove easier said than done!If you can reduce your opponent's health to zero, you win!

On your turn, you will pick a plate of beads pick them all up and leave one behind on each plate you pass, whatever plate you end on will give you an action to perform. You can also call on the aid of your "plus ones" to the event. They have powerful abilities that give each player a different approach and strategy.

—description from the publisher

name: Magazine
description:
In Magazine, each player runs their own magazine company. Your goal is to investigate important or intriguing topics and publish magazines that resonate with your readers. The better your articles align with your magazine’s theme, the more influence you’ll gain.
Build your reputation through smart editorial choices and timely publications — when the game ends, the player with the highest influence points will be crowned the most renowned publisher!

—description from the publisher

name: Marvel Dice Throne: X-Men
publisher: Dice Throne, Inc.; The Op Games; Roxley
description:
In Marvel Dice Throne: X-Men, you become one of eight of Marvel's iconic X-Men, including Wolverine, Storm, Cyclops, Rogue, Gambit, Psylocke, Iceman, and Jean Grey! Featuring all-new mechanisms and asymmetrical designs, these are some of our most innovative and exciting heroes yet!

Marvel Dice Throne: X-Men is a game of skilled card play and dice manipulation supporting multiple modes of play, including 1v1, 2v2, 3v3, 2v2v2, or free-for-all.

Attack your opponents and activate abilities by rolling your hero's unique set of five dice. Accumulate combat points and spend them on cards with an extensive range of effects, such as granting permanent hero upgrades, applying status effects, and manipulating dice directly (yours, your teammate's, or even your opponent's).

All eight heroes are compatible with the entire Dice Throne ecosystem, and features a deluxe, highly functional, Battle Chest storage system, with a set of custom swirl dice for each hero!

name: Magic Number: The Party Game of Wild Guesstimation
description:
Will you be able to guess the Magic Number? In this new party game, the answer to every question is a number, and the player with the closest guess wins!

Magic Number features hundreds of questions across three categories that will test your knowledge (or lack thereof) of random facts and how well you know your friends. Will your guess be spot-on, just a little off, or mind-bogglingly awful?

With the ability to customize questions, indicated by blue, underlined text found on most cards, Magic Number will always be unique and exciting, no matter how many times you play.

Gather your friends, and let the guessing games begin!

—description from the publisher

name: Marvel Dice Throne: X-Men – Cyclops v. Gambit v. Rogue v. Jean Grey
publisher: Dice Throne, Inc.; The Op Games; Roxley; Grimspire; Lucky Duck Games
description:
In Marvel Dice Throne: X-Men, you become one of four of Marvel's iconic X-Men, including Cyclops, Rogue, Gambit, and Jean Grey!

Every Marvel Dice Throne hero is painstakingly designed and balanced to provide the most thematic experience possible, allowing you to truly embody your favorite heroes like no other game. Featuring all-new mechanisms and asymmetrical designs, these are some of our most innovative and exciting heroes yet!

Marvel Dice Throne: X-Men is a heart-pumping, fast-playing game of skilled card play and dice manipulation supporting multiple modes of play, including 1v1, 2v2, 3v3, 2v2v2, or free-for-all.

Attack your opponents and activate abilities by rolling your hero's unique set of five dice. Accumulate combat points and spend them on cards with an extensive range of effects, such as granting permanent hero upgrades, applying status effects, and manipulating dice directly (yours, your teammate's, or even your opponent's).

All four heroes are compatible with the entire Dice Throne ecosystem.

name: Magical Athlete
publisher: CMYK; Geekach LLC; Gém Klub Kft.; IELLO
description:
Magical Athlete is a racing game of pure chaos! Roll a die and move your racer that many spaces — but all the racers have wacky, game-breaking abilities. Race four times, then whoever has the most points wins!

Before the racing begins, players will draft the four racers they will have in the game and choose before each race which to use. Races alternate between the "mild" side of the board and the "wild" side of the board. A race ends once two racers have crossed the finish line — with, generally, only these two players receiving points.

—description from the publisher

name: Magicarta: Le Fantôme de la Sorcière
description:
Enter the mysterious world of Magicarta, an evolving narrative puzzle game. You play as the ghost of a witch seeking to regain her memory and uncover the secrets of her past. Each game invites you to explore a fascinating universe, meet intriguing characters and solve puzzles to advance in your quest.

Magicarta combines captivating narration and intellectual challenges in an adventure accessible to the whole family. Discover a world that gradually unfolds as you progress, for games full of surprises and twists. Will you be able to lift the veil on your origins?

Explore the world of Magicarta on the 9 large boards forming a giant map and which will be revealed chapter after chapter.

Solve puzzles using the game boards and hidden details, Modify the environment with the event cards, collect artifact cards throughout your adventure that will help you understand the puzzle mechanics to solve.

Once your adventure is over, discover the little bonus game as a reward: Form words and advance on the game boards discovered during the puzzles for an infinite number of games. This game reuses all the elements of your adventure and will give a second wind to your equipment!

—description from the publisher

name: Magnate: The Anarcho-Capitalist Card Game
description:
Magnate is a 3-6 player card game in which the players take on the roles of the 0.01%. Their goal is to collapse the 'elected' government (past the point where money-printing will save it) and to take control of the anarcho-capitalist 'utopia' that unfolds following the governmental collapse.

This is a game of two halves.

During the first phase of the game the players must hoard as many commodities and pay as little tax as possible. Players play minions which they use to tactically attack other the players and the government. The government functions as a non-player entity. The goal of the first phase of the game is to strategically build up your position while cooperating with the other players to take down the government. Beware! The government can, and does, win if players focus too much on building their own positions.

In the second phase, triggered after the government is bankrupted, a new deck of player cards are unlocked. Hasn’t everyone wanted their own private air force from time to time?

Within an anarcho-capitalist tundra, players fight over an increasingly scarce resource base. The game continues until only one Magnate worthy of the name is left (in possession of commodities) and wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Magneterra
description:
Embark on a cosmic adventure in the rugged world of Magneterra, a distant planet characterized by its towering mountains, deep valleys, and flowing rivers. This unique terrain, enriched with rare elements, is the birthplace of the mystical Tochon Magnets—ancient artifacts infused with immense magical energies. Drawn by the allure of these powerful entities, human Mage Warriors have come to Magneterra, driven by a thirst for magical knowledge, each aspiring to become the most powerful mage.

Magneterra introduces an innovative game mechanic centered around the fascinating properties of magnetism. Players begin the game with the ability to attract Tochon Magnets from the shortest pillars on the game board, utilizing specially designed figurines that interact with magnetic fields. As players gather more magnets, their magnetic powers increase, enabling them to draw from increasingly taller pillars. The ultimate challenge lies in being the first to claim the Tochon Magnet from the tallest pillar, a feat that not only requires strategic maneuvering and skillful play but also crowns the winner as the supreme Mage Warrior of Magneterra.

However, the quest for magnetic supremacy is fraught with danger. The native Thians—part metal, part flesh giants—and their loyal Ankylocat companions fiercely defend the Tochons. These formidable opponents roam the landscape, determined to thwart the Mage Warriors and preserve the natural balance of their planet. As tensions rise, players must decide whether to confront these monsters directly or find more cunning ways to navigate the perilous terrains and claim the ultimate magnetic prize. With every move fraught with peril and opportunity, who will emerge victorious, and at what cost? The battle for Magneterra's Tochon Magnets is about to begin!

—description from the publisher

name: Make Your Bubble Tea
description:
Black Tea Base with Lychee and Tapioca, or Milk Base with Passion Fruit and Strawberry? Prepare your Bubble Tea, the famous Asian drink! Choose the size, put on the base, don't forget the pearls and manage your orders in the most efficient way possible. Discover this refreshing drink and have fun making as many Bubble Teas as you can, to be the one who leads the expansion of this wonderful Asian drink.

Shuffle all the cards and form a deck with the orders face up. Place in the center of the table forming 4 columns: 4 orders in a row and 4 Bubble Tea below. Put all the pearls in the bag and place 2 at random between each order and Bubble Tea. Choose one of the four columns and take the order, the two pearls and the Bubble Tea to your particular area, keeping it vertical in front of you. Make a Bubble Tea recipe (only one per turn). To do this, look at the card you want to make and discard the necessary materials from your area to a common discard area. The Bubble Tea made, leave it horizontally to one side in your particular area. Replenish the empty column by flipping the top Order of the deck placing it as Bubble Tea, place the next card from the deck as Order and 2 random pearls from the bag. When the deck of cards is finished, the end of the game is activated and the round ends.

name: Marvel Dice Throne: X-Men – Iceman v. Psylocke v. Storm v. Wolverine
publisher: Dice Throne, Inc.; The Op Games; Roxley; Grimspire; Lucky Duck Games
description:
In Marvel Dice Throne: X-Men, you become one of four of Marvel's iconic X-Men, including Wolverine, Storm, Psylocke, and Iceman!

Every Marvel Dice Throne hero is painstakingly designed and balanced to provide the most thematic experience possible, allowing you to truly embody your favorite heroes like no other game. Featuring all-new mechanisms and asymmetrical designs, these are some of our most innovative and exciting heroes yet!

Marvel Dice Throne: X-Men is a heart-pumping, fast-playing game of skilled card play and dice manipulation supporting multiple modes of play, including 1v1, 2v2, 3v3, 2v2v2, or free-for-all.

Attack your opponents and activate abilities by rolling your hero's unique set of five dice. Accumulate combat points and spend them on cards with an extensive range of effects, such as granting permanent hero upgrades, applying status effects, and manipulating dice directly (yours, your teammate's, or even your opponent's).

All four heroes are compatible with the entire Dice Throne ecosystem.

name: Mal Ardent
description:
HELL HAS BROKEN LOOSE IN SAINT-ANTOINE
Bread is cursed... it's driven us all mad! Faithful, pray to restore order, and destroy the possessed!
... Or have you gone mad too?

Mal Ardent (Fiery Evil) is an atmospheric hidden-role game pitting the Faithful against the Possessed.

The world is set in a village ravaged by four plagues: Pestilence, War, Famine and Madness.

Each player will offer a Judge a Prayer card to deliver the village from Evil, while the Possessed, hidden among the Faithful and knowing each other, will have to parasitize the game in order to destroy the village.

The Faithful must take one of the Scourges to Redemption, and the Possessed must draw one of the Scourges into the Evil of the Fiery, which inevitably falls on the village at every turn, trying not to be unmasked.

—description from the designer

L’ENFER S’EST RÉPANDU EN SAINT-ANTOINE
Le pain est maudit... il nous a tous rendus fous ! Fidèles, priez pour rétablir l'ordre, et anéantissez les possédés !
... À moins que vous n'ayez, vous aussi, perdu la raison ?

Mal Ardent est un jeu d'ambiance à rôles cachés où s'affrontent Fidèles et Possédés.

L’univers s’installe dans un village rongé par quatre fléaux : la Malepeste, la Guerre, la Famine et la Folie.

Chaque joueur proposera à un Juge une carte Prière pour délivrer le village du Mal, alors que les Possédés, cachés parmi les Fidèles et se connaissant entre eux, devront parasiter la partie afin d’anéantir le village.

Les Fidèles devront emmener l’un des Fléaux vers la Rédemption et les Possédés devront tirer l’un des Fléaux vers le Mal des Ardents, qui s’abat inéluctablement sur le village à chaque tour, en tâchant de ne pas être démasqués.

—description from the designer (French)

name: Mala Suerte
description:
Bad Luck  is a family-friendly, short-game card game that tests your ability to handle luck. Your mission is clear: instead of seeking good luck, you must avoid four-leaf clovers and make your opponents accumulate them or run out of cards. Interaction is intense, as players can lie about their cards, adding an element of strategy and deception. With quick decisions and strategic card management, Bad Luck offers an experience full of surprises.Think you can get unlucky? Figure it out and prove that luck is not on your side!

—description from the designer

name: Malabares
description:
The year is 1922 and the famous Circo Alcibíades is bringing joy to the crowds in São Paulo. You are budding clowns looking to make a living through juggling, and the great clown Piolin is ready to teach you how to amaze the audience. Only one of you will be able to join the circus… and the show is about to begin!

Malabares is a 18-card micro trick-taking game inspired by juggling. Players start with cards in hand, and some cards begin on the table representing what it's "in the air". A trick goes by playing cards in a must-follow fashion, and the numbers determine the order of drafting for the "in the air" cards.

Players score depending of the circus card, that indicates if the show is going on day or night - knives score more during the day, torches at night. Players can also "shoot the moon" by performing the Piolin Move, getting a full hand of low-scoring cards.

Game #03 of the Piquinim Collection.

—description from the publisher

name: Malediction
description:
Clash forces with your opponents in this blend of miniature gaming and deck construction, where resource management is key as you draw cards and gain more echo every round to pay for the units, items, and spells you play, building up you warband as you go and making sure each match is a constant surprise.

You play as a Seeker, a champion of your faction, leading a warband into the accursed grounds of the Malediction and battling enemies to claim relics from the husks of their former wielders. The game can be played head-to-head or in teams. Players bring their choice of terrain set to create a battlefield and face one another using their custom decks, with each Seeker offering distinct play styles and creative ways to combine cards from their associated factions.

The object of the game is to reach a scenario’s mastery threshold. Players gain mastery by defeating enemies and holding onto relics that can be claimed if their units are nearby an uncontested husk at the end of a round.

Malediction is played over a series of rounds. Each round consists of 4 phases:
1. Refresh Phase: Players gain echo equal to 2 times the number of the round, refresh their units, draw 2 cards, and resolve an initiative bid.
2. Deploy Phase: Players deploy units and items onto the battlefield.
3. Action Phase: Players alternate taking turns activating their units.
4. End Phase: Players try to claim relics from nearby husks and check for victory.
After finishing the end phase, if no player has won the game, a new game round begins, starting with the refresh phase.

name: Malhya: Lands of Legends
description:
With the balance of the planet Malhya threatened, a group of heroes awake.

You are one of those heroes with extraordinary abilities. Master the power of the Aura, the energy of the planet, complete the missions one by one, and thwart the plans of your enemies while overcoming all obstacles placed in your path.

In this great narrative adventure, you will be able to enjoy a complete experience, exploring regions as well as dungeons while testing your abilities on several levels. Infiltrate, fight, craft, negotiate, solve riddles, but above all live a story that will be told according to your own choices.

Multiple scenarios, miniatures, high replay value, save progress without blocking your material.

—description from the publisher

name: Slam Throne
description:
Stack. Slam. Repeat.

The heroes of Dice Throne have entered a new arena in Slam Throne! Use your hero slammer to flip your opponent's caps, reducing their health to zero in this dueling throwdown challenge.

—description from the publisher

name: Malus Hortus
description:
Malus Hortus is a cooperative game, all players win or lose together. Players are a party of Nymphs who have been lured in to this beautiful garden by day, only to find it turns evil at night and does not want you to leave. Do not let the word ‘garden’ fool you, this place is a vast woodland with shifting terrain and it will take many days to find your way to freedom.

The main aim of the game is to work together to ensure every Nymph leaves the board, escaping Malus Hortus. Along the way there are evil Flowers to avoid and Critters to save from the garden.

Magical creatures from many different realms find themselves ensnared by, and lost in Malus Hortus; through Night Cards and Critter Cards you will encounter some of them along your journey, as well as being affected by the enchantments they use to try and flee. Be warned, not all of them are quite as kind natured as your fellow Nymphs, it is not just the Flowers of Malus Hortus that you need fear.

—description from the designer

name: Manatee Sanctuary
description:
Hungry Manatees, Playful Manatees, Common Manatees, attract them all to your ever growing habitat to create the best Manatee Sanctuary and win the game!

Manatee Sanctuary is a family weight game in which players will draft cards using an "I split you choose" method over the course of 3 rounds. Once the draft is complete players will decide whether to use their cards for their top action, thereby attracting manatees and producing food, or grow their sanctuary by tucking the top portion of the card under their ever expanding board creating more room for manatees and increasing their food production.
