At this time, Vichy French forces controlled Madagascar with the potential of turning the island into a base for Axis attacks against Allied sea lanes in the western Indian Ocean. Ironclad was the first phase of the invasion which began in May and concluded in November.

The game has two players: British and Vichy French. Each player is provided with cardboard pieces called “units,” representing land, air and naval formations. Players move their units on the map to engage enemy forces and take critical objectives. Each player has a set of Operations markers which enhance unit actions and take special actions.

Overall, the game system models operations which were conducted in sometimes inhospitable terrain. Most actions were along major lines of communications for control of critical towns, ports, and airfields. Many of the combat losses were due to disease (British) and desertion (Vichy French), and this is reflected in the combat system.

name: Operation Tidal Wave: The Raid on the Ploesti Oil Refineries August 1, 1943
description:
Operation Tidal Wave is a solitaire play simulation game on the US Eighth (44th and 93rd Bomber Groups) and Ninth Air Forces’ (98th, 376th and 389th Bomber Groups) raid on the Romanian oil refineries on August 1, 1943. In the game the active player takes on the role of the American airstrike commanders who must defeat the Romanian and German air defenses and inflict as much damage on the oil complexes as possible.

—description from the publisher

name: OPPIDUM: Celtic Warriors Against Roman Legionaries
description:
OPPIDUM is a Tactical level skirmish board wargame that takes place during the 50s BC, when Julius Caesar successively attacked the various Celtic and Germanic peoples in Western Europe and (future Great) Britain.

The game uses the concepts and scale of the Cry Havoc series. The different scenarios will allow you to simulate ambushes, attempts by the defenders of Alesia to break the siege or the landing of Roman legionnaires on a Britannia beach defended by warriors on chariots.

—description from the publisher

name: Opération Noisettes
description:
Oh no, winter's coming and the weasel has stolen all the squirrels' nuts before falling asleep at the foot of the tree!

In Opération Noisettes, help the squirrels to recover their entire stash, but beware: the weasel only sleeps with one eye open!

Will you manage to get all the hazelnuts back into the tree without waking her up?

How to play this collaborative board game?


     Roll the dice and retrieve one or more hazelnuts from the weasel
     Gently place the hazelnut in the hole of the tree indicated by the dice
     Be careful, if the hazelnut falls into the tree and falls on the table, a leaf is removed from the weasel
     If all the hazelnuts have been stored in the tree before the weasel has no more leaves on it, you won!

name: Opération Zèbre
description:
Try to make people guess your classified document by crossing out superfluous lines directly on your card. Read what's left out loud, but be careful to leave enough information for your teammates to guess!

To do this, you will first have to cross out as many lines as possible directly on the card because each piece of information left visible generates suspicion about your group and too much suspicion will cause you to lose the game. Read your text out loud, and hope your team understands the message.

Novice or advanced mode, in cooperation or in teams, adjust the difficulty as you wish for games that are always just as interesting regardless of the number of players or the gaming habits of the participants around the table.

8 themes (Films, Series, Characters, Personalities, Monuments, Natural sites, Cities and territories), 490 classified documents to guess await you for a game of knowledge like you've never seen before!

—description from the designer

name: Orapa Space
description:
A Brilliant Laser-Based Deduction Challenge!
The Aerospace Department has sent us a mission: use laser beams to uncover the hidden positions, directions, and colors of mysterious planet-shaped pieces. By carefully analyzing the laser signals that bounce back, players must deduce the exact setup of the planets. But beware—lasers don't always behave predictably!

With just a few components—2 Space Boards, 2 Planet Sets, and a Solution Sheet—this game delivers a clever, quick-playing deduction puzzle for 2 to 5 players in around 20 minutes. Recommended for ages 8 and up.


     Discover the position and ‘color’ of the planets using only reflected laser signals.
     A step up from Orapa Mine, this game offers a deeper level of logical challenge.


—description from the publisher

name: Hedge Mage
description:
In Hedge Mage, you build a hedge maze of polyominoes to prevent your rival from stealing your gnomes, while simultaneously navigating your other neighbor's maze to nab their gnomes.

In this puzzly combination of polyomino placement and tactical movement, these moderately powered wizards have only two powers: grow shrubs, and animate garden gnomes. To sneak into your neighboring mage's yard to yoink their gnomes, while keeping another rival mage from snagging yours, it's going to take both powers you've got. Harness your horticulture magic to gather the greatest gnome collection!

In more detail, each player builds their hedge maze piece by piece at the same time. By using clever placement, you'll both hinder your rival's mages and gain movement points each round. Each player uses their movement points to maneuver their mages through their rival's maze in order to awaken each gnome according to specific enchantment cards. If all ten hedge cards have been revealed, or if a player has rescued all gnomes from their rival's board, the game ends and you move on to scoring. Whoever has the most points wins!

name: Orbit Master
description:
Orbit Master is a trick-taking strategy card game that is based on the Zodiac. In a turn by turn gameplay, players choose 1 Sign to play and the first player to build a House of the other 11 Signs under their Master Sign wins the game. But beware, the 13th Sign Ophiuchus can poison your Master Sign and change the course of the game.

The 12 signs of the Zodiac have existed in peaceful harmony since the beginning of time. However, the murmurs of a 13th sign have persisted without worry until now. The Snake Bearer, otherwise known as Ophiuchus has taken drink of the snakes venom and become corrupt with poisonous power. That poison has opened a black hole ripping the Celestial Orbit asunder releasing the balance of the 12 signs.

The Celestial Orbit needs to be restored, but with an Orbit Master to keep its hold. Which sign has the ability to muster the other 11 signs to re-establish the orbit?  And which sign can keep itself from being poisoned by Ophiuchus as well?

Each player must choose a sign to play and the first to bring the other 11 signs under their house becomes the Orbit Master!

—description from the designer

name: Squirrel Away
description:
You and your ragtag crew of squirrely thieves just pulled off the biggest heist of your bushy-tailed lives, grabbing a whole winter's worth of acorns back from the clutches of a greedy raccoon. Now you're at the rendezvous point, up to your cheeks in nuts, and it's time to split up the haul. To get away with more than your fair share, it'll take sneaky sleight-of-paw and every underhanded trick you can think of. Will you successfully scurry off with the biggest pile of acorns, or will another rogue rodent call you out as a scoundrel?

In each round of Squirrel Away, a player will pick a card that determines what they're allowed to take, then grab acorn gems from the middle of the table...possibly sneakily grabbing more than they should or acorns other than the ones indicated. They then claim to the group how many they grabbed, and the other players decide whether that player is telling the truth — that is, squirreling away what they took — or if they're a scoundrel, taking something they're not supposed to.

In the end, the player who squirrels away the most sets — that is, one gem of each color — wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Order of the Day: Normandy
description:
Order of the Day: Normandy is an Operational  level two-player board-wargame about the Normandy invasion of June, 1944 - playable in 45-120 minutes this is not a complicated wargame.

Played in IGO-UGO fashion, players move units from area to area across northern France and Belgium.  Combat occurs at the end of a turn in any area where both sides have forces and is resolved with a draw of cards.  The cards inflict hits on opposing units with 'bonus hits' caused by having specific types of units in the battle (Panzers, Rangers, Artillery, etc).

—description from the publisher

name: Flintlock!: Global Warfare in 20 Minutes
description:
Based on Paolo Mori's Blitzkrieg!, Flintlock!: Global Warfare in 20 Minutes is set during the events of the first full-scale global conflict in the 18th Century. Play one of two different two-player games: the Seven Years War in the theaters of Europe, India, and the Atlantic; or the French and Indian War in North America — or combine both boards for the ultimate 2v2 team-based battle.

Make crucial alliances to bolster your troops, boost your strategic support for more tiles, take down forts for new bonuses, plus more twists and surprises for Blitzkrieg! players, or anyone who loves a head-to-head tactical skirmish.

—description from the publisher

name: Order Up! Diner
description:
Serve up some excitement with the Order Up! Diner Game Set — the fast-paced stacking game everyone will enjoy!

Experience the fast-food frenzy with Order Up! Diner, the stacking game that will have you serving the most delicious dishes in the quickest time. Games Hub brings you this high-speed conveyor belt challenge where timing is key. In this game, players work to stack orders of delicious dishes before the conveyor belt takes them away. It's the perfect blend of strategy and fun for family game nights or competitive play with friends. Get ready to serve up some entertainment with Order Up! Diner.

—description from the publisher

name: Shadows of Brimstone: Cursed Tombs of Khamuntet
description:
In the Cursed Tombs of Khamuntet Core Set (initially called Lost Tombs of Khamuntet), players take on the role of a group of 1930s pulp adventure Heroes, exploring the dark chambers and crumbling passages of ancient Tombs, in search of fortune and glory! Lost in the desert sands of Egypt for thousands of years, these cursed temples are overrun with terrifying mummies, flesh-eating scarab swarms, and mythological guardians from Egyptian lore, brought to life through the power of the Dark Stone.

The Heroes of your expedition include the fearless Archaeologist, using her mastery of Egyptian Lore to explore the tombs while seeking out ancient artifacts and relics to bring back to the museums of Cairo, the combat-ready Soldier of Fortune, blazing away at dangers with his twin .45s, the scholarly Professor, using his knowledge of the occult and vast academic expertise to solve the riddles of the past, and the heavy-hitting Mechanic, using her hefty wrench to smash Enemies and her mechanical knowhow to overcome the deadly traps that litter the ancient halls.

New Enemies include Crypt Mummies, bursting forth from their burial chambers to take their revenge on the living, vicious Scarab Swarms that pour out of infested Sarcophagi to consume anything that lay in their path, the Cult of Horus, fanatical followers of the ancient ways working to resurrect the corrupted sorcerer Khamuntet, Anubite Jackals, terrifying supernatural hunters and warriors of Anubis, and the towering Tomb King, an ancient and massive statue brought to life to bring ruin on intruders!

This set also features the Sunken City of Pharrox, a brand new OtherWorld to explore. Once a powerful kingdom of the ancient world, ruled by a dynasty of ruthless vampires, the island city of Pharrox Atlantea was destroyed in a cataclysm of war with the Ancient Egyptians and their gods. Submerged beneath the roaring seas, the ancient city has been lost for millennia; its remaining inhabitants lay in twilight slumber until the long dormant gateways to the ancient city are activated once more.

—description from the publisher

name: ORIGINE
description:
Play as gods who wish to create an ideal world from elements such as water, minerals, animals, etc... 
This cooperative game is played without communication, requiring deduction to guess the partners' intentions and actions! 
Players take it in turns to place one of the elements on the different continents, while trying to respect its needs.
At the end of the game, we'll check whether each element has been ideally placed to score the most points and enter the pantheon of the gods!

—description from the publisher

name: Shadows of Brimstone: The Impossible Hell Train
description:
In The Impossible Hell Train Core Set, players take on the role of a group of traveling Heroes riding the railroad through the corrupted territory of the American Southwest. With the long-awaited rail lines of the Western Express now up and running, an influx of new blood have set their sights on making a name for themselves in the Badlands of Brimstone. But these are dangerous times, and swarms of HellBats darken the sky while gangs of Train Robbers lay in wait for the next locomotive carrying precious Dark Stone and wealthy passengers looking for adventure.

Players take on the role of Heroes like the Bounty Hunter, boarding trains to seek out her next bounty, dead or alive, the daring Cavalry Officer, master of Hit and Run attacks, wielding a pistol and sabre, the cunning Reporter from the big city, searching for the story of a lifetime, and the hearty Rail Worker, swinging his two-handed sledgehammer to smash demons as easily as he drives rail spikes to build the lines.

New Enemies include hordes of Soulless, demon-possessed undead passengers that have had their souls ripped out, Mounted Train Robbers on horseback to ride up alongside the train for a high speed shootout, as well as Train Robbers on foot for when they board the train searching for goods and Dark Stone to steal, Grotesques, nightmarish winged gargoyles from the Badlands that descend from the skies to tear their way into the train, and the hulking Hellborn Engineer, fused with the burning coals and twisted iron of the train itself, this brute burns hot with the power of the Darkness!

This set also features the otherworldly Hell Train, itself; a nightmare locomotive that runs on rails of fire, barreling through the Void and burning its mark across all worlds! Flickering in and out of reality, the runaway Hell Train belches black smoke from its stacks, and the sound of its whistle splits the night as the thunderous rumble of its engine shakes the foundations of the earth as it approaches.

—description from the publisher

name: OrthoGnomes
description:
Long ago in Gnomish lore, the Fire God and the Ice God played games to stave off boredom. 
If the Fire God won the world would heat up, and if the Ice God won the world would grow cold.
Resulting in the seasons of summer and winter in this world.

On your turn place your block of 3 with various sides of light and darkness, to try to connect four of your colors only seen on the outside. 
After all blocks have been placed, see if light or darkness prevails!

With one move you will transform five perspectives!

name: Oshiya Tokio
description:
Rush hour on the subway in Tokyo: In ‘Oshiya,’ players take on the role of legendary pushers who will do anything to get the maximum number of 21 people into the subway car. So play your cards cleverly, take new cards, and collect the maximum points to reach exactly 21 - but you can't go over 21 or else another player could snatch the deck away! A tactical card game full of excitement and Japanese rush hour charm!

—description from the publisher

name: Oslob
description:
Discover the fascinating world of whale sharks in Oslob! In this semi-cooperative board game for 2-5 players, you immerse yourself in the breathtaking environment of Oslob, where the goal is to skillfully bid on the movements of a whale shark to achieve your personal objectives.

Step into the shoes of a dedicated environmentalist and passionately advocate for the protection of the majestic whale sharks in Oslob. But be vigilant, for you are not alone. Tourists and researchers are also exploring the waters of Oslob Bay, each with their own interests.

Embark on the adventure, play Oslob, and become an active part of the change our world needs. Dive into the world of whale sharks and experience the challenges and responsibilities of environmental conservation up close.

—description from the designer

name: Osmosis
description:
The cooperative card-association game where you (almost) talk freely.
Discuss the combination of cards you think you're about to create together.
Make your associations.
Reveal your choices.
If most of you are in sync, you win!
You can describe your combination or the connections between cards —
but not anything that would clearly point to one or more specific cards.
Get in sync… and prepare to be surprised!

name: Duel for Cardia
publisher: Hans im Glück; 999 Games; asmodee; Brain Games; Devir; Feelindigo; Games4you; Giochi Uniti; Kaissa Chess & Games; Lucky Duck Games; Mandoo Games; MINDOK; Piatnik Distribution; Ponva d.o.o.
description:
Cardia is a fast paced, strategic card game for two players: Choose your card wisely to win each encounter against your opponent.
 In gratitude for her liberation, a mighty djinn created the wondrous city of Cardia. Legend has it that whoever wins over the four factions and gains their five powerful signet rings will rule the city. Your goal is set!
 Players will each pilot one of two Decks, made up of the same cards for each, with values from 1-16 and with each card having unique abilities. Play your cards at the moment your opponent does not expect them and use their abilities wisely to outwit them!

—description from the publisher

name: Otters
description:
In Otters, you play the role of a playful otter who searches for the most valuable pearls.

In your turn, pick a card and play one of your cards. Pick pearls, attack other otters, defend yourself and avoid sea urchins. If at the end of your turn you have two sea urchins in your hand, you are out, but you can still win because, at the end, the value of the pearls you have collected counts.

—description from the publisher

name: Flow
description:
Flow is a cooperative game where players work together to connect four animal spaces to the boat tile in the center of the board by drawing and playing tiles. Do you have what it takes to save the animals?

If players run out of tiles they and the animals have not been connected to the boat, they all lose.

The game uses a timer, and each time it runs out, players roll two dice that tell them where the giant wave strikes and washes away tiles already placed.

—description from the publisher

name: Out of Words
description:
Out of Words is a cooperative game in which the whole group tries to achieve the best score possible.

Each round, one player has to get the others to guess a specific word using as few words as possible. Clues consist of single words, and each clue must start with a letter from a 5x5 grid. If the group doesn’t guess the correct word, another clue may be given – up to five in total. Once the word has been guessed correctly, or after the fifth clue without success, all letters used from the grid are removed.

The game ends once the grid is completely empty. Players then count the number of words they successfully guessed.

In addition to this basic mode, Out of Words also includes a couple of extra challenges for ambitious groups.

—description from the publisher

name: Out There Waiting
description:
The Lazarus Event changed everything.

Three days of horror. The dead rose—not mindless, but vengeful. Cities fell. Millions perished. And when the dust settled, the world belonged to the dead.

Out There Waiting is a tabletop role-playing game that explores themes of survival, sacrifice, and hope.

You are a Runner—a survivor tasked with scavenging for Supplies, recruiting Survivors, and completing dangerous Missions to support the Colony.

The game is played over a series of turns, ending when the Colony either reaches 10 Prosperity Points through your life-risking efforts or falls due to the destruction of barricades or a loss of hope.

—description from the designer

name: Outbreak
description:
A Cooperative hybrid; Defensive Combat, Area Control, Worker Placement, Territory Building, Push Your Luck, Strategic Survival Game.

Outbreak is a cooperative board game. You play as a survivor group in a post-apocalyptic world where you are trying to protect the Survivor City from the zombie hordes, before they reach the Main Base and kill the helpless inside. Players control a skilled survivor or team of survivors (in solo play), that must work together to fight back the hordes of zombies.

Players start by constructing the survivor city around the Main Base. This safe area is now surrounded by zombie hordes whose goal is to reach the main base and eat all the survivors inside, overrunning settlements along the way. When a settlement is overrun, players can no longer request its support, so each turn players must attempt to destroy zombie hordes and prepare for the next wave of attacks. This is a very challenging game where cooperation is the key to surviving the zombie apocalypse!

No two games will ever be the same. The game features over 100 different zombies, over 20 survivor settlements and over 150 action cards, which combine for a fresh challenge every time you play.

Features:
Fully cooperative immersive game play
Solo or up to eight players!    
Unique drop in/out game feature
Build your very own city    
Resource gathering & management  
Construct: weapons, vehicles, buildings and much more    
Unique zombies
10 playable characters!

—description from the designer

name: OUTFOX the FOX
description:
A sly party game of Top Five lists!

Each Round one player is the FOX. They will choose a Top Five list card category, examine all the answers and then make up an answer they think the group will rank as one of the Top Five answers.
They read all six possible answers in random order as one of the players writes them on dry erase tiles. (The list source and date are part of the clue)

Then everyone else (up to 9 other players) have two minutes to debate the ranking order of the Top Five answers - and identify which answer is the Fox's false answer.

Player will all get one point for each correctly ranked answer and the Fox will gain a number of points based on how high the other ranked their answer as one of the Top Five... BUT before the correct rankings are revealed, the other players will take their colored token and place it on the one answer they PERSONALLY feel best about. Maybe they disagreed with the concusses at the table. You can even place your token on the answer you think was made up. If you are right, you get three bonus points.
Then, it is the next players turn to be the Fox as the game continues.

The fun comes in the group debate on whether Ranch Dressing or BBQ Sauce is highest on the list of Best Selling Condiments - or what were the Most Popular Baby Names in the 1980's. AND the sometimes surprising results!

Because it is a group discussion, it is a trivia game where you don't have to be 'on the spot' or singled out and everyone has an equally great time.

—description from the publisher

name: Outremer
description:
The year is 1099. The crusader armies besiege and capture Jerusalem, and new Christian states appear in the Levant. The Arab tribes — known to them as the Saracens — seek vengeance against them as they fight one another for favours from Vatican and control over trade. Their struggle is far from over…

Outremer is a grand strategy game that combines area control with well-crafted Euro-style mechanics. The action takes place in the Levant—on the eastern coast of the Mediterranean Sea—in the 12th century, right after the First Crusade. Each player takes control of one of four Crusader states and uses every available means to expand their influence and increase the wealth of their domain.

You'll develop cities, manage trade, appoint viceroys, send spies, and lead armies of battle-hardened knights into war. But victory in these lands requires more than just the sword—it demands strategy. Event cards and relentless Saracen raids can shatter even the most careful plans.

In the Levant, only the bold survive.

Gameplay Features:


     The Cross of Orders: a central element of planning and the struggle for resources and initiative. Players will face tough dilemmas: would you occupy an empty slot to profit at the expense of others? Choose a valuable action but pay another player for it? Or sacrifice a turn to perform a powerful action in the next round?
     Two layers of territory control: traditional military dominance and religious influence through bishops, using an area majority mechanic.
     Combat system: battles against other players and the game-driven common enemy (Saracens) depend on a smart combination of cards and a bit of luck. Players must decide what they are willing to sacrifice to achieve a coveted victory.
     Story-driven campaign: in addition to the main standalone game mode, players can explore 4 interconnected scenarios with persistent progress. Each scenario introduces a new mechanic, offering a fresh perspective on the familiar gameplay.


—description from the designer

name: Overparked
description:
It's the day of the big concert and vehicles are coming in from all directions! Can you handle the rush of traffic by cleverly parking all incoming vehicles to maximize your points? From veteran strategy puzzle game designer Daryl Chow and acclaimed Japanese illustrator TANSAN, Overparked brings an interactive puzzle strategy experience like no other!

Players take turns to rotate the steering wheel, determining the vehicles that will come to each player's lot. Then, all players decide which vehicles to place. The game ends when one player has no space left and all players will score for their connected vehicles, surrounded trucks and objectives to see who is the master parker!

name: OverPower
description:
In Lazarus Rising Games' modern revival of the classic card game, OverPower sees players assembling a team of 4 characters and building a custom deck containing associated Special cards for their team, numerical Power cards, and other tactical actions.

Each character possesses a "power grid" which defines their proficiency in the areas of Energy, Combat, Brute Force, and Intelligence -- represented by a numerical value from 1 - 8. Characters also have a Threat value which determines how many points they count towards for assembling a legal team less than or equal to the maximum point threshold. Some characters may also have Inherent Ability text which affords the character an additional, ongoing effect.

The game is played across shared rounds, where players draw 8 cards, encounter various Events which change the landscape of the impending battle, and can strategize by "placing" a number of cards to each of their characters as a way to save them for future battles and build card advantage. Battles consist of alternating actions between players, where the active player makes an attack from one of their characters to an opponent's character, using either cards from hand or placed cards. Attacks then open a response window for the opponent who can choose whether or not to defend the attack. Then, priority is passed to the next player who can make an attack or even concede the battle. A character can be knocked out of the game should they receive 20 or more points of damage, or hits with 3 or more of the 4 power types (Energy, Combat, Brute Force, Intelligence). At the end of the battle, the total value of successful attacks is calculated to determine the victor of the match.

A unique aspect of OverPower is the Venture system. Each round prior to the battle, players must wager a number of their 7 Mission cards, which function similar to poker chips, based on how confident they are that they'll win the upcoming battle. The winner of each battle, determined by how many successful points were scored by their team, then wins the number of Mission cards they wagered at the start of the round. Players can win the game either by knocking out all of their opponent's characters, or by successfully advancing all 7 of their Mission cards.

—description from the publisher

name: Pacific
description:
We journey now to the Pacific Ocean. From California to Japan, the peaceful sea is ringed by rumbling mountains. Animals, some of them tourists, fill every conceivable niche; boats dot the waves; and businesses and industries thrive on the coasts. It is this world that you will exploit, or make friends with, or perhaps just pass through.

Your goal in Pacific is to earn more money than anyone else, whether through fishing, hotels, factory work, or business. The game lasts ten rounds, and at the start of each round, each player reveals one card from their hand at the same time. Next, all players reveal which one of the revealed cards they want to use, then they simultaneously use their chosen card.

Each player has their own playing board with five areas on it in a circle: Japan, California, Peru, Polynesia, and Coral Sea. To use a card, you carry out the text in the box, then "run" the 1-2 areas listed on it.

Most cards have text like "[area]:[symbols]", such as "California: (hotel)" or "Each area: (fish)" or "An empty area: (boat)(boat)", so you'll place the appropriate token(s) in the named area(s). The card might have other text as well instructing you to move tokens, swap one token for another, "run" an area, etc.

To "run" an area, you take an action with each token in it: hotels earn you money, boats earn you money based on fish in the area, fish move clockwise to the next area, and factories let you remove tokens for money. Special tokens have unique abilities, and you can carry out these actions in whatever order you wish.

After ten turns, whoever has the most money wins.

name: Spot it! Catan
publisher: Zygomatic; Brain Games; Hobby Japan; Igroljub; MEBO Games; MIPL; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
Spot it! CATAN takes you to Klaus Teuber's iconic island for a real-time game of discovery and exploration. In the game, players recreate the island using cards and experience five CATAN-themed adventures. In "Welcome to Catan!", for example, players race to find the matching symbol between their card in hand and one of the cards on the table, covering as much of the island as possible with their cards.

The four other mini-games include "Ports", "Longest Route", and "Barbarians and Knights", and in each game, the first player or team to score 10 points wins.

name: Pacifica
description:
The islands of the pacific produce and value many different resources. Pacifica is a light strategy card game in which players trade these resources throughout the Pacific, trying to put together baskets of goods for sale. On your turn you can take a free resource from an island local to you, trade in the market, or use canoes to take or trade resources from a more distant island.

—description from the publisher

name: Pack the Essentials
publisher: Wacky Wizard Games; Pudgy Cat Games
description:
Pack the Essentials is a lightweight, abstract strategy game about packing cats in suitcases.

Throughout the game, players work to score as many points as possible by drafting and placing tiles in their suitcase to pack items, cats, and kittens; collect cat toys; and use the friendly neighborhood Pack Rat Service. Players also attempt to complete "To Do" list goals and create the largest sections of each color tile. The game plays over twelve rounds, then the player with the most points wins.

When playing with fewer than four people, players will additionally compete against The Cat Ladies Club, a simple AI opponent that creates the sensation of a four-player game by removing tiles from the draft pool just as other players do.

name: It's Obvious
description:
In It's Obvious, the host reveals one of the two hundred questions included in the box, then players secretly choose the "correct" side. Man fish or fish man? Cilantro is soapy or cilantro is delicious?

Once all players have voted, their vote cards are shuffled, then flipped face up to reveal which answer received more votes. The side with the most cards is the obvious choice, while the other is the oblivious choice. Now players debate!

If you're on the oblivious team, it's time to lie! If you're on the obvious team, it's time to find those oblivious players. Toss out outlandish accusations and engage in heated debate about the topic before eliminating a player. If the oblivious player(s) slide by without being caught, they win! If the obvious players can catch all of the oblivious players, then they win!

Will you choose the obvious choice?

name: Paddy
description:
In Paddy, you transform the landscape by creating terraces of rice paddies in the mountains of southeast Asia. On each turn, you decide what type of tile to add to the paddy and whether to place it in the day or night half. With each new tile, the paddy grows and adapts to the flow of water, preparing the ground for your species to thrive.

While you collaborate with others to sculpt a landscape of terraces and water channels, you also compete to secure the best pastures for your species. With each decision, you influence the growth of the paddy and the irrigation of its fields. The winner will be whoever has the most points at the end of four cycles.

Paddy is the fourth installment in the "Natural Wonders" series that includes Coral, Islet, and Gold Nugget.

—description from the publisher

Microbadge:  Paddy fan

name: Pairish: The Building of Sonnie Village
description:
Pairish: The Building of Sonnie Village is a fast cooperative board game for 2 to 8 players. You gather crops and care for pets and farm animals while building the picturesque Sonnie village. Pairish is suitable for big and small, experienced players and those new to the hobby.

Pairish has two play modes: Newcomers and Old-timers. The Newcomers mode is suitable for kids, people new to playing board games and for a first game so that you get familiar with the rules. The Old-timers mode is for more experienced players or those who want to feel a challenge. In both modes, the goal is for every player to collect a Pairish. You have collected a Pairish when at least 6 out of the 7 cards in your hand are equal by one of the stats - number of windows, floors or slopes.

In Old-timers mode you have to also complete the Mayor’s task. He decides what crops you should grow and what animals to take care of and in return, finances you with the village’s grant.

During one turn, you complete 4 actions: draw a card from the deck, build a house with the card face down, flip the card face up and give one card from your hand to the player to their right. To win, every player needs to have collected their Pairish so you have to take care not only of your Pairish but help the other players as well.

Will you succeed in completing the Mayor's task before the clock strikes? It’s up to you and your fellow villagers. Good luck! And take care of each other’s Pairish…

—description from the designer

name: Pandamonium
description:
Pandamonium is a lightweight board game with card drafting and set collection mechanics. It's played over 4 rounds of simultaneous play where you'll be drafting cards to collect tributes for the Panda Lords.

In Pandamonium, you will bribe the Panda Lords and Usurpers to secure your place of influence within the Pandapire. Select your Tributes wisely and navigate the chaos of the Pandamonium Cards to ensure that when the dust settles, your influence remains supreme.

Gather your tribute and bribe your way to victory by gaining the favour of as many of the Panda Lords and Usurpers as you can. But don't get too comfortable with your hand it won't be yours for long.

At the end of the 4th round, the winner is the player with the most unique Favour Tiles.

—description from the designer

name: Pandora
description:
Embark on an epic journey into the enchanting realm of Pandora, a world teeming with adventure and strategy. Prepare to immerse yourself in a universe filled with excitement, where your destiny awaits, formidable challenges arise, and triumph is the ultimate goal in this captivating board game experience.

The game's heart lies in Secret Missions. Each player pursues their own path, striving to complete missions that unfurl throughout the game. As the game nears its conclusion, victory hinges on accumulating Victory Points.

Each turn includes the following actions, which can be performed in any order:

1. Movement: Navigate the board to the desired destination.

2. Build: Build bases to strengthen your character and gain advantages.

3. Fight: Engage in a battle for points among players or attack monsters where you team up with other players in the same territory to defeat enemies.

4. Train: Improve your skills and gain lasting benefits by training at a base. Ending your turn after training.

5. Gather: Obtain gold from the board or try to draw Pandora cards. Gold collection and Pandora card attempts are mutually exclusive.

6. Completing secret Missions: Try to complete secret missions to set you up towards the final scoring at the end of the game.

7. Character actions and resource trading: Use character-specific abilities and possibly exchange resources with other players.

The game continues until either the last card in the Pandora deck is revealed or a player reaches the indicated victory points on the VP (Victory Points) tracker. If any player would be defeated during the game, all players will lose the game all together.

After game reach it’s end the player's bonus points from secret missions are then tallied, and the player with the highest total emerges as the victor, etching their name among the legends of Pandora.

-description from designer

name: Pandora Celeste
description:
Woken by the Ship’s Computer, the crew of the CSS Pandora discover that their Ship may be even more deadly than the menacing Nasties lurking in its dark corners.  Because, as every Crewmember knows, the Ship's Emergency Protocols are there to protect the Cargo - they're not designed to protect the Crew.

Players play Action Cards from asymmetric personal decks to race around the ship searching for the elusive cards that will help them survive, in a semi-cooperative action-selection game with elements of deckbuilding built into it.  But hidden amongst those cards is a Pandora's Box of evils from the Sci-Fi universe that trigger when their cards are revealed.

The Crew's first task is to work together to shut down the logic puzzles of the Emergency Protocols (number based on difficulty). This then triggers a twist in which a Big Nasty emerges from the shadows and each player is transmitted a Hidden Agenda. Some Crew are looking for the Smoking Gun that will bring the Company down.  Others are working to protect the Company's interests. All are trying to survive.  Because what doesn’t make you stronger will probably kill you!

Everything they do generates Noise, but unlike most games in this genre, Noise can be used to manipulate the Nasties hunting you, sending them in a different direction - or even diverting them towards another member of the Crew!

The game ends when any member of the Crew Decouples one of the escape modules and gets away - but to do that without the other Crew on board, they have to first achieve their Agenda: otherwise they must wait for all surviving Crew to board before the module will let them evacuate the Ship.

-description from publisher

name: MonsDRAWsity: Unusual Suspects
description:
MonsDRAWsity is back with MonsDRAWsity: Unusual Suspects, a brand new, stand-alone edition to one of 2020 and 2021's best party games!

So when Deep Water Games decided to make another version, it made perfect sense to collaborate with the brilliant weirdos at Shut Up and Sit Down, a group of people known for being hilarious, energetic, wonderfully bizarre, and original. MonsDRAWsity: Unusual Suspects features over 100 new monsters conjured up by Shut Up and Sit Down and illustrated by some of your favorite (or soon to be favorite) artists.

—description from the publisher

name: Paneveggio
description:
Paneveggio will immerse you in 1700 close to the Paneveggio Forest where generations of renowned luthiers such as Amati, Stradivarius or Guardani took the precious wood to build the famous violins we still hear about today.
Players will embody young luthiers who are launching their own workshop after leaving their mentor.
They will try to earn as much Violin points (VP) as possible and offer their most beautiful work of art to prestigious musicians of that time by alternating work sessions and rest.
The game is based on a musical score mechanics, the notes are then representing planned actions.

—description from the publisher

name: Panots
description:
Panots is a competitive filler card game in which your goal is to build the most valuable sidewalk using the iconic panot tiles of Barcelona, Spain.

In each round, you must quickly choose between several panots and place them so that they fit perfectly with the existing ones on your board, thus maximizing your score. Strategy plays a crucial role: you must not only design your sidewalk carefully, but also be skillful in your choices so as not to miss opportunities. In addition, paying attention to the moves of your rivals can offer you advantages to overcome them.

In the end, whoever has the best-valued sidewalk will win the game.

name: Pantheum: Demigods of Olympia
description:
Recruit your own team of powerful Greek Demigods to reshape the world!

The war between the Titans and Olympians has left the world barren and empty. As humans begin to settle Farms, Cities and Temples, Zeus calls upon the gods to reshape the desert land. Play as one of the major Greek gods tasked with adding Forests, Mountains, and Rivers according to your Divine Plan. But watch out, the other gods have a different vision for how the world should be reformed.

Combine Area Control mechanics by moving your god around the map to influence different areas and an Engine Building system of recruiting powerful Demigods to augment and enhance your abilities each turn. The winner is the player who can score the highest by reshaping the world to according to their secret plan and hiring powerful Demigods.

—description from the publisher

name: Flickering Stars
description:
Transform your tabletop into a galaxy at your fingertips in Flickering Stars! Choose from two rival factions — the Children of Arha or the Terran Coalition — then take command of a powerful fleet, discover planets rich with resources, and battle it out with your spacefaring rivals in a quest to claim a piece of the stars!

1. FLICK your ships across the table.
2. FIRE missiles and plasma balls at your rivals to thwart their plans.
3. FINISH your objectives for the win!

With over one hundred custom-designed plastic pieces in the box, you can transport your table from the dining room to a war room in space as you face off in three scenarios. Start with an evacuation drill in scenario 1 to learn the basics of the game, then step it up in scenario 2 with a new ship and objectives. Scenario 3 brings it all together and more, adding refineries, outposts, and hubs. Each faction comes with five ships that serve different functions, including launching projectiles!

name: Forsaken
description:
Far from the galactic core, Thyrria and its moons have been strip-mined and left for dead. Abandoned workers huddle together in makeshift settlements, struggling to survive in a world of scarce resources and lawlessness. Native nomads and bizarre creatures resurface to take back the wasteland. Factions and adventurers rise and fall, but only the greatest will be remembered in legend.

Forsaken is an immersive sandbox adventure game where you take the role of a character looking to leave their mark in the harshest of worlds. Every character has a personalized branching story, with every path uniquely-tailored to the choices you make along the way. How will you change the face of Thyrria, and how will Thyrria change you?

Your goal is to secure your place as a legend in any way you can, but there are many ways to become a legend. Navigating through personal and public story objectives, doing odd jobs, hunting down bounties, fulfilling prophecies, and even gambling at the Cantina can all advance your legend tracker. Finding the right opportunities to upgrade your gear, weapons, and skills can help you along the way. Once a player reaches the end of the track, the player with the greatest legend wins.

At the end of your turn, you may trigger an event or encounter, which allows you an opportunity to permanently change the game and the emergent story based on the decisions you make. These changes can determine your character’s motives and goals personally, or guide the shared stories to impact the world itself. The more you change about the world, the bigger the mark you make and the greater your legend will be.

name: Paradise Resort
description:
Build the holiday resort of your dreams!
Paradise Resort is a strategic board game for 2 to 4 players in which you compete to become the best resort designer. Each player develops their own resort by combining land, buildings and objective cards to attract visitors and earn victory points.
With tile placement mechanics, resource management, and tactical planning, players must collect resources, build beach resorts, hotels, and mountain cabins, and fulfil objectives to maximise their score.
The aim of the game is to earn the most victory points through completed buildings and objectives at the end of the game. Plan your resort wisely and become the best tourist manager in paradise!

—description from the publisher

¡Construye el complejo vacacional de tus sueños!
Paradise Resort es un juego de mesa estratégico para 2 a 4 jugadores donde competirás por convertirte en el mejor diseñador de resorts. Cada jugador desarrolla su propio complejo combinando terrenos, construcciones y cartas de objetivo para atraer visitantes y sumar puntos de victoria.
Con mecánicas de colocación de losetas, gestión de recursos y planificación táctica, los jugadores deberán recolectar recursos, construir resorts de playa, hoteles y cabañas de montaña, y cumplir objetivos para maximizar su puntuación.
El Objetivo del juego es conseguir la mayor cantidad de puntos de victoria a través de construcciones y objetivos cumplidos al final de la partida. ¡Planea con astucia tu complejo y sé el mejor gestor turístico del paraíso!

—description from the publisher (Spanish)

name: Paradox Island
description:
Paradox Island is an adventure deduction game, in which all players except one will be exploring the island that only that one player can see. By moving blindly across the island players will be recreating the map and try to complete their missions.

GAME OBJECTIVE
One of the players takes on the role of the Omnipotence Paradox (OP) – the only player who sees the island and other players’ movements. Their mission is to have captives perished 5 times.

The rest players become captives of the island. Their missions are connected with movement across the island, visiting certain spaces or fulfilling certain conditions 5 times. The one to complete their mission first wins.

GAME FLOW
Captives take their turns one by one going clockwise with the OP finishing the circle.

On their turn, a captive can perform up to 2 actions, announcing them and getting feedback from the OP:

     move 1 space in any of the six directions automatically activating it. However, they can spend 1 energy to
         move 1 space over;
         move safely, which means you decide whether to activate the space or not after they know what it is.
    
     restore energy.


After a captive announced their movement, the OP names the destination point aloud.
Everyone hears the movements of the other players and can take notes on the map. However, they only know their own starting point, so during the game they need to think and put pieces together to have a better view of the map.

Spaces have good and bad effects, making players get some bonus actions and movements or lose their health and energy instead.

The OP controls 3 pieces on the island – the Rock, the Bush and the Wave. On the OP’s turn they can move the pieces around the island meddling into captives’ plans by making them harm or pushing to unwanted spaces.

—description from the publisher

name: Paragon: Monsters & Mayhem
description:
Paragon: Monsters & Mayhem is a fast paced fantasy TCG in which you command monsters and magic to dominate a gridded battlefield and eliminate your opponent's essence to be victorious! With an expansive array of creature cards, spell cards, ritual cards and item cards at your disposal, you'll strategize, adapt, and conquer in this thrilling game of tactics and glory!

In Paragon: Monsters & Mayhem you play as the Paragon of your choice. Players will take turns commanding cards into the different zones of the battlefield in order to reach victory. Winning the game consists of removing your opponents essence. Each time you strike a Player directly with one of your uncontested creatures or a direct damage spell they reveal one essence card and gain power from it. When a player with no essence cards is striked they are knocked out of the game!

Players construct 3 decks each with their own card types. One deck is your main deck which consists of creatures, spells, rituals and items. Your essence deck which consists of essence cards that you choose the order of before play to give you a tactical advantage against your opponent. And your mana deck of 10 to 20 mana cards that you will gain over the course of the match in order to pay for and command cards. The play area consists of the Combat Zone, a 4x4 grid where you command your creatures into in order to attack your opponents creatures or strike directly at your opponent, damaging their essence. The Support Zone, for playing your items and rituals which have longer lasting effects and can change the tide of battle. The Paragon Zone, for your Paragon to start in and use its abilities before advancing into the Combat Zone to join the battle.

—description from the publisher

name: Corgi Pileup
description:
The cutie pie corgi pups just want to snuggle. They cluster and clamber, making adorable doggie pyramids. Sadly, it’s not always so easy to climb and some pups will be left below the pile. But at the end of the day, for a little corgi pup, that may not be such a bad thing. After all, no one wants to fall off the top of a big corgi pileup!

Corgi Pileup is a trick-taking game in which only the last trick counts. During each trick, you must “climb” by playing cards greater than or equal to the highest card played so far, or else play your lowest card. Each round, you score your final card and increase your score. Rounds are played until someone’s score exceeds 15.  All players whose score exceeds 15 lose, and the remaining player with the highest score wins.

In the "Underdog Variant" the game ends as usual, but the player with the lowest score wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Paranormal
description:
Paranormal is a game about hunting monsters, helping people, and preventing the end of the world. Take on the role of different members of the Remington family as you hunt down ghosts, vampires, witches, and demons across the United States. Along the way, you'll collect clues about the whereabouts of the Big Bad who's trying to end the world, and then you'll try to go stop it.

At its core, Paranormal is an action point game with dice-rolling combat. Spend action points to move, fight, and find helpful asset cards. Roll dice to meet monster card requirements and slow down the doom track. Use item, weapon, and ally cards to mitigate dice rolls and manipulate monsters.

Put together enough clues to figure out where the Big Bad, a missing family member, and a special weapon are, and then head to that town to prevent the end of the world and win the game. All in about 45 minutes.

If you enjoy campy TV shows and movies about hunting monsters, I think you'll really enjoy this game!

—description from the publisher

name: First-Class Letters
description:
That mail truck is driving way too fast. Packages are rolling down the street and letters are flying everywhere. We’d better get this in order or else it spells disaster.

First Class Letters is a roll-and-write word game played over 7 rounds. Each round players write a word on their sheet using letters rolled on dice, as much as they can. The words on their sheet must be kept in alphabetical order, or be cancelled out!

The "dead letter" die provides a letter players must not use each round, and "priority mail" provides a letter that must be used.

First-Class Letters can be played competitively, cooperatively, or solo.

—description from the publisher

name: Foolish Fool
description:
Foolish Fool is a goofy party game for folks who want to have silly fun together. Each turn you read the rule on a new card. From then on, you must follow that rule, which gets harder and harder since you get a new rule each turn! Some rules apply only to you, while others apply to the whole group. Get caught breaking the rules, and you lose a token; lose all three of your tokens, and you lose the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Parlay: The Betting Game
description:
In this unique, family-friendly game, players wager on how many tricks they'll win each round. Every correct bet advances your pawn along the track, bringing you closer to victory. But place your bets carefully, one wrong move, and your competition might leave you in the dust!

First player to reach the finish line wins. Ideal for 2 to 8 players, Parlay embraces the thrill of competitive race and ensures every game is unpredictable and exciting.

—description from the designer

name: Pass the Word
description:
Pass the Word is a cooperative party game. Everyone plays together to get the best score!

Each player takes a card from the deck of the chosen category and a card from the numbers deck. Your number card indicates which of the secret mystery words on your category card another player must guess. Players check their cards and then place them face down beside them.

Each player writes their name at the bottom of their clue sheet. Then, simultaneously each player writes on the top line of their clue sheet a word that gives a clue to their mystery word. Then they pass their clue sheet to the player to their left.
Read the word on your new clue sheet, then turn the page to cover the word. Directly below the covered word, write a new word that is a clue to the covered word and belongs to the chosen category. Then pass your clue sheet back to the player on your left.

Repeat this phase three times until each clue sheet contains three words, two of which are covered.
In the next phase, each player takes the category card from the player whose name is on the clue sheet they were just dealt. Using the last revealed word on their current clue sheet, the player attempts to guess the mystery word on the drawn category card.

Players work together to guess as many mystery words as possible!

name: Passage
description:
The gameboard has recesses into which you initially fill the small red and black disks. Over the course of the game, you move all your big playing pieces to the other side of the board as quickly as possible.

You only move diagonally over disks and playing pieces of your own color, but you may change directions anytime.

Your turn always ends on a disk of your opponent's color. With this, you cover the space with a piece of your color, build a bridge and thus enhance your moving options.

If you are the first player to reach the target spaces on the opposite side with all 4 of your playing pieces, you win.

—description from the publisher

name: Patchistory: The Fabric of Ages
description:
Civilizations are built upon the technological innovations of past eras, the ambitions and ideas of people who left their mark on the course of time, and the social advancements demanded by each moment in history. Some of these events, structures, and ideas remain to this day, while others form part of the sediment that shapes our slice of History.

In Patchistory: The Fabric of Ages, you will develop civilizations through an auction system where you acquire a series of tiles that will overlap and interweave, evoking the art of patchwork. Over the course of three eras, you will grow your population, produce, and manage the resources generated by your territory.  
You will explore beyond your borders, facing or allying with neighboring civilizations. Leaders will rise and fall, swept away by the tides of time. You will construct monuments that reflect the glory of your people—perhaps fleetingly.

At the end of three eras, the player with the most Culture points wins the game, ensuring their civilization will never be erased from History.

Patchistory: The Fabric of Ages reimplements the cult-classic Patchistory adding new variants to offer a quicker game without losing the deepness and fun of the original. Some minor adjustments are made to make a smoother experience and added a solitaire mode to this original approach to civilization games.

name: Pathfinder Dice Conquest
description:
Face a gauntlet of iconic Pathfinder monsters, solo or with up to 3 friends, using a set of 7 polyhedral dice as your weapons! Use the included set or any of your favorite standard sets! It’s perfect for travel, as all you need is dice and the deck of cards!

Each round, you’ll roll the dice and take turns placing them on monsters, doing damage equal to the die’s value. Defeat them by doing damage equal to or greater than their health, using your character’s abilities and items to increase the damage!

Many monsters will have special requirements, like the Jinkin, who must be defeated with seven damage EXACTLY! Or the Hydra, who must be defeated before it re-grows its head! Defeat one of three randomly-determined bosses at the bottom of the deck for your heroes to stand triumphant and win the game!

Pick from 6 unique characters to play, and, to make things more challenging, add in advanced spell cards!

Contents:
7 Polyhedral Dice
23 Creature cards
3 Boss cards
6 Hero cards
8 Spell cards
4 Health Tracker cards
4 Player Aid cards
5 Tokens
1 Rulebook

-description from publisher

name: No Loose Ends
description:
Crime pays if you’re careful. Still, a bank heist is no easy job. The precious loot is heavily guarded, and each thing you steal leaves a trail of evidence behind. Risk leads to reward if you can cover up the evidence and leave no loose end untied.

No Loose Ends is a trick-taking game in which players use cards from their hand to bid, carefully planning their heist. Winning tricks with the right suit or number will cover up the evidence in your bid and earn you points. Uncovered evidence and extra tricks not according to plan will lose you points for leaving loose ends from the robbery.

Will you pull off the perfect crime or snitch on your fellow thieves?

—description from the publisher

name: Paw by Paw
description:
Your dog is scratching at the front door because it is time for your daily walk in the park. Try to make it as fun as possible, but also avoid the temptations your dog might encounter. Paw by Paw is a competitive roll and write, print and play game for 1 to 99 players ages 10+.

In Paw by Paw, players walk their dog around the park over sixteen rounds, finding bushes to pee in, other animals or people to interact with, or even some unique spots in each park that present a different challenge each time. Players choose a dog with a unique talent and each round they roll three dice and perform three actions in this specific order: Move, Sniff and Play. Their goal is to keep their dog as happy as possible to earn points at the end of the game. The player with the most points is the winner and their dog wins the Golden Dog Ribbon!

Grab some pencils and dice and take your dog for a Paw by Paw walk in the park.

—description from the publisher

name: Trinket Trove
description:
Beneath the floor boards and between the walls, a secret world thrives. By moonlight, the collectors scurry into quiet corners in search of tiny treasures: mirrored lockets, shiny buttons, gleaming gems, and more. When dawn breaks, the animals retreat to their snug little burrows to share stories and trade the night’s trinkets.

OVERVIEW
In a game of Trinket Trove, you are a collector – a cute little critter living in the margins of the human world. You trade and collect sets of trinkets to decorate your burrow. You begin with a hand of 4 trinket cards, and each round new trinket cards will be drawn face up into the center of the table. You and the other players will take turns bidding for draft order, by offering up trinket cards from your hand. Then players will take turns claiming the trinkets on the table, including the bids offered up by other players, and placing them in their hands. At the end of 5 or 6 rounds you score your hand of trinkets and the player with the most points wins!

—description from the publisher

name: PAWSUM Pets Collectible Card Game
description:
Match cats, dogs, and Best Friends while using sneaky moves to outsmart your opponents. The first player to collect 2 matching rows of CATS or DOGS, or 1 row of BEST FRIENDS, wins!

How to Play:

     Each player has a board with 6 spaces.
     On your turn: Draw a card, then play a card to your board.
     Play special cards to steal pets or lock spaces and block others.
     Race to complete your winning rows before anyone else!


—description from the designer

name: Pax Feudalis
description:
Pax Feudalis places players in the role of rising Marquises in 13th-century Italy, a land fractured by rival factions, political turmoil, and constant power struggles. Each player builds a personal tableau of characters, constructions, and influences, all represented by cards. The game’s tension comes from balancing your resources, expanding your engine, and reacting to historical pressures such as Wars, Shortages, and shifting faction power. The market steadily advances the timeline, revealing events and investiture cards that mark key moments in the struggle for dominance.

On their turn, players rotate cooldowns, resolve income, and then take two actions. Actions include buying cards from the Market Town, playing cards to their tableau by paying resources, bribing cards to gain additional resources, selling cards for money, or activating all actions of a chosen color in their tableau. Resources themselves are tracked through rotating cards that rise and fall throughout play, encouraging timely spending. Cards may produce resources, grant abilities, build structures, or add faction symbols — all of which shape your strategy. Every decision matters because the timing of each action influences not only your own engine but also the opportunities available to opponents.

The goal of the game is to earn two of the three Investitures: Papal, Imperial, and Communal Autonomy. Whenever a Signoria Check card appears or is discarded, players compare the relevant faction symbols in their tableaus. The player with the highest influence in that faction gains the corresponding Investiture card. The moment a player earns their second Investiture, they win immediately. If no one wins by the third check, the game moves to tiebreakers based on symbols, cards, and total wealth. Victory comes from clever timing, engine mastery, and outmaneuvering your rivals in a land where power is never secure.

—description from the designer

name: Friendly Fishing
description:
A reel and a rod, some friends, and a boat - is there anything more relaxing? Let's spend the day together, fishing this pond. And hey, I'll give you a hand and help you catch that big fish you've been after.

Friendly Fishing is a semi-cooperative set collection game in which players share a fishing boat. On your turn you simply move the boat and claim a fish token. You'll want to set the next player up for a good move, because there's a twist.  At the end of the game, everyone scores the tokens in front of them, but each player's final score is their own fish score, plus their left neighbor's fish score! Most points wins.

Friendly Fishing offers a casual day on the pond with a unique style of player iteration.

-description from publisher

name: Payback
description:
This is a modded version of Palace, also known as Shithead or Karma.

We made it more intuitive so kids can pick it up easily. We also made it more vengeful by introducing mechanics to get back at the person on your right (the one who's usually bullying you).

Here are some of the changes:

Redesigned and simplified the card hierarchy: 1 to 10. No suits, no color, no faces, no aces.

Special cards now have unique designs instead of numbers (BURN, RESET, GHOST).

New special cards were added to get back at the person on your right: SKIP, MIRROR. This increases the deck size from 52 to 58 cards.

Rules were modified to speed up gameplay. If you lose with a face-up card, you take it with the pile.

If the 1st place player is out of the game, they can decide that 3 cards make a BURN, instead of 4.

Expansion includes spell cards. These cards can reveal game information or cast spells on other players. For example, if they don’t address you with a silly name, they have to pick up the pile.

Card sizes are increased to 7 cm by 10 cm.

Game modes have been added to introduce gambling and drinking mechanics.

Roulette mode: All the cards are placed face-down in a giant circle.

The art was drawn in MS Paint and features bold, flashy graphics, with big influences from Keith Haring and Justice, the band.

—description from the designer

name: PAYBACK
publisher: シュピールディスオーダー (Spieldisorder)
description:
In Payback, cunning is your currency and survival is your only strategy. Each player builds their own stage of play, using card combinations not only to rid their hand but to strike at opponents to the left and right. As players rush to go out first or outlast the chaos, every move could provoke retaliation, or open the door to fortune.

Payback is a climbing and shedding game where each player plays combinations to their own personal board instead of a shared central pile. There are only two types of valid combinations, simplifying choices while sharpening strategic tension. Every play can affect adjacent opponents via "paybacks," which force them into tough decisions or directly attack their hand. The game rewards those who either go out first or survive longest without being eliminated, striking a balance between aggression and endurance.

name: Peaks
description:
In Peaks, you are aspiring mountaineers, beginning the game hiking up iconic hills from around the world as you build your stamina and experience. You will gather equipment and meet companions to assist you in climbing the world's tallest mountains!

On your turn, choose one of three actions: rest to regain your stamina; prepare to gain mountain passes and equipment; or climb to climb a mountain and reap its rewards. A "tag along" mechanism keeps players engaged even when it's not their turn, adding a collaborative element. Mechanical player mats with moving tiles and dials, a custom die, and flag minis make for a new, tactile experience.

At game's end, the player with the most flags on the board — plus any extras from bonus cards — wins.

Simple set-up, quick turns, and fun interactions along with a ruleset that organically develops throughout the game all bring about a satisfying adventure.

-description from developer

name: Peanuts Talent Show!
description:
In Peanuts Talent Show, 2–4 players compete in a fast and lively card game that combines trick-taking with light deck-building. Each round, you’ll lead your cast of performers like Snoopy, Charlie Brown, Woodstock, and more, into the spotlight. Win tricks to earn Coins, then use them to recruit new acts and expand your deck with bigger talents.

Peanuts Talent Show! plays in about 30 minutes, is easy to learn, and offers the perfect mix of familiar characters, light strategy, and playful competition.

—description from the publisher

name: Trick to the Future
description:
They thought we were crazy, but they’re the fools, I tell you. With the temporal transistors finally operational, we have the power to travel time - to past, present, future, and beyond. Oh, but the fuel must be managed carefully! One too many time jumps and we’ll be unable to make that fateful, final leap home. Who will master the timeline, and who may be lost in time forever?

Trick to the Future is a trick-taking game in which you use cards from your hand to time travel. You begin each round with a number of fuel rods on your player board, which may be used to change the values of your cards! Each trick you win represents a successful time jump and earns you points. In addition, you receive points for the spent fuel rods you collect during the round. However, at the end of a round, if you have more tricks won than unspent fuel rods, you score no points. After 3 rounds, the time traveler with the most points wins!

Cards use 7-segment digital numbers (like you would see on a digital clock). The "fuel rods" are additional segments that players can place on a card to change the number. For example, a 1 could become a 7 by adding a segment at the top.  Or a 7 could become a 0, using 3 fuel rods.

—description from the publisher

name: Pencil Book Quest
description:
Pencil Book Quest is a solo, pencil-and-paper adventure designed to be played anywhere. Fight monsters, collect loot, and complete quests in this compact book that easily slips into a pocket or bag.

Instead of dice, the game uses a pencil-based mechanic where randomness comes from your own aim and coordination. It’s a simple system that adds a layer of tactile challenge while keeping the game fast and portable.

With its compact components, no setup, and the ability to pause and resume anytime, Pencil Book Quest is perfect for commutes, waiting rooms, standing in line, or any moment when your brain needs a short side quest.

—description from the designer

name: Pencil Express: Yugoslavia
description:
Pencil Express is a route-building and drawing game set in 1960s Yugoslavia, during a time of ambitious railway modernization and expansion. Taking up the roles of engineers, the Players compete to design the most efficient and well-connected railway network across the country.

Each turn, players choose whether to play route cards to pursue long-distance connections, or to place track cards that shape the central rail layout and determine which rail patterns must be drawn. As the network grows, players draw rail shapes on their personal maps, striving to connect towns, cities, capitals, and border crossings. Strategic planning, spatial optimization, and careful use of limited bonus actions are key to building the most successful network.

name: Wild Magic
description:
The Wild Magic lives beyond our walls, untamed and ever-flowing.  There, it gathers into sacred elemental pools protected by the Guardians. Channel this magic as it ebbs and flows from the elemental pools, through you, and into our world. Command the power of the elements and you alone will join the Guardians to protect the Wild Magic forever.

Wild Magic is a set-collection game in which you aim to collect cards of the same element to play as “melds” in front of you. These melds score you points based on their strength. However, at the end of the game, if you have the weakest meld of an element, you must discard it and score nothing for that element. In addition, the player with the strongest meld of each element gains a power token worth bonus points.

On your turn you may draw 2 cards, but will likely discard a card to its pool in the center of the table. In this way, cards tend to pool up in growing piles until someone spends their turn taking all of the cards in one pool, in which case they must meld cards in front of them.

—description from the publisher

name: Marble Football
description:
Marble Football is a fast-paced tabletop sports game where players take turns moving their team of marbles around a football pitch, outmaneuvering opponents, and setting up strategic shots to score goals. Every move matters; positioning, timing, and reading your opponent creates a game of tactics, tension, and dramatic moments.

The game blends dexterity and decision-making. Players alternate activating marbles, executing passes, long balls, defensive plays, and attacks on goal. The simple core rules make it accessible for families, while experienced players discover surprising depth as they develop team strategies and effective formations.

Matches are quick, competitive, and full of highlight-reel plays. Whether playing casual kickabouts or full tournaments with multiple teams, Marble Football delivers a fun, energetic sports experience on the tabletop.

name: Penguin Kaboom
description:
Penguin Kaboom is a fast-paced cooperative game where players become an elite (and slightly clumsy) squad of penguins tasked with defusing bombs across the icy city of Penguinvania.

Each mission presents a unique scenario, as players race against the clock to stop the villainous Orca Bomber—a dramatic mastermind determined to turn Penguinvania into frozen rubble.

Choose one of the 15 replayable missions, each with its own difficulty and setup.

On your turn, take all available dice along with any previously assigned ones you choose to re-roll. Each hammer result becomes locked in the recharge zone. The remaining dice can be placed to defuse bombs by matching their icons with those shown on the bombs and alerts. Think fast, every time you assign at least one die, you may roll the remaining available ones again.

Work together to defuse all bombs before time runs out or too many alerts trigger.

With 3 difficulty levels, quick turns, and an escalating sense of urgency, Penguin Kaboomb delivers teamwork, tension, and a lot of frozen feathers.

The clock is ticking. Can your team keep cool under pressure?

—description from the publisher

name: Penguins Can't Fly
description:
So, you and your overconfident penguin friends have decided to prove the world wrong and take flight off an icy cliff. Unsurprisingly, it's not going well. Your only goal? Stay in the air longer than the others because the first penguin to hit the water -well, there are three hungry orcas waiting below.

In Penguins Can't Fly, each player selects a penguin character and begins at the top of the laid-out track cards. Players then take turns drawing cards from the deck. Most cards will send you closer to the water, bad news. But action cards let you mess with your opponents, switch places, look ahead, or force someone else to drop faster. Track cards can cause mid-air chaos or slow some penguins down, while others are unaffected.

One by one, penguins plummet until only one remains, the last true believer in penguin aviation. That player wins. Play cards, avoid falling, sabotage your friends, and most importantly, don’t become orca lunch.

—description from the publisher

name: Pengy Pals: Antarctica's Greatest Heroes
description:
Welcome to Pengy Island where you and your friends take on the role of Antarctica's greatest heroes - yes, we're talking about superhero penguins. Pengy and his Pals need your help to fight off the Walrus Gang, the Albatross Alliance, and more. The easy to learn mechanics help you get new players to enjoy the cooperative combat genre, while experienced gamers will find the strategic depth rewarding.

Pengy Pals is a cooperative, dice rolling, combat game. Each Pal comes with two unique dice that are added to a community dice pool. The unique symbols and dice create challenging and fun decision-making for you and your pals. But be careful! The Enemies will use the dice you choose to instantly react.

Take on the role of four unique penguin superheroes. Each penguin comes with unique action cards, dice, and abilities. Choose your favorite playstyle, and discover the hidden ways that every Pal can kick some Albartross butt. Let's just say, even the healer can pack some serious punch once you learn how.

Characters must also balance the amount of Fish they have in their community Fish Storage. Players work together to build up the supply and will need to cooperate on the best ways to use the Fish available. Not only will you eat Fish to perform abilities, you will need to make sure you have enough Fish to keep your Pals well fed.

The three unique Enemies create new challenges and new ways to play the game. This game isn't just about combat. Unique win conditions, like securing resources or surviving a killer whale attack, keep players on their toes. Challenging variants also keep the game fresh and rewarding for more experienced gamers!

—description from the publisher

name: Peninsula
description:
Peninsula is a challenging and very strategic flip & write in which you are drawing the map of a fictional island. 
You draft symbols and draw them on adjacent hexes of your architect token, while offering symbols to your competitors to draw. 
Try to build an infrastructure, so your architect can move more efficiently over your map and stay flexible. Draw symbols, which increase your victory points and fulfill contracts along the way with your drawn patterns to please the monarch of your Peninsula.
The winner is determined, by points for the most efficient peninsula after the last symbol card is drafted.

The novel mechanism is that you cannot draw anywhere but only on adjacent hexes to your architect token. This forces players to move at the right time to the right place, otherwise players run out of hexes where they can draw new symbols.

name: DragonIsles
description:
Journey to a mystical fantasy world in the Far East, drawing on inspiration from Japanese culture and folklore. Players take on the role of daring adventurers, exploring the isles, collecting treasures, and overcoming thrilling challenges. With exciting new mechanics—like individual character boards, collectible trophies, and powerful potion tokens—DragonIsles brings fresh strategy and depth to the beloved series. Will you rise as the ultimate adventurer in DragonIsles?

●    A NEW IMMERSIVE FANTASY ADVENTURE IN THE DRAGON SERIES: DragonIsles builds upon the themes of Dragonwood and Dragon Realm while introducing a vibrant new world inspired by Japanese mythology, landscapes, and traditions. This fusion of Eastern themes with classic fantasy elements creates a new and thrilling adventure for you to discover!

●    DEVELOP YOUR CHARACTER AND UNLOCK NEW ABILITIES: Each player selects a character with unique strengths, who will grow over the course of the game.
