When she married Songtsen Gampo, she brought with her as part of her dowry a precious statue of the Buddha that awaken a demon living in the Red Mountain during the construction of the Potala Palace, he tried to disrupt the work every night by destroying what had been built during the day. To prevent this, King Songtsen Gampo consulted an oracle, which advised that the demon be appeased with the offering of the body of a man or woman. Princess Wencheng, with great courage, volunteered to be sacrificed.

After two hundred years, with the perdition of Tubo Dynasty, the Potala Palace were damaged during wars in 9th century, there were only ruins left, making the demon awaken again. 
Until in 17th century when the 5th Dalai Lama came to power, he commanded his Rinpoches (the players) with they monk-workers, to rebuilding the palace immediately and vanish the demon once for all, making the Potala Palace a new home and a spiritual tower for the next generations of the Dalai Lamas.

Potala Palace is a euro-game with deck building and worker/dice placement mechanics, where players take on the roles of Rinpoches who must assist in the reconstruction of the palace using their dice (workers) to acquire new resources and cards to improve their decks, allowing them to build new facilities such as halls, statues, reliquaries, thangkas (a type of Tibetan tapestry), thus accumulating "merit points" (victory points) and achieving enlightenment by completing the "Great Mandala" at the end of the game. The game features a day and night mechanics where players' deck cards can be flipped upside down, completely changing their effects, further expanding the strategic possibilities of the game, but beware of the demon's jealousy, as he may come during the nighttime to destroy something the players have built.

—description from the designer

name: Potato Party: Mashterworks
description:
Auction nights are a tradition among you and your friends, but tonight’s art pieces are exquisite. You grab your trust fund debit card and take a seat, eager to walk home with a Mashterwork. Or several. Point being, you really want to be able to show off your collection of art to your friends to kindly remind them of what they didn’t win.

Potato Party: Mashterworks is a lightweight auctioneering party game for 3-8 players. Players begin the game with a single Painting, assigned a random value from the Value Points (VP) deck. During the game, paintings will be auctioned off, change value, and traded (stolen..) around the table. When all available Paintings have been auctioned off, all players total up their VP. The player with the highest VP wins and thus may gloat about their superior taste in the fine arts.

—description from the publisher

name: Potemkin Villages
description:
Potemkin Villages is a fully cooperative trick-taking game set during Catherine the Great’s journey to Crimea. Each player takes on a different character, winning tricks to unleash unique abilities. Together, you’ll dismantle, move, and rebuild villages along the Dnepr River, creating an illusion of prosperity. Cooperation is key: the Governor can amplify the Builder’s strength, while the Painter shifts trumps to aid allies. If Catherine still beholds beauty, after there are no more cards in play, you succeed; if she sees through the ruse, you all lose.

—description from the designer

name: Holiday Hijinks #11: The New Year Nightmare
description:
It's the cusp of a new year and you find yourself in Prof Timely‘s manor. You never thought you'd return after your February adventure, but it’s funny how time has a way of repeating itself. With the clock ticking down to midnight and the professor's experiments going haywire, you prepare yourself for the calamity to come. Only your New Year resolve will ensure a bright future, instead of dwelling in the past…

The New Year Nightmare, title #11 in the Holiday Hijinks line, is an escape room style game in just 18 cards! As a group, you will solve a series of puzzles to unravel a mystery. Puzzles may test your perception, wordplay, and lateral thinking. English language fluency is required.

When you have solved a puzzle on the cards, you will enter the answer into the companion website (compatible with all smart phones and computers) and it will check whether you are correct. If you are, the website will tell you which card or cards to take next. The website also contains a graduated hint system, so if you get stuck you can get just a small hint about the current puzzle to get moving again without giving too much away.

This system is non-destructible: some groups may choose to write on cards, but this is not required. A group cannot re-play the game, but can pass it on to another group for their use. This entry in the series takes about an hour to solve, and is rated 3 out of 3 in difficulty.

name: Potion Express
description:
Hurry, hurry, there's not a second to lose! The moon is barely shining, and already the Potion Express pilots are taking to the skies to meet the orders of the village witches.

Pumpkins, mushrooms and earthworms - it's going to be a rough night!

Be the first to deliver 3 Potions to win the game. (4 Potions in a 2-player game)

Ingredient cards are shuffled, half face down, half face up, and 9 are placed on the table in a square grid. On your turn, select a row or column, flip all cards in that row or column, and take all face up ingredients. At the end of your turn, use the gathered ingredients to brew as many potions as you can, keeping any remaining ingredients until next turn.

name: Holiday Hijinks #12: The Krampus Caper
description:
One thing we can always rely on is Santa Claus making the rounds at Christmas. But when he decides to take the year off, it's up to some unlikely assistance to get the job done. Join forces with the Krampus as he steps up to the plate and keeps the North Pole operation running. If all goes well, nobody will be the wiser!

The Krampus Caper, title #12 in the Holiday Hijinks line, is an escape room-style game in just 18 cards! As a group, you will solve a series of puzzles to unravel a mystery. Puzzles may test your perception, wordplay, and lateral thinking. English language fluency is required.

When you have solved a puzzle on the cards, you will enter the answer into the companion website (compatible with all smart phones and computers) and it will check whether you are correct. If you are, the website will tell you which card or cards to take next. The website also contains a graduated hint system, so if you get stuck you can get just a small hint about the current puzzle to get moving again without giving too much away.

This system is non-destructible: some groups may choose to write on cards, but this is not required. A group cannot re-play the game, but can pass it on to another group for their use. This entry in the series takes about an hour to solve and is rated 2 out of 3 in difficulty.

name: Power City Arena
description:
In Power City Arena you control a team of unique super heroes that fight for the control of Power City. All character have a unique ability that is always active and 2 super power that need energy to be used. Your goal will be to defeat other players' teams and be the last one standing on the board.

You start the game with a 15 actions cards deck that allow you to boost your characters, mainly charge their energy for their powers, you can also attack your ennemies or protect yourself. During the game you will be able to move around the board to seek for bonus that let you draw extra action cards, more powerful, or draw equipments that would increase your range, add extra damage to your attacks or give you extra health. If you seek for bonuses, you will make your deck stronger, give you advantage to your oponents by enlarge the possibility of actions.

Bonuses and turn order are set randomly at the begining of the game, each turn is by character order and not by players. The active character make all the action for himself but share the cards in hand with all the team the player control, so choose wisely wich character will use wich cards.

You start the game with a hand of 5 cards, each character's turn, you start by drawing 2 cards from your deck (if you start your turn on a bonus, you may draw card from the designated deck), you have 1 free movement to do whenever you want in your turn, you may use any number of cards from your hand, the only limit is for the attacks that are limited by 1 per turn (some bonuses can break this limit), then when you end your turn, you can't have more than 7 cards in your hand so discard the surplus.

When a character's health reach 0 he is eliminated and there is no way for him to come back, when all the characters from a team are eliminated, the team is eliminated and lose. When all other team are eliminated, you win the game.

-description from designer

name: Power Creep: Core Set
description:
When the lights went out it didn’t take long for civilization to start crumbling. After years of scavenging your fledgling society has found a way to restore power to the settlement. But the evil forces thrive in the darkness and they desire to keep it that way. You’ll need to outrun the Creep before it overtakes your settlement, dooming you and your fellow survivors and maybe all of humanity!

Hook and updates to the system: The third game in the system takes players into a post-apocalyptic future filled with dangerous wastelanders and an ominous dark threat, and most importantly a lack of stable power. Players will craft items, and attempt to power buildings, giving them long term special abilities that can assist throughout the entire game.

Power Creep offers a new spin on the single-page, six-dice game thrusting you into the role of a survivor who must restore the settlement before an evil force overtakes humanity.

Power Creep features:

     All new structure blueprint and crafting mechanics.
     Streamlined gameplay pulls the best puzzle-like play from Dungeon Pages, combined with the tactical choices of Dangerous Space.

name: Power Tricks
description:
The barbarians of Castle Power Skull are battling in an epic confrontation full of magic and muscles to determine who will truly have the ultimate power. Power Tricks is a trick taking game for 3-5 players that pushes tricks to their maximum power level.

Players can grab the magical power to enhance the cards they play to tricks, but the more power they grab, the less points they may be able to earn.

—description from the publisher

name: Prado
description:
Prado is a family board game for 1 to 4 players. You become a photographer tasked with creating a photo report at the Prado Museum. The rooms are full of people getting between your camera and the artworks.

Step into the role of a photographer trying to capture the most representative works of the museum. Even though it sounds simple, the challenge is tricky: you must take photos quickly while avoiding the heads and bodies blocking your view. And you only have one day to succeed! Each turn, you’ll need to optimize your moves through the museum, overcome the chaos, and make sure no one steals the photos you need to complete your mission.

The game includes 35 different cards featuring the Prado’s most iconic paintings, along with detailed descriptions. This adds an authentic touch and gives players the chance to learn more about art and culture while enjoying the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Prelude to Leipzig: Napoleon's Spring 1813 Campaign
description:
Prelude to Leipzig: Napoleon's Spring 1813 Campaign is an Operational level board-wargame.

This is a prequel to John Theissen's Campaign of Nations. That game tackled the autumn 1813 campaign that culminated in the climactic Battle of Nations, covering those events with his clean, streamlined approach to operational hex-and-counter gaming. In this game, he turns his attention to the spring campaign. Historically, Napoleon failed to achieve the decisive victory he was looking for, resulting in a summer truce - giving his enemies precious time to plan and prepare for the battle that would signal the end of his rule. But perhaps your French Coalition can realize his ambitions? Or maybe your Prussian and Russian forces will stop him in the spring?

Like Mr. Theissen's other titles, what happens is up to the players. Pursue your objectives aggressively for an exciting clash. Dilly-dally for an indecisive campaign. This approach, which trusts players to use the tools they've been given, has won these designs their ardent fans. In an attempt to bring these joys to a wider audience, the mapsheet - our largest-ever, measuring 32" x 32" - uses roomy extra-large hexes, with terrain effects printed directly on the map.

—description from the publisher

name: Pride of Ninja
description:
In Pride of Ninja, you draft 7 cards, 4 in the front row face up and 3 in the back row face down. Some cards have different ability depending on the row it is played. 
The goal is to win Temporary Points (TP) by playing these cards in the best spot. You may get slain during the round which means you will lose all the TP you've won so far. 
After resolving all cards, you convert all your TPs into Victory Points (VP). Play multiple rounds until one player has scored 20 or more VPs.

—description from the publisher

name: Primacy: A Coyote & Crow Card Game
description:
In Primacy: A Coyote & Crow Card Game, two players take on the role of one of the five factions of Makasing, the nations first laid out in the award-winning roleplaying game, Coyote & Crow. Players will construct a deck of 50 cards from a pool of 250 that allow them to gain status and prestige against their opponents by completing daunting mutual challenges.

The world of Coyote & Crow is an alternate future where the Americas were never colonized. Instead, powerful Native nations rose in their stead. The world is a mix of science and fantasy. Players will have advanced technology, powerful ceremonies, and epic heroes at their disposal. Each of the five nations available to play have unique asymmetric advantages and disadvantages to create distinct play styles for every kind of gamer.

—description from the publisher

name: Primates
description:
Primates is an evolutionary board game where you can explore the evolution of more than 100 different primate species.

Evolve and try to outmaneuver your opponents as you forage for food and build social bonds.

As your primates evolve, they gain special abilities.

Whether you prefer the agility of gibbons or the remarkable memory of chimpanzees, the choice is yours. You determine which evolutionary path to take.

—description from the designer

name: Primordial: Creatures of Pandemonium
description:
Mages, the land of Cathaira needs your help!

The last Celestial War with the Titans of Yarre` has left the landscape changed. Entropic Energy spreads at an unprecedented rate and the Creatures are becoming volatile and unpredictable as their environment shifts. They are vital to the health of the continent and must be preserved!

Each of you are masters of a Sanctuary, which Entropic Energy cannot easily penetrate. Your distinct prowess and your historical harmony with the land of Cathaira means that only you can Tame these Creatures! Can you manage to offer them protection, and return the presence of Entropic Energy to normal levels?

Honor is to be had, and each of you has the opportunity to be held in the highest regard by mastering the use of Energy, advancing in knowledge, and Taming these Creatures who need your help!

Primordial: Creatures of Pandemonium is a mid-weight, euro resource management game that is played over rounds. During the game, Mages will traverse the landscape, tame mythical creatures, learn skills, become more proficient in Energy use, and manage a Sanctuary to earn more honor than other Mages.

Primary mechanisms of the game include resource management, tableau building, skill-tree progression, and area movement. Additionally, the game features a unique communal bag building element!

-description from designer

name: Priorities: Fourth Wing
description:
Welcome to Basgiath, cadet! See how well you know your squadmates in this Priorities Fourth Wing Edition game, inspired by the bestselling Empyrean series by Rebecca Yarros! In this game of epic choices, one player – the Wingleader – draws 5 cards featuring favorites from the first 3 Empyrean books: Fourth Wing, Iron Flame, and Onyx Storm. They secretly rank the cards from love to loathe. Everyone else – the Iron Squad – works together to guess the Wingleader’s order. It’s everyone versus the game! Earn a card for every correctly guessed rank, and the game earns the rest. To win, spell PRIORITIES using the letters on the backs of your earned cards before the game does.

INSPIRED BY EMPYREAN SERIES: Find out how well you know your Iron Squad in the officially licensed Priorities Fourth Wing Edition! A party game of epic choices that will have you questioning their priorities – and your own.
BREAKING AN ARMOIRE OR BECOMING THE IRON SQUAD?: One player, the Wingleader, secretly ranks 5 cards featuring faves from the Fourth Wing world from love to loathe. Includes top-tier book boyfriends, villains you love to hate, and nods to spicy scenes.
WINGLEADER & SQUAD VS. THE GAME: Everyone else, the Iron Squad, works together to guess the Wingleader’s choices. Win a card for every rank correctly guessed – or the game wins it! Get ready for lively debates and laughs.

—description from the publisher

name: Prop Hunt the Board Game
description:
As a Prop, you must become one with your surroundings - disguising yourself as a humble pair of shoes, a guitar, maybe even.. a rubber duckie? But beware — the Hunters are closing in, ready to smash, bash and reduce everything to rubble. Will you vanish in the clutter or will you crush the hidden deceivers?

Inspired by the hit video game mode played by over 70 Million Gamers!

A game of deception and ridiculous disguises! Whether you are outsmarting your friends or frantically searching for the sneaky apple that was just on the table, laughter is guaranteed!

Each game has between 25 and 40 fake Props on the board, 25+ hiding spaces and no limit to the deception the other team is willing to use!

Utilize distinct movement and action abilities with Action Cards that force both Props and Hunters to adapt. Even the most keen eyed Hunter might lose sight of a Prop that changes into another and sprints away to safety!

You can Hide in one of the 25+ spots around the map OR you can make a play for the Action Keys and Escape! Just remember You only have 5 turns you can Hide and those Hunters are searching high and low!

—description from the publisher

name: Propeller Islands
description:
Imagine a realm where adorable and clever animals live in harmony, crafting mechanical islands with an array of whirring gears, spinning propellers, and gleaming steel. This is the world of Propeller Islands, a board game where players become island architects, harnessing the power of energy crystals to build marvels of wonder and ingenuity.

Each turn, you take dice from a shrinking pool and use them to gain new structures, produce resources, or populate your buildings. The game features a wide variety of buildings, many of which can be upgraded, allowing for countless combinations of island layouts and strategic possibilities. As you build your islands, they can unlock unique and powerful new abilities. You must carefully manage their resources, balance risk and reward, and outwit your opponents to emerge victorious.

The game will end after a round when one of the following conditions occurs:
- the supply of building tiles is exhausted
- one player completed their seventh blueprint 
- one player transferred all their workers onto their island.

At this point you flip over the Forge to reveal the victory point track. Players receive points for their fame, leftover resources, island tiles and completed blue prints. The player with the most points wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Journey to Tír na nÓg
description:
Your backpacking trip through the lush greenery of the Irish countryside is interrupted by a strange visitor. This giant man, calling himself The Dagda, presents you with a series of challenges to overcome. Only the clever and pure of heart will solve them all and gain entry to Tír na nÓg!

Journey to Tír na nÓg is a game in the 18Escape series of cooperative puzzle games from Grand Gamers Guild. In each game, you solve a full-length, escape-room-style mystery using just 18 playing cards! Puzzles may test your perception, wordplay, and lateral thinking. English language fluency is required.

This game uses a website to check your answers and provide hints and information. When you have solved a puzzle on the cards, you will enter the answer into the website (compatible with all smart phones and computers) and you will be instructed on what to do next. The website also contains a graduated hint system, so if you get stuck you can get just a small hint about the current puzzle to get moving again without giving too much away.

This system is non-destructible: some groups may choose to write on cards, but this is not required. A group cannot re-play the game, but can pass it on to another group for their use.

—description from the publisher

name: Prosper with Dragons
description:
Prosper with Dragons is a cooperative card game with Afrofuturistic art set in a post-apocalyptic world.

In a post-apocalyptic world, disasters lurk around every corner and only a combination of human ingenuity and dragon might can fend them off. Players must work together to strategize on how to use their limited resources to befriend dragons while also preparing for inevitable floods, locust swarms, tornados, and more. Dragons can aid in dealing with the destruction, but careful, that help might come with a steep price.

For players to win, they must collectively befriend all twelve dragons and survive increasingly destructive disasters before their resources run out. Games of Prosper with Dragons are exciting and nerve-bending and have a game length of about 30 minutes.

—description from the designer

name: Proving Ground
description:
A trick-taking skirmish game set in the fantasy world of Zanziar. You’re an orc chieftain winning competitions where each point scored allows you to choose the best spot for placing the sacred totems. Proving grounds reside between villages and are jointly populated and scored. In the end, only one village will honor the ancestral spirits the best!

In The Proving Ground deck you'll find six suits, all the suits are used regardless of player count. Each card has two values (shown on both ends of the card), representing different suits and ranks. Each suit and rank is thus represented twice in the deck. Players can use either value at any time. Ranks form a hexagon, where each rank has adjacent and opposite ranks. Playmat hexagons have two sides, one for 3 player, one for 4-5 players. All playmats have to use the same side in the game.

The lead player plays a single card at a time. In clockwise order, other players need to play a single card, doing one of the following:
a) Play a card of the led suit of any value.
b) Play a card of one of the two adjacent suits with a value greater than any previously played card. 
c) Pass. You can only pass if you have played something to this trick previously.

So, each time a suit is led, there are three legal suits to play. If a player cannot play any of the three legal suits even once, they must discard a card of their choice and take a Penalty. A game lasts 3 rounds. The closer the end of the game reaches, the more restricting the board states are for the players - forcing them to think which suit of tricks you can try to win and which suits you just would need to give a pass.

name: MegaMart Mogul
description:
Having mastered the local supermarket economy with your friends, it's time to take the next steps in your retail management careers. Now you're vying to become the MegaMart Mogul! Competition is fierce, and only one of you gets the job. And with growth comes growing pains. More employees, more threats, and more bureaucracy will all need to be handled as you work to lead your team.

You'll begin with a small stash of cash, a core group of loyal and enthusiastic employees, and some product. After that it's up to you to manage those assets as you build your retail empire.

MegaMart Mogul twists the deck building mechanic, giving you control over the flow of cards from bank to deck to market to shared supply. Money flows out of your deck when spent, and into your bank before it returns to your deck. Staff cards have multiple uses - which one will you activate? The game rewards players who know how to best manage the constant flux of their decks, plan their turns, and make the best use of the hand they are given.

—description from the publisher

name: Pillars of Heracles
description:
Join us on an epic journey through the world of Archaic Period Greece, where heroes are born, city-states clash in bitter rivalries, and the gods themselves shape the destiny of mortals. Prepare to immerse yourself in a strategic and immersive board game experience.  Will you channel the wisdom of the mighty Olympian gods to lead your city-state to greatness? Or will you rely on cunning tactics and military might to conquer your rivals?

In Pillars of Heracles, you will embark on a quest to build and shape your own city-state, compete against formidable adversaries, and navigate the intricacies of ancient Greek society. As you explore the game's intricately designed world, you will encounter iconic figures from Greek history and mythology, engage in trade and diplomacy, and face the challenges and rewards of city-building. Every decision you make will shape the fate of your city-state and determine your path to victory.

Against its rich historical and mythological backdrop, the game offers a unique blend of area control, rondel mechanics, and deckbuilding, tableau building, set collection, and resource management. As you expand your city-state and manage your resources, you'll need to strategize your moves on the rondel, carefully planning your actions. Building and managing your deck allows you to customize your strategy and prepare for exciting challenges.

The objective of the game is to become the most glorious City-state of them all! You can gain Glory in the game by Controlling Cities and Regions, Building Monuments, and Fulfilling Prophecies. The game ends when players have collectively reached the end of a number of Region tracks equal to the number of players, when a player controls 6 Cities, or when 3 Era III Prophecy cards have been removed from the Game board.

The player with the most Glory wins the game!

name: 3-2-1 Countdown
description:
3-2-1 Countdown is a retro space travel-themed game in which players race to blast off by earning points with the lowest total hand value. Shed your cards onto one of the two discard piles by playing singles or sets, ending your turn by drawing a single card.

The goal is to declare "countdown" and end the round with the lowest total value in your hand.


     If the player who declares "countdown" has the lowest hand, they earn points and bonuses.
     If another player has a lower hand, the declarer earns no points, and other players score instead.


Deciding whether to keep shedding cards on your turn or risk declaring "countdown" is a strategic gamble!

—description from the publisher

name: Whoa There Cowboy
description:
Join the card-slinging fun in this thrilling race to victory! Outsmart opponents by playing higher or lower value cards from your hand—bluff boldly to stack points, but beware: get caught and face a penalty! Prove your honesty to earn point tokens quicker, and play all your cards for even bigger scores. 
Win by shedding out your hand.

name: Pulp Romance
description:
Pulp Romance is a solitaire card game about searching for your lost love in Europe between the wars. The two main mechanisms are placement and adjacency.

From a "journey row", you acquire cards in five suits — cities, friends, detectives, newspapers, and bankers - and place them in your search tableau, activating them, with their actions dependent on cards previously played. You need to defeat a sixth suit — rivals — when they're dealt to the journey row through management of your tableau. Custom dice give bonus abilities to your chosen character, with the game including four double-sided characters and four double-sided love loves.

name: Rhymes with Duck
description:
Gather your flock and dive into a whirlwind of wordplay. Score points by matching your rhyming word with other players and bonus points by matching Chuck.

Watch out though! If you don't match with anyone, you get a letter of shame -
spell Q-U-A-C-K and you're kicked out of the pond.  First player to 20 points is the DUCKY winner!

name: Punica: Rome vs Carthage
description:
Set during the Punic Wars (264–146 BC), PUNICA allows players to command either Rome or Carthage in a contest of military might, territorial dominance, and cunning cardplay. The Romans seek steady expansion through disciplined ranks and sheer persistence. Carthage relies on its wealth, maneuverability, and the daring tactics of generals like Hannibal Barca. Both factions feel distinct, with asymmetrical starting positions and access to different regional advantages on the map.

At its heart, Punica is a blend of area control and hand management, designed to offer strategic bite without requiring hours at the table. The compact playtime (20 minutes) makes it perfect for tournament play, travel, or as a high-stakes warm-up between longer sessions.

—description from the publisher

name: Puppets in High Places
description:
Puppets in High Places is set in the same universe as With a Smile & a Gun, but it is a standalone game, not an expansion.

After gaining control of the streets of Gattory City, mob bosses are setting their sights to the next level: getting a foothold in City Hall.

Puppets in High Places is a cutthroat game of underhanded power. Players will go through the Streets to obtain the resources they need to bribe VIPs and gain their favour. They will then proceed to the Speakeasy, where they will fight over these VIPs through a dynamic tug-of-war mechanism. Of course, mob bosses that they are, they have tricks up their sleeves and goons working the back alleys.

Puppets in High Places uses an evolving rondel, which the players will modify throughout the game, and a tug-of-war mechanism where players try to score VIP's represented by dice, whose value the players will also influence.

—description from the publisher

name: Pura Vida
description:
Pura Vida is not only the life motto in Costa Rica, but also stands for the country's enormous biodiversity and its stated goal of living in harmony with nature and wildlife. The approximately 30 national parks, which make up around 26% of Costa Rica's area, also make an important contribution to the protection of its biodiversity. 
All kinds of landscapes can be discovered here: from dense rainforests and mangrove forests to rocky volcanoes, dry savannahs and sandy coasts. The wildlife is equally diverse: toucans, sloths, snakes, butterflies and many other species live here – not least the red-eyed tree frogs, which are so iconic for the country.
As a ranger, your task is to create a balanced animal population in the numerous nature parks. The particular challenge is to take the animals’ individual and natural movements into account. Besides taking numerous tricky decisions, you will also get to know Costa Rica's cheerful and relaxed attitude to life - Pura Vida!

Gameplay:
On your turn you must choose between these two actions:
a) Move
b) Rest 
Move: Move your ranger along the path and take the tile where you end your movement. Place the tile in your own national park, trying to align animals and/or landscapes the best way to get points.
Rest: Move your ranger to the rest area. You are not allowed to make any more moves this round.

Scoring: Every time you place a tile in your national park, you check whether you meet one of the biodiversity criteria and receive points for it:
For 3/4/5 tiles directly next to each other in a row or column with different animals and the same landscape, you get 2/2/3 points. 
For 3/4/5 tiles directly next to each other in a row or column with different landscapes and the same animals, you get 2/2/3 points. 
For 3/4/5 tiles directly next to each other in a row or column with different animals and different landscapes you get 1/1/2 points.

The game ends as soon as someone has reached at least 20 points. This person wins.

name: Vampire Survivors: The Board Game
description:
Vampire Survivors: The Board Game is a tabletop version of the video game. Brave heroes battle seemingly unending waves of enemies as they hope to survive as long as possible!

This cooperative deck building game has several unique characters, which players will deploy on the gameboard. They must do battle with with fiendish creatures who seek only to exterminate their existence. Players gather weapons and items to increase their powers and gather new abilities so they may outlast the vampire onslaught.

If the players can live long enough, they will make it to the end and win the game, even though Death itself will arrive to destroy them utterly.

But maybe, even Death can die.

—description from the publisher

name: 7 for Luck
description:
This game calls for brigth minds!
Players have to complete 7 task cards with increasing degrees of difficulty, one after the other. Who will be quickest to uncover the lucky animals they’re looking for? 
A rainbow grows as each task card is completed.

The first player to master all 7 phases and complete their own rainbow wins the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Puru Puru Paradice
description:
Players play as Puru Puru and her friends, who are all striving to live a puru-fect life full of Love and Excitement so they can enter PARADICE. But beware, bouncy jellies don’t last long on the table!

The game is played in turns starting from the starting player clockwise. Each player’s turn consists of rolling the dice and resolving the result of the dice. The game ends immediately when either one player obtains 20 Love or Excitement, or one player drips to 0!

The key mechanic in this game is if you roll too much of one side, your neighbours get that result instead! That applies to both good - and bad sides.

Don't forget to try the advanced game where each jelly has their own unique game-changing power!

—description from the publisher

name: Push Push Penguin
description:
In Push Push Penguin, you will compete in a race filled with slides, snacks, and seals.

But there is a catch! An Orca approaches, and it will chase away the first penguin to cross paths with it – so the Penguin who finishes second in this race is the winner!

To play, all players roll their Penguin Dice. Players use their Penguin Cup to shake their dice and hide them. They secretly select which of their dice they want to use for movement then reveal the dice at the same time. Starting with whoever has the Orca Die, each player takes a turn gobbling up fish and moving their penguin. They push any penguins they land on or interact with special spaces. After all players have taken their turn, the player with the Orca Die rolls it and moves the Orca.

The game ends when the Orca moves onto a Penguin’s space and the Penguin is not able to gobble up fish tokens to keep from being scared away by the Orca.

The player with the penguin in second place wins!

—description from the designer

name: PWNED!
description:
PWNED! is a two-player abstract strategy game where the cyberpunk theme meets tactical depth. Set in a digital battlefield inspired by hacker culture, players command opposing hacker factions—Red vs. Blue—in a race to infiltrate each other’s servers. The narrative pits two hacker armies, led by the legendary Hacker Pangolin, in an explosive clash of logic, deception, and domination.

Players take turns performing two out of four possible actions: move, copy, zip, or unzip their pieces across a network of nodes. Strategic placement is essential, as players can stack three pieces into a powerful compressed “zip file,” which can later be unpacked to dispatch pieces on free directions. Along the way, Trojan bombs add layers of bluffing and chaos, capable of triggering chain reactions when revealed or deliberately detonated.

Beyond positioning and movement, players must remain connected—literally. Each side must maintain a network path to their own server at all times, or risk violating the “disconnection” rule. Meanwhile, deleting enemy pieces through strategic flanking is a key part of control and sabotage.

The objective is clear: be the first to send any of your pieces into the opponent’s server and shout “PWNED!” to declare victory! With its sleek mechanics, hidden traps, and layered decision-making, PWNED! delivers a highly replayable battle of minds, ideal for fans of tactical board games and digital warfare alike.

—description from the designer

name: Animals Around the World BINGO
description:
Sharpen your knowledge by correctly guessing the characteristics on the various animal cards.
Players each have 16 characteristic tiles and must guess the characteristics of animals shown on picture cards. Each player marks 1 or 2 characteristics with guessing chips on their grid based on the animals shown and compares these to the animal's actual characteristics revealed on the back of the card. The goal is to be the first to complete a row, column or diagonal with your own marked tiles and shout “Bingo!” Whoever shouts “Bingo!” twice wins the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Carni Flora
description:
The carnivorous plants are hungry – verrry hungry! So try your best to grow quickly and snap up as many yummy flies as you can. Attract the buzzing tasty treats with your scent and catch them in your traps. 
But beware! Any flies that escape will cost you both points and patience.

The player who’s eaten the most flies while letting the fewest get away wins the game!

A happy snappy arranging game.

     Arranging game for clever and greedy minds
     Score points with 50 wooden flies
     The longer the game, the more beautiful the plants


—description from the publisher

name: Pyrotechnics
description:
Meet Pyrotechnics, the two‑player card duel that fits in your pocket and delivers ten minute bursts of lightly strategic gameplay. With just eighteen cards and thirty‑six spark tokens, it’s the perfect travel game or quick filler between activities—yet beneath its compact size lies surprising depth.

To begin, shuffle the deck and remove the top three cards from play. Deal five cards face down to each player, then lay out five cards face up in the center of play as a shared tableau. Place the spark tokens and reference guide within reach. Choose who will take the first turn and give the other player one spark token in red, yellow, or blue.

On your turn, you’ll perform two steps. First, Research: select one card from your hand, play it in front of you, and carry out the actions shown in the upper‑left corner. Then, from the shared tableau, choose a card to Discover or Showcase. If you Discover, do the actions in the lower-left and add the card to your hand, expanding your options. If you Showcase, pay the cost in the lower-right, remove the card from the game, and shrink your hand—bringing you closer to victory.

Every time you Showcase, your hand grows smaller. The duel accelerates as both players balance the lure of helpful cards against the need to whittle down their hand. The first pyrotechnical engineer to Showcase five cards and end their turn with no cards in hand wins instantly.
Pyrotechnics is easy to learn but endlessly replayable. You’ll bluff, block, and bait your opponent—timing your Research, Discover and Showcase just right to outmaneuver them. It’s a micro‑game with macro thrills.

Pyrotechnics brings big excitement in a tiny package. Ready to spark your next game night? Start it with a bang!

—description from the publisher

name: Póker a Voces
description:
In Póker a Voces (Shouting Póker), bluffs are shouted, hands are built mid-chaos, and silence is not an option.
This fast-paced party game reimagines poker in a wild, shouty format. Players simultaneously trade cards by yelling out how many they want to exchange — but never revealing what they’re trading. Build three hands of five cards, assign your bets, and go head-to-head in a battle of memory, bluffing, and quick decisions.
The twist? Special animal cards like Raccoons, Mandrills, and Emperor Penguins add unpredictable effects and wild combos that can flip the table (figuratively… hopefully).
Raccoon: Wild card. If 2 or more in the same hand, those players are eliminated.

Dove: Wild card only if another is revealed. If you have 2, you're eliminated.

Capybara: Cannot be combined. If an odd number is revealed, the worst hand wins.

Mandrill: Draw 3 cards; each player with a mandrill chooses 1 to replace it.

Penguin: Cannot be combined, but if you win with it, gain +10 extra points.

—description from the publisher

name: Dragonella
description:
Dragon Dragonella guards her stolen treasure. Will the players manage to win back the precious cups from her? Everyone plays at the same time: Who is the fastest, strikes at the right moment and doesn't get caught by Dragonella? Fast-paced fun with three levels of difficulty, where the first person to collect the required number of cups wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Quacks: All-In Edition
description:
In Quacks, players are charlatans — or quack doctors — each making their own secret brew by adding ingredients one at a time. Take care with what you add, though, for a pinch too much of this or that will spoil the whole mixture!

Each player has their own bag of ingredient chips. During each round, they simultaneously draw chips from their bags and add them to their pots. The higher the face value of the drawn chip, the further it is placed in the pot's swirling pattern, increasing how much the potion will be worth. Push your luck as far as you can, but if you add too many cherry bombs, your pot will explode!

At the end of each round, players gain victory points and coins to spend on new ingredients, depending on how well they managed to fill up their pots. But players whose pots have exploded must choose points or coins — not both! The player with the most victory points at the end of nine rounds wins the game.

Quacks: All-In Edition includes the original The Quacks of Quedlinburg base game, as well as two expansions previously released separately — The Witches and The Alchemists — as well as deluxe components.

name: Quantum Quest
description:
In the 20th century, quantum physics revolutionized our understanding of the atomic and subatomic world, paving the way for quantum technologies. These promise breakthroughs in communication, sensing, simulation, and computation.

However, to engineer these futuristic technologies, our labs and industries must master the art of controlling single atoms and manipulating them to create specific states characterized by unique quantum properties, known as entanglement. This is the quest ahead of us, already undertaken by many researchers and innovators worldwide, which Quantum Quest represents.

During each turn, players may:


     Take a card from the display
     Play a card in the Quantum Technologies Pyramid
     Convert Qubits to advance on the Entanglement Scale


Join us in the challenge of developing quantum technologies, increasing your research capability, creating thousands of qubits, and entangling them faster than your adversaries. Be the first to climb the Pyramid of Quantum Technologies and claim your space in the history of science and technology!

Quantum Quest is an educational board game developed by the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Padua. It explores key elements of quantum physics, such as qubits and entanglement, aiming to make the principles behind the race for Quantum Advantage accessible to everyone—all through an engaging and immersive gaming experience.

—description from the designer

name: Galaxolotl
description:
The Galaxolotls had a great time on Earth! But now it’s time for them to return to their home planet. However, as soon as they land, the old rivalry between the two big Galaxolotl families rears its head. Who arrived there first? And who will claim the best spots?
Exciting thrills and risky decisions are guaranteed!
The player with the most star points at the end wins the game!


     Thrills through exciting risk-taking decisions
     Simple rules, clever tactics
     Features hilariously alien Axolotl cards


—description from the designer

name: Quashars
description:
The fiery feline spirits, released from their sealed book, are up to mischief again today. They do as they please, meddling with others' plans just for fun. Freed from the pages of ancient books, the mischievous fire-cat spirits known as Quashars roam the world in search of chaos and fun. Driven by impulse and mischief, they chase their whims while sabotaging the plans of others. Every round is a new prank, a new diversion, and a new challenge. You are one of them... can you cause the most playful mayhem?

Quashars is a trick-taking game with a unique condition-based bidding system. The bid is not about how many tricks you’ll win, but how many conditions you’ll fulfill. A single trick may satisfy multiple conditions or none at all. This twist shifts the focus from pure trick prediction to clever hand timing, card play manipulation, and goal juggling.

name: Quattro Trick-Taking
description:
In Quattro Trick-Taking, players lay their cards into shared tricks as in a normal trick-taking game, but each player has a different bidding method for scoring, so you're not necessarily fighting over the same cards throughout the round.

A four-player game lasts four rounds, and in each round you'll use a different method for bidding. You can take colored chips to indicate the color of the winning card that you'll play in a trick, or you can indicate the sum of the cards that you'll collect over the entire hand. You can indicate which colors and/or ranks (even or odd) you will not use to win tricks, or you'll choose condition cards that you think you'll satisfy during the hand, such as taking two 7s or winning a trick with a 4-6, with you scoring only if you satisfy all of the chosen conditions.

The deck consists of four suits, each numbered 1-12, with red always being the trump suit. Standard trick-taking rules apply, with players needing to follow suit, if possible, so the tricky part of the game is navigating the different goals that your fellow players have set for themselves and ensuring that you satisfy your bid.

name: Queen Carrom To Go
description:
Queen Carrom To Go: The perfect blend of skill and fun - anywhere, anytime!

Queen Carrom To Go is accessible for players of all ages.
With a simple rule set and two game modes, anyone can play and learn  Queen Carrom!
The goal is simple: Flick the striker and pocket the coins. For each coin pocketed you get a point. The first player to reach 25 points wins!

The back of the board shows an alternative way of playing that can also be used for practicing your shooting skills!

—description from the designer

name: Queen Marie-Antoinette
description:
A game of strategy and influence at the court of Versailles

Step into the intrigues of the royal court!
In Queen Marie-Antoinette, you play as ambitious courtesans vying for favor in the opulent court of Louis XVI. Recruit influential characters from five distinct factions (Favorites, Merchants, Military, Clergy, Aristocrats), fulfill secret Plots, and adapt to the Queen’s ever-changing demands to earn influence points.

The Queen’s Requirements and shifting Conditions will disrupt your plans and force you to rethink your strategy each turn. Only the most cunning courtier will rise to the top.

Core Mechanics:

     Hand management: Play character cards to manipulate the court in your favor.
     Objective completion: Combine characters to fulfill Plots and score.
     Dynamic scoring: The Queen’s shifting preferences give bonuses to specific factions.
     High player interaction: Tactics and timing are key to outmaneuvering opponents.


Why you'll love it:

     Easy to learn rules with surprising strategic depth.
     A richly illustrated immersive theme based on historical intrigue.
     Fast and fluid gameplay, ideal for 2 to 4 players.
     High replayability thanks to modular setup and evolving conditions each game.


Queen Marie-Antoinette is designed by Julien Griffon, illustrated by Alice Piernet, and published by Oka Luda. It blends historical charm with accessible yet clever gameplay in a game of courtly ambition and subtle tactics.

—description from the publisher

name: Quest Calendar 2026: The Souls of Saraku
description:
Souls of Saraku is a solo tabletop RPG disguised as a daily calendar, where you take on the role of a villain rising to power through a year-long fantasy adventure.

Heroes have killed the Overlord. Will you rise to claim the throne and seek vengeance on the heroes?

Each day reveals a new page with story-driven encounters, dice-based challenges, moral decisions, and darkly satisfying rewards. You’ll level up, collect loot, recruit minions, and face off against heroes, monsters, and rival overlords—one bite-sized session at a time. With simple mechanics, immersive writing, and epic choices that ripple through the story, it’s a dangerously fun way to conquer your desk and your destiny.

—description from the publisher

name: Quest Inc.
description:
In Quest Inc. you are an NPC in an electronic RPG game that owns a mission distribution company. Your plan is to make profit through the quest industry.

It's that old story, people need to solve problems and they won't mind paying a few gold coins to solve it. And that's where you come in! Your company will take on the mission to receive the treasure, but for that you'll need to hire the bravest (and why not the cheapest) heroes, after all, the money left over is yours!

Furthermore, no one will question if some valuable items rescued by the heroes ended up in your hands. “It's part of the mission,” you'll reply. In case of your mission to profit more.

But be careful, competing companies will be around, trying to take the best opportunities before you!

The game is played in rounds, each round has 2 phases: in the first one players engage in an inverted auction to see who gets what quest and the money.

In the next phase players go to a location in the city, to pay to contract adventures (such as Rogues, Warriors, Mages or Clerics), each location has a special rule change.

By completing a quest a player receives loot cards that can give single use abilities and/or can be sold at the end of the game, and if this is part of a set the profit will be higher.

The game ends after some rounds (depending on the number of players), then the player with the most money wins.

name: Quest Snakes
description:
In Quest Snakes, you take on the role of a guild leader tasked to recruit heroic snakes into your ranks.

In the first phase of the game, players will take turns hiring pairs of Snakes. Once you have a guild of 10 snakes, you enter the second phase.

In the second phase, quests are posted one at a time, offering loot to the strongest guild. Guild leaders will assemble a party of Snakes in secrecy.  Once parties are assembled, guilds reveal their snakes. Snakes have power values assigned to them, and the party with the most power wins. But be aware, some classes of Snakes are better equipped for certain quests. And snakes need to rest after the questing - the stronger the Snake, the more turns they rest.

The guild with the most loot after a set number of Quests wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Quests & Cannons: The Risen Islands
description:
A high fantasy on the high seas competitive, sandbox-style adventure game for 1-6 players.

Quests & Cannons: The Risen Islands takes place in the original fantasy world of Miraheim, where a set of mysterious islands have risen from the sea. With the delicate balance of the world disrupted, the people of Miraheim begin to leave their homelands and to settle on the islands, finding them to be plentiful in resources. Ancient writings have begun to be uncovered telling of a mythical artifact hidden among the islands through a series of map clues that could be the key to restoring balance to the world. Players are adventurers sent from one of the three prominent kingdoms of Miraheim to ensure the prosperity of their kingdom's settlers as well as search for this fabled treasure that could save their homes.

Quests & Cannons: The Risen Islands is an accessible, deep strategy game about exploration, epic quests, and exciting combat. Players use action points each turn on an open movement, modular game board to explore the various islands, receive quests from the settlers, gather resources, find map clues, upgrade their ships, collect loot, and trade cannon fire with rival adventurers. The object of the game is to get to the most prosperity at the end of the game. Players earn prosperity by finishing quests, completing map clues, and attacking other players.

—description from the publisher

name: Quietbell
description:
Quietbell is an adventure detective game inspired by the works of Howard Phillips Lovecraft.

You’ll experience an engaging interactive story whose outcome depends entirely on you and your choices. Throughout the game, you will piece together a larger picture and unravel the tangled fates and events that took place in the mysterious town of Quietbell.

The game features a "nonlinear communication" mechanic, allowing the player to interact with various in-game characters on different topics at their discretion.

The game also features a "strokes" mechanic using transparent plastic cards, allowing the player to create their own unique picture.

—description from the designer

name: Quintet
publisher: メリーアンドリューワークス(merry-andrew-works)
description:
In a smoky jazz club filled with feline musicians, improvisation is everything. Each round flows like a syncopated rhythm, where playing the perfect note at the right moment is more important than overpowering the melody. As hands shrink and risks rise, only the most composed players can build the harmony they need.

Quintet is a trick-taking game in which players try to collect cards that sum exactly to five, while avoiding cards worth negative points. The lead player must play two cards instead of one, causing hands to shrink unevenly over time. The game ends when any player runs out of cards, and players score based on collected sets and remaining cards.

name: QUIZ-O-METER
description:
QUIZ-O-METER: The Guessing Game Full of Fun, Surprises and “Aha!” Moments!

With 240 diverse questions and clever answer boards, QUIZ-O-METER brings fresh excitement to the game table. In four thrilling rounds packed with surprises, strategy and intuition, players must estimate answers, outsmart their opponents, and hit as close to the mark as possible.

Whether you rely on knowledge, gut feeling, or a touch of bluff – the right move scores points! And when things get really close, the tie-breaker delivers edge-of-your-seat suspense right up to the very end. The perfect game for family nights, parties, and everyone who loves quiz games with a special twist!

—description from the publisher

name: Quodd Heroes (2nd Edition)
description:
ABOUT THE GAME:

You are a cube-shaped hero in a dangerous, sometimes chaotic, but always fun-filled world. Choose a scenario, gather your friends, select  your Heroes and prepare yourselves for loads of fast-paced adventure!

In order to move around the board, a Quodd must tumble! Tumbling activates one of five upgradable movement skills, or your Q skill (is it Q-Power?) based on the side of your Hero that is facing up after you tumble. While moving, you'll be interacting with special board obstacles and tiles like raging rivers, springs, teleporters, dangerous pits, and of course your opponents (or teammates). But don't worry... I'm sure your friends always have your best interests at heart.

Along your journey, be sure to collect the crystals you find on the board. They'll activate special abilities unique to your Hero, but be careful—other Heroes can steal the crystals you’re carrying! During your turn you will also discover food, runes and other useful stuff to enhance your natural abilities, modify the board, and slow down your opponents.

Out in the world you’ll also occasionally find secrets, usually hidden away in difficult to reach places, but always worth the journey as they often contain game-changing advantages for your Hero. A Hero who slows down by activating their Q will also discover the secrets of the world which are available only to those who look for them.

At the end of your turn you will read an event card out loud. Event cards affect all players, but don’t panic, usually nothing bad happens… and sometimes they’ll even invite you to upgrade your Hero!
 WHAT'S IN THE BOX:

The game includes beautiful miniatures, exceptional components, and eight beautifully illustrated, infinitely-replayable scenario maps, each offering a fun new challenge. Scenarios include races, Rallies, pick-up-and-deliver challenges, and team games like capture the crystal, sheep soccer and more!

On top of all that, the Quodd Heroes game system is truly a sandbox and lends itself to quick and easy building of your own home-crafted scenarios—the sky's the limit!  
 What’s New in 2nd Edition

- Vastly improved, professionally written and edited rulebook, with more example images, an index, and quick reference for frequent rules questions

- Streamlined player experience with more intuitive upgrade system, player board design
- New Q-Powers and Crystal Powers create a more thematically immersive, and unique feel to each Hero.
- Reworked turn structure and event system remove the feeling of uncontrolled chaos and being “beat by the game” that some players had issues with in 1st Edition while still maintaining the feeling of an ever-changing environment.
- Game ships with an organizer for fast setup
- Reduced component count keeps setup and cleanup to a minimum.
- Improved visual and usability design across almost every component in the game.
- Hero cubes and painted miniatures replace the unpainted minis from First Edition for a more intuitive player experience.
- A scenario book with durable, high quality fold out maps greatly improves setup time, and scenario quality, compared to the fully modular boards in 1st Edition.
- There’s so much more, too!

Quodd Heroes 2nd Edition is truly a must-experience game!

name: It's High Tide!
description:
Sandworms ahoy! The big Sandworm Race is about to begin! The crowd cheers as the sandworm teams speed along the racetrack to
reach the reef as quickly as they can. But beware, if you don’t take cover in your hole in time, the tide will wash you back to the beginning.
The winner is the first player to use clever tactics and a bit of luck to get all their sandworms to the finish line.

Fun and playful 3D design brings a real beach atmosphere to the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Karuba Since 2015
description:
Welcome back to Karuba! 
The expedition begins – and you are not alone. As you uncover winding paths and search for forgotten temples, other teams move forward. The jungle is unpredictable, time is running out… and every decision counts!
The player who retrieves the most valuable treasures wins this exciting expedition race.

With 3 expansions: Unlock special actions and complete exciting missions! Or curse your competitors' paths and place obstacles in their way…


     Big box with 3 brand new expansions
     With game material for up to 6 players
     Entertaining: everyone plays at the same time!
     Adventure classic in a fresh design


—description from the publisher

name: R.A.V.E.L.
description:
Can you pierce the secrets of the R.A.V.E.L. (Rare Artefact Vertiginous Enigmatic Logical)?

R.A.V.E.L. is an endlessly resettable puzzle, where you’ll have to manipulate 8 dice placed in the centre of a grid in order to solve the Cog cards placed around it. Each solved Cog card will grant you a unique opportunity to further unlock the remaining cards, but only the clever use of your limited resources will allow you to pierce the secrets of this strange contraption.

name: Let's talk NEON: Blue
description:
Welcome to NEON! A vibrant and exciting city full of opportunities, where communication happens through gestures and sounds. Dive into the action and experience NEON in your own unique way!

A party game of gestures and sounds! Describe two secret images using only one noise and one gesture. Others race to guess and grab the right tiles. No words, just pure creativity and chaos — in two fun modes!

Entertaining fun: combine sounds and gestures in a hilarious way
Simple rules and set up to start playing immediately
Original packaging in a handy carry-along edition
Let’s Talk MORE NEON: The game comes in a variety of color editions, each with different sets of motifs for even more replayability and laughs.

—description from the publisher

name: Nature
publisher: NorthStar Game Studio; HABA; Hobby World; Yaofish Games
description:
Nature is a redesign of the blockbuster Evolution to be more streamlined, more forgiving, strategically deeper, and seamlessly expandable. The secret sauce is a modular system that allows players to create a unique ecosystem each time they play. Every combination creates a unique environment to discover.

Adapt to the Changing Environment:
The goal of Nature is to grow thriving populations in an ecosystem where food is scarce and predators lurk. Evolve traits like Tusked for foraging, Fast for escaping danger, or Clawed for hunting.

Create a Unique Ecosystem Each Time You Play:
The core game of Nature is an accessible gateway into a world of dynamic ecosystems. Each game can be tailored to the tastes of the people at the table. Add Nature: Flight for people who prefer to avoid conflict, Nature: Jurassic for a more aggressive game, or Nature: Arctic Tundra for a survival game on the edge of the livable world.  There are 5 modules and 2 mini-modules that can be combined to create 96 different ecosystems. After the Summer 2026 releases there will be over 700 combinations to explore!

How to Play:
Nature is a card-driven tableau-builder played over 4 rounds. Each round is split between the Adapting Phase and the Feeding Phase.

Adapting Phase: Use 5 cards as actions to do the following: 
- Increase Population
- Increase Body Size
- Play as a Trait to power-up your species
- Save to be used as food during the Feeding Phase

Feeding Phase: Feed as many of your population as possible. At the end of the round, players get 1 point for each population they kept alive. The winner is the player that kept the most population alive over all 4 rounds.



Nature Digital: Learn to play with an interactive tutorial on the free-to-try Nature app (iOS, Android, and Steam).
https://www.naturedigitalgame.com/


A Living Game System:
NorthStar Studio will release the Climate module in 2026, followed by one to two new modules per year for the next decade.
Vote for future modules here:
https://boardgamegeek.com/blog/308/blogpost/166360/future-nature-modules-poll


Designer Diary
Dominic Crapuchettes discusses the inspiration behind Nature, which began during his time as a professional Magic player.
https://boardgamegeek.com/blog/1/blogpost/179068/designer-diary-the-evolution-of-nature

name: Pencil Pirates
description:
Ahoy there, pirates! A vast, wide ocean with many unknown islands lies ahead of you. Get ready and sharpen your pencils.
Draw lines on your nautical maps to sail from one island to another. On your travels, collect as much treasure and pirate booty as you can.
The player with the most points after 7 rounds wins the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Race to Reactor
description:
Welcome to Race to Reactor, a nuclear power-themed card game for 2-4 players where strategy and sabotage are the keys to victory. Get ready to race against your fellow competitors to build the most powerful nuclear reactors!

However, it’s not just about building your reactors - it's about slowing down and supplanting others to seize the advantage. But beware! Your rivals will be playing cards designed to delay your progress, from component limitations to technical malfunctions. You'll need to strike a balance between advancing your own reactors and disrupting the plans of others. In the battle to power the planet your strength can turn on a single card.

Will you be forced to play a rival's components to get your reactor over the line? Or will you bide your time waiting for the perfect opportunity to strike? Shifting strategies abound in this fast-paced card game, will you win the Race to Reactor?

—description from the publisher

name: Racket
description:
Step into the seedy world of 1920s organized crime in Racket, a mafia-themed board game filled with mobsters, influence, and deadly ambition. Designed for 2–4 players, Racket casts each participant as the boss of a fledgling criminal empire vying for dominance. The objective: become the most powerful and profitable syndicate in the city by the end of the game.

Each player leads a mob faction—each with unique abilities—competing for control of valuable city turf and acquiring assets to expand their operation. From acquiring useful assets through shady backroom deals to sending goons to sabotage rival enterprises and dodging entanglements with the police, every decision shapes the rise—or fall—of a player's criminal empire. In Racket, strategic asset management, well-timed mob hits, and a keen eye for identifying critical business opportunities are all essential to outmaneuvering the competition and staying ahead of the law.

Racket blends classic area control and dice-rolling mechanics with asset acquisition and use, all within a richly thematic 1920s mafia setting. With dynamic gameplay, variations in both set-up and play, and good old-fashioned cutthroat player interaction, Racket is ideal for players who enjoy light strategy and luck, wrapped in a vintage underworld flair. Whether it’s an early power grab or a final, calculated strike, every move matters in this exciting board game where players battle for power and control.

—description from the publisher

name: Raging Kingdoms
description:
Raging Kingdoms is a medieval-themed real-time strategy (RTS) inspired board game.

Command one of history’s great kingdoms and lead it to victory through skillful economic development, technological advancement, and, of course, the art of war!

Raging Kingdoms is a game for one to six players. A typical game takes 90 to 120 minutes.

Win by conquering all enemy empires, or by leaving them in awe of your Wonder Victory. Each turn, you'll roll a special die for your action moves. Make the most of your action moves to march closer to your goal.


     Create new units - villagers to gather resources, scouts to discover the hidden map, or swordsmen, archers and knights to crush threatening neighbors.
     Construct new buildings - camps to exploit resources, blacksmiths to equip your army, and towers to defend against aggressive opponents.
     Research new technologies to help your empire reach new heights.
     Devise the perfect attack to conquer new land and show your enemies your rage!


At the end of your turn, collect the resources your villagers have gathered for you and start planning your next moves!

Highlights:

     Immersive: Play as exciting historical civilizations like the Romans, Vikings, Mongols, and more!
     RTS Appeal: Intuitive for fans of classic medieval real-time strategy (RTS) games!
     Replayability: Newly generated map to discover each game, exciting game variants, single player and multiplayer campaigns!


Raging Kingdoms delivers in a tabletop game all the best parts of classic RTS video games, like:

     A randomly generated map that players discover, making each game different
     Managing the gathering and stockpiling of 4 resources
     Finding the perfect balance between reinvesting in your economy, strengthening your military, and researching new technology
     Choosing which military units will be most effective in which battle situations
     Strategically deciding when, where, and how to strike your opponents
     Tactically commanding units to lead them to victory


—description from the publisher

name: Raidents
description:
Raidents are pun-packed anthropomorphic cartoon rodents resolved to raid your opponent’s home. A 2-player strategy board game for all Chess enthusiasts but with portals, explosives, and a plant-the-flag win condition.

With the modular terrain tiles there are nearly 92 million unique board combinations before the game has even begun, ensuring fresh strategies and endless replayability. The terrain unlocks each Raident’s signature abilities, but only 3 of your 11 Raidents can be on the battlefield at a time. Do you need the puppeteering Moustermind, the Squerrilla’s AKORN47, the Chinzhilla’s Kaijujitsu, or the Porcupyro to nuke some hot cross bunnies?

Cycle through your Queue quickly and sabotage your enemies’ plans before they thwart yours. Adapt to the map, improvise your battle cries, and overcome your opponent’s rodents in the game of wacky warfare and silly strategy!

-description from designer

name: Point of View: 1 Session – Clash Club
description:
Point of View: Clash Club is a fast-paced, cooperative puzzle game where communication is everything.

While chasing a fugitive, your team investigates the bizarre “Clash Club” – a surreal mix of techno, wellness, casino, and interior design. But the mission takes an unexpected twist...

Each player sees the same 3D scene from a different angle on their own fold-out map – and sharing visuals is not allowed. Only by talking and piecing together your unique perspectives can you solve the 60 puzzles and uncover the truth.

A compact, one-session game full of surprises, teamwork, and fresh “aha!” moments.

—description from the publisher

name: Point of View: Spooky Festival
description:
The Spooky Festival is an aging amusement park that leads a dreary existence surrounded by high-rise buildings and harbor terminals. But the small patch of land has recently sparked significant interest and that‘s where the problems begin.

Four large folding maps show you a hidden object scene in a cool 3D style. But: Each folding plan shows this scene from a different angle. And: Each of you only gets to see one folding plan at a time, showing each other is taboo. As a result, no one has a complete overview. Communication is the key to joint success!

To solve the puzzles, you have to talk to each other intensively - both about what you see and about what you don't see. 
In four chapters, you will immerse yourself in exciting and crazy adventures and constantly face new challenges.

name: Rails and Cargo: Think and Write
description:
Rails and Cargo is a solitaire train game played using just two sheets of paper. All you need to get started is one regular pencil and four colored pencils or crayons.

As the railway planner and operator, you’ll rebuild tracks, construct new factories, produce valuable goods, and deliver them to their intended destinations.
There’s no luck involved in the gameplay - dice are used only during setup to create variety in each session.

—description from the designer

name: Railway Boom
publisher: Arclight Games; Cranio Creations; Strohmann Games
description:
In the late 19th century, during the early Meiji era, Japan opened its first railway line between Shimbashi and Yokohama. This new mode of transportation sparked a railway boom across the country.

Local entrepreneurs, and later powerful tycoons, established new companies that grew into large railway corporations throughout the Taishō and Shōwa eras.

As players, you will take on the roles of these tycoons, building and managing your own railway empires as you compete for the most renown.

Railway Boom recreates this era of industry through gameplay by having players balance resource management with the growth of their railways connecting various cities across Japan.

—description from the publisher

name: The Mix
description:
Are you ready to become a master mixologist? As a young recruit at the renowned Foxtrot Bar, your mission is to craft mouthwatering cocktails to delight your customers. Grab your shaker, hone your skills, and prove your mixology expertise! The Mix is THE ultimate cocktail-themed strategy board game!

Gain experience, enhance your bartending skills, explore new recipes, expand your bar to serve more customers, and establish yourself as the top mixologist at the Foxtrot Bar!

The Mix offers a blend of engine building, actions, resource management, and worker placement. Prepare to be immersed in the world of mixology!

One round consists of players placing all their Mixologists and resolving the actions.  The game ends when 15 orders have been finished. The player with the most victory points wins.

name: Raven Manor
description:
Something strange has been happening in the Manor lately. Black feathers appeared all around the Manor, seemingly out of nowhere. Members of the Family started to act out of character and some have died under mysterious circumstances. But these are no accidents - someone is pulling the strings behind the scenes and he needs to be stopped as soon as possible. Can the surviving members of the Family find and kill him before it’s too late?

Raven Manor is a social deduction party game with stunning dark graphics, inspired by Sin City comics and with easy-to-learn rules that lead to deep gameplay.

One of you will play as the Raven. The rest will take on the role of the Family. As the Raven, your goal is to possess or kill the other players. As the Family, you must use your wits and deduction skills to uncover the Raven's identity and eliminate them before it's too late. Death doesn’t stop you from enjoying the game. If you’re killed, you’re playing just as before, but with a restriction - from now on you can’t kill anyone else. No more waiting for other players to finish the game!

Use deduction, lie, bluff and simply have a good time with your friends. Will you be able to catch the Raven?

name: Rayman: The Board Game
publisher: FLYOS; Ubisoft Entertainment S.A. (Ubisoft); Red Square Games
description: Discover Rayman like never before in an all-new board game adventure! Team up with your favorite heroes in an epic race, dodging dangers and saving the Teensies!

name: Bango
publisher: Funnyfox; AllGo-Games; Gém Klub Kft.; Hachette Boardgames Benelux
description:
Push your luck to complete your sequences…but your opponents also suffer the consequences!

Bango is an easy to learn, easy to play card game for the whole family.

Your goal is to score the most points by building up to 3 sequences of cards in front of you. Fill up your hand by revealing cards one by one, but make sure you stop at the right time to prevent an explosion! Avoid penalties by ridding yourself of excess cards before you play your cards down. When the game ends, your score depends on the length of your sequences and the most frequent color in each sequence.

name: Celestia Duo
publisher: BLAM !; Elznir Games; Geronimo Games; Hachette Boardgames UK
description:
Pirates are plundering Celestia's flying cities and escaping. Embark on a perilous chase in your aircraft to catch them before it's too late! Coordinate efficiently to foil numerous ambushes... but without being able to tell each other everything. Includes 2 3D aircraft to assemble!

The Celestia universe expands in this cooperative game for 2 players with limited communication, mixing chase, risk-taking and strategy. During your journey, cleverly share cards to foil ambushes. Anticipate your partner's hand, because if one of you, on his turn, can't fight a die, the aircraft will take damage. Stop off at the right time in the flying cities to refuel and recruit passengers with useful skills... At the risk of letting the pirate leader get away!

—description from the publisher

name: Moonshine
description:
Moonshine is a dice-based engine-building game in which players play simultaneously. On each turn, each player exploits the dice results obtained by the active player for their own purposes, in order to enhance the appeal of their speakeasy. The aim of the game is to attract enough customers to reach 12 prestige points. When a player achieves this, the game ends and the player with the highest score wins.

A game consists of a succession of rounds, all of which take place in the same way: first, the active player rolls - and possibly re-rolls - all the dice to which he has access, to validate a pool of dice. Each player then disposes of the resulting icons as they see fit. These icons represent prohibited resources prized by potential customers (each player has their own potential customers). By satisfying a customer's specific needs, they enters the bar and benefits from the permanent bonus: prestige points, resource icons, access to other dice (blue and red dice), to raises, to other potential customers, etc. If ever a player doesn't want to or can't exploit the dice result, they is not stuck! They can either pick up a Moon token to place on one of their cards to unlock a temporary bonus; or replace one of their potential customers with a new one.

The game also includes an asymmetric start variant: each speakeasy has completely different abilities and temporary bonuses!

—description from the publisher

name: Présages
publisher: Spiral Éditions; 999 Games; Ghenos Games; Hachette Boardgames USA; Happy Baobab; Ravensburger AG; Swan Panasia Co., Ltd.
description:
You've found a mysterious box filled with strange cards. As you try to decipher their meaning, you soon realize that you won't be able to do it without help. Surrounded by your friends, you begin to unravel their secret: played the right way, the cards eventually disappear. But they always come back, safely tucked away in the box, for the next game.

In Présages, you team up to get rid of your cards until you have only one left in your hand.

Each of your cards interacts with the cards played by your partner, as well as those of your opponents, so you need to play them at the right moment!

The team that sheds its cards first wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Red Partisans: The War Behind Army Group Center, 1942-44
description:
Red Partisans (RP) is a two-player simulation of the brutal fighting that took place behind Army Group Center on the eastern front in 1942-44. The Partisan player, representing the Central Staff of the Partisan Movement, must destroy as many targets as possible, interdict the Axis armies’ lines of supply and control as much terrain as possible.
