Choose from 8 wildly asymmetrical characters with their own unique magical powers. Will you win by having a strong economy, purchasing powerful Gems and even Dragons? Will you rush them down with red Fire cards? Or do you lean more into the long-term Ice magics, overwhelming the opponent's deck and causing them to slide helplessly into the depths of the Spellstorm. You'll constantly have to adapt your strategy after each battle.

Players draft a new card between each battle, slightly shifting their strategy. During a battle, players simultaneously play Spell cards, blasting each other and dealing damage.

Spellstorm is a game that's easy to learn but takes years to master all of its systems.

-description from publisher

name: Spetzi
description:
Spetzi is a two-player domino trick-taking game inspired by Texas 42 and Schnapsen.
The game blends aspects from both games to create a brand new experience.

Each hand is a race to reach 25 points.
The first player to reach 25 points gets 1 mark.
If a player thinks they can win with just the tiles left in hand, they can close the boneyard to try and win another mark.

If a player has already reached 25 points, but they think they can push it further, they can call Another! and try to reach reach 35 points.
Succeeding this, also awards another mark.

—description from the designer

name: Spire of Dioronna
description:
Spire of Dioronna is an amazing modular-designed light strategy game where players get to move around the map and make their way to the exit. Meanwhile, players need to tactfully utilize the map, use map functions to obtain resources and weaken your opponents, ultimately obtain the props they need to win the game!

In this thrilling game, you can collect props and escape with one mind. Alternatively, You can go empty-handed and use the room feature to repeatedly send your opponents back to the starting point. Communication and negotiation are very important in this game.

This game is suitable for 2 - 4 players and lasts about 20 to 40 minutes.  Players must place map cards, move around the map, complete quests, and compete with other players for resources.

—description from the publisher

name: Spire's End: Rangitaki
description:
Spire’s End: Rangitaki is the next installment in the Spire's End series. Not unlike Hildegard, this game unveils the untold story of Rangitaki, another pivotal party member from Spire's End. Rangitaki is a solo choose-your-path card game that can be enjoyed with or without prior experience with the Spire's End games. It consists of three chapters, each composed of 100 Tarot-sized cards (300 total). There's minimal setup and no need for extensive statistics or bookkeeping. To play, you just begin at the top of the card deck and let the journey unfold!
​
Rangitaki is set in a swashbuckling fantasy world. It’s charming, beautiful, violent, and unquestionably unique. You won’t find another game like this anywhere.

—description from the publisher

name: Spirit Path
description:
Ghosts tour the graveyard (Rondel), 
carrying spirits with them (Pick-up and Deliver).

Game objective
Ghosts (players) collect bones, which are worth points, for return to their former selves.
The player with the most bones wins the game.
Can you collect the bones and return to your former selves?

A medium to heavyweight game with a Japanese horror theme that is highly re-playable!

name: Spirits of Christmas
Galactic Cruise
publisher: Kinson Key Games; CrowD Games; Dranda Games; HIT Games; Maldito Games; PD-Verlag; Pendragon Game Studio; Portal Games; Super Meeple
description:
Hello, and welcome to Galactic Cruise. Here, we offer our guests something special: the comfort of a luxury cruise with the innovation of space travel. As the first company to offer extended-stay space vacations, we are excited to have you working for us! As a supervisor of this company, you’ll be expected to not only build these ships and satisfy our guests, but also to help the company thrive by enhancing our company network, inventing new technologies, and growing our workforce.  We are a united company, and you’ll often find that what another supervisor does will make your job easier. Let me be clear, though, this is a competition. Our current CEO will be stepping down in three years, and the supervisor who comes out on top will take his place.

On your turn, you will either place a worker to take two actions in the ever-expanding network, launch a ship and send one of your workers to space as a pilot, or recall all your earthbound workers to collect funding bonuses. Actions include acquiring blueprints, constructing ships, attracting guests, and building developments–connections between locations that increase action selection throughout the game. You will also be affecting resource markets that ebb and flow with the actions of all the players.

Throughout the game, you will also be competing with your fellow supervisors to complete company goals, which will earn you progress cubes throughout the game. Progress cubes are also placed when you launch ships, and when a certain number of cubes are placed onto the company’s progress track, the game ends, and the player with the most Victory Points becomes the new CEO of Galactic Cruise.

Do you still think you have what it takes to work for us? You do? Great. Let’s get started.

—description from the publisher

name: Necromancer
description:
You are a sorcerer commanding dark legions. Fools try to thwart you at every turn! Those do-gooders, rivals, and busybodies interfere with your wicked plans, but someday they’ll see, oh yes . . .

Necromancer is a fast-paced card game of raising legions of undead. Overwhelm your enemies with an unstoppable army or sacrifice a circle of underlings to seize the Well of Eternal Life and declare victory.

Your only obstacle? The pitiable cretins who think themselves your equal! Other necromancers!

—description from the publisher

name: Split the Hoard
description:
The dragon is dead and with your companions you stand in the hoard looking at unimaginable wealth. Knowing that you can’t possibly carry it all, and still battered from the epic fight with the dragon, you've agreed you’ll leave as soon as you hear the approach of enemies. With gold and silver all around you each of you sifts through the hoard for items of special value before returning to the group to divide and claim what you’ve collected. As each of you will undoubtedly leave with more wealth than you can spend in several lifetimes, you’re competing to collect the most impressive loot from this seemingly endless hoard.

Split the Hoard is strategic card game for 2 - 5 players and takes about twenty minutes to play.

In the game you take on the role of an adventurer who has achieved the pinnacle of any character’s career, the slaying of an ancient dragon. You and the other players are attempting to claim the best rewards from the hoard. You score points for treasures specific to your adventurers need and secret agendas. Negotiate, steal or bluff to ensure you get the loot you desire! The game ends when all the treasure has been split and the players with the highest score wins.

name: Splitrick
description:
In Splitrick, you're surrounded by adorable but mischievous cats. Each one looks sweet, but hide a mean streak: some will give you points, others will scratch you with penalties. To survive, you'll have to split your hand and tread carefully: play too eagerly and you'll fall into their trap. Play too cautiously and you'll miss your chance. Only those who can sniff out the tricks and stay one paw ahead will come out unscathed.

Splitrick is a must-follow trick-taking game without trumps. At the start of each round, players choose to split their hand into two parts or play normally, gaining bonus points for no-split choices. As tricks unfold, specific cards or outcomes may trigger significant point losses from randomly drawn minus cards. The game ends after three rounds.

name: Beaver House
description:
Beaver House is a fast-paced and strategic family board game where players assume the roles of beaver builders competing to construct the perfect house for a particularly picky customer. Designed by Eddie Lee and published by Korea Boardgames Co., Ltd., this game combines quick thinking, precise placement, and a touch of luck.

With its charming artwork by Makoto Takami and dynamic gameplay, it invites players to balance speed with strategy as they arrange material tiles on their construction boards. Whether you’re racing to complete your board or planning your next move in apprentice mode, Beaver House offers an engaging experience for 2-4 players ages 8 and up, with games lasting around 20 minutes.

At the start of each round, an order card is revealed. This card specifies the placement rules for that round. Players then race to arrange their material tiles on their board to meet the conditions outlined on the order card (e.g., certain tiles cannot touch, or specific tiles must be placed in designated slots). The first player to complete their board grabs the hourglass and flips it, giving the other players a limited amount of time to finish. Once the time runs out, players check their boards in the order of completion. Only players who have correctly met the conditions win the order card. The first player to collect 4 order cards (or 3 in apprentice mode) wins and becomes the ultimate beaver builder!

—description from the publisher

name: Sports Dice: Basketball
description:
Roll into the action with Sports Dice: Basketball includes all the drama of a real game. Throw your ball at the net and try to dunk to score. Try to stop the opposing team by  stealing the ball in the defensive zone. Win the jump ball at center court and push your team to the offensive zone. The closer you are to the net, the better. Throw the ball on the net and beat the opponent dice number to score! Both teams simultaneously roll all their dice. The symbol that appears the most on each team’s set of dice becomes their play. The team that rolled the most dice with the same symbol wins the roll. Apply the outcome of the winning play by moving the puck accordingly. See the Dice chart for a description of each symbol. The game ends when a team has scored 21 points. '

—description from the publisher

name: Bingsu
description:
Bingsu is a light and hilarious card game where players race to build a perfect Korean shaved ice dessert, but with one twist: you can’t play your own cards!

To win, you must complete your dessert step by step—bowl, shaved ice, toppings, and ice cream—then finish it off with the spoon. The first player to complete their bingsu claims victory.

On your turn, you draw a card from another player’s hand (or from the deck) and immediately play it. If it’s an Ingredient card, you add the matching ingredient to your bowl, but only if it follows the correct order (bowl → shaved ice → toppings → ice cream → spoon). If it doesn’t fit, nothing happens. If it’s an Action card, you carry out its effect right away, perhaps messing with another player’s dessert, swapping cards, or causing an unexpected twist. After playing the card, you add it to your hand.

With its simple rules, quick turns, and table-wide interaction, Bingsu is a chaotic, laugh-out-loud filler game for 3–8 players that captures the joy of sharing desserts with friends.

—description from the publisher

name: Spot it!: GIANT
description:
Spot the match first! With 4 mini-games designed specifically for this Giant version, play Spot it! like you’ve never played it before!? Challenge your family and friends to play everywhere, who has the best reactivity and speed

—description from the publisher

name: SPQR: The Battle of Alesia 52 BC
description:
In SPQR Battle of Alesia 52 BC, you recreate the historical final battle of Alesia in 52 BC, during Caesar’s Conquest of Gaul.

In the heart of Gaul, 52 BC, a battle unfolded that would reshape history. Julius Caesar had been carving a bloody path through the Gaul lands. Vercingetorix, the famed Celtic warrior-king, confident, rallied the scattered tribes of Gaul into a desperate stand on a fortified hilltop in Alesia. From within the encircled settlement, he watched as a vast Gaul relief army of some 250,000 men gathered to finally crush the brutally outnumbered Romans, a storm cloud promising a final, glorious clash.

Unknowingly, Vercingetorix had cornered Caesar into taking one of three potential actions; assault an entrenched enemy in the Alesia oppidum, lay a long-protracted siege with the specter of a large army of Gaul tribes that could arrive at any time from his rear, or retreat. He placed Caesar in an untenable position.

Julius Caesar then did something extraordinary, defying the convention and military doctrine of the time, even by today's standards; Caesar elected a fourth option. He ordered his army to construct two massive walls and fortifications; one facing and encircling the Alesia oppidum, and the other the outside. He encircled himself and his legions within the two walls, thus deliberately placing himself in a position to be attacked on two fronts. However, the walls were not hastily built parapets, it was an intricate system of fortifications, towers, pits, and earthworks designed to place the attackers at a great disadvantage. This is where Julius Caesar’s military genius and unflinching commitment to the conquest of Gaul would be tested in the crucible of combat. A defeat at Alesia meant the end of Roman incursions into Gaul and the most brutal defeat in the history of the Roman Army. The stakes could not be higher for Caesar, Rome, and his legionnaires.

The day of reckoning arrived. The massive Gaul relief army surged against the Roman circumvallation lines. Inside Alesia, Vercingetorix’s warriors, driven by both hope and desperation, slammed against the Roman contravallation wall. It was a battle on two fronts, a desperate gamble for freedom for the Gauls.

Will you lead the Roman Legions to glorious victory, or be annihilated in the muddy fields of Alesia far from the light of Rome?

Available Now: https://www.bluepantherllc.com/products/spqr-the-battle-of-alesia

Promo Video: https://youtu.be/lIW3SApoaY8?si=8cP33F3VChSd0J3e

Solitaire Game (Roman)
Chit Pull 
Card-Driven ROBATA and Events
Simple differential D6 combat mechanic
Easy to Set Up and Play. 30 Min. playing time
Five-page rulebook plus additional color examples of play, detailed how to play, and historical background.

—description from the designer

name: Blooming Sea
description:
Blooming Sea is a colourful tile-laying game by Reiner Knizia, where players take on the role of environmentalists working to restore vibrant coral reefs.

On their turn, players place tiles containing clusters of corals, aiming to build or expand reefs of matching colours. They score points by creating larger reefs and by surrounding fish tokens with corals of their colour.

—description from the publisher

name: Spring Prelude: Second Kharkov, May 1942
description:
This stand alone game covers the Second Battle of Kharkov, 12-27 May 1942 and is a descendant of Nathan Kilgore's Variable Combat Series (VCS) Salerno: The 1943 Allied Invasion of Italy from MMP.

With this system most of the units (usually representing the larger formations) have a variable unit strength.  A strength chit is drawn during combat to determine the exact combat value of the unit; the strength chit once pulled is hidden under the unit to increase the "fog of war".  The Second Battle of Kharkov is the perfect gaming situation to entice players into the world of strength chits.

Spring Prelude is a simulation of the failed Soviet offensive to recapture that city, and the subsequent German counterattack, during the spring of 1942, which produced the last great pocket of Soviet prisoners.  Players conduct operations as either Soviet Direction Commander Semyon Timoshenko, or as the German commander of Army Group South, Fedor von Bock.

The game is based primarily on "Kharkov 1942: Anatomy of a Military Disaster" by David Glantz, with some order of battle enhancement by George Nafziger, and maps based on post-war USGS surveys (which were themselves taken from wartime Soviet surveys).

It's a battle not often covered by other titles, and features actions where both sides were attacker and defender.

The game scale is 3 miles per hex and one day per turn.  Units are primarily German regiments and Soviet divisions.  Components include two 22" x 34" maps (total area 44"x34"), and 700 1/2" counters, including over 350 units.

Scenarios include:

1. Northern Pincer: This historical scenario uses a portion of one map as an introduction to the full campaign. It provides players a look at one thrust of a two-part plan designed to capture Kharkov. The goal of this scenario is to study the true threat to German intentions posed by the Soviet forces east of the city. Lasts 6 turns (12-17 May), one map.

2. Izyum Salient: This is the full historical campaign, covering both offensives, as the battle flows back and forth across the steppe. You can use all the bells and whistles for this one. Lasts 16 turns (12-27 May), both maps.

3. Aggressive Timoshenko: This is a hypothetical situation that assumes the Soviets are ready to attack on the original planned kick-off date. The scenario plays the same as the historical campaign, but is shifted to 8 days earlier. The initial setup is slightly modified and some German reinforcements take longer to arrive. Lasts 20 turns (4-23 May), both maps.

4. Passive Timoshenko: This is another hypothetical situation that places the Soviets on a stronger footing. The scenario postulates that Timoshenko did not propose his attack plans to Stalin who himself was more occupied with other sections of the front. In this case, FRIDERICUS is launched as planned by the Germans against a dug-in and defensive-minded Soviet force. Will there still be a pocket? Lasts 10 turns (18-27 May), one map.

New rules include:

• The effect of rain, mud, and swollen rivers on the early stages of the battle.
• Stacking of Soviet units is different than that of Axis units.
• The addition of headquarters is used to portray the Soviet command structure in a more accurate way.
• Air missions are expanded to cover interdiction sorties.
• Soviet doctrine restrictions reflect the rigidity of the Soviet command structure in the early years of the war.

The game designer, Greg Blanchett, has a folder on Consimworld (http://talk.consimworld.com/WebX/.1dd4d844/831).

name: Springsign
publisher: The End Games; Trap Mountain Studio
description:
In Springsign, you and your friends are influential town councilors in a growing frontier settlement. Right now, Springsign is a "quaint" little town (some might even say "dead-end" or "completely-untamable"), but under the right leadership its potential is limitless! Together, you will need to grow the town by constructing new buildings, keeping settlers fed, fending off bandits, and in many other ways keeping the town humming along. But there's a catch: this is not a cooperative game! The townsfolk will vote for a new mayor soon, and helping your political opponents won't get you elected. As the players develop town, they'll also have to outmaneuver and outwit one another to garner more support for their own campaign.

Springsign is a light/medium-weight, town-building, resource-management game. Over the course of a 90-minute playthrough, you will influence and make use of the town's interactive economy, develop powerful card engines, and find ways of snagging invaluable votes from your opponents. The game's innovative "Popularity & Votes" point system, where the players must time when to make best use of their popularity to win a vote, ensures that the game remains tight up till the end. The balance of powerful actions and limited resources make each turn tense and memorable, while the deeply-asymmetric player boards give each player a completely different playstyle and way of interacting with the game.

The goal of Springsign is to win The Election at the end of the game by having the most votes. To get votes, you'll need popularity, which is collected through a variety of actions and abilities.

When the chips are down, will you do what's right for Springsign, or will you push your way into office through anything (and anyone) who stands in your way? Those greedy enough to steal victory from their opponents will be able to win, and some players may be willing to risk the town itself in their race to the top!

—description from the publisher

name: Burger Master
description:
Test your mettle in this competition to be the greatest burger chef of them all! Compete with other players in this fast-paced puzzle game to see who can complete the ever-more complicated orders to perfection in the shortest steps possible. Think you can do better than other players? Step up to the grill and prove it!

Complete the burger orders in the fewest steps possible to earn fries. Claim your title as the greatest burger chef by winning 5 fries!
. 40 unique challenges, hundreds of solutions.
. No down time.
. Play with up to six players. Solo mode included.

—description from the publisher

name: Spółka ZOO
description: We are enterprising animals who trade apples, lemons and pineapples, but above all, buy shares in guilds. Every three turns, what they produce is divided among the shareholders. Anyone can add cards to the mentioned guilds that influence their operation. Purchasing and selling goods/shares dynamically changes their prices. We can hire helpers for the goods we have - they not only give you points, but also unique abilities. At the end of the game, we turn every five money we have into a victory point.

name: Square One
description:
Square One is an engine-building strategy game, similar to its predecessor Project L. Its easy-to-learn yet hard-to-master mechanics offer high replayability for the whole family.

In Square One is players match tiles with patterns to pattern cards on the board.  Build more patterns and make more combos to earn points.  The person who completes all their patterns first, wins the game.

 

—description from the publisher

name: Coffee Rush: Grab & Go
description:
Coffee Rush: Grab & Go is a speedy, travel-friendly spin on the hit game Coffee Rush, keeping the same order-fulfilling tension but stripping it down for fast, portable play. Players race in real time to grab ingredient cards from a shared stock, complete drink orders before rivals, and keep customers happy.

At the start, each player has two open orders to fulfill. On the count of three, everyone plays simultaneously—flipping ingredient cards one at a time with one hand, grabbing what they need, and slotting them under the right orders. Takeout orders add a twist: their ingredients are placed face down, forcing players to remember what they’ve collected.

The first player to complete five orders ends the round, and revenue is tallied. Flawless drinks earn full value, while mistakes and missing items cut into your profits. In takeout orders, correct ingredients are worth even more. The player with the highest revenue wins.

With quick setup, simple rules, and variants for solo play, longer games, and expert memory challenges, Coffee Rush: Grab & Go serves the same caffeinated competition as the original, now in a fast, on-the-go format for 1–6 players.

—description from the publisher

name: Squirrels Gone WIld
description:
In Squirrels Gone Wild, You'll be tasked with helping Chester the squirrel scour through an adorable, silly and devious scrapbook that belongs to his (possibly, slightly unhinged) ex-squirrelfriend, Lucy. This scrapbook is packed full of happy memories, sentimental artifacts, AND BETRAYAL!

Every page of the scrapbook contains one puzzle and offline hints are included on the back of each page if you'd like an extra nudge or two :)
You'll need to solve all the puzzles to find Chester's stolen nuts and save the day. Make it to the end for a prize and an important choice!

name: Dogfight: 1917
description:
Join in the fierce battle for the skies above the Western Front!

The aerial battlefield of WWI will stretch your tactical acumen to its limits, where a split-second decision can mean the difference between life and death. Fight for survival and glory, and go down in history as one of the greatest pilots of the war!

Dogfight: 1917 is a one-on-one game. The game itself is deceptively simple, but victory demands precise positioning and bold maneuvering. On your turn, you’ll perform limited movement by playing one maneuver flight card, carefully selecting your path to gain a tactical advantage. Basic attacks have no cost to use, but can only be performed when you are facing the enemy's backside. This creates the tense and authentic dogfight experience of World War I. Outmaneuver the enemy with your fighter’s unique abilities, and use your pilot’s skills to deliver a decisive blow. With variant rules, up to 4 players can experience the aerial battles of WWI.

—description from the publisher

name: Stable Times
description:
As a skilled horse trainer, it's your job to guide a herd of show horses back to the stable, arranging each one just right to keep them content. Each horse has its own personality; some are shy, some are social, and some just want their favorite stall. Use smart planning and a bit of intuition to corral the perfect layout. With strategic Grouping, Placing, and Scoring, the stable is where champions are made!

Horse cards are taken from the pasture. Once per turn the player may draw a face up horse from the pasture, or a random one from the deck. Then the player will place up to two horses from their hand into their stable. Each stable has 4 aisles, and each aisle can only house the same type of horse. Each horse has unique scoring; some like to be next to certain types of horses, whereas some just like to be in their preferred aisle. Once a player has filled up at least 3 aisles of their stable, the game ends and players count up points as listed on each horse card, on their unique stable, as well as per set of disciplines. The player with the most points wins!

—description from the publisher

name: STACCS
description:
STACCS is a mind-bending card game of matching and stacking. The 60-card hexagonal deck features classic suits and numbers, plus wilds and zeroes. The cards are designed to look like cubes, creating a trippy optical illusion. Players take turns matching cards to build one shared, three-dimensional STACC. First one out of cards wins!

There are 3 cardinal rules that govern STACCS and all its Play Modes:
- Matching suits STACC on the TOP surface of a card.
- Matching numbers STACC on the SIDE of a card.
- Matching face cards STACC on the FACE of a card.

Special cards (O, J, Q, K, A) add a little chaos with blocks, attacks, counters, and extra turns — but Wilds are the real game-changers: they let you call your suit and steer the STACC in a brand new direction. When you’re down to one card, make sure to let other players know by saying “UH OH!”

There are also extra game modes including:

     SOLOSTACCS - the solitaire mode for 1 player
     WILD OUT - a collaborative four-STACC game
     UH OH! PARTY - increase the total players to 10 by combining 2 DECCS


—description from the designer

name: Stack City
description:
Stack City is a competitive, 3D city-building Engine Building, Resource management style board game where you represent one of four unique enterprises.

Each enterprise focuses on different strategies - building, earning money, earning permits, or acquiring action cards. Players compete to stack and expand their buildings, carefully managing limited space and resources. Every move counts as you advance on the board, earn rewards, and accumulate Economy Points.

The game ends when a player reaches 32 build spaces or all buildings that can be placed have been.  The player with the most Economy points wins.

—description from the designer

name: Stack O' Cats
description:
Stack O' Cats is a balancing game, with a little press-your luck element thrown in. Gather up to six friends for the most fun you’ll ever have trying to get a cat to do what you want them to! Take turns stacking wooden cats of all sorts one on top of another, but beware - these cat’s won’t stay still for long! Be the best at keeping the cats under control, and you’ll come out the victor!

Players take turns drawing a cat meeple from the big Bag o’ Cats, and balancing it anywhere on top of the cat stack, then gaining points for that cat’s placement. The game has multiple point variants to encourage different stacking styles! You can play for most points or least to be crowned victor, you decide which way to play. Thirty two unique shaped cat meeples and forty meeples total ensure that every game will be different!  Our sturdy base also ensures that you have a firm foundation to work from to build fun and crazy cat stacks.  Solo and coop modes are also available.

-description from designer

name: Staked!
description:
In the depths of Victorian Europe, circa 1898, a chilling presence looms — vampires are on the prowl! You and up to 9 friends play as members of a legendary vampire hunter's guild, forming the last line of defense against the encroaching undead menace. But as the night creeps on, can you determine which of your fellow guild members can be trusted, and which are actually vampires themselves? Investigate and assassinate as you stake your way to the top in this fast-paced evening of betrayal and deception. Last team at the table wins!

Staked! is a social deduction game for 6-10 players, with most players acting as vampire hunters, while a few others are acting as secret vampires. The hunters have superior numbers, but no information. The vampires are fewer, but know each other, and can coordinate attacks.

Each game consists of multiple rounds, with each round consisting of two phases: the Mingling Phase, followed by the Dining Phase. In the Mingling Phase, players discuss suspicions and cast votes for other players, using a series of voting tiles, which keep their vote obscured. Once the votes have all been cast, play moves to the Dining Phase, where votes are revealed. Depending on the votes, 1 player is eliminated, becoming a Ghost, and 1 player is elected Alpha Hunter, granting them special abilities in the next round.

Staked! was designed specifically in an attempt to improve upon traditional social deduction game shortcomings. Eliminated players have much more agency through Ghost actions. There is no narrator required, so everyone plays. Rounds keep moving, and maintain tension, through the use of timed discussion phases. And players can choose between the simpler base game, or a more advanced and engaging play mode, featuring character abilities.

—description from the designer

name: Stalin's Lost Chance
description:
Stalin's Lost Chance: The Soviet Attack on Finland, through Karelia-Ladoga, 1939-1940 depicts the Winter War from 30th November 1939 to 13th March 1940. This is the 9th game in Three Crowns Games WWII Battle Series.

The Finnish defence plan was made on the belief that the Soviet army would target its primary offensive on the Karelian isthmus. An offensive was also expected on the north-western and northern side of Lake Ladoga, where the road network was relatively good. This is the area upon which Stalin’s Lost Chance focuses. Two divisions of the Finnish IV Army Corps were located there. North of Ilomantsi, the entire long eastern frontier was manned only with detached battalions and border companies, when the war broke.

The Soviet Union’s 8th Army, comprising six divisions and a tank brigade, had grouped a division or two on every road up north leading from east to west. Its mission was to execute a flanking manoeuvre around the northern shore of Lake Ladoga to strike at the rear of the Mannerheim Line.

—description from the publisher

The map scale is about 3.7 miles per hex, or about 5.5 kilometres per hex.  Turns represent one week.
Units are Companies and Battalions for the Finns; Battalions and Regiments for the Soviets. Plus the odd armoured train and more ad-hoc Groups.

—Source: Paul Shackleton, 29 May 2025 [on a BGG thread for Stalin's Lost Chance].

name: Stamps
description: Fit the stamps cleverly into the grid and secure the most points. Stamps is easy to learn and instantly transports you to summer vacation with its beautiful designs. Boring trips are a thing of the past! Whether at the beach, on a plane, or on your own terrace, this compact yet captivating card game for the whole family brings a vacation vibe to every game table!

name: Stan Lee's Genesis
description:
In Stan Lee's Genesis, players must harness their creative energy to give birth to a unique universe. Genesis is intended to put the power of creation into the hands of the players and honor the legacy of Stan’s brilliance as one of the preeminent creative forces of the 20th century. Every game is different as players both compete and collaborate as they construct a comic book universe full of heroes, villains, super team, evil syndicates, galactic threats, and all-encompassing cross over events!

—description from the publisher

name: Star Chart
description:
Star Chart is a deep puzzle game; pass cards around the table, forming your star chart to match as many constellations as possible. Get 15 points first to win!

The game also comes with a booklet of puzzles to solve yourself or with friends :)

Star Chart is a drafting game, each turn all players pick a card from their hand to add to their chart, and one card to pass on to the player to their right. Then, each player checks if they have matched a constellation in the sky or in their hand, and if they have, they can take one and score points.

Then, players may use one of their three once-per-game abilities which allow them to modify their chart and match once more. Finally, players pick up the card passed to them and draw up to 5 cards.

This is then repeated until a player reaches 15 points or the deck runs out.

—description from the publisher

name: Star Smugglers
description:
Star Smugglers is a lightweight roll-and-write sci-fi adventure where you captain a ship, trade across dangerous systems, and slip contraband past patrols. Explore new planets, upgrade your vessel, and outwit raiders while chasing fortune among the stars. Every run is a gamble of risk and reward.

Load your cargo hold and set a course for distant destinations. Along the way you might rob neutral caravans for quick loot, strike profitable deals with fellow smugglers, or clash with Patrols, Nomads, and Raiders. A streamlined combat system brings tension and excitement to every encounter, making each journey feel like a daring heist in the void.

—description from the designer

name: Star Trek: Adventures in the Final Frontier
description:
This is partly a card game and partly a paragraph game-book.

It is a thematic adventure game for a solo player. You play as one of the famous ‘Affiliations’ in the Star Trek universe, such as the noble Federation, the war-like Klingons or the treacherous Romulans.

To win the game you must gain 100 points and 5 Objective Tokens, mainly by completing Missions before your ‘Tour’ of 50 Turns elapses and the game ends. While exploring space and completing Missions, you may encounter problems, including hostile Ships or Away Teams that will hinder your progress. There are plenty of Missions to choose, and situations to encounter, so each game will be a new, fresh experience.

Star Trek: Adventures in the Final Frontier (STAFF) has three booklets: Rules, Missions and Encounters. There is also an LCARS Encounter Log Sheet, a Mission Log mat and a Captain’s Log mats for players. These play alongside a Draw deck of cards from the Star Trek CCG (Personnel, Equipment etc) and automate the game without an opponent. You also need two six-sided dice (2D6) and tokens to keep track of current totals such as Challenges, Points, and Turns in the game.

All the Booklets plus all cards and support materials are available from the designer's coffee website: https://buymeacoffee.com/dragoncymru

name: Star Trek: Captain's Chair
description:
In Star Trek: Captain's Chair, you will go head-to-head with an opponent, each stepping into the shoes of an iconic captain from across Star Trek's galaxy and history. Command ships, crew, and away teams while you manage resources and alliances!

Each of the six captains comes with a unique, asymmetric deck of cards themed to that captain's personality strategies, allies, and assets. Each deck creates different strategic directions based on which common cards are available and what strategy your opponent deploys. The captains to choose from are:


     Jean-Luc Picard
     Benjamin Sisko
     Michael Burnham
     Koloth, The Dahar Master
     Sela
     Thy'lek Shran


True to Star Trek, antagonism will not win every game. You will need to pursue diplomacy, exploration, and science, with different captains excelling at different paths. With hundreds of unique, deeply thematic cards, you'll want to explore the galaxy again and again! The chair is yours, Captain!

—description from the publisher

name: Grandma's Recipe
description:
Grandma’s Recipe is a lighthearted set-collection and recipe-building game by Carlo A. Rossi, where players compete to create the most delicious dishes using Grandma’s secret know-how.

Each turn, gather fresh ingredients from the market or cutting boards—stock up on staples like tomatoes, carrots, meat, fish, and pasta, or pick up rare special ingredients. Create new recipes using basic ingredients to claim recipe books, or improve someone else’s dish by adding your own special twist and stealing their book!

The game ends when the whistle card appears, and the player with the most points from recipe books wins. With its quick turns and playful “recipe theft” mechanic, Grandma’s Recipe serves up a perfect mix of friendly rivalry and family-table fun.

—description from the publisher

name: Hot Streak
publisher: CMYK; Choo Choo Games; Korea Boardgames; Strohmann Games
description:
Hot Streak is a game for hard luck gamblers who love to bet on and scream at the racers, who in this case happen to be mascots who may (or may not) keep running in the right direction.

At the start of the game, set up the racing deck with one card for each mascot and a number of random cards based on the player count. Reveal these cards to all players, after which players draft a betting ticket from those on display, then in reverse order draft a second bet. For each bet, you can play it safe — or flip it to the risky side, which might pay out more - or cost you money if you lose. After betting, each player chooses one of three cards in their hand to secretly add to the racing deck.

Shuffle the deck, burn three cards, then reveal cards one by one from the deck, moving the mascots along the track, with them sometimes swerving into another lane and knocking over another racer, sometimes turning around, sometimes all moving at once, and sometimes just going backwards! If a racer runs off the track or would be knocked over while already fallen, they're disqualified. If needed, shuffle all cards in the deck, burn three cards again, and keep racing until all four spots on the box podium are filled. Pay out bets based on these results.

For races #2-3, first deal each player a random card from the deck, then place bets again, then have each player contribute a card from their hand to the deck. After race #3, everyone tallies their money.

name: Star Trek: Tribble Match!
description:
Star Trek: Tribble Match can be played like a regular memory game, with players flipping over two tiles at a time in search of a match, which allows them to claim the tiles. Whoever collects the most tiles wins.

Alternatively, you can play with tribble rules, with players trying to collect the fewest tribbles from the tiles that they pick up.

name: Orbita
description:
Orbita is a tactical two-player card game of planetary influence and precise timing. Players are rival astronomers, tracking the movement of four planets whose power shifts as their positions change in orbit.

Each round, players play 1–3 cards of a single planet type to move its marker along the orbital track. The planet in the higher position wins the round, and the player who moved that planet claims all the cards played. Because the order of cards in your hand can never be changed, every turn demands careful hand management and precise timing.

Here’s the twist: victory comes from winning by just the right margin. When one player can no longer play, the players compare their collections for each planet. For each planet, the player with fewer cards must surrender them to their rival for points. Winning by too much can backfire, so success depends on balancing short-term wins with long-term control across all planets.

—description from the publisher

name: Star Wars: Battle of Hoth
publisher: Days of Wonder; Geekach LLC; MIPL
description:
Star Wars: Battle of Hoth is a game of heroic and fast-paced battles of miniatures that's set on the ice planet Hoth and reenacts one of the most famous scenes of Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back.

Using the popular Command and Colors system, players take turns choosing command cards each turn to activate units and decide how to move and attack, across seventeen scenarios included in the box.

For a deeper gaming experience, players have the option to add leader cards to their battle for support from six iconic Star Wars characters, or they try the two multi-scenario campaigns in which successes and failures shape the next battles.

name: Star Wars: Super Teams
description:
Star Wars: Super Teams is a racing game full of fun and strategy for the whole family. You'll compete with your team on a track full of obstacles and bonuses.

By strategically using your movement cards, you'll have to try to get your starships to the finish line first and slow down your opponents by sending them into asteroid fields and maw spaces.

Can you lead your team of the X-Wing and Millennium Falcon, the Star Destroyer and Death Star, the Tie Fighter and Advanced Tie Fighter, or the Jedi Starfighter and Tantive IV to victory?

name: Star Wars: Unlimited – Intro Battle: Hoth
description:
Launch into a game of unlimited possibilities with Intro Battle: Hoth! This carefully curated, self-contained gaming experience is the perfect introduction to Star Wars: Unlimited, especially for players who may be less familiar with trading card games. Players choose to either take command of Darth Vader's invading Imperial Army or lead Leia Organa's entrenched Rebel forces in defense of Echo Base. Detailed rules and a handy game board help newcomers jump into the fray as quickly as possible, all while recreating one of the most iconic battles of the Star Wars saga.

—description from the publisher

name: Starfront Scouting Academy
description:
The final exams have brought you and your fellow planetary scouting cadets to an uninhabited planet with a toxic atmosphere that you’ve been tasked with analyzing remotely. You’ll unlock new skills throughout the game as you build your proficiency with the available reconnaissance equipment - rovers, drones, hovercraft, and buggies. If you are having issues with the equipment, you can also utilize the state of the art SCOUT canine companion droids in a pinch! Claim the most strategic sections of the map and score points for charting the alien terrain to become top of your class!

Use the unique number generator system to select which spots to claim on the map as you explore Kharsibecc. But watch out for what your fellow students are up to because the planet surface is limited and you're each vying for similar objectives.

name: Starleap
description:
Starleap is an intergalactic race between space-faring animals in a prestigious affair hosted by King Wa from planet Amphibia.
 Each player is in charge of a team of 3 frogs who are racing back home. The objective of the game is to have the most points. Points are gained by collecting bugs along the way and by finishing before the other players.

Each player has an identical hand of movement cards, 1 interrupt card, and 1 special card unique to them. On your turn, you play a card and resolve its movement, leap frogging over occupied spaces. Each space you land on triggers some effect: rockets let you move further, portals teleport you, stars allow you to draw powerful boost cards, asteroids earn you bugs, and planets give you one of 5 permanent upgrades. Timing is crucial in the game, so each player's single interrupt card allows them to make a movement on their off-turn to capitalize on the positioning of other player's frogs.

When you play a card, you keep it in front of you and don't have access to it again until you pick all your cards back up by ending your turn with no cards in hand. The game ends when one player has made it home with all 3 frogs. The frogs earn points based on their relative positions, with the frogs in last losing points. The player with the most points wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Starligned
description:
Use your telescope to search the night sky for the most beautiful constellations. It can be difficult to get everything in the picture and the other astronomers will make it as difficult as possible for you.

Get the most points by capturing the most beautiful starry sky. You do this by playing a row of ten star cards, using their effects cleverly and passing cards tactically. There are five constellations that you can find. Each card is divided into two halves, the highest value half has a ful version of the constellation and the lowest value half has an incomplete version of the constellation. Each star card has an effect which can be used to sabotage other players’ telescopes or increase your own telescopes value.

The game is played in two stages of five rounds. Each round consists of the following four phases:

     Each player plays a card face down from their hand in front of them.
     All players reveal the card in front of them. If there is a card with the stop effect in play, you skip the next phase. 
     In turn order, the players check for moon bonusses and play the effect shown on their played card.
     Each player chooses one card in their hand to rotate and passes their hand to the player to their left.


When players have a total of ten star cards played in front of them, the game ends and the final scoring begins. The players add up the points shown on the top half of the card in front of them and apply any end game effects that are visible. The player with the most points, wins the game!

—description from the publisher

name: STASH Card Game
description:
There is a town, unguarded, and you are intent on raiding it and leaving with a massive bounty of loot!
But be careful, there are others who share a similar interest… Play your cards right and take home the biggest stash!​

STASH is quick, simple, and easy to learn.
Designed to be endlessly re-playable by both casual partygoers and dedicated strategists, STASH will have you hooked. It has the simplicity of UNO, the anticipation of Poker, and the interaction of Unstable Unicorns.

Released by the independent Australian game developer in 2025, STASH received overwhelmingly positive feedback from play-testers, and delivers on its promise to strike the balance between a casual family favourite and a medium for competitive play.

Gameplay:
Players are villains, taking turns adding to their loot pile, accumulating treasure. Until it is stashed, however, it is at the mercy of the other players.
Players start with a hidden villain - each with their own special action. On a player's turn, they either raid the town by drawing and playing a card, or they reveal their hidden character card, allowing them to stash, steal, trade, or burn each other's loot.

The game ends when no more cards can be played from player's hands, and the highest accumulated loot score determines the winner. There are a predetermined number of each card type within the deck, allowing competitive players to strategically assess the risk vs reward of their actions.

—description from designer

name: Stay Away!
description:
In Stay Away!, 4-12 players try to track down "The Thing", a creature that has the capability of possessing the human body, cloning it, then taking its place, so as you play you won't know who "The Thing" is or when someone will become "The Thing" or who is infected or not. The researchers are looking for The Thing; their goal is to work together to identify which player is The Thing and roast it with a "Flamethrower" card. You remain Human until The Thing passes an "Infected!" card to you during a card exchange, at which point you become an Infected and take on that new Role: You are now an ally of The Thing and must take care that its identity is not revealed.

What's new in this new version:

All-new graphics and illustrations in pure Escape Studios style.
Minor bug fixes.
Rules improvements.
Introduction of the "Adrenaline" mode that allows you to play more cards during your turn.

New Stay Away cards!

- Grenade!
Throw a grenade that rolls on the table, but be careful 
because after 4 turns it will explode!

- Mirror Reflection!
Avoid being roasted and roast whoever wanted to eliminate you! With this card you will eliminate the player who wanted to eliminate you with a grenade or flamethrower!

- Rage!
If you are the target of an Analysis card, avoid showing your cards and exchange a card with each of the players!

- Dynamite! (Exclusive card for Gamefound pre-order only).
Leave it in front of a teammate, but be careful because whoever is in that place after four turns will explode!

New Panic card effects including the one we are most proud of:

- Feign Death!
The first player who was
eliminated returns to the game in the
role he had before
being eliminated.
Draw 4 “Stay Away!” cards and occupy
the place where you were playing.

What else to say. This is a completely new version that we are sure will give you endless hours of fun, but the real question is another: Can you trust your Friends?

—description from the publisher

name: Staying Alive
description:
The whole city is swarming with zombies, and your group has little time to reach safety.

Each mission in Staying Alive requires equipment, supplies, items, and weapons, with additional cards providing further challenges. The game is played co-operatively and in real time – the hourglass is ticking and must be kept in check!

Each player tries to combine and discard their cards, but only the player whose turn it is can speak. What information and reactions are important? Who can you help, and what should you remember?

name: Steam Power
description:
In Steam Power, players "race" to build the best rail network to meet their contractual obligations and make the most money.

On your turn, you can perform two actions from a selection of choices, letting you lay tracks, build factories, fulfill contracts, earn money, or collect more contracts. Building a factory brings resources to the board that all players have access to...at a price.

The game ends when a certain number of contracts are fulfilled, which varies by player count. The player with the most points (and money, which converts to points) wins.

name: Steam Power: Deluxe Edition
description:
In Steam Power, players "race" to build the best rail network to meet their contractual obligations and make the most money.

On your turn, you can perform two actions from a selection of choices, letting you lay tracks, build factories, fulfill contracts, earn money, or collect more contracts. Building a factory brings resources to the board that all players have access to...at a price.

The game ends when a certain number of contracts are fulfilled, which varies by player count. The player with the most points (and money, which converts to points) wins.

Steam Power: Deluxe Edition differs from the Steam Power base game as a four-map expansion is included in the box, and the components have been upgraded.

name: Steel Wolves and German Fleet Boats: Deluxe Edition
description:
Steel Wolves is a solitaire simulation of the German submarine war against British and Allied shipping, the follow-on title to Silent War. Volume I covers the period from the start of the War in 1939 to the early months of 1943. You serve as the Supreme Commander of Uboats, Kreigsmarine. Your mission is to deploy your forces with maximum effect to destroy British and Allied shipping while limiting your submarine losses.

Featured scenarios cover actions ranging from famous short single sub patrols through short campaigns, ending with the full campaign covering 1939 to 1943. The game map breaks the Atlantic, Mediterranean, South Atlantic, and Western Indian Ocean into historical Operations Areas through which subs patrol in search of shipping. Special rules feature historical events such as the invasion of Norway and Torch; b-dienst, ULTRA, and the intelligence war; torpedo improvements, German wolfpack tactics, Super-Skippers, large vs. small U-boat philosophy, appeals to Berlin for resources, and many others. Every German sub deployed between 1939 and 1943 (as well as some what-if classes) is represented.

Steel Wolves Expansion 1: German Fleet Boats assumes that Germany never entered into the 1935 Naval agreement. German Fleet Boats assumes significant changes to the historic design strategy. It assumes that early Type I, II, and VII submarines are built as historically occurred, but prior to starting a more extensive building program, OKM decides to build cruiser/fleet type submarines starting with more Type Is and four of the even larger (projected) Type III, the designs for which were based on the IA, then followed by the VIII, XI, and XII.

German Fleet Boats alters the opening of the campaign, allowing players to play through to the end of the England Imperiled scenario, which ends at the start of Operation Barbarossa. Modifications include changes to allied task forces and the availability of additional allied units. Also included are three additional Italian Cagni class submarines.

This new edition features a mounted game board, an updated full-color rule book incorporating all changes and improvements, and an updated map and charts/tables. Steel Wolves and German Fleet Boats, Deluxe Edition, is the definitive game of the German submarine war against British and Allied shipping.

Product Information
Complexity: Medium
Playing Time: 1 hour (scenarios), 125 hours (full campaign)
Solitaire Suitability: Perfect (designed for solitaire play)

name: Stellar Horizons II: Galactic Frontier
description:
“The Next Leap Forward!”

Stellar Horizons 2: Galactic Frontier traces humanity’s journey into the galaxy over the coming centuries (2100-2900) by Andrew Rader. Players will control one of seven factions vying to establish an interstellar empire, each with unique advantages, drawbacks, and special abilities. Through competitive and cooperative scenarios and campaigns, each new star brings the discovery of new planet types, and new opportunities for settlement, trade, or conquest. Along the way, you’ll develop technologies and customize your ships, building a faster, stronger, and more capable starfaring fleet.

Will you focus on science vessels to probe the secrets of distant systems, mining ships to exploit their riches, or combat ships to claim them as your own? The choice is yours. Meanwhile, you’ll deploy genetic manipulations to enhance your species’ size, strength, survivability, and intelligence, or even guide its transformation into a different kind of species better suited to subterranean, aquatic, desert, low gravity, or gaseous worlds.

Product Information:
    Complexity: Medium
    Time Scale: 1 year/turn
    Map Scale: The Solar System
    Unit Scale: Manned and Robotic Starships
    Players: 1 to 7
    Solitaire Suitability: MEDIUM
    Playing Time: 20-90 minutes for Scenarios, 6+ hours for Campaign
    Campaign & Scenarios can be played competitively and cooperatively

—description from the publisher

name: Stitch: The Fix for 626
publisher: Z-Man Games; asmodee; CoolPlay; Delta Vision Publishing; Laguna
description:
Uh-oh... Jumba is up to his mad scientist tricks again. Stitch is back to his destructive ways, and it's up to you to help get him back to being on his best behavior.

In Stitch: The Fix for 626, each player will compete to capture Stitch and recruit help from his most beloved friends — but beware as some experiments may cause chaos!

The game is played in a series of rounds. During the game, Stitch can be either Experiment 626 or Good Stitch — never both. At all times, a single player has Stitch.

You win a round if you hold the highest-value card once the deck runs out or if all other players are knocked out of the round. Will you find the fix for 626?

—description from the publisher

name: Stokerverse
description:
Compete in a series of perilous quests in the first card game officially supported by the family of legendary author Bram Stoker.

The game is played using 4 decks of cards - North, South, East, and West. The winner is the first person to complete 7 quest cards, or 5 if you get at least 1 from each location.

There are 3 types of quests:
VANQUISH MONSTERS - Requires 2 specific object cards.  
SHATTER CURSES - Requires a set number of cards from each specified location. 
DEFEAT HUNTERS - Requires a rival to draw from specified locations during their turn.

But beware... 
The sinister Count Dracula is poised to strike when least expected! Play powerful Dracula cards to help complete your quests, or hinder the competition.

Stokerverse is quick to learn, fun and strategic to play, and features a beautiful Gothic horror art style.

—description from the designer

name: Stone Layer
description: Players build on six shared stacks with bricks of different sizes and shapes. When it is a player's turn, the player chooses a brick token and selects 1 brick. The active player tries to place the chosen brick on top of the designated stack without knocking it over. If the stack falls over, the other players who added bricks to the stack receive points. The first player to collect 10 points wins.

name: Stone Shedding Game
description:
Stone Shedding Game is a dynamic card game with a ladder-climbing mechanic where players make sets of stones for the shared garden. The goal is to get rid of all the cards on your hand and gain the most Victory Points for your stone set. Players can't shuffle their hand and must play sets of cards with consecutive or identical numbers to beat the previous one. If you can’t beat the last opponent’s combination, you can pass and exchange some of the cards on your hand.
Create the ultimate winning combination and profit from other players’ actions in this dynamic card battle!

—description from the publisher

name: Stones of Æver
description:
A handful of long-lost Paleolithic stones have been found deep inside a secret cave.

It's believed the enigmatic Æver People used them for a lunar ritual, the rules of which have recently been deciphered by an international team of researchers. Now you, too, can partake in this ancient tradition with this minimalist 18-card wallet game.

Build your 4x2 ALTAR using various Stone Cards that you collect during your tasks. Lay a stone only if one of its etched symbols can form an adjacent connection with a stone already on the grid.

Each turn, spend allotted Action Points to rearrange your stones as you see fit. Abilities may include shifting, rotating, adding, or discarding altar stones.

At the end of a turn, LOOK AROUND by checking the "Configuration Cards" to the Left & Right sides of the draw pile. If the Right card's altar description is currently true, & the Left is false, leave them alone. If they aren't, simply replace them with new cards from the draw pile. During a full moon, these "Left/Right" designation rules are reversed.

As time progresses throughout the game, Rotate the Moon Card to its successive phase above your campfire. Repeat this entire phase cycle until game's end.

TO WIN: Lay the 8th & final altar stone during a FULL MOON, with proper "Left" & "Right" descriptions in place. If you do so during any other moon phase, or when your configuration designations aren't appropriate, you lose.

—description from the designer

name: Stop Krampus! ... and save Christmas!
description:
With just six nights before Santa’s big ride, Krampus, the Christmas trickster, has cast a spell on all of Santa’s reindeer! Now they’re all dizzy and confused, and they’ll never be able to make the trip if Santa’s elves can’t do something to dispel the mischievous magic. Play as Santa’s loyal elves to find the right combination of magical cookies to cure each of the reindeer. Or play as Krampus to try and eat the magic cookies, and ruin Christmas!

In this one-versus-many print-and-play game, one player plays as Krampus (often a grown-up, older sibling, or anyone who enjoys a bit of mischief) while the remaining players cooperate as Santa’s elves, working together to try and save Christmas!  

Each elf player places one "worker" per turn onto the action spaces, moving cookies around the Christmas wreath. Line up 3 cookies to cure a reindeer. But when all 6 elves have taken their actions, Krampus zooms around the wreath eating the cookies! The elves only have 6 nights (rounds) to cure all the reindeer, or Krampus will win and Christmas will be ruined!

Note, regarding the age range for this game: Players under 8 can play an elf with some help from teammates.

—description from the publisher

name: Storeroom Inc. Trasteros S.A.
description:
Storeroom Inc. Trasteros S.A. is the best storeroom company in the world. A unique opportunity for lovers of exclusive treasures in a constantly growing market that moves billions of dollars each year.

Access the most promising storerooms before anyone else, choose the locations well and obtain the most coveted pieces to satisfy your demanding clientele. Don't forget to stop by the Coffee Machine from time to time; you can always extract interesting information. And… keep an eye on your rivals as they will try to snatch any valuables right under your nose!

Get more money than your rivals by selling the objects from the storerooms and win the award for Best Storeroom Hunter of the Year.

—description from the designer

name: Storm Raiders
description:
For thousands of years all we have known is the Rift Storm. It destroyed our empire, sundered our land and severed us from the Old World we once ruled. Sheltered within the eye of the storm we fought to survive, imprisoned in our last remaining city, desperately clinging to life. As the ages passed the eye slowly grew in size enabling exploration beyond the city and a startling discovery. The storm was still connected to the Old World, its erratic rift capturing hapless Atlantic crossings and wrecking them upon Atlantis' broken shores. The age of the Storm Raider was born: Brave souls who for fame and fortune would dare the might of the Rift Storm, to save these precious offerings and bring hope to our dying world.

The Storm Season is upon us, all eyes look to the sky and we wonder are you the Storm Raider Atlantis has been waiting for?

The aim of Storm Raiders is to be the player with the most prestige at the game's end. Storm raiding is a perilous task, filled with many dangers - the most devastating being the mighty Rift Storm that encircles the many islands. Players will want to stay close to the storm, without being overcome by its immeasurable force.
Prestige is gained by salvaging wreck sites, fulfilling contracts, acquiring crew, upgrading their vehicles, and earning medals. Players will be drafting dice each turn to either travel using their trike, plane, or sub, or to instead take some much-needed time to rest and repair their battered vehicles.

After 6 rounds of traversing the splintered landscape, players will add up their prestige points to determine who will be remembered as the greatest Storm Raider of their time.

—description from publisher

name: Storybook Saga
description:
Build a team of classic heroes to take on classic villains in this combo-building dice manipulation game!

Draft heroes like Winnie the Pooh, Robin Hood, Dorothy, and Steamboat Willie to take on villains like Captain Hook, the Queen of Hearts, and the Great Oz. Then, roll and place dice to activate special abilities. Eliminate villains to gain special items and prepare for the boss. Defeat the final boss to win the game!

name: Storycaster: Fantasy Realms
description:
Storycaster is a game designed to help people run a Session Zero for their TTRPG campaigns. By using a combination of illustrated prompts and motivating questions, players will quickly find themselves building worlds, creating characters, items, monsters, adventures, and more. It has a single player mode, but it is best played collaboratively with up to 8 friends during a Session Zero.  Compatible with any TTRPG.

—description from the publisher

name: Purrfect Place
description:
Swap, flip, and stack the cats! Move cat cards from the sofa to the shelf, or the shelf to the playtime area. Make two rows match with each other and score minus(-) points. The player with the lowest score wins a bottle. Collect two bottles to triumph in this adorable and strategic cat game!


     Packed with irresistibly cute (and totally relatable) cat illustrations.
     Easy-to-learn gameplay with a clever stacking twist for added depth.
     Stacking: Score double minus(-) points and an extra turn, but only at the risk of a big penalty!


—description from the publisher

name: Strataugury
description:
Strataugury is a fantastical card game of strategy, magic, and war.  All a player requires is a standard deck of cards and the Strataugury Manual.

Each player takes turns summoning units and casting spells using combinations of cards from their hand.  The goal of the game is to reduce the opponent's health to 0, or to increase their own health to 60.

The game is split into Basic and Advanced Gameplay elements to ensure that players are not immediately overwhelmed by the game's complexity.

Solo players are also welcome as Single-Player Campaigns offer narrative-driven challenges to test their skills and experience epic legends.

—description from the publisher

name: Strategeti
description:
PLAY:
Try to rule the Serengeti by cleverly placing and moving your animals on the 4x4 game board!

Elephants push other animals back, maybe even into the croc infested river or into the ravine. Lions eat gazelles and zebras. 
Gazelles can jump over other animals, even several times in one turn! Zebras, finally, can run freely in any direction.
Make them work together and you will maximize your chances to win!

ADAPT:
Every animal moves differently and has its own strengths and weaknesses! So anticipate your opponent’s moves and adapt your own strategy when needed, 
especially as 1 move can change everything!

The double sided game board has different entry points and will challenge you to completely change your strategy between the 2 game levels.

WIN:
To rule the Serengeti and win the game, position 4 of your animals in a horizontal, vertical or diagonal line, eliminate 5 of your opponent’s animals or block them from moving.

name: Strattegee
description:
Strattegee is a tactical board game of modern warfare that reimagines the timeless strategy of chess with a bold, 3D battlefield and no reliance on luck. Designed for those who crave pure, skill-based competition, the game unfolds across land and air, challenging players to command infantry, artillery, and air units with precision and foresight.

In Strattegee, every unit has unique movement and attack capabilities that mirror real-world military roles. Ground units capture territory and block advancement, while air units strike from above, creating dynamic vertical and horizontal threats. Ammunition is limited, resources are visible to both players, and every decision counts—there are no dice, no hidden information, and zero chance elements.

The gameplay is built for both 1v1 and 2v2 formats, offering tightly contested duels or large-scale coordinated assaults. Players win by eliminating the opponent’s Command Piece — a mission that demands strategic depth, forward planning, and creative problem-solving. With quick setup, high replayability, and elegant mechanics, Strattegee is easy to learn but difficult to master.

Whether you’re a chess lover, a war gamer, or a strategist at heart, Strattegee offers an immersive test of battlefield command where only the most skilled tactician survives.

—description from the designer

name: Strawberry Shortcake: Berry Besties Bakeoff Card Game
description: In Strawberry Shortcake: Berry Besties Bakeoff Card Game, players bid for cards featuring familiar Strawberry Shortcake characters and items, trying to place them well to complete their cake recipe and out-bake their opponents. The cards bid in one round become the pool of what's available in the next one. Whoever builds the best shortcake and scores the most flavor points wins.

name: Shell We?
description:
Shell We? is a family-friendly, vibrant, and strategic tile-placement game by Reiner Knizia.

The goal is to be the first to play all your tiles or minimize penalty points when the game ends. With its easy-to-learn rules and intriguing mechanics, such as bonus actions, starfish tiles, and optional bottle tile effects, Shell We? provides an engaging experience for players of all ages and skill levels.

Set against the backdrop of a serene beach, players race to arrange colourful shell tiles on the board, following specific placement rules to outsmart their opponents and gain strategic advantages.


     Each shell tile is marked with a specific color and number. Tiles can only be placed on spaces on the board that match both their colour and number.
     A tile must be placed adjacent (horizontally or vertically, but not diagonally) to another tile already on the board.
     Starfish tiles act as wilds and can be placed on any space next to an existing tile. If another player has the matching shell tile, they can replace the starfish tile with the correct one.
     Placing tiles in specific ways, such as on "pearl spaces" or in consecutive order (ascending or descending), can trigger bonus actions, like placing additional tiles or gaining special effects.


Whether you're a seasoned gamer or a casual enthusiast, Shell We? offers a versatile gameplay experience enhanced by variant rules, bonus effects, and beautiful components. Choose from different board layouts, explore the Message in a Bottle, and dive into this seaside strategy adventure!

—description from the publisher

name: Splendor Kids
publisher: Space Cowboys; Belleville (Бельвіль); Korea Boardgames; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
Play as travelers, who deliver food across the kingdom. Splendor is a game of chip-collecting.

On your turn, you may (1) collect chips (food), or (2) move forward on the paths.

If you collect chips, you take either three different kinds of chips, two chips of the same kind or one joker chip, which you can use as any food.

If you move forward, you pay its price in chips and add it to your playing area.

Some place on the board let you take food that you can use and reactivate, some place let you play again.

Be the first to reach the Palace of Splendor and earn the Queen’s Medal!

name: The Lord of the Rings: Fate of the Fellowship
publisher: Z-Man Games; Galápagos Jogos; Geekach LLC; Gém Klub Kft.; GoKids 玩樂小子; Hobby Japan; Korea Boardgames; NeoTroy Games; Rebel Sp. z o.o.; Regatul Jocurilor
description:
As members of The Fellowship and the allies who rise to aid them, you must embark on a journey that may either save or doom Middle-earth. Navigate a world beset by shadow, where every choice forges a new path. The threads of destiny weave together, and the fate of The Free Peoples lies in your valor, friendship, and resolve. Will the One Ring be cast into the fire, or will the bearer be lost to despair?

The Lord of the Rings: Fate of the Fellowship is a co-operative game in which each player controls two characters, lending their unique abilities to protect Frodo, battle enemies in pivotal locations, and evade the menacing Nazgûl and Sauron's searching Eye.

Each playthrough presents new challenges with 24 different objectives, 14 events, and 13 playable characters. The game is won if the group destroys the One Ring before Frodo loses all hope.

A solo adventure is included.

—description from the publisher

name: Street Masters: Tide of the Dragon
description:
Street Masters: Tide of the Dragon is a standalone expansion for Street Masters, the cooperative miniatures board game of street brawling action. Heavily influenced by classic “beat ‘em up” arcade games and Hong Kong action movies of yesteryear, Tide of the Dragon is a standalone experience that contains everything needed to play, but also allows returning Street Masters fans to use its all-new fighters, enemy factions, stages, and other modular elements with the rest of the products in the game series.

Expanding on the modular nature of Streets Masters, Tide of the Dragon includes a new way to further customize players’ experiences. Terrain cards allow fighters to introduce new terrain elements to their battles, such as ladders that can be used to climb up and away from enemies or fire hydrants that can launch a powerful water stream to damage opponents.

Street Masters: Tide of the Dragon includes 52 highly detailed miniatures; 4 New Fighters with their own unique Fighter and Hero Story Decks; a New Double-Sided Map Tile with 2 New Stage Decks; 2 New Enemy Factions with unique Enemy and Showdown Decks; 4 Terrain Cards; a Tide of the Dragon Story Deck; 12 New Ally/Rival cards, and all the dice, tokens, dividers and base rings needed to play right out of the box.

-description from designer

name: Streets of Revenge
description:
Get ready to relive the golden age of arcades with Streets of Revenge! Inspired by the frantic action and unmistakable spirit of 80s beat 'em up arcade games, this micro-game plunges you directly into adrenaline-fueled street fights.

With just a handful of cards and a few dice, every game of Streets of Revenge is an explosion of nostalgia and quick strategy. Forget complicated rules and long setups; here, the action is instant. Choose your hero, master your moves, and face hordes of enemies to clear the streets of thugs and reach the dreaded Final Boss. It's time to roll the dice and unleash your arcade fury!

In this game, you'll use dice to represent both your hero and the enemies, where the dice score indicates health points. You'll face enemies of different levels, each distinguished by their color and possessing unique abilities.

Your hero will have special skills and upgrades as you move across the scenario map. During your adventure, you'll be able to break reward crates (containing weapons, health, credits, among other things) and shoot explosive barrels to inflict additional damage on enemies. Your goal is to defeat all enemies to finally confront the stage bosses, each with their own distinct rewards and abilities.

name: Streets of Tokyo
description:
Streets of Tokyo is a cooperative drawing game in which players try to guess words drawn by other players on maps of Tokyo. The twists are that players draw and guess simultaneously, they may only draw on the streets of the maps.

The game is played with an evolutive timer: every time a word is correctly guessed, it is validated in the application, and players earn more time as well as points depending on the difficulty of the word.

The game ends either when players run out of time, they lose the game, or when they manage to validate a word on each of the 16 maps in the game. In either case, they get a final score that they can try to beat on their next attempt.

The game also features a campaign mode, starting easy and getting progressively harder with various constraints added with the levels.

—description from the designer

name: Strike of the Heron: The Approach to Stalingrad Aug-Sep 1942
description:
Strike of the Heron - The Approach to Stalingrad explores the sudden and astonishing breakthrough operation “Fischreiher” (Heron) by the German XIV Panzer Korps and other supporting units, to the Volga River in August, 1942. It sent shock waves all the way up to Stalin and his Front commanders as the Soviets had been able to previously repel German attacks, allowing only a slow advance. This rapid breakthrough and arrival of German units along the banks of Volga River at Rynok (just north of Stalingrad proper) on August 23rd also cutoff chances of a general offensive by Soviet forces on the German’s left flank to the north. This had been part of STAVKA's overall plan but had to be hastily abandoned.

The Soviets did react quickly and by Aug. 24th were launching counter thrusts against the base of the German corridor (near the Don), on both the German's right and left flanks. But, like the Germans, the Soviets were also weak. Their divisions were really at brigade strength, with around 4000 men. Their tank corps averaged 50 AFVs, but many times half of these were light tanks. The Soviet euphoric attacks managed to cut the corridor briefly, forcing the Germans to re-supply themselves by air, but had turned into a dire defensive action within a few days. A second Soviet "pincher" offensive against the corridor nearer to Stalingrad was launched from Kotluban' to the north and Orlovka to the south in early Sept.

Designed by Perry Moore, Strike of the Heron includes one map with 280 counters. Units are at the division/brigade level for the Soviets while German forces are depicted from battalion to division. Each turn is 12 hours and a hex is around one mile.

In terms of game play, the Soviet player must not only ensure sufficient forces escape the intended German encirclement, but then maintain constant pressure on the overextended Panzer Korps with a series of counterattacks from both north and south of the corridor.

Maps - One full color 17"x44" hex mapsheet
Counters - 280 full color 1/2" die-cut pieces
Rules length - 15 pages
Charts and tables - 1 page
Complexity - Medium
Playing time - Up to 4 hours
How challenging is it solitaire? - Average

—description from the publisher

name: Studium | No Exit
description:
Dive into a unique Gothic horror fantasy board game experience that will keep you on the edge of your seat! Featuring more than 40 beautifully-sculpted miniatures, stunning gothic horror artwork, and a compelling campaign style gameplay, this tile based dungeon crawler will keep you and up to three fellow victims of the Studium coming back for more.

Players take on the role of newcomers held at the mercy of the menacing forces that control the labyrinthian Studium. Having been brought together to form a house, they are tasked with delving into the darkest depths of the Studium to eradicate unspeakable horrors. While exploring the ruined halls of the Studium, players will be challenged by engaging story events. The choices that players make may have grave consequences for their characters, their companions, or even the whole of the Studium.
