Mystery Fluxx features a larger-than-normal number of card types: Meta Rules, Keepers, Creepers, Goals, New Rules, Actions, Surprises, Dangers (which eliminate you for one turn), and a brand new card type: Secrets!

name: The Hunters A.D. 1492
description:
The Hunters A. D. 1492 is a fully cooperative game which enables you to play solo or with a group of friends.

Players are monster hunters who participate in a complex and gripping campaign comprised of hundreds event, road and town cards and tome of tales. The narrative presented on the cards and book is full of story twists and difficult decisions to make.

During the campaign, players execute quests. Each quest has its own win conditions. It may take place during the day or at nighttime, in various weather conditions. Every time players must choose proper tactics and equipment matching current circumstances. Players may barter with local inhabitants, undertake various jobs, overcome unexpected obstacles or expand their wagon in order to manufacture over 70 different types of equipment from resources found during the game.

—description from the designer

name: The Kaiser's High Seas Fleet: The Great War at Sea 1914-18
description:
Utilizing a refined version of the basic system for War at Sea, The Kaiser's High Seas Fleet takes us back to World War I prior to the invention of Radar and no air power.

This is a two player game in which one player represents the Central Powers consisting of Germany, Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire. The other represents the Entente Powers consisting of Great Britain, France, Italy, and Russia. The USA is neutral until Turn 7, when it joins the Entente. Portugal and Greece are always neutral.

Players will move and fight Dreadnoughts (Battleships) to seize and control ocean areas for victory. U-Boat campaigns are reflected by placing U-Boat counters for Victory Points. Pre-Dreadnoughts are included but their effectiveness is greatly reduced. There are no auxiliary ships.

The objective is to score as many Victory Points (VP) as possible at the end of each turn. These are marked on the Victory Point Track (VPT) during the Area Control Phase. The player whose marker is on the track is ahead in points. At the end of the July/December 1918 turn, the player whose marker is showing wins the game. If the marker is at 0, the Entente Powers win but the Central Powers have gained a ‘moral’ victory.

name: The Keymaster: A Dungeon Escape Game
description:
The Keymaster | A Dungeon Escape Game is a tabletop strategy game, where adventurers risk their souls on a gambit of survival, sabotage, and luck to escape the underworld.

"You are dead. You’ve made a deal with the devil: If you can escape the 7th circle of hell, you will be reborn as the Master of Death. If you fail, you will be subjected to horrors unimaginable for all of time..."

Players break into a rat race treasure hunt for the key to escape the underworld. They find springs of resources, a river of fire and blood, and dark runes. They can collect up to 9 unique resources, sacrificing and combining them to progress in the game. They are not alone, and must avoid the minotaur—a dangerous beast who can take them temporarily or permanently out of the game. They must march through the land’s 3 power levels to find the key. Unlocking a player's freedom requires some forethought and a little luck...

The game's simultaneous gameplay ensures everyone is always engaged, its repetitive nature reinforces the rules and reveals new strategies, and the different paths to victory make winning more attainable and rewarding.

—NL Games

name: The Kittens of Mont Saint Michel
description:
See them there, those little balls of fluff, so full of mischief and curiosity? You won’t believe it now, but this is how heroes start. Join the four kittens Leon, Adara, Nera and Guy in their adventures as they learn, spar and explore the streets and secret places of the ancient fortress island of Mont Saint Michel...and it’s not just play. They’ll need to work together to put their lessons of the Warrior Virtues to good use against a hidden foe before this little tale is done.
Before you can achieve great things, you must learn the little things. Let us get started, oui?

The Kittens of Mont Saint Michel is a co-op adventure card game where each players takes the role of one of the would-be heroes of Mont Saint Michel. In this game you will explore the town and castle while learning the virtues courage, patience, competence, selflessness, perseverance and integrity on the path to becoming a true warrior.

The object of the Kittens of Mont Saint Michel is for your heroic kitten to earn as many warrior virtues as possible and defeat the vermin army in the Final Battle.

After selecting your little furry hero and setting up the play area, you will have actions to perform each turn including moving to new locations, sparing with fellow kittens and earning warrior virtues.

The locations in Mont Saint Michel are represented by cards that occupy the center of the table. When your kittens venture there they will be able to test their skills to earn the corresponding virtue on the card as well as collecting loot items to use in their mission to save the monastery

The game is played over three chapters. Chapter 1: Train Hard is where the kittens earn Warrior Virtues by adventuring in the town, monastery and fortress of Mont Saint-Michel, represented by Location cards. In Chapter 2: The Search, the would-be heroes continue to earn virtue while seeking out the foe and Chapter 3: The Final Battle is the moment everyone has been working towards! Foil the Vermin Army’s plan to harm the monastery and its inhabitants.

—description from the designer

name: The Last Command
description:
The Last Command is a detail-oriented space combat strategy game, lovingly crafted to simulate the relationship between a starship and its crew. Whether playing as the Federation Remnant or the Sunder, victory hinges on maximizing the potential of your crew and ship systems with gameplay utilizing dual deckbuilding, worker placement and resource management!

Ready your crew and Man all stations!
At the heart of The Last Command is an intuitive dual deckbuilding system that has players constructing a powerful ship system deck and a second deck consisting of crew members that can maximize those systems potential and provide the energy to power them. Multiple system cards can be played into a ship location, but the topmost card has the potential of unlocking powerful end of turn bonus abilities if crew with matching expertise are present in that system.

Become A Legendary Fleet Captain!
Cards played to your ship remain in play until you attempt to draw from their respective deck and that deck is empty. To achieve victory, captains must learn when to push their system’s limits and when to recall them. If a captain is able to reduce the hull strength of his opponent’s ship to zero, then the battle has been won and glory and honor is theirs!

—description from the publisher

name: The Last Droids
publisher: Blue Cocker Games; Gen-X Games; Strohmann Games
description:
In The Last Droids, you take on the role of robot repairmen in a world of depleted natural resources. Your goal: to help humanity survive by recycling the last droids.
Select the best robot wrecks, manage your resources and build the most efficient droid collection!

A simple game turn:
- The active player draws 2 Droids.
- He then chooses which droid to give to his opponent, and which to keep.
- Finally, at the same time, each player chooses to recycle or repair his Droid, or to sacrifice it to build a Dwelling.

There are 6 different types of Droid and 14 Habitations, each with its own scoring system. In each game, you play 4 of the 14 Habitations. 
All this adds up to game variety and replayability.

Simultaneous, high-impact choices make for an intense gaming experience with no downtime.
At 4 players, team play calls for planning and involves many strategic exchanges with your partner.

At the end, each droid repaired scores Leaf points. The droid maker with the most Leaf points wins!

—description from the publisher

name: The Last Wizard
publisher: スパイラルゲーム  (Spiral Game); Spiral Éditions
description:
Players are dealt a two-card hand each, and two cards are revealed for everyone in the center of the table. Then each player chooses three cards among the four available (two in hand and two on the table), to make the strongest combination they can to get the highest total power and win.

The twist is that the player will be offered a choice with betting tokens! Your position in the round might have a big impact on how much you win or lose! Every bet you make grants you victory points or make you lose some victory points depending how strong your hand really was.

name: The League of the Extraordinary Collectors
description:
In a world where ideas, images, and words take physical form, Dr. Gregory Faustroll’s prophetic monkeys type the future on a skyscreeper-high typewriter: the Oracle. In this detective game you and your fellow Investigators must question this living oracle to answer 8 difficult question about eight surreal characters: the Extraordinary Collectors.

				
				
					OverviewOne player becomes the Oracle, who can cheat knowing all the answers to the 8 questions (peeking the end of the booklet), but can only speak through Rebus— abstract images built from overlapping tiles. The others are Investigators, who must interpret those images, propose meanings, and slowly construct a shared symbolic language between human and machine.
This booklet is not merely a prop — it is the game’s true grammar. In fact the game involves the innovative mechanism of the Referents: a system that players will use to anchor the symbols they see to this book texts and illustrations. Without it, communication between Oracle and Investigators would collapse into pure abstraction.

Your notes, drawings, and guesses become the game’s evolving dictionary that you will use through your 8 adventures.

By the end, you will not just have solved the mysteries —you will have invented a language, one glyph at a time.

				
				
					What Makes it UniqueIn most detective games, events are mysterious but language is clear. In The League, it’s the opposite: the story is obvious, but the language is the mystery.
Other detective games hide the facts — The League hides the language.
Here, the crime is visible, but the words to describe it must be invented.

name: Word Fluxx
description:
Fluxx is a card game in which the cards themselves determine the current rules of the game. By playing cards, you change numerous aspects of the game: how to draw cards, how to play cards, and even how to win.

At the start of the game, each player holds three cards and on a turn a player draws one card, then plays one card. By playing cards, you can put new rules into play that change numerous aspects of the game: how many cards to draw or play, how many cards you can hold in hand or keep on the table in front of you, and (most importantly) how to win the game.

In Word Fluxx, the word-building version of the ever-changing card game, the keepers each feature a letter, and the goals involve making words of various types. With twice the typical number of keepers, you'll have plenty of letters to build nouns and verbs, palindromes, three-letter acronyms (TLAs), Roman numerals, and more.

name: The Line
description:
Guess the numbers, fill in the Line.

How much does a great white shark weigh? How far is the Earth from the Moon? How hot is the surface of Mercury? These figures have nothing to do with each other, but if you had to classify them, where would you put them on the Line?

The Line’s principle is simple: each card has a piece of information on the front, and its corresponding numerical value on the back. Estimate the value, and place it correctly on a scale made up of the previous cards. In co-op mode, line up as many cards as possible! In competitive mode, be the first to get rid of all your cards!

—description from the publisher

name: The Lions of El Alamein
description:
In the summer of 1942, after the capture of Tobruk, the German-Italian forces under the command of Field Marshal Erwin Rommel were in a strategic position to continue their advance in North Africa. The fall of Tobruk, a major Libyan port defended by British forces, was a severe blow to the British Eighth Army, which was forced to retreat rapidly eastwards towards Alexandria and the Suez Canal.

Rommel, having accumulated a series of successes, intended to use the opportunity to pursue the retreating British army, aiming to defeat it definitively and take control of the Suez Canal, vital to Allied supplies. His plan was to maintain constant pressure on the British forces, who were exhausted and ill-equipped, with the aim of forcing them to retreat further.

However, the situation of the Axis forces was not without its difficulties: Rommel suffered from supply problems, especially fuel, and logistics posed a significant challenge in the advance into the desert. Nevertheless, his determination to continue the pursuit and exploit the strategic momentum did not waver, and he prepared for what would become one of the decisive battles of the North African campaign: the Battle of El Alamein.

The game uses a new supply system based on the use and management of various types of resources: supplies, motor vehicles, ammo, manpower, afv and more.

The game offers five scenarios: two tutorial for learning the SLIT and three to relive the three battles of El Alamein, from July 1 till November 5.

One player is the Axis, the other is the Commonwealth.

In each Impulse a player may play a Pass, a Tactical Impulse or a Strategic Impulse.

Scale: 
Monthly Rounds, divided in alternated Turns. Rounds ends after two consecutive passes.
Units are Regiments (Axis) or Brigades (CW)
Map is 86x64cm, 1:10000, with one hex side corresponding to 6 km

Each scenario has its own victory conditions, with victory points for each eliminated enemy units and captured Logistics Hub.

Includes convoy wars in the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean.

-description from the publisher

name: The Long Hours Till Dawn
description:
A Fully Electronic Survival-Horror Board Game — No Moving Parts. Just Pure Tension. Inspired by the classics, this is a love letter to the golden age of zombie horror — drawing heavily from iconic films and survival-horror video games that defined the genre. Featuring a fully original musical score composed exclusively for the game and real voice performances from four professional actors, the experience is rich with cinematic atmosphere and escalating dread.

You're part of a four-person military unit trapped in a remote farmhouse. It’s 6:00 PM. Outside, the undead swarm. Rescue won’t arrive until 6:00 AM. Armed with only what you can scavenge, you must survive 12 relentless in-game hours as the horde breaks through the defenses.

Driven entirely by LEDs, this one-of-a-kind game eliminates moving parts — every action, threat, and shift in the environment is signified through immersive light cues.

Search for ammo. Barricade the doors. Fend off the dead. Scavenge supplies. Make impossible choices. With multiple endings, no two playthroughs are the same — your story of survival is yours alone.

Dawn is your only escape. Can you survive the night?

—description from the designer

name: Bad Apples
description:
The goal of Bad Apples is to be the player with the most points after ten rounds. Each player starts with a set of apples and bidding tokens. The numbers on the apples represent the point values. Each round, every player discretely puts one of their apples into the burlap sack. These apples will be collectively auctioned off to the highest bidder.

Moving clockwise, players either raise the bid using their bidding tokens or pass. Every time a player passes, that player receives a small amount of bidding tokens as a consolation. Next, an apple is withdrawn from the burlap sack for everyone to see. The remaining players now have more insight to determine the
potential point total of all the submitted apples. The last player remaining wins the auction and collects all the apples.

—description from the designer

name: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring – Trick-Taking Game
publisher: Office Dog; ADC Blackfire Entertainment; asmodee; Galápagos Jogos; Gameology (Gameology Romania); Geekach LLC; Gém Klub Kft.; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
The Fellowship of the Ring: Trick-Taking Game is a co-operative card game that plays out over eighteen chapters that lead players through the events of the novel The Fellowship of the Ring. The chapters can be played in any order, but ideally you play them in sequence.

In each chapter, each player takes a different character role — Frodo, Gandalf, Sam, Pippin, Farmer Maggot, etc. — and each character has a condition that must be met in order to pass the chapter and advance in the story. Frodo needs to capture ring cards, for example, while Pippin wants to take as few tricks as possible. As you advance through the chapters, new characters, items, and challenges are introduced to the game.

The deck consists of 37 cards, with one card being set aside as "lost" each hand. Whoever is dealt the One Ring becomes Frodo, then other players choose from the available characters based on their hand. The One Ring is the game's only trump card, but initially rings can't be led until someone plays one off-suit.

In the two-player game, one hand of cards is dealt to a dummy player, with some cards being face up and others face down. This dummy is assigned a character, and one of the human players will play cards for it based on which cards are free to be played.

In the solitaire game, one player plays four hands of face-up cards, with each hand being assigned a character and only a few cards being available at a time. After you play a trick, deal each hand a new card.

If you own The Fellowship of the Ring: Trick-Taking Game, you can add the following characters to this version of the Road Goes Ever On...:
Bilbo (Peculiar), Gandalf (Grey Wizard), Gildor Inglorion, Fatty Bolger, Tom Bombadil, Goldberry, Barliman, Glorfindel, Bill the Pony, Glóin, Arwen, Boromir (Captain of Gondor), Gwaihir, Shadowfax (Lord of Horses), Radagast, Gandalf (Servant of the Secret Fire), Galadriel, and Celeborn.

name: The Lost Lands of Verne
description:
Six centuries have passed since the Great War shattered the once-united kingdoms of Verne. Now, adventurers from distant shores arrive in a fractured land filled with opportunity, danger, and ambition. Some seek to rebuild… others to rule.

The Lost Lands of Verne is a game of deals, duels, and dominion for 1 to 6 players, blending the strategic depth of classic fantasy RPGs with the accessibility of beloved family board games. Players take on the roles of bold adventurers vying to reclaim Verne by exploring dangerous lands, collecting powerful items, constructing mighty castles, and clashing in thrilling battles.

During the game, you’ll:

Rule shires and unite kingdoms to grow your influence.

Wield items, spells, and equipment to outwit rivals and gain the upper hand in combat.

Encounter monsters, bosses, and hidden dangers as you journey through Verne.

Form alliances—or betray them—as you negotiate, trade, and scheme your way to victory.

Your ultimate goal is to earn Quest Points through exploration, combat, and control. Whether through diplomacy, might, or cunning, the first adventurer to get 4 Quest Points takes the throne and reshapes the fate of Verne.

With easy-to-learn mechanics, dynamic player interaction, and endless replayability, The Lost Lands of Verne is perfect for both newcomers to fantasy gaming and seasoned veterans alike.

-description from the creators

name: The Magic Shop
description:
All who enter the Magic Shop experience the ultimate mysteries. But in the end, they are unable to resist its allure and are absorbed forever as part of the shop. There is only one way to escape the impending doom: to prove yourself a true magician by performing a trick powerful enough to surpass the magic of the shop itself.

There are 5 suits in the game, each possessing its own unique Magic Effect.
The Wine reshapes order and changes the trump suit.
The Time Machine turns back time to alter predictions.
The Eye flips the strength of numbers each time it blinks.
The Door sends a card into another dimension, beyond everyone’s reach.
The Invisible Man steals a trick you were about to win, then vanishes.

The winner of each trick must use one of the revealed Magic Effects,
so timing your choices and avoiding dangerous effects at the right moment is key to victory.
Keep in mind that sometimes, your choice comes with a price—
a penalty known as Thirst.

-With a cheeky wink, the invisible man steps into the time machine and says, “Have a drink, and take this card.”

—description from the publisher

name: Burst
publisher: Lost Boy Entertainment; Gém Klub Kft.; Pegasus Spiele
description:
Every card has a number ranging from -3 to 15. Players can hold a max of three cards. Each round, players either draw a card from the deck or play a card faceup. Faceup cards are placed in a row next to the deck. If a player plays a card that brings the total value of the row over twenty-one, that player bursts. If a player bursts, the round ends and that player receives zero points. All other players collect the points in their hand.

—description from the publisher

name: Detonate
description:
Detonate is played in rounds. On your turn, you either roll the die or grab the lowest-value tile. If you decide to grab the tile, you’re out for the remainder of the round but you’ve locked in points. If you decide to roll, you want to avoid rolling an explosion number. If you roll an explosion number, you receive zero points and are out for the round.

On your first turn, the explosion number is one. On your second turn, the explosion numbers are now one and two, and so on. You want to keep rolling and stay in the round to collect a high-value tile, but don’t want to roll an explosion number and collect nothing.

—description from the designer

name: Miniature Adventures: Adventure 1 – Goblin Troubles
description:
The Kingdom of Delriah has a little trouble with some goblins! They need the help of an adventuring party! Will you answer their call?

Miniature Adventures is an exciting co-op adventure card game inspired by old-school 16-bit RPGs and designed to be portable while still challenging!

Choose a Hero and overcome four Levels of challenges in order to complete the entire Adventure Level.  Adventure solo, or with up to four players!

Players take turns performing actions or Rolling for Adventure.  Players will slot dice rolled into their three Points value locations on their Character cards.  These values will help determine their Initiative (speed), Power (ability), and Actions.

There are several types of Encounters players will need to overcome such as Mobs (enemies) and Challenges (perils).  Survive through every Encounter in a level to progress to the next level and gain a reward!  Once all four levels are complete, the Players win and are victorious!

name: A Wild Venture
publisher: PIKA Games; Cranio Creations; DSV Games; GaGa Games; Lucky Duck Games; Maldito Games; Mosaico Jogos; Steinbock Brettspiele; Ігромаг
description:
A Wild Venture is a fast-paced, strategic 2-player game where you don’t just build engines… you dismantle them too!

In this quirky world, you’ll share a deck of cards packed with wild characters, clever combos, and unexpected twists. Each turn, you’ll race to build powerful synergies... only to tear them apart when the time is right. Cards won’t last forever, but only the ones you have fully used up score points, making timing everything.

With 108 unique cards, a double-sided adventuring board, and two themed sets for endless variety, no two games feel the same. It’s strategic. It’s deep. It’s delightfully wild.

If you love tactical duels, fast decisions, and games with real personality then A Wild Venture is definitely for you!

name: Children of Morta: The Board Game
publisher: Roomiz Games; Board Zeppelin; Lucky Duck Games
description:
A family that SLAYS together STAYS together!

Children of Morta: The Board Game is a cooperative adventure game with a unique shared bag-building mechanism, permanent character development, an emphasis on family growth, simultaneous turns, and interconnected cooperation. In this game, you take on the role of a member of the Bergson family as they try to stop the spreading corruption of evil in their beloved land of Rea. Defeat monsters and bosses to unlock upgrades for your hero, making them stronger and more prepared for what comes next.

—description from the publisher

name: Food Chain Magnate: Deluxe Edition
description:
The Deluxe Edition contains the base game Food Chain Magnate and the expansion Food Chain Magnate: The Ketchup Mechanism & Other Ideas in a single box featuring entirely new artwork, deluxe wooden tokens, and tabletop organizers!

It is planned as a one-off print run and there is no retail release coming for this edition.

So what does the Deluxe Edition Offer?

- All new artwork for every component
- Employee Organizer and Storage solution
- Screen-printed restaurants & coffee shops
- Wooden food tokens in full-color heat-transferred detail
- Storage trays for your food tokens and money bills
- Triple-layered Milestone Trackers
- Both the base game and expansion in a single box

The Deluxe Edition focuses on wood and punchboard components and does NOT include miniatures from the Special Edition, also part of the same Gamefound campaign.

name: The Masters
description: In The Masters, each player selects a character and engages in three rounds of duels. A player wins a round by reducing their opponent's HP to 0. The first player to win two duels is the overall winner.

name: The Meerkats Family
description:
A terrible sandstorm is raging in the desert. By dawn, when everything finally quiets down, the suricata family's burrow is covered in dust, their items scattered everywhere. Worst of all, Kiki, the youngest member of the family, is missing! The suricata family band together and do something they've never done before: they leave the burrow and its surroundings to travel the desert together to find Kiki. You control a member of the family, build your own deck and if you complete the adventure deck fast enough, you might just save Kiki.

The game's special feature is that you build not only your own deck, but also a shared deck. In your own turn, you first play some of your cards in order to:

     get a new card for yourself
     add a new card to the common deck
     perform a special action
     reveal the next adventure card
     "defeat" the current adventure card.


You can do any number of these as long as you have enough cards. At the end of your turn, you draw new cards.

This simple card game puts a twist on the familiar deck-building mechanic.

Can you hide from the eagles? Will you be able to defeat the rattlesnake? Or perhaps make new friends along the way? But most importantly, will you be able to save Kiki and bring the family back together? It depends on your decisions!

—description from the publisher

name: The Mire
description:
Outmaneuver your opponent in a mysterious swamp that Shifts with every glance and sinks with every step.

The Mire is a 2 person strategy game in which players take turns moving, swapping, and locking down tiles with the goal of backing your opponent into a corner so they are unable to move on their turn.

—description from the publisher

name: The NecroNomNomNom: A Card Game of Dark Deliciousness
description:
A card game of omnivorous peril and delectable danger. This luxuriantly appointed deck of 100+ cards to feed insanity compels you and a cohort of fellow cultists (2 to 4 players) to stir up the foul fixin’s of H. P. Lovecraft's Cosmos and compete in a grimly hilarious, ravenous race against fate, luck, your opponents, and the Stars themselves. Are you ready to play with your food?
Within the disturbing depths of this bloodcurdling box lie four subdecks: Eldritch Horrors from beyond time and space that affect play for each cultist holding that card; Rituals (recipes) to satisfy the unearthly appetites of the Ancient Ones; Offerings (ingredients) to assemble for a given ritual; and The Stars, which lambast celebrity chefs and give players a task for that round.
Be the first cultist to complete a ritual that quells the hunger of your Eldritch Horror—before you become the main course. You don’t have to know how to boil water or skin a nightgaunt to make these recipes, though. You merely need to answer that age-old question posed by unhinged necromancers everywhere: “Now that I’ve summoned Ghatanothoa, what to feed it?” Friends make a fine choice, but can you consign them to their just desserts?

name: Hutan: Life in the Rainforest
publisher: Sidekick Games; ADC Blackfire Entertainment; asmodee; Gém Klub Kft.; Hobby Japan; Hobby World; Lord of Boards; Lucky Duck Games; The Op Games; Ravensburger AG
description:
Step into a world of wonder and natural splendor with HUTAN: Life in the Rainforest, an immersive family game inspired by the Indonesian word for rainforest.

In HUTAN, all players have their own rainforest patch where they will plant sprouts and flowers that over time grow into towering trees. When a habitat is created, an iconic forest animal arrives: the orangutan, the sumatran tiger, the rhinoceros hornbill, the cassowary, or the sumatran rhino.

HUTAN plays over nine rounds, and all players have two turns each round. On your turn, you take a flower card from the shared market pool and place the flowers into your rainforest. If you place a flower on top of a matching flower, you grow a tree. When an area is completed with trees, the last tree is replaced by an animal.

At the end of the game, the player who grew the best rainforest and attracted the most animals will score the most points and win.

—description from the publisher

name: Potions of Azerland
publisher: Warped Reality Games; Lucky Duck Games
description:
In Potions of Azerland you will, you guessed it, make potions!

Gather resources from the forest, increase your knowledge in various potion types, go to the market to collect and trade goods, then make your potions to drink for unique powers or fulfill the orders of travelers who come to your town!

Potions of Azerland utilizes a unique simultaneous action selection mechanism where understanding the goals of your opponents in each round will give you the upper hand. Decide whether to drink your newly made potions for temporary boosts and prolonged powers or give them to an ever changing group of travelers for points and other bonuses. After 6 rounds the player who has garnered the most prestige will be the winner!

—description from the publisher

name: The Order
description:
The Order is a tabletop card game that blends strategic gameplay with biting satire and a dash of luck. Players navigate the treacherous waters of modern society, vying for Influence and Wealth to become the leader of The Order, a mysterious organisation pulling the strings behind global events.

Play as one of eight Candidates across four different sectors: business, government, media, and cult figures. Each player embodies a unique character, strategically deploying cards to build their empire and undermine their rivals’ attempts to lead The Order.

Using Attack, Defense, Executive Order, Wealth, Influence, and News cards, players experience the thrill (and the absurdity) of manipulating public opinion, embezzling tax money, and maybe even using gangs or robbers to steal Wealth. When the first Candidate reaches their required number of Wealth and Influence points, they are the winner and become the new leader of The Order, ending the game.

The Order mirrors current events, with cards inspired by today's headlines. Rolls of the dice keep things unpredictable, ensuring that every game is a unique and engaging experience.

—description from the designer

name: The Oregon Trail: Ultimate Trek Card Game – You Are All Going to Die
description:
The year is 1847, and you are about to discover who amongst your wagon party will die of dysentery and who will make the successful trek to Oregon. Face illness, death, thieves, fire, and so much more in this nostalgic simulation game. We wish you the best of luck on your perilous journey!

• BEWARE THE DANGERS OF THE TRAIL: Welcome to the Oregon Trail, where dysentery, cholera, and rattlesnakes await.
• A NEW TWIST ON AN OLD FAVORITE: The classic simulation game brings on the nostalgia to any game night.
• CAN YOU COUNT ON YOUR TEAM TO SURVIVE?: Play as a wagon party and try your hand at survival - win together or die together.
• THE TRUE OG, BUT BETTER: The most complete physical game representation of the classic computer game.

- description from publisher

Contents:
• 10 Trail Cards
• 40 Calamity Cards
• 26 Supply Cards
• 10 Party Member Cards
• Wagon Board
• Wagon Mover With Base
• Dry Erase Marker

name: The Path Seekers
description:
The Path Seekers is a sandbox tabletop experience that brings players back to an ancient China fantasy world. You are playing as one of the young protagonists who starts off with a modest background. With tremendous hard work and determination, you set off living your dream to make a difference in this treacherous time.

On players' turn, they will perform up to 3 main actions using multi-use Actions cards to move around and interact with locations on the board to improve their protagonist's attributes, and to befriend all kinds of interesting characters to help you with their special powers.

You may travel to visit different clans, learn from more than 20 new skills in the form of Action cards to execute more challenging missions, explore the uncharted cave for what lies within or hunt dangerous animals to gain precious resources and go on many more adventures. Prestige will be earned in many ways from successful missions, event interactions, gold and virtue etc.

At the end of nine months, the player with the most Prestige will be titled the winner.

Will you succeed on your quests to gain a prestigious reputation or succumb to the growing pressure and regress into obscurity? Your journey starts now as The Path Seekers.

-description from designer

name: The Path to Victory: Middle East 1941
description:
The Path to Victory: Middle East, 1941, is a simulation of the operations in Iraq, Syria and Iran (Persia) during the Spring and Summer of 1941. In this game, both players must carefully use their limited resources (military and political) to try to wrestle control of the Middle East away from their enemies.

The game begins with the Iraqi coup in early April 1941. The Axis player may attempt a number of diplomatic/military actions: supporting the Iraqi coup, trying to take control of Persia, unleash an Arab revolt in Palestine, send aid to Iraq, Vichy Syria and possibly Persia. The Allied player must use their limited resources to assert control in Iraq, Persia, Syria and Lebanon as soon as possible to protect the rearguard of the Suez Canal and the Western Desert Front.

Each game turn represents about 10 days. Each hexagon is 37 miles (60 kilometers) from side to the opposite side. Units are army, divisions, brigades, regiments, and battalions or equivalent, and some specialized smaller units.

name: The Peak Team
publisher: Matagot; Hobby Japan; Hutter Trade GmbH + Co KG
description:
As a team of wildlife rangers, your mission is to ensure the well-being of different species in your wildlife reserve while protecting them from potential threats. In The Peak Team, a cooperative game by Scott Almes, 1-5 rangers work together to complete a variety of challenging tasks.

The main board represents the wildlife reserve, dominated by a towering mountain divided into distinct regions. Using a "reverse-drafting" mechanic, where each player assigns their cards to others, rangers will acquire the tools they need to explore the mountain via different paths and transportation systems.

By reaching various locations and observing wildlife, players will complete their personal missions and earn bonuses. Each ranger has two mission slots that fill up as soon as tasks are accomplished. Only by completing all missions before running out of actions will the rangers successfully fulfill their duty!

The Peak Team is built around a tiered level system, with the game increasing in difficulty and complexity as sessions progress. It strikes a careful balance between accessibility for newcomers and a rewarding challenge for seasoned players.

Enhanced by Crocotame's stunning illustrations, The Peak Team is set for release at Essen 2025.

—description from the publisher

name: The Plank
description:
Part of the pirate crew has decided to mutiny. You find yourself forced out on the plank, but there is one last hope. The last one left on the plank will be spared and allowed back on the ship!

The plank is a push your luck dice game where you try to move as little as possible each turn. But as you get closer to the edge of the plank, you need to adjust your rolls to roll lower and lower. You can collect coins to gain extra rolls or ignore dice, or collect swords to push the other pirates closer to the edge.

—description from the designer

name: The Presence
description:
The Presence is a strategic horror-game that puts you in a Victorian-era ghost story. Each game is either fully cooperative or one-versus-all, only you have no way of knowing which one. One player plays as a spirit with unknown intentions. The others play as the visitors, who need to work together to determine whether the spirit is on their side, while also trying to find out what it wants. The visitors will try to work together while struggling with darkness, isolation, and the constant haunting of the spirit, who in turn either tries to earn their trust or secretly plan their demise.

Regardless of the intentions of the spirit-player, the trust of the visitors is valuable to its goals. A benevolent spirit needs their trust to play its more powerful actions. If it does not believe that they will manage in time, it can instead turn on them and win by other means. A vengeful spirit can bide its time, sabotaging their efforts in hidden ways and use their trust to make the visitors expose themselves. Then, when they are vulnerable it can reveal its true nature.

The visitors are represented on the board while the spirit moves through the house ethereally and can be in multiple locations at once. While visitors are limited by doors and passageways, the spirit can move freely, surrounding them. While the spirit-player may have very limited means to communicate, the visitors have an even tougher choice to make. If they separate and go different ways, they will not be able to speak at all. Then, they can only watch on in horror as their friend must make a perilous choice with no support.

The actions of the spirit leave clues as to its true intentions and, when the secrets of the house are gradually revealed, the visitors may realize what they think they know is fatally wrong.

name: The Promise
description:
In a merciless and desolate world live Tom and Anna Thumb — no taller than a finger, but with the courage of giants. The siblings roam the land, driven by hunger, ambition, and the hope of earning a few coins. They take on jobs from those who can afford their services — nobles, merchants, and kings — people who, in times of desperation, make foolish promises they later regret. And the two siblings are there to ensure that these promises do not have to be kept. 

The Promise is a game for one or two players, where you face a series of battles against increasingly powerful foes. Your goal is to survive five intense fights, grow stronger with each victory, and ultimately confront the final boss in the sixth and last showdown. Use the remains of your defeated enemies to forge new weapons and armor—only then will you be strong enough to endure the final battle. Defeat the final boss, and you've won the game... and with that, you've also broken the promise that started it all.

—description from the designer

name: The Publish or Perish Game
description:
Welcome to the chaotic life of academic publishing.

In Publish or Perish, you are a clueless researcher trying to do the one and only thing that matters in your academic life: churning out publications, fast. You will publish useless nonsense, sabotage your colleagues’ research, and provide unhelpful comments, Reviewer 2 style. Your goal is to gain as many citations as possible when the game ends, ideally with your sanity and self-respect intact.

Publish or Perish is a card game where players attempt to publish 5 manuscripts and collect the most citations to win.  Using Action cards, players move their own publications along or sabotage the work of other players. After a player publishes 5 manuscripts, the game goes into the Defense round, where players defend their manuscripts  and a voting round is held to vote for awards (giving bonus citations).  The player with the most citations after the voting, wins.

name: The Pursuit of John Wilkes Booth
description:
The sixteenth President of the United States has been shot at Ford’s Theatre in Washington, DC, and Abraham Lincoln’s near lifeless body is carried to the Peterson Boarding House across the street. Secretary-of-War Stanton springs into action. Well-known actor, John Wilkes Booth, has been identified as the culprit and earns his place as the most reviled villain in US history. Meanwhile, blocks away, Secretary-of-State Seward and his family have been savagely attacked by Booth’s accomplice, Lewis Powell. Soon other accomplices are identified, and the pursuit of Booth and his cronies begins in earnest.

In The Pursuit of John Wilkes Booth, players control Detectives searching for the assassin. Historically, Union authorities did not know where Booth might head since it would be reasonable to expect that Booth might go to Canada, the less-populated West, or to a Northern or Southern port with an eventual goal of reaching Europe, Mexico, or South America. As Detectives in the game, players must process Leads for Clues and uncover Booth’s Trail as he attempts his escape. Players may call on Stanton to aid them in their task. Detectives must eventually complete a successful Search and Raid on Booth’s exact location and win the game by killing or capturing him.

—description from the publisher

name: The Race: Das Brettspiel
description:
Get ready for an exciting journey across Europe. But beware! No journey is smooth sailing. Unexpected twists and turns, challenging obstacles and nerve-wracking decisions await you. Play strategically, stay flexible and use every opportunity to get ahead. The motto is: Be faster than the rest, reach the finish line first and win THE RACE!

In your turn you take the following steps:


     Spin the wheel of fortune
     Throw the dices to move forwards
     Draw an event card every time you reach a new city

name: Tag Team
publisher: Scorpion Masqué; asmodee; Geekach LLC; KOSMOS; Lavka Games; Lucky Duck Games; Reflexshop; YOKA Games
description:
Inspired by classic arcade-fighting games, Tag Team is an auto battler combined with a deck-building game. Make your team of two fighters from the twelve available — each with their own techniques and special moves — and build an unbeatable synergy by combining their two unique decks!

In more detail, you start with a deck of only two cards, and the fight unfolds automatically: Flip your cards one at a time and apply their effects. At the end of each round, you get to turn up the heat on the opposing team by strategically adding new cards to program your deck — but without reordering the cards already present. Determine what makes your tag team tick, play devastating combos, and dominate your opponent by deftly blocking their attacks. Timing is everything if you want to emerge victorious and knock out your foe!

AWARDS -
2025 - Best of Gen Con 2025

name: The Republic of Rome: Remastered
description:
The Republic of Rome Remastered is a game of negotiation, power and betrayal that simulates the 250 years of history between the First Punic War (264 B.C.) and the Civil War that followed the assassination of Julius Caesar (44 B.C.)

Each player will lead a political faction which includes senators from the most prominent families in the Republic. Players will compete against each other for government positions, economic concessions, control of the armies, and to attract new members to their faction, all with the ultimate goal of becoming the dominant political faction in Rome. Players will not only have to contend with each other, but also with the game itself, as Rome will be in constant danger. All players will lose the game if wars are not properly managed, if discontent turns into popular revolt, or if the Republic goes bankrupt. At the same time, players will have to cooperate closely to push through laws to manage internal politics and preserve social peace, declare wars to expand the borders of the Republic, or confront enemies who seek to destroy Rome. They will also have to compromise to attend to the recreational and religious needs of the people, purge the corrupt from office, and much, much more.

Thus, in order to win the game, players will need to balance service to Rome with personal gain. Usually, the faction with the most total influence will win the game, if Rome prevails. However, if a single senator stands out individually, he may aspire to become Dictator for life and achieve victory for his faction. The most dramatic and difficult path to victory is to revolt against the senate to seize power by force of arms.

This is an all-new edition that builds on the original and adds many new features that will make The Republic of Rome a fresh experience both for old and new players. These are the most relevant new features in The Republic of Rome Remastered:

    All the typos and inconsistencies in the previous edition have been corrected, and some rules that slowed down or overcomplicated gameplay have been streamlined.
    The game’s graphic design has been entirely reworked, including new illustrations for all the game components.
    For the first time, miniature busts are included to represent the main political offices in the game, while the option of using tokens is maintained for those who prefer them.
    The board has been fully redesigned to reduce the demand for table space, and all tables will be moved to a Play Aid for the Herald of the senate.
    New Event cards have been added and some of the existing ones have been modified. Additionally, a new Fate deck has been introduced to help balance Event results.
    The influence of games and religious affairs in the Republic has been emphasized.
    The rules have been completely rewritten and numerous examples have been added to facilitate learning and playing the game. In addition, a Playbook has been included with extended examples of play.
    A set of new optional rules has been developed to mitigate the influence of luck during the game.


We are also working on a new solitaire mode to streamline solo gameplay and on the introduction of improved bots for 2- and 3-player games. All this and much more awaits you in The Republic of Rome Remastered!

—description from the publisher

name: The Republic's Struggle
description:
The Republic's Struggle is a thematic game with card engine for 2 players, set during the historical events that took place in Spain after the resignation to the throne of King Alfonso XIII, and the proclamation of the II Spanish Republic, in 1931. With the creation of the new regime, the struggle for power between the different social, political and ideological sectors increased, which gave rise to continuous changes of political power, alterations of the public order, armed uprisings and violent acts, carried out by the numerous ideological factions of the moment; which culminated in 1936, in a failed military uprising. The failure of this coup d'état originated the Spanish Civil War.

The game represents all the events of this turbulent period in the history of Spain, which led to a bloody civil war and the destiny of the nation. Spain was not isolated from the rest of the world and especially from the old Europe, so it was a victim of the tensions of the so-called interwar period. During the development of a game, one player on the Republican side, and another on the National side, will be able to recreate events of the period to increase their popularity in the localities by carrying out political propaganda, recruiting troops or militias, generating revolts or assaults, establishing diplomatic relations or carrying out bloody bombardments. All this will be done by playing their hand of cards in an alternative way, either by increasing the events or by playing the action points or icons to perform any of the other actions available to the players.

But both factions will not only seek to control the country, but will also look abroad through diplomatic relations for international support. In the interior, localities of great importance are the localities of barracks, air bases and naval bases. Their control will give important advantages to the player faction for the control of the different fronts. But although Republic Struggle may be inspired by the famous Twilight Struggle, it is not a copy of this game but has its own independent spirit and enough differences and adaptations to the conflict it represents to make it an essential piece that cannot be missing in your toy library. The role of armies and armed roadblocks that can prevent political propaganda from spreading makes it all very interesting. In addition, armies can move from one front to another and defeating enemy armies will help you take control of certain regions even if the politically full people support your rival. And don't forget that it is possible to bombard your opponent.

—description from the publisher

name: The Restless
description:
The Restless takes place thirty years after a pantheon of gods betrayed humanity and condemned them to extinction. In the chaos that followed, panic and blame caused the great nations of the world to wage brutal crusades against themselves and their rivals. While humanity tore itself apart, the membrane that separated the mortal realm from the countless other dimensions of heaven, hell, and the places beyond, began to split open. All manner of cruel angels, grotesque demons, and unknowable creatures spilled into to mortal realm. What followed was not a war, but a frantic, internecine bloodbath that crushed the great kingdoms and drove their warbands to their graves. The world is a endless cemetery and only the dregs of humanity remain alive.  As the sun sets on the human race, a suffocating storm of ink black smoke appears on the far western horizon and begins sweeping across the world. Every living creature must run from the smoke or die. You must gather your party, collect meager equipment, and flee to the east. At the far end of the world, you will confront the gods that condemned your species to extinction. There is no hope for survival, but there is hope for revenge.

The Restless is a cooperative, dungeon-crawler style card game set during the final days of an infertility apocalypse. The game creates a uniquely challenging collaborative experience that pits a team of weak, resource-starved characters against an increasingly hostile world of shapeshifting monsters, bizarre traps, and treacherous environments. Players must move through 5 realms - with multiple fight encounters - to get to the Final Battle with the Traitor God.

After the final encounter in the Fifth Realm, the surviving party members arrive at the Rapturous East and the final battle.  They will have the choice of trying to defeat the Traitor God or not fighting (and lose)  If the Traitor God is defeated, the game is over.

—description from the designer

name: The Rock of Chickamauga
description:
The Rock of Chickamauga is the next game in the Black Swan series and follows closely on the heels of A Most Fearful Sacrifice. Using the same proven game system, The Rock of Chickamauga covers the entire Battle of Chickamauga, fought from September 18th through the 20th, 1863 in northern Georgia. The Union Army of the Cumberland, under William Rosecrans, is driving south from Chattanooga, hoping to envelop and trap Braxton Bragg’s Confederate Army of Tennessee in its vise. But Bragg anticipates the maneuver, pulls back and then counterattacks the overextended Union forces. They meet along Chickamauga Creek, the “River of Death”, in an epic struggle.

This scenario-driven, two-player war-game utilizes the ACW operating system called the Black Swan system, which is closely related to the  Blind Swords game system first introduced in the game The Devil’s To Pay!. This version of the system is specifically designed to handle larger-scale battles yet keep rules overhead low. players will trigger activations by Corps instead of by lower-level formations but they still have tactical decision-making choices by needing to determine which Divisions get activation priority. Players will use card draws rather than chit pulls.

name: The Dark Quarter
publisher: Lucky Duck Games; Van Ryder Games; Grimspire
description:
Welcome to New Orleans, Louisiana, circa 1980: a vibrant city of music, food, and magic. Neon lights flicker in dirty puddles up and down Bourbon street; the innovations of the modern world clash with ancient and terrible traditions; and murder is never simple. The Beaumont Agency, staffed with a roster of brilliant, colorful, and ultimately ﬂawed private investigators, specializes in solving cases that no one else can crack.

In The Dark Quarter, a co-operative app-driven adventure game set in a dark, fantastical vision of 1980s New Orleans, players each take control of a Beaumont agent and work alongside one another to solve the worst crimes that New Orleans has to offer. It's a world full of magic, where hexing curses are sold on every street, where voodoo priestesses and creatures of the night are lurking around every corner, and where even the most mundane crimes have a tinge of the supernatural to them.

Through multi-scenario campaigns, the game tells a rich, dynamic story and invites players to make critical decisions that will not only affect their characters, but change the direction and course of the story. The characters are not simply avatars, easily replaceable from scenario to scenario; instead, they are woven into the very fabric of the story itself. Their destiny and the destiny of New Orleans are inextricably linked together.

—description from the publisher

name: The Smurfs: Hidden Village
publisher: Maestro Media; Last Level; Lucky Duck Games
description: In The Smurfs: Hidden Village, players are Smurfs who are tasked with rebuilding the mushroom village from scratch following the evil sorcerer Gargamel's latest scheme. To succeed, you need to work together as a team, collecting resources, building inventions, and locating missing Smurfs to help rebuild mushroom houses. Each Smurf has a unique set of skills that you must use strategically to outsmart Gargamel and his cat Azrael.

name: The Royal Study
description:
Look over the current situation, and try to get to the new situation in as few moves as possible. But beware! If your opponent can do it fewer moves, they get the points.

This game uses familiar chess pieces to make a series of challenging puzzles, where both speed and economy of movement are required to win.

name: Borealis: Arctic Expeditions
publisher: Lucky Duck Games; Gém Klub Kft.; Kobold Spieleverlag
description:
Become the leaders of scientific teams venturing into uncharted boreal territories to observe and photograph the Arctic’s most adorable inhabitants.

Play cards from your hand to one of 3 locations on your player board to snap a photo and send your scientists sliding to the left and to the right - but only if their colors match the ones printed on your card!

Line up vehicle symbols, race to claim objectives, and arrange animals in pre-determined end-game scoring patterns to earn the most points and gain everlasting fame at the Society for Polar Inquiry. Who knows? Maybe you’ll even get your own tiny snow-covered island named after you.

—description from the publisher

name: The Secrets of Zorro
description:
California, 1840.
The legendary Zorro has been missing for months. The sad truth is that Don Diego de la Vega, the man behind the mask, has died among his loved ones. Taking advantage of this absence, the new governor has started to put his devious plan into action: he's oppressing the people to fuel his power grab in California. But he didn't anticipate the heirs of the masked vigilante — you!
Together, you must work to topple the Governor before his scheme succeeds. You'll need to step into the shoes of vigilantes, sharpening your slyness and combat skills. With guidance from Zorro's teachings and the secrets he left, you'll fight to continue his legacy of justice.

The Secrets of Zorro is a light strategy game with hidden information, some placement, many cards and combos.

—description from the publisher

name: The Shackleton Series: Interactive Puzzle Adventure
description:
Solve an epic adventure.

The Shackleton Series is a 6-episode (1-2 hours/episode) puzzle game that blends escape rooms and board games with historical fiction. The storyline follows the true account of how 28 men got trapped in Antarctica...for 2 years.

As the player, you will get transported to 1914 where you join Ernest Shackleton's historic crew. This voyage is often described as one of the greatest survival stories of all time. Will you survive the harsh landscape of Antarctica in this 6-episode interactive puzzle adventure?

—description from the publisher

name: The Shadow Theater: The Legend of the Monkey King
description:
The curtain rises. A monkey hatches from a stone egg. He becomes known as the Monkey King Sun Wukong and travels west in search of the secret of immortality.

The Shadow Theater is a fast and exciting two-player family-friendly competitive game. Deploy your monkeys, harvest the sweet fruits of eternal life, hoard jade stones, and become a legend! To win, you have to play tactically and seize your chance. To help you, you can gain some advantages with the powerful dragon weapons. Are you ready to dive into an ancient legend?

Dive into the legend of the Monkey King in a strategic duel filled with cunning and challenges!

name: The Sims Board Game
description:
Join your friends and family — and memorable Sims from years past — in The Sims Board Game as you chart your journey. Will you create chaos and try to outrun Grim, or aim for career success? What will you do next when you have to start all over again? The possibilities are endless as you explore familiar venues, connect with iconic Sims, and achieve your aspirations to claim victory!

Gather up to 5 players as you each craft your own story while collecting matching SIMbols along the way. Dive into the neighborhood, meet iconic Sims, and fulfill your life’s aspirations like never before!

—description from the publisher

name: The Six
description:
The Six is a fast paced card collection game. The aim is to be the first to collect 6 of the same character to win, with the current characters being spooky themed.

2 to 6 players can play the game and there are 88 cards in a standard deck. Each player starts the game with 6 cards in their hand, drawing from the main deck, discarding cards and playing action cards to prevent other players from winning.

—description from the designer

name: Chronicles of Crime: Courtroom Justice
description:
You're no longer hunting suspects. You're defending them. All rise.

For the first time in the Chronicles of Crime series, take on the role of a defense attorney instead of a detective. The evidence has been gathered, the suspects arrested, but you're not convinced the prosecution has the whole story.

A solo or cooperative team investigate to find clues and solve the mystery.  But remember, time waits for no one!

Each Chronicle of Crime is a standalone game with it's own settings,  rules, and components.  An app is used to deliver the game scenarios and time the game.

-description from publisher

name: The Smoky Valley
description:
The Smoky Valley is a complex economic and industrial development game set along the historic Lachine Canal in the Griffintown neighborhood of Montréal, Canada.

In The Smoky Valley, you are a 19th-century investor helping to elevate Griffintown as a prominent industrial hub in North America by building and upgrading industries, producing and transforming goods, and shipping products abroad.

Beyond these efforts for Griffintown's prosperity and your personal fortune, you’ll need to stimulate the city’s development to enhance economic activities. You'll also collaborate with other investors to construct the Victoria Bridge and earn valuable bonuses—but only one of you will claim the ultimate reward.

Do you have what it takes to be remembered as the greatest builder in The Smoky Valley?

This new edition of The Smoky Valley offers an entirely fresh experience. All city cards have been enhanced, canal tiles and districts now generate new combos, and canal development opens up new options for direct warehouse and train delivery in McCord and St. Ann.

—description from the publisher

name: Chronicles of Crime: Cryptid Cases
description:
1990s small-town America. They say nothing exciting ever happens here. And yet, something unspeakable has happened in the woods...

You're part of the FBI's Paranormal Division. A small, elite force trained to see through folklore, but wise enough to know every legend often has a seed of truth. The locals stay quiet. The sheriff says it's all just bedtime stories. It's your job to separate fact from fiction - even if it means questioning everything you thought you knew.

A solo or cooperative team investigate to find clues and solve the mystery.  But remember, time waits for no one!

Each Chronicle of Crime is a standalone game with it's own settings,  rules, and components.  An app is used to deliver the game scenarios and time the game.

—description from publisher

name: The Source CCG
description:
The Source CCG is a deck building game with both Collectible Cards and an app for users to create their own cards to be submitted add official. It also functions as the battle mechanism for the Tabletop component.

The goal of both games is to eliminate your opponents Source Orb, capture all opposing Character Cards, or perform a win-condition set of actions from your deck. In addition, the Tabletop Game has scenarios chosen by both competing players or the Lore Master that allow a user to win. (Ex. Capture the Ark of Aena to Win)

The Tabletop game functions as the most comprehensive way to play in that it allows for various game styles similar to MOBAs, RTS, and DnD.

—description from the designer

name: The Spanish-American War, 1898
description:
Spanish-American War, 1898 is a two-player game of the Spanish-American War of 1898 by Vance von Borries. It recreates the strategic naval and land campaign against Spanish forces in Cuba and Puerto Rico. One player controls the American and Cuban units, while the other controls the Spanish ones. The game is played in game turns, consisting of alternating player turns in which each player moves his pieces and resolves any resulting combat. When all the game turns have been completed, the game is over, and the winner is determined.

The game is divided into separate but closely related land and sea systems. A campaign game combines both of these into one strategic game. The introductory scenarios should be played before attempting the full Campaign Game. Some specially marked land and sea rules apply only to the Campaign Game. You can ignore them when you play introductory scenarios. The Campaign Game uses all the rules. Using separate land and sea commanders, up to four players can play the Campaign Game.

Product Information:

Complexity: Medium
Playing time: 3 to 6 hours
Solitaire Suitability: Medium
Players: Two to Four (suitable for solitaire play)
Map Scale: variable (for both areas and hexes based on map)
Time Scale: 1 Turn = 20 Minutes
Unit Scale: 1 Unit = 1 ship or battalion/regiment

—description from the publisher

name: The Strange Forgeries of Mr. S.C.Rheber
description:
The Strange Forgeries Of Mr. S.C. Rheber is a game about forging art using the scientific method.

is a Game Of Induction wherein 2-6 players (the Collectors) will purchase art from their Gallerist trying to fill their museums. However some of the paintings are fakes crafted by the talented forger Simon Charles Rheber. The Collectors will master their inductive reasoning to determine which painting is one of the strange forgeries of Mr. S.C.Rheber.

				
				
					OverviewThe Gallerist invents a secret rule and it’s the Collectors’ objective is to guess it. During the game, the Collectors will produce many Drawings, and the Gallerist will secretly tell them whether it follows the secret rule or not, aka whether the Drawings are Originals or Fakes.
At the end of the game, the Collectors will put their knowledge to the test, and try to guess whether their opponents' displayed Drawings follow the rule or not. Mistakes determine the winner, so they’ll want to try to make as few Mistakes as possible. The Gallerist moderates the game giving out hints as they like.

				
				
					What Makes It UniqueOut of more than 100,000 games and hundreds of different mechanics, induction-based games rank among the rarest 5%, making them some of the industry’s most unusual and peculiar designs. They are, in fact, the only type of games in which players themselves create part of the rules.
Among these, Strange Forgeries stands out as the most radical example, offering unparalleled freedom through several innovations centered on its unique use of the drawing mechanic.

name: The String Railway Collection
description:
Originally published in 2009 and designed by Hisashi Hayashi (Yokohama, Trains, Metro X), String Railway is a 20-minute game in which players create their own map directly onto the table, complete with borders, mountains and rivers, then build atop it a network of railways, all made out of string.

The sequel String Railway: Transport (now renamed String Railway: Cubed) combined the premise of String Railway with the weighty decision-making of games like Railways of the World, producing a mid-weight 45-minute game. In the game, players start with a map of stations already built and must balance the desire to upgrade their engines, and fulfill bespoke delivery contracts, with the need to quickly build a flexible train network that can transport goods to a range of destinations.

The String Railway Collection packs both of these standalone games into a single small-box package and features vibrant updated artwork, improved graphic design, and a refined ruleset.

-description from publisher

name: The Thinning Veil: Cormac Mac Airt on the Other Side of Midnight
description:
A solo dungeon crawling adventure game now featuring a 2 player mode, set in the world of The Thinning Veil & featuring Cormac Mac Airt, High King of Inis Fael!

Learn the game in a highly replayable 3 act path as Young Cormac! Then play 'On the Other Side of Midnight' consisting of a four act path playable as Cormac in solo, Grainne in solo, or as father & daughter together! Heed the call to adventure, on the Other Side of Midnight!

Inspired by Celtic mythology and the folklore of the British Isles, this game uses the Thinning Veil game mechanics, and is compatible with all future releases. It is a rogue-like game with narrative trigger points that uses a tile stack system, ensuring a lot of replayability.

—description from the publisher

name: The Third Man
description:
Footsteps echo through the alleys of New York—who ate our pizza?
As players lay down their cards, suspicion and strategy deepen with each trick.

The Third Man is a trick-taking game for 3–4 players, where the goal is to avoid collecting suspicion—represented by penalty points. The rules are simple: play the highest-numbered card of each suit. But as the game progresses, players must carefully choose their moves to shift suspicion onto others. When the pressure rises, escaping the scene might be your only option.

Stand your ground to prove your innocence. In the end, the player with the most penalty points is condemned as The Third Man—the pizza thief.

Quick to play but rich in mind games, this suspenseful and darkly humorous game is all about dodging blame and turning the tables.

name: The Tragedy of Othello
description:
"The Tragedy of Othello" is a Tragic and Treacherous Shakespeare-themed card game. In The Tragedy of Othello, you and your opponents are actors auditioning for the lead role of the villainous Iago, trying to impress the casting director with your ability to embody Iago’s treachery and deceit! You will play script cards from the cast of characters to gain points as you advance Shakespeare’s script, and play staging cards to disrupt the play of your rivals. Also play intrigue tokens, character coins and spotlight tokens to strategically improve your position. When you control the lead character, Iago, your opportunities to gain points increase.

Alas, opportunities also exist to steal points, so take heed: opponents playing the other characters as 'The Company' may try to upstage you! The actor who accumulates the most points at the end of Act V wins the game by stealing the spotlight and landing the role of Iago!

No Shakespeare knowledge required.

-description from publisher

name: The Trash Travelers
description:
The Trash Travelers: A Cooperative Adventure to Save the Ocean!

Based on a true story, you will embark on an extraordinary journey with "The Trash Traveler" to save the world's most important ecosystem: the ocean. 
The game takes you as a team on a thrilling adventure through picturesque landscapes that are flooded with trash. On your clean up journey, you save endangered animals, meet experts and scientists to understand the complexity of environmental issues, and use creativity to find solutions and inspire people.
While trying to clean up the planet, we learn along the journey that it is not about cleaning but about working together and achieving common goals.
The Trash Travelers invites you to dive deep into ocean and climate issues, making every play an educational and impactful experience. Work together, make strategic decisions, and see our world become a better place, one step at a time.
Your mission: Raise awareness and inspire as many people as possible to save our base to life - a healthy ocean.

Highlights:
Cooperative Gameplay: Work as a team to find solutions and achieve common goals.
Educational Fun: Learn about plastic pollution and environmental issues.
Dynamic Challenges: Face unique obstacles and save animals.
Creative Outcomes: Deliver trash to artists and witness art come to life.
Impactful Story: Raise awareness and contribute to a better planet.

name: The Treasure Ship of Zheng He
description:
In The Treasure Ship of Zheng He, players become commanders of the Zheng He fleet and aim to contribute to his grand voyage.

The game lasts seven rounds, with each round representing one of Zheng He's voyages. At the start of a round, players visit the High Officials, choosing one of them in turn. The higher the rank of the official you visit, the better the gift that you must offer them, and the better the items you receive in exchange.

Whoever visited the highest ranked official goes first in the planning phase, choosing which leg of the voyage they will captain. More specifically, in turn players claim one of the 3-4 face-down voyage cards, with the leftmost leg being the first part of the voyage away from China.

In order from left to right, the appropriate captain for each leg reveals their card, takes the number of ships indicated, and places them on the main game board, leading everyone away from China. If a fork is present on the game board, the captain decides where the voyage goes. The voyage card might have actions on it, or the voyage might stop at a port, which also has actions. The captain places the lead ship token on the space they want, then all other players can choose one of the smaller action spaces — unless they have an "Emperor's directive" that lets them use the same action as the captain. If you encounter pirates, the captain can try to fight or bribe them, moving up the military track or gaining rewards if successful, or they can decline to fight, which ends their turn.

As you take actions, you can gain resources, gold, and weapons; trade with merchants; send out diplomats to raise your diplomatic level (which nets you rewards and possible endgame points); and collect animals, trying to cover as much of your player board as possible. If you have the funds, you can build a monument, which lets you repeat the action on which you build; build next to one of your earlier monuments, and you take that action, too.

Once all players have been captain in turn, you start the next voyage, and after seven voyages, you take a final trip to the High Officials — or by offering two of each rare good, you can get a grand reward from the Emperor himself. In the end, the player who contributes the most to Zheng He's voyages wins.

name: The Tricktaker's Guide To The Galaxy
description:
Across the galaxy, countless civilizations have devised their own unique trick-taking games and now, their rules are gathered in one cosmic compendium. Players compete as interstellar editors, wagering precious coins to determine which risky and eccentric rules to include before diving into a single, universal game of galactic trick-taking.

The Tricktaker's Guide To The Galaxy is a trick-taking game for 3–5 players that combines traditional play with an innovative pre-game auction. Before the main game begins, players enter an Editing Phase, where they use coins (which also serve as points) to bid for or avoid strange and risky rule cards that modify gameplay.

Once all rules are assigned, players proceed to a single trick-taking phase using a standard deck of playing cards with must-follow and trump mechanics. Success depends on carefully balancing risk and reward, fulfilling the conditions of the rules you’ve accepted while navigating the shifting chaos of galactic house rules.

name: The Twelfth Battle: the Caporetto Campaign 1917
description:
The Twelfth Battle is a solitaire wargame that simulates the Central Powers offensive in Italy that began on October 24th, 1917, with an all-out assault around the town of Caporetto. Using gas and stormtroopers, German and Austro-Hungarian formations assaulted the Italian defensive lines along the Isonzo River and around the town of Caporetto, creating a huge breach in their positions. Hundreds of thousands of Italian troops, demoralized and fatigued from the first eleven attritional battles along the Isonzo, were made casualties or surrendered.

In this game, you play as the Central Powers forces and must attempt to achieve a level of success exceeding that which they were able to historically obtain.

name: The UFO Disclosure Game: We are not alone
description:
You have realized that the UFO phenomenon is real, and you want to get to the bottom of it, bringing it to the attention of the whole world. But you can't do it by yourself. You must acquire knowledge and credibility by collecting evidence and persuading individuals with high credibility to validate the evidence, all while avoiding the stigma and potential pitfalls of the path. The whole game is an amazing travel through real UFO/UAP cases that happened worldwide!

Each player chooses a different character who has a specific background related to the phenomenon of UAP/UFOs and starts his globetrotting from the continent where her/his character was born. To fulfil his mission, each player moves on the board, launching a die to travel around the world to collect the best UFO events. At the same time, the player needs to meet qualified persons who could confirm your evidence. Be aware that skeptics, debunkers, and other traps will try to stop you!

As soon as you have an event matching a specific qualified person (e.g., a scientist), you have access to the “Disclosure’s Path." The trivia starts there: you need to prove your knowledge about the topic, answering some questions about the history of the UFO phenomenon while defending your reputation with media!
Though everyone is building their own collection of UFO case investigation, the game offers ways for players to interfere with each other.

The first player who collects three different confirmations can handle the truth and can expose her/his theory to humankind, winning the run for the final disclosure!

—description from the designer

name: Chronicles of Crime: Eldritch Secrets
description:
Chronicles of Crime has never dared to tread this path - until now. Follow a team of investigators as they take to the fog-drenched streets of Arkham, and the shadowed halls of Miskatonic University.

Set in the 1920s, this Lovecraftian storyline explores cases no sane detective would touch - disappearances tied to forgotten cults, mysteries of otherworldly artifacts, and encounters that defy the rules of reality.

A solo or cooperative team investigate to find clues and solve the mystery.  But remember, time waits for no one!

Each Chronicle of Crime is a standalone game with it's own settings,  rules, and components.  An app is used to deliver the game scenarios and time the game.

-description from publisher

name: FLOE
publisher: PIKA Games; Gém Klub Kft.; Lucky Duck Games; Maldito Games; Rebel Sp. z o.o.; Skellig Games; Ігромаг
description:
FLOE is an adventure-strategy game where players embark on heroic quests across an icy landscape. You’ll discover long-lost secrets on uncharted icebergs, sail the seas to find adventure and sunken treasure and delve into perilous caves to find precious crystals and battle fearsome monsters.  Despite the dangers ahead, you won’t be alone in your travels. Always at your side, your loyal familiar may help gather resources or jump into the fray to turn the tide of battle. During their travels, heroes will also gain helpful allies, powerful abilities, and rare items. In time, heroes may also build shrines across the map, ensuring their legacy will be long remembered. However, always beware of the cold. Venturing into the icy wasteland is perilous: almost everything heroes do outside the safety of the village will cost them warmth. From time to time, they will need to return to the village to warm up, improve their homestead, purchase upgrades, and prepare for their next big adventure. Will you be the boldest explorer of them all?

Floe features a unique region-to-region movement system that allows heroes and sailboats to navigate the realm with ease; only the natural shapes of the ice and seas are used to determine movement, so you never need to count squares on a grid.
