The first player to finish the final lap claims the title of quickest critter in the city!

—description from the designer

name: Trash to Table
description:
You are a hungry, hungry rat, but the hard part of your pizza heist is finally over: You have obtained your coveted greasy, cheesy slices. No matter how you ethically sourced your slices (kid's birthday party in Central Park, late-night leftovers from the frat basement, sad scraps in the office kitchenette) all that za is going to the same place — down the sewer grate to feed your rat families, friends, and situationships.

And when your hard-earned pizza slice hits that sewer floor, you **want it landing faceup!**

From there, place those faceup slices on table cards, guessing how many slices each card needs to sate the appetites of your rat brethren.


     CARD AND DICE PARTY GAME ABOUT PIZZA. AND RATS: Play as a pizza-fiending rat in the Trash to Table game, a fast and fun push-your-luck game! Feed fellow rats by tossing pizza down the sewer grate – and place bets to win.
     7 RAT-APPROVED “PIZZA SLICE” DICE: The plastic molded dice are each shaped like different pizza slices with hilarious toppings. Like Meatball Surprise (topped with a cockroach surprise!)
     BUILT-IN SEWER GRATE DICE TOWER: Open the game to find a built-in “sewer grate”! Is there anything more thrilling than dropping pizza dice down it? No, we say! Every toss brings edge-of-your-seat anticipation. How many slices will land faceup?


HOW TO PLAY: 

     Toss pizza dice down the sewer grate dice tower.
     Using only the dice that land faceup, bet on how many slices will feed the rats hidden on the back of each card. Guess correctly to earn points.
     The first to 22 wins


—description from the publisher

name: Traumatarium Deckulus
description:
Traumatarium Deckulus is a solo dungeon crawler card game. Based on the Traumatarium [Game Boy] game, Deckulus puts a dungeon in your pocket. Quick to set up and play, each card tells a story!

Almost everything you need comes inside the deck box!

Only thing needed are some dice for tracking health and items, and a D6 for the rolls. The cards will complete the narrative of your journey.

—description from the publisher

name: Travelers: Tokyo
description:
In Travelers: Tokyo, 2-5 players will enjoy a weekend in Tokyo. Over the course of 3 days will they explore the city and use the existing metro and train network to travel to the most interesting places. They will gain souvenirs when they do, eat, see or buy something. To do this, players will have to manage their time, money and energy. Additionally, there are cultural experiences, events and missions.
When the weekend is over, the player with the most souvenirs, culture, missions and placed visited first will win the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Dead Man's Draw: 10-Year Anniversary Edition
description:
Dead Man's Draw is a simple and strategic card game of risk and reward for 2 to 4 players. Players take turns drawing cards and combining their special abilities to plunder the most loot without busting their entire hands.

The core of your turn in Dead Man’s Draw is all in the flip: pulling the top card off the deck and using its special ability. Your turn isn’t over until you say it is, though. You can keep pulling cards as long as you like – until you play a card of a suit already seen, at which point you lose everything. Knowing when to stop and "bank" your cards is the biggest decision you make in Dead Man’s Draw, but being too timid lets braver opponents pass you up with bigger, more profitable turns.

The cards’ special abilities are key to success in Dead Man’s Draw, and they build off of each other. Each suit in DMD has an effect that the player can target when they flip a card of that suit.

Anchor – Keep everything you drew before the Anchor even if you bust.

Cannon – Destroy one card an opponent has previously banked.

Chest – Double your haul by banking as many cards directly from the discard pile as are in the river when you bank the Chest – but only if you also bank a Key.

Hook – Play one of your previously banked cards.

Key – Enables the Chest special.

Kraken – Oh no! You’re forced to draw at least two more cards.

Map – Draw three cards from the discard pile and play one.

Mermaid – No ability, but worth more points (Mermaids are numbered 4-9 instead of 2-7).

Oracle – Look at the next card before deciding if you want to play it.

Sword – Steal an opponent’s previously banked card and play it.

Many of these work well together, like using a Hook to re-play a Sword from your hand to steal an opponent’s Chest to go with your Key – racking up huge points by playing abilities well and not solely through the luck of the draw.

As soon as the deck is depleted, players total up the value of the highest card they’ve banked from each suit. High score wins.

This 10-year anniversary edition features:

Addition of the 4-sided "bone die" used in the expanded game play
Three additional "Death" cards
Three additional "Storm" cards
Six additional "Swashbuckler" cards
4 larger (127 x 153mm) Active Swashbuckler/Completed Cards
Longer rulebook to include all the extra gameplay and variants

All in a tin box!

—description from the publisher

name: Trench Crusade
description:
Trench Crusade is a skirmish-scale tabletop miniatures game that will plunge players deep into a horrifying alternate timeline.  During the Crusades at 1066, a heretical band of Templars dared defy the Almighty and, casting aside their sacred vows, unleashed the forces of Hell upon the Earth. Over 800 years later, in the Year of Our Lord 1914, this brutal, merciless war between the forces of Heaven and Hell rages on. This is not just a fight for survival, but a cataclysmic struggle that will decide the very fate of humanity's soul.

Set in a blasphemously alternate WW1 era, players take command of the forces of heaven and hell, leading skirmish size warbands in daring assaults and devious counter operations. From the humble bolt action rifle to the bones of cursed saints, you can tailor each loadout to complement your play style and your miniatures, making each of your troops unique.

Players activate their models in alternating order to fight their way across the battlefield. Actions are resolved by rolling two D6s. There are more unpredictable modifiers, however, that will ebb and flow as the battle draws on and these come from the game’s main mechanic: Blood and Blessings.

—description from the publisher

name: Trench Raid: Solitaire Patrol Command on the WW1 Western Front
description:
Trench Raid is a single-player game set on the Western Front in World War One. The player assembles a group of 10 raiders and plots their course on a map towards the enemy lines on the other side of No Man’s Land. With 12 different raid objectives and 20 random events that can take place during the crossing, no two playthroughs will be exactly the same.

The game also includes rules for campaign play — whether their raid was successful or not, the soldiers who make it back to their trench lines relatively unscathed will steadily get better at raiding, learning through experience how to survive.

“The generals would want to know which German units were in the line opposite you. And so they’d send up the order for us to raid. ‘Go get prisoners,’ they’d say. We knew it was a waste of time, and we hated it, but we did it. The idea was to crawl through the wire and jump into the enemy trench. We had to be quiet, so we fought with our bayonets, or with a studded club or the butt of our rifle. If we weren’t quick, the enemy would shout, and then the fun would start. Our bomber would throw a Mills bomb into the next bay, and after it went off the rifleman would dash forward and dispose of anyone who was left.”  -British officer Murray Rymer-Jones

Complexity: Low
Playing time: 1 Hour Per Raid
Solitaire Suitability: Very High (Designed For Solitaire)
Players: 1
Map Scale: 1 Hex = Several Yards
Time Scale: 1 Game = 1 Raid
Unit Scale: Individuals

—description from the publisher

name: Trials of Maya
description:
Trials of MAYA is a expandable card‑driven combat game where you command champions across an arena using customizable decks.

Each Champion has their own personality and several potential playstyles, breaking the game in exciting and unique ways. Playing around your enemies’ strengths is as vital as exploiting your own.

Pick from several game modes, each with its own arena and rules. Each game mode requires varying game plans, and rewards different kinds of tactical skill.

Each Champion comes with a starter deck, but you may also freely construct your deck instead before each game begins! Customize your deck based on the playstyle you feel comfortable with.

Pilot your hero, manage your energy well, chain together mind-boggling combos, and strike at the most opportune of moments to win!

About MAYA:
MAYA is an epic high-fantasy universe unfolding over films, games, graphic novels, books, toys, immersive and physical experiences. MAYA chronicles the paradoxes of a civilization where technological marvels coexist with primitive suffering - across the chasm of haves and have-nots.

MAYA is a new mythology for the new age. Enter MAYA with Trials of MAYA.

-description from publisher

name: Tribulation
description:
Tribulation is a scenario-driven cooperative tactical card game with a dark, biblically-inspired fantasy setting for 1-2 players. You play as an agent of the Lord holding the forces of evil at bay at the end of the world to give humanity one last chance.

In Tribulation you succeed if you vanquish the forces of evil before they defeat you and your teammate. In a solo game, you control two agents of the Lord. If both are destroyed before you can vanquish your foes, you lose. The primary mechanism of Tribulation is tactical combat via card play and action management. You move your character through 3 zones, play cards from your hand to resolve actions, and rest to regain action points, cards and health at strategic intervals. Tribulation can be played as a one-off battle game or a progressive campaign-style game with an advancing narrative and character progression between battles.

—description from the rulebook

name: Trick or Bid
description:
Trick or Bid is a trick-taking game for 3-4 hungry players trick-or-treating for cards and candy. Players must make interesting choices when they win a trick in this game, whether the trick will be counted towards the tricks they won for the hand or if one of the cards in the trick will become their bid.

—description from the publisher

name: Trick Tac Toe
description:
Trick Tac Toe is a 10 card microgame where two players play for best two out of three tricks in order to claim a space on the board. You could concede early, giving your opponent the space, but then you get to control the next spot to play for.

There are no suits, but a simple rule twist where the 1 can beat the highest three cards makes each situation a bit of a threat. Once a player hits three in a row or wins five of the spaces on the board, the game has ended.

—description from the designer

name: Trick Tac Toe: A Cat's Game
description:
Trick-taking and area control collide in Trick Tac Toe: A Cat's Game. The goal of this two player competitive game is to mark your territory by placing three control markers in a straight line.

After each trick resolves, whomever played the strongest card then places a control marker on a contested location. Whomever, played the weakest, will activate the ability of the location itself.

name: Trickadee
description:
Trickadee is a clever trick-taking game where sometimes you win by coming in last. Play birds to the feeder and collect them into flocks. Cleverly play the right birds to come in first, third, or last place to gain abilities that allow you to make better flocks.

—description from the designer

name: Empire Builder: Europe
description:
Empire Builder: Europe invites you to embark on a strategic rail-building journey across the European continent.

The game board unfolds to reveal a map of Europe, segmented into dots. Armed with grease pencils, players strategically connect these dots, constructing an intricate network of railways that spans mountains, rivers, and cities.

Dive into the challenge of managing your cash as you deliver commodity-laden trains across the continent. A stack of demand cards dictates the values of transporting specific goods to their designated cities. The farther the distance traveled, the greater the financial rewards. Choose your routes wisely, balancing the demands of efficiency and profitability.

As your rail empire grows, so does your earning potential. Expand your network, link major cities, and adapt your strategy to the dynamic market demands. Will you focus on high-yield cargo over long distances, or opt for shorter, more frequent deliveries to build a steady income? Watch out for disasters that might hit—floods, storms, strikes, and more await in the demand deck.

Empire Builder: Europe combines the excitement of strategic planning with the dynamic challenges of economic development. The ultimate goal is to amass a predetermined fortune and successfully connect almost all the major cities, solidifying your status as a rail tycoon.

name: Makoto
description:
Makoto, which means “sincerity" in Japanese, is a climbing card game with hidden depths and beautiful illustrations that show the journey of a Ronin through the countryside of Japan. Each player starts a round with a hand of cards that range from 1-16, and a number of cards are dealt face up in the center of the table as a "blind".

The lead player of a round plays a combination — a set of one or more cards of the same value or a run of at least three cards — then players in turn either play the same combination (with at least one higher card) or pass, which does not remove you from the round. A four-of-a-kind — a Kensei — can be played over any combination and is beaten only by a higher Kensei. When all players pass in turn, the round ends, and whoever played last collects the played cards and leads the next round.

After playing on your turn, you can discard to the blind one card from your hand that's lower than anything you played, or you can pick up cards from the blind as long as they're the same value, lower than what you played, and at most the same number of cards you played.

When you've emptied your hand, you receive a bonus, with the bonus diminishing for those who go out later. After all but one person has gone out, players score for the cards they've collected — but only for 2s, 5s, and 10s. After a certain number of rounds, whoever has the highest score wins.

Makoto is all about cleverly improving your hand cards and weighing when to continue playing versus when to pass.

name: Tricky Landing
description:
The circus has come to town, and the troupe of clowns have an extravaganza prepared. All participants are ready for a series of death-defying stunts as they are fired from colorful cannons across the big top. Who will make the most spectacular landings and put their competitors to shame?

Find out in Tricky Landing, a dexterity-based trick-taking game in which rather than play cards, you throw cards toward a target card! Make a successful landing for your card to be part of the trick, with the order in which cards land determining the lead suit. Miss the target and you'll set the trump for the next trick, but if more than one player misses the target, you all take a penalty.

Play three rounds to determine which death-defying clowns have put on the best performance.

—description from the designer

name: Tricky Seasons: Finland
description:
Tricky Seasons takes trick-taking, tic-tac-toe and bidding and blends them together! The rules are easy to grasp, but each round offers a unique challenge that will need strategic thinking. Immerse yourself in this delightful journey through the Finnish landscapes as you compete in the Battle of Seasons.

The aim in each game round is to score as many points as you can by getting your player number into complete lines of dice of the same colour on the Gameboard and correctly bidding to predict your score for the round.

End of the game
The standard game lasts for as many Rounds as there are players.
Alternatively, you may play until someone has scored an agreed number of VP. In lieu of any other decision we recommend 13VP, which typically takes 2-3 hands. 
Whoever has the most VP wins.
In the case of a tie, whoever scored more VP in the final Round wins. If it’s still a tie, it is a joint victory.

name: Tricky Time Crisis: the Spawn of Time
description:
Sequel to Tricky Time Crisis. Dr. Tricky Time's daughter seeks revenge in this trick taking game with missions.

Tricky Time Crisis: the Spawn of Time is a must not follow trick-taking game. During each trick, each player must play a different suit represented by different super heroes and a super villain.

Players are split into the hero and villain team depending on which card they played. One team will be the winner of the trick and the winners may take cards to their score pile first, while the losers must take a card to their score pile after the winners get their first pick.

Scoring at the end of the hand is dependant on how many cards of each suit a player has in their score pile. If a player has a single card of a suit in their score pile, they score points equal to the printed number on that card. If a player has 2 or more cards in the same suit, they score 2 points per card.

Unlike in the first Tricky Time Crisis, heroes cannot win just with high numbers alone. This new villain, Dr. Tricky Task, instead gives missions to the heroes such as telling them what their final sum should be, or making all heroes play the same number.

—description from the publisher

name: Historica Arcanum: Cults of London
description:
Cults of London is an Asymmetric Deck Builder & Area Control Hybrid set in the Award winning Historical Dark fantasy setting of Historica Arcanum. Set in the Victorian London, players will take on the role of factions vying for the control of the arcane society of the city. Every turn, you will match your operators with actions and locations to send them on missions to gather resources, eliminate enemy opponents, and fulfill victory conditions. Before the missions commence, you and your enemies will have a chance to uncover aspects of each mission. After all, knowledge is power.

—description from the publisher

name: Tricky Treats
publisher: Cranio Creations; 999 Games; Elznir Games; Maldito Games
description:
Trick or Treats? Tricky Treats!
Dress up your children with funny and colorful costumes to collect sweets and play tricks!

In the game each player will create the costumes on their board by combining transparent cards with hats, tops and bottoms.

It is possible to create matching outfits in order to score points at the end of the game but also get weird combinations to collect different icons that will be useful during the game to collect more sweets and play tricks.
Tricks will activate end-game scoring mechanisms.

The game ends when a player has visited 8 houses.

—description from the publisher

name: Tricky Twist
publisher: Gém Klub Kft.; Gotcha Gotcha Games; Sit Down!
description:
In Tricky Twist, losing tricks can often be more important than winning them. If you manage to retrieve the card you played, it comes back to you face up as a “false trick.” To multiply your victory points (★), you must not only balance the number of tricks and false tricks you have but also optimize the cards you’ve transformed into false tricks. For example, you might try to align all your false tricks into a perfect sequence of values. Simply devilish…

—description from the publisher

name: Trigger Warning
description:
A high-stakes memory game where strategy and risk-taking determine your survival. Outsmart your opponents by making calculated moves, shooting wisely, and using your resources to your advantage.

In Trigger Warning, you have one goal: be the last survivor.

Players build an 8-card gun magazine from a set of 13 chamber cards (6 CLIC and 7 POW!). On their turn, they may use any number of items and then target another player or themselves. Lose all 3 life tokens, and you’re eliminated. The game continues until only one player remains.

Items are used to heal you, protect you, amplify damage, and even manipulate the magazine, turning the tide of the game in unexpected ways.

Other game modes include Team, Expert and Scoring mode.


Un jeu de mémoire à haut risque, où stratégie et prise de décisions font toute la différence. Surpassez vos adversaires en prenant des risques calculés, en tirant avec intelligence et en utilisant vos ressources à bon escient.

Dans Trigger Warning, l'objectif est simple: être le dernier survivant.

Les joueurs construisent un chargeur de revolver de 8 cartes à partir de 13 cartes chambre (6 CLIC et 7 POW!). À son tour, un joueur peut utiliser autant d'objets qu'il le souhaite et cible ensuite un autre joueur ou sur lui-même. Un joueur est éliminé lorsqu’il perd ses 3 jetons de vie. La partie continue jusqu’à ce qu’il ne reste plus qu’un seul survivant.

Les objets peuvent vous soigner, vous protéger, infliger plus de dégâts ou même manipuler le chargeur, bouleversant ainsi le cours du jeu.

De plus, d'autres modes de jeu sont inclus, comme Expert, Équipe et le mode Pointage.

—description from the designer

name: Pinched!
description:
As the wealthy flaunt their valuables, with their infinite money and privilege, the less fortunate of us are left to scheme on how to skim a bit off the top. You are not wealthy. You call your esteemed profession: “Wealth Redistribution” or, in layperson’s terms - burglary, ah -  but burglary is such a harsh word -  pinching, merely, and you're darn good at it. Unfortunately, so are your “friends”.

Each turn, one player (burglar) becomes “The Mastermind”, planning their perfect, infallible Heist. In the meantime, the other burglars in town have been busy trying to guess where the break-in will be. If The Mastermind manages to go alone, they will take all valuables in that location for themselves, but if the other burglars guess correctly, and show up in the right place, they will be able to pinch some Valuables from The Mastermind’s Heist! The player who steals and sells the most Valuables, and hence “Redistributes” the most wealth is the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Triple Threes!
description:
Triple Threes! is the ultimate card game where strategy meets fun!

Dive into the exciting challenge of creating matching card sets while outsmarting your opponents. The game includes 54 vibrantly colored cards that are a treat for the eyes and 6 special cards that bring energy and exciting twists to every game! Aim to be the first to build three color sets of three cards each and yell "Triple Threes" to claim victory! But beware of the Special Cards. They have the power to turn your strategies upside down!

Want to play tournament style? Just keep score after each round and race to be the first one to cross 100 points! Boost your score by collecting all 4 cards of one color or hold onto the coveted Gold Card until the end for bonus points. 

Whether you're playing with family or friends, 333 promises endless entertainment. Compact and portable, it is perfect for parties, travel, and gatherings. Get your deck now and start the fun!

Playing with a big group? Bring everyone into the fun by combining two decks for 5-8 players.

—description from the publisher

name: Red North
description:
Battle horns echo across the North...the time for conquest has come! Sharpen your axes and send your fiercest heroes and raiders to seize control of the Northern Outposts. Early victories may bring glory, but beware for during Ragnarok, the Gods themselves may tip the scales. Only those who outsmart their enemies will claim victory.

Red North is a combative game of hidden information and bluffing for 2-4 players that plays in 30 minutes. It's a strategic card game full of tense excitement in which players compete, through hidden hands of various factions of warriors, to conquer outposts of corresponding factions. Knowing when to commit and when to bow out is key in winning you the game!

Players will deploy raiding parties to try to gain control of various outposts. By deploying more raiders, jarls, and heroes, a player reveals which outposts they are battling for, giving away their strategic position. Resources are scarce, so players must balance their deployed warriors with the need to reserve a party large enough to compete in the final "Ragnarok" round — where even the Norse Gods become involved.

Red North is a new edition of Saer, a game originally published by La Mame Games in 2024, that features a remixed set of outpost abilities, with some outposts giving tokens that you can use despite not owning the outpost, as well as eight unique gods.

—description from the publisher

name: Tenby
publisher: Cosy Cub Games; DSV Games; Mighty Boards
description:
Tenby is one of the most beautiful towns in Wales. Wander our colourful streets, walk along our piers with some scrumptious fish and chips, and relax on our stunning beaches with a nice cold ice cream and a warm feeling in your heart.

The aim of Tenby is to create the best town you can using the available cards. On your turn, you will draft and place cards to add terraces, piers, and Tenby town’s landmarks into your streets. If you can persuade a hard working local resident to help, you might just pick up some extra points! Whoever has the most points at the end of the game is the winner!

Each round consists of 3 phases: Day, Night, and Cleanup.  The Day cards and Night Cards are closely connected to each other. The Night Cards provide the order in which players will select Day Cards. The Day Cards provide the order in which players will take their actions that round, and will also set the Night Card player order for the next round. The game ends immediately after the last player has taken their last available action at the end of the tenth round.

—description from the publisher

name: Trombone Champ
description:
Only one of you can become the Trombone Champ! Based on the award winning video game, this is the definitive card game about trombones! But there are also lots of hot dogs and baboons.

This is a dedicated deck game where you are playing note cards to extend trombone slides and complete the song to score toots! The first player to score 15 toots is the winner.

name: Tropicalia
description:
Even this morning, the sky is clear and the sun is high over Tropicalia Island. It is time to collect mangoes, sugar apples and coconuts and to sell them at the various markets: your little island won't build itself!

In Tropicalia, you and your opponents will send your workers to the different tiles that make up the ever-changing island of Tropicalia to collect and sell fruit. Then, you will use your earnings to purchase various elements, such as buildings and events, to add to your personal board, which will grant you bonuses and points.

At the end of the game, whoever has the most valuable island wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Yotei
description:
Create the most charming town at the foot of Mt Yotei, also known as Ezo Fuji, located in Hokkaido Japan


     ︎ Expand your land with limited manpower, win bids using potatoes, and develop your town.
     ︎ There are multiple paths to victory. The person who maximizes the charm of their town and collects the most “Charm Points” wins!


Set in Niseko, a breathtaking region on Japan’s northern island of Hokkaido, this board game brings the local scenery, people, and wildlife to life. We’ve paid special attention to environmental sustainability by using Hokkaido-sourced wood for the tokens, while the artwork—created by a talented Japanese illustrator—is based on real people, landscapes, and events from the community.

In this game, you’ll craft the most enchanting Hokkaido town. Your currency? Potatoes. Bid with them, unearth more when you run short, and welcome the delights of the north: savory ramen, melt-in-your-mouth wagyu, delicate sushi; wild trout, mighty Ezo-bears, curious red foxes; and iconic developments from snowy ski resorts to serene hot-spring villages. With evolving tactics each round, the game stays fresh and captivating from start to finish.

Play this game to experience an authentic slice of life in Hokkaido. Despite the adorable “kawaii” illustrations, it’s a highly strategic, heart-pounding contest that will leave you eager for “just one more round.”

The game comes in a medium-sized box that’s perfect for game nights—substantial enough to satisfy experienced players yet welcoming to newcomers. It’s light enough for casual evenings but packed with enough depth and replayability to keep even seasoned board-gamers coming back again and again.

—description from the publisher

name: Troublebot
description:
Cause trouble – 'cause causing trouble is fun!

Troublebot is a lean, mean card game of many small but meaningful decisions. Whenever it is your turn, you get to pick up a new shroombot. Then you play one of the two shroombots in your hand and perform its action.

While most effects help you take care of your seedlings, some will cause the other players trouble. If you have the most valuable seedlings in the end, you win.

—description from the publisher

name: For the Gods!
description:
As a seafaring builder in ancient Greece, in For the Gods! you'll navigate the archipelago, constructing towering monuments to the gods and vying for control of sacred islands.

For the Gods! is a tactical area majority game in which every stone shapes your path to victory. The rules are simple: Sail the seas to establish new temples or elevate existing ones. Along the way, collect God stones and unleash their divine powers at the right moment. With twelve unique God powers, each game offers fresh strategies and dynamic gameplay, ensuring high variability.

—description from the publisher

name: Trust Me
description:
It already feels like the start of a great day on the Island of Toys! As you stand in the park, you smell the scent of toasted sugar, hear the laughter coming from the puppet theater, and gaze up at the colorful kites soaring across the sky. You listen to the music of the merry-go-round and long to ride it. There’s only one problem: you don’t have any tickets. Only the most famous children have them. If you were famous, you could use your reputation to gain tickets! All you need to do is convince the other children of the great adventures you’ve had with the different Characters on the Island, even if a bit of embellishment is required… after all, who will be able to tell the difference?

Trust Me is a bluffing game. Players have one day and one night to grow their reputation and gain Tickets by gaining the trust of their opponents or by tricking them. The player with the most valuable Tickets at the end of the game wins.

On your turn, you must perform one of the following three actions:

     Tell a Tale
     Use Reputation to Gain a Ticket
     Take a Character from the Park


Honest players who are not trusted will get both cards and play a second round while bluffing players who are trusted will get both cards and a precious ticket, but if you’re caught lying, you get nothing! Cards gained during your turn go into your reputation, which can be discarded to redeem more tickets. As the game progresses your reputation will get bigger, and bluffing will get much more tricky!

At the end of the game, the player with the most points is the coolest kid in the group!

—description from the publisher

name: Tsukiji Market
description:
Early morning at the Tsukiji market. The two best cooks of Tokyo are contesting the freshest fish. As new fish are unloaded from ships, each of them wants to have the first pick ... with the minimum offer.

Immerse yourself in the hustle and bustle of Tokyo's fish market with Tsukiji Market, a strategic duel in which two chefs compete for the freshest ingredients. This game combines bluff, speed and anticipation, inspired by the frenetic atmosphere of Tsukiji.

You'll need to constantly evaluate your bets, as wagering significantly more than your opponent will dramatically increase your opponent's chances of stealing a fish:  The "price" for a card is determined by the weight on a scale, which shifts towards the player who lost the bet. If the weight reaches the end of the scale, the player on that side can steal a card from their opponent!

You'll also be able to use the special effects of various fish cards to turn the tide of the game!

At the end of the game, you'll score points based on each of your different color piles of fish cards, the wasabi symbols on your cards, and the position of the weight in your direction.

Designed by Emanuele Briano, Tsukiji Market features stunning illustrations by Samuel Bouvant. The game is part of Matagot's microgames line (wallet-sized games), which includes 6 Suspects, Le Roy des Ribauds, Coucou la Girafe, and Room 25: Double Rush, among other titles

—description from the publisher

name: Tsumooo!
description:
Long ago, humanity lived without knowing the joy of drawing cards... until Galileo, inspired by the pull of gravity, supposedly cried, "Why not just draw?!" In the spirit of this fictional "Law of Universal Draw," players now dive into a new kind of trick-taking where every move reshapes their hand, blending clever setup and on-the-fly adaptation.

Tsumooo! is a trick-taking game where players must follow suit and draw a new card from special draw decks after every play. At the start, players create draw piles, sneaking cards into them as traps or opportunities. Choosing where to draw from and managing what others left behind becomes as important as playing the right cards. To win, players must fulfill their declared trick targets, adapting constantly as their hand evolves.

name: Emberheart
publisher: Mindclash Games; CrowD Games; Devir; DiceTree Games; Maldito Games; Super Meeple; White Goblin Games; YOKA Games
description:
The mystical island of Emberheart is home to the last dragons. They were living in harmony with the villagers until poachers from the Distant Lands arrived to capture, raid, and plunder. To keep the island safe, the Dragon Ambassador now seeks the King’s support. As one of the King’s champions, your mission is to join forces with the villagers, rescue and protect the dragons, and stand against the evil poachers.

Emberheart is a quick-playing, medium-weight worker placement game . As one of the King’s Champions, your task is to recruit heroes, rescue dragons and expand their preserves, train your own dragon companion, and oppose the roaming poachers.

On your turn, you can either take an Aide token (granting you a unique bonus for the round), or send a party of hirelings to one of the locations on the island. The number of hirelings you send matters just as much as where you send them: the more you commit to a location, the earlier you get to choose from its limited rewards, and the less likely your opponents are to outbid you with a larger party. There are various hirelings at your disposal: Grunts are versatile but single-use, while Scouts, Rangers and Wardens are permanent, but limited to specific locations. Your Dragon Companion can also join a party of hirelings as you place them, giving them various bonuses based on how you trained it.

The locations’ rewards allow you to recruit Heroes with unique abilities, rescue Dragons from the poachers’ grasp to get them to safety in matching Preserves, and launch counterattacks against the poachers. In the heat of some actions, and during the Poachers’ Raid at the end of each round, you may get burned, and advancing too far on the Flame track will take its toll at the end of the game.

Rescuing Dragons, recruiting Heroes, training your Dragon Companion, and keeping your Flame low will earn you Glory at the end of the game. After five rounds, the Champion with the most Glory wins, inheriting the title of Dragon Ambassador.

—description from the publisher

name: Tulip
description:
Tulip is a strategic card game inspired by the famous 17th-century tulip market bubble. Players take on the role of merchants seeking to maximize their profits by buying and selling tulips while anticipating market fluctuations.

Game Mechanics:
Each player has a garden where they place Tulip, Black Tulip, or Action cards. On their turn, they must play one card and draw a new one to maintain a hand of four cards. Tulip cards cause the market value to shift, Black Tulips provide a fixed income, and Action cards influence the game by changing tulip values or interacting with opponents.

Turn Structure:
The player plays a card in their garden.
They apply its effect (market value change, action activation, etc.).
They draw a new card to refill their hand.

Endgame and Victory Conditions:
The game ends when a fourth market crash occurs, a fourth Black Tulip is played, or the draw pile is depleted. Players then calculate their total florins based on their tulip holdings and actions. The player with the most florins wins!

With constant market shifts and direct player interactions, Tulip is a fast-paced, clever, and accessible game, perfect for fans of bluffing and risk management!

-description from artist

name: Tundra
description:
Tundra is a competitive strategy game with worker distribution and resource gathering. You become a representative of one of the estates in the kingdom of Tundra and develop lands to earn the favor of the society and the Tsar.

The game is played over four rounds. In each round, the actions of all players are determined by the values of the dice rolled by the first player. Players take turns using the dice to perform a variety of actions: send workers to gather resources, build towers and hire advisors at the market, fulfill common and personal goals, and so on. During the course of the game, you can earn victory points in various ways. The player with the most victory points after four rounds wins and is named Viceroy of Tundra.

—description from the publisher

name: Turbo Tiere
description:
Turbo Tiere is a fast-paced racing game where you win by being the first Turbo Tier to cross the finish line. Each round, you draw up to three green standard chips to move your vehicle forward, block opponents, or activate tunings.
The track reveals itself progressively, introducing sudden obstacles and tricky sections, which can lead to both lucky and unlucky events.

You can freely combine the vehicles with the animal drivers.

name: Perseverance: Castaway Chronicles – Episodes 3 & 4
description:
As the months since the shipwreck turn into years and memories of our past life fade, we now call this strange new land our home. Perseverance has grown from a weathered foothold to a bustling city, where new landmarks improve our living standards, and expansive ranches contribute to society’s welfare and the ongoing exploration. The once ferocious Shieldheads now walk among us tamed, and our brave Dino Riders are finally able to chart even the most distant parts of the wilderness. They come back with tales of abandoned structures in the far reaches of the island, similar to the one that held the secret of Shieldhead taming. If the rumors are true, we may be able to make our peace with even the stalwart Thunderhorns and the fearsome Ironjaws, and our society’s influence will soon span the entire island! And while these eerie ruins hold answers, they raise even more questions. Who are their creators? What happened to them? Are they truly gone? The answers are out there, waiting to be discovered. Let’s hope we’re ready for them!

Perseverance: Castaway Chronicles - Episodes 3 and 4 are two medium-heavy, thematic Euro games, concluding the story of time-lost survivors on a dinosaur island. Each Episode is playable as a standalone game, or in the Chronicle mode that ties four games - one with each Episode - into a continuous story. As the hallmark of the Perseverance series, each Episode features many unique characteristics and a very distinct game feel, but their core mechanisms and concepts are similar, making each new Episode much easier to learn.

In Episode 3, Perseverance is finally safe from the dinosaur attacks and has grown into a bustling city. As players discover how to tame and ride the Dinosaurs (including the new Thunderhorn and Ironjaw species), as their primary action, they may now choose to send a Dino Rider into the far reaches of the island instead of placing a die in the city. Besides streamlining some of the usual area majority elements, Episode 3 takes a new approach, focusing on engine and tableau building. City Landmarks provide powerful passive benefits, while players may build and customize their own Ranches on their player boards, activating them as a secondary action using the new Supply resource acquired from the wilderness.

Episode 4 brings the story to an epic conclusion as you face off against the Ancients, a mysterious race that once ruled the island. Even though the situation is dire, the dimensional storm that made their return possible also presents an almost impossible opportunity: to refit the hollowed-out husk of the Pearl of the Seas ocean liner for one last journey, back to your homeworld.

name: TwinStar Valley
description:
Welcome to Twinstar Valley, a small universe of untamed beauty and boundless opportunity, nestled deep in the heart of Norway. Rich with rare minerals and thriving ecosystems, this fertile paradise is the launchpad for Project Twinstar, a high-stakes competition where only the smartest logistics masterminds will thrive. Their ultimate test? Successfully cultivating and processing every conceivable fruit, no matter the challenge.

Your mission? Conquer the terrain, master a living economy, and outwit your rivals as you build a powerful network of roads, bridges, and trade routes. Every turn is a strategic puzzle, thanks to the game’s innovative Action Selection system, a clever mechanism where you lay down a chain of Action discs, branching in bold new directions or tactically blocking your opponents’ paths.
But the game doesn’t stop when it’s not your turn. In Project Twinstar, your infrastructure earns income whenever others use it, creating a dynamic, shared economy where you’re always in the game, always profiting...if you plan wisely. And with a fluctuating market that shifts each round, timing becomes everything. Will you stock up before prices soar, or sell just as the bottom drops out?

Grow your legacy, one fruit at a time. Build smart, sell smarter, and claim your place as the ultimate architect of Twinstar Valley.

—description from the designer

name: Trickerion: Anniversary Edition
publisher: Mindclash Games; Corax Games; Engames; Maldito Games; Old Dawg; Portal Games; Super Meeple; TTGames CZ
description:
Trickerion - Legends of Illusion is a thematic, medium-heavy Euro-style game of rival stage illusionists. In this game, you are a Victorian-era magician, with a team of apprentices and specialists you can assign to various tasks using worker placement and simultaneous action selection. These tasks include collecting magical components, expanding your assortment of Tricks, and preparing magnificent magic shows in the Theater for you to perform at the end of each round. Performances can earn you money, but ultimately, you are in it for Fame: the more famous you are, the better Tricks you can learn, and the Magician with the most Fame points will win the game.

To celebrate the 10th anniversary of the first Kickstarter campaign, Mindclash Games is releasing a special Anniversary Edition of Trickerion. This edition includes:


     Trickerion - Legends of Illusion base game
     Trickerion - Dahlgaard's Academy expansion
     Trickerion - Dahlgaard's Gifts add-on pack
     Trickerion - Dawn of Technology Expansion
     Trickerion - Arcane Arts Expansion
     Trickerion - Secret Workshop Promo
     Alternate art box with metallic foil effect
     Revised core rulebook
     A set of Metal Coins, with two unique Arcane Drachma coins
     4 new sturdy standing pouches
     New Alternate Art version on one side of the main board
     GameTrayz custom tray system
     Tray manual to keep everything organized easily


—description from the publisher

name: Revenant
publisher: Mindclash Games; Portal Games; Skellig Games; Super Meeple
description:
From the void between dimensions, an ancient cosmic entity emerged—corrupting, consuming, and devouring all in its path. In the wake of the cataclysm known as Voidfall, the admirals of the fallen galactic empire, the Domineum, forged a desperate contingency plan. To preserve the legacy of the human civilization from the Voidborn threat, a former imperial flagship, the Revenant, was retrofitted to carry vast databanks containing the accumulated knowledge of humanity and escape the fallen empire. Now, bearing humanity’s last hope and escorted by the ships of the Domineum’s last Great Houses, you must guide the fleet to safety beyond the known galaxy, balance fragile alliances, and secure not only the survival of humankind—but also your own political destiny.

Revenant is a standalone, competitive worker placement game of shifting allegiances, set in the Voidfall universe. Players take on the role of rival admirals coordinating the defense of a fleeing starfleet, and competing to earn influence with the factions that stand to survive the journey.

Across four rounds, players assign crew to ships throughout the fleet, from which they will fight corrupted ships, explore planets in search of resources, upgrade their ship and crew, deploy new vessels, and more. Each ship is affiliated with one of the Great Houses, and each time you assign crew there, you gain influence with that House.

The journey won’t be an easy one. The Voidborn’s corrupted forces will continuously attack the fleet, dealing damage to various ships at the end of every round. You can take your part in protecting the fleet by destroying enemy ships, repairing friendly vessels or maneuvering them to safe areas, or ultimately activating the Revenant’s hyperdrive to jump to a safer sector. Regardless of your efforts, there will be casualties - you have to make sure that the Houses you have influence in are protected above others.

Revenant spices up the resource management and engine-building of a mid-weight euro with dynamic tactical challenges, constant player interaction, and shifting allegiances.

—description from the publisher

name: Qwirkle Flex
description:
Take your Qwirkle strategy in a whole new direction! Tiles with three different backgrounds create surprising opportunities to score diagonally. Points add up quickly when you place even one tile that scores in multiple directions. Adjust your focus from foreground shapes to background colors for the thrill of next-level maneuvers.

How flexible is your Qwirkle stategy?

—description from the publisher

name: Twittens
description:
Twittens is an old Sussex word to describe the little alleyways and lanes that run between houses and fields. They thread their way through towns and suburbs like veins, walled by red bricks, garden fencing and rusted chicken wire. Elsewhere they're known as ginnels, snicks and vennels.

Twittens is a tile laying game set in an everyday English suburb. Work your way through the seasons exploring your local twittens, discovering their houses, wildlife, allotments, playgrounds, railways and electrical substations. Complete your wanderings and get home in time for tea.

—description from the publisher

name: Tycoon: India 1981
description:
Post independence from colonial rule, India had been left in shambles. It was the combined efforts of bureaucrats, politicians, and industrialists who worked together (and sometimes not so much together) to start a new industrial revolution following the five-year plans. It is the dawn of a new era, for liberalization and globalization has removed much of the licensing and red-taping that had hindered development of the industries.

In the game of Tycoon: India 1981, players represent big industrial houses of India that are trying to dominate the six key industrial sectors — minerals, fuel, agro, power, transport, and finance — by obtaining the rights from the government and building factories on a map of India. Although the goal is to be rich, they must try to influence national policies to their favor, as well as gain political votes to break ties, all while balancing wealth and fame in a series of rounds that will ultimately decide one winner!

—description from the designer

name: Uffbasse!
description:
The Palatine slang word Uffbasse! has the meaning of “Watch out!”.
Uffbasse! is a trick-taking card game in which the players take on the role of chefs. They play to gain ingredients and use them to “cook” original Palatinate dishes. The chef who has cooked the most stars after four rounds becomes the new Palatinate Star Chef!

name: Ringer
description: Play cards in numerical order or different colors to try and match the dice in the center of the pile. Do you take the pile now or do you keep it going to score more when you do take it?

name: Ukiyo-e
publisher: さとーふぁみりあ (Sato Familie)
description:
In 1867, the World's Fair in Paris sparked a craze for Japanese art and culture known as Japonisme. Art galleries specializing in Japanese ukiyo-e prints were established, and ukiyo-e became known around the world.

In Ukiyo-e / ウキヨエ, players take on the role of art dealers specializing in ukiyo-e and aim to hold successful solo ukiyo-e exhibitions. To lay down a set of cards, you need at least two cards if that type hasn't been played or more cards than are already on the table if it has been played, after which any cards of the same type on the table are discarded. The round ends when one player has six types of art (out of seven) or the deck runs out. Players score the lowest-valued card in each set on the table, which speeds up future rounds and can make sets more valuable.

Ukiyo-e is based on Michael Schacht's 2003 game Crazy Chicken, with this new version being designed in consultation with him.

1867年、パリで開催された万博をきっかけに、ジャポニズムと呼ばれる日本ブームが起こりました。
浮世絵を扱う画廊も設立され、日本の浮世絵が世界的に注目されるようになりました。
プレイヤーは浮世絵を扱う美術商となり、浮世絵の個展を開いて成功を収めることを目指します。
個展を開くことで得点を得ます。多くの個展を開いて多くの点数を稼ぎましょう。

—Japanese description from the publisher

name: Ukraine Battles 2014: Ilovaisk & Debal'tseve
description:
Initially scheduled for Modern War #68 (September 2023), Ukraine Battles is a grand tactical two-player simulation (battalion-brigade level) of the battles fought in the Donbass in 2014-2015. The game system incorporates the tactical and operational lessons learned from the operations in Ukraine, including tactical and operational drones, improved sub munitions, expanded range and lethality of artillery and MRLS systems, improved thermobaric ammunitions, Russian Battalion Tactical Groups, artillery radars, PSYOPs, Special Forces (Spetsnaz) as combat force multipliers, or networked Anti-Aircraft (AA) systems. The system simulates armor superiority, reactive armor, Shtora systems vs. Anti-Tank (AT) missiles and Rocket Propelled Grenades (RPGs), defensive positions and pre-arranged artillery fire, as well as the difficulties of command control and coordination of hybrid armies formed by regulars and militias.

Each game turn represents two to three days, each hex represents 10km or 6 miles, and combat units range from battalions to brigade sized units.

name: Ultimate PAC-MAN
description:
CHOMP YOUR WAY TO VICTORY with multiplayer PAC-MAN action! Relive the arcade magic in this fast-paced, battle to master the maze in this officially PAC-MAN& Bandai Namco Entertainment licensed adventure! Each player controls their very own PAC-MAN, gobbling up PAC-DOTs, Fruit, and POWER PELLETS while dodging Ghosts and other rival PAC-MAN players. But beware, players also control the Ghosts, chasing down opponents and forcing them to lose lives! Activate power-ups, flip Ghosts to TURN-TO-BLUE mode, and rack up the highest score to become the ULTIMATE CHOMPION! Will your PAC-MAN claim the top spot? Add this beloved arcade classic to your collection of family board games for ultimate nostalgia!


     CLASSIC PAC-MAN FUN WITH A COMPETITIVE TWIST: Experience the nostalgia of the legendary arcade game in an exciting tabletop board game format! Players race their PAC-MAN through the maze, collecting PAC-DOTS and fruit while dodging Ghosts and rival PAC-MAN players. Outsmart opponents, plan your route, and earn points in this thrilling multiplayer showdown.


 

     MULTIPLAYER ACTION FOR 2-4 PLAYERS: Every player controls their own PAC-MAN! Quick decision-making and strategy are crucial as players race to collect PAC-DOTs, power up, and fight to stay alive! Designed for two to four players, it's an ideal choice for retro gaming fans and families looking for the next addition to their board game collection! 



     DODGE, CHOMP, OR CONTROL GHOSTS: This is not just a race to eat the most PAC-DOTs, players also strategically control the Ghosts! Carefully move BLINKY, PINKY, INKY, and CLYDE to block paths, chase down rival PAC-MAN players, and force them to lose valuable 1UP tokens, all while trying to escape! 



     POWER-UP FOR POINTS AND GAME-CHANGING MOVES: Enhance gameplay with power-up cards that give you extra movement, teleportation, or the ability to eat Ghosts. Each power-up changes the game, offering new ways to challenge opponents and climb to the top of the scoreboard! Every match plays differently, making for endless nostalgic, arcade-inspired fun! 



     CALLING ALL PAC-MAN FANS, RETRO GAMERS, AND ARCADE CLASSIC COLLECTORS: As an officially licensed PAC-MAN product, this game is a must-have for fans of the iconic franchise. Whether you grew up playing PAC-MAN in the arcade or are introducing your family or friends to the fun, Ultimate PAC-MAN delivers a nostalgic experience with a modern twist, making it a great addition to any games collection.


—description from the publisher

name: Ultimate Palace
description:
Ultimate Palace is a fast-paced, easy-to-learn card game inspired by the classic game Palace (also known as Sh*thead). Redesigned with custom cards and streamlined rules, it creates a smoother play experience and bigger “wow” moments.

Players race to be the first to get rid of all their cards by beating or matching the one on top of the pile. You can play multiple of the same card at once. Special cards change the rules in an instant — skipping turns, flipping the flow, or burning the pile completely. And if you can’t beat it or match it? You pick up the whole thing.

The first person who sheds all their cards, wins.

—description from the designer

name: Ultimate Voyage
description:
1431, Ming China. The emperor is dead, whispers of dissent echo through the court. You stand alongside an aging Admiral Zheng He, the greatest maritime explorer of East Asia. As he embarks on his final voyage to the West Ocean, can you seize this last opportunity to reverse the empire’s fate and define your legacy?

Ultimate Voyage is an action selection, thematic expedition game where you Sail, Trade, Combat, Explore, Negotiate, and Construct, to bring back Prestige and Profit, attain Open and Secret Objectives, build the Porcelain Tower, and write the most captivating story of exotic encounters.  With 4 paths to victory, 4 distinct endgame triggers, and a wide array of random setups, events, and encounters, you must continually adapt your strategies to navigate ever-changing situations.

Each player character has a unique backstory, abilities, and initial resources, fostering a blend of competition and cooperation, ensuring varied player interaction in every game. Explore 16 historical ports across 7 regions, through authentic monsoon wind patterns and events, in over 100 meticulously researched illustrations. Each port features its own iconic landmark and offers unique trade goods, knowledge, encounters, and shifting affiliations with the Ming Empire.

Enjoy a streamlined version of the game with quick-play rules, or challenge yourself in solo mode as Admiral Zheng He himself, facing off against an automated European explorer, Niccolò de' Conti.

name: Ultimatum: can you turn the tide?
description:
In Ultimatum the world is on the brink of disaster. As members of the global climate prevention team, your mission is to combat the most severe natural disasters of our time. Floods, hurricanes, and bushfires threaten cities worldwide, and every decision you make could be the difference between survival and catastrophe. This is your ultimatum - can you turn the tide?

The game board represents various cities across the globe. On each turn, players must choose between taking preventive actions in their current city or traveling to assist teammates elsewhere. The unpredictability of Mother Nature means that disasters can strike anywhere, at any time, with devastating effects. Players must collaborate, adapt their strategies, and act swiftly. Each turn presents new challenges, requiring players to reconsider their plans and work together to save the world. Only with the right strategy, you can prevent the destruction and ensure a thriving future for humanity.

To win the game, your team must secure three regions on the board and complete the selected mission, before three regions are lost or the mission becomes impossible to complete.

Every game is unique, demanding fresh strategies and teamwork. Are you ready to turn the tide and save the world?

—description from the publisher

name: Ultimediation
description:
A sci-fi board game where you don’t just stop a war… you redefine what peace really means!

A very very very cooperative board game!

? Ultimediation® is a 100% cooperative… and 100% crucial board game.
Earth is on the brink of collapse. A global war is raging. Humanity is falling apart.

You are part of an extraordinary team: the finest human mediators, supported by three extraterrestrials from a highly advanced civilization. Together, you return to Earth — not to fight… but to restore peace.

? Your mission?
Evacuate civilians. Stop the attacks. And above all: succeed in mediating between the warring factions… by uncovering the human needs hidden beneath the violence.

⏳ Time is running out.
? The survival of the planet is in your hands.
? Will you manage to build lasting peace — before it’s too late?

? GAMEPLAY OVERVIEW

Welcome to the mission. As mediators, you're not just observers — you're history shapers. Every decision you make can rewrite the fate of humanity.

? REMOVING ATTACKS
With each turn, new attack tiles strike different regions of Earth.
Your task? Undo the devastation left by war.

Thanks to your extraordinary power — the ability to travel slightly back in time — you can reverse these events before they become irreversible. In the game, this is known as “removing an attack.” It’s not just damage control… it’s rewriting the present.

?‍♂️ EVACUATION OF HUMANITY
Every life counts.

When an attack hits a zone inhabited by civilians, they either flee… or perish.
Your team’s mission is to save as many as possible — by teleporting them to safe zones: the "U base" the mothership in orbit.

Move fast. Time is running out, and lives are on the line.

?️ MEDIATION — THE HEART OF THE MISSION
Peace won’t come through power. Only through understanding.

To fulfill your mission, you must initiate mediation sessions with both warring governments — hidden deep within their submarines. There, you’ll need to decode their true motivations and guide them to express not just demands… but the human needs behind them.

Only then can real peace begin !

? WINNING & LOSING THE GAME

The fate of Earth hangs in the balance. The game ends when one of three conditions is met:

✅ Victory — Humanity Unites in Peace
You’ve successfully mediated with both factions. Congratulations — you've achieved what history never could!

❌ Defeat — Earth Overrun by War
A full horizontal line of attack tiles appears on the board.
That region is lost. Humanity follows.

❌ Defeat — Too Many Lives Lost, Too Little Time
The turn tracker and lost humanity cube meet.
Too many are gone, and time has run out for mediation.

-description from designer

name: ULTRAMASSIVE
description:
Far beyond the Milky Way Galaxy, in the uncharted depths of space, a black hole looms just outside a vibrant galactic cluster. This black hole is enormous, by all standards of the universe, and entirely ungovernable. But its daunting size and power is not unmatched. Other black holes tear through the expanse, fulfilling their one purpose: consume. Like this looming mass, their consumption leads to growth, and growth leads to power. As they expand, they will inevitably confront one another and adopt strategies for overtaking their unruly adversaries. Ultimately, one black hole will emerge as the most powerful, and more importantly, largest: the "king" of the universe. Or, as the infinitesimally small creatures on Earth call it, ULTRAMASSIVE.

In ULTRAMASSIVE, you play as one of these black holes. Your goal is to become the largest class of black hole known to man: Ultramassive. To do so, you must consume a myriad of other celestial bodies, each with a certain amount of Solar Mass (victory points), which is added to your point total. Absorbing enough Solar Mass causes your black hole to expand, changing the landscape of your board and accelerating your growth.

Like the black holes in our universe, yours is unique. Amass and exchange your resources for Anomalies which augment how your black hole acquires and consumes matter. Each Anomaly improves your abilities in different ways depending on your chosen trajectory to victory. Bolster your strategy with potent Anomaly combinations to counteract and out-pace your opponents. Modeled after skill-trees common in digital RPGs, the Anomalies provide a multitude of approaches to engine building, especially for those drawn to experimentation.

Adding to the tools at your disposal, each black hole is equipped with several wormholes which act as bridges across the vast orbit of your black hole. Wield your wormholes with tact to maximize every opportunity.

Opportunist or long-term plotter, speed orbiter or matter behemoth; decide how you will out-consume your opponents to ultimately become the largest entity in existence and claim your title as ULTRAMASSIVE.

—description from the designer

name: Ultraviolett
description:
Demonstrate your artistic talent by drawing a completely absurd sentence with a UV pen with invisible ink so well that your fellow artists can guess what it is.
Collect extra points by guessing other people's artwork. The player with the most points at the end wins the game.

name: Umami
description:
Fire up your stalls under a full moon in a rustling forest! Ramen, takoyaki, miso soup, and more sizzle as you race to serve dishes packed with umami — that savory taste that makes mouths water and crowds gather.

In Umami, you will whip up the tastiest dishes possible of just three ingredients each. Spot a better bite? "Borrow" it off a rival's plate! Forest denizens have special tastes, so match your ingredients to their appetites to win them over!

In more detail, start with four ingredient cards in hand; ingredients range from 1-9, with each card also having a star, steal, or blossom icon. Four ingredient cards are in a face-up market. Each player has a secret "favorite" card, with four favorites in a face-up market; each favorite shows three cards that make up the dish they want, e.g., two medium (4-6) and a high (7-9), with the highest total possible.

On a turn, play one ingredient from your hand and another from the market, creating over time at most five dishes of three cards each. (You can replace a card in a dish, if desired.) Once per turn, you can discard a card with a steal icon to take an opponent's ingredient and add it to your dish; they draw and play a replacement card. As soon as you qualify for a favorite on display, place it in front of that dish, which keeps others from stealing your ingredients...although they can still steal the favorite by having a dish that better meets their tastes or has more blossoms in it.

When the last favorite is claimed or someone has a full table, everyone reveals their secret favorite, then run through one more round, after which the player with the most stars — summed from ingredients played and favorites claimed — wins.

name: Umami Friends
description:
A group of animal friends set out on an epic journey to catch rare foods and to combine them to make Legendary Recipes. Create the ultimate Recipe to help them unlock the secrets of the Umamiverse!

Umami Friends invites players to choose a umami chef, each with a distinct type and ability, providing unique advantages in culinary battles. The core of gameplay revolves around collecting ingredients to craft recipes.

These recipes evolve into more potent combinations, culminating in the creation of Legendary Recipes through strategic layering. With numerous character and ingredient combinations to discover, every cook-off is a fresh experience!

The player or team that has earned 30 Umami Points at the end of the game wins!

—description from the designer

name: Umbra Morfes
description:
Having condemned their homeworld, the Memges made the planet Zimi their last hope. But this refuge has rebelled. Their efforts to cultivate, build, and preserve life proved poisonous to the Umbra Morfes, unleashing a generation of mutant horrors created by the twisted fusion of the native Umbra with the colonists themselves and their chimeras. These monsters emerge from the Umbral Rifts, forcing you into a war of survival where there is no moral victory: you must destroy the planet's ancestral inhabitants to secure the future of your race.

 Umbra Morfes is a combination of role-playing game and wargame, with solo, cooperative, and arena modes where players can compete against each other, either in teams or one-on-one. Its unique terrain creation system, based on hexagonal tiles, allows players to design dynamic, customizable maps. Additionally, the game includes cards that grant new abilities to heroes, ensuring that each adventure is completely different.

Create your terrain map, choose a character, and place it on the space truck tile. You’ll start with basic abilities, but as you defeat creatures and gain experience, you’ll unlock new skills and improve your character's stats with better modifiers. Choose from six unique heroes, each fitting different playstyles, whether you prefer dealing heavy damage, strategic ranged attacks, healing, or tanking.

The mission of the Heroes is to seal the umbral Rifts, cracks that connect to Zimi’s inner layers, where the Umbra Morfes reside. Only by doing so can the Memges create an optimal ecosystem for life, ensuring water, air, and vegetation — elements that are deadly to the Umbra Morfes.

The game ends without victory if your life points are below 0. The game ends with victory if you complete all the objectives.

name: Uncharted Passage
description:
In the 1400s, you are tasked by the Portuguese royal family to explore and chart unknown territories.

Over the next year, you will traverse the globe, discovering exotic ports, rare goods, strange creatures, and breathtaking vistas.

However, long voyages may endanger your crew with scurvy, and ruthless pirates lurk around every corner, ready to strike.

Can you overcome these challenges and hardships to forge the greatest trade routes in history?

name: Unconditional Surrender! Western Campaigns
description:
Unconditional Surrender! Western Campaigns (USWC) is an strategic-level game covering World War 2 campaigns fought between the Axis and Western Allied factions in Western Europe. With its emphasis on force projection, players focus on the big picture of managing their military forces. Using simple mechanics and low on-map counter density, players easily handle the action without complicated subsystems or tall stacks of counters.

Plucked from the game Unconditional Surrender! WW2 in Europe (USE), USWC provides shorter, smaller footprint scenarios for those wanting to play the Unconditional Surrender! design but lacking the space and time needed for the much larger USE. USWC also serves as an alternative way to teach it to other players. Owners of USE that have the space and time for it, do not have to buy this game. However, it may be worth it, if you are looking for something much more portable to bring somewhere else to play or for an inexpensive gift for a wargaming friend.

DESIGN HIGHLIGHTS:

Low On-Map Counter Density: The number of counters on the map is incredibly low.
Simple Stacking: No more than one of the same type of unit per hex.
No Factors on Counters: No combat or movement factors on counters.
Single Combat System: One combat resolution sequence and Combat Results Table covers all types of combat, yet the results differ for air or ground combat.
Integrated Movement & Combat System: Units move and fight in a combined activation.
Ergonomically Friendly: Easily fits in extremely limited gaming space.
"Use it or lose it." Economic System: Simple math with minimal record keeping.
Easy to Modify: The relatively simple mechanics make it easy to modify the game.
Unconditional Surrender! World War 2 in Europe Compatibility: The ground and air units, event markers, and combat system are the same in both games. The scenarios are similar except for the elements that were abstracted. If you later decide to play USE, you will have additional rules to learn but little to unlearn.

TIME SCALE: Monthly Turns
MAP SCALE:  30 to 40 miles per hex
UNIT SCALE: Army, Fleet, or Wing
NUMBER OF PLAYERS: 2


COMPONENT LIST 
5 8.5"x11" maps
1 8.5"x22" map
1 sheet with 280 counters
1 Rules Booklet
1 Play Book with 9 scenarios
2 foldable 11"x17" Player Aid Cards
1 8.5"x11" Faction Card
2 6-sided dice
Game Box

-description from designer

name: Five Parsecs From Home: Planetfall
description:
Prepare to embark on the grandest Five Parsecs adventure yet as you make planetfall on a world filled with wonders, terrors, and difficult challenges.

Planetfall is a solo and co-op adventure game where you take the role of a crew of colonists, scientists, and explorers from the mighty Unity of Humankind, building a colony on an alien world packed full of long-overgrown crashed starships and dangerous ancient ruins, while contending with mysterious and hostile lifeforms.

You will have to direct your colony’s expansion and research as well as commanding your characters and troops in tactical miniatures combat. Over time, your colonists will gain experience and improve their combat abilities, while the R&D department adapts alien tech to upgrade your armories... and perhaps even your very bodies.

STAND-ALONE, COMPATIBLE RULES
The game is playable with any miniatures you would like to use and requires only a small figure count per battle. Rules are compatible with characters brought over from Five Parsecs from Home, Tactics, and Bug Hunt, allowing you to chain together the grandest space adventure you have ever experienced.

FEATURES:

Easy combat rules, allowing a single player to handle action quickly.
Packed with random tables including artifacts, colony events, crises, and more.
14 mission types ranging from exploration to pitched battles to delves among alien ruins.
Tactical enemies including pirates, renegades, outlaws, alien raiders, K’Erin landing parties, Converted recon teams... even hostile fellow colonists.
In-depth research system with 13 scientific theories, 40 buildings, and 8 augmentations to unlock.
As you explore, you will map out the world around your colony, and create your own unique encounter tables, filled with bizarre and evolving table-generated lifeforms.
Assailants specific to the Kensington Reach setting: Introducing the psionic, saurian Slyn and ancient robot guardians, the Sleepers.
Multiple epic endings possible for your colony.

name: Paranoia: The Uncooperative Board Game
description:
Welcome to Alpha Complex, the perfect (and in no way dystopian) city run by the benevolent and infallible Computer! Alpha Complex is a dangerous place, full of mutants, secret societies, and other troublemakers. It’s quite likely that Troubleshooters will die. (It’s also quite likely that they will, in fact, be mutants, members of secret societies, and troublemakers.) Sometimes, the only way to get ahead (or, indeed, get anywhere at all) is to bend the strict rules of Alpha Complex but watch your back. If anyone witnesses your (justifiable?) acts of despicable treason, and lets the Computer know things might not go so well for you. Especially if the roving GuardBots have anything to do with it. Best of luck, and remember: the Computer is your friend! Trust the Computer!

To celebrate the 40th anniversary of the Paranoia RPG, Modiphius has released Paranoia: The Uncooperative Board Game a highly replayable game of sci-fi slapstick one-upmanship

Each player controls a Troubleshooter, tasked with carrying out the Computer’s orders in the hope of being promoted through the spectrum of Clearance Levels, and hopefully attaining the rank of Ultraviolet. When a Troubleshooter dies, high-tech rapid cloning procedures ensure that they can get back to work almost instantly. Clones are limited though, so don’t be too frivolous.

You start as a Red level Troubleshooter and can get promoted by completing Tasks.  Your Secret Agendas – each player has a token for this – start at the other side of the Tracker. As your character is promoted, your ‘rainbow’ token moves right on this Tracker, and as you complete Secret Agendas , your counter for that moves left. If the tokens cross first, that player is considered the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: UnderQuest
description:
In UnderQuest you are an adventurer setting out into a dark and grim world to make a name for yourself. Evil plagues and vile creatures lurk around every corner. Your task is to complete quest cards in order to drive the narrative, while building up your character by finding new loot, learning new skills, and defeating nasty foes. Doing this will allow you to embark on even tougher quests.

You will start your adventure in UnderQuest at the Lonely Troll Inn, where you will create a new character by picking a race and class, each with different skills and perks. You will then equip your adventurer with trappings. You then must build your quest deck and embark on your adventure. UnderQuest uses a unique draw two, pick one mechanic while you are exploring the huge underground world, along with a tactical dice system for combat. Each enemy feels quite different. You will find powerful weapons, armor, and items along the way to aid you in your quest. There is even a clever alchemy system that allows you to craft potions.

During your adventure you will encounter not just foes, but also treasure, campsites, traps, and random encounters. When you have to resolve a random encounter, you will get to draw from a special random encounters deck with dozens of outcomes. These can range from strange caravans and wandering merchants to poisonous mushroom groves and snake pits! Whenever you gain the required quest tokens for the current quest card, you complete that leg of the journey and must reveal the next quest card. You win the game once you have exhausted the quest deck, typically ending in an epic boss fight. This allows UnderQuest to have a strong narrative to drive the storytelling aspect of the game and make each quest feel fleshed out.

Will you be able to build a lowly adventure into a mighty hero, or will your adventurer fall to the darkness that sleeps below. You can only find out by taking on the UnderQuest!

name: The DUNGENERATOR: DIE in a Dungeon
description:
DIE in a Dungeon is a solo/cooperative, narrative dungeon crawler that turns your tabletop RPG dice into doomed heroes battling to protect and rebuild a doomed village on the outskirts of an ever-shifting dungeon! What say you, Adventurer? Will you defeat the evil threatening the hamlet? Or will you DIE in a Dungeon?

It features a double-sized deck of standard-sized cards. To play, a standard set of 7 polyhedral dice and a DUNGENERATOR deck is required.

DIE in a Dungeon is a campaign-based deckbuilding game of multiple sessions in which players cooperate to either defeat the Boss Monster (winning the campaign) or complete quests, train, unlock buildings, and gather loot to add new actions to their decks. The open-ended, "sandbox" style sessions are driven by a tight action economy that leads to tough decisions and generates narratives. Easy rules for dropping players in and out of the game (even mid-session) make it a flexible filler game.

Though dice are prominently used (as they represent the Heroes of the story, and each is mapped to a fantasy character archetype), rarely does the outcome of a player's plan rely on the roll of a die. Instead, the current faces of their Heroes are a resource used to accomplish a variety of actions (and are able to be mitigated). Cards in-hand can be played as actions or used as a resource themselves (and discarded to power other actions).

—description from the designer

name: Uninvited Guests at a Wedding
description:
You and your gang weren't invited to the big Indian wedding — but the buffet was calling, the DJ was fire, and someone had to photobomb the selfies. You danced like no one's watching (amongst thousands of guests), raided the chaat (snack) counter, and devoured the biryani...but now there's evidence. Photos. Suspicious chachis (aunties) watching your every move. And now the khandaan (family) is on high alert — ready to unmask the wedding crashers. Time to cover your tracks, pin the blame on your friends, and make a clean escape!

In Uninvited Guests at a Wedding, you are one of those guests, and you want to remove evidence where you are spotted, expose your friends' identities, and escape the shaadi with the most points. On a turn, you can either clear evidence or make an accusation to guess another player's identity. Guess correctly, and you earn points and take the opponent's identity card; if not, you are immediately eliminated from the round. You can also play misleading evidence cards that don't contain your photo, which earn negative points at game's end.

Your goal? Have the most points from evidence cards removed from the grid. Even if eliminated, you still have a chance to win, especially with the added twist of the informant card that's revealed from the fifth round onwards to shake up the game.

name: Unlock!: Enchanted Adventures
description:
Unlock! is a series of escape adventures for up to six players. With one hour on the clock, players work through a deck of sixty cards as a team, searching for clues, combining objects, and solving puzzles. The free Unlock! companion app runs the timer while also providing clues, offering hints, and confirming successes. Once the team has reached a solution and entered the correct code into the app, they will escape and win the game!

Unlock!: Enchanted Adventures contains three scenarios revolving around these themes.
