description: Lambada is a game of skill and planning.  Strategically play letter cards on top of the word Lambada, while avoiding the forbidden color.  Each turn demands planning as you navigate shifting colors and dodge penalties, while racing to try to empty your hand.

name: Zombie Diner
description:
A solo apocalyptic-themed game where your goal is to survive a relentless zombie horde as the heroic attendant of your Fast Food Diner.

Build new rooms, gather resources to feed the zombies, and make sure you don't become their meal! Be careful not to get trapped, or you'll end up as... their buffet.
Choose among 3 difficulty levels to match your courage. Will you make it out alive?

—description from the publisher

name: Zombie Horde
description:
Zombie Horde is a cooperative board game for 1 to 5 players. In Zombie Horde, survivors live in a colony, trying to survive the aftermath of the zombie apocalypse. The colony is the heart of the game.

GAMEPLAY
The game is divided into rounds, and one round is composed of 2 phases: the Colony phase, and the Exploration phase.

Each phase is divided into steps.

COLONY PHASE: the Colony Phase takes place on the Colony Board, and is played following 7 steps in order. These 7 steps form one phase.

EXPLORATION PHASE: The Exploration Phase takes place on the mission map tiles. During this phase, players activate their survivors in any order, even alternating them, and perform up to 3 actions. When the survivors finish their activation, the zombies activate. Players resolve the effects of zombie activation, then the phase is over.

When both phases have finished, that is 1 round. The next round starts from the first step in the Colony Phase.
The game ends when the cure is found, or all survivors are dead.

-description from designer

name: Zoo and More
description:
A 5 card game compendium with 4 decks of custom cards comes with rules for several games:


     Chai Tea Jazz: Modern version of Coiffeur-Jass with all the fixings.
     Hodge Podge Dodgeball: Team Avoidance game as you play a must-not-follow trick-taking
     Bug House Millionaire: Climbing/shedding game about passing your partner cards in real-time
     Short Zoot Suit: Trick-taking game about short-suiting.
     Through the Zoo: Meta game about standard deck games


—description from the designer

name: Zoo On
description:
Collect, shelter and feed the cutest animals to build the most incredible zoo. Choose a pawn companion and cross points paths. In order to shelter and feed them, you will need to build parks by drawing enclosure, habitat, food and animal cards. Layer and combine your cards to accumulate points and help your pawn companion progress faster throughout his adventure. The best animal combinations will bring you closer to victory.

Zoo On is available in four game modes: Solo, Family, Team and Advanced. In Advanced mode, you will be able to swap cards, upgrade your Zoo and score more points with end-of-game bonuses.

name: ZooJourn
description:
Welcome to ZooJourn, a wild adventure where you are a zoologist and your mission is to journey around the world and collect animals of the Animal Alphabet from A to Z.

Journey around the world and collect Color Animal Cards or Mystery Animal Cards. As you collect animals, you create alphabetic animal straights to collect points. Good Luck and Have Fun! (Just watch out for the Pernicious Poacher!)

Along the way, you will encounter many fun challenges against your fellow zoologists.

The first zoologist to earn 12 points wins the game and will be known as The World's Greatest Zoologist - at least until next time!

—description from the designer

name: Zoology
description:
When the pages of the Great Encyclopedia Zoologica burst open, the wild is unleashed and only sharp minds can restore order.

The Great Encyclopedia Zoologica has cracked, scattering creatures from alpacas to platypuses into a chaotic world where instincts run wild and facts matter more than ever. In Zoology, you become a team of curious and quick-witted zoologists, trying to identify animals based on clues and characteristics before the Age of Discovery slips into an Age of Chaos.

Zoology is a 2–6 player deduction game where you become zoologists identifying animals scattered from the Great Encyclopedia Zoologica. Players secretly receive an animal card (visible only to others) and must deduce their own identity by asking comparative questions about characteristics, appearance, and behavior.

The game blends analytical thinking and clever communication into a lively 15–30 minute puzzle. Play competitively to identify your animal first, or co-operatively to identify all animals within a turn limit. Optional modules and fun facts add variety to this social deduction challenge.

—description from the publisher

name: Zoordinates
description:
The zoo animals are on the loose and need to be pulled back in.

Use multi-functional cards to fulfill goals and capture the animals in this 18-card cooperative wallet game.

name: Cat Earth
description:
ATTENTION all you round earthers out there..."the world is flat"...and cats know it too!  To prove it, they're going to knock stuff off the edges of the world!

Take turns playing movement cards to send the mischievous giant cats bounding across the board, toppling rival houses off the edge of the earth.

Be the last player to have houses standing and claim victory in this ultimate feline free-for-all.

name: ZU Tiles: Fruits Basket – Starter Set 2
description:
ZU Tiles: Fruits Basket turns the popular zodiac cursed family into a strategic tile placement game. Comprise your team with various members of the Soma family who have been possessed by the Japanese Zodiac animals and take family rivalry to a whole new level!

Players can capture tiles thought compatibility matches or battles. The first to collect 12 zodiac animals to join their banquet wins the game. To achieve this, players will place their tiles down in combination with actions and battles.

This ZU Tiles: Fruits Basket 1st Edition comes with a ton of components and limited run Kickstarter items! The tiles and other components feature the fantastic artwork of the Fruits Basket animated series!

Each Set has everything you need to start playing right out of the box. There are 2 decks in a Starter Set for a total of 6 Soma family members per Set. Players strategize to obtain points through battle or by mending family relationships and matching everyone's compatibility with one another. Earning enough points will break the curse of the Japanese Zodiac and allow members to finally become free.

Keep adding to the collection with Zu Tile Slabs, which are found in ZU Tiles: Fruits Basket – Booster Pack! Each starter set comes with one booster pack.

Starter Set 1 consists of the Rabbit, Boar, Ram, Dog, Horse, and Tiger tiles.

Starter Set 2 consists of the Dragon, Snake, Rooster, Rat, Ox, and Monkey tiles.

name: Zurvivor Zchool
description:
Zurvivor Zchool (Z refers Zombies) is a semi-cooperative game in which players take the role of a survivor with difference abilities to against obstacles by test type of status.

Each turn, one player takes on the role of leader and chooses 1-3 members that will face off against the crossroads. If you pass the test, leader gets a card, and members get to level up. In other words, if you don't, you could get hit and injured, which could infect you.

Some cards have mission items to send missions. Once complete, you'll go to the next mission, and if you complete all 3, you'll face the boss! That's the final battle.

When you defeat the boss, the game ends. Check objective and score points. The player who most points win!

This is just a great game for zombie world enthusiasts.

—description from the designer

name: Zwai
description:
Shark alarm off the coast of Hawaii! The infamous shark twins Bob and Ruth are doing their rounds and they’ve worked up an appetite! So look after your fish and get them to safety fast by creating shoals. With a bit of luck, they will slip by the hungry maws of Bob and Ruth. Whoever is the best at schooling their fish will be declared the finner!

Goal:
The goal is to get the most points. To win, place cards with as many of your own fish as possible in the group shoal, taking care they don’t get caught by the two sharks.

Gameplay:
Each player takes 1 set of 23 cards in one colour, shuffle them and place them in front of you in a face-down pile.
On your turn, play 1 card from your hand, placing it face up in the middle of the table. 
The first card is the start of the shoal, which must be exactly 4x4 cards at the end of the round. Place 1 shark next to as well as above the first card played.
Check after each turn whether you need to change the position of the sharks. Whenever there are more fish (regardless of their colour) in a row or column than in those being shadowed by the sharks, move the sharks accordingly to that row or column.
Once there are 16 cards in the shoal, the round ends. Now remove all cards from the row and column that the two sharks are currently shadowing.
Set aside any remaining cards from the shoal as a points pile.

Game end:
The game ends after the third round. 
Count up all the fish in each colour. The winner is the player with the most fish in the points stack in their own colour.

name: À la lettre
description:
A letter game flip and write. Every round, chose one of the two letter cards and place it in your 5x5 grid, trying to make the most 5 letter words. You can use a few special actions during the game, erasing a letter, swapping two letters, adding a 6th letter in the margins, but you get a large bonus in the end if you didn't use any.

—description from the designer

name: Âm Binh
description:
Am Binh is a competitive, strategic card game for 3-6 players. 
Players will become rival exorcists capturing and commanding spirits from Vietnamese folklore. On your turn, draw two cards, then play any number of Action Cards from your hand to attack wild spirits or other players. Capturing spirits grants you their unique powers. Uniquely, defeated players are not eliminated but are reincarnated back into the game. The game ends when all spirits are captured; accumulate the most Spiritual Energy Points from your captured spirits to claim victory!

—description from the publisher

name: Pathfinder Monster Match! Card Game
description:
The only thing more dangerous than the denizens of the world of Pathfinder is Golarion’s monstrous dating scene! In Pathfinder Monster Match!, compete with your friends to court all kinds of curious creatures, from vivacious vampires and dashing dragons to… a sentient pile of ooze? Why not! When animus turns to amorousness, a whole new world of romantic possibilities opens up!

Players will take their monstrous romantic prospects on a wide array of dates to get to know them better and give gifts to demonstrate their affection, all in hopes of finding their perfect match!

Pathfinder Monster Match! supports 2 to 6 love-starved adventurers and plays in about 30 minutes. The game includes 80 cards, 90 wooden heart tokens, and 84 MATCH! tokens.

—description from the publisher

name: Über den Wolken
description:
Winter is coming, so it's time to head south!

In Über den Wolken ("Above the Clouds"), players maneuver their birds to ideal starting points for their great migratory journey, whether that's at the front of the flock or nestled somewhere amongst their companions. To set up, shuffle three birds for each player with three neutral birds, then place them at random on the rows of the game board.

On a turn, you either take one of the four standard actions — with the cost of an action increasing for each subsequent player — or pay the cost of a a maneuver card in hand, then play it. The standard actions allow you to swap adjacent birds, add a new bird to the flock, or take a new maneuver card, whereas the maneuver cards let you swap distant birds or take unique actions. (You can pass as well, but that still has a cost.)

Once all players have exhausted their action cubes, the first bird in each column lands. The more birds you land at once, the more you score — with a bonus if you land a male and female pair at the same time. What's more, you can use maneuver cards to score birds still in flight should they be in ideal positions. After the first and second rounds, move birds in flight forward, then fill gaps with birds from the deck. After three rounds, whoever has the most points wins.

name: Čmeláci
description:
Fuzzy bumblebees buzz through the blooming meadow, flying from flower to flower and collecting pollen from the colorful blossoms. Can you help your bumblebee pollinate as many flowers of the same color as possible in one flight? And will you manage to spot all the meadow dwellers hidden among the grass?

The goal is to collect as many victory points as possible over six rounds. Each player builds their own meadow from cards, trying to form the longest continuous rows of flowers of the same color to pollinate with their bumblebee. In each round, players choose two out of three cards to add to their meadow, then fly their bee along a selected row of flowers. But watch out — you can’t fly along the same row two rounds in a row!

—description from the publisher

name: Изнанка (The Upside Down)
description:
Изнанка ("The Upside Down") is a cooperative adventure board game for 1–4 players, set in a surreal, ever-shifting world filled with strange creatures, hidden secrets, and dark humour. Players explore eerie landscapes, help locals, battle terrifying monsters, and make meaningful decisions that shape a branching storyline with multiple endings.

Gameplay Overview
Each game unfolds over a series of turns where players move across a modular map, explore mysterious locations, and interact with characters and environments. Using action cards, dice rolls, tokens, and special abilities, players work together to complete objectives, overcome challenges, and survive in a world that constantly changes around them.

Exploration & Combat
New areas are revealed by uncovering map tiles, triggering events, finding resources, and meeting NPCs. Combat is resolved through a combination of dice and cards, encouraging teamwork and strategic choices. As the game progresses, characters can upgrade skills and gain new powers, unlocking different paths through the story.

Victory & Replayability
To win, players must complete the central mission, such as defeating a powerful enemy, solving a major mystery, or surviving a critical event. However, every decision influences the outcome. With a nonlinear story and multiple endings, The Upside Down offers high replayability and a unique narrative each time you play.

name: Пенумбра: Испытания Арканы (Penumbra: Trials of Arcana)
description:
Пенумбра: Испытания Арканы (Penumbra: Trials of Arcana) is a competitive euro-style game that blends dice placement, tableau-building card comboing and dice manipulation into an epic adventure with an RPG feel to it.

In Penumbra, you are a young wizard studying in a magical school. Go to classes, develop skills in several magical disciplines, brew potions, summon familiars, gather artifacts — all the sweet stuff that wizarding students usually do.

Every once in a while, the magical world will test your might and resolve with a dangerous ordeal. Angry basilisks, sorrowful ghosts and enchanted wildwood are out there, waiting for you to challenge them and awaken even more magical powers sleeping inside you.

The wizard who best proves their worth during studying and arcane trials will acquire the School Cup and be declared the winner of the game.

—description from the designer

name: Трик-н-Шеф (Trick-n-Chef)
description:
It's time to open your own restaurants. But what kind of establishment would it be without delicious food prepared by a real professional? In this trick-taking game, you will not only have to acquire restaurants, but also hire suitable Chefs, and only then you will be able to earn enough prestige to demonstrate your talent as a real restaurateur!

Players play tricks with restaurant cards each turn. The highest card wins the trick and the player takes the restaurant cards from that trick. The player who played the lowest card hires a chef from the center of the table. At the end of the round, the player gets points for the combination of restaurant cards won and chefs of the corresponding color hired. Based on the results of three rounds, one of the players becomes the winner.

name: Чёрная книга (Black Book: The Board Game)
description:
Чёрная книга ("Black Book") is an adventure cooperative game for 1-4 players based on the Black Book video game developed by Morteshka.

Over the course of six stories, you will have to make many choices: which path to take in the story, how to evolve your character, how to deal with the demons that beset him. Each choice can affect the final story and the entire campaign.

Key features:

     6 atmospheric stories with multiple branches and endings.
     Ability to combine them into a campaign with achievements and new components.
     Unique combat and checkpointing system that reinvents the cooperative genre of games.


—description from the publisher (translated)

name: さいころ民主主義: デメクラシー (Dice Democracy)
description:
Guessocracy: Roll & Vote is a fast-paced party game where players compete to identify the most or least common face value on dice rolled into a central box.

In each round, players have three seconds to assess the dice and vote secretly. The majority vote for the most or least common face value earns points for those players. Players in the minority can use objection tokens to argue for a different result, potentially earning bonus points if are correct, but they suffer a significant penalty if their objection is wrong.

name: ウロボロストリック (Ouroboros Trick)
publisher: 篠原遊戯重工 (Shinohara Yugi Juko)
description:
In a world where the eternal serpent consumes itself in an endless cycle, players embody fragments of that fate: striving to outlast one another in a loop of creation and destruction. Each card played represents a step closer to renewal or demise, as the ouroboros winds tighter with every trick. The only way to endure is to master the rhythm of the cycle before it devours you entirely.

Ouroboros Trick is a trick-taking game for 3–5 players in which survival, not points, determines the winner. Each round, players play one card in turn; the highest card of the lead suit or trump wins the trick. However, the winner must discard cards from their hand equal to the lowest card played that trick, gradually consuming their own hand. When a player runs out of both cards and reserves, they lose, and all others still alive win. This cyclical rhythm of depletion and renewal creates a tense, self-balancing game of timing and risk management.

name: タイムボムQ (Time Bomb Q)
description:
A new original entry in the Time Bomb series to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the original. Shares some elements with the original but is not an expansion or reimplementation.

A team-based game where players use conversation to uncover friend and foe.

The setting is a cyberworld. Amid intense noise, the identities of everyone except yourself are unknown.

The Quantum Police team wins by flipping over all of their Quantum Break Cards, while the Noise Bombers team wins by flipping over four Noise Cards of the same type.

One player becomes the Observer and flips over one card from their hand.

If a Break card is flipped over, the Quantum Police are closer to victory; if it's a Noise Card, the Noise Bombers are closer to victory.

Break and Noise cards have a wide variety of effects that activate when they are flipped over.

Each player has to bluff to negotiate with others on which cards to flip.

Since luck plays a part in which cards are flipped over, even players who aren't good at lying can enjoy this game.

—description from publisher (translated)

name: ダンジャン (Dungeon Mahjong)
description:
Centuries have passed since the old Demon King had been defeated. After a long struggle for influence (playable in Monster Hex), one of the 4 Demon Lords rises to become the new King.

In Dungeon Mahjong players are young adventurers delving into the Royal Dungeon to defeat the Monsters lurking within. Starting with a hand of 6 Guild Cards representing a party of followers from one of 5 classes (Thief, Warrior, Sorcerer, Knight and Monk, corresponding to numbers 1 to 5), each player on their turn chooses one of two actions:


     Discard a Guild Card for its effects
     Reveal a number of cards from the hand to defeat a Monster


The Monster Cards come in 3 levels, each requiring a matching number of Mahjong-like melds (either 3 sequential numbers, or 3 identical numbers), along with additional requirements, to defeat. Defeated monsters join the player's party to bring victory points and helpful special effects. Among the level 3 Monsters, there are the 4 Demon Lords, and to trigger the game end players need to defeat at least one of them (or at least 3 of the other level 3 Monsters). The player with the most victory points at the end of the game wins and is pronounced Hero.

name: ホワイトランナー (White Runner)
description:
Set forth into a thrilling world of speed and snow! Compete against other cross-country skiing animals in the once in a century "White Runner" race to prove your agility, speed, and endurance. Play as the swift rabbit, clever fox, mighty bear, or athletic deer, using their unique skills to outmaneuver your opponents and win the race!

Each round is divided into two sequential phases:


     Skating Style Phase
     Skiing Phase


During the Skating Style Phase, players select one of their four skating style cards to play. The cards will dictate the player order, the amount of available dice, and the possible movement spaces for the next phase. They also modify the players' speed, potentially granting them more dice to use throughout the game.

In the Skiing Phase, players go in order dictated by the stamina cost of their skating style cards. Depending on the card played, players will roll a certain number of dice to earn their movement points. These movement points are spent to proceed in the race, fulfilling the requirements of each movement space ahead. However, players may only move as many spaces as their played skating style card allows.

Being in the lead isn't always beneficial though - jumping over other players counts as one move, so you can advance multiple spaces with just one move!

name: ラーテル (Ratel)
description:
Adorable, ferocious animals appear out of nowhere and survival is not an option. You can’t fight them, you can’t reason with them, but you might trick them into fighting each other while you slip away. Outsmart the chaos before you're the last one left… and the one who pays the price.

Ratel is a climbing game where players try to shed their hands by playing cards with values from +5 to -5. Cards must be played in ascending order, but each card has a twist: positive numbers are strong but add that many cards to your hand, while negative numbers are weak but let you discard extra cards. The trade-off between strength and penalty is constant, and the goal is to escape before the last player is left holding their hand and their fate.

name: 代われそのジョブ (Kaware Sono Job)
description:
Players are members of a peculiar workplace where each person must accomplish specific “job goals,” but after every round, everyone swaps roles entirely—handing off their tasks, tools, and responsibilities to someone else. Success depends on teamwork, coordination, and understanding your colleagues’ work rhythm as you collectively strive to fulfill as many objectives as possible before time runs out.

Kaware Sono Job ("Take Over That Job") is a cooperative trick-taking game for four players played over four rounds. Each player begins with a set of Goal Cards representing how many tricks they aim to win in a round. When a player's actual number of tricks matches one of their goals, that card is discarded as a success. After each round, players pass their entire hand and goals to the next player, forcing everyone to work with the same cards and objectives in rotation.

Gameplay features a “Defensive Stance” system in which only the currently strongest card in a trick remains face up, while weaker cards are turned face down, creating hidden information and tension. Over the course of the game, players also select permanent bonuses—such as setting trump or unfavorable suits—adding layers of strategic coordination to achieve the best collective score.

name: 何食べたい (What Do You Want to Eat?)
description:
何食べたい (What Do You Want to Eat?), a.k.a., Guessing Foodies in Taiwan, is a deduction card game themed around delicious Taiwanese cuisine. Use clues of color and number to guess which dish your opponent has secretly chosen!

In more detail, each turn one player selects a dish card from their hand and places it behind their preference card, hidden from others. In turn, the other players place a card from their hand face up, and the player who chose the dish places the card by "Like" or "Dislike" depending on whether the target dish matches in color or number with the one presented. Using clues from these hints, the other players try to guess the target dish. Whoever guesses correctly first wins a point, and whoever scores the most wins.

Enjoy a flavorful deduction battle with family and friends as you explore Taiwan's tasty treats! Who will be the first to uncover what their opponent really wants to eat? Take the challenge and find out!

name: 如鲠在喉：1940~1942年地中海战役 (A Stick in the Throat: Battle of the Mediterranean 1940-1942)
description:
如鲠在喉 (A Stick in the Throat) is a historical wargame that simulates naval campaigns in the Mediterranean theater of World War II. Players are to step into the position of commanding officers, such as Italian Navy commanders (e.g., Riccardi) or British Royal Navy front-line commanders (Cunningham and Somerville), leading their respective forces in a struggle for the control of the Mediterranean during the 28 months period of intense naval operations, starting from July 1940 (Operation Catapult) and ends in October 1942 (just before Operation Torch).

While the standard ruleset provides a streamlined experience of the operational level naval actions. There are also a range of optional rules that brings additional what-if units extra historical details and fog-of-war rules which can stir up the play and brings additional flavors.

The game includes a 2-turn long learning scenario (covering the 3 major resupply operation of Malta: Harpoon, Vigorous, and Pedestal),3 standard scenario (covering the naval operations during 1940, 41 and 42 respectively), 1 campaign scenario covering the entire 28 month period, and 1 alt-history scenario where Italy has finished its war preparations and enters the war in 1942 into a grand showdown with the reinforced and modernized British Mediterranean Fleet.

Components:
1 Rulebook
5 Player Aids
1 594x420mm Map
280 Counters
44 Cards
1 10-sided die

name: 私だけの晴天 (Watashi dake no Seiten)
description:
Rain pours gently as each player waits for their own clear skies. In a game of restraint and precision, players choose the moment to declare their personal trump color — not to dominate, but to balance. The goal isn’t to win the most, but to win just enough, exactly when the timing feels right.

私だけの晴天 (My Own Sunny Day) is a must-follow trick-taking game where each player can independently declare a personal trump suit mid-round. This declaration (called the “umbrella”) acts as a bid and players must aim to match the number of tricks won before and after it. Overcommit, and you’ll overshoot. Wait too long, and the timing might slip away. The second half flips the challenge by weakening hands while still requiring finesse in timing.

私だけの晴天 is a trick-taking card game with a poetic and thematic twist: each player experiences a "journey" of departure and return home under shifting weather, symbolized by umbrellas. The game adds a whimsical yet strategic layer where players must choose the perfect moment to open and close an umbrella, aligning with their position and the color of the cards they play.

The gameplay centers on traditional trick-taking mechanics—each player plays one card per round, and the highest card in the lead suit typically wins the trick. However, a unique twist occurs when players possess an umbrella that matches the color of the card they play. In that case, they become “Sunny,” gaining a powerful advantage that can override the usual hierarchy. But each player may only open and close their umbrella once per phase, making timing and planning essential.

The game unfolds in two phases: Departure and Return Home, each consisting of 13–14 tricks. In Departure, players must choose a moment to open their umbrella, and in Return Home, they must close it. Each trick won with or without an umbrella contributes differently to the player's final score: tricks won with an umbrella count as positive points, while those without count against you.

The goal is to finish the game with the lowest total score. Success requires balancing risk and restraint—sometimes winning a trick hurts you more than losing it. With its blend of light storytelling and clever card play, My Own Sunny Day is a contemplative game about finding just the right moment to step into the sun.

name: 街コロ (新装版) (Machi Koro: Revised Edition)
description:
街コロ (新装版) (Machi Koro: Revised Edition) features the same gameplay as the original Machi Koro, with each player developing their own city and trying to be the first to build all of their landmarks.

This new edition supports up to five players instead of only up to four, with the card balance being slightly adjusted and the card design and size being updated — which makes it incompatible with previous Machi Koro titles and expansions.

name: 重ねて色をつくるゲーム (Kasanete Irowo Tsukuru)
description:
It is a game in which 7 types of cards are superimposed to create the colors of the illustrations written on the 16 theme cards.
The color cards are made of transparent PET material, and the colors blend together by layering.

There are seven types of cards, including the three primary colors of the color material (cyan, magenta, and yellow), dark and thin, respectively, with black added.

The way to play is to reproduce the colors of the 16 theme cards.
It is difficult to match the colors of objects with different materials (paper and PET), and you will not know if you are reproducing the colors correctly until you put them side by side.

You can play with up to 6 people.

name: "Normal" Human
description:
Act Natural! Because "Normal" Human is hilarious. It's new. And it's arriving soon!

Aliens have landed. But don't worry, they're friendly. ?

In fact, one has become your buddy. His name is "Al" and he's been on the run from government Agents. You must protect him by acting "normal".

Each round drops players into a new setting with a fresh "normal" activity to play out. Get ready for goofy scenes, quick improv, and nonstop laughs as everyone scrambles to keep Al hidden!

—description from the publisher

name: Pathfinder Quest
description:
Sharpen your swords and ready your spells because the people of the Darkmoon Vale are in danger and they need your help! Gather up to three friends and explore the mysteries of the vale and uncover the villain behind the sinister forces that threaten to reduce the entire region to a pile of smoldering ash.

Pathfinder Quest is a cooperative adventure board game for 1–4 players. Build your character(s) from the ground up by choosing their ancestry, class, and ability cards—or dive right in and play a prebuilt iconic hero! From character creation to combat challenges and exploration, each player’s actions matter, with choices that ripple throughout the entire multisession campaign.

Designed to bridge the gap between quick, randomized dungeon crawlers and sprawling, prep-heavy delves, Pathfinder Quest offers a full campaign of 12 possible adventures, each lasting approximately 2 hours. With no GM required, an introduction that swiftly teaches the rules as you play, and a rich narrative that rewards teamwork, this game is sure to be a hit whether your group is new to tabletop gaming or seasoned veterans of the adventuring life!

Pathfinder Quest includes an Adventure Book (detailing each one of the possible dozen adventures you might experience), a Challenge Book (containing the hidden outcomes for many of your choices), map tiles, custom dice, hundreds of cards, monster pawns, and select miniatures as well!

—description from the publisher

Pathfinder Quest: Endless Adventure Mode uses the creatures, map tiles, and components within Pathfinder Quest's box to generate random encounters and challenges. Don't have time for a full session? Roll up some encounters and dive right in!

name: 100vs1: Gorilla Clash
description:
100vs1 – Gorilla Clash is a fast-paced co-op card game where you and your friends chain human combos to force the Gorilla Deck to discard, while the Gorilla fights back, trying to dump your humans into the K.O. Pile. The first deck to run out of cards loses.

On the humans’ turn, each player chooses and plays one of the 5 types of human cards: Athletes, Fighters, Rescuers, Strategists, and Peels. Combo 3 or more of the same type, and you trigger a specific effect. Then, on the Gorilla turn, reveal the top card of the Gorilla Deck and apply its effects.

Peels are the hot potato of the arena: play them in a combo, and nothing happens; keep them in your hand, and if the Gorilla makes you discard, chaos follows. Talk and joke around the table to guess what others are holding, plan big, game-changing combos, choose the right moment to ditch the trouble cards in your hand, clash to block the Gorilla’s biggest moves… and peel your way to glory.

—description from the publisher

name: 1066: Year of Destiny
description:
1066 is a three player game covering the various claimants to the crown of England following the death of Edward the Confessor in January 1066.

The players fulfill the roles of Harald Hardrada, Harold Godwinson and William of Normandy. The game is split into 4 phases each of which is designed to illustrate a key component in determining who takes the crown.

Firstly there is a Pre-Invasion Political Event phase (PIPE) which is designed to showcase the political intrigue that took place prior to the death of Edward. During this phase the players can gain additional support from other leaders and regions and, crucially, they can gain additionally legitimacy from various monarchs, religious bodies and events. Many events are outside their control; death of the Aethling, Scandinavian Wars and the activities of Tostig but they will also be crucial.  This simple game preamble will provide an infinite variety of starting points to be played out on the map itself. In addition this phase can be a time of acquiring operational and tactical chits to use advantageously later.
Legitimacy is central to the game. Unless a player gains an automatic victory then a players legitimacy level will be key in determining who has won the war. As well as during the PIPE phase it can also be changed by winning and losing battles and by taking controlling of areas on the map.

However before the Operational phase there are the perils of the sea crossings. When to sail is a crucial decision by both William and Hardrada. Go early and the weather should be kinder, go later and you can recruit more troops.  Lady luck, in the form of stormy seas can destroy the best laid plans, in addition the prevailing winds can prevent you invading, even when you  are ready to go (as occurred to William). If a crossing goes badly wrong, or you lose an early decisive battle your claim lies in shreds. Don’t despair – ‘Become a Dane’. A player can abandon their attempt, as William or Hardrada, and instead take up the cause of Sweyn of Denmark and try and gain the throne for the Danes (they historically invaded in 1069). It won’t be easy winning as the Danes but it means you are still in the game.

The first week in September is a dangerous time for Harold as the Fyrd stand down to collect the harvest, is this the time to strike? , will the weather conditions be in your favour.
In the operational players move around the map of England to gain control of areas and improve their legitimacy as well as deciding when to strike to win a decisive battle against one of the two opponents. The operational phase is a real ‘rock, paper, scissors’ problem. How to square the problems of keeping your forces concentrated to win battles, spreading them out to take control of areas whilst keeping them feed without turning areas into wastelands.

 When battle is joined them the action is transferred to a battle board where the individual characteristics of the differing armies is highlighted. The longer you stay on the battlefield the bigger the loss if you are defeated; often the losses from pursuit are greater than the losses from the battle itself. Winning and losing battles result in big legitimacy swings which can decide the game.  
 Never before has this iconic campaign been gamed with all four key facets illustrated (politics, invasion, operational campaign and battles)
There are a number of very good battle games but not much for the operational phase and nothing showing the political interplay or the perils of the sea crossings themselves.
The victory conditions for each player differ slightly, requiring differing strategies for each side. 
Sweyn of Denmark is waiting in the wings. If no one ‘Becomes a Dane’ then the system takes over the game system will determine if he arrives or not. Leave London inadequately protected and he will take it and without it neither William or Harold can win a decisive victory.

The game is easily playable in a single session (4-5 hours)
4 Kings 1 Crown – have you got what it takes to become the undisputed King of England.

—description from the designer

name: 12 Monks
description:
The story unfolds in the 12th century, at a time when Portugal was still taking shape.

With his armies advancing southward, King Afonso Henriques could not abandon the lands newly conquered from the Moors and decided to donate a huge plot of land in the heart of the country (44,000 hectares) to a monastic order of French origin called Cistercians. This community of monks, which had already settled in other regions, would have to manage the territory and resources of this place. In order to do that, an enormous monastery was built in Alcobaça and that same monastery would go on to become one of the most important for the Order.

The Cistercians' motto was Ora et Labora (prayer and work), so their abbeys were usually in secluded locations. Silence for their prayers was paramount, as was easy access to stone (in order to build the monastery) and several other goods, such as wood in order to build boats through which the produced goods were exported, and iron (essential to build farming equipment and tools). Fertile land and access to water (necessary for food, hygiene, and agriculture) were also essential to achieve self-sufficiency. 
Alcobaça filled all the requirements for the task, so the Cistercians accepted the king's challenge — and this is the historical background from which this game was born.

12 MONKS, is a competitive game in which players take on the role of the Cistercians monks entrusted by the King to promote the settlement, explore and manage the goods and resources of the couto of Alcobaça while building the monumental Monastery of Alcobaça.

—description from the designer

name: 13 Nightmares
description:
13 Nightmares is a solo print-and-play board game about lucid dreams, surreal experiences, and facing your inner fears. Each dream is a unique mini-game with its own rules and challenges, but they all connect through a shared hero board that develops with every attempt. Gain focus and control over your dreams with every attempt,  collect objects and carry them over from one dream to another, survive all nightmares one by one to break the loop and finally wake up.

—description from the designer

name: 14ers
description:
Colorado is a state full of adventure, but its greatest challenges are the mighty mountains towering above. The highest of these peaks reach over 14,000 feet elevation, and are called "14ers." Can you conquer these climbs and assemble the best collection of peaks bagged and stories earned across one summer?

14ers is a quick tableau-building card game where you will take turns adding one "Climb card," each representing a different 14er, to your Hiker by tucking the Climb card under one of the four sides of your Hiker card to reveal a specific ability they can now use for the rest of the game. These abilities can either help you gain more difficult and powerful Climb cards or score points at the end of the game. You may also have to deal with  weather along the way, or have the chance to hire Guides to help you climb difficult routes! After 9 rounds, count up your score based on which 14ers you have climbed and what abilities from them you chose; the player with the highest score is the winner!

We are excited to feature original artwork from Hinterland Outdoors based in Colorado. All art is made without any use of AI and is licensed from the original creator.

—description from the designer

name: 15th Stamp
publisher: Dragon Dawn Productions; Dragon Dawn Games
description:
The '15th Stamp' takes place in the great Halls of Bureaucracy in Odrixia, continuing the story of Factory 42 and Mine 77. Many documents flood across the desks of overworked government officials, and they all have to be stamped and authorised according to due process. In this fast-paced trick-taking game, mistakes happen and tables turn - just make sure you’re one of the officials who get to make their mark.

15th Stamp supports 3-7 players and plays in about 15-20 minutes.

Components:
80 suit cards in 8 suits
scoring pad

Play
For each Trick, beginning with the Lead player, you play 1 card at a time in clockwise order around the table until the combined Rank value of played cards hits the Target Value of 15.

You do not have to follow suit and can play any Suit with any Rank into the Trick. As soon as the total Rank value of the cards reaches or exceeds 15, the Trick ends immediately. This may mean that players may have played different numbers of cards into the Trick. Some may not have played a card at all.

When playing cards to the Trick be sure to play them separate from the other player’s cards so it it easy to remember and retrieve your own.

name: 17 Dice Bets
description:
In 17 Dice Bet, you score points by predicting which dice(8D) combinations you can form by freely choosing dice from both the Shared Dice and your Personal Dice.
After the final round, the player with the highest score wins.

—description from the publisher

name: 1807: The Big Four
description:
18BF is a game in the 18xx series set in Great Britain.

A game of route building and running trains to make money. The player with the most assets (cash and share value) at the end wins.

Corporations start out small and grow into larger ones through growth, merger and/or acquisition. Then, later in the game, these larger corporations can merge to form systems: the "Big Four".

—description from the designer

name: 1809: Talavera
description:
1809: Talavera is the second volume in the"Fix Bayonets!" series of Napoleonic tactical wargames. It covers, at the battalion level, the two days of the battle with one player in charge of the Anglo-Spanish armies and the other leading the French forces. It can be played solo, playing both sides.

Components:

    One (2-panel) 55 1/2" x 22" mounted map.
    6 double-sided color counter sheets with 18 "Fix Bayonets!" markers, 168 3/8x3/4" markers, 220 1/2x1/2" markers, 372 3/4x3/4" unit counters.
    One 24-pages Battle booklet.
    One 56-pages Rules booklet.
    Two identical 17x11" player aid cards.
    One 17x11" Turn & Tracks sheet (similar to the one in Albuera) 
     two custom 10-sided dice, one for each side.
    One 11x8.5" + two 17x11" Order of Battle sheets
    47 Leader and Special Event cards

name: 1812!: War on the Atlantic Seaboard
description:
1812! War on the Atlantic Seaboard is a card-driven strategic wargame that simulates the naval and land actions fought on and around the Eastern Coast of North America and the Gulf of Mexico during The War of 1812. This is a stand alone sequel to 1812! War on the Great Lakes Frontier.

This is a two-player game with either player commanding the naval and land forces of the United States of America or the British Empire. It can be played with four players when combined with the original game into an entire war campaign.

Players will alternate playing Strategy cards, spending Operation Points and causing historical events to occur. Operation Points are the currency used to move and fight battles with military units.

The scale of fighting units is regimental and single ship with some naval units grouped or removed to create solid gameplay. Each leader, regiment and naval vessel has been researched to determine its relative strength and weaknesses based on battle performance, unit size, and type. With limited land armies and naval battles mostly confined to single ship frigate and privateer actions the forces are manageable although challenging to coordinate compared to the original game.

Also contains expansion content for the original Great Lakes Frontier game including new regiments, errata updates and the counters, cards and order of battle for a new scenario.

—description from the publisher

name: 1813: Napoleon's Struggle for Germany
description:
THE SITUATION
Spring 1813. Napoleon´s 1812 invasion of Russia ended in catastrophe and the loss of practically the entire army.
Prussia has switched sides and they and the Russians are now invading the lands of Napoleon´s German client states.
Austria has so far opted for neutrality but is biding its time to intervene.
Napoleon, in a impressive administrative feat, has hastily raised a new army and is now returning to Germany to reverse the situation.

The Spring campaign saw the Coalition forces pushed almost to the breaking point and only saved by the Truce of Pläswitz, which allowed both sides a long period of rest and buildup.
The Fall campaign would be a totally different kind of campaign with 2 massive opposing armies fighting a series of battles which culminated Napoleon´s defeat at the battle of Leipzig - the largest battle in world history at that time.
   
Will Napoleon and his hastily raised army be able to break up the Coalition and restore French dominance over Germany or will 1813 become the year of German liberation?

THE GAME
1813: The Struggle for Germany is a 2-player game that simulates the 1813 campaigns in Germany at the operational level.
There are scenarios covering both the Spring campaign and the Fall campaign as well as rules for linking them into a combined game.
It is volume 2 in the "Marshals & Quartermasters" series which is an easy to play card-driven system that utilizes secret order placement which ensures constant tension and little to no downtime.
As befits the period, the system features a strong focus on logistic planning and attrition with a set of simple but highly narrative mechanics.

—description from the designer

name: 1848: The Springtime of Nations
description:
"Do you not feel, through a kind of instinctive intuition that cannot be analyzed but that is certain, that the ground is shaking once again in Europe? Do you not feel—how shall I call it?—that a revolutionary wind is blowing?"
– Alexis de Tocqueville, Souvenir (January, 1848)

33 years after the Congress of Vienna, Continental Europe still lives under the reactionary system designed by the Austrian Prince Metternich, the dominant figure of the age. Outside of England and France, absolute monarchy is the norm - and even in the latter, Louis-Philippe, the “bourgeois king”, is busy rolling back the people’s hard-fought liberties.

In the east, the empires of the “Holy Alliance”, Austria, Russia, and Prussia, enforce ruthless repression against progressive ideas - whether nationalist, republican, democratic, liberal, or socialist. But the time is ripe for revolution, and the conflagration of 1848 will shake this old system to its core in a whirlwind of insurrection and new ideas. “People’s wars” will rage.

1848: Springtime of Nations is a 2-player CDG depicting the unprecedented wave of revolutionary activity that swept across Europe in the titular year of 1848. Based on the hit area control system pioneered by GMT’s 1989: Dawn of Freedom, and Twilight Struggle, it pits the forces of “the Revolution” against those of the “Counterrevolution” in a struggle to decide the future of Europe, and the world.

The Revolutionary player controls the various insurgent and progressive movements trying to usher in a new order, while the Counter-Revolutionary player leads the forces of reaction aiming to preserve the status quo. They will fight over and across the empires and nations of Europe, attempting to suppress their enemy’s influence and extend their own through a combination of political and military force - all the while navigating myriad historical events of the time.

—description from the publisher

name: 1877: Stockholm Tramways
description:
In 1872 Stockholm Tramway Company was founded with the ambition of constructing tramways in Stockholm. Having failed to do so the company was dissolved in 1874 only to be founded again two years later under the new name Stockholm New Tramway Company. The new company was successful and on July 10, 1877, the first horse-drawn carriage traversed the streets of Stockholm. The tramway era had begun.

1877: Stockholm Tramways is a game in the 18xx series set in Stockholm. The players are investors in tramway companies during the late 19th century and the first half of the 20th century (1877 - 1966). In contrast to other games in the 18xx series, 1877 allows players to perform hostile takeovers under certain circumstances.

—description from the designer

If you want to make your own PnP copy, see PnP Files.

name: 1878 Gotland: Railways in the Baltic Sea
description:
18xx set on the island of Gotland in the Baltic Sea off of Sweden´s east coast. 3 to 5 players invest in and manage a total of 10 railway companies with the ultimate goal of becoming the wealthiest investor.
Questionable stock manipulation, fierce rusting of trains AND tracks, and existential dread is ever present - all while laying rail on an island so small you can see your bad decisions from the other side.
Unique features of 1878 Gotland compared to most other 18xx titles is an unusual initial Private auction featuring Entanglement cards, Privates with different powers depending on ownership, a map full of "dits" which emphasizes the importance of creating lucrative routes more than ever before, both full and incremental capitalization, and more...

name: 1880: Romania
description:
In 1880: Romania, based on 1880: China, the players become railway barons in Romania, experiencing the country's railway history in a game that was designed to represent related historical events as correctly as possible within its own game mechanisms. Being a classic 18xx game, the players compete to become the richest. In order to gain money, they buy and sell shares of Romania's historical railway companies, build and expand their railway network, and let trains travel on the networks. Shares of successful companies are worth more, and owning them will increase the chance to win the game. In the end, the player with the highest wealth combined from cash and shares wins.

1880: Romania uses the mechanisms of its sister game 1880: China which uses the 1829 rules from Francis Tresham as a base, and features a few innovations:


    Turn order for companies doesn't change with the evolving stock prices; it is set along with the par price when a player opens a company.
    The game includes a player-manipulated ratio of stock rounds and operation rounds. For example, a new stock round occurs when the last of a type of train is bought.
    Foreign investors develop track independently and once they are connected to a railway, they add their accumulated wealth to that railway
    The historical border between Austria-Hungary and Romania cannot be crossed in the yellow phase


1880: Romania offers the full experience as its Chinese sister game, but with a smaller map and significantly less playtime. A special map used for 2 and 3 player games can be found on the back of the regular map.

—description from the designer

name: 18Hedjaz
description:
18Hedjaz is a strategic railroad game set in the Ottoman Empire in the late 19th century. It centers on the construction of the Hedjaz railroad from Damascus to Medina - a project with religious, military and geopolitical significance. Players take on the roles of investors and railroad directors, build routes, trade in shares and influence the development of the region. But resistance, for example from Lawrence of Arabia, threatens progress.

The game is based on the mechanics of the 18xx series:

     Switch between stock market rounds (share trading, dividends) and operating rounds (train operation, line construction).
     New elements: Hedjaz phase (route development in the Ottoman Empire) and Lawrence phase (sabotage, loss of income).


Special features:

     Unique faction abilities (e.g. money bonuses, espionage) that create asymmetrical starting conditions.
     Private companies that are auctioned off and offer tactical advantages.


18Hedjaz combines historical themes and economic strategy. It offers high replayability through diverse combinations of abilities, companies and geopolitical events. Whoever controls the railroad shapes the future of the Middle East - but must be prepared for disruptions and power games.

—description from the designer

name: 18Saxonia
description:
18SX Saxony is an 18XX design that contains thirteen corporations, with up to ten of them being put into play over the course of the game, with "concessions" being made to determine who may start which companies distributed in a start-packet system.

The game has a unique track system in which directors have to choose between single and double track, with those choices having an effect on route length.

18SX Saxony is a heavy reworking of 18SX from the same author.

—description from the publisher

name: 1942: Battle for the Mediterranean
description:
1942: Battle for the Mediterranean is a two-player wargame simulation of the naval operations in the Mediterranean in January-October 1942. The objective in the game is to sink the largest possible number of enemy warships and enemy shipping, and to keep supplied their respective ground forces and bases in North Africa (for the Axis) and Malta (for the Allies).

Combat units represent individual capital ships (battleships, battlecruisers, heavy cruisers, light cruisers, fleet carriers, light carriers), destroyer or smaller escort divisions of 2-3 ships, individual submarines, groups of merchant ships and escorts vessels, and aircraft squadrons of 20-25 planes.

Each game turn represents 1 month of naval operations. The campaign game covers 10 game turns, from January to October 1942. There are also shorter 1-turn scenarios simulating the major convoy battles of the 1942 campaign: Second Sirte, Harpoon/Vigorous (Battaglia di Mezzo Giugno), or Pedestal (Battaglia di Mezzo Agosto).

name: 1943: Race to Rabaul
description:
In 1943 the Allied push across the Pacific reached a critical phase. Every step toward Rabaul demanded nerve, planning and a constant fight with the limits of supply. 1943: Race to Rabaul puts you right in the middle of that pressure.

This time the series introduces opposed play. You can play as a team or head-to-head, with one or two players commanding the Japanese side and one or two leading the Americans. Both fronts chase momentum, both struggle with logistics and both try to outthink the other before their plans run dry. The map is wide, resources are tight and every choice has weight.

The result is a game where ambition always meets resistance, and the path to Rabaul is never straightforward.

—description from the publisher

name: 2D6 Void: A Sci-fi Dungeon Crawler
description:
2D6 Void is set in a modern day Coradine, which is the setting from 2D6 Dungeon. You play as a pilot adventurer, with a specific profession and set of skills.   You have volunteered to infiltrate the Dark Hulk and battle your way through ten levels to the engine room where you will blow up the ship that is laying waste to your planet. You will then become a Hero.  2D6 Void is a standalone game that uses the 2D6 Dungeon Engine. It is a sci-fi dungeon crawler, print and play, roll and write game.

You will need the 2D6 Void rules, two different colour six sided dice, an additional two six sided dice, a pencil and a dot grid sheet to draw the map on, and the Character Sheet (provided at the rear of the book).

If you know how to play 2D6 Dungeon then you’ll be ahead of the game when it comes to this new sci-fi version. Rooms are generated the same way with several additions and have many new features to explore. The core engine of the combat is the same but now we also have ranged combat as well.

2D6 Void is a standalone game that is loyal to 2D6 Dungeon and brings with it a whole range of new engaging thematic elements that take you into the future!

—description from the publisher

name: 5-Minute One Piece
publisher: Wiggles 3D; asmodee; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
5-Minute One Piece is a real-time co-operative game where players assemble a pirate crew and race to finish an island adventure before time runs out. Inspired by the Netflix live-action adaptation of One Piece, 5-Minute One Piece is a reimplementation of 5-Minute Dungeon: players work together to match symbols with cards in their hand like in 5-Minute Dungeon, but have the additional challenge of matching sequence by slotting cards onto the Going Merry game board.

In detail: The group chooses one of five Adventure Decks to face together, then each player picks a Straw Hat character card (Luffy, Zoro, Nami, Usopp, Sanji, Chopper) and their unique deck for themselves. Once the timer starts, players reveal the top card from the Adventure Deck which may show an enemy, event or ally. Defeating enemies (which may have their own passive abilities) is accomplished by clearing Challenge Cards, which are all 4-symbol sequences. Players play cards in real-time onto the Going Merry game board until the sequence of cards played match the sequence of symbols on the Challenge Card. Once enough Challenge Cards have been matched in this way, the Adventure Card is complete and can be replaced with the next one.

5-Minute One Piece is designed to be playable for all ages: while players have a variety of character abilities and special symbol card actions to get out of tight spots and succeed on high difficulty modes, teams of newcomers can still win using just the symbol-matching gameplay if they prefer. Higher difficulty modes add cumulative time pressure and incentive to utilize special abilities for players seeking a challenge.

—description from the designer

name: 5Pairs
description:
5Pairs is a quick, clever, and colorful card game that anyone can learn in a minute. Players race to collect matching cards, form sets, and outsmart each other in a fast-paced battle of wits and timing. With simple rules and snappy turns, it’s designed to be the perfect “just one more round” game for families, casual players, and game-night warmups alike.

Each turn, you’ll draw cards or try to build valuable pairs. Make a pair of the same color or number to score points — but the right timing can earn you double! Every decision matters, and every move can swing the momentum in your favor.

As players race toward their fifth pair, things heat up — bonuses appear, points can be stolen, and clever combos turn simple moves into big swings. The first to collect five pairs ends the round, but getting there takes equal parts luck, observation, and timing.

Bright, fast, and endlessly replayable, 5Pairs fits in your pocket but brings big-table energy. It’s a filler game that rewards quick thinking, light strategy, and friendly competition — a simple game for simply everyone (except Steve).

—description from the publishe

name: 7 Ages: Collector's Edition
description:
7 Ages is a game covering 6000 years of human history from 4000 BCE to today. Players lead dynasties that decide the fate of the world across the ages. You, as a dynastic head of one or more civilisations, must guide your people through history gaining glory points for historical, scientific, religious, and cultural advances as you increase their health, wealth, and prestige. All the leading figures of history are included, as they attempt to influence events and their society through their great words and deeds. Are you game to change history?

7 Ages: the Collector's edition has been enhanced, expanded and streamlined. It includes 67 new civilisation cards, 165 in total. There are counters for 6 new empires, 21 in total, allowing up to 7 players to control 3 empires each, as you vie for a peaceful prosperous planet.


    Maps have been graphically updated, new areas included and they will be hard-mounted on linen boards.
    Artefacts have been expanded and improved. There are 17 new artefact types you can build and 155 artefacts in total, more than double the 70 in the original game.
    Leadership has also been enhanced, with 130 named leaders and 43 unnamed leaders (up from 72 and 22 respectively) throughout history.


The number of options has been doubled from 6 to 12 and includes 3 that are part of the 7 Ages Expansion sets, Secret Victory, Neutral Kingdoms and Deus Vult!.


    Secret Victory is an easy way to keep everyone's glory secret so no one knows who is really winning.
    Neutral Kingdoms means provinces are no longer denuded when an empire is discarded. Even if you have given up on them, the people still live there and don't take kindly to strangers (not to mention former overlords).
    Deus Vult! is a religious expansion that allows empires to explore a variety of religions and the building of temples to their God or Gods. Not cheap, but what price Glory?


-description from publisher's website

name: Beasts
description:
Beasts is a co-operative card game in which players work together to climb ever higher through a series of three-digit numbers, transforming the current number by strategically covering one digit at a time. Each player plays all cards of a single suit from their hand on their turn, always aiming to create a new number that's higher than the last.

But things get wild when the beasts arrive. These mischievous creatures correspond to specific card types — like Whole Hearts or Broken Spades — and once they show up, they restrict where those card types can be played on the board. Beasts are startled when placed above matching cards, which makes them move (or even flee), and part of your team's challenge is luring and managing these creatures so that they don't block your most valuable options.

Each player has limited information they can communicate, so the game hinges on clever planning, interpreting your teammates' cues, and maximizing every turn. With just a few shared discard tokens and an ever-growing number, your group will need to work in perfect sync to survive all the beasts and play every card in the deck.

Complete the deck, tame the chaos, and claim victory with the highest number possible — if you can outwit the beasts.

—description from the publisher

name: 8 Dragons
description:
Legend has it that eight mighty Dragons once rose from the mountains as darkness swept across Sinistra and Dextra. They drove out the evil and restored peace. Since then, they have guarded the two kingdoms.

A new generation of Dragons is rising. You are one of them.
And you don't fly alone.

Dragon Swarm placement meets lair building.
Minimal downtime. Maximum Dragon time.

In 8 Dragons you play a mighty Dragon soaring across two kingdoms. But you don't fly alone. Your Wyrmlings have just hatched and are eager to fly. You form Swarms, with your own Wyrmlings and those of the other Dragons.

On your turn, you visit wondrous locations and activate effects for yourself and every Wyrmling in your Swarm. When your Wyrmlings fly with others, you benefit from their turns too.

Along the way, friendly villagers help you expand your Lair, chamber by chamber. Collect artifacts, fulfill Missions, and hoard as much Gold as you can.

And as befits true dragons: whoever hoards the most Gold wins.

name: A Dragon's Gift
description:
High atop the mountain, a single dragon looms over a peaceful village. Each year, the local craftspeople placate the dragon with an impressive gift to ensure the village's safety. Help out by making sure each villager has what they need to deliver the final gift!

Connect roads and use transports to supply villagers with the goods they need. Create the final gift to please the dragon and win!

Build your map by adding new cards, connecting along road lines. Deliver goods along existing roads or use a special transport to enable unusual routes. As you fulfill villagers’ needs, they’ll offer higher-grade goods. Put together all three goods for the dragon’s gift to show your full appreciation!

name: A Fading Star: Insurgency and Piracy in Somalia
description:
A Fading Star: Insurgency and Piracy in Somalia is Volume XV of the COIN Series originally designed by Volko Ruhnke. The year is 2007. We reach the climax of the several decades of civil war that have ravaged Somalia since the fall of dictator Siad Barre in 1991. An African Union coalition, assisted by the Ethiopian army, enters Mogadishu to support a nascent but corrupt Transitional Federal Government. They face a relentless and violent insurgency waged by Harakat al-Shabaab al-Mujahideen, an Islamic group seeking both to expel the "invaders" and to transcend the traditional clan-based government structure of Somalia. In the middle of this power vacuum, minor clans and warlords organize themselves to administrate otherwise ungoverned regions, while others engage in large-scale piracy operations, painting their acts as a fight against foreign trawlers pillaging Somali fishing resources.

Highlights:

     An updated take on contemporary aspects of insurgency and peacebuilding. The Al-Shabaab insurgent enjoys intelligence supremacy that allows them to conduct deadly out-of-turn ambushes, while facing a slightly less pronounced asymmetrical disadvantage than insurgent factions in previous volumes (due to the comparative weakness of the Transitional Federal Government). On the other hand, the African Union Mission's logistical, kinetic, and peacebuilding capacities will evolve as contributing countries join or leave the coalition throughout the game. 
     Intense urban warfare is depicted in more detail through the struggle for control of the capital city Mogadishu. Controlling a majority of districts will provide the ruling faction with further legitimacy and enhanced capabilities. However, limited operational effectiveness, mobility restrictions, and the looming threat from a major Al-Shabaab offensive will greatly slow the COIN factions' progress toward stabilizing the city.
     A new ‘Clan Struggle’ interphase draws out some of the conflict's unique uncertainties. All sides bid to forge new alliances with local clans, bringing new blood to the battlefield, while the African Union must deal with the consequences of delayed reinforcements or unilateral withdrawals by member countries, and the Pirate warlords collect lucrative tolls from roads and ports that they control. 
     A unique piracy subsystem debunks the Somali pirate mythos and explores how piracy stakeholders' interests actually intersected with other local actors during the golden age of Indian Ocean hostage-taking.  


Each turn eligible players will select from a faction-specific menu of Operations and Special Activities in an order determined by the current Event card, or choose to trigger the Event text. Typical Operations include Sweep, Assault, March, and Attack, with more unique Operations and Special Activities reflecting the specific nature of this conflict and the factions involved. Regular play is periodically interrupted by Propaganda rounds, during which early victory is possible and some upkeep is conducted; and by Clan Struggle rounds (unique to this game), during which all players have the opportunity to bid for the loyalty of an unaligned regional clan. If nobody achieves an early victory then the winner will be determined by comparing victory thresholds in the final Propaganda round. Each faction has unique victory conditions relating to their aims and objectives during this period of history.

Faction descriptions:

     Al-Shabaab wages a deadly Islamist insurgency against the African Union ‘occupiers’ and their dependent Transitional Federal Government allies. A clear edge in media warfare provides them with significant recruiting capacities that will help them build a Somali caliphate transcending the customary clan system.  
     Ugandan and Burundian troops serving in the African Union Mission in Somalia (AMISOM) aim to enforce peace, build support for the Transitional Federal Government, and train the weak federal army. Neighboring Ethiopia and Kenya may also enter the scene to stabilize their respective borders while interfering in Somali politics. 
     An abysmally weak Transitional Federal Government seeks to survive in a besieged Mogadishu while reaching out into the rest of the country to advance the federalization process. Unprecedented embezzlement capacities and partnerships with like-minded clans may offer the consecutive administrations an opportunity to survive the conflict unharmed and more prosperous than ever, and a new kind of militia unit emphasizes the opportunistic nature of the Somali clans' agendas. 
     Pirates, minor clans, and unaligned warlords pursue their enrichment projects by raiding the high seas or setting up roadblocks across unruly parts of the country. They'll settle for a "customary" Somalia, neither rooted in sharia law nor totally anchored to the liberal world order. 


-description from developer

name: Gatsby
publisher: Catch Up Games; 999 Games; Pandasaurus Games
description:
Welcome to the Roaring Twenties! Gatsby is a two-player game in which you take on the role of either Dorothy Williams or James Miller, competing to spread their influence and draw the attention of the great Jay Gatsby.

On the board are three locations, each offering different opportunities to get character tiles: the cabaret, the finance center, and the racetrack. To claim these characters, each player will take turns moving the action marker on one of the four action spaces — but not the one just taken by the opponent — then activating it.

These actions let you place two influence tokens on one or two locations, allowing you to claim characters in different ways, depending on the location. In the cabaret, your tokens must form a continuous line from one side of the board to the opposite side or cover the four-star icons at the same time. In the finance center, influence lets you climb up the track. In the racetrack, your tokens are placed in races, trying to be the player with the most tokens on that race line when it's filled.

On all three locations, some special spaces on the board grant bonuses when you place a token on them: swapping two tokens on the board, forcing your opponent to take a specific action, or gaining a special action tile!

A player wins immediately if they control three characters of the same color or one character of each of the five colors. If all character tiles from a single location have been claimed before one of these conditions is met, the player with the most stars on their characters wins.

—description from the publisher

name: A Forlorn Hope
description:
A Forlorn Hope is an abstract simulation wargame of a typical trench assault, modeling those attacks that were conducted during the First World War (1914-1918). The player represents an attacking regiment of troops consisting of three battalions, with each battalion made up of two or three assault companies (depending on the number of players).

The game uses a "press-your-luck" design philosophy that will challenge you with tough decision-making and risk-taking throughout the game. The goal is for the player(s) to drive their forces across No Man's Land in the quickest and most efficient manner possible to achieve the best level of victory.

A Forlorn Hope is designed both for solitaire and multiplayer co-operative play. Numerous scenarios are included, starting with a basic assault scenario (which is ideal for learning the intricacies of the game system), then adding multiple historically-based scenarios simulating actual battles from World War I that offer a slightly more complex and layered gaming experience. Each scenario features singular aspects of the historical battle it is simulating, and each will therefore be a unique gaming experience.

—description from the publisher

name: A Strong War: The Conflict for North America
description:
The title, A Strong War, refers to the type of war the Abenaki Nation threatened to unleash on the land-grabbing British in 1753. The sparks of war, ignited in 1754 near Fort Duquesne by an obscure colonel of Virginia militia, George Washington, spread quickly; soon, flames engulfed the entire globe as England and France vied for control of empire.  Over the next 5 years, Regular regiments from the French and British armies, American and French-Canadian provincial units, and Native warriors all fought in a chaotic and violent series of campaigns and frontier raids that culminated in the British conquest of French Canada and the defeat of the Native Nations (most of which had sided with the French).
A Strong War brings this war to life in a simple, fast-playing game.  The map (covering the region stretching from Louisbourg to Alexandria, and from New York to Lake Erie) uses point-to-point connections to highlight the key locations that were targeted during the war.  Using wooden cubes to represent the different types of forces used (French and British Regulars, British Colonials, French-Canadian Marines, French Bush Rangers, and Native American warriors), each player has only a few pieces (maximum 13 for the British and 10 for the French) to use each turn (one turn = one year, so there are 6 turns/years total). 
The heart of the game is the unique combat system where players can deploy forces to a chosen battle and then commit them one by one; or they can call off the battle if it goes badly and save some of those forces for use later in the year.  The types of forces committed also play a critical role in combat – the British want to mass their Regulars but the French want to bring in a mixed force to take advantage of the different skill sets each provides.  Thus, tension is created in trying to decide if/when (or where) it is best to commit one’s forces: do you avoid combat completely; do you call off a combat that is going badly; or, do you go all in and commit your entire force?  But if you lose a battle, initiative then swings to your opponent who may then launch an offensive. 
Each player has several paths to victory, leading to a “different” game each time, and forcing players to choose between different strategies each turn.  Finally, it is a quick game, taking just a couple of minutes to set up, and usually taking less than an hour to play to completion.  The game also plays well solitaire, though there is no dedicated solitaire system.

—description from the publisher

name: A Time of Heroes: The Battle of Kursk
description:
Η διάσημη αρματομαχια του Β 'Παγκοσμίου Πολέμου, μεταξύ του Κόκκινου Στρατού και του Γερμανικού Στρατού, ζει μέσα από τις εξαιρετικές κάρτες του παιχνιδιού. Τα ακριβή στοιχεία όλων των μονάδων, οι μοναδικές τακτικές, η στρατηγική υψηλού επιπέδου και η δυνατότητα δημιουργίας μιας μοναδικής σύγκρουσης σε κάθε ξεκίνημα ενός νέου γύρου παιχνιδιών, αυξάνονται το μέγιστο, τόσο στην αναπαραγωγή όσο και στην απόλαυση του παιχνιδιού, και για τους 2 και 4 παίκτες ...

The famous tank battle of World War II, between the Red Army & the German Army, lives through the exceptional cards of the game. The accurate elements of all the units, the unique tactics, the high level strategy & the ability to create a unique conflict in every start of a new game round, are growing the most, in both playability & enjoyment of the game, for both 2 and 4 players.

How to play:
The game can be played either with 1 vs 1 or 2 vs 2 as pairs.
Each player or pair, takes the role of either the German Army or the Soviet Army.

The game has a damage point system to figure the winner. The first player who reaches 20 points (40 points for 4 players) on board meter, will be the winner of the battle. Damage points are equal to life points (red cross with specific number in each card).

Every card has 7 different sectors (boxes):

Upper: from left to right :
First box - Velocity of weapon
Second box -  Weapon's Penetration level 
Third box - Own armor level
Fourth box - Own life points

Lower:
First box - movement 
Middle Double number target - 2 x 12sided dice (black for German/White for Soviet), both numbers in dice is the damage area for the weapon. A 10 on the dice is a Critical hit & any unit who receives this damage must be removed from the battle ground.
Finally, the blue pointer with the specific number is the encounter points needed for this unit to use it in the deployment phase of the battle.

Each turn:
1. Encounter points (both armies start with 5 each)
2. Draw phase - each player draws 2 cards
3. Move phase - each player can move their units
4. Deployment phase - each player can deploy any unit if he has the necessary encounter points
5. Engagement phase - each player can attack the enemy player based on the abilities of their units
6. Discard phase
7. End of turn

Before the first turn all players must draw 5 cards each and receives 5 encounter tokens. There is a 7 card hand limit. Some cards can give the player the ability to draw a general commander
card from their own general deck.

There can be no more than 2 generals active during the battle, but a player can change a general card by discarding the old one and playing a new one.

Each general gives 1 additional encounter points in the beginning of each turn. Also, each player receives 1 encounter point every turn and 1 additional point for every unit deployed in the battlefield.

Players can combine cards if it is allowed in the card's description but only until the end of the turn (except the end of battle for some cards)

Air units are visible during the battle and while performing an attack. If enemy anti-aircraft wapons are available, they must be countered

Units with low penetration levels cannot attach enemy units with higher armor level.

Special cards can give the player's units unique abilities during each battle.

First player who reach 20/40 points will be the winner of the battle & the game ends.
