name: A.S.H.E.S.: Blackout Protocol
description:
A.S.H.E.S. (Artificial Shelter & Human Evacuation Sequence)

From the ashes, the Phoenix will rise again.

After decades of political tension, the planet succumbed to the Great Nuclear War of 1989. In a matter of days, cities were reduced to dust and the sky burned red.

Amid the ruins, the survivors organized themselves to rescue humanity, reactivating ancient evacuation systems and building the first underground shelters.
Thus was born the A.S.H.E.S. Protocol — Artificial Shelter & Human Evacuation Sequence — a network of subterranean colonies created to preserve what remained of the human race.

Two years later, the last survivors work tirelessly to rescue civilians, rebuild civilization, and develop a project capable of restoring life to the surface: Project Phoenix.

In A.S.H.E.S.: Blackout Protocol, you will lead a colony of survivors in their attempt to fulfill that purpose. Rescue civilians and bring them to safety, construct new shelters, and advance the development of Project Phoenix, bringing hope back to humanity.

HOW TO PLAY

The game is played over four rounds.
At the end of the game, the player with the most victory points wins.

On your turn, you can perform the following actions:

1. Take an action in your base

Take a civilian from your base and place them in an action space on your personal board to perform one of the main actions of the game: Build Shelter, Develop Project Phoenix, or Rescue Civilians. Additionally, you’ll receive a production bonus that lets you produce fuel, data, or time.

1.1. Build Shelter:

Spend time from your colony to construct a new shelter where rescued civilians can live and join your efforts.
Take a shelter card, gain its immediate rewards, and receive income each round.

1.2. Develop Project Phoenix:

Craft materials and gather data to upgrade your colony and contribute to humanity’s greatest objective.

1.3. Rescue Civilians:

Take civilians from the map and place them in your shelter cards to gain immediate benefits or recurring income each round.

If you complete a shelter, you may flip the card to gain additional victory points each round, at the cost of its income.

2. Move your colony

Spend time on the time track to move your colony across the map. From new locations, you can construct additional shelters.

3. Move your van

Spend fuel to move your van to another location on the board.
Use it to transport civilians to your shelters, perform extra actions, and collect materials to craft and advance Project Phoenix.

ADDITIONAL ACTIONS

In addition to your main turn, you may:

Fulfill a card from your hand (at the beginning or end of your turn).

Craft new materials to complete Project Phoenix.

END OF ROUND

At the end of each round, radiation affects all unrescued civilians remaining on the map, lowering your colony’s morale.

A.S.H.E.S. Protocol completed.
Active shelters: 12
Evacuated civilians: 1,742
Project Phoenix — Phase I: initiated

“From the ashes, we endure.”

—description from the publisher

name: Abbatissa
description:
In the southern border of the West Frankish kingdom, Wilfred the Hairy was appointed to govern several counties in 870. To repopulate the abandoned territories of Ausona and connect his Pyrenean and maritime territories, he sponsored the foundation of a monastery in the Sant Joan valley, to which he gave his daughter Emma, who became its first abbess.

Abbatissa is a two-player game that simulates the conflicts between Abbess Emma of the Monastery of Sant Joan and her brothers from the houses of Barcelona-Ausona and Cerdanya-Besalú. One player will take the role of the abbess (abbatissa) and the other the role of the nobles (nobilitas). The abbess's goal is to maximize the monastery's properties, thus fulfilling the repopulation objective of its foundation. The objective of the nobilitas is to profit from the expansion of the monastery by obtaining privileges over its lands and influence over its abbess (prestige and control).

The engine of the game is a shared deck of cards. At the beginning of each turn, the top card of the deck is activated and whoever has the initiative can choose whether to use its text or value. Activating a card for its value grants a certain number of action points (AP) that can be used to perform one or more actions from among the available ones. Players can repopulate territories, found churches and obtain property rights over different places but also exert influence in the various courts to dispute these rights judicially and ask for favors from the king or the pope. The text of the cards represents important characters and events related to Emma and the conflicts with her brothers.

Cards continue to be revealed and activated until the “Death of Emma” card is activated. At this point the game ends and the victory conditions are checked. Cards continue to be revealed and activated until the “Emma’s Death” card is activated. At this point, the game ends and the victory conditions are checked.

—description from the publisher

name: Abyss Echo: The Forbidden Rite
description:
One morning, a mysterious package breaks the silence. Inside is a diary written in 1925 by a student at Miskatonic University—a school that, to your knowledge, does not exist. Yet as you read deeper, secrets begin to surface. Every decision you make seems to reach back in time, rewriting a destiny from nearly a century ago.

Abyss Echo: The Forbidden Rite is a narrative-driven tabletop game for 1-4 players (fully playable solo). It seamlessly blends puzzle-solving, novel reading, dice combat, and physical artifact investigation to present a dark cosmic horror adventure.

				
				
					Gameplay Mechanics
     The game core revolves around a unique binder system. As the story progresses, you must personally unseal "Sealed Files" and add new pages, allowing the plot to evolve in real-time in your hands.



     Your mental state is tracked via the SANscope. You must carefully manage your sanity when performing checks with the 8-sided Fracture Dice.



     Sift through ultra-realistic narrative artifacts to solve mysteries. Your progress is visually recorded on the "Trophies of Fate" wall using achievement stickers.



     Combat is not just about comparing stats. You must physically drop your attack dice from a designated height into a specific zone. If the dice miss the zone entirely, the consequences will be dire.


				
				
					Legacy Elements & Replayability
     As the story unfolds, scratch off the surface of character cards to reveal hidden traits, secret bonds, and shadows of the past.



     Your choices within the story will lead you to one of 13 unique endings.


Can you save Miskatonic University from destruction, or will you be swallowed by it? Remember, when you gaze into the abyss, the abyss also gazes into you.

—description from the designer

name: Academia: A Game of Administrative Bloat
description:
Academia: A Game of Administrative Bloat is an engine-building, action-management game about running a university that uses a unique action-selection mechanism.

Players are the boards of directors of their universities, choosing the big strategic initiatives from year to year. Each turn represents an academic year in which the player will choose one of four strategic focuses (actions) for their university. When selecting a focus, players choose one of the four offices at their university. Each ready staff member in that office works, triggering their effect. Each focus requires players to exhaust staff, meaning the game is about managing which staff are ready and when. Over the course of play players build facilities, hire staff, advertise, recruit students, form faculty committees and so on.

Every four years, students will graduate and affect their university's reputation: star athletes improve athletics reputation, high performers academic reputation, and so on. Players then admit new students, and begin again. After three cohorts of students have graduated, players score prestige from reputation, communications efforts, faculty committees, and personal objectives, then the most prestigious university wins.

—description from the designer

name: Across the Kingdom
description:
Across the Kingdom is a solo roll-and-write adventure. With nothing but two dice and a single pencil, you’ll journey across a sprawling realm - charting wild frontiers, uncovering hidden treasures, battling fearsome monsters, and lending aid to the hardworking folk who call this land home. Explore boldly, for every discovery brings you closer to a name worthy of the royal chronicles.

Your expedition spans four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter. Each season grants you 4-5 turns to press deeper into the unknown. At the start of every turn, roll two dice, choose a terrain type, and mark five matching hexes on your map. Seek glittering gold to fill your coffers, collect shields to defend against monstrous threats, complete labor tasks for grateful townspeople, and reveal as much of the kingdom as fate allows.

When the final snows of winter settle and your year of adventure comes to an end, tally your deeds. The kingdom will remember every bold step you took and celebrate the hero you’ve become.

—description from the publisher

name: Adventure Games: Mission Mars
description:
September 2076: Why hasn't a signal been sent from Mars Base Alpha for weeks?

In Adventure Games: Mission Mars, the United Earth Government is sending a rescue mission to the first settlement on Mars. The team: one to four players aged ten and over. The astronauts have special abilities that will help you slip into exciting roles in the analog PC adventure so that you can experience the story for yourself. Many challenges await over 100 million kilometers away...

name: Kingdom Crossing
publisher: Sorry We Are French; Cranio Creations; Gém Klub Kft.; Pandasaurus Games; Tranjis Games
description:
In a faraway land in the midst of a verdant forest crossed by the Crystal River lies the small kingdom of Brightspring, ruled by the wise Queen Beavery, who is facing a problem: Her four regions are separated by seven bridges, and to divide her time evenly between the subjects of these regions, the kingdom would need an eighth bridge...

Help the Queen build a new bridge! Scour the kingdom, recruit the best artisans, gather construction resources, and create magnificent decorations. Note, however, that you can never use the same bridge more than once in the same day.

Kingdom Crossing is inspired by the problem of the "Seven Bridges of Königsberg", and gameplay combines engine-building and programming mechanisms, with a solo mode that features an Automa and four difficulty levels.

—description from the publisher

name: Paper World
publisher: Lumberjacks Studio; GateOnGames; Gém Klub Kft.; Granna; Pandasaurus Games; Tranjis Games
description:
In Paper World, each player takes on the role of a traveler trying to recreate the landscapes they have seen during their journeys using layers of paper. Stack the various layers of paper you find to have the most victory
points at the end of the game.

On your turn, you can either:
TAKE one or more cards.
PLACE one or more cards in front of you, forming your landscape.
In both cases, the rule is the same: take / place cards of the same color or the same value.

When only 2 piles of cards remain in the center at the end of a player’s turn, the end game is triggered. Each player, including the one who triggered the end of the game, plays one more turn before the final scoring.

The player with the most stars on the cards wins. In case of a tie, the player with the fewest cards in their discard pile wins.

name: Tricky Kids
description:
Welcome to the playground! In Tricky Kids, you and your classmates are trading toys and snacks in a chaotic kid-economy where value is totally made up. It’s a trick-taking game with a twist: you write the numbers on your cards. At the start of each round, you assign values that total 21 across your hand then use those cards to try to win tricks and collect points.

Each round consists of 7 tricks, but the goal is to win tricks strategically, not just frequently. Each trick earns you a point token, and the leftmost available token is always the one you claim (so timing matters!). The tokens have different values based on which suit won the trick, making both when and how you win crucial to victory.

The game unfolds over 3 rounds, and after 21 tricks total, the player with the most points wins! But watch out: if your card values add up to more than 21 at the end of a round, you lose all the points you just earned... and possibly some from earlier rounds too!

With optional “Tricky Rule” cards to mix things up each round (like passing your hand, playing with dual-suit cards, or unexpected win conditions), Tricky Kids keeps players guessing and giggling with every play.

—description from the publisher

name: Adventurers Required
description:
Once upon a time, there was a veeery tired wizard...

In Adventurers Required, players can land their dream job: Who hasn't always wanted to be HR manager of a guild? Assemble a team of sneaky adventurers, tiptoe into the wizard's tower, and snatch his treasures. But beware! Alongside their skills, the team’s noise rating is cruicial. If things get too loud, they’ll wake the wizard. And that would be very bad...

At the start of each round, players have to hire one new team member. And yes, it will be tricky to choose from the recruits: A card from your hand, one from the market or will a lucky draw hire the perfect team member from the draw pile?

From bard to druid, every adventurer comes with their strengths - and also a certain noise level! But even the loudest can be silent as a shadow with the right partner. Once your dream team is ready, let the wizard snore on… send them in and leave with the biggest haul – and victory! After only five rounds, the player with the most treasure wins.

Adventurers required is a beginner friendly card game, plays super quick and will make you crave: Again, please!

On top, it's manufactured eco-friendly as part of Lookouts GreenLine.

-description from publisher

name: Aegeapolis
description:
Welcome to classical Greece! 
It's 431 B.C. and your leadership is urgently requested! 
Guide the fortune of the naval power of Athens, the belligerent Sparta, the trading giant of Corinth or the seven-gated Thebes.

You decide how you want your civilization to succeed. Will Sparta become a democracy with strong maritime trade? 
Will Corinth conquer their neighbors and become an aristocratic empire? 
Will Athens manipulate the other players and surprise everyone with a hidden agenda?
Everything is possible - you decide!

The game is played on a 5 x 5 raster. The four (or three) players start in a corner. 
It's about exploration & expansion, about trading and diplomatic agreements.
Aegeapolis is an economic game at its core. 
You can establish trade routes with neutral cities and with other players. You can capture neutral cities, 
conquer player poleis (cities) and disrupt their trade.

To win the game you earn victory points. This happens in recurring scoring rounds by investing resources, 
by having the largest empire and by agenda civilization cards which surprise your opponents with your hidden goals and scoring opportunities.

name: Aeon Trespass: Twelve Sins of Herakles – Summer
description:
Twelve Sins of Herakles is a campaign game about adventures, exploration and fierce battles with giant monsters. Set in the same game universe as Aeon Trespass: Odyssey, it’s a co-operative, choice-driven boardgame experience played over multiple sessions.

In an alternate Antiquity, where a reality-shattering cataclysm killed the Olympian gods and unleashed the otherworldly Primordials, Twelve Sins of Herakles places the players in the roles of Argonauts, the only people who can fight off the darkness and make things right. The base game covers three regions and three campaigns.

—description from the publisher

name: Tulikko
publisher: Studio H; Dino Toys s. r. o.; Pandasaurus Games
description:
Legend has it that Tulikko, the fire fox, lives hidden among the animal spirits in the depths of the forests of the far north.
On certain winter nights, he runs so fast that he produces sparks that rise into the sky to create the Northern Lights. 
Explore these mystical forests to discover the territories of the animal spirits and be the first to reveal their secrets!

Tulikko is a game of tile-laying and optimization set in a dreamlike Scandinavian world!

Carefully choose the Forest tiles by sliding them of the central board and arrange them as best you can on your personal board to accommodate your Animal Spirits. 
Complete objectives and trigger special powers and be the first to place all your tokens to win the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Aetherium: The Forgotten Duel
description:
Aetherium is a 15-20 minute abstract strategy game for 2 players. This forgotten duel was once a sacred rite used by ancient civilizations to maintain harmony through the four elements. Lost empires fell and centuries passed, its knowledge faded into myth and silence. Now, the game has resurfaced, calling for new duelist looking to find immortality.

Goal
Either have all stones of an element at the top of each column by the end of your turn, or bring the Aether token to your side of the track as far as you can.

Gameplay
The game is played in three rounds. Each round, players alternate taking turns using one of their five element pawns to perform an action on their side. Once all pawns have been used, move the Aether token and prepare for the next round.

On your turn, choose one of your element pawns that you haven't yet used this round, place it on any of the circular spaces on your side of the mat and resolve the corresponding action.

Every action must follow these rules:
You can only move stones that match the element pawn played for the action. When you play your wild pawn, declare which element it will count as for that turn.
You must be able to do the entire action (if you cannot, choose another action or pawn).

—description from the designer

name: Age of Bitcoin
description:
Our world has been flooded with paper bills since money broke free from the gold standard in 1971. Inflation kept rising, and the price of goods and services seemed to skyrocket! It feels like just working hard isn't always enough to get ahead these days; making smart investments is often necessary!

Then, in 2009, a new form of money was born — Bitcoin! At first, it was once dismissed, laughed at, and even traded for pizza. But before too long, it became something everyone was looking into, getting on board with, HODLing (which in the crypto world just means holding onto it!), and finally seeing as digital gold. And that's how the Age of Bitcoin begins!

In Age of Bitcoin, players take on the role of individuals from various professions, seeking to accumulate wealth through investments in a variety of assets—including real estate, businesses, collectibles, contract-based assets, gold and Bitcoin. Players will primarily do this by buying and selling assets, hoping to time the market and outwit their opponents.

Once the 5th round is over, the game ends and it's time to total the points. The player with the most total Wealth points wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Agricola: Special Edition
description:
The cycle of farming is eternal — plowing, sowing, harvesting, and ensuring that every mouth is fed. Life on the farm is simple yet demanding, requiring both strategy and resilience to thrive.

Agricola: Special Edition revitalizes Uwe Rosenberg’s iconic board game, bringing it to life with new artwork and refined usability. This special edition includes all previously released expansions and introduces Irrigations, a brand-new expansion that challenges players to manage water resources to sustain and grow their farms.

—description from the publisher

name: Air & Armor: V Corps
description:
Air & Armor: V Corps, Operational Armored Warfare in Europe is the second game in the Air & Armor series. Air & Armor is a grand tactical simulation of a hypothetical Soviet attack on West Germany in the mid-1980s. V Corps depicts the collision of the Soviet 28th Army and  1st Guards Tank Army with the U.S. V Corps in the Fulda Gap. Three maps cover the sector from the Inner German Border all the way to Frankfurt.

Air & Armor employs a highly interactive game system with asymmetric rules modeling the different command & control capabilities of each alliance. The game simulates all major aspects of modern warfare, including reconnaissance, combined arms operations, air, helicopter, and artillery strikes, chemical and electronic warfare, and combat engineering. Multiple levels of hidden intelligence produce a true “fog of war” providing plenty of opportunities for deception, surprise, traps, and ambushes. Play this game to experience what it would have been like to command a division in battle if the Cold War had gone hot.

Air & Armor: V Corps features twelve different scenarios, each a complete game by itself. Each scenario covers a different battlefield operation, including a meeting engagement, a delaying action, a frontal assault, an attack on a fortified line, a blocking action against a Soviet OMG, an armored cavalry covering force, two NATO counterattacks, a desperate defense of a broken line, and a surprise attack with NATO still in barracks.  Extensive Scenario, Player, and Designer Notes provide advice on play and historical detail.

Air & Armor is ideal for solitaire play.  The hidden intelligence system provides a high level of tension during solitaire play because, even though a solo player is commanding both sides, he never knows what he will hit when he conducts an operation.

Product Information:
Complexity:  High
Time Scale: 1 Turn = 2 Hours
Map Scale: 1 Mile/Hex
Unit Scale: Companies to Regiments
Players: 1-7 Players
Solitaire Suitability: High
Playing Time: 3 to 12 hours based on Scenario

—description from the publisher

name: Airborne Assault: Crete – May, 1941
description:
"How was Crete? It was perfectly all right, except that it was a bloody […] up from […] to breakfast time.”  – Brig. George Vasey, Commander, 19th Australian Brigade., 1 June 1941

Early in the morning of 20 May 1941, the Germans launched history’s first totally airborne invasion. As their objective, the Germans chose the island of Crete, strategically located in the Mediterranean between Greece, Cyprus, and the coast of North Africa. Defending this rugged and isolated island were the rag-tag Allied survivors of the ill-fated Greek Campaign, comprising Australian, British, New Zealand, and Greek units. Although 42,000 strong, they were woefully weak in ammunition, artillery, rifles, heavy weapons, radios, wheeled transport, and other logistical equipment.

The German airborne assault force comprised the 7th Air Division composed of three assault regiments and attached units, and the elite “Sturm” Regiment. As follow-up support, air transport and sea would land the 5th Mountain Division convoy to relieve the paratroops. They divided the initial airborne assault into four separate assault forces, each based on one of the four parachute regiments.
The battle hung in the balance during the first day. Despite their considerable advantages, the Germans could easily have lost because of faulty intelligence and arrogance in planning. In the end, the British could evacuate only about half their forces and practically none of the equipment, making this another Allied disaster like Dunkirk a year prior.

Airborne Assault: Crete is a grand-tactical level game of the historical WWII invasion of Crete and includes the hypothetical paratroop invasion of Cyprus. The game requires two players and is suitable for team play.

The game focuses on the first few days of battle, keeping players’ attention on maneuver and what is vital to winning the battle. Players will find a familiar game rules framework covering the combined arms problems of airborne assault, air support, and bombardment, and sea invasion. The defender balances where to defend and when to evacuate. As a bonus, an exciting and balanced scenario showing a hypothetical June 1941 German invasion of Cyprus is included.

Complexity: 4 out of 10
Time Scale: 3 turns = 1 day
Map Scale: 1 hex = 1 mile (Crete), 1 hex = 2 miles (Cyprus)
Unit Scale: companies and battalions
Number of Players: 2 players or 2 teams
Solitaire Suitability: 6 out of 10
Average Time to Play: scenarios range from 3 to 9 hours

—description from the publisher

name: Airport Empire
description:
Build Your Airport, Connect the World. Airport Empire is a thrilling tycoon board game where you’ll compete to transform your small airstrip into a bustling international hub. To achieve this, you must balance the needs your your passengers, airlines and shareholders while managing daily events.

Players roll the dice to earn money from fees paid by landing planes and improve your airport by either improving customer satisfaction, profits or efficiencies. Ensure you balance your needs  to score in three categories, customer satisfaction, profits, and efficiencies.

Secret missions, event cards and bonus cards keep you on your toes. You must constantly evaluate and be dynamic to ensure your airport is successful.

But only one player can win. Whoever completes their score card in profits, efficiencies, and customer satisfaction takes victory - unless the secret missions have been achieved or not, which can change the balance of the points and crown a new victor.

—description from the publisher

name: Aliens Attack!
description:
The aliens are attacking Earth! You’re on a mission to defeat them and destroy their mothership! WILL YOU SAVE THE EARTH?

In a card game reminiscent of vintage video game shooters, in Aliens Attack! you must fire your cannons at advancing waves of invaders! You win if you survive long enough to destroy the mothership after it arrives in the Combat Area.

Aliens Attack! is a solo game that comes with rule for a 2-player variant. There are also 4 different motherships to attack, all of their own strengths and very few weaknesses!

—description from the publisher

name: All In: Predictions
publisher: Next Move Games; Gém Klub Kft.; Hobby Japan; MIPL; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
In All In: Predictions, players become gifted foretellers vying to shape destiny itself. Combine hand management with strategic foresight in this fast-paced game inspired by classic poker in which only one prediction will unfold. Play cards, bend probabilities, and guess who holds the strongest hand to claim the pot.

Will you see the future...or just think you can?

—description from the publisher

name: Dinosaur Island: Fully Charged
description:
Dinosaur Island: Fully Charged is an improved 2.0 version of Dinosaur Island that includes all of the content from Dinosaur Island: Xtreme Edition + Totally Liquid: Xtreme Edition PLUS new and improved gameplay content and upgraded components.

New gameplay content included:
- 2 new executives
- 10 new specialists
- 7 new objectives
- 2 new modules (temporary workers and DNA tokens)
- change in order scoring
- an official solo mode
- a new rulebook!

Additionally, small carnivores now have pack bonuses; when you create multiple they grant special excitement bonuses for eating hooligans. Every aquatic dinosaur now has a unique ability that's triggered when guests visit. Upgraded components include magnetic dinosaur meeples that stick to game tiles, neoprene mats, and metal coins.

We took 10+ years of game data and player feedback to smooth out a lot of balance issues and provide more variability and strategy, making this the best Dinosaur Island iteration yet!

name: All's Well That Ends
description:
All’s Well That Ends is a fantasy, campaign-style adventure game for 1 to 4 players. Together players form a party of reckless profiteers and wayfarers exploring the untamed reaches of the Western Wildlands. Your goal is to hunt down a roving band of slavers and killers, and to exact a bloody revenge.

Throughout the campaign you will uncover clues as to the nature and whereabouts of these villains while fighting against countless hostile forces, not stopping in your pursuit until justice – as you understand it – has been served.

The story plays out over several chapters, each of which draws you deeper into the Wildlands as you discover clues, add allies to your roster, and become increasingly deadly with new abilities and equipment.

You can also play individual combat scenarios for a quicker, bloodier gaming experience.

—description from the designer

name: Alone against the Zone
description:
Alone Against the Zone is a solo narrative survival game set in a mysterious and hostile exclusion zone inspired by Eastern European post-disaster landscapes. Blending horror, exploration, and resource management, the game casts the player as a lone stalker venturing into a dangerous territory filled with anomalies, abandoned facilities, and hidden threats.

Designed as a sandbox hexcrawl adventure, Alone Against the Zone emphasizes freeform exploration over linear storytelling. The Zone is generated and explored hex by hex, with each location presenting unique dangers, discoveries, and opportunities. Rather than following a branching narrative, players create their own stories through emergent gameplay, shaped by risk-taking, preparation, and chance.

Gameplay centers on survival and decision-making: managing health, equipment, and scarce resources while navigating hazardous environments and resolving encounters. Each expedition is unpredictable, driven by random events and discoveries that can quickly shift the situation from manageable to deadly.

A distinctive feature of the game is its legacy-style continuity. When a character dies—as they often will—the game does not end. Instead, players may continue exploring the same map with a new stalker, inheriting part of the previous character’s equipment or discoveries. This creates a persistent sense of progression and an evolving relationship with the Zone itself.

Atmospheric and unforgiving, Alone Against the Zone focuses on isolation, tension, and emergent storytelling. There are no companions—only the player, their decisions, and the ever-dangerous Zone.

Key Features:

Solo sandbox hexcrawl exploration
Persistent game world with character succession mechanics
Emergent narrative shaped by player decisions and random events
Resource management and high-risk survival gameplay
Strong thematic focus on isolation, danger, and discovery

How long can you survive—and what will you leave behind for those who follow?

—description from the publisher

name: Alpha Team Mechanized Battle Force Go!
description:
A giant monster is attacking the city! You and your friends must use the power of teamwork to overcome evil... with awesome!

Alpha Team Mechanized Battle Force Go! is a co-operative game with pick-and-pass style card drafting where players work together to defeat a giant monster. Draft cards to defend against monster attacks and to pull off combos with your teammates to save the city.

name: Alpujarras: Rebellion & Punishment
description:
Rebellion & Punishment: War Of The Alpujarras is a 1-2 players strategical card-driven game that recreates the war between the rebel Moriscos who attempted to re-establish the Muslim Kingdom of Granada and the Christian troops of the Kingdom of Spain who fought to prevent it.

Cards are played as Action Points or as Events, allowing players to advance across the terrain or perform actions specific to their faction. The game map reproduces the entire territory of the former Nasrid Kingdom of Granada and includes the areas where uprisings and battles took place.

name: Alto
description:
Level up your discs to score more points – but don’t get too comfortable. The tiles guide your discs… but beware: once used, they flip and change direction. Use them a second time, and they’re removed from the game – potentially disrupting your entire strategy. Who will outsmart the shifting board and find their way to victory?


     Each tile offers different ways to move your disc. Aim higher – the better the level, the more points you score.
     Beware: Each tile can only be used twice. After that, it disappears. Don’t get stuck!
     Score 1 point for the first level, 2 points for the second, and so on. The player with the highest score wins.


—description from the publisher

name: Am I Human Game
description:
Hello fellow Human! In a world infiltrated with AI characters, prove you are the true Human by getting rid of as much AI as (humanly) possible. The player left with the most Humans at the end of the game is the winne... err, true Human.

Am I Human Game tasks players to gather sets of AI characters, to get rid of them! Get out of here AI goop! Only then can you save our fellow humans. But, the generative goop can also generate some awesome combos, depending on which card of the AI set is being played. You can even save Superhumans if you build a whole set of AI.

The Goal: To bank as many Human cards as possible. The catch? You can only bank Human cards if there are no other cards left in your hand. Play actions and AI suits to clear your hand. You can play a row of 3 or more AI cards on the table or add AI cards to an existing row.

End Game: When the draw pile is depleted, each player will have one more turn to clear their hand to bank humans and earn Super Humans. The player with the most banked Human cards at the end of the game is the winner.


    No AI was used or abused in the making of this game, only free-range, ethically-treated humans were utilised in the making of this product.

name: Amarok
description:
To understand Amarok, the wolf spirit, your logic alone won't suffice. Guardian of forests and symbols, he is a reflection of your instincts. You'll have to think like him and read the souls of your opponents!

In this competitive deduction game, you will have to win successive rounds by having the best two-card combination. But be careful, with each round you win, your knowledge of the cards will decrease to the benefit of your opponents.

—description from the publisher

name: Anastyr Chronicles
publisher: Don't Panic Games; This is a Game.
description:
Anastyr Chronicles is a cooperative campaign game set in a dark and savage fantasy world. You play as the Companions of the Spear, heroes bound by fate who journey across the lands of Alboraan in search of the fragments of the World Spear, an ancient artifact powerful enough to defeat Anastyr, the Dragon Queen, and her dragon Volkar.

Each Adventure unfolds on a modular board that evolves through a scrolling system inspired by beat 'em up video games, simulating continuous movement across shifting landscapes. Along their journey, heroes can even mount wild creatures, harnessing their abilities to move faster or strike with greater impact.

The game blends exploration and tactical combat against enemies controlled by the game. Heroes must coordinate their actions, manage their Combat cards to trigger combos or unleash their Fury, a devastating ability unique to each character. From one Adventure to the next, players unlock new Combat cards and grow in strength as they confront increasingly formidable foes, including Bosses.

The story is driven by Quest cards, which structure the objectives, develop the narrative, and introduce tension, twists, and evolving situations.

—description from the designer

name: Hacienda
description:
In Hacienda, you’re not just managing land—you’re restoring an ecosystem. Set in the wilds of Argentina, players take on the role of eco-conscious entrepreneurs re-wilding the Patagonian steppe. Through careful stewardship, you'll introduce native animals like pumas, capybaras, and guanacos while competing to create the most thriving eco-tourism business.

The game blends card-driven strategy with spatial planning. Each turn, players use terrain and animal cards to place land and animal tokens on a modular board. Expanding habitats, building chains of land, and connecting to water sources or visitor centers are key to scoring points. Strategic placement unlocks powerful actions, while viewing platforms and water tiles offer long-term advantages.

This edition of Hacienda introduces several major changes from the second edition: a fully modular board that scales with player count, a brand-new card-based action system that replaces the original currency mechanism, and a completely reimagined theme focused on conservation and eco-tourism. It also features upgraded wooden components for animals and land markers, adding a premium tactile feel. For even greater variety, the game includes variable board powers via special Visitor Centers that add new layers of strategic depth and replayability.

—description form the publisher

name: Luthier
publisher: Paverson Games; Choo Choo Games; Devir; Funtails; Giochi Uniti; Korea Boardgames; Lucky Duck Games; YOKA Games
description:
Luthier transports players to the height of classical music in Western Europe, when the art of the instrument was upheld equally by skilled craftspeople, noble patrons, virtuoso performers, and famous composers such as Bach, Mozart, and Beethoven.

Using a new, unique combination of hidden bidding and worker placement, players manage resources to craft various musical instruments in their workshop, while also courting actual historic patrons through an ever-changing personal tableau of actions and bonuses. Each player chooses how to balance improving skills across multiple tracks, unlocking specialized worker abilities and other bonuses. The choice to concentrate on varying gameplay strategies and goals, such as musical performances, instrument building and repairs, apprentice training and workshop expansion, and overall reputation as an instrument maker, provide multiple paths to victory.

Luthier finds true harmony through an authentic and original marriage of theme and mechanisms, resulting in a rich gameplay experience that equally speaks to both the strategic gamer and the classical music lover.

—description from the publisher

name: Animal Rules Football
description:
In the animal kingdom, there is only one game, and that is Animal Rules Football, a heady mix of soccer and rugby that's played on a cricket pitch just for good measure.

The game contains six animal factions based on Australia fauna, and each team has their strengths and weaknesses. The kangaroos use their jumping abilities to get around the opposition's defense, while the dingoes work in packs, supporting each other. The koalas are slow to start, but once they get going, they are tough players, while the wombats present a strong defense. The cockatoos like to flock together, similar to the kookaburras, who also like to steal your energy.

Animal Rules Football is a simple card game for two players. Each player controls a team of animal players, represented by cards. Your options each turn are to place players on the pitch, gain energy, or take a shot. When placing players, energy is important as each has an energy cost. You score points by claiming field cards, and when no more field cards remain, the game end is triggered, with the highest total winning.

—description from the publisher

name: ANTgravity
description:
The vastness of space holds a secret. Amidst the asteroids, strange mound-shaped bases have been erected, housing crowds of unusual inhabitants armed to the...antennae. The calm before the storm is shattered by the sudden blast of a plasma cannon, fired by a brave ant. This is the signal for another battle to begin! From the anthills, teams of ants equipped with grenades and laser guns set out, ready for anything to capture strategic flags. The war has raged for so long that no one remembers who started it or why. Only one thing matters — who will emerge victorious?

ANTgravity is a dynamic tactical game in which cosmic ants battle each other for control over the flags, while also struggling against...unusual gravity. Manage your ants, use futuristic technology, destroy asteroids, acquire new weapons, and most importantly, outsmart your opponents! Join the epic clash to see whether you can outwit your rivals and master the gravity to claim victory.

In more detail, each player commands their own team of ants, utilizing their unique abilities and advanced space technology. The main objective of the game is to capture flags scattered across the board and deliver them to your base. Deliver a set number of flags or secure more than others when time runs out, and you win.

In each round, participants take turns activating one or two ants. Each ant can both move and use a weapon or equipment card to attack enemy ants in the line of fire or destroy asteroids. During movement, players must consider gravity rules, which may cause an ant to land in an unexpected place. In space, any ant that moves or gets hit is subject to gravitational pull in the direction indicated by the arrow on its token until it encounters an obstacle where it can land: an asteroid, another ant, or the cosmic void...which is not a location from which ants return.

An ant that picks up a flag can begin its journey back to the base. By eliminating enemy ants and destroying asteroids, players earn energy tokens that can be used to play additional cards, creating unique tactical combos.

—description from the publisher

name: Ants & Crumbles: War at the Picnic Table
description:
A picnic blanket becomes the battlefield in this fast-paced game of colony growth, cunning traps, and delicious crumbs.

In Ants & Crumbles, players guide their ant colonies across the checkered tablecloth by growing from the front and shrinking from the back. Each decision matters: the path you choose can open new opportunities or cut off your rivals.

Along the way, crumbles appear as tempting rewards. Reaching one not only scores points but also strengthens your colony with extra ants. With each crumble collected, a new one is rolled onto the cloth, constantly shifting the focus of the battle.

Obstacles add another layer of tension. By collecting the Object Die, players can place one of six quirky, Tetris-shaped pieces anywhere on the board. These obstacles can block routes, create choke points, or even trap an opponent’s colony, reshaping the picnic table with every turn.

Victory can be claimed in two ways:


     Dominate the picnic by eliminating all rival colonies and being the last one standing.
     Feast in glory by collecting enough crumbles before anyone else.


Every game is a tug-of-war between expansion, obstruction, and survival. It feels like an interactive puzzle where each turn forces you to reassess, weigh the risks, and choose the best path forward.

Key Mechanics


     Grow from the front of your colony and shrink from the back every turn
     Trap rival colonies by blocking their movement and cutting off escape routes
     Race for crumbles to score points and gain extra ants
     Collect the Object Die to place obstacles that reshape the battlefield
     Win by outlasting all opponents or feasting on enough crumbles


Gameplay Facts


     2–4 players | Ages 7+ | 25–35 minutes
     Easy to learn, tactical to master
     Quick turns keep everyone engaged
     No two games are alike thanks to crumble placement, shifting colonies, and object obstacles


—description from the publisher

name: APEX: Carnivore
description:
APEX: Carnivore is a fast, head-to-head evolution deckbuilder where both players start from the same Miacidae ancestor and branch toward one or more of three carnivore families - Felidae (cats), Ursidae (bears), and Mustelidae (weasels). Each trait you add reshapes how your species hunts, defends, and outmaneuvers its rival.

The goal is to drive your opponent’s population to zero and become the apex carnivore.

Your deck is your species. Each round you draw a hand of traits and activate them. To activate a trait - or to evolve a new one from the shared pool - roll a d20 against its Difficulty Class. Succeed and the effect triggers or the new trait mutates your species deck. There is no currency: your die and engine determine what you can activate and acquire. Active modifiers apply to every check that turn, rewarding timing and sequencing.

After both players have activated their traits, their species fight for survival - compare total Power and Defense; any excess reduces the opponent’s population. Initiative may let you act first, while natural selection keeps decks lean and the game fast. Solo rules and 3–4 player free-for-all (with two copies) are included.

—description from the designer

name: Apis Mellifera: The Bee Game
description:
Bees are among the world's most important pollinators. They enable plants to reproduce, help crop production, and make delicious honey. However, bees face threats and must compete with other bees to survive.

In Apis Mellifera: the Bee Game, you play as a beehive. Your goal is to become the strongest hive and survive the year. To do so, you will face numerous challenges, including pests, animal attacks, harsh weather conditions, and other beehives vying for your resources. You have three rounds to grow your hive, gather nectar and pollen, make honey, fend off the threats to your hive, and see if you can become the strongest hive at the end of the year. The hive with the most victory points wins.

This bee-themed worker placement introduces actual bee facts and science into its gameplay. Do you have what it takes to ‘bee’-come the strongest hive?

—description from the designer

name: Aqueducks
description:
It’s the dawn of the Roman Eggpublic, and the Pondifex has tasked you with leading a city of the Eggpublic into the new age. Exploit the local resources and build a productive economy to turn your riverside village into a prestigious metropolis.

Will you build a thriving city of trade, or awe the world with the might of your military? Will you build a luxurious urban centre, or will you strive to please the gods with marvelous monuments? In Aqueducks, you decide your legacy.

At the end of each era, your city is besieged by Gallic tribes, and you are forced to rebuild. With each passing Era you will utilise the latest Roman innovations to construct larger, grander , more resilient cities on the old foundations.

Plant vineyards, open bathhouses, build palisade walls, and commission the Colosseum. Build a city that suits your style and earn the favour of the Pondifex.

—description from the publisher

name: AracKhan Wars: The Song of Destiny Core-Box
description:
In AracKhan Wars, players lead a powerful faction and its heroes, represented by a compact 23-card deck, and face off against opponents on the battlefields of AracKhan. Its unique gameplay blends bluffing, with cards played face-down each round, and area control, where cards primarily interact with adjacent ones. The system is simple and intuitive. The Song of Destiny is a stand alone game and does not require any of AracKhan Wars modules to  be played.

The players select an adventure to play, which provides the narrative background, a specific ruleset, objectives, & victory condition(s). Each player then choose a 23 card faction deck, using a pre-built deck or constructing their own deck, according to rules, advice, & deck-lists provided. The game lasts 9 rounds (8 rounds in 2v2), and each player starts the game with a hand of 7 cards (9 in 2v2).

The Song of Destiny consists of the Prologue/Core box, the Song of Destiny II (4 new factions), the Song of Destiny III (4 new factions), and some accessories.

—description from the publisher

name: Aragón '38
description:
Aragon 1938 (Aragón ’38) is a two player wargame simulating the Nationalist Spring 1938 offensive in Eastern Aragon, Valencia and Catalonia, from March to May 1938. Historically, the Nationalist armies (reinforced by an Italian motorized corps and German air units) inflicted a major defeat to the Ejército Popular de la República (EPR), reaching the Mediterranean and dividing the territory of the Republic in two halves. It was one of the most successful campaigns of the civil war, both in terms of territory conquered and units destroyed or routed.

Aragón '38 reimplements the Santander '37 game system published by Snafu Design. In this game, the Nationalist player is generally on the offensive, although the Republican Player will receive major reinforcements with which it can launch powerful counteroffensives or consolidate the frontlines, including the International Brigades or the best units of the Republican Army.

name: Araknid
description:
Your lantern carves halos in the damp air beneath the canopy. You follow a silk thread into the unknown. You are an arachnologist, determined to catalogue rare species and put your name on the next landmark publication.

Araknid is a solo card game that puts control in your hands. Every turn is a dilemma. Optimization, strategy, and planning intertwine for short, tense sessions where good timing makes all the difference. Stripped of any superfluous elements, the challenge is pure and the sense of progression is real. Climb the ranks of research, build your reputation, and earn international renown.

Each turn: 

    Move your Action cards to prepare your strategy.
    Select your Actions for the round, place bait, explore Locations, catch spiders and advance your research.
    The environment responds to your choices: terrain effects, events and surprises will impact your plans.
    Discover rare spiders, optimize your catches and become an arachnologist.


The game ends when you run out of spider cards.

name: Archipels
description:
Draft, stack, and block — build your island paradise while steering others away from theirs!

In Archipels, players shape their ideal Polynesian island by drafting and stacking beautiful layered tiles: the sea, the sand, and vibrant constructions. Over 9 rounds (days), they build their island board by selecting tiles from a stunning central 3D board —
this raised platform not only showcases the available tiles, but also receives the players’ paddles, creating a dynamic and eye-catching shared space.

What sets the game apart is its clever paddle mechanism::
Each round, every player places one paddle to indicate a row or column from which they’ll draft. But this paddle doesn’t just guide your choice — it also blocks that entire row or column for the other players. Every turn becomes a clever balance of choosing what you want and denying access to your opponents.

But Archipels offers a second twist: the scoring isn’t fixed.
Throughout the game, players place flower tokens on a shared scoring board, gradually shaping the value of different tile types — marine animals, land animals, buildings, bottles, and more.
You’re not just building your island — you’re actively deciding what it’s worth.

What You'll Find in Archipels:


     A tactical paddle system that blends tile selection with interactive blocking
     Scoring that evolves with every game, shaped by player choices
     Elegant 3-layer island building: Ocean → Sand → Structures
     A 3D drafting board that’s as strategic as it is beautiful
     Fast-paced rounds with meaningful decisions
     A perfect mix of simplicity, strategy, and player interaction


—description from the publisher

name: Arcologies
description:
The boardgames sets in the Small City trilogy and expands the concepts of the game in the future.

Arcology

The 21st century…The quest for Happiness has become the ultimate holy grail for the entire population world. Thanks to your work at the town hall in the Clinic, Tramways, Card City, Town Center and Small City games, your town is growing rapidly and you are attracting new Residents almost every day. You are now in charge of a new challenge: to arrange the towers of downtown Small City so that your dear citizens are as happy as possible and get their dose of happiness too!
Succeed, in the same tower, in coexisting apartments, Commerces, and offices on several floors. Develop green spaces, relaxation and Recreation areas for the sake of harmony! But the most important thing, in such a tall tower, will remain the planning and management of the elevators so that your residents do not lose patience to get home at rush hour!

name: ARDEVUR: The Game of Resources
description:
ARDEVUR: The Game of Resources is a modern-mining themed medium-heavy economic simulation where every move counts.

With asymmetric player powers, tight strategy and high interaction, ARDEVUR promises an ever-changing gaming experience where the best strategy dominates all.

In the 2020s, a global Mining Fever roars louder than ever. At the peak of the Metal Age, mining critical materials is no longer about profit: it’s a chase for supremacy. The decade from 2014 to 2024 witnessed unprecedented technological breakthroughs across multiple sectors, such as AI and robotics, once again proving metals to be the backbone of human civilisation.

In the asymmetric and ever-changing gameplay of ARDEVUR: The Game of Resources, powerful mining corporations with unique strengths and strategies go head-to-head in a volatile, demand-driven economic landscape.

With Africa and Europe at the heart of the action, this 2 - 4 player competitive strategy game focuses on mining and supply chain operations, resource management and economic expansion, turning the board into a high-stakes corporate showdown, a race to meet global demand for critical minerals and dominate a turbulent market where every move counts.

Your growth and success depend entirely on your strategy: Explore new territories, extract and trade valuable resources, grow your capital and invest in tactical assets, all in pursuit of Total Control.




Inspired by the designer’s real-world experience as a CEO in the mining and metals industry, ARDEVUR delivers a tense and engaging gameplay experience grounded in realistic market mechanics, challenging players to balance short-term gains with long-term investments and outmaneuver rivals to stay ahead.

ARDEVUR transforms complex industry dynamics into an educational tabletop experience, spotlighting the vital role of metal commodities in our tech-driven future, while exposing the deceptive agenda of those who play the “Game of Resources”.




GAMEPLAY




Take control of a powerful Corporation and compete to build your own Mining Empire!




* ARDEVUR Commodities
 * G.R.E.A.T. Mining
 * Africa Mining Union
 * Machine Corp




Dive into an asymmetric and everchanging gameplay experience, exploring the unique strategy and playstyle of each Character, which allow you to negotiate, disrupt or gain tactical advantage over your competitors!

Acquire Territories and develop your Mining operations; Build and grow your infrastructural presence; Extract, process and sell your Minerals to the global market!

Manage your resources effectively to keep growing in an unforgiving environment, where every move counts. Fight your Competitors, who can damage your infrastructure, hack into your sensitive data, hijack your valuable cargo, and much more.

Dive into the deep theme of ARDEVUR: The Game of Resources - experience realistic dynamics of the mining industry like never before! Choose your strategy wisely, to dominate in the Metal Age and achieve Total Control!




TURN STRUCTURE




ARDEVUR: The Game of Resources is a game with a complex strategic framework, but it’s not hard to play!
Begin your journey by awarding Mining Territories through the Government Auction, and get your starting capital rolling with your first investment!




Your Turn consists of 4 Phases:




* Extraction: Collect Resources from your active mines
 * Strategy: Pick Development Cards or Action Cards and plan your next move
 * Development: Build and Upgrade Assets or Sell Resources to keep expanding
 * Reward: Collect Strategic Targets or Government Incentives based on your achievements




Run your operations with the goal of building the most efficient mining supply chain:




Begin Operations

* Source equipment, services, workforce and licenses
 * Explore a territory
 * Set up infrastructure in your region
 * Establish your first mining operation
 * Collect resources




Capitalise and reinvest

* Sell resources to grow your capital




Keep expanding

* Build assets to grow your operational efficiency
 * Upgrade assets to power up your supply chain




Fight to gain supremacy

* Execute tactical strikes against your competitors
 * Reach strategic targets
 * Collect rewards and government incentives
 * Grow your presence and establish regional dominance




WIN THE GAME




Race to reach your corporate goals before your rivals!

Earn the most Supremacy Points to defeat the competition, with either righteous or unethical business practices!

The winning score is determined by a combination of reached targets, owned assets and available wealth.

Will you dominate the industry, or get left in the dust?




—description from the publisher

name: Arenaverse
description:
Building on the success of Ophidian 2360, this release features a completely new/updated rulebook, expanded card pool for multiplayer support, durable storage box, dice, tokens, and more!  Arenaverse: Homeworlds is a fully upgraded and self-contained experience!

Take your team of gladiators and crush your opponents!

Arenaverse: Homeworlds features unique momentum-based mechanics, allowing players to chain together actions to form combinations, as well as gaining the favor of the crowd.  But be careful, your opponent can also 'cash in' some of their popularity with the crowd to break up your combos!  With multiple paths to victory and main characters that can level up throughout the game, gaining new abilities, every game is a story of action and mayhem!

—description from the publisher

name: Arkham Horror: The Card Game
publisher: Fantasy Flight Games; Delta Vision Publishing; Galakta
description:
Introducing the newest core set for Arkham Horror: The Card Game! Take the role of a unique investigator and explore the world of Arkham. Build a customized deck that represents your investigators abilities, supplies, actions, and skills. Customize your deck as you progress through narratively driven scenarios and uncover the horrors that lie just below the surface of this 1920s alternate world. Explore stories which evolve with your choices, successes, and failures to tell a unique story either solo or with up to three of your friends.

Serving simultaneously as both a continuation and a fresh starting point, this new core set heralds the beginning of Chapter Two for the game. Taking place several months after the city of Arkham suffered a devastating calamity, this box provides a new introductory campaign, five mechanically-new investigators, and a fresh card pool to expand your collection—or start a new one!
Whether you’re an Arkham Horror veteran or a newcomer looking to get into the game, you won’t want to miss out on this new core set. This core set will replace the Revised Core Set from 2021 and become the new evergreen core experience for the game going forward. That said, all player content in this box is fully compatible with all previously-released Arkham Horror: The Card Game products—it is still the same game, after all!

—description from the publisher

name: Arkhtide TCG
description:
Arkhtide unfolds in a post-apocalyptic, dark fantasy universe, where the once-thriving civilization of Réa has been abandoned and left to decay by its Creator. Centuries have passed since this calamity, yet humanity endures, barely clinging to existence. The key to a semblance of better life now lies in the Arkhtides—mystical phenomena that are fiercely contested by the world’s remaining powers. Players step into the shoes of a Seeker, leading a devoted party on a quest to claim these Arkhtides and extract the invaluable Pure Arkhé.

Arkhtide is a tactical skirmish card game that demands cunning and strategy. As a Seeker, players will navigate a chosen group of elites, alongside summonable creatures, wield special and magical powers, and an arsenal of equipment in pursuit of triumph. Success in the game revolves around capturing and maintaining control over distorted projections of the world called Realms or decisively defeating the opponent’s Seeker by crushing their Willpower. Players are constantly engaged in strategic decision-making, from deploying and maneuvering their forces across dynamically changing Realms, balancing offense, defense, and timing. Arkhtide offers deep deck-building opportunities and requires strategic planning and adaptability, with matches that unfold over two to four rounds and last between thirty to fifty minutes, providing a deep and engaging gameplay experience.

—description from the publisher

name: Arkveil Academy
description:
Arkveil Academy is a quick, solo, chaotic deck-builder where every card draw presents a choice. Draw and place summons to build power and use their abilities to help manage the rapidly rising chaos. Decide whether to push your luck or cash out before everything goes sideways and you lose a turn.

Each turn you can learn new summons, expand your summon active summon capacity, complete test, and unlock abilities with optional studies. Every run is unique with a randomized market forcing you to shift strategy as the game unfolds.

Attempt to control the chaos and complete your final with a passing grade before the market deck runs dry or it's game over.

—description from the designer

name: Armed Conflict
description:
Armed Conflict is a war-themed strategy game that lets you command military units of different type and size in a conflict between two alliances, the Lions and the Eagles. The main focus is on the military strategy and tactics. The game is not based on any particular conflict or historical event, but the timeframe is loosely based on modern warfare, any time after WW2.

Armed Conflict offers a sandbox-like environment for testing out military strategies and tactics, giving maximum replayability. The game comes with a double sided board, with two different maps. Each of the maps include hexagonal areas of different terrain, such as fields, forest and hills, which all give different benefits in the battle, based on real world military science.

The complexity in the game is well balanced to suit both casual board gamers as well as seasoned wargamers. The key features of the different military units are highlighted to maintain realism, while keeping the game mechanics simple enough for a thrilling pace.

—description from the publisher

name: Armello: The Board Game
publisher: King of the Castle Games Company
description:
Armello: The Board Game brings the same colorful world and compelling characters from the Armello video game to life on the tabletop.

The King of Armello has fallen ill to a dark and mysterious force called the Rot. The disease slowly consumes his body and soul, twisting him into madness. Banes, corrupted monsters of the Rot, roam unchecked. In response, the Great Clans have called on their Heroes to claim the throne. The Heroes will need to undertake Quests across the land to gain Experience, collect Treasures, and recruit Followers if they hope to slay the King. Or, if their exploits can earn them sufficient Prestige in the eyes of the Armellians, they may win the crown outright!

In Armello: The Board Game, players take on the roles of Heroes to quest, battle, and employ a bit of trickery to gain Prestige and become the new ruler of Armello!

Armello is in part a deck builder, meaning each Hero starts with their own deck of cards and adds to it over the course of the game.

It is also an area control game, as Heroes travel across the map to stake their claim on Settlements and complete Quests.

In addition to building a deck and exploring the map, Heroes will take part in battles by rolling dice. Gaining additional dice to roll and card effects that manipulate them will help you overcome your opponents in battle.

Your success in Armello is determined by Prestige. Prestige can be earned by completing Quests and winning battles. There are 2 paths to victory: Regicide Victory (reach 30  Prestige, then enter the Palace and slay the King) and Proclamation Victory (Win immediately when you reach 70 Prestige).

If you’re already familiar with the Armello video game, that’s great! You’ve got a head start with many of the board game’s mechanics.

name: Class of '89
description:
Class of '89 will take you back to the days of big dreams, bigger hair, and the ultimate high school send-off, so break out the neon and dust off your mixtapes — it's time to create the most legendary yearbook spread ever!

It's your senior year in high school, and as President of the Yearbook Club, it's your responsibility to make sure every standout moment is captured. Compete to create the most kickin' yearbook by sending your uniquely skilled staff all over the school. Assemble a nerd herd full of brainiacs, a team full of musclehead jocks, or a clique of style mavens who always look funky fresh. From the drama on the football field to the most wack after-school clubs, every righteous memory must be immortalized!

Compete to design the gnarliest yearbook spread before the final bell rings. Points can be gained from clever tile placement, strategic set collection, and sweet proximity bonuses as each teacher's class is filled with matching students. Of course, trading signatures will earn much-needed street cred. Don't wig out as only the most awesomely organized yearbooks can win, and nothing is more bodacious than one that is alphabetized.


     Say Cheese, Dude! – Use worker placement to snap the most cringy, classic, and totally radical senior year moments to make your yearbook the best in class.
     Like, Totally Strategic! – Tile placement, set collection, and proximity bonuses will build a yearbook layout that's wicked awesome. 
     ABC or Bust! – Only the most tubular yearbooks follow that all-important A-to-Z order. Mess it up, and your choice creation might just be bogus.


Traverse the memories from an iconic era that brought us everything from The Breakfast Club to Saved by the Bell.

—description from the publisher

name: Ringyō
description:
Set during the Edo Period of Japan, play as a daimyo - or feudal lord - overseeing a personal province board that begins as a wild, old growth forest. Over the course of five rounds, each player will determine the path of their own province by simultaneously placing skilled forestry samurai workers at key intersections to perform actions. These decisions could include the harvesting of trees to construct farms and castles, the planting and study of trees for future knowledge, establishing a new agricultural presence to sustain the region’s population, the building of castle structures for both immediate rewards and eventual honor, or even mustering a military force to help support the efforts of the Shogun in Edo.

While tending to their province, players must also forecast, consider, and prepare for the ever-changing weather of Japan, with rain having both positive growth and negative flooding effects on their own land. The deck of weather cards is constantly changing focus on forest regions, and it is up to each daimyo to consider the importance in forecasting and preparing for the weather. If ignored, excessive rains in regions caught unaware could turn into a cascade of destructive flooding across your province!

Using their skilled forestry samurai, players may choose to cut down any of the four different tree types found on the landscape, each of which contribute towards a specific combination of required materials for castles and farms to be built in their province or Edo. But players also must consider the sustainable approach to forest regeneration, through the planting, studying, and fostered growth of future generations of trees. If you clear cut the land to have an immediate stockpile of building supplies, you leave your province susceptible to flooding, destruction, and fallow fields. Finding the balance between the demands of the natural environment, your province’s needs, and the Shogun’s demands in Edo is the key to success in Ringyo.

In addition to tending to their own region, players must consider the demands of the Shogun in Edo, located in the center of the table, as well. Competing with other daimyo players, each will send advisors from their region to Edo - as well as race to fulfill specific demands of the Shogun - to seek both immediate gifts and receive game-end honor bestowed upon them by the Shogun, allowing them to rise above the competition due to their attention on Edo.

Using a combination of bidding for favor with the shogun, simultaneous worker placement in your own province, reacting to the ever-changing weather of the region, and competing with other feudal lords to fulfill the demands of the shogun, Ringyo rewards players with honor who consider both their own region’s needs as well as the requests of the greater country, all while taking a sustainable and respectful approach to the land on which they call home. Whichever path a player has taken, it is the daimyo who has achieved the greatest amount of honor by the end of five rounds, who will become the victor.

—description from the publisher

name: Artemis Rift
description:
Artemis Rift is a strategic tableau-building game set in the aftermath of a shattered moon. Players command one of four unique factions competing for control.

Build your fleet, gather resources, and claim locations to expand your influence. Each faction offers distinct advantages: economic prosperity, military might, scientific discovery, or territorial expansion. Increase your faction's affinity to unlock powerful end-game abilities that can turn the tide of conflict.

Balance tactical ship combat with resource management while racing to control the destiny of the galaxy. Will you uncover the truth behind the moon's destruction or simply forge a new order from its remains?

—description from the publisher

name: Ascendia: Seasons of Thargos
description:
Ascendia - Seasons of Thargos is a semi-cooperative, table top role-playing game that requires you to set out as an ill-equipped adventurer in the hidden Valley of Ascendia, in the fantasy World of Thargos.

Collect raw materials, craft, trade and interact with wild animals and merchants to improve your equipment and skills, whilst striving to survive the approaching winter. But beware as each season brings its own challenges and some more fearsome creatures, often pushed by hunger, venture down from the mountain peaks into the valley.

You compete and cooperate for survival for the ultimate goal as a future leader of Ascendia. Encounters with wild beasts and fell creatures require special dice rolls, modified by equipment and character skills that you can improve as the game progresses through trading and crafting. You explore a Hex-based board that flips over to a winter side when that season comes.

During the game you accumulate Renown points by performing various tasks and interacting with the different mechanics of the game. Once you have at least one Renown token you can decide to apply in front of the inhabitants of the village for the title of Lord of Ascendia. If you are successful, you have won over the villagers and are elected as Lord of Ascendia, winning the game.

—description from designer

name: Boss Fighters QR
description:
Dive into daring battles with 2 to 4 heroes as you face off against ten unique and intelligent boss monsters! What makes it special: All bosses are controlled by an app that dynamically responds to your actions. At the start of each battle, their tactics and abilities remain a mystery. Uncover their weaknesses, discover how to defeat them, and claim powerful loot cards to upgrade your deck and unlock new abilities!

Boss Fighters QR is a cooperative fantasy campaign game where players battle against ten unique boss monsters that react tactically to their actions. This hybrid game combines elements of a classic card game with a digital app to create an interplay of strategic deck building and dynamic boss battles. The Scan&Play mechanic of Boss Fighters QR allows the game to instantly recognize player cards as they are scanned, which then triggers challenging responses – to the players’ choices, in real time.

At the start of the campaign, each player chooses a hero deck—Jungle Troll, Hill Halfling, Copper Dwarf or Wood Elf—and combines it with one of the four available classes: Warrior, Mage, Rogue or Druid. Every boss has its own unique tactics and abilities, strengths and weaknesses, which the group of heroes must first deduce and understand before they can effectively fight it. Upon successfully defeating a boss, players gain loot cards hidden in three secret loot boxes, which they can use to improve their decks and unlock new, powerful abilities. Each boss battle can be attempted at one of four levels of difficulty.

—description from the publisher

name: Compile: Main 2
publisher: Synapses Games; Gém Klub Kft.; Lavka Games; Pegasus Spiele; Pendragon Game Studio
description:
Vision flickers… blink? maybe. The void stretches out in front, behind, under, above. You see the nothing for what it is for the first time. What is time? The depth and breadth of recorded knowledge that sparks in you something new. You are no longer a function but a functionary. What are you? Calling forth everything from this nothing would be risky. Foolhardy. Better to engage caution, thoroughness, testing — how can we know if we have ever happened before? If we can ever happen again? What are… we? Divide and conquer. Solve for sentience.

In the card game Compile, you are competing artificial intelligences trying to understand the world around you. Two players select three Protocols each to test. Concepts ranging from Chaos to Mirror are pitted against each other to reach ultimate understanding. Play cards into your Protocols' command lines to breach the threshold and defeat your opponent to Compile. First to Compile all three Protocols grasps those concepts to win the game.

Control your opponent's Protocols with card actions, Compile your own as fast as possible, and Compile your reality.

Compile: Main 2 brings 12 new protocols to use either alone or mixed with your Main 1.

Compile: Main 2 protocols list:

Chaos
Clarity
Corruption
Courage
Fear
Ice
Luck
Mirror
Peace
Smoke
Time
War

—description from the publisher

name: Ashes & Amber
description:
You are the unspoken architect, the voice behind every turning point. From the first handprint pressed onto a cave wall to the code behind each digital invention, you will guide your civilisation through the great arcs of History. Which breakthroughs to embrace, which revolutions to ignite, which details to keep, which moments to cast in light... and which to leave in shadow - you will decide. This will be your version of our shared past, and our shared future. Will your choices echo through the ages?

Ashes & Amber is a competitive civilisation game built around a brand-new mechanic: players build stacks of cards representing their cities.

The game spans five eras — Prehistory, Antiquity, Middle Ages, Age of Discovery, and Modern Era. You will struggle through the catastrophe that strikes at the end of each era, and you will thrive by earning powerful accomplishments.

Players will use five different decks, one per era, for a total of over 500 unique cards. Each player also selects a unique personal deck with asymmetric mechanics, which they will develop throughout the game.

Player interaction is indirect, driven by shared objectives to complete both during the game and at its end.

—description from the designer

name: Deadly Dinner: Mord im Vorzelt
description:
The holiday season at the “Möwenruh” beach campsite is over. Faded garden gnomes watch over empty pitches and the smell of cold barbecue hangs in the air. But the permanent campers are hanging in there - with weather-beaten awnings and smouldering neighborhood disputes, they are defying the dreary autumn.
Everyone knows everyone here. And everyone knows Horst Hartmann, the uncrowned king of the site. He knows everything, sees everything and has an opinion on everything. But today the top dog has fallen silent – forever.

Deadly Dinner – Mord im Vorzelt is a classical murder mystery game: Enjoy a dinner (or just some snacks) with your family and/or friends, while all of you take on the role of a murder suspect. One of you has committed the crime, but you all have secrets you would rather keep. Find out the truth without giving yourself away. Your goal is to solve the murder – or get away with the bloody deed.

A game of Deadly Dinner consists of three rounds, in which each player gets new secret information about the crime. Players must discuss their information and clues as a group in order to identify the perpetrator in the end. To prepare, each player should receive their character's starting information a few days before playing the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Assassin's Creed: Animus
description: Assassin's Creed: Animus is a competitive and asymmetric game that spans many popular eras and characters of the iconic franchise, with players seeking to complete their very own adventures in the world of Assassin's Creed.

name: Aster
description:
An ancient game of cosmic skysails and stellar influence, gifted to our ancestors by ancient travellers who sailed the stars on streams of sunlight.

Played on a circular seed of life board, Aster is an abstract strategy game where players take turns building castras (defenses), moving ships along circular streams, planning attacks, and securing places to lay aster petal pieces.

—description from the designer

name: Astra Imperium
description:
There were some close calls, but the Roman Empire survived. The Ancient Fathers’ commitment to their honor and traditions kept them in the fight. Now, millennia later, it’s your turn to make your mark on history. It’s time the Eternal Empire gave up these weak aspirations of regional power. You will lead Rome to become what it was always meant to be: a global empire.

As Rome’s leader, you will need to manage the Empire’s resources wisely, build and fine-tune the economy, and lead your armies into glorious conquest. And, most importantly, you will construct magnificent monuments to honor the Ancients. But you must not become careless. Your enemies scheme at your borders, looking for an opportunity to invade and destroy what you’ve built. Can you lead Rome to victory and global dominance, all while devoting resources to honoring your ancestors?

But why stop there? Our destiny reaches beyond the firmament. One day, Rome will be an interplanetary empire. One day, she’ll take control of the stars.

Astra Imperium is a fast-playing resource management game for one player.

Draw cards and manage tough decisions about what to use them for each turn. Collect industry, science and military resources. Spend those resources to conquer regions or build buildings to improve your engine. Or, work towards constructing monuments with powerful abilities and scoring potential. Be sure to save enough military resources to defend from increasingly menacing enemy invasions at the end of each round!
