After round 3, compare your score to the history books to gauge your success.

Instead of one-off games, you can play through 5 multi-stage campaigns that drastically change up gameplay and help you discover new strategies. Play the campaigns in order to guide Rome through an epic saga of rising to power, struggling through decline, traveling through space to find a new home planet, fighting off unique invading forces, and even terraforming.

—description from the publisher

name: Astra Titanus: Deluxe Edition
description:
Astra Titanus Deluxe is a solitaire game of space ship fleet battles against a titanic alien AI controlled death machine. You command fleets of warships against a lone Titan or two. The Titan is controlled by a deck of AI cards that drives the Titan unerringly towards its objectives. Defeat the Titan before the objectives are destroyed to achieve victory.

What's New in Astra Titanus Deluxe:

All components are upgraded - including a stunning sturdy full color box, hard mounted game board, large thick counters with rounded corners, high quality poker size cards, counter tray, and more!
Astra Titanus Deluxe can be played by two or more players cooperatively against the Titan or with one player taking control of the Titan.
Astra Titanus Deluxe comes with 12 scenarios as well as a random scenario generator.

-description from publisher

name: Astro Out
description:
The stage is set on the distant planet "Virtus." This planet is home to four distinct species: "Teo", "Bitter", "Plu", and "Mick". Each species lives by making the most of their unique abilities. In recent years, the most flourishing industry on this planet has been "Space Business". With countless planets and satellites in this planetary system, there is a growing movement to efficiently utilize the energy and resources available from each celestial body.

You are the ambitious CEO of a space exploration venture. You will acquire numerous planets and build the strongest team to work with. At times, you will receive support from major corporations, while competing against other venture companies to grow your business. Your aim to become the No. 1 space exploration venture company!

Astro Out is a medium-weight board game themed around space exploration. Players take on the role of CEOs of venture companies engaged in the space business, traveling across planets, constructing buildings, and gathering allies.

Each round consists of 4 phases: Action, Income, Settlement, Cleanup. The game ends after the Settlement phase during the 4th round and points are counted. The player with the highest point total from all the categories is the winner and is recognized as the most outstanding CEO.

—description from the publisher

name: Astro ROVE: Results-Oriented Versatile Explorer
description:
The end of the galaxy doesn’t mean the end of the mission! As a ROVE (Results-Oriented Universal Explorer) you must push your modules past their normal operating parameters as you explore the furthest reaches of space.

Astro ROVE is a standalone entry in the ROVE series. In this solo spatial puzzler, the player must complete missions by using their movement cards to align ROVE’s modules in the proper pattern. As ROVE travels further, efficient use of movement points and module abilities becomes paramount to achieve success.

Astro ROVE adds a few new spins to the ROVE formula. Firstly, each movement card provides a set number of movement points and directional limits on how modules may move. However, each card also includes an optional ability to help players align their modules, as well as a bonus icon that provides additional movement if it matches the current mission.

Beyond that, each module has its own unique ability allowing it to convert directly into one of the other module types. But beware: once changed, these modules can never be returned to their original purpose.

—description from the publisher

name: AstroNavigators
description:
In AstroNavigators, you embark on an epic journey of discovery, from the quiet contemplation of stargazing to the adrenaline rush of a lunar landing. As a pioneering astronomer, you'll meticulously chart the cosmos and gather the crucial knowledge needed for humankind's greatest adventure. Then, prepare for the ultimate challenge: a daring race to the Moon and back! Outmanoeuvre your rivals, manage your resources wisely, and push your luck as you navigate the treacherous void. Will you be the first to leave your mark on the Moon?

AstroNavigators is a board game simulating the celestial mechanics within a space race themed worker placement game. In Phase 1, you'll explore the world, making observations and discoveries to earn Navigation Knowledge (NK) and Reputation Points (RP). In Phase 2, using your hard-earned NK, you'll become an Astronaut and race to the Moon!

The end of the game is immediately triggered when one of the following conditions occurs:


    All the players are ‘lost in space’.
    All the players went to the Moon and returned to Earth.
    The Sun disc is in the leftmost space on the Star map for the first time (Astronomer mode) or the second time (Astronavigator mode).


Players will assess the outcome of their mission and earn additional points for their achievements.  The player with the most Reputation Points (RP) wins the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Astrum
description:
Alfonso X, who was called the Wise or the Astrologer, ruled Castile and Leon in the XIII century. He was an extraordinary monarch: being engaged in the publication of laws and economy, poetry and writing, he was also obsessed with stars.
At the very beginning of his reign, Alfonso X invited the best astronomers and asked them to compile detailed astronomical tables with coordinates of celestial objects. The Alfonsine tables laid the foundation for scientific works of Copernicus and revolution in astronomy.
In 1283 under his leadership the translation of the Arabic composition “Libro de los Juegos” (“Book of games”) was completed into Spanish and this brought chess and many other board games from East to Europe. Among the translated rules were “astronomical games”. One of them is right in front of you.

In the game Astrum you will become stargazers who make up the atlas of the starry sky commissioned by Alfonse X Astrologer.

Your goal is to fill your personal playing board with figures of various constellations so as to satisfy the requirements of the enlightened king.
Each board is divided into 4 colored sectors, which corresponds to one of the stacks of constellation figures. By placing a figure on one of colored sectors at your board, you determine the color for figure that the next player will take. However, he is also free to place this figure anywhere on his board.  
Each figure combines several bright stars on the board and has 1 or 2 external connections, allowing you to continue the constellation. When you finish the constellation (it has no longer open external connections), you get victory points by the number of bright stars in it.

When one of figures’ pile ends, all players lay out a new pack and complete the round. At the end of rounds 1, 3, and 5, King Alfonso pays a visit to astronomers and checks their work.  Before the start of the game, players open cards of King’s vagaries, which determine the conditions for obtaining victory points in the rounds.

—description from the designer

name: Deckers
publisher: Deep Print Games; DiceTree Games; Intrafin Games; Pegasus Spiele
description:
In Deckers, you will hack into a network of five servers, either solo or co-operatively as a team of up to four, winning or losing together.

The network is operated by one of the available super-massive computers (SMCs), each with a different level of complexity and its own unique style of defenses that you will need to overcome.

Once jacked into the servers, you will assume decker profiles, each with a special ability, moving across the server's spaces and uploading decker pieces onto the network to expand your control while removing as many of the SMC's pieces as possible. Each round, you get a new objective you try to fulfill to gain the upper hand. If you manage to complete the final objective, you ultimately claim victory.

name: Atlas: Explore the World
description:
Atlas is a tableau-building game where you take the role of a backpacker with a special ability, personality, and language. You have saved up money for a journey of a lifetime around the world! Like any long journey, strategic decisions have to be made as you balance traveling and exploring with your available money and energy level.  With 235 Countries and 865 unique destinations to visit, each play of Atlas creates a unique journey and offers interesting real world facts about each of these areas. Where will you go next?

When you explore a destination you gain experience icons. Each experience will reward points in the end based on its popularity which the players will shift during the game.

Develop as you learn new languages, make new friends, complete personal goals while racing against other players for Public Goals, collecting souvenirs first or posting the most popular Blog Posts. Tough decisions have to be made for every action, boost yourself by experiencing things you like to gain possibilities to perform bonus actions. This might bring you closer to achieving even more points.

The game ends when a player places their last explorer token. The player with the most points wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Dice Pool Party
publisher: Deep Print Games; BoardM Factory; Gém Klub Kft.; Gigamic; Pegasus Spiele; Rexhry
description:
The Dice Pool Party will start in 3 ... 2 ... 1 ... Splash!
Shake the pool and take a good look at the dice. 
Can you single out the ones that give you the most points? You have only a brief moment.

—description from the publisher

name: Aura Hunters
description:
Aura Hunters

Welcome to Lunaria. Young orphans become friends and bear the mark of the Aura Hunters.

Updates will follow...

name: Aural Battle
description:
A fighting board game inspired by games such as Shin Megami Tensei or Pokémon where you'll form a team of five Aural and fight to beat your opponent.
First, on the Adventure Stage, you'll draft your team, choosing from five different decks, each corresponding to an archetype. Then the match will begin and you'll give secret orders covering your commands with your Guardian Screen. Once everything's set, your Aurals will fight in real time using their initiative.

—description from the designer

name: Austerlitz, 1805: Coup de Tonnerre!
description:
Based on U&P Games' W1815, Austerlitz, 1805 takes the system to a new level.

The game is playable by one, two or four players (arguably by 0 since the innovative solitaire system can be used to drive both sides). The small number of rules means the game is quick to learn or to teach and it is equally quick to play (typically 20-40 minutes).

Optional Tactics Cards extend the game and introduce additional historical flavour and uncertainty - enhancing the already excellent replayability.

The game comes with:

A 600mm x 600 mounted map
A dual-layer admin board
36 wooden formation blocks
4 wooden admin blocks
8 counters
12 formation cards
27 tactics cards

There will also be a 'meeple' based edition.

—description from the publisher

name: Avalon: The Riven Veil
description:
Arthur and Mordred fell at Camlann field, Arthur's body has been taken to Avalon, and unknown to the fey, Mordred followed...for the shattered son of King Arthur is not dead. By way of forbidden lore, his body endured the wounds of Excalibur and followed along the hidden ways to Avalon. Now the veil between the magical and the mundane has been pierced, and the wound calls like a beacon. The way is open, and all those with the sight now see it, so they come — some to defile the land, some to defend it.

In Avalon: The Riven Veil, an Arthurian-based area-control and exploration game, you lead mighty factions through the misty veil to discover what awaits on the mystical isle of Avalon. Explore the mists, discover legendary items of power, bond mythic beasts, hunt for the grail, and prepare for war.

The game ends when you reach the end of the final season (season 2 or 3 depending on your selected game length). Each player gains the Victory Points from the revealed settlement slots of their Faction Board then whoever has the most Victory Points at the end of that Season, wins the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Awaken the Ancients
description:
It is time to awaken the Ancients from their hibernation! As Warden of the Grove, your duty is to perform awakening rituals on the slumbering Ancients. Each awakening ritual is uniquely attuned to a specific Ancient, drawing its power from a combination of limited Wildseeds. Once awakened, some Ancients may need to consume seeds to restore their vitality. Plan your actions wisely to ensure you have enough seeds to awaken all the Ancients and preserve the grove’s harmony under your careful stewardship.

In Awaken the Ancients, carefully manage your limited supply of seed tokens to perform unique awakening rituals attuned to each Ancient. You'll strategically move seeds Mancala style around a grid of 8 Ancients, placing them on specific Ancients to match their awakening requirements. Once an Ancient is awakened, it may consume certain seeds for nourishment, removing them from play.

The challenge lies in planning your moves to ensure all eight Ancients are awakened before you run out of seeds or it becomes impossible to complete the rituals. Manage your resources wisely and use the Keepers' abilities to control the direction of seed movement, striving to achieve victory by awakening all Ancients. After a win, you final score is equal to the number of seeds remaining in the game.

This version of the game also includes the following expansions: Blight and Bother, Starstones, and the Dream Eater.

—description from the publisher

name: Away Team: The Voyages of the Pandora
DONE I AM
description:
DONE I AM is an especially silly game. If you take it seriously, then it’s your own fault!
The game consists of a handful of cards. Theoretically, there are 83 cards. But because curious things happen in this game, there may be fewer. However, it doesn’t matter. On your turn, you may either draw 1 card from the draw pile into your hand or play 1 card from your hand face-up into the discard pile and perform its effect (if it has any).
What’s it all about? Quite simply, whoever is first to have the phrase “I AM DONE” in front of them wins the game. Well, maybe not, if anyone has read the T&Cs...
You can play DONE I AM as it is — or you can shuffle it together with the cards from I AM DONE for the ultimate “I AM DONE I AM” experience.

—description from the publisher

name: Baba's House
description:
You come to your senses in a poorly lit place. Standing up and looking around you see others you know. Friends, family? You can't seem to remember. Tracing the room you slowly become aware of an uncanny feeling, the fear of being prey. You need to find a way out. Now.

Baba's House is a horror board game about surviving an intelligent nightmare alongside others. DREAMERS will have to explore and combat an odd environment and its disturbing inhabitants to find an escape. They will have to watch their backs as secret agendas grip their fellow survivors while lucidity rises. They will need to manage a rising anticipation lest a greater horror of the dark arrives. And finally, should they fall to the dark, they will rise again as a twisted amalgamation of their own psyche, and try to take the life of a fellow player, in an attempt to restore their own.

—description from the designer

name: Dorfromantik: Light Luggage
description:
Dorfromantik – Light Luggage is a cooperative tile-laying game. Work together to create a beautiful world of hexagonal landscapes and earn as many points as possible.
You’ll place tiles to build a beautiful Landscape while trying to complete tasks and create the longest possible River. The better you succeed, the more points you’ll score at the end of the game. From game to game, the points you earn can unlock new tiles and cards. These present you with new challenges and help you push your high score even further.
This compact edition offers a quick and easy introduction to the high-score hunt of Dorfromantik!

—description from the publisher

name: BADFLIX Scareville
description:
In this fast-paced, dice-based push-your-luck game for 1–5 players, you take on the role of quirky horror villains who use the streaming service BADFLIX to sneak into living rooms and give movie watchers the fright of their lives by snatching them through their TV screens and dragging them to the world of horror: Scareville.

Players compete in a race through haunted horror films, trying to collect souls by reaching the screen at the end of each film track. The first player to collect 3 souls (or 5 for a longer game) triggers the final round.

On their turn, players roll dice and combine results to move progress markers forward on film tracks. If all dice are used efficiently, players can keep rolling to push further - risking it all for greater rewards. But unused dice or failed combinations can end the turn or even reset progress.

Reaching a screen earns a soul and resets that film for all opponents. Risk, timing, and clever combos are key to success. Optional “Deleted Scenes” introduce unpredictable effects for added chaos and tension. And by using optional action cards (as hand cards), players can annoy their opponents (e.g. by changing their dice rolls) or give themselves an advantage - but beware: once an action card is played, it's gone!

—Description from the designer

name: Bag & Snatch: Backyard Brawl
description:
Chase tricky animals, recover stolen loot & outsmart rivals in this fast-paced, push-your-luck board game for 1-5 players.

Bag & Snatch! is a fast-paced, strategic card game designed by David Spada and Nestore Mangone. Each match lasts around 15 minutes—perfect for quick, exciting sessions!
In this dynamic game, players use their cards to snatch tokens from the center of the table. These tokens are divided into four animal groups, each with a unique ability that can shift the tide of the game, disrupt opponents, and open new strategic opportunities.

Strategy is everything! Points are scored at the start of each turn based on how many tokens of the same type you’ve collected—the more you have, the more you earn! But beware: if a player depletes the central supply of an animal, everyone else must return their matching tokens, losing valuable points in the process.

To win, you’ll need to master the balance between hoarding and diversifying, knowing when to go all-in and when to play it safe. Will you take risks for a big payout or play the long game for steady gains? Bag & Snatch! is easy to learn but full of clever twists—dive in and outsmart your rivals!

—description from the publisher

name: Bagged & Boarded
description:
In Bagged & Boarded, you're a kid who loves comics. You can't merely focus on collecting your favorite issues, though. You also need to make enough money to afford them!

By savvy investment of your time, allowance, and chores money, you'll amass an impressive collection in no time! But wait—then what? Do you sell your expensive issues to buy others? Or do you put them on display, banking points for the end of the game while also increasing that series's value for everyone else?

Each morning, you'll plan your day, then resolve everyone's plans in order. Will you search the catalogs? Preorder from the comic store or dig through the bargain bin? Wait in line at the convention for autographs and swag? Or, maybe you'll spend your time at home doing chores, bagging and boarding old issues, and putting them on display.

Collecting and displaying a large series is worth a lot, but keep an eye on your clever friends. They might be holding onto that issue you're looking for, eagerly waiting for you to boost its value!

—description from the designer

name: Bailiff of Boscoop
Bailén 1808: Una victoria decisiva
description:
Bailen 1808: A Decisive Victory, recreates this pivotal battle, an unexpected confrontation that marked a turning point in the struggle against Napoleonic domination.

The game shares the same system as our other Napoleonic titles, such as Waterloo 1815 and Austerlitz 1805. Units are represented by wooden blocks, which not only offer a unique visual appeal but also facilitate a clear visualization of movements on the battlefield.

—description from the designer

Bailén 1808: Una Victoria Decisiva, recrea esta trascendental batalla, un enfrentamiento inesperado que marcó un punto de inflexión en la lucha contra el dominio napoleónico.

El juego comparte el mismo sistema que otros títulos napoleónicos de nuestra editorial, como Waterloo 1815 y Austerlitz 1805. Las unidades se representan mediante bloques de madera, lo que no solo ofrece un atractivo visual único, sino que también facilita la clara visualización de los movimientos en el campo de batalla.

—description from the designer (Spanish)

name: Baja Sardinia
description:
You are the owner of one of the most evocative resorts in the North of Sardinia and you must manage your spaces in this incredible stretch of coastline. Make your stay special in this piece of paradise and if, at the end of the summer, your Resort will be the most famous in Sardinia, you will gain victory leaving an indelible memory in the heart of your guests.

A simple but deep worker placement game where each action will require a different amount of time to be performed, forcing your workers to stay still for multiple rounds. Build bungalows, hire staff members, book and welcome tourists; find the right time to earn Money and invest It to fulfill tourists' wishes, make your Resort achieve the most fame and win the game at the end of the seventh round.

In 2010 Sun, Sea & Sand made a name for itself, introducing Corné van Moorsel as a cult author. Baja Sardinia resumes the original game and, after a new development, brings it again in a more modern guise and an astonishing artwork: multiple ways to earn money and fame points add more depth to every choice and the addition of different characters grants high replayability without extending game length.

-description from developer

name: Baltic Empires: The Northern Wars of 1558-1721
description:
"Baltic Empires" is an approachable 2-5 player strategic level wargame about conflicts between the states of the Baltic region during the early modern era, a transformative period of religious conflict, large scale warfare, and constant struggles for power. Players will have to develop their economy, strengthen their administration, secure trade hubs, and finally build armies to become the dominant power of the Baltics. Denmark-Norway, Sweden, Russia, Poland-Lithuania, and Prussia will fight for hegemony, using variable victory conditions that reflect their respective historical objectives. Gameplay involves collecting resources, building new infrastructure and units, recruiting historical figures to your court, and finally going to war to expand your empire and fulfil your national ambition.

Highlights:

     Five asymmetric factions with unique abilities and objectives
     A highly thematic deck of historical Dramatis Personae to constitute your royal court
     A simple yet deep economic system that forces players to make tough decisions regarding their finances and wage war for key resources
     A streamlined battle system based on custom dice per unit type
     Variable player counts, from 2 to 5 players, and variable game lengths, with scenarios ranging from a tight duel to a diplomatic heavy conflict with alliances and betrayals


—description from the publisher

name: Banana Magnate
description:
Banana Magnate is a chill, slightly twisted economic card game for 2–4 players, where you run your own banana plantation… and make sure your rivals regret ever planting anything. Build stuff, upgrade it, harvest your sweet yellow goods, and scrump like there’s no tomorrow.
Oh yeah — and then scrump even more..

What’s inside this fruity madness:

     A banana-oriented economy that’s easy to pick up and oddly satisfying.
     Your very own banana plantation — totally wacky and different every single time.
     12 eccentric characters with wild abilities, all fighting for the title of Banana Magnate.
     Sabotaging your neighbors? 100% socially acceptable here.
     A goofy, cartoonish vibe that makes everything feel light and fun — even when you’re being robbed blind.


“scrump”, in game dev lingo, means sneakily “borrowing” someone’s crops — without asking, without telling, and definitely without giving them back. Ever.

—description from the publisher

name: Bandido Alcatraz (10th Anniversary Edition)
description:
For a whole decade, Bandido has outsmarted everyone and become a true legend. Now, it's time to celebrate his anniversary! Help Bandido make his daring escape from the legendary prison of Alcatraz. Dig tunnels, gather equipment and try to avoid the coming tide around the island. If the tunnels are flooded, you can’t escape! Work together and build a single exit to make it off the Rock.


     Build tunnels and collect equipment. 
     Stop the incoming water by covering it. 
     Create dead ends and keep a single exit route. 


—description from the publisher

name: Bantam West (2nd Edition): Graves of Gold
description:
Graves of Gold is a standalone western-horror expansion for Bantam West (2nd Edition). Play solo with the expansion on its own, or 1-5 players when combined with Bantam West (2nd Edition) in all-new solo, co-op, and competitive game modes.

Search for relics and riches, but beware of cultists, creatures, and the unspeakable terrors that lurk below. In a world where the source of gold has been lost to time, will you be the first to rediscover it?

—description from the publisher

name: Bantam West: 2nd Edition
description:
Howdy there, Deadly Stranger...

Bantam West (2nd Edition) is a competitive open-world roleplaying game for 2 to 4 players. Step into the boots of our Deadly Strangers, immortal outlaws, as you explore the Western town of Gallow Springs and the surrounding Wilderness, Wetlands, Mountains, and Plains. Live life however you please as you work, fight, build, trade, and burn to become the Most Notorious!

You’ll harvest resources to craft powerful goods, acquire deadly weapons and gear, level your character’s skills and endeavors, navigate the terrain’s hazards, build cabins and recruit a posse to assert your influence. Watch for events and encounters across the terrain that might bring riches–or ruin. In the end, only one Deadly Stranger can come out on top!

2nd Edition walks back into the saloon with a fresh shave, polished iron, and a brand new pair of boots. Since the release of 1st Edition in 2023, our team has scoured the internet to gather and analyze input from all players we could possibly find. Building on this foundation, Ike and the team refined the game into its most accessible, exciting, and replayable form yet!

Updates include:


     Rewritten rulebook (with professional Co-Author)
     UI/UX Overhaul
     Combat System Overhaul
     To-Do List Overhaul
     Event System Overhaul
     4 Additional Endeavors
     More Variation in the Characters
     12 New “Classic” Cowboy Guns


…and much more!

—description from the publisher

name: Everdell Duo
publisher: Starling Games (II); Delight; Gém Klub Kft.; Maldito Games; Pegasus Spiele; Rebel Sp. z o.o.; Tycoon Games; White Goblin Games; Ігромаг
description:
In Everdell Duo, you either compete against your single opponent or play co-operatively with another player to earn the most points. You accomplish this by placing workers to gather resources, then use those resources to play cards face up in front of you, creating your own woodland city.

Cards may be played from your hand or from the face-up area on the board called the meadow. However, only cards touching the sun or moon token may be played from the meadow, and players move these tokens each time they perform a turn. Therefore, planning for and timing which cards you play is critical.

Each game you try to achieve various events, the requirements of which differ from game to game, making certain cards and combinations more important to pursue.

The game lasts for four seasons, then players add their scores to determine the winner. If you're playing co-operatively, check the requirements for the chapter you are playing to see whether you have won.

—description from the publisher

name: Barista
description:
Barista is a one-hour game for 1-4 players designed by Marc Musso.

Own, operate, and upgrade your own coffee shop to become the most popular spot in town!

In Barista, you start with a basic coffee shop and three interns in your staff. This can change very quickly. You decide if/when you want to hire one of the dozens of unique employees or hire Baristas to make coffee faster. You decide if you want to buy trucks that go out and gain you resources or benefits. You decide when and how to upgrade your coffee shop to hold more ingredients, brew different types of coffee, or brew beans quicker.

You will perform actions to gain ingredients and use them to make delicious cups of coffee for your customers. Serving these coffee orders will turn the customers into regulars and they'll come back again and again, giving you a benefit for each future order served. You will compete and make strategic decisions when it comes to placing your workers on actions as well. Many actions have powerful effects that only go to the first worker on the space so it's crucial to pick the right time to act.

Hire employees, fulfill orders, upgrade your shop, and more in this competitive worker placement, engine-building game.

—description from the publisher

name: Baseball Diamante
description:
Baseball Diamante is a game of strategy and chance. From 2 to 4 players, play short or long games in a real baseball simulator. With an easy and simple gameplay you may choose to play the Amateur or Major League modes with everything a fan of the sports need to bring the magic of baseball home.

The game uses 3 die and one ball in the shape of a coin. Players have different skills so you may bat stronger or run faster depending on the batter in turn. The turn is not as quick as drawing a card, the play will develop in phases, Pitch, Bat, Determine Zone, Catch, Run, Throw the ball, making the game as real as the real one. The game uses a free app with immersive Audio and an interactive scoreboard.

There are more team colors available as expansions.

The stadium folds into a box.

name: Battle Box: Age of Sail
description:
Battle Box - Age of Sail is a complete naval wargame within a small tin box that fits in your pocket, perfect for a quick game on the go or even full naval campaigns. It includes ships, battle mat, dice, narrative scenarios, and cards for in-game effects such as critical hits and special ship rules.

The set of four ships, each of a different colour, are used to represent generic men-of-war and merchant ships. The status, crew quality, ship upgrades, and critical hits on each ship are tracked by means of cards and a token matching the ship's colour.

The rules are perfect for fun and short battles at sea during the 18th and 19th centuries, such as French privateers attacking an East India Company convoy, or a British squadron intercepting the Spanish treasure fleet. Easy to learn but with a tactical depth that makes strategic choices decisive.

Players roll for initiative and take turns activating each of their ships, with advantages for ships sailing in line. The wind might change depending on the initiative roll, forcing players to adapt to the new situation. When a ship is activated, it can sail on the hex grid provided with the game, fire broadsides (devastating critical hits might happen too, such a bringing down a mast), and perform crew tests to repair the ship, maneuver for better positioning or board enemy ships. The game continues until the enemy ships strike their colours or the scenario objectives are met.

—description from the designer

name: Battle Commander: Volume I
publisher: Sound of Drums GmbH; Wargame Mate
description:
Battle Commander is a new wargame system whose intent is to replay historical 18th-19th century battles.
It features a fresh framework focused on providing two key play aspects: command decisions and playability. Eventually, the system is planned to expand into other similar eras, such as the American Civil War.

It uses a granular cube-pull activation system for all game phases (player movement, combat, rally, card draws, etc.) and in interactive Combat system using Event cards. No Dice!

There will be six Battles per volume, more or less in chronological order, that'll cover the Napoleonic wars from start to finish. A series about the American Civil War is also in the works.

The package will be done deluxe, with three two-sided mounted map-boards, painted-on wood pieces (no stickers), large scenario set-up cards, a 3D Army mat, and numerous bonus features.

Volume I:
LONATO 1796, CASTIGLIONE 1796, ARCOLE 1796, RIVOLI 1797, MONTEBELLO 1800, MARENGO, 1800.

Volume I - Scenario Kit:
MONDOVI 1796 - 1st, 2nd and 3rd RIVOLI clashes 1796 - 1st CALDIERO 1796 - 2nd CALDIERO 1805.

Volume II:
THE PYRAMIDS 1798 - ZURICH 1799 - HOHENLINDEN 1800 - ELCHINGEN 1805 - WERTINGEN 1805 - AUSTERLITZ 1805.

Volume II - Scenario Kit:
STOCKACH 1799 - SAN GUILIANO 1799 - TREBBIA 1799  CASSINA GROSSA 1799 - NOVI 1799 - HELIOPOLIS 1800.

Volume III:
JENA 1806 - AUERSTADT 1806 - PULTUSK 1806 - EYLAU 1807 - HEILSBERG 1807 - FRIEDLAND 1807.

—description from the designer

name: Battle Decisions: Kriegsspiel
description:
Everything you need to run a modern version of the game that started modern wargaming. Box has maps, counters and tracking sheets for the umpire, and 2 players (or teams).

Kriegsspiel is the original military simulation game, developed by the Prussian Army in the 1800s, designed to train officers by replicating the "fog of war" and command complexities, using an umpire to process double-blind orders on maps. It emphasizes realistic command, communication delays, and decision-making with limited information, inspiring today's modern wargames.

This version includes 10 scenarios, all using the same map.

name: Battle Hymn Vol. 2: Shiloh, Bentonville & Gettysburg
description:
Battle Hymn: Volume Two is the sequel game release to Battle Hymn - Volume One and includes two complete games: Shiloh and Bentonville. Battle Hymn is a brigade-level system based upon research into Civil War combat. This new entry introduces a new solitaire system to the series and an extension map for Gettysburg (Volume One) for a complete alternative history of the entire battle.

Shiloh: The First Great Battle depicts the two-day battle of Shiloh. The Confederate army surprises the Union forces of General Grant and a fierce battle blazes for two days, with first the Confederate on the offensive and then the Union turning to the attack on the second day. Shiloh shocked to the nation. Left dead or injured were more men than in all of America’s previous wars combined. The game includes four scenarios.

Bentonville: The Last Great Battle simulates the final major battle of the war. Sherman is marching through North Carolina when a surprise attack by the much-weakened Army of Tennessee catches one wing of the US army exposed. The first day ends in a bloody stalemate, and continues on for two more days. Can the Confederates escape? This game has both two-player and solitaire scenarios, and introduces an innovative new solitaire system to the game series.

Bonus One: Gettysburg ’62: No Lost Orders depicts an alternative history — the Confederates do not lose their orders for the 1862 invasion, Antietam never happens, and Jeb Stuart’s cavalry begins the battle of Gettysburg with a major engagement south of the Round Tops. The battle grows as a Union corps arrives to face off with Heth’s Division.

Bonus Two: the Gettysburg extension map attaches to Gettysburg: The Tide Turns making a complete alternative history of the entire battle. Plus, a new scenario explores the alternative that Pickett’s Charge never happens; instead the Confederates drive south around the Round Tops on their way to Baltimore.

—description from the publisher

name: Everdell Silverfrost
publisher: Starling Games (II); Tabletop Tycoon Inc.; Gém Klub Kft.; Matagot; Pegasus Spiele; Rebel Sp. z o.o.; Tycoon Games; White Goblin Games
description:
Silverfrost is the next standalone edge of the map series of Everdell.  Beyond the snow-capped Spirecrest mountains to the south of Everdell Valley, lies the bold country of Silverfrost. It is your task to build and maintain a city in this challenging landscape. You must clear the piling snow, burn the fires to keep your citizens warm and prosperous, and complete important quests for the Ranger’s Guild.

In Silverfrost, you send critter workers to various Locations on the board, cards, or the mountain to gather resources and activate unique effects. You use these resources to play cards face up in front of you, forming your own city. Each turn, you take 1 of 3 possible actions — Place a worker, Play a card, or Prepare for the next season.

You may place 1 of your workers on any Basic Location, Red Destination card in your city or opponent’s cities, the Forge, the Hot Springs, or a mountaintop Beacon, so long as it is not blocked by Snow or another worker. You then claim the listed resources or perform the action. If there is Snow at the location, you must first spend a Fire resource to clear the snow pile. If you use your unique Ranger worker, you can visit an occupied location, or gain a Fire resource if visiting a location alone.

To play a card, you must pay the listed cost of resources. If it is a Critter, you may instead play it for free by using 1 of your 2 Chimneys, so long as you have the necessary Fire to light it. Cards may be played either from your hand, or from the area of face-up cards on the board known as the Valley. Nearly all of the cards in Silverfrost feature new and powerful abilities, offering a huge variety of strategic depth and combos to explore.

If all of your workers are deployed, you may prepare for the next season by bringing back all of your workers, gaining a new worker, and performing the action described for the following season, introducing new snowfall to the board and to your city, as well as other challenges. A player is finished when they have played through the last season (Spring) and cannot perform any more actions. After all players have finished, the player with the most points is the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Ghostbumpers
publisher: Deep Print Games; Hobby Japan; Pegasus Spiele
description:
The monsters are terrorizing the fairground. You dive into a crazy bumper-car ride and try not to lose your nerve. Who will be the first to get scared?

In this trick-taking game, you don’t want to win too many tricks, because each trick carries the risk that your character gets scared. The braver you play, the more points you can earn.

—description from the publisher

name: Battlecrest: Deadrock Base Game
description:
Return to the Neververse with Battlecrest: Deadrock, our third year base set. Only the toughest and most brutal fighters can survive this desolate landscape. As with Fellwoods and Metronn, Deadrock comes with a new 6-card map and two new heroes. More heroes will be added throughout the year to test their might against each other and their environment.


     Deadrock Map Set: 6 Landmark cards


The all-new Deadrock map is as dangerous a place as the Neververse has ever seen. This rocky desert offers plenty of opportunities for clever heroes to rain damage on their foes, but the twin storms at its center can bring down even the toughest warrior all by themselves. Don’t get caught in their path or you might not ever get out.


     Cirrus Hero set.
     Cirrus AI Sheet: for solo play, requires Imperator expansion.



     Noster Hero set.
     Noster AI Sheet: for solo play, requires Imperator expansion.



What is the mark of a true champion? Legendary heroes clash across the Neververse to find out.

Battlecrest is a card-based tactical skirmish game for 2 players (1-4 with expansions). With perfect information, players must truly outwit their opponent to win.

Characters are composed of 6-card sets featuring a hero card, a health tracker, and action cards. Occasionally a minion or item will replace an action card.

The map is built of 6 cards as well, with the cards randomly placed in a set pattern.

Players take turns maneuvering their characters around the dynamic, and often dangerous map while unleashing powerful attacks. As action cards are used they open up new possibilities and empower the character’s battlecrests. Build up to decisive strikes or refocus to get powers back. Every character has a unique set of actions and preferred tactics, so no two battles play the same.

—description from the publisher

name: Battlefields: Deluxe Edition
description:
Battlefields is a tactical combat game between two armies of heroes from the Catacombs universe. First, players spend points to draft their army of heroes, then they place their chosen heroes on the hex-based neoprene playmat. Different heroes have different movement rates and attacks. Combat is resolved by either dexterity (dice flicking) or non-dexterity mechanisms.

The game provides a variety of units for both the Heroic and Lich Lord forces and supports two players. It also features a solo mode.

—description from the publisher

name: BattleForge: Berserker
description:
You are a warrior reborn in the wrath of Fenrir, rising from Valhalla not for glory, but for vengeance. Strike down biomechanical monstrosities, face the Ironborn gods, and unleash your fury in a desperate war to bring Ragnarök back on track — or die trying.

BattleForge: Berserker is a 1–4 player cooperative board game where you and your allies face off against corrupted Norse gods and biomechanical monstrosities. Each hero has unique abilities and a personal progression path — as you level up, you unleash your inner Berserker, transforming into a more powerful form.
Strategic dice management, evolving skills, and team synergy are key to surviving the chaos.

—description from the designer

name: Battles of Divine Right: Shrieker's Scrub
description:
From The History of Zorn and the Goblins: During Zorn's "Brothers' War", Ortwir boldly raided Immer for supplies. In reply, King Reglissar made common cause with Sirdar Nystul and helped destroy Ortwir's army at Shrieker's Scrub. Ortwir escaped capture and fled far to the South, offering his services to the dreaded lord of the Witchlands, in whose employ he would later achieve great fame and power.

Battles of Divine Right: Shrieker's Scrub, The first in a new lineup of travel-sized games based on the lore of Minaria with the Battles of Divine Right series. Games in this series take a single battle from anywhere in Divine Right's expansive world and allow two players to experience the conflict themselves.

The Battle of Shrieker's Scrub takes players back in time, as borders were still being established, and zooms in on the final escalation of tensions between the northern nations of Immer and Zorn, as Immer presses deep into Zorn's territory and forces the goblins to defend their home.

name: Bayou Boss
description:
Down in the Big Bayou, you’re just gettin’ started, lookin’ to make a name for yourself.  

Bayou Boss is a sly ol’ trick-takin’ card game, loaded with two BIG honkin’ twists:


     Y’all don’t wanna be winnin’ them tricks, no sir! The one with the fewest tricks at the end struts out as the champ. Your job’s to bamboozle the rest into haulin’ in more tricks than you.
     There'll be cards sittin’ pretty, face-up in the middle o’ the table. When the round’s done, folks take turns reachin’ in to grab what they fancy. Best be plannin’, cher, ‘cause you don’t wanna be left gnawin’ on them sorry scraps.


Outsmart ‘em, outplay ‘em, and claim your crown as the Boss o’ the Bayou!

Bayou Boss is a fun must-follow, must-trump Trick-Taking game in which players compete to take the least tricks possible. During the game players will also compete to take good cards from a central pool, the Swamp - but the only way to ensure you get the good cards is to win tricks...which is precisely what you don't want to do! Aided and exacerbated by Characters from the Bayou, the game allows players to manipulate the run of the tricks to their advantage - or to fall victim to a Character who may force you to win a trick or may change the trump. The game is highly replayable, including 10 different character cards, not all of whom will appear in each game, and is deliberately designed to scale well from 2-8 players.

—description from the publisher

name: Beasts and Diplomacy
publisher: Dragon Dawn Games; Dragon Dawn Productions
description:
Beasts and Diplomacy is a card drafting, tableau-building game where players become Knights of the land of Aterra, competing to assemble the best Exhibition of wild and rare Beasts that appeal to the Diplomats of the land. Players must also try to fulfill their secret Quests while ensuring they have enough Ore to maintain their ever-growing Maintenance costs. Like many card drafting games, Beasts and Diplomacy offers interactions like players taking cards before others can get to them, however, unlike other drafting games the design focus isn't on scarcity, but on opportunity. As you play you will have to constantly react to your opponents' actions and formulate new short term plans to achieve your long term goal of having the most balanced Exhibition. When one door closes, several new ones open. It's up to you to find your own path.

While the game's actions are fundamentally simple (e.g. icon matching and drafting), Beasts and Diplomacy offers lots of depth and replayability. Your first playthroughs will leave you with a sense that you are just scratching the surface of what is possible, but with experience you'll learn to manage risk, finances, and action sequencing, which will lead to highly tense and competitive playthroughs.

After 3 days of drafting cards, undercutting each other and building the perfect exhibition, your exhibitions will be evaluated by your Diplomats and your secret Quests. The Knight with the most Influence Points wins!

name: Beastward: Monster Hunt RPG
description:
When all heroes fall, the King calls for the Beastward Hunters.

Your task is to reclaim cursed lands overrun by monsters and push back the darkness spreading across the realm.

Explore a dangerous map filled with hostile regions, hidden treasures, and limited resources. Fight varied monsters, collect loot, and trade supplies in towns and remote locations. As you progress, you develop your hero through a dedicated skill tree, shaping your playstyle and growing noticeably stronger over time.

Master tactical combat to survive increasingly powerful enemies. Clear three towns of monster infestations and purify three ancient idols scattered across the map. Only then can you summon Fernobog from the Dark Tower and face the final confrontation.

—description from the designer

name: Beetown Beatdown
description:
RECRUIT. MIGRATE. SURVIVE.

Take command as a Queen Bee, guiding your COLONY through daring exploration and strategic area control.

Expand your HIVES, claim lucrative resources, and harness a unique combat system – where a calculated defeat can be more valuable than a victory.

To claim dominance, you must gain unrivalled control of 3 or more HIVES by the end of any Season. Compete solo against up to 3 adaptive AI opponents, or challenge others in a highly replayable and unpredictable showdown!

name: Before The Rain
description:
Players take on the role of busy bees, set out to gather as much pollen as they can before the rainy weather comes in. Score points by taking valuable pollen from the five different flowers back to your hive. Be careful, timing your return against your opponents and the weather is crucial. Push your luck to contribute and collect as much pollen as possible, and always keep an eye on the skies to head back to the hive before the rain ends the round.

Each turn, all players will simultaneously play a card facedown from their hand. When revealed, players will either add pollen to the growing central pile or play their "Return to Hive" card to safely collect everything accumulated so far and back out of the round.

After each turn, Weather Cards are revealed to show if the rain is approaching. Once three rain symbols accumulate, anyone still in the field loses all their pollen for that round. The game will end after three rounds, adding up your best score from each round to find your total score!

Will you be the first to take the pollen for yourself, or will you push your luck further and race against the rain? Before The Rain is an easy-to-learn, push-your-luck game featuring beautiful hand-illustrated artwork.

—description from the publisher

name: Behind Gold
description:
Analyze, assemble, admire — in Behind "Gold", you'll find one scene to solve, each with its own unique mechanisms and reflection. You want to observe the tiles laid out in front of you, then assemble them logically and turn them over to admire the result on the reverse! Six clue cards are available for each scene and should be turned over in numerical order. The scenes in the box are:

• The game : A mother and her son just finished to play a boardgame.

Once you've reconstructed the picture, you can read all of the clues at your disposal, even if none of them were turned over while you were solving the picture. They'll help you validate your thinking and confirm your thoughts! Finally, flip each tile to reveal the final image...

name: Beijing
description:
Beijing is a strategy game in which players aim to maximize the prosperity and prestige of their province. They must call upon diverse courtiers like scholars, monks, warriors, and craftsmen to help them manage their province and withstand various unfortunate events. After twelve rounds, which represent the twelve months of a year, the player who best manages their province and endures these challenging times will earn the most honor and victory points.

The game consists of exactly 12 rounds, symbolizing the 12 months in a year. After the event and any decay, players move their scoring marker forward for each of their streets, each musician, and each spiral on their scrolls. The game ends after the scoring phase of the 12th round.

Additional Victory Points are awarded person tiles, Monks, and money. The player with the most victory points wins.

Beijing revitalizes In the Year of the Dragon, staying true to its core while introducing fresh improvements and increased variability. With refined mechanisms and new strategic options, Beijing enhances the tension and depth of the original.

name: Believe in Me! (Please)
description:
Believe in Me! (Please) is a satirical strategy game in which 2-4 players embody mischievous, self-proclaimed gods vying for the faith of gullible mortals. Through cunning, persuasion, and divine theatrics, you claim natural phenomena as your miracles to grow your cult and define your godly form by assembling a unique combination of chaotic, serene, or wrathful body parts. Beware of meddlesome heretics, inquisitors, and rival gods, who will stop at nothing to undermine your holy reputation!

With its mix of card-driven mechanisms, worker placement, and over-the-top humor, Believe in Me! (Please) is a battle of wits, strategy, and divine improvisation to see whose cult becomes the world's ultimate religion. Hallelujah!

—description from the publisher

name: Bella Vista
description:
You are architects, striving to offer your residents the best possible view of the city’s parks. To achieve this, you must construct buildings of eight different heights, always aiming to be the tallest in the neighborhood to score the most points!
Find the perfect location to meet City Hall’s requirements and complete your objectives… but beware: you surely won’t be the only one who has spotted it! Choose your place in the turn order wisely, and be ready to pay a high price if you want to be the first to build!
The game ends once you have constructed all eight of your buildings. Be the richest architect to claim victory!

—description from the publisher

name: Kronologic: Cuzco 1450
publisher: Origames; Super Meeple; Gém Klub Kft.; Ghenos Games; HIT Games; Pegasus Spiele; Tranjis Games
description:
Kronologic are modern alternatives to Clue: find the culprit, the weapon and the location. Each turn, the active player needs to interrogate a suspect (by aligning cards under perforated cardboard tiles), giving away information to everyone at the table, but giving the active player extra information (how many times a suspect visited a specific location, at what time, etc.)

Set in the majestic city of Cuzco during the year 1450, Kronologic: Cuzco 1450 offers 15 exciting challenges spread across 3 immersive scenarios. By sharing some - but not all  - of the you gather, you race with the other players to solve 3 Inca-themed mystery scenarios.

Be the first to solve the mystery to win the game.

name: Berserk: The Board Game
description:
Berserk: The Board Game is a cooperative miniatures game for 1 to 5 players, set in the iconic universe of the legendary manga created by Kentaro Miura.

Each Hero has a unique set of Action Cards, used to move, attack, defend, and trigger special abilities or game effects. But beware- the more Action Cards a Hero uses in a single turn, the more fatigue sets in!

As the shadow of the Falcon spreads across the world, blurring the lines between reality and the occult, Guts relentlessly pursues his quest for vengeance. In this struggle against his fate, the Black Swordsman and his colossal blade stand firm time and time again – striking, cutting, and defying the inevitable.

Though his wandering, he unexpectedly finds souls willing to follow him in his impossible fight: Schireke, the young witch with dormant power; Farnese, lost between fervor and redemption; Serpico, the silent shadow with a razor-sharp blade; and Isidro, still searching for confidence in himself. 
Together, they tread a path paved with nightmares, facing Guts’ sworn enemies and horrific creatures that should not exist. But what can mere mortals do against mocking gods and the demonic hordes that engulf the world?

—description from the publisher

name: Best Eleven
description:
You are the manager of a soccer club seeking to build your Best Eleven, a team to represent your club on Matchday.

Recruit players to your team by bidding on Free Agents over seven transfer windows. Each Free Agent you add to your team can add speed, savvy, strength, and skill and help increase the performance of your Best Eleven.

Win the game by having the team with the most points accumulated from team synergy and tactics on Matchday.

—description from the designer

name: Beyond the Sky
description:
In Beyond the Sky, our planet has become uninhabitable, time has collapsed, mixing with wars and catastrophes from the past, present, and future. Enemies at all levels have appeared: tank battalions, aircraft squadrons, flying saucers, star fleets, meteor showers, and even space monsters.  Now, you must be one of the heroes who rescues the last survivors of humanity from the atmosphere and takes them to another planet.

The quadrant is divided into a 5x10 grid, and every 2 rows are attacked by an enemy type associated with 2 or more dice colors.  Each space can offer immediate rewards (extra moves, repairs, extra turns, etc.) or protection against certain types of dice.

In each round, players can draw cards from the deck or play a card. The cards played will determine our movement by 1, 2, or 3 spaces, and there is even a type of card that moves two spaceships at once.  At the end of the round, after each player has finished their turn and moved their spaceships, the 4 dice (white, yellow, blue, and red) are rolled according to the position of each spaceship, the enemies, and the value of the corresponding die. Enemies will damage spaceships. Each spaceship can withstand 1 damage; the second damage eliminates it.

Take as many spaceships as you can into outer space, as quickly as possible, to get the highest score before a player runs out of spaceships to move and the game ends.

name: Bharat: Kings of Legend
description:
Welcome to Bharat: Kings of Legend, an epic game of power, mysticism, and romance set in ancient India. Players take on the roles of kings from powerful clans, all striving to become the greatest emperor in the land. To achieve this, you must expand your influence, form alliances, earn the blessings of the gods, and practice yoga to gain mastery over your life energies. The game ends after three Sun cycles or when all kingdoms are consolidated. The player with the most points wins.

Bharat offers a rich, dynamic experience in which every turn counts. Players must choose to advance the Sun or Moon cycle, affecting not only their own strategy but the game's overall pace. This core mechanism drives deep interaction as players battle for kingdoms, seek favor through rituals, and compete in marriage contests. The Dharma track adds a unique layer of competition and can even decide tied outcomes. With multiple paths to victory, from military conquest and political influence to divine blessings and strategic pilgrimages, the game rewards diverse playstyles and ensures high replayability.

—description from the publisher

name: Bible Clash: Gospels
description:
At Bible Clash, the gospel is woven into the gameplay itself. Every matchup forces players to think: What made Peter faithful? Why was John the Baptist courageous? How did Mary demonstrate obedience? The six categories—Faith, Wisdom, Courage, Obedience, Service, and Strategy—aren't random stats. They're the Christ-like virtues Scripture calls us to pursue.
Bible Clash doesn't just teach Bible facts. It sparks real conversations about biblical character—and shapes how we think about following Jesus. This is discipleship disguised as fun.

"And He went up on the mountain and called to Him those He Himself wanted." — Mark 3:13

WHAT'S IN THE BOX: 

     32 Character Cards (split 16 per player) 
     Each card features a Gospel character rated across 6 biblical categories: Faith, Wisdom, Courage, Obedience, Service, Strategy • Rules Cards


HOW TO PLAY: 

     Shuffle the deck and deal 16 cards to each player. Hold your deck face-down in your hand so only the top card is visible to you.
     The starting player (youngest player) looks at the top card of his deck, chooses one category, and announces it. For example: "Peter... Faith 8!" 
     The other player looks at the top card of his deck and reads the score for the same category. For example: “Pilate: Faith 3.”
     The higher score wins! The winner takes both cards and places them at the bottom of his deck.
     The winner of the round chooses the category in the next round. The same category cannot be chosen twice in a row.
     The first player to win all the cards wins the game! 


Extra Rules: 
Tie Breaker: If scores are tied, put both cards on the table and compare the same category of the next card. Winner takes all 4 cards (or 6…)!
Time Limit (Optional): If a game lasts longer than 15 minutes, start a 3-minute timer. When time runs out, the player with the most cards wins.

—description from the designer

name: Biblioclash
description:
Biblioclash is a fast-paced Finnish tactical deck-building game where players become mages dueling inside a magical library using spells, artifacts, and minions. You win when your opponent’s Mage reaches zero health.

Each match begins with both players choosing a Mage and building a personal Library of nine piles. During the duel, Wisdom is used to obtain cards from the Library into the deck, which represents everything the Mage can do. Turn by turn, the Mage grows stronger, combining spells into powerful plays.

At the heart of the game is the Striking Phase, a dynamic back-and-forth duel of timing and power. When spells collide, players react in real time, trading bursts of magic until one side breaks through. It’s a contest of focus and skill — a true clash of mages.

Biblioclash combines TCG and deck-building in one game, bringing both systems together. It features constant interaction and a fast pace, with many game modes to keep the game feeling fresh.

—description from the publisher

name: Bichos Bajo la Lluvia
description:
In the tiny world of insects, a rainy day can unleash maximum chaos.
Run to protect yourself and compete to get the most bugs in the shelters while the rain ends!


En el diminuto mundo de los insectos, un día lluvioso puede desatar el caos máximo. 
¡Corre a protegerte y compite por lograr el mayor número de bichos en los refugios mientras la lluvia acaba!

name: Billionaires and Guillotines
description:
Take on the role of 2-5 rival plutocrats vying to grab the wealth of the world before your actions trigger a revolution and you all lose… a lot more than your assets.

Will you play the media baron or the property speculator? The aristocrat or the tech overlord or the war profiteer? Whoever you play, you will be trying to buy a collection of five extravagant assets prized by the super-rich (a mega yacht, a celebrity spouse, a disaster bunker, an art masterpiece and more!) and prevent your opponents from achieving their dreams first.

But watch out - as you gobble up ever more resources, crises start to cascade out of control: wildfires and floods, pandemics and militias, killer robots and doomsday cults… Will you collaborate to suppress the growing rebellions, or will you try to get off the planet with your toys?

Billionaires and Guillotines is designed to get you playing right away with a simple set of rules. But once you’re ready, you can add more chaotic complexity and wicked fun.

You'll bribe politicians to ensure that government policy favours you over your rivals, and you'll take on a secret role that offers special powers and ways to win. Maybe you’ll be the Banker, who gets to break the rules? Or the Disaster Speculator, who is betting on the crisis?  Or the Elite Prepper, decorating your deluxe bunker? Or the Celebrity, who hopes to be spared by the revolution?

And yes, you can play the revolutionaries! In an optional expansion of the game, one player gets to be an agitator. But are you a well-meaning reformist, trying to work with the billionaires to solve the crises and suppress the rebellion, or are you a diabolical revolutionary, eager to wheel out the guillotine?

Billionaires and Guillotines is designed by Max Haiven and will be published in 2025 by London-based Pluto Press. The crowdfunding campaign for the game will launch on March 26 with a party in London on April 13. Games should be in stores and available to order worldwide by October. The game artwork is by Berlin-based artist Amanda Priebe.

name: Bio Blitz
description:
Bio Blitz is a fast-paced resource management game that’s easy to learn and compact enough to take on the go! In Bio Blitz, players assemble a team of real-world wildlife, strategically combining their unique traits to gain a tactical edge against their opponents. Gather your team and compete to see who reigns supreme in the wild world of the animal kingdom!

Bio Blitz is a game where the goal is to win by either reaching 30 points or being the first to assemble a full team. To succeed, players must strategically manage their resources and carefully choose which cards to add to their team. 

On each turn, players must take one of three main actions: forage for resources, discover animal and ecosystem cards, or compete to gain points. In addition to main actions, players may take two optional actions—trading and exploring — any number of times at the start of their turn.  As you build your team, you’ll combine your animals’ special abilities, giving you a tactical advantage. If you’re ready to rack up some extra points and take a gamble, challenge one of your opponent’s animals to a head-to-head competition!

Pick one of your animals and call out an opponent’s creature for a showdown. Both players roll a die and add their animal’s bonuses—the highest total wins! If your total power matches or exceeds the opponent’s animal’s defense, you defeat them, sending them to the discard pile and scoring points equal to their value.

—description from the designer

name: Biomes of Nilgiris
description:
Biomes of Nilgiris is a board game in which players venture into India's surreal Nilgiri biosphere, teeming with unique flora and fauna. As conservationists — ecologists, photographers, and citizen scientists — they aim to discover new species, address ecological issues, complete conservation missions, and earn ecology points.

Players collaboratively adapt to two ever-changing scenarios in each game, introducing fresh concepts and objectives. As specialists, they explore the vast reaches of Nilgiris, journal field entries, gain experience at the station, equip themselves with tools, conserve species in their habitat, and skillfully resolve ecological challenges. The game is intended to be an immersive experience celebrating nature's wonders and the art of conservation.

The game is set in a turn-based, mission-oriented format. Each turn, players can take three of eight actions:


     TRAVEL on the modular board
     EXPLORE to open up new biome cards
     JOURNAL to take notes on a field guide
     STUDY to gain usable XP from your notes
     DISCOVER new species 
     EQUIP a new equipment
     CONSERVE species or biomes, primarily to gain ecology points


—description from the designer

name: Last Minute
description:
You’re an elite (?) bomb squad and have just one minute to defuse a series of dangerous devices before everything goes… you know. Will this be your last minute?

Last Minute is a solo/coop game that plays in real time. You have to play the right defuse cards on the appropriate bomb cards, respecting a double timer condition. A cool head, fine planning and (if you face the challenge with friends) good teamwork will be necessary to avoid an explosive defeat!

—description from the publisher

name: Black Rose Wars: Revised Edition
description:
Turin, Year of Our Lord 1528

To whomever dares to cross the threshold of the Lodge, Beware. The Lodge is not what it appears to be. It lives. It watches. It waits. Heresy runs deep within these ancient walls, entwined with the very stones that hold them up. Dark practices are whispered here — rituals shaped by forbidden knowledge, led by men who call themselves Perceivers. Their power grows unchecked. Their secrets fester beneath the surface. This place must be investigated. Observed. Judged. For corruption does not sleep — and neither shall we.

In faith, Inquisitor Ezechiele

Black Rose Wars is a competitive deck-building experience with area control elements, focused on magical combat and set within the dark and mysterious halls of the Black Rose Lodge. Each player takes on the role of a powerful Mage, master of their own School of Magic, chosen to compete in a deadly contest to become the next Grand Magister. But beware — the Black Rose is a sentient force and she will fight to preserve the status quo.

The Revised edition features a fully rewritten rules set with Avatars, new room point scoring system, and new spells. There are new miniature prints and the artwork has been enhanced on both cards and boards.

name: BLAST: Operation Paradox
description:
It's 1996. Reality is cracking, and the timeline is infected with deadly anomalies. Your mission? Travel back to 1943, hunt down the source of corruption, and restore the timeline before it collapses for good. Fight the undead, fix the timeline, and BLAST your way through history in this, retro, tactical, chibi-style game!

Players join an elite Time Commando unit to destroy a zombie army. Play solo against a smart enemy AI, cooperate to take down the horde together, or jump into asymmetrical mode where one player turns traitor and takes command of the zombie horde.

Each round consists of 4 phases: Spawn, Commando, Enemy, Clean-up.  Players process through a deck of Mission cards. When you reveal the final Mission Card, It's time for the final Boss Battle.  Win - or die!

name: Blood Economy
description:
You are a vampire managing a tableau of human thralls. Each thrall provides powerful abilities while alive. But you must devour them for blood to survive the night.

Every turn you choose: Play a thrall for future power or devour one for blood. 16 turns to survive, 4 escalating blood requirements. As you devour thralls, you collect bond symbols that unlock vampire abilities: Spades for explosive blood generation, Hearts for suspicion management, Diamonds for card advantage.

Blood Economy is designed under a 36-card constraint: 30 thralls, 5 vampires, 1 reference/tracker. No dice, no boards, no tokens beyond what you have at home to track turns and resources.

Each vampire transforms the strategy completely: the Elder rewards balanced play, the Beast demands aggressive feeding, the Socialite focuses on preservation, and others. With 30 scenarios printed on card backs (ranging from beginner tutorials to expert challenges), you get 150 unique combinations.

—description from the designer

name: Light Speed: Arena
publisher: Tablescope; Cranio Creations; Dino Toys s. r. o.; Intrafin Games; Lucrum Games; Pegasus Spiele
description:
A real-time tabletop shooter in which you aim with your tiles and take a smartphone picture to let the app unfold the battle for you. As the roar of the crowd resonates, the arena is lit with the brilliant glow of sponsor ads: Pick your faction and step into battle.  Tactically place and orient your spaceships to score the most points by taking down enemy vehicles, collecting mineral units from asteroids, and impressing the game sponsors.

This is a real-time, tile laying game. The game begins with two tiles in the center and starting the timer.

Every round, each player places one spaceship anywhere on the battlefield while everybody else is doing the same! Aim at enemies and asteroids, while appealing to the sponsors and avoiding friendly fire. After 8 rounds, players stop and take a photo with the companion app.

The companion app will play the battle for you and calculate the scores.

Scores can also be calculated manually with the Downgrade Pack.

name: Bloodlines
description:
In Bloodlines, players take on the roles of influential families vying for power and territory in a richly detailed setting inspired by the historical dynamics of 10th-century Western Europe. Each family line, or dynasty, has unique attributes, strengths, and weaknesses that can influence their strategies throughout the game.

As the game unfolds over multiple turns—each representing approximately five to ten years—players will expand their influence through diplomacy, assassinations, alliances and marriages, and military campaigns.

Players can also invest in technological advancements, religious power and cultural influence or simply amass more wealth than opponents. These options may strengthen their position and give them an edge over their opponents. Special events, such as plagues, revolts, and natural disasters, may take place, adding unpredictability to the game and requiring players to adapt their strategies on the fly.

Victory is achieved by one of two conditions: controlling four nations or having the highest score at the time of reaching the pre-agreed number of turns. This culminates in a rich tapestry of storytelling, where players' decisions shape the course of their families’ legacies and the fate of nations.

In Bloodlines, players are encouraged to immerse themselves in the historical context and narrative, making each game experience unique as they craft their stories of ambition, betrayal, and power in a turbulent time. The interplay of strategy, chance, and player interaction creates a dynamic environment where every choice can alter the trajectory of dynasties and the world around them.

name: Living Forest Duel
publisher: Ludonaute; CMON Global Limited; GateOnGames; Maldito Games; Pegasus Spiele; 株式会社ケンビル (KenBill)
description:
Living Forest Duel or how to experience all the thrills of the award-winning Living Forest in a tense and tactical two-player showdown!

SUMMARY:
In Living Forest Duel, two players face off as the spirits of Summer and Winter, each striving to save the sacred forest and be recognized as its ultimate protector. Although their goals are similar, only one season will claim the honors.

Your goal? Be the first to achieve one of the four victory conditions:

     Plant a 3×3 rectangle of Guardian Tree cards in your Forest
     Have only cards of your season on the recruitment line
     Collect 8 Fire tokens
     Move the Onibi creature to your opponent's side once the Onibi card is in their possession.


The game is played in alternating turns. On each turn, choose one of the following options:

     Draw 1 guardian animal card from the shared draw pile and add it to the shared help line
     Use 1 action token on 1 guardian animal card in the shared help line


• Draw a guardian animal card
Draw a card from the shared draw pile and place it face up on one of the three help lines:

     the shared help line if it’s a neutral animal
     your help line if it’s an animal of your season
     your opponent’s help line if it’s an animal of their season


Each animal provides elements that you can use later with one of your two Action tokens.

Be careful: revealing too many solitary animals can be detrimental. After 3 solitary symbols, you lose an Action token, which will significantly reduce your ability to act.

• Use an action token
Place one of your Action tokens on a card to point to the last element corresponding to the action you want to perform. Count all elements of this type visible from the start of the common aid line OR from the last Action token pointing to this element.

Possible Actions:

     Recruiting one or more Guardian Animals
     Extinguishing the fire by collecting one or more Fire tokens
     Planting one or more protective trees
     Advancing Onibi toward your opponent


• End of the turn
The turn ends when both Summer and Winter have used up their 2 action tokens.

Add up the value of the fire tokens in the clearing: the value of each fire token is determined by its location. Then, add up your water values. Check to see whether the fire value in the clearing is strictly higher than your water value. If so, add a fire varan card corresponding to your season to the shared discard pile for each fire token present in the clearing.

Next, place a fire token on each of the cards on either side of the Onibi standee.

Retrieve your 2 action tokens back in front of you, and place all of the cards in the help line, as well as the cards in the players' personal lines on the shared discard pile.

———————

No prior knowledge of Living Forest is required to enjoy Living Forest Duel.

—description from the publisher

name: Bluffosaurus
description:
Bluffosaurus is a clever and fast-paced bluffing game where players compete to build the best sequence of dinosaurs—based not on what they see, but on what they think they know.
Each dinosaur card shows a charming prehistoric creature on the front and a set of numeric values on the back, representing stats like weight, speed, or lifespan. Players hold their cards so that only they can see the values; opponents can only see the image. Throughout the game, players place these dinos into a central row—left if they believe their dino’s value is lower than the others, right if it's higher—all without knowing any values except their own.
The twist? A scoring card defines the active category for the round, and only that stat matters. Can you accurately guess where your dino fits in the line-up? Or are you just hoping not to get called out?

After each dinosaur is played, the next player may choose to continue the sequence or challenge it. If a challenge is made, all dinosaurs in the row are revealed and checked for correct order. If the sequence is valid, the last player who played a dino earns the scoring card. If not, the challenger scores instead. Either way, the game continues with a new round and a new category until one player collects five scoring cards and claims victory.

Key Features:


     Unique combination of open images and hidden information
     Tense decision-making and psychological mind games
     Replayable with different stat combinations and bluffing dynamics
     Quick turns and constant engagement


Perfect for players who enjoy deduction, bluffing, and a little prehistoric mischief, Bluffosaurus is easy to learn, quick to play, and always surprising. Will your dino strategy stand the test of time, or will you get outbluffed?

—description from the publisher

name: Boaromia Festival
description:
Ever tried organizing a group photo at a festival? With six people, two dead phones, one who's at the loo, and someone who’s definitely not okay? That’s Boaromia Festival. A co-op board game where you and your friends try to survive the most gloriously chaotic festival ever created, without leaving your house, or needing a tetanus shot.

In Boaromia Festival, you’ll chase your favorite artists, dodge an old acquaintance, hit the food court like it’s a quest, forget to pee, and probably end up at the first aid because you forgot to eat. It’s messy, it’s loud, and just like a real festival, you’ll probably forget half of it but tell the stories forever. Your mission? Simple, in theory, hard in execution: Get the whole crew together at the right stage, at the right time, with enough joy in your souls to snap that iconic group photo.

The game is played in 12 rounds  At the start of each round, draw an event card and resolve it. Players take turns (in any order, plan together) and can move up to 6 steps, taking actions along the way or at your destination. At the end of a round: all players lower their energy by 1, move the line-up token forward. At round 7, night begins: replace day goals with night goals, from now on only draw night events.

Players win by snapping a group photo when all players are at the same stage while an artist is performing and everyone has an 8+ fun level.

—description from the publisher

name: Bog Hollow Brigade
description:
Bog Hollow Brigade is a whimsical, push-your-luck deck-building game set in the tangled woods of 1920s England. Players take on the roles of imaginative kids braving Traps, tricky terrain, and the curious Bogborn. Each turn is a gamble—press forward for greater rewards or retreat to regroup. Build your deck, time your tools, and earn glory through bold adventures and clever decisions.

—description from the publisher

name: Boktor
description:
Boktor is a cooperative adventure game for 1 to 6 players, blending dungeon-crawling, tactical combat, and character progression in a world where elemental chaos threatens to consume everything.
