Each game is a self-contained mission in which players take on the role of legendary heroes sent to explore a dynamically generated dungeon. Their goal: survive waves of enemies, gather powerful abilities, and confront the final Tyrant before the Vortex obliterates the land.

Highlights:

Fast setup and streamlined rules for quick access to the action.

Unique hero boards with energy and health tracking.

Modular dungeons with endless replayability.

Cooperative gameplay with evolving challenges and decisions.

Epic Boss fights that require real teamwork.

Every choice matters: will you rush toward the Tyrant to stop the Vortex, or take your time gathering strength at the risk of being too late?

Easy to learn, hard to master, Boktor is ideal for families and core gamers alike who seek tactical tension and epic moments in under 60 minutes.

—description from the publisher

name: Bolted!: The Game of Creative Necromancy
description:
Bolted! is a puzzle game where players race to assemble a bizarre creature -- or "make friends" -- by piecing together mismatched body part cards.

Players are "creature-crafters" apprenticing under the famous Doctor von Gravenstein. Each player builds one Friend by playing body part cards onto the creature they’re assembling in front of them.

In the Build phase, play as many part cards as you can onto any one limb of your Friend. New parts must connect to an existing part with the same socket color. In this way, you can create branching groups and chains of parts on your Friend. Part cards may also be scrapped (ground up into fuel) in order to power Tools, which give you advantages and allow you to build in different ways. Scrapped cards become resources you can hoard to power big moves and combos at crucial moments.

Following each Build phase, there is a Parade. Your creations in-progress are displayed to the Doctor's gallery of billionaire Patrons, each of whom have expressed a desire to see very particular patterns of parts on your Friends. Any Patron whose pattern you have matched will pay you in coins matching the number of parts you used in that pattern.  Having earned these points, players return to Build again, attempting to modify their Friend in order to satisfy additional patterns before the next Parade.

Every time a Patron pays a player, they leave the gallery and are replaced. After six Patrons have paid any player, all the Patrons will help activate the Doctor's giant electrical switch to bring the Friends to life! This triggers the final round of the game, after which all players compare their accumulated points.

The player with the most points has built the Best Friend, and wins the game. (The other players are recycled into new body parts to make more Friends.)

name: Bomb5
publisher: Matagot; ADC Blackfire Entertainment; Tranjis Games
description:
What’s more satisfying than triggering a fun chain reaction to outsmart your opponents?

Bomb5 is a clever and super accessible tile-laying game where you place numbered tiles and combine them to make a total of 5. Do that five times(you guessed it) and you win! Turns are quick and full of surprises, as explosive tiles can turn the play area upside down when you least expect it.

Each player starts with a hand of three numbered tiles (going from 1–4). On their turn, players place a tile orthogonally adjacent to another on the play area. If the sum of connected number tiles equals 5, a chain reaction is triggered: you place one of your cup tiles on one end of the line and flip the tile at the other end —whether it's a cup... or a bomb. Be the first to place 5 face-up cups to win!

Bomb tiles add a twist, with effects ranging from flipping a specific tile to disrupting entire rows or columns. With simple rules and a dynamic gameplay loop, Bomb5 strikes a fun balance between strategy and surprise.

—description from the publisher

name: Book Collectors
description:
In this game, you are all competitive, wealthy book collectors attempting to have the most notable personal library. Having the best combination of books, you will be able to accomplish this feat. Players want to get victory points before the other collectors. With specific book collections and goal cards, players will need a winning combination of books and goals to claim victory!

There are eight kinds of books in this game, along with game influencing action cards. Each book you can lay down is worth one victory point. Collecting certain books and sets of books will get you extra points. The players in this game draw from the deck, which has both action and book cards in it. You can play two cards on your turn. They can be two books you lay down, a book and an action card, or two action cards.

You lay down books in front of you to gather enough points to win. You can also trade books you have with other players. It may benefit them, but it could benefit you more so trade carefully. By collecting certain books, playing action cards, and effective trading, you will reach victory sooner than your rivals and win the game!

name: Magic Maze Pocket
publisher: Sit Down!; Ghenos Games; Meanbook Games; Pegasus Spiele; SYNKA Games
description:
After being stripped of all their possessions, a mage, a warrior, an elf, and a dwarf are forced to go rob the local Magic Maze shopping mall for all the equipment necessary for their next adventure. They agree to map out the labyrinth in its entirety first, then find each individual’s favorite store, and then locate the exit. In order to evade the surveillance of the guards who eyed their arrival suspiciously, all four will pull off their heists simultaneously, then dash to the exit. That's the plan anyway…but can they pull it off?

Magic Maze is a real-time, cooperative game. Each player can control any hero in order to make that hero perform a very specific action, to which the other players do not have access: Move north, explore a new area, ride an escalator… All this requires rigorous cooperation between the players in order to succeed at moving the heroes prudently. However, you are allowed to communicate only for short periods during the game; the rest of the time, you must play without giving any visual or audio cues to each other. If all of the heroes succeed in leaving the shopping mall in the limited time allotted for the game, each having stolen a very specific item, then everyone wins together.

At the start of the game, you have only three minutes in which to take actions. Hourglass spaces you encounter along the way give you more time. If the sand timer ever completely runs out, all players lose the game: Your loitering has aroused suspicion, and the mall security guards nab you!

—description from the publisher

name: Bordeaux
description:
You are a winemaker from Bordeaux making, aging, and selling your artisanal wines. You strive to create the highest quality and most prestigious wines in France.

Bordeaux is a condensed, paper-and-pencil version of the board game Fromage. This travel-sized game easily fits in a backpack and doesn't require a table, so it can be played anywhere: the backseat of a car, an airplane, the beach, or even while you stand in a long line at a game convention!

The game lasts 13 turns (years). Each year, assign workers    to Make Wine or Gather Resources, choosing a duration of 1, 2, or 3 years for each action. Longer duration means a more powerful action, but it will take longer for that worker to be ready again. At game-end, score points for your wine and resources.

—description from the publisher

name: Paws Up
description:
In the card game Paws Up, players are pet influencers who try to collect the most "paws" with their photos and stories.

Each player starts with five photo cards in hand, with each card having a small number of paws, which are the points in this game. Each turn, reveal three cards from the deck, then players simultaneously choose and reveal a card from their hand. Whoever reveals the most valuable card swaps it with one of the cards on display, then the player with the next highest card swaps for one of the three cards, etc.

Whenever you have the right combination of cards in hand — that is, three animals of the same type, worth the same amount of paws, or in the same environment — you can claim one of the trophies on display. The earlier you claim a particular trophy, the more valuable it's worth, and while the trophies diminish in value over time, the animals become more valuable as the cards are divided into three decks.

name: Recall
publisher: Alion – by Dr Ø; Frost Bite Games; Galakta; Ghenos Games; HIT Games; Maldito Games; Niza Gams; Pegasus Spiele
description:
Recall is a deep strategy game from the designers of Revive that focuses on engine building and exploration. Each player begins the game with one of fourteen unique tribes and one of eighteen unique gadgets, both of which will heavily influence your strategy and opportunities. Throughout the game, you will lead your tribe, explore the lands, and discover traces of ancient civilizations to learn from them. On your turn, you either:

• Use a keycard to activate an action box, or
• Recall to produce resources and regain your keycards.

When you use a keycard, you activate the abilities of the keycard itself and the effects of the chosen action box. The chosen combination of keycard and action box will therefore determine what you get to do on your turn: populate the lands, move your followers, explore new regions, and build workshops, vaults, or monuments. During the game, you will improve your tribe by acquiring new keycards, upgrading your action boxes, or collecting ability stones and relics.

An important part of the game is searching dig sites for traces of ancient civilizations. These sites unlock access to the abilities and gadgets of ancient tribes, in addition to providing important scoring opportunities.

Three times during the game, players must choose one of two paths, with the chosen path providing an immediate bonus, as well as boosting one of the endgame scoring categories.

By using the optional digital companion website, players can archive their tribes at the end of their game, thereby making their tribes discoverable as ancient civilizations in other players' games.

—description from the designer

name: Botany: Floral Dragons
description:
As the sun rises upon your garden, the dew glistening on your cherished blooms, you pause to reflect on the labour, patience, and affection required to transform it into something truly beautiful. Still, you sense that something remains wanting: that final, ineffable touch which might elevate the garden from merely lovely to utterly magnificent. Ah, yes. Of course! What it lacks are floral dragons! Those exquisite creatures, imbued with the very essence of the flowers you so dearly treasure, would lend your garden the liveliness and wonder it so clearly deserves. The world of Ghardinn positively teems with them, and yet, for reasons most puzzling, not a single one has seen fit to take up residence within the estate you have so carefully prepared. This, plainly, will not do! It is time to set matters right. Gather your expedition supplies, assemble a capable party, and venture forth upon a journey of adventure, discovery, and, most importantly, floral dragons. But beware, the wider world is rife with many perils. Outbreaks of pleurossa corruption spread with alarming persistence, and not every floral dragon greets outsiders with kindness. Nevertheless, you have never been one to shrink from danger where flowers are concerned, and you certainly will not begin now, not when floral dragons are involved!

In Botany: Floral Dragons you will assume the role of a botanist, travelling the world in search of fame, fortune, and the coveted honor of floral dragons residing in your garden. As you travel the globe to befriend floral dragons, you will need to manage your expedition funds, experience thrilling events, and acquire support for your journey. Each player begins the game with a set of randomized goals that they then use to plot their path to victory. When players set out from their estate, they have access only to the coins they can carry with them. They can use these coins to traverse the globe and gain crew members and items to improve their odds of surviving the unknown, enhance their abilities, and increase the efficiency with which they traverse the map. However, there is danger in spending too freely, and players must ensure they have enough wealth on hand to return to England with their specimens intact. Whenever you return to your estate, you will add new floral dragons and build new garden features to gain points. At the end of the game, the player with the most points (a combination of the most magnificent garden and the most dragons residing there) will be declared the winner!

name: Boxo Blox
description:
Boxo Blox is an all ages block stacking party game.  Be the first player to stack your blocks on the tower without them falling off. Take turns rolling dice, drawing challenge cards, and stacking blocks in ridiculous ways.

Players take turns rolling either 1 or 2 dice. Then matching the number that you roll, with the sum of your blocks. So if you roll a 6, you can stack your #6 block on the stacking base, or you can stack a #1 and a #5 block etc, it just has to equal your roll. If you don’t have the blocks to match your roll, you can’t go and the next player rolls. If you can go, before you stack, you must draw a challenge card and stack accordingly.

To win the game, be the first player to get rid of your blocks by stacking them. However, on your final turn, in order to win the game you have an extra challenge. You must draw 3 challenge cards and play them all together.

—description from the publisher

name: Rival Cities
publisher: Deep Print Games; 999 Games; DiceTree Games; Game Harbor; Ghenos Games; Gigamic; Lucrum Games; Maldito Games; Pegasus Spiele
description:
In the 16th century, the small fishing village of Altona was founded in Northern Germany, initially posing no threat to its long-established neighbor, Hamburg. However, as Altona rapidly grew, a fierce rivalry emerged between the two cities, each constantly trying to outdo the other.

In Rival Cities, you face off in an enthralling city duel. Outmaneuver your opponent to achieve an instant victory — but beware as either of you can pull this off in many ways. Only by combining foresight with the art of deflection will you lead your city to victory. The suspenseful back and forth between the players makes it a very confrontational gaming experience full of weighty decisions.

—description from the publisher

name: Breakers
description:
In this competitive trick-taking game, players battle against unique monsters that change the rules of play each round.

Each monsters’ special abilities can alter trump suits, trick conditions, and create unique win conditions. Keeping players on their toes. Each battle consists of 10 tricks — unless the monster's special ability dictates otherwise — forcing players to adapt on the fly. To win, players must be the first to defeat three monsters.

After defeating a monster, players gain access to its trophy, which they can use in later rounds to gain an edge in future battles. Those who don’t win a round aren’t left behind — they receive equipment to strengthen their chances in the next encounter. With constantly evolving gameplay, strategic use of monster abilities, and clever planning, no two games are ever the same.

-description from designer

name: Skybridge
publisher: Deep Print Games; Pegasus Spiele; White Goblin Games
description:
Dive into a fantastic world beyond imagination. A world that stretches along the inner walls of a colossal sphere, enclosed by a cosmos of stone. A hollow world known as Thraen. Home to noble Drakhes, and home to diverse factions whose ambitions and myths constantly collide with one another. But the most wondrous sight lies at the very center of this world — a verdant planet that fills the sky, ever present yet always out of reach. They call it Beeledhan’s Eye, a supposed paradise that promises a better future.
As life in Thraen grows ever more difficult, its factions form a fragile alliance and embark on a desperate endeavor: the construction of a bridge. A bridge between Thraen and Beeledhan’s Eye. A Skybridge.

In Skybridge You each lead your people through the ages of bridge building. Equipped with an individual ability, you have a clear goal: Once the construction is complete, you want to have accumulated more power than the others. With the help of an exciting card activation mechanism, you collect building materials for the bridge, increase your military might, and vie for the favor of the deities. Who will achieve victory for their people?

—description from the publisher

name: Bug Detectives: The Epipocalypse
description:
Bug Detectives: The Epipocalypse is a medical educational card game providing a more enjoyable and engaging way to learn infectious diseases.

In Bug Detectives, players draft a team of scientists to combat the rising tide of infectious disease. Players match scientists to infections from a shared play area to score points in a race against either each other (versus mode) or time (solo). Different scientists look for different disease traits and can be scored with multiple infections allowing for combination scoring. Game play is easy to learn and games are quick to play.

The solo campaign progresses in difficulty as you go. Satisfy enough mission requirements to obtain bonus scientists to help you along the way.

—description from the designer

name: Bug Fight
description:
Bug Fight is a 2-player lane-battler and deck-builder!

The lightweight, 80-card deck is packed with cute Bugs, tons of strategy, and plays in 30-45 minutes.

Gameplay:

     Each player starts with a base deck of Bugs, Area Cards are placed in lanes, and a Recruit Shop is set up with unique Bugs
     Each round, players place cards from their hand face down in each lane.
     Flip the cards and resolve their effects! When a player gets enough Bugs on an Area, they capture it.
     Recruit Bugs from Shop and win Areas until the Flag Area is captured.
     Count up your victory points! The player with the most wins.

name: Stupor Mundi
publisher: Quined Games; Emperor Penguin Games; HOT Games; Mosaico Jogos; Pegasus Spiele; Pixie Games; 数寄ゲームズ (Suki Games); Tesla Games
description:
Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor and King of Germany and Italy, was a man of extraordinary culture, energy, and ability. His contemporaries called him "stupor mundi" ("the wonder of the world"), and many historians consider him Europe's first modern ruler. The kingdom Frederick established in Sicily and southern Italy ran on an efficient bureaucracy similar to modern, centrally governed kingdoms.

As one of Frederick II's vassals in Stupor Mundi, you will summon allies from around the Mediterranean, build structures in your castle, and promote specialists to improve your kingdom. You may improve your chances by upgrading your castles: towers house additional allies, walls store more resources, and keeps aid in managing action cards. Through a clever card-selection mechanism, you will have to choose actions carefully, some of which will trigger edicts that affect Frederick's palace, and determine the rewards players may receive from their allies. Do you stay loyal to the Emperor, or do you support independent allies? Keep a close eye on what your opponents do and form alliances at the right time — or go your own way when things get too heated...

—description from the publisher

name: Bunny Kingdom Town
description:
Become the leader of one of the two most powerful families in the royal court as you compete to build a new city and nurture it to greatness. In doing so, you will be awarded prestigious "golden carrots", a sure way to outclass your rival.

In Bunny Kingdom Town, you purchase buildings that best suit your strategy and place them in the best locations to grow your districts and earn more golden carrots...unless, of course, you instead choose the exact location your opponent had their eye on in order to thwart their expansion plans.

The town's inhabitants will send you their requests, which will guide you in your construction choices and can bring you, yes, more golden carrots.

name: Burger Battle Shake Up
description:
In Burger Battle Shake Up, burgers aren’t just built—they’re under attack! Roll the dice to grab ingredients, steal from opponents, or blow their burgers to bits with the dreaded Burger Bomb. Strategy meets sabotage in this fast-paced food fight for ultimate burger glory.

Quick to learn, fast to play, and packed with laughs, this all ages game is perfect for family dinners, game nights with friends, or backyard cookouts. And thanks to its portable Shake Up Tube, you can take the chaos anywhere.

Ingredient Dice: Roll all 6 dice and match symbols.
 
     3 of a kind → grab that ingredient.
     5 of a kind → make it PERMANENT and safe from stealing.
     6 of a kind → PERMANENT + a free Battle Dice roll.


One of each ingredient → pick any ingredient from the Burger Bank.

Battle Dice: Trigger special effects to steal ingredients, destroy toppings, swap with opponents, or shield your burger. Roll six matching Ingredient Dice on your turn, and you earn a free Battle Dice roll!

Collect all six ingredients to complete your burger—but watch out! Regular tokens can be stolen or destroyed, so plan your rolls carefully. The first player to finish their burger wins—and earns the title of Burger Battle Shake Up Champion

—description from the publisher

name: Burgle Bros 3: Future Flip
description:
The Burgle Bros are back with a cyberpunk sheen! After a dynamite-induced mishap, the team is propelled to a future dominated by AI and oppressive corporations. The classic Burgle Bros crew will use their old tricks as well as newfound skills to infiltrate and take down these corporations from the inside.

In this upgraded version of the classic cooperative heist, the players must leverage disguises to evade security. They need to find program cards to disable the ICE guarding the safe. All the room tiles are now double sided for more dynamic and intelligent level layouts. Players must effectively manipulate the corporate workers to gain info and even frame them when things go bad.

name: Burma 1945
description:
Burma 1945 is a conflict simulation of the decisive campaign in Burma from November 1944 to May 1945. In this game, the Allies are on the offensive, trying to reconquer most of Burma from the Japanese before the onset of the monsoon season.

Each Game Turn represents about 15 days for 12 total turns. Each hex on the map represents 25 miles (some 40 kilometers). Units are armies, corps, divisions, brigades, regiments, and battalions. Air units represent transport and combat aircraft.

22x34 inch game map and a sheet of 228 9/16 inch counters

name: Burnout
description:
A promotion is on the line, but so is your sanity in Burnout, a chaotic strategic party game.

Burnout drops players into a familiar battlefield: the modern office. Over six relentless weeks, you’ll juggle Projects, navigate company politics, and sabotage or support your coworkers.

But the real challenge? Managing your Mental Health. Push too hard, and you risk burning out. The line between high performance and total collapse is paper-thin, just like in real life.

The player with the highest Reputation wins the promotion. But you’ll need to balance ambition, sabotage, chaos and strategy to make it through the grind.

—description from the designer

name: Thebai
publisher: Board&Dice; Intrafin Games; Maldito Games; Pegasus Spiele
description:
Dark times loom over the kingdom of Thebes. The blind, old king Oedipus left the throne in disgrace and asked Polynices and Eteocles, his own sons, to rule the city together. But power corrupts and ancient feuds call for new blood to be spilled. Soon, Polynices finds himself leading an army from the rival city of Argos against his own brother. The Theban nobles support Eteocles as he maintains precarious rule over Thebes. The young king calls for defenders to man the seven gates of the city, while the invaders’ seven champions lead the attack on the gates. Meanwhile, the famous citadel of Thebes, the Cadmea, lies in disarray. It is as if the Fates themselves have lined everything up against the current rulers of Thebes!

While the common folks prepare for war, the noble families whisper among themselves that the time for new leadership has come, and the time to rebuild the Cadmea is now!

In Thebai, players assume the role of influential leaders from noble families during the tumultuous late Bronze Age. Throughout the game, players are tasked with rebuilding the Cadmea, the citadel of Thebes, while restoring the city’s exports, praying to the gods of the city, and protecting the lives of the citizens as grand heroes spill each other’s blood outside the gates.

The game lasts 10 rounds, each divided into an Action phase and a Fate phase. During the Action phase, players use one Citizen die, and then move their Archon on the Cadmea. During the Fate phase, players may get additional scoring opportunities, depending on their accomplishments and for protecting the city gates. After final scoring the player with the most Victory Points is the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Byzantion: The Justinian Era
description:
Byzantion is a deeply thematic, highly detailed competitive miniature board game set in the shadowed halls of imperial power.

In Byzantion, you assume the role of one of the four great Demoi, powerful factions that influenced the fate of the Eastern Roman Empire during the reign of Autokrator Justinian. Across nine rounds, players face a series of nine randomized historical events (ensuring replayability), revealed at the start of the game, allowing for long-term strategic planning and political maneuvering.

At the beginning of each round, factions vie for influence over the Emperor’s decisions. Through a bidding system, players attempt to sway Justinian toward one of two possible responses to each crisis. Each decision reshapes the course of the Empire and history itself. Once a path is chosen, all factions must contribute to its execution. Success rewards the most committed faction; failure punishes the least. Your ability to anticipate, adapt, and manipulate will offer your Victory points and determine your legacy.  To meet the challenges ahead, you will recruit renowned personalities and specialists of the time from all kinds of trades. “Build your engine“ and secure the required resources to meet the challenges that history will unveil.

But this is the Byzantine court, where daggers are as sharp in the shadows as on the battlefield.

    Use diplomacy to align rival interests with your own.
    Employ espionage to outmaneuver your enemies with your intrigue cards.
    Strike alliances, break them, and strike again, at just the right moment.


At the game’s end, unveil the secret objectives you’ve fulfilled, adding their value to your accumulated Doxa (Victory Points). Only then will it be revealed which faction truly ruled from behind the veil, the unseen hand that shaped the Emperor’s will and steered the fate of Byzantion.

—description from the designer

name: Cabriole
description:
Cabriole is a medium-weight worker placement, card drafting, and resource management game for 2-4 players aged 14 and up. Playable in 60-90 minutes, the worker placement aspect is queue-based, with a simultaneously strategic and tactical resolution phase that might require players to adjust their plans.

The game is set in London during the late 18th century, with players aiming to create the most successful furniture studios by hiring and promoting craftsmen such as carvers, joiners, turners, and upholders; purchasing raw materials such as wood and silk for the best prices; and fulfilling customer orders for different types of furniture. Players will find themselves constantly balancing the need for capital with increasing their studio's prestige throughout the city.

The player who has scored the most prestige points at the end of six rounds is the winner.

name: Tricky Traders
description:
The stalls are set up, and the first customers are already admiring the extensive range of products on offer. But they have no idea what‘s going on behind the scenes! As two rivaling trade guilds, you compete for influence over the marketplace, trying to improve the reputation of your own stalls, while getting rid of the unwanted competition.

You and your opponent each have 2 goals: To support 1 market stall (the more fame, the better) and to ruin 1 market stall (the less fame, the better).

The game takes place over 3 market days, with each day split into Morning, Noon and Evening. At each time of day, you play 2 influence cards to influence customers, rats and characters. At the end of each market day, each market stall will gain fame depending on how many customers and rats are at the stall along with which characters are also present.

The player who best succeeds in both pursuing their own goals and thwarting those of their opponent will be victorious.

—description from the publisher

name: Under the Mango Tree
description:
In the card-drafting game Under the Mango Tree, you stand before a small slice of Australian wilderness that's entrusted to your care and brimming with potential. Heaps of litter mar the landscape, waiting to be cleared. A once-majestic mango tree yearns to bear fruit again, its branches aching for the playful chatter of animals in its shade.

Your mission is to breathe new life into this patch of nature. On each turn, you and your fellow players simultaneously select a card from your individual hands, then pass the rest to the next player. The twist: Each card you choose has two halves. You tuck one half under your board, removing it from the game, while the other remains visible to score points. This adds a layer of strategy as you must consider not only which halves to use for yourself, but also which to deny your opponents.

When all cards have been played, the player who has created the most vibrant and point-rich ecosystem around their mango tree wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Bloom Kingdom
publisher: Deep Print Games; Pegasus Spiele; Pulento; TLAMA games
description:
Flourishing times in the kingdom! With every card played, the kingdom’s display grows in power – but only your last two cards in hand will score at the end of the round.
Will you build up a character’s strength, or go for their victory points? And are the conditions met for a particularly lucrative scoring?

Bloom Kingdom is a clever card game with stunning artwork. On each turn, players simultaneously choose character cards from their hands and play them into a common display. Your goal is to manipulate the display in your favor and make certain character types more valuable than others. However, to make a character type more valuable, this usually means you have to add cards of that type to the display. But you also want to keep such cards as your final two in your hand, in order to score them at the end of the round.
This way, the display and the scoring potential grows over 3 rounds and whoever has the most points at the end of the third round wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Capital: 1929 – Wall Street
description:
In Capital: 1929 - Wall Street players find themselves in New York, only a few years before the onset of the Great Depression of 1929. Each player takes the role of executive characters, such as prominent personalities or ambitious entrepreneurs, who try to dominate over the U.S. Economy using the mechanisms of the game. The game unfolds over four Eras, each representing a historical period in America, starting with the Second Industrial Revolution, from the Gilded Age (around 1865) and heading through the Progressive Era and Roaring Twenties to the Great Depression (1929). Players must work to prevent the economic collapse, saving the U.S. economy and rewriting history. 
The game is played in four rounds which represent the four eras as listed above, and each round is divided into two main phases. In the Operation Phase, the characters try, through the mechanisms of worker placement, engine building, resource management and bidding to build factories and produce resources which will trade them at the market place or exchange them in order to get shares from industries listed on the Wall Street — all in pursuit of expanding their capital. In the Stock Market Phase, that capital can be invested in the volatile stock market to multiply fortunes… or risk ruin. 
Each round consists of four turns, during which the players place a worker and perform the related action. Additionally, they may, optionally, load cargo ships, fulfill contracts or repay loans. During the game, due to the economic crisis, all state-owned industries are getting privatized, through the thrilling auctions. 
The game is won by the one who accumulates the most wealth in CPs (Capital Points). However, if the Great Crash of 1929 occurs, everything changes: the rules of wealth are rewritten, and a new winner emerges from the New Deals.

—description from the designer

name: Caps & Stems: Mushrooms of the World
description:
In Caps & Stems: Mushrooms of the World, players compete to earn the most Reputation points by playing cards to add mushrooms on the map. Caps & Stems: Mushrooms of the World has nearly 150 different mushroom species in the base game based on the traits of real mushrooms.

Players play cards representing a variety of fungi, stacking them according to similar traits, to score points and gain spores. Spend spores to acquire the traits you need to assemble your mushroom (delicious, poisonous, smelly, ringed, pored, etc.) then grow them onto a shared map - scoring points based on the traits of neighboring mushrooms. Earn expertise in a particular trait to unlock special powers and collect secret bonus cards give additional points.

—description from the designer

name: Clash of Clans: The Epic Raid
publisher: Maestro Media; ADC Blackfire Entertainment; Cranio Creations; Pegasus Spiele
description:
Inspired by the hit mobile game Clash of Clans, the board game Clash of Clans: The Epic Raid allows players to build defenses, deploy units, and raid friends' bases in a fast-paced, highly strategic battle that brings the thrill of the mobile game to the tabletop. Build up your village, unleash your troops, and smash your rivals in a  race for dominance! No base is safe. No clan goes unchallenged. Let the raids begin!

Raiding is the goal of this combat, engine-building game. Send your armies, roll the dice, and watch their cities burn. Destroying your opponents structures earns you points, resources, and bonuses.

The end of the game is triggered when at least 1 player has 40 or more stars.  The player with the most victory stars (points), wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Capybaras vs Pelicans
description:
Capybaras vs Pelicans is a lighthearted card game in which players guide cheeky capybaras safely to a hot spring while avoiding other players' pesky pelicans.

Players can play capybaras from their hand or use a pelican to claim one from an opponent. But beware - until the capybaras make it to a hot spring, other players can steal capybaras back. Once all cards have been played, the player with the most capybaras safely at a hot spring wins the game.

Strategic use of pelicans and timely hot springs can make the difference between victory and defeat. With a simple setup and fast-paced play, the game is suitable for a wide range of players.

—description from the publisher

name: Care Bears: Unlock the Magic – Deckbuilding Game
description:
Care Bears: Unlock The Magic is a strategy based game for adults, but easy to play for less experienced players or children. With this easy to learn, fun and positive deckbuilding game, adult gamers can share their passion with their kids and families! This is the very first deckbuilding game for the Care Bears franchise.

Players will draft cards and work cooperatively to use Care Energy to remove bad guys and other obstacles from the Adventure Track. When a Boss's Caring Meter reaches zero, they are removed from the board and placed into the Score Pile of the Player who overcame the Boss.

Players share a Caring Meter that is tracked by a token moving along the players collective Caring Meter. Each time a Player is instructed to “move a color on the Caring Meter" they must move the Caring Meter down a color. When the Caring Meter has run out of colors, the Players lose the game.

To win the game, players must defeat the Bad Crowd and overcome all of the objectives that will appear throughout the game as you play, as well as the final Boss, Bluster.  Once you have defeated Bluster, the game is complete and you are victorious!

—description from the publisher

name: Carl Linné
description:
Carl Linné is a strategic board game set in the early 18th century, where players take on the roles of natural historians inspired by the work of Carl Linnaeus and his contemporaries. Through exploring distant regions, collecting and researching specimens, cultivating botanical gardens, corresponding with scientific institutions, and publishing influential books, players gradually build knowledge and reputation. By carefully managing actions through a unique lens system and balancing fieldwork with scholarly study, players compete to contribute most to the emerging system of taxonomy and leave a lasting mark on the history of natural science.

—description from the publisher

name: Carnuta
publisher: Repos Production; Gém Klub Kft.; MTS Games; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
Welcome to the annual ceremony that brings together druids from distant lands! Eight secret ingredients have been selected, and your task in Carnuta is to combine them carefully and assemble your runes to create an exceptional potion.

To your billhooks, set, go!

A game of Carnuta plays over a series of turns. On your turn, you will take 2 actions, the same or different, out of the 4 possible. The goal of the game is to create a potion by playing cards in front of you. Each card is worth points depending on the ingredients in your potion. The game ends once one player plays an 11th card in front of them.

Optimize the combinations of your ingredients to gain the highest score
and win the game!

name: Munchkin: Vox Machina – A Critical Role Game
description:
Based on the first campaign of the award-winning livestream TTRPG show Critical Role, Munchkin: Vox Machina is packed with the most infamous villains, memorable NPCs, and legendary treasures that filled that campaign's many adventures.

Dive into your own episode of Critical Role, battle against foes like Delilah Briarwood and Thordak, wield items like Fenthrasand the Titanstone Knuckles, and reach Level 10!

name: Cassette Zombies!
description:
A big game packed in a small cassette tape case for the bloodiest zombie experience you can have. Take the role of one of the survivors and try to stop the zombie hordes marching toward the last human town!

Cassette Zombies is a simple, tactical game of survival terror. Face down brutal, brain-hungry zombies and complete unique missions. Are you brave enough to survive the most metal and brutal zombie apocalypse?

Easy but compelling game system for multiple tactical challenges. each character has different abilities and each mission has different difficulty levels for more replayability.

Can be played as a solo or cooperative experience - win or fail together!

—description from publisher

name: Castelnuovo 1539: Come whenever you dare!
description:
Come whenever you want! ¡Venid cuando queráis!

On August 7, 1539 the last resistance of the Spanish garrison of the Albanian village of Castelnuovo (Novi for the Turks) ceased. After 22 days of open trench and more than a month of combats, skirmishes, assaults and bombardments, the last Spanish defenders fulfilled the destiny they promised themselves when they rejected the offers of surrender that, according to the rules of war, Jareidin Barbarossa, admiral of the Ottoman fleet and general in chief of the operation, had made to them. 
The city and its fortifications, rather meager and outdated, had been taken by the forces of the Holy League in October 1538, so as not to close the campaign with the bad taste of the naval defeat at Preveza. Fourteen companies of Spanish infantry under the command of D. Francisco Sarmiento de Mendoza y Manuel, some 3,500 soldiers, were garrisoned there for the winter. 
The following summer brought a tide of 54,000 Turks and a fleet of 200 sails before its walls. After Venice's defection from the League, there was no possibility of naval relief and the Spanish command authorized capitulation, however Sarmiento and his men decided to respond to Barbarossa's offer with the phrase “Come whenever you want”, which sealed their fate. 
In this game two sides face each other in a desperate battle: the town and its fortifications will eventually yield to Turkish power, but the question is, at what cost?

In Castelnuovo we will manage our army with wooden pieces in vertical with sticker, where we will not be able to see the type of unit of the opponent. The board is divided into areas and we will have other types of units such as cannon batteries, walls, bastions, trenches, etc. The confrontations will be made by rolling 6-sided dice and a deck of cards for each side, allowing us to play them to give orders, improve the fighting, dig trenches and special events.

(Español)
El 7 de agosto de 1539 cesaba la última resistencia de la guarnición española de la villa albanesa de Castelnuovo (Novi para los turcos). Tras 22 días de trinchera abierta y más de un mes de combates, escaramuzas, asaltos y bombardeos, los últimos defensores españoles cumplieron el destino que se prometieron cuando rechazaron las ofertas de rendición que, conforme a las reglas de la guerra, les había hecho Jareidin Barbarroja, almirante de la flota otomana y general en jefe de la operación. 
La ciudad y sus fortificaciones, más bien exiguas y anticuadas, habían sido tomadas por las fuerzas de la Liga Santa en octubre de 1538, para no cerrar la campaña con el mal sabor de la derrota naval en Preveza. 14 compañías de infantería española al mando de D. Francisco Sarmiento de Mendoza y Manuel, unos 3.500 soldados, quedaron guarnecidas en ella para pasar el invierno. 
El verano siguiente trajo una marea de 54.000 turcos y una flota de 200 velas ante sus muros. Tras la defección de Venecia de la Liga, no había posibilidad de socorro naval y el mando español autorizó la capitulación, no obstante Sarmiento y sus hombres decidieron responder a la oferta de Barbarroja con la frase “Venid cuando queráis”, que selló su destino. 
En este juego dos bandos se enfrentan en una batalla desesperada: la villa y sus fortificaciones acabarán cediendo ante el poder turco, pero la cuestión es ¿a qué coste?
El bando otomano debe hacerse con el control de los puntos neurálgicos de la fortaleza o eliminar todas las fuerzas españolas. El jugador español deberá asegurarse de que pague un precio muy alto por su victoria… No hay otra salida.

En Castelnuovo gestionaremos nuestro ejército con piezas de madera en vertical con pegatina, donde no podremos ver el tipo de unidad del contrario. El tablero está dividido en áreas y tendremos otro tipo de unidades de baterías de cañones, murallas, bastiones, trincheras, etc. Los enfrentamientos se harán mediante tirada de dados de 6 caras y un mazo de cartas para cada bando, nos permitirán jugarlas para dar órdenes, mejorar los combates, cavar trincheras y eventos especiales.

name: Castle Nightingale
description:
Castle Nightingale looms out of the night, both intimidating and full of promise. Three ninjas have slipped inside, searching for the fabled treasure hidden within...yet a vigilant samurai patrols the halls, watching and listening for intruders.

Two players face off in Castle Nightingale, with the ninja player trying to steal five relics before the samurai player can capture the three ninja thieves. The castle is comprised of an inaccessible garden surrounded by four double-sided floor boards, each showing two secret passage spaces and areas in five colors.

Each turn, the ninja and samurai each choose one of three action cards in hand, with the samurai also choosing a nightingale tile not used on the previous turn. The ninja player resolves their action, then moves across the floor, marking each space of their movement with a footstep token. If they step on a colored space matching the samurai's hidden nightingale tile, the ninja stands revealed; otherwise, next turn the ninja can treat any of their footsteps as their starting space.

If the ninja picks up a vase, the samurai can still recover it on their turn by either closing the final secret passage or landing on the ninja's space...as long as the ninja has been revealed that turn. While the ninja moves space to space, the samurai treats each colored area as a single space, allowing them to move quickly within the castle.

Each player has specialized one-shot equipment they can use at any time, starting with one item and gaining more as they play certain cards. Each player has ten cards that they'll cycle through until either the samurai has captured all three ninja or the ninja have stolen five of the six relics hidden in the eight vases.

name: Casus Belli
description:
Casus Belli is a game of exploration, settlement, and warfare in space.

Over a thousand years ago, humanity spread to the stars, creating a massive empire. This empire grew too big and split into four main factions, a period now known as the 'Great Split', which then led to a time of war. Conflict led to an era of darkness for humanity. Now after many years, the four faction have started to expand again. How they act is determined by by their prevailing ideology, who knows if this will lead to a new war.

Each faction will explore and colonize the systems in the region. In doing so, they will come across ancient alien technologies. However, some of these technologies will lead to corruption. The game starts in a period of peace. Some actions may lead to an increase in tension, which in turn may lead to war. While peace reigns, factions cannot fight each other...unless they have a casus belli. Once war breaks out, the factions will divide into alliances and major battles can occur.

The game plays over seven to nine rounds, and at game's end, each faction scores differently for assets they have on the board.

—description from the publisher

name: Next Station: Berlin
description:
In Next Station: Berlin, you are competing to design the most efficient metro network in the German capital. Over four rounds, each player draws colored metro lines on their own map, starting from two designated departure stations on opposite sides of the city. As Station cards are revealed, everyone simultaneously extends their current line to matching symbols, carefully following the printed connections and strict building rules—no crossing tracks, no loops, and no retracing your path.

Each round introduces a new color, gradually layering your network across Berlin’s districts. Special cards allow you to create railway switches or mark key hubs as National Train Stations, opening up new tactical possibilities. Across the game, you will aim to link your two starting stations, spread through multiple districts, and create valuable interchange stations where different colored lines meet.

After four rounds, players total their points from completed lines and interchanges. The player with the highest score is declared Berlin’s best metro planner.

—description from the publisher

name: Cat Saga: Tangled Tails
description:
Cat Saga is a cooperative, story-driven adventure game. Explore the world together and make decisions that impact your unique saga.

Story
Looking back, adventure has called you since you were just a kitten. Now, setting off on a journey that's beyond your wildest dreams, you are faced with an important question: Are you prepared to embrace an epic saga and forge your very own heroic tale?

Overview
Cat Saga is a cooperative, story-driven game, where you explore the world together over the course of five Sagas. As a team you will make decisions that impact the story, engage in combat and use your abilities to overcome danger. You will create a wonderful Saga together, try epic actions, get in fights, find valueble items, and level up!

Objective
You win together if you manage to reach the end of the final Saga. You lose together if one Catventurer reaches zero health.

Gameplay
Start reading the Saga together, out loud. Your decisions and accomplishments will lead you to certain Saga Numbers. All players will follow the Saga together and a decision or accomplishment counts for the entire group.

—description from the designer

name: Cat Spotting
description:
Cat Spotting is a fun and fast series of games where the objective is simple: be the first player to spot the hidden cat in the crowd! These games are best played with 2 players, but can be enjoyed with more.

Race to spot cats the fastest or work together to find them all!

There are 4 sets of Crowd Cards, 120 unique, hand-drawn Cat Cards and 7 ways to play.

Each game requires a set of Crowd Cards and some Cat Cards, depending on the game.
 A cat will ONLY be on 1 of the 3 Crowd Cards.

They will look exactly as pictured on the Cat Card, although part of it may be hidden behind other cats.

Have fun Spotting Cats!

—description from the designer

name: Cat Trick
description:
Kittens are obsessed with their toys! They're on a mission to collect as many different ones as possible. But watch out: if players get too greedy and keep collecting the same toy over and over, they'll crash—and the others will pounce on their toys. Who has the cunning of a cat and knows when to hold back?


     Play any card—no need to follow suit.
     Play the highest card or a trump to win the trick.
     Collect 5 different colors—but don’t take more than 4 of any one!


—description from the publisher

name: Catacombs Alpha
description:
Catacombs Alpha is a cooperative dungeon crawler where a party of up to 3 heroes work together against a "dungeon master / DM" player. The DM controls the various monsters the heroes encounter.

To resolve combat, players flick wooden discs representing their heroes across the game board. Ranged shots such as missiles and fireballs are represented by separate discs of various sizes. The heroes must fight through a series of monster-filled rooms to reach and defeat the final boss - a Catacomb Lord.

Catacombs Alpha features a streamlined rule set and introduces all new heroes, monsters, items, and Catacomb Lords. The game remains fully compatible with all existing Catacombs Third Edition expansions.

—description from the designer

name: Catacombs: Fortress of Nazemoor
description:
Catacombs: Fortress of Nazemoor is a core, standalone dungeon crawler that uses the same rules and Dexterity Game System as Catacombs Third Edition (3E). As a result this game both re-implements and expands Catacombs 3E. All Catacombs 3E expansions are compatible with Fortress.

In the Catacombs related games, players must skilfully flick wooden discs that represent one of the characters under their control. Usually this is a hero or a monster, if playing as the Dungeon Master or "Overseer". Flicking a disc represents a "shot". The basic shots are rush (for moving) and melee (for both moving and attacking). When performing a ranged shot, a separate disc is used instead of a hero or monster's disc. Ranged shots include fireballs, ice boulders, missiles and hook shots. Some shots inflict damage while others enable special effects. When all of the monsters in a room have been cleared, the heroes can advance further up the fortress.

New features: Crates (treasure chests) that contain both rewards and traps appear on runes during the Battle Phase. Assistants can be rescued that will help the heroes in their quest through the Fortress. Items may be purchased during the Battle Phase.

—description from the publisher

name: Wine & Cheese
publisher: Deep Print Games; Pegasus Spiele; 999 Games; Albi
description:
In the heart of beautiful Burgundy, you and your opponent run traditional farms that produce both wine and cheese. You’ll gather ingredients using an innovative paired-worker system, and carefully time the production, aging, and sale of your goods. Balance is key, as you’ll have to earn from both wine and cheese equally to claim victory.
Wine & Cheese is a deep, strategic game for two connoisseurs that will captivate you with its unique blend of worker placement and card management.

—description from the publisher

name: Catch 33
description:
Catch 33 is a dice based, flicking dexterity game using a ramp and two dice. It's typically 2 player head-to-head but can be played in teams.

Slide the first of your dice up the ramp to try and make it land in the cup. If you get the first shot in the cup, try to get the second one in, to add to your score. If both make it in the cup, add them together for your score and also set out a "defender post" on one of the four dots on the playfield. If your opponent knocks your post over on their turn, you get three points and get to reset it. If you accidently knock your own post over, it simply comes off the board. Getting four posts on the court is an instant win.

If your first die lands in the cup, and your second die lands outside the cup, but they land on the same numbers (two 1's,2s or 3s), you can chance it. Take the die outside the cup and shoot it again for more points... beware though, if you miss the "chance shot", then you score 0 points, thereby losing the points in the cup.

Scoring with double 1's ( snake eyes) scores 2 points, but also limits your opponent to one shot on their next turn (so the opponent's scoring opportunity is limited to one die, only if it lands in the cup, and no chance for a defender post).

name: Cats & Dragons
description:
In Cats & Dragons, players are cats leading their armies against hordes of dragons that infest their land. But these cats are devious and always out for themselves as well, scheming to take the glory and the spoils of every battle. Armies are deployed stealthily, hiding their strength from the other cat leaders. Will this lead to glory and victory, or will all this deviousness hand the victory to the invading dragons?

On each player's turn, they add a new tile to the landscape and possibly deploy new army units to this tile with their strength hidden from the other players. They may even hire the big wild cats to help them win the battle and best their peers. When a region closes, all army units are revealed, and players see whether they have defeated the dragons. If they did, the strongest armies get the most spoils, and all players earn glory. Spoils and glory are the path to victory over the other players.

Player choices in Cats & Dragons are relatively simple, but the board becomes very dynamic. Will you try to jump into a battle underway to earn spoils and glory? Or will you work hard to dominate a battle you know you can win and best all your rivals? The combination of blind bidding for area control and tile placement means that your interaction with the other players — as well as the dragons coming onto the board — will determine your fate.

-description from writer

name: Bamboo Smash
description:
In Bamboo Smash, players step into a chaotic and humorous battle where mighty pandas, called Pandemons, clash to prove who will dominate the bamboo forest. The game mixes lighthearted fun with tactical choices, offering a blend of speed, combos, and unpredictable twists. Its theme leans on frenetic action, with players smashing bamboo and unleashing the powers of their Pandemons.

Gameplay revolves around collecting Bamboo cards—divided into Tops, Trunks, and Roots—which can be combined to summon Pandemons with unique abilities. Players also use Action cards to boost their strategies, disrupt opponents, or unleash unexpected effects, adding to the chaotic rhythm of play. The iconic mechanic is the Smash, a disruptive attack that shakes the game balance and keeps tension high until the end.

The goal is straightforward but tense: be the first to summon two Pandemons. Every turn forces you to decide whether to build toward your Pandemon, mess with opponents, or survive the chaos caused by Smashes and Action cards. Timing is crucial—knowing when to push for victory or hold back can mean the difference between triumph and defeat.

Fast-paced, interactive, and packed with hilarious moments, Bamboo Smash is designed for players who love competitive card games full of clever combos, unexpected reversals, and constant table talk.

—description from the publisher

name: Pyramido: Forgotten Treasures
publisher: Synapses Games; Elznir Games; Pendragon Game Studio; White Goblin Games
description:
Deep within the heart of a lush and mysterious jungle lies proof of a vanished tribe’s existence: the emerald canopy of Pyramido. Tales speak of majestic pyramids concealed beneath dense vegetation, each cradling precious gems of unimaginable worth. You’ll embark on a daring quest to unveil these wonders.

Pyramido: Forgotten Treasures is a standalone game where you become an intrepid explorer venturing into hidden ruins with one precise goal: collect the largest fortune possible!

During their adventure, each player uses Dominoes to explore their own Pyramid. As a tile placement game, players take turns choosing a Domino and an available Gem from the corresponding space. To maximize their points, players must create areas with colored gem icons while placing their Dominoes and use Gems of the matching color to activate these as scoring areas. Each choice of Domino and its positioning has a significant impact since the previous stages influence the score throughout the game. A game is played over 4 stages and each stage is scored once completed.

Whoever earns the most points wins the game and the title of Great Explorer.

name: Catvale
description:
After another harsh winter in Catvale, 2 to 6 players take control of ambitious cats who emerge from their homes ready to race for dominance over the land. What might appear to humans as a simple valley is an epic realm to the cats, filled with enchanted forests, perilous foes, and countless adventures offering opportunities to gain luxury and prestige. The goal? Become the most feared, worshipped, or envied ruler of Catvale - how you get there is entirely up to you.

The game unfolds on a dynamic, tile-based map that creates a unique, ever-changing environment, ensuring no two games are ever the same. A fresh take on the adventure genre, Catvale blends exploration, resource management, and tactical decision-making. Players can choose from different playstyles—eco-focused, brawler, builder, adventurer, or a hybrid approach. Action dice, rolled at the start of each round, determine the strength of the actions players can take, adding an element of strategy and unpredictability. As the game progresses, players can level up their cat once, improving their base stats.

Each player shapes their cat’s path: will you be the aggressor, stealing prestige and robbing opponents of their dignity? Or perhaps you’ll focus on foraging and construction, fancying up your backyard with luxurious structures? Live off adventure by completing quests, fulfilling ambitions, and dueling for glory, or dominate the market through cunning auctions and hiring the best workers? With multiple paths to victory and high replayability, Catvale offers a delightful mix of strategy, luck, and creativity, where the future of the land rests in the paws of the most cunning and ambitious cat.

—description from the designer

name: Cauldron Call
description:
A mysterious force sweeps you into a kingdom on the brink of collapse. The king urgently begs for help, and the Undead Legion roam the streets — only magical cuisine can soothe their restless spirits. You and your companions step forward as the kingdom’s Magic Chefs: craft powerful enchanted dishes and present them to calm the Undead Legion’s spirits. Bring peace back to the kingdom.

Cauldron Call is cooperative board game. The game unfolds over a limited number of rounds; players must work together to complete a series of food orders before the finale. The true source of the chaos is a motorized, sensor-equipped autonomous cauldron! It darts around the kitchen — sometimes helping, sometimes hindering, disrupting your plans. Work swiftly with friends to complete each order within 15 rounds.

Each game begins with a DIY kitchen layout: assemble modular map tiles into a unique kitchen and place furniture, ingredients, and plates. Players use their special abilities to clash around the kitchen — chopping, cooking, plating, and serving. Event cards and the cauldron’s movement constantly reshape the situation, keeping every session fresh. Beyond the main quest, embark on optional adventures to solve deeper mysteries and discover the world’s true nature.

Finish 6 Orders within 15 turns to win.

—description from the publisher

name: CENTCOM: Persian Gulf War 2001-2003
description:
CENTCOM is an operational one-player simulation of US-CENTCOM military operations in Afghanistan and Iraq during 2001 to 2003 and optionally 2005. The player controls the forces of the CENTCOM (US, NATO, Northern Alliance, and other Allies). The game system controls the opposing OPFOR forces (Al Qaeda, Taliban, and Iraqi). The objective of the game is for CENTCOM to destroy both the forces of Al Qaeda and Saddam Hussein thereby establishing the basis for a stable Persian Gulf.

The standard scenario covers the period of October 2001 (the initial US invasion of Afghanistan) to June 2003 (the anticipated conclusion of Operation Iraqi Freedom). The optional scenario extends the game to early 2005. The player mobilizes forces and conducts operations by expending Expeditionary Warfare Points (EP). When a rule calls for the OPFOR to take an action, you the player must execute that action.

OPFOR actions can be affected by the Persian Gulf Instability Index (PGII), which can shift throughout the game and generate events. CENTCOM can also be played by two or more players, controlling different parts of CENTCOM operations. This is explained in the Optional rules.

Each game turn represents from three weeks of intense combat to six months of logistical buildup and counterinsurgency operations. Each hex represents 43 miles (69.2 km). Units range in size from brigade groups, divisions, and corps.

name: Champions of Rokugan
description:
Champions of Rokugan is a cooperative board game with miniatures for 1 to 5 players set in the fabulous world of the Legend of the Five Rings. These Rings, representing the 5 elements of this universe (Fire, Air, Void, Water and Earth) will serve your characters both in their actions and to trigger special abilities.

Each player will embody a Champion of the major Clans (or a Ronin) of the Emerald Empire, vying for the Emperor’s favor. Samurai, Master of the Elements, Courtier or Ninja, their talents will be put to the test in these tormented times, where danger lurks everywhere: from corrupt beings coming from the Outworld to the enemy within and the many factions ready to overthrow the Empire.

The Empire’s path to Honor and Glory is demanding, and there are many dilemmas and pitfalls to keep you from it.

Succeed in honorably facing the dangers that stand in your way, or fail collectively. But … remember that saving the empire doesn’t exempt you from your duties to your clan, and that one man’s glory is another man’s disgrace…

—description from the publisher

name: The Eternaut
description:
A deadly snowfall is killing everyone it touches, but not everyone has fallen victim to this mysterious threat. Four people have survived in a workshop, and now they're venturing into the world at the start of a survival adventure in which they must face menaces far more dangerous than the deadly snowflakes.

The Eternaut is a story-driven co-operative survival board game for 1-5 players set in Buenos Aires that uses simple game mechanisms to create a survival experience with strong narrative elements. You must build a team, gather items, fight enemies, resolve objectives, and decide how to proceed with your unique story.

Most of the entities in the game are marked with an Identification Number (called ID). When you want to instruct one of your Characters to interact with another entity (with another ID), you must play the correct Action card and read the matching paragraph, numbered with the combination of the 2 IDs. example: The player wants Simon to scavenge a metal cabinet, so they assign him a Rummage card. This action lets Simon (904) interact with the cabinet (124):  the player must read the Paragraph 124-904 in the Storybook to discover the result of the interaction. Each Scenario has a dedicated Storybook, so the same interaction between two entities is completely different in distinct scenarios.

name: Chaos: The Card Game
description:
Chaos: The Card Game is a whirlwind of madness, strategy, and pure chaos. In a world ruled by a divine Cat, four absurd factions battle for glory and the ultimate prize: the Forbidden Fruit. Psycho Elves, Alluring Sirens, Bureaucratic Demons, and Thirsty Vampires clash in a ridiculous, glorious war where nothing is sacred and mercy simply does not exist. Victory demands cunning, timing, and a knack for embracing the chaos. Winning the side rows allows you to unleash the central card’s Chaos Value, creating moments of shocking reversals and brilliant strategy. Claim the Forbidden Fruit, taste it, and the first to fully enjoy it becomes the undisputed King of Chaos.

Chaos: The Card Game is mainly about a crazy army of absurd creatures fighting over the Forbidden Fruit, which grants unlimited power. Each character has a Power value), some a Chaos value, and a special ability or description. Each round consists of 5 phases: Deployment, Reveal, Battle, Resolution, and Recruitment.

Each player picks a faction, draws five cards, and sets three face-down in their line-up across three rows. Then the chaos begins: reveal cards one by one, triggering unpredictable effects and hilarious combos that can completely turn the tide. When all cards are revealed, the “Battle Phase” erupts, fists fly, creatures clash, and the highest values win unless the card’s hidden Chaos Value flips the script. At the end of every round, players "recruit" new cards.  If a player has less than 3 cards at this point, the game ends and the player with the fruit begins.

—description from the publisher

name: Charuma
description:
Charuma is a trick-taking game with a fast bidding phase and a partially closed hand. The card game has only two suit colours (blue and red). The cards are numbered from 1 (Ace) to 10, and there are two copies of each card.
In a game of Charuma, each player has two cards in their hand, which they do not show to the other players. The rest of their hand is placed on the table in front of them, face up.

At the start of each round, you must use your victory points to buy these visible cards in a quick bidding phase based on the cards you have in your hand, your position in the turn order, and the other cards you see on the table. It is up to you to decide which hand is best for you and how much you are willing to pay to get it.
Once the auction is over, the game phase begins. The first player starts the first trick by playing 1 or 2 cards. If you play 2 cards, you must play a pair (two-coloured or single-coloured), i.e. 2 cards of the same value.
Charuma offers some fairly simple tricks to disrupt the natural value of the cards and ensure that it is not always the 10 that wins the trick:
- If two identical cards are in a trick, the second card played is stronger than the first. This will occasionally prompt you to lose the hand to reverse the cards' value.
- If you have the suit requested visible in your hand, you must play it. If you do not have the requested suit visible in your hand, or if you have it but it is hidden, you are not obliged to play it. You must discard the number of cards requested, but you cannot win the trick.
- If an ace and a 10 of the same suit are in the same trick, then the ace is not worth 1, but, in this case and only in this case, it beats the 10.
If you open a trick with a pair of cards (e.g. two suits), you force your opponents to play pairs (in this case, two suits). The three rules above apply.
If a player does not have a two-colour pair, they discard two cards without any colour restrictions but cannot win the trick.A pair 2 reds cards can therefore beat a nine and a ten.
Each trick earns you 1 point, or 2 points if it is an open trick with a pair (2 cards per player). Each Ace earns you a bonus of 1 point, and the last trick earns you another bonus of 2 points. 
Charuma thus encourages you to take risks with the cards you keep for the end of the round. There are quite a few points to be earned, but you don't know whether to keep blue, red, or a specific combination.
All this means that each bidding phase requires you to make choices and manage your victory points throughout the game.
Charuma is a trick-taking game that involves analysis, control, and a degree of risk-taking. It's up to you to find or place the cursor between these different factors.

—description from the publisher

name: Cherry on Top
description:
In Cherry on Top, you try to place your cards as cleverly as possible in the common display to form larger groups than the players before you. Whoever does this best and discards their own cards first wins!

Gameplay:
On your turn you can (a) place cards or (b) pass.
(a): Place any number of cards from your hand face up in the center of the table. This creates the common display. Follow these rules:

     All cards played during your turn must show the same color or the same fruit.
     You must place all cards played during your turn horizontally or vertically next to cards already in the common display, or you may cover cards already in the display.
     The cards played during your turn always form the basis of a group. A group consists of cards placed horizontally or vertically directly next to each other that show either the same color or the same fruit.
     You may include cards already in the display to form your group! Note: This means you don't necessarily have to play more cards than the last person!
     The group you form in the common display must always be at least one card larger than the group of the last person to play cards.


End of the round:
If everyone else passes after the last person to place a group, the round ends.
The last person to place a group begins a new round by forming a new group with the action (a) place cards.
The common display is not removed at the end of the round! It always remains for the next round.

End of the game:
The game ends immediately when someone places their last card into the common display. That person wins.

name: Last Aurora: Firelands
description:
In Last Aurora: Firelands, a standalone expansion of Last Aurora, players are again thrust into the harsh, frozen world of the original game. This time, however, the action moves to a new, scorching region: a desolate desert where an atmospheric processor holds back the clouds, allowing the sun to bake the surface into a post-apocalyptic wasteland.

At the heart of this wasteland lies the Citadel, a massive, fortified city. The atmospheric processor within the Citadel demands immense energy to operate. Unfortunately, various survivor factions and marauding raiders frequently sabotage the massive power cables running through the desert, disrupting the flow of electricity. With the threat of a catastrophic blackout, the players must guide their group of survivors through the wasteland to reach the Citadel before the processor fails and an enormous electrostatic storm engulfs the land.

In this new chapter, players will embody asymmetric teams, each with unique abilities, along with a brand-new resource system. Strategic decisions and tactical combat are key, as players must gather resources, fend off enemies, and navigate the dangerous desert terrain while racing against the impending storm. Last Aurora: Firelands introduces exciting new mechanics and modular features that add depth to the gameplay, ensuring that every journey through the wasteland is different.

Will you and your crew make it to the Citadel before the lights go out for good?

The race for survival has never been more intense.

name: Chicken Fried Dice
description:
Order up! Become Top Chef at a Food Truck Festival by serving up delicious dishes to hungry customers. You'll be chuckin' and pluckin' dice in this frantic, puzzly roll 'n write for 1-5 players! Upgrade your truck to out serve your competition featuring dry erase customer cards and dual layer food truck player boards.

Operate your own food truck serving up delicious dishes to hungry customers. Each food truck is represented by a double-layer board with different food stations that help you feed customers.

Upgrade your truck with dry-erase tiles to out-serve the competition. Insert tiles onto your truck to change the way each station works and make your job easier.

Pluck ingredients from the market before the other chefs get a chance. It's a race to grab the ingredients you need each round.

Use plucked ingredients to fulfill customer orders before they get hangry! Every customer is unique and gives you a review score and a bonus ability once fed. Plus, if you exactly match their order, you'll earn a tip!

name: Chronicle of Kings
description:
Chronicle of Kings is set during the Viking age (700-1000) in the Fate of the Norns universe. Players take on a dynasty of Viking rulers who wish to be immortalized in legend.

Victory is achieved by being the bloodline with the most renown, and the game rewards players for memorable play. There are many ways to achieve renown, allowing players to pursue different paths to victory.

Every turn the players perform many actions, which include: quests, military conquests, trade/raid, diplomatic intrigue, etc. Each turn spans several years, meaning that the bloodline will need to plan for marriage and children. Mechanics are designed to tell a vivid and memorable story.

The world is not static, and every turn events occur necessitating that sometimes the player work together to overcome a shared challenge.

The game also features a campaign book, allowing for solitaire play.

name: Last Aurora: Frostlands
description:
The radioactive dust of the Last War has left the northern countries frozen.

In the ice desert, the few survivors live in a nice little hell: the “old world” resources are now exhausted, and traveling to the south is too long and dangerous.
 But a radio message is rekindling hope: the last icebreaker ship, the Aurora, is cruising along the coast, looking for survivors. In only a few days, those who cannot get on board the ship will be doomed by the ice.

It will be a race against time: to make it to the ship or surrender to despair. There’s still the light of hope on the horizon—a light to grab before it’s too late! Last Aurora is a post-apocalyptic game for 2-4 players set in a frozen, desolate land.

Each player has to manage their crew to gather resources, recruit survivors, improve their vehicle, and fight their enemies as they race to reach the ship before it’s too late!

Frostlands, the revisited edition of Last Aurora, includes new features like:

     modular maps, 
     modular bonus actions, 
     new combat system and loot mechanism.

name: No More Dead: New York
description:
In a New York devastated by a zombie outbreak, survivor communities fight to endure the chaos and rebuild civilization. As the leader of one of these groups, you must navigate the city's iconic neighborhoods with your caravan, making critical decisions along the way: deploy your team strategically to gather vital resources, conquer and reactivate key locations, and eliminate imminent threats.

With a blend of area control, resource management, and tactical decision-making, No More Dead: New York will make you witness either the rebirth or the downfall of civilization, all within 90 minutes. But beware, a threat even greater than the zombies lurks in the shadows - other survivors!

The fate of New York is in your hands. Will you ensure your community's survival, find a cure, or succumb to the chaos?

—description from the publisher

name: Aetherspire
description:
The realm of Elementis, once a harmonious balance of earth, air, fire, and water, is now under siege. Elemental Aetherfiends have dispatched waves of invaders to drain our aethercore, the realm's lifeblood, causing chaos to reign. You and your companions must build powerful elemental spires to lure away and defeat these invaders. As each spire grows stronger, it will unleash a devastating resurgence against the Aetherfiends. Can you restore balance before it's too late?

Aetherspire is a cooperative 3D tile placement and tower defense game for 1-4 players.

You and your companions will take on the role of Elementis heroes, working together to mold elemental power into four spires, one of each element: earth, air, fire, and water. A spire is a set of four floor tiles, one on top of another, all of the same element. Each time you complete a spire, that element’s aether fiend is defeated. Once all four aether fiends have been defeated, the heroes share in glorious victory, having restored balance to the realm of Elementis!

However, if the precious aethercore is depleted, or if you take too long to defeat the aether fiends, then the heroes lose the game, and chaos will overtake your world!

—description from the publisher

name: Chronocritters
description:
Earth, 2562. Following a cataclysmic event, time and space are ripping apart at the seams.

Players must help save the world by rediscovering ancient technologies, enlisting the help of robotic time-travelling, portal-building animals known as CHRONOCRITTERS. The availability of the different actions and resources will change and flow with the passing of time. Players will gain access to more locations via time portals, but they only remain stable for a short time and will begin to decay, requiring players to constantly maintain them or build anew.

The player who can best master the chronocritters, and persuade the AI about their abilities, will restore reality, and win the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Chronofiends!!
description:
Chronofiends!! is a cooperative sci-fi board game set on a space station trapped in a time loop, where players must navigate through chaotic environments filled with danger and excitement. The Hearthseekers, a fanatical group erased from history due to their reckless time experiments, have broken the flow of time, causing the station to loop in time endlessly. They’ve kidnapped and experimented on aliens from across the galaxy, who are now also loose and throwing the station into chaos.
