The winner is the player who manages to be the first to find their  Perfect Place and collect 15 units of Food, 20 of Wood, and 40 units of Strength (Help).

NOTE: With one deck can play 2 Players; With 2 decks of Forest Fellowship can play up to 4 Players; With 3 decks can Play up to 6 Players.

name: Forest Shuffle: Smoky Mountains
description:
A new continent awaits in the Forest Shuffle universe: After exploring Central Europe in Forest Shuffle and the wilds of southern England in Forest Shuffle – Dartmoor, this new standalone game invites players on a journey to North America.

As the third standalone game in the Forest Shuffle series, Forest Shuffle - Smoky Mountains takes us to this popular North American National Park. Building on the familiar gameplay of the series, it introduces new species and clever twists in mechanics. This keeping the experience as fresh as the bubbling waters on the new terrain cards!

Here’s what Forest Shuffle – Smoky Mountains is all about:

     New terrain types centered around water, playable on their own or tucked as universal waters under trees.
     New synergies between flora and fauna, all revolving around the element of water
     In addition to a variety of species around the water, the game is also home to various large animals, such as black bears or bobcats.


Once again, the player who collected the most points, wins.

Forest Shuffle - Smoky Mountains is part of the Lookout GreenLine, manufactured 100% eco-friendly.

—description from the publisher

name: Forfort
description:
Forfort is a little card game of 124 cards (31 cards per player) to build fortifications, attack your opponent and win!  Players play tug-of-war, destroying their opponent forts while building their own.

Your deck (donjon) is in the center of your fort. Use a card to build on one of 8 placements or discard (with symbol) to apply its effect (catapult, army, drawbridge, etc.). You have an extra bonus if you associate two symbols one next to the other in your fort.

You win if you finish building your fort first or you build the most fortifications.

name: The Sandcastles of Burgundy
description:
Queen Crab is coming to visit Burgundy, and you want to decorate your village for her royal beach party. Find the right decorations and collect points. The animals of the royal guild will help you when you have finished decorating their shops - but can you find the animals before the others?

In The Sandcastles of Burgundy, you collect points by finding the right decorations, so can you remember under which sand castle the animals of the royal guild are hiding? Roll your two dice at the same time, then you can use them to either look for decorations in sand castles, putting them in your warehouse if you find one, or transport previously collected decorations to your village with your cart. If you have collected two decorations of one color, you can look for the matching animal of the royal guild.

As soon as a player reaches Queen Crab's beach party, the dice round ends. Whoever has collected the most points wins!

name: Ventopia: Die fliegende Insel
description:
On the flying island of Ventopia, the protective light shield has collapsed. Nyxara, the ruler of the Dark World, wants to take control of Ventopia and sends out her dark creatures.

In Ventopia: Die fliegende Insel, which features an electronic game board, players need to use their fighting skills and a bit of luck to save the flying island from its imminent fall into the dark depths.

name: Fox Grove
description:
Deep within the whispering woods, a bustling community is coming to life.

In Fox Grove, you are trying to build the most prosperous little animal village in the forest. Over the course of 4 rounds, you must skillfully manage your hand of cards and your resources to outshine your rivals.

At its heart, Fox Grove is a unique blend of mechanics. Each round begins with a trick-taking phase where playing the right cards is key to gather essential resources. However, veteran card players should stay on their toes: there is a twist in the trick-taking rules that will force you to rethink your standard strategies and adapt to the changing rhythm of the forest.

Using the resources gathered from your tricks, you will expand your personal tableau. 

     Expand your Village: Turn resources into buildings to generate Victory Points.
     Unlock Abilities: Gain special skills that provide powerful advantages in future rounds.


Whether you are a seasoned gamer or new to the hobby, Fox Grove welcomes you. The game features a dedicated Introductory Mode, designed to offer an easy entry point for families and beginners before diving into the full strategic depth of the standard game.

After four rounds, the player with the most magnificent village and the most Victory Points wins the game!

—description from the publisher

name: France Overseas, 1940
description:
A two player alternative history wargame that examines the possibilities inherent in the campaign that could have occurred in northwest Africa late in 1940 if the French had resolved not to give up. The assumption is they instead chose to evacuate as much of the French Army as possible to Tunisia, Algeria and French Morocco.

Both sides’ orders of battle are historically based. That is, the German force in Spain is what they had intended to use for the invasion of England around this same time. The assumption there is, if they believed they could lift that force across the English Channel, the Strait of Gibraltar would have presented less difficulty – eight miles wide vs. 21 at the Pas de Calais – once Spain had been dragooned into joining the Axis.

The Spanish divisions are the two corps of their Army of North Africa (the original supporters of Franco). The rest of their ground force is assumed to be invading Portugal, as was their plan had things gone this way. During the game the Allied player will have to cope with decisions made ‘above his head’ in London in regard to fleet commitment and the BEF’s initial landing site. That arbitrariness is reflective of the Allies’ historic inability to create smoothly operating joint service headquarters during the war’s first half.

Each game turn represents half a month. Each hex represents about 10 days. Each hex is 20 miles (32.4 km) from side-to-side. Units are divisions.

name: Freigard
Wer stiehlt mir die Show?
description:
Wer stiehlt mir die Show? is the Boardgame Version from a famous German TV Show. Each Round you have to participate in different Quiz Categories to earn Credits and host the next round. After 6 Rounds one Player is qualified for the grand finale. His Opponent will be decided in the seventh round.

After an epic final Quiz round the winner will be crownd and not only takes the trophy with him home, he also wins the boardgame itself!

—user summary

Joko Winterscheidt präsentiert: Das perfekte Quizspiel für 3-5 Spieler ab 10 Jahren mit der genau richtigen Portion Spaß! Die beliebte ProSieben-Show „Wer stiehlt mir die Show?" gibt es jetzt nämlich als Brettspiel mit vielen verrückten Quiz-Kategorien. Wer einzelne Spielrunden gewinnt, wird Moderator der nächsten Kategorie. Doch wer kann das Spiel am Ende für sich gewinnen und stiehlt nicht nur die Show, sondern auch das Brettspiel? (Ja, wirklich!)

Wie in der TV-Sendung dreht sich alles um die Frage „Wer stiehlt die Show?". Denn wer eine Quiz-Kategorie gewinnt, moderiert die nächste Stufe und bekommt eine wertvolle Münze. Als Moderator darf man die nächste Kategorie auswählen und es den anderen so möglichst schwer machen zu punkten. Nach sechs Runden zieht der beste Kandidat vorzeitig ins Finale ein und verteidigt die Show in bester Joko-Manier. Der Verteidiger moderiert eine letzte Gewinnstufe, in der sein Herausforderer fürs Finale bestimmt wird. Hier entscheidet sich dann, wer die Show stiehlt - und natürlich das Brettspiel mit nach Hause nimmt! (Ja, wirklich!!) Das Spiel zur Show enthält für alle Fans bekannte Kategorien wie: Die leichten Fünf, Wie du mir, so ich buchstabier, Riskier die Gier und viele mehr.

—description from the publisher

name: Disney Villainous: Come, We Fly!
description:
Disney Villainous: Come, We Fly! brings the Sanderson Sisters from Disney's Hocus Pocus to the game as a playable Villain.

On a turn, the active player moves their character to a different location on their player board, takes one or more of the actions visible on that space (often by playing cards from their hand), then refills their hand to four cards. Cards are allies, items, effects, and conditions. You need to use your cards to fulfill your unique win condition.

One of the actions allows you to choose another player, draw two cards from that player's fate deck, then play one of them on that player's board, covering two of the four action spaces on one of that player's locations. The fate deck contains heroes, items, and effects from that villain's movie, and these cards allow other players to mess with that particular villain.

Disney Villainous: Come, We Fly! is playable on its own, and its characters can also face off against those in the other Disney Villainous games.

name: Disney Villainous: Success at Any Cost
description:
Disney Villainous: Success at Any Cost will introduce Ernesto de la Cruz from Disney Pixar's Coco and Prince Hans from Disney's Frozen.

On a turn, the active player moves their character to a different location on their player board, takes one or more of the actions visible on that space (often by playing cards from their hand), then refills their hand to four cards. Cards are allies, items, effects, and conditions. You need to use your cards to fulfill your unique win condition.

One of the actions allows you to choose another player, draw two cards from that player's fate deck, then play one of them on that player's board, covering two of the four action spaces on one of that player's locations. The fate deck contains heroes, items, and effects from that villain's movie, and these cards allow other players to mess with that particular villain.

Disney Villainous: Success at Any Cost is playable on its own, and its characters can also face off against those in the other Disney Villainous games.

name: Fruit Boss
description:
You crave power. You crave respect. But first—you need the Fruit. In Fruit Boss, players take on the role of "junior fruit executives" and battle for marketplace dominance by collecting the most valuable sets of fruit. Pay into market stalls to snatch neighboring stacks, but beware: every move opens a door for your opponent. It’s not personal. It’s just business.

The goal of this quick and easy card game is to collect stacks from the market to build high-scoring sets in your private collection. To claim a stack, you must create a more valuable stack in an adjacent stall. On your turn, you'll take actions like stacking, sliding, and combining to achieve your goals. Stacks must have at least two cards to be collected. But be careful—if any stack hits five or more cards, it topples, removing itself and a neighboring stack from the game. And watch out for Maneki-neko, he want to the fruit too.

At the end of the round, you’ll score your top three fruit sets. Sets are scored by multiplying the highest-value fruit by the number of cards in that suit. Extra fruit? That’s a penalty. The player with the highest score wins.

Fruit Boss plays great at two and includes rules for up to four players. It has a classic card game feel with modern tactics and mechanics. And also fruit. It has fruit.

—description from the publisher

name: Fury of Dracula (Fifth Edition)
description:
Fury of Dracula (Fifth Edition) is a one-versus-many deduction game inspired by Bram Stoker's classic novel: Dracula. One player controls Dracula and up to four players assume the roles of his hunters. During the game, Dracula will attempt to elude the hunters as he spawns new vampires across Europe, while the hunters try to find and destroy Dracula, thereby ending his reign of terror.

What's different about this edition: The fifth edition core gameplay is consistent with the gameplay in Third/Fourth edition but includes an all-new hunter to play as (Jonathan Harker) and a "Quick-Play Variant".

—description from the publisher

name: Fury of the Elements
description:
Long before mankind, the world of Elemoria was forged by Elemond, the God of Elements. However, he shattered a part of himself, his divine hammer, Rok’nir. From the hammer’s shards scattered across Elemoria, rose the Primordial Titans, immortal guardians of Fire, Water, Earth, and Air—empowered further by the fury of Elemoria herself, the Mother of Nature.

Fury of the Elements is an expandable strategy card game where 2 players will compete to Capture, Command, and Conquer the elements manipulating nature's forces to obtain the most Elemental Power. The player with the most Elemental Power at the end of the game wins.

Bend the elements of fire, water, earth, and air, in a strategic battle for supremacy. Harness the ancient power of the Titans, letting you manipulate the elements, rules, and battlefield to your advantage. Craft powerful combinations, anticipate your opponent’s tactics, and master the art of elemental warfare. Offering multiple paths to victory, every move matters, and every turn demands cunning.

Multiple game modes allow players to learn and teach at their own pace. Play a simple game on a 3 x 3 grid, or a more strategic mode on a 5 x 5 grid.

—description from the designer

name: Futory Cards Duality
description:
Futory Cards Duality takes players on an exciting ride through the universe. Exotic landmarks and creatures will serve those able to control them. It offers an expanded battle system with intuitive card combinations that make every game unique.

Futory Cards is a deck building game in which up to four players buy cards from the Bazaar to create the strongest deck and defeat their opponents. With Landmarks, Creatures and Artifacts, the players go through four phases in which they try to remove the 24 Time Points from the other players.

Once 12 Time Points are lost, the Light Die gets removed from the player and they can no longer get up to 24 Time Points. A player has lost the game after their Dark Die gets removed.

If a player can no longer draw cards from their Future Pile, their History Pile gets shuffled and creates a new Future Pile. This dynamic feature enables long term strategic thinking.

Futory Cards Duality can also be linked with other titles from the Trilogy, allowing even more strategic variety and a higher player count.

—description from the publisher

name: Horrified: Dungeons & Dragons – Ravenloft
description:
Horrified: DUNGEONS & DRAGONS Ravenloft is a standalone game with four new mechanically-unique monsters to challenge: Carrionette, Gulthias Tree, Baba Lysaga and the Dark Lord of Barovia Strahd von Zarovich. In their quest to defend Barovia, each player gets to take on the role of a hero with one of 5 iconic D&D classes. 
 In Horrified, players work together, alternating between the hero phase, where one player gets to move around the board, guide villagers, pick up valuable items, and work to defeat the monsters; and the monster phase, where the monsters wreak havoc, attacking both heroes and villagers alike.  
 It’s up to the heroes to strategize, adapt, and solve each monster’s unique puzzle before they’re overwhelmed with terror!

—description from the designer

name: G.I. JOE: Operation Cobra
description:
G.I. Joe: Operation Cobra invites you to step into the boots of the legendary G.I. Joe team in a cooperative tactical action game brimming with adventure and strategy. This immersive experience combines the thrill of daring missions with the challenge of outwitting Cobra’s relentless forces. Whether you’re strategizing solo or rallying a team, every session feels like a blockbuster battle for freedom and justice.

In Skirmish Mode, players can dive into fast-paced action-packed encounters, perfect for a quick session. For those seeking a deeper and more immersive experience, Campaign Mode offers an interconnected series of missions where your choices shape the course of the game. Upgrading equipment, honing tactics, and adapting to new threats are key to overcoming Cobra’s evolving schemes. No two campaigns are the same, ensuring replayability and endless excitement.

—description from the publisher

name: Gal4Xeon
description:
The galaxy is ripe for the picking. You have ten eons to expand out from your home sector, exploring sectors and then exploiting their resources or trading with and conquering their inhabitants. Do you race out to the alien precursor ruins at the edge of the galaxy? Or consolidate your power in the centre? Do you focus your scientific advances on exploring and trading with the aliens you find, or build a military machine that is unstoppable?

Who can make the biggest mark on their galaxy? Back Gal4Xeon to find out!

—description from the designer

name: Galileo's Truth
description:
The year is 1610. The world, as we know it, is on the precipice of change, a fragile balance between ancient dogma and dawning reason. Whispers of a new truth echo through the hallowed halls of academia and across bustling piazzas. Nicolaus Copernicus's radical theory, once a fringe idea, now finds a formidable champion in Galileo Galilei, whose revolutionary observations of the cosmos threaten to dismantle the very foundations of accepted knowledge.
You are a scholar, a brilliant mind in an age of intellectual ferment, drawn into the exhilarating and perilous quest for understanding. Armed with your intellect, you'll write groundbreaking treatises, unveil ingenious inventions and turn your gaze skyward, observing the celestial dance through newly crafted telescopes; while the shadow of the Inquisition looms large, its watchful eyes scrutinizing every discovery, every whispered theory. One misstep, one too-bold pronouncement, could lead to your arrest, your work condemned, and perhaps, a fiery end. Will you pursue the truth, or will the chilling grip of fear force you to recant? The fate of knowledge, and perhaps your very life, rests in your hands.

Galileo’s Truth is a competitive game for 1 to 4 players featuring mechanics like deck building, worker placement, resource management and the threatening management of the Suspicion…  
Players will alternate turns performing actions such as:

Write a Treatise to add more cards to their deck, increasing their opportunities to do big and articulate actions.
Create an Invention to gain powerful abilities, increase their income and grow their scoring opportunities.
Observe the Sky to unlock a sequence of progressively stronger bonuses and actions.

And many others!

But be careful, because the watchful eye of the Inquisition will judge all your actions. As Suspicion grows, you'll gain Penance cards that clog up your deck and potentially score negative points at the end of the game. Most dangerously, you could end up in jail, unable to use your only worker, or even worse… the fire of purification will await you.

The intense mechanic of Suspicion is further enriched by the victory point track. As you pull ahead on the victory point track, leaving others behind, you'll gain even more Suspicion. Will you boldly pursue the truth and risk the Inquisition's punishment, or will you choose a more cautious path, perhaps even appearing assertive towards the Church?

—description from the publisher

name: Garage Rock
description:
Garage Rock is a medium-weight, worker-placement game that transports you back to the 1980s — a time when big hair, cassette tapes, and BMX bikes ruled the neighborhood streets. Step into the shoes of a teenage garage band, fighting for glory in the high-stakes "Battle of the Bands," hosted by the infamous local pirate radio DJ, Johnny Law. As you compete for fans, you'll upgrade your skills, post flyers around town, sell band merch, and pour your heart into writing songs that make your fans shout for more! Record demos at the local studio, complete your album, and hand your demo tape to Johnny Law to get your music aired on his Pirate Radio station, broadcast from his secret treehouse.

On your turn, you'll place band members at various locations on the town board, visiting shops to gather the skills needed to qualify for one of four available gigs. Use the money earned from gigs to visit the Music Shop to upgrade your instrument or swing by the Clothing Store to boost your band’s image with a fresh new look. Pump some quarters into the copy machine to print flyers and spread the word about your band all over town. Record a demo tape that will boost your popularity when it’s played on Pirate Radio by dropping radio cubes down the treehouse cube tower.

The game unfolds over sixteen weeks of summer, with the grand finale being the "Battle of the Bands" contest. The band with the most fans at the end wins the game.

Garage Rock adds a layer of strategy, combining the excitement of worker placement and resource management with a thematic and nostalgic teenage music scene experience. It's time to build your band, rock the garage, and dominate the neighborhood!

—description from the publisher

name: Garbage Gobblers
description:
In Garbage Gobblers, you will lead your gang of street critters to raid the neighborhood trashcans and score today’s meal. Garbage will pile up in four trashcans throughout the game, and you’ll need to make clever use of your Gobblers to make the most of even the nastiest scraps.

On your turn, you may add garbage to the trashcans, replenish your Gobblers, or start a trashcan raid! During a raid, rival gangs may jump into the fray, while special Gobblers can stir things up and mess with your plans. Once the dust settles, only the gang with the highest strength gets to claim the trashcan’s garbage!

It's not all about strength though! The different Gobbler types affect how you score, and you might even end up with a stomachache if you’re not careful.

Your goal? Out-scavenge your opponents and create the ultimate Garbage Feast, earning you the highest score by the end of the game!

—description from the designer

name: Labyrinth: Chronicles
description:
Once upon a time, there was a Labyrinth, a magical place full of wonders and mysteries. Adventurers who returned told unbelievable stories of its ever-changing walls and shifting corridors, a mind-boggling challenge indeed that only the bravest could tackle. But it was worth it, they say, as the dark nooks of the Labyrinth hide real treasures. The Labyrinth waits for you. Are you brave enough to enter?

Labyrinth: Chronicles brings a new Co-op Campaign mode to one of the best-selling board games ever. Enter the mysterious Labyrinth, now with a stunning 3D board and graphic design from Awaken Realms, to gather the resources required to help a nearby faefolk village. But beware! Inside dwell grasping goblins who want to snatch valuables before you! As you progress, you will rebuild the damaged village, meet new friends, unlock new skills, and many more!

—description from the publisher

name: Gateway
description:
Step into the enchanting alleys of Gateway, a city where shadows whisper secrets and power is seized in the flicker of a gas lamp.

In this thrilling deck builder for 2-4 players you´ll recruit a motley crew of infamous characters and rely on the power of runestones to conquer the city´s guarded districts.

Immerse yourself in a world where Victorian elegance meets fantastical whimsy, and every decision could tip the balance of power.

Will you dominate the dark alleys and opulent parlors, weaving your influence through cunning schemes? Or will your rivals outwit you in this game of strategy and rising infamy? Dare to play in the city of Gateway.

—description from the publisher

name: Las Vegas
description:
Try your luck in the colorful glittering world of Las Vegas. Visit 6 different casinos and try to rake in as much money as possible.

Roll all your available dice. Then choose exactly one of the numbers you rolled. Place all of the dice showing this number on the corresponding casino. Then the next player will roll. Continue until you've all placed all your dice.

At the end of each round players will assess each casino in turn. Ties cancel out, and the players remaining with the first and second most dice will claim their rewards.

The key is figuring out where to place your dice to win the most cash or snatch a tidy sum from someone else-- with a little bit of luck.

This is a refresh of the classic version which streamlines play with fewer rounds, powerful Big Dice, and larger casino rewards. Includes a sixth player and a One-Armed Bandit variant.

—description from the publisher

name: GEMMiS: Fures Codice
description:
Gemmis: Fures Codice is a competitive game for two players wrapped in a medieval market aesthetic, in which gems appear from a bag filling the market (a board) and players have to swap gems from the market in order to get combinations that give them points. When a combination is made, the gems involved are removed from the market and new gems appear from the bag. The player with the most points at the end wins.

-description from designer

name: Gentle Jack
description:
Gentle Jack is a gothic-comedy party/drinking card game for 3-10 players where dark humor, strategic card play, and a healthy disregard for friendships collide.
Set in a world of macabre whimsy, the game uses hand-illustrated card art to breathe life to an atmosphere that sits somewhere between a Victorian séance and occult pirate fantasy. Beneath the crude (but clever) humor lies a game with more strategic texture than your average party fare.

name: Get Gnomed!
description:
In Get Gnomed!, be the first player to steal your opponents' lawn ornaments and claim victory in this wacky and whimsical board game. Mix strategy, stealth, and high fashion as you command your gnome army to become the backyard champs!

During a turn, players play cards and roll dice to fight their opponents and search their mushrooms for a lawn ornament.  But there are traps and bombs under mushrooms too, so you better watch out!

The first player to find a lawn ornament underneath one of their opponent's mushroom tokens wins!

—description from the designer

name: Ghostland
description:
Jurassic Park meets Ghosts in this Co-operative boardgame about a theme park gone mad! It's opening day at Ghostland, a theme park that contains actual ghosts! However, havok has immediately broken loose, and the ghosts are attacking guests left and right. It's up to you and your friends to stop the ghosts, build Field Generators to contain them, and finally face off against the most sinister ghost in the park, the infamous Rex Garrote!

Each players picks a character that is unique and contains their own stats and abilities to help you not only survive the theme park, but hopefully save the day as well! The game is played in rounds where players move arounds the park, fight ghosts, buy items, or try to build a Recurrence Field Generator.

Once players have successfully built three Recurrence Field Generators they will summon the big bad himself, Rex Garrote, for them to defeat! But if the park's human population reaches zero, it's Game Over!

—description from the designer

name: Ghosts Galore
description:
In Ghosts Galore you're helping monsters to build a fun ghost train in an abandoned mineshaft. Every monster want's the track tiles laid their way - so YOU have to keep them calm, coordinate and optimize their track. Over the course of 8 rounds, each player builds a unique track on their 3x3 playground for the ghost train.

This family friendly tile placement game comes with a unique drafting mechanism and is quick to play while offering various strategies​: Will you stick with your drafted tile or go for a bold move which brings you even more scares?

After only 8 rounds, all tracks are set and the project is done. Sounds easy? Well, only the master who lines up the best scares, wins!

Ghosts Galore is another addition to the Lookout GreenLine,  manufactured 100% eco-friendly.

—description from the publisher

name: Glimmerdeep
description:
Far below the surface, where echoes dance and crystals gleam, lies Glimmerdeep—a forgotten realm teeming with possibility. Here, critters craft wonders from the earth, forging bonds and burrows in the shimmering dark.

In Glimmerdeep, you lead a small faction of animals that thrive underground.  You have just found a new home and it is time to expand and build your subterranean civilization.  You must efficiently leverage your unique faction capabilities to excavate tunnels, gather resources, and construct workshops to enhance your society.  Can you become the most successful subterranean society?

Glimmerdeep is an engine-building game that is played over 5 rounds.  Each round, players will excavate spaces across their map to gather resources and clear space for new buildings, construct workshops and forges, and run their workshops and forges for various benefits.

At the end of the 5th round, the player with the most Victory Points (VP) is the winner.  Players will gain VP by constructing Workshops and Forges, running their Workshops and Forges, completing the unique Map Objective, leveraging their faction’s unique Calling, and for any unspent resources.

—description from the publisher

name: JOYRIDE DUEL: Next Gen
description:
JOYRIDE DUEL: Next Gen is an stand-alone two-player game of electric head-to-head racing. Tactically plan your route, push your luck to take corners at speed. and crash into your rival to knock them off course. This is the full Joyride experience in a smaller footprint.

Next Gen includes 2 unique cars, 4 powerful items, and 12 tracks across 2 maps, all of which are compatible with any other Joyride game. Tracks in this version can accommodate 3 players with the addition of a car from any other set.

Cars: 

    The Electric – robotic control that comes at a price.
    The Learner – an instructor’s assistance when your driving is too risky.


Maps

    The Driving School – wind through chicanes on different lines every lap.
    The Warehouse – dodge the attacks of the security bots.


—description from the publisher

name: Go Viking
description:
Go Viking is a fast-playing, push-your-luck dice game steeped in Norse mythology. As Viking leaders, players seek glory through daring Raids, divine favor, and bold decisions.

Each turn, draw Mythic Powers through sacred carvings in the Runestones—then roll and let the Destiny Dice shape your fate, raid for Loot, and carve your legend in the sagas of the North.

Easy to learn and quick to play, Go Viking is a compact filler game that packs mythic adventure into every turn. When one Jarl’s hoard becomes legendary, the final round begins—and only the richest warrior will have their saga sung.

Raid • Roll • Glory

The title Go Viking comes from the Old Norse “fara i víking”—to leave home, embrace risk, and earn your place in legend.

—description from the designer

name: Goat Simulator: The Card Game
description:
Goat Simulator is a fast-paced party card game where you draw goats, play goats, and battle other goats. Gear up your goats, sabotage your so-called “friends”, and unleash chaos so marvelous it’ll make even the most stoic goat bleat. Who needs friends anyway, when you have goats?

Players draw and discard cards to equip their goats adding gear effects and points to their score.  They also play Karma cards for extra powerful effects and earn bonus points if they finish a personal mission. The game ends when a player makes it to 10 Chaos points.

Rules for a simpler kids version are included.

—description from the publisher

name: Goblin Cave
description:
Goblin Cave is an asymmetrical team-based tactics game featuring strategic, card-based combat driven by unique character abilities and player decisions.

Each player takes control of two unique characters, drawing cards with powerful abilities and moving freely around the board. Players will control tactical locations, place traps, launch fireballs, destroy walls, teleport across pits, climb ledges, sling arrows, swing great-axes, steal relics, and much, much more!

Each team of players has their own win conditions, and will go toe-to-toe with their opponents to achieve them through fast-paced strategy-fueled combat. Adventurers traverse the Goblins’ cave in order to steal Relics—objects of great arcane power. Goblins must defend their homes from the greedy invaders who are trying to steal their relics, navigating the cave through tunnels only they can use! Each team is comprised of unique characters with rich lore and powerful specialized abilities, not unlike a board game version of a MOBA (like League of Legends) or hero shooter (like Overwatch or Apex Legends).

Players control two characters simultaneously. On a player’s turn, they draw an ability card from each character's ability deck, roll a die for each character’s movement, then move and use an ability card for each character, in any order they wish. The game ends either when all characters on a team are incapacitated, when the Adventurers escape with a relic, or when 10 rounds have passed.

With 10 playable characters, multiple cave maps, and several planned expansions, Goblin Cave offers a great deal of replayability and long-term support.

—description from the publisher

name: Goblin Party
description:
Goblin Party is a quick tactical hero-crushing card game where players are underdogs of fantasy and take revenge on those pesky Heroes for years of being the favorite punching bags.

The first Player to satisfy the appetite of 3 Warchiefs around the cooking pot wins the game! Each hero slain is used as an ingredient for the cooking pot to please the Warchiefs. Defeating the most Heroes is the key to winning!

Before each game begins, players choose a Warchief. This Warchief changes the way you play with your deck each game.

Each turn you play 1 Goblin to create Parties together with your fellow Goblin Clans to attract Heroes. 3 Heroes are placed next to the draw pile in the middle of the table. There can be multiple Parties that consist of multiple clans.

Each player has over 20 unique Goblins in their deck. The trick is to play your Goblins in the best way possible. Every Goblin card has a unique skill that changes the playing field drastically.  No game is the same as there are more than 30+ Heroes that are always randomized and you will have a different Warchief each game, completely altering your playstyle.

—description from the designer

name: God of War: The Board Game
publisher: CMON Global Limited; Sony Interactive Entertainment, LLC
description:
God of War: The Board Game is a co-operative dungeon crawler filled with epic fights and puzzles for players who will encounter various iconic monsters in the form of highly detailed miniatures. The game also features a unique combat and leveling system based on the bonding of characters and co-operation. Take on the role of Kratos and Atreus, and follow a series of adventures that imagine scenarios during the years between the 2018 God of War video game and 2022's God of War: Ragnarök when Fimbulwinter descends on Midgard.

To play God of War, players must first choose a Scenario and follow any setup instructions and exceptions described. The game is played through a series of Rounds. Each round is separated into 2 Game Phases, starting with the Hero Phase and followed by the Enemy Phase. Once both phases are complete, a new Round begins.

To win any Scenario, unless otherwise specified, players will need to complete the Scenario Objective and kill the Boss. To complete the Scenario Objective, players will have to complete the Scenario Quest Tokens for each Scenario that are placed during the setup or have specified rules for it on the special rules of each Scenario (see Scenario book).

The game is lost if either Hero has its life reduced to 0 or if the Tracker Cube reaches the end of the Menace Track.

—description from the publisher

name: Gods & Mortals
description:
Step into the sandals of an ancient Greek god. As Zeus, Athena, Hades, and other deities, raise armies, spark conflicts, erect temples, and unleash unique special powers — all to outmaneuver your divine rivals.

Mortals are your pawns, their devotion to you is a weapon, and betrayal is divine tradition. The throne of Olympus is yours... if you can seize it.

—description from the publisher

name: JOYRIDE: Full Throttle
description:
Buckle up for the next instalment in the Joyride series, Joyride: Full Throttle!

Joyride: Full Throttle is a high-octane stand-alone racing game in the Joyride range. Keeping the same core gameplay while expanding the player count to 6 players! Race through 20 tracks across 2 new maps – the sun-soaked Beach and the neon-drenched Abandoned Mall, and harness powerful new items and dangerous obstacles. Joyride: Full Throttle is for learner drivers and seasoned racers.

Expanded for Joyride: Full Throttle is the Team Mode facilitating 2v2 or 2v2v2 racing. Players work together to speed their Super Fan around the track as fast as possible, swapping the Fan between their cars mid-race. New in-game Portals can launch you through glowing gateways to leap around the track, pull off daring shortcuts, and even chain multiple maps together to create custom circuits.

Full Throttle is fully compatible with previous Joyride games allowing players to mix and match cars, items, and more from across the series

—description from publisher

name: Above and Below: Haunted
description:
You and your family have lived in the marshlands for generations. But your hometown is getting crowded and you’ve heard of a group of villages to the west, in a landscape of azure lakes, where the constantly flowing water has created a maze of watery caves, sinkholes, underground streams, and porous bedrock. There’s opportunity to start a new life there, catching fish, living in a stilt house on the lake, and exploring the deep sinkholes for rare ingredients and rusty treasures. You’ve packed up your favorite fishing pole and strapped the baby to your back, ready for a fresh start. If only you’d known about the ghosts, you might have stayed where you were.

Above and Below: Haunted is a standalone sequel to Above and Below (The character tokens are compatible between editions), planned to release on the 10th anniversary of the original game. As in the original game, players compete to build the best village by recruiting villagers, constructing buildings, and exploring the caves below ground. Above and Below: Haunted features new stories and explores a new setting in the world of Arzium.

Above and Below: Haunted includes some new features:


     Ghosts! Your buildings can become haunted, lowering your reputation. The game includes wooden ghost tokens that are placed on building cards. Players can perform a banish action to remove their ghosts, placing one of the ghosts on another player's building and gaining a reward.
     Two Cave Types! There are now two types of cave cards: normal and dangerous. Dangerous caves have higher lantern requirements, but give larger rewards, including a pearl. Pearls are a new type of token that count as your highest placed good at the end of the game.
     New Buildings! There are many new types of key and star buildings included in the game to encourage new strategies. All buildings have been designed from the ground up especially for Above and Below: Haunted.
     Boats! Players can gain boat tokens, which can be used to alter die rolls or gain coins.
     Adventure Cards! There are now 40 unique adventure cards which are gained as specific rewards for exploring the caves.


—description from the publisher

name: Gothic: A Shadow's Quest
description:
Immerse yourself in the epic world of one of the most influential RPGs of all time - Gothic. In Gothic: A Shadow's Quest, slip into the role of a “Shadow”, an aspiring member of the Old Camp who wants to make a name for himself in the Colony. Risky tasks and deadly opponents await you in the dangerous Valley of Mines. Alone or cooperatively with up to three other players - and an optional Game Master – fight against aggressive scavengers, sneaky minecrawlers, cruel hordes of orcs, and other bloodthirsty creatures. Explore, complete quests, and develop your character; master swordplay, unleash magical powers, or wield a bow to defeat enemies from afar. The choice is yours!

Customise your Shadows according to their skills and abilities and stock up on gear in the Old Camp. Then take a Quest from one of the NPCs and your party can set out on their Journey! Explore the valley of Mines where you will find treasure and encounter characters that might help or hinder your adventures depending on your decisions. The Journey ends with a Final Encounter where you might battle a big boss monster, have to solve a series of puzzles, or destroy a magical artefact. Then return to the Old Camp to cash in your loot and level up!

—description from the publisher

name: Graantje de Voorste: Het Bordspel
description:
There is chaos on the farms! Loose chickens are pecking every patch of land clean.
They must be quick, however, because the hungry fox is on the prowl. Will you strike at the right time, steal the tastiest foods, and score the most points?

Brief game overview

Six farms are about to be pecked by chickens. Each round you choose which foods to take, but you often get in each other’s way. The longer a chicken stays on a farm, the more food they can find. At the same time, however, the fox is closing in. Once the fox strikes, you lose everything. During the game, the number of points you get for your food varies. The chicken with the most points at the end of the game wins.

—description from the publisher (translated)

name: Greathelm
description:
Greathelm is a tabletop miniatures agnostic skirmish game played with dice and hand-painted miniatures.

Each miniature represents a ‘knight’, a heroic and heavily armored warrior ready for combat. 
In every game, you and your opponent each control a team of six knights who face off in intense, close-quarters fights. 
Rather than depicting an entire battlefield in the conventional standards of tables sized 2"x2" to 4"x6", Greathelm focuses on a much smaller play area. This represents small slices of a much larger battlefield — think of it as the camera zooming in on key moments that decide the course of a battle happening off-screen. 
The gameplay reflects pivotal moments like breaking through enemy lines, toppling castle gates, or seizing control of a siege weapon. Games are fast-paced, easy to learn, and deeply tactical.

Game Round / Turn:

     Initiative Phase: activation of knights
     Battle Phase: use dice to perform actions
     Courage Phase: test courage of knights


Round ends once each phase has been played through, the battle ends or goes to a new round

—description from the designer

name: Greedy Goose
description:
In Greedy Goose, you want to snatch as many snacks as possible, but if you get too grabby, you'll lose some of what you already hold.

The deck consists of cards numbered 1-4, with 3s being present in both green and yellow; twelve action cards are present as well. Spread all of these cards face down on the table. Each player takes three cards in hand.

On a turn, you must turn a face-down card face up. If two identical cards are now face up, you must end your turn and add all face-up cards to your hand. If not, you can either reveal another card (and again check for matching cards), stop and collect all face-up cards, or end your turn, leaving all face-up cards for the next player.

If you reveal an action card, you can either steal a card from an opponent or give them one of your cards, depending on what the card shows. You can also ignore it, and in either case, you then discard this card.

If you ever hold more cards of the same type than the number showing on that card, you must discard all of those cards, removing them from the game. Pick up a second 1 — gone! Hold more than three green 3s — gone!

Continue play until all face-down cards have been revealed, then score your hand. A 1 is worth 3 points, and each other card is 1 point. Whoever holds the most points wins.

name: Green City
description:
In Green City, players act as urban planners building a sustainable transit network to connect Riders to their destinations before the supply of tiles runs out. You will score points for every successful Walking, Biking, Bus, or Tram connection you make. Longer Tram/Bus route scores more points, while Bike/Walking Path is best in medium/short lengths.

The game is played in clockwise turns. The game ends when the Cloth Bag is empty, then each player places their last tile on hand.
On your turn, perform the following 3 steps in order:

     Place a Path Tile
     Send Riders
     Draw a New Tile



As you lay down tiles and paths, you immediately dispatch your Riders along these new routes. You may activate bonus tiles to gain more points for routing through specific points on the map. 
  
Try to send as many Riders as you can to avoid significant penalties for leaving them stranded at the end. The player with the most Victory Points at the end of the game wins.

name: Grendel: The Game of Crime and Mayhem
description:
Leaving a trail of blood and corpses, Grendel has executed the leaders of the 23 most powerful crime families in the US. While Grendel now dominates the criminal underworld, the assassin’s series of coordinated attacks has also, predictably, created a power vacuum. Now, some upstarts think that New York City – the crown jewel of the East Coast–is up for grabs. Grendel needs to set things straight but wherever he goes, the werewolf, Argent, is soon to follow. Will the cold and calculating Grendel secure his grip after the so-called “Seaboard Massacre” or will the Mob rise up and take back what was theirs? Will Argent, the tireless hunter, finally corner his prey or will the Police put an end to this rampant crime spree?

Fight for control of the city as one of the four factions, each playing differently than the other. Focus your aggression, knowing that power and, ultimately, victory hang in the balance. Weigh your decisions carefully as each one could tip the scales in your favor.

Play out one bloody night in New York as Grendel, the Mob, the Police, and Argent seek to secure control of the city. While the Mob attempts to rally their forces and regain a foothold, Grendel sweeps in to subdue them once more. The Police work to forestall all conflict in the city, while Argent hunts Grendel.

During a round, players will take turns using their faction’s unique mechanics to deploy and move units, place Influence tokens on the board, draw cards, and put Aggression tokens in the Towers. When a Tower drops, that triggers a Mayhem. After 3 Mayhems, the player with the most points wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Gretchen's Garden
description:
In Gretchen’s Garden, players compete in selecting the most precious succulents available for their very own collection! You don’t even need a green thumb to win this easy to grasp tableau builder.

Over the course of 12 rounds, players try their very best, to optimize their collection by adding extraordinary pots and rare specimen. This might request snatching the odd leave from your opponents plant. The player with the trendiest collection (and most points) wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Greylune
description:
Greylune is a strategic game combining worker placement and adventure, set in a rich and captivating medieval fantasy world. Skillfully manage your villagers by placing them between the cards that form the city of Greylune, then remove them at the right moment to gather resources, recruit companions, acquire items, and visit important locations.
But the adventure doesn’t stop there: embark on quests, experience unexpected encounters, and accomplish heroic feats that you can proudly recount in the lively taverns of the city!

With its unique mechanics, intense interactions, and constant dilemmas, Greylune delivers a highly tactical experience where every decision matters.

—description from the publisher

name: Grimm Fairy Tales: Unbound
description:
The threat of The Dark One has never loomed larger over the realms of the Grimm Fairy Tales Universe in Zenescope’s first deck-building card game!

Combine heroes from the realms of Earth, Oz, Wonderland, and Neverland to defeat The Dark Horde!  Work together to stop them before time runs out and the universe is lost to darkness forever!

This is a self contained deck building game with TCG elements. To win the game you must defeat the all of the Villains and he Dark One that will appear throughout the game as you play.  Once you have defeated all four of the Villains, the game is complete and you are victorious!
 —description from the publisher

name: Grinivil
description:
Build Grinivil together, but win!

Players compete and collaborate to build a modern town and fulfill its residents' desires. Players take turns on the TAR (Time Action Ring) ring. Each turn a player performs takes a different time. All competing developers feel the impact of your actions and vice versa.

Players buy land, plant trees, build roads and develop the town. Effectively gain resources and construct houses, schools, shops, and other facilities wanted by Grinivil residents.

Some future inhabitants are open about their wishes for their living space. The desires of others remain hidden. To be successful, you must timely choose the proper actions, work with other developers and cunningly guide them to do what you want. Or better to say, what you think suits the modern and eco-oriented Grinivil the best.

You earn money and success victory points depending on how skillfully you develop a Grinivil.

—description from the publisher

name: Six Sojourns
description:
Six Sojourns is a reimagining of Eight-Minute Empire. It's a short area control game full of tough choices, creative strategy and tactics, and high player interaction.

Your goal in Six Sojourns is to grow your family and broaden their influence. Players take turns selecting a card from five on display. Each card has actions that let players build houses, gain ships, move, and gain new family members.  The cards also have special abilities and sets of icons that represent your family's expertise in various trades: cooking, carpentry, sewing, shoe-making, art, blacksmithing, and jewelry. Each game, you only select nine cards, and you'll be faced with meaty choices each turn as you focus on trades, abilities, or the map.

When all players have 9 cards, the game ends. Players count victory points and the player with the most points wins.

Each sojourn adds new cards and rules to the game. You can customize your experience by playing the six journeys as a campaign or play through each sojourn in order!

—description from the designer

name: Gundam Assemble
description:
Gundam Assemble is a tabletop miniatures game that uses approximately 2-inch-sized Gunpla for battles.

Each unit has abilities that reflect their unique characteristics, allowing players to enjoy scenarios that follow the original story, or diverge into situations that transcend the world of the Mobile Suit Gundam series; thus, providing both a sense of recreation and distinct battles.

name: Gunsen: The Battle for Toshi Ranbo
description:
In Gunsen: The Battle for Toshi Ranbo, Rokugan teeters on the brink of upheaval as the Great Clans—the Crab, Crane, Dragon, Lion, Phoenix, Scorpion, and Unicorn—clash for control of the legendary fortress, Toshi Ranbo. Once a strategic gem on the borderlands, the castle now stands at the heart of a war-torn battlefield, its banners contested by rival warlords seeking glory and vengeance. The air hums with the tension of drawn steel and elemental magic, as ancient shrines smolder and village alliances shift like the wind.

In this strategy game, players take on the role of ambitious daimyō representing one of the seven Great Clans: recruiting samurai heroes, drafting powerful orders, and building their clan's military might and strategic influence. Through tactical maneuvers and clever engine-building, they strive to fulfill seven victory objectives—from capturing and holding the coveted castle to completing secret missions and claiming sacred locations. Only one clan will write its legend in the blood-soaked chronicles of Toshi Ranbo.

—description from the publisher

name: Six Sojourns: Deluxe Edition
description:
The Deluxe version of Six Sojourns contains all the boards and expansions in one box! It includes the Volcano Expansion, Economy Expansion, Foil Title, Metal Coins, and Storage Tuck Boxes.

Six Sojourns is a reimagining of Ryan Laukat's third published design, Eight-Minute Empire. It's a short area control game full of tough choices, creative strategy and tactics, and high player interaction.

Your goal in Six Sojourns is to grow your family and broaden their influence. Players take turns selecting a card from five on display. Each card has actions that let players build houses, gain ships, move, and gain new family members.

The cards also have special abilities and sets of icons that represent your family's expertise in various trades: cooking, carpentry, sewing, shoe-making, art, blacksmithing, and jewelry. Each game, you only select nine cards, and you'll be faced with meaty choices each turn as you focus on trades, abilities, or the map.

Six Sojourns has a larger board and more cards than Eight-Minute Empire, in addition to many exciting new features.


     People can be moved in groups, instead of one at a time, allowing for more dynamic play. 



     You can now build ships to travel the seas, moving between regions. Players can also pay you to use your ships for travel over the water. 



     Sea spaces give majority and goods.



     Houses, which replace cities, are worth two control, and only one house can be built in each space.


Choose Your Sojourn
Each sojourn adds new cards and rules to the game. You can customize your experience or play through each sojourn in order!

—description from the designer

name: Hair Band
description:
Rock the stage and Rule the Strip!

In Hair Band, you're an upstart 80’s glam metal band vying for Hollywood’s next record deal. But to get it, you'll need to convince the label you're the next big thing - get awesome, get fans, perfect your show, and complete your demo to sign on the dotted line.

Each round, you’ll place your dice-as-rockers around Hollywood to write, rehearse, promote, gig, and party all night. But watch out! Musicians can be a reckless and unruly bunch. So, you’ll need to choose wisely to steer clear of drama that can derail your ambitions. The first band to complete 3  of the 4 record label requirements gets the deal and wins the game.

Hair Band is a dynamic dice placement, engine-building, and resource management game.

name: Hamlet
description:
Hamlet is an asymmetric card game for 2–4 players, with a playtime of 40–60 minutes, inspired by the inner conflict of Shakespeare’s tragic hero. During the game, players embody the emotions that tear Hamlet’s mind apart: Fear, Despair, Doubt, Envy, Pride, and Anger.

The game is played over two acts, each representing a key stage of the tragedy. In every act, players use character cards to compete for dominance across four different scenes. Winning a scene grants Influence points, strengthening that emotion’s hold over Hamlet’s thoughts. The more influence an emotion accumulates, the closer it comes to fully consuming Hamlet’s mind - and winning the game.

One role stands apart: Harmony. The player who takes on this special emotion also plays character cards, but instead of competing for dominance, their goal is to balance the conflicting emotions. By carefully steering the game toward balance, Harmony seeks to end the tragedy in a draw, denying all other players a clear victory.

—description from the publisher

name: Axis & Allies: Stalingrad
description:
In the summer of 1942, the German juggernaut could not be stopped, and both sides believed that Stalingrad would fall within mere weeks, but six months later, winter weather, a lack of supplies, and a failed relief effort saw the entire German 6th Army, or what was left of it, surrender.

In Axis & Allies: Stalingrad, you can take command of the German forces (plus some minor Axis powers) to see whether you can match their lightning thrust into the fateful city — or you can command the Soviet forces and put up a desperate defense as you await the winter and a massive counter-offensive that could turn the tide of the war. The famous city of Stalingrad gets its own game board featuring ferries, snipers, and notoriously close-quarters fighting. Buy time with blood, prepare for the winter, and keep your supply lines open!

Features


     Command the German or the Soviet Forces and fight in the famous city of Stalingrad!
     Buy time with blood, prepare for the winter, and keep your supply lines open!
     Contains two scenarios:  Race to Stalingrad and Operation Uranus!
     Over 150 plastic miniatures including 2 new units:  German StuG III Assault Gun & Soviet Katyusha Rocket Launcher!
     Two gameboards! The famous city of Stalingrad gets its own board and features ferries, snipers, and notoriously close-quarters fighting.
     Order cards control the flow of the game making learning the rules easy!


—description from the publisher

name: Happy Holiday
description:
Barcelona, ​​Paris – and then a side trip to Amsterdam? Three weeks of vacation in Europe call for careful planning. Players choose city tiles from seven popular European destinations in three different categories and enter them into their weekly planner. The tiles depict sights, shopping ideas, cultural tips, local dishes, and much more. They determine whether a city is visited during the week, on the weekend, or on a specific day. Longer stays earn more points, while the clever choice of transportation ensures smooth travel between cities. The best planning is rewarded with victory. For two to four players aged ten and up who want to put their vacation planning skills to the test.

—description from the publisher (translated)

name: Battle for the Deep: Powered by Axis & Allies
description:
In Battle for the Deep, four aquatic factions vie for control of the vast oceans: the Undersea Kingdom led by Coraline Oceanus, the Leviathans commanded by Scyphozoa Regina, the Protectors and their Turtle Mother, and the Denizens of the Deep, who are controlled by the necromancer Azazel Dreadborne.

After centuries of battle, it has become obvious that no one kingdom is powerful enough to bring peace to their world. The factions must choose an ally to win the day.

Battle for the Deep is a 2v2 battle experience where the players choose the teams and starting locations. Using gameplay mechanics from Axis & Allies, players battle for control of the underwater world.

—description from publisher

name: Diplomacy: Era of Empire
description:
The 19th Century was a dynamic, yet turbulent time when huge areas of the Ottoman Empire, the Indian sub-continent, China, Indochina, and the East Indies were fought over by competing empires.

In Diplomacy: Era of Empire, seven great empires — Britain, France, Russia, Turkey, China, Japan, and the Netherlands — vie for control as alliances are formed and trust is betrayed. Players negotiate and outwit one another in a delicate balance of co-operation and competition to gain dominance of the region. Players must rely on their own cunning and cleverness, not dice, to determine the outcome of this game of conspiracies and conquest.

Diplomacy: Era of Empire is a standalone game for new or experienced Diplomacy players that's based on 1994's Colonial Diplomacy, but with an updated map for balance purposes, the removal of certain mechanisms that required three pages of errata, and other rule tweaks.

—description from the publisher

name: Harbour of Fortune
description:
Harbour of Fortune is a strategic board game for 2–4 players, set in 1653 New Amsterdam.
Players lead rival merchant families, building canal houses, sailing ships, and navigating political power to amass wealth.

Designed around custom playing cards, each family plays by its own strengths.

Build canal houses along the bustling harbor, sail ships to secure trade routes, and invest in ventures to grow your fortune, all while navigating disasters and outsmarting opponents. On your turn, roll dice to determine actions, play custom cards like the Red Ace of Hearts or Diamonds for a “Great Investment,” and use wild cards to trigger unexpected events. Claim the title of Director-General, collecting taxes from opponents to gain an edge. The game ends after 8, 10 or 12 rounds, and the player with the most money, earned by controlling canal houses, household growth, amassing wealth, and achieving key objectives, wins. This game features premium components, including custom theme designed (poker) card decks, ships, canal houses, dice, and a Director-General hat, bringing the colonial era to life with historical depth and strategic gameplay.

—description from the designer

name: Hard Drive
description:
Step up to your keyboard and race to be the first to hack the mainframe in this analog game about racing in a digital universe.

In Hard Drive, players roll a pool of dice, then use them to navigate an evolving race course. Collect charge to set up drift combos or change your die results, collect plug-ins to gain abilities that help you or hinder your opponent, cross overclock spaces to increase your speed, and use course mods to hack the system and pull off crazy maneuvers like rotating course cards.

As you advance, the track recreates itself in front of you. The first player to cross the finish line wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Harry Potter Miniatures Adventure Game: Wizarding Duels Starter Box
description:
Wizarding Duels is here! A new beginning for the Harry Potter Miniatures Adventure Game. A faster and more intuitive game with fast-paced magic combat full of emotion and great epic moments.

Assemble your party of witches and wizards and challenge your rivals, now with amazing plastic miniatures fully assembled and ready to paint.

Join the battle for the Wizarding World with the definitive game in the wonderful Harry Potter saga.

—description from the publisher

name: Monsters Menace the World
description:
The year was 2005, and the largest animal recorded alive was the blue whale. But suddenly, the world was shocked by the appearance of terrifying creatures that could have the blue whale for a light midnight snack. Gargantis, Toxicor, Tomanagi, and others rampaged across the United States as the rest of the world watched in horror, in an event that has become known as the 2005 Rampage. Though many cities and famous landmarks were demolished, after a stunning battle for supremacy the monsters disappeared into the wilderness, the world was left to pick up the pieces. Now, many years later, the colossal creatures have discovered the rest of the continents of the world, and all of humanity are threatened by their gargantuan struggle.

Monsters Menace the World is a 2-4 player game where each player controls a Monster that they use to menace the planet in order to gain Infamy, as well as one Military faction to slow down or stop the other players’ Monsters from doing the same. Play as Chupacoloso, Konk, Nessie, Strigoika, Tomanagi, Zorb, and The Minions. The player with the most Infamy wins!

Features


     Control a monster and menace the planet to gain Infamy!
     Play as Chupacoloso, Konk, Nessie, Strigoika, Tomanagi, Zorb, and The Minions.
     Stop other players' monsters using your Military faction and cunning strategy!
     Features fresh and updated gameplay!
     Stunning art and graphic design along with detailed miniatures!


—description from the publisher

name: My Little Pony: Festival of Lanterns
description:
Join Twilight Sparkle and her friends as they visit Mistmane's Eastern Village, where they will celebrate all of their accomplishments in restoring Equestria to its peaceful ways by releasing Cutie Mark lanterns. As the glowing lanterns rise up to form patterns in the sky, they all can feel the magic of friendship abound!

In My Little Pony: Festival of Lanterns, players have a hand of tiles depicting various color arrangements of floating lanterns, as well as an inventory of individual lantern cards of specific colors. When you place a tile, all players — both you and your opponents — receive a lantern card corresponding to the color on the side of the tile facing them. Trade mooncake tokens for new lantern cards, and return lantern cards to claim a dedication tile worth points. After all tiles have been placed, all players get one final turn, then whoever has the most points wins.

My Little Pony: Festival of Lanterns features gameplay similar to Christopher Chung's earlier game Lanterns: The Harvest Festival with some modifications, including a solo mode and a "Gala" expansion in which you add up to four friend cards to the game from the sixteen included; on a turn, you can now spend mooncakes to use the power of a friend to fain a bonus lantern, make a second dedication on a turn, force someone else to trade lanterns with you, and so on.

name: Heavy is the Crown
description:
The king is dead! – The news fell upon the kingdom like a thunderbolt from a clear blue sky. The ruler did not leave a descendant who could take over the crown, and with it, responsibility for the fate of the state. None of the contenders have enough support to take power on their own. So they must do what they can to gain more prestige, form alliances with other pretenders, cooperate with them, and sometimes betray them - all in the name of the crown.

Heavy is the Crown is a board game for 2-4 players, in which players take on the roles of pretenders for the legacy and crown, in a kingdom that has lost its ruler.

Initially, each participant only observes and manipulates the struggles of the armies fighting for domination over the regions on the board that depictes the orphaned kingdom, to take sides with one of the factions at the most convenient moment, become its leader and steer it to a victorious campaign.

However, the political and military situation of the kingdom is so complicated that, in addition to brute force, the second important factor may be the right alliances, and even supporting one of the other pretenders in the final clash may be key to the ultimate victory.

—description from the publisher

name: Heist Team: The Fortuna Diamond
description:
Heist Team: The Fortuna Diamond is a tabletop game inspired by escape rooms and heist movies.

Gather your friends, plan the heist, and execute it as you face
interactive escape room puzzles, unexpected twists, and a dramatic finale. For 1 - 6 players.

It’s like an Escape Room meets Ocean’s Eleven, enhanced with digital interaction and RPG-inspired strategy!

name: Hell of a Deal
description:
Hell of a Deal is a cooperative poker game against The Devil Himself & all the minions of Hell. Of course, they all cheat! To compete, you’ll have to cheat like Hell...  and the more you do, the more doomed you all become.

Welcome to The Last Resort & Casino… and winning IS your last resort. To get to the Big Table, you’ll face off against diabolical bosses like Dedly Aloor, Jack Potts, The Brothers Dreadful, & Roul-ette, each of whom twists the game in unique ways.

It’s real poker - as far as playing poker in Hell goes, with you all trying individually to beat the house. Every Boss changes how you will approach the hand and has a bare minimum hand to beat, should their dealt cards not pan out.

It's a Texas Hold'em style game - and players get not two but three cards dealt to them (one up their sleeve for more options). You may earn powerful Favor cards that let you cheat, like making a four-card Flush, but at the cost of a Curse or suffering Temptation.

Your chips will earn you Souls (the coin of the realm) which you'll need at the Big Table against The Devil Himself - or betting one of your five Power chips will gain you immediate abilities, like revealing one of the Boss's cards, or taking a face-up discard into your hand. But lose the hand and your wagered chips flip over to deliver harsh penalties. Suffer too much Temptation and the game ends in a loss. Manage to win against The Devil Himself and you might just earn your way back to the living.

It has the feel of high stakes poker, with no cash on the table. And delivers a whole Poker Night in just 90 minutes.

The retail edition of the game features 52 custom 11.5g poker chips and six neoprene play mats inside the box. The Community board mats alone fill a 28"x20" space at the center of the table making it feel like a full poker table.

Hell of a Deal is made for board gamers who love poker - and even if you are relatively new to poker, its cooperative nature and in-game guides make it approachable enough for anyone to play.

Poker is 100% skill and 50% luck. 
Being a good cheat helps too.
Have a Lucky Day!

—description from the publisher

name: Hell Raisers in Kanawha County
description:
In Hell Raisers in Kanawha County, two players take on the role of two mining companies — Cabin Creek Consolidated Coal Company and Paint Creek Collieries Company — while the third player takes on the role of the uprising Labor Movement.

The game begins in early 1912 when the miners at Paint Creek demanded increased wages, increased transparency surrounding their payment, abolishment of Company-owned stores, acceptance of the union, and their right to free speech and peaceful assembly. The estimated cost of these demands was 15 cents (worth $3.66 today) per worker per day and was promptly refused. The workers of Paint Creek went on strike, and Cabin Creek followed shortly after.

Within the next year, martial law would be declared three times within the region. Countless people were evicted from their homes, the legendary labor leader Mary "Mother" Jones was sentenced to twenty years in penitentiary for inciting riot by reading the constitution, and an armored train with mounted machine guns was used to attack the strikers.

Hell Raisers offers an asymmetric twist on a Pax-style game. As one of the game's two mining companies, you'll concern yourself with speculation and mining logistics as you fight for larger market share. Meanwhile, the labor player will attempt to drum up popular support for their demands, shining a light on incredible acts of abuse and corporate maleficence while organizing strikes — but they must be careful. If they go too far, they may find the corporations bringing in paid thugs or even the national guard!

Hell Raisers includes modes for one, two, and three players and is easily playable in 60-90 minutes.

name: HELL: Legends
description:
The gates of Hell opened up and swallowed our world whole. Brave heroes stand against the hordes from Hell.

Hell: Legends is a hack & slay dungeon crawl board game you play cooperatively or in solitaire mode. Slay monsters and complete objectives to gain XP and level up your characters to make them more powerful. Each character offers a specialized skill tree. Each skill offers various levels. In combination with powerful items, each character is built exactly as you want.

Hell has 3 game modes Legends (story-driven - requires an app), Hunt, and Defense, allowing players to change up their game experience and victory requirements.

This game has mature themes!

—description from the designer

name: Skara Brae
publisher: Garphill Games; CHUR GAMES; Pixie Games; Renegade Game Studios; Schwerkraft-Verlag; Tesla Games
description:
Around five thousand years ago, a resilient group of farmers and hunters built a thriving community on the Orkney Islands of Northern Scotland. Rather than discarding their empty shells, broken tools, bones, and other waste, they used them to form large mounds of earth over hundreds of years. Later generations dug into these midden piles to create a series of rooms and tunnels to shelter from the harsh winds and cold winter months.

The aim of Skara Brae is to gather various resources in order to feed, clothe, and shelter the growing number of settlers. Players take turns drafting cards and using their workers to furnish, cook, craft, clean, and trade. At the end of each round, players need to provide for their settlers and will likely create more midden that needs to be cleaned up. After four rounds, the player with the most points wins.

—description from designer

name: Helm's Slain
description:
In Helm’s Slain, players are adventurers in a cooperative dungeon crawl campaign, defending the Kingdom of Helm from monsters emerging from nearby dungeons. Over nine levels of the dungeon, the party must survive increasingly difficult encounters and defeat the final threat.

Players choose from five character classes, each with distinct abilities that influence strategy. Turns are taken simultaneously, with players rolling dice to resolve combat and allocating hits across enemies. A character’s level determines how many d6 they roll—the higher the level, the more dice they can throw. Players pair these dice strategically in a unique combat system to land hits on enemies. Combat takes place on battle boards. Each board has a front row for melee, and a back row for spells and ranged attacks. Positioning matters: front-row heroes can't cast spells, and spellcasters forced into melee can't cast at all.  A light Game Master role manages scenarios and monster actions. A free companion app (optional) can run the GM and provides a player view for tracking stats digitally if players prefer.
  
The game includes over 550 unique monster encounters, combining cooperative tactics, resource management, and unpredictable challenges in every session.

—description from the publisher

name: Helpdesk Hero
description: Helpdesk Hero is a card game where players take on the role of Interns competing for a permanent position in technical support. During their shift (round), a player is assigned a Ticket and attempts to resolve it by playing an Solucion card. Success is determined by revealing the Character who opened the ticket and matching their Ticket Level and the Priority. The first player to accumulate the agreed-upon Productivity Points secures the job. The rest may continue playing, but the workload will remain the same as at the start of the game.

name: The Anarchy
publisher: Garphill Games; CHUR GAMES; Pixie Games; Renegade Game Studios; Tesla Games
description:
At the end of 1135, Henry I, King of England, died unexpectedly leaving no male heir to reign in his stead. Henry's daughter, Empress Matilda, believed she should rule by succession. However, the late king's favorite nephew, Stephen de Blois ("blue-a"), was quicker to the throne, and with the help of his brother, the Bishop of Winchester, was crowned king.

Those loyal to the empress were enraged by Stephen's coronation and would not accept him as their new ruler. Over the next eighteen years, England saw a breakdown in law and order as civil war spread throughout the country. This conflict came to be known as "The Anarchy"...

In The Anarchy, players take on the role of English nobles loyal to King Stephen. Over five rounds, players must build their domain, defend their castle from attacks by the approaching Angevin armies, and storm strongholds loyal to Matilda with their own crafted siege weapons. The player who can accumulate the most bravery, loyalty, influence and might — while avoiding discontent — will prove to King Stephen they are his most loyal ally, thereby earning his largest earldom.

—description from publisher

name: Heroes of the Pacific
description:
In Heroes of the Pacific, you take command of the American or Japanese armed forces in a no-holds-barred skirmish. The chosen scenario determines the number of troops you have under your command, as well as your objectives. All you have to do is win!

Fight on a battlefield made up of Terrain Boards containing Terrain Elements that your soldiers must deal with. 
On the field, your forces are represented by Unit counters. Each counter has all the information you need to play the Unit: Combat Value, Defense Value, Movement Value, as well as the Special Abilities the Unit can use.

To help you build and organize your army, Heroes of the Pacific offers a system of Recruitment Tiles and Recruitment Options. These tiles allow you to better track your army and its capabilities.

Each Game Turn, you secretly use your Order Tokens to command some of your Units and determine the order in which they will act.

Each of these Units may perform a Movement Action – to occupy a strategic position or capture an Objective – or attack the enemy by performing a Firing Action. You and your opponent activate Units one after the other, alternating between them. Once all your Order Tokens are activated, the rest of your forces will have the opportunity to maneuver. 
Then you prepare for the next turn.

But Heroes of the Pacific is not just a tactical combat game. It is also a heroic action game. For you will command not only loyal soldiers,
but also brave characters, cunning leaders with talents of their own.

The whims and eccentricities of the gods of war are represented by Action Cards, which can give you that little edge you're missing, or turn the tide of battle completely with a well-planned strategy.

In the end, the commander who best leads his troops in accomplishing his objectives wins. So read on, soldier, and prepare for the test of war.

—description from the publisher

name: Heroes of the Shire: Light & Shadow
description:
Heroes of the Shire is a turn-based combat game where players cast spells, use abilities, and learn combos to defeat their enemies. With 20 characters, 12 bosses, and over 800 spells and abilities, no two games will ever be the same.

There are 2 main game modes: Arena & Scenario.

Arena Mode: Players battle it out in the arena to become victorious. There are many different arena modes, with the most common being free-for-all and teams.

Scenario Mode: A cooperative mode where players travel through a themed scenario, defeating bosses and trash mobs via an adventure tile system. One pre-selected player (Villain) will defend the enemies, by taking actions for each enemy unit. Each scenario contains 3 epic boss battles which can last anywhere from 1.5 to 4 hours. Players can adjust the difficulty of a boss at any stage in the game, and players can join or leave a game as they see fit. Bosses' stats can be modified even mid-battle. A saved game sheet is available for those lengthy adventures that can't be completed in one evening.

—description from the designer

The base Light & Shadow box contains the following 6 heroes: Beastmaster, Clairvoyant, Hydromancer, Light Mage, Mercenary, and Shadow Knight.

4 additional heroes were added as an addon in the Gamefound campaign: Enchantress, Mad Scientist, Necromancer and Swashbuckler.

name: Hex Factor
description:
Hex Factor is a fast-paced abstract puzzle game for 1-4 players in which you are racing to claim territory by solving puzzles.
