You use colorful, wooden hexagonal tiles as puzzle pieces to try to replicate the black and white clusters of hexes — the puzzles —  on shared game boards. The tiles and the game board hexes have the same symbols in the middle (circle, star, hex) — that’s what you’re trying to match. But each tile is bi-colored (half violet, half yellow, for example), and you can only put the colorful tiles alongside each other WITH LIKE-COLORS TOUCHING (blue against blue, etc.)

There is no turn order. All players work at the same time. Each player starts with 10 tiles randomly pulled from the box lid. You will try to find a puzzle cluster on one of the game boards that you think you can replicate using the tiles you have. 
Once you have a puzzle cluster solved,  hurry up and claim that cluster (before one of your opponents does) by placing one of your 5 personal Marker-Cubes onto it. That puzzle can’t be solved again now that you’ve claimed it.

Now replace the tiles you just used with new ones from the box lid, so that you always have 10 tiles. 
Game ends when any player has used all 5 of her player markers. Then add up points: 1 point for an easy hex, 2 for a medium, 4 for a tricky one.

There are various bonus point opportunities to incentivize focusing on certain puzzles. These opportunities involve the mechanics of Area Majority and Set-Collection. The optional Attack Cards add a take-that dimension.

—description from the publisher

name: Hidden Realms: The Mummy's Tomb
description:
Hidden Realms: The Mummy’s Tomb is a single-page, Print & Play, Roll & Write dungeon crawl inspired by classic D&D maps. Draw polyomino shapes to map a new dungeon every game. Uncover treasure in the form of coins, keys, and magic items. Face deadly guardians, like oozes, skeletons, zombies, golems, mimics, and the Mummy itself. Plan carefully, because defeating it is not for the faint of heart. Are you up for the challenge?

The game is played over the course of 20 rounds. At the end of the 20th round, all players tally up their fame points, and whoever has the most wins. If you’re playing solo, you’re trying to set the most points possible or Beat Your Own Score. There are also achievements that can be completed in both solo and multiplayer modes.

During the game, the players roll dice and use their values to create the map and defeat monsters. The map is created by choosing and placing polyomino tiles. As the map expands, monsters, keys, coins and magic items will be found and collected. These items are useful in different ways. Defeated monsters provide coins but they also alert the Mummy to the intruder! The Mummy is the most powerful enemy and is quite hard to defeat!

Points are scored at the end of the game based on defeated monsters and the state of the map!

name: Hide the Body
description:
An easy to learn family/party card shedding game with artwork modelled after the classic inspector comic books like Dick Tracy.

Hide the Body is a fast-paced card game where players race to dispose of their victims’ bodies while trying to direct the Inspector and the Cadaver Dog to discover and dig up bodies hidden by their opponents!

Each player starts with six bodies. Players (the villains) have to dispose of them and have a limited number of holes in which to hide the bodies.  They can work together to get their bodies safely buried or get the Inspector or his cadaver dog to dig up their opponents’ bodies!

The first player to get rid of all six bodies is the winner.

—description from the designer

name: High Moon
description:
Drive your skelecows from your ranches through Death Valley to the breweries, where spooky liquors are distilled.

High Moon is a route-building spooky western game with very simple rules: On your turn, you simply place a card covering part of those already on the table and then place your markers to connect points of interest.

However, the decisions each turn are challenging: When placing cards, you can get extra route tokens but you may also give some to your rivals. When placing your route tokens, you may advance on 3 different spirit tracks or gain Spirit Tokens that grant you special bonuses, allowing you to place some extra route pieces.

High Moon is a game you can explain in 5 minutes, but it will challenge your mind during the game!

—description from the publisher

name: Hispania
description:
Hispania describes 1,500 years of Spanish and Portuguese history, from 320 BC to 1200 AD. During this period, many peoples and empires invaded Hispania. Many of these peoples or empires, called “Nations” in this game, attempted to colonize or conquer Hispania. But the new conquerors were unable to maintain their power for long. In turn, they were defeated by other invaders.

The game ends after the great migrations, at the dawn of the Reconquista of Muslim Hispania by its Catholic half.

In Hispania, each player controls several different Nations. During the game, the player accumulates victory points with each of their Nations. The player with the most victory points will be victorious at the end of the game!

During the game, a series of historical events unfold, which players will see represented by the various appearances on the scene of the nations that intervened in the history of Hispania, as well as numerous events that will occur over the course of the game.

—description from the designer

name: Hitman: The Board Game
description:
A 1-4 player competitive board game where success depends on improvisation, creativity, and surgical precision. Travel the world, infiltrate exotic locations, and eliminate high-profile targets - but this time, you won't be alone. Other agents have also been assigned the contract, and they’ll stop at nothing to sabotage your mission and deliver the killing blow. Guns blazing or silent assassin? The choice is yours.

The game is based on the Hitman video game franchise and was developed in collaboration with IO Interactive.

—description from the publisher

name: Hocus Pocus Hyperfocus: The ADHD Oracle Game
description:
Conjure up stories where the familiars are as fluffy as they are fiendish.
Hocus Pocus Hyperfocus is a passion project of two ADHDers years in the making. A game that expresses the absurdity and hilarity of our experiences with ADHD.  One that evokes the time game designer, Allison, lost her phone and then later found it *inside* a fruit salad she’d prepared for a party that evening. Or the time when feverishly preparing for a meeting, Brandy lit her notes on fire with the candle she forgot she had on her desk.

The stories in Hocus Pocus Hyperfocus are structured using the Deck of Distractions—an oracle deck full of both the tasks that your witch needs to accomplish as well as all the ways that she could be distracted from these very tasks. She has limited energy to complete a seemingly limitless number of tasks. Both task switching and hyper-focusing will take their toll on her over the course of the day.

We wanted to create game systems that reflect some of the ways our brains work, and then let our friends and family play with all of the wild inspiration and intense frustration that comes with such a brain?. And of course, we wanted there to be magic.

name: Hollow Pact
description:
Hollow Pact is a fast-paced, semi-co-operative game that blends horror, strategy, survival, and betrayal.

In the game, you join a group of scoundrels; enter a ruined town, the lair of a deadly Beast; grab cargo precious to you, your fellow scoundrels, and that Beast; play to your strengths; plead with the spirits for aid; and find a route to escape with the loot and your life - if you can - because even if the Beast doesn't get you, your fellow scoundrels might as they follow their own hidden agendas.

One player-controlled Beast uses its powers and the aid of spirits to hunt down the scoundrels and recover what they stole. The Beast also has secret goals, and accomplishing them makes thwarting the scoundrels easier. Hollow Pact plays out this thrilling, treacherous chase, with no two sessions playing the same.

The game includes a modular map and multiple scenario setups/goals as well as solo and cooperative play variations.

—description from the designer

name: Homestead Hyperjump!
description:
Homestead Hyperjump! is an epic co-operative space adventure game set at the dawn of the 25th century. Players assume the role of Homesteaders, intrepid pioneers from across the Sol System whose unique backgrounds and experiences make them ideal candidates for service aboard an experimental Homesteader-class vessel, a cutting-edge starship commissioned by the United Interests of Sol to explore the vast, uncharted galaxy.

Equipped with newly discovered hyperjump technology, you and your crew will navigate anomalies and chart dozens of sectors across three distant star clusters. Along the way, players will encounter strange phenomena, face dangerous foes, and make critical decisions that could shape the fate of humanity.

Each session of Homestead Hyperjump! immerses players in a galaxy brimming with life, danger, and discovery. Your choices will define the journey as you make first contact with alien civilizations, navigate perilous anomalies, and uncover the mysteries of uncharted space. With more than thirty narrative-driven scenarios, sixty branching paths, and countless decisions to make, no two games will ever be the same.

Choose from six key roles — captain, engineer, tactician, doctor, scientist, or pilot — and build your crew from eighteen characters, each with unique abilities essential for survival. Together, you'll manage your ship's critical systems, balance resources, and overcome escalating threats like space madness and hostile forces.

The future of humanity is in your hands. Will your crew rise to the challenge and discover a habitable world to claim as your own — or die trying?

—description from the publisher

name: Unstoppable
publisher: Renegade Game Studios; GaGa Games; Gen-X Games; Intrafin Games; Rexhry; Schwerkraft-Verlag
description:
On the city-planet of Ceres II, every alleyway invites a quick and quiet death. In the lush forests of Virenos, a single misstep could land you in the belly of a beast. The harsh wasteland of Mithras holds both grave danger and a great treasure for those who search its stacks of discarded rubbish. Amidst this chaos, you find yourself thriving, learning, and growing — a child of rank, touched by fate — but a new danger shadows the future of all three worlds. Gather your allies and sharpen your skills, for the darkest days are yet to come.

Unstoppable is a solo or co-operative roguelike, momentum deck-building game. Use card crafting and deck building wisely in the face of unlimited threats, maintaining action and card-draw momentum to become unstoppable!

The goal of Unstoppable is to defeat the boss, a world-ending menace that threatens the very way of life in your star system. Even as a heroic figure with cosmic potential, you won’t be capable of such a monumental task at the start. And there are many other smaller threats that you must keep at bay in the meantime. So train your powers, use your resources, and recruit new allies to your side.

• You win the game if you defeat the boss.
• You lose the game if your health is reduced to zero.
• You lose the game if the danger level is too high.

—description from the publisher

name: Wraith & The Giants
description:
Every 23 years since time unknown, giants have risen from the lands beyond, marching towards the village to feed. Your grandmother fought and defeated these monsters while she was alive; the duty had fallen to her upon the death of her grandmother, and so forth back as far as legend records. Your grandmother is gone, so you now must take up her sword and bow as a living shadow. Can you continue the story and protect the village from a catastrophic end?

Wraith & The Giants is a solitaire game of epic battles against elemental giants. Progress through four unique boss fights at three different wraith ages. Chain your card combos to scar and defeat the giants.

—description from the publisher

name: Diplomacy: The Golden Blade
description:
In the prelude to World War I, the seven great European powers contend for supremacy, both with their military might and political maneuvering.  In Diplomacy: The Golden Blade, players must choose and negotiate alliances carefully, knowing when to expand...and when to stab. Only the most cunning leader will emerge victorious as "The Golden Blade".

Diplomacy: The Golden Blade is a standalone card game for new or experienced Diplomacy players that features no player elimination.

—description from the publisher

name: Dungeon Crawler Carl: Unstoppable
description:
Don’t have a full party? No problem.

Dungeon Crawler Carl Unstoppable is a solo or 2-player co-op card-crafting deck-builder set in the World Dungeon. You’ll battle against neighborhood, borough, and city bosses while gearing up and leveling your chosen hero to survive and reach the next floor. Play solo or bring along your own Princess Donut for a co-op run!

Key Features:

Solo or 2-player deck-building adventure based on John D. Clair’s acclaimed Unstoppable system.
Card-crafting mechanic allows you to upgrade abilities and equipment as you play.
Manage risk as upgrading your abilities and equipment also causes the boss to grow in power.
Luciano Fleitas Returns for Artwork:
We’re thrilled to confirm that Luciano Fleitas, the long-time artist for the Dungeon Crawler Carl series, is returning to illustrate for both games!

name: Hostage Crisis
description:
Hostage Crisis is a game about teenage love-stories in which one player is out to rescue their lover held hostage and fighting to keep alive hope. The other player will do their best to suppress the rescue attempt at all cost.

The hero will be able to choose among different personality types, stats and equipment that will determine their approach for the rescue mission.

The villain will be able to choose between different characters that impact how the hero will have to go about rescuing their lover, type of enemies and overall mission objective.

—description from the publisher

name: Hover
description:
A brutal game of hummingbirds.

Play as hummingbirds thirsty for nectar… and a mate. The first bird to build a nest and perform a successful courting call wins the game.

Each species has different abilities that can alter your strategy:
Will you bully your way to the top? 
Bluff your way ahead? 
Or get clever and sneak in a victory?

But watch out! The chatter, competition, and annoying displays from other hummingbirds can easily distract your potential mate from paying attention as you expend precious energy to win their 1,260 bpm heart.

Based on real hummingbird behaviors, Hover is a strategic game featuring high-player interaction, tight action economy, asymmetric abilities, bidding/bluffing, and area control to create a highly immersive and intuitive game.

Be the hummingbird - beautiful and brutal.

name: Huey Leader
description:
Huey Leader puts you in the cockpits of the Vietnam War’s best Close Air Support aircraft. In Huey Leader, fly search and destroy missions to attack enemy troops, fly missions to deploy US ground troops into hostile Landing Zones and then provide Close Air Support to help the troops complete their mission, and even fly resupply missions to keep US Forward Bases supplied.  Huey Leader is based on our popular Thunderbolt-Apache Leader game system. If you've played TAL, you'll be up and flying missions against the Vietcong in minutes.

Huey Leader features an operation combat sheet that tracks the progress of enemy formations attempting to overrun your sector. You get to select the formation you want to engage each day and assign the air assets you think are best suited to the task.

A major part of the game is mission planning. You decide how to arm your aircraft and which pilots are best for the mission. Pilots are rated for skill level. Deciding which pilots to fly each mission is a major consideration. Your pilots will become fatigued with every mission. If you fly a pilot too often, his skills will degrade. Your pilots also gain experience with every mission flown. Should you keep flying the top pilots and further fatigue them to get the job done, or fly the new guys to prep them for the tough missions ahead?

Missions are quickly resolved using an area movement system to display tactical combat over the target. Speed and realism take top priority in this game. Terrain cards randomly generate each battlefield. The cards include mountain ranges that block lines of sight from both you and the enemy forces. If you plan it right, you get to fly nap of the earth through the canyons and come screaming over the ridgeline to rain fire down on the enemy before they can react. Beware! During each battle enemy air defenses will pop-up on the map to ruin your day, so watch were you’re flying!

name: G.I. JOE Heroscape: Rumble at the Rift Battle Box
description:
On Earth, G.I. JOE is the codename of a highly trained covert special missions force. Their enemy: COBRA, a terrorist organization bent on ruling the world!

Thanks to the bizarre inventions of the crazed Doctor Mindbender, both forces have been transported far from Earth, to another world known only as “Valhalla”. While they search for a way back home, both factions must get accustomed to this new place, where magic and mystery are afoot. All that is different here are the stakes. Now not only Earth hangs in the balance: for on Valhalla, when troops battle, they battle for ALL TIME!

This Battle Box includes everything two players need to jump into Heroscape, featuring 8 highly detailed miniatures, modular hex terrain, COBRA Fortifications, dice, Wound Markers, Order Markers, and all the Army Cards, rules, and scenarios needed for endless replayability. Duke, Scarlett, Roadblock, Snake Eyes, COBRA Commander, Destro, Storm Shadow, and Doctor Mindbender are here to wage all-out war in this new world! This Battle Box is fully compatible with all other Heroscape releases. Expand your forces with any Heroscape expansion for even greater battles!

Features

New Shadow Tiles and glow-in-the-dark Toxic Land and Water Tiles!
Snake Eyes strikes silently with deadly precision using Assassinate, and can bypass enemies to eliminate isolated targets using Phantom Walk.
Duke rallies your troops with YO JOE and unleashes coordinated attacks using his Lead by Example ability.
Scarlett outsmarts opponents, disrupts their plans with Now You Know, and delivers relentless follow-up strikes using Lethal to the Bone.
Roadblock lays down relentless suppressive fire with triple-target machine gun bursts using his Machine Gun Special Attack.
COBRA Commander strikes hard in close combat with Cutlassss of COBRA and slips away with I’ll Get You Next Time.
Doctor Mindbender manipulates allies with A Little Suggestion, controls enemy minds, and turns their own forces against them with Bend Mind.
Storm Shadow blinds enemies with the Nanite Smoke Grenade, carves through multiple foes in a single turn with Whirlwind Assault, and vanishes without a trace.
Destro arms his allies with powerful tech, shrugs off enemy fire with Beryllium Steel Mask, and can attack an additional time using the Personal Arsenal special ability.

—description from the publisher

name: Hunt for Blackbeard
description:
The Hunt for Blackbeard is on again. As Blackbeard, you must select your anchorage carefully, as you’ll need all your guile to survive. The hunters are coming — evade them, or prepare defenses and risk luring them in? As the Hunters, how long can you afford to press your stable of informants and arm your expedition? You know Blackbeard: he will not sit idle. His ambitions may expose him, but he is getting stronger day by day. How will you approach — a flushing strategy, or a precision strike? Be careful, as your quarry is apt to bite!

Hunt for Blackbeard is a two-player boardgame that portrays the effort in 1718 by the colony of Virginia and the Royal Navy to track down the notorious pirate Blackbeard (Edward Thatch) as he sought refuge in colonial North Carolina. It features the historical events, places, and personages involved in Blackbeard’s demise 300 years ago, and the real-world challenges of “golden-age” piracy and pirate hunting. One player takes the role of Blackbeard and the other the pirate hunters. Blackbeard seeks to commit acts of piracy or to enjoy a pirate’s life while remaining free. The hunters try to discern Blackbeard’s plans to thwart his piracy. The game may end in a battle in which either the hunters capture Blackbeard or the pirate wins by seizing a hunters’ ship as his prize!

In each of up to four turns, players draw secret tiles that gradually reveal opportunities for Blackbeard to pursue his piratical aims and for the hunters to interview informants who may know of Blackbeard’s whereabouts.

The players next commit Action pawns behind their screens to prepare defenses, sail, scout, or plan piracy. Blackbeard then secretly records any changes to the information on the main map. As the hunters take their turn, they inspect markers on the map — often secretly — as they seek Blackbeard, his camp, or any wake of his passage. Blackbeard will not know how much the hunters have learned before they strike!

Combat ensues if hunters catch up with Blackbeard’s sloop. If Blackbeard remains unchallenged at the right location, he carries out his piracy, placing gold cubes onto tiles among those drawn. Blackbeard can win through piracy while evading the hunters. But if a boarding action occurs, the winner automatically takes the game, enabling the pirate to win by girding for a fight and luring the hunters in.

-extract from publisher description, with a correction from the designer

name: Hunter's Crest: Darkwood
description:
Hunter's Crest - Darkwood is a 1-4 player cooperative campaign board game set in the mystical and treacherous forests of Darkwood, where players become hunters using cunning, strategy, and strength to capture or slay the enchanted wildlife that roams under the light of the full moon. It’s a choice-driven, narrative-rich experience played over multiple sessions, blending elements of strategy, adventure, and survival into a unique board gaming experience.

In Hunter's Crest - Darkwood, players are thrust into a fantastical world where each full moon brings about the resurrection of the wildlife with the "Kill Memory System," a groundbreaking mechanic where animals not only come back to life but remember previous encounters with hunters, adapting and becoming more cunning with each cycle. This feature ensures a dynamic gameplay experience, challenging players to evolve their strategies and adapt to the ever-changing behaviors of their prey.

Players start their journey at the Eden Lodge, a hub for hunters to prepare for their expeditions into the woods, boast about their conquests, and trade valuable resources and animal parts harvested during the hunt. Here, hunters can upgrade their equipment, purchase new grappling hooks for strategic navigation during hunts, and prepare for the challenges that lie in the shadowy depths of Darkwood.

The game unfolds through a series of hunts, each presenting unique challenges and opportunities. Utilizing the innovative Grappling Hook System, players can traverse difficult terrain, escape impending danger, or engage in thrilling combat with beasts. Success in the hunt requires teamwork, strategic planning, and the ability to think on one's feet.

As the campaign progresses, the decisions made by players at the Eden Lodge and during hunts have lasting effects on the world and the narrative, shaping the future of Darkwood and the hunters' quest within it. Players must manage their resources carefully, develop their lodge, and strengthen alliances to ensure their survival against the dark forces that lurk in the forest.

Hunter's Crest - Darkwood is not just a game of hunt and battle; it's a saga of survival, strategy, and the bonds formed in the face of the unknown. With multiple paths to victory and countless ways to fail, the fate of Darkwood and its hunters hangs in the balance. Will you rise to the challenge and carve your name into the legends of the forest, or will the woods claim you as another forgotten soul? The hunt begins.

—description from the designer

name: Risk G.I. JOE: Special Missions
description:
In RISK G.I. JOE: Special Missions, 2-4 players each join one of two factions — G.I. Joe or Cobra — and seek to complete missions or resolve plots in an effort to score the most objective points (OP) after three rounds of play.

One of five master scenarios guides the action, leading to conflicts erupting in hotspots around the world. The game includes multiple unit types — GIs, Skystrikers, Wolverines, Cobra Troopers, Rattlers, and H.I.S.S. — with variable movement, initiative, and battle bonuses, and units defeated in battle are only temporarily lost, cycling back into play over time. Action cards create new avenues for moving and gaining units not present in the traditional game, and scenario and objective cards will influence player strategy.

name: Iberia: Kings and Emirs
description:
Welcome to 11th century Iberia! In this historical game, take on the role of a king or an emir and compete to build the greatest kingdom on the peninsula through territory expansion, constructing buildings and wonders, and by attracting a diverse court. As you expand and grow your kingdom, the population faiths of your kingdom will change depending on the lands you conquer, the buildings you build, and the courtiers you play. Be sure to maintain balance between the faiths of your kingdom and your ruler's political stance or suffer the consequences through lost income or victory points.

To play Iberia, a player's turn takes place over four steps.  

     Step 1, players collect maravedi coins (income).  
     Step 2, players use their maravedi to take actions.  Some of these actions include, constructing buildings and wonders, training soldiers, building castles, reforming politics, or upgrading mobility. During this step players may also play, and gain the benefits of, any courtier cards they have acquired.
     Step 3, players move their army to consolidate or take new lands.
     Step 4, if a player moves into region they do not occupy, they immediately enter battle and move to subdue the region.  If the player wins and subdues the population, they gain income, and their populations rise on their kingdom board.


Once all four steps are complete, play passes to the next player. Game play continues over a series of turns until on player raises the required number of flags or a player acquires two wonders.

—description from the designer

name: Robo Rally Dice
description:
Robo Rally Dice is a competitive racing game full of robotic pandemonium! Use real-time dice rolling to program your robot to tag checkpoints, attach powerful upgrades, and turn this dreary old warehouse into a fabulous, fast, and frenzied fun factory! Robo Rally Dice is a standalone game, but the gameboards can be used as an expansion for any version of Robo Rally.

—description from the publisher

name: Imperial Borders
description:
With Napoleon's abdication in 1815, the major powers of Europe convene the Congress of Vienna in Austria.

Explore an alternate history with each player taking the reins of a great European nation of the period. It is now up to each of you to decide how the borders of Europe will be redrawn.

Establish a dominating presence of power and wealth through clever diplomacy and strategic warfare.

Features include:

     Simultaneous & secret plotting of movement orders on a dry-erase planning map
     Free-form diplomacy, negotiations, and backstabbing
     Dice-based combat system with tactical stance choices
     Battle with cannons, cavalry, and infantry columns on land
     Battle with frigates and ships of the line in ports or at sea
     Purchase new forces with gold taxes collected from territories
     Earn prestige points by winning battles, earning elite forces, and controlling territories
     Earn and then clip shiny medals to your lapel that indicate your sublime grandeur (and offer in-game bonuses) 


—description from the publisher

name: Impresario: A Colosseum Card Game
description: The Emperor demands entertainment! As an Impresario, you will produce the greatest and grandest spectacles to earn the emperor's favor. But beware, as your rivals will also try their best to snatch the best Performers, as they are also vying for the coved spot alongside the emperor. Through savvy market manipulation and skillful tableau management, you will build the greatest troupe of of performers the world has ever seen, spreading the legend of your name throughout time immemorial.

name: Impropriety: A Regency Era Game
description:
An exquisite, witty, Regency era board game of sabotage, scandal, opportunity & intrigue for Jane Austen & Bridgerton fans alike!

Impropriety is a set-collection, story-based game in which players take on the roles within a family of young ladies in English society in the early 19th century to win the affections and eventual proposal of the exceedingly wealthy Lord Duffling. Players seek to acquire the most attractive ensemble for the Grand Ball, all the while navigating through cutting sabotage, ruinous scandal, delicious opportunities, delightful intrigue, and the occasional tragedy. With over 84 different scenario vignettes with multiple choice-based outcomes, the story is varied each time with infinite replayability!

The Lancaster sisters must travel through the “ton” to attain the most exquisite gown, luxurious accessory, stately transportation, and brotherly escort. They then ascend the stairs to the ball, where they will socialize, dance, and attempt to woo the rich eligible bachelor, who leaves much to be desired other than his deep pocketbook. The marriage game is a dangerous sport, as many a scenario will reveal obstacles that the players must attempt to navigate with social grace… but achieving your goals may require creative manoeuvring outside of society’s definition of what is ladylike. Shall the players attempt to maintain their dear Mama’s ideal of superior morality, or wade into the waters of impropriety to gain the advantage?

Utilize charm, cunning, boldness and wit to fill your dance cards and marry into your rightful place at the peak of Society.

Inspired by the literature of Jane Austen, the drama of Bridgerton, the zany humour of Austenland, the scandal of Lost in Austen, and paying homage to the thousands of women who found themselves in similar social-climbing circumstances in the Regency era, this game (both competitive and solo modes) features an original cast of over 50 characters, 84 unique vignettes of story, stunning historical Regency era illustrations and fashion plates, and countless moments of sheer hilarity that will not soon be forgotten.

Impropriety is simple to learn, light in game play, stunning to table, and everlasting in impression. So, who shall the next Lady Duffling be?

—description from the publisher

name: In Fours to Heaven
description:
In Fours to Heaven is a strategic level board wargame about the first campaign of the Second World War. Battle for Poland, that took place September 1st to October 6th, 1939.

The game portrays dramatic clash between Poland and Hitler's Third Reich. It was the first introduction of what will be later called "Blitzkrieg" tactics. From military point of view, Poland was doomed from the start due to many reasons. Because of this, this story cannot be told without taking them into consideration. The biggest issue for Polish defenders was stubborn implementation of defensive "Plan West". It assumed Allied intervention or opening of the second front days after the potential attack. Many flaws of the plan and pointless actions, if the circumstances were different, caused quick downfall of Polish defenders.

The story in this game is told mostly from the Polish perspective, introducing Polish propaganda, morale and General Staffs standpoint. All of this combined creates many layers of the campaign beyond simple hex&counter wargame, which is crucial to the gameplay and makes Polish player really decide, how to play.

The game covers the whole campaign from it's start on the September 1st to the bitter end on October 6th and can be played in many ways, as a whole campaign or in series of smaller scenarios. Unit scale is division/regiment, 1 hex covers 10km of the real terrain.

—description from the designer

name: Infernal Machine: Dawn of Submarine Warfare
description:
The time: late evening
The date: 17 February 1864
The Place: Breach Inlet, South Carolina

Standing in the submarine’s forward hatch, Lieutenant George E. Dixon pulled his cap down and tightened up his oilskin watch coat. The February sea cut through to his bones. This was the third night he ventured from behind Battery Marshall on Sullivan’s Island, and his seven-man crew was grumpy from having had no luck spotting, let alone attacking even one of the Yankee warships blockading Charleston harbor.

Dixon fingered the dented $20 gold piece in his trouser pocket. It was a gift from Queenie, his sweetheart, a keepsake that already earned its place aboard ship. A few months earlier at a wooded tangle of a place called Shiloh, the coin stopped a minie ball from shattering his leg. The dent reminded him how fickle fate and fortune are in this war, and it reminded him of home. He had that coin engraved “Shiloh April 6th, 1862. My life Preserver” and added his initials “G.E.D.”, so sure was he of the coin’s power.
Well, tonight that power was napping. Frustrated and cold, Dixon took one last look to the southeast through his telescope. The weather wasn’t likely to improve and he hoped that this would be the night he and the crew of the “CSS Hunley” would strike a blow against the Yankee blockade.

Here now… was that a light?
There!
And once again, low and to the south-southeast. A light!

He rapped the coin against the hull to startle the men. “Look sharp,” he muttered. Then, in a voice low and tense, he said “Look sharp and prepare to crank!”

Game Overview

Infernal Machine: Dawn of Submarine Warfare is a solitaire board game that casts the player in the role of inventor/entrepreneur in mid-19th century America. The game is set during a historical moment when the business environment has gotten rather dynamic – it is the tumultuous landscape of the American Civil War. The player’s task is to design, build, and put to use a submarine during that war.

Infernal Machine can be played either in scenario form or campaign. In a campaign, you can choose the city or port where the project’s machine shop will be located. Since construction materials and labor costs money, your role as entrepreneur comes into play as you seek out Investors to join your team; their cash will provide the funds that help your Fishboat take shape. As Inventor, your design gives form and substance to the size and shape of your submarine, and to its capabilities. Will it carry a snorkel? Will its prow be an armored ram? Will it have dive planes? Will it push a spar torpedo? Will it be powered by the muscle strength of a crew cranking the propeller or will you install a boiler engine?

To bring blueprints to life, you will need to hire Mechanics, whose engineering expertise keeps the machine’s construction on schedule. Once assembly is complete, your Mechanics can join the crew, using their repair capability to keep the machinery and the vessel running smoothly. Journeymen can also lend a hand on the shop floor and inside the Fishboat, while Sailors bring nautical know-how as well as sheer brawn.

While that machine shop is busy with the submarine’s construction, the game reminds you that the war drags on and it is an unstable business environment. Prices for materials and labor fluctuate. Current events can affect your construction schedule and your machine shop’s performance. Public, and even personal circumstances may force your hand. You may decide to push your Fishboat into the water before you feel it is optimal, or push your crew into battle with little training.

In this game you assign crew, taking their characteristics into consideration, such as morale, strength, engineering expertise. Your first mission will most likely be a simple affair, propelling the infernal machine forward, submerging, turning about, and returning to the surface. It will garner valuable experience that improves your crew’s Training Level. But even that simple affair could prove treacherous. Will the Fishboat drift? Will it sink and become irretrievable? Will your crew panic in the dark as they breathe in the exhalation of their comrades in that cramped machine? Will you be forced to evacuate the crew and salvage the Fishboat later? Will the crew survive the ordeal?

Later missions will be directed at the enemy. In this game, you may play either side, Union or Confederate. There are a variety of missions and targets. Will your Fishboat be aimed at the Federal blockade? Will it pull a mine at the end of a rope, or push a torpedo at the end of a spar? Will the crew survive contact with the enemy? Will they survive their own weapon’s detonation? Perhaps the nature of the mission will be quite different. Will you carry a spy into enemy territory? Will your Fishboat unload a raiding party?

Secrecy is vital. Will you send your machine out under a moonless sky? That will help conceal crew and machine but it will make navigation difficult. Will you limit the number of machinists and investors, thereby reducing the chance of rumor or gossip leaking out? Too few and you compromise your machine’s capabilities. Your Fishboat’s chances are much better if that machine is kept a secret, but it is a cantankerous machine that will punish mistakes.

A successful mission means your coffers will be filled with prize money. This is a capitalist’s war, and the War Department is offering juicy bounties. In contrast, there are many ways to fail. Coming back without making contact with the enemy is one way, but it could be far worse. Will you add the names of your crew to the Rolls of the Missing?

Scenarios and Campaign

Historical scenarios use only part of the rules to present such events as the CSS Hunley’s successful attack outside Charleston Harbor in 1864. It was the first time a submarine sank its target, a landmark event in military history. The heart of the game is the campaign, which allows you to design and build your Infernal Machine, select a crew, train that crew, and perform missions against the enemy. You manage funds and personnel, and navigate the fortunes of war as well as the waterways in enemy territory. A scenario will take approximately two hours to play while a campaign can last several gaming sessions as it spans the calendar from 1861 to the end of the war in 1865.

Sequence of Play

Each monthly turn gives you an opportunity to recruit personnel (Investors, Mechanics, Journeymen, or Sailors), each represented by a deck of cards. Each recruit comes with one or more benefits as well as costs or drawbacks. An Investor, for example, may be a generous provider of funds, but he may insist on being the captain of the ship. Does he know what he’s doing?! A Sailor may prove to be strong and cool under pressure, but he may be clumsy. Will that clumsiness jeopardize his crewmates?

Each turn also provides you an opportunity to work on your Fishboat. You purchase Bulkheads and other major sections of the submarine, each represented by tiles. They cost funds and require engineering expertise to incorporate into a seaworthy vessel. You also purchase a variety of mechanisms as you make decisions about the capability of your Fishboat.

Recruitment and Building is followed by the passage of time when the Month marker is moved forward on the calendar. Debts must be paid, if you have any, and you must check the Fortunes of War table to see if something unexpected happens that month. Will prices rise? Will one of your Journeymen get engaged and leave your shop? Will the enemy shell the wharf where your Fishboat is waiting to go into action? Will you get an offer to use your machine shop to make parts for the War Department, giving you a contract and additional funds? Will the enemy capture the town, forcing you to move to another location? Each month has its own table of random events, and there is one set used when playing Union and another when playing Confederate. This adds to the feel of the historical experience while also increasing replayability. The Confederate experience is quite different from playing the Union. The latter is an industrial business environment while the Confederacy’s economy gradually spirals into oblivion.

Each month you have the option to finish the turn by taking your seaworthy Fishboat into action. There are four Action Boards in the box, each providing its own unique historical and nautical conditions (Charleston, Mobile, New Orleans, and the James River from City Point to Richmond).

You setup a mission by establishing meteorological conditions on the Action Board (drift direction, drift intensity, visibility, and weather), and assign each crewman a position inside your Fishboat. Will you call off the mission because the current is too strong? Will you wait for a better opportunity, or will you push ahead despite the risk?

Your submarine will move from one space to the next as it executes its mission. During a mission you assign jobs to each crewman (crank, repair, rally, or operating a mechanism). This is new technology and the submarine is an untried machine, so malfunctions are likely and you will assign crew to manage and hopefully repair them. In many cases, just getting out there and locating a target is a victory of sorts, and getting the crew back home can feel like a triumph. Of course, your mandate is to do more than make contact with the enemy and survive. To gain prize money, you will have to prove your machine’s efficacy against the enemy. It’s an old story: higher the risk, greater the reward.

If you manage to navigate your machine and crew to make contact with its target, action shifts to the Tactical Board. There, the Fishboat closes in and you hope conditions are right so that it remains concealed. Decisions you made leading up to this tense moment have put your crew in a good position, or maybe in a bad one. In either case, history is watching.

Game Components
4 Actions Boards (12” x 18”),
1 Mechanics Board (8” x 18”),
1 Tactical Board (8.5” x 11”),
3 Countersheets (including boat tiles),
3 Card Decks (Recruits, Navigation, Discovery),
2 d10 dice
Booklets and Player Aids

-description from publisher's website

name: InfiniBrix
description:
InfiniBrix is a rules light, story-first tabletop game that empowers families and friends of all ages tell wild, wonderful stories and play epic action scenes with their own construction bricks and miniature figures! If you can build it, you can play it!

InfiniBrix is a game where one player helps guide the story as the "Game Manager," while the rest take on the role of Figments - aka "Figs" - on heroic adventures!

Play happens in three phases:

- BUILD MODE - create your Fig in minutes with our story-focused, multi-genre character creation system.​
- STORY MODE - collaboratively create crazy stories with no-prep, fill-in-the-blanks adventure paths, then play through to see how your Figs face epic challenges!
- ARENA MODE - build, break, and modify Figs, terrain, and items for zany tactical action, whether a battle, capture-the-flag, or a massive title showdown in a sport you dream up!

Resolve every challenge with our descriptive, fiction-first dice pool mechanic, where every advantage adds a Triumph die, and every Challenge a Trouble die!​  Will you battle to victory?

—description from the designer

name: INKtentions
description:
In INKtentions, players become cunning octopuses vying for the most food in the treacherous depths of the ocean. Using ink clouds, sneaky hiding spots, and well-placed tentacle maneuvers, they must outwit their rivals while dodging hungry sharks and relentless eels. Strategy and deception go hand in hand as players secretly place cards, protecting themselves—or misleading their opponents—while striving to collect the most valuable food.

Each round, players take turns playing one of their 9 cards (one for each brain) facedown near a scoring pile. After 8 cards are played (one for each arm) the cards are revealed and resolved. Ink cards protect everyone in a pile, but at the cost of helping opponents. Hide cards offer personal safety but leave others exposed. Punch cards shift the tides, moving threats or disrupting well-laid plans. With every decision, players must weigh risk and reward—protecting their own octopuses while ensuring their rivals don’t get ahead.

At the end of each round, surviving octopuses claim food, with set collection bonuses encouraging competition for the best meals. After three rounds (one for each heart) the player with the most food wins. INKtentions is a game of calculated risks, clever plays, and just the right amount of betrayal, where only the craftiest cephalopod will reign supreme!

—description from the designer

name: Sea Scroll
description:
Sea Scroll is a quick-playing, deceptively strategic set collection card game where players will guide schools of fish from the Reef, or the central discard area, to their personal Habitat to form schools of fish, or card sets in front of them.  At the end of the game, each player will combine their schools with fish cards remaining in their hands to score!

Each species of fish is evaluated to see who has collected the most of that type fish. The player with the most of each species scores point equal to that fish’s value, while all other players lose points equal to its value!

Collect, Curate and Combine beautiful fish to emerge the victor!

—description from the publisher

name: Insania
description:
Insania is a highly-immersive cooperative horror adventure game for 1-4 players. Step into the sandals of Roman legionaries defending the empire from nightmarish monsters. Set in a terrorized town, players must explore, scavenge for items, destroy dimensional portals and fight to keep their sanities. As you progress, develop your character’s stats and create unique item combinations to receive powerful blessings.

Choose from some of the bravest sons of Rome: Triarius, a centurion whose commands may turn the tide of battle, Laverna, a diviner who reads the future in the entrails of her dead enemies; Atticus; a fierce gladiator with melee mastery; Quintus, a physician with a sharp mind and sharp tools; among others.

The game comprises several missions that can be played independently. For groups looking for longer thrills, an expansion (sold separately) brings a thrilling legacy-lite campaign. For those who find it hard to hold a steady group for many sessions, INSANIA also introduces short, one-night campaigns.

Insania’s unique blend of dungeon crawling and strategy elements crafts an immersive experience where your every victory feels hard-earned. The system rewards cooperation, making each session a collective catharsis.

Insania draws inspiration from H.P. Lovecraft’s writings but has its own mythos, built around Ose, a demon from Ars Goetia. The narrative, driven by player decisions and full of “can’t unsee” moments, wouldn’t be out of place in a Tarantino film or Garth Ennis comic book. Players face sensitive content and immoral choices, such as whether or not to kill babies or recapture runaway slaves, making INSANIA a game for mature audiences.

How to Play:
In your turn, you must first replenish your hand of effort cards, drawing up to three - your limit is five cards at any moment. Then you take three actions, such as: movement, combat, breaking mystical barriers, item scavenging, destroying dimensional portals, inventory, revealing districts etc. Some points of interest in the map, like the circus, the forum and public baths have their own action you can take.

For most of your actions, you will need to use effort cards to meet a certain value. You can play only one card per action, unless you have cards that connect to each other, in which case you can add their values.

When your character is attacked, you may choose where to take damage: on your armor or shield (if any), health points, or effort cards (representing a dodge, block or parry). You can even human shield your partners with your effort cards.

Your character may sometimes stumble upon an encounter: narrative scenes in which you must make a choice that may lead to upgrades and bonuses, but will ultimately show you what kind of person you really are.

Turn order is defined by an initiative queue comprising all characters and enemies on the board. Beware: some enemies have the ability to cut in line, frustrating your plans. Every time you reach the end of the queue, an event happens, usually adding to the difficulty of the game.

Some enemies and conditions damage your sanity. If it drops to zero, your character gets a mental disorder: a permanent handicap that affects the way you play for the remainder of the game. Does it make the endgame easier? Well, no.

You win the game by meeting the mission’s goal. You lose if: a) all characters die or b) the deck of effort cards ends. Some missions may have additional conditions of failure.

Key Features:
Unique setting: Inspired by H.P. Lovecraft, but with a distinctive mythos, INSANIA’s universe is gory, sexy, unsettling and full of WTF moments, offering adult content board games seldom (if not never) display.

Handmade Art Style: Watercolor artwork by a master of “demonic erotica” adds an original and haunting visual appeal.

Over 40 highly-detailed, NSFW Miniatures: Immediately immerses players in INSANIA’s twisted world.

Strategic Gameplay: INSANIA replaces dice rolls with card-driven mechanics reminiscent of games like Pandemic, making strategy and cooperation paramount.

Unapologetic insanity mechanics: Losing your mind isn’t the end for your character. Just makes the challenge even more impossible.
Character Development: Enhance your hero’s abilities and stats to better face the horrors ahead.

Solo mode: Cause sometimes you want glory to be yours and yours alone.

—description from the designer

name: Intelliwar: Accession To The Throne
description:
In Inteliwar, players will employ all their tactical and strategic skills to claim their rightful place on the Silver Throne. To do that, you will move units around the board, activate special abilities, upgrade your forces, and strike with calculated attacks. The goal is to eliminate the enemy Prince or wipe out all enemy units except the Prince. The first player to fulfill at least one of these two victory conditions wins.

At the beginning of the game, units are drafted. All of them are unique, so choose carefully!

On their turn, a player places Activation tokens on two different Unit Cards that don’t have Activation Tokens, with the player-colored side facing up. When you place an Activation Token on a card with the player-colored side up, you “activate” this unit. On a turn, each Unit may perform up to 2 of the following actions: Move, Attack, or Use a Special Ability.

A player immediately wins the game when they fulfill at least one of the following victory conditions: 
eliminate the Enemy Prince OR eliminate all the enemy Unit Tokens except for the Prince.

—description from the publisher

name: Interregnum
description:
The death of a king without an heir begins a time of anarchy and power struggles. The powerful begin a race - the start of a new dynasty is at stake. 
In this fast and simple card game, each player gathers card subjects and sends them to one of his five fiefs. The serfs give their seniors access to their skills, as well as give them prestige and silver. After 12 short rounds, the holder of the most money and prestige wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Into the Machine
description:
Do robots dream of electric sheep after a long day of manufacturing widgets and thingamabobs? Or do they sleep at all? Maybe they break off into teams and hop into the machine to blow off a little steam with a race for anodic glory and a chance at upgrading themselves into more skilled bots.

Into the Machine is a highly tactical race in which circle-bots race to one end of the machine to tag in their hex-bot teammates who race in reverse on the same track to win. A pit crew of bots outside the machine are sent to work the terminals, moving and manipulating their teammates in the machine.

—description from the publisher

name: Invasion Z: Zombie Genesys
description:
Invasion Z is a Zombie Survival Game. The story is about an outbreak of Zombie-like creatures after a Meteor disintegrates in the atmosphere raining a strange color into Buenos Aires City. This rain causes the population to get sick and then die, only to become the dreaded ghouls that crave for the flesh.

Gameplay has 5 basic steps:

1) MAINTENCANCE: Operatives untap all the used items and Profile card, and Mission penalties are applied to the main Counters.

2) OPERATIVES STEP: Heroes move around the board, hunting zombies, rescueing people, finding useful items and trying to avoid the inevitable fate that awaits them.

3) ZOMBIES MOVE: All zombies move closer to the base in the center of the board.

4) EVENTS STEP: Depending on the levels of the Event Counter one or two events might happen. A special die is rolled and the event takes effect.

5) ZOMBIE STEP: Depending on the levels of the Zombie Counter one or two extra zombies will be added to the Zombie Roll. Usually 1 die per rescuer is roll (between 3 and 4 die total) plus any extra die added by the Zombie Counter placing zombies in the suburbs of the map. A 6 rolled is a miss and do not adds any zombie.

The objective of the game is to rescue the 8 survivors that stand hidden on the locations of the outer ring of the board and then return to the center tile to be retrieved by the rescue team.

The Heroes lose if at any time there are 3 zombies on the central location tile.

The Items deck works as a counter that will increase the difficulty as the game progresses with some "bad luck" cards that can be a devastating force against the heroes.

There are several ways of losing the game and only one way to win so usually players will feel very rewarded when they win as it´s usually on the edge of oblivion.

name: The Fox in the Forest Deluxe
description:
Fairy Tales come to life in this deluxe version of the beloved trick-taking game.

Use special abilities to change the trump suit, lead even after losing a trick, and more. Aim for the majority of tricks each hand, but don’t get greedy! If you win too many, you will fall like the villain in so many fairy tales.

This deluxe edition includes three all-new modules: special cards, goal cards, and poison cards! Features new illustrations, foil stamping, and acrylic tokens.

—description from the publisher

name: Ion Core
description:
Enter Ion Core, a thematic sandbox game set in a post-apocalyptic dystopian world. Humanity has been driven to piracy to secure a brighter future and it's up to you to guide your faction to victory!

Procedurally generated maps by placing tiles using specific actions ensure a diverse and different seafaring and treacherous landscape each time you play. How will you navigate in order to brave the perils of Ion Core’s world? Plan your course well or enemy factions will take all the glory!

Enjoy an adventure with minimal luck factor – actions like Scavenge or Plunder can be enhanced using a deck or upgrades to allow players to either enhance or mitigate chances, shifting the outcome to your favor.

Pillage or visit cities to upgrade your ship, gather spoils and forgotten relics, hunt dangerous beasts, enlist new crewmembers or entertain them to increase their morale, trade your way to riches or plunder your way to victory!

With a variety of ways to play and different aspects to focus on, there is never a dull moment - reading through your opponent’s intent is just as important as planning your own. No matter how you choose to advance, make sure to set your sights on controlling the energy source of this cruel world, and gather the most renown at the end! The choice is yours!

Beautifully hand-drawn artwork and components will suck you into Ion Core’s world and its unparalleled aesthetic! Each character comes to life through backstory and art to immerse players and make bonds, not just progress.

But beware, you are not alone in sailing the seas... Enemy ships and a mysterious, relentless adversary haunt your every move so plan well, take risks and brave your way to total control!

—description from the publisher

name: Isabel: The War of Castilian Succession
description:
Isabel is a two-player game portraying the War of Castilian Succession (1475-1479). It is a free print-and-play game: all necessary files are posted here.

The death of King Enrique IV in 1474 created a domestic crisis in the Kingdom of Castile. The two contenders for the throne were Isabel, Enrique’s half-sister, and Juana, the 13-year-old daughter of the late monarch. Both women counted with powerful allies in their fight for the throne: in 1469 Isabel’s had wed Fernando, heir to the Crown of Aragon, and Juana married King Alfonso V of Portugal during the early stages of the war. In Isabel, the players assume the role of Isabel and Juana and their respective allies as they compete to garnish domestic and international support for their cause. The players face a multifaceted conflict fought as much in the arenas of Spain and the African coast as in the undecided hearts of the Castilian nobility and population at large.

Over four rounds, the players compete by maneuvering troops on the Iberian Peninsula and the Atlantic coast, and by gaining the alliance of various noble houses, public opinion, and international powers. Isabel incorporates streamlined mechanics that are attentive to the historical circumstances of the conflict. Every turn, players face multiple strategic choices which, taken secretly, require tactical reconsideration made in reaction to the opponent’s chosen actions. Isabel forces the players to constantly consider the risk-reward of their choices. With a limited amount of available resources, players have to decide when to sacrifice assets to obtain substantial one-time benefits.
 
—description from the designer

name: Jackpot: Set the Reel
description:
Jackpot: Set the Reel puts you in control of your own luck! This 'slotbuilder' challenges you to master the art of hand manipulation as you aim to make lines of three of the same symbol. But the twist is, you never shuffle your cards! Instead, through clever planning, tactical upgrades, and precise card swaps, you’ll manipulate your hand to strike massive payouts.

Gain victory points by matching symbols, with bigger combos scoring bigger payouts. Upgrade cards to unlock rewards, and claim bonus tiles to boost your score or gain special abilities. Every choice matters.

The game is played simultaneously and with each round, you’ll place three adjacent cards from your hand into your slot machine, forming a row. You'll repeat this twice more, building a grid and claiming points for completed matches. Then, pass your last card to the player on your left while receiving a card from the right, and placing it strategically to optimise your next move.

Next, collect coins from one column of your slot machine, then reorder your columns in your hand while keeping each column’s cards in the sequence you just played them in. With your hand reset, you're ready for another round.

Will you manipulate the cards, stack the odds, and hit the jackpot?

—description from the publisher

name: Jarren's Outpost
description:
The city of Jarren’s Outpost has once again fallen into disarray. Although no-one has been formally charged with the minor crime of regicide, the search for a new democratically elected leader has commenced. Unfortunately the people of Jarren’s Outpost aren’t quite sure what ‘democratically elected’ means so instead a week long competition has been set up to find the next King and/or Queen for this fine city. Surely the new ruler will know what to do about that dragon. And the blood cult. And the rampant wererat problem. And the orcs. And the taxes…


     For 2-5 players, inspired by the D&D is for Nerds podcast.



     Gain Prestige in a mission-based programming game with resource management and dice-based combat.



     Plan your perfect day using unique Movement Cards for each character while you compete for quests and resources.



     25 different locations, a variety of items, NPCs and quests, with every playable character having their own abilities, movements and playstyles, will ensure no two games are the same.


—description from the publisher

name: Jounce
description:
In Jounce, you’re a frog bouncing around a pond, snacking on bugs, and trying to out-hop your friends and end the game with the prized water lily. Every turn, everyone will simultaneously play a movement card to leap to a new lily pad, but there’s a catch—you can only jump in certain directions. Figuring out the best way to jounce from pad to pad can be challenging, and rewarding!

Every time you land, you grab a bug. If you collect several of the same kind, you can use special abilities to get ahead, But collecting a variety of bugs will be worth more at the end of the game! The game ends when one type of bug is completely eaten, and whoever has the most points wins.

It’s a game of tricky jumps, clever planning, and a little bit of chaos. Sometimes you’ll land exactly where you need to, and sometimes you’ll get stuck in a spot that makes you rethink everything. Either way, it’s all part of the fun—just don’t let the other frogs eat all the good bugs before you get there!

—description from the publisher

name: Unmatched Adventures: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
publisher: Geekach LLC; IELLO; Ogry Games; Restoration Games
description:
Unmatched Adventures: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is the second title in the co-operative Unmatched Adventures series.

Play as Leonardo, Raphael, Donatello, and Michelangelo to take down Shredder or fight off Krang. They'll be joined by a host of TMNT characters.

—description from the publisher

name: Unmatched: Battle of Legends, Volume Three
publisher: Restoration Games; GaGa Games; Geekach LLC; IELLO; Ogry Games; Reflexshop; White Goblin Games
description:
In battle, there are no equals.

Unmatched is a highly asymmetrical miniature fighting game for two or four players. Each hero is represented by a unique deck designed to evoke their style and legend. Tactical movement and no-luck combat resolution create a unique play experience that rewards expertise, but just when you've mastered one set, new heroes arrive to provide all new match-ups.

Battle of Legends, Volume Three features four disparate heroes: the pirate Blackbeard, the beastly Chupacabra, the trickster Loki, and the cursed and gifted Pandora. (Blackbeard, Chupacabra, and Loki are all runners-up from a deck-design contest.)

Combat is resolved quickly by comparing attack and defense cards. However, each card's unique effects and a simple but deep timing system lead to interesting decisions each time.

The game includes a double-sided board with two different battlefields (one of which is Santa's Workshop, which features a new map mechanism), pre-washed miniatures for each hero, and custom life trackers. As with every Unmatched set, these heroes can face off against fighters from other sets – even the villains in Unmatched Adventures.

name: Jump Masters!
description:
Introducing Jump Masters, a cutthroat battler inspired by Chinese checkers! This easy-to-jump, hard-to-master game from the talented Manny Trembley is the colorful caper of your tabletop dreams.

In Jump Masters, players command a drafted team of heroes in a skirmish. Taking turns, players jump their heroes around the arena to defeat their opponents and gain victory points! When you jump over a friendly hero, you gain energy! When you jump over an opposing hero, you attack, reducing the two heroes’ energy until one is defeated! Chain multiple jumps together to pull off more powerful turns. Each hero has its own unique ability; Drafting the right combination of heroes and using their abilities to your advantage are key to success! Terrain will block you (or empower you!), so you’ll need to plan accordingly. Be the first to collect the required amount of victory points by defeating your opponents, and you’ll be declared the Jump Master!

-description from publisher

name: Jurassic Crisis
description: Jurassic Crisis is a semi-competitive, PvPvE survival board game for 1–4 players, inspired by the video game ARK Survival Evolved. You must survive on an island inhabited by dinosaurs while mastering various mechanics – from resource management and positioning to character development, base building, and dinosaur taming.

name: Jure Grando: The First Vampire
description:
In Jure Grando: The First Vampire, you step into the shoes of the desperate townsfolk of Kringa.

Move around with your chosen townsfolk and explore the streets of Kringa, find items and protect the other townsfolk from Jure. But be careful; each encounter with Jure or failed objective will increase the terror in your town.

Complete your objectives and banish Jure once and for all before it is too late and your once peaceful town becomes a place of the dead.

—description from the publisher

name: Kadath
description:
Since ancient times, the Dreamlands have been the refuge of the dreamers: a vast dream world where the mythical city of Kadath lies hidden. The dreamer Randolph Carter penetrates into these lands in search of the lost city, while the Crawling Chaos Nyarlathotep does everything possible to divert him, sowing chaos in his path. Will you protect the purity of the dream, or drag it into the eternal abyss?

Kadath, is a game where each player places tiles in a 5x5 square grid, trying to form groups of four tiles from the same side to create enclaves on the board, whether they belong to the Dreamer or Chaos. The first player to create 5 enclaves and place their 5 enclave tokens  on the playing area wins.

name: Kaelora
description:
Drop anchor by a mysterious island and set out on an expedition to uncover and record the strange new life you encounter. You are an explorer and this is the discovery of a lifetime!

Delightfully puzzly and refreshingly simple, Kaelora is a game of competitive and clever collation. Move about the board to collect discovery tokens, recording them wisely in your journal to maximize points, while keeping an eye on shifting and secret end game objectives.

—description from the publisher

name: Unmatched: Lee vs Ali
publisher: Restoration Games; Geekach LLC; IELLO; White Goblin Games
description:
Sting Like a Bee…Strike Like a Dragon!

Two of the greatest martial artists to ever throw a punch face off in the latest set for Unmatched, the critically acclaimed, best-selling game of tactical combat between unlikely opponents. Muhammad Ali floats like a butterfly and stings like a bee. Ali’s deck boasts all-new art from Rob Zilla III. This set sees the return of the out-of-print and highly demanded Bruce Lee deck from the solo pack published at the game’s launch in 2019, illustrated by Unmatched veteran Oliver Barrett.

—description from the publisher

name: Kangaroo Island
description:
Off the coast of southern Australia sits Kangaroo Island, home to an abundance of diverse wildlife. Mobs of kangaroo inhabit the scrublands, while local little penguin colonies thrive in nearby rocky burrows. If you look up into the occasional eucalyptus tree, you're sure to see a pair of koalas, and if you peer into one of the many waterholes, you may spy the venomous platypus.

In Kangaroo Island, you'll control a growing herd of these animals as you explore and lay claim to the island's finite territory. Earn nature stars by taking a balanced approach to claiming territory, while unlocking new abilities for your animals and watching out for bushfires and human construction sites along the way.

—description from the publisher

name: Unmatched: The Witcher – Realms Fall
publisher: Restoration Games; Albi; GaGa Games; Geekach LLC; HANALL M&C; IELLO; Ogry Games; Reflexshop; White Goblin Games
description:
In battle, there are no equals.

Unmatched is a highly asymmetrical miniature fighting game for two or four players. Each hero is represented by a unique deck designed to evoke their style and legend. Tactical movement and no-luck combat resolution create a unique play experience that rewards expertise, but just when you've mastered one set, new heroes arrive to provide all new match-ups.

Unmatched: Realms Fall features Eredin, Philippa, and Triss & Yennefe. and two battlefields, featuring a brand new map mechanic, from the Witcher series.

Yennefer and Triss introduce an Unmatched first: You choose who is the hero and who is the sidekick, with different special abilities for each. Philippa is a powerful sorceress and schemer, who never runs out of cards. 
King Eredin commands a horde of Wild Hunt Riders, only growing stronger when they are struck down.

name: Karnivorous
description:
Seeking to end world hunger with giant apples, scientists used their discovery on the wrong plants, and now the apples will be feasting on them! Soon the rest of mankind will be snacks, too, unless you brave gardener-robots — the only non-vegetable sentient beings in the lab not yet eaten — take care of this infestation.

In the 1-4 co-operative game Karnivorous, players must allocate their dice to trigger actions: run through the lab, fight plants, and resolve crisis cards that increase their knowledge of these aggressive plants. Only the best use of your dice results will allow you to stop this rampant deadly growth!

—description from the publisher

name: Unmatched: The Witcher – Steel and Silver
publisher: Restoration Games; Albi; GaGa Games; Geekach LLC; HANALL M&C; IELLO; Ogry Games; Reflexshop; White Goblin Games
description:
In battle, there are no equals.

Unmatched is a highly asymmetrical miniature fighting game for two or four players. Each hero is represented by a unique deck designed to evoke their style and legend. Tactical movement and no-luck combat resolution create a unique play experience that rewards expertise, but just when you've mastered one set, new heroes arrive to provide all new match-ups.

Unmatched: Steel and Silver has three playable characters: Geralt of Rivia, Ciri, and the Ancient Leshen. Each character comes with one or two companion tokens. Also has two battlefields from the Witcher series including the Witcher stronghold, Kaer Morhen.

name: Kickabout
description:
Take on your opponent in this tiny but brilliant take on a 5 on 5 soccer match.  Push your luck, outmaneuver your opponent, and score!  GOOOOOOOOAL!
 Kickabout is a game by Evan Wilcock with art by Leo Aquino.  Each turn both players play one card from their hand of 6 cards: Players 1-5 or the Shoot / Save Card.

If the Defender matches the Attacker's card, the ball is intercepted and possession changes. Otherwise, a pass is made and play continues.
 When the Attacker plays their shoot card, they will roll a number of dice equal to the passes made. All dice that match the last played card number or lower count as shots on goal.  The Defender will roll 3 dice if they matched the Shoot Card with the Save, 2 if they didn't, and only 1 if they played it early.

Defender blocks all matching numbers and may assign a 6 to block any 1 die.  If any shots on goal remain, the Attacker scores!  First to 3 wins.

This is a very simple game to learn and play with gamers and non-gamers; young and old.

—description from the publisher

name: Killer Queen
description:
Highschool can be a pain - literally.

It’s the end of Prom Night, 1989. The Killer Queen stalks you and your friends through the school halls, and she’s turned the games you used to play into a fight for survival. Hide and Seek, Would You Rather and Truth Or Dare are now choices between life and death, and the only way to survive is to play along. Outrun and outsmart your friends, and hope you’re not the one left alone with the Killer Queen.

The aim of Killer Queen is to be the player with the fewest points in their injury pile at the end of the game. Try to escape the Killer Queen by removing all the cards from your hand, but beware, for every Power card you play in your fight for survival, you’ll have to draw a card from the deck - or from your fellow survivor's hands - in return. Cross your fingers because hidden in each are dangerous Weapon Cards, sinister Plot Twists, and, deadlier still, the Killer Queen herself.

—description from the publisher

name: Kimbap Klash
description:
Kimbap Klash is a fast, flavorful K-food card battler where players race to craft the ultimate kimbap roll. Draft tasty ingredients, dodge (or weaponize!) yucky ones, and stir up chaos with action cards that let you steal, swap, or sabotage.

At the end of the game, everyone reveals their hidden character card, triggering a unique power that can completely flip the table. Stack smart combos, chase bold flavors, and build the most creative roll you can — because only the highest-scoring kimbap earns bragging rights!

—description from the publisher

name: KING
description:
A flip-and-write game in which we take on the role of a medieval King ruling his kingdom. The game is a direct sequel to Knight, shifting the focus from the deeds of a single warrior to the personal decisions of the monarch himself. Every royal choice - political, military, or economic - has a direct and far-reaching impact on the entire realm and shapes its future.

During the game, the King faces complex challenges affecting the whole kingdom, such as declaring and conducting wars, expanding borders, managing internal politics, appointing or removing lords, negotiating alliances, suppressing rebellions, and responding to crises like plague, famine, drought, or devastating floods. Each scenario emphasizes different aspects of rulership and requires the player to adapt their strategy to changing circumstances.

In each turn, the player draws 6 cards that determine the events of that turn. These cards define the available actions, provide a specific pool of resources, and indicate which actions are currently active. In solo mode, they also determine the consequences of decisions and the behavior of the automa. A major new element is the introduction of Advisor cards - influential figures at court whose unique abilities significantly affect strategy. Choosing and managing advisors is crucial, as they can strongly shape the direction of the kingdom and open powerful tactical and strategic options.

The game is played over 2 rounds, each consisting of 6 turns. After every 3 turns, a Goal card is revealed, introducing new conditions that define rewards and penalties based on the King’s achievements during that phase. This creates shifting priorities and forces the player to make difficult decisions as the state of the kingdom evolves.

The player wins by fulfilling the objectives defined by the selected scenario. There are always multiple paths to victory - for example, achieving a certain number of victory points, securing full control of the map, maintaining high stability and prosperity, or winning a required number of key battles. The player can also lose before the game ends if any of the scenario’s loss conditions are met, such as the collapse of royal authority, a successful rebellion, the enemy conquering the entire realm, or the fall of the capital due to invasion or neglect.

—description from the designer

name: King of Tokyo Godzilla
description:
The True King of Monsters is finally here!

Toho’s legendary Kaijus clash in an epic battle to decide who will be the definitive King of Tokyo. Play as Godzilla, King Ghidorah, Hedorah, Rodan, Mothra, and Mechagodzilla.

For those familiar with the original game, discover a new mechanic: “Event cards” that affect all monsters. And for fans, yes, evolution cards are included!

King of Tokyo: Godzilla is a family game with dice, cards, and smashes, inspired by the yams system.

In King of Tokyo Godzilla, you play the legendary ToHo's monsters of whom are destroying Tokyo and whacking each other in order to become the one and only King of Tokyo.

At the start of each turn, you roll six dice, which show the following six symbols: 1, 2, or 3 Victory Points, Energy, Heal, and Attack. Over three successive throws, choose whether to keep or discard each die in order to win victory points, gain energy, restore health, or attack other players into understanding that Tokyo is YOUR territory.

The fiercest player will occupy Tokyo, and earn extra victory points, but that player can't heal and must face all the other monsters alone!

Top this off with special cards purchased with energy that have a permanent or temporary effect, such as the growing of a second head which grants you an additional die, body armor, nova death ray, and more.... and it's one of the most explosive games of the year!

In order to win the game, one must either destroy Tokyo by accumulating 20 victory points, or be the only surviving monster once the fighting has ended.

-description from publisher

name: Kraken
description:
Kraken is a fast-paced pirate-themed fishing game in which each player secretly pursues a unique objective. A typical game lasts around 30 minutes and blends strategy, sabotage, and a pinch of luck.

On your turn, you draw cards, play actions, roll dice to catch fish, and upgrade your gear using goldfish tokens. Each pirate has a unique ability that influences their playstyle and strategy, and the first player to fulfill their secret objective or to capture the legendary Kraken wins.

The game features action cards, attribute cards, sabotage cards, and fish cards divided into different environments: lake, sea, river. Managing sabotage and maximizing bonus effects are key to success. Multiple tactics are viable: boosting your gear, slowing down your rivals, or outright stealing their resources.

With its quick turns and unpredictable twists, Kraken creates a dynamic, high-energy experience full of spectacular comebacks and pirate mischief.

—description from the publisher

name: Kringa
description:
This is based on a true story: for 16 years, the town of Kringa has been terrorized by an evil Strigoi named Jure Grando. While the families struggle to survive day-to-day, they must gather the courage and tools to defeat the undead fiend!

Kringa is a cooperative horror worker-placement game with a strong push-your-luck component.

Players start with a family of four workers - each with unique abilities. Assign workers to locations to collect resources. Use resources to craft helpful items, hire helpers and overcome dangers. As dusk descends, you can choose to risk danger and stay to gather more resources, or return home to feed and protect your family with blessings and hexes.
