Engage in intense battles on the board, with Heroes facing off against Enemies amidst the fluctuating conditions of the "Battleflux" cards at the board's center.

Choose from six distinct Heroes, each with their own story arcs and unique abilities, ensuring diverse and exciting gameplay experiences. With multiple branching paths and outcomes, coupled with the dynamic mechanics of each Hero, no two adventures are ever alike.

Enhance your journey with the Forteller app, providing immersive storytelling, original music, and over two novels' worth of voice acting to guide you through this epic RPG experience.

—description from the publisher

name: Elden Ring: Stormveil Castle
description:
Behold, the stronghold of the Grafted King himself! On the cliffs of Stormhill, the crumbling castle of Stormveil glares out over the land of Limgrave. Within lurks Godrick the Grafted, demi-god and descendent of the first Elden Lord...

The ELDEN RING video game was a smash-hit with more than 28 million copies sold, winning multiple awards and gaining high reviews across the board. Now, this official adaptation will take you once more into the Lands Between — this time, on your tabletop.

A co-operative board game for 1-4 players, ELDEN RING: Stormveil Castle challenges you to enter the crumbling stronghold of the Grafted King, perched high on the cliffs of Stormhill.

This set includes a complete, 20+ hour replayable campaign that's playable standalone, and can also be combined with other ELDEN RING board game sets for even bigger adventures. Inside you’ll find a range of player classes with updated gameplay, including two Tarnished unique to this set — the Confessor and Prisoner — along with a huge Godrick the Grafted miniature on a 120mm base.

Will you cast down this demi-god from his misbegotten throne? Go it alone or work with friends to slay the horrific abominations he has let loose in the castle halls, before facing the Grafted King himself.

Featuring pulse-pounding gameplay and gorgeously detailed miniatures, this set faithfully recreates the intense battles and intoxicating atmosphere of the video game. Its intelligent, card-driven combat uses a unique grid system that will challenge your strategic skills with every encounter.

- Huge Godrick the Grafted miniature (120mm base)
- Play as the Confessor or Prisoner, unique to this set
- Unique, grid-based combat system
- 22 highly detailed miniatures
- Expansive world to explore
- 20+ hours of replayable gameplay
- Play single-session games with Arena Mode
- Combine with the Realm of the Grafted King set for even bigger campaigns, more player characters, and more enemies

Will you heed the call to adventure?

name: Off With Their Heads!
description:
Off With Their Heads! is a clever reveal-and-write game where players serve as loyal Card Soldiers tasked with keeping the mercurial Red Queen pleased. Influenced by a wide range of classic card games including poker, hearts, and euchre, players secretly choose and reveal cards from their hands to compete for position in each bout. The ranking of the revealed cards determines whether you place highest, lowest, or somewhere in between, and that result dictates where you record the card’s value on your personal score sheet.

Each section of your sheet rewards a different strategy. Claim the highest card to mark the Meadow and complete mushrooms for points, land in the middle to carefully place numbers throughout the Woods while following the Jabberwock’s rule, or take the lowest rank to navigate the maze-like Keep where every number you record becomes valuable. Along the way you can earn bonuses, invite iconic Wonderlandians to your Tea Party, and manipulate your marks using helpful teacups.

At the end of each round, two cards are set aside. After three rounds, those cards form a six-card pool from which players create their best five-card poker hand for bonus points before final scoring. The player who has earned the most favor with the Queen across their sheet wins the game… and keeps their head.

—description from the publisher

name: Offworld Empires
description:
Offworld Empires is a light 4X space strategy game for 2 to 4 players. Each player chooses a unique space civilization with its own strengths and weaknesses and builds their space empire in a far flung galaxy.

At the head of your galactic empire, you will explore an unknown galaxy full of various planets, asteroids, wormholes, and much more. Use colony ships to settle on new planets and gather their resources, or send your marines to pacify those that resist your expansion.

Erect buildings to harvest food and grow your population of workers, search for new technologies from a unique tech wheel, assemble spaceships to secure your own airspace or battle enemy fleets, and appoint senators to vote military or economic laws that will give you an edge over your opponents.

The customized worker placement mechanism is a key point of the game. Every player can build the buildings of their liking – provided they have the necessary resources – and assign their workers to them to maximize their efficiency. You need to find the proper balance between population growth, scientific research and raw production, or choose to specialize in a single domain at the expense of others.

Will you manage to lead you galactic civilization to victory?

—description from the publisher

name: OFMOS Classic
description: Ofmos is a family of business games.

name: On Hell's Highway
description:
On Hell's Highway is a 2-map simulation of the massive Allied airborne assault and ground offensive into Nazi held Netherlands in September, 1944. Taking advantage of a disorganized and retreating German Army, more than three British and American airborne divisions were dropped along a 60 mile corridor in an attempt to capture key bridges across multiple rivers and canals, allowing the British XXX Corps to race northward and cross the Lower Rhine and into the industrial heartland of Germany. But Allied overconfidence, hasty planning, and some bad luck, along with a surprisingly tenacious and coordinated German defence, produced the last Allied operational failure and the destruction of an entire British Airborne division.

Designed by John Butterfield, On Hell's Highway is not simply a brush up and repackaging of the highly acclaimed original Hell's Highway game, but a reimagined treatment that truly makes it a new gaming experience. Taking advantage of recent and more extensive historical works, this redesign includes a much revised OB and reinforcement schedule with an enriched and more accurate map treatment based on more detailed source materials. The revised game system includes a more straightforward combat fire table that now allows for situational results which adds uncertainty and volatility while still retaining  many of the core features that makes it feel familiar.

—description from the publisher

name: On the Edge of Time
description:
The year is 2301, and you are operating an agency to travel in time to correct issues created by beings called the Altuli.

On the Edge of Time is a cooperative 1-3 player game (with a 1 v all option).

The players attempt to complete missions to protect their timeline. These missions must be completed before the temporal stress reaches a critical mass, the universe splits and is destroyed.

During the game, two missions will be revealed, the Altuli will land on the game board and restrict your resources, temporal stress will be evaluated, and then players will take their turn.

In the player phase, individuals can spend credits to acquire units, use their temporal energy to travel and eliminate Altuli and utilize research to develop technologies.

Actions taken back in time will affect future points in time, sometimes with unintended consequences. Complete 6 missions and one final mission to succeed. Failure occurs if the temporal stress becomes excessive.

-description from designer

name: One Card Wonders
description:
Fight a titan, wage a war of conquest, have a drawing contest using only dots, or just try to build better words than your friends - all in the palm of your hand.

One Card Wonders is a library of single-card games that covers a wide range of genres and mechanisms, including area control, dexterity, hidden movement, abstract, racing, pattern recognition, dice games, drawing games, word games, and more!

The set includes the few simple components needed to play all of the games, each of which can be set up in seconds, and you can learn and play in minutes. The games can also all be played pretty much anywhere. You can have a space battle on an airplane tray, or

The games included in this set are:

     Space Ace
     Blown Away
     Zomboy +
     UFO Go!
     Fly, You Fools
     Tiny Titan
     Tug of Paw
     Clash of Coins
     Haring Around
     Dungeon Dash
     Realm of Ironfist
     Max Tagger
     Squarcles
     Astronomix
     The Letterator
     Tumble Bots
     Killer Looks
     One Card Maze

name: Elden Ring: Weeping Peninsula
description:
Named for its neverending rainfall, the Weeping Peninsula that lies south of Limgrave is a melancholy land filled with hidden secrets, powerful artifacts, and grave danger. All who set foot on this cursed headland are sure to cross paths with a host of misbegotten creatures, determined to cast out any Tarnished foolish enough to intrude.

The ELDEN RING video game was a smash-hit with more than 28 million copies sold, winning multiple awards and gaining high reviews across the board. Now, this official adaptation will take you once more into the Lands Between — this time, on your tabletop.

Created for 1-4 players, ELDEN RING: Weeping Peninsula plunges you into a melancholy land of secrets, powerful artefacts, and grave danger.

This board game includes a complete, 20+ hour replayable campaign that's playable standalone, and can also be combined with other ELDEN RING board game sets for even grander adventures. Inside you’ll find a range of player classes with updated gameplay, including two Tarnished unique to this set — the Hero and Bandit.

Customise your Tarnished, weave your story, and explore the grim landscape for treasure. Go it alone or ally with friends to survive deadly, tactical combat with a host of misbegotten creatures, culminating in a climactic battle with the nightmarish Leonine Misbegotten.

Featuring pulse-pounding gameplay and gorgeously detailed miniatures, this set faithfully recreates the intense battles and intoxicating atmosphere of the video game. Its intelligent, card-driven combat uses a unique grid system that will challenge players to strategise for every encounter.

- Play as the Hero or Bandit, unique to this set
- Unique, grid-based combat system
- 20 highly detailed miniatures
- Expansive world to explore
- 20+ hours of replayable gameplay
- Play single-session games with Arena Mode
- Combine with ELDEN RING: Realm of the Grafted King for even bigger campaigns, more player characters, and more enemies

Will you heed the call to adventure?

name: Horizon Forbidden West: Seeds of Rebellion
description:
In the distant lands of a far-future Earth, where colossal machines rule, and humans exist in pre-industrial tribes, the seeds of rebellion are taking root amongst the warlike Tenakth.

Return to the post-apocalyptic world of Horizon and discover the untold stories of the Forbidden West — a majestic, dangerous frontier where massive new machines roam and which astonishing new tribes call home.

Inspired by the award-winning video game, this fully cooperative board game for 1-4 players will take players to the Forbidden West before Aloy’s arrival. A rebellion is fomenting in the dark corners of this mysterious frontier. It aims to shatter the hard-won, fragile peace between the Tenakth clans.

You and your fellow Marshals must uncover, investigate, and fight this threat before unnecessary blood is shed and the fate of the Clan Lands is changed for generations to come. Along the way, you’ll explore the vibrant world, earn powerful equipment, and undertake life-or-death quests, testing your skills against an ever-present menace: the deadly, ever-evolving machines.

Will you fall to the spear, the claw, or the toxic blight? Or will you rise against the odds together and unravel the untold mysteries of the Forbidden West?

name: One Word Away
description:
One Word Away is party word game which can be played either co-operative or Team vs. Team. You write down 3 clues for your secret word. But before your fellow players can guess, one of the clues is erased, either by a dice roll or the other team.

Can they still guess the secret word?

—description from the designer

name: Operation Overlord
description:
Operation Overlord is a deep, historically grounded strategic wargame that simulates the Normandy invasion and the critical battles that followed from June to August 1944. One player commands the Allied SHAEF forces, planning and executing the largest amphibious operation in history, while the opposing player takes the role of Oberbefehlshaber West, defending the Atlantic Wall and attempting to delay the Allied advance long enough to alter the course of the war.

Rather than focusing on tactical skirmishes, Operation Overlord operates at the operational–strategic level, where timing, logistics, intelligence, and command structure are decisive. Players maneuver divisions and army corps across a detailed map of Normandy, manage supply networks and reinforcements, execute historical and fictional operations, and influence battles through doctrine, supports, and event cards.

Each month begins with high-level planning: the Allied player secretly schedules strategic and special operations, while the German player designates key cities as Festungen, to be held at all costs. Weekly turns then unfold through intelligence gathering, supply allocation, reinforcement arrivals, and alternating unit activations that combine maneuver and combat into a tense, fluid system. Fog of war is maintained through hidden unit values and simultaneous combat card reveals, ensuring constant uncertainty and meaningful decision-making.

Victory is not measured simply by territory, but by time and consequences. The German player is unlikely to drive the Allies back into the sea—but every week gained has far-reaching implications for morale, resources, and other fronts of the war. Likewise, an Allied breakthrough ahead of schedule can dramatically reshape history. Each scenario and campaign outcome includes historically reasoned consequences that frame the result within the broader context of World War II.

With multiple scenarios (June, July, August, and a full campaign), robust asymmetry, and a strong emphasis on planning and operational art, Operation Overlord offers a demanding and rewarding experience for players seeking a serious, historically informed wargame.

—description from the publisher

name: Operation Valkyrie
description:
Operation Valkyrie is a solitaire game that simulates the events immediately after the attempt to kill Hitler on the 20th of July 1944, when the military coup was attempted to take control of the Reich.
The player will control the effort of the conspirators against the Reich forces controlled by the game system.
Each turn the player draws cards that provide him with action point or events to use for his cause or that is used against him by the bot. The player needs to control critical locations on the map in order to gain control over Berlin and overthrow the regime. The player is under enormous time pressure, as the bot becomes stronger with each round of the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Orbitstar: Expedition To Darwin IV
description:
It is the year 2358, and a massive spaceship is locked into orbit around the newly discovered world Darwin IV. With the help of the Yma, our alien patrons, humanity has finally achieved one of its cherished goals – to reach a distant exoplanet. Descending to the surface in sealed hovercones, a multitude of scientists and researchers, both human and otherworldly, will spread across this virginal world to study the diverse and often bizarre fauna found in all of its varied biomes. From vast savannahs and scattered pocket forests to the frozen tundra and the mystifying Amoebic Sea, explorers will rise to the challenges of a world teeming with biological wonders. It is here on Darwin IV that the human race will begin to fulfill its age-old yearning to explore the universe and understand the intricacies of an alien planet.

Based on Wayne Barlowe's beautifully illustrated book "Expedition", in Expedition To Darwin IV players take on the role of human scientists in the year 2358 AD, exploring the alien world Darwin IV in search of new life. Piloting their hovercones across different biomes, scientists will locate and study the unique indigenous species of Darwin IV in an effort to learn more about the planet's strange and wondrous inhabitants. With the data they've collected, each scientist will share their work with their benign custodians, the Yma, earning them reputation.

But Darwin IV isn't without its dangers as scientists must also be cautious with the planet's more aggressive predators, navigate its unpredictable weather patterns, and avoid other deadly off-world threats...

—description from the publisher

name: ORBORA
description:
In the co-operative game ORBORA, you play together to restore balance to the planet. Each card will help you progress toward your goal by allowing you to organize the tiles on your personal board and send elements to the central shared board. You'll also trigger bonuses as you progress on the mission board. Each scenario will be a different challenge to overcome thanks to the randomly placed mission tiles and the difficulty you choose. The planet's balance must be restored before the end of the card deck, or you're defeated.

Good luck, and remember: the fate of the planet is in your hands.

—description from the publisher

name: Orchestra
description:
In Orchestra, players lead rival music academies, each striving to train talented musicians and elevate their institution’s prestige. Over the course of the game, players evolve their academies, develop students across multiple skill levels, and strategically send their best performers to the orchestra for a grand concert.

Gameplay unfolds through rounds divided into allocation and resolution phases. Players assign musicians to various action spaces to upgrade their academy, fulfill performance scenarios, and influence the structure and leadership of the concert hall. Musicians progress from beginners to professionals and instrument specialists, with virtuosos being rare and powerful additions.

The goal is to earn mastery points by excelling in orchestral performance, audience placement, scenario fulfillment, and strategic development. Players compete for influence in the orchestra, complete secret objectives, and manage resources like prestige and money to optimize their academy’s growth.

At the end of the game, the academy with the highest mastery score is declared the most prestigious, having delivered the most unforgettable performance of all time.

—description from the publisher

name: Orcs up!
description:
Here's the plan: stack your bumbling orcs up a castle wall and reach the top. 
Easy peasy. 
Except your opponents had the exact same idea, and they've got boulders, tricks, and a competitive streak a mile wide.

Welcome to Orcs Up!, where controlled chaos is the name of the game.

Every round throws you into a tornado of frantic card plays, stacking, and climbing your way to victory while your tower constantly threatens to crumble.

Victory loves the bold.

—description from the publisher

name: ORGANISM
description:
Your new awareness emerges all at once. You know immediately, before you even recognize your own existence, an all-consuming hunger. Hunger and also…. fear? Because somehow you know, you are not alone. Beneath these immediate drives lies something deeper, a spark, a joy, a hope. The glee, the audacity to split, to drive a wedge in your very self and become two. And through two, infinity.

Organism is a game of growth, multiplication, and struggle. Wielding the simple actions of EAT / GROW / MOVE / CIRCULATE the minimal ruleset is maximally integrated and generates a tight yet boundless decision space. Amplified by a set of mutation cards which expand the rules in countless subtle and not-so-subtle ways, it is really a family of related games in a single box that can never be truly exhausted.

Each player controls an Organism composed of three elements: EAT, MOVE, and GROW. In the beginning, each organism contains one of each element, which is a requirement for your organism to live. If an organism lacks one of these three elements at the end of the turn, it dies.

Players take turns either eating food, moving into new positions (possibly coming into contact with other organisms or even dividing into separate organisms), growing new elements, or circulating food within their organism. When any elements of opposing organisms meet, the conflict is resolved by removing one or more elements from the board.

You win the game if you capture a certain number of the opposing player’s elements (or just eliminate them entirely from the board), or if you attain three separate organisms at the end of your turn, in which case they are well on their way to spreading across the globe.

—description from the publisher

name: ORMAN
description:
ORMAN is a print-and-play roll and write game where players cultivate their own forests using just regular dice and a pencil. Each round, everyone uses the same roll of two white dice and two black dice to determine both the shape of the area to plant, and the type and density of trees to place.

The white dice define your planting shape, you may use one value, the other, their sum, or their difference. The colored dice let you choose a tree type and set the tree density. Rolling doubles on the colored dice also gives you the option to place a lake anywhere on your grid instead of planting.

Trees must be placed orthogonally adjacent to water or existing trees, starting from a pre-drawn lake. The goal is to grow large, connected groups near lakes, diversify tree species in marked columns, and fill your entire forest grid. Scoring rewards lakeside groves, column variety, and a complete map, while empty squares cost points.

ORMAN includes both multiplayer and solo modes, offering a relaxing yet strategic roll-and-write experience rooted in spatial planning and adaptability.

—description from the publihser

name: Ortomnia: Broken Trinity
description:
Developed and Selfpublished by: Mystic Shelter

Factsheet: 
Competetive 1v1 Expandable Cardgame

- PvPvE
- 2 Players
- 14 Years or older
- 30+ Minutes per Play (Deckbuilding not included)

Includes:
- 305 Cards in total (112 unique Cards in the Amount to use in a deck + Game Accessoire Cards)
- Pre-punched Tokensheet
- Rulebook

Recommended Retail Price: 44,- Euro

Perfect for:
- Boardgame Experts who love to tinker with Synergies while building their Deck.
- Story Enthusiasts who enjoy new original Universes and want to dive into the Story and Lore of the Game itself

Gather 40 Essence by Generating them with Cards, fullfilling Quests,
destroying enemy Cards or attacking the Enemy.

You take turns with your Enemy and choose between different possible
Actions you can take in your turn instead of having a fixed Turn Process.

Quests come up in your self-built Questdeck, giving them different objectives while playing against each other, 
you can build your Questdeck as well as your Main Deck yourself before the Game starts.

While playing, the Corruption – an environmental Threat – rises, 
once it reaches the highest Stage both players lose, so they have to keep an eye on it and manipulate it if necessary. 
Different Cards interact differently with the Corruption.

There are 5 upcoming Expansions planned, each with roughly 20-30 new unique Cards each (60-70 in Total).

name: Otter Chaos
description:
Otter Chaos is the third game in our Otterverse.

A terrible storm has destroyed the otter den, and the fractious otters can’t agree on a new home. Convince the other otters that your favorite environment is the best choice to avoid otter chaos!

Play and compare otters to stack the final vote in your favor. Outscore your opponent on the chosen environment to win!

Each round, both players play an otter and directly compare them. Otters are valued by color and rank. The winner adds a card to the center. At the end of the game, the center cards determine which environment the otters pick. If you have the highest number of stars in that environment, you win!

name: Overgrown
description:
In Overgrown, players attempt to reclaim an abandoned city with new growth and wildlife, while competing for the resources needed to do so.

Inspired by tile-combination & match-3 games, Overgrown offers a fun twist on fighting the tide of tiles with clever placement and combination: each player determines the tiles their opponents receive from where they place their own tiles!

You and your friends are the forces of nature, attempting to transform polluted and abandoned cities into lush paradises brimming with wildlife. Each turn, players gather the elements needed to regrow flora and reintroduce fauna from a shared pool. Unfortunately, the elements are limited and mixed in with pollution so not every city will fully revive.

Unlike other tile-laying games, you control the drafting pool not only by what you take, but also how you use it, giving you plenty to think about as your city slowly recovers. At the end of the game, the player with the most verdant city is declared the winner.

—description from the designer

name: Overtake: Race Manager
description:
Overtake: Race Manager is an exhilarating, competitive racing management board game. Players represent managers of corporations vying for supremacy in the high-stakes world of motorsport racing. You're tasked to build your fleet of cutting-edge cars, strategically allocate staff and resources, and outmaneuver rival corporations on the track to secure the prestigious title of Motorsport Racing Champion.

Scoring rounds resolve through races, where skilled drivers in finely-tuned machines compete for the podium. Success translates to prestige, points, and funding - assuming you've managed to entice sponsors.

Gameplay scales with game progression and is tightly crafted to reflect the tension of racing management. Features include:

An original cast featuring men and women from 31 countries.
Action prioritization of resources to recruit staff, build cars, and acquire sponsors. 
Set collection bonuses unlock through headquarter expansion.
Streamlined 10-car racing events, including variable skill level automa corporations.
Racing that factors strategic decisions with car development and team agility with track weather conditions.

Compete over a year, a series comprised of 6 races, to etch your name into the halls of racing history!

—description from the designer

name: Ozob: A Cyberpunk Board Game
description:
In Ozob: A Cyberpunk Boardgame, players take on the roles of hackers, mercenaries, post-humans, and other rebels to fight against the oppression of megacorporations. Embark on various missions, with different levels of difficulty, that can be played freely or in campaign mode. Face corporate security, corrupt police officers, and destructive robots. Rely on your friends...and only them, for in this dystopian world the system itself will be against you.

Each character has a unique deck, different special abilities, a set of unique initial items, and a different constitution on their health bar. During the game, players take turns pressing their luck to reveal their stat cards, then take three actions each turn. Actions can be moving, taking a test, or attacking enemies. After that, an event will be drawn from the events deck and the board will suffer some changes. Enemies attack, then the turn ends.

The game is divided into ten scenarios, each with its particular events deck and a unique win condition. Players always lose if one of their characters dies.

name: Panopticon
description:
A cooperative and immersive experience in which you must coordinate as best you can by taking advantage of every glimpse from the lines of sight and overhearing every bit of information.

The game is divided into 3 days, each of which consists of 4 rounds. At each turn, players use up to 3 action points and, clockwise, choose whether to perform 1 or 2 actions until they run out of tokens.

During your turn you can move within the Panopticon, interact with rooms to activate or inspect them, or talk to prisoners you encounter.

Different actions carry an associated risk, to be checked by flipping the cards of the Panopticon deck. The risk will be gradual and will increase day by day.
 It is necessary to survive all together until the final showdown, otherwise the game will be lost before any escape attempt is made.

The heart of the game is to discover and execute at least 4 out of 5 phases of the same escape plan by dropping resource cards to accomplish the demands of the prisoners who possess this information.

In the meanwhile you will create objects in the workshop to dig a tunnel or damage the electrical system. You will whisper a prayer in the chapel and maybe you will take on a temporary job...

Communication is prohibited, but you can take advantage of lines of sight and adjacencies to cooperate and coordinate in order to acquire as much knowledge as possible by lowering the risk. Should the plan be too fragmented, you will have to gather in one room to interact, at the risk of being spotted.

The perception of control will be defeated: run away from the Panopticon!

Will you be able to grasp your new freedom, or will you die at your last step?

-description from developer

name: Panorama
description:
What a lovely sunny day. Relax and enjoy the view from your hot air balloon!

In this leisurely tile placement game for 2-4 players, each player will try to create the most beautiful Panorama before the sun sets.

Put your panorama together one tile at a time, and choose them wisely: At the end of the game, you’ll score points based on the number of animals and flowers in each type of terrain (yes, even animals love flowers)! But watch out...
The further you move to select a tile, the more you leave behind for the hot air balloons of your opponents to pick up!

Games stay fresh and replayable through the common objectives, such as the longest river or the sky with the fewest clouds.

—description from the publisher

name: Parade of the Bruges Fools
description:
The government of Maximilian, who inherited the reign over Bruges in 1482, is harsh and taxes are high, leading to public discontent. When Maximilian visited Bruges in 1488, the people decided to revolt. They were able to imprison their monarch for over four months. Out of vengeance, Maximilian imposed a prohibition to organize festivities and fairs. To calm him down, you as the people of Bruges decided to organize a celebration to honor Maximilian.

In Parade of the Bruges fools players take on the role of a medieval labourer living in Bruges. Together, you try to gather musicians, acrobats and jesters to join a big parade in honour of Maximilian in order to earn his respect and therefore more freedom. However, the player who surpasses the expectations of grumpy Maximilian, wins this game and becomes mayor in Bruges.

Each turn, players perform one of three actions:

     persuade an artist by offering a drink in the local bar
     play an artist into the parade and score (some artists have the possibility to move other cards one space or to swap with a card)
     rest (by taking back into your hand all of the cards you needed to persuade artists)


When an artist reached the seventh column, the parade is complete and the game ends.

In the advanced game mood bonusses are dealt to the player(s) who took most notice of the King's temper (3 out of 20 mission cards).

name: Paradise: A Wastepunk Boardgame
description:
Paradise – A Wastepunk Boardgame is a skirmish game set in a post-apocalyptic world.
With stunning artwork and deep tactical gameplay, Paradise blends wasteland survival with a unique "wastepunk" aesthetic in a brutal fight for dominance.

Players lead rival factions fighting for control over a dying land. Each faction consists of four main characters (one of whom is the leader) and two henchmen.

The game is played in rounds, where each player alternates turns, activating one miniature each.

Miniatures can move on the map using some range tools to check distances.

Fights are based on dice rolls, and characters are not eliminated; they don’t die. They get KOed instead.

There is also a deck of cards that helps players in their strategies and fights. Those cards are dealt and drafted at the beginning of the game.

There are some objectives in each scenario, which are represented by points of interest on the map.

There are some terrain features that can be used to players’ own advantage.

Players earn points from controlling those points of interest and knocking out the opponent’s characters.

The first player to get to a specific number of victory points (according to the scenario) is the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Paragliders
description:
Impersonate a paraglider racing to reach three antennas before landing on the central target. Victory points are earned for flying above those antennas and other landmarks as well as performing stunts during your race. Always be prepared to adjust your navigation strategy in response to the changing weather and the terrain configuration.
This game could be classified as a navigation puzzle. During your turn you just need to move your pawn, while managing your unique precious resource: your altitude. Moving fast will make you lose altitude but let you take the lead of the race, while taking a detour to move above mountains or under clouds will make you gain altitude but avoid landing prematurely. With a smart map setup procedure generating unique maps, and a random weather forecast, the game will bring you a different navigation challenge every time.

—description from the designer

name: Pariah Card Game
description:
As the Elementals awaken, the fragile Order the God Pariah imposed upon ancient Chaos is threatened, and his world begins to tear itself apart.

Pariah is a dark-fantasy tactical battle game where players control opposing armies on a shared battlefield. Choose from four factions, the Humans of Cimeria, the Elementals, the Beastmen, and the Undead, each with distinct playstyles built around positioning, timing, and unit synergies. The game is designed to bring the feel of wargame-style army clashes and battlefield tactics to a non-TCG card game format.

Each player uses a 30-card unit deck, consisting of two copies of 15 unique unit cards. After drawing 10 cards, players secretly build a starting army worth up to 20 points, then deploy units alternately into the battle line, where formation and adjacency come into play. The game lasts up to 5 combat rounds, with units activating based on their Priority to attack or use abilities, while the evolving board state rewards smart trades and protecting key units.

When units are destroyed, the controlling player gains Elemental Energy equal to their point cost. Between rounds, players enter a Shop Phase to spend Energy on Relics and Evolutions that power their army. You win by Annihilation if you destroy all enemy units before the end of Round 5; otherwise, after Round 5 the winner is decided by Attrition: the player with the higher total point value of surviving units wins.

—description from the publisher

name: Monster Hunter World: Iceborne – The Board Game
description:
A mysterious song is echoing over the New World and causing the mass migration of Legiana. Now, the Research Commission needs YOU to investigate. Become a hunter of the Fifth Fleet and head to an uncharted arctic tundra where unknown threats roam wild. Protect the new Seliana basecamp from monsters unlike any you’ve faced before. Claim monster loot from your successful hunts to craft awesome new equipment, so you can hunt bigger and badder beasts until you’ve mastered Hoarfrost Reach!

The follow-up to Monster Hunter World, Monster Hunter World Iceborne: The Board Game is a cooperative arena combat game bursting with all new quests, exciting new gameplay, and a whole new line-up of MASSIVE monsters to hunt! It introduces some game-changing Iceborne twists. Navigate frozen terrain. Use your Clutch Claw to get close to the beasts. Find bonus info when tracking to help in the fight ahead. Manage your stamina in a new way.

Like World, Iceborne will plunge you into an open world where monsters won’t sit back and be hunted. Every fight is a boss fight. The monster controls the flow of combat, pushing you and your party to the limit — and each monster is wildly different. It’s crush-or-be-crushed with beasts as mobile as these!

Choose your hunter based on their unique weapon and playstyle. Pick which infamous monster you’ll be hunting across the ice. Track the creature in a quest driven by your decisions, avoiding pitfalls and collecting bonus resources to help you in the challenges ahead. Then dive into card-driven combat where teamwork, positioning, and stamina are key, targeting the monster parts you need for the equipment you want to craft — without getting wiped out!


     Play multiple epic campaigns with different combos of hunters, monsters, and equipment. The more monsters you slay, the better the weapons you can craft, the bigger the monsters you can hunt!
     Every monster comes with single session arena quests, so you can plunge right into combat.
     Monster Hunter World Iceborne: The Board Game includes solo mode.

name: Rivet Wars: Reloaded
description:
Brace yourself for the reload! WW1 history meets dieselpunk fantasy in an alternate universe of fast-paced chibi battles and unorthodox invention.

Rivet Wars: Reloaded is a reload of Rivet Wars: Eastern Front. A tactical miniatures board game with quickfire combat and customisable units, Rivet Wars: Reloaded also introduces competitive, co-op, solo, and team modes.

The game starts with almost zero setup, as each scenario just needs a selection of tiles to begin. Players choose their Rivet faction — Allied or Blight — and deploy waves of fresh units to stay one strategic step ahead.

The turn-based gameplay, speed, and visual theme make Rivet Wars: Reloaded feel like an RTS or mobile game come to life. Each turn, players have new deployment points to spend to bring fresh units into battle, meaning adaptive tactics as well as longer-term planning are key to claiming the strategic objectives and scoring victory points.

Battles can be played individually or as a campaign. The premise is simple and gameplay is speedy. The mechanics and RTS-style introduce tactical nuance to keep players on their toes, letting them switch up tactics mid-game with tide-turning action cards.  The plug system also lets players customise individual units to create combo effects, giving them the edge right when it counts.

—description from the publisher

name: Street Masters III: Tide of the Dragon
description:
SteamForged repack of:

     Tide of the Dragon Expansion
     Rumble Pack
     New Challengers Pack

name: Paws
description:
PAWS is a tableau- and engine-building game for 1–5 players.

You step into the boots of a wildlife conservationist, rescuing Africa’s endangered animals and building the most biodiverse sanctuary. Restore habitats and complete shared goals across legendary regions like the Serengeti and Okavango Delta.

On your turn, draft a die from the shared pool to perform one of five conservation actions everyone resolves together simultaneously:


    Adopt: Draw cards, set adoption fees, and adopt animals from each other to find the best home for each species. 
    Place: Place animals in fitting habitats like Grasslands or Waterholes, or tuck under others for synergies.
    Feed: Feed your adopted animals their specific diets to trigger abilities and build toward endgame Conservation Points.
    Protect Land: Draft land tiles (revealing more underneath), pursue goals, and score at game end when complete.
    Collect Reserve: Reclaim your stashed food from reserves back to your food bank for that satisfying payoff!


Use these actions to race for Region goals and trigger the Rain Dance. The conservationist with the most Conservation Points wins!

PAWS is for you if:


     You love positive player interaction without mean-spirited take-that.
     You enjoy low-downtime games with simultaneous actions by all players.
     You crave building powerful engines with satisfying combos.
     You want meaningful themes woven into every rule, not just pasted on.
     You appreciate flexible game length with tension in the race to trigger the finale.
     You like games that play well at every player count, including an Automa-style solo mode against wildlife ranger Naledi.


—description from the publisher

name: Pax Porfiriana: Ultimate Edition
description:
Pax Porfiriana – Latin for "The Porfirian Peace" – refers to the 33-year reign of dictator Porfirio Díaz, who ruled Mexico with an iron hand until toppled by the 1910 Revolution.

As a rich businessman (Hacendado) in the turbulent pre-revolutionary borderlands of the U.S. and Mexico, players compete to build business empires of ranches, mines, rails, troops, and banks while subverting opponents with bandidos, Native Americans, and lawsuits. Each turn goes as follows:

1. Action Phase: Perform three actions, such as play new cards, get new cards from the market, speculate on cards in the market, buy land, or redeploy troops.
2. Discard Headlines: Remove any Headlines (i.e. cards with the Bull-Bear icon) that have reached the leftmost position in the Market.
3. Restore Market: Restore the Market to twelve cards.
4. Income Phase: Collect one gold per Income, Extortion, and Connection Cube in play. If Depression, pay one gold for each card in play (includes Partners and Enterprises in your Row, and all of your Troops).

Four "scoring" cards (Toppling) are in the game and their effect depends on the current form of government. The government can change if troops are played and as a result of other cards. The form of government also influences different production values of the game, such as how much mines produce. Players win by toppling Díaz, either by coup, succession, revolution, or annexation of Mexico by the U.S. If Díaz remains firmly seated at the end of the game, then the player with the most gold wins.

The Ultimate edition features a brand-new card Era II set that extends the gameplay into the aftermath of the original events.

name: PDX
description:
Portland's airport is expanding and airlines are racing to become the city's favorite. In PDX, you take on the role of an airline competing to expand your concourse, open destinations, and optimize your routes through strategic resource management.

Each turn, players assign workers to airport offices to secure new destinations, construct gates, open service hubs, and invest in advertising campaigns. As planes arrive and depart, airlines gain actions and service tokens representing resources such as comfort, shopping, and food — that are used to unlock new routes and enhance airport infrastructure. Efficiently managing destinations and aligning services with market demand is key to outpacing the competition.

Throughout the game, players must balance long-term growth with tactical decisions, rearranging destinations on their gates, launching flights, and leveraging executive actions for strategic advantages. Effectively manage routes to chain bonus actions and time advertising campaigns to get ahead. The game ends when the airport reaches full capacity—either through office expansion or market saturation—at which point the airline with the most prestige wins.

PDX is a breezy 2-4 player game that blends worker placement, tableau management, and economic strategy into a highly interactive airport expansion race where every decision impacts the evolving air travel landscape. The game includes variants for seasoned players and can be played with the dice-based automa in solo mode or added to a 2 or 3 player game as an extra player.

—description from the publisher

name: Peace 1905
description:
By August 1905 the Russo-Japanese War had been raging for 18 months, with over a million soldiers, sailors, and engineers in arms,  it had cost the lives of between 100,000 to 200,000 participants and brought death and destruction to civilians. The war had seen the sinking of the Russian Pacific and Baltic fleets, and the great sieges at Port Arthur and Mukden. The world was shaken by the emphatic rise of Imperial Japan as a land and naval power. Russia had been blooded and humiliated.

But Russia was not yet done. Although both sides were financially exhausted it was Russia who continued to funnel troops into the war, while Japan’s manpower reserves were depleted. The war might yet continue, with further loss of life and property, and protracted instability in the Far East. With this would come the risk of further Russian humiliation. Both sides needed a way out. The door to that way out was opened by US President Theodore Roosevelt when he invited delegations of both sides to Portsmouth, New Hampshire - to a peace conference through August 1905. But with the sides so far apart on numerous key issues - the Russian Czar had stipulated no territorial concessions or reparation payments, and the Japanese Emperor wanted exactly those things and much more - what real hope was there that both sides could find a mutually satisfactory resolution?

In history, the answer is found in the Treaty of Portsmouth, a complex and significant diplomatic achievement, for which, for his part in facilitating and assisting, President Roosevelt was the first American to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. In Peace 1905, you - the players - will have Roosevelt’s assistance, but the work of successfully negotiating is down to you. Will you end the war, and bring a peace your governments approve of, or will the conference end in failure, and the war ignite again?

—description from the publisher

name: Street Masters: Rise of the Kingdom
description:
A SteamForged Games KS repack of

     Street Masters
     Street Masters SG
     Legend of Oni Expansion
     Twin Tiger Expansion
     Redemption Pack 1

name: Bardsung: Tale of the Forsaken Glade
description:
Bardsung: Tale of the Forsaken Glade remasters the gameplay of the first ENNIE award-winning Bardsung game for an all-new adventure.

The world of Bardsung is filled with tales of legendary heroes, sung by bards who travel from tavern to tavern. Players live out their versions of these fables, exploring branching paths to create their own legends.

Now, far from the Ancient Forge of the first game, a new tale unfolds. Forsaken Glade is the song of a sprawling forest realm where gods once walked, yet now withers from the corrupting influence of a vile black dragon. Abandoned by their gods, the elves waged war against the creature, yet only sacrifices have held the decay at bay.

There, a group of heroes must help bring the forest back from the brink of annihilation. Not only will they have to navigate the labyrinthine woods, but the corrupted threats and clashing peoples that lurk within. Twisted fae creatures like the Overseer; wretched, many-limbed cultists who feed on the dragon’s dark aura; hostile Rustblood tribes with ever-burning furnaces, and uneasy treaties between the elves themselves.

Embark on a grand campaign spanning ten chapters with deep, evolving story arcs and expansive quests. Along the way, you'll face stunning and grotesque enemies, encounter compelling NPCs, and uncover tempting side quests.

Once again, the story is yours to shape. Each choice you make could alter the path of your campaign, leaving a lasting impact on future events.

The trails and clearings are procedurally generated, starting from a single tile, so no two campaigns are the same. As you draw new tiles, the forest will unfold, revealing dangerous enemies, wandering monsters, challenging puzzles, and valuable treasure.

Your character is also yours to create. As you level up, you’ll unlock a wide range of possibilities, giving you the option to follow a set path or build a unique, multiclass hero. Explore stat upgrades, enhance existing skills, and access powerful new abilities.

From grunts to bosses, combat in the Forsaken Glade is more than just a battle—it’s a puzzle. Encounters unfold across multiple tiles, with heroes battling on several fronts. Expect advanced puzzles and more varied enemies with distinct behaviours. Enemies adapt to the battlefield, ensuring no two fights are the same. Positioning and teamwork are key, and just like your hero, enemies can level up, evolve their attacks, and even hold grudges.

The marching order system keeps gameplay flowing in a fast-paced, natural way, letting you assist friends at critical moments and keeping everyone at the table engaged. But not all challenges require a sword—the new Challenge system tests your party in non-combat encounters, where resource management and hero coordination are vital.

Bardsung: Tale of the Forsaken Glade can be played as a cooperative campaign for up to five players or in true solo mode. Explore the forest in standalone sessions or as part of a far-reaching campaign that evolves based on your decisions.

Inspire the songs. Live your legend. Become Bardsung.

—description from the publisher

name: Peking: 55 Days Of Fury
description:
Peking: 55 Days of Fury is a tactical wargame that places players in the heart of the 1900 Boxer Rebellion. Players choose to command either the besieged Eight-Nation Alliance or the attacking Chinese forces, each with unique objectives and strategies.

The game is designed for 1-2 players and offers a tense, immersive experience lasting approximately 1.5 hours. In solo play, players take control of the beleaguered Eight-Nation Alliance.

Each turn represents roughly 11 days of the siege. The game board depicts the International Legations, divided into four main areas. Players use a combination of event cards and operation points to execute actions, such as firefights, raids, artillery attacks, and barricade repairs.

The game begins with an initiative phase, determining the order of play. The player with the initiative initiates a mandatory firefight, followed by the other player. Players then play event cards to trigger various effects, supported by additional cards if conditions are met.

Next, the eight nation alliance player must manage supplies, with shortages potentially leading to epidemics or desertions. In the operation phase, players use remaining cards as operation points to perform actions. Finally, the maintenance phase involves checking victory conditions, handling fog of war cards, and preparing for the next turn.

A distinctive fog-of-war mechanic sets this games apart. Mastering this element is key to outmaneuvering opponents.

Will you be able to withstand the siege and protect the International Legations?

Experience the intensity of the Boxer Rebellion in this tactical wargame.

—description from the designer

name: Penitent
description:
Penitent is a solitaire game where players take the role of Quaker reformers, tasked with designing a visionary American penitentiary in the early 19th century.

Players will draw a floorplan for their model penitentiary and determine how it is governed by resolving a sequence of event cards. Your model will be evaluated at the end of each era based on its influence among reforms and architecture, funding, and the impact it has on the moral fiber of its inmates. Players will expand and renovate their blueprint at the conclusion of each era. Your penitentiary must endure three eras of events to win.

Will your penitentiary adhere to the Auburn reform's silent system or Pennsylvania's bold solitary confinement system? Will your inmates achieve rehabilitation through ceaseless labor or intense religious instruction? Will your penitentiary serve as a model of reform or be instructive only for its failure.

—description from the designer

name: Pensacola 1779-1782
description:
Pensacola 1779-1782 is a two-player, strategic-level wargame simulating Spanish, French, and Patriot operations against British and Loyalist forces in the territories of Louisiana and East and West Florida, from the Mississippi basin to Georgia, during the American Revolution. The campaign involved all major participants in the Revolution and was something of a microcosm of the larger global conflict of which the Revolution was just one theatre. The resulting operations saw British control of the northern coastline of the Gulf of Mexico come to an end.

Each game turn represents three months. Each hex on the map is approximately 40 kilometers (24 miles) across.
22x34 inch game map and a sheet of 176 5/8 inch counters.

name: Perfect Murder
description:
A murder shocks the mansion – but who is behind it? In this duel for two players, one side takes on the role of the murderer, the other that of the detective.

At the beginning, the murderer secretly decides which suspect committed the crime, which weapon was used, and through which of the eight rooms the mansion was entered. The detective tries to uncover all three secrets within eight rounds by playing cards, cleverly combining information, and ruling out false leads. 
Meanwhile, the murderer actively works against them, covering up traces and laying misleading clues. The result is a suspenseful deduction game full of bluffing and logic for two players aged 10 and up.

—description from the designer

name: Personal Demons
description:
A group therapy ritual where 1-4 players summon and seal away their own personal demons. This fast-paced, simultaneous-action drafting-style game has each player populating their own summoning circle in a tableau-style puzzler, aiming to form complete seals and conquer their demons. Hefty and colossal Demons of increasingly larger card sizes can be summoned and sealed once their requirements are met, and each one gives all players unique benefits that can change the way you play the game. Courage cards gained over the course of play grant player-specific abilities, sins are built up and spent as currency to take bonus actions, seals are cracked and replaced as the game progresses. Build an engine, choose your path to victory and score the most over three rounds to show your demons who's boss.

An optional upgrade pack adds the option to play with 5 or 6 players, and all of the components will fit into the base game box!

—description from the designer

name: Phanerozoic
description:
Simulate the evolution of plants and animals over roughly 500 million years during the Phanerozoic period. Each player has a unique goal to score points, so they will try to influence the ecosystem in different ways.

During the action phase, players will draft cards and play mutations, evolve species or use events to their advantage.
Each round ends with a nature phase, where the ecosystem finds its balance as plants grow and animals feed.

Will you cause the extinction of the dinosaurs or will you rejoice when inventive animals thrive?

—description from the designer

name: Phantom Division
description:
Phantom Division is a fully co-operative tactical combat game set in a sci-fi world of impending danger. Players choose a member of the elite Phantom Division defence force and are dispatched on a mission to protect a remote colony planet against an unknown and implacable enemy. The game features an innovative, challenging AI system that efficiently controls the enemies, different primary and secondary objectives for each mission, and "plot twists" that can introduce unexpected events into the game.

Combat is resolved either by rolling dice or by flicking the Phantom's bullets. The flicking based combat is completely optional. It also includes several mini-games where players will pilot shuttles, hack computer terminals, and defuse bombs. At the end of a mission, the players will have the opportunity to upgrade their Phantom for the next mission using XP they collected.

The game has full solo player support.

—description from the publisher

name: Phasmophobia: The Board Game
description:
Build a haunted property complete with foreboding rooms, full of unpredictable, randomised items. Then, draw a Ghost Type card from the Investigation File. Each Ghost has its own powers, paired with an evidence pool randomised for each playthrough, offering a terrifying challenge for even the most seasoned ghost hunters.

Using the Ghost Behavior board the ghost’s actions become unpredictable, driven by abilities presenting ever-changing challenges that take a psychological toll. The threat escalates as your sanity deteriorates, giving way to more aggressive and dangerous manifestations. So make sure you prepare before heading inside: equip your team with the best ghost hunting equipment found in your Van.

Venture into the residence to uncover cursed possessions and ghostly phenomena before, at last, arriving at the Ghost Room. Can your team conquer its surroundings and gather paranormal evidence before escaping?

You win if you survive and guess the correct ghost. You lose if everyone dies.

name: Phoenix
description:
Phoenix invites players to compose their phoenix with the prettiest feathers. Collect the feathers with the most points to win the game. You’ll have to collect feathers from other players’ nests, or your own.

But be careful: if you go home to collect a feather, you may be the last to play. To select a feather, each player has a token with the order of play.

By picking up a feather from an opponent, you give them your token, and therefore your place in the turn. If you play at home, you’ll have to turn it over and move further back in the turn order.

It’s all a question of strategy, whether you want to be among the first to select a feather, or whether you want to pick up a super-interesting feather.

Make the right choice...

—description from the publisher

name: Pierian Court
description:
The Royal Bard is Dead!

Hark ye! By Decree of the Monarchy, all who seek to become the Royal Bard shall gather in court to test words and wits. Don't be a bum, whether rhyme or hum, and weave a tale sending your competitors in fits!

In Pierian Court, you and your fellow players act as poets competing for the coveted role of Royal Bard. You take turns playing word cards, completing poems by fulfilling specific poetry style criteria. Once completed, you perform your poem for the Court! After being read aloud, your peers then judge for quality and performance. You receive points based on votes. Whoever obtains the most points at the end of the game wins! Congrats ye Royal Bard!

—description from designer

name: Hearts of Iron: The Board Game
description:
Hearts of Iron: The Board Game is a game of grand strategy warfare, tactical battles, and shrewd diplomatic choices based on the Hearts of Iron video game franchise released on PC by Paradox Interactive.

In the game, you lead one of five nations — United Kingdom, France, Italy, the Soviet Union, or the German Reich — during World War II, but will you re-enact history as it happened...or play out an alternative timeline, leading your nation down a new path? During set-up, you pair your nation with one of a suite of ideologies. You might choose, for example, to enact real history by playing the German Reich under fascism — or you could return the Kaiser to power and play the German Reich under monarchism. Each ideology has access to different focus decks, which will affect your resources and your routes to victory; these cards are played turn to turn and can influence everything from scoring victory points, to making lucrative trade agreements or declarations of war.

Each board game nation has its own player boards, ideologies, cards, tokens, and minis. Each player's tracker board shows their current supply levels of vital resources, such as political power, stability, production, and manpower.

At the start of each round, you receive resources based on how many territories you control with resource icons and factories. (You also gain resources during the game for trade agreements and engine cards that grant bonus resources.) You must pay to upkeep your stability, or pay even more to improve it. High stability grants bonuses to your nation, but with a high cost — although possibly not higher than letting your stability plummet.

You have a political board that shows all playable and non-playable nations, and you use it to manage who you're allied with, who you're at war with, and everything in between. During the political phase, you can spend political power to adjust your alliances and conflicts; for each point you spend, you move one of your flag tokens, changing your political stance with one other nation. Changing your stance aggressively will eventually lead to a state of war, whereas changing your stance peacefully will lead to forming an alliance — and the more your ideologies match, the less political power you need.

While at war with another nation, when your units move into their territory, you'll start combat. If you win, you'll conquer and take control of that territory, which is the fastest way to gain more resources. While in an alliance with another nation, you can move your units through their territory without starting a fight. You can also deploy units in your allies' territory! By forming an alliance, you can send units across the board to invade a distant nation.

The game lasts six rounds, covering 1939-1944, and you need the most points to win.

name: Pixie Trails
description:
Enter a whimsical world of Pixies! In Pixie Trails, you play as a Pixie foraging for snacks, collecting feathers, building friendships and playing with charms. Pixies are playful albeit an innately competitive species. Will you emerge the smartest Pixie with the most snacks or the social butterfly with the most Friendship accumulated?

On your turn, play direction cards face down simultaneously with other players and reveal to move your pixie around. Take actions at your location depending on the number of pixies at that location. Collecting Charms grant you unique powers to use to your advantage. Collect the most amount of Food during the four rounds of play to win the game. Or be the first Pixie to collect 7 Friendship to snatch an instant victory!

Outwit other players to seize the win in this cute but strategic game!

—description from the designer

name: Planet Bee
description:
Pioneers, you have been chosen for a mission of vital importance: to develop a prosperous and thriving ecosystem on this new, barren planet.

In Planet Bee, a strategic tile-placement game, your goal is to place the Ecosystem tiles at your disposal optimally to generate new life inside your geodesic dome. To win, you must make the most of your oxygen and water resources!

An effective tile placement strategy will allow you to house all kinds of plants and animals in your dome and earn points.

But be careful! Pay attention to bees, the true keepers of the new ecosystems here, just as they are on Earth. Meet their needs and they will reward you with plenty of points.

Your mission starts now: bee smart, bee victorious!

—description from the publisher

name: HELLDIVERS 2: The Board Game
description:
HELLDIVERS 2: The Board Game conveys the fast-paced, tactical, tongue-in-cheek energy of the video game, plunging players into the role of elite shocktroopers — the valiant Helldivers — who must protect Super Earth and rid the galaxy of alien threats in the name of liberty and democracy. Armed with deadly weapons (pistols, machine guns, flamethrowers), powerful stratagems (turrets, airstrikes, etc.), and co-ordinated tactics, players will work in squads to complete high-risk missions, navigate hostile battlefields, call in reinforcements, and overcome enemy swarms. As in the video game, players need to contend with evolving threats and objectives, in addition to watching for explosions and friendly fire. Every decision can mean the difference between glorious victory or total annihilation in service of Super Earth.

Helldivers win the game by selecting a mission and completing their objective. While doing so, they collect medals by defeating enemies, completing sub-objectives, and successfully extracting from the warzone, which will determine their overall performance. If a Helldiver falls in glorious battle, another is sent in their place. If they run out of reinforcements or time to complete the mission, the game is lost.

name: PocketParks
description:
PocketParks is a set collecting card game featuring all 63 US national parks with gameplay inspired by Chinese Mahjong. From Acadia to Zion, it has it all! Each cards features original photography of the park shot by the designer. Cards also include GPS coordinates of the location where each photo was taken to help inspire others to go explore the US national parks.

The goal of the game is to get the most points over 3 rounds and points are earned based on how many and how big your sets are. Sets are created based on 16 different distinguishing theme icons that help define features of the parks (ex desert, volcanoe, island, biggest parks, smallest parks, etc).

At the start of the round players begin with 6 cards, one card is flipped face up to form the discard pile and the rest of the cards are the draw pile. On a players turn, they can do one of three different actions: 1) Play/build on a single set. 2) Draw two then discard one card or play an event card. 3) Pay cards to steal from another players set or hand. The player that has three sets: a set of ≥2, set of ≥3, set of ≥4 will end the round, but all players score points with their sets. sets of 3 are one point, sets of ≥4 are 2 points, and the round winner gets 1 point for each set of 2.

Special rules: 

     Set of 5: with 4-of-a-kind hidden in your hand, once the 5th card is discarded, you can stop the game and claim the set of 5 off turn (play continues on as if you just had your turn)
     Set of 9: if you get 9-of-a-kind in your hand then you can just win from your hand and there is no need play your sets. 


—description from the designer

name: Politik
description:
Politik is a dynamic strategy game of military, political, and corporate control for 2–6 players.  Representing any of 12 nations, players develop distinct identities during their struggle for global supremacy.  They seize territories, orchestrate propaganda campaigns, and pilot companies to conquer markets.  500+ unique cards provide the landscapes, propaganda, companies, assets, and events for each nation to forge its path to power.

Following the Great Collapse, the world is fragmented but finding its way after decades of Imperial disinformation.  Ascending from those ashes, pirate signals entangle the airwaves.  Deserted broadcast stations spark back to life, trumpeting new anthems.  With right and wrong blurred, a disoriented world yearns for truth.  And one nation will decide it.

-description from designer

name: Pop Art
description:
Create and arrange silkscreen prints in your gallery and become the next pop art sensation of the 1960s.

Layering a foreground card on a background card blends their colors. Depending on which cards you layer together, you'll also craft unique goals that score your prints’ colors or illustration types.

Select and combine a foreground and background card from your hand and add them to your 3x3 tableau. Then pass the remaining cards to the player on your left, and draw a foreground and background card. Once all players have completed their tableau, the game ends. The player with the most points wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Portamentals
description:
Step into the thrilling world of Portamentals, where you take on the role of a daring Portamental guild leader, venturing through mystical elemental portals. Engage in epic battles, recruit awe-inspiring dragon-like creatures known as Portamentals, and harness their powers to dominate the elements. In this dice-battling, engine-building, and worker-placement board game, every move you make is a step closer to earning victory points and achieving the ultimate title: Master of the Elements. Strategize, upgrade your abilities, and command your team of Portamentals to outwit your rivals. Adventure, strategy, and a world of elemental power await—do you have what it takes to rise to the challenge? Let the portal adventures begin!

—description from the publisher

name: Last Shot
description:
The Cold War is winding down. You've played your part so far, but now the loose ends are being tied up. Will you get out of the cloak-and-dagger trade alive?

Enter the world of international espionage with Last Shot, a fast-playing game of intrigue and strategy that's never the same game twice. Play your hand wisely to protect yourself. Draw — or steal — a "terminated" card, then choose the right time to eliminate your rivals. The last player standing wins.

—description from the publisher

name: President
description:
President is a strategic bluffing and negotiation game for 3 to 10 players, where ambitious animals vie for leadership within their political party. Your goal: reach 7 victory points to claim the presidency.

Use your cards to climb the party ranks, gain media influence, or trigger surprise actions. Make (and break) alliances, accuse rivals, and fight for the Corruption token, which brings valuable points while in your possession.

Expect shady deals, strategic betrayals, and chaotic twists. In President, reading your opponents is just as important as playing your hand. How far will you go for power? In politics, all moves are fair game.

—description from the publisher

name: President Maker
description:
President Maker is a 2–4 player board game that captures the fierce intrigue and strategic maneuvers of a Korean presidential election through immersive gameplay.

Each player becomes a fictional presidential candidate, traveling across the country to hold campaign rallies, gain public support through policies, and—at times—resort to political maneuvers. The election consists of two rounds before the final vote. Your total Support, along with the Engagement levels formed in each region over those two rounds, will ultimately determine the outcome of the Vote Count.

The fate of each candidate hinges on two forces: the loyal base built throughout the campaign, and the voters who show up on election day to cast their decisive ballots. Step into a parallel Korea and challenge yourself to become its next president—through strategy, nerve, and a bit of political drama.

—description from the publisher

name: Prestige
description:
Build beautiful palaces in this expert level Euro game. Place your overseers in different areas, but also pay attention to the order for the upcoming rounds. Acquire resources and decorate your buildings to create a masterpiece.

Prestige is a strategic game that offers many different possibilities.  We are in the time of the Rococo. The nobility is vying for the most prestige and we take on the role of lords of the castle. In the course of the game, we want to expand and decorate our small castle. We have 5 instructors at our disposal to do this. We use the instructors to create building contracts and hire ambitious craftsmen who gain experience and improve their skills, which are important for the further expansion of our castle. The craftsmen will be used to carry out different building contracts with varying degrees of efficiency.

The game takes place over 3 years, each with the 4 seasons. The seasons can have an influence on construction and the procurement of resources. For this reason, it is very important to plan your individual actions carefully and to keep a close eye on your fellow players.

In each season, we have various actions available to us by deploying our instructors:
        • Acquire resources from the resource plant
        • Place a building order
        • Buy, sell or exchange resources on the market and buy workers
        • Expand the land
        • Hire a new craftsman
        • Become the starting player for the next round
        
The placement of the instructors also controls the player order in the next season. It can and will happen that a player has several consecutive turns. This allows for many strategies.
        
Only those who cleverly expand their castle, adapt to current events and keep a close eye on their fellow players will win this game.

—description from the publisher

name: Primacy
description:
Primacy is a sci-fi strategy game for 2-4 players, set in a city where the line between reality and cyberspace is blurred. Players represent factions vying for control of the city after a mysterious mind-control program turns off, creating a power vacuum. Seek power through battle, intrigue, public relations, and propaganda.

Conquer 3 types of sector throughout the city for different benefits, including income, soldier recruitment, bonus actions, and access to terminals to spread propaganda. Controlling terminals will score victory points, but won't help you improve your power or position. Balance is key to achieving victory.

Battles are resolved by secretly committing gear cards to 3 different objectives, and simultaneously revealing. Choose wisely between PR to boost your propaganda, loot for resources, and conquest to control new territory.

Each game contains 112 soldiers, 60 control markers, 29 modular hex tiles, 4 3-layer player boards with variable inserts, 4 double-sided faction tiles, a public console board, and tons of cards and credits, all with beautiful illustrations by Calder Moore. The game can be played with symmetrical player boards for an easier teach, or with various combinations of asymmetrical boards and faction powers for additional variability and richness.

name: Primal Hex
description:
Primal Hex is a highly tactical game for 2–4 players. Together with your Warchief and an Advisor, you'll lead your tribe in a battle for control over a paradise-like land, where the soil is fertile and the game is plentiful.

Over the course of four seasons, you'll use ever-changing resources (represented by the roll of 10 dice) to execute strategic orders you've planned in advance. You'll conquer territories, harvest crops, and clash with rival tribes. But remember — only one tribe can claim victory!

—description from the publisher

name: Principes
publisher: (Self-Published); Ediciones MasQueOca; Fox in the Box
description:
Year 1202, the Kingdom of Poland has been divided for 64 years. The last, respected Senior-Prince, Mesco the Old, dies in peace, but with his death the fragile order collapses.

In Principes, Poland is broken into 4 Principalities, led by 4 branches of the Piast dynasty. The players' task is to take control of their part of the Kingdom and lead to the coronation of one of their Princes. To do this, players will develop and expand their lands, wage wars and form alliances with neighboring factions. Only the most persistent and clever will succeed!

Players will compete with each other for a maximum of 6 Rounds, which are divided into 3 Periods. Each Round begins with the revealing of the History Card (through them, the Teutonic Knights and the Mongols can appear on the board, among others). The core mechanism of the game consist of secretly programming 3 of 6 available Actions, which are: Progress, Taxes, Assembly, Movement, Building and Politics. The goal of the participants is to climb up the 3 Tracks (the Track of Power, Support of the People and the Clergy) to the highest position - then they can crown their prince, and thus immediately end the game with their glorious victory!

The game is being created thanks to a scholarship from the Minister of Culture and National Heritage of Poland and tells the story of a key, extremely interesting period of confusion, chaos and growth in Polish history - it is called the time of great disruption, after which (with the help of players) the rebirth will come.

—description from the designer

name: Project Skyline
description:
Project Skyline is a city building game with a unique blend of strategic deck-building and area control in three dimensions. Each game will take 2-4 players to a famous city such as New York or Tokyo, where they will collectively shape the skyline of the city while trying to stay on top of the competition.

The goal of the game is simple: whoever has the most money at the end of the game is the winner. The road to victory however may prove not as straightforward. Throughout the game, players will gain money by building apartments in the city and spend money to improve their personal decks of construction cards, allowing them to build more efficiently or unlocking completely new avenues of scoring altogether. Finding the right balance between investment and pay-off is the key to success.

At the end of each turn, the current player will score all monuments in the city that they have connected to the central landmark. The twist: Only the topmost apartment in each building counts towards connections, locking the players in a tense back-and-forth race for those precious top spots in the most important buildings. Can you win the race to the top or will you find a different route to victory?

name: Propagation Station
description:
Watch your plants grow and propagate clippings to share with your friends in this cozy auction and tableau game for 2 to 4 plant lovers. Acquire the most valuable collection to make your friends green with envy!

In Propagation Station, players cultivate a thriving house plant collection by bidding on a variety of plants and essential equipment. Strategic auctions let you outbid opponents — but winning means sharing your bid with them! Balance growth and inventory while battling pests and optimizing your setup with grow lights and equipment. Each turn presents choices: nurture your plants, expand your collection, or disrupt rivals. The goal? Build the most efficient propagation station and prove your green thumb reigns supreme!

—description from the publisher

name: Prophet Without Honor
description:
In early September 1925, two separate military disasters rocked the United States: a bungled flight during which three Navy seaplanes failed to make it from the West Coast to Hawaii; and, the loss of the Navy's first helium-filled airship and prized treasure, USS Shenandoah and 14 of its crew while flying over the Midwest on an ill-advised public relations tour.

Were these accidents?

Or were they the "result of the incompetency, the criminal negligence, and the almost treasonable negligence of our national defense by the Navy and the War Departments?”

One man would sacrifice his career to take-on the Army, the Navy and the White House to answer these questions.

Blood was on someone's hands and unless something changed, more aviators were going to die in the “old flaming coffins."
