—description from the publisher

name: The Adventurers: The Temple of Chac
description:
The Adventurers: The Temple of Chac is a exciting, push-your-luck adventure game where players take on the roles of rival treasure hunters exploring a dangerous, ancient temple deep in the Guatemalan jungle. Dedicated to Chac, the Mayan god of rain and thunder, this temple is filled with priceless artifacts...and deadly traps.

Players explore the temple by rolling dice, to gather treasures and unique artifacts dedicated to different Mayan gods. They must navigate hazards like lava rooms with hidden trap tiles, shifting crushing walls, rapids that can sweep them away, and a massive rolling boulder that steadily advances, threatening to trap them inside forever. The more treasure they carry, the fewer actions they can perform, making greed very dangerous.

The goal is to escape the temple alive with the most valuable collection of treasures. Only those who can balance risk and reward, avoid injuries, and outsmart both their rivals and the temple’s traps will come out as the greatest adventurer.

—description from the publisher

This new edition of The Adventurers: The Temple of Chac is part of a 3-game collection that uses the same system and has complete compatibility of adventurers and their starting gear.


     An entirely new Action System where players do not only roll their own dice, but assign them to specific actions.
     A new encumbrance system that still penalizes players for being too greedy, but never results in them completely skipping their turn.
     Zotz’s Cave tunnel, dedicated to the God of the bats. Adventurers can find Zotz’s treasures when searching but may also encounter vampire bats and large, venomous spiders that have made their home in the cave.
     The removal of character death/player elimination from the core rules except at the very end of the game.
     A new lockpicking system that uses bag pulls instead of dice rolls.
     The addition of being able to steal treasures from the opposing adventurers.
     A new scoring system that accounts for a type of set collection as well as for wounds and injuries.

name: The Adventurers: The Tomb of the Pirate Queen
description:
Descend into the sunken tomb of the infamous Pirate Queen Shi Yang. Floodwaters rise with every turn, blocking paths and sealing away treasure. Avoid deadly booby traps set by her loyal crew, uncover secret passageways hidden in the flooded stone, and desecrate the altars of the Dragon Gods to seize their guarded riches. Outmaneuver your rivals and escape before the tomb becomes your grave.

—description from the publisher

name: The Adventures of Tintin: The Trick-Taking Game
description:
In The Adventures of Tintin: The Trick-Taking Game, players must uncover the hidden plot cards of their opponents by searching for clues in locations scattered across the world. Each location card has a different rule for winning tricks, so the player who wins the trick in a given round can ask a question about the plot card belonging to the owner of the location card — provided they meet the requirements of the character cards played that round.

As the game progresses, players eliminate false leads in their notebooks until someone reaches a conclusion and correctly deduces another player's plot card, earning points toward the final score.

—description from the designer

name: The Anarchy
description:
This is a hybrid card/board game inspired by William Dalrymple’s book The Anarchy on the relentless rise of the East India Company.

The board is a political area map of India circa 1740. Each area on the map has a corresponding card suit identified by the background color and name on top for clarity.

The core mechanics are taken from the The Great Khan Game which used a Rummy-like draw-and-discard system whereby players take initial control of an area by placing a "meld" from their hand which has to have a leader.

There are 126 cards, each of which represents a place, leader, army, or commodity within a given area which when melded together represent an area’s political strength (crown symbols), defense strength (castles), attack or defense strength (swords), and economic strength (treasure chests).

The first player to reach 20 treasure chests in their combined melds in their income phase at the end of a turn wins the game.

Once placed, a meld/area can be captured by rival players either through political coups or military attacks.

Coups are done by placing an "alternative government" meld with more crowns than the incumbent. The defender can thwart these by adding cards from their hand to strengthen their government. The winner gets to steal the loser's meld.

Military attacks from neighboring areas are made uncertain using simultaneous bidding. Money played a bigger part in battles than soldiers in this history. For instance, the English East India Company’s Robert Clive won his celebrated Battle of Plassey by bribing his opposing general not to pitch.

Evenly matched battles tend to be disastrous with both sides suffering three cards "killed" as in placed at the bottom of the draw pile, possibly causing both areas to revert to neutral.

—description from the designer

name: The Atlantean Wars
description:
The Atlantean Wars depicts the ancient and mythical war between three all powerful civilizations: Atlantis, set in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, the empire of Mu, set in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, and the Matriarchy of Lemuria, set around the island of Madagascar. The board depicts the entire world, divided in land and maritime zones.

After a long time of peace, and with the oncoming apocalypse, war pits once again those 3 mighty titans, war for the domination of the world, war for the control of the rich zones of Orichalc, this fabulous alloy allowing them to build wondrous machines of war, war for the gaining the alliance of the numerous small nations around the world. The Empires will be able, to win this war once and for all, to expand their territory with their troops, to build new colonies which will grow in power, to build strange and beautiful wonders allowing for teleport movements, to further their knowledge of technology, all the while battling their neighbors and exchanging with them deadly "fire of God" (read nuclear)attacks.

Players proceed through 4 phases, Initiative, Tech, Build, and Activation, leading to combat which is resolved with a die roll on a differential of strength chart, adding a number of "artefact events" according to the tech level of the engaged units. During the end of the Acitvation phase, the players check to see if a sudden death victory occurs, when a player dominates a majority of the orichalc zones, or of the wonders.

name: The Brightview Haunting
description:
One night, a superstitious teen named Bert Hudson ventured a bit too far into Brightview's dark past. As he stumbled across strange markings in the forest, Bert inadvertently broke a seal from an ancient Elder Tree that would awaken a demon known as the Whisperer.

The Brightview Haunting is a one versus many cooperative horror game. Play as either Exorcists, working together to save Bert and banish the Whisperer, or as the Whisperer, tracking them down to spread corruption and attempting to possess them all.

Experience asymmetric gameplay as each Exorcist utilizes different passive actions, and the Whisperer uses a set of unique abilities that get upgraded as the game progresses. As Exorcists, trigger random Events through key actions like invoking ritual items, or using corrupted artifacts.  Determine when to use special items, manage your corruption, and strategically move around the map to outwit the Whisperer. As the Whisperer, possessing Exorcists turn them against their allies. When this happens, the game becomes team based, and a possessed Exorcist coordinates with the Whisperer. Any Exorcist who gets possessed during the game is able to be saved in different ways, in which they'd switch back to their original team.

Will you become vessels for the demon or banish the Whisperer back into the Elder Tree for good?

—description from the publisher

name: The Cask
description:
"The thousand injuries of Fortunato I had borne as I best could, but when he ventured upon insult, I vowed revenge."

Open The Cask to immerse yourself in the world of Edgar Allan Poe! Based on his classic suspense tale "The Cask of Amontillado", this two-player game allows you to step into the roles of Fortunato and Montresor as you work to escape the vault — or exact your revenge.

On your turn, play one of the cards in your hand by revealing it, performing that card action, and placing it in your discard pile. The Fortunato player must move around the board to collect a combination of items while evading Montresor's brick tiles. To avoid the avenger's terrible plan, be sure to work quickly before Montresor can completely surround you!

—description from the publisher

name: The Cats of New Orleans
description:
Welcome to The Cats of New Orleans. The year is 1868, and the city has acquired a modicum of peace in the aftermath of the Civil War. Cats — and even dogs — lick their wounds and look toward building a better life. However, the discontent of the city’s vermin bubbles like a cauldron full of crawfish that’s about to boil over.
 The Cats of New Orleans. is a miniatures solo/cooperative campaign game set in a turbulent time in the Crescent City. The game plays out over a series of linked scenarios that form a campaign and ongoing story. Each scenario in the campaign affects the next. In fact, many end with choices the players must make that lead them to the next. You will be playing directly on the coil bound scenario book and using 12 sided dice for combat and collecting cards for loot, skills and powers.

As you play each scenario, the heroes learn who’s behind the recent troubles in New Orleans and come closer to putting a permanent stop to their awful ambitions. Along the way, they must defeat swarms of mosquitos, rats, snakes, and other foul creatures. The heroes also gain loot and experience to unlock skills they can use to face stronger and tougher foes.

The Cats of New Orleans takes several sittings to play all the way through, but you can save your progress easily, especially between scenarios. This rulebook helps you learn to play the game by guiding you through the first three scenarios. Just play the game as you read through the text.

The first three scenarios are meant to be played until thoroughly understood. If you fail to finish a scenario or feel like you need a bit more time to master the rules they introduce, play them again.

Once you proceed past these first few scenarios, the game often offers you choices as to which scenario you can play next. The path you choose can change events in the campaign, so pick carefully. Once you’re done with one play through the campaign, though, be sure to come back and try different options to see how they pan out for you.

In the first scenario we teach you how to set up a scenario, move your heroes on the map, search for essential loot, and pick up items. In addition, you learn how to move the Vermin Army’s figures, starting with the vicious mosquitos.

-description from designer

name: The Coming Storm II: Quadrigame of the Fourth Coalition
description:
Quadrigame of the Fourth Coalition 
October 1806 – June 1807

These four games explore the major battles of 1806–07, where the French Army encountered two different opponents with different capabilities, from the leadership-challenged Prussians in Saxony to the chaotic battle conditions in winter against the Russians. Based on OSG's Special Studies, which provide a turn-by-turn narrative of the four battles. Each game shows the approach to the battlefield on the day before battle. The Jena-Auerstadt game has both battlefields on one map and allows both sides to redeploy before battle.

We are offering a new edition, with new maps—not too much different in detail—but rendered in Charles Kibler's naturalistic style. TCS2 will be updated to use the Universal Deck and latest series rules (deck not included). With few exceptions, the counters will be identical to the first edition.

JENA-AUERSTADT  13–14 October, 1806
PULTUSK/GOLYMIN  24–25 December, 1806
EYLAU  7–8 February, 1807
FRIEDLAND  13–14 June, 1807

NOT INCLUDED: Optional Card Decks

—description from the publisher

name: The Creeps: The Monster-Trapping Game
description:
Monsters are attacking the town, and kid detectives known as the Creeps have to figure out which ones they can trap! Only the monsters with the most cards under them will score, but you also need those same monster cards in your hand to get points, so you have to decide when to play a monster card and when to keep it in your hand.

With The Creeps: The Monster-Trapping Game, you can play the "family game" for quicker games and younger audiences, or play the "full game" for asymmetric powers, game-changing trap cards, and more strategic scoring options.

—description from the publisher

name: Scoville: 2nd Edition
publisher: Trick or Treat Studios; Arclight Games; Grail Games
description:
An updated printing of a modern classic! Players will plant peppers, harvest them, cross-breed them, sell them, and make delicious chili to score points!

This edition includes colorblind-friendly plastic peppers, new art, and The Labs Expansion.

—description from the publisher

name: The Crimson Queen: The Battle for Wonderland Combo Edition
description:
Step into a twisted, enchanted version of Wonderland where every card is a weapon, every suit a kingdom, and every round an all‑out battle for power. The Crimson Queen takes the traditional trick‑taking games of Hearts and  turns it into total mayhem.

Players lead five distinct realms — the traditional Hearts, Spades, Diamonds, Clubs, and the all new Moons — into a cunning struggle for control of the throne. With vibrant illustrations that bring Alice, the Mad Hatter, and the enigmatic Queen of Hearts to life, every card is infused with whimsical character and strategic potential in The Crimson Queen. Traditional trick‑taking mechanics are elevated by combo‑driven scoring and the unpredictable Chaos Deck with one‑time effects that can upend an entire round and reward bold, creative play.  The player who reaches 150 points - or has the highest score - wins.

The Crimson Queen contains the four standard card suits from Hearts.
The Crimson Chaos expansion adds rule-changing Chaos cards.
The White Queen's Gambit expansion expands player count by adding the Moons suit.

—description from the designer

name: The Daily Weather
description:
As The Daily Weather’s newest meteorologist, it’s your duty to get the weather report ready. However, first you must arrange the weather map so only the current day and month are visible, and the weather pattern of the day is visible. Can you make today’s map?

Determine today’s unique setup using the real-world date and season, then use overlapping cards to work your way towards a solution. Score points for more effective solutions as you try to predict the unpredictable weather!

name: The Dawn of Pangaea
description:
At the dawn of time, the first spirits were born - gentle and tireless in their mission to spread life across the barren land of Pangaea. As players, you enter this mythical age, growing your trees and performing rituals to awaken Gaia’s dormant energy and summon elemental creatures to roam and nurture the growing continent.

In the Dawn of Pangaea, you and your fellow players act as the first spirits of Pangaea. On your turn, you must choose 2 of the 5 actions that are available to you e.g. planting seeds, growing trees and expanding your forest. Anytime during your turn, you may also play blessing or favor tokens, that you have collected during the game. These tokens will also allow you to summon the ancient guardians with their powerful abilities. Play Ritual cards to score points for growing your trees across different biomes or for attracting creatures that require a specific weather condition. With every point that you gain from these rituals, you climb higher up the sacred Mountain.

The first player who reaches the top of the mountain, triggers the end of the game and initiates the final scoring. The player with the most points wins the game and gains the high blessing of Gaia.

—description from the publisher

name: The Final Curse of Dracula
description:
Dracula's Curse is a 1 vs All social deduction game where players take the roles of Villagers in a town cursed by Dracula's powers. The goal of the game for the villagers is to find who Dracula is and kill him before is too late, while Dracula's goal is to turn all the living villagers into vampires and spread his reign of fear. However, villagers won't have it easy. With each night that passes, a new vampire will emerge among them. Villagers will have to work together to kill Dracula before they get turned into vampires and not be able to kill him.

—description from the publisher

name: Treasure of the Dwarves
description:
Deep in the mountains of the dwarven realm is where you'll find the best deals!

In Treasure of the Dwarves, you place treasures up for sale, then evaluate secret bids from the other players. Consider their offers carefully because once you look at a new bid, you can't go back to a previous one. Some treasure is just worth points; others provide special abilities. Only the shrewdest deal-maker will come out on top!

Everyone is involved on every turn of the game as you puzzle over how to collect coins, gems and magical treasures. Knowing what your treasure is worth is important — but so is knowing whose offer to look at first!

name: TROLLympics
description:
Set in the same world as TrollFest, players will put together teams of fantasy denizens to compete in the TROLLympics! Events are revealed and then athletes and action cards are drafted. Then for each event, players will put together a team to compete, wager on who the winner will be, play action cards, and then add their athletes values to corresponding dice rolls to determine the winner.

Score points by doing well AND by correctly guessing the winners of events. The player with the most points after a winter season and a summer season of events will be the winner!

—description from the publisher

name: At the Gates of Loyang: Second Edition
description:
The classic economic strategy game from acclaimed designer Uwe Rosenberg, At the Gates of Loyang, is back with a brand new second edition. This game rewards careful planning, clever trading, and tactical use of resources.

China, 2000 years ago. Loyang (Luòyáng) capital of the Han Dynasty, flourishes as one of the great centers of ancient civilization. The growing city hungers for fresh food, and local farmers rise to the challenge - cultivating wheat, pumpkins, turnips, cabbages, beans, and leeks in the fertile fields surrounding the city walls. After each harvest, they gather at the gates of Loyang to sell, trade, and expand their farms, vying to become the most prosperous farmer.

This second edition includes an all new cooperative mode by Ralph Bruhn and ode. In the cooperative mode you are asked to provide the City Festival with vegetables, and to fulfill special requests for certain customers. You are confident you can deliver vegetables, serve customers, collect donations . . . and still assure your own prosperity. But can you keep your promises? Work together as a team to try to manage all the appointed tasks.

name: Camp Grizzly: Second Edition
description:
Camp Grizzly is a semi-cooperative survival horror game in which you and your group take on the roles of camp counselors being stalked by Otis, a homicidal maniac in a bear mask. To win, players must collect a set of objectives to trigger (and survive!) one of four available Finales. Along the way, the counselors will find items and weapons to help them survive and fight back, encounter cameos and plot twists, bump into errant campers in need of help, and maybe even sneak off for some foolin' around.

Rife with Easter eggs and steeped in lore, Camp Grizzly is a love letter to the horror genre that creates unforgettable moments and stories at the table, and we can't wait to get this new edition into your hands!

Camp Grizzly Second Edition will include the full game and all previous expansions, and is being created in collaboration with the original designer and artist. Here is what's new:


     Double-sided game board with an all-new camp layout
     Great quality components and cards
     A few rules tweaks including adjustments based on player count
     Optional rules to remove player elimination
     Updated art & graphics


—description from the publisher

name: The Great Escape
description:
An exciting cooperative WWII game where players try to successfully escape their POW from Stalag Luft III. Designed by Philip duBarry. In the Great Escape, you and your fellow air force officers will follow in the footsteps of the prisoners of Stalag Luft III, as you attempt to dig tunnels under the wire and escape. This will require exceptional timing, resourcefulness, and some luck. Outsmart the guards and carry on the war in the only way you can. If you help twelve prisoner pawns escape before the Gestapo locks down the camp, you and your comrades will have won the game. Each turn you have action points and with these action points you dig tunnels, move your pawns or collect valuable resources.

—description from the publisher

name: Dark Pact
description:
To win the deck-building game Dark Pact, you need to complete one of the game's thirteen Dark Pacts, each of which has a unique winning condition.

To set up, each player has a deck of ten cards, with cards being either actions, treasures, or multipliers. Players take turns clockwise until someone achieves a Dark Pact: "Keeper" Dark Pacts can stay in play, and if you ever meet their condition based on the cards you have in play, you win; "Instant" Dark Pacts are played as an action, and if you meet their condition based on the cards you have in hand, you win. (Alternatively, if the deck runs out, the player with the highest sum of Insight minus Curses wins.)

On a turn, you play one action from your hand, and an action might let you play additional actions; draw cards; gain cards from the supply; exile cards; and so on. Some cards attack opponents, and they can reveal a react card in response. Played cards stay in your play area.

Next, you can buy cards, first playing treasures from your hand to gain coins. (Action cards played earlier might also have coins on them.) You can purchase cards from the ten-card supply, as well as one card from your grimoire, which starts with three specific cards and to which you can add other cards during play.

You can modify an action or a treasure by playing x2 and x3 multipliers at the same time. Multipliers affect all numerals on the action or treasure, whether for coins, curses, draws, actions, etc.

To end your turn, clean up, first carrying out "clean up" effects on played cards, then discarding all played cards (except those that can remain in play, such as some Dark Pacts) and cards from your hand that you don't want. If necessary, draw to fill your hand to five cards.

Dark Pact includes solitaire rules in which you compete against a bot that tries to win in one of three ways.

name: The Great Hunger: Ireland's Tragedy in the 19th Century
description:
The Great Hunger begins as a game that simulates good times in Ireland at the start of the 19th century, as the Irish population expanded - thanks to the potato. This new crop was a godsend, allowing people to raise enough food for a whole family on a small, rocky plot of land. They became dependent on the prolific tubers. But in 1845 the blight arrived, utterly destroying the potato harvest.

Dependence on a single variety and growing on marginal land helped the blight; soon hunger and disease spread through the island. British economic policy discouraged assistance, fearing a collapse of farm prices and a population dependent on public welfare. But assistance did arrive, often from unexpected sources. Some people found work in new industries, or on the expanding English estates. Millions emigrated, booking passage on dangerous “coffin ships”, usually heading to America. The famine was a defining moment in the history of Ireland, as well as the USA and other countries. Today it is remembered by the Irish people as "an Gorta Mór" – The Great Hunger.

Players represent families of tenant farmers and itinerant field hands. At first, your people will grow, using the events on the top half of your cards to help add more population cubes to the map. But then the blight arrives, and you use the events on the bottom half: finding aid or employment for your people, scrambling to the emigrant ship, or representing the spread of disease and English estates.

The game ends when the "Blight Abates" card is drawn.  The player with the most population wins.

—description from the designer

name: The Great Library
publisher: Eagle-Gryphon Games; Delta Vision Publishing; DiceTree Games; Editions Philibert; YOKA Games
description:
In the third century B.C., Ptolemy I envisioned the creation of the Great Library of Alexandria, a monumental repository of human knowledge housed within a space known as the Mouseion, which was dedicated to the Muses, the nine goddesses of the arts. Ptolemy's dream was to amass the world's knowledge, and the library housed countless manuscripts, reflecting his Herculean effort to collect and preserve the intellectual heritage of the ancient world and gain renown to his name. The Great Library, situated near the bustling port of Alexandria, welcomed ships carrying relics, scholars, and the wisdom of distant lands. The Chief of Librarians oversaw the organization of the vast collection. The library's shelves whispered with the rustling of ancient parchment, embodying the spirit of intellectual curiosity and cross-cultural exchange.

As players step into the sandals of Librarians in the Great Library, you take on the crucial responsibilities of leading the institution within the Mouseion, navigating the challenges and opportunities presented by this legendary center of knowledge. Amidst the relics, diverse minds, and bustling port activity, the Librarians became the primary custodians of knowledge, shaping the legacy of the Great Library and contributing to the rich tapestry of ancient history.

During this game, you research Great Works, deliver Crafts to the kingdom, and train Scribes to translate Manuscripts. Then, you send the Manuscripts, Great Works, and Crafts to the Great Library to gain Renown, Improvements, and other benefits, and attract the great Scholars of the time to the Library to work with you. You will need to manage resources to achieve your aims, including the most important resource of all: Time.

As Scholars perform their work, Generations will pass triggering Events and the Great Library will fill. When the second Event is triggered or when 2 or fewer empty spaces remain in the Library, the end of the game is triggered and the player with the most Renown is named the Greatest Librarian and wins the game.

—description from the publisher

name: The Great Sea
description:
From their homeland in the Levant to the distant shores of Carthage, the Phoenicians made a name for themselves as master traders, seafarers, and navigators. Their fierce bireme galleys dominated the Mediterranean, with a focus on protecting their vital trade networks. They developed a new script for writing and produced jewelry, pottery, intricate glassware, and highly valuable purple fabrics. As a city state leader of Tyre, Sidon, Byblos, or Arwad, you need to assemble your fleet and establish your influence across The Great Sea.

The aim of The Great Sea is to be the first player to gain victory through conquest or commerce. Players must construct and mobilize their ships, fortify their trade routes, and research new technologies for land and sea. Key to their success will be controlling the various ancient temple sites across the map. The game ends immediately once a player's temple marker reaches the same space as either their combat or trade marker.

—description from the publisher

name: Dracula's Fortune
description:
Count Dracula is dead for the second and final time, and unfortunately, he didn't leave a will. As one of his favorite vampiric students, you believe that you should be first in line to inherit. However, all the other acolytes feel the same way! Connive to collect the best mementos for yourself, splitting and sharing Count Dracula's possessions so you get the lion's share of the loot and the bat's share of the glory.

Each round, you'll draw 4 cards from the deck, containing some of Dracula’s belongings that need to be divided up. Then, you'll split those cards into two piles between you and one of your neighbors.

They'll choose one of the piles and give the other one back to you, while you do the same thing with the opposite neighbor. Try to split the piles so that you get the cards you need while preventing your opponents from getting the stuff they want!

Your inheritance is made up of all the cards in front of you, and will grow each round. After placing all the cards you receive that turn into your inheritance, you can sacrifice a single card. Sacrificing a card removes it from your inheritance, but can win you Dracula’s Favor from beyond the grave.

The game ends after 6 rounds, shown on the Central Board in the center of the table. The player with the most Vampire Points (VPs) wins the game, ascending to the highest echelons of vampiric society!

—description from the designer

name: The Guerrilla Generation: Cold War Insurgencies in Latin America
description:
The Guerrilla Generation: Cold War Insurgencies in Latin America is the second COIN multipack, containing four separate games exploring a series of thematically related insurgencies. Building on the The British Way, this new multipack allows players to explore variations in insurgent groups’ organizational structures, strategies, and relationship with civilians, across four insurgencies in Central and South America between 1968 and 1992. During this part of the Cold War era, Latin America experienced an incredible number of different insurgent groups, many inspired by the Cuban Revolution featured in Cuba Libre, ranging from popular backed rural insurgencies, flexible urban guerrillas, externally sponsored raiders, and brutal ideologically rigid groups. This multipack features a game exemplifying each of these types of insurgencies, to offer players the chance to compare different approaches to rebellion. The four games included in the multipack cover conflicts in Uruguay (1968-1972), Nicaragua (1979-1990), El Salvador (1979-1992), and Peru (1980-1992). The Nicaragua and El Salvador games can also be played in a linked campaign scenario, which combines them into a simultaneous side-by-side experience.

—description from the publisher

name: The Halls of Montezuma
description:
Following the annexation of Texas by the United States in December 1845, war between the United States and Mexico became inevitable.  From 1846-1848, the two countries fought a bloody and bruising war culminating in Mexico surrendering significant territory to the United States.

The Halls of Montezuma tasks two players to recreate this pivotal war in American and Mexican history.  As the United States, you will be tasked with taking California and invading Mexico while facing mounting political opposition at home.  As Mexico, you will be forced to fight a defensive war of attrition against the better trained and led American troops.

The Halls of Montezuma is a low complexity, card driven game for two players (with solitaire rules). Players relive the decisions and dilemmas of this crucial period in history. Fast setup and a playtime of 60-75 minutes.

—description from the publisher

name: The Happiest Cat In The World
description:
Compete with others to create the coziest, happiest space for your  cat and win their eternal contentment – or at least their grudging  approval. 
Buy new tiles for your deck to expand your cat's apartment and make attractive combos. Move your cat to take advantage of attractions, collect points for doing so, and use the best combinations between attractions. Manage your deck wisely.

—description from the publisher

name: The Idles
description:
Is your team dragging its heels? Productivity in the pits? Not anymore!
Say Hello to Maxwell — The Supercomputer of Tomorrow, Today!
From the fine folks at Moloch Industries, this marvel of modern engineering keeps your team on track and sends your company’s productivity soaring to brand-new heights!
It’s simple, it’s effective, and it’s 100% guaranteed to boost results.
The top companies in the country are already on board — what are you waiting for?

The Idles is an asymmetric card game for two players. Set in a nostalgic 1950s America with dystopian undertones, the game pits a mysterious supercomputer — obsessed with maximizing corporate productivity — against a lowly employee struggling under that very weight.

The supercomputer, Maxwell, will line up his programs and defend them with supervisors until they can be executed successfully...by any means necessary! Meanwhile, the employee must constantly prove their worth by grinding out productivity awards, or else risk being branded an idler.

And bad things are said to happen to those who idle. Better not find out!

—description from the publisher

The Idles is a game conceived as a satire of AI and capitalism. As such, we have taken the artistic liberty to use genAI in order to create its illustrations. No AI has been used in any other area of the making of the game, nor on our digital platform, Babll.

-description from the AI disclaimer

name: The Jetsons
description:
Welcome to Orbit City! Play as a member of the futuristic Jetsons family — George, Jane, Judy, Elroy, or Rosie — and explore the towering spires of the city of tomorrow. Across three episodes (rounds), you'll traverse the city collecting items and experiences that correspond to your Demand Cards.

In each episode, players take turns based on their position on a linear track of locations. On your turn, you choose the distance you wish to travel and then reveal cards at your destination. The number of steps you take becomes your currency for acquiring these cards. The further you advance, the more money you can spend — but once you pass a location, it cannot be revisited!

The game features an optional Mini-Expansion with the dog Astro, introducing new powers and strategic choices, activated by a single-use Astro token during each episode.

—description from the publisher

name: The Last In The Woods
description:
Face unpredictable weather, hungry animals, and your own fear. Test your skills and find out if you can survive… and become the last one left in the forest.

Imagine you are stranded in the middle of the wilderness with no equipment at all. You have nothing — only your decisions and your ability to adapt. You’ll need to gather resources, craft equipment, start a fire, and secure food and water. Every decision has consequences.

Each round reveals an event that players must respond to. Will a storm hit? Or will a hungry animal appear?

Be careful — you only have three actions each turn. How will you use them?

Players take turns clockwise and face the wilderness in three game modes:

Solo – survive on your own and complete set objectives
Cooperative – work together, survive as a group, and complete a series of challenges
Competitive – the winner is the last player remaining in the forest

Can you survive? 🌲🔥

—description from the designer

name: The Lord of the Rings: Circle of Conflict
description:
It is the Third Age of Middle-earth, and a great war between the many nations is unfolding. In The Lord of the Rings: Circle of Conflict, you simultaneously command both The Shadow and The Free Peoples armies; your Free Peoples will fight the Shadow of the opponent to your left, and your Shadow will fight the Free Peoples of the opponent to your right.

As the dice are rolled, you will decide how to apply the results. Will you recruit iconic characters for The Free Peoples or perhaps muster the troops of Mordor to fight for The Shadow in one of two pivotal battles? Will you hunt your opponent’s Fellowship with your Nazgûl or secretly move your Fellowship to evade Sauron’s watchful Eye?

To win as The Free Peoples, get The Fellowship to reach Mount Doom or defeat The Shadow in battle. As The Shadow, you must fully corrupt The Fellowship or defeat them in battle.

When all the victory points have been tallied, the player with the most points wins!

—description from the publisher

name: The Lord of the Rings: Foes of Middle-earth
description:
Based upon the marvelous movies, in Lord of the Rings: Foes of Middle-earth, players will be put in the Fellowship's shoes and explore a randomized Middle-earth, reliving iconic moments of their travels, gathering strength and fighting iconic enemies.

The game is divided upon three phases: Exploration, Challenge and final Boss Battle, against the Bane of Durin itself. In this game, cooperation and strategy is vital for the success of the Fellowship, avoiding any of them to fall in battle and to defeat once and for all the Balrog of Moria.

—description from the publisher

name: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers – Trick-Taking Game
publisher: Office Dog; ADC Blackfire Entertainment; asmodee; Gameology (Gameology Romania); Geekach LLC; Gém Klub Kft.; Rebel Sp. z o.o.
description:
The journey continues in the magical world of Middle-earth in The Two Towers: Trick-Taking Game, a narrative-driven co-operative card game that lets players take on the roles of heroes and villains in Tolkien's legendary work, The Two Towers. This standalone game follows 2025's The Fellowship of the Ring: Trick-Taking Game with chapters 19-36 of gameplay. The chapters can be played in any order and playing the earlier game isn't required, but ideally you play them in sequence.

In each chapter, each player takes a different character role and each character has a condition that must be met in order to pass the chapter and advance in the story. As you advance through the chapters, new characters, items, and challenges are introduced to the game. The One Ring is the game's only trump card, but initially rings can't be led until someone plays one off-suit.

In the two-player game, one hand of cards is dealt to a dummy player, with some cards being face up and others face down. This dummy is assigned a character, and one of the human players will play cards for it based on which cards are free to be played.

In the solitaire game, one player plays four hands of face-up cards, with each hand being assigned a character and only a few cards being available at a time. After you play a trick, deal each hand a new card.

—description from the publisher

name: The Malice of Light Adventures
description:
The Malice of Light Adventures is a cooperative roguelike boss-battler based on Brady J. Sadler’s epic fantasy book series, The Malice of Light. Designed for 1–4 players, the game combines modular gameplay, quick character progression, and elegant combat in a fast-paced, replayable format inspired by the Sadlers’ previous titles like Heroes of Terrinoth and Street Masters.

Players will battle dangerous foes in iconic locations from the books while contending with escalating villain schemes across multiple acts, culminating in a dramatic boss encounter. The game also serves as a great entry point for those new to The Malice of Light, offering a unique way to explore its vibrant world of classic high fantasy—separate from the story told in the novels.

—description from the publisher

name: The Maniac
description:
The Maniac is a hidden movement horror board game in which you will have to survive the murderous rampage of a psychopath, but you could also be the murderous Maniac! A group of college students decide to reopen the old Black Pine Lodge in the mountains of Crystal Country. A place closed several times due to various misfortunes that have occurred over the years, but as soon as they arrive they realize that the place actually seems contaminated by something ancient and evil. They decide to explore the place, but it will only be when one of them finds a cursed mask that the real nightmare will begin!

In The Maniac at the beginning of the game everyone is a "Survivor" but the real game begins when one of them finds the cursed mask. From that moment on he will become "The Maniac" and will have the goal of eliminating everyone else. The Survivors instead will have to try to escape from Black Pine Lodge by activating one or more endings. The Maniac is a hidden movement game where no one will ever know exactly where the other is.

-description from publisher

name: Trailblazer: The Arizona Trail
description:
Travel the spectacular 800 mile long Arizona Trail as you take in the sights and sounds of the mountains, canyons, plateaus and deserts seeking out the amazing variety of wildlife such as the Roadrunner and Javelina, while avoiding the Gila Monster. From Saguaro National Park, the Sonoran desert, through the largest Ponderosa pine forest on Earth and into the Grand Canyon, you will interact with the incredible diversity of Terrain, Flora and Fauna found in State 48 aka - Arizona.

Players will call upon the legendary Jackalope and Lost Dutchman to aid in their travel. Turn order is determined for each round of travel and actions through a unique movement and observation mechanism. Players will need to acquire an interesting blend of key Natural and Personal resources to obtain advantages and create their own mural of Arizona wonders through efficient placement of polyomino depictions.

After 8 weeks/rounds of travel, the player who builds a reserve of the most Arizona Grit and Superstition Gold is declared TRAILBLAZER!

-description from publisher

name: The Old Ones of El Dorado
description:
In the shadows of forgotten epochs, before cultists whispered secrets in and around Arkham, there lay the hidden city of El Dorado. Contrary to tales of gold, El Dorado’s true treasure was immortality, bestowed upon it by the Old Ones.

In The Old Ones of El Dorado, you seek immortality by any means necessary in this mythical city. Together, you and your rivals are constructing a pyramid to Cthulhu. But within your personal temple, you worship your own Elder God. To fulfil your mission, you'll dispatch followers to labour in the Physical Realm and seek forbidden knowledge in the Other-Lands, all whilst striving to cling to your sanity.

The Old Ones of El Dorado is a hand management and drafting game in which the cards form a closed economy of actions. You can play a card into one of four action rows and perform both the action of the space and the action on top of your card.

However, the next player may choose to play into the same row, if there’s space, gaining them the action on their card, your card, and the action associated with that row. Each card offers two actions to choose from, but once played, the orientation becomes fixed.

Alternatively, you may decide the time is right to collect the cards from an action row. Performing the alternate actions shown at the bottom of these cards, you'll then gather them back into your hand, ready to use on a later turn. If it just so happens that a rival house has only just added to this row, then paranoia and insanity awaits them. Every creeping madness token gained in this way will block part of your resource limited storage space.

Throughout The Old Ones of El Dorado, you'll gather resources to construct temples, craft sacred masks, and raise shrines. You’ll make dark sacrifices to the Old Ones and send cultists into the village to obtain knowledge and goods. These efforts will earn you points and bring you closer to immortality as promised to you by the Old Ones of El Dorado... but is it a blessing or a curse?

—description from the publisher

name: The Pirate Code
description:
Welcome the Sparkling Seas in the golden age of piracy!

The Pirate Code is a deck-building sandbox game where you are left to chart your own storied legacy. Each card in your hand presents you with a compelling choice - do you leverage their resource icons, allowing you to complete contracts, attack others, bury treasure, resupply, and more? Or do you discard them to move, potentially activating their powerful and unique ability as well? This choice underpins each turn as you wrestle with how best to utilize your crew.

No two victories in The Pirate Code look exactly alike. There are many avenues to make a name for yourself, and as Captain, you’ll need to decide which are worth your time.

There are a variety of contracts, which offer you a mixture of Victory Points, Coins, and Reputation for completing them. Coins can be buried for victory points, and other players can attempt to dig them up. Reputation is checked several times during the game, awarding points to the most Infamous players.

When the time is right, you may even be willing to turn your cannons onto another player and attempt to procure their cargo in a way that befits a real pirate. If they’ve got nothing worth stealing, you can always blow a few holes in their hull and sail away to safety.

Improve the efficiency of the crew through leadership and sometimes, tough love. Spend Hearts to mitigate randomness. Red hearts allow you to draw new crew, letting you cultivate the perfect crew for the job. Black hearts allow you to reroll dice, turning a missed shot or failed gamble into a winning one. Leveraging these hearts will cause your Captains Log to advance, awarding new abilities to your crew based on your style of leadership.

—description from the publisher

name: The Pirate Republic: Africa Gambit
description:
Return to 1713, the dawn of the Golden Age of Piracy. After a decade of war, a rare peace comes to the Spanish Main. With thousands of demobilized sailors, pirating explodes in the West Indies and across the Atlantic.

One crew of pirates, calling themselves the Flying Gang, seek fame, fortune, and self-governance by building their own Republic free from the constraints of kings, queens, and imperialism. Will you work together to build the Pirate Republic? Or will you betray your brethren in pursuit of greater riches? The sea is your territory; anyone on or near it, your prey.

The Pirate Republic: Africa Gambit is a second edition to the original  The Pirate Republic. It is a thematic deck building, sandbox adventure game for 1-5 players which also adds West Africa riches, new Pirates, the Portuguese, and a campaign mode into the mix.   Set in the early 18th-century, each player is an famous pirate captain weaving their own tale by performing daring feats and plundering on the high seas.

It's a time of conquest and the lure of riches, indomitable spirit and fat treasure galleons, pirate utopias and watery graves!

Are you ready to get your Pirate on?

How does it play?

You start with a deck of 12 cards, 2 of which are unique to your Pirate while 10 are shared. As you acquire cards and build your deck, your decisions will shape your Pirates’ personality.

Using your cards you will sail across the map, strike fear on enemies, recruit crew, attack, defend, form a pirate haven, sack forts, complete global missions, or build infamy (which lets you gain even stronger cards). Each turn you will draw a hand of cards and take actions with them. Once you are out of cards, play goes to the next Pirate, and this continues until everyone has exhausted their decks.

Individually you are amassing Swagger as quickly as you can while collectively completing the global missions. The game ends when the global mission (chosen by the players before the game begins) is completed Alternatively, whoever reaches 120 Swagger first is the winner.

.....

name: Valkyrie: A Black Orchestra Game
publisher: Tabletop Tycoon Inc.; Victory Point Games; Tycoon Games
description:
Valkyrie is a Black Orchestra game with quicker, simpler gameplay, and new strategic elements. Focus on assassinating Hitler with explosives, completing Operation Valkyrie with the Gestapo always close at hand to pull you in for questioning. Stay one step ahead of the Gestapo and defeat Hitler before they collect enough evidence to have you tried for treason and executed.

In this stand-alone version of Black Orchestra, players experience the familiar tension and dread but in about half the time of the original. Gameplay has been streamlined even as new strategic elements have been added. In this version the conspirators must focus on assassinating Hitler with explosives, completing Operation Valkyrie. This can be accomplished in a number of ways, with the Gestapo always close at hand to pull you in for questioning.

The game ends either when you successfully defeat Hitler or when the Gestapo collect enough evidence to have you tried for treason and executed. The game also ends in failure if you exhaust the interrogation deck.

—description from the publisher

name: Blood Rage: Valhalla
description:
Occurring after Ragnarök ends the world, Blood Rage: Valhalla is a standalone sequel that will feature gameplay similar to the original 2015 Blood Rage, with the gameplay differences mirroring the game's new setting of Valhalla.

Valhalla will feature many new, detailed miniatures for players to set against one another in combat.

name: The Rise of a Jarl
description:
The Viking Age is at hand and with prosperity comes power. As an ambitious ruling jarl, chart a new future for your people through careful development and expansion to secure your eternal legacy throughout the world.

Build up your Viking civilization through resource management, balancing expansion with defense to protect your gains. Devote your efforts to long-term innovations or focus on accumulating wealth and increasing your population. Forge your own path through the Viking Age and leave your mark on the known world!

In this engine-building game, carefully marshal your resources to guide your Viking civilization to greatness. Across 4 rounds of play, you’ll use cards in hand to take a variety of actions: Trade to gain wealth, Raid for resources, Develop new technologies, and more. Balancing your current needs against your future plans is crucial to your survival. After each round, defend against encroaching civilizations who wish to sabotage your position. After the final round, determine your score to determine how the Vikings fared under your leadership.

name: The Rise of Nerath: A Mythralis Chronicle
description:
The Rise of Nerath: A Mythralis Chronicle is an epic fantasy board game that merges deep narrative exploration, strategic battles, and breathtaking miniatures into a cohesive, immersive experience.

Set in the ancient, magic-infused continent of Mythralis, players lead unique factions in a world where gods walk among mortals, ancient creatures rise, and the lines between power and faith blur. Every decision leaves a mark on the world, every battle shapes the dawn of a new era.

Multiple Game Modes

Narrative Campaign: Embark on a story-driven journey through interconnected quests where choices and victories impact your path, shaping your faction’s legacy across different scenarios.

Dungeon Crawling: Explore dungeons using modular double-sided tiles with traps, treasures, bosses, and evolving challenges in cooperative or solo play.

Divine Battle: Engage in fast-paced, competitive tactical battles on the main board, combining card-driven action, dice, and modular terrain.

Solo & Coop: Fully supported solo play and cooperative modes where players face the game’s AI and narrative challenges together.

Deep Customization & Progression

Manage your party of 3 characters per player, equipping weapons, artifacts, and relics that grant unique abilities and status effects during combat.

Advance along skill trees using Glory Points earned through quests, conquest, and building temples to your chosen deity, unlocking powerful abilities and special actions.

Summon creatures, build temples for your deity, and conquer strategic areas to expand your influence on the map.

Engaging Systems

Status Effects System: Inflict or suffer poison, burning, paralysis, and many other effects, tracked visually through custom tokens, adding depth and tension to each encounter.

Action Card Management: Each equipment grants specific action cards, enabling tailored combat strategies and deck optimization as your party evolves.

Dynamic Quest System: Experience branching paths, side quests, and evolving objectives that ensure each game session is unique.

Premium Miniatures & Art
The game features a collection of highly detailed miniatures representing heroes, creatures, and gods, bringing the world of Mythralis vividly to life on your table. Paired with modular tiles, custom tokens, and beautifully illustrated cards, each session becomes a visual and strategic spectacle.

Whether you seek deep narrative campaigns, tense dungeon-crawling challenges, or competitive skirmishes, The Rise of Nerath offers a complete gaming experience for 1–6 players, with rich replayability, strategic depth, and an evolving world where every game becomes your legend.

—description from the publisher

name: Colt Express: The Complete Collection
description:
The gang rides again! With the core game, all expansions, and promos from over 10+ years of train heisting, the Colt Express: Complete Collection is a haul of loot packaged into an all-in-one storage box for easy setup and a clean getaway.

—description from the publisher

name: The Siege of Shaddis Horne
description:
The fairies have gone mad. Their once quaint magic threatens all of Brighthelm, and the golems they created to protect the villages are now tearing them apart. Now the little forest town of Shaddis Horne, with its elemental college, is under siege. The fairies know that without this source of magic, Brighthelm’s chemists will be dealt a severe blow. They must be stopped. Your Hawkguard soldiers have been sent to repel the fairies and their minions, inspire the villagers and keep Shaddis Horne standing until the siege is over. It won't be easy.

The Siege of Shaddis Horne is a co-operative resource gathering tower defence game with a smattering of push-your-luck dungeon crawling to boot.

—description from the designer

name: The Souls Rebirth
description:
The Souls offers an immersive experience with the option to play solo, cooperatively, or competitively. Players assume the role of spirits navigating unique fates, unraveling mysteries, crafting items, gathering resources, and interacting with mythical beings. The game emphasizes growth through reincarnation, where each death opens the door to new possibilities.  How many incarnations will it take to free your soul once more?

Four modes of play are available:

    Full Cooperative Mode: All players unite as a team.
    Full Competitive Mode: Each player competes individually.
    Team Competitive Mode: Players form teams and compete.
    Solitaire Mode


The objective of the game varies for each player, team, or group based on the scenario they choose at the beginning of the game. Each participant works toward achieving their unique scenario objective, which may differ from others. In Full Competitive Mode, even after a player successfully completes their scenario, the remaining players can continue playing if they wish, pursuing their own objectives to complete the game. This allows for a more dynamic and extended gameplay experience.

When a player's vitality reaches zero, they die and are reborn with a new backstory card and set of stats. The cycle of life and death is key to the gameplay, offering players new opportunities with each incarnation.

-description from publisher

name: The Trial of the Forest
description:
As the day of the equinox approached, crowds gathered in the heart of the Green Valley to witness the annual Trial of the Forest - an ancient ritual to select from among the bravest daredevils a new Guardian, a protector against the darkness lurking in the shadows.
Players collect resources, play cards, fight opponents and embark on dangerous expeditions. In the course of the game, the cards played build the player's history by defining his deeds.

—description from the designer

name: The Void Unveiled: Echoes of Arkham
description:
The Void Unveiled: Echoes of Arkham is a story-driven Lovecraftian board game of investigation, madness, and cosmic horror, designed for 1–4 players.
Fully cooperative, rich in narrative, and steeped in creeping insanity, it invites you to descend into a world where every choice matters—and madness is never far behind.

Step into the role of investigators unraveling a series of eerie mysteries in 1930s Arkham, each told through branching narrative chapters filled with meaningful choices, unique events, and escalating dread. As you read the story, your decisions shape the course of the game, leading to different outcomes and consequences.

Each creature you encounter is governed by its own distinct set of rules and behaviors—not a single generic AI system in sight. Every monster feels unique, each one changing how you fight, think, and survive.

Survive the unfolding horrors and defeat the Elder, only then will you truly unveil the Void.

Combat is tactical and unpredictable. Sanity is fragile. And the Void is waiting.

—description from the publisher

name: The Wandmaker's Apprentice
description:
Craft your legacy or wield the shadows.
The choice is yours.

Following the fallout between master and apprentice, we find the apprentice recessed in the shadows, where the law's light seldom reaches. There, in the dark alleyways, he has set up his own trade, selling wands and other magical objects imbued with wild, untamed magic (and questionable legality). The street lamps flicker with the tension of a town caught between light and darkness. Master and apprentice locked in an unspoken war, each wand sold — a silent challenge to the other’s legacy.

In The Wandmaker's Apprentice, you will take on the role of either:

The Wandmaker — crafting genuine wands from resources such as wood, gems, dragonbone, and stardust.

or

The Apprentice — perfecting the art of persuasion to peddle dark magical objects, while avoiding the Magical Authorities.

This asymmetric 2-player game utilizes unique mechanics and components for each player, combining elements of resource management, end-of-round-bonus building, a twist on set collection, and a clever dice management system.

—description from the publisher

name: The War of the Worlds: One More Day
description:
A solo story driven, deck building, exploration and survival game - based on the events in the novel The War of the Worlds, by H.G.Wells.

Take on the role of a journalist or infantry soldier during the Martian invasion of Victorian England.  Explore various locations around London as you play through one of six challenging and varied stories.

Build your deck each turn to improve your chances of staying alive against the events and engagements that threaten mankind's survival.  From Martian fighting-machines and heat-rays, to black smoke and red weed, ruffian gangs, Martian harvesters, packs of savage dogs and more!

Finish the story by completing objectives and overcoming challenges, before learning about the weaknesses of the invaders and survive long enough to witness their death!

—description from the designer

name: Everdell Emerland
publisher: Tycoon Games; Gém Klub Kft.; White Goblin Games
description:
Deep in the tropical jungle to the west of the Everdell Valley lies the country of Emerland, a vibrant land known for its artistic and musical culture, and for its abundance of natural resources, including valuable gems mined from its many underground caverns. Tiny critters found here — mostly insects — are fastidious and clever Helpers, often assisting the larger critters in their work and in optimizing or bringing beauty to their cities and homes.

The jungles are vast and dense, and expeditions into the further realms of the land are undertaken often. There was once a mysterious civilization that dwelt here, long lost to history, but archaeological discoveries are beginning to shed a light on the ancients.

In Emerland, you send critter Workers to various locations on the board to gather resources. You use these resources to play cards face-up in front of you, forming your jungle city and helping you to score points. Each turn, you take one of 6 possible actions: Place a Worker (with or without Helpers), Place a Helper, Play a Card, Use an Artisan Card, Excavate with your Archaeologist or Prepare for Season.

The game ends when all players have reached the end of Spring and can no longer make any actions.  The player with the most points wins.

—description from the publisher

name: The Weimar Republic: Political Struggle in Germany, 1919-1933
description:
January 19, 1919.  The Great War is over, the Kaiser has abdicated, and Germany is on its knees. After suffering a humiliating loss at the hands of the Allied nations, the former Great Power is now confronted not only with the death of millions of its citizens, but also with a severe economic crisis and a political turmoil that threatens to plunge the entire nation into civil war. The November Revolution of 1918 ushered in a new era of liberal democracy in a country traditionally ruled by noblemen warriors. The first democratic election has now been held, but democracy’s enemies are numerous, and the future of the fledgling Republic appears grim. No one can tell whether the democratic Coalition will prevail or whether any of the extremist factions will rise out of the chaos and seize power.
 One thing is perfectly clear, however: the coming years will not be remembered for their peace and stability.
 The Weimar Republic is a Card Driven Game of political struggle in interwar Germany. Four factions compete for dominance: the democratic Coalition, the Soviet-backed Communist Party, Hitler’s National Socialists, and the far-right Radical Conservatives.

The game follows a timeline of 15 years (1919-1933) with two rounds in each year. During a round, players take turns using their faction-specific abilities to increase their influence in Germany’s regions and major cities, to maneuver the political landscape of the Republic, and to dominate through a combination of propaganda, parliamentary elections, street violence, economic influence, and ideological zeal. Typical actions include agitation, reforms, recruitment and deployment of fighting men, strikes, uprisings, assassinations, and coups. General and regional elections are held at irregular intervals throughout the game, potentially shifting local power balances in sometimes radical ways. The timeline moves through three distinct eras, each with its own deck of event cards. There are also several special cards like Elections and Parliamentary Control Cards.

Gameplay is fast-paced; initiative flows back and forth, and the direction of the game may change rapidly and unexpectedly. Although competition between the factions is fierce, some of the faction-specific mechanics overlap, and players can often take advantage of each other--including the making and unmaking of alliances.
 The Weimar Republic includes scenarios ranging in length from 3 to 8 hours and a special tutorial scenario that can be played by new players in only 90 minutes. Victory is absolute and generally achieved through “sudden death”; there is no final scoring or adding up of different objectives. Each faction can be replaced by a "bot" player, allowing 1-4 players to play with any combination of factions.

name: Everdell Journeys
description:
Set out from the hustle and bustle of the big city and see the cozy world of Everdell on your own two paws in Everdell Journeys.

In this card-drafting adventure, you'll lay down a path of cards featuring the breathtaking landmarks, riveting cities, and new friends you'll find on the road. Send your traveler along the path of cards to activate them, scoring points and gaining resources. Chart your course wisely and score powerful combos based on the cards in your path, filling your journal with memories to share by the hearth at your journey's end!

—description from the publisher

name: Theocratia
description:
Sometimes, eternity can feel like it's dragging on, so to overcome the boredom, you and your friends decide to make a little wager: you give yourselves a couple of thousand years to meddle in the lives of the folks on a distant planet. Once the time's up, whoever has earned the most love and admiration from these people wins the bet.

Theocratia is a civilization game where you and up to three other players attempt to shape the destiny of four civilizations on this world. You'll help them grow, establish new cities, engage in battles, and throw grand celebrations in your honor, all in a bid to become the most revered deity by the game's end.

Theocratia is set on an imaginary island where 4 civilizations thrive and develop, explore the lands, build new structures and, more generically, forge their own fate. Players take on the roles of highly advanced aliens that manipulate the lives of these four civilizations, who view them as Gods, in a wager to determine which alien/god will be the most worshiped.

The goal of the aliens is to be adored by the most successful civilizations more than their rivals, and to do that they try to influence the way the civilizations develop to their own advantage (i.e. if you are the Blue player, you want the 4 civilizations to do their actions on the Blue hexes, showing the lakes).

The player (alien) with the most points at the end of the game wins the bet.

--description from publisher

name: Thessaloniki
description:
Thessaloniki, 4th century: the sun ascended, illuminating the Forum and the harbor's masts, bathing a city vibrant with ambition in a golden glow. Its bustling markets teemed with merchants from every corner of the empire: Greeks, Romans, Syrians, and Illyrians, all engaged in trade, intrigue, and the pursuit of wealth. Amidst the clamor, rumors of imperial favor and trade monopolies permeate the agora. Ships, laden with grains, oil, grapes, and meat, creak under their bounty, destined for distant ports or the vast granaries of powerful patricians. You are one of these patricians, competing for riches and influence. Yet only the shrewdest will rise above the chaos. In a city where commerce and politics are inseparable, your eloquence and strategic acumen forge your legacy in the annals of history.

Thessaloniki is a game set during the vibrant merchant era of the Tetrarchy in the 4th century Roman Empire. Players take on the roles of ambitious traders fulfilling contracts, acquiring commodities, and trading with allied cities.

Compete to sell your wares at the best prices or secure shipments to high-scoring destinations. As the game unfolds, you can climb the Influence track to sway the popularity of destinations, reaping extra rewards for aligning your shipments accordingly. Resolving contracts that offer powerful bonuses is key to becoming the most influential merchant in Thessaloniki!

—description from the publisher

name: Tiny Epic Invincible
description:
Step into the beloved, brutal world of Invincible and put your life on the line to defend the people of Earth from merciless supervillains and otherworldly invaders in this cooperative race against the clock that'll push you to your limits as you zoom from Chicago to Atlantis and back again to save lives before it's too late.

In Tiny Epic Invincible, players will assemble a team of 1-4 superheroes, each with their own unique powers, and face off against a randomly selected supervillain seeking world domination.

The game plays across five different locations, with players beginning at the Guardians of the Globe HQ and traveling out to four unique locations pulled from the location deck at the start of the game. The ultimate goal of the players is to rescue and secure civilians at each location before they're caught up in the villain's warpath.

More foes will pile onto these locations as the game progresses, taking advantage of the chaos, and players will need to effectively use the push-your-luck action system to keep up with their opponents. Recruit iconic, non-player allies to station around the world and creatively combine your actions to keep the villains at bay, save lives, and prevent the conquest of Earth!

-description from publisher

name: Our Secret Society
description:
On your turn, you will play a card and introduce a new rule - while following that rule as well as all previous rules. If you make a mistake, you're out.
The last player standing wins and becomes the leader of the secret society.

name: Thirty Years of Misery
description:
Thirty Years of Misery is an easy to play game on the Thirty Years War of 1618-1648 for up to 4 players. 
Players on the same side must coordinate and work together to win the war, but the victory conditions only allow a single faction within the victorious alliance to win the game.

Carddriven mechanics with lots of events, random chit pull based turn order and combat resolution using custom dice ensures a strong narrative and lots of thematic unpredictability.

As befitting a bitter religious war, players are striving not only to secure military control over the various political entities of Germany but also to enforce their religious policies in them.

—description from the publisher

name: This War of Mine: The Board Game – Second Edition
description:
This cooperative experience of This War of Mine immerses players into the harrowing lives of civilians trapped in a war-torn city, facing relentless challenges that test the limits of human resilience. They must navigate a series of morally complex decisions, manage scarce resources, and confront the stark realities of survival in a besieged environment. The Book of Scripts provides a rich narrative layer, making each playthrough different and adding to the game's replayability with a wide range of events and encounters.

The Second Edition elevates the experience with improved miniatures, double-layered character boards, and a complete rulebook. It also includes the story-rich Tales from the Ruined City and Days of the Siege, along with a new expansion introducing another set of heart-wrenching stories of survival woven into scenarios with a more dynamic, shortened playtime. With refined gameplay mechanics, these enhancements offer both new and returning players the most immersive and polished version of the game.

—description from the publisher

name: The Vibe
description:
In this collaborative game, players take turns taking on the role of "The Vibe," selecting a theme and arranging pictures in a specific order to provide clues.

The postcard-sized cards with pictures are arranged from left to right, indicating how well they fit the chosen theme — from least to most fitting.

The other players, the "Mind Readers," then try to guess the theme based on the sequence of pictures.

The game's challenge comes from The Vibe's selection of artwork, where each picture carries just the right amount of ambiguity to encourage thoughtful discussion and interpretation.

Different volumes:
Each volume of The Vibe includes 64 large postcard-sized cards, featuring diverse and evocative imagery on one side and thematic words on the other.

The first volume offers a blend of classic and quirky art from around the world, paired with a wide range of thematic words.

Later volumes explore specific topics and styles, with more closely related words, making the game more challenging and requiring sharper focus and greater attention to detail.

Volumes can be mixed and matched to create new and varied play experiences.

—description from the publisher

name: Three Days of Gettysburg: Deluxe Edition
description:
Three Days of Gettysburg traces its lineage back to Richard Berg's "Terrible Swift Sword" (1976). Take command of the Union Army of the Potomac or the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia in the 1863 Battle of Gettysburg, the largest battle of the American Civil War.

Players command their armies via the chain of command from corps down through divisions and brigades to the individual units - regiments of infantry and batteries of artillery. The series relies on interactive chit-pull mechanics to simulate the often-chaotic nature of the 19th Century battlefield at the regimental level.

Three Days of Gettysburg Deluxe Edition will include ten-plus scenarios. They range from small skirmisher contests on half-sized maps to the ultimate Gettysburg experience on four full full-sized maps depicting the entire battle, including the East Cavalry Battlefield! Other scenarios will depict the first day’s fight for the hills surrounding Gettysburg; the second day’s assault on Sickle’s salient; the third day’s cavalry fight on Cress Ridge; Buford’s defense against Heth as his division approaches Gettysburg using the new skirmisher rules; the July 2nd evening assault on Cemetery Hill; the fight north of town on July 1st, and several others. The game includes smaller scenario maps; experienced players will be able to play many of the scenarios in one sitting. The 3DoG Deluxe edition will include many exclusive rules to represent the special situations at Gettysburg. However, many rules are optional, allowing players to decide what level of complexity they want.

New components include cavalry counters of four strength points or less that allow the player’s tactics to resemble historical cavalry tactics at Gettysburg better. Confederate dismounted cavalry counters allow for the dismounted and mounted fight on the East Cavalry Battlefield. Many artillery units have corrected weapon types, and some batteries can be broken into sections for the smaller scenarios (think of Calef’s battery on the first day!). Additionally, artillery overshoot rules elegantly show the Confederate defective fuse issues.

There are two types of skirmisher units, detachments from infantry and dismounted cavalry and breakdown skirmish units of specialized units. Players will find skirmishers well suited for their historical missions and challenging to move (or remove) unless faced with formed units. The Bliss Farm can be the problem it was in the actual battle.

New rules allow artillery to take losses in lieu of a Disorder result. Now, Alonzo Cushing can make his heroic final stand at the Angle! New rules for when units Collapse allow elite units like the Iron Brigade and the 26th North Carolina to continue to fight as they did historically, even after severe losses. Revised rules better represent how units recover manpower losses; no longer are the better Cohesion units more likely to recover, and players will find it beneficial not to run regiments into the ground. With a new battle-book rule, refused units with plenty of manpower are no longer the weak links in your firing line.

New town rules help show the difficulties formed units faced moving through the streets and limit the firepower of units in town when firing. Shock in town hexes will be less deadly, and Gettysburg will not be the defensive bastion of previous editions. However, skirmishers can duplicate the problems they caused the enemy when sniping from the houses of Gettysburg.

The new maps continue to use Mark Simonitch’s beautiful artwork but include the following:

Stonewalls.
    The house-sized rocks specific to the Devil’s Den.
    Sloping hexes that better represent the uneven terrain and slopes at Gettysburg.

While woods have no Shock benefit, Rebels facing entrenched Yankees on Culp’s Hill will suffer like their historical counterparts. The many rock formations are presented differently from earlier editions, and artillery moving into a hex that takes more than four movement points will roll for Disorder. Players will find moving cannons up the slopes of Little Round Top as tricky in the game as it was in the battle.

We have added the eastern map that covers the cavalry battle between Hampton and Gregg on July 3rd. However, the addition allows for much more than just that. Both sides will find themselves using infantry to protect or threaten flanks on the new map, and Williams’ division of the Union 12th Corps can be in its historical position near the Daniel Lady farm on the afternoon of the first day.

-description from publisher's website

Game Scale:
Game Turn: 1 hour
Hex: 125 yards / 114.3 meters / 40ft elevation lines
Units: Battalion/Regiment - 50 men or 1 artillery piece per strength point

Game Inventory:
Two single-sided 22 x 34" full-color maps (northern battlefield)
One double-sided 22 x 34" full-color map (front: southern battlefield, Rear: enlarged Pickett’s Charge map)
One double-sided 22 x 34" full-color map (front: East Cavalry battlefield, rear: Combined map)
One double-sided 17 x 22" full-color small-scenario map
One double-sided 11 x 17" full-color small-scenario map
Eight double-sided countersheets (2,240 1/2" counters - includes 4 blanks and 25 errata for Dead of Winter, 5 errata for Twin Peaks and 92 optional for Into the Woods)

Two 11  × 17" (2-sided) Combat Tables Player Aid Cards
Two 11  × 17" (2-sided) Terrain Effects Charts + 2nd Disorder Tables & Range Effects Charts w/o Overshoot
One 8.5 × 11" (2-sided) Turn Record Track & VP/BCI Track
One 11  × 17" (1-sided) Union AM Chart
One 8.5 × 11" (1-sided) Confederate AM Chart
One 8.5 × 11" (2-sided) Confederate Reinforcement Schedule
One 8.5 × 11" (2-sided) Random Events Table + Confederate Release Schedule for Longstreet’s Assault
One 8.5 × 11" (2-sided) Union Reinforcement, 2-map + Federal Longstreet’s Assault Schedules
One 8.5 × 11" (2-sided) Union Reinforcement Schedule, 3-map
One 8.5 × 11" (2-sided) Union Reinforcement Schedule, 4-map

One 44-page GBACW Series Rule Book (2026 Edition)
One 32-page Gettysburg Deluxe Edition Battle Book
One 64-page Gettysburg Deluxe Edition Scenario Book
One 16-page GBACW Simple Version Rules Manual
One 52-page Gettysburg Simple Version Battle Book & Scenarios manual
Two 8½"×11" Simple Version (2-sided) TEC + Combat Charts
Two ten-sided dice

Solitaire Playability: High
Complexity Level: Medium
Players: 2 or more
Playing Time: 3-25+ hours

name: Three Kobolds in a Trench Coat
description:
Three Kobolds in a Trench Coat is a bluffing, party game for 2-4 players. After spending too long in the dark, the Kobolds are ready to see what life is like in the village of Crumblebatch. But there's a problem: the villagers aren’t exactly welcoming to monsters.
To blend in, the Kobolds have come up with a cunning plan - to dress up in a trench coat and pretend to be a regular person.

Now, as a “citizen”, players must avoid suspicion.
Each player must keep their Kobolds hidden by completing Quests, collecting Gold, and defeating opponents in Challenges.
Pay the Guards to redirect attention toward others and use Items to protect themselves or expose their rivals’ Kobolds one by one. The last player with hidden Kobolds wins the game.

name: Duat
description:
Made from solid marble, Duat is a true return to form for gaming, both in material and complexity of gameplay.
