In this beautiful abstract strategy game, 2 players will need to navigate the board carefully so as not to leave themselves vulnerable to an attack. With only 3 actions per turn and a 4x4 grid to take them on, each turn could spell your last!

Each turn players choose between taking 1 or 3 actions which can be split among their pieces in any way. Those actions are either to rotate a piece a quarter turn, or to move a piece forward in the direction of its sun. When moving, they can push any other pieces friend or foe, so long as none of them are facing the moving piece. First player to knock one of their opponent's pieces off the board wins!

Will you outmaneuver your opponent and emerge victorious? Or will you be pushed over the edge and be lost to the darkness?

—description from the publisher

name: HALO: Mission Command
description:
The USNC continues the war against Atriox and and the Banished. Mission control needs you to help the Master Chief organize units and complete missions all around the galaxy as quickly as possible.

Use weapons, vehicles, soldiers, and more to sabotage your enemies and finish your missions first. Destroy, steal, and swap cards in HALO: Mission Command, which is based on the HALO video game series.

name: Tiberpunk: Streets of Rome
description:
Tiberpunk: Streets of Rome takes you to an alternate version of ancient Rome during the reign of Emperor Trajan, where the crash of an alien spacecraft has altered the course of history. All extraterrestrial visitors perished, but their advanced technologies survived — and became an integral part of the Empire. Rome has maintained its social hierarchy and cultural traditions, but now its streets are patrolled by drones, and access to power can be gained through implants and hacking devices.

This game offers a unique perspective on classical Rome. You take on the roles of those who strive to rise from the city’s poor districts. In a brutal environment of gang rivalry and technological chaos, you will complete missions, control drones, upgrade your skills, pray at temples, and recover artifacts from alien ships — all to outpace your rivals and achieve the objectives faster.

Tiberpunk: Streets of Rome is a game for 2–4 players with a playtime of approximately 90–120 minutes. Combining sandbox elements with a race to complete missions, it offers a wide array of tactical options, strategic planning, and character development. Thanks to the balanced action system, diverse goal combinations, and over 20 storylines, each game unfolds in a new way — delivering a truly unique experience every time.

—description from the publisher

name: Tibetana
description:
In the mystical lands of the Himalayas, two ancient tribes compete for resources and divine favour... 

Tibetana is a two-player strategy game designed to be easily accessible and deeply strategic, with an infinite replay value. Thrilling 30-minute duels you’ll want to relive again and again!

A collector’s game crafted as a work of art that includes:

     24 detailed player miniatures
     19 hex territories for a modular board
     17 acrylic pagodas, portals and demon standees
     Over 100 premium components, including a custom die, tokens, tarot-sized cards, and energy crystals



				
				
					How to PlayIn Tibetana, your goal is to complete three pagodas before your opponent does. Control the map with your guardians and extract energy with your priestesses, expanding your influence through new settlements.

On your turn, you can perform up to three actions: Move your pieces, Train new ones, Build pagodas, Expel demons or even Regenerate magic portals.

Your presence will disturb the ancient demons that live in those territories. There are five of them, each wielding unique effects that may enhance or disrupt your plans. As the game advances, they grow increasingly powerful. Sometimes, even explosive!

				
				
					The MythsTibetana’s aesthetics and mechanics are inspired by the spiritual traditions of the Himalayas and Central Asia, with roots deeply grounded in Tibetan Buddhism.

name: Tiger Wings
description:
The Fighting Wings series of games covers air combat in World War II. The series goes into great detail in attempting to model all aspects of the air war as realistically as possible, which results in a fair amount of complexity. Tiger Wings is a stand-alone game and also an expansion module of tactical air combat in the Far East in WWII between the Japanese and the Allies from 1941 to the end of 1942.

Each of the games focuses on a particular place and time period and includes a large number of scenarios, Aircraft Data Cards (ADCs), and historical background. The aircraft cards and scenarios in Tiger Wings are fully compatible with the rest of the FW series games.

The game is played in three dimensions. Aircraft may be in level, climbing or diving flight. Some may be at higher or lower altitudes than others. Players must mentally visualize the vertical altitude relationship between AC but horizontal relationships will be clearly visible on the map. The rules also allow players to recreate important aspects of WW-II tactical air combat beyond simply the technical aspects of the aircraft involved.

We are up to 32 Aircraft Data Cards (although the last 16 will not be part of the retail version).

Kickstarter Ended. FABULOUS load of extra Stretch Goals-- far more than a retail/store edition can hold.

You can still get lots of extra content with a Late Pledge (until March 18!). https://www.atomagazine.com/Details.cfm?ProdID=198

name: Tikal Legend
description:
Tikal Legend is a game of exploration, placement, and majority in which the players explore the Central American jungles and search for lost temples and treasures.

As in the award-winning Tikal, your ultimate goal is to score the most prestige points during the in-game scoring phases, but the toolbox to do so in Tikal Legend becomes way wider!

In addition to exploring the jungle, controlling temples, and collecting treasures, you get to pick and perform actions in the order of your choosing — and spending your action points is only one of the available options! Claim different terrains, benefit from card effects, manipulate the map, recruit additional expedition members, and do so much more — all to excavate a whole new level of tactical and strategic planning in Tikal Legend!

				
				
					Note:Two different versions of the game (standard and deluxe with upgrade components) will be available in both English and French. With either version, you'll get everything to play the base game of Tikal, a whole new game of Tikal Legend, and a new solo mode developed by John Albertson, Aleksandr Saranac, and Jeremy Avery, with Dávid Turczi. It is NOT possible to play Tikal Legend with only a copy of Tikal.

name: Time Fenix
description:
A spiritual successor to Twisty Little Passages that elevates the experience as a full-blown tabletop game with card management mechanics, a non-linear campaign, meta-play strategy, and an all new setting, characters, and story.'Play as Fenix, a warrior sage, protecting a magitek world from an ancient threat with the help of a sentient AI. Manage power levels and resources on your player board as you navigate mazelike areas on laminated adventure sheets with a dry-erase pen. Seek out resources and power boosts, carefully defeat enemies standing in your way to advance, and plan how to defeat floor bosses to reach the powerful Time Crystals. Strategize when to perform mystical meditative actions to draw and play crucial resource cards from your Focus Deck.

Time Fenix is a solo-only tabletop campaign game blending puzzle-solving and dungeon-crawling in a richly imagined futuristic fantasy world. This is a fully resettable, narrative-driven adventure where every mission is a handcrafted experience designed for discovery and mastery.

With 20 interconnected areas and 59 challenging missions, you’ll manage resources, collect powerful cards and items, unlock shortcuts, and battle sinister manifestations, all while navigating intricate mazes that are tightly woven into the mechanics of deck-building, legacy progression, and adventure-write play. As you explore each area, you’ll uncover clever paths to boost your score, uncover hidden rewards, and earn Time Crystals to permanently upgrade your stats, abilities, and inventory, and advance the story. Every decision shapes your journey.

The game rewards more efficient play and clever meta-gaming strategy and supports adaptive difficulty levels. Learn as you play: Story sections reveal additional game elements, rules, and mechanics as you progress. Seek out hidden bonuses and areas to unlock greater power-ups. By growing your stats and gaining new Focus cards and special abilities, you can replay familiar areas in new ways to complete tougher objectives and unlock additional powers.

—description from the designer

name: Timeless Journeys: The Italian Grand Tour
description:
In Timeless Journeys: The Italian Grand Tour you step into the shoes of Europe’s first true tourists. In the 18th and 19th centuries, curious minds crossed Italy in search of art, history, and inspiration, a rite of passage that shaped their legacy. From Turin to Palermo you will explore cities, debate in cafés, and fill your Travel Journals with discoveries that turn fleeting impressions into lasting achievements.

At its heart, the game blends deck building, card chaining, set collection, and route planning. Travel, Friendship, and Inspiration cards let you journey across Italy, meet locals, gather ideas, and commit them to your Journals. Playing cards of the same type reactivates earlier actions in powerful chains, while the shared market of Advanced Action cards expands your strategy.

In this game you will follow that same route. Travel cards move you from Venice to Florence, Rome, Naples, and beyond. Each journal entry in your Travel journal turns fleeting impressions into lasting Victory Points.

The game is played in 5 rounds.  After the Famous Travelers phase and the Market phase of the 5th round are completed, the game ends and the player with the most Victory points wins.

name: Timespan
description:
Timespan is a streamlined, friendly and highly varied civilization game from the designers of Automania and Bad Company.

Combine one of six asymmetric civilizations with one of six unique technology boards, and customize your civilization further by recruiting among 175 historic persons, buildings, technologies and wonders.

Large parts of the game are played simultaneously, allowing you to lead your civilization from the stone age to the space age in about 90 minutes.

There is no warfare: Timespan focuses on the peaceful sides of civilization building, the exploration and on building an economic engine.

>>>

The game is played over 5 rounds. Each round consists of an exploration phase and an action phase.

In the exploration phase players take turns (in order of their positions on the harmony track) to draft cards and discovery tiles from the current age.

Then, players move their camels, possibly visiting the other players' wonders for various effects and rewards.

Then follows the action phase, which is played simultaneously by all players:

Each player has a civilization board with a timeline, where they can play up to 4 cards. As new cards are played, older cards are pushed out of the timeline, and goes into the player's heritage.

Players use their workers to activate cards in their timeline, as well as action boxes on their civilization boards and their own wonders.

All activations provide various rewards such as resources or advancements on the culture track (to gain wonders and new workers), on the science track (to unlock technologies on the player's technology board), or on the ship track, the flight track or even the space track (giving access to various rare luxury resources). Luxuries can be used to upgrade your cards' effects, and when luxuries are moved into your heritage, they continue to provide permanent passive income.

At the end of the second and fourth round, a new age begins, and new cards and discovery tiles are introduced to the players.

—description from the designer

name: Tinctura
description:
In the gamers' game Tinctura, welcome patients to your pharmacy and cure them of their ailments by making ointments, tinctures, and tablets for them. To do this, you must collect ingredients, train apprentices, and develop your skills so that you can meet even the most difficult challenges.

Plan your day secretly in hour shifts to work in your pharmacy, in the town or in the woods. Collect resources in the forest and create the medicine your patients need. For every medicine you need certain skills. These can be improved by studying in the town or do some research on your own. Buy some equipment to get advantages through bonus tracks. And hire apprentices to help them with creating medicines. Get the most victory points to win the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Tiny Epic Dungeons Adventures
description:
Tiny Epic Dungeons Adventures is a standalone dungeon crawler that builds on the Tiny Epic Dungeons system. This story-driven adventure introduces new heroes, deadly enemies, and hidden secrets to uncover.

Explore the dungeon like never before with an Adventure Booklet, a spiral-bound Dungeon Booklet, and secret Chapter Envelopes that unlock thrilling plot twists. Discover powerful loot, face unexpected challenges, and open mysterious packages that push your party to the limit!

Featuring a chapter-based Dungeon Booklet and modular dungeon rooms, each playthrough offers new surprises. The latest gameplay addition, Exploration, changes the way you approach danger—search for keys to unlock forbidden doors, use bombs to blast through walls, and find loot to survive the journey’s perils. Every decision matters as you navigate the depths.

It’s fully compatible with the original Tiny Epic Dungeons. Mix and match heroes, loot, spells, dungeon rooms, and enemies to create your ultimate dungeon-crawling experience.

—description from the publisher

name: Tiny Epic Dungeons Adventures: Deluxe Edition
description:
The Deluxe Edition includes The Skyward Revenge mini expansion which introduces a modular side-quest chapter that acts as its own play session and can be integrated at any point in the storyline.

Additionally, the mini expansion brings new Mobs and Minions to the Tiny Epic Dungeons System. Each presenting a unique challenge that will test even the best players!

name: Legendary: Game of Thrones Deck Building Game
description:
In this competitive version of Legendary, players seek to claim the ultimate prize: the Iron Throne! Take control of one of the great houses of Westeros with fan-favorite characters and locations. Brand new game content including Masterminds, Heroes, Villains, and more! All cards will contain original art based on the characters from the Game of Thrones! 550 cards, a rule book, deluxe play mat, player boards and everything you will need to play!

Winter is coming, and the houses of Westeros are locked in a bitter battle. Experience a thrilling world of epic warfare with Legendary: Game of Thrones Deck Building Game, in which you play as one of the Great Houses, with your own heroes to recruit and masterminds to protect. No matter who you choose, be prepared! It will take more than brute strength to prevail. You will need skill, guile, and a steady hand if you are to sit on the Iron Throne!

—description from the publisher

name: Tiny Toe Beans: Ultimate Mischief
description:
Step into the paws of mischievous house cats on a mission to cause maximum chaos! Explore a quirky, modular mansion where every room, from the sun-drenched Garden to the shadowy Basement, holds unique opportunities for mayhem. Outsmart the ever-watchful Human, sabotage rival felines, and unleash your inner agent of chaos in this lighthearted game of tactical pranks and purr-fect timing.

Players roam a tile-based house, rolling a custom die to move their cat meeples. Each turn, you’ll play Mischief Cards (room-specific actions like "Sofa Scratch" or "Toilet Paper Shred") to earn Mischief Tokens (victory points) while adding Chaos Tokens to rooms. Use Prank Cards ("Laser Pointer Chase," "Spray Bottle Surprise") to steal tokens, move opponents, or manipulate the Human! Every room has a Special Rule (e.g., swap cards in the Art Studio, teleport from the Front Door), creating dynamic combos.

But beware: Chaos Tokens attract the Human! At the end of each turn, the Human storms toward the messiest room, removing tokens and punishing cats caught in their path. Balance risk and reward as you plot paths, time pranks, and decide when to go all-in — or flee!

Earn tokens by playing Mischief Cards, cleverly activating room powers, and outmaneuvering rivals. Victory demands cunning tactics: harvest chaos efficiently, sabotage foes with pranks, and avoid the Human’s wrath. Be the cat with the most Mischief Tokens when the shared pool runs out!

—description from the designer

name: Tippi Toppi: Hoch Hinaus!
description:
Tippi Toppi – Hoch Hinaus! is a new interpretation of the card game Cahoots - using domino tiles instead of cards. Up to four players work together to complete a series of goals by strategically placing tiles from their own hand into a 4x3 grid, stacking the tiles on top of each other.

The team only wins if all tasks are completed before anyone runs out of tiles.

name: Tomb Raider: The Crypt of Chronos
description:
Tomb Raider: The Crypt of Chronos is more than just a board game: this is a full Tomb Raider experience!  Lara Croft must embark on a journey to the elusive island of Kairos in search of an artifact said to hold the reins of time. She will have to navigate treacherous terrain, evade cunning traps, and confront an enemy from her past.

Tomb Raider: The Crypt of Chronos is a single-player adventure game. There are 2 different ways to play:
Adventure book - A structured adventure split into 20-60 minute missions.
Island campaign - A randomized complete campaign, lasting around 3 hours.

—description from the publisher

name: Top Tale: Tall Tale
description:
Top Tale: Tall Tale is a spin off of Top Tale: The Original Game (O.G.), where the twist is that for each topic a fantastical element must be added into the players' responses. Similar to The O.G. series, the game can be played with 2-10 players, ages 10+, and a typical game lasts 30+ minutes, taking less than two minutes to learn.

In Top Tale: Tall Tale, players will still get to know each other, however the stories aren't expected to be based solely on the truth. The stories are expected to be exaggerated and unbelievable, which makes the best story often times the most entertaining story.

Top Tale: Tall Tale can be integrated with other Top Tale volumes during gameplay, where the Tall Tale cards are clearly marked to cue players to stretch the truth. The other game play mechanics are all the same as the rest of the Top Tale series.

-description from publisher

name: Toppings
description:
In Toppings, players sit around a pizza and try to get the most points by collecting their favorite toppings, and avoid the toppings they despise!

Players take turns in three phases that consist of cutting the pizza into slices, choosing a slice to claim, and then taking actions that allow you to pick-off, trade or swap toppings.

Players win by having the most victory points at the end of the game. Victory points are gained by collecting your favorite toppings but be careful, points can be lost by collecting too many despised toppings!

-description from designer

name: Tora Tora Tora!
description:
Tora Tora Tora! is a two-player Strategic level board-wargame that presents a holistic and dynamic view of the Pacific Front of World War II. Rather than focusing on individual historical battles, the game captures the broader struggle for control across the theater, emphasizing tempo, positioning, and resource management.

Players take command of either Japan or the Allies, each operating under a different economic logic. Japan pays to expand across areas of the map, while the Allies pay per unit regardless of distance. This fundamental asymmetry shapes every decision, forcing each side to approach movement, expansion, and confrontation in a distinct way.

Actions require limited resources, and battles involve hidden commitments before resolution, creating tension even before dice are rolled. Overextending can leave forces undersupplied and vulnerable, so players must constantly balance immediate gains against long-term sustainability. The game rewards careful pressure, territorial control, and forcing the opponent into inefficient responses.

The game ends after a fixed number of rounds, and victory is determined by strategic control of key areas and overall position on the map. Winning is less about a single decisive clash and more about managing tempo, preserving strength, and gradually exhausting the opponent’s options.

—description from the designer

name: Rush of Ikorr
description:
In Rush of Ikorr, you will assume the role of a powerful Avatar, infusing and summoning legendary champions, building iconic locations, and casting mystical spells to claim your dominance in this battle for ultimate possibility! Join two other Avatars to defeat your foes and fight toward a common goal of the Rush of Ikorr.

Rush of Ikorr redefines the TCG experience by blending the allure of ancient mythologies with innovative gameplay. Unique Infusion cards provide the ability for card customization and the option to engage in 3v3 team battles allow for unprecedented strategic depth. This game isn’t just about collecting cards; it’s about crafting legends, making it an ideal experience for anyone who loves innovation, strategy, and epic mythological tales.

—description from the publisher

name: Tournament Arc
description:
Tournament Arc is a comedic strategy card game where you draft and coach a team of ragtag student athletes to win the ultimate sports competition! But what sport exactly? You'll find out along the way!

Build a story with your friends as you train your team and hinder others with a delightful blend of strategy and chaos! No knowledge of sports or anime required.

The game consists of 3 phases: drafting, training, and competing. In the drafting phase, players draw and pass athlete cards to build out their initial team of 3 athletes. In the training phase, players take turns playing episode cards to buff/debuff athletes and activate events while building a story. Half-way through the training phase, the sport card is revealed which determines which stats matter and how many athletes will be sent out per team. In the competition phase, players total their respective team scores according to the active sport card to determine the winner.

—description from the publisher

name: Towers of Ra!
description:
Towers of Ra! immerses you and up to eight players in a mythic struggle to regain control over the god of Chaos, Apophis and aid the fallen god of the Sun, Ra. As the gods of ancient Egypt, you wield unique abilities to shape gameplay and tactics in this cooperative experience. Your ultimate goal: building a magnificent tower to Ra, granting him the strength to ascend once more and thwart the collapse of creation.

Drawing on elements of dexterity, cooperation, and unwavering resolve, you’ll utilise statues, temples, and card components to build a structure capable of supporting all four of Ra’s temples. But beware: should a single component falter, Apophis claims victory, plunging the world into darkness.

Can you and your fellow deities aid Ra in time to preserve existence itself?

—description from the designer

name: Towers of Sifnos
description:
Following the aftermath of the Samian invasion, the Greek inhabitants of Sifnos sought to better defend their mineral rich land. Over the course of several centuries, they constructed a network of over seventy beacon towers scattered across the small island. This system would allow them to quickly communicate a variety of messages, and most importantly, warn of incoming sea invasions. Now's your chance to step into the role of an ancient Greek military commander! Prepare your people against raiding pirates by constructing towers, mustering soldiers, and investing into the future of Sifnos.

Your goal in Towers of Sifnos is to have the most victory points (VP) at game's end. Points are primarily gained by increasing your influence and successfully defending the mining operations of the island's three predominant minerals: gold, silver, and lead. Players track their influence over these minerals on their player boards. Several invasions will occur over the course of the game, granting players the opportunity to prove their proficiency and might. After each invasion, the pirates will either grow in number or much needed allied reinforcements will arrive. The game ends immediately after three waves of reinforcements have arrived at the island.

—description from the publisher

name: Towndraft
description:
The gears of progress are turning, the engines are humming, and the smoke of industry curls into the sky. In Towndraft, you and your fellow visionaries step into the role of city founders in a steampunk world of brass and iron. Each decision you make shapes the future skyline - whether your town thrives as a bustling hub of commerce, a haven of green parks, or a fortress of governance and order is entirely in your hands.

Towndraft is a card game for 2–4 players, ages 10 and up. It’s a drafting experience where players select Site Cards to construct the most prosperous town. Each city is built from 18 cards, but no two games play alike thanks to a modular deck system. Before the game begins, players decide which types of buildings will be available, shaping unique strategies and towns every time.

—description from the designer

name: Trailblazer: The Colorado Trail
description:
Travel, explore and experience the adventures found along the spectacular Colorado Trail. Sweeping vistas, mountain peaks, rivers, lakes, and passes await as you discover and observe the amazing diversity of Rocky Mountain wildlife and vegetation. Manage your resources to advance along the trail, allowing you to experience the variety of adventures that make the Colorado Trail wonderfully unique.

Trailblazer: The Colorado Trail takes place over the course of six weeks (rounds) that represent around eighty miles of actual trail distance traveled per week. Along the way, players can experience off-trail adventures such as river rafting, climbing 14ers, hot springs, horseback riding, biking, or even taking a ride on a historic train! The more you adventure, the more columbines — Colorado's state flower, which are the game's points — you gain. Columbines can also be acquired by taking in the amazing vistas, going over mountain passes, or spending time by the numerous lakes, rivers, and creeks. The numerous flowers, trees, birds, and animals discovered and observed on your journey can help you earn needed supplies and score more columbines.

Players need to manage their supplies as they journey on the Colorado Trail, gain rungs on the elevation ladder, and move along the unique adventure path. Each player must organize and play their deck of action cards to maximize their abilities, adventures, and actions.

—description from the publisher

name: Tranquility: The Descent
description:
In Tranquility: The Descent players work together to descend into the depths in search of Tranquility.

Players take turns placing cards to pave the way for their teammates. Journey together through glittering caverns and underground glades in this exploration of the earth. Like all games in the Tranquility series, The Descent is played in silence. Deep underground you will need to find new ways to cooperate in order to overcome the perils that lurk beneath the surface.

Players must complete the full grid of 40 cards. Starting at the surface players must descend through 5 layers of 8 underground caverns in order to complete The Descent. Rows are completed in order and cards may be freely played anywhere within the row you are working on. Each row must be completed with numbers ascending from left to right before a new row can be started.

The goal of the game is for the team to complete the grid before any player runs out of available actions.

—description from the designer

name: Transperceneige, le jeu
description:
Transperceneige, the game is an asymmetrical semi-cooperative game. Following a climatic catastrophe, the Earth has been plunged into a new ice age, removing all life from the planet. Only one group of humans has managed to board the Transperceneige, a train that runs around the planet forever, keeping them alive. The players, in command of the different groups of passengers, will have to make choices and collaborate with each other (or not!) to take control of the Transperceneige. But they still have to survive the trip.

To gain influence, you must satisfy your passengers, prepare revolts and achieve secret objectives. However, selfish choices will jeopardize the survival of the whole train, leading to defeat. Can you make the right decisions? Action planning, cooperation, resource management and bluffing will be your best assets on board the train of a thousand and one cars. Welcome to the Transperceneige!

Each player controls a class made up of the passengers of the train. Each class is different and corresponds to a specific hierarchy and function in the train (high, medium, low class). Players will have to manage cars using a deck of cards unique to each player, representing the possible actions to be performed during the game turn. Players will have to cooperate (or not!) to survive together to one of 5 possible endgames: 4 defeat scenarios, one victory scenario.

If the train reaches its destination, symbolized by a "Sun" marker on the central board, the game ends immediately. The player who was the most clever, and therefore with the most influence points at the end of the game, will take control of the Transperceneige!

Otherwise, when one of the conditions listed below is met, the game ends immediately and the game is lost.

     The train stops.
     The train does not go in the right direction (the "Death" marker is reached on the central board)
     There are no more Event cards to draw
     A player loses all his passengers


—description from the publisher (translated)

name: Trash Rush
description:
Every year, the town of Otterdam hosts the grand and spirited Wild Boar Parade, a lively festival celebrating the pride of the wild pigs as they descend en masse from the forests surrounding Boarcelona. This year, the festivities were more boisterous than ever, leaving the city in a state of joyful chaos. As coordinators, your mission is to lead your teams of patient and ingenious raccoons to clean up the aftermath of the festivities. Strategize and manage your teams efficiently to tackle various challenges and obstacles, from scattered trash to displaced items, ensuring Otterdam is restored to its pristine state as quickly as possible.

in Trash Rush, players coordinate a team of raccoons to clean up the city. In each round, players choose an action sequence for their team. Steering your garbage trucks around the city, gather as much rubbish as possible over four rounds.  Make the most of your rubbish: use it to repair the city to gain bonuses and victory points. Alternatively, deliver it to recycling plants to score big! After 4 rounds, the game ends and the player with the most victory points wins.

Trash Rush comes with solo, competitive, and cooperative modes.

—description from the publisher

name: Travail
description:
Travail is a 1–2 player cooperative roguelike adventure, blending choose-your-own-path storytelling with fast-paced, tactical card-driven combat.

Across three acts, you’ll journey through desecrated hamlets, haunted ruins, and corrupted sanctums, confronting the grotesque fallen angels who plague this land with their blasphemy.

Every choice forges the path ahead, uncovering new discoveries with each run. Every battle is a test of positioning, synergy, and survival. And even in death, there is strength, as each attempt offers fresh encounters, branching paths, and hard-won victories, unlocking new cards and relics for your next run.

Heaven’s banished wander the earth. It falls to you to end their heresy.

-description from designer

name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands: The Chaos Chamber
description:
Tiny Tina's Wonderlands: The Chaos Chamber is a trick-taking game that features characters from Tiny Tina's Wonderlands franchise such as Paladin Mike, The Dragon Lord, and Wastard, alongside classes that include Spore Warden and Brr-Zerker.

To play, each player chooses a class to start, then enters the Chaos Chamber. Using a strategic trick-taking combat system, players can blast, slash, and cast their way through the hordes of enemies like Skeleton Warriors, Trolls, Goblins, and other fearsome foes like the Banshee, Dry'l, Ribula, and more to gain legendary loot and victory points.

name: Enemies of Gotham City
description:
Enemies of Gotham City is an area-control game based off the beloved show Batman: The Animated Series. Play as one of twelve unique asymmetric villains like The Joker, Harley Quinn, Mr. Freeze, and more in an effort to take control of Gotham City's districts. Make some cash, thwart Batman, and become the most infamous villain of them all.

To do this, you have to plan out your moves and strategize, but you must also be adaptable; Gotham is in chaos, and your plans may not always go as intended! Wrestle for control of Gotham's districts with rival villains and out-think your opponents by using your power and weapons. Watch out for Batman and his allies, who are looking to bring peace to Gotham and send your goons to the Arkham Asylum cube tower!

—description from the publisher

name: Legendary: A DC Deck Building Game
description:
Legendary: A DC Deck-Building Game is a standalone deck-building game that brings the DC Universe into the Legendary family. Players assume the roles of DC superheroes working cooperatively to thwart the schemes of a Mastermind villain and their associated threats.

Each game features a randomly selected Mastermind who pursues a unique evil Scheme, creating a distinct challenge for players. Throughout the game, players build their decks by recruiting Heroes and acquiring powerful cards to strengthen their capabilities. Sidekick cards provide crucial support in defeating Villains and completing objectives that emerge during play.

The game incorporates a Hope and Fear Tracker that measures the overall state of the conflict. As the tracker shifts, it influences when and how players can activate special abilities tied to their Heroes, requiring strategic timing and decision-making to overcome increasingly difficult threats.

The core set includes a diverse array of characters from the DC Universe, each represented through original artwork. These Heroes, Villains, Masterminds, and various card types provide multiple paths to victory and strategic variety across different games.

Players win by working together to defeat the Mastermind's Scheme before either the Mastermind achieves their objectives or the game state becomes unwinnable. Success requires careful deck management, tactical card play, and coordinated use of each Hero's unique abilities.

—description from the publisher

name: Tricky Teams
description:
Do you dare venture into the Tricky Forest?
In the shade of the trees, the gangs of field mice, tree frogs, lizards, and finches are planning their next raids.
New alliances are formed in each trick-taking round, and every decision can change the course of the game.
Four cleverly illustrated animal teams with numerical values ​​from one to ten and special abilities ensure surprising twists and turns.
Joining the winning team at the right moment earns you silver coins.
Fast-paced rounds keep the excitement high and make the game an entertaining experience for trick-taking game fans, families, groups of friends, and anyone who wants to combine a bit of teamwork with some strategy.
After four raids, the player with the most silver coins wins.

— description from the publisher

name: Trifle
description:
Trifle is based on the classic Italian card game, Briscola. You can play it competitively with older children or as a breezy pastime with other adults.

It is a may-follow trick-taker. Which means, you can always play whichever card you want. No restrictions.

Cards are worth the number printed on them (if a card doesn't have a number, it is worth zero).  Your goal is to capture the most card points. Catch more than 30 and you win a game. Win three games to win a match.

—description from the designer

name: Trismegistus
publisher: Board&Dice; CMON Global Limited; DiceTree Games; Giant Roc; Maldito Games
description:
In the 19th century, alchemy was regarded as an occult science—a blend of modern discoveries and ancient wisdom. Though the golden age of alchemy has long passed, the dream of bending the laws of nature and creating the Philosopher’s Stone remains alive. A new generation now walks in the footsteps of the legendary Hermes Trismegistus, seeking forbidden knowledge and craving power. Their imagination and resolve are unrivaled. Some view them with fear; others, with awe and admiration. As you take your first steps into the world of alchemy, your goal is to uncover the mysteries hidden since the dawn of time and outshine all others in the quest to become the greatest alchemist the world has ever known.

In Trismegistus, players take on the role of 19th-century researchers who have discovered Trismegistus' notes and attempt to follow his formula for creating the Philosopher's Stone. Over the course of three rounds — representing the years of their doctoral studies — they will perform various experiments, gaining and transmuting metals with the aid of mysterious artifacts. At the end of the game, players are awarded points based on their published research and their knowledge of the primal elements, as well as their progress toward creating the Philosopher's Stone itself.

The new edition features a more accessible and less complex set of game mechanics.

name: Trismegistus: Roll & Write
publisher: Board&Dice; CMON Global Limited; DiceTree Games; Giant Roc
description:
In Trismegistus: Roll & Write, players take on the role of apprentices in the alchemist's sanctum. Drawing from a shared pool of experiments, artifacts, and dice, each apprentice works independently to impress their esteemed mentor.

—description from the publisher

name: Triumph
description:
Lead Rome to greatness and become its first Emperor!

In Triumph, you want to turn the Roman Republic from a small city into a vast empire as the leader of a great noble family. Vie for dominance on every front of the Republic's life, and outmaneuver your rivals as you compete for power and prestige. Vanquish all external enemies and secure new provinces for the glory of Rome. Will you rise to the challenge and lead your family to ultimate triumph?

With a deck of cards representing your family's most illustrious figures, you'll bid to secure the offices of consuls, praetors, and censors. Those will, in turn, provide you with clients, gold, and legions to govern provinces, lead successful military campaigns, and control key sites within Rome itself – all to gain enough prestige to proclaim yourself the first Emperor of Rome!

name: Trouble on the Tempus
description:
Trouble on the Tempus is a game about travelling through the depths of space in a lovely spaceship - as it catches fire and the electronics explode and it falls apart around you. You're pretty much doomed. Luckily you're in a time machine, part of an exploratory mission to test the latest time traversing technology, but you pushed the ship too far and things have gone horribly wrong. Your science officers have jury-rigged it to perform very localised jumps of the crew, allowing you to transport yourselves back to a time when you were not about to explode hoping that if you can gather enough information about the future you may be able to prevent the your ultimate destruction. Of course it's not a perfect system, if you cause too many paradoxes the ship may find itself trapped in a fate much worse than exploding in the depth of space, if such a thing is possible.

Trouble on the Tempus is a co-operative game of disaster management where the players must prevent fires, electrical faults, and mechanical failures, as they work to fix the hyperdrive of the Tempus so they can power themselves home. Tragically this is a truly impossible task so the players will have no choice but to engage the ships time drive, resetting the board to the way it was at the start of the game so the players can try again with the added knowledge of when and where the disasters will appear.

If you can repeat the timeline enough, collecting the right equipment and positioning yourselves to pre-empt the disasters as they happen, you should be able to predict enough rounds to fix the hyper-drive and win the game. However, each time you time travel you cause a paradox, and the difficulty of the game can be adjusted by how many paradox's you can cause before reality collapses in on itself.

—description from the designer

name: Trying Men's Souls: The Campaign for New York, August-October 1776
description:
Following the British defeat at Bunker Hill and their evacuation of Boston Harbor, the American colonies essentially held all the land of the former colonies. However, the American invasion of Canada ended in humiliating defeat and King George III won enough support from hardliners in the Parliament to raise a massive army and fleet that the British monarch hoped would bring the rebellion to an end and the colonists to heel. A month after the colonies declared their independence, in August 1776, a British fleet of over 30 warships and 400 transports carrying over 32,000 men arrived in New York harbor. Opposing them was the largest American army ever assembled of 23,000 men under the command of General George Washington. What ensued was the largest campaign of the Revolutionary War, one that could have either restored the monarchy’s rule to the thirteen British colonies or allowed the “Great Experiment” of democracy in America to grow.

Trying Men's Souls is a moderate complexity level simulation wargame on the campaign for New York. Players are cast in the roles of Generals Washington and Howe as they command their forces in the battles to take control of the American colonies’ largest city and port. Can you do as well or better?

—description from the publisher

name: TRÖK
description:
Goal : 
- Collect 50 Aare,
- OR possess the perfect combination, i.e., all different equipment and an Arcane Stone.

A turn consists of 4 phases:

- Supply: Receive 5 Equipment cards, or more depending on your upgrades.

- Trade: Choose 3 of your cards and reveal them. The highest total value determines the trade master. On your turn, choose a card from another player and add it to your hand, or trade it with the market. The player from whom you just took a card then takes a card from another player, and so on until all the cards have been taken.

- Combination: Create a combination of at least 3 identical cards to gain Aare AND a combination of at least 3 different cards to obtain one of the available upgrades.

End of Turn: Discard your unused cards and gain Aare based on your upgrades.

name: Legendary: A Marvel Deck Building Game (Second Edition)
description:
Welcome to Legendary®: A Marvel Deck-Building Game! Evil Masterminds like Red Skull, Doctor Doom, and Loki lead a horde of powerful Villains to crush the Marvel Universe. Every time you play, the Mastermind will choose a different evil Scheme to pursue. Only you can stop them, leading awesome Marvel Heroes like Spider-Man, Iron Man, and Wolverine! Celebrating over 10 years after Legendary® first launched, this is the expanded-and-improved Core Set Second Edition.

In this game for 1-5 players, each player starts with their own deck of basic Hero cards. At the start of your turn, you play the top card of the Villain Deck, representing moments when Villains invade the city, capture Bystanders, and create special events. Then, you play Hero cards from your hand to generate Attack, Recruit, and special abilities. You use Attack to fight Villains. You use Recruit to gain stronger Heroes to improve your deck.

Whenever your deck runs out of cards and you need more, you shuffle your discard pile to make a new deck, including all the new Heroes you recruited. This way your deck gets stronger and stronger over time. Build up enough Attack and you can fight the evil Mastermind! But be careful: if the players don’t defeat them quickly enough, then the Mastermind will complete their dark Scheme, win the game for evil, and all players lose!

Even with about 250 cards that have been redeveloped to be more flavorful, fun, and balanced, this Second Edition Core Set is completely compatible with previous Legendary Marvel releases.

Contents:
550 Cards
1 Rubber backed playmat
1 Rulebook

name: Tales of Myth & Legend
description:
Tales of Myth & Legend is a paragraph book game set in the time of ancient Greece. Players each control a fledgling hero or heroine that has their sights set on power and glory. The players compete not only with each other, but also against the Alexander the Great himself.

In each round of the game, players simultaneously play a movement card that determines how far they will travel. Based on the results, the turn order will be adjusted, with players traveling farther distances going last, and those traveling shorter going first. In turn order, each player visits a city or location and has an encounter there, choosing a type — e.g., political, religion, or strength — based on the types available. The encounter is read aloud to the player, then they have to choose how to proceed.

Tales of Myth & Legend features many surprises and hidden components that are unlocked only based on certain events! With thousands of possible stories and encounters, this is a game you'll be playing for years to come!

—description from the publisher

name: Tunnel Story
description:
Tunnel Story directly taps into the golden age of 8-bit and 16-bit JRPGs from the 1980s and 90s. It's for anyone who remembers the magic of discovering a new world in a cartridge, with only the box art and a paper manual to guide them.

This isn't just a fantasy game with JRPG themes. It's built from the ground up to emulate the core JRPG loop: grinding, strategic leveling, and powerful boss encounters for an authentic, analog JRPG experience. Our pixel art is a deliberate, striking choice that celebrates a beloved digital art form.

in Tunnel Story, players explore an unknown map, turning tiles over to battle monsters, find loot, and locate the tunnel to the Boss Monster.  Players must defeat the 3 curses of the Boss Monster to defeat him.  But, if any member of the team fails, the game is lost.

—description from the publisher

name: Turbofans
description:
Turbofans is a action- and set-selection game of operations at 15 major, U.S. Airports and 20 minor airports, over the course of 50 years, from 1960 (about the time turbofan-powered, jet aircraft first came on the scene in the U.S.) to 2010, in 10 5-year turns.

The Players will alternate taking actions, performing one or more such actions (depending on how efficient their company is) to purchase Aircraft or Hangars, creating new Flights, or upgrading their airline, so that it is more effective in future actions.

The aircraft return net profits every turn, but each model of aircraft is different and can generate different profits, for varying numbers of turns.  And aircraft will be forced to "retire", as newer, better aircraft become available.

Victory conditions are two-fold, and are scored at the end of each turn - most cash on hand, and most major airports under control.

In addition to this, the game has a Bot system that not only allows every game to have 5 companies, but actually speed up play in the process.

Turbofans comes in two flavors - the Introductory game can be played in 60-90 minutes, and the Standard game comes in around the time it takes to play most 18XX games.  There are also optional rules, regional startup scenarios, and more.

—description from the designer

name: Twilight Struggle: 20th Anniversary Hall of Fame Edition
description:
In 1945, unlikely allies toppled Hitler's war machine, while humanity's most devastating weapons forced the Japanese Empire to its knees in a storm of fire. Where once there stood many great powers, there then stood only two. The world had scant months to sigh its collective relief before a new conflict threatened. Unlike the titanic struggles of the preceding decades, this conflict would be waged not primarily by soldiers and tanks, but by spies and politicians, scientists and intellectuals, artists and traitors.

Twilight Struggle is a two-player game simulating the forty-five year dance of intrigue, prestige, and occasional flares of warfare between the Soviet Union and the United States. The entire world is the stage on which these two titans fight to make the world safe for their own ideologies and ways of life. The game begins amidst the ruins of Europe as the two new "superpowers" scramble over the wreckage of the Second World War, and ends in 1989, when only the United States remained standing. Twilight Struggle inherits its fundamental systems from the card-driven classics We the People and Hannibal: Rome vs. Carthage. It is a quick-playing, low-complexity game in that tradition. The game map is a world map of the period, whereon players move units and exert influence in attempts to gain allies and control for their superpower. As with GMT's other card-driven games, decision-making is a challenge; how to best use one's cards and units given consistently limited resources?

Twilight Struggle's Event cards add detail and flavor to the game. They cover a vast array of historical happenings, from the Arab-Israeli conflicts of 1948 and 1967, to Vietnam and the U.S. peace movement, to the Cuban Missile Crisis and other such incidents that brought the world to the brink of nuclear annihilation. Subsystems capture the prestige-laden Space Race as well as nuclear tensions, with the possibility of game-ending nuclear war.

Twilight Struggle 20th Anniversary Hall of Fame Edition adds even more beauty and play options to the original game. Here are some of the additions you'll see in this new Edition:

     A double sided map with a new map on the front and the familiar Deluxe Edition  map on the back.
     The Turn Zero and Alternative Space Race variants included.
     A new alt-history scenario, "Red Sun Rising" with new cards.
     A collection of promotional cards including the Kickstarter Promo Packs #1 and #2 and promo cards from foreign editions of Twilight Struggle
     A background booklet including retrospective essays from the designers


—description from the designer

name: Umbral Knights
description:
Umbral Knights is a 2-4 player cooperative exploration Board Game in the astral realms of Umbral.
Play as a Knight rescuing lost souls from oblivion, testing yourself during combats and encounters, choosing among the various paths presented, which will lead you to glory.
Choose your blessing, develop your skills, conquer better items, and delve into this incredible and dark adventure.

—description from the designer

name: Unclaimed Victory: Fuentes de Onoro
description:
Unclaimed Victory: Fuentes de Oñoro is the next game in the Glory & Empire system which took place from May 3--5, 1811 on the border between Portugal and Spain.

The French Army of Portugal had just completed its retreat from Portugal after being confronted with failure due to the extensive fortifications of Torres Vedras ringing Lisbon. The French army, under Marshal Masséna, arrived in Spain bereft of much of its equipment and artillery. The British army, under Wellington, followed and harried the French out of Portugal, investing the Portuguese frontier fortress of Almeida and attempting to invest Spain's opposing border fortress of Cuidad-Rodrigo.

Wellington believed that it would take the French many weeks to recover from their trials in Portugal and with a small number of staff officers headed to the south to prepare the siege of Badajoz. Masséna had other ideas and energetically set about reorganizing his army to prepare to revictual Almeida. He managed to rebuild his army much sooner than Wellington believed possible and took the field on May 1 concentrating his forces around Cuidad-Rodrigo. Wellington hearing reports of French activity arrived back at Fuentes de Oñoro in the nick of time. On May 3 the French pushed back the British Light Division and Cotton's cavalry and marched on Fuentes de Oñoro.

The armies were closely matched in terms of raw numbers although the British had more cannon than the French while the French had more cavalry. Masséna displayed some of the brilliance for which he was known, but ultimately was unable to overcome the British and Portuguese forces and unable to retrieve his reputation as one of Napoleons finest marshals.

The Series
Glory and Empire is a game series devoted to grand tactical command, maneuver and combat during the horse and musket period. The map scale is 125m per hex. Units are battalions and companies for infantry, regiments and squadrons for cavalry and companies for artillery. Each strength point is 100 men for infantry, 50 men and horses for cavalry or one section, or 2 guns, for artillery. Turns are 20 minutes. Unit counters and some markers are 5/8" and other markers are 1/2".

The Game
The main Fuentes de Oñoro game has three 34x22 maps and six counter sheets. There are 10 scenarios which covers the fighting around the village of Fuentes de Oñoro and the French left hook around the British right flank. Most of the fighting occurred on these three maps in the southern portion of the battlefield.

North Map
The entire battlefield of Fuentes de Oñoro was quite extensive. To manage this without requiring an excessive number of maps the game splits the battlefield in a south and north part. The north map adds one 34x22 map and an additional sheet of unit counters. There are 4 additional scenarios for the north map, some of which can be played in conjunction with the south map.

Marshal's Game
With Fuentes de Onoro we'll introduce the Marshal's Game which is a simple grand tactical scale system which overlays the main Fuentes de Onoro map and the North map. The Marshal's Game Add On, provides an additional 34x22 map and a sheet of 3/4" counters.

The Marshal's Game will not only cover forces moving between the two tactical maps, but will also allow the players to maneuver their forces in a different manner than occurred historically offering much more replay and what-if opportunities. The Marshal's Game for Fuentes de Onoro covers from May 3-8, 1811 which allows players to be as tenacious as Wellington and Massena.

The scale of this map is approximately 4x the scale of the tactical maps. It uses an area movement map and has rules for entering and exiting the tactical maps. Players can maneuver their forces on the grand tactical scale map to enter the tactical map at different locations to try alternate strategies.

The south map, north map and Marshal's Game will be offered in a single game. No add-ons, no gimicks, just a game with a lot of play value.

—description from the publisher

name: Jurassic Feud
description:
Jurassic Feud is a standalone spinoff of Catapult Feud, and the goal of both games is the same: Knock down all of your opponent's warriors and be the last one standing.

In short, choose your warriors, then use your bricks to build a prehistoric-style fortress on your player board. Place your warriors on top of your fort, then take turns using your dino-catapults to launch boulders in an attempt to destroy your opponent's fortress and knock over their warriors. Each turn consists of four phases: tactics (playing an action card), aim, fire, and clean-up. When all warriors of one side are knocked over, the battle is over. The winner must have at least one warrior miniature standing upright.

Jurassic Feud is a standalone game, but can be played with Catapult Feud and its expansions.

—description from the publisher

name: Underleaf
description:
Uncover the trinkets and the critters of the forest in this tiny, forest floor inspired set collection card game for two!

Players take turns collecting beetles, berries and mushrooms to create the highest scoring collections. Forage the right cards to score perfect pairs and use abilities to snatch up the goods before your opponent!

Underleaf is designed to be quick to learn and easy to play in 20 minutes - perfect for your next coffee date, camping trip or chill afternoon! Every card in Underleaf is hand illustrated and features over 15 unique, real life species and scientific names!

—description from the publisher

name: Omertà: The Five Families
description:
Step into the gritty underworld of 20th-century New York City with Omertà: The Five Families, an area-control and action-point game. In this high-stakes game of power, you'll navigate the treacherous landscape as the head of a crime family, vying for control and dominion over the sprawling city. The question looms large: Will you be the one to etch your family's legacy into the unforgiving concrete of New York City's underworld?

Each turn starts with a play of a plot card to gain action points — the currency of your authority — which you then strategically spend to strengthen your grip on the city. Recruit and strategically place your capos in key locations, expanding your territory and boosting your coffers with the proceeds of illegal activities. Dabble in legal enterprises, establishing businesses that promise lucrative returns, while dispatching your trusted associates to maintain control.

The game isn't just about expanding your empire; it's about playing the political game. Throw caution to the wind as you bribe the police to disrupt your rivals or the newspapers to polish your public image and increase your respect.

Amidst the chaos, you need to carefully manage alliances and rivalries with the other crime families, eliminating hostile family leaders who stand in the way of your ascent.

—description from the publisher

name: March of the Ants: Evolved Edition
publisher: Weird City Games; Choo Choo Games; Delirium Games; Galakta; Giant Roc; Mosaico Jogos
description:
As spring dawns, the great thaw begins. Deep beneath the sprouting meadow grasses the queen stirs in her nest and the colony comes to life. Soldiers venture forth, battling centipedes while clashing with opposing colonies for territory. Workers dig an ever-expanding network of tunnels in their tireless search for food. The first larvae hatch and it is clear this generation will be different: the young colonies rapidly evolve into a multitude of new forms. The ants march out to claim the meadow as their own!

March of the Ants: Evolved Edition is a revised and upgraded version of the original base game from 2015 featuring:

     New artwork and graphic design
     Revised and updated Mechanics
     New Resting cards and Great Tunnel Battles
     Wooden Ant Meeples
     Same quick playtime that delivers a rich 4X feel in under 90 minutes.


March of the Ants puts players in control of an ant nest, competing for success with rival nests. You will explore the unknown reaches of the Meadow, evolve your ants to create new species, and vie for control of the Great Tunnel. March of the Ants is an open-ended strategy game with many paths to victory. As your nest grows and your ants evolve, you must carefully craft your strategy to emerge victorious.

—description from the publisher

name: Upside Down Kingdom
description:
The Upside Down Kingdom is a cooperative, family-friendly game that blends the simplicity of Candy Land and Chutes and Ladders with more strategic mechanics like card matching, milestone jumping, and light deck management.
Players advance by rolling the die and moving their pawn along a spiral pathway. The space that they land on determines their action. They draw cards, from different decks to make color-based matches that allow them to flip tiles and leap forward on the board.

They face the risk of setbacks triggered by specific board spaces. Landing on cloud spaces advances the white horse pawn along the clouds at the top of the board. Players must race to make it to the Ends of the Earth before the white horse pawn reaches the last cloud space.

A shared draft row adds a layer of decision-making, allowing players to choose between a face-down draw or selecting from a pool of face-up Attribute cards. Each player also takes on a unique character role with a one-time special ability, encouraging teamwork and strategic planning throughout the journey.

name: Upside Town
description:
In Upside Town, buildings rise rapidly from modular pre-fabricated units, but constructing the skyline is no simple task. Single-level units can be stacked freely but they are slow to build. Double and triple-level units, however, obey strict rules: they (magnetically) repel units of their own kind, above or below. These unique constraints create a constant puzzle of balance and strategy as players rush to fulfill and chain multiple city contracts to shape the skyline of Upside Town.

Upside Town is the first-ever boardgame to feature a new Magnetic Polarity game mechanic, where the orientation and polarity of building units matter. Throughout the game, players need to plan and build based on how units magnetically attract or repel each other. With immaculately well-designed and produced game components, Upside Town is a tactile and refreshing gaming experience for families, casual and serious gamers alike.

name: March of the Ants: Evolved Edition – Deluxe Edition
description:
The Deluxe Edition includes the Predator and Prey expansion ($39 value), full art food tokens, thick 2mm punchboard Nest Mats and Major Worker boards, and a deluxe box with a full art back that holds everything (base game and expansion) inside! The Tiny Titans: Mini Expansion is not included

The Predator and Prey expansion combines the best elements from the first edition Minions of the Meadow and Empire of the Earth expansions. The deluxe pledge includes the expansion inside the base game box. The expansion will only be available in retail as a separate box.

name: Thistleden
description:
Guide the animal folk of the forest from their humble beginnings in the village of Thistleden as they explore new lands, develop tools and abilities, and ward off predators and dangers in this civilization-building game for 1-5 players.

Each player has a 3x3 card tableau  representing their Den. During the planning phase, each player chooses a Denizen card in secret to add to their Den. Then all cards are revealed, and players place their Denizens cards in their grid, and activate all the cards in that row or column, each of which grants actions based on its type: Harvesters, Builders, Scientists, and Explorers.

At the end of the round, if the row is full, the player discards two of the cards from their active row (keeping only the one they played). Discarded cards are placed in their Legacy tableau, and adding strength to future actions as their civilization grows in age and knowledge.
 Players compete to explore new areas, build new Dens, research new technology, attract helpful Denizens and Leaders, and to defend Thistleden from threats.

-description from developer

name: Satchel Quest
description:
Venture into the dungeon with naught but your wits and your trusty bag! Satchel Quest is a competitive bag-building dungeon adventure in which every draw shapes your fate. Armed with a bag full of double-sided chips, you'll delve into the dungeon, battling enemies, disarming traps, and unlocking treasure chests while earning gold, experience, and valor.

In Satchel Quest, players draw double-sided chips, choose which side to play, and place it strategically on the current floor of your dungeon map to attack monsters, block damage, trigger ranged effects, or set up for big combos. Exact placement matters as chips interact with adjacent spaces and can chain together for powerful results.

Each round has 6 phases where players build the dungeon, resolve actions, visit the village to heal, upgrade your skills, and buy new chips at the market that expand your strategy. The game ends during the Path Phase when there are no more Path cards to reveal. The player with the most Valor points wins.

With multiple adventure paths, asymmetric heroes, and a wealth of clever combos, Satchel Quest combines bag building with a fresh, spatial puzzle twist.

—description from the publisher

name: Valls 1809: Battle of the Goi Bridge
publisher: (Looking for a publisher); Neva Game Press; Neva Wargames
description:
The French defeat at the Battle of Bailén (July 19, 1808), which saw an entire army corps surrender, was a shocking blow. It forced the Napoleonic troops to abandon Madrid and retreat to the Ebro river, marking a spectacular failure for the first French invasion of Spain.

In response, Emperor Napoleon I decided to intervene directly, leading an army of his best troops. In November, General Gouvion Saint-Cyr entered Catalonia with about 22,000 men. After defeating Spanish troops at Cardedeu, he reached Barcelona on November 17, lifting the city's blockade.

Shortly after, Saint-Cyr demonstrated his tactical prowess at the Battle of Molins de Rei, where he again defeated the Spanish forces. Despite the French victory, the Spanish troops managed to escape before being completely surrounded and captured.

After these two successive defeats, the Swiss general Teodor Reding took command of the Army of the Right. He reorganized and rearmed his men in Tarragona and set out with a small column to regroup his scattered units. The French army, aware of his movements, deployed around Valls.

Learning that Valls was occupied, Reding changed course towards Montblanc. After several days of skirmishes and maneuvers, and a difficult night march, his troops arrived near the Pont de Goi on the morning of February 25. The Battle of Valls began around 5:30 a.m.

The initial combat was intense. The Spanish attack was repelled, and after several hours of fighting, the arrival of the French Fontane brigade around noon shifted the battle's momentum. Seeing the new enemy reinforcements, General Reding realized it was pointless to continue attacking and losing more men.

This is where the second phase of the battle begins, fought at the Pont de Goi. The Napoleonic objective is simple and direct: a decisive confrontation to annihilate the Spanish army before nightfall. For the Spanish, the mission is to survive, to wear down the enemy with minimal casualties, and to hold out until dusk to make a safe and orderly retreat.

This game presents an asymmetrical and dynamic challenge. The key is not just what actions you take, but the precise moment you execute them.

If you play as the French, your strategy must be aggressive and coordinated. Can you break through the Spanish defensive lines and achieve victory before nightfall?
If you play as the Spanish, your goal is survival. Can you withstand the onslaught of the terrible French charge across the Francolí river and escape with your army intact?

name: Vamp Order
description:
Displeased with his subordinates and facing the difficult task of deciding which vampire will be his right-hand ally, Dracula decides to summon the most influential vampires to Transylvania and propose a competition in which, for three days, they must compete to determine who is the most powerful vampire, after Dracula, of course! But they must be cautious, as Van Helsing is in the region.

The game accommodates 1 to 6 players, with each player controlling a vampire. Over three days, they traverse the map of Transylvania, taking actions based on the location and the time of day. Terrorize lesser creatures, engage in a power struggle with other vampires, and prove your devotion to the legendary Dracula.

[Solo Mode]  
Has eternal life made you lazier? 
With multiple difficulty levels and extra cards, prove your worth to Dracula while being hunted by Van Helsing and his allies.

—description from the publisher

name: Logic & Lore
description:
Logic & Lore is a cozy-but-competitive deduction game for two players.

Rivals race to be the first to align their hidden stars, numbered 1-9. Each player has dragons and mice working together to organize the cosmos: they send their dragons out to gather information and the mice stay back to take notes and make conclusions based on the knowledge brought back by their dragons.

Players each start with their set of cards face-down and shuffled. The game ends when either one player aligns all of their cards correctly OR a player chooses to reveal all of their cards. If the cards are correct, they win; otherwise, their opponent wins.

A player's turn is made up of the following steps:

Choose Focus - Pick two cards to find more information
Search the Skies - Ask questions about the cards 
Move the Heavens - Move cards to new locations - (Optional)
Align the Stars (Optional)
If a player either thinks that all of their cards are aligned, they reveal all of their face-down cards and, if they are all correct, they win. Otherwise, they lose.

—description from the publisher

name: Vanguard: Normandy
description:
Set during the Normandy Campaign of World War Two, Vanguard places players in control of USA and German forces fighting to defeat one another in a desperate and high-stakes struggle for the French mainland.

The huge range of US and German forces fighting in the Normandy Campaign is represented by beautiful miniatures and bespoke unit cards, which handily track special rules for a streamlined playing experience.

These units are entirely unique, each featuring distinct rules, attack profiles, and artwork inspired by the design team’s passion for history.

Combat is fast-paced and intuitive, thanks to a streamlined dice system that eliminates complex calculations and line-of-sight mechanics.

Vanguard’s unit activation is both fun and intense. Players add Faction Tokens to a shared Activation Bag for each unit they control, before drawing tokens randomly to determine the order these units activate.

This system creates nail-biting, cinematic gameplay where players are never sure which units will activate first!

Vanguard also features a dynamic army-building system. Both players start with limited forces and a requisition income, building up their army and economy over the course of the game through the control of battlefield sectors.

The more sectors a player controls, the more resources their forces receive—but if the Victory Point gap grows too wide, the trailing player can unleash powerful Underdog abilities to even the odds.

Setting up the battlefield is quick and simple.

By arranging nine of the 15 double-sided battlefield tiles into a grid, players can create a visually stunning and unique play area in seconds.

Each tile features beautifully detailed artwork depicting historical locations from D-Day and the Normandy Campaign, including airfields, radar stations, manors, farms, and more.

The solo campaign allows a single player to fight through a historical campaign as the USA, battling across six historical engagements against a fiendish German AI opponent.

name: Reef & Ruins
description:
Hydras & Otters team up to unlock satisfying combos while exploring reefs and ship ruins for treasure in Reef & Ruins, a Roll & Write that gives you the satisfaction of a crunchy large sheet, small font Roll & Write spatial puzzle engine builder in a smaller, quicker, more approachable manor.

There’s one die for each head of the Hydra, either for them to venture into shipwrecks to search for treasure, work together to enchant their treasure, or send otters to the reef to get pearls. Each head of the hydra typically wants to do something different, but they occasionally can agree to work together, for hydra’s sake.

At the start of each game, players will choose Ship Ruins, Enchantments, and Reef sheets and all compete to unearth the most valuable items. Players play simultaneously, each choosing between sending their hydras into the ruins for treasure, their otters to enchant the treasures, or to send both into the reef to gain bonuses there. After 18 rounds, players figure out the values of their found treasures, then enchant them for more points, then add in any reef benefits. The game ends before players will be able to finish everything, so they must make the best choices for what Ruins to complete, how many enchantments to work on, and when to go searching the Reef for pearls!

Reef & Ruins is a roll and write standalone game set in the Wicked & Wise universe.

-description from publisher

name: Scents and Sensibility
description:
Scents and Sensibility is a engine building and deconstruction game in which players are hedgehogs running a flower shop. Players pick flowers, make bouquets, and gain loyal customers, but must choose the right times to sell off their bouquets to get the most out of them before they're gone.

Can you run the best flower shop and gain the most customers?

—description from the publisher

name: Verrago: The Fantasy Globe Game
description:
A Hybrid Fantasy Civilization RPG that plays 1-10 players. Verrago combines traditional board game mechanics, light legacy mechanics with Table Top Role Playing Games.  You will be using magnetic pieces on a globe that acts as a new form of game board, called Vaeya, A mysterious planet layered in stories and magic.  Play as any level of political unit : Characters, Families, Guilds, Roles, Kingdoms, Empires)on a world where everything hangs in a dynamic Balance.  Should this Balance be disrupted by you and your fellow players (and it surely will), the planet will try to end your (usually) evil ways by uniquely trying to exterminate everyone, starting with the worst perpetrators. This is a world where nothing stays the same, mysteries deepen as you explore the Veridian and attempt to master it and you can choose to band together to fight the apocalypse, or become it.
With 5 main paths to victory(Epic Story, Strongest Lineage, Veridian Imprint, Strategic Survivor and Richest Delve) you choose how and where your victories can occur over your opponents.  Victories, over many plays of Verrago, create a historical record of your globe that becomes unique to your gaming group. The globe itself acts as your "save file" so that your playthrough's matter, your time playing the game works more for you. This allows you to create a long term dialogue with your board game group and weave ever more elaborate stories that add value to your group and add additional meaning to your friendships

Designed also as a fully developed TTRPG, this game will have many familiar TTRPG themes and structures.  Dungeon Masters, this game will help you relieve your creative burdens and allow you to get immediate player investment into your game when doing your session zero game! Players, this will give you a TTRPG experience like no other, a true blend of concepts at a deep level with extensive options for pushing your own narratives. Verrago uses a co-created history mechanic for telling epic, memorable stories that can also be used for your Table Top Role Playing Games. Vaeya, the planet of our setting, is an INTERACTIVE SETTING, the cards allow for a dynamic storytelling experience that also gives you(and your characters) direct control over a range of theme/lore heavy game mechanics.  Verrago also has an event system that helps you generate a world spanning, geopolitical and Veridian situation EACH GAME, with care to minimize the burdens of recording the history during the game.  A more detailed record is possible, yet this will be at your own discretion.  Verrago also has a Campaign Book that works with the card generation system so that you get the best of both worlds, the strength of linear storytelling AND the strength of the "choose your own adventure" style of storytelling. There is nothing that approaches the scope and scale of Verrago on the board game market.  There's something special about creating a world with others...

The game has 3 main parts, of which the first is optional and the third won't always occur.  Here is a rough overview of how it will play(subject to change as the game is currently in development):

1. The Pre-Game(Optional): You play with your friends to set the precise magical conditions you want to play and feel out and fine tune the game so that you aren't limited to randomization. This pre-game is about generating the world you will play next and takes about 30-60min.  There are 25 preset scenarios that allow you to skip this pre-game and are recommended for your first few times playing the game.

2. Verrago: You will us 5x game mechanics (Explore, Expand, Exploit, Experiment and Exterminate) to overcome your opponents(should you have any), sometimes needing to create temporary/permanent alliances to survive the more dangerous events that occur randomly(or by player action).  As you acquire power in the world, the planet fights back as you are disrupting the careful magical balance of the world.  
Once you've disrupted the balance enough, through your own actions or that of the planetary response, the apocalypse will begin.
  
3. Sudden Death Apocalypse: Featuring 125 different ways to destroy the world, each apocalypse will demonstrate something new about Veridian and the world.  The Apocalypse has 5 randomly drawn event cards at the beginning of the game that slowly get turned over revealing the apocalypse code that players look up in the event book.  Players take their most empowered character(s), their Verrago, and attempt to maneuver them so that the apocalypse affects other players more than themselves.  Whatever remains is yours to keep for the next game.  At the end of the apocalypse, the game will be recorded using pen and paper and you can choose to continue your play and build upon the remains of the previous age. You win when you survive and no one else does, or you survive better than everyone else.  You can also win by creating the strongest legacy and other forms of victory.  Victory is more of a long term goal, with challenges like "survive the 25 preset scenarios in different configurations".

Verrago is a multi-layered game, with 5 expansions already designed to work with the existing game, so that you will only ever need to purchase 1 globe to play it.  Each expansion will provide the scope of a full game, using cards and add an in depth focus to the game, changing it into many different forms of popular game mechanics like: Warfare, Trade, Technology, More Veridian(Magic), Culture, and Survival/CO-OP. The game is designed to fundamentally change into your preferred style of game by purchasing an expansion.
