Or play all expansions together, they are interchangeable and don't have dependencies on each other.  Future expansions WILL have dependencies on the core expansions. Bring whichever expansion you like to the table to try to shift the focus of the game "your" way as you unlock the option to play your expansion by your in game actions.

About this project and the designer:

This unique Role Playing Game(RPG) setting has undergone rigorous craft, research and extreme care in it's composition as a passion project beginning in 2003. S.A. Heinichen was trained at Navy Nuclear Power Training Command and then at Submarine Base Groton in the U.S. Navy, in addition to having held a Top Secret security clearance.  S.A. Heinichen's extensive training in multiple applied engineering fields has allowed him to incorporate many scientific disciplines into the magic system, represented simply by the rune system.  The Cloak and Dagger excitement of the intelligence community is a theme throughout Verrago.  Verrago strikes a balance between science fiction and high fantasy and you can actively change this balance during the course of the game as part of your strategic storytelling goals.

—description from the designer

name: Vestige
description:
In a bold age of neo-humanistic advancement and technological breakthrough, life evolved, and the lines between biology and engineering blurred. The limits of possibility were shattered. A great civilization rose toward the stars, toward an enlightenment increasingly within reach. That civilization collapsed. How and why are long since forgotten. Chaos reigned. Technological understanding was lost to generations of strife and survivalism as time rendered everything (humanity included) into discarded scraps of what once was. In this fallen world, the last wretched vestiges of humanity vie for the only hope for significance that remains: leverage.

Vestige is a highly-strategic, competitive modern euro that you can play in an hour. It is built around a resource alchemy system modeled on the color wheel that offers great depth but can be understood almost instantly; for example, mix might (red) and cunning (yellow) to attain guile (orange). A modular game board; variable end-game conditions; and a card-tableau, engine-building heart makes every game crunchy, and combo-driven. Derived from Vindication, Vestige reimagines its systems in a new setting and with a new depth-to-approachability ratio.

Each turn you move around a randomly generated map of locations, each offering a unique action or effect. Visiting these locations you unlock your potential, spread your influence, develop your attributes, build your network of contacts across three factions (smugglers, mercenaries, lawmakers), and then work with that network to complete jobs your contacts are suited for (unearthing artifacts, claiming bounties, and developing augmentations). Through action selection, card-tableau combo building, area control, and careful resource management you seek to gain more leverage than your opponents, all while the powers-that-be use any and all insidious tricks at their disposal to keep you down where they want you.

-description from publisher

name: Surplus of Sloths
description:
In Surplus of Sloths, the rivers are flooding, and players are wildlife rescuers each trying to save sloths and make them happy so that they can be awarded even more sloths!

To set up, use as many types of sloths as the number of players, plus one. Each player takes three cards in hand, then discards one card to the "surplus net". Deal out two rows of cards, with each row having one more card than the number of players. The active player drafts one card from a row, then each other player drafts from the same row, with the final card falling into the surplus net. Add a new row of cards, then the next player clockwise starts the next turn.

When you all the rows have been drafted, with remaining cards falling into the net, players compare their longest run of each sloth type. A type has cards numbered 1-7, along with three Xs, which are wild. Whoever has the longest run of a type, with ties being broken by whoever has the highest numeral in their run, claims all cards in the surplus net of that type. The value of a type equals the sum of the numbers in the net multiplied by 1-4 depending on how many sloths of that type (0-3) are also in the net. Whoever has the most points wins.

You can also play with four baby sloths of value 0 that count as all types. They aren't worth any points in the surplus net, but they can lengthen all of your runs...assuming they would otherwise start with 1, that is.

name: Vine
description:
Guide the growth of your beanstalk while diverting the plants of your neighbors. Tile placement is crucial as you must balance maintaining control over your plant’s direction with ensuring you have the right structure to support optimal bean growth.

The light engine-building tile game Vine leverages simple yet strategic gameplay, challenging players to develop the highest-yielding garden of pole beans. Prune your plant to create more options later in the season, close off sections to prevent unwanted growth, and let your vines climb high to maximize points by the end of the game.

—description from the publisher

name: HERD: The Dinosaur Survival Card Game
description:
HERD: A Dinosaur Survival Card Game is a beautifully illustrated semi-cooperative card game with the goal of keeping your herd safe from rapacious predators during the Mesozoic Era.

Every player has a Herd card: Triceratops, Stegosaurus, Parasaurolophus, Ankylosaurus, or Brontosaurus. Each turn, Predator, and Prey cards are drawn, and players must fend off the attacks of terrifying monsters before their herd is eliminated! The Countdown Clock ticks down, and if it reaches zero, you’ve won…or, rather, you’ve survived to fight for survival another day.

The goal of HERD is to survive until the end of the game, which is played over five turns. There are three types of cards: Herds, Predators, and Prey.

Your Herd is your responsibility - sacrificing weaker Prey to survive attacks by Predators. Prey cards represent smaller dinosaur species in the vicinity that can distract a Predator or invoke specially evolved defenses and behaviors to protect the Herd from harm.

Whether your Herd survives to the end of the game is dependent upon your tactics, but HERD is also a semi-cooperative game - if you want to have a chance to win, all Herds have to survive!

—description from the publisher

name: Lucha Lucha Three Four Five
description:
Welcome to the Arena! As the lead luchador (wrestler), you will guide your team to outcompete your rival with muscle and wits. Tackling, bumping, luring your rival into traps, all cool moves and other tricks guarantee a contest full of twists and turns!

As you embark on this game, players take turns to move their Luchador pieces to Lucha! and try to form as many of their advantage stacks as possible. After moving one of the advantage stacks through several empty spaces until it Lucha, the moved stack will stack onto an opponent's advantage stack and resolve the outcome. The game ends when neither of the players can Lucha! anymore. Then calculate how many cheers each player has received; whoever receives the most cheers wins the game and the Gold Belt!

LUCHA LUCHA 345! encourages players to develop Spatial Awareness Intelligence, which is based on the well-known ‘theory of multiple intelligences’ proposed by American psychologist and Harvard Professor Howard Gardner. Easy to learn but tough to win, this game is perfect for strategic minds and casual players alike!

—description from the publisher

name: Visions
description:
On your turn, you must:

1 - Play a card from your hand (triggering its effects)

2 - Replenish your hand to 3 cards from the river

The game ends:

Either when a player reaches the Wake-up space and that player wins the game!

Or when there are no more cards in either the draw pile or the river. All players continue to play their cards in hand. If a player can no longer start or continue one of their dreams, they pass their turn (instead of playing). When all players have passed, proceed to the scoring.

Your final score is the sum of the following 3 scores:
For the first Dream, multiply the most frequent Environment by the most frequent Category.
For the second Dream, do the same.
Add the Reflections track.
And the highest score wins!

name: Vitals
description:
Vitals is a real-time cooperative dice-rolling game about working together as a surgical team.
Players work together in real-time mimicking the atmosphere of an operating room to perform all of the tasks of the procedure while keeping your patient alive.

Teams are made up of 3 to 6 players consisting of the following roles: Surgeon, Scrub Tech, Anesthesiologist, (4th player) Circulator Nurse, (5th player) First Assist, and (6th player) Student Intern.

The gameplay begins by pulling a card from the Operation deck. Cards drawn from the operation deck explain the type of surgery about to be performed. It will show which side of the game board to use, what instrument cards will be required, and the locations of the surgery.

Each player assumes one role and works together to roll dice in real-time to perform their individual tasks needed to perform the operation. A core game concept is the Wellness button. This button needs to be pressed by one of the players when achieving their initial task at least every 15 seconds or the patient flatlines. This must be done throughout the entire surgery. If the patient flatlines, all players must stop what they are doing and roll the defibrillator dice and place the proper face on the defibrillator track next to the patient within 15 seconds to revive them. If the players succeed in reviving them, play continues. If they fail, the patient is lost and the players lose.

Roles:
Surgeon (required) - This player rolls dice when working with tools. He must roll dice until he has the dice faces of the tool he is using. Once he meets the required faces, he may use the tool to perform the task and reveal the next tool needed.

Surgical (Scrub) Tech (required) - This individual rolls dice to match the tools the surgeon asks for. When they roll the correct dice faces, they may hand that tool to the surgeon.

Anesthesiologist (required) - This player rolls dice to check the vitals of the patient. They must alternate between checking temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and awareness. This player is responsible for keeping the patient alive when other professionals are tending to their tasks.

(4th player) Circulator Nurse - This player prepares the patient for surgery and collects tools to give to the Scrub Tech and Medical supplies to give to the Anesthetist.

(5th player) First Assist - Assists the surgeon in performing surgical tasks that require more than one person.

(6th player) Student Intern - Assists all players in dice rolling. This player has one of each die for all of the other players.

—description from the designer

name: Moving Company
description:
As experienced employees, you must judge the spatial relationship of furniture combinations and make the most reasonable arrangement on the truck. It requires a delicate sense of balance, and a little luck.

In this game, each time has a total of 4 rounds. and each round consists of 4 phases in the following orders:

     Order phase
     Loading phase
     Rating phase
     End of round phase


Players take turns to roll the dice, then try to figure out how to load the different shapes of furniture onto the truck efficiently, and obtain the service rating points. Game ends after 4 rounds. The player with the highest service rating points wins, and receives the "Best Employee Award"!

Let’s get moving!

name: Vrahode: The Calteeryn Ascension
description:
Vrahode - The Calteeryn Acension is an adventure/dungeon crawl board game, the second in a series of five games, designed by Jeffrey Irving. Following the initial game Age of Prophecy (2024) this massive "core box" is a solo/co-op game for 1-6 players where players can choose to journey through huge multi-quest campaign that sprawls over the heights and depths of the mysterious world of Vrahode or choose one of five other modes of play as well as four difficulty levels!

The core box campaign victory condition: "Calteeryn" (the chosen one) must learn the ruhl (magic) of each crafted race in the game while facing mounting threats. This is done by journeying through the eight unique biomes of the Overlands, Underlands, and Oceans of the world of Vrahode.

Dice-based combat is enhanced by powerful skill deck building and racial abilities unique to each race. Every enemy encounter is different, with the enemy behavior deck threatening to change how the heroes must fight them each battle!

The world of Vrahode is based on a narrative first imagined in 1990 by designer Jeffrey Irving. The Vrahode series of games includes a introductory game Vrahode - Age of Prophecy and three additional expansions: The Enlightened & The Enslaved, Facing The Storm, and The False Gods' Deceit. All are part of the Vrahode Game System which invites players to generate their own content, adding to the expanding lore of Vrahode! This game is compatible with our proprietary 3D terrain system called Harbinger, players can create dynamic, multi-level dungeons up to five levels deep.

—description from the publisher

name: Werewolf: Duel!
description:
An immersive two-player board game where deduction skills and strategic thinking are key to victory. In Werewolf: Duel!, you and your opponent take on changing roles that belong to the Werewolf Faction or the Human Faction, where identities shift and bluffs are everywhere.

Each round, you’ll secretly choose one character card from a hidden hand, each with a unique ability and initiative number. At the same time, you must guess which character your opponent has chosen. The twist? You can spend precious Hourglass Markers to change the initiative, turning a sure defeat into a stunning victory.

The game ends when you deplete your opponent’s health or collect enough tokens for the Werewolf or Human faction. Will you outsmart your opponent, or fall victim to their cunning? Let the duel begin!

—description from the publisher

name: Warleague
description:
Prepare to dive into Warleague, a revolutionary tactical board game. Combining the strategic depth of wargaming with the immersive interactivity of dungeon crawlers, Warleague is set in an AI-controlled arena where players craft and customize heroes and units. Players will navigate through dynamic, grid-based interconnected rooms to engage in strategic battles and explore an evolving storyline. Offering modes for solo, co-op, and competitive PvP gameplay, Warleague caters to all types of gamers.

Developed to provide a unique gaming experience, Warleague fuses detailed customization with dynamic game mechanics, tailored for enthusiasts of deep strategic planning and interactive storytelling. Unlike traditional dungeon crawlers that demand extensive time commitments, Warleague offers tactical depth with reduced playtime. Furthermore, Warleague sets itself apart with a light-hearted, humor-infused adventure world that draws inspiration from childhood animation series of the 90s and energetic speed metal music, creating a nostalgic yet exhilarating environment.

Players can engage in Warleague through various game modes, including challenging solo campaigns and thrilling competitive PvP battles. The game focuses on strategic planning and adaptability, with customizable heroes and units allowing for diverse tactical approaches. Gameplay features include navigating complex rooms, avoiding traps, and engaging in combat with both AI and player-controlled adversaries.

Warleague is designed for a broad audience:

- Veteran wargamers seeking new challenges with a fresh blend of mechanics.
- Fans of dungeon crawlers and story-driven games desiring interactive, rich narrative experiences.
- New players attracted to tactical and strategic board games looking for an engaging alternative to conventional options.
- Competitive players who thrive on PvP dynamics and strategic confrontations.

—description from the designer

name: Water Wars
description:
Our galaxy is on the brink of collapse, overpopulation is depleting resources, and water is becoming scarce, making it the most precious commodity in the galaxy. The four most powerful races in our system have embarked on a battle to secure their supplies and will fight on countless planets to secure every last drop of water.

Water Wars is a confrontation game in which each player takes a 12-card army deck, draws 6 cards per round, and each turn plays a card from their hand on a planet, trying to end the round with the most power among the armies fighting for it to obtain rewards.

The armies are asymmetrical, with different distributions of strength and abilities that differentiate them from each other. Some use shields, others set fire traps, others throw acid when damaged, others repair themselves, etc.
Each round, we will improve our deck with elite cards and face off on different planets. We will end the game after the third round and count the water points obtained. The winner of the game will be the player with the most water points.

The base game has 4 armies, but it can be expanded with 2 expansions (Invasion and The Ancestors), each providing 3 armies and planets with new abilities.

—description from the publisher

name: Watson & Holmes: The lost diaries
description:
After the original Watson & Holmes, more adventures are coming.

Watson & Holmes 2 is a game of deduction. One to seven aspiring detectives step into the shoes of Doctor Watson, working alongside the detective Sherlock Holmes to try to solve a series of so far unpublished cases directly extracted from Doctor John H. Watson's diaries. Those who accept the challenge relive the adventures of the crime-solving duo, visiting each of the locations where the inquiries were made. Following the trail, each clue brings players closer to solving the case.

New adventures, new special rules and new challenges. Now you can play the game competitively, in teams, cooperatively or solo. The game is afoot again!

name: Win or Die
description:
Long ago, the world’s origins shrouded in mystery. According to the temple and sage, the ancient god named this fabulous world "Taiyi". A million years ago, a world-destroying catastrophe split the world into two closely related continents: the Dark and the Glory, following ancient gods' principles.

After billions of years of internal friction, the resources of "Taiyi" have become scarce. The continuous infiltration of chaos power from outside the continent has created extremely harsh living conditions for creatures. Due to the restraint of the truth power, the chaos power cannot directly invade "Taiyi". However, it uses the desires of sentient beings in "Taiyi" and manipulates puppets to greedily devour the world of "Taiyi"……

Win or Die stands as a fast-paced and highly competitive multiplayer strategic board game, focusing on 1V1 game mode. Its core mechanism akin to the classic game of Stratego. Game elements includes legion formation, fog of war, terrain occupation, unit countering, collection and allocation of resources, etc.
Players engage in battles without prior knowledge of their opponent's legion, launching attacks or using skills to unveil their deployment and lay them to ruin.

There are five selectable factions for players. Each faction has one leader and 6 different units. Each leader has two skill combinations, allowing players to form different legions.

Win or Die released in China in 2020 and received a score of 7.9 on Gstone (the largest Chinese board game database and social app). After three years of optimization, the game has improved its components and artworks. Ensuring the readability of unit information and making the game operations more convenient and intuitive for players.

name: Vines and Flowers: Blooming Harmony
description:
Hi, landscaper! There is a peaceful flower bed filled with elegant roses and lively trumpet creepers, eagerly awaiting you to make it blossom in full bloom. Together, players embark on a collaborative journey to build a stunning floral pergola.

In this game, you aim to complete as many full flowers as possible by connecting vines to vines and flowers with flowers of the same color. It takes strategy and a touch of luck. Special insects will have bonus effects! This brings thrilling moments to the gameplay. Each turn, players perform the following phases:


     Action Phase
     Fulfillment Phase
     Hummingbird Phase
     Replenish Phase


The game ends when the cloth bag tiles run out or the fourth Hummingbird tile appeares on the market. The player with the highest score wins.

name: Welcome to Susberg
description:
Welcome to Susberg is a cooperative deck-building game. Join your friends in a problem solving adventure where each player has a unique style of play. Buy cards and manipulate your deck to create the best possible combinations for you and your friends.

Each player chooses one of four characters. The athlete, who trashes cards and removes them from the game. The artist who mixes paints together and stashes cards aside for later turns. The musician who makes and spends music. The inventor who grows their energy, and puts cards back into their decks.

A deck of 18 foes is randomly stacked and the players must defeat them all to win the game. If each player loses their 5 health, it's game over.

Each turn follows the same pattern. You attack. You defend. You buy. You'll first combine your power cards to defeat foes. Then you defend from foes using your block cards. Then you buy new cards with the coin earned from defeated foes.

—description from the designer

name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse – RETALIATION
description:
A new violent, mature and Visceral roleplaying board gameboard game set in the World of Darkness.

Intended for solo play as well as up to four players, Werewolf: The Apocalypse — RETALIATION takes place in Yosemite Valley, following a deadly battle that left your pack all but decimated. With only a full lunar cycle to recover, rebuild your Caern, and prepare for your final revenge against Wyrm entities, your choices will weigh heavily upon the fate of your characters.

The game includes immersive branching scenarios, intense combats, mesmerizing investigations, beautiful minis, and a profound roleplaying experience.

—description from the designer

name: West Front '44
description:
West Front '44 is a two-player wargame of the campaigns along the Rhine in the winter of 1944-45 (December to March). The Allies are attempting to establish bridgeheads across the Rhine River while the Germans are planning for their Ardennes counteroffensive. The game uses a variant of the Boots/Manstein's War system to model command, control, and logistics on an operational scale.

Both players have a wide range of operational plans which they can execute to attempt to seize certain strategic objectives The general structure of the game is that each player uses command markers to activate their forces, which are divided into sub-commands (army groups and similar echelons). Each player has special markers which provide additional operational capabilities. Can you turn the tide of history in that decisive winter of 1944-45?

Each game turn (GT) represents two weeks. Each hex on the map represents 27 kilometers (17 miles) from side to opposite side. Units are primarily corps. Air units (Allied numbered air forces and German Flieger Korps). represent air cover for a sector of the front.

name: Western Legends Stories
description:
Western Legends Stories offers a unique narrative twist on the acclaimed Western Legends universe. Help found a frontier town – a beacon of civilization in the untamed American wilderness.  Over six thrilling episodes, watch the settlement grow from a remote trading post to a bustling center of commerce, facing the challenges and opportunities that society brings.

Inspired by the open-world design of Western Legends, Stories offers deeper exploration and a dynamic action system. Build, explore, and carve your legend in this captivating new chapter of the West.

—description from the publisher

name: What Lies Before
description:
Dragons breathe fiery judgment upon the dwarfs. As a lowly but mighty golem of the dwarfs, you must help reunite the shattered Houses, reclaim lost arcana, and spark a rebirth of civilization. Or erode into history with all of Dwarfdom.

The game includes 5 Missions leading to 7 unique victories (and dozens of endings where you're destroyed).

Structured as a branching narrative, this solo RPG gamebook invites you to direct the plot – but only if you master a unique combination of game mechanisms.


     Level up your character: Upgrade your attributes and skills
     Calculated gambits: Roll and gather dice to beat target thresholds
     Intellectual puzzles: Manipulate dice using limited actions
     Dexterity tests (optional): Slam dice at targets in battle


—description from the publisher

name: What the Pixel!
description:
Welcome to What the Pixel!, the only board game that asks you to express complex ideas using chunky pixels, shaky hands, and way too much confidence!

What the Pixel!! is a party game where you’ll use a screen to draw things for other players to guess. All clarity disappears as everything boils down to ridiculously limited little squares. All drawings stop being art and instead level down to pure instinct, chaos and laughter! Enjoy abstraction, frustration and glory in 8-bits or less!

Each turn a player turns over a card and randomly picks a image to create by laying down tiles - imitating 80's pixel video game illustration.  The rest of the players try to guess the image presented.  Each correct guesser wins coins, as does the artist.  The first player to 15 coins wins.

Optional cards can be added to change up the rules and add replayability to the game.

—description from the publisher

name: Whistlewood Express
description:
Whistlewood Express is a two-player strategic duel (with solo mode) where you play as freightmasters delivering goods to the towns of Whistlewood. From the train car tiles in your hand you build a shared train, but you’ll fiercely compete for the most valuable station spots. Each turn you must decide whether to attach a new car, advance the whole train, or claim a station. Every action shifts the train’s position and composition while the available stations steadily run out.

Thanks to the variable arrangement of Location Cards, every game is different and asks for a fresh strategy.

The box also includes the Freightmaster’s Logbook with 10 unlockable challenges. These scenarios take the shared train across new corners of Whistlewood and unlock new game modes and modules: additional train cars, new location cards, a drawstring bag, plus environment and cargo tokens. Modules can be mixed and matched, letting you dial in more complex, tougher, or longer sessions.

—description from the publisher

name: Who's a Good Boy?
description:
For as long as man and beast have been companions, one crucial question has haunted them both: Who, if anyone, is a good boy? Choose your dog and begin doing sins and good deeds to show your friends your true character. Gathering positive and negative traits to discover who your dog really is. Who's a Good Boy will let you gather your friends and family to ask important questions like "Are we inherently good or evil?" or "Can people change?" or "What if a dog did sins?"

In Who's A Good Boy, you begin the game by selecting a dog character card with a unique ability. From there, each round consists of a trait being flipped. Each trait has a point value that is either positive or negative. Then, players bid on these traits using Action cards that describe sins or good deeds. Positive traits are awarded to whichever dog was best and negative traits are awarded to whichever was worst.

Once a player reached five traits, their game is over. The game continues until only one player is left without five traits, at which point players count up their trait scores, resolve any remaining events, and declare which dog is the Goodest Boy.

—description from the designer

name: Draconis 8
description:
Draconis 8, where the thrill of a trading card game meets the balance and strategy of a tile-laying board game. Each pack includes a terrain card and a complete, balanced eight-card deck for one player — featuring one powerful dragon and seven champions ready for battle. With millions of possible stat combinations, every card is individually generated to provide endless possibilities. No two cards are alike, yet all are designed to be fair and balanced. The Starter Set has 4 different decks.

Each turn, both players draw a card, giving them a two card hand. Then both players choose one of their two cards to play, and reveal them simultaneously.  The player who played the card with the higher initiative (the number in the circle in the upper left) claims a yellow bead (worth 1 victory point). They play their card onto the table next to (orthogonally or diagonally adjacent to) any card in play. Then the player with the lower initiative card plays it onto the table.  If at any time, a card's challenge strength number (in the shield) is next to a smaller combat number on an opposing (or terrain) card, then the owner places a bead of their color on that combat number to show they will get a victory point at the end of the game.  Note that some abilities may cause cards in play to shift. If a card moves, remove all beads from fights it was involved in and recalculate, placing beads based on its new position.

Over the 7 turns of the game, cards will form a 4x4 grid. Once there are 4 cards in a row or column, the edges of the grid on that side are locked and cards can't be played beyond those edges. At the end of the 7th turn, players add up their score summing their beads in play plus the yellow initiative beads they won. The player with the higher score wins!

—description from the publisher

name: Wild World
description:
Wild World is a dynamic 1–4 player strategy game that blends worker placement, multi-use cards, engine-building, and tactical monster combat into one seamless, combo-driven experience. Set across five elemental realms — Forest, Ocean, Fire, Frost, and Magic — players gather fantastical creatures, explore vivid regions, evolve their champions, and brew powerful potions as they race to score the most points over three rounds.

What makes Wild World stand out is the freedom and flexibility baked into every turn. You may perform a number of different free actions — placing cards to strengthen your engine, traveling through realms for rewards and prestige, or discarding for resources — allowing each turn to unfold as a meaningful puzzle. Every card has multiple uses, and clever sequencing often triggers reward chains that lead to explosive, satisfying combos.

At the heart of the game are the mighty monsters guarding the world. Defeating them will give you permanent abilities, immediate bonuses, scoring conditions, new workers, and prestige, but reaching them requires smart planning: evolving creatures, upgrading your potion-brewing, unlocking stronger foes, and assembling the perfect moment to strike.

With multiple strategic paths, escalating tension, and thrilling bursts of synergy, Wild World offers a richly re-playable adventure in which every decision matters — and every turn can become something special.

—description from the publisher

name: Wilderness: May 5-6, 1864
publisher: Old School Wargames; Worthington Publishing, LLC
description:
Wilderness: May 5-6, 1864 is a Grand-Tactical level for 2 players (though you can play solitaire by playing both sides).  The game is designed to be played in 2 - 10 hours depending on the scenario.  
The game comes with a beautiful full color hard mounted map and counters by José Ramon Faura.

Refight the first battle between the two great generals of the American Civil War - Grant and Lee. 
As Lee can you block Grant's juggernaut in the Wilderness sending him reeling back north of the Rapidan ?  
As Grant can you finish Lee off now and end the war in 1864 saving thousands of lives?  
The decisions are yours....

Wilderness: May 5-6, 1864 has 5 scenarios counting the full 2 day battle.  
This includes several half map scenarios portraying the fierce fighting separately along Orange Plank Road and Orange Turnpike on both May 5 and 6, 1864.

Volume VII in the Civil War Brigade Battle Series, Wilderness: May 5-6, 1864 comes with the latest version (1.5) of the series rules.

—description from the publisher

name: Wildflower
description:
Wildflower immerses players in the world of competing bee colonies, where you serve as the leader of two bustling Hives. This domino-based card game captures the essence of bee society through colorful artwork and thematic mechanics that reflect the industrious nature of these vital pollinators. Players command different types of bees - from honey-producing economy bees to fierce offensive wasps - each serving a unique role in your thriving ecosystem.

Gameplay: The game revolves around a structured five-phase turn system of resource generation, management, and strategic attacks. Players begin each turn by collecting honey from their economy bees, then pay upkeep costs for bees in their Garden area. The shop phase allows card acquisition, with powerful Wildflower cards providing additional draw opportunities. During the garden phase, players deploy new bees either to their Garden (requiring ongoing upkeep) or directly to their Hives (upkeep-free but limited space). The attack phase uses domino-style matching mechanics, where players chain together matching bee types to create devastating combination attacks.

Goal: Victory comes through tactical destruction - players must reduce one of their opponent's two Hives from 35 health to zero. This requires a balance between defensive positioning and offensive aggression, as players must protect their own Hives while building the card combinations necessary to breach their opponent's defenses. The dual-Hive system adds strategic depth, forcing players to spread their defensive resources while choosing which enemy Hive to target for maximum impact.

—description from the publisher

name: Wildscape
description:
In Wildscape, you will restore barren lands in Africa with rich habitats -- woodlands, wetlands, savanna, deserts, and rivers -- to create areas for a diverse animal ecosystem to return and to thrive.

Each player must expand their land and fill it with specific habitat tiles based on the needs of both common (but variable) objective cards and personal goal cards acquired throughout the game. Your habitats' size and type will attract various herbivores that grant end-game points and will support predators and primates that give powerful bonuses. You will hire specialists for their on-going effects to accelerate your revitalization effort in unique ways. The backbone of all of this is an action selection system on the community roundel where each space contains a unique combination of possible actions. Driven by this choice, action tokens cascade around the roundel creating an ever-changing strength for these actions throughout the game.

The winner will be the one who develops the most valuable ecosystem of herbivores, predators, primates, birds, and indigenous fauna.

—description from the publisher

name: Windmill Valley: Duel
description:
The sun rises over the tulip fields in the valley, where tall windmills stand against the horizon and ships wait to carry your blooms across the sea. In Windmill Valley Duel, two rival horticulturists compete for prestige, wealth, and victory by cultivating the finest tulips, investing in powerful enhancements, and claiming the most strategic ports in this vibrant and picturesque land. In this valley, you are not alone. Your windmill’s gears interlock with your opponent’s, forcing every decision you make to send ripples through the land while setting your rival’s plans in motion. Will you offer them an advantage to gain the edge you need, or will you wait for the perfect move? 
Plant your tulips with care. Build your windmills with purpose. Navigate the seas for trade. In a world where beauty and timing reign supreme, only the best horticulturist blooms victorious!

—description from the publisher

name: Elemystic
description:
Elemystic is a 9-card duel of harnessing chaotic elements. Harness the power of the elements in a fast-paced battle of strategy and intuition!  Draft, play, and combine elemental forces to outmaneuver your opponent in a contest of strength and skill. Will you master the balance of fire, water, air, and shadow — or be consumed by chaos? Every round offers new tactical decisions.

In Elemystic, players are elementals in a contest of wills, clashing over which will rule the elements. Call on the strengths of each element to defeat your opponent and claim your right to rule!

Elemystic is played over several rounds. Your goal is to reduce your opponent’s Energy to 0 first, using the elements you play.

—description from the publisher

name: Wishland: The Card Game
description:
Wishland, The card game  is a compact version of Wishland.  It is played over a series of turns.

There are 5 different types of cards and each one of theme scores differently at the end of the game.

    Rides: Provide victory points depending on the total number of rides played in all parks
    Actors: Provide victory points depending on the total number of actors played on their park.
    Restaurants: Provide victory points depending on the total number of cards played on their park. Short parks gives more points.
    Hotels: Provide victory points depending on the total number of cards played on their park. Large parks gives more points.
    Mascots: Provide victory points depending on the number range where the mascot card is played.


Every turn, each player will lay down a card from their hand to build their park. The game ends when all players have laid down 10 cards (10 turns) or a player can not legally lay down a card on his turn.

Each player score the cards they have played. The winner is the player with the most victory points.

—description from the designer

name: Witch Hunter
description:
Witch Hunter is a solo card game where you step into a land choked by curses, crawling with monsters, and abandoned by hope. As a Witch Hunter, driven by grim resolve, you take on contracts no one else survives. Trading pain, preparation, and willpower to hold the darkness at bay. Every hunt is brutal and personal, where steel, alchemy, and hard choices decide whether the land is cleansed or claimed by terror.

Each Monster you face is a living threat, fueled by dread and corruption that spreads across the world as Doom. Left unchecked, the Monster’s influence grows stronger, warping the battlefield with curses, minions, and escalating horrors. The longer a hunt drags on, the more desperate it becomes—forcing you to decide when to press the attack, when to endure, and when to sacrifice safety for victory.

In Witch Hunter, you begin by choosing a Witch Hunter and an Aspect that defines your approach, then shuffling those two decks together to form your personal deck. Next, select a Monster to hunt, each with its own deck, mechanics, and escalating terror. Each round, you play cards by discarding others to pay their cost, balancing offense, defense, and threat management as the Monster attacks, terrorizes, and unleashes minions. Win by slaying the Monster and breaking its grip on the land. Fail, and the world falls one hunt closer to oblivion.

-description from designer

name: Wiz'N'Bang
description:
Wiz’N’Bang is a card-drafting, dice-rolling and tower-building game where players take on the role of a grumpy old wizard attempting to construct the perfect tower on the perfect hill. The only problem: every other wizard trying to do the same.

Players take turns drawing cards, building their tower, playing spells and moving their wizard, all with the intention of building a tower seven cards high and getting their wizard to the top.

Make use of tower cards such as Cannons, Dragons, Portals and more to construct your tower one floor at a time in the most offensive or defensive way you please. Use spells such as Fireball, Counter, Deadeye and more to defend your tower against the nefarious machinations of your enemies.

Simple in concept but with amazing depth, Wiz’N’Bang brings together open drafting, tower building, dice rolling, meeple management, action distribution and spell casting into a delightfully small package that won’t break the bank or hog the table.

name: Star Realms: Deluxe Colonial Collection
description:
Get the ultimate travel version of the Star Realms Deckbuilding Game! The Deluxe Colonial Collection is an all-foil player card set with 4 high-quality score dials and game board in sturdy magnetically sealed box!

The Colonial Collection features 234 foil cards. That includes foil versions of every card from Colony Wars, Scenarios, all 4 United Packs, Stellar Allies, and the Year 2 Promo Pack. Plus, you’ll get Alt Art Scouts and Vipers in the four included starter decks.

-description from developer

name: Wiñay Kawsay
description:
Machu Picchu has captivated the imagination of the world and academia alike. There's been plenty of theories about what its purpose could have been. Was it a lost city? Perhaps a citadel? Or maybe something else entirely? That is for you to decide!

In Wiñay Kawsay — roughly pronounced win-nyay cow-say — you will step into the shoes of historical scholars. Uncover artifacts, reexamine evidence, publish your histories, and navigate the impact of your actions on this enigmatic wonder. In the deeply competitive world of publish-or-perish academia, will you succeed in influencing perception of what Machu Picchu really was? Or will your theories be one of many forgotten attempts at unravelling this mystery?

In slightly more detail, over the course of the game you place researchers to pick up evidence cards across the site of Machu Picchu, then commit evidence cards to support different interpretations of Machu Picchu's past to win publications and bonuses, while also trying to mitigate your disturbance of the site by returning artifacts to the land.

—description from the publisher

name: Wombat Poo
description:
Did you know wombat poo is shaped like cubes? It’s true! In this game you take turns stacking poo cubes of different sizes onto a teetering tower. Choose the right time to score one point per cube in the tower and exit the round. But don’t wait too long, or the tower will fall over and you’ll score nothing!

—description from the designer

name: Wonderland's War Duel
description:
Wonderland's War Duel is a 2 player version of the original game with it's own twists and flavor. This tug-of-war inspired version of the classic bag builder has 3 win conditions instead of the "most points win" of the original. It plays in 60-90 minutes and takes up a fraction of the table space of Wonderland's War classic.

(Wonderland's War the original game we are referencing can be found here on BGG. It features bag building, area control, and card drafting. You take on one of the asymmetric characters in Wonderland and fight to be the leader after the war has concluded.)

In Wonderland's War you are building your bag of special powers to battle against other players that are also vying for control of Wonderland! Use strategy to prefect your choices and with a little luck the madness will be avoided and you will be victorious.

—description from the publisher

name: Work of Heart!
description:
Have you ever wanted to fall in love at a very legitimate and not-at-all-sketchy art university? In the year 19XX, Johnathan Dromathan invented Art. It went well. He then used the funds to open up the first art academy, which you - the player - are attending...just to ignore your education in the pursuit of "love."

GOAL

Romance the group's love interest of choice by gaining the most affection via end of game cards, maximizing stats, and successfully beating the romantic interest's current affection threshold.

GAMPEPLAY

At the beginning of the game, 2-4 players each agree upon a game mode and love interest, placing their pawns in the center of the map on the Quad space. Players then take turns rolling the movement dice and moving that many spaces landing on one of several different type of spaces, skipping over spaces that have players already occupying them.

After the 5th turn of the 5th round, play ends. The player with the most affection is the winner of the game and the love interest's heart!

-description from publisher

name: Castle Raisers
description:
The three little pigs are no longer so little, and as for the big bad wolf—well—it’s not just one, but an army. A house, even one of brick, has proven unable to repel the legions of wolves on the prowl, and so the pigs have turned to raising castles!

Little pigs, little pigs, let us come in!

Castle Raisers is a 2 to 4-player (incl. solo and coop modes) tile placement game with drafting elements that is played over twelve rounds. Each player drafts a tile, placing it on earlier one to build a vertical castle. As icons are covered, players activate one of five abilities: placing village tokens inside the castle to strengthen the other abilities, increasing prestige to earn victory points, placing fortification tiles to heighten the walls, dispatching wolves to attack other players’ castles, and pouring cauldrons of soup to repel the invaders.  
Players aim to prepare for the final wolf assault while simultaneously maximizing their final score by fulfilling the scoring conditions found on the village tokens. Balancing which walls need to be strengthened with which abilities need to be activated are the keys to victory.

Raise your castle walls before—we’ll huff and we’ll puff—being razed to the ground!

name: X-ODUS: Rise of the Corruption (Second Edition)
description:
X-ODUS: Rise of the Corruption – Second Edition is a cooperative sci-fi game that blends tactical exploration, asymmetric ship abilities, and dynamic threats into a rich, replayable experience. Explore a modular galaxy, reveal hidden systems, and uncover powerful signals left behind by a forgotten civilization. Face enemies that adapt and escalate. Manage time, navigate danger, and cooperate to survive.

Each ship offers a distinct role — some scouts, some brawlers, some support — all essential to the fleet. You’ll unlock upgrades, manage resources, and react to the unexpected, all while racing against an enemy that never stops advancing. The new edition features streamlined mechanics, faster setup, new visuals, and deeper narrative immersion.

In X-ODUS: Rise of the Corruption, players take on the role of starship captains united by a critical mission: to recover the Precursor Keys. These powerful sources of energy, left behind by the ancient Precursors, are the only force strong enough to seal the Main Rift and stop the spread of the Corruption that threatens to consume the galaxy.

To win the game, Ships must find and activate all the Precursor Keys on the Main Rift and defeat any Avatars that may reach the Main Rift after the final Key is activated.

If the Corruption tracker reaches the Rise of the Corruption before the Ships seal the Main Rift, or if the all your Ships are
defeated, the galaxy will fall to darkness, and the game is lost.

—description from the publisher

name: Last Lantern
description:
Last Lantern is a 2 to 4-player co-operative polyomino game with set-collection and bag-building elements. As residents of the canopy, players puzzle their way forwards to the now dimming last lantern by placing tiles. Rely on the powers of familiars to not give in to the isolating fog and—perhaps—discover a way to ward it off forever.

The game is played over seven to nine rounds. Players, without communicating, simultaneously choose one set comprised of a tile and a token. The tile is placed on the path before you, moving you closer to your goal, while gaining three different tokens that activate powerful abilities. Echoing the best co-ops, discover ways to communicate by analyzing both the board state and tokens in hand, bettering your group dynamic with each play.

—description from the publisher

name: Dragonarium
description:
Dragonarium is a tile-placement game with drafting and resource management elements. Players are welcomed into the Imperial Hatchery to construct the ideal dragon-arium. While placing tiles to make connected domains, make full use of elements circling the player board — an innovative resource mechanism — to breathe life into your dragons.

The game is played over twelve rounds. Each player drafts a tile with one or two land types, placing it to build their dragonarium out and up! Then choose one of the land types just placed to activate an element token (fire, water, wind, and light) circling the player board. As the token passes by a row or column, it provides the energy needed to hatch the dragons found on placed tiles.

Once ready to hatch, place a tile on top, releasing it into the dragonarium. The land where the dragon nests, however, allows players to further connect domains as the tile now shares the element of the placed dragon. Aside from being a robust (more traditional) spatial puzzle, Dragonarium challenges your timing for when and where to release your dragons so as to interweave their domains.

—description from the publisher

name: Yonder
description:
The ancients have granted you the charter you need to found a settlement on the distant shore. It is up to you to journey there, and turn the boatload of workers, resources, and food that will accompany you on your voyage into a sprawling settlement, and a thriving community.

Yonder is a mid-weight worker placement game. Over the course of five rounds, you will collect resources, gather food, and build your settlement at the edge of a mysterious city. Place your workers carefully, harnessing each species' special power to its fullest extent. Direct the expansion of your settlement, constructing the buildings you’ll need in order to thrive. Dispatch workers to other player's settlements where necessary, trading manpower for the use of their facilities. Meet with a steady stream of envoys, each of whom offer lucrative contracts, and cash in on as many as you can while trying to avoid unsustainable commitments. There are the challenges that await you over yonder.

—description from the designer

name: Malifaux (Fourth Edition)
description:
You have been with us through the deep, dark Soulstone mines of First Edition; out into the bloody streets of Second Edition; and finally ventured with us into the vast wilds of Third Edition. With each step, the game has built on the editions before it, making Third Edition the best iteration yet. Through it all, Malifaux has always emphasized putting Fate directly into the hands of the players.

Now, we ask you to pull on those threads of fate once again by joining the Malifaux Fourth Edition open beta! Our plan is to begin the open beta next week on April 21st and run it for the next several months, finalizing the new edition by Gen Con 2025!

—description from the publisher

Malifaux is a card-driven miniatures skirmish game set in the otherworldly titular city, where players compete to execute "schemes" and "strategies" rather than necessarily killing the opposition. The fourth edition brings improved and streamlined gameplay, with particular focus on speed of play and meaningful interaction with terrain.

—user summary

name: Shuffle Dungeons
description:
Shuffle Dungeons is a cooperative dungeon crawler for 1-4 Players. All players work together to fight monsters, build a route through the dungeons, and fight the boss waiting in their lair.

Players will loot and equip powerful items to survive the dangers that lurk around every corner. Fighting deadly monsters, crossing dangerous traps, unearthing mystical wards, and discovering powerful shrines are some of the many things to discover in the dungeon.

Defeat the boss to escape the dungeon and be victorious!

—description from the publisher

name: Zombicide: Dead Men Tales
publisher: asmodee; Fantasy Flight Games; Guillotine Games
description:
Fantasy Zombicide is back, and this time it’s a pirate invasion! Dead Men Tales brings the popular Zombicide gameplay to paradisiacal pirate islands, where gold is plentiful and grom flows freely. Command crews of humans, orcs, elves, and more as you face off against relentless zombie hordes. Fire cannons, swing from ropes, and fight for survival as the undead attack from every direction, including the sea itself!

Gamefound Campaign: https://gamefound.com/en/projects/asmodee/dead-men-tales

—description from the publisher

name: The Sheep
description:
The Sheep is a comedy-horror game where sheep have pushed humanity to brink of extinction. The Shepherds were founded to face this threat.

Work together with your fellow Shepherds to protect Caravans as they travel through the wilderness. Each Day is preparation for the unknown threat that will come at Night.

Simultaneous turn-based gameplay that features random events, individual character mats, and gear upgrades.

—description from the publisher

name: ¡Tierra a la Vista!
description:
Tierra a la Vista is a cooperative game for 2 to 4 players and 40 minute games, where we will become treasure hunters, crew members of a drifting ship trying to return to the mainland with their coffers as full as possible.

The game consists of 2 phases. A planning phase where players will move their characters around the ship collecting action points in the cannons, sails, spyglass, among others, that they will have to collect and then use in the exploration phase.

In the exploration phase, players will take turns drawing cards from the exploration decks trying to get treasures, avoid the weather and defeat the pirates, while they are running out of supplies and the ship suffers damage that will have to be repaired if they do not want to sink. All this using their action points in the best possible way.

The objective is to find in the depths of each deck the three map fragments that will take them back home.
You will win the game if you succeed, and if you have the required amount of treasure in your coffers. But if a crew member drowns, they run out of supplies, or the ship sinks, they will have failed, and their ship will be one more lost in the depths of the sea.

It will not be an easy task. Only cooperation, coordination and teamwork will bring you back.

Beware of Pirates!

The prototype of this game was awarded the "Best New Latin Game" award in the Quarantine Challenge 2020 organized by the game makers community in Mexico.

name: Écorcheurs! Skirmish Wargaming in the Hundred Years War
description:
Écorcheurs! is a new set of skirmish rules developed to fight small actions between retinues in the Hundred Years War - the series of conflicts fought between England (and her allies) and France (and her allies) from 1337 to 1453, ostensibly over the right of the kings of England to the throne of France.


     Ideal for smaller tables, and between 20 and 40 15mm to 28mm figures per side.
     Scenario-driven and narrative in nature.
     Focus on the leader’s ability to command, and the warrior’s prowess in combat.
     Innovative melee rules that reflect the back and forth of medieval combat, the strength of armour, and the chaos of the field.
     Rewards tactical thinking, and encourages a chivalric mindset.


Rulebook will provide the rules, suggested retinues, as well as scenarios and a mini-campaign centered on Edward III's 1346 campaign, the one that led to the battle of Crécy.

Although the Écorcheurs rules are for the Hundred Years War, they’re not tied down to it. They’re more flexible than that. The armour classes – fully armoured, part-armoured, and unarmoured – aren’t period specific. Fully armoured is fully armoured, whether it’s full mail or gothic plate. And a bow is a bow is a bow... so long as you’re not putting wildly different period warbows up against each other.

—description from the publisher
